title: rf/route-link raises :rf.error/no-frame-context on first render — every example that renders one fails to boot at tip d1e6a707a3
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 02:55 AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, running the operator half of docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/workspace.md. Tip d1e6a707a3.

SYMPTOM. A browser build that renders `rf/route-link` anywhere in its tree throws on first render and mounts NOTHING — #app innerHTML length 0, blank page. The throw is a CLJS ExceptionInfo carrying [:rf.error/no-frame-context], :operation :route-link, :recovery :supply-frame, :where re-frame.routing.link/route-link-render. React reports it as 'An error occurred in the <re_frame.core_routing.route_link> component'.

The message text is the standard no-frame-context ladder: 'a frame-scoped route-link ran with no frame context — no carried frame stamp and no established scope...'.

MEASURED ACROSS FOUR APPS, all compiled with 'npx shadow-cljs compile <build>' from implementation/ in a clean full clone of this tip (own node_modules, npm install exit 0), then served as static files over a local HTTP server and loaded in headless Chrome via playwright-core. Every serve root carried index.html, main.js, cljs-runtime/ and examples/_shared/, and every run reported ZERO failed requests, so nothing here is an asset or 404 artefact.

  FAILS  :examples/routing            (examples/capabilities/routing/routing/) — the canonical routing example, 10 route-link sites
  FAILS  :examples/realworld          (examples/real-apps/realworld_http/)     — pilot 1's application
  FAILS  linearlite                   (examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/) — pilot 2's application, 1 route-link site
  BOOTS  :examples/login              (examples/core/login/)                   — no route-link; #app 643 chars, renders 'Sign in', 0 errors

The login row is the instrument control: the same harness, the same serving method, the same tip, exit 0. So the harness is sound and the discriminator is the presence of a route-link, not the build or the server.

NOT A WORKSPACE ARTEFACT. The failure reproduces identically in-repo (the repo's own shadow-cljs build, the example's own unmodified index.html, all _shared assets present, 0 failed requests) and in a pilot workspace built from :local/root per workspace.md. Both routes, same error, same :where.

NOT A URL ARTEFACT. Loading '/' and '/index.html' fail identically, so it is not the missing SPA push-state fallback.

STRUCTURE LOOKS CORRECT AT THE CALL SITES. realworld_http/core.cljs mounts [rf/frame-root {:id :rf/default ...} [root-view]] and every route-link sits inside a reg-view under root-view; linearlite/core.cljs has the same shape at core.cljs:630. So this is not an obviously mis-wired application — which is what makes three independent applications failing the same way read as a framework regression rather than three app bugs.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE EXAMPLES. It blocks rf2-t4jpz at hour zero: workspace.md step 5 is an OPERATOR boot check that must pass with the app still on Reagent BEFORE a pilot agent is dispatched, and it fails for BOTH ratified pilots. rf2-hic-063's 2026-09-02 ruling makes that check a precondition of dispatch. It also removes outcome 2's baseline — pilot 1's brief tells the agent 'it works today. Run it before you change anything', which is false at this tip.

NOTE THE BEHAVIOURAL SUITES DO NOT CATCH IT. Both pilot baselines are green at this tip (realworld 4 tests / 123 assertions exit 0; linearlite 10 tests / 51 assertions exit 0). They drive events and read subscriptions without rendering, so a render-time route-link failure is invisible to them. Examples are test-free by policy and the browser smoke coverage is one adapter-level smoke per adapter, so nothing currently renders these three apps in CI.

REPRODUCE. From a clean clone at this tip: cd implementation && npm install && npx shadow-cljs compile :examples/routing; then serve out/examples/routing/ together with examples/capabilities/routing/routing/index.html and examples/_shared/ and open it. Expect a blank page and the ExceptionInfo above. Control: the same procedure on :examples/login renders 'Sign in'.

FILED, NOT FIXED — the rehearsal is a harvest task and re-frame.routing / implementation are held by live workers.
notes:
SHARPENED 2026-09-03 03:10 AUSEST, same rehearsal, and this CORRECTS a reading in the description above.

THE RULE IS EXACT: route-link fails whenever it actually RENDERS. Not 'these apps are broken', not 'dev builds are broken'. Dev and release both fail; the discriminator is solely whether a route-link is on the screen being rendered.

THE DECISIVE PAIR — ONE BUILD, ONE SERVER, TWO URLS. linearlite's release bundle (npx shadow-cljs release app, exit 0, 217 files, 0 warnings), served as static files, loaded twice:

  /             -> matches :linearlite.app/board, board-page renders, NO route-link on screen
                   BOOTS. #app innerHTML 2295 chars, 0 page errors, full board text renders
                   ('Linearlite — optimistic issue board', the three status columns, the
                   armed-failure toggle).

  /index.html   -> matches no route, so root-view falls through to not-found-page, whose
                   single route-link (core.cljs:591, {:to :linearlite.app/board}) renders
                   FAILS. #app innerHTML 0, 1 page error, the same [:rf.error/no-frame-context].

Nothing differs but the URL. That is the cleanest possible isolation and it is why the earlier
'linearlite FAILS' row needs qualifying: the application is fine, the component is not.

THE DEV/RELEASE AXIS IS A RED HERRING — I RAISED IT AND IT IS WRONG. It looked briefly as though
the guard might be a development-only assertion elided by :advanced, because linearlite's release
booted where its dev build had not. That comparison was mine and it was invalid: I had loaded the
dev build at /index.html and the release at /. Corrected, the guard fires under :advanced too —
realworld's release build (exit 0, 332 files, 1.66MB) raises the identical error with the identical
:where. Recording the false trail because it is the natural first hypothesis and the next person
should not spend the same run on it.

FULL MATRIX at tip d1e6a707a3, every row a captured exit code and a headless-Chrome load:

  app                              route-link on loaded screen   build     result
  examples/core/login  /           no (app has none)             dev       BOOTS  (#app 643, 'Sign in')
  examples/capabilities/routing /  yes (10 sites)                dev       FAILS
  examples/capabilities/routing /  yes                           release   FAILS
  realworld_http  / and /index.html yes (navbar, every screen)   dev       FAILS
  realworld_http  /                yes                           release   FAILS
  linearlite  /                    NO                            release   BOOTS  (#app 2295)
  linearlite  /index.html          yes (not-found-page)          release   FAILS

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE FIX. The failing path is the render of re-frame.routing.link/route-link-render
itself, not application wiring, not the frame-root, not the build mode, and not the workspace. Any
application that puts a route-link on screen — which is every routed application — cannot render at
this tip.

WHAT IT CHANGES FOR THE PILOTS. Pilot 1 is blocked outright: realworld's navbar carries route-links on
every screen, so no screen renders. Pilot 2's board route happens to avoid the one site, so its board
DOES render and pilot 2 has a usable baseline screen — but its card-detail work (the authoring half,
which the ruling calls the more important of its two jobs) requires routing to and from a new screen,
which is exactly the surface that fails.

NOTE ON PRIORITY. Filed P0 on the strength of 'no example renders'; the sharpened rule does not soften
it — a routed application cannot show a link to another route.
MAYOR TRIAGE 2026-09-03 03:2x AUSEST. THIS IS THE TOP OF THE DISPATCH QUEUE AND THE ONLY P0 ON THE BOARD.

WHY I AM NOT DISPATCHING IT THIS MINUTE, stated so nobody reads the delay as a judgement about severity: the fleet ceiling is 6 (Mike, in his own words) and all six slots are live. I will not displace a running worker to make room — killing live work strands uncommitted changes, which is the one thing the stranded-sweep rule forbids building around. Three of the six have been running over an hour, so a slot frees on its own; this bead takes it, ahead of every P2 already queued.

WHAT MAKES THIS REPORT UNUSUALLY CREDIBLE, and worth saying because a P0 filed by a rehearsal agent deserves scrutiny rather than reflex: it carries an INSTRUMENT CONTROL. :examples/login has no route-link and BOOTS on the same tip, same harness, same serving method, #app 643 chars, 0 errors — while three apps that DO render a route-link mount nothing at all. So the discriminator is isolated to the presence of a route-link rather than to the build, the server, the assets or the clone. It also rules out two artefact classes explicitly: it reproduces both in-repo and in a :local/root pilot workspace, and "/" and "/index.html" fail identically, so it is not the missing SPA push-state fallback. Zero failed requests on every run.

A POINTER, EXPLICITLY NOT A DIAGNOSIS. I ran one cheap history read and stopped there, because a plausible-looking candidate stated confidently is how this project has burned itself before. Commit aa9e90af7f "hicasso: retire hframe; core admits the pure frame doors inside a refusing extent (rf2-6c12m.13, rf2-t32wg)" is the most recent change touching frame-context admission that a -S search over no-frame-context surfaces. That is a place to START a bisect, nothing more. DO NOT TREAT IT AS THE CAUSE. The honest first step is the bisect the bead earns: find the commit at which :examples/routing stops booting, using the login example as the control at every step.

WHAT THE FIXING WORKER MUST NOT DO: do not "fix" this by wrapping the call sites in a frame context. Three independent applications, each already mounting [rf/frame-root {:id :rf/default ...} [root-view]] with every route-link inside a reg-view under root-view, is the shape of a framework regression, not three app bugs. If the applications turn out genuinely wrong, that is a finding and a much bigger one.

IT ALSO BLOCKS rf2-t4jpz AT HOUR ZERO: workspace.md step 5 is an OPERATOR boot check that must pass with the app still on Reagent before a pilot agent is dispatched, and it fails for both pilots. So the pre-pilot rehearsal cannot proceed past its own first gate until this lands.

FIXED 2026-09-03 by PR #9050 (worker routelink-a). Root cause, bisect and the
browser evidence are on the PR; the load-bearing findings are recorded here so a
fresh maintainer needs nothing else.

BOTH BRIEFED MECHANISMS ARE REFUTED, and the reproduction refutes them by itself.
:examples/routing's root-view is a reg-view whose body is an AMBIENT
@(subscribe [:rf.route/id]) with no explicit frame, and it renders BEFORE any
route-link. The raised error names :operation :route-link / :where
re-frame.routing.link/route-link-render, never a subs site — so the ambient
resolution in root-view had already SUCCEEDED through the React-context tier that
frame-root establishes. The scope was present and readable (refuting "frame-root
no longer establishes the scope"), and require-current-frame! admitted it for
every reg-view in the tree (refuting "the admission changed").

THE CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL, one level up from both. rf/route-link is a defwrapper
(re-frame.core-routing), so its body is (apply <hook-fn> args) — an ORDINARY
FUNCTION CALL. The :routing/route-link hook carried the registered :route/link
view HEAD, so that head ran INSIDE the component the substrate mounted for
rf/route-link itself, instead of becoming a component of its own. A plain Reagent
fn carries no {:contextType frame-context}, so (.-context cmp) was React's empty
default, views.provider/current-frame resolved nil, and route-link-render's
render-time require-current-frame! raised. This is precisely the failure mode
re-frame.views.provider/current-frame's own docstring already describes for plain
fns; nobody had noticed rf/route-link was one.

FIX: publish an element-emitting shim. The hook now returns
[(views/view-head :route/link) props & children], so the head reaches the
substrate as an element TYPE and is componentized exactly as a reg-view view is —
[rf/route-link ...] and [home-page ...] now take one path. The head is resolved
per render through view-head rather than closed over, because it is a property of
(registration x installed substrate) and the reg-view* seed is taken at ns-load
before rf/init! seats an adapter (rf2-8mkmb). SSR untouched. Confined to
implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc; no call site was wrapped in a
frame context, and none needed to be.

THE BISECT POINTER IN THE TRIAGE NOTE WAS WRONG, and by two and a half months.
aa9e90af7f (2026-08-30) is NOT the cause. The break is fda84bb117 (2026-06-16),
"fix(routing): route-link click carries the render-time frame (rf2-o3nam4)" — the
commit that introduced the render-time require-current-frame! into link.cljc. A
-S pickaxe over that symbol scoped to link.cljc returns EXACTLY ONE commit and the
count goes 0 -> 2 across it. Measured in the browser at both ends with
:examples/login as the control (the example lived at examples/reagent/routing/
before the #4999 reorg):
  1e443dde7a (fda84bb117^)  routing BOOTS  #app 267, 0 page errors ; login 627
  fda84bb117                routing FAILS  #app 0, the identical
                            :rf.error/no-frame-context :where route-link-render ; login 627
Note what that dating means: examples/capabilities/routing/routing/ did not exist
at fda84bb117, and realworld_http / linearlite did not exist at all. The routing
example was born into a tree that already carried the defect — this was never a
recent regression.

BROWSER ACCEPTANCE (headless Chromium, static serve, 0 failed requests every run):
  :examples/routing   before  #app 0    1 page error   / after  #app 268, 0 errors
  :examples/login     before  #app 643  0 errors       / after  #app 643, 0 errors  (control, unmoved)
  :examples/realworld  (pilot 1) after  #app 2350, navbar renders, 0 errors
  :examples/linearlite (pilot 2) after  #app 3535, 0 errors
  linearlite /index.html (the bead's decisive pair, the not-found-page route-link)
                       after  #app 274 "Not found / Back to the board", 0 errors
The link also NAVIGATES: clicking "See the articles" moves / -> /articles and
re-renders, 0 page errors — so rf2-o3nam4's render-time frame capture, which
fda84bb117 existed to add, still works.

THE DURABLE REGRESSION, and why the old coverage could not catch its own case.
EVERY pre-existing route-link suite calls routing/route-link-render directly and
establishes the frame with rf/with-frame — the DYNAMIC-VAR tier, which answers
from anywhere. Not one mounts [rf/route-link ...] through a substrate, so all of
them were green about a component no application could render. New file
implementation/routing/test/re_frame/route_link_frame_context_dom_cljs_test.cljs
adds two rows in the :browser-test lane (unguarded PR-time job in test.yml) that
mount through the Reagent adapter into a real document with :ambient-frame nil,
establishing the frame ONLY through a React-context boundary — frame-provider in
one row, frame-root in the other. Proven to bite: reverting only routing.cljc to
its pre-fix blob and re-running gave exit 1 with exactly 2 failures, both the new
rows, both reporting container innerHTML = "" — the blank-page signature — while
the other 774 tests were unmoved.

GATES (exit codes captured from each runner): test:browser 776 tests / 4211
assertions 0F 0E exit 0; routing clojure -M:test 554 / 3454 0F 0E exit 0;
test:cljs 11193 / 55780 0F 0E exit 0; test-fast-pr.sh exit 0. test-fast-pr
--plan prints "No browser, bundle, adapter, Xray, MCP or tool-JVM gate is in any
tier" for this diff, which is this bead's thesis restated by the tool: the spine
cannot see this class of bug, which is why the regression is in the browser lane.

NOT FIXED, DELIBERATELY: rf2-6sqv obstructed the diagnosis exactly as the brief
predicted — the raw ExceptionInfo reaching console.error showed only
{meta: null, cnt: 7, arr: Array(14), ...}. Worked around locally by pr-str-ing
inside the (uncommitted, out-of-repo) measurement harness. Follow-on filed for the
defwrapper sharp edge underneath this: rf2-nvcp's cause generalises to any
late-bound hook whose value is a COMPONENT but whose wrapper CALLS it.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #9050. rf/route-link now renders as a component (the :routing/route-link hook emits [(views/view-head :route/link) props & children]) instead of being called as a function, so the frame-root's React context reaches it. Browser acceptance: :examples/routing #app 0 -> 268 with 0 page errors, :examples/login control unmoved at 643/0 before and after; realworld (2350) and linearlite (3535) both boot, and linearlite /index.html — the bead's decisive pair — renders its not-found route-link at 274. Durable regression added in the browser lane (route_link_frame_context_dom_cljs_test.cljs, 2 rows) and proven red against the pre-fix blob. Bisect: the break is fda84bb117 (2026-06-16, rf2-o3nam4), NOT the triage note's aa9e90af7f. Follow-on rf2-02w1 filed for the defwrapper sharp edge underneath. Note beads close on PR-open in this repo; #9050 is open and green-pending, not yet merged.

title: hic: workspace.md step 6 says copy the brief FROM brief-<pilot>.md, not the block INSIDE it — a literal copy hands the blinded pilot 4 bead ids and a link to the operator page
notes:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, operator half, re-run after PR #9050 and #9049. Workspace pin cfcc30ae93. This is a BLINDING LEAK on the dispatch path and should be fixed BEFORE the two pilots are dispatched.

THE DEFECT. workspace.md step 6 reads: "Copy the brief and the blank log into <pilot-root>/, from brief-realworld.md or brief-linearlite.md, and from friction-log.md's template section." Note the asymmetry inside that one sentence. For the friction log it names the SUB-PART ("template section"). For the brief it names the WHOLE FILE. But brief-realworld.md's own line 3 says "Copy the block below into <pilot-root>/BRIEF.md. Everything inside it is written to the pilot agent and is the only thing that agent is given" -- the pilot's brief is the content of the fenced markdown block, not the file.

So an operator executing step 6 literally runs "cp brief-realworld.md <pilot-root>/BRIEF.md" and hands a BLINDED pilot all of the following, none of which is inside the fence:

  1. Four tracker ids -- rf2-v04s, rf2-hic-063, rf2-xkhul, rf2-lpfz -- where the read fence's "Not allowed" column explicitly bars "Reading the tracker, git log, or any branch".
  2. A relative link to README.md#what-governs-this-directory -- the governance page, under docs/design/, out of bounds by the fence's own mkdocs rule.
  3. A relative link to workspace.md -- THE OPERATOR PAGE, of which workspace.md line 5 says "A pilot agent is never sent here". The pilot's own brief links it.
  4. The meta-paragraph explaining that the brief "is deliberately free of in-tree references" and that "a brief that leaks in-tree knowledge does not bend a rule, it invalidates the evidence the pilot exists to produce". That tells the pilot it is inside a blinding experiment being measured -- which is itself the leak the paragraph warns about.
  5. The enclosing markdown code fence, left as literal lines 11 and 157 of the delivered file.

MEASURED, BOTH PILOTS, AND THE TWO OPERATORS DIVERGED -- which is the evidence the instruction is ambiguous rather than merely terse:

  source brief-realworld.md ................ 8738 bytes, 4 bead ids
  my LITERAL step-6 copy ................... 8829 bytes, 4 bead ids, starts "# Brief -- Pilot 1: RealWorld/Conduit"
  the PREVIOUS rehearsal operator's copy ... 7066 bytes, 0 bead ids, starts "# Your brief"

The previous operator INTERPRETED step 6 and extracted the fenced block. I executed it literally and did not. Same page, same step, two different artefacts, and only one of them is blind. Both pilots are affected: the linearlite copy carries 2 bead ids by the same route.

WHY IT FAILS OPEN. The copy succeeds, exits 0, and produces a file that reads like a brief -- the pilot-facing content is all present and correct, just preceded by front matter. Nothing errors, nothing is missing, and the operator has no reason to look. The damage is invisible until somebody re-reads the delivered file, and by then the pilot has read it.

MINIMAL FIX, and it is one clause. Make step 6's brief half name the sub-part the way its friction-log half already does: "from the fenced block inside brief-realworld.md or brief-linearlite.md". Optionally add the same "Copy from here into <pilot-root>/BRIEF.md" pointer that friction-log.md's template section carries, so the two halves of step 6 are shaped alike. Do NOT restructure the briefs, move the front matter, or touch the fence -- the briefs are correct as written and say so themselves on line 3; it is workspace.md that under-specifies.

RELATION TO rf2-lpfz. Distinct. rf2-lpfz's reopened residue is pilots/README.md line 30, an operator-facing page a pilot never receives. This bead is about a pilot-facing artefact that step 6 mis-specifies, and it is the one that reaches the agent.

NOT A BLOCKER for the boot check or the baselines, both of which pass; see the rehearsal report on rf2-t4jpz. It IS a blocker for a CORRECT dispatch: per rf2-hic-063's revisit trigger (a), a leaky rehearsal finds no friction and is worthless, so dispatching on the literal artefact would burn both pilots.
close_reason: FIXED in PR #9058. workspace.md step 6 now names the sub-part for the brief exactly as it already did for the friction log: 'from the fenced block inside brief-realworld.md or brief-linearlite.md, and from the fenced block inside friction-log.md's template section', plus one sentence saying it is the block that is copied and why the front matter above it is a leak. The briefs' front matter, the fence and the briefs themselves are untouched, as the bead directs. PROVEN BY EXECUTION, not by reading: I ran the corrected step 6 literally against both briefs and the log template and asserted on the products -- realworld/BRIEF.md 7433 bytes/143 lines, linearlite/BRIEF.md 8967/170, FRICTION-LOG.md 1290/54, and all three carry 0 lines with a bead id, 0 links to workspace.md and 0 stray fence lines. The same three patterns run against the source pages as controls and all bite (brief-realworld.md 2/1/2, brief-linearlite.md 2/1/2, friction-log.md 6/4/6), so the zeroes are checks that passed rather than patterns that missed. Extraction boundaries checked at both ends. For contrast the pre-fix literal copy is 8738 bytes carrying 4 unique bead ids and a workspace.md link.

title: machines/SSR: hydration leaves pre-existing timers absent from the replacement snapshot
description:
## Scope

Repair the SSR-to-client handoff for state-machine `:after` transitions. The scope is active singleton and spawned snapshots under `[:rf.runtime/machines :snapshots]`, including flat/compound states, active paths in root-parallel regions, and a root-parallel `:after`. Keep ordinary transition semantics and epoch restore semantics unchanged.

## Correctness finding

The server intentionally suppresses machine wall-clock timers, but the client hydration path only installs the serialized runtime-db snapshot. It does not reconstruct the host-side timer table for active `:after` declarations and does not re-run machine entry. A machine hydrated while sitting in an `:after`-bearing state therefore has the right durable `:state`, `:data`, and `:rf/after-epoch`, but no live timer. It can remain in that state forever unless some unrelated external event moves it.

This contradicts the local contract that timers begin on the client after hydration. It is also the relevant conformity lesson from XState v6 persistence: durable state and host work are distinct, and restoring a snapshot must explicitly reconstruct the timer runtime without replaying historical effects.

## Evidence

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc` (`build-after-fx`, around lines 2059-2144) emits `:rf.machine/after-schedule` only while processing newly-entered nodes. In server mode the effect carries `:server? true` and the timer is skipped.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/timer.cljc` keeps timer handles/watchers in a process-local timer table; they are not part of the hydration payload.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc` (`hydrate-event-handler*`) installs the payload's runtime-db and has one late-bound reconciliation hook for Resources. There is no Machines hydration/re-arm hook or machine scheduling effect.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc` inventories Machines hooks for SSR projection, timer cleanup on frame destroy/epoch restore, and timer scheduling, but no hydration reconstruction hook.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/ssr.cljc` projects durable machine snapshots only; it cannot carry host timer handles.
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md` lines 1323 and 2444-2448 say server timers no-op and the client schedules them after hydration.
- `spec/011-SSR.md`, section “`:after` is no-op under SSR”, requires `:after` timers to begin running on the client against the preserved snapshot epoch.
- `docs/machines/automatic-transitions.md` states: “The client re-arms timers after hydration.”
- XState v6's official persistence contract includes timers in the durable snapshot shape and restores without replaying historical entry effects: https://stately.ai/docs/xstate/v6/persistence and https://stately.ai/docs/xstate/v6/how-xstate-runs-machines . Exact comparison baseline: `xstate@6.0.0-alpha.50` (`0b52534e`), released 2026-08-27.

## Steps to Reproduce

### Failure scenario/invariant

Given a server-rendered machine whose active state declares `:after {5000 {:target :timeout}}`:

1. Server entry bumps/stores the node's `:rf/after-epoch`, emits the skipped-on-server trace, and schedules no host timer.
2. The hydration payload carries the active snapshot and epoch.
3. `:rf/hydrate` installs that snapshot on the client without entering the state.
4. No client timer exists, so advancing beyond 5000 ms never dispatches the synthetic elapsed event and the machine remains stuck.

Required invariant: after a successful client hydration commit, every live active `:after` declaration represented by the hydrated snapshot has exactly one client timer/watch armed for that snapshot's existing epoch, without replaying unrelated entry behavior.

## Recommended minimal fix

Add one hydration-only Machines reconciliation seam, analogous in ownership to the existing Resources hydration hook:

- Have the Machines artefact publish a late-bound hydration hook/effect that runs only after a valid client `:rf/hydrate` has committed the payload runtime-db.
- Walk the hydrated live snapshots, resolve each actor's registered/inline machine definition using existing resolver paths, enumerate only the currently active nodes (plus the root-parallel node), and schedule their declared `:after` entries through the existing timer scheduler.
- Reuse the persisted `:rf/after-epoch`; do not bump it.
- Resolve literal/function/subscription delays on the client. Because the wire does not carry a schedule timestamp or due-at value, arm the full declared client-relative delay, matching the repository's existing SSR contract.
- Do not re-run `:entry`, actions, raises, spawns, or other effects. Do not reuse the epoch-restore callback: epoch restore deliberately cancels host work and must continue not to revive it.
- Make repeated hydration/scheduling idempotent by the existing timer-table key or an equally small guard, so it never leaves duplicate handles/watchers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused hydration integration test registers an `:after` machine, produces/installs an SSR-shaped runtime-db snapshot, hydrates on a client frame, and proves exactly one timer is armed with the persisted epoch and its callback performs the declared transition.
- The test proves the timer was not armed on the server and that hydration does not re-run an entry action, raise, or spawn.
- Coverage includes a compound active path and root-parallel coverage sufficient to prove active region nodes and root-owned `:after` declarations are enumerated correctly.
- A dynamic subscription/function delay is resolved on the client through the existing scheduling path; watcher teardown/cancellation remains correct.
- Negative controls prove that a snapshot with no active `:after`, a rejected malformed/wrong-frame hydration, and a server-side hydrate arm no timers.
- Existing epoch-restore coverage continues to prove `:machines/on-frame-restored!` cancels timers and does not re-arm them.
- Existing timer traces remain coherent; hydration-created timers emit one normal scheduled trace (with actor, path/state, delay source, epoch, and frame) rather than a misleading state-entry replay.
- Relevant spec/docs wording and late-bind directory inventory match the implemented hydration-only seam.

## Non-goals

- A general durable workflow engine, snapshot migration framework, elapsed-time/due-at persistence, or cross-process clock reconciliation.
- Replaying all machine entry behavior during hydration.
- Reviving timers during epoch/time-travel restore.
- Serializing browser timer handles or subscription objects.
- Matching XState's actor API or persistence wire format.

## Related/duplicate search

All-status tracker searches covered titles/descriptions containing: `machine timer`, `after hydration`, `hydration timer`, `re-arm`, `rearm`, `skipped-on-server`, `after-epoch`, `hydrate`, `restore`, `SSR`, and `rf.runtime/machines`. AUDIT PR #8915: reopened after the three-lens review. The new hydration seam reconstructs every live declaration correctly, but it does not reconcile away host timers that are absent from the replacement snapshot. :rf/hydrate replaces runtime-db wholesale; timer/after-timers is separate host state. rearm-after-timers! only walks the newly installed snapshots and calls schedule-after-timer! for their active declarations. That function supersedes an old entry only when the new declaration has the same {actor, invoke-id, delay-key}; there is no frame-level cancellation or set difference. The idempotence test repeats the identical snapshot, so it proves only the same-key case.

A frame with a pre-hydration timer, or a documented direct second :rf/hydrate, can therefore replace an :after state with a no-:after state, remove an actor, or shrink a delay set while leaving the old host handle in after-timers. Literal handles linger until firing; subscription-delay entries can keep a reaction/watcher alive and reschedule. Epoch/active-path checks may suppress the eventual stale transition, but they do not release the host work or give the replacement operation coherent scheduled-to-cancelled tracing.

Minimal repair: after the payload runtime-db commit, reconcile this frame's timer table to the exact declaration keys enumerated from the installed snapshots: cancel entries not in that set, then retain/supersede or arm the live set. Preserve the client/payload/hook gates, existing epochs, no-entry-replay rule, and epoch-restore semantics. Add a changed-snapshot control (active :after to no :after or absent actor) and a dynamic-delay watcher/ref-count control; do not add a general persistence layer or public API.

AUDIT PR #8965: REOPENED exact owner; no duplicate.

Completeness: the regressions cover a synchronous /scheduled listener, but not the concurrent-cleanup boundary created by moving the reservation before the emit.

Correctness: on the JVM, any cleanup path can claim the token-owned sentinel after the after-timers reservation and before trace/emit!. claim-emit-release! emits /cancelled immediately. The arming thread then emits /scheduled; if the frame incarnation still owns the id (for example state exit, restore, actor cleanup, or supersede), owner-gone? remains false, the host arm is attempted, publication loses to the earlier claim, and no later row closes the now-last /scheduled. Frame destruction has the same cancelled-before-scheduled ordering, followed by a token-exact abort that finds nothing. The PR therefore trades the synchronous scheduled-without-cancelled orphan for a real JVM interleaving that yields /cancelled then orphan /scheduled, contradicting the pairing and ordering contract its tests assert.

Implementation quality: the existing token-owned sentinel remains the right small mechanism, but claimability and announcement are not coordinated. Minimal completion: add a deterministic controlled-interleaving regression at the reserve-to-emit boundary and make an attempt unable to publish cancellation before its /scheduled, while still ensuring every announced attempt is cancellable and host arming stays after the announcement. Preserve the existing trace vocabulary and public API; no general trace transaction framework.

So a JVM cleanup in that window published /cancelled ahead of the /scheduled it closes, and the arming thread's owner check still passed (state exit, actor destroy, restore and the frame-destroy sweep all leave the incarnation in place), so the host arm was attempted, publication lost, and the now-last /scheduled had nothing to close it. The new regression reproduced exactly that on the unmodified source before any fix was written: actual [:rf.machine.timer/cancelled :rf.machine.timer/scheduled], plus one wasted host arm — for every one of the four cleanup owners.

THE REPAIR. The token-owned sentinel stays the mechanism; the coordination rides on the reservation itself. The reservation gains an announcement cell (:announce, an atom, present ONLY when the arm emits its own /scheduled — the hydration re-arm and the dynamic-delay reschedule; an ordinary state-entry arm has no cell because the pure side announced it before the fx ran). A claimant that wins the sentinel CASes its reason into the cell (defer-to-announcer?): winning means the row is not yet out, so it releases the entry's resources as before and emits nothing; losing means the cell already reads ::announced, so it emits its own /cancelled exactly as before. The announcer, once trace/emit! has returned, CASes the same cell nil -> ::announced (announced!): winning means no claim reached the sentinel first and the existing recheck/arm path runs unchanged; losing means one did, so it emits the deferred /cancelled immediately after its /scheduled — stamped with the CLAIMANT's reason — and arms nothing. Whichever CAS lands second reads the other's verdict; neither side waits. A claim made ON the announcing thread — a synchronous listener on the row — bypasses the cell through *announcing*, a dynamic set of tokens bound around the emit, because for it the row is already out. That last part is load-bearing rather than decoration: a listener that destroys A, publishes same-id B and hydrates the same snapshot into B re-arms the same key, and B's /scheduled is indistinguishable from A's by (actor-id, state, epoch), so an A /cancelled deferred past it would read as B's closure. git diff -w on timer.cljc is 116 insertions / 10 deletions, about 17 of them code; the raw 264/158 is a one-column shift of the abort/arm block under the new cond, and the ten non-whitespace deletions are exactly the lines this change replaces — nothing of passes two, three or four is reverted (read from the deletions of git diff -w origin/main...HEAD directly).

THE RULES FROM PRIOR ROUNDS, EACH KEPT AND STILL PINNED. owner-gone? is captured once per reconcile and threaded — the new clause captures nothing, and it does not consult the predicate because the claimant already decided the shared release under its own and the announcer releases nothing. The abort still releases nothing beyond the sentinel's nil handle and never-attached watcher; the shared (frame, query-v) decrement stays skipped (rf2-i4aj9c). The closed six-value :reason set (reply/timer-cancel-reasons) is unchanged and no trace event is added: the deferred row carries the claimant's own reason. No entry or cascade replay. :machines/on-frame-restored! is untouched, and the epoch lane is green. The host clock is still armed AFTER the /scheduled emit. Every announced attempt is cancellable from the instant it is visible — the sentinel is in the table before the row and claimability is never gated; only the EMISSION of a pre-announcement claim's row is coordinated. spec/005-StateMachines.md is untouched and no spec change is owed. No new public API; no trace transaction framework. Every existing tooth in machine_hydration_reconcile_incarnation_fence_cljs_test, machine_after_hydration_reconcile_cljs_test, machine_after_hydration_rearm_cljs_test, after_timer_arm_publish_race_cljs_test and machine_timer_incarnation_fence_cljs_test is green on both hosts.

A VERSUS B, WITH THE NUMBERS. (A) hand-off on the reservation — shipped: ~17 code lines; keeps every announced attempt cancellable and the arm behind the announcement; no new vocabulary; the regression drives the interleaving with a wrapped trace/emit! and a raw Thread joined at the row — no latch, no timeout. (B) announced?-gated claimability: the gate in claim-entry! (+2) and a post-emit swap (+3) are cheap, but a REFUSED cleanup has no "after" to re-check from — state exit runs once — so either (B-i) it spins until announced (JVM loop, +6; deadlocks for a same-thread claim inside the emit, so it needs the same thread mark anyway, +8; and the deterministic regression's second thread then blocks on the announcer, so the join deadlocks unless bounded by a timeout — which is what the audit ruled out), or (B-ii) it leaves a cancel request on the table entry for the announcer to honour (+6) — which is (A) with the reason travelling through the table slot, and that slot is overwritten by a same-key successor's assoc-in reservation on the listener's stack, so the deferred /cancelled is lost unless the reservation, publish and claim swaps all carry the mark forward (+4 each): 25-30 lines, more states, more places to get wrong. A thread marker in the cell (a fourth cell state) instead of the dynamic var was the same line count; the var reads better. No smaller mechanism was already present on the bead or in the code.

CONTROLS. New JVM-only namespace implementation/machines/test/re_frame/after_timer_announce_claim_race_test.clj (2 deftests, 50 assertions). a-claim-before-the-row-is-out-closes-the-row-rather-than-preceding-it wraps trace/emit! for one hydration and, on the attempt's own /scheduled row — sentinel reserved, row not yet delivered — runs the cleanup to completion on a raw Thread and joins it before the real emit proceeds; once per cleanup owner (frame destroy, epoch restore, actor destroy, state exit). It asserts the row order, exactly one of each row, the claimant's reason, the mirrored payload slots, an empty table and ZERO host arms. A raw Thread rather than a future on purpose: future conveys dynamic bindings, and the repair marks the announcing thread through one. a-same-thread-claim-from-the-rows-own-listener-closes-it-before-a-successor-announces is the control on the other side of that mark: a /scheduled listener destroys A, publishes same-id B and hydrates the same snapshot into B; the stream must read A /scheduled, A /cancelled (:on-frame-destroy), B /scheduled, with B's timer surviving A's abort. That control passes on the base too; it fails only under a cell-only design that defers every pre-consummation claim, which is why it is there. No CLJS mirror: the window needs a second thread, and the same-thread case is already pinned on both hosts.

SABOTAGE RESULT (the deliverable). With both commits in place, ONLY the source half was reverted to origin/main (git checkout origin/main -- implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/timer.cljc), the new regression left in place: machines JVM lane exit 1, 1241 tests / 4495 assertions — the SAME totals as the clean run, so no namespace was skipped or crashed — with 8 failures, all in a-claim-before-the-row-is-out-closes-the-row-rather-than-preceding-it: the row-order assertion for each of the four cleanup owners, printing actual [:rf.machine.timer/cancelled :rf.machine.timer/scheduled] — the audit's mechanism verbatim — and the zero-host-arms assertion for each, actual (not (zero? 1)). GREEN under the same revert: the same-thread control, every precondition, and every other machines test. Restored by checkout and verified by git BLOB hash against the committed object: 55da753f2eb300afd882654934d3379d8772ad40 before the plant, eb5b11fcf93e13b72759a6f89fea0cbd9d27b750 planted (equal to origin/main's blob for the path, and defer-to-announcer? absent from the working file), 55da753f2eb300afd882654934d3379d8772ad40 after the restore — identical to HEAD's.

title: migration: path lowering misclassifies custom */path interceptors
description:
## Scope

Repair the v1-to-v2 event-registration migration path where the shipped M-73 scanner/codemod encounters interceptor-bearing reg-event-db or reg-event-fx calls. Scope includes migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod, its focused tests/README, the directly coupled re-frame-migration reference/eval, and one focused integration proof against the actual v2 reg-event contract.

## Correctness finding

The guide promises that M-73 composes with M-70, but the implementation performs a head/handler-only rewrite and deliberately preserves every middle slot. For the canonical path-interceptor example it emits an rf/reg-event whose metadata still contains the removed inline (rf/path ...) call; for historical positional chains it emits a reg-event with the retired vector middle slot. Both outputs are invalid v2 and hard-fail while the namespace loads. The codemod then reports the site as :rewrite/:rename rather than an unresolved M-70 finding, so its green unit suite certifies a broken migration.

## Evidence

- skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md:482-505 tells users to prefer the shipped codemod and specifies the mechanical conversion from {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]} to {:interceptors [[:rf.interceptor/path [:counter]]]}.
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:883-903 calls the codemod first-class/tested and gives the same positional [(rf/path :counter)] to metadata-ref conversion.
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/src/re_frame/migration/reg_event_codemod.clj:31-33 instead states that path-interceptor metadata is preserved untouched. analyse-call at 301-342 classifies every reg-event-fx as a pure rename and simple reg-event-db solely by its last handler; it never analyses middle-slot shape or entries. apply-rewrite-at at 665-688 replaces only the registrar head and db handler.
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/test/re_frame/migration/reg_event_codemod_test.clj:102-114 and 125-134 explicitly assert that {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]} survives while the call is renamed to reg-event, pinning the invalid output.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1962-1983 makes rf/path a throwing removal stub (:rf.error/path-removed). implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:71-82 and 126-165 require interceptor refs and reject inline values with :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed; 803-837 rejects a positional vector middle slot with :rf.error/reg-event-bad-middle-slot.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the shipped codemod rewrite over this v1 source:

       (rf/reg-event-db :counter/inc
         {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]}
         (fn [db _] (update db :value inc)))

2. Observe that it reports :action :rewrite and emits reg-event while preserving {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]}.
3. Load/evaluate the emitted registration with the actual v2 re-frame.core namespace.
4. Observe the namespace-load hard failure :rf.error/path-removed before the handler registers. The positional-vector variant is also retained and is rejected as :rf.error/reg-event-bad-middle-slot; a custom inline value retained in metadata is rejected as :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed.

## Failure scenario / invariant

The current successful rewrite is:

    (rf/reg-event :counter/inc
      {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]}
      (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (update db :value inc)}))

Loading it against v2 calls the removed rf/path stub before the handler can register. A positional v1 chain is likewise left as the now-illegal vector middle slot, and a custom inline value carried into metadata is rejected by reg-event.

Invariant: every site the codemod reports as mechanically rewritten must be a valid v2 registration shape, or it must remain an explicit unresolved M-70 finding. A source transform is not successful merely because it parses and no retired registrar name remains.

## Recommended minimal fix

Teach the codemod one small middle-slot normalization that composes M-70 with M-73:

1. Recognize the standard path constructor in bare, positional-vector, metadata-interceptors, and metadata-plus-vector source shapes; lower each (rf/path p...) to [:rf.interceptor/path [p...]], create or merge the metadata map, and preserve chain order/comments.
2. Preserve entries that are already v2 refs.
3. For any other inline/bare interceptor whose stable registered id cannot be derived without author intent, emit an explicit M-70 Type-B finding and do not claim the event migration complete. Do not leave an invalid inline value hidden behind a successful M-73 result.
4. Scan both retired reg-event-* forms and already rewritten reg-event forms for these invalid middle-slot/inline survivors so a rerun can recover a partially migrated tree.
5. Replace the string-only preservation assertions with exact normalization tests plus a focused registration integration test using the actual v2 core.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A codemod test rewrites the canonical metadata source above to a reg-event containing exactly [:rf.interceptor/path [:counter]], with no executable rf/path call, and preserves the db-handler transformation.
- A codemod test rewrites a historical positional path vector and a metadata-plus-vector path chain into the one metadata-map :interceptors ref shape; multiple entries preserve declaration order.
- An executable integration test evaluates/registers the canonical transformed result against the actual v2 core and completes without :rf.error/path-removed, :rf.error/reg-event-bad-middle-slot, :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed, or :rf.error/unregistered-interceptor.
- Negative control: feeding the current preserved-inline output to that same integration harness deterministically throws :rf.error/path-removed (or the inline-value equivalent throws :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed), proving the test observes registration rather than only parsing/substring shape. Restoring the old preserve-middle behavior makes the positive test red.
- A custom inline interceptor with no stable id is surfaced as an unresolved M-70 Type-B finding and is not reported as a completed :rename/:rewrite; a rerun over an already-renamed invalid reg-event finds it.
- Non-vacuity controls show interceptor-free reg-event-fx still pure-renames, interceptor-free simple reg-event-db still performs its existing db wrap, already-canonical ref chains remain valid, and running the codemod twice is stable.
- Add a focused re-frame-migration eval fixture whose v1 event contains a path interceptor; its expected result uses the standard ref and the eval fails if the removed inline call or positional vector survives.
- The codemod unit suite and the focused runtime integration test pass.

## Non-goals

- No general Clojure analyser or arbitrary macro evaluation.
- No auto-naming or semantic re-authoring of custom interceptors; those remain M-70 Type B.
- No compatibility alias restoring rf/path, inline interceptor values, or positional reg-event chains in v2.
- No unrelated migration-rule rewrite, formatting cleanup, or broad runtime hardening.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status title and description searches were run for: M-73 codemod, reg-event codemod, path interceptor codemod, inline interceptor migration, rf.interceptor/path, middle slot codemod, preserved metadata interceptor, M-70, M-73, reg-event-db, and codemod. A full all-status issue export was also scanned across title/description/notes for the same vocabulary. No existing open, in-progress, blocked, deferred, or closed bead owns this codemod-output/runtime-registration mismatch. rf2-0qzh covered CI discovery/classification for the codemod, not transform correctness; reagent/hicasso codemod beads are different tools and surfaces.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Canonical metadata, positional-vector, and metadata-plus-vector path-interceptor inputs lower to metadata :interceptors entries of [:rf.interceptor/path <path-vector>] while preserving handler semantics and chain order.
2. The canonical transformed output is executed against actual v2 reg-event and registers successfully.
3. A negative-control fixture containing the old preserved inline rf/path output throws the expected hard error in that same harness; reverting the normalization makes the positive test fail.
4. Custom inline interceptors without a stable id become explicit unresolved M-70 Type-B findings rather than successful M-73 rewrites, including when found in an already-renamed reg-event.
5. Interceptor-free fx/db rewrites, already-canonical ref chains, and a second codemod run remain successful and stable.
6. A focused migration-skill eval rejects any answer/output that leaves rf/path executable or a positional interceptor vector in reg-event.
7. Focused codemod and runtime integration suites pass.

AUDIT PR #8828 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

Correctness: path-call-info identifies the standard re-frame constructor only by (= "path" (name hv)). It therefore treats every qualified custom function named path as rf/path. A deterministic probe on merged main with (app.interceptors/path :tenant) inside a real rf/reg-event-db returned :action :rewrite and emitted [:rf.interceptor/path [:tenant]], silently replacing the custom interceptor's semantics instead of producing the promised unresolved M-70 :flag :interceptors. This contradicts the PR's central boundary that only the standard constructor is mechanical and every other custom inline call stays unchanged for author intent. Existing tests cover a custom var, rf/debug, and a dynamic rf/path arg, but not a custom qualified function sharing the simple name. Minimal repair: resolve the call head to re-frame.core/path from the namespace's require/refer aliases, or conservatively flag ambiguous qualified path symbols; add a custom/path negative test while retaining the standard qualified/alias/bare fixtures and idempotence.

Implementation-quality/completeness: the new :integration alias is not invoked by .github/workflows/test.yml or scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh. PR checks ran only clojure -M:test, so the real-v2 registration proof and all four negative controls are currently manual/orphaned. Add clojure -M:integration to the existing changed-surface codemod CI job (keeping it separate from the self-contained :test classpath).

Duplicate search across all statuses for custom path interceptor, symbol named path, path alias codemod, and M-70 custom call found no separate owner. Both residues are exact acceptance/quality gaps in rf2-8odvg.
AUDIT PR #8846 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

Correctness/completeness: the new namespace resolver still treats namespace-level availability as call-site resolution. In a file that refers re-frame.core/path, a lexically shadowing `let` binding named `path` is therefore silently lowered as the framework constructor. Deterministic probe on merge b38d2e0: `(ns app.events (:require [re-frame.core :refer [reg-event-db path]])) (let [path app.interceptors/path] (reg-event-db ... {:interceptors [(path :tenant)]} ...))` returned `[:rewrite nil true]` — a successful rewrite containing `:rf.interceptor/path` — even though the call denotes the custom binding. This contradicts the implementation comment at lines 344-350 and the README guarantee that a local/custom path function flags rather than changes semantics.

Minimal repair: for bare `path`, account for lexical bindings at the interceptor call site, or conservatively refuse lowering when an enclosing scope binds `path`; add one deterministic local-shadow negative fixture plus idempotence. This does not require a general analyser. The separate orphaned integration-CI residue remains owned by rf2-36u96 and is not duplicated here.
REPAIRED 2026-09-01 12:14:32 AUSEST (worker, PR #8857, commit ae9a7d7e59). The reopen's probe was reproduced verbatim at branch base 4e27fbbe49 BEFORE any edit and returned [:rewrite nil true] — premise confirmed at source, not assumed. Root cause exactly as the note stated: path-head resolution was a per-SOURCE fact derived from the ns form (path-head-context), with no call-site half, so ns-level AVAILABILITY stood in for what a bare head DENOTES.

FIX: reused the in-file machinery rather than adding a second mechanism. The free-occurrence analysis already carried a binding-form vocabulary (binding-vector-forms, seq-binding-forms, collect-binding-names); that vocabulary is hoisted into one shared section above both consumers, and a new enclosing-scope-binds? walks OUT from the registrar call over the same table. The two analyses now ask opposite questions in opposite directions over one vocabulary. Added the defn family (defn/defn-/defmacro), whose params scope over a registration in the body and which the downward walk had no reason to know. standard-path-head? consults the new :shadowed-bare-path? for BARE heads only — a namespace-qualified symbol names a var and cannot be shadowed by a local.

Conservative refusal, as the note permitted: an enclosing binder routes the site to the existing :flag :interceptors (unresolved M-70 Type B) and leaves the source byte-for-byte unchanged. Position-insensitive inside a binding vector, and an unreadable binding vector counts as binding the name — both errors can only produce a flag where a lowering was possible, never a silent semantic swap.

EVIDENCE (exits captured in the same shell as each run): probe [:rewrite nil true] -> [:flag :interceptors false] with the source byte-identical. clojure -M:test exit 0, 72/245 -> exit 0, 77/276. clojure -M:integration exit 0, 6/10 both sides. NON-VACUITY: one-line revert ((not shadowed-bare-path?) -> true) gives captured exit 1 with 25 failures falling in exactly the three new shadow deftests, at unchanged 77/276 totals so nothing was skipped; the two non-over-reach controls (qualified head inside a shadowing let still lowers; a sibling-form path binding does not suppress the site) stayed green. Restore verified by git blob hash against the committed object, not by reading a diff.

Tests added: shadowed-bare-path-flagged-not-lowered (the audit probe), shadowed-bare-path-flagged-across-binding-forms (let / if-let / fn / defn / letfn / doseq), shadowing-does-not-suppress-a-qualified-head, shadowing-elsewhere-does-not-suppress-a-referred-bare-path, shadowed-bare-path-idempotent. README's path-resolution guarantee updated to state the call-site half; its gate is check_doc_slugs.py, NOT check_readme_links.py (migration/ is in the latter's DOCS_GATE_ROOTS exclusion and in the former's DEFAULT_ROOTS) — established by planting a broken link: docs gate exit 1 naming file and line, readme gate exit 0.

The orphaned-integration-CI residue is rf2-36u96's, landed as the second commit of the same PR.
AUDIT PR #8857 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

Correctness: the lexical-shadow repair recognizes only unqualified binding-form heads. A valid qualified macro such as `clojure.core/let` is absent from `binding-vector-forms`, so `enclosing-scope-binds?` misses its local `path`. Deterministic probe at merge db8949e406: `(clojure.core/let [path app.interceptors/path] (reg-event-db ... {:interceptors [(path :tenant)]} ...))` returned `[:rewrite nil]` and emitted `[:rf.interceptor/path [:tenant]]`, silently replacing the custom interceptor. The same checkout evaluates `(clojure.core/let [path (fn [x] [:custom x])] (path :tenant))` as `[:custom :tenant]`, proving the source form is valid rather than synthetic.

Minimal repair: normalize recognized binding heads by simple name only when they resolve to clojure.core, or explicitly include their qualified clojure.core spellings; retain conservative refusal for ambiguous/custom macros. Add a qualified-let negative fixture plus the existing bare and sibling controls. All-status searches for `clojure.core/let`, qualified/namespaced binding forms, qualified binders, and `enclosing-scope-binds?` found no separate owner; this is the exact unresolved lexical-shadow acceptance boundary of rf2-8odvg.
REPAIRED 2026-09-01 (worker, PR #8896, commit b57bbac2f2). Scope: the AUDIT PR #8857 reopen only — the newest text-bearing mutation on this bead, established by walking bd history newest-first to the bead beginning (394 entries, 5 text-bearing changes, oldest entry notes-length 0 so the walk reached creation). The DESCRIPTION is historical: its central premise (head/handler-only rewrite, every middle slot preserved) was discharged by the three merged PRs #8828 / #8846 / #8857, and the two sibling acceptance items were confirmed present at tip — the migration-skill eval fixture in skills/re-frame-migration/evals/evals.json, and clojure -M:integration wired into .github/workflows/test.yml.

PREMISE CONFIRMED AT SOURCE, NOT ASSUMED. The audit probe was reproduced verbatim at branch base a272031831 BEFORE any edit: the clojure.core/let form returned [:rewrite nil] and emitted the framework ref, while the bare-let control on the same run returned [:flag :interceptors] — isolating qualification, not shadowing, as the cause. The validity control evaluated the probe form to [:custom :tenant] in the same JVM, so it is real Clojure.

ROOT CAUSE: form-binds? asked the binding vocabulary whether it held a head VERBATIM. The vocabulary is keyed by unqualified symbols, so a qualified spelling of a binder was not a binder, and an unrecognised head bound nothing at all.

FIX — A RULE, NOT A ROSTER. Enumerating binder spellings one at a time is what reopened this bead three times, each on the next spelling of one hole, so the roster lookup is replaced by two rules that both fail CLOSED, towards the flag: (1) a recognised binder is matched by its SIMPLE name (binding-head), so clojure.core/let, cljs.core/let and an aliased c/let all count — the namespace is DISCARDED rather than resolved, deliberately, because resolving it is the fail-open choice that would leave an unrecognised my.macros/let binding nothing; (2) a head outside the vocabulary falls to unrecognised-form-binds?, where a vector child that binds the name — read as either a binding vector or a params vector — makes the form a binder, covering defmethod, when-first, dotimes, deftype methods and project macros without a general analyser (excluded by the non-goals). The catch-all is narrow: it fires only when a form enclosing the registration has a vector child that literally binds the name, and can only ever add a flag.

DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: the free-occurrence walk (free-in-form?) shares this vocabulary but consults it in the opposite direction, and a miss there fails SAFE — an unrecognised head falls through to free-in-children?, whose bare LHS occurrence reads as free, and referenced is the branch that keeps the name-preserving rebind. Normalising it would have been an unrelated behaviour change. The asymmetry is now stated at the shared vocabulary in-source.

EVIDENCE, each exit captured with the redirect and echo on one command line in one shell: clojure -M:test exit 0 at 77 tests / 276 assertions before, exit 0 at 82 / 310 after; clojure -M:integration exit 0 at 6 / 10 both sides; python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py exit 0. The probe flipped from [:rewrite nil] to [:flag :interceptors] with the source byte-identical. Doc-gate coverage was PROVEN rather than assumed by planting a broken link in the codemod README: exit 1 naming the file and line, restored and verified by git blob hash against the committed object rather than by reading a diff.

TESTS ADDED (5): shadowed-bare-path-flagged-under-a-qualified-binder (the audit probe, plus cljs.core/let, an aliased c/let, clojure.core/fn); shadowed-bare-path-flagged-under-an-unrecognised-binder (defmethod, when-first, dotimes, a project macro); unrecognised-head-without-a-path-binding-still-lowers (NON-VACUITY for the catch-all: deftest/testing, comment, a defmethod binding another param, a doseq binding another name all still lower); qualified-binder-shadowing-does-not-suppress-a-qualified-head (over-reach control); qualified-binder-shadow-idempotent.

DOCS: migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/README.md carried this guarantee in two places and both now state that kin is a rule rather than a roster. The HOT-ZONE migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md was NOT touched — it does not state the shadow guarantee, so nothing in it became untrue.
close_reason: Lexical-shadow boundary closed by PR #8896 (commit b57bbac2f2). The AUDIT PR #8857 reopen — the newest text-bearing mutation, found by walking bd history to the bead beginning — was reproduced at source before any edit: a qualified binder such as clojure.core/let around a registration left a bare path head reading as the framework constructor, and the site lowered to the interceptor ref, silently replacing the custom interceptor. Cause: form-binds? matched heads VERBATIM against a vocabulary keyed by unqualified symbols. Repaired with two fail-closed rules replacing the roster lookup — binders matched by simple name, and an unrecognised head whose vector child binds the name treated as a binder — which also covers defmethod / when-first / dotimes / project macros without a general analyser. Five tests added including a non-vacuity control that unrecognised heads NOT binding path still lower. Gates, exits captured in-shell: clojure -M:test exit 0 (77/276 to 82/310), clojure -M:integration exit 0 (6/10), check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 with coverage proven by a planted broken link (exit 1) and restore verified by blob hash. The bead DESCRIPTION is historical — its original premise was discharged by merged PRs #8828 / #8846 / #8857, and both sibling acceptance items (the migration-skill eval fixture, and clojure -M:integration wired into test.yml) were confirmed present at tip.

title: implementor skill: foundation gate can pass a reference-keyed live sub-cache
description:
## Scope

Correct the completion and EP-006 verification workflow in `skills/re-frame2-implementor/**` so a non-CLJS port cannot be declared foundation-complete while its live subscription cache is keyed by host reference identity. Keep the corpus score as an honest corpus score; add only the one port-owned live witness needed for the observability gap already acknowledged by the pinned Spec. Limit supporting checks/evals to this outcome.

## Correctness finding

The skill makes the conformance corpus the acceptance test and its Done gate accepts a green `:core/* + :identity/* + :data-classification/*` run as foundation completion. Its EP-006 row specifically calls the two `:identity/cedn1` Mode-B fixtures "sub-cache fixtures." Those fixtures never touch a frame, `subscribe`, a cache slot, ref-counting, or disposal: they call the canonical-identity primitive directly. The owning Spec explicitly says the missing live assertion would subscribe one query through two distinct host allocations and observe one cache-slot creation.

A TypeScript port can therefore implement CEDN-1 correctly, use Immer for structural sharing, but store query arrays in a native reference-keyed `Map`. Every required fixture can pass and the skill can report v1 completion even though equal freshly allocated queries create separate derived containers forever. This is a false-green proof of a pattern-required runtime contract, not a request for broader coverage.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md:9-10,31,52,70-75` repeatedly says the corpus is the acceptance test and defines Done as the three required fixture families being green.
- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/phase-2-impl-order.md:35` describes `:identity/cedn1` as the EP-006 "sub-cache fixtures"; lines 40 and 68 make fixture-set greens acceptance gates, and line 78 permits completion after those discovered gates.
- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/conformance.md:78-90` requires a port-owned self-test only when a mandated surface has no fixture. It does not cover a fixture that exists but observes only a prerequisite, and line 90 equates `N / N` with conformance against the claim.
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:793-820` requires `rf=`-keyed live lookup and explains that native JS `Map`/array identity breaks de-duplication, ref-count convergence, and disposal. It also notes that Immer supplies neither value equality nor a value-keyed map.
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:824-829` says the two fixtures assert only canonical cache-key identity and explicitly leaves the deeper live-runtime assertion as follow-up because the current Mode-A DSL cannot subscribe two distinct host allocations.
- `spec/conformance/fixtures/sub-cache-dedupes-equal-query-v.edn:36-76` is a Mode-B `:fixture/calls` file containing only `:canonical-identical` and `:canonical-distinct` calls. Its companion `sub-cache-key-map-arg-order.edn` likewise tests canonical bytes/identity only.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_runner.cljc:1026-1039` executes those calls through `identity/identical-identity?`; no subscription-cache code is reached.
- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/evals/evals.json:4-25` is trigger-only, so no outcome regression prevents the skill from accepting this corpus-green/runtime-red port.
- The focused implementor guards are currently green, but they check EP order, required family names, partition vocabulary, and bead leakage; neither exercises this completion invariant (`python scripts/check_skill_implementor_order.py --self-test`, `python scripts/check_skill_implementor_order.py --verbose --ci`, `python scripts/check_skill_implementor_partition_drift.py --self-test`, and `python scripts/check_skill_implementor_partition_drift.py --verbose --ci`).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a minimum TypeScript-shaped port, implement the CEDN-1 canonical operations correctly and use a native `Map<QueryVector, CacheEntry>` for the live sub-cache.
2. Run all claimed required-family fixtures. The two named sub-cache fixtures pass because they invoke only the canonical identity functions, and the required-foundation score can reach `claimed-applicable / claimed-applicable`.
3. Allocate two separate arrays with equal contents, for example `q1 = ['editor/field-error', 'title']` and `q2 = ['editor/field-error', 'title']`, and subscribe both in one frame.
4. Observe two native-Map keys, two derived containers, and two first-run computations. Releasing the readers cannot converge on one slot's last-reader disposal even though the skill's current completion proof is green.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A React view constructs its query array afresh on every render. Under reference-keyed lookup, every render misses the cache, repeats the subscription computation, and leaves an independently referenced entry whose lifecycle cannot converge with the prior readers. The port is reported conformant despite violating the required invariant: two separately allocated query vectors that are `rf=` must resolve to one live cache entry, one shared computation, and one ref-count; that entry disposes exactly once after the last equal reader releases it. A non-equal query must remain a different entry.

## Recommended minimal fix

Add one explicit EP-006 completion proof to the skill: on a host whose ordinary map keys collections by reference (or whenever the selected cache mechanism does not intrinsically provide `rf=` keys), run a port-owned live test using two separately allocated but `rf=`-equal query values. Require the result at the EP-006 checkpoint and in the v1 Done gate alongside the corpus score. In `conformance.md`, name this as the pinned Spec's known observability gap: the existing identity fixtures prove the canonical-key prerequisite, not live cache wiring, so a port-owned self-test is required even though fixture files exist.

Keep the proof mechanism-agnostic. The port may use an `rf=`-keyed persistent map or an interned canonical key; the skill should require the observable one-slot/one-lifecycle result, not prescribe a library. Add a focused outcome regression for the skill so a corpus-green/live-red TypeScript-shaped port is diagnosed as incomplete.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The published EP-006 workflow and Done checklist explicitly distinguish canonical-identity fixture success from live sub-cache success. A non-CLJS/reference-keyed host cannot be called EP-006-, foundation-, or v1-complete until the live witness below has run green; the reported conformance fraction remains the fixture result rather than being silently inflated.
2. The required executable witness creates `q1` and `q2` through separate host allocations, first proves `rf=(q1,q2)`, subscribes both in the same frame through the public/runtime subscription path, and observes exactly one cache slot, one derived container/first-run computation, and a shared ref-count. Releasing one reader keeps the slot live; releasing the second removes it and invokes disposal exactly once.
3. Negative control: a third query with a different argument value is not `rf=` to `q1` and produces a second cache slot and second first-run computation. This prevents a degenerate implementation that interns or collapses every query from satisfying the positive witness.
4. Non-vacuity mutation control: temporarily replace the value-keyed lookup in the test port with the host's native reference-keyed `Map`. The existing `sub-cache-dedupes-equal-query-v.edn`, `sub-cache-key-map-arg-order.edn`, and required-foundation corpus run remain green, while the live witness exits nonzero on two slots/two first-runs. Restore the conforming lookup and record the same witness green.
5. A focused checked-in skill outcome eval presents that exact corpus-green/live-red TypeScript-shaped checkpoint. The expected result withholds EP-006/v1 completion, names reference-keyed live lookup as the port bug, and asks/runs the live witness; a paired one-slot control is accepted. The eval must execute through the skill's normal route, not merely search for a phrase in Markdown.
6. Existing implementor order/partition self-tests and CI modes remain green. Any focused guard added for this invariant has its own red control (remove the live-proof requirement and the guard/eval fails) and does not pin a copied fixture catalogue or implementation token.

## Non-goals

- No new Mode-A conformance operator, cross-host fixture protocol, generated fixture translation, or rewrite of the conformance corpus.
- No mandate for Immutable.js, CEDN interning, or any one cache implementation.
- No expansion into every subscription invalidation/performance law; this issue owns only equal-query live cache identity and its reader lifecycle.
- No change to CEDN-1, `rf=` semantics, capability tags, scoring arithmetic, or the CLJS reference implementation.
- No broad behavioral-eval platform, generic conformance hardening, compatibility layer, or documentation polish.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status census covered 1,133 beads. Exact title/description/notes searches for `sub-cache`, `value-keyed`, `reference-keyed`, `rf=`, `Immer`, `sub-cache-dedupes`, `live-runtime assertion`, `Mode-A harness primitive`, `cache key`, and implementor/conformance acceptance found no bead owning this false-green port-completion outcome.

- `rf2-nuy8x` (closed) reduced the implementor skill to the pinned-spec/fixture loop and added the current required-family gates; it did not require a live two-allocation sub-cache proof. This bug is a correctness residual of that completed workflow, not a duplicate of its ergonomic reduction.
- `rf2-rzeko` (open) owns exactly-once disposal of stock Reagent `Reaction`s in the CLJS adapter. It does not cover non-CLJS query-key equality, duplicate live cache slots, or implementor-skill completion evidence.
- `rf2-a9l6e` (open) owns the MCP conformance tool's compatibility-profile UX, not a port runtime or this skill's proof boundary.
- The owning Spec's line-829 follow-up note is prose, not a tracked bead, and it proposes a future corpus primitive; this task deliberately takes the smaller skill-level port-owned witness.

SKILL.md Done gate = three required fixture families green; phase-2-impl-order.md :35 calls :identity/cedn1 the sub-cache fixtures; conformance.md :78-90 self-test rule covers only surfaces with NO fixture and :90 equates N/N with conformant; sub-cache-dedupes-equal-query-v.edn is :canonical-identical/:canonical-distinct calls only; conformance_runner.cljc :1026-1041 routes them to identity/identical-identity? (no cache code reached); spec/006 conformance-observability note explicitly leaves the live two-allocation assertion as follow-up; evals.json is trigger-only. The corpus-green/reference-keyed false-green is real. SURFACES: skills/re-frame2-implementor/** only; no hot-zone. COLLISIONS: none live or sibling. GATES: python scripts/check_skill_implementor_order.py --self-test then --verbose --ci; python scripts/check_skill_implementor_partition_drift.py --self-test then --verbose --ci; python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py (skills/ is in its roots); all light. SHAPE: solo.
close_reason: Skill completion gate hardened (PR #8829): the implementor skill's EP-006 workflow and Done checklist now distinguish canonical-identity fixture success from live sub-cache success. phase-2-impl-order.md: EP-006 row corrected (the :identity/cedn1 fixtures are cache-KEY fixtures, canonical-identity only) and a new port-owned 'EP-006 live sub-cache witness' section specifies exactly the Spec-acknowledged missing assertion (spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md conformance-observability note): two distinct host allocations of one rf= query value subscribed through the public path -> exactly one cache-slot creation, one derived container/first-run, one shared ref-count, exactly-once last-reader disposal, plus a non-rf= negative control; required whenever the cache mechanism does not intrinsically key by rf=; mechanism-agnostic.
