title: surface-review(skill-setup): make one prompt produce one mounted SPA
description:
## Scope

Treat `skills/re-frame2-setup/**` as one installed product and make its unqualified greenfield request do one thing well: turn an empty directory into a running Reagent counter SPA in one pass. The default path owns the exact files, resolving dependency baseline, commands, verification, and handoff. Keep UIx and merge-into-an-empty-CLJS-project support only when the author explicitly asks for those routes. Align the emitted result with the reduced canonical scaffold owned by `rf2-zq34m`; do not maintain a second independent project template.

## Findings

1. The advertised six-step path is not a fast path. A brand-new Reagent run needs `SKILL.md` plus `deps-versions.md`, `shadow-cljs.md`, and `first-counter.md`: 75,697 bytes and about 9,942 words before the agent writes the project. If it follows the boot explanation pointer too, `entry-namespace.md` adds another 22,547 bytes. Four of the five reference leaves are over the family 16 KB ceiling, while `spec/design.md` says only `entry-namespace.md` is slightly over and that a typical session reads two leaves.
2. The default request is forced into an interview. `deps-versions.md` says the author must choose a pin and the skill must stop before editing if none was supplied. `SKILL.md` also forbids the skill from executing the repo's one-command generator and tells it to hand the command back to the author. Thus “Scaffold a re-frame2 app for me” cannot complete without a choice and a second actor.
3. The first-mount route carries decisions unrelated to mounting: schemas, Xray, `@xyflow/react`, `elkjs`, a right-side host column, CSP/production-hardening prose, publication-state branching, and substrate-specific devtools policy. Reagent is nominally the default, but UIx/Xray/Hicasso distinctions occupy cardinal rules, the main checklist, troubleshooting, and handoff before the default counter exists.
4. The copyable runtime code is currently sound: it uses the current `rf/init!` + explicit `frame-root` seed, frame-targeted schema attach, retained React root, and measured-correct `^:dev/after-load` mount path; the local-root compile cover exercises both Reagent and UIx. The gap is the product journey, not a need for more API explanation.
5. The strongest setup compile test does not materialise the documented dependency file. It synthesises a separate deps map with placeholder Maven versions, rewrites framework coordinates to monorepo `:local/root`, and proves only `compile app`. It neither proves that the exact default dependency command/coordinate resolves from an empty consumer project nor boots the page and clicks 0→1.
6. The 16 evals are explicitly trigger-only (`should_trigger`); none grades the response, resulting files, commands, no-question default, mounted DOM, or handoff. The 1,162-line structural suite instead locks Xray layout, CSP wording, publication branches, UIx routing, and the prohibition on executing the generator. It protects accumulated policy better than the outcome named by the skill.
7. History shows accretion. The initial skill commit shipped `SKILL.md` plus four references at 36,433 bytes and taught core + adapter as the day-one path. The current corresponding shipped corpus is 105,173 bytes after schema, Xray, UIx, CSP/release, troubleshooting, and parity rules accumulated. The useful hot-reload correction in `rf2-r0kk7` / `rf2-ms6r8` came from a real watch-and-browser measurement, demonstrating the kind of outcome proof this skill still lacks.

## Recommended Action

- Define a zero-interview default: an unqualified request in an empty directory chooses Reagent, a single reviewed resolving baseline appropriate to the current publication state, the conventional app namespace/build id/port, and the smallest runnable counter. A user-supplied pin or UIx request overrides the default; absence of either is not a reason to stop.
- Make the main skill a short executor and router. Put the entire default in one copy-complete shipped source (or an asset mechanically derived from the canonical reduced template) with exact filenames and commands. The skill should never reassemble one project from three large prose leaves or hand-maintain a second template.
- Execute the normal work under the explicit invocation: create the files, run `npm install`, run a terminating compile check, start the dev server, and report the URL. Broaden the routine command grants as needed; do not preserve the current user-run-generator prohibition as policy.
- Match `rf2-zq34m`'s small SPA contract. Keep only dependencies and source needed for the counter and selected adapter. Move schemas, Xray, Story, HTTP, production CSP/hosting, Pair, and other capabilities to a compact next-steps link instead of installing or explaining them on the default route.
- Keep explicit UIx and empty-project merge recipes as secondary leaves. They may share the substrate-neutral counter, but they must not introduce a wizard, option matrix, compatibility aliases, or questions into the default.
- Replace prose-lock emphasis with an exact-output behavioral contract: consume the same shipped source the skill uses, resolve its real deps, compile it, serve its real page, and assert the counter paints and advances 0→1. Keep small structural checks only where they prevent a false-green.
- End with a factual handoff: files created, command verified, URL, and the single next skill for application authoring. Mention optional tools only when requested.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:51-63` makes schemas/Xray and their npm dependencies day-one, carries the substrate/tool matrix, and makes the generator user-run only; lines 68-81 repeat route-specific checks and handoff text.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/references/deps-versions.md:65-73` requires an author-selected pin and explicitly says to stop before editing; line 77 begins a long publication-state/manual coordinate branch.
- Current measured sizes: `SKILL.md` 16,439 B; `deps-versions.md` 21,457 B; `entry-namespace.md` 22,547 B; `first-counter.md` 18,660 B; `shadow-cljs.md` 19,141 B; `shared-dataflow.md` 6,929 B. `skills/README.md` sets a 16 KB leaf ceiling.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/spec/design.md:17,46` locks “the author runs the build; the skill doesn't”; line 109 claims the smaller progressive-disclosure shape that the current file sizes and happy-path routing contradict.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/evals/evals.json:4-22` is trigger-only despite prompts explicitly asking the skill to start from nothing and mount a counter.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/setup_drift_test.clj:109-1153` contains 15 numbered structural locks (including Xray, CSP, publication state, and generator prohibition).
- `tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/emitted_test_run_test.clj:1204-1490` synthesises setup deps, rewrites them to local roots, and stops at compile.
- Git history: initial commit `1806995740`; measured hot-reload repairs `rf2-r0kk7` and `rf2-ms6r8`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. From an empty directory, the positive prompt “Scaffold a re-frame2 app for me” takes no clarification round, writes a deterministic Reagent project with no `<VERSION>`/`<SHA>` placeholders, and uses one resolving baseline stored in one source of truth.
2. The default route requires `SKILL.md` plus at most one one-level-deep leaf/asset. Shipped leaves meet the family size discipline or have a demonstrated per-session token-saving exception; no default-path leaf routes onward to another required leaf.
3. The default direct dependency/file manifest matches the reduced runnable SPA contract from `rf2-zq34m`: no schema/Xray/Story/SSR/HTTP coordinate, no `@xyflow/react` or `elkjs`, no Xray host, and no generated policy/toolchain bundle unless the author explicitly requested that capability.
4. The skill executes file creation, install, and a terminating compile verification itself. Its handoff names the successful command and the actual local URL; it does not claim the browser mounted from compile success alone.
5. A black-box setup fixture consumes the exact shipped default source in a fresh temp project, resolves the documented coordinates, compiles, starts the real generated page, asserts the heading and initial `0`, clicks `+1`, and observes `1`. A red witness proves that breaking the adapter/init/build wiring or click path fails the fixture.
6. An explicit UIx prompt and an explicit merge-into-empty-CLJS prompt still reach complete focused routes, but the unqualified route contains no substrate/version/devtools questionnaire, option matrix, or compatibility mode.
7. Evals cover both routing and outcome: at least the start-from-nothing/minimum-wiring prompts assert no clarification, expected manifest/commands, successful verification, and concise handoff. Trigger-only fixtures may remain but are not the sole evaluation.
8. Root instructions, README/plugin metadata, references, internal design notes, and tests describe the same one-pass contract. Stale locks that require user-run generation, Xray/schema day-one wiring, or prose minutiae are removed rather than wrapped in compatibility wording.

## Non-goals

- No setup wizard, interactive questionnaire, `:minimal?` flag, profile system, deprecated aliases, or old-shape compatibility scaffold.
- No re-frame2 runtime, adapter, schema, Xray, Story, Pair, HTTP, SSR, CSP, or deployment redesign.
- No second generator implementation. Reuse or mechanically derive from the canonical reduced template contract; do not duplicate its variant machinery in the skill.
- No Hicasso substrate addition and no widening beyond the existing explicit UIx route.
- No authoring guidance beyond the mounted counter and concise next-step link.
- No Clojars group verification, coordinate rename, tag, repo split, or publication work; those remain with their existing owners.

## Related beads

- `rf2-zq34m` (open): owns collapsing `tools/template/**` to one small runnable SPA contract. This skill should consume that contract, not duplicate or broaden it.
- `rf2-r0kk7` and `rf2-ms6r8` (closed): established and propagated the measured-correct hot-reload lifecycle; preserve the behavior while removing the surrounding ceremony.
- `rf2-uelji` and `rf2-fo4ng` (deferred): own public-coordinate verification and rename. This task must not bypass or absorb them.
- `rf2-k5r9t` (open): adapter-owned client-root work may later shorten boot code but is not a prerequisite for fixing this skill journey.

title: surface-review(skill-re-frame2): let the authoring agent run the gate it already discovers
description:
## Scope

Turn the published `skills/re-frame2/` authoring skill from an edit-then-handoff recipe emitter into a closed-loop author for an existing re-frame2 ClojureScript application. Let a tool-capable agent discover and run the project's own narrow, noninteractive compile/test/lint gate after it writes code. Keep live-runtime inspection and run-side Story MCP work with `re-frame2-pair`, and keep interactive or visual verification with the programmer when no drivable runtime exists.

The coherent change includes the published skill, its normative design/index wording, the Q14 enforcement arm in the drift guard, and one focused behavioural eval. It does not change any re-frame2 framework API.

## Findings

1. The contract defeats its own outcome. `skills/re-frame2/spec/design.md:9` says the output should compile, run, and pass the author's tests, but `SKILL.md:29-32` removes every Bash compile/test/lint tool and `SKILL.md:153` requires a gate handoff. `skills/README.md:201` goes further and describes the agent as emitting a recipe for a human to paste, even though the skill is allowed to Read/Edit/Write the application.
2. The handoff is pure programmer relay work. `references/cross-cutting/testing.md:355-364` already teaches the agent how to inspect `deps.edn`, `shadow-cljs.edn`, `package.json`, and the nearest README to select the exact narrow gate. It then spends its final instruction telling the programmer to execute that command and return the result. Running the already-discovered noninteractive command closes the loop in the same turn.
3. There is no matching trust rationale. The published-skill policy at `skills/README.md:261-281` explicitly trusts the invoker and accepts routine `npm`, `npx`, `clojure`, `shadow-cljs`, and `clj-kondo` wildcards while barring genuinely dangerous commands. The migration row names a hard trust boundary; the re-frame2 authoring row names only the old Q14 decision.
4. Static drift checks do not substitute for compiling authored code. `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/skills_check.clj` verifies that call-position `(rf/<var>` names exist plus three retired-keyword families; it cannot check arity, option maps, requires, macro expansion, or composition. `scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py:140-147` explicitly says its rules are retrospective token patterns and a green run is not evidence a leaf agrees with its source.
5. History shows this gap is active under pre-alpha API churn. Representative follow-ups include six wrong-arity `reg-*` examples (`7075f1d079`), a deleted `dispatch-to-system` recipe (`b73f3b5949`), the retired Managed HTTP reply contract (`d78fabd19d`), and a fail-open CSRF recipe (`887fd87d67`). These all needed later correction despite the structural gates.
6. The eval corpus does not validate the handoff posture. `evals/` contains eleven rich JSON scenarios but no runner output or `benchmark.json`; `spec/design.md:135` calls it not yet load-bearing and `evals/README.md:16,89-110` describes a future/tool-agnostic manual runner. No eval requires the agent to compile or test an authored change, while the Q14 drift guard rejects the capability by construction.
7. Routing and progressive disclosure are broadly sound and should be preserved: the central skill matrix distinguishes setup/migration/pairing, `SKILL.md` is a 166-line router, and depth is one leaf away. Token economy argues against adding a verification module: the router is already about 1,700 words and `testing.md` is 379 lines/about 3,700 words. The useful move is to delete handoff ceremony and add one short execution rule.

## Recommended Action

Explicitly unlock L3/Q14 for safe project-local verification. Remove the author-runs-the-gate wording from `spec/design.md`, `spec/authoring-prompt.md`, `SKILL.md`, `references/cross-cutting/testing.md`, and the verification-posture row in `skills/README.md`. Retire only the Q14/verification-posture classifier and self-test cases from `scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py`; retain its unrelated correctness guards.

Give the skill the smallest routine command surface needed to run gates already declared by the consumer project, aligned with the repository's existing published-skill baseline: focused `clojure` test aliases, declared `npm test` / `npm run test:*` scripts, `npx shadow-cljs` or `shadow-cljs` compile/test targets, and `clj-kondo --lint`. Do not grant a blanket Bash wildcard.

Replace the discover-then-handoff prose with one concise workflow: after an edit, discover the nearest declared noninteractive gate, run it, repair a relevant failure, and report the exact command and result. Hand off only when the gate is interactive/visual, requires a live runtime owned by Pair, is unavailable, or the user asked not to run it. Add one focused existing-project eval/fixture whose transcript proves the agent edits and invokes the declared gate; do not build a general eval platform as part of this task.

## Evidence

- Contradictory goal/posture: `skills/re-frame2/spec/design.md:9,13,30-32`; `skills/re-frame2/SKILL.md:29-32,153`; `skills/README.md:195-201`.
- Existing gate discovery that ends in a relay: `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing.md:3,355-374`.
- Trust-the-invoker command policy: `skills/README.md:261-281`.
- Limits of structural coverage: `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/skills_check.clj:4-16,41-80`; `scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py:140-147`.
- Non-load-bearing evals: `skills/re-frame2/spec/design.md:133-135`; `skills/re-frame2/evals/README.md:89-128`; the directory contains only `README.md` and `evals.json`.
- Token census at current main: `SKILL.md` 166 lines/1,713 words; `testing.md` 379 lines/3,704 words; many task leaves are already 1,800-3,500 words. A new verification leaf would tax every routed task without improving the binding.
- Decision history: commit `d96a6026d0` (`rf2-tnikip`, historical tracker id) removed an already-existing narrow Bash allow-list and "Verify what you changed" section solely to reconcile the skill to Q14, then added CI that makes reintroducing agent-run verification fail. This task consciously reverses that decision rather than layering an exception around it.
- Duplicate search: all-status bead title/description/notes searches for `Q14`, `verification posture`, `authoring-only`, `allowed-tools`, `run tests`, `eval runner`, `eval harness`, `recipe correctness`, and `re-frame2 skill` found no current owner for this outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A tool-capable `re-frame2` authoring session on an existing project may run narrowly scoped, project-declared, noninteractive compile/test/lint commands; no published or normative text tells it to delegate such a runnable gate to the programmer by default.
2. L3/Q14, `skills/README.md`'s verification table, frontmatter `allowed-tools`, the done checklist, the testing leaf, and `check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py` agree on the new posture. The drift script retains its non-Q14 rules and self-tests.
3. A focused checked-in eval/fixture gives the agent an existing project plus an authoring change. The captured tool transcript shows it discovers the gate from project files, invokes that exact gate, and reports the real exit/result. A controlled wrong API shape makes the fixture gate red, proving the signal is non-vacuous.
4. The routing evals for greenfield setup and v1 migration still hand off, and the Story authoring/run-boundary eval still forbids `run-variant` / `read-failures` here. Safe compile/test permission does not absorb `re-frame2-pair` or live-runtime work.
5. No `references/verify.md`, generic verification framework, policy essay, compatibility mode, or blanket `Bash(*)` is added. Across `SKILL.md` plus `references/cross-cutting/testing.md`, the new instruction is no longer than the handoff/discovery ceremony it replaces; target a net prose reduction.
6. The PR reports the focused eval result and the existing skill drift, eval-doc, packaging, link, and API-manifest projection checks relevant to its changed paths.

## Non-goals

- No framework, registrar, macro, test-support, Story MCP, or Pair MCP API change.
- No new live-runtime driver in the authoring skill and no access to Pair-owned run-side Story tools.
- No automatic dependency installation, daemon/watch-server launch, browser interaction, visual sign-off, network mutation, or destructive shell permission.
- No general runner for all eleven skill evals; one repeatable behavioural witness is enough for this outcome.
- No rewrite of the routing matrix, two-leaf progressive-disclosure model, pattern catalogue, or canonical recipes.

## Related beads

- `rf2-tnikip` is the historical decision carrier named by commit `d96a6026d0`; it is no longer present in the current beads database, but its Q14 enforcement is the code and prose this task reverses.
- `rf2-ms6r8` (closed) is a useful measured precedent: a skill's false hot-reload premise was enforced by its own structural guard until a real compile/browser loop disproved it.
- No active or closed current-database bead found in the duplicate searches owns this re-frame2-authoring verification outcome.

title: websocket pattern trusts inbound correlation before validation
description:
## Scope

Align the canonical runnable WebSocket pattern across examples/patterns/websocket/, its external CLJS test wrapper, spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md, and the WebSocket skill so the code programmers and coding agents copy is safe at both trust boundaries: credentials leaving the app and frames entering it.

Preserve the example's existing lifecycle machine, mock transport, UI, queue/correlation semantics, and the repository's test-free-examples policy. This is a focused correction to one worked pattern, not a new WebSocket facility.

## Findings

The four pattern examples are generally current and copyable: they use the public reg-event/reg-sub/reg-view and reg-machine/defmachine idioms, explicit frame roots and initial events, machine data schemas, recordable durable coeffects, and external headless wrappers. Every declared pattern build is derived by the examples compile gate, including the Nine States story build.

The WebSocket example is also unusually well covered for reconnects, stale socket epochs, queueing, correlation, timeouts, subscription replay, loss semantics, and teardown. Its two trust boundaries nevertheless contradict the newer canonical guidance:

- connection.cljs persists the raw :auth-token in the connection machine's :data, accepts it on :ws/connect and :ws/refresh-token events, dispatches it to the child, and copies it into the socket actor's machine :data. schema.cljs and README.md teach the same shape, and the wrapper tests assert the token is present in snapshots.
- skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md now says raw bearer/cookie/refresh credentials must never enter machine :data or dispatch. Its canonical declaration carries only an opaque :cred-ref and resolves the bearer through an app-owned, client-only host seam.
- messages.cljs writes both pushes and correlated replies into app-db without an inbound message schema or :rf.schema/at-boundary. Its Message schema describes values after storage and is not a closed wire contract. The callback event :ws.app/request-reply is a second app-db-writing ingress with the same omission.
- spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md added the correct closed InboundMessage plus production boundary interceptor requirement, including the correlated reply path, but its main worked machine and re-authentication prose still carry raw :auth-token. The runnable example implements neither correction.

History explains the split rather than justifying it. Commit bc861c1d17 introduced the runnable WebSocket example on 2026-05-12. Commit ae12ce9b43 (historical bead rf2-x3u46) moved canonical credentials out of machine :data two days later, but changed the skill rather than the example. Commit d667871dae (historical bead rf2-096js) added the inbound-frame obligation to the spec on 2026-08-03, again without updating the runnable source or wrapper. ## Acceptance Criteria

1. The connection and socket actor machine schemas/data carry an opaque :cred-ref, never a raw bearer, cookie, password, refresh token, or equivalent credential. Connect/reconnect/rotation event payloads and queued application events likewise carry only the reference.

title: surface-review(template): collapse the generator to one small runnable SPA contract
description:
## Scope

Reduce `tools/template/**` to one deliberate product contract: scaffold a small client-side counter SPA that a programmer or agent can read, run, test, and replace. Keep the Reagent default and the UIx substrate selector because that choice changes authored source and adapter wiring. Remove feature/style modes and the generated policy/toolchain bundle. Update the generated resources, hook API, tests, and normative spec together; touch directly coupled template release-gate assertions only where the smaller contract requires it.

## Findings

1. The default Reagent scaffold is not minimal. Before compiled output or `node_modules`, it emits 20 files, 75,816 bytes, and 1,579 lines. The generated README alone is 677 lines; `events.cljs` is 232 lines for two tiny handlers; `deps.edn` is 76 lines. The actual counter cycle is a handful of forms.
2. The default installs decisions the app has not made: schemas, a git-pinned Xray tool plus `@xyflow/react` and `elkjs`, a trace error sink, a whole-app-db schema, a long commented HTTP handler, CSP and production-hosting policy, GitHub Actions, Lefthook, cljfmt, clj-kondo, `dev/user.clj`, and a REPL scratch namespace. These are useful recipes, not requirements for the first SPA.
3. The generator exposes three feature/style flags (`:include-story?`, `:include-ssr?`, `:css`) on top of the substrate axis, yielding eight accepted output cells and mutual-exclusion/capability machinery. `hooks.clj` is 774 lines; the template tests are 5,608 lines; the spec is 3,295 lines. Much of the suite pins explanatory prose, badges, CSP snippets, Xray layout details, and variant combinations instead of the first-run contract.
4. The shared README teaches Story even when Story was not requested. The generated source teaches HTTP, privacy/egress, production schema elision, Xray, and deployment hardening before the reader has replaced the counter. This makes both humans and agents distinguish essential code from a framework handbook on their first edit.
5. The public descriptions have already drifted under the matrix: `template.edn` advertises Story but omits the live SSR and Tailwind modes; Principles P3 says React and ReactDOM are the only npm dependencies while the default Reagent path injects Xray's two additional npm packages. The canonical Clojure name `acme/my-app` is copied verbatim into `package.json`; npm 11's bundled `validate-npm-package-name` rejects that unscoped slash form.
6. History shows accretion, not an intentional current baseline. The initial scaffold at `2313a8d85a` emitted 10 files / 8,966 bytes / 272 lines. Subsequent commits separately added the dev bundle (`d9830dc2fc`), cljfmt (`3cdc6f3b26`), Lefthook (`bfe4aa3ee8`), Xray's predecessor (`efbdd60a94`), CSP/production hardening (`f61b816163`), best-practice demos (`f6f770bfc0`), and CI (`b04c304614`). Correct later fixes hardened that accumulated shape, but no product pass re-asked what belongs in a starter.
7. Public distribution is a separate known blocker: `.github/workflows/template-release.yml` states that it rewrites emitted framework coordinates to local roots and that the advertised public template coordinate is not yet usable. Existing publication beads own that. Adding another invocation mode or a `:minimal?` flag would compound both problems.

## Recommended Action

- Make the template emit one SPA shape per supported view substrate. `:name` remains required; `:substrate :reagent|:uix` is the only template-specific option, with Reagent as the obvious default.
- Delete `:include-story?`, `:include-ssr?`, and `:css` from the hook API, resources, errors, docs, and matrix tests. Story, SSR, and Tailwind remain learnable through their focused examples/guides; do not replace the flags with a wizard, profiles, or separate compatibility modes in this task.
- Emit only the files needed to run, test, release, and understand the counter: `.gitignore`, a short README, `deps.edn`, `package.json`, `shadow-cljs.edn`, the HTML/CSS shell, `core.cljs`, `events.cljs`, `subs.cljs`, `views.cljs`, and one focused event-flow test. Remove generated CI, hook-manager/editor/formatter/linter configs, REPL scratch scaffolding, and schema source.
- Keep direct dependencies to the runnable counter: Clojure/ClojureScript, re-frame2 core, the selected adapter and view library, shadow-cljs, React, and ReactDOM. Do not preload Xray or pull schemas/tool coordinates into every Reagent app.
- Keep comments local and brief. Preserve the measured-correct `^:dev/after-load` lifecycle, but move HTTP, schema, privacy, CSP, production-host, Xray, Story, SSR, migration, and tooling tutorials to existing public docs and link to them from a compact next-steps section.
- Derive an npm-valid package name from the Clojure project coordinate instead of copying `acme/my-app` verbatim.
- Replace prose- and combination-heavy tests with a small black-box contract: exact emit manifest, parseable/valid manifests, compile/test/release, real browser boot and 0→1 counter interaction for both substrates, and absence of retired files/dependencies/options. Keep history in git rather than carrying completed migration/validation reports as live normative surface.

## Evidence

- `tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/template_test.clj:37-66` enumerates the 20-file default; lines 364-712 assert the generated handbook, CI, Xray host, CSP, privacy, schema, and HTTP prose.
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/root/README.md` is 677 lines and includes Hot reload, Story, Production hardening, REPL, schemas, privacy/egress, HTTP, migration, and future skill-install sections.
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_shared/events.cljs` is 232 lines; the counter handlers occupy only the small initialisation/increment blocks, while the rest is an error sink and commented HTTP exemplar.
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/deps.edn` adds schemas, Xray, cljfmt, clj-kondo, and tools.namespace around the base app; `_shared/package.json` injects Xray npm packages and uses `{{name}}` as the npm name.
- `tools/template/src/day8/re_frame2_template/hooks.clj:179-291,321-643,655-741` owns the flag gate, coercions, capability-conditioned substitution prose, and file-selection matrix.
- `tools/template/spec/000-Vision.md`, `API.md`, `001-Substrate-Variants.md`, and `002-Generated-Shape.md` claim a minimal counter while specifying the larger matrix and tooling bundle.
- `.github/workflows/template-release.yml:114-129,257-273` explicitly says the release smoke masks unresolved consumer coordinates; this task must not invent a second distribution route around that separate owner.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The documented template API has exactly one template-specific selector: optional `:substrate` with Reagent default and UIx alternative. The removed Story, SSR, and CSS keys fail as unknown; there are no aliases, deprecation warnings, reserved gates, or compatibility shims for them.
2. Reagent and UIx emit the same small project manifest apart from `core.cljs`, `views.cljs`, and required dependency differences. The emitted tree contains the run/test/release essentials named above and does not contain `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `lefthook.yml`, `.cljfmt.edn`, `.clj-kondo/`, `.editorconfig`, `dev/`, `schema.cljs`, Story files, SSR files, or Tailwind overlays.
3. The default direct dependency graph contains no Xray, Story, SSR, schemas, machines, cljfmt, clj-kondo, or tools.namespace coordinate and no Xray-only npm package. `package.json` has an npm-valid name derived deterministically from both qualified and bare Clojure project names.
4. Each substrate's generated app parses, compiles, runs its focused test, builds an advanced release, opens its real generated page, paints the counter, and moves 0→1 on click. The correct one-time init plus `^:dev/after-load` re-render lifecycle from `rf2-r0kk7` remains covered.
5. Generated source contains the counter dataflow and the lifecycle facts needed to edit it, without embedded HTTP/schema/privacy/security/tooling tutorials. The generated README gives the run, test, release, and guide/docs links without conditional sections for modes that were not emitted.
6. Template tests assert the behavioral and manifest contract, including red witnesses for a retired flag, an advanced dependency/file reappearing, an invalid npm name, and a broken browser boot. They do not pin badges, prose paragraphs, server-specific CSP snippets, or removed variant cells.
7. Normative template docs and metadata describe the same reduced surface. Completed migration/validation records are removed from the live contract or clearly historical; no document advertises a mode the generator no longer accepts.

## Non-goals

- No new wizard, `:minimal?` switch, profile system, second template, prompt sequence, or replacement feature flag.
- No compatibility layer for pre-alpha Story/SSR/Tailwind invocations; git history is the migration record.
- No runtime, adapter, Xray, Story, SSR, Tailwind, schema, HTTP, or security-policy redesign.
- No Hicasso substrate addition.
- No operator-owned repository split, coordinate rename, Clojars verification, tag, or publication work. The reduced scaffold must compose with that work when it lands, not duplicate it.
- Do not delete the focused examples or guides that become the on-ramp for advanced capabilities.

## Related beads

- `rf2-r0kk7` (closed): established the correct generated hot-reload lifecycle; preserve its behavior while shrinking the prose.
- `rf2-48rk3` (closed): made feature capability selection fail closed; most of that machinery becomes unnecessary when feature modes are retired, while the substrate registry can remain small.
- `rf2-8urba` (deferred): proposed a future Hicasso template variant; distinct and explicitly outside this minimal-contract change.
- `rf2-uelji` (deferred) and `rf2-fo4ng` (deferred): own verified-group/public-coordinate work; this task does not bypass or duplicate them.
- `rf2-k5r9t` (open): adapter-owned client-root work may later shorten generated Reagent boot code, but is not a prerequisite for removing template ceremony.

== 2. HOW THE OPINIONS WERE WEIGHED ==

THE DOSSIER AUTHOR (§Recommendation): "Affirm the collapse and strip both." Grounds: pre-alpha, elegance over accumulation, trust the programmer; a starter's job is to be read, run and replaced in one sitting, and today's scaffold hands a newcomer a 719-line handbook and five installed decisions before their first edit; Xray and Story each have a copy-paste attach recipe surfaced from the README's next-steps and from the setup skill at the moment the user wants it. Option B was called "the only defensible keep", tipped against by mechanics rather than aesthetics: the preload drags in a sha-pinned monorepo git dep and two npm packages, keeps the substrates asymmetric, and couples the template to the tools' release cadence. Reversible: re-adding one preload line later is a smaller act than carrying the machinery meanwhile.

THE REVIEWER (§Codex Recommendation): AGREES on every point that matters — "Affirm the collapse and strip both the default Xray wiring and the `:include-story?` generator flag. Make `:substrate` the only template-specific choice" — and says it reached that "from the current resources, hooks, tests, tool dependency graphs, documentation, and git history rather than from the bead's findings." It ADDED four things the dossier did not carry, all adopted here: (i) the strongest keep-Xray argument named at source — tools/template/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md §9 ("Xray on by default", rf2-y9zqc) treats immediate runtime feedback as part of the first-run experience, and a devtools preload never enters an advanced release — answered by "'no production bundle cost' is narrower than 'no scaffold cost'", with the scaffold cost itemised (git-pinned coordinate, `@xyflow/react`, `elkjs`, a preload, a layout host, CSS, CSP qualifications, README material, and the lockstep tests at version_lockstep_test.clj:227-251) and Xray's own dependency graph (tools/xray/deps.edn:15-100 reaches epoch, routing, flows, schemas, resources, machines, Hicasso, machines-viz, reagent-slim, Reagent, Editscript and zprint, and records that Xray cannot publish while Hicasso lacks a coordinate); (ii) Story is "even less suitable as the one surviving flag" — the flag selects a 123-line routing/lifecycle entry point, a separate 102-line deps.edn and a 76-line registration example, and Story hard-depends on Reagent, machines, HTTP and Xray (tools/story/deps.edn:14-75); (iii) an explicit warning, adopted verbatim as a non-goal: "Do not replace the removed Xray wiring with an `:include-xray?` flag: that would immediately recreate the option matrix this decision is trying to eliminate"; (iv) the concrete test shape — explicit ABSENCE assertions for Xray/Story coordinates, npm packages, preloads, hosts and variant files, and the README's Xray and Story links kept as TESTED escape hatches.

WHERE THEY DIFFERED, in the reviewer's own words: "The real tradeoff is discoverability. A new Reagent user will no longer see the project's most distinctive devtools automatically, and some users will never follow a next-steps link. That is a product-marketing loss, not a runtime correctness loss, and it should be acknowledged rather than hidden behind the word 'minimal'. If the desired front door is a showcase rather than a neutral starter, then keeping Xray only is the coherent fallback; keeping Story or adding more flags is not. I would revisit default-on Xray only after there is evidence from first-run testing that auto-opening the panel materially improves successful onboarding, preferably once it has a stable consumer coordinate and can mount on every supported default substrate." The dossier called the same loss "the one real ergonomic loss" and mitigated it by the next-steps link; the reviewer weighted it higher and named the fallback. This ruling sides with both on the outcome and ADOPTS THE REVIEWER'S REVISIT CONDITION AS THE RECORDED ONE: default-on Xray is reconsidered only on first-run evidence, only once Xray has a stable published coordinate (`xray-v*`), and only if it can mount on every default substrate — today it cannot mount on UIx (rf2-p6f6u; Xray's mount refuses that adapter kind by name), and its Reagent-only preload is exactly the asymmetry that would force AC2/AC3 here and rc0yh's AC3 to be reworded around an exception. The front door is a neutral starter, not a showcase; the showcase is the docs, the testbeds and the setup skill, each of which teaches the tool at the moment the reader wants it.

WHY THE RULING WENT THIS WAY, in one paragraph: everything in the bead except the taste question is machinery removal, and both opinions plus the 2026-08-30 triage and the 2026-09-01 backlog reread hold it settled. On the taste question the two opinions converge from different evidence bases; the only dissent is about how loudly to acknowledge a discoverability cost; and that cost is reversible in a one-line PR, while the machinery a keep would retain (a git-pinned monorepo coord in every newborn app, lockstep npm pins, `xray?` substitutions in four hook slots, a permanent manifest asymmetry, release-cadence coupling) is exactly the class of coupling this surface review exists to cut. Posture applies in full: pre-alpha, no back-compat shims, trust the programmer to paste four lines when they want a panel.

title: surface-review(story): make :setup/:script the one variant vocabulary end to end
description:
## Scope

Converge Story's variant/fragment data contract on the already-documented public vocabulary, `:setup` + `:script` (retaining `:plays` for named multi-play), across `tools/story/**` and the directly coupled Story-MCP read/write boundary. Migrate the remaining registry, plan, identity, canvas/workspace, runner, recorder/save-variant, test-mode/watch/CI, docs, testbeds, and MCP consumers that still depend on transitional body keys.

## Verified Findings

1. Story teaches one language but stores another. `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md` calls this a clean pre-alpha rename; `schemas.cljc` still accepts both pairs, and `registrar/reg-variant*` rewrites authored `:setup` -> `:events` and `:script` -> `:play-script` through `lower-public-vocabulary`.
2. The rewrite is publicly observable. `story/variant->edn` promises the side-table body verbatim, so canonical registration changes keys on read-back. Story-MCP's recorder explicitly documents that canonical `:script` write-back returns as `:play-script`. Humans and agents therefore need two vocabularies and cannot round-trip a body by inspection.
3. The runtime is ready for the cut: `runtime.cljc` executes compiled `[:world :setup]` and `[:world :scripts]`, while `plan.cljc` owns normalized semantics. Remaining direct legacy reads are concrete in `identity.cljc`, `play.cljc`, `play/ci_runner.cljc`, `play/runner_events.cljc`, `ui/state/tests.cljc`, `ui/test_mode/pure.cljc`, and `ui/sidebar_signals.cljc`.
4. Drift is broad: measured text hits include 165 `:play-script` references in `tools/story/src`, 277 in tests, 81 in specs, and 42 in `tools/story-mcp` (some are prose/test names, but the production readers above are direct). The template, current testbeds, tutorials, recorder snippets, and promotion output already author the target keys.
5. History shows unfinished convergence, not a new feature. Commit `a9e3f07523` (finish public `:script` rename) completed author-facing emission/docs but not storage/readers. The current spec says to remove lowering once remaining readers consume the plan.
6. No new API is needed: `re-frame.story` already has 88 `defn`/`defmacro` entries inventoried in `spec/api-manifest.edn`. This outcome should shrink a data contract.

## Recommended Action

- Store `:setup` and `:script` verbatim in registered variant/fragment bodies; keep `:plays` as named multi-play.
- Remove `:events`/`:play-script` from authoring schemas, xor/precedence branches, and `lower-public-vocabulary`.
- Route consumers through the compiled plan where they need resolved semantics; raw-author-data readers use canonical keys only.
- Make Story-MCP registration, record/write-back, discovery, and read-back accept and emit those same keys.
- Migrate Story-owned fixtures, tests, specs, API/tutorial prose in the same change. Use the pre-alpha posture: delete aliases outright, with no warnings, shim, or deprecation ceremony.
- Do not mechanically rename unrelated `:events` collections such as recorder capture state or trace channels.

## Evidence

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/registrar.cljc` `reg-variant*` validates canonical input, lowers it, then stores legacy keys.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/schemas.cljc` `Variant` and `lower-public-vocabulary` contain dual schemas and the rewrite.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc` `variant->edn` is a verbatim side-table read.
- `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md` names the clean rename, plan-routed runtime, remaining readers, and removal condition.
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/recorder.cljc` documents canonical write / legacy read-back.
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_shared/stories.cljs` and Story testbeds already use the target form.
- Commit `a9e3f07523` landed the author-facing half only.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `reg-variant` and `reg-fragment` accept `:setup`, `:script`, and `:plays`; authoring-body `:events` or `:play-script` fail shape validation. `:plays` remains mutually exclusive with single `:script`.
2. `handler-meta`, `variant->edn`, Story-MCP `get-variant`, `register-variant`, and `record-as-variant` preserve canonical key names through write/read round trips, apart from documented source/origin/provenance stamps.
3. A canonical-only fixture exercises frame setup, canvas/workspace rendering, auto-play, step debugger, watch/test discovery, snapshot identity, recorder write-back, save/promote, static build, and the browser CI runner.
4. Plan/hash/snapshot behavior remains deterministic for migrated fixtures, and named multi-play remains covered.
5. Public docs, API tables, examples, MCP descriptors/instructions, and production source no longer describe or inspect transitional variant `:play-script`/`:events` slots. Retained `events` wording denotes a real collection/channel.
6. Focused JVM, CLJS/browser Story, Story-MCP, feature-load/play-runner, descriptor-generation, and API-manifest gates pass. Tests include a red witness for each removed key and a canonical register -> read-back identity witness.
7. No facade symbol or manifest row is added unless proven unavoidable and explicitly classified.

## Non-goals

- No new DSL, convenience macro, migration mode, warning framework, compatibility alias, or versioned schema.
- Do not remove or redesign named `:plays`.
- Do not rename generic recorder `:events` state, trace channels, or historical command/job names merely because their English name contains play script.
- No shell/chrome redesign or new MCP capability.
- No retrospective pruning of the Story facade; that is separate API-freeze work.

## Related beads

- `rf2-1s53x` (closed): CI play-runner prose correction; no ownership of body-key convergence.
- `rf2-2hpxo` (deferred): retrospective facade classification; distinct because this task should add no export.

title: surface-review(routing): make server-rendered route links honor pure URL encoding
description:
## Scope

Correct the routing artefact's server/JVM link projection so a declared frame `:url-strategy` controls the pure `href` encoding on both hosts. Cover both routing-owned link doors (`re-frame.routing/route-link-render-ssr` and the JVM arm of the late-bound `:routing/link-model` seam), focused tests, the SSR parity witness, and the normative/user-facing routing prose. Keep the artefact split and manifest dependency surface unchanged.

## Findings

The strategy contract already makes `:encode` pure and host-agnostic, ships it on both hosts, and requires it during JVM frame preflight. Browser `route-link` uses that encoder, but both JVM link paths hard-code `identity`. This makes supported configurations disagree across hosts:

- `(with-base-path history-url-strategy "/realworld")` renders `/article/x` on the server and `/realworld/article/x` on the hydrated client. The server link leaves the deployment mount if clicked before hydration, by a crawler, or without JavaScript.
- `hash-url-strategy` renders `/active` on the server and `#/active` on the client; base + hash similarly loses both outbound decorations server-side.
- The server and client render trees differ at `:href`, contrary to Spec 011's structural-hydration rule. Spec 012 currently calls that difference "no hydration mismatch", but canonical render-tree hashing treats an attribute value change as structural.

The gap is not defended by tests. `route_link_test.clj` covers only the default identity strategy, while `routing_url_strategy_test.clj` proves the pure encoders/combinator independently; no test composes a seated server frame strategy with either SSR link surface. Two shipped RealWorld examples use `with-base-path`, so this is a real supported deployment shape rather than speculative custom-strategy machinery.

## Recommended Action

Refine the rule to: SSR ignores browser side effects (`:decode`'s host read, `:push!`, `:replace!`, `:install-listener!`), not the pure `:encode` projection used to author an anchor.

Resolve the rendering frame's already-validated strategy and apply its `:encode` in both JVM link paths. Preserve the current default-history/path-form result when the public SSR render helper is called without a frame. Keep the click/navigation payload path-form; only the rendered `href` is encoded. Add one shared parity fixture or equally direct cross-host assertions for history, base-path history, hash, and base-path hash, plus a server-frame integration assertion that reaches the registered `rf/route-link` view. Update Spec 012, the routing API reference, and guide prose so they describe the narrowed SSR rule and no longer claim differing hrefs are hydration-equivalent.

## Evidence

- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc:394`-`:410`: `route-link-render-ssr` passes `identity` to `href-attrs`.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc:490`-`:495`: `link-model` selects the frame encoder only on CLJS and hard-codes `identity` on CLJ.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc:273`-`:320`: `with-base-path` adds the deployment prefix only in `:encode`, explicitly calling it the single outbound base-composition point used by route links.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc:367`-`:376`: JVM strategies are required to carry callable `:encode` and `:decode`; the docstring even says SSR route-link renders through `:encode`, contradicting the live link code.
- `spec/012-Routing.md:1865`-`:1873` calls `:encode` pure and host-agnostic; `:1899`-`:1911` says only strategy consult points see the base; `:1913`-`:1915` then exempts SSR and asserts differing hrefs are not a mismatch.
- `spec/011-SSR.md:52`-`:54` requires the client to compute the same structural render tree as the server; attribute ordering may differ, attribute values may not.
- `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/route_link_test.clj` has default path-form SSR href cases only. `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_url_strategy_test.clj:322` onward tests base encoding without composing it with SSR link rendering.
- History explains the drift: commit `38366dc386` introduced the "SSR ignores strategies" rule on 2026-07-03; commit `5b9bab33fa` added `with-base-path` on 2026-07-08; commit `d8cb5cbae8` then made `:encode` the single outbound base authority, without revisiting the earlier SSR exemption.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A server frame declaring `(with-base-path history-url-strategy "/demos")` renders a route link to `/demos/<route-path>` through both the routing-owned SSR view and `:routing/link-model`; its navigation payload remains the unencoded app-relative path.
- Hash and base + hash configurations render `#/...` and `/demos#/...` respectively on the JVM, matching the first CLJS render for the same frame config.
- The default/no-frame JVM helper behavior remains path-form, so existing direct-call ergonomics do not regress.
- A cross-host render-tree/hash fixture (or an equivalent explicit parity assertion using the production render paths) proves a strategy-bearing route link has the same `:href` on server and client; changing either JVM path back to `identity` makes the fixture red.
- Existing route URL matching, path-form event payloads, push/replace behavior, and listener decoding stay unchanged.
- Spec 012, `docs/api/re-frame.routing.md`, and relevant routing guide text say SSR skips side effects but honors pure link encoding; the false "different href, no hydration mismatch" claim is removed.
- No new runtime dependency, public wrapper, compatibility shim, or strategy type is introduced.

## Non-goals

- Do not change `route-url` or `match-url` from their app-relative path-form contract.
- Do not infer a base path from the request, servlet/proxy headers, or browser globals; programmers continue to declare the strategy explicitly.
- Do not add relative-route syntax, a redirect object, a router provider, or another URL-strategy abstraction.
- Do not refactor unrelated link click, prefetch, native-anchor, history, or listener code.
- Do not preserve the current divergent SSR href as a compatibility mode; this is pre-alpha and the supported contract should be coherent.

## Related beads

No duplicate found after searching all statuses by `route-link`, `url-strategy`, `with-base-path`, `base path`, `SSR ignores`, `path-form href`, `hydration mismatch`, `hash app`, and `server shell`. Historical source/commit annotations cite `rf2-aerrz5`, `rf2-g8pbwg`, and `rf2-irygd6`; `bd show` reports those ids absent from the current tracker, so commits `38366dc386`, `5b9bab33fa`, and `d8cb5cbae8` are the durable history anchors rather than active related beads.

Worker closes this bead on PR-ready.

title: surface-review(reagent-slim): make reagent2.core/reaction a stock-compatible macro
description:
## Scope

Restore the public `reagent2.core/reaction` call shape promised by the bounded Reagent-compat surface. Touch only the reagent-slim core macro/runtime surface, focused tests, and the directly coupled surface/migration documentation needed to make the contract truthful.

## Findings

`reagent2.core/reaction` is currently a runtime function taking a thunk (`[f]`), but the pinned stock Reagent 2.0.1 surface it claims to preserve exposes `reagent.core/reaction` as a variadic macro that wraps its body in `(fn [])`. There is no `src/reagent2/core.clj` macro namespace. A documented mechanical require rename therefore changes `(r/reaction (* @a @a))` from a lazy reactive expression into an eager call that passes the computed value as `f`; dereferencing the resulting Reaction later attempts to call that value as a function.

This is not covered by the current tests. `reagent2.core-cljs-test` says the core reaction surface has dedicated coverage but never calls `r/reaction`; `reagent2.ratom-cljs-test` covers the different `reagent2.ratom/reaction` macro. IMPL-SPEC §2.2 and §14.2 encode the same incorrect “function form” reading while §13.1 promises that `s/reagent\./reagent2./g` is sufficient inside the bounded surface.

## Recommended Action

Make `reagent2.core/reaction` a co-located CLJ macro with stock Reagent's body syntax and expansion to `reagent2.ratom/make-reaction`. Remove the misleading thunk-taking runtime function from that public spelling; callers that intentionally have a thunk already have the explicit `reagent2.ratom/make-reaction` factory. Reconcile the public-surface inventory and migration prose with the actual macro contract.

## Evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn:15` pins `reagent/reagent` 2.0.1.
- In that artefact, `reagent/core.clj` defines `(defmacro reaction [& body] ...)`; `reagent/core.cljs` defines no `reaction` function.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/core.cljs:65-73` instead defines `(defn reaction [f] ...)`, and `src/reagent2/core.clj` does not exist.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md:224` and `:1187-1191` classify the core spelling as a function, while `:1129` promises a namespace-only import rewrite.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/core_cljs_test.cljs:22-25` claims indirect coverage but contains no `r/reaction` call; the only expression-body proof is for the sibling ratom macro at `test/reagent2/ratom_cljs_test.cljs:425-432`.
- The spec cites 25 Dash8 plus 1 rf8 `reagent.core/reaction` sites as reasons this surface ships, so the mismatch is on an audited, used path rather than speculative compatibility.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With only `(:require [reagent2.core :as r])`, `(r/reaction <body...>)` compiles with the same body syntax as stock Reagent and produces a `reagent2.ratom/Reaction`.
- A focused regression proves the body is deferred until deref, captures a reagent2 atom dependency, and recomputes after that atom changes.
- Macro expansion or an equivalent structural assertion proves the body is wrapped in a zero-argument function passed to `reagent2.ratom/make-reaction`.
- No public `reagent2.core/reaction` thunk-taking function remains; explicit thunk construction remains available as `reagent2.ratom/make-reaction`.
- Core namespace docs, IMPL-SPEC surface tables/§14.2, and migration guidance describe the macro accurately, with no claim that the old function form exists in stock Reagent.
- The reagent-slim package/test gates include and exercise the new `.clj` macro file from the published `src` path.

## Non-goals

- Adding dropped Reagent surfaces such as `track`, `track!`, `run!`, or `with-let`.
- Changing the Reaction kernel, batching scheduler, renderer, adapter map, or ratom macro semantics.
- Preserving the pre-alpha thunk-taking core spelling via a compatibility shim or introducing a second public factory alias.
- A broad stock-Reagent parity audit or migration codemod.

## Related beads

- Historical `rf2-6hyy` introduced the Stage-4 reagent-slim surface.
- Historical `rf2-kfpf` is the consumer audit cited for the 25 Dash8 core-reaction sites.
- Historical `rf2-n71j3q` clarified that `reagent2.ratom.clj` ships the ratom macro only; this task closes the distinct missing core macro.
- No duplicate was found across current Bead titles, descriptions, notes, close reasons, or comments for `reagent2.core/reaction`, `reagent.core/reaction`, `reaction macro`, or combined `reagent-slim` + `reaction` searches.

title: CLAUDE.md: record that 'bd update --notes' REPLACES notes — it has now silently destroyed accumulated notes twice
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-22 11:0x AUSEST by the mayor, on its own damage, and RECOVERED in full before
filing. This is a silent data-loss hazard in the tracker workflow CLAUDE.md governs, and CLAUDE.md
says nothing about it.

THE DEFECT. `bd update <id> --notes "<text>"` REPLACES the notes field. Its own help text reads
"Additional notes", which is what a reader takes it to mean. The append form exists and is a
different flag: `--append-notes` ("Append to existing notes (with newline separator)").

Nothing errors. bd prints its normal success line. The loss is invisible until somebody re-reads
the bead, which on a held bead may be never.

MEASURED LOSS IN ONE SESSION, five beads, ~72,800 characters:

  rf2-uelji     23641 -> 3094
  rf2-9wmqd     46569 -> 3294
  rf2-hic-063    8319 -> 2027
  rf2-hic-090    3729 -> 1766
  rf2-0puue      3218 -> 2504

IT HAS HAPPENED AT LEAST TWICE. rf2-y1jkm carries an earlier mayor's account of the same thing, in
its own words: "`bd update --notes` REPLACES the notes field; it does not append. I read the LANE
ORDER off rf2-0puue's notes, saw this bead named in it, and wrote a dispatch-readiness note without
first reading the note already on this bead. The warning that would have stopped me was the very
text I destroyed." That account survives only because that mayor restored it by hand from the
tracker's git history. A caveat recorded on ONE bead cannot reach the next person to run the
command; that is why this belongs in CLAUDE.md.

WHY CLAUDE.md AND NOT ONLY A MEMORY. The repo already carries a "Beads durability" section whose
whole subject is silent tracker data loss and the fact that the Dolt database, not the working
file, is the source of truth. This is the same class one level down: a routine command that
destroys tracker content with a success message. A `bd remember` has been written and is the
searchable store, but the durability section is where somebody about to mutate a bead is reading.

RECOVERY WORKS, IS CHEAP, AND SHOULD BE RECORDED WITH THE HAZARD -- an unrecoverable-sounding
warning invites panic, and this one is fully recoverable. `.beads/issues.jsonl` in git history is a
FULL DATABASE EXPORT, so the pre-damage notes sit in any checkpoint commit before the update:
extract with `git show <rev>:.beads/issues.jsonl`, rebuild as old + newline + current, write back.

TWO MECHANICAL TRAPS IN THE RECOVERY ITSELF, both measured here:
  * AN ARGUMENT-LENGTH CEILING between 26736 and 49864 characters on this shell. A longer --notes
    value fails SILENTLY -- non-zero exit, no message. Split at LINE boundaries into <=18000-char
    chunks, first via --notes then --append-notes, and verify by content probes taken from the
    start, middle and end rather than by exact length, because chunking shifts the length by a
    byte or two.
  * THE EXPORT IS STALE until `bd export` runs. Reading `.beads/issues.jsonl` straight after a
    successful `bd update` returns the PRE-update file, which reads as "the write failed" and
    invites a second destructive attempt. Checkpoint first, then measure.

THE REPAIR. A short entry in CLAUDE.md's Beads durability section: use --append-notes, never
--notes, to add to a bead; --notes is a replace and its help text says otherwise; recovery is from
the JSONL export in git history. Keep it to a few sentences with the recovery named -- the section
is already long and this is a command caveat, not a new subject.

BOUNDS. CLAUDE.md only. Do NOT edit AGENTS.md separately unless it is a symlink to CLAUDE.md --
check first with `ls -l`; the repo notes they are independent files that must be mirrored, so if
they are separate files the same edit belongs in both and the PR body should say which case held.
No new top-level section; this goes inside the existing Beads durability block. Nothing else in
CLAUDE.md moves.

GATES. CLAUDE.md is repo-root markdown, which is OUTSIDE scripts/check_doc_slugs.py's roots -- that
gate exits 0 on a broken link there. The gate that covers it is scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci.
Both run in test.yml's verify-readme-links job on every PR. mkdocs build --strict does NOT cover
repo-root markdown at all: docs_dir is `docs`, so CLAUDE.md was never a candidate. Do not nominate
it. Plant against check_readme_links.py.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-22 by worker notesrepl. PR #8698 (draft -> ready), branch worker/notesrepl-oaj6, rebased onto 7f0677cb89. This note was written with --append-notes, which is the subject of the bead.

WHAT LANDED. One bullet appended to CLAUDE.md's existing "## Beads durability" list, after the skip-worktree bullet. 1 insertion, 0 deletions; no heading added, renamed or removed; no new top-level section; nothing else in the file moves. The entry states that --notes REPLACES and --append-notes adds, that the help text ("Additional notes") reads the other way, that nothing errors, and that recovery from the JSONL export in git history is complete and cheap.

RECOVERY DETAIL: ONE OF THE TWO TRAPS KEPT, ONE DROPPED, DELIBERATELY.
- KEPT the argument-length ceiling (~27,000 characters; non-zero exit, no message; split at line boundaries into ~18,000-char chunks, --notes then --append-notes, verify by content probes from start/middle/end). It fails SILENTLY, which is this section's whole failure signature, and the worst measured loss (46,569 chars) is well over the ceiling, so a real recovery meets it.
- DROPPED the stale-export trap. Its general form is already the subject of the bullet three above mine ("A checkpoint re-exports; it never trusts the working file") and of the section's opening paragraph. Restating it would spend words on the one thing the section already establishes twice.

PREMISES CHECKED AT SOURCE.
- --notes REPLACES: CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not taken on trust. Throwaway bead: --notes AAA, then --notes BBB read back as BBB alone (AAA gone), then --append-notes CCC read back as BBB + newline + CCC. Probe bead deleted; re-read returns "no issue found". Help strings confirmed verbatim.
- Recovery source: CONFIRMED. .beads/issues.jsonl carries a "notes" key on 461 of 3222 rows (omitted when empty), so git show <rev>:.beads/issues.jsonl really does hold pre-damage notes.
- Earlier occurrence: CONFIRMED on rf2-y1jkm.
- AGENTS.md is not a symlink: CONFIRMED. Both mode 100644 in the index; 13426 bytes vs CLAUDE.md's 25840.
- CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN TEXT: the description says "the repo notes they are independent files that must be mirrored". THAT DOES NOT HOLD AT SOURCE. CLAUDE.md names AGENTS.md exactly once, at line 117, and only as a member of the repo-root-markdown roster explaining which link gate covers which path. No mirroring instruction exists in CLAUDE.md, in AGENTS.md, or anywhere under docs/the-mayor-method/.

AGENTS.md: NOT MIRRORED. Four reasons. (1) The receiving section does not exist there — AGENTS.md has no Beads-durability section, and this bead forbids a new top-level section. (2) The only beads content AGENTS.md has is TOOL-GENERATED: its "## Beads Issue Tracker" and "## Session Completion" sit inside the BEGIN/END BEADS INTEGRATION comment pair at lines 208-253, which carries a content hash (ca08a54f) and is regenerated by the beads integration, so a hand edit there is transient by design. CLAUDE.md carries the byte-identical block with the identical hash at lines 5-50, and its "## Beads durability" section sits deliberately OUTSIDE it, two lines past the END marker — that placement is the repo's existing answer to where hand-written beads guidance goes. (3) The mirroring premise does not hold (above). (4) The two files have already diverged by design: AGENTS.md's subject is worker mechanics (worktree guard, node_modules junction, backgrounded-gate absolute paths, gate-artefact naming, docs gates) and it carries none of CLAUDE.md's Beads durability, Git Conventions, ai/ tree, Workflow or Architecture sections.

GATES. scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci is the gate for this path; every exit code captured with echo $? on the run's own command line.
  baseline (edit committed, no plant)     check_readme_links --ci = 0
  sabotage (broken relative target planted MID-LINE at CLAUDE.md:72)
                                          check_readme_links --ci = 1, reporting
                                          "BROKEN TARGET: CLAUDE.md:72 -> docs/no-such-file-rf2-oaj6.md"
                                          check_doc_slugs.py      = 0, log never names CLAUDE.md
  restored                                check_readme_links --ci = 0
  re-run on final base after rebase       check_readme_links --ci = 0

The check_doc_slugs.py 0 on the same break is POSITIVE EVIDENCE for the gate-nomination claim rather than an assertion of it: repo-root markdown is outside that gate's roots.

CONTROL MECHANICS. Plant mid-line because this checkout is CRLF and an end-of-line anchor matches nothing. Match count read BEFORE patching: the anchor occurred exactly once, so the plant could not silently no-op. The gate prints nothing on success, so it affords no root-printing route — the discrimination is the red itself, since the fault existed only in the worker worktree. Restore verified by BLOB hash against the committed object (167721802beb74deaad624d2523f3165a5d33696 -> 062942c71a3daa9e0cc9c1ff3f4ce06cee3a5f5b under the plant -> 167721802beb74deaad624d2523f3165a5d33696 restored, equal to git rev-parse HEAD:CLAUDE.md), not by reading a diff. Own edit committed before planting, so the checkout restore could not discard it.

NOT NOMINATED: mkdocs build --strict (docs_dir is docs, so CLAUDE.md was never a candidate and its absence from exclude_docs is not evidence of coverage); no CLJS, browser, compile or lint lane.

HAND CHECKS (nothing gates this file's prose), each with a positive control so a zero is a check that passed:
- merge-base diff read for what it would REVERT: 1 insertion, 0 deletions; deletion lines excluding the header = 0, while the same pipeline reads 19 against commit 521e4628 which does delete from this file. main moved twice while the work ran (two .beads checkpoints, no CLAUDE.md change); rebased and re-ran the gate on the final base.
- headings added/changed = 0 on my diff; same pattern reads 1 against 521e4628.
- no absolute paths, no operator-specific content in the added line; pattern fires against a control string containing one.
- the addition contains no markdown links at all, so no new link target or anchor exists to follow; no table, so no column count to check.

title: ci: the Playwright --with-deps hang leaves NO annotation and now reds the trunk — the '0 failures in 183 samples' trade in test.yml has gone stale
description:
MEASURED by the mayor 2026-08-20 from CI, not from memory. Every premise below is a CLAIM — check each at source before acting.

THE TRUNK IS RED AND THE CAUSE IS ONE STEP. On main run 32206828695 (push, head 03b76d4eede2) FIVE browser jobs died together: CLJS hicasso HMR cancelled at 40.3 min (cap 40), CLJS hicasso controlled-input cancelled at 25.3 min (cap 25), Adapter testbed smokes cancelled at 30.3 min, docs/cljs playground cancelled at 15.3 min, Tenant-switcher testbed smoke FAILURE at 5.6 min. On the later main run 32216390799 (head 989680b16f, the trunk tip at filing) MCP conformance FAILED at 6.2 min and docs/cljs playground cancelled at 15.3 min again.

THE FAILING STEP NAMES ITSELF. In job 95959283361 the log reads: Playwright cache HIT and restored (key Linux-playwright-96be61e0...), then `Run npx playwright install --with-deps chromium || .github/scripts/playwright-install-failed.sh` at 04:41:54Z, then at 04:47:06Z `The action 'Install Playwright chromium (for hermetic browser preload)' has timed out after 5 minutes`, then `Terminate orphan process: pid (2730) (npm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium)`. The browser DOWNLOAD was cached and skipped, so the hang is in the apt hop under `--with-deps` — exactly the second mode `.github/scripts/playwright-install-failed.sh:176` already names under rf2-swos.

THE DEFECT THIS BEAD IS FILED ON IS NOT THE OUTAGE. It is that the hang is INVISIBLE. The `|| playwright-install-failed.sh` handler fires only on a NON-ZERO EXIT. A step the runner guillotines on `timeout-minutes` is KILLED, not failed, so the handler never runs: the job reports `cancelled`, prints no "no gate ran" annotation, and carries no verdict on the code under test. A reader then cannot tell provisioning from a real regression without opening the raw log, which is what this diagnosis cost.

THE TRADE IS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN AND ITS NUMBER HAS GONE STALE. `.github/workflows/test.yml` (the comment block immediately above the `Install Playwright (Chromium + system deps)` step near line 4451) records the gap as deliberately unpatched: moving the cap into the command (`timeout 270 npx playwright install ...`) would fix it but breaks `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py`'s `^npx playwright install\b` setup pattern and would fail-open the gap map — "At 0 failures in 183 samples that trade is not worth taking." THAT DENOMINATOR IS NOW WRONG. This is at minimum SEVEN job-level incidents across two main runs and one PR run inside a single day. Re-derive the rate at the tip; do not carry my count forward by adding to it.

IN SCOPE
1. Re-derive the true failure rate from CI at the tip, and correct the stale comment wherever that trade is written down.
2. Close the no-annotation gap WITHOUT fail-opening `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py`. The gap map's pattern and the install call sites must keep agreeing, so whatever shape is chosen, change the pattern AND the call sites in ONE commit and prove the gap map still resolves every site.
3. Verify by PLANTING, not by assertion: make the chosen mechanism actually produce the annotation on a simulated hang, and show the red.

OUT OF SCOPE — do not widen any job cap. Do not remove `--with-deps` without evidence the system deps are already present on the runner image. Do not touch any measurement threshold or budget constant.

A reasoned REFUSAL is a complete and good deliverable: "the trade still holds at the re-derived rate, here is the number" is a correct outcome if that is what the evidence says.

HOT ZONE: `.github/workflows/*` and `.github/scripts/*` are one-toucher-at-a-time. This bead owns them.
close_reason: PR #8539 (ready, mergeable). 14 job-capped Playwright install sites take an in-command deadline (timeout -k 10 720 ... || <handler> $?) so the guillotine now fires the handler; the 3 step-capped sites keep the bare form because the runner ALREADY annotates those by step name (measured verbatim on jobs 95959283361/95932283494), while a job-cap guillotine names nothing (95959283484/95932283700). check_fast_pr_gap.py's setup pattern gained a narrow optional timeout group in the SAME commit; --list is byte-identical to the trunk baseline, proved discriminating by two plants (pattern revert -> 96->106 unrun; nice -n 5 prefix -> 96->97). Rate re-derived over 140 completed test.yml runs, all attempts: 7/377 non-success = 1.86%, of which 5 are install stalls = 1.33% — the written '0 in 183' is stale. title: hicasso: arm the within-run LEVEL witness — both modes still certify, and the high population is now n=3
description:
THE DEFECT SURVIVES ITS PARENT. rf2-77gz8 closed because its DECISION RULE was
discharged — the work count is identical across the mode, so different-work-per-
write is excluded. But the BUG that bead is named for is untouched: BOTH MODES
STILL CERTIFY. The leg witness asks whether a window's legs are ALIKE, and in
both modes they are; it has nothing to say about which of two LEVELS the window
sits at. So the gate passes a window whose level is ~13-20% off, and any figure
quoted from this arm from a single run is still a coin toss.

WHY IT CAN NOW BE ARMED, WHICH IS WHAT CHANGED. rf2-77gz8 held a within-run level
witness as a PROPOSAL explicitly because the high population was n = 1 RUN, which
cannot set a threshold. It is now n = 3 runs: alloc-9jrhi/bisect-1 (+3,792 B,
unarmed) and alloc-77gz8 run09 and run19 (+2,532 B, armed) — the latter two
committed with full per-round data and a work census.

THE WITNESS. Every run already records what it needs: compare the certified level
BEFORE the transition against the certified level after it, WITHIN one run, and
refuse when the step exceeds a declared bound. Both high runs hold ~19,004 at
rounds 1-3, ramp over rounds 4-5, and settle from round 6 — so the two populations
are separated inside a single run's own data, with no new instrument and no
second run.

THE POPULATIONS, from the committed corpus (this is the part to re-derive rather
than trust): the normal population's round-3-to-4 movement sits in the low
hundreds of bytes, and the mode's is thousands. rf2-77gz8's re-analysis quoted
-43 to +158 B normal against 3,912-3,948 B in the mode. NOTE that a re-derivation
using median-of-rounds-1-3 against median-of-rounds-4-6 gives a WIDER normal band
(about -961 to +896 B on the same datasets), so THE BAND DEPENDS ON THE
DEFINITION and the definition must be pinned before a threshold is set. Do not
take either band on trust.

WHAT TO DECIDE. Whether this becomes a REFUSAL (exit non-zero, like the leg
witness) or a recorded verdict that gates only what may be QUOTED. The arm's
figures are load-bearing for the published allocation series, and a refusal that
fires on a legitimate run is expensive; a verdict that nobody reads is useless.
rf2-77gz8's own framing was a refusal "when the step exceeds a declared bound".

CONSTRAINT. The rig blobs are the constancy guarantee the whole published series
rests on. Any witness must be computable from data ALREADY recorded — it is, see
above — so this is an analysis-side change, not a rig change, and must not alter
the bundle the arm compiles.

Two bench-class workers on one box WEDGE rather than fail.

AND IT IS COUPLED TO rf2-zu82n — dispatch them TOGETHER, a233t FIRST. rf2-zu82n registers alloc_level_witness.test.cjs into the test:script-helpers spine; this bead is the fail-open INSIDE that same witness, where segmentsOf creates entries only for segment names that occur and adjudicates only when zero segments occur, so a record missing one whole measured segment formats CERTIFIED. Arming the spine gate before fixing the fail-open would wire in a gate that cannot fire on the defect it exists to catch — the exact shape this project keeps finding. Neither bead names the other; that is why this is recorded here.
close_reason:
FAIL-OPEN CLOSED, and the two decisions the bead asked for were already discharged. PR #8569, first of two commits.

THE PREMISE HELD AND WAS REPRODUCED FIRST. segmentsOf instantiated a map entry only the first time a segment name OCCURRED; the consumer loop iterated over exactly what existed; the only guard fired when ZERO occurred. Measured on the committed alloc-77gz8/run01 with uix-subs deleted from every one of its 18 rounds: CERTIFIED, half the arm's measurement gone, the verdict line still reading 'every segment holds its level across the transition'.

THE REPAIR. MEASURED_SEGMENTS declares what the floor arm measures. segmentsOf seeds its map from that roster, so a declared segment the record never mentions arrives at the consumer loop as an empty row list rather than as no entry at all, and is refused there under a third code, level-segment. A segment PRESENT but not declared is still adjudicated: the roster is a floor on what must be there, not a whitelist of what may be. adjudicate and scoreCorpus both take it as an option.

THE BAND DEFINITION, RE-DERIVED RATHER THAN TAKEN ON TRUST. Pinned form is min(certified r1-5) -> median(certified r>=6). Re-derived: normal n=60 at 96..194 B (0.494%..1.015%), elevated n=40 at 2,616..3,984 B (13.766%..21.070%). NEITHER band this bead quoted is that one — -43..+158 B is the one-round form, which OVERLAPS the elevated band by 1,452 B on the larger corpus, and -961..+896 B is the median-of-r4-6 form. Both were already tabulated and defended in the shipped header; my re-derivation reproduces it exactly, so nothing was re-pinned.

REFUSAL vs RECORDED VERDICT was likewise already settled by this bead's earlier commits on main: it is a REFUSAL that exits non-zero. level-segment is a refusal for the same reason level-window is — a segment never recorded has no level to compare and no figure to quote, so refusing it and quoting nothing from it are the same statement.

COSTS THE CORPUS NOTHING, MEASURED. All 103 records carrying an alloc object carry exactly reagent-subs and uix-subs in every round. Corpus control unchanged in every figure: 101 admissible, 100 scored, 40 elevated, 60 normal, zero false refusals, zero misses, same bands, missing-segment 0.

PROVED AGAINST A REAL RECORD. The gate reads alloc-77gz8/run01 from disk, asserts it certifies intact, deletes one whole segment in memory, and asserts the result refuses with level-segment, reports the absent segment, still reads the survivor, and no longer formats CERTIFIED. Reverting the witness to its pre-repair state takes the gate to 9/14. Ten fixtures added, 26 -> 36.

ANALYSIS-SIDE ONLY: no dataset changed, no rig file changed, no bench window taken, and the bundle the arm compiles is untouched.
