title: hicasso: bisect F_old's surviving ~1-3.5 KB drop across 2026-08-08 -> 2026-08-13, on ONE instrument
description:
MEASURED BY rf2-nkeba, 2026-08-17, PR #8434, record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-controls-target-is-not-the-quantity-it-is-read-against.md

WHAT rf2-nkeba SETTLED, so this bead starts from the right place. V1's across-time clause failed by a published 16 - 20%. Most of that is a comparison artefact: the 2026-08-08 target is a round MEDIAN of rise/W taken on a pre-prime, pre-certificate instrument over an UNSELECTED population, while today's figures are per-window values on a CERTIFIED subset with the prime excluded. Three differences at once, none of them documented.

WHAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION, and it is this bead's subject. Against the LOWEST of the six 2026-08-08 rounds with its largest step removed — the most generous like-for-like the surviving artefacts support — today's certified readings are still low by:

  reagent-subs   >= 982 B   (4.7% - 7.0%)
  uix-subs       >= 2,472 B (10.7% - 14.9%)

A gap at every cell. Smaller than published, and real.

WHAT IS ALREADY ELIMINATED, so this bead does not re-tread it:

- THE RESEEDED PAGE WIDTH — REFUTED on two independent grounds. `:p0/write-all` is byte-identical at 4a1537cb71 and 2e993181f8 and rebuilds `cells-n` = 300 regardless of the seed; the floor arm holds no subscription and the seed runs inside `prepare!` outside the measured region; and V1's own first clause reads F_old flat to <= 117 B over a 24x seeded-width range, i.e. <= ~351 B extrapolated to 300 cells.
- THE PRIME — accounted, and re-derived on the 2026-08-08 data itself at ~6,231 / ~6,267 B (1,038 / 1,045 per write), SMALLER than the pooled 6,966 the corpus subtracts.
- THE WORK UNIT — byte-identical at both revisions: same three statements, same drain split, same stride-2 sampling, same `write-all!` and `dispatch-sync!`.
- THE TOOLCHAIN — playwright 1.59.1, react/react-dom 19.2.0, shadow-cljs 3.4.10 at both revisions. CAVEAT: the 2026-08-08 dataset records no runtime version, so a resident-binary difference is neither ruled in nor out.

WHAT IS LEFT. Drift in the event pipeline. The drop was already present by 2026-08-13 (legMedian 19,781 / 20,446), so it happened inside 2026-08-08 -> 2026-08-13. Twenty-two commits landed under implementation/core/src in that interval and NONE was shown to be it.

WHAT THIS BEAD WOULD RUN. A bisection: the floor arm at B = 24 under write-all, at two or three revisions spanning that interval, on the CURRENT instrument at every point so the estimator is constant and only the substrate moves. That is the one design constraint that matters — a bisection that also moves the rig measures nothing.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN WINDOW rather than an extension of rf2-nkeba's. It needs a browser, it needs the rig frozen across several revisions, and Shape 6 forbids adding a rung or an arm inside a running window. rf2-nkeba added neither and launched no browser.

NOT ASSUMED: that the substrate is where it went. That is the surviving candidate, not an established one, and a bisection that comes back flat across the interval is a legitimate and informative result — it would push the question onto the runtime, which the pins cannot settle.

comments.text:
PREMISE CORRECTED ON THE RECORD, and this beads brief is reframed. PR #8442, commit 089448794a.

WHAT THIS BEAD MAY NOT ASSUME. Its description says the drop is "Smaller than published, and real." It is not established. The 982 - 3,456 B range is the arithmetic difference between a round MEDIAN of rise/W over an UNSELECTED pre-prime 2026-08-08 population and PER-WINDOW values on a CERTIFIED 2026-08-17 subset. The record itself establishes those two are not comparable on three axes at once, and then differences them anyway. Non-comparability forecloses the comparison; it does not shrink the effect. The range has no defined estimand, so there is no residual for this bead to locate.

The non-overlap argument does not rescue it. Todays five readings lying below all six 2026-08-08 per-round values does not bound the selection effect, because certification can correlate with level - a subpopulation selected by the leg witness can sit wholly below the unselected range with nothing having moved at all.

ALSO NOT ESTABLISHED: that the event pipeline is where it went. The record says in its own words that a resident-binary difference is neither ruled in nor out, and that the selection effect is unquantified. Naming the pipeline "what is left" contradicts both. Three candidates survive untested and none is preferred: event-pipeline drift, resident runtime, selection.

WHAT STANDS, and it is what makes this bead still worth running: the seed-width refutation (source plus the controls own first clause), the byte-identical work unit, the identical toolchain pins, and the prime term re-derived on the 2026-08-08 data at ~6,231 / ~6,267 B. Those are re-derivations from committed artefacts and none depends on the comparison.

REFRAMED SUBJECT, which supersedes the descriptions framing. Run the floor arm at B = 24 under write-all at two or three revisions spanning 2026-08-08 -> 2026-08-13, on ONE instrument throughout, as a HYPOTHESIS TEST of the event-pipeline candidate. It measures a within-instrument difference across revisions, which is a comparable quantity and is exactly what the across-time clause is not. A flat result is a full result: it does not confirm a residual it was never entitled to assume, and it pushes the question onto the runtime and the selection effect.

The description stands as the original filing; this comment is the operative brief. Bead stays OPEN - the audit item is discharged, the measurement window it exists to run is unstarted and out of a prose workers fence.

title: hicasso: the allocation arms' leg dispersion is round-indexed — 6/6 runs, mechanism unidentified
description:
MEASURED by rf2-e9wr's window on 2026-08-16 (PR #8377), on the instrument
rf2-oiy1 primed at ecd4f6e7f3. Filed rather than chased: identifying the
mechanism needs an instrument a measurement window may not build mid-window.

THE OBSERVATION. Over 72 floor-arm windows (P0_ALLOC_PLAN=floor, B in {4,24,96},
both writes, six rounds each), the relative dispersion of a window's MEASURED
work legs is a function of the ROUND INDEX, not of the page, the write or the
substrate. Restricting to windows with no observed collection (the falls gate,
which is independent of tau):

  round 0   n=5    16.67% - 1,407.95%
  round 1   n=6     0.07% - 1,835.79%
  round 2   n=11    2.66% -    20.37%   <- NONE below 2.66%
  round 3   n=11    0.00% -     0.19%   <- ALL at or below 0.19%
  round 4   n=7     0.06% - 1,505.41%
  round 5   n=7     0.00% -    13.29%

Rounds 2 and 3 are the clean statement and THEY HOLD IN EACH OF THE SIX RUNS
SEPARATELY -- six independent browser launches, each with both round-2 windows
wide and both round-3 windows tight. Machine load does not align to a round
index across six separate processes, so this is a property of the arm work unit
and its round schedule rather than of the box.

WHY IT MATTERS, and it is not cosmetic. The leg witness rests on the premise
that a window's legs are W repetitions of ONE work unit. On the controls that
premise holds exactly (17 of 18 windows byte-identical). On the arms it does
not, and rf2-oiy1's prime did not fix it -- the prime removes the FIRST leg,
and this is a term that recurs in later legs. Consequence for rf2-e9wr: tau
calibrated on the arms' own clean windows lands at ~0.004 read at round 3 and
~0.41 read at round 2, two orders of magnitude apart, so tau is NOT IDENTIFIED
by the arms' data. That is why rf2-e9wr refused to pin it.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. Instrument the arm work unit's allocation by site across
the round sequence -- the excesses are positive legs against a byte-identical
cohort with ZERO falling steps, so they are allocation by the page's own heap,
not a collector artefact and not another process. A candidate worth excluding
first: the excess magnitudes (+476 to +7,456 B, median 2,640 B over 20 windows)
overlap the prime excess's own scale (median 6,864 B), which would suggest the
same term recurring rather than a distinct one -- but that is a HYPOTHESIS this
window did not test, and the byte values do not fall into clean quanta.

DO NOT DISCHARGE THIS BY WIDENING tau. rf2-e9wr established that no honest
calibration exists in either direction; widening runs against that and against
Shape 6.

EVIDENCE: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-arms-spread-does-not-collapse.md
(PR #8377), sections 'The bimodality is round-indexed, in all six runs' and
'Why no tau follows, on either calibration population'.

stride of 3 instead of 2, taking one extra counter reading at the work unit's
ONE seam — between the `dispatch-sync` through the event pipeline and signal
graph, and the `flushSync` commit that follows it. A leg then decomposes as
`dispatch + drain`, exactly, over the same outer pair of readings the shipped
window takes.

THERE IS NO THIRD SEAM that does not change what the arm measures. A finer
split means instrumenting re-frame's own pipeline from a bench fixture, and an
arm carrying instrumentation is not the arm whose figures are published. Two
sites is what the work unit affords, and it is the split that separates the
framework's write from the substrate's commit.

FENCES HELD. Off by default; the collapse is the identity on a stride-2
stream, so every published row is byte-identical and every `allocSteps` /
`allocPrimeSplit` pin stands unedited. The certificate is read off the
COLLAPSED stream, so `allocSteps` never sees a by-site stream and `rise`,
`falls` and `maxStep` cannot move. TAU IS UNTOUCHED in either direction, and a
pin drives every certificate constant in fresh processes with the mode armed
and without it, requiring them equal.

dispatch could not exclude it — that needs a window. What changed is that it is
now DECIDABLE, and asymmetrically: sites DISAGREEING settles it (one term

statements wide), and a window with no dispersion reports `null` rather than
`false`.

excess is extraordinarily tight (p25 6,800, p75 6,888 — 1.3% of its median,

title: [method] the stranded sweep starts from the worktrees — the in-progress list is empty while workers run
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD-REREAD LOOP 2026-08-15 22:52. The mayor wrote this fix, the mayor-checkout pre-commit hook refused it for touching worker-tracked surfaces, and that hook was right — so it is filed here with the fix written out, exactly as docs/the-mayor-method/README.md instructs.

THE DRIFT. Both copies of the stranded-sweep rule tell the reader to start from the tracker's in-progress list. On this repo that list is routinely EMPTY WHILE WORKERS ARE RUNNING, because dispatches do not claim their beads.

MEASURED, 2026-08-15 22:14. `bd list --status in_progress --limit 0` returned nothing at a moment when worker/retire-final was demonstrably alive: 80 files touched in 15 minutes and a JVM gate started 3 seconds before the read. The three beads it held — rf2-0yp7w.4, rf2-0yp7w.6, rf2-0yp7w.10 — all read `open`.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A MISSED STRAND. The loop's nominal input is empty by construction rather than by health, so a "0 in progress, sweep clean" report is not evidence of anything, and the handoff's "15 consecutive clean stranded sweeps" may be 15 reads of an empty set. Worse: when a worker does die, its beads sit `open`, look dispatchable, and the next dispatch tick is free to send a SECOND WORKER AT THE SAME BRANCH — the collision the method spends a section forbidding. The blindness converts a strand into a collision. This is not hypothetical: retire-final died on a session limit at 22:26 and its three beads read `open` throughout.

TWO FILES, BOTH IN ONE PR, because two copies of one rule disagree within days and the method-reread loop names exactly that failure.

=== FILE 1: docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md, section 4, the stranded sweep ===
AFTER the existing line "Look for items marked in-progress. If no live worker holds one, it may be stranded." INSERT two paragraphs. Keep this file GENERIC — no bd commands, no repo paths, no PowerShell:

**But start from the worktrees, because that set is routinely empty while workers are running.** Unless your dispatches explicitly claim their items, a worker holds items that still read *open*, and this loop's nominal input is empty by construction rather than by health. Measured here: the in-progress list returned nothing while a worker was provably alive — files being written seconds earlier, a gate process burning CPU — and the three items it held all read open. A *"nothing in progress, sweep clean"* report is then not evidence of anything, and a streak of them is a streak of reads of an empty set.

The failure is worse than a missed strand. A dead worker's items sit open, look dispatchable, and the next dispatch tick sends a **second worker to the same branch** — the collision this method spends a section forbidding. So enumerate the worktrees first, sweep each for recent file activity, and map trees to items; where an item *is* marked in-progress, read it too. It is a real signal, just never the complete one.

=== FILE 2: .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md, after the line beginning "Read the in-progress beads:" ===
INSERT two paragraphs. This file pins CONCRETE commands, so name them:

**START FROM THE WORKTREES, NOT FROM THAT LIST — the in-progress set is routinely EMPTY while workers are running, because dispatches do not claim their beads.** Measured 2026-08-15 22:14: `bd list --status in_progress` returned nothing at a moment when `worker/retire-final` was demonstrably alive — 80 files touched in 15 minutes, a JVM gate started 3 seconds earlier — and the three beads it held (`rf2-0yp7w.4`, `.6`, `.10`) all read `open`. So this loop's nominal input is empty by construction rather than by health, and a "0 in progress, sweep clean" report is **not evidence of anything**. Do not quote a streak of clean sweeps as assurance; a streak of reads of an empty set is what it may be. The failure is worse than a missed strand: the dead worker's beads sit `open`, look dispatchable, and the next dispatch tick is free to send a **second worker at the same branch** — the collision the method spends a section forbidding.

So enumerate `git worktree list` first and sweep each worker worktree for activity, then map trees to beads. One command settles a tree: count files touched recently, excluding `node_modules` and `.git`, and **read the newest filenames** — paths under `.cpcache`, `.scratch` or `implementation/out` mean a gate is running, a tracked source or doc file means the worker is editing, near-zero means a strand. Cross-check against processes started recently (`java`, `node`). That test is keyed to the worktree, which is where the truth is, rather than to a tracker field nobody sets. Where a bead IS marked in-progress, read it too — it is a real signal, just not the only one, and never the complete one.

=== SCOPE FENCE ===
Those two files only. Do NOT add a claim step to dispatch briefs — that is the operator's open call between (a) briefs claim their beads and (b) the sweep reads worktrees; this bead implements (b) while leaving (a) available, and the two are not exclusive. Do NOT touch mayor-dispatch.md, mayor-hygiene.md, or the dispatch-prompt-template.

=== GATE ===
`python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` covers docs/the-mayor-method/ link targets and heading anchors, and runs unconditionally in test.yml's verify-readme-links job. `mkdocs build --strict` also covers docs/the-mayor-method/ (it is NOT under the exclude_docs block that hides docs/design/). Run both. No fenced code blocks are added, so the guide-samples digest gate is untouched — say so in the PR body rather than leaving it unstated.

MAYOR, METHOD-REREAD LOOP 2026-08-15 23:44 — SCOPE AMENDED. Two further drifts found, both in mayor-hygiene.md, and they ride THIS bead rather than a sibling because they are the same surface and two workers on the method files would conflict. The original two-file scope in the description is SUPERSEDED by this note: the fence is now THREE files.

=== DRIFT 2: TWO COMMAND FILES DIRECTLY CONTRADICT EACH OTHER, AND THE READER IS SENT TO THE STALE ONE ===

`.claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md:8` says the liveness discriminator is:
    "The discriminator is `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/worker/<name>` against the SHA you recorded last tick"

`.claude/commands/mayor-posture.md:26` says the OPPOSITE, and says so as an explicit correction:
    "Read the LOCAL ref, not `git ls-remote` — this line said 'ask the REMOTE' until 2026-08-14 and it produced a false strand signal on three workers at once."

posture carries the measurement: on 2026-08-14 05:15 `ls-remote` reported all three live workers unchanged since the previous tick, while their local refs showed `ciretire-cluster` at `b26de366d4` committed 04:59 and `walkctl-1huc` at `73508c1339` committed 05:08. Every worker worktree here is a LINKED worktree sharing one `.git`, so a commit moves the local ref instantly while `origin` moves only when the worker chooses to push — the remote lags, and it lags in the direction that reads as death.

*** AND IT IS WORSE THAN A PLAIN DISAGREEMENT. *** mayor-posture.md:24 tells the reader that "`mayor-hygiene.md` carries why each misleads and IS THE ONE PLACE THAT REASONING LIVES". So posture DEFERS to hygiene for the reasoning while contradicting its conclusion. A reader following that pointer lands on the superseded rule with nothing to warn them.

FIX: correct mayor-hygiene.md:8 to name the LOCAL ref (`git rev-parse worker/<name>`), keep its ahead-count and two-clocks reasoning, which is correct and is genuinely the one place it lives, and fold in posture's measured false-strand evidence so the correction carries its own warrant. Do not delete the `ls-remote` discussion — record it as the superseded rule with the date and the reason, the way this project treats every other superseded record.

=== DRIFT 3: THE CONTAINMENT TEST IS ENFORCED BUT NOWHERE WRITTEN ===

Neither `mayor-hygiene.md` nor `loops.md` §5 contains the words cherry, patch-id or patch-equivalent. Both files answer "is this worker ALIVE?" and neither answers "is this branch's work ALREADY ON MAIN, so may I delete it?"

That second question is the one branch and worktree cleanup actually turns on, and THE OBVIOUS TEST IS WRONG HERE. This repository merges by REBASE, so a merged branch's commits get new SHAs and never become ancestors of main. Measured tonight over 63 worktrees: 60 branches read "ahead of main by 1 to 3 commits" and 58 of them were fully merged. Reading the ahead count would have kept all 58 forever; ignoring it would have deleted the 3 genuinely unmerged spike commits on `worker/receipts-hic081`. `git cherry origin/main <branch>` settled both directions in one command — `-` means an equivalent patch is already upstream, `+` means genuinely new. It returned `-` for all 58 and `+` for receipts-hic081.

FIX: add the containment test to mayor-hygiene.md's branch/worktree cleanup guidance, stating (a) that ancestry and the ahead count are both useless under rebase-merge, (b) that `git cherry origin/main <branch>` is the test, (c) that it protects in BOTH directions, and (d) the measured 58-versus-1 result as its warrant. Note the existing ahead-count paragraph already explains WHY the count misleads for liveness — this is the same trap on a different question, so cross-reference rather than restate.

=== WHY ALL THREE RIDE ONE PR ===
loops.md §4 (drift 1), mayor-posture.md (drift 1), mayor-hygiene.md (drifts 2 and 3). Method and command files are one surface and a hot zone; splitting them across two workers guarantees a conflict. Keep the same gate: `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` plus `mkdocs build --strict` (which DOES cover docs/the-mayor-method/, unlike docs/design/). Still no fenced code blocks added, so the guide-samples digest gate stays untouched — say so in the PR body rather than leaving it unstated.

comments.text:
MAYOR, METHOD-REREAD LOOP 2026-08-16 00:52 — SCOPE AMENDED AGAIN. Two more drifts, both in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md's Shape 6. The fence is now FOUR files. Both were verified absent by grep before filing.

These are rules I ENFORCED in live briefs tonight and which the template does not carry, so the next mayor writing a Shape 6 brief will not include them.

=== DRIFT 4: SHAPE 6 GOVERNS THE RUN AND SAYS NOTHING ABOUT THE WRITE-UP ===

Every measurement PR merged on 2026-08-15/16 was audited, and EVERY ONE had its published claim stated slightly stronger than its evidence. Three for three, three different workers, all exemplary on the run itself:

  #8326 / rf2-pqyxz — the page calls three values "run-medians" and their spans "effect medians" and "null medians". lane/ratio-between computes no median; it stores the ARITHMETIC MEAN of five per-round ratios in :mean. The effect-versus-null separation is the whole stated basis for "outside instrument resolution", so the conclusion rests on the estimator being what it says it is.
  #8327 / rf2-d360z — a 0.058 spread is said to "loosely bracket" 0.9718, but the three measured ratios are 0.8864 / 0.9444 / 0.9189 and 0.9718 is ABOVE their maximum. It brackets nothing. Separately, the whole 0.100 ms spread is attributed to "the instrument's own run-to-run noise" with "nothing changing between runs", while the SAME paragraph records queue readings of 1, 1 and 2 and concedes two cannot be proven outside a measurement phase.
  #8328 / rf2-3l6hf — see drift 5 below; the write-up asserted a bound its data could not support.

THE SHAPE, AND IT IS NOT CARELESSNESS: what slipped every time is the prose ONE LAYER ABOVE the number. A worker that has just spent an hour being rigorous writes its summary in ordinary confident English, and ordinary confident English overclaims. Not one audit overturned a measurement or a refusal — what they corrected is the sentence a future reader will quote, and readers quote the sentence, not the log. That is how a measured result becomes a false premise in someone else's brief three weeks later, which is exactly what premises-are-claims catches on the INPUT side. This is the same defect on the OUTPUT side and nothing was checking it.

ADD TO SHAPE 6, wording as enforced tonight:

  "Your published sentences are claims too, and they are audited. For every summarising
   statement you write, name the exact evidence that licenses it and check the arithmetic
   of any comparison in it. Do not attribute an observed spread to a single cause unless
   your own data excludes the others — if your queue samples include a non-zero inside a
   measurement phase, you may not call the dispersion the instrument's alone. Name the
   estimator you actually computed, not the one the surrounding prose habitually says.
   A hedged sentence that survives audit is worth more than a confident one that does not."

=== DRIFT 5: NOTHING SAYS AN IMPOSSIBLE READING CANNOT BOUND THE QUANTITY ===

rf2-3l6hf reported reader membership as "bounded: < 0.006 ms/commit", derived from its own most-negative reading. I believed it, wrote it into rf2-07rnj's brief AS GUIDANCE, and reported it to the operator. The merged-PR audit of #8328 refuted it, and rf2-07rnj's own run 2 then read -0.0141 — more than twice the claimed floor — refuting it a second time on independent arithmetic.

THE RULE: let an observed delta y equal an unknown positive true cost t plus estimator error e. A reading of y = -0.0062 proves only that the negative error excursion exceeded 0.0062 + t. It does NOT make +/-0.0062 a calibrated symmetric floor and it CANNOT upper-bound t. A most-negative observation is a statement about the ERROR TERM, not about the quantity. Comparing most-negative readings from DIFFERENT positive-cost arms at two window widths likewise cannot establish a floor-scaling factor.

ADD TO SHAPE 6:

  "An impossible reading tells you the instrument's error reached at least that far. It does
   not calibrate the error and it does not bound the thing you are measuring. If you report a
   bound, name the NULL OR CONTROL ARM that produced it. A bound derived from the impossible
   readings themselves is not a bound — report the term as UNRESOLVED instead."

AND ONE LINE FOR THE MAYOR'S SIDE, because the process failure was mine and premises-are-claims did not catch it: a NUMBER THE BRIEF ASSERTS IS A LEAN TOO. Workers read guidance as instruction and premises as claims, so anything phrased as guidance bypasses the check entirely. Before writing a predecessor's figure into a brief, ask what produced it. Here one question would have caught it: what null arm produced that bound?

=== FENCE, UPDATED ===
Four files, ONE PR, one agent: docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md, docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md, .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md. PR #8632 rewrote `.claude/commands/mayor-posture.md` in full, including the current stranded-sweep block. Its executable fallback is still:

  find <worktree> -newermt '20 minutes ago' -type f | grep -v '/\.git/' | wc -l

It excludes `.git` but still descends `node_modules`. In these worktrees that may be the shared junction or a large local dependency tree, so package mtimes can manufacture thousands of “recent” files unrelated to the worker and make a real strand look alive. The next sentence still says “near-zero means a strand” even though the generic method correctly classifies file activity as a fallible write-clock signal. Align the command with the already-recorded exclusion and describe the result as corroboration, not a verdict. Preserve the harness-first and message-before-redispatch rules.

The second standing #8330 correction also remains at dispatch-prompt-template.md:431: “If you report a bound, name the NULL OR CONTROL ARM that produced it.” Narrow it to bounds inferred from estimator/noise-floor behaviour and permit direct analytic or independently calibrated warrants; do not require an unnecessary experimental arm for every valid bound. This line was outside #8632's added block, but it is part of this exact owner's unresolved audit record and is why the owner must not remain closed.

title: EPIC: retire and REMOVE re-frame.freehand and re-frame.ui — 821 tracked files plus live core and ssr references
description:
MIKE'S RULING 2026-08-14: 'Freehand and re-frame2.ui are to be retired and removed ASAP.' The architecture is a Reagent adapter and a UIx adapter, plus hicasso as re-frame2 native.

CENSUS TAKEN AT TRUNK TIP, 2026-08-14 — these are measurements, and a later pass must re-take them rather than trust them:

  implementation/freehand   590 tracked files
  implementation/ui         231 tracked files

REFERENCES OUTSIDE THOSE TREES, by directory, highest first: spec/conformance/freehand/fixtures 46, implementation/scripts 19, spec 18, docs/design/freehand/decisions 17, docs/api 12, scripts 11, examples/real-apps/realworld_resources 10, docs/EP 10, implementation/ssr/test 9, docs/design/hicasso/studio 9, implementation/core/test 8, implementation/core/src 7, tools/xray/src 6, implementation/ssr/src 6.

THE LINE THAT MAKES THIS AN EPIC RATHER THAN A DELETION: implementation/core/src and implementation/ssr/src BOTH reference Freehand. These are live runtime dependencies in first-class artefacts, not documentation. Deleting the trees without untangling those breaks the build.

ALSO IMPLICATED: implementation/shadow-cljs.edn carries freehand source paths and a :node-test-freehand build; .github/scripts and .github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml name freehand; spec/ has 18 referencing files and 46 conformance fixtures — spec is HOT ZONE and takes one toucher.

SUGGESTED PHASING, not ruled — the first dispatch should propose the order and defend it:
  1. Map every reference and classify each as (a) a live dependency that must be re-homed, (b) a test or fixture that dies with the tree, (c) prose that must be re-pointed or deleted.
  2. Re-home or delete the core and ssr dependencies FIRST. Nothing else is safe until those are clear.
  3. Then the build configuration, workflows and scripts.
  4. Then the trees themselves.
  5. Then spec, docs and skills prose — largest by count, lowest by risk.

RELATED AND ALREADY OPEN: rf2-5gka migrates Story's presence bridge OFF Freehand and points the right way. rf2-r4j91 re-aims the Reagent migration skill at hicasso. Neither is blocked by this epic; both reduce it.

DO NOT DELETE ANYTHING IN THE FIRST DISPATCH. The first pass produces the map and the order. A blind removal of 821 files with live core references is how a tree goes red for a day.
notes:
RETURNED TO OPEN by the mayor's stranded sweep, 2026-08-14 23:10 AUSEST. STALE CLAIM, NOT LOST WORK, and nothing was salvaged because nothing needed to be.

DISCRIMINATED BEFORE ACTING, per the sweep's own rule. Branch worker/guidepromo-0yp7w exists at tip d1497a6148, last commit 2026-08-14T14:38:31 -- roughly eight and a half hours ago, against live workers whose tips move every one to ten minutes. Its PR #8199 is MERGED. There is no live task to message: that worker died with the session cleared at ~21:20, and its worktree carries no recent activity. So no live task AND no tip movement, which is the only combination that authorises this step.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE STATUS FIELD SUGGESTS. bd list --status open does NOT show in_progress items, so a P1 EPIC sat invisible to every backlog read this session. That is the second time today the same shape hid real work: rf2-umjv was found the same way an hour ago, and rf2-b6jkj a few minutes after it. A stale in_progress claim is not merely untidy -- it removes a bead from the queue as effectively as closing it, without the record a closure would leave.

IT IS STILL NOT DISPATCHABLE, and that is by design rather than by fence. mayor-dispatch.md filters EPICs out of the dispatch pass: an EPIC is a deliberately serial structure whose children are dispatched, not the EPIC itself. Returning it to open makes it VISIBLE, which is the point; it does not make it a work item. Whoever reads it next should dispatch its next CHILD, not the parent.

ONE CAUTION FOR THAT NEXT READER: this EPIC's scope line says 821 tracked files plus live core and ssr references. That is a census, so it is a claim -- and the tree has moved substantially today, including re-frame.hicasso.server landing and a naming packet publishing 54 rows. Re-derive the file count before planning any wave off it.
PHASE 1 SURVEY COMPLETE (worker/retire-survey, 2026-08-15 15:34 AUSEST, off 85a70687e4). Plan tracked at docs/design/retirement/freehand-and-ui.md; nine phases filed as rf2-0yp7w.1 .. .9 with dependencies wired.

THE CENSUS IN THIS EPIC'S DESCRIPTION IS STALE BY 214 FILES, AND I RE-TOOK IT AS INSTRUCTED.
  implementation/freehand  376 tracked files (not 590) -- git ls-files, verified three ways
  implementation/ui        231 tracked files (unchanged)
  both trees               607 (not 821)
The 214 are the hicasso bench harness, which PRs #8202 and #8210 already moved into implementation/hicasso/test/ (205 files) and implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/ (4 shared Node helpers). THIS EPIC'S OWN COMMENT-DECLARED PHASE 0 HAS ALREADY LANDED, and so has the migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod re-point that depended on it.

References outside the two trees, re-measured with rg (not git grep) and cross-checked tracked: 425 files name freehand, 235 name re-frame.ui / implementation/ui, union 508 (excluding .beads/issues.jsonl). NOTE: rg SKIPS HIDDEN DIRECTORIES BY DEFAULT, so a census without --hidden silently omits all of .github/ -- that cost this survey one wrong count before it was caught. Classification: (a) live dependency 91, (b) dies with the tree 180, (c) prose 237.

THIS EPIC'S CENTRAL PREMISE IS FALSE. I re-derived it from scratch rather than trusting the earlier mapper who said so. There is NOT ONE :require of re-frame.freehand.* or re-frame.ui.* in implementation/core/src, implementation/ssr/src or implementation/ssr-ring/src. Of 31+49 freehand/ui reference lines in core/src and 4+34 in ssr/src, exactly SEVEN are not prose: two safe-call-hook! call sites addressed BY KEYWORD (frame.cljc:4488, :4616), two late-bind registry ROWS whose :producer-ns is a quoted symbol (directory.cljc:1159, :1164), two producer VECTORS that merely list re-frame.ui.substrate among five entries (:962, :1038), and the ssr/ui_tree.cljc conversion tables -- which are LIVE PRODUCTION CODE THAT SURVIVES, since the Independence rule always forbade ssr requiring ui.

FIVE OF THE SEVEN DIE WITH THE TREES. Two are one-element edits. NONE is a re-homing or a re-implementation. That is the difference between "untangle a dependency" and "delete a branch", and it is the whole answer to the question this dispatch was asked.

WHAT ACTUALLY ORDERS THE WORK, since core does not:
1. The two trees are INDEPENDENT and CI asserts it (test.yml's jvm-freehand greps implementation/freehand for re-frame.ui). Two parallel lanes.
2. implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:528 carries :build-defaults {:build-hooks [(re-frame.ui.compiler.build-hook/hook)]} -- a REPO-WIDE DEFAULT ON EVERY BUILD. Same commit as the ui/src deletion or every build in the repo fails to resolve the symbol. Freehand's counterparts: deps.edn:63, and package.json's test:bspine-compile, a step of the REQUIRED cljs job that runs a file inside implementation/freehand/.
3. SPEC PROSE IS A BLOCKER, NOT A TRAILER -- which inverts this epic's phasing for that one surface. 28 links across 8 spec files target the conformance index, and scripts/check_doc_slugs.py runs UNCONDITIONALLY in test.yml's verify-readme-links under All required checks passed. Delete the corpus first and a required check reds on every PR.
4. The api-manifest generator chain (gen.clj's 62-namespace freehand roster -> spec/api-manifest.edn -> docs/api -> the committed skills ui-context sheet) serialises merges and takes one toucher.

TESTING.md ALREADY CARRIES A RULED THREE-STAGE RETIREMENT for the Freehand CI lanes, with checkable triggers, and it must be reconciled rather than duplicated. Its stage-2 trigger includes HD-018's win conditions, which it records as UNDISCHARGED -- "the fork is decided; the deletion is not yet authorised" -- and HD-018 reopens ONLY by operator ruling. MIKE'S 2026-08-14 RULING IS THAT RULING. Until TESTING.md says so, every worker tracing stage 2 finds an undischarged trigger and stalls. That is rf2-0yp7w.1 and it is why it is first. Its stage-3 quantities reproduce exactly under rg: 68 FH-* refs across 7 files, 28 index links across 8 files.

THE POINT OF NO RETURN is rf2-0yp7w.4 and .6 -- the two atomic deletion commits. Everything after is cleanup.

TWO QUESTIONS THIS SURVEY DELIBERATELY DID NOT ANSWER FOR MIKE:
- spec/004D-Freehand-Compiled-Grammar.md is NAMED for the retiring substrate. Does it die, or is it renamed and re-aimed at hicasso's grammar? A spec-shape decision, not a mechanical unpointing. rf2-0yp7w.2 stops at the unpointing and surfaces it.
- :ui/on-frame-destroyed! is STEP 4 of the NORMATIVE Spec 002 destroy recipe (002-Frames.md:722). Removing it renumbers a normative recipe in a hot-zone file, and the four core tests that drive it are testing GENERIC teardown mechanics that survive -- they get REPOINTED, not deleted. rf2-0yp7w.7.

XRAY: filed rf2-wtznc. The retirement needs NO xray change -- mount.cljs already puts :rf.adapter/freehand on the same defensive footing as the removed :rf.adapter/helix and already cites this epic. The health question is separate: that live refusal set names two retiring substrates and omits hicasso, and :rf.adapter/hicasso does not exist anywhere in the tree.

DO NOT CLOSE THIS EPIC -- dispatch its children. rf2-0yp7w.1, .2, .3 and .5 are unblocked and can run at once on four non-overlapping surfaces. .2 is spec HOT ZONE, one toucher.

204 OF ROUGHLY 209 HICASSO BENCHMARK FILES LIVE UNDER implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/. Four more sit under implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/bench/, one under implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/. THEY STOP CONFLICTING IF THE HARNESS MOVES FIRST. Re-home the hicasso benchmark harness out of implementation/freehand/ and into implementation/hicasso/. It measures hicasso; it belongs there ON THE MERITS, independently of any retirement. That is now phase 0 of this epic, ahead of every deletion.

WHAT MUST BE ESTABLISHED BEFORE THE MOVE, and worker/fhmap-0yp7w has been asked for exactly this: how many of the 204 are hicasso's OWN harness versus Freehand benchmarks that merely reference hicasso in a comparison — a Freehand benchmark dies with Freehand, a hicasso benchmark must survive it. And whether the harness has a HARD dependency on re-frame.freehand namespaces or merely lives in that directory. If it only lives there, the re-home is a move. comments.text:
PHASE 1 MAP COMPLETE — AND THIS EPIC'S CENTRAL PREMISE, WHICH I WROTE, IS FALSE (mayor, 2026-08-14).

I said core/src and ssr/src carry LIVE RUNTIME DEPENDENCIES on Freehand, and that nothing else was safe until they were untangled. The mapper extracted every ns form across core/src, ssr/src and ssr-ring/src and grepped it: ZERO requires of re-frame.freehand.* or re-frame.ui.*. All 13 references are PROSE in comments and docstrings, plus three data facts — two registry rows and a producer vector in late_bind/directory.cljc, one call BY KEYWORD in frame.cljc (a documented no-op when the artefact is absent), and verbatim COPIES of the ui conversion tables in ssr/ui_tree.cljc that exist precisely because the Independence rule forbids ssr requiring ui.

SO FREEHAND AND re-frame.ui CAN BE DELETED WITHOUT CHANGING A LINE OF SHIPPED CORE OR SSR RUNTIME CODE. My reading of a directory histogram as evidence of coupling was wrong; a reference count cannot distinguish a require from a comment, and I treated it as though it could.

THE FIVE REAL BLOCKERS, none where I was looking:

B1 — implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:526 carries :build-defaults {:build-hooks [(re-frame.ui.compiler.build-hook/hook)]}. That is a REPO-WIDE DEFAULT ON EVERY BUILD. Delete implementation/ui/src without editing that line and every build in the repository fails to resolve the hook symbol. It must land in the SAME COMMIT as the ui/src deletion — not before, not after. This is the sharpest item in the epic and it was invisible in the census.

B2 — the hicasso bench harness lives inside Freehand. 204 files, and implementation/hicasso has no bench directory at all.

B3 — migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod carries ../../../implementation/freehand/test on its production :paths, and two src files genuinely require re-frame.bench.hicasso.front.slot. A shipped JVM artefact reaching into the tree being deleted. B2's re-home resolves it for free.

B4 — core/test/re_frame/late_bind_drift_test.clj walks directory.cljc and scans for matching call sites; deleting the trees reds it. Trivial data edit, but mandatory.

B5 — implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/.../gen.clj hardcodes a roster of ~60 freehand namespaces plus the ui set, gated by three JVM tests, generating spec/api-manifest.edn which ui_context.clj then reads to generate the committed ui-context sheet. Crosses into spec (hot zone) AND skills. That generated sheet serial-bottlenecks merges — sequence it, never parallelise it.

ORDER: P0 re-home the bench harness. P1 the tools/ and migration/ live requires. P2 core/src data plus the gen.clj roster plus spec regen. P3 build configuration, atomically with the deletion. P4 delete the trees. P5 prose — 152 docs files, 19 spec files, mkdocs nav — largest, lowest risk, fully parallelisable once P4 lands.

Freehand and re-frame.ui are INDEPENDENT OF EACH OTHER and CI asserts it: test.yml's JVM freehand job carries a step 'Assert no dependency on the re-frame.ui donor'. So P3 through P5 can run as two parallel lanes after P2, except that B1 forces the ui lane to own shadow-cljs.edn first.

THREE REQUIRED CHECKS THE FAST SPINE DOES NOT RUN are load-bearing here and must be run directly by whoever does P3 and P4: the donor-independence assertion, npm run test:ui-isolation, and npm run test:bspine-compile.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
P0 WORKER STALLED MID-REVERT, RESUMED — AND IT FOUND SOMETHING THE MAP DID NOT (mayor, 2026-08-14).

WHAT HAPPENED. The bench re-home worker hit the harness watchdog after 600 seconds with no progress. Its last words: the JSON rewrites hit BLOB-PINNED PROVENANCE RECORDS inside the recorded measurements, and it was reverting them because they must move verbatim.

THAT FINDING IS IMPORTANT AND SHOULD SURVIVE ANY RESTART. The 36 .json and 4 .edn recorded-measurement files are not inert data — they carry blob-pinned provenance. So the mechanical path rewrite that the .cjs runners need is exactly WRONG for the .json and .edn records: rewriting a path inside one breaks the pin that ties the record to the run that produced it. My brief said move them verbatim; the worker discovered WHY, which is stronger.

STATE WHEN IT STOPPED: 219 modified files, ZERO commits. Roughly two hours of work entirely in the working tree. I did not commit on its behalf — a half-reverted state committed by someone else is worse than no commit, and only that worker knows how far its revert reached. Resumed via message instead.

THE LIKELY CAUSE IS MACHINE LOAD, NOT THE CHANGE. Processor queue read 81 with five workers plus CI contending. That is the same condition behind the par-compile abort another worker saw today.

ALSO FLAGGED TO IT: its dirty list includes implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs, .gitattributes, implementation/README.md and two docs/design/hicasso/studio pages — NONE of them in its fence. Most likely a path-rewrite sweep that widened. core/src especially needs a specific reason, because the phase-1 map established core has ZERO requires on Freehand.

LESSON FOR THE NEXT P0 BRIEF, whoever writes it: require commits at milestones rather than at the end. A branch with commits survives a stall; a working tree does not. This move is large enough that the natural rhythm — move files, fix requires, fix paths, run gates — is four commits, and any of them would have been worth keeping.

TWO LIVE FREEHAND DEPENDENCIES I DID NOT KNOW ABOUT, and one measurement spelling that hides pointers (mayor, 2026-08-14, from the rf2-c5j7w worker).

THE TWO DEPENDENCIES, verified by that worker in package.json and test.yml rather than assumed:

MAYOR — A CENSUS-PATTERN TRAP THAT READS DOWN EVERY COUNT THIS EPIC HAS PUBLISHED. Found by rf2-0yp7w.9's slice-5 worker (PR #8525), re-measured by me from the mayor checkout at origin/main 7c0d95b040 before recording it.

THE TRAP. 're-frame2-ui' is a PREFIX OF 're-frame2-uix', the coordinate of the LIVE, first-class UIx adapter. So every unanchored census over the retirement spellings sweeps up healthy UIx surfaces as donor residue. My own measurement, tracked files, .beads excluded:

  re-frame2-uix           36 files
The worker's fuller pattern read 196 files at its base and 174 once anchored — 22 files of pure false positive, and it reproduced my 196 exactly before correcting it.

WHICH DIRECTION IT FAILS IN, and it is the expensive one. A prefix over-counts, so the census sends a worker to edit surfaces that are healthy — the same class as a fence naming a path that does not exist, except it fails toward action rather than inaction. Every count this epic and its children have published over an unanchored pattern should be READ DOWN, and none should be re-used without re-derivation. Controls that establish the pattern discriminates rather than merely returning few: 'hicasso' returns 966 files, a nonsense token returns 0, and 're-frame.uix'/'re_frame.uix' return 0 — so 're-frame\.ui' carries no equivalent trap and only the hyphenated coordinate form does.

TWO CONSEQUENCES FOR WHOEVER TAKES THE NEXT SLICE:
1. Anchor the coordinate form: 're-frame2-ui([^x]|$)'. Do not anchor by adding 'uix' to an exclusion list — a list re-opens the gap on the next sibling coordinate.
2. Re-derive rather than inherit. This epic's description already carries the standing caution that its own 821-file scope line is a census and therefore a claim; this is the same lesson one level down, and it now has a named mechanism.

title: hicasso: :p0/write-all's fixed per-write cost makes the allocation ladder uncertifiable at any page size
description:
MEASURED by rf2-2rtt6.138's window on 2026-08-08 (PR #7691). This is the
structural result of that window and it outranks the sizing question.

THE FIXED COST, measured for the first time on this rig. :p0/write-all
rebuilds a 300-element vector and drives the whole event pipeline whether
one boundary is mounted or 1,200. The floor arm is precisely that write with
no subscription under it, and it reads:

  reagent-subs  24,108 B per write
  uix-subs      24,730 B per write

Call it F ~ 24.4 KB. F DOES NOT SHRINK WHEN B DOES.

WHY THAT IS FATAL TO THE CURRENT ROUTE. The masking bound (rf2-n6w7o)
charges (W+1).perWrite <= 300,000 B. At the six-write averaging floor that
allows 42,857 B per write -- and F alone is 57% of it, before a single
boundary has been measured. Modelling perWrite ~ F + B.s(R) off the run's
own arms, the largest page each rung admits (worst arm per rung, since a
ladder holds ONE B fixed across all rungs) is:

  rung   s (B/bnd/write)   W=1   W=3   W=6
  R=1      2,031- 4,067     30    12     4
  R=3      4,888- 5,904     21     8     3
  R=7      9,246-10,158     12     4     1
  R=20     6,800-22,174      5     2     0

AT SIX WRITES THERE IS NO PAGE OF ONE BOUNDARY OR MORE THAT CERTIFIES THE
1/3/7/20 LADDER. At W=1 there is (B <= 5), but W=1 is the configuration that
produced r2 0.75/0.28/0.94/0.31 for want of averaging, and at B=5 the fixed
cost is F/B ~ 4,884 B/boundary/write -- close to twice the entire first-read
signal, with a round-to-round spread (floor moves 21,840-24,432 B/write over
six rounds) that lands on the fit as noise on the rung with the least signal.
Those s(R) are read off windows the run refused as under-reading, so each is
a LOWER bound and the squeeze is at least this tight.

SO 'SHRINK THE MEASURED UNIT' HAS A FLOOR, and the floor is F. The route
docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-survival-metrics-allocation-half.md
recommended has now been tried and measured, and the page records it.

THE TWO ROUTES LEFT, both design questions rather than sizing ones:

  (a) A CHEAPER WRITE on this bench, so F stops consuming the budget. The
      300-element vector rebuild is per-write and independent of the arm; if
      the write could touch only the mounted boundaries, F would fall with B
      and the whole squeeze relaxes. This is the likelier route and it is a
      p0_arms.cljs / p0_heap.cljs question.
  (b) A BOUND THAT DOES NOT CHARGE (W+1).perWrite -- i.e. route (a) of
      rf2-n6w7o, an independent in-window collection witness, which would
      let a window be certified by what it OBSERVED rather than by its size.
      Note the merged-PR audit of #7682 already disputes the present bound's
      soundness on separate grounds (see the sibling bead).

DO NOT discharge this by widening the budget or by dropping the R=20 rung:
R=20 is HD-002's own ladder and the budget exists to refuse under-reads.
notes:
WINDOW REFUSED $D, and the refusal is the deliverable. Branch worker/allocfloor-140 carried ZERO commits and no PR was opened - there was no honest change to make and the worker did not manufacture one.

WHAT REFUSED IT: V1, V2 and V3 CANNOT BE CONFIGURED ON THE SHIPPED INSTRUMENT. Not "came back out of band" - cannot be expressed. No browser launched, no bundle built.

  V1  its control arm is PINNED OUT. V1 is the floor at three pages under BOTH writes, and
      F_old is V1's control - the only way the two writes compare like for like. p0_heap.cljs:1111
      hard-codes (arms/write-page! @alloc-tick); no env var, no kind, no parameter reaches
      write-all!. And p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs:978 ASSERTS the absence of write-all!.
      The three V1 pages are fine - B = 4/24/96 all admissible. Only the control is unreachable.
  V2  refused by its own package's preflight (P0_ALLOC_CELLS=1 P0_ALLOC_WRITES=1 gives
      admissible:false, the 6-write averaging floor), AND independently by V1's blocker.
  V3  no controls-only mode. --only alloc runs controls AND the full ladder every round. V3's
      controls are reachable only by riding ~108 ladder windows that criterion 5 freezes.

PROVED EXECUTABLY, NOT BY READING. A fault planted at p0_heap.cljs:1111 turned the structural suite from 53-passed/exit-0 to 1-failed/exit-1, the single failure being "and never write-all!". One plant did triple duty: proved the gate read the worker's own tree, proved the plant was scoped with no cascade, and proved the central claim. Restore verified byte-identical by git hash-object against ef9b5adcf0.

THE BOX WOULD HAVE ADMITTED THE WINDOW - it is not why this refused. Queue length 0 in ALL TWELVE samples across every phase. And the worker did not stop at the queue: it measured the 93 resident processes directly and found 0.16 cpu-seconds accrued across all of them over six seconds - 0.027 of one core - with 72 being the operator's own Chrome. No shadow-cljs server.pid in either checkout, so no zombie could serve a stale build.

FOUR SHORTCUTS REFUSED, and the second is the one that matters:
  1. Did not build the write selector and measure through it - about one line, box idle and granted.
     A window on an instrument written minutes earlier with no red-then-green proof IS the
     uncertified-instrument window criterion 5 exists to prevent.
  2. DID NOT RUN A PARTIAL V1 with F_old omitted. THE NUMBERS WOULD HAVE COME OUT. F_old IS
     V1's control, and a run reported without its control does not contribute data - tonight's
     hardest lesson in a new costume, recognised unprompted.
  3. Did not measure F_old off an older commit. Two builds is not a control that the rig has not moved.
  4. Did not ride a full ladder run for V3's controls - tempting precisely because it needs no rig change.
  WIDENED NOTHING: ALLOC_MIN_WRITES 6, ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B 600000, R=20, tau placeholder, all untouched.

BLOCKED ON TWO NEW P1 BEADS, both filed with the graph corrected by the worker itself:
  rf2-gxrr  the missing measurement surface - write selector plus controls-only mode. HERMETIC
            INSTRUMENT WORK, NEEDS NO QUIET BOX, dispatchable alongside anything.
  rf2-qomo  a RULING, not a widening: V2's one-write window against the package's 6-write floor.
            The obvious fix is not free - B=4/R=20/W=6 lands near 630 KB against a measured
            collection onset of 600,000 B, so V2 is squeezed from both sides.

The worker initially hung the ruling off the instrument bead and CORRECTED ITSELF: the ruling blocks V2's RUN, not the instrument BUILD, and stalling the build behind a ruling would have stalled the lane.

WHAT THIS COST AND BOUGHT: no box time beyond hermetic checks. It located the lane's actual blocker to the line. The brief specified four validity witnesses and the implementation built the artefacts they judge but not the surface that lets them run - invisible until someone tried.

NEXT RUNNABLE LANE WINDOW IS rf2-y1jkm. rf2-2rtt6.140 and rf2-2rtt6.139 are both parked behind rf2-gxrr.
MAYOR CORRECTION 2026-08-21 06:05 AUSEST — I RE-CLOSED THIS BEAD AGAINST A LIVE AUDIT, THE SAME ERROR I MADE ON rf2-onozm AND FOR THE SAME REASON. THE AUDIT IS RIGHT AND I HAVE NOW VERIFIED EVERY ONE OF ITS CITED FACTS AT SOURCE.

MY ERROR. The MERGED-PR AUDIT #8591 comment landed at 18:33:02Z. I re-closed at 18:36:52Z with a reason asserting 'no AUDIT-REOPEN marker anywhere on the bead'. That is factually false. I searched the NOTES; the audit writes COMMENTS. Same mechanism as rf2-onozm, same tick, two beads.

THE AUDIT'S FINDING, AND IT IS CORRECT. PR #8591's fixed-cost page, README row, reader and close record all treat the 300,000 B (W+1) * perWrite masking budget as a LIVE requirement, conclude that R20 still forces B=0 on that basis, and record as an UNANSWERED OPERATOR DECISION whether the bound remains binding. That state was already settled on main and had been for nearly two weeks.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE THIS TICK, each independently:
1. Commit a4eb7226893 (2026-08-08) IS ANCESTRAL to origin/main — git merge-base --is-ancestor returns true. So the settlement predates the PR rather than racing it.
2. docs/design/hicasso/allocation-instrument-rework.md:556-568 says it in terms, under a heading 'Constraint semantics — what is retired and what stands': 'The budget is RETIRED, and retiring is not widening. rf2-2rtt6.140 criterion 4 sanctions exactly this: replacing the (W+1)*perWrite <= ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B mechanism with the witness is route (b) itself. ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B and allocMaxWrites are DELETED, NOT LOOSENED. Retaining the bound as a belt-and-braces refusal was considered and REJECTED ON ARITHMETIC': at the composed operating point B=4, R=20, W=6 a window is about 630 KB of rise-plus-largest-step, so a retained bound would refuse everything.
3. :445-451 records WHY: the #7682 audit objected that the premises did not support the bound — 600 KB is an UPPER bound on where the first collection runs while safety needs a LOWER one, and halving an upper bound does not create one; and a masked leg's true A_k is not bounded by the observed maxStep, which sees only NET positive deltas. rf2-2rtt6.141 accepted both.
4. The deletion is GATED, not merely done. implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs:583 pins lacks(/const ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B/, 'the budget constant is deleted'). The only other tracked mentions are prose citing the reasoning — p0_run.cjs:1184 and the same test at :538 — not live constants.

SO THIS BEAD'S OWN CRITERION 4 SANCTIONED THE REPLACEMENT. The PR resurrects a constraint this bead itself authorised deleting.

WHAT I OWE MIKE, AND IT IS A RETRACTION. I have repeatedly surfaced 'rf2-2rtt6.140 — is the 300,000 B masking bound still a binding validity requirement?' as an item on his queue. IT IS NOT AN OPEN QUESTION. It was settled on 2026-08-08, by this bead's own criterion, and retaining the bound was rejected on arithmetic rather than left undecided. That item comes OFF his queue and I have said so in chat.

TWO UNMET OBLIGATIONS REMAIN, both in the landed record rather than in the instrument: the stale live-bound conclusion, and a reversed set-relationship sentence. Neither needs a window.

ROUTED to worker/ledgerclust, which already owns docs/design/hicasso/studio/README.md and is already correcting the sibling finding from this same PR audit on rf2-onozm. Resuming that worker beats dispatching a second one into the same ledger.

ALL FOUR CITED FACTS RE-DERIVED AT SOURCE:
1. a4eb7226893 (2026-08-08) is ANCESTRAL to origin/main - git merge-base --is-ancestor returns true. The settlement predates PR #8591 by twelve days rather than racing it.

OBLIGATION (a) - THE STALE LIVE-BOUND CONCLUSION. The page said in terms 'The masking bound is NOT retired, widened, replaced or recalibrated ... The question is recorded for the operator and left open.' Both halves false since 2026-08-08. The DECISION NEEDED FROM THE OPERATOR block is replaced by the answer with its evidence and its gate, in the page, the README row and the reader.

The premise is RECAST, not deleted. Every max-B figure divides by the deleted constant, so the ladder arithmetic is now labelled a RECONSTRUCTION of this bead's own case with no live warrant. What carries the conclusion instead is measured and owes the bound nothing: R20 certifies 24/96 where every rung beneath it certifies 88-95%, and rf2-onozm's observed 884,280 B ceiling reaches the same rung on a quantity rather than a constant.

OBLIGATION (b) - THE REVERSED SENTENCE, and here it is by name. The reader now DERIVES both directions from the corpus and prints exactly the 3/5/10 the audit predicted; three synthetic self-test checks pin the set relationship so the sentence cannot return.

WHAT IS NOT DISCHARGED, and it is now sharper than before rather than resolved. This bead's uncertifiability argument is written in a constant that no longer exists. The FINDING survives on the measured certified column and on rf2-onozm's ceiling, but the bead's own PHRASING of it has no live warrant, and restating it in live terms is work PR #8597 deliberately does not do - it is named on the page as outstanding. comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-08, operator-overturnable): THE COMPOSED PACKAGE IS RULED — route (a) AND route (b), designed together in ONE brief. Not (a) alone, not (b) alone.

WHY BOTH, verified before ruling (mechanics confirmed against source: the charging rule `(W+1).B.c <= ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B` and `ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B = ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B / 2` at p0_run.cjs:1081,1119 — note the p0 instrument actually lives at implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/{p0_run.cjs,p0_arms.cljs,p0_heap.cljs}, not under freehand/; workers should land there):
- (a) alone leaves the disputed bound certifying windows: the #7682 audit's objection stands unanswered (an observed 240 KB collection under the 300 KB "no-collection" budget — see rf2-2rtt6.141), so every certification would rest on arithmetic the data already contradicts.
- (b) alone yields a sound instrument that rarely produces data: with F ~ 24.4 KB fixed per write, removing the budget admits larger B on paper, but per-write allocation F + B.s(R) then approaches the observed collection cadence at meaningful B (at R=20, B=24: ~24.4K + 24x~22K ~ 550 KB/write) — the witness would correctly refuse nearly every window. Sound but useless.
- Together: the boundary-proportional write keeps per-write allocation small enough that clean windows exist at real page sizes, and the witness certifies them by observation rather than by a disputed model. This is the minimal complete fix; sequential single-route attempts risk two design cycles for the same artefacts.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (bounded — no stats research project; one brief, then worker-sized implementation):
1. ONE design brief covering both artefacts and their validity witnesses BEFORE any code: (i) the boundary-proportional write, (ii) the in-window collection witness.
2. Write half: a :p0/write-* variant whose machinery cost scales with mounted boundaries (today :p0/write-all rebuilds a 300-element vector and drives the whole event pipeline regardless of B). Validity: a floor arm at >= 2 page sizes showing the fixed residue no longer dominant (per-boundary fixed residue below the R=1 signal, ~2 KB/bnd/write); and the brief states the equivalence argument that the new write still exercises the same per-boundary read/render work HD-002's ladder claims to measure.
3. Witness half: certification by observation replaces the (W+1).perWrite arithmetic. The #7682 audit's two executable probes become pinned regression tests: windows with true allocation 300 KB and 600 KB at headroom=0 must be REFUSED by the witness (both were admitted by the old bound); the net-growth masking case is pinned.
4. Constraint semantics, stated to prevent a false contradiction: the bead forbids WIDENING the budget or dropping R=20 — both stand. RETIRING the budget mechanism in favour of the witness is route (b) itself, sanctioned by this bead; replacement is not widening. ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B is not loosened; R=20 stays.
5. Sequencing: rf2-2rtt6.139 re-derives sizing per-rung from the NEW instrument's own floor data (or retires the preflight constant) only after the brief — ruling it against the current instrument would be immediately obsoleted. rf2-2rtt6.142's preflight fix rides the same rework, not ahead of it. NO further allocation window (incl. rf2-2rtt6.138 re-runs) before the brief's validity witnesses are green — any window before that is wasted by this bead's own arithmetic.
6. Supersession honesty: once the new write lands, the 2026-08-07/08 floor-arm and ladder rows are superseded-not-comparable; the-survival-metrics-allocation-half.md annotates, never erases.

DURABLE RECORD (already in this bead's description, restated here only by pointer): F = 24,108/24,730 B/write (reagent-subs/uix-subs); the per-rung admissibility table (W=6 admits B=4/3/1/0 across R=1/3/7/20); s(R) lower-bound ranges 2,031-4,067 (R=1) to 6,800-22,174 (R=20); the W=1 failure history (r^2 0.75/0.28/0.94/0.31; F/B ~ 4,884 B ~ 2x the first-read signal; floor spread 21,840-24,432 B/write).

Siblings ruled concurrently in the same review wave: rf2-2rtt6.141 (bound soundness — the witness above is its remedy), rf2-2rtt6.139 (sizing — folded behind this per criterion 5). Route (b)'s lineage: rf2-n6w7o route (a).

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
CRITERION 1 DISCHARGED — the design brief is written and open as PR #7697 (branch worker/allocdesign-140). The bead STAYS OPEN: criteria 2-6 are the implementation and its validity witnesses.

WHERE IT LIVES: docs/design/hicasso/allocation-instrument-rework.md, tracked, linked from docs/design/hicasso/README.md, with a forward pointer from the studio page's "next attempt" item. No code, no measurement.

WHAT THE BRIEF SETTLES:

WRITE HALF. A new :p0/write-page rebuilds :cells at the width the mounted page actually reads. The grid width becomes a property of the seeded app-db (seed-db takes it; :p0/fan's modulus reads (count (:cells db))), so it cannot live in two places and drift. :p0/write-all is left byte-identical and the clock/bulk rows keep driving it. The EQUIVALENCE ARGUMENT: same dispatch-sync through the same pipeline and signal graph; every one of the E = B.R edges sees a changed value so the invalidation set is identical; the rendered text is (str (* R v)) under either write so the read-back and canonical-DOM gate are unchanged; B, E, Q and the key rule untouched. The only difference is the width of a vector no boundary reads beyond its own slot -- machinery on both sides of the floor subtraction. On the 24-boundary page 276 of the 300 rebuilt cells were read by nothing.

WITNESS HALF. (W+1).perWrite <= ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B is RETIRED and replaced by a rule read off the window's own samples: the work legs are W repetitions of ONE work unit, so refuse if any leg deviates from the cohort MEDIAN by more than tau.m. A leg below the cohort is a leg something removed bytes from; a leg above it means the one-work-unit premise has failed, and refusing is then correct rather than merely conservative. The certificate is checkable rather than asserted: this window's rise under-reads by at most 2.tau, and here is the worst leg deviation observed.

THE TWO #7682 PROBES ARE REFUSED, and independently of the calibration. Probe A (60K x4 then a leg reading 0) and probe B (50K x5 then a leg reading 0) both have their offending leg at exactly zero against a strictly positive median, so both are refused for EVERY tau < 1 -- a re-calibration cannot silently re-admit them, and that property gets a test of its own. The net-growth masking fixture already in p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs is re-pointed at the new grounds.

CONSTRAINT SEMANTICS, as criterion 4 asks. The budget is RETIRED, not widened. Retaining it belt-and-braces was considered and REJECTED ON ARITHMETIC: at the composed operating point (B=4, R=20, W=6) a window is ~630 KB of rise+maxStep, so a retained bound would refuse every window the witness certifies and the package would deliver nothing. ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B stays at its measured 600,000 B and gates nothing. R=20 stays. ALLOC_MIN_WRITES=6 stays a floor. The falls gate is untouched.

FOUR VALIDITY WITNESSES, none of which publishes a slope. V1: the floor at B in {4,24,96} under BOTH writes -- the old write's flat F is the control that licenses the comparison, and an agreement at B=24 with the 2026-08-08 figures is what makes the two writes comparable at all. V2: the equivalence cross-check, one write per window at B=4, requiring (arm-floor)/B to AGREE between writes while the floor DROPS. V3: tau calibrated on control windows independently corroborated clean by their own 8 B/double prediction -- rf2-2rtt6.141's carried-in criterion answered. V4: the pinned probes, red-then-green.

ALSO CARRIED: the seam with rf2-2rtt6.139 (P0_ALLOC_CELLS becomes MANDATORY rather than a substituted constant -- no honest default exists without a sizing model, and it makes an accidental publication run impossible while criterion 5's freeze holds); a disposition for EVERY structural test the change supersedes (37 rows, KEPT / AMENDED / REPLACED / RETIRED); the criterion-6 supersession obligation; and one option recorded with its trigger and explicitly NOT taken.

WHY BOTH HALVES, NUMERICALLY (at R=20, worst arm s=22,174 B/bnd/write, W=6): today (42,857-24,400)/22,174 = B 0. Route (a) alone, bound kept: B 1 -- a one-boundary "ladder" is not one. Route (b) alone, write kept: B 3, on which F/B = 8,133 B/bnd is 2x-4x the whole R=1 signal. Composed: B 4 with F/B targeted under the R=1 signal. The ruling's claim reproduces arithmetically.

WHAT REMAINS OPEN AND WHY:

1. HOW MUCH OF F ~ 24.4 KB IS THE 300-CELL REBUILD AND HOW MUCH IS THE EVENT PIPELINE. Nobody has measured it and the brief may not. It is the single number the write half turns on. V1 answers it directly, and V1 is the gate on the whole write half -- if the pipeline residue F0 dominates, the write half narrows the gap without closing it, and the brief carries a three-step contingency ladder (raise B; carry F0 as a stated instrument constant; or the reserve option), with an explicit fence against responding by shrinking the page further.
2. THE VALUE OF tau. V3's to measure, on the stated calibration rule. Not a knob (ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B's reasoning unchanged).
3. THE OPERATING PAGE. B, and whether one B serves all four rungs, is rf2-2rtt6.139's per-rung re-derivation off the NEW instrument's floor data. The brief names B in {4,24,96} for V1 and B=4 for V2 as MEASUREMENT configurations, not as the row's page, and derives no sizing constant.
4. WHETHER A 3-TO-5 BOUNDARY PAGE IS A CREDIBLE WITNESS OF A PER-BOUNDARY QUANTITY AT ALL. The arm's per-page constants (React root, frame provider, root subscription) do not cancel against the floor and are divided by a very small B. The expectation is that an R-independent constant lands in the fit's INTERCEPT rather than its slope, and the R=0 shell rung is the direct check -- at B=24 it already reads close to the floor. V2's per-rung comparison is where it shows if that is wrong.
5. THE FINER-SAMPLING OPTION (3-4 samples per write instead of 2) is filed as an option rather than designed: a real sensitivity improvement and allocation-free, but it changes the leg cohort's meaning. V3 decides whether it is needed.

ONE DOWNSTREAM EFFECT ON A CLOSED BEAD, flagged rather than silently taken: rf2-2rtt6.142's refusal text BRANCHES on whether the page can carry six writes, and that second branch is computed from the budget. With the budget retired its trigger no longer exists and the refusal collapses to one branch. That is not a regression -- with no page-size model there is nothing to name, and the endorsed property (never advise the shape being refused) is preserved by there being no such advice to give -- but .142 is CLOSED and its close reason describes the two-branch behaviour, so the implementer records the collapse on that bead when the change lands. .142's ROUTE 2 pin (an explicit one-write window is refused) survives unchanged and must stay green; its ROUTE 1 pin is re-pointed at the mandatory-page refusal.

GATES: check_doc_slugs.py 0, probed red-then-green at the edit site (exit 1 naming file and line 43); check_provenance_pins.py --changed-since origin/main 0 (the page cites no commit SHAs); check-beads-pr-boundary.sh origin/main 0. mkdocs build --strict is NOT the gate (exclude_docs keeps docs/design/** off the site), so anchors and table column counts were hand-verified: 28 headings, 3 same-file anchors all resolving, 6 tables with 0 column mismatches.

CRITERION 5 STANDS: no allocation window, including any rf2-2rtt6.138 re-run, before V1-V4 are green. V1-V4 are the permitted measurements and they publish nothing.

comments.text:
CRITERIA 2, 3, 4 AND 6 IMPLEMENTED — PR #7702 (branch worker/allocbuild-140), open, NOT merged. THE BEAD STAYS OPEN: criterion 5's measurement freeze stands and V1/V2/V3 remain.

NEITHER ARTEFACT HAS BEEN EXECUTED AGAINST A REAL PAGE, and that is the deliverable rather than a caveat on it. No allocation window was opened, no ladder row taken, no quiet box requested. :p0/write-page has never written to a mounted page; the leg witness has never read a real sample stream. Both are proven STRUCTURALLY ONLY — 50 hermetic pins in p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs and 9 hermetic CLJS deftests, every window a synthetic sample buffer and every frame a plain-atom test frame.

WHAT LANDED

WRITE (criterion 2). :p0/write-page rebuilds :cells at the width the mounted page reads. The grid width is a property of the SEEDED APP-DB — seed-db takes it, :p0/seed carries it, enter-segment! and p0-heap/prepare! thread it from the driver — and :p0/fan's modulus reads (count (:cells db)), so it cannot live in two places and drift. :p0/write-all is byte-identical, literal cells-n and all; the clock, bulk, fan-out and retention rows keep driving it at the published 300, and a structural pin reads that off the CLJS sources rather than trusting it. The width threaded is B = ROOTS x P0_ALLOC_CELLS — one cell per mounted boundary, which keeps the change FULL-PAGE (the brief rejects a one-cell grid as converting a full-page change into a point change, and HD-002's law is stated about the change).

WITNESS (criterion 3). The budget is retired; refusal is now "any leg deviates from the cohort MEDIAN by more than tau.m". allocSteps grows legs, gaps, legMedian, legWorstDeviation, refusals and certified, mirroring allocArmSizing's verdict shape since .142. rise/fall/falls/maxStep/endpoints keep their definitions, so no published total changes meaning. allocMaskableWindows -> allocRefusedWindows, naming every refused window with its reason.

CONSTRAINTS (criterion 4). ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B stays at 600,000 B and gates nothing (the summary prints the largest arm rise as a percentage of it). R=20 stays. ALLOC_MIN_WRITES=6 stays a floor. Falls gate and r2 floor untouched. ALLOC_B_PER_BOUNDARY_WRITE, allocMaxWrites, predictedWindowB, headroom, maxBoundaries, floorBoundaries and maskable are deleted. P0_ALLOC_CELLS is MANDATORY.

CRITERION 6 WAS DONE HERE, and the dispatch said it was outstanding — the bead governs. Criterion 6 says the studio page annotates "once the new write lands", and the brief says "the implementation PR adds a dated note to that page". The write lands in #7702, so the annotation rides with it: a dated supersession note at the head and at the small-witness section of the-survival-metrics-allocation-half.md, every figure and every table standing, F_old named as the one figure that keeps its full force because V1 re-measures it as the control that licenses the comparison.

TAU IS AN UNCALIBRATED PLACEHOLDER at 0.25, marked as such in the source with V3 named as what calibrates it. Conservative in the direction that matters (a smaller tau refuses more). No window may be published on it. Nothing pinned depends on it.

MUTATION PROOFS, red-then-green in two commits (059d4fb red, 72d4eaa green). p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs: 6/56 failed at the red commit. Five pins reported `certified` undefined; the MANDATORY-PAGE pin failed on a value — `true !== false` — which is the sharper red, because the shipped preflight really did derive and admit an arm with no page stated. Structural counts 50 -> 49 (disposition) -> 50 (the certificate pin below).

NOTHING LOOSENED, established three ways because the phrase means three things once criterion 4 retires the budget:
(1) FALLS GATE: exhaustive over 17,496 synthetic window shapes against the shipped module — 0 violations, every falling-step window still refused.
(2) PREFLIGHT: exhaustive over W 0..40 x cells 0..40 x roots {0,1,4,50} — 4,200 admitted, every one satisfying both surviving .142 terms, and ZERO arms satisfying those terms refused. The one new refusal is the unstated page.
(3) WINDOW GATE: subset is the WRONG test and I say so rather than claiming otherwise — retiring the budget necessarily admits windows it refused, the brief's arithmetic requires it (a ~630 KB window must be admittable), and the disposition retires THE CHANGE ONLY EVER REFUSES MORE for exactly that reason. In the sweep 36 of 17,496 moved refused->admitted and ALL 36 are over the retired 300,000 B budget, so none is a masked window slipping through. What replaces the subset claim: both audit probes moved from admitted (headroom exactly 0, true allocations 300 KB and 600 KB) to refused; 98.1% of masked windows (4,527 of 4,617) are refused by the leg rule; and the 2-tau certificate HOLDS TIGHT.

THE 2-TAU CERTIFICATE IS NOW PINNED, and this is the one addition worth the operator's attention. Swept over 20,096 windows INSIDE THE COHORT PREMISE (the certificate's own stated antecedent): worst per-leg masked reclamation 50.00% of the median against a 2-tau ceiling of 50%, worst whole-window under-read 10.00%. The worst case is EXACTLY the shape the brief predicts — a leg sitting tau.m high on its own merits, losing 2.tau.m, reading tau.m low, admitted at the very edge — and one byte further refuses. So 2-tau is a bound rather than an approximation, and the implementation realises the certificate the brief specified, tight. Outside the premise the certificate says nothing and the brief says so.

GATES, all foreground to completion from WORKTREE_ROOT=/c/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/allocbuild-140: node --check both .cjs 0; p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs 0 (50 passed); npm run test:script-helpers 0; npm run test:cljs 0 (12,812 tests / 64,426 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors); sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh 0; npm run lint:js 0; python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py 0; sh scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh origin/main 0. One flake, diagnosed: the first spine run exited 1 on "aborted par-compile ... still waiting for", cascading across namespaces unrelated to this change and naming different ones each attempt. scripts/compile-node-test.cjs's own header documents that signature as par-compile-one's 60s :par-timeout under box load, self-healing because the cache is keyed by source hash. It cleared on re-run and the full spine went green.

WHAT REMAINS ON THIS BEAD:
- CRITERION 5 stands. No allocation window, including any .138 re-run, until V1-V4 are green. V4 is discharged (pure test, no browser). V1, V2 and V3 need a granted quiet box.
- V1 — the floor at P0_ALLOC_CELLS in {1,6,24} against P0_ROOTS=4 (B in {4,24,96}) under BOTH writes, both segments, six rounds. The control is F_old coming back flat in B and landing on the 2026-08-08 figures at B=24. The criterion is F_new(B)/B below ~2 KB/bnd/write. This is the gate on the whole write half and the brief carries a three-step contingency ladder under it.
- V2 — the equivalence cross-check at B=4, one write per window, five windows a cell, comparing (arm-floor)/B between the two writes: it must AGREE while the floor DROPS.
- V3 — calibrating tau on control windows corroborated clean by their own 8 B/double prediction, plus the floor arm's leg spread at each of V1's three pages. Then tau is pinned and the placeholder line goes.
- Then rf2-2rtt6.139 re-derives sizing PER RUNG off V1's floor data, and may restore a derived default page on those grounds.

DISCREPANCIES FOUND, reported not resolved: the bead's criterion-1 note and the brief's prose both say "37 rows" in the test disposition table; the table as written has 36. All 36 are dispositioned and nothing appears missing — I read it as a miscount in the prose, not a lost row.

A REAL PRE-EXISTING COLLISION SURFACED: :p0/cell is registered in THREE namespaces — p0_fixture.cljc, hicasso/clock_views.cljs and hicasso/p0_reagent_views.cljs — each with its own implementation. The p0 release builds carry one, so it is unreachable there; the consolidated :node-test build loads all three and image assembly correctly refuses to let selection order decide (:rf.error/image-duplicate-id). The new CLJS suite is scoped with :select-ns over re-frame.bench.p0-fixture, which is the error's own first remedy. Filing no bead: nothing is broken today, and the three registrations are three different benches' fixtures rather than a drift.
