comments.text:
DELEGATED DECISION (dossier review, 2026-08-13, operator-reversible): OPTION 1 — THE STANDING QUIET-BOX AUTHORISATION IS THE GRANT for this bead's V1, V2 and V3 windows, INCLUDING any contingency re-runs the design brief's ladder calls for. No further grant is needed per bead or per window. The dossier's Codex Recommendation was weighed and CONCURS with Option 1; it further cites Mike's later direct chat grant ("The moment you have no more beads to action, you can do the quiet box measurements stuff. Go for it. Get it done."), already recorded in this bead's notes, which settles the question independently and more broadly. This ruling ratifies that reading and makes it durable.

THE GENERAL RULE, so this ask does not regenerate down the lane: "granted quiet box" in bead text written BEFORE 2026-08-10 is the idiom of the then-only per-window regime, not a deliberate demand for something stronger than the regime that replaced it. It is SATISFIED by the standing authorisation's measurable condition — dispatchable queue exhausted, no live worker, quiet verified by real counters, one window at a time, Shape 6 — unless a bead explicitly reserves a per-window ask. This covers rf2-hic-036, rf2-hic-040 and rf2-hic-045, which carry the same lane record: do not re-ask.

WHY (distilled from both reviews):
- Criterion 5's purpose is to stop allocation windows being WASTED ON AN UNCERTIFIED INSTRUMENT. V1-V3 ARE the certification — the only path out of the freeze — and they publish nothing, so running them serves the criterion rather than evading it.
- Cost asymmetry runs toward running: a wrong "yes" wastes one guarded, non-publishing window; the hold parks the project's three highest-priority items (.140, rf2-2rtt6.139 blocked on V1's floor data, rf2-y1jkm) plus the lane behind them.
- The refusal discipline is the safety net and has worked before (two of three windows in one day came back as correct refusals). Those burns were the instrument working as designed, not permission failures.
- Record correction: the earlier mayor note claimed the authorisation record names a four-bead list excluding this bead. No such record exists in the tracker or memories. What the tracker records (rf2-5yn9 comment 2026-08-12 22:11, repeated on hic-036/040) is the lane order naming THIS bead second.

DISPATCH INSTRUCTIONS (mayor):
- Run only when the standing condition is true: no dispatchable beads/background workers; the box verified quiet with Get-Counter on System Processor Queue Length and Processor _Total % Processor Time (NOT Win32_Processor LoadPercentage — it read 93% when the truth was 11; queue length is the decisive number); no other measurement owns the box. At this writing the machine is occupied by the TESTING.md cluster (rf2-my7c, rf2-bkhi, rf2-h6js, rf2-w9ip) — take up after it reports and quiet re-verifies.
- Lane order per this bead's notes, STRICTLY ONE WINDOW AT A TIME. Defer already cleared.
- Shape 6 binds every window: the controls arbitrate, a refusal is a deliverable, never loosen a gate to admit a run, no rig changes mid-window (file and run as its own window), publish no slope from these validity witnesses.
- Record on this bead either the passing evidence or the precise refusal; then rf2-2rtt6.139 consumes V1's floor data.

IMPLEMENTATION POINTERS carried from the reviews (the worker runs from these, not the dossier):
- V1: floor at P0_ALLOC_CELLS in {1,6,24} x P0_ROOTS=4 (B in {4,24,96}) under BOTH writes, both segments, six rounds. Control: F_old flat in B, landing on the 2026-08-08 figures at B=24. Pass: F_new(B)/B below ~2 KB/bnd/write. V1 gates the whole write half; the brief carries a three-step contingency ladder under it (raise B; carry F0 as a stated instrument constant; reserve option) with an explicit fence against shrinking the page further.
- V2: equivalence cross-check at B=4, one write per window, five windows a cell; (arm-floor)/B must AGREE between writes while the floor DROPS.
- V3: calibrate tau on control windows independently corroborated clean by their own 8 B/double prediction, plus the floor arm's leg spread at each of V1's three pages; then pin tau and delete the placeholder line (ALLOC_LEG_TOLERANCE = 0.25, marked uncalibrated, p0_run.cjs ~lines 1100-1123; leg-median witness ~1317-1356; mandatory P0_ALLOC_CELLS ~1148-1237).
- Codex independently verified main carries the full pre-measurement state: design a4eb722689, page-proportional write + observed-leg witness eb17886c5b, scoped fixture test 614643f397, exact 2-tau boundary pin 709c89ba6d; node --check p0_run.cjs exit 0; p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs 53 passed (grown from 50 at implementation time).
- Acceptance is the EXISTING evidence contract — no new machinery. The only live uncertainty is whether machine and controls admit the windows, answerable only by running them.

REJECTED from the reviews: Option 2 (one explicit grant per bead) and Option 3 (per-window grants) — permission ceremony against the trust-the-programmer posture, adding round-trips to the critical path of three P1s while buying nothing, given the windows publish nothing and the controls arbitrate. Even the pre-authorisation regime granted boxes by tranche, not by window.

REVISIT TRIGGER: if a V-window ever runs on a box that was not actually quiet AND the controls fail to refuse it, the fix is tightening the measurable condition (counters, Shape 6) — not reintroducing per-window permission slips.

comments.text:
MEASUREMENT WINDOW REFUSED — 2026-08-13 23:49 AUSEST, on the granted quiet box,
branch worker/allocfloor-140 off dac7f439dd. First of the nine lane windows.
NO ALLOCATION WINDOW WAS OPENED, no browser was launched, no bundle was built.
The refusal is structural and it is located in source.

THE BOX WAS QUIET AND THAT IS NOT WHY IT REFUSED. Recorded because the next
window should not have to re-establish it: queue length 0 across every sample in
every phase (5 before, 4 during); CPU 5.7-13.0%; free RAM 30.0 of 63.4 GB. 93
node/java/chrome processes were resident holding 13.4 GB — materially more than
the previous lane window's 20 at 1.2 GB — and I judged them immaterial on
evidence rather than on the queue alone: across all 93, total CPU accrued over a
6-second interval was 0.16 cpu-seconds, i.e. 0.027 of one core on a 24-thread
box, with no single process above 0.05. 72 of them are the operator's own Chrome
session. No `.shadow-cljs/server.pid` exists in either checkout, so no zombie
compile server could have served a stale build. The box would have admitted the
window.

WHAT REFUSED IT: V1, V2 AND V3 CANNOT BE CONFIGURED ON THE SHIPPED INSTRUMENT.
Not "came back out of band" — cannot be expressed. Each verified against source
and reproduced executably.

V1 — ITS CONTROL ARM IS PINNED OUT OF THE INSTRUMENT.
V1 is "the floor at three page sizes ... under BOTH writes", and F_old is not
decoration: the brief makes it V1's control ("it says the rig has not moved
under the instrument, and it is the only way the two writes can be compared like
for like", :260-263), and criterion 6 rests on it (":631"). The allocation
window cannot drive it. `p0_heap.cljs:1111` hard-codes
`(arms/write-page! @alloc-tick)`; no env var, no `kind`, no parameter reaches
`write-all!`. And `p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs:978` PINS that:
`assert.doesNotMatch(HEAP, /\(arms\/write-all! /, 'and never write-all!')`.

Demonstrated rather than asserted. A one-line plant at p0_heap.cljs:1111 adding
a selector took the suite from 53 passed / exit 0 to 1/53 failed / exit 1, the
single failure being that pin — which simultaneously proves the gate read this
worktree, proves the plant was scoped (one failure, no cascade), and proves the
claim. Restore verified byte-identical by `git hash-object` against the
committed object (ef9b5adcf0), re-run 53 passed / exit 0.

The three V1 pages themselves are fine — P0_ROOTS=4 with P0_ALLOC_CELLS 1/6/24
derives B = 4/24/96, all admissible, no refusals. It is only the control arm
that is unreachable.

V2 — REFUSED BY ITS OWN PACKAGE'S PREFLIGHT, AND INDEPENDENTLY BY V1'S BLOCKER.
V2 specifies one write per window (:293). `allocArmSizing` refuses
`writes < ALLOC_MIN_WRITES = 6` before a browser launches, pinned as ROUTE 2.
Reproduced: `P0_ALLOC_CELLS=1 P0_ALLOC_WRITES=1` -> admissible:false. V2 also
needs both writes in the same run, so V1's blocker takes it a second time.
Filed as rf2-qomo, which is a RULING and not a widening — the floor's stated
ground is a precondition on FITTING and V2 takes no fit, but the obvious fix
("run V2 at six writes") is not free: the brief's own arithmetic puts B=4/R=20/
W=6 at ~630 KB against a measured collection onset of 600,000 B.

V3 — NO CONTROLS-ONLY MODE EXISTS.
V3 is "the controls only ... No arms" (:443-445). `--only alloc` has one shape:
preflight, then controls AND the full ladder plan every round. The mode surface
is closed (`clock | heap | fanout | ladder | alloc`) and the no-arms route is
shut by the preflight — `P0_ALLOC_CELLS=0` refuses correctly for want of a
per-boundary quantity. V3's controls are reachable only by riding a full ladder
run: ~108 ladder-arm windows to harvest 18 control windows, and criterion 5
freezes every allocation window that is not V1-V4.

WHAT I REFUSED TO DO, each with its reason, because these were live choices.

1. I did NOT build the write selector and measure through it. It is ~one line in
   `alloc-window!` plus a pin amendment, and the box was granted and idle. Shape
   6 forbids improving the rig mid-window, and the substantive reason is
   criterion 5's own: a window taken on an instrument written minutes earlier,
   with no red-then-green proof and no review, is exactly the uncertified-
   instrument window the freeze exists to prevent. Filed as rf2-gxrr instead.

2. I did NOT run a partial V1 — F_new(B)/B at the three pages against the ~2
   KB/bnd/write bar, with F_old omitted. This was the tempting one: the pass/
   fail criterion depends only on the new write, so the numbers would have come
   out. It is precisely tonight's hardest-won lesson in a new costume — F_old IS
   V1's control, and a run reported without its control does not contribute
   data. The brief says why in its own words: "take both writes, because that
   turns an assertion into an experiment with a control in it" (:250-251).

3. I did NOT measure F_old by building an older commit. Two writes measured on
   two builds is not a control that the rig has not moved — it measures a
   different rig — and checking out a pre-merge commit to compile inside a
   measurement window is a rig change wearing another hat.

4. I did NOT ride a full ladder run to harvest V3's controls. It needs no rig
   change, which is what made it tempting. But it is not V3's configuration, it
   takes ~108 windows criterion 5 freezes to get 18 it permits, and half of V3's
   deliverable (the floor's leg spread "at each of V1's three pages", :463) is
   defined against a comparison V1 cannot make. Substituting a different witness
   because the primary one cannot run is the same move as (2).

5. I widened NOTHING. ALLOC_MIN_WRITES stays 6, ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B stays
   600,000, R = 20 stays, tau stays the uncalibrated placeholder. No gate, band
   or threshold was touched, and the branch carries no commits — there was no
   honest change to make.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LANE. This bead cannot discharge and rf2-2rtt6.139 stays
blocked behind it until rf2-gxrr lands (and rf2-qomo is ruled, for V2's half).
rf2-gxrr is ordinary implementation work needing no quiet box — it is instrument
code with hermetic pins and no measurement — so it can be dispatched
concurrently with the rest of the lane rather than holding the box. The next
window in lane order that is actually runnable tonight is rf2-y1jkm.

THE HONEST SUMMARY: the design brief specified four validity witnesses and the
implementation PR built the artefacts they judge, but not the surface that lets
them be run. That gap was invisible until someone tried to run one, and this
window is what trying looked like. Cost: no box time beyond hermetic checks.
Bought: the lane's actual blocker, located to the line.

MEASUREMENT WINDOW RUN AND REPORTED — 2026-08-14 04:18-04:42 AUSEST, granted
quiet box, branch worker/allocv1-140 off 457ac7f173, PR #8152 (docs only).
V1, V2 AND V3 ALL RAN. Nine browser runs, one at a time. THE BEAD STAYS OPEN:
V1's and V2's criteria came back UNASSESSED rather than answered, and two new P1
blockers are filed.

EVERY RUN'S POSITIVE CONTROL PASSED, reported per run and never pooled: 8.08
B/double direct, 8.00 B/double differential against a predicted 8, idle 32
B/iteration, in all nine. No run was excluded and none was pooled with another.

THE BOX. Queue length 0 or 1 in every sample of every measured phase (5 before,
8 during V1, 7 during V2). Two spikes -- 26/14 at 04:23 and 38 at 04:34 -- both
inside this window's own shadow-cljs release compile, not a measured phase.
Measured rather than assumed: 96 resident node/java/chrome processes accrued
54.97 cpu-seconds over six seconds, of which 53.41 was ONE java pid (the compile
itself); the other 95 accrued 1.56 cpu-seconds, 0.26 of one core on 24 threads,
73 of them the operator's Chrome.

THE INSTRUMENT WAS VERIFIED BEFORE IT WAS BELIEVED. P0_ALLOC_WRITE=pge and
P0_ALLOC_PLAN=contols each refused BY NAME before a browser launched, captured
exit 1 each (the harness reported 0 for the first -- the captured number governs).
p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs 59 passed / exit 0 on this worktree.

=== V1 -- THE BRIEF'S LARGEST OPEN QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND IT WENT THE WAY THE
BRIEF FEARED ===

The question was how much of F ~ 24.4 KB is the 300-cell rebuild and how much is
the event pipeline. IT IS THE PIPELINE.

  F_old - F_new = 1.1 - 1.9 KB per write, at EVERY page size
  w = 3.6 - 7.3 B/cell, consistent across six independent readings
  F0 ~ 18 - 19.4 KB, i.e. OVER 90% OF F

The boundary-proportional write works exactly as designed and removes roughly 7%
of the problem. F_new is flat in B for the same reason F_old is.

THE CONTROL LANDED ON ITS FIRST CLAUSE AND IS UNASSESSED ON ITS SECOND.
  - "F_old flat in B" -- HOLDS. reagent-subs 19,898/19,781/19,898 and uix-subs
    20,487/20,446/20,487 across B in {4,24,96}: flat to 0.6% over a 24x range.
  - "lands on the 2026-08-08 figures (24,108/24,730) at B=24" -- UNASSESSED. Those
    are rise/W figures; this window's rise/W at B=24 under write-all reads 22,000
    and 33,512, off windows the witness REFUSED. The published figures sit inside
    the per-round ranges, but no certified window exists to read the clause from.
    Not missed -- not assessed.

V1's CRITERION, F_new(B)/B under the ~2 KB bar (read off refused windows):
  B=4    4,497 / 4,854 B/bnd/write   OVER
  B=24     767 /   798               under
  B=96     192 /   200               under

THE TWO CONSTRAINTS DO NOT CROSS, and this closes contingency (i) by measurement.
Clearing the fixed-residue bar needs B >= 9.0-9.7 (F0/B <= 2,000). Keeping a
six-write R=20 window under the 600,000 B onset needs B <= 1.9-2.5 (perWrite <=
100,000 with s(20) = 32,058-43,263 B/bnd/write measured by V2). THE SMALLEST PAGE
THIS RIG CAN MOUNT IS B=4 AND IT SATISFIES NEITHER. Raising B relieves one bound
and worsens the other at the rate the worst rung sets, so the gap does not close
by moving B. Contingency (ii) -- carry F0 as a stated instrument constant the
floor subtracts -- is the step the data points at.

=== V2 -- THE R=20 RUNG'S VERDICT UNDER rf2-qomo: REFUSED, AND THE PREDICTION WAS
OPTIMISTIC ===

Run at SIX WRITES as ruled. The ruling forecast ~630 KB against the 600,000 B
onset. MEASURED: 900 KB - 1.5 MB, i.e. 1.5x-2.5x the onset rather than 1.05x --
the brief's estimate was low by about 45%.

  all  reagent|hicasso R20   920,386 - 1,172,582   7 falls
  all  reagent|reagent R20   983,866 - 1,510,710   9 falls
  all  uix|hicasso R20       903,386 - 1,494,586   8 falls
  all  uix|uix R20           912,926 -   933,082   0 falls  <- certified 6/6
  page reagent|hicasso R20   908,454 - 1,095,490   7 falls
  page reagent|reagent R20   976,130 - 1,013,450   7 falls
  page uix|hicasso R20       897,054 - 1,412,554   5 falls
  page uix|uix R20           904,014 - 1,030,330   1 fall

Falls concentrate there: 24 of the all run's 27 and 20 of the page run's 28.
ONE ARM IS NAMED RATHER THAN AVERAGED AWAY: uix|uix R20 under write-all certified
6/6 with zero falls -- the cheapest R=20 arm (leg median ~150 KB against ~180-200
KB) sitting just under the onset. Under write-page it refused 1/6. One arm, one
write, one segment is not the rung passing.

THE RUNG WAS NOT DROPPED, NOT RE-RUN UNTIL IT PASSED, AND
ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B WAS NOT WIDENED. The refusal is the result, as ruled.

V2's OWN CRITERION IS UNASSESSED. (arm-floor)/B needs a certified floor and THE
FLOOR CERTIFIED 0 OF 6 WINDOWS IN BOTH RUNS ON BOTH SEGMENTS. Recorded as an
INDICATION ONLY, off refused windows: agreement is 0.0-2.4% at every
subscription-bearing rung on both substrates and both segments, and the floor
drops 1,688/1,719 B (7.3%). That is the shape the equivalence argument predicts
and it is NOT V2 passing.

=== V3 -- DELIVERED, AND ITS ANSWER HAS A STING ===

The only run of the nine to exit 0. Controls' worst relative leg deviation 0.99%;
11 of 12 windows read EXACTLY 0.00% with six byte-identical legs; idle 0.00%.

TAU WAS NOT PINNED. Pinning is a source edit and a measurement window does not
amend the instrument it measures on. And the calibration has a consequence worth
the operator's attention: applying V3's stated rule lands tau at ~0.02-0.05, at
which a window certifies only above ~230 KB leg median -- which NO ARM reaches
except R=20, and R=20 is already refused by the collector. AN HONEST CALIBRATION
WOULD REFUSE THE ENTIRE LADDER. The 0.25 placeholder is more permissive than the
calibrated value, and it already refuses every floor window. Filed as rf2-e9wr.

=== WHAT REFUSED EVERYTHING, AND IT IS ONE TERM ===

EVERY ARM WINDOW MEASURED -- 336 OF 336 across eight browser runs -- has a
positive first-leg excess over its own cohort median: min 3,441 / median 6,966 /
max 28,448 B. CONSTANT IN ABSOLUTE BYTES across a 24x page range, IDENTICAL under
both writes, surviving all three full-size warm-ups. Tail legs are byte-identical
to each other (one window: 26044, 19256, 19256, 19256, 19256, 19256), so the
precision is excellent and leg 1 is the sole deviant. Collector events look
different and appear separately as NEGATIVE legs.

A fixed ~7 KB excess refuses any window whose median is under 6,966/0.25 ~ 27,900
B. That predicts the observed refusal in 290 of 336 windows (86.3%), and all 46
disagreements are windows refused for an ADDITIONAL reason, never ones the rule
spared. The admissible band is two-sided: above ~28 KB/write for the excess to sit
inside tau, below ~100 KB/write for six writes to clear the onset.

THE FLOOR IS BELOW THAT BAND IN ALL SIXTEEN RUN x SEGMENT CASES, and the floor is
F, and F IS FLAT IN B -- so NO PAGE SIZE MOVES IT IN. Since arm - floor is what
every witness is stated over, the rungs that certify cannot be differenced against
a floor that never does. THIS IS THIS BEAD'S OWN SHAPE ONE LEVEL DOWN: the bead
recorded that shrinking the measured unit has a floor and it is F; the window

DEFERRAL LIFTED — MIKE 2026-08-14: 'I want hicasso fully implemented, nothing deferred. I want a complete library. I want a sophisticated library.'

This bead was parked under the earlier direction to run measurement later. That direction is superseded. It is now live work.

ONE PHYSICAL CONSTRAINT REMAINS AND IS NOT A DEFERRAL. A clock estimand needs a quiet box: one measurement at a time, controls arbitrating, no other worker compiling. That is a property of the instrument, not a scheduling preference — a reading taken against six concurrent compiles measures the fleet, not the library. COUNTER estimands have no such constraint; monotone counters read the same on a loaded box, which is why the deterministic censuses landed while the clock tables did not.

SO THE PLAN IS: build every instrument NOW, in parallel, on a loaded box — that work is edit-shaped and unconstrained. Then run the windows themselves back to back when the fleet is idle. That is the same split that produced rf2-w01c from rf2-hic-036 and rf2-d6ai8 from rf2-hic-088, and it means the quiet-box time is spent measuring rather than writing drivers.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWES, restated: if it needs an instrument that does not exist, that half dispatches immediately. If the instrument exists and only the window is missing, it queues for the next quiet period. Whoever picks it up should say which case it is in the first paragraph of its report.

CROSS-REFERENCE FROM THE BACKLOG REREAD, mayor 2026-08-18 10:46 AUSEST. Bears on the evidence, not on the ruling.

rf2-77gz8, measured today, reports the floor arm's rise/W as BIMODAL at exactly 3,792 B with BOTH modes certifying - two runs twelve minutes apart on the same instrument and the same implementation/core/src commit, differing by that exact figure on both segments, from a step that occurs WITHIN a run rather than between revisions.

THE RELEVANCE HERE: 3,792 B is larger than the 1,769 / 1,765 B floor drop this bead's V2 accepted. So that accepted drop is smaller than the demonstrated single-run uncertainty at one revision, and cannot be distinguished from mode selection on the evidence available.

STATED AT ITS OWN STRENGTH: rf2-77gz8 does not claim the drop WAS mode selection. It observed the high mode once in eight runs and records that whether the mode is revision-dependent is UNRESOLVED. What it establishes is that a single-run floor figure carries an uncertainty exceeding the effect, which is a fact about the measurement rather than about the ladder.

IMPLICATION FOR THE RULING, and it strengthens rather than changes the mayor's recommendation on the sibling rf2-2rtt6.139: sizing anything from a single-run constant is now doubly unsound - the 2026-08-07 run was refused, and single runs at one revision are now known to differ by more than the quantities being sized. Option b there - stop sizing from a constant and let the preflight refuse only on grounds it can defend - is the shape that survives this finding. Option a, re-deriving a decomposition from measured runs, would need enough runs per rung to separate the modes, which is a materially larger programme than it looked yesterday.

NOT DISPATCHED. This bead remains yours to rule, and nothing in rf2-77gz8 forces the ruling either way - it changes what evidence a defensible ruling can rest on.

comments.text:
SECOND CROSS-REFERENCE FROM THE BACKLOG REREAD, mayor 2026-08-18 11:45 AUSEST. This one bears on whether V2's residual can be ASSESSED at all, not just on how precisely.

rf2-irxrw, filed today by rf2-0gjqi's re-analysis and derived at source without taking a window, reports that THE INSTRUMENT CANNOT DRIVE BOTH WRITES IN ONE PROCESS. ALLOC_WRITE is read once from process.env at module scope (p0_run.cjs:1504), ALLOC_WRITE_SPECS has exactly two members and no paired option (:1490), and the resolved kind is passed into every arm window of the run (:2335, :2342). So one process drives ONE write, necessarily.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is structural rather than statistical: every write-all versus write-page comparison this instrument has ever produced differences TWO SEQUENTIAL PROCESS RUNS IN A FIXED ORDER. allocation-instrument-rework.md:231-232 requires those two writes to be compared as a same-page, same-run pair. They never have been.

WHY THIS TOUCHES THIS BEAD. V2's criterion is about the arm-floor residual, and the residual is exactly the quantity that comparison produces. Until a paired mode exists, V2's residual is UNASSESSED rather than small - and that is the merged-PR audit's own word, recorded on rf2-0gjqi on 2026-08-17.

WHAT THE RE-ANALYSIS ADDED to that audit, and it sharpens it considerably. The eight mid-rung sign comparisons that looked like 1-in-256 are EIGHT CELLS, ONE DRAW: they share one run order; the four reagent-subs cells difference against the SAME four certified floor windows; and rf2-77gz8's second floor mode moves both segments by exactly the same 3,792 B, which merges the segments too. A shared floor offset of 2,472 B/write on reagent-subs, or 928 on uix-subs, reverses every sign - and three runs at one revision under one write span 3,852 / 3,912 B/write in certified floor median. Both exceed what it takes to flip the result.

WHAT IT DID NOT CLAIM, and the restraint is worth preserving: it did NOT adopt the mode account. A floor offset is additive and identical across a segment's arms, while the observed mid-rung offsets span 1,948 / 740 B/write and within an arm family the residual is closer to a constant proportion. Right magnitude, wrong shape - neither excluded nor supported. The cause is UNRESOLVED; only the inferential claim is refuted.

MAYOR RULING ON CRITERION 5, 2026-08-19 00:05 AUSEST, taken on Mike's standing delegation. This criterion has owed a ruling since the paired mode landed, and the 2026-08-18 re-read poses it cleanly enough to answer.

WHAT I AM NOT RULING ON. rf2-0gjqi's question — whether ~1-4% of non-cancellation is tolerable — is WITHDRAWN, and rightly: under matched within-round pairing the agreement half no longer shows a direction at all (page reads below all at 10 of 16 mid-rung cell medians, not 8 of 8, with the absolute median falling from 1.68% to 0.46%), and the sign that WAS there tracks which leg pass ran SECOND rather than which write it was. That is rf2-fk6pj's subject, not this one.

THE QUESTION AS IT NOW STANDS: is the instrument's residual non-cancellation acceptable, given that its R=0 NULL ARM — boundaries that read nothing, so arm minus floor must be exactly zero under either write — reads an absolute median of 1.5 B per boundary and a 90th percentile of 4.5, over 38 paired certified observations?

RULING: ACCEPT IT, AND PUBLISH IT AS A NAMED FLOOR RATHER THAN AS A TOLERANCE.

WHY ACCEPT. The null arm's reading is the instrument's own noise floor measured directly, which is the best possible way to have it: not inferred, not modelled, but read off an arm whose true value is known to be zero. And it is three orders of magnitude below the quantities the ladder publishes — the per-boundary terms this programme reports run 2,031 to 22,174 B per boundary per write, against which 1.5 B is roughly 0.07% and the p90 of 4.5 B is roughly 0.2%. An instrument does not need perfect cancellation; it needs a floor small against its signal and HONESTLY STATED.

WHY 'A NAMED FLOOR' RATHER THAN 'A TOLERANCE', and this is the part that matters. Ruling a PERCENTAGE tolerable would be the wrong shape: percentages travel, and a figure that is 0.07% of a 2,031 B term is 100% of a 1.5 B one. The number that is stable is the FLOOR ITSELF, in bytes per boundary, because that is what the null arm measures.

SO THE OBLIGATION THIS RULING CREATES, and it is one line of code and one of prose rather than new machinery:
  1. Record 1.5 B per boundary (median) and 4.5 B (p90) over 38 paired certified observations as the instrument's NON-CANCELLATION FLOOR, in the record beside the figures it qualifies.
  2. REFUSE, rather than publish, any per-boundary figure that is not comfortably above it. I set that bar at ten times the p90 — 45 B per boundary — because a figure within an order of magnitude of the noise floor is not a measurement, and the honest answer there is the same one rf2-2rtt6.139 reached about sizing: an instrument that says 'I cannot resolve this' is not a worse instrument.
Do NOT add a new gate, a new constant, or a rung parameter. The floor is a published number and a refusal the preflight can already express.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DISCHARGE. The floor-drop half stands as the re-read left it: 1,652 B (8.6%) on reagent-subs and 1,652-1,658 B (8.4%) on uix-subs, the same number on both segments to within 6 B across 21 paired certified rounds, against published unpaired figures of 1,769 / 1,765 B. QUESTION: Is the 300,000 B masking bound (rf2-n6w7o) still a binding VALIDITY requirement, independent of the certificate?

Three facts bear on it, measured first-hand from data/alloc-0gjqi/{paired-run1,paired-run2}.json at origin/main b524ba71ce. None of them decides it.

So certification and the bound are different criteria and they disagree on two of five rungs.

(b) THE BOUND IS CHARGED ON A QUANTITY THAT CANNOT SEE A COLLECTION. Two identities hold over all 528 arm windows in the corpus, checked rather than asserted:
      perWrite == rise / writes                       0 mismatches of 528
      rise     == sum(max(leg,0)) + sum(max(gap,0))   0 mismatches of 528
rise sums POSITIVE deltas only, over legs and over the inter-leg gaps alike. A collection inside a window therefore makes that window's rise SMALLER, its perWrite smaller, and its charge against the masking bound smaller. The bound is loosest exactly where masking is worst. The 72 R20 refusals carry a median rise of 879,080 B against a would-be total of 1,035,036 B — charged on about 85% of what the window actually asked for.

title: hic: rf2-t4jpz METHOD (b)'s 'PRE-PILOT — NOT §13 EVIDENCE' log header vs rf2-dc0c's blinding rationale — the blank log a BLINDED pilot receives cannot both name the run's kind and stay silent about it
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 07:1x AUSEST by the operator assembly for rf2-t4jpz, at the
point of actually writing the two FRICTION-LOG.md copies. UNRESOLVED — the
operator did NOT write the header, and says so, because writing it is the
irreversible half.

THE CONFLICT. rf2-t4jpz METHOD (b) says: "Each friction log's header reads
PRE-PILOT — NOT §13 EVIDENCE and records the pinned commit."

workspace.md's rehearsal section (added under rf2-dc0c, PR #9049) says of the
two operator-applied replacements: "Both replacements are written to be read
alone. Neither names a rehearsal, a counted run, or this page, so the pilot
meets one instruction rather than a choice between two."

These pull opposite ways on the SAME artefact. The friction log is handed to a
BLINDED pilot. A header reading "PRE-PILOT — NOT §13 EVIDENCE" tells that pilot
(a) that a section 13 exists, (b) that it is inside an experiment whose
evidence status is contested, and (c) that its own run does not count — which
is precisely the kind of framing rf2-dc0c removed from outcome 7 on the
reasoning that a blinded pilot must not be asked to reason about which kind of
run it is in. The read fence separately bars reading the tracker, and "§13" is
an in-tree design reference.

WHAT IS GENUINELY UNDECIDED, and why the operator stopped rather than choosing:
METHOD (b) does not say WHO writes that header or WHEN. Part 4 of the log is
explicitly the operator's section, written after the pilot ends, so the label
can be applied at disposition time without ever reaching the pilot — which
would satisfy both texts. But that is a reading, not a ruling, and the previous
rehearsal's logs did carry the header.

TIMING NOTE. rf2-t4jpz's METHOD was written 2026-09-02, BEFORE the rf2-dc0c
operator-applied variant landed with its blinding rationale, so the newer
package text may simply refine the older method rather than contradict it.

WHAT THE OPERATOR DID on the pilotasm-a run, pending a ruling: applied
workspace.md's two mandated rehearsal edits verbatim, filled the pin and the
baseline exit code that step 1 and step 5b make the operator's, and left the
PRE-PILOT header OFF the blank logs. Rationale: adding the line later is
trivial; un-leaking a blinded pilot is impossible. Both FRICTION-LOG.md copies
therefore currently carry 0 bead-id lines, 0 workspace.md links and 0 stray
fence lines, verified against source-page controls that bite.

DECISION NEEDED BEFORE DISPATCH: does the blank log a pilot receives carry the
PRE-PILOT — NOT §13 EVIDENCE header, or is that label applied by the operator
in Part 4 after the pilot ends? Either answer is cheap to apply to the two
assembled workspaces.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 07:4x AUSEST. LEAVE THE HEADER OFF THE PILOT TEMPLATE. THE OPERATOR STAMPS IT ON COLLECTION.

THE CONFLICT IS REAL AND BOTH SIDES ARE RIGHT, WHICH IS WHY IT NEEDED A RULING RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE. rf2-t4jpz METHOD (b) wants a "PRE-PILOT - NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE" header on the friction log, so the archived artefact cannot later be mistaken for adoption proof. workspace.md says the operator replacements deliberately "name no rehearsal... so the pilot meets one instruction rather than a choice between two", which is the blinding rationale rf2-dc0c established.

THEY BELONG TO DIFFERENT READERS, AND THAT DISSOLVES IT. The header exists for whoever reads the log LATER - an auditor, or rf2-hic-064 section 13 checkpoint. It does nothing for the pilot except tell it it is inside an experiment, which is the one thing the blinding forbids: a pilot that knows it is rehearsing reports differently, and every outcome it records is then evidence about a pilot who knew.

THE RULING: the pilot TEMPLATE carries no such header. THE OPERATOR STAMPS IT WHEN THE LOG IS COLLECTED, before it is filed under ai/findings/. METHOD (b) purpose is fully served - the archived artefact is marked - and the blinding is untouched. That is one line of operator work at collection time and zero risk.

THE WORKER INSTINCT WAS ALREADY RIGHT AND I AM CONFIRMING RATHER THAN OVERRIDING IT: it left the header off and said "adding a line later is trivial, un-blinding a pilot is not." That is the correct asymmetry and it is the reason this ruling goes the way it does. An error in the reversible direction beats an error in the irreversible one, and only one of these two errors can be undone after the pilots run.

RECORD THE MECHANISM IN THE PACKAGE, not just here: workspace.md operator section should say the header is stamped at collection, so the next operator does not re-derive this and does not leave the artefact unmarked. That edit is NOT urgent and must NOT delay the pilot dispatch - file it or fold it into the next pilots-package pass.

title: hic: workspace.md hardcodes :dev-http 8080 for BOTH pilots — a parallel second pilot boot-checks the FIRST pilot's app and passes
notes:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, operator half, re-run after PR #9050 and #9049. Workspace pin cfcc30ae93. Measured, not reasoned.

SYMPTOM. docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/workspace.md gives BOTH pilots the identical shadow-cljs.edn line ':dev-http {8080 "public"}' and step 5 says 'npx shadow-cljs watch app  # then open http://localhost:8080'. rf2-hic-063's ruling explicitly permits the two pilots to run IN PARALLEL ('separate workspaces, no shared branch'). Those two facts are incompatible, and the failure mode is silent.

MEASURED. Both pilot watches started ~20s apart from their own assembled workspaces:
  - workspace A (realworld) binds 8080 and serves conduit.
  - workspace B (linearlite) prints, as a WARNING and not an error, ':shadow.cljs.devtools.server.dev-http/http-start-ex ... BindException Address already in use: bind' — then continues and prints '[:app] Build completed. (277 files, 0 compiled, 0 warnings, 9.82s)'.
  - With both live, the operator boot check against http://localhost:8080 returns #app innerHTML length 2350, 0 page errors, 0 console errors, 0 failed requests, and renders 'conduit / Home / Sign in / Sign up'.

That is pilot A's application, returned to pilot B, with a clean bill of health. LinearLite's own boot reading in isolation is 3535; the collided reading is 2350, i.e. entirely the other app.

WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT FAILS OPEN. The BindException is a WARNING sitting ABOVE the 'Build completed' line, so the last thing on screen is success. A blinded pilot executing step 5 literally gets a compile that says it worked, a page that renders, and a boot check that passes — while reading the other pilot's app. Nothing in the log the pilot is looking at contradicts it. The blinding is intact but the INSTRUMENT is cross-wired, and every outcome-1..6 observation the second pilot records would be about the wrong application.

SCOPE. This bites only when the two pilots run concurrently on one machine, which is precisely what the ruling authorises. It did not bite the first rehearsal or this one, because both ran the pilots sequentially.

REMEDY IS THE OPERATOR'S CALL, NOT FILED AS RULED. Options, cheapest first: (a) give pilot 2 a different :dev-http port in workspace.md's 'Pilot 2 uses :init-fn linearlite.core/run' sentence, which already exists as the place where pilot 2's shadow-cljs.edn is said to differ, and update step 5's URL alongside it; (b) say in step 5 that the two pilots must not run concurrently on one host, which contradicts the ruling and is worse; (c) have step 5 tell the operator to read the ':dev-http' line shadow actually prints rather than assuming 8080. (a) is the smallest change and keeps the parallel run the ruling wants.

title: PR #9043 red: the derivation-egress bundle-isolation POSITIVE CONTROL lost its sentinel when rf2-g1vu replaced the keyword with an identity value
notes:
DIAGNOSED BY THE MAYOR 2026-09-03 04:0x AUSEST from the failing job log. PR #9043 is converted to DRAFT (confirmed draft=true, state=OPEN) so it cannot be merged while red.

THE RED IS REAL, IT IS CORRECT, AND IT IS THE GATE DOING EXACTLY WHAT IT WAS BUILT FOR. Job: tests :: CLJS bundle isolation (counter, rf2-51x5), run 33661478278. The failure is not the negative check — it is the POSITIVE CONTROL:

  "Positive control FAILED - a sentinel is no longer PRESENT where it should be (rf2-e6qmxk). The sentinel string has DRIFTED ... so the negative counter-bundle check above has LOST ITS TEETH for that artefact: it would pass whether or not the artefact actually leaked."
  "  - derivation-egress: only 0/1 sentinels present in emitted module derivation-egress"

THE CAUSE, and it is a genuinely instructive one. Under rf2-g1vu the worker replaced dead-frame-sentinel in implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc — correctly, on my ruling, and having first REPRODUCED the raw-secret leak — changing it from the keyword ::no-egress-frame to #?(:clj (Object.) :cljs (js/Object.)). A keyword literal compiles into the emitted bundle as a STRING. An identity value does not. So the literal the bundle-isolation script had pinned as its positive-control sentinel for the derivation-egress module simply stopped existing in the artefact.

SO A CORRECT SECURITY FIX SILENTLY DISARMED AN UNRELATED CONTROL, AND THE ONLY REASON WE KNOW IS THAT THE CONTROL CHECKS ITSELF. That is the same defect class this session keeps meeting — a control that cannot catch its own case — except here the control DOES catch its own case, which is why this is a red on a PR rather than a vacuous green on main for the next six months. rf2-e6qmxk built that self-check; it has now paid for itself.

THE FIX IS SMALL AND THE GATE PRINTS IT: "re-derive the sentinel from the artefact source and update the matching internalSentinels entry (keep it a live, unique literal)." The roster lives in implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs, with implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.test.cjs beside it.

AND THE GATE ALSO PRINTS THE ANTI-FIX, WHICH MUST BE HONOURED: "Never delete the sentinel to make this pass — that restores the vacuous-green hole this control exists to close." Deleting the derivation-egress entry would turn the job green and leave that artefact permanently unguarded. Do not do it, and do not weaken the positive control.

WHAT THE FIXER MUST DO: pick a LIVE, UNIQUE string literal that survives release compilation of the derivation-egress module — an error id or message literal is the shape the roster already uses — verify it actually appears in the emitted bundle, and prove the choice by the gate going red again if that literal is removed. A sentinel chosen by reading source and not verified in the EMITTED artefact is how this recurs.

title: framework logs ExceptionInfo to console.error as a raw CLJS object — the browser shows {meta: null, cnt: 7, arr: Array(14)} instead of the error message
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 02:55 AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, while diagnosing the route-link boot failure (rf2-nvcp). Tip d1e6a707a3.

WHAT AN ADOPTER SEES. When the runtime reports an error through its own console channel, the browser console shows:

  [re-frame2] {meta: null, cnt: 7, arr: Array(14), __hash: null, cljs$: 16647951}

That is a raw cljs.core/ExceptionInfo (or its ex-data map) handed to console.error as an object. Chrome renders its JS fields. The actual message — a long, genuinely well-written recovery ladder naming the operation, the recovery and three ways to establish a frame scope — is inside the object and is never printed.

MEASURED. Captured from headless Chrome on the linearlite example at this tip: three such lines, each an ExceptionInfo. The same run's window 'error' event carried the full text, so the message exists and is reachable; only the console rendering loses it. The realworld example produced the same shape. Both were reached through ordinary page load, not through any test harness.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE PILOTS. Outcome 5 is 'diagnose one induced failure through the documented diagnostic path', and the console is where a reader looks first — chapter 16 sends them to Xray, but every reader checks the console before installing a tool. An opaque object teaches the reader that re-frame2's errors are unreadable, which is the opposite of what the error text actually achieves. Three of my own diagnostic steps were spent recovering a message the framework already had.

THE CONTRAST IS SHARP. In the same console, the framework's own reg-view warning prints perfectly as text: '[re-frame] reg-view :linearlite.core/root-view — root element is #object[cljs.core.MetaFn]; data-rf2-source-coord skipped (Spec 006 §Source-coord annotation ...)'. So the string path is fine; it is the error path that hands over an object.

LIKELY FIX. At the console sink, print (ex-message e) — and the id from (ex-data e) — as a string, and attach the object as a second argument if the inspectable value is wanted. That keeps the object expandable in devtools while making the first line readable.

NOT the same defect as rf2-nvcp. That one is why the error is raised at all; this one is that the error is unreadable when it is. Fixing route-link removes these three particular lines and leaves the rendering defect in place for the next error.

FILED, NOT FIXED — implementation/ is held by live workers.
notes:
PRODUCTION EVIDENCE, added 2026-09-03 03:00 AUSEST by the same rehearsal.

Under advanced compilation the error is not merely opaque, it is anonymous. A production release of pilot 1's workspace (npx shadow-cljs release app, exit 0, 332 files, 0 warnings, main.js 1.66MB) loads to a blank page whose only diagnostic is:

  Error: zm

That is the minified constructor name. The recovery ladder, the [:rf.error/no-frame-context] id, the :operation / :recovery / :where keys — everything an adopter could act on, and everything the catalogue could be looked up by — is gone from the shipped bundle.

This is the same underlying failure as the dev build (rf2-nvcp), seen through the release path, and it sharpens this bead in two ways. First, it is the exact case friction-log.md says outcome 6 exists to catch: 'Advanced compilation removes diagnostics and warning strings, and a bundle that compiles but does not boot is the failure this outcome exists to catch.' Second, it means the console-rendering defect recorded above degrades from unreadable to unattributable in production: in dev the message at least exists inside the logged object, and in release there is no message at all.

Worth considering alongside any fix here: whether a stable complaint id (not the minified symbol) should survive advanced compilation, so a production error can still be looked up. Chapter 16 promises stable complaint ids and a catalogue; 'Error: zm' cannot reach either. Recording the observation, not proposing the design.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #9060 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9060). Two halves, both measured in headless Chromium on the linearlite dev build, not asserted in a unit test.

(1) CONSOLE CHANNEL. re-frame.error-emit/report-unowned-error! passed only the record, and a CLJS map is not a JS object — Chrome rendered PersistentArrayMap's interior fields, which is the reported '{meta: null, cnt: 7, arr: Array(14), ...}' (cnt 7 = the seven-key record). A readable summary line now LEADS: the exception's ex-message, else the record's :reason, else the bare category keyword. Composes no new error text. The record AND the exception still ride as their own console arguments, so structured consumers and DevTools inspection are unchanged.

(2) THE EMIT SITE, which a console-only fix could not have reached. The bead's diagnosis was one step off and it mattered: the logged object is the error-emit RECORD, not an ExceptionInfo or its ex-data, and for :rf.error/no-frame-context that record carried NEITHER an exception NOR a reason — emit-no-frame-context! dropped the payload's composed ladder. Measured: {:error :rf.error/no-frame-context, :event :rf/redacted, :event-id nil, :frame nil, :time 334.3, :exception nil, :elapsed-ms 0}. The premise 'the message exists and is reachable, only the console rendering loses it' is therefore FALSE for this category, and so is 'the window error event carried the full text' — the pageerror message was 23 characters: cljs$core$ExceptionInfo. The emit site now threads :reason/:recovery through dispatch-on-error!'s EXISTING attrs attribution seam. Its mirrored sibling emit-bad-frame-provider-arg! had the identical shape and got the same one-line treatment.

BEFORE: [re-frame2] {meta: null, cnt: 7, arr: Array(14), __hash: null, cljs$lang$protocol_mask$partition0$: 16647951, ...}
AFTER:  [re-frame2] :rf.error/no-frame-context — a frame-scoped route-link ran with no frame context — ... (full recovery ladder) ... Per Spec 002 §The error and its ladder. {meta: null, cnt: 9, root: Object, ...}

error_emit_dev_console_dom_cljs_test.cljs pinned the old two-argument shape and is updated; two new tests pin the ladder reaching the line and the sibling's symmetry. No assertion weakened. Gates: test:cljs 11197/55794 exit 0; core JVM 2175/11144 exit 0; test:browser 778/4233 exit 0; fast-pr spine exit 0, clj-kondo errors 0.

NOT DONE (deliberately, per the stance): the production-anonymity observation in this bead's NOTES ('Error: zm' under advanced compilation) is a separate design question and is untouched.

title: pilots package: nothing tells the pilot WHERE to read the published documentation, and the read fence does not affirmatively allow docs/core/ in the checkout
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 02:55 AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, assembling both workspaces from docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/. Tip d1e6a707a3.

THE GAP. The pilot's brief makes the published documentation the reference for everything: 'Everything you need is in the published Hicasso documentation... It is your reference for everything: what to type, what things are called, why something broke, how to test, how to build for production.' Nothing in the package then says where that documentation IS.

- workspace.md's six assembly steps never build the docs site, never copy the pages in, and never record a URL. Step 6 copies only the brief and the blank log.
- The workspace layout block lists re-frame2/, app/, BRIEF.md and FRICTION-LOG.md. No docs.
- friction-log.md's template header asks the pilot to fill in 'Docs read from: <published site URL or local build>' — a field whose answer the package never supplies. There is no published site (the installation page still says the artefact is not published), so 'published site URL' is not available, and 'local build' is never described.

AND THE FENCE DOES NOT CLEARLY PERMIT THE ONE COPY THAT EXISTS. The only copy of those 29 pages is docs/core/hicasso/ inside the re-frame2/ checkout. workspace.md's read fence is headed 'The checkout is a build input, not a reference work' and its Allowed column has exactly three rows: resolving dependencies via :local/root; running a tool a published page names, at the path that page gives; reading error text and stack traces. Reading documentation is not among them. The Not-allowed column names spec/, docs/design/ and other examples — but not docs/core/, so the page neither permits nor forbids it.

A pilot reading the fence literally concludes the checkout may not be read as a reference work, that docs/core/ is part of the checkout, and therefore that it has no reachable documentation at all. A pilot reading it loosely reads the docs and cannot tell whether it has just logged a leak. Either way the citation-enforced fence — which is the instrument rf2-hic-069's audit consumes, and the thing that makes the blinding mechanical rather than impressionistic — is ambiguous at the one point it is used on every single entry.

WHAT IT IS NOT. This is not the same as gap G1/G2/G3 in pilots/README.md. Those record that the published happy path routes through a checkout at three points. This is that the package never states where the pilot's primary reference lives, nor that reading it is allowed.

FIX (the least thing). One line in workspace.md's assembly — an explicit step naming where the pilot reads the 29 pages from, either a locally built site or the docs/core/hicasso/ path — and one row in the fence's Allowed column saying that reading docs/core/hicasso/ IS the published documentation and is clean, so a citation to it is not a leak. The friction-log header field then has a defined answer.

WHY IT SURVIVED REVIEW. The package was written before any workspace was assembled; the omission is only visible to somebody executing the page, which is what this rehearsal did.

FILED, NOT FIXED.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 03:5x AUSEST. THE PILOT READS THE PUBLISHED DOCUMENTATION, AND UNTIL A SITE EXISTS THE PUBLISHED DOCUMENTATION IS THE CHECKOUT COPY OF IT. The fence must say so affirmatively; ambiguity at the one point the fence is used on every task is worse than either answer.

THE RULE, and it is mechanically decidable rather than a list that will drift: ALLOWED is anything under docs/ THAT THE PUBLISHED SITE BUILDS. That set is exactly mkdocs.yml docs_dir minus its exclude_docs block, so it is checkable by running the build rather than by consulting prose — and it gives the right answer for free on the hard cases: docs/design/ is in exclude_docs, so it stays forbidden by the same rule that permits docs/core/hicasso/, with no second sentence needed. NOT ALLOWED is everything else in the checkout: spec/, implementation/ source, other examples, ai/, and the design trees.

WHY THIS AND NOT THE NARROW FORM. Writing "docs/core/hicasso/ is allowed" would work today and reintroduce the ambiguity the moment a pilot follows a link out of those 29 pages into docs/core/ or docs/ssr/ — which the pages themselves do. A real adopter browsing a site can reach any published page; the fence should model that reader, not a subdirectory.

WHAT ELSE HAS TO MOVE WITH IT, because a permission that the assembly steps do not realise is still a gap:
  - workspace.md read fence: add the Allowed row, in the table own voice, and keep the heading "The checkout is a build input, not a reference work" HONEST by saying what the exception is and why it exists — there is no published site yet, and the installation page says so.
  - friction-log.md "Docs read from:" must have a supplied answer. Give it one: the local checkout copy of the published documentation, at the path, with the note that no published site exists yet.
  - The workspace layout block lists re-frame2/, app/, BRIEF.md, FRICTION-LOG.md and no docs. Say where the docs are in that block, or the pilot has to infer it.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: the citation-enforced fence stays the instrument rf2-hic-069 audit consumes, and it stays MECHANICAL. This ruling makes it decidable; it does not loosen it. A pilot that reads spec/ has still leaked.
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 04:2x AUSEST, on the judgement call the pilotpkg-a worker referred up. THE BRIEF CHANGE STAYS. It is inside my ruling intent and the worker found a carrier I missed.

WHAT IT DID BEYOND THE RULED THREE SITES. My ruling named three things that had to move together: the read fence in workspace.md, friction-log.md "Docs read from:", and the workspace layout block. The worker also changed BOTH PILOT BRIEFS, and its reasoning is the correct one: the brief is what the assembly ACTUALLY HANDS THE PILOT, and it said the checkout may not be read "for anything other than the two mechanical uses". So with the permission recorded only in the operator page and the prohibition still in the pilot own document, THE PILOT RECEIVES THE PROHIBITION AND NEVER THE PERMISSION — which is this bead defect restated one document over.

That is not scope creep. My three-site list was an enumeration of carriers, and I enumerated it wrong; a ruling that fixes three of four carriers leaves the bug live. Outcome 7 in both briefs was correctly left untouched, which is the line I would have drawn myself.

AND THE WORKER CAUGHT A HOLE IN MY RULING OWN MECHANISM, which is the part worth recording. I wrote the permitted set as "anything under docs/ THAT THE PUBLISHED SITE BUILDS — exactly docs_dir minus exclude_docs", specifically so it would be mechanically decidable and would settle the hard case (docs/design/ is in exclude_docs, so it stays forbidden by the same rule that permits docs/core/hicasso/). IT FAILS ON A DIFFERENT HARD CASE I DID NOT CONSIDER: mkdocs_hooks.py on_pre_build STAGES ROOT spec/ INTO docs_dir, so the built site DOES serve spec/ — and a rule worded that way would have PERMITTED the one tree the fence most needs to forbid. The worker scoped the rule to the CHECKOUT docs/ tree instead, which closes it without a second sentence.

I find that instructive against myself: the staging hook is the exact mechanism I have been correcting other people about all session, after being measured wrong on it twice, and I still wrote a rule that the hook silently inverts. A mechanically-decidable rule is only as good as the mechanism you checked it against, and I checked mine against exclude_docs and not against the hook.

VERIFICATION I AM SATISFIED WITH: exclude_docs read at source (six entries) AND confirmed by RUNNING the build — site/design does not exist, site/core/hicasso/ has exactly 29 pages. That is the difference between reading a config and observing its effect.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9049 — reopened the exact owner for one missed carrier. The four edited pages correctly make the checkout copy of the published docs reachable, but docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/README.md:30 remains untouched and still states categorically that the checkout is only a build input, that a pilot may not read it for answers, and that the permitted boundary is dependency/tool execution. That directly contradicts the new workspace/brief rule allowing the published pages under docs/ that the site builds. Minimal completion: amend this one governing-package paragraph to name the documentation exception in the same terms; do not widen the fence or reopen the settled manifest/outcome-7 work. No duplicate issue.
close_reason: FIXED in PR #9058, the one missed carrier the #9049 audit reopened this for. docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/README.md:30 now names the documentation exception in the four already-edited pages' own terms rather than a fifth phrasing: 'build input, not a reference work - with one exception' and 'an exception about where the documentation is kept, not about what may be studied' from workspace.md:39; 'anything under docs/ the site builds, which is where docs/core/hicasso/'s 29 pages live' from the read-fence table row at workspace.md:43; 'Reading them is not reading the checkout' from inside both briefs' fences; 'there is no published site yet' from friction-log.md's template header. The paragraph's second half -- the prohibition list (implementation/, spec/, docs/design/, other examples, tracker, history) and the executing-versus-browsing line -- is carried over verbatim, so the fence is not widened. The manifest and outcome 7 were not reopened. Heading text unchanged, since the audit cites headings as anchors. title: pilots workspace.md: the source manifest omits examples/_shared/, so both pilot workspaces 404 their stylesheet and favicon
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 02:55 AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, executing docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/workspace.md step 2 literally. Tip d1e6a707a3.

WHAT HAPPENS. Both apps' index.html (copied in by the manifest, unmodified except the script tag the page tells you to change) link three assets under a sibling _shared/ directory:

  <link rel="stylesheet" href="_shared/css/style.css">
  <link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="_shared/img/favicon.svg">
  <meta property="og:image" content="_shared/img/og.png">

workspace.md's per-pilot manifest copies neither the directory nor any of those files. Measured against a workspace built exactly per the page, served from app/public:

  index.html                 200
  js/main.js                 200
  default-avatar.svg         200
  _shared/css/style.css      404
  _shared/img/favicon.svg    404

Confirmed a second time through headless Chrome: two failed requests, and body computed style falls back to "Times New Roman" on a transparent background. With the stylesheet present (the in-repo control) the same page computes Inter / rgb(247,243,236).

WHERE THE FILES ARE. examples/_shared/css/style.css (274 lines), examples/_shared/img/favicon.svg, examples/_shared/img/og.png — at the root of the examples tree, one level above each app's own directory, which is why a manifest written per-app misses them. The repo serves them through its dev-http root cascade rather than by copying, so the omission is invisible in-repo.

WHY IT MATTERS. RealWorld/Conduit is a CSS-heavy Medium clone and the shared sheet carries the 'Editorial Warm' visual identity the examples are designed against (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn cites it at the :examples/notebook and :examples/dashboard-uix builds). A pilot judging outcome 2 — 'the same behaviour a user sees today' — and an operator running step 5's boot check both meet an unstyled page, and the natural reading is that the scaffolding is broken. workspace.md step 5 exists precisely so 'the friction log records the operator's mistakes as the framework's' does not happen; this is that failure mode, in the page's own manifest.

THE PAGE ALREADY ASSUMES THE FILES ARE THERE. Its 'four project files' section says 'The copied index.html already carries each app's markup and stylesheet links. Change only the script tag' — so it knows about the stylesheet link and still never brings the stylesheet across.

FIX. Add to both manifests in workspace.md step 2, e.g.:

  cp -r re-frame2/examples/_shared app/public/_shared

Both pilots need it; the paths are identical for each.

SEPARATE FROM rf2-nvcp. That bead is the route-link boot failure, which reproduces with all _shared assets present and 0 failed requests. Fixing this one does not make either app boot.

FILED, NOT FIXED.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9049 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9049). Both step-2 manifests in workspace.md now copy the directory (cp -r re-frame2/examples/_shared app/public/_shared) rather than the three named files. Proven by measurement on workspaces assembled exactly per the page and served over HTTP: all four shared assets 404 before and 200 after, for BOTH pilots. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE BEAD, both verified at tip. (1) There is a FOURTH, transitive asset the bead does not name: style.css line 14 is @import url('structure.css'), a further 256 lines owning reusable geometry and the inline-Xray layout — so a three-file manifest would still have served a partly unstyled page, which is why the fix copies the directory. (2) The dev-http root cascade claim is REFUTED: the repo stages _shared/ by RECURSIVE COPY, not by serving it from where it lives — examples/scripts/examples-staging.cjs stageShared() calls copyDirRecursive(SHARED_SRC, outDir/_shared), invoked from serve-example.cjs and serve-and-run-adapter-smokes.cjs; examples/README.md says so and warns a bare 'shadow-cljs watch' copies no _shared assets; and LinearLite's dev-http entry (port 8044) cascades only the app source dir and out/examples/linearlite, neither of which contains _shared/. The defect and its invisibility in-repo are real; only the stated mechanism was wrong.
