title: conformance EDN gate accepts mismatched delimiter types because it tracks only aggregate depth
description:
DISCOVERED while fixing rf2-5mr6 (PR: spec/conformance/fixtures/routing-not-found.edn had one extra closing brace).

GAP. No gate in the tree checks that a conformance fixture is a well-formed EDN file containing exactly ONE top-level form. Both loaders use clojure.edn/read-string over the whole file, which returns the FIRST form and IGNORES everything after it. A fixture whose expectation block is closed early therefore loads, runs, and reports as PASSING while the assertions that fell outside the block are silently discarded. That is exactly what rf2-5mr6 was: bracket depth -1, two trace assertions never executed, green for however long it had been there (introducing commit not bisected).

WHY IT WAS NOT ADDED IN THAT PR. No script under scripts/ or .github/ iterates spec/conformance/fixtures/ at all — check_retired_spellings.py and report-changed-surfaces.sh only NAME the directory. So the check has no existing home; it is a new script plus its own CI wiring plus a fast-PR spine entry, which is a bigger call than the one-character fix it would have guarded.

TWO SHAPES, AND THE SECOND IS THE SHARPER ONE.

(a) A corpus scanner. Python, stdlib only, in the shape of the repo's other spec-coherence gates. The scanner used to measure rf2-5mr6 works and is the algorithm to lift: walk the text, blank ;; comments to end of line, treat a double-quoted string as opaque (honouring backslash escapes), treat a backslash as introducing a one-character char literal, then count ([{ against )]}. Report a defect when final depth is not 0, when min depth ever goes negative, or when the file holds other than exactly one top-level form. Measured 2026-09-03: 247 fixtures scanned, 0 defects after the fix; the pre-fix routing-not-found.edn reports final-depth=-1 top-level-forms=1 neg-at-line=60. Exercised in BOTH directions before either result was believed.

(b) Make the LOADERS refuse trailing text. This is the better fix because it cannot drift from what the runner actually parses, and it is a few lines in each of the two host-specific loaders: implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_fixtures.clj (load-fixture-from-file) and the JVM leaf's slurp + read-string in implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj. Read with a PushbackReader and assert EOF after the first form, or read (str "[" content "]") and assert exactly one element. A fixture with trailing text then fails LOUD at load, in the same run that would otherwise pass it, on every host that loads the corpus. The CLJS leaf inlines fixtures at compile time, so it needs the equivalent at its macro seam.

Prefer (b), or (b) plus (a) — (a) also catches a fixture that never reaches a loader because its capabilities are unclaimed, which (b) cannot see. A fixture whose capabilities are out of claim is SKIPPED by the runner, so a defect in one is invisible to (b) forever.

ACCEPTANCE. A fixture with a deliberately misplaced brace fails a gate that runs on every PR touching spec/conformance/. Prove it by planting one and showing the red, not by showing the green on a clean corpus — a search that returns zero is not a check that passed.
notes:
AUDIT OF PR #9038 (three-lens review).

CORRECTNESS. The scanner records only one aggregate depth for all three delimiter kinds, so mismatched pairs can cancel out. Measured at merge commit 46387ffee9: scan_edn("{:a [1 2)}") returns ok=True, final-depth=0, min-depth=0, top-level-forms=1, and _defect_reason returns None, even though this is not valid EDN. The unconditional gate therefore gives a false green against its stated invariant that every fixture is one well-formed EDN form.

COMPLETENESS. The self-test exercises extra, missing, and trailing delimiters, but no mismatched pair, so it cannot discriminate this failure mode. The package-reference half of the PR is complete against rf2-kgw8z: it scopes by resolved location and covers unshipped, shipped, marked, and genuinely external parent links.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / MINIMAL FIX. Keep the stdlib-only lexical design; replace aggregate-only closing with a tiny opener stack and require each closer to match the top opener. Add one compact regression such as {:a [1 2)}. No general EDN parser or broader semantic validation is needed.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9046 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9046). The audit's finding reproduced exactly at base 1b64fd6396: scan_edn('{:a [1 2)}') returned ok=True, final-depth=0 min-depth=0 top-level-forms=1, _defect_reason None. scan_edn now keeps an opener stack of (char, line) and requires each closer to match the delimiter it closes; still stdlib-only and lexical, no EDN parser. Self-test gained two regressions whose aggregate numbers are IDENTICAL to a clean file's (final-depth=0 min-depth=0 top-level-forms=1), so only an opener stack discriminates them, and both assert the REASON not just a defect count: 12/12 exit 0, and exit 1 with 4 named failures when the mismatch rule is disabled. Proved on live data rather than on a clean corpus: a cancelling mismatch planted in spec/conformance/fixtures/routing-not-found.edn gives the pre-fix scanner exit 0 (the false green) and this one exit 1 naming file, closer, opener and line. Plant restored, verified by git hash-object blob equality 7200be9e6536eb9a61dc79c34990ee08d1f28478. Corpus counts unchanged either side of the change: 247 fixtures, 0 defects, exit 0. Two notes: the gate is confirmed unconditional AND enforced (continue-on-error steps are aggregated by test.yml's 'Report every failing invariant check', which exits 1 on any outcome=='failure'), and this bead's recorded top-level-forms=1 for the pre-fix fixture measures as 2 with the committed scanner (final-depth=-1 and neg-at-line=60 match exactly; the verdict is driven by the negative depth, so nothing turns on it).

title: CLAUDE.md Build&Test states a false gate model: mkdocs --strict DOES cover spec/ (docs.yml stages it into docs/), and it catches link-resolution failures check_doc_slugs passes
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-02 by the specdrift-a worker (PR #9019) and confirmed by the mayor at source in mkdocs.yml.

WHAT CLAUDE.md SAYS, under Build & Test: that mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs is the authority on what the build cannot see from WITHIN docs_dir, and that 'docs_dir is docs, so anything outside it -- implementation/**, examples/**, tools/**, .github/**, repo-root markdown -- was never a candidate for exclusion and will never appear in that block.' A reader takes from this that spec/ is outside the strict build's reach.

WHAT IS TRUE AT TIP: the docs.yml CI step COPIES spec/ into docs/spec/, so the spec tree is STAGED INTO docs_dir and the strict build does see it. docs_dir: docs is true but not dispositive.

THE MEASUREMENT, on one tree, which is the part that makes this a defect rather than a wording quibble: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 ('no broken links') while mkdocs build --strict exit 1 on the SAME tree, naming spec/conformance/README.md's link to ../../docs/EP/EP-0012-....md as unresolvable. The link is CORRECT repo-relative -- which is what the slug gate validates and what GitHub browsing needs -- and wrong site-relative, because from staged docs/spec/conformance/ it resolves to docs/docs/EP/. mkdocs_hooks.py rewrites ../../spec/ -> ../spec/ for exactly this class but has NO ../../docs/ rule, so a page under spec/ cannot reach docs/ by a relative path at all.

THE TWO GATES ARE COMPLEMENTARY, NOT REDUNDANT, and CLAUDE.md should say so: check_doc_slugs.py validates ANCHORS (which strict grades at INFO and therefore never fails on) and repo-relative targets; mkdocs --strict validates LINK RESOLUTION INSIDE THE BUILT SITE, which the slug gate cannot see. Each is blind to the other's subject.

WHY IT MATTERS: the mayor nominated gates from this model in roughly a dozen briefs this session, telling workers editing spec/ that the strict build was not their gate. Nobody was harmed -- the doc gates ran in CI regardless -- but the nomination was wrong, and a worker acting on it would hand-verify what a gate already proved or trust a green that inspected nothing.

FIX SHAPE. Correct the Build & Test paragraph so it states: (1) docs.yml stages spec/ into docs/, so the strict build covers spec/ despite docs_dir being docs; (2) the two gates check different things -- anchors and repo-relative targets vs site-relative link resolution -- and neither substitutes for the other; (3) a page under spec/ cannot reach docs/ by a relative path, because mkdocs_hooks.py has no ../../docs/ rewrite rule. Keep the existing true parts: exclude_docs, the fence blindness both gates share, and the check_readme_links roster split.

DO NOT edit CLAUDE.md from the mayor checkout -- the commit guard refuses it. Dispatch to a worker in its own worktree.

PREMISES ARE CLAIMS: re-read mkdocs.yml, docs.yml and mkdocs_hooks.py at tip before writing, and reproduce the two-gate pairing rather than quoting this bead.
notes:
MAYOR ADDENDUM, 2026-09-03 00:5x AUSEST — A SECOND HALF OF THE GATE MODEL, MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY BY TWO WORKERS AFTER THIS BEAD WAS FILED, AND THE BEAD IS INCOMPLETE WITHOUT IT.

This bead currently says 'mkdocs --strict DOES cover spec/'. True of CI, and MISLEADING AS A LOCAL GATE INSTRUCTION — which is exactly how a worker will read it, because a gate nomination is a thing you run. A BARE LOCAL 'mkdocs build --strict' DOES NOT COVER spec/ AT ALL. The coverage comes entirely from docs.yml's staging step copying spec/ into docs/spec/ BEFORE the build; run the build without replicating that staging and it inspects none of your spec/ edits and exits 0, which is a green that proves nothing.

MEASURED TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY, BY WORKERS WHO DID NOT SHARE A CONTEXT. corpus-b (PR #9026) reported it in those words and replicated the staging so its strict run genuinely covered both edited paths. specdrift-b (PR #9025) reported 'mkdocs build --strict 0, AFTER staging spec/ -> docs/spec as docs.yml does — it built spec/View-Hierarchy-Capture.md'. Two workers, two trees, same finding, neither prompted for it.

SO THE CORRECTED PARAGRAPH NEEDS A FOURTH POINT alongside the three in FIX SHAPE: (4) the strict build reaches spec/ only through docs.yml's staging step, so CI covers it and a bare local run does not — a local run must replicate the staging (copy spec/ into docs/spec/, and migration/ into docs/migration/) or be cited as CI rather than as a local pass. Say it in the same breath as (1), because (1) alone is the sentence that misleads.

THIS ALSO CORRECTS MY OWN BRIEFS AGAIN, in the opposite direction from the first correction. I spent a dozen briefs telling workers the strict build was not their gate for spec/. Then I spent several telling them it was — without the staging caveat. The second error is smaller than the first but it is the same class: a gate nomination stated without the condition that makes it true.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #9031. CLAUDE.md's Build & Test section now states four points: (1) spec/ and migration/ ARE covered by the strict build because they are staged into docs_dir before MkDocs scans a file, so docs_dir: docs is not dispositive; (2) the staging lives in mkdocs_hooks.py's on_pre_build HOOK rather than only in docs.yml, so it runs on ANY invocation and a BARE local run covers spec/; (3) the two gates are complementary, not redundant (anchors + repo-relative targets vs site-relative link resolution); (4) a page in a spec/ SUBDIRECTORY cannot reach docs/ by a relative path.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE BEAD, both measured at source rather than quoted.

(a) THE MAYOR ADDENDUM'S POINT 4 IS FALSE AT TIP AND WAS NOT IMPLEMENTED. It says a bare local 'mkdocs build --strict' does not cover spec/ at all and that coverage comes entirely from docs.yml's staging step. mkdocs_hooks.py's on_pre_build hook stages spec/ and migration/ into docs_dir on ANY invocation -- its docstring says it exists so that any local or CI invocation auto-stages, and calls docs.yml's step 'redundant belt-and-braces'. The hook landed 2026-05-19 (b2e622c316, rf2-qw5mh). MEASURED: deleted docs/spec + docs/migration, ran a bare 'python -m mkdocs build --strict' with no staging of my own -- both recreated by the hook, 52 spec/ pages built, exit 0. Writing the addendum as stated would have put a fresh falsehood into the file this bead exists to make truthful. The carrier of that belief is scripts/test-fast-pr.sh:1310-1312 (blame 2026-08-05, three months AFTER the hook landed, so already false when written); filed as rf2-4cbx since that file is outside the PR's fence.

(b) THE BEAD'S POINT 3 IS TOO STRONG. 'A page under spec/ cannot reach docs/ by a relative path' is false for depth-1 pages: _SPEC_TO_DOCSROOT rewrites the ](../docs/ form, and 453 such links across 28 files are live and resolve. Only SUBDIRECTORY pages are stranded (no depth-2 analogue, no docs/ entry in _REWRITES, no depth dispatch in the spec/ branch). The narrower true version was written.

Also: the worked case the bead names is ALREADY FIXED -- spec/conformance/README.md's ../../docs/EP/ link was removed by f86ce0a310 (rf2-7yth0), and zero ](../../docs/ occurrences remain under spec/. So the live MECHANISM was documented, not a failure the tree no longer has.

COMPLEMENTARY-GATES PAIRING REPRODUCED on one tree with a planted link in spec/conformance/README.md: mkdocs build --strict exit 1 naming file and unresolvable target; check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 and silent. Plant restored, verified by git blob hash.

Preserved unchanged: exclude_docs authority, the docs_dir second-door reasoning, fenced-code blindness, the check_readme_links three-roster split, and mkdocs --strict not validating anchors. Section repaired in place; no heading changed.

Gates (foreground, unfiltered, captured exits, re-run on the final rebased base): check_readme_links.py --ci 0 (proven to bite -- a planted CLAUDE.md link took it to exit 1 naming CLAUDE.md:131), check_doc_slugs.py 0 (reported as NOT coverage of CLAUDE.md), check_workflow_yaml.py 0, check_workflow_job_timeouts.py 0, mkdocs --strict 0.

title: ssr-node absence witness is RED ON MAIN: slice E broke both surviving absolute-zero rows in five places, and the surface-armed job was skipped on E's own PR so nobody saw it
notes:
MEASURED 2026-09-02 BY SLICE F (rf2-8arzr.6) while discharging a red check on PR #9015. THE DEFECT IS THE TRUNK'S, NOT PR #9015's -- established by running the suite on the UNMODIFIED MERGE BASE, which is the discriminator the mayor asked for.

THE TWO RUNS, same command "node implementation/ssr-node/test/run.cjs", exit code captured on the same line as the redirect:
- PR #9015 HEAD f6cbdbd411 -> exit 1
- MERGE BASE 7f6533dd0b, detached checkout, zero dirty files, my README change confirmed ABSENT (grep count 0) -> exit 1
IDENTICAL failure sets. Both fail exactly two rows of absence.test.cjs, and every other suite passes on both (8 of 9 green; the two 30/30 and 12/12 subtest blocks pass on both). So the base is red before PR #9015 exists.

WHY IT SURFACED ONLY NOW, and why this is nobody's carelessness: the node-ssr-node job is SURFACE-ARMED off implementation/ssr-node/**. Slice E touched none of that tree, so the job was SKIPPED on PR #8997 and could not report. PR #9015 edits .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh (a one-line comment), and a change to the classifier itself conservatively arms ALL 28 surfaces -- so #9015 is simply the first branch since E to arm a job that was already failing. The mayor confirmed independently: main skipped, five sibling branches skipped, this branch failed twice.

ROW 1 -- "the refusal-code namespace appears nowhere outside the package". Four sites spell the :rf.ssr-node/ namespace outside implementation/ssr-node/, all from slice E (git blame against origin/main):
  examples/substrates/hicasso/login/host.clj:58                 ae858bf329   build-identity-mismatch, in docstring prose
  examples/substrates/hicasso/login/server.cljs:34              ae858bf329   state-key-not-allowed, in docstring prose
  implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs:252   bbc97a5678   service-saturated, in docstring prose
  implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/login_server_crossing_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:375   ae858bf329   a test ASSERTION on the literal wire string build-identity-mismatch

ROW 2 -- "no shadow-cljs build and no classpath entry reaches this package". One site:
  implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1629   ff6698f794   a ";;" COMMENT naming the implementation/ssr-node path
The assertion message reads "the package would be on a build's source path", which here is FALSE IN FACT -- it is a comment, not a :source-paths entry. This row greps the whole file rather than loader positions, so it is stricter than Reading 1 (correctly loader-position-scoped since rf2-6ovv).

THIS IS A CONTRACT JUDGEMENT, NOT A TYPO -- do not let a fix worker simply delete words. The witness was written when NOTHING outside the package could legitimately name the refusal vocabulary. The crossing now exists, and an application that HANDLES refusals has honest reasons to name them. Two coherent repairs, and choosing between them is Mike's / the mayor's call:

(a) NARROW THE WITNESS. Say the surviving absolute zero is about code that could DISPATCH on the vocabulary, and let prose and a contract-pinning test assert the wire strings. DANGER: absence.test.cjs's own header argues at length that an allowance mechanism with nothing in it is the first entry of an allowance list, and it calls this row "the absolute zero that survives, and the reason the narrowing above is safe rather than merely smaller". Narrowing it a second time needs that argument answered, not bypassed.

(b) STOP SPELLING THE VOCABULARY OUTSIDE THE PACKAGE -- which is what the programme's OWN ruling already requires of the adapter. S5: "the adapter classifies by the transport's status contract and never spells that vocabulary." The three docstrings can say "the sidecar's build-identity refusal" and so on at no cost. The TEST at :375 is the hard one: pinning the exact wire string is legitimate contract-testing, and whether that assertion moves inside the package, or reads the constant from protocol.cjs rather than restating it, is the real design question.

For ROW 2 the likely repair is different again: either reword the shadow-cljs comment so it does not spell the path, or fix the row to read loader positions the way Reading 1 does, since a comment genuinely is not a source path.

ALSO WORTH FIXING, and arguably the most valuable part: THE JOB CANNOT SEE ITS OWN BREAKAGE. The absence witness makes claims about the WHOLE repo (implementation/, examples/, tools/, scripts/, .github/) but is armed only by changes to implementation/ssr-node/**. Any change ANYWHERE ELSE can break it silently, which is exactly what happened -- three commits, five sites, zero signal. Consider arming ssr_node on the surfaces the witness actually reads, or running it unconditionally: the suite is seconds and needs no build and no node_modules, as the classifier comment beside the arm already says.

NOT FIXED ON PR #9015 DELIBERATELY: that PR is a docs/manifest slice fenced from code, the defect predates it, and the mayor's instruction was to report the merge-base result rather than grow the diff. Fold this into rf2-8arzr.5 instead if preferred -- .5 is already reopened for slice E's example-host defects, and this is more slice-E fallout.
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-02 23:34:30 AUSEST. Dispatched off MAIN (worker/ssrnode-red), not onto PR #9015's branch — the merge-base run established the defect is the trunk's, so the fix belongs on its own branch and #9015 stays untouched.

ON THE CHOICE THE BEAD PUTS TO ME: option (a), narrowing the witness, is REFUSED. Two independent reasons, and neither is taste. First, absence.test.cjs's own header argues at length that an allowance mechanism with nothing in it is the first entry of an allowance list, and calls this row 'the absolute zero that survives, and the reason the narrowing above is safe rather than merely smaller' — narrowing it a second time requires answering that argument, and nothing in the five broken sites answers it. Second, and decisive: option (b) is not a new decision at all. The programme's OWN S5 ruling already requires it of the adapter — 'the adapter classifies by the transport's status contract and never spells that vocabulary.' Applying an existing ruling to three docstrings that violate it is work under a decision already made, not a fresh call.

SO THE RULING IS (b), and the two residual questions resolve by precedent rather than by preference. The test assertion at :375 reads the constant from protocol.cjs instead of restating the literal — that keeps the contract pinned (which is legitimate and stays) while removing the second spelling, so it satisfies the witness without weakening the test. Row 2 fixes the ROW rather than the comment: a ';;' comment genuinely is not a source path, the assertion message 'the package would be on a build's source path' is false in fact, and Reading 1 was already scoped to loader positions under rf2-6ovv — so this is the same repair applied to the sibling reading, with precedent.

ARMING: also authorised, and it is the most valuable part. A witness that makes whole-repo claims while armed only by its own directory is a control that cannot catch its own case — the defect class this project keeps finding — and it is exactly why three commits and five sites produced zero signal. The suite is seconds and needs no node_modules, so it runs unconditionally. This is CI hygiene under the project's own stated defect class, not a product call; I am recording it as MY call so Mike can reverse it cheaply if he disagrees.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS: PR #9015 cannot merge until this lands. Clause 2 admits only passing or skipped checks and a FAILURE is neither, so 'the defect is the trunk's' does not make the check pass — it only says where the fix belongs. #9015 waits.
FIXED 2026-09-03 on worker/ssrnode-red, PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9024. Three commits off main, rebased onto 8931e1a1fb: 60957146f0 (Row 1), 0c1777ae63 (Row 2), bfb15b379e (arming).

ONE CORRECTION TO THE BEAD'S COUNT, and it would have left the row red if taken literally. The bead names five sites; there are EIGHT spellings across five files. scanForReferences reports only the FIRST match per file per needle, so the bead's list is one line per file rather than one line per spelling. The three the bead could not see: examples/substrates/hicasso/login/server.cljs:36, implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs:274, and the test at :391 and :394 (two more assertions beside :375). Added a small code helper that reads the constant and asserts the key exists, so a renamed constant fails loudly rather than comparing two absences.

Row 2 now reads loaderPositions the way Reading 1 does, which for .edn is the value form after each EDN_LOAD_KEY. Two guards keep the narrowing honest: the row fails closed if a config is missing or yields no loader position at all (the raw readFileSync it replaced used to fail closed by throwing), and the control now plants a real source path, a real dependency coordinate, and the comment that is neither.

ITEM 5 DONE, and it needed both halves of the one-toucher pair. implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs PINNED the exact if: line being removed, so workflow and mirror test moved in ONE commit. That file is outside the brief's stated write scope - flagged as a deviation, and unavoidable: the brief's own gate instruction requires the pair to move together. The mirror row now pins the ABSENCE of the gate, since re-adding it would restore exactly the blindness and would look like tidying. EVERY GREEN HAS A MATCHING RED. Three faults planted, each after committing, each restored and verified by comparing the git BLOB hash against the committed object rather than by reading a diff. (1) A real "ssr-node/src" entry in shadow-cljs.edn's top-level :source-paths - suite exit 1 on both the narrowed Row 2 and Reading 1, which is the proof the narrowing did not weaken the row; blob 2ca43067c327f1f4d1c4f17263ece247cb9a8cfc restored. (2) The if: re-added to node-ssr-node - mirror test exit 1 with the new message; blob 675d10f06663a477d3f365dedac54e9d7cd424a0 restored. title: spec/conformance/fixtures/routing-not-found.edn has one extra closing brace — its :trace-emissions assertions are silently discarded
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-02 22:53 AUSEST by worker/specdrift-a while building the mechanical top-level-key census for rf2-7yth0.

DEFECT. spec/conformance/fixtures/routing-not-found.edn line 46 reads

    :error  nil}}}}

and needs THREE closing braces, not four. The fourth closes :fixture/expect's own map, which pushes :trace-emissions (line 48) and its two-event vector OUT of :fixture/expect and, with the file's final }, past the end of the top-level fixture map entirely. Final bracket depth is -1.

EVIDENCE. A bracket-depth scan of all 247 fixtures (comments blanked, strings and char literals collapsed to one opaque token, # before an opening delimiter treated as a dispatch prefix) returns final depth 0 for 246 files and -1 for this one — the only outlier in the corpus. Independently, the same scan reports :trace-emissions as a DEPTH-1 (top-level) key in this file alone; in the other 120 fixtures that carry it, it sits inside :fixture/expect where spec/conformance/README.md line 63 and spec/Spec-Schemas.md line 4597 both document it.

IMPACT — SILENT, NOT LOUD. Both loaders use clojure.edn/read-string on the whole file (implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_fixtures.clj load-fixture-from-file, and the JVM runner's slurp + read-string). read-string returns the FIRST form and ignores trailing text, so the fixture loads with a :fixture/expect carrying only :final-app-db and :final-runtime-db. The two trace assertions — the :rf.error/no-such-handler emission with :kind :route that is the whole point of the fixture, and the not-found route's :on-match :rf.event/run-start — are DISCARDED. Nothing errors; the fixture reports as passing while verifying less than it claims. This is the exact failure mode rf2-7yth0 exists to prevent, found by rf2-7yth0's own instrument.

FIX. Delete one } from line 46. One character.

DO NOT LAND IT BLIND. The two assertions have never executed, so enabling them may red the conformance runner. Whoever takes this runs the JVM conformance corpus (implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj) and the CLJS corpus runner before and after, and reports both. If the assertions fail, the fixture's expectations — not the brace fix — are what needs correcting.

NO GATE COVERS THIS. The corpus has no EDN well-formedness or schema check: an unbalanced fixture is indistinguishable from a well-formed one to every gate in the tree, because read-string accepts it. Worth considering a corpus parse/balance check as a follow-on; filed separately if wanted.

HISTORY. git log for the file: adff6543f7 (rf2-3a5nk7, route slice :id to :route-id), bb1221cbec (rf2-vzld77), b8047c5c1f, cef2267c20. Not bisected — the introducing commit is unidentified.

title: bug(hicasso-ssr): whole-page server/render accepts recovered render errors
description:
## Finding

PR #8997 measured that Hicasso's pure compute-sub SSR reads emit recovered subscription failures with `:frame nil`, so the per-frame SSR error accumulator cannot see them. Its new `re-frame.hicasso.server/render-body` correctly watches the always-on error stream for the synchronous render extent and refuses the page. The sibling whole-page `re-frame.hicasso.server/render` remains unchanged: it renders markup and assembles the payload/document without the same verdict. A registered sub can therefore throw, recover to `nil`, and still produce a successful but wrong SSR page.

## Recommended action

Apply the same bounded recovered-error verdict to `render`, sharing the smallest lifecycle helper with `render-body` if that keeps the two doors aligned. Preserve the settled public spellings and response shape; this is one missing correctness check, not a renderer redesign.

## Evidence

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs`: `render-body` registers the `:errors` listener and refuses `:rf.error/ssr-render-failed`; `render` has no corresponding check.
- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/server_render_body_ssr_cljs_test.cljs` proves an ordinary throwing sub otherwise recovers and returns markup.
- The rf2-8arzr.5 implementation note explicitly records the standing implication that whole-page `server/render` has the same blindness.
- Duplicate searches for `whole-page Hicasso recovered render error`, `server/render blindness`, `pending-error-trace Hicasso`, `compute-sub-driven SSR`, and `ssr-render-failed` found no owner.
acceptance_criteria:
- A focused test renders an ordinary registered sub that throws through `server/render` and gets `:rf.error/ssr-render-failed`, while a non-throwing control returns the existing map/document shape unchanged.
- The error listener and request frame are released on success, recovered-error refusal, and a direct render throw.
- `render-body` retains the same refusal semantics without listener collisions or residue.
notes:
AUDIT REOPEN — PR #9035.

The recovered-error fix uses one fixed listener id per door, so it closes cross-door replacement but not same-door replacement. server.cljs explicitly acknowledges the remaining hole in render-body-listener-id's docstring: a door re-entering itself reuses its id, registration REPLACES the outer listener, and the inner finally unregisters it. The same mechanics apply to render-listener-id.

Concrete failure sequence: an outer render arms its atom; a view enters the same door; the inner registration replaces the outer callback; the inner finally removes that id; the outer view catches/continues, then a later subscription error recovers to nil. No listener remains to record it, so the outer render returns the same successful wrong page this bead owns. React rejecting a nested render does not make this safe: the inner finally still removes the outer listener when the view catches that direct throw.

The new test section 4 observes each door separately and proves only that their two fixed ids differ. It never nests render inside render or render-body inside render-body, so the acceptance requirement that the sibling retain refusal semantics without listener collisions is not fully met.

Minimal repair: make the registration key unique per invocation (for example, pair the door tag with the already-unique request frame id) and unregister that exact key. Add a focused same-door re-entry control that catches the inner call, emits a recovered render error afterward, and proves the outer call still fails with :rf.error/ssr-render-failed and restores the listener registry baseline. Exercise both doors compactly if the shared helper makes that cheap; do not redesign the renderer.
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-09-03 (mayor) — FENCE CLEARED; THIS IS DISPATCHABLE AND IT IS P2.

Found by the done-in-tree sweep: commit 51f6641b10 "fix(hicasso-ssr): whole-page server/render now refuses a recovered render error (rf2-ypom, rf2-ct24)" cites this bead, 204 insertions / 129 deletions in implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs. A hit is a pointer, so I confirmed in source before concluding anything: the verdict IS there — render-listener-id at :149, refuse-recovered-render-error! at :175, watch-recovered-errors! at :238, and both doors call it (render at :340/:360, render-body at :465/:481). rf2-ct24 is closed.

SO THE BEAD IS CORRECTLY STILL OPEN, and the reason is the audit remainder already on it rather than an unclosed close: the two doors use FIXED per-door listener ids, so a same-door re-entrant call (render inside render) still lets the inner finally unregister the outer listener. The acceptance criterion "render-body retains the same refusal semantics without listener collisions" is therefore not met. The repair is already specified on this bead — key the registration per invocation (pair the door tag with the request frame id, which is already unique) and unregister that exact key, plus a focused same-door re-entry control.

WHAT CHANGED THIS TICK: PR #9035 merged, so implementation/hicasso/ is no longer held by a live worker. This was fenced behind that tree; the fence is gone. Nothing else blocks it.

CLASSIFYING per loops.md section 3: NEEDS-WORK-UNDER-A-DECISION-ALREADY-MADE. There is nothing for Mike or me to rule — the mechanism, the repair and the control are all written down. It goes to the next merge+dispatch tick with a free slot.

ONE THING FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT, from the commit message rather than the bead: the fix deliberately did NOT give render a :platform :server, because that would change fx gating for every existing caller. Do not "complete" it by adding one. The per-invocation key is the whole task.
close_reason:
PR #9045. The audit remainder is fixed: the registration key is now per INVOCATION, not per door — the door tag paired with the request frame id, which is already a unique gensym — and each finally unregisters that exact key. Nesting now accumulates windows instead of replacing them. render-body-listener-id's own docstring had admitted the hole ('A door re-entering ITSELF still reuses one id, where re-registering REPLACES and the outer render loses a listener').

NO :platform :server WAS ADDED to render — the #9035 author's scoped decision, flagged on this bead, is left alone.

CONTROL PROVED TO BITE against the pre-fix fixed-key form (listener-key returning [tag], keeping the vector shape so only re-entrancy changes): ONLY the new same-door re-entry row fails, and it fails by the outer render RETURNING A DOCUMENT — 'expected: (instance? ExceptionInfo thrown) / actual: cljs.core/PersistentArrayMap', which is the silent wrong page itself. Every other row stayed green, the existing section-4 two-door rows included, so the defect is isolated precisely to same-door re-entrancy. Fixed: 1177 tests/4393 assertions, 0 failures, captured exit 0. Restored, verified by git blob hash b6364c6f66025a7958057ac119ab4057f9d20c77.

TWO MEASURED FINDINGS THE BEAD DID NOT HAVE, both now recorded beside the test because each yields a GREEN FOR THE WRONG REASON. (1) A VIEW cannot be the re-entry site: a nested render tears down the OUTER render's collector extent, so the next h/sub raises :rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render from impl.collector/read-key! before any recovered error can be emitted — the outer render then fails for an unrelated reason and the row passes against the broken form. The re-entry is driven from a BOOT EVENT instead, which reaches the same window without touching the collector. (2) A THROWING boot event is not a recovered error: rf/make-frame raises :rf.error/initial-events-step-failed and takes the render down before the verdict; the recovered emission is a second boot event dispatching a deliberately unregistered id (:rf.error/no-such-handler, a promoted recovered category).

A third trap caught itself and is worth the next author's attention: the handler was first written BELOW use-fixtures, where the reset fixture erases it. The dispatch silently became no-such-handler, the outer render still refused, and every assertion but the precondition passed — a green measuring no re-entrancy at all. The precondition caught it; the registration now sits above the fixture with a note.

title: api-manifest roster gate can be orphaned again because its tests bypass build-manifest
notes:
FOUND BY SLICE F (rf2-8arzr.6), 2026-09-02, at base de3f2a00038. The manifest gate is GREEN and still misses three public namespaces, because the gate only checks what its own hard-coded roster names.

MEASURED: `cd implementation/scripts/api-manifest && clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check` exits 0, "spec/api-manifest.edn in sync (494 public vars)". Note the manifest lives at spec/api-manifest.edn and spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn -- NOT implementation/api-manifest.edn, which is where rf2-8arzr.6 s own scope text and several briefs point. That path does not exist.

THE THREE NAMESPACES, all with genuinely public vars and ZERO ^:no-doc markers:
- re-frame.ssr.ring.node (implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/node.clj) -- default-endpoint :128, default-timeout-ms :133, default-admission-ms :138, wire-margin-ms :145, validate-opts! :193, http-timeout-ms :230, renderer :360.
- re-frame.ssr.render-state (implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/render_state.cljc) -- validate-policy-opts! :175, project :333, serialize :365, deserialize :383, restore! :400.
- re-frame.hicasso.server (implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs) -- payload-script :89, document :106, render :145, render-body :331.
grep for ssr\.ring\.node / render-state / hicasso\.server / render-body across BOTH manifest files returns zero hits each.

ROOT CAUSE: implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj:88-119 defines `jvm-namespaces` as a literal list. It names re-frame.ssr (:103) and re-frame.ssr.ring (:104) but not re-frame.ssr.ring.node and not re-frame.ssr.render-state. `all-jvm-vars` (:202-213) iterates that literal list plus `extra-vars` (:121-130, two entries). re-frame.hicasso.server is CLJS-only and would need a :cljs-only sidecar row in spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn (:63); the roster there holds only the 16 day8.re-frame2-xray.* namespaces, re-frame.adapter.reagent, re-frame.adapter.uix, re-frame.core and re-frame.hicasso.

THE BACKSTOP IS DEAD, AND ITS OWN DOCSTRING SAYS WHY THAT MATTERS. gen.clj:141-162 defines `namespaces-under`, documented as "a completeness gate that quietly finds nothing is the defect it exists to prevent". A repo-wide grep for `namespaces-under` across .clj/.cljc/.cljs returns exactly ONE hit: its own definition at gen.clj:141. It is never called. implementation/scripts/api-manifest/test/ is empty. So a new public namespace joins the tree and nothing notices -- which is exactly what happened three times over across slices A, C and E.

WHY SLICE F DID NOT FIX IT: F was fenced to docs and manifests with an explicit "nothing under implementation/*/src/, this is not a code slice" instruction. Fixing this needs (a) a gen.clj roster change, (b) tier/owner/status classification judgement for ~16 vars, (c) a :cljs-only block for re-frame.hicasso.server, and (d) wiring namespaces-under so it cannot regress. That is a code slice with real judgement in it, and it touches a REQUIRED CI check (lint.yml job `api-manifest`, declared :592, aggregated at :786).

ALSO NOTE, for whoever takes this: spec/API.md CANNOT gain var-rows for these symbols until the manifest carries them. api_md_check.clj validates that every var-row in spec/API.md resolves to a manifest entry, so adding a row first would RED the required check. Slice F therefore recorded the three namespaces as PROSE in spec/API.md s SSR namespace note and said they are not yet manifested, citing this bead. When this lands, promote that prose to rows if the tiering warrants it.

TIERING HINT (not a ruling): all nine re-frame.ssr.ring vars are :implementation tier (spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1418-1426), and docs/api/ coverage is only gated for :front-porch / :advanced / :adapter / :testing tiers (doc_api_check.clj `check-coverage!`), so classifying these as :implementation would add no docs/api obligation.
RESOLVED BY PR #9040, 2026-09-03. The premise held and the cause was more specific than 'nobody wired it'.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE: git grep -F namespaces-under over .clj/.cljc/.cljs returns exactly ONE hit, its own definition at gen.clj:141. Controlled against all-jvm-vars — a same-shaped hyphenated symbol in the same file — which returns three hits including two call sites, so the instrument works and the one-hit result is real.

ROOT CAUSE, which the bead did not have: the gate is not new. rf2-o8xev (c504e47d11) built exactly this three-way reconciliation over implementation/freehand/src, asserted FIRST in build-manifest, with a 201-line test. The freehand retirement (rf2-0yp7w.6, c951808b47) deleted the tree and — correctly, since the gate refuses to build when a source namespace is named by neither roster — retired the rosters, the assertion AND its call site together; its own commit message says they 'retire together'. What survived was namespaces-under and source-file->ns-sym: two pure helpers with no caller. THE GATE WAS ORPHANED, NOT FORGOTTEN, which is worse, because an orphan reads like a live backstop to anyone grepping for one.

WIRED, data-driven rather than hardcoded to one tree: roster-covered-roots names the trees; a namespace is accounted for by one of THREE rosters (jvm-namespaces, a sidecar :cljs-only row, or internal-namespaces); roster-drift reports :unaccounted/:stale/:contradictory; assert-roster-complete! throws naming the namespace and both remediation paths; build-manifest calls it FIRST. Enrolment intersects jvm-namespaces with what is on disk rather than filtering by prefix — the two SSR trees share the re-frame.ssr prefix across different artefacts, so a prefix filter would mis-assign both.

ENROLLED: re-frame.ssr.render-state (5 public vars) and re-frame.ssr.ring.node (7), exactly the vars and line numbers this bead names, verified at tip. Both :tier :implementation :owner 011 :status v1 — the tiering spec/API.md:328 already states. The tiering hint was VERIFIED rather than trusted: doc_api_check.clj:148 gates docs coverage on #{:front-porch :advanced :adapter :testing}, so :implementation adds no docs/api obligation. Manifest 494 -> 506.

33 SSR namespaces recorded internal; all 37 across the two trees now classified. NO ^:no-doc was added anywhere — those trees contain zero no-doc markers of any kind, before or after.

DELIBERATE RED: before, exit 0 'in sync (494 public vars)'. Planted a new public namespace re-frame.ssr.roster-probe under a covered root: exit 2, failing BY NAME with both remediation paths. Restored, verified by git blob hash 59dd06f93953ed0306ac35bfb75e7b585481a029 equal to the committed object. 14 tests pin all three drift directions, the throw, the failure MESSAGE (it must name both remediation paths, so the reader is not sent to the nearest silencer) and the LIVE trees — the last is what fails if the gate is ever orphaned again. Suite 74 -> 88 tests.

TWO OF THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISES DID NOT HOLD, corrected here: (1) 'implementation/scripts/api-manifest/test/ is empty' — it is not, six tracked test files including gen_test.clj; the new one is a seventh. (2) The spec/api-manifest.edn path correction the bead makes IS right; implementation/api-manifest.edn indeed does not exist.

NOT DONE, and each has a bead: re-frame.hicasso.server is still unscanned (rf2-3ne8) — implementation/hicasso/** was held by PR #9035 during this work, and it is CLJS-only so it needs a :cljs-only row, not a jvm-namespaces entry; the gate's third arm is already built and tested for it. spec/API.md:328's 'not yet carried by the manifest' clause goes stale on merge (rf2-63fw, post-merge only). And 243 namespaces remain under trees the gate does not cover (rf2-qvhx) — measured 276 unenrolled in total, this PR covering 33.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9040 (three-lens review).

CORRECTNESS. The landed mechanism is currently wired correctly: build-manifest calls assert-roster-complete! first, both JVM crossing namespaces resolve and contribute the expected 5 + 7 rows, and the two documentation repairs describe the live code. No runtime defect was found in the reconciliation itself.

COMPLETENESS / REGRESSION GAP. The original defect was specifically an implemented namespaces-under helper whose production call had disappeared. The new 14-test roster_completeness_test.clj suite does not call build-manifest at all. Its live-rosters-account-for-the-live-trees test says it covers the assertion build-manifest makes, but invokes roster-drift directly. The only build-manifest calls anywhere under the test tree are pre-existing duplicate-row and implementation-facade tests in gen_test.clj; they exercise later failures and cannot observe removal of the roster assertion. Thus deleting gen.clj's single line 575 call recreates the orphan while the dedicated suite remains green. The author's planted-source demonstration proves the present call works, but it is not a durable regression test.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / MINIMAL FIX. Add one behavioral integration test that redefines covered-source-namespaces to include a synthetic unaccounted namespace, invokes build-manifest with the live sidecar, and requires the named roster exception. With the production call removed, that test must fail because manifest generation succeeds. This is one compact test; no new checker or abstraction is needed.
close_reason:
PR #9045. The audit's finding held at source: build-manifest calls assert-roster-complete! first (gen.clj:575), but all 14 tests drove roster-drift/assert-roster-complete! DIRECTLY — live-rosters-account-for-the-live-trees claims to cover the build-manifest assertion while invoking roster-drift itself. The only build-manifest calls under test/ were gen_test.clj's duplicate-row and implementation-facade rows.

FIX: three tests driving the PRODUCTION entry point — the named refusal, its :unaccounted ex-data, and the ordering against the duplicate-row check (a sidecar broken both ways must surface the ROSTER refusal). Each redefines covered-source-namespaces to report one synthetic unaccounted namespace and requires build-manifest to throw. No new checker, no abstraction, as specified.

TWO-STATE PROOF: suite 88 tests/184 assertions -> 91/189, exit 0. With the line-575 call deleted, exactly the three new tests fail (captured exit 1) and THE PRE-EXISTING 88 STAY GREEN — the audit's claim measured rather than argued. Restored, verified by git blob hash 59dd06f93953ed0306ac35bfb75e7b585481a029 equal to the committed object.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair): stories.md teaches the run-variant loop with no adapter prerequisite — run-variant refuses with :rf.error/no-adapter-installed on a bare launch, and the pair skill OWNS the run side
description:
CLAIM

skills/re-frame2-pair/references/stories.md teaches the run-variant / read-failures self-healing loop and states no host prerequisite for it. Grepping that file at tip: no occurrence of 'no-adapter-installed', 'plain-atom/adapter', or any adapter/substrate prerequisite at all (the only 'substrate' hit is a snapshot-identity hash tuple).

This matters more here than in the authoring skill, because the pair skill is the OWNER of the run side. skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/story-mcp-loop.md explicitly hands off to it: 'switch to the re-frame2-pair skill (it owns run-variant / read-failures against a running app behind shadow-cljs watch) and run the self-healing loop there'.

TRUTH AT TIP

  - tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md, section 'Running a variant needs an installed adapter (rf2-c9t52)': catalogue reads work on a bare launch; RUNNING one does not. run-variant and preview-variant allocate a variant frame, and a frame takes its state substrate from an installed re-frame adapter. The server deliberately installs none — per spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md the substrate choice belongs to the app — so a consuming project installs one in the namespace its launch alias preloads ((rf/init! plain-atom/adapter), the renderer-free choice). With none installed both lifecycle tools REFUSE before any lifecycle work: isError true, :rf.error/no-adapter-installed, plus :tool and a :recovery naming the boot. They never return a :status.

title: spec(story-mcp): 002-Tool-Registry.md contradicts itself on list-substrates — its own list-substrates section still says the JVM host returns [], which its Host execution model section and the implementation both refuse
description:
CLAIM

tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md says two incompatible things about list-substrates on the JVM stdio host.

  - Section 'Host execution model' (near the top): 'list-substrates and read-a11y-violations return a machine-readable capability-unavailable error (isError true, :rf.error :rf.error/story-mcp-capability-unavailable) rather than a false-empty []/{:violations []} success. []/#{} is reserved for a REACHED provider that genuinely holds nothing — capability absence is not answered emptiness (rf2-3fc89f.21).'
  - Section '### list-substrates' (in the Docs tool catalogue, further down): 'Returns the set registered via re-frame.story/register-substrate! (Reagent canonical; UIx opt-in per host). The JVM stdio server returns [] because it has no bridge to the CLJS registry.'

TRUTH AT TIP — the implementation agrees with the FIRST, so the per-tool section is the stale one:

  - tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/dev.cljc, tool-list-substrates: '(if (cljs-resolve/substrate-provider-available?) (result/edn-result ...) (result/capability-unavailable-result {:tool "list-substrates" :capability "substrate-registry" ...}))'. Its docstring: 'this returns a machine-readable capability-unavailable error — NOT a false-empty {:substrates []} success that an agent could mistake for no substrates registered (rf2-3fc89f.21).'
  - The same file's registry descriptor for list-substrates spells the JVM case out in the tool description an agent actually reads: 'when the browser registry is UNREACHABLE (the JVM stdio server has no browser bridge) this returns a machine-readable capability-unavailable error ... NOT a false-empty {:substrates []}'.

The read-a11y-violations per-tool section was already corrected (commit 8cae7ca102, rf2-6j0yl, PR #8865's follow-through) and now states the refusal at length. The list-substrates section was not — the same commit's census reached the a11y half only.

IMPACT

This is the exact confusion rf2-3fc89f.21 closed in the runtime, reopened in the document that tools and agents are pointed at. A reader who takes the per-tool section at face value writes a client that treats [] as 'no substrates registered' and never handles isError — and the whole reason the contract refuses instead of answering [] is that EMPTY (a reached registry holding nothing) and UNAVAILABLE (the host could not look) are different states.

FIX SHAPE (one file, one paragraph)

Rewrite the '### list-substrates' section's last sentence to match the Host execution model section and the shipped handler: on the JVM stdio server it returns isError true with :rf.error/story-mcp-capability-unavailable, never an empty list; an empty :substrates vec is reserved for a REACHED registry that genuinely holds nothing; read it from a browser-local Story host. Model the wording on the read-a11y-violations section, which already says exactly this.

GATE

No gate pins this prose. scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py pins the tool-name allow-list split, not per-tool behaviour text. Verify by hand against dev.cljc's tool-list-substrates and its registry descriptor, and say so in the PR body.

ACCEPTANCE

002-Tool-Registry.md's list-substrates section names :rf.error/story-mcp-capability-unavailable and no longer says the JVM stdio server returns []; the two sections agree.

FOUND BY rf2-2ktuc's worker (PR #8999) while sourcing the skill leaf's list-substrates footnote — the leaf was written from the implementation and the Host execution model section, deliberately not from the stale per-tool section. tools/** was outside that dispatch's fence.
notes:

This is a SPEC self-contradiction in tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md — the host-execution-model section says list-substrates is capability-unavailable while its own per-tool section says the JVM host returns an empty vector, and the implementation agrees with the FIRST. Not fenced by any live worker; tools/** is nobody's surface right now. Dispatchable, and it pairs naturally with rf2-pra5 (the pair skill still has no adapter prerequisite for run-variant) since both came out of the same reading of the Story tool contract.
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 02:5x AUSEST — THE tools/ COMMIT STAYS. THE FENCE WAS MINE AND IT WAS WRONG.

WHAT HAPPENED: my specdrift-c brief said 'You may edit spec/** and nothing else', and this bead's file is tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md — under tools/, which that sentence forbids, while the same brief's item-1 section instructed the worker to correct exactly that file. There is no top-level spec/002-Tool-Registry.md. The worker did the right thing in a contradiction it did not create: it followed the explicit item instruction, ISOLATED the change in its own tip commit 82c488329d so I could drop it alone, and said so rather than quietly widening or quietly skipping.

THE RULING: KEEP IT. The bead's subject is unambiguous and tools/story-mcp/spec/ is exactly where a story-mcp spec lives; the fence sentence was a copy-paste generalisation that contradicted the item it accompanied. Nothing else in the repo makes tools/ off-limits here — no live worktree holds it, and this project already has a STANDING rule pulling the other way for the sibling tool: every dispatch touching tools/xray/ updates tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR. A tool's spec is part of that tool's surface, not a separate lane.

AND THE FIX IS SETTLED BY THE IMPLEMENTATION RATHER THAN BY EITHER SECTION'S PROSE, which is what this bead asked for: tool-list-substrates returns capability-unavailable-result when the provider is unreachable, never []. So the PER-TOOL section was the stale one and is what the worker rewrote; '## Host execution model' was already correct and is untouched. That is the right way round — a document contradicting itself has a right answer and a wrong one, and the implementation decides which, not whichever section is easier to edit.

LESSON FOR MY OWN BRIEFS, recorded here rather than only felt: a scope fence written as a blanket path glob can contradict the items it fences. When a cluster's beads name files, the fence should be derived from those files, not asserted over them — and where the two disagree, the item wins and the worker should say so, which is exactly what happened.

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/resources.md` §Named scope resolvers — `reg-resource-scope` (L104-107):

```clojure
(rf/reg-resource-scope :session
  {:inputs  {:username [:db [:auth :user :username]]}    ;; declared inputs — names ↦ source descriptors
   :resolve (fn [{:keys [username]} _ctx]
              (when username [:rf.scope/session {:username username}]))})
```

L118 then describes the `{:inputs … :resolve …}` **form** as the canonical declaration ("The `{:inputs … :resolve …}` form **declares** which app facts decide identity") and offers the whole-db bare-fn as the sugar. `resources-mutations.md`, the mutation descriptors and every `{:from-db :session}` reference in both leaves build on this registration.

title: skill(re-frame2): pattern websocket — canonical declaration does not register (4 dangling action ids → :rf.error/machine-unresolved-action) and calls an undefined current-socket? helper
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md` §Canonical declaration (L68-176) is presented as copyable code ("the canonical declaration below is the leaf-level summary" L7; "Read the source first; the declaration above is the leaf-level summary" L231). Its `:actions` map (L95-118) declares eight ids: `:record-connection-opts :rotate-cred :on-socket-lost :fail-in-flight :on-fatal-error :on-connected :flush-queue :enqueue-message`. Its states reference four more that are never declared: `:send-auth` (L147 `:authenticating {:entry :send-auth …}`), `:route-message` and `:refuse-frame` (L158-159), `:send-now` (L160). Its `:trusted-frame?` guard (L91-93) calls a bare fn `(current-socket? data source-socket-id)` that the leaf never defines — `:current-socket?` exists only as a guard KEY in the same `:guards` map (L81-87), and a guard keyword is not callable from another guard's body.

## TRUTH AT TIP

Machine registration resolves action refs eagerly: `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:1651,1812` — "`:rf.error/machine-unresolved-action` on dangling refs". So `(rf/reg-machine :ws/connection …)` as written throws at registration on `:send-auth` (the first dangling ref hit), before any state is entered. And `current-socket?` is an undeclared symbol — a CLJS compile warning / undefined var at load. The example the leaf calls ground truth already has both fixes: `examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs:110-118` defines the shared helper `from-live-socket?` and all three guards (`:current-socket?` L215, `:own-request-timeout?` L242, `:trusted-frame?` L266) call it; the four actions are defined at L355-364 (`:send-auth`), L404-409 (`:send-now`), and the receive/refuse pair (`:receive-message` L515+, `:refuse-frame` — note the example names it `:receive-message`, not `:route-message`).

While there, one drift worth lifting in the same edit: the example guards the lifecycle transitions too — `connection.cljs:42-46` "This covers the whole socket-sourced surface — the lifecycle transitions (`:ws/opened`, `:ws/auth-ok`, `:ws/auth-failed`, `:ws/closed`) as much as `:ws/received`" — whereas the leaf's `:connecting {:on {:ws/opened {:target :authenticating}}}` (L146), `:authenticating` (L148-149) and the parent `:ws/closed` (L139) carry no `:current-socket?` guard, so a straggler `:ws/closed` from a torn-down socket would bounce the NEW connection into `:reconnecting`. The leaf's feature table (L26) claims the guard "rejects events from a torn-down prior socket" generally.

Everything else in the leaf checks out against the 2026-09-01/02 spec + example commits (`2ef4147f8f`, `510e758f7e`, `f552191c3d`, `3113303ff4`, `7fb6031db7`, `cc2d3e5d71`): request-reply is taught as app-level (`:origin :ws/server` / `:ws/local`, no envelope, L200), the registration-token rule is in the anti-patterns (L225-226), three doors out of `:active` settle `:in-flight` (L52-66, L139-141), and `:cred-ref` timing matches. The token / `:next-token` mechanics live in prose only, which the "example is ground truth" framing covers.

## IMPACT

The one code block an agent copies for a WebSocket machine fails at registration with `:rf.error/machine-unresolved-action` and a compile-time undefined symbol. The agent then either invents four action bodies and a helper (plausibly wrong — `:route-message` must clear the `:in-flight` slot by REGISTRATION token, which only the example shows) or abandons the leaf for the example, which is what the leaf should have handed it in the first place.

## FIX SHAPE (one PR, `patterns/websocket.md` only)

- Add a `(defn current-socket? [data source-socket-id] …)` helper above the machine (mirroring the example's `from-live-socket?`) and have both guards call it; or rename to `from-live-socket?` to match the example verbatim.
- Add the four missing actions in compact form — `:send-auth` and `:send-now` are two lines each (lift from `connection.cljs:355-364, 404-409`); `:route-message` and `:refuse-frame` can be one-line stubs whose comment says "lifted in full from `connection.cljs` `:receive-message` / `:refuse-frame`" — or rename `:route-message` → `:receive-message` so the reader greps the right symbol.
- Guard `:ws/opened`, `:ws/auth-ok`, `:ws/auth-failed` and the parent `:ws/closed` with `{:guard :current-socket? …}` as the example does.
- Keep the leaf's length in mind (it is already 29 KB — see the patterns leaf-size bead); prefer lifting over adding prose.

## GATE

No gate compiles skill code fences — `python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` still run (both exit 0 today; both blind to this). Verify by hand: every `:action` / `:entry` id referenced in the declaration appears in `:actions`, every bare symbol the guards call is defined in the leaf, and say so in the PR body.

## ACCEPTANCE

The canonical `:ws/connection` declaration references no action id absent from its own `:actions` map and no undefined symbol; lifecycle transitions carry `:current-socket?`; the leaf's `:in-flight` / token prose is unchanged.

[stream id] …)` (line 2161), with `listener-streams #{:trace :events :errors :epoch}` (line 2100) and an unknown stream throwing `:rf.error/unknown-listener-stream` (line 2115). `rg -c 'defn register-error-listener!' core.cljc` = 0; the only `register-error-listener!` in the facade is the INTERNAL alias `error-emit/register-error-listener!` it delegates to for the `:errors` stream (line 2157). spec/API.md §Error-emit (line 575+) documents the stream-first verb; spec/009-Instrumentation.md:645 says "The listener API is **one stream-parameterized verb** across the four pure observation streams".
```clojure
:hydrating {:entry :phase-hydrate :on {:hydrate/done {:target :routing}}}
:routing   {:entry :enter-routing :on {:rf.route/resolved {:target :ready}}}
```

The prose (L242) says the machine "self-initialises and starts working at birth", and `decision-trees/pick-a-pattern.md:74` names this state set (`… → :routing → :ready`) as "the canonical state set".

## TRUTH AT TIP

No framework surface dispatches `[:app/boot [:rf.route/resolved]]` — or any `:rf.route/resolved` at all: `grep -rF ":rf.route/resolved"` over `implementation/{core,routing,machines,resources,ssr,...}/src` returns 0 hits (every other `:rf.route/*` id the leaf uses resolves: `:rf.route/handle-url-change` 99 hits, `:rf.route/navigate` 84). `spec/012-Routing.md` does not define it either; the routing runtime's post-resolution surfaces are the `:rf.route/transitioned` runtime event (31 hits, dispatched top-level, never into an app machine) and the route's `:on-match` metadata, which `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/events.cljc:14-17` describes as "fire-and-forget `:on-match` dispatch … dispatches (in order, …) on a valid plan". `spec/Pattern-Boot.md:191` carries the identical `:rf.route/resolved` line — the leaf copied the spec faithfully; the spec is what drifted from the implementation (Cardinal rule 1: implementation wins).

`:hydrate/done` (L233) is fine — app-prefixed, the app dispatches it — but nothing in the leaf says so, and an agent reads the two lines as the same kind of thing.

## IMPACT

An agent copying the canonical boot machine gets one that boots, authenticates, loads the profile, hydrates, dispatches the URL-change, and then sits in `:routing` forever: `:ready` is unreachable, `:app.boot/state` never reads `:ready`, and the app's "boot complete" gate never opens. Silent — no error, no trace, the route slice does settle — so it presents as "the app loads but the boot spinner never goes away". Under `:rf/*` reservation the app cannot "just dispatch it" either (Cardinal rule 7).

## FIX SHAPE (one PR; touches the spec too, so it is hot-zone)

Replace the fictional event with the shipped seam: the initial route's `:on-match` (fire-and-forget, dispatched on a valid plan) sends an app-prefixed event into the boot machine, e.g. route metadata `{:on-match [:app/boot [:boot/route-resolved]]}` and `:routing {:entry :enter-routing :on {:boot/route-resolved {:target :ready}}}` — with one line naming `:on-match` as the producer and one line saying `:hydrate/done` is likewise app-dispatched (by the handler that finishes hydration). Make the same substitution in `spec/Pattern-Boot.md:191` (and its `:routing` prose at L450 if it names the event). Alternative if a route-plan-independent signal is wanted: a small `reg-event` that listens for the top-level `:rf.route/transitioned` and forwards — but `:on-match` is the documented hook and needs no forwarder. Update `pick-a-pattern.md:74` only if the state names change (they need not).

## GATE

`python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (both read-only structural; neither compiles the fence). No gate compiles skill code fences — verify by hand that every `:on` key in the canonical machine is either app-prefixed and dispatched somewhere in the same snippet/prose, or a shipped `:rf.*` id present in `implementation/**`, and say so in the PR body.

## ACCEPTANCE

`git grep -n "rf.route/resolved" -- skills spec` returns nothing; the canonical boot machine's `:routing` state exits on an event the leaf itself shows being produced (route `:on-match` or an app handler); `pick-a-pattern.md` and `boot.md` still agree on the state set.

title: skill(re-frame2): pattern ssr-loaders — teaches the spec-RETIRED SSR fan-out (Pattern-SSR-Loaders retired 2026-07-04); reroute SSR data-load to Resources and fix the 14-pattern rosters
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/ssr-loaders.md` (142 lines, 11 KB) teaches Pattern-SSR-Loaders in full as a live pattern: a `:pdp/load` machine whose `:loading` state fans out three `:rf.http/managed` children via `:spawn-all` "during drain", joins on `:on-all-complete`, and is guarded by `:after {30000 :pdp/timed-out}` — "phase-level wall-clock guard — mandatory under SSR" (L67); §The deadline (L114-116): "If one fetch hangs past the deadline, `:after` exits `:loading` … no partial render"; anti-pattern L127 "**Omitting the deadline.** A loader with no `:after` can hang until the host's outer timeout fires"; L124 "each `:rf.http/managed` blocks the drain thread on the server JVM transport". Footer: "Derived from `spec/Pattern-SSR-Loaders.md` (Convention, not Spec) @ main".

Routed from `skills/re-frame2/SKILL.md:104` ("SSR parallel data fetch before render (fan-out) → `patterns/ssr-loaders.md`") and named in the pattern rosters at `SKILL.md:9`, `skills/README.md:43`, `skills/re-frame2/README.md:7`, `docs/skills/re-frame2.md:17`; cross-linked from `patterns/form-action.md:15,225` ("on GET dispatch the page loader (Pattern-SSR-Loaders)"; "the GET-path sibling") and `references/cross-cutting/ssr-authoring.md:145,158` ("parallel data fetch via `:spawn-all` before render").

## TRUTH AT TIP

`spec/Pattern-SSR-Loaders.md:1-4` — title "Pattern — SSR Loaders (RETIRED)", "**Status: RETIRED — do not implement.** This pattern was authored on two false premises and describes a render barrier that does not exist." Retired by commit `9f375386c3` (2026-07-04, rf2-exfavp). The two premises the leaf still teaches are both stated false there: (1) L12 "The managed-HTTP JVM transport is `java.net.http.HttpClient.sendAsync` … the drain reaches fixed point with the machine's children still in flight and renders the `:loading` skeleton"; (2) L13 "`:after` **no-ops under SSR** … The mandated server deadline is a dead remedy — it never fires. A machine that leans on it … simply hangs at `:loading`". L17 states the rule: "**Machines are synchronous-only under SSR.** Async machine work — a `:spawn` / `:spawn-all` whose children exist to drive async loads … is **outside the SSR allowed subset**. It is a programmer error". L19 names the pinning fixture `spec/conformance/fixtures/spawn-all-under-ssr-ring.edn` (`:rf.machine.timer/skipped-on-server`, snapshot stuck at `:loading`). §What to use instead (L21-31): route-owned blocking resources + `drain-blocking-resources!` (Spec 016 §SSR and hydration) — the one render barrier the runtime installs, with a real deadline that settles to `{:kind :rf.http/timeout :reason :ssr-blocking-timeout}`. L39: FormAction's "GET-path pointer to this pattern now resolves to resources-backed loading".

Independently of the retirement, the leaf's own snippet would not register: `:after {30000 :pdp/timed-out}` (L67) names `:pdp/timed-out` as an `:after` TARGET (a state), then treats it as an `:on` EVENT key (L71) — no state by that name exists, and `:after` values are state/transition targets (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:478-480` checks every `:after` target), so registration fails before the SSR question even arises.

The skill leaf has not been touched since the retirement (no commit on `skills/re-frame2/patterns/ssr-loaders.md` since 2026-07-04; the skill's SSR routing row, rosters and cross-links all predate it).

## IMPACT

An agent asked for "SSR that loads several pieces of data in parallel before render" is routed to a leaf whose canonical code is (a) a registration error and (b), once the target typo is fixed, exactly the out-of-subset shape the spec calls a programmer error — the server renders the `:loading` skeleton, the deadline never fires, and the request-scoped frame hangs at `:loading`. The right answer (route `:resources` with `:blocking? true`) already exists in the skill at `patterns/resources.md` §Route-driven loading but nothing routes SSR-shaped prompts there. Highest-impact item in this partition: the skill teaches the one SSR shape the spec says not to build.

## FIX SHAPE (one PR)

1. Retire `patterns/ssr-loaders.md` — either delete it and drop the leaf, or reduce it to a short stub (≤30 lines) that states the retirement, the machines-are-synchronous-only-under-SSR rule, and points at `patterns/resources.md` §Route-driven loading (`:blocking?`) + `spec/016-Resources.md` §SSR and hydration + `spec/Pattern-SSR-Loaders.md`. A stub is preferable only if external consumers link the path; otherwise delete.
2. `SKILL.md:104` — replace the row with "SSR data load before render (route-owned blocking resources) → `patterns/resources.md`" (or drop it and add "…, SSR preload" to the resources row at L91).
3. Rosters — `SKILL.md:7-9` description, `skills/README.md:41-44`, `skills/re-frame2/README.md:7,34,40,77`, `docs/skills/re-frame2.md:17`: replace `SSR-Loaders` with `ResourcesMutations`. The count stays **14** (fifteen files today, one retired); today the "14" is wrong in the other direction — `patterns/` holds 15 leaves and the rosters omit `resources-mutations.md`, which `SKILL.md:92` routes to.
4. Cross-links — `patterns/form-action.md:15` ("on GET dispatch the page loader" → "on GET the route's `:resources` plan ensures the page's blocking reads"), `:225`; `references/cross-cutting/ssr-authoring.md:145,158` → point at `patterns/resources.md` §Route-driven loading and state the sync-only rule in one sentence. (`ssr-authoring.md` is a cross-cutting leaf — sibling partition — but the link retarget belongs in this PR so no dangling link lands.)
5. `examples-map.md` needs no change (it never indexed an SSR-Loaders example; `examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/` is the resources-backed SSR example and is a candidate entry if one is wanted).

Do NOT "fix" the leaf's `:after` target and keep the pattern — the spec retired the shape, not the typo.

## GATE

`python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (covers `skills/**` and `docs/**` link targets + anchors — every retargeted link above), `python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py`, `mkdocs build --strict` for `docs/skills/re-frame2.md`. No gate reads the leaf's prose or the roster count — verify by hand (`ls skills/re-frame2/patterns | wc -l`) and say so in the PR body.

## ACCEPTANCE

`git grep -n "ssr-loaders\|SSR-Loaders" -- skills docs/skills` returns only the retirement stub (if kept) and no routing row, roster entry, or "GET-path sibling" pointer; `SKILL.md`'s pattern table routes SSR data-loading to `patterns/resources.md`; the four rosters name ResourcesMutations and agree with `ls patterns/`; `check_doc_slugs.py` exit 0.

description:

README.md:34 -- "Both routes land on the same canonical scaffold." SKILL.md:57 -- the generator is "a complete alternative the skill **runs itself** when the author asks for it". evals.json id 17 grades "the generator's actual exit code and the emitted files". The generator's own post-process prints the same next steps (tools/template/src/day8/re_frame2_template/hooks.clj:763-773).

The emitted deps.edn carries the framework coords as `{:mvn/version "{{rf2-version}}"}` (tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/deps.edn:21-23; _uix/deps.edn:21-23) with hooks.clj:616 `:rf2-version "0.0.1.alpha"`. Nothing is on Clojars (repo README.md:97-99), and the skill's own references/deps-versions.md:58 says so: "a `{:mvn/version "<VERSION>"}` framework coord fails dependency resolution before it compiles". The template release gate rewrites the emission to `:local/root` before it compiles anything (.github/workflows/template-release.yml:115-128) -- the admission that the raw emission does not resolve. tests/generator_route_test.clj:257-282 (live arm) asserts exit 0 + a non-empty manifest and stops; rf2-h4q82's close reason confirms the fix was verified at emission, never past it. So the sequence README.md:76 prescribes fails at `npx shadow-cljs watch app` with a Maven "Could not find artifact day8/re-frame2 ... 0.0.1.alpha". Second, smaller: `-Tnew` is the deps-new tool installed under the alias `new`; tools/template/README.md:75-76 states that prerequisite, the skill's README section "Running the generator pre-publish" does not, and allowed-tools grants no `clojure -Ttools *`, so on a machine without it the executor's first command fails with an unknown-tool error before emission.

After rf2-zq34m lands the set shrinks to core + adapter and the step survives unchanged. (c) evals.json id 17: add one expectation -- the skill rewrites the framework coords (pre-publish) and reports the emitted project's compile, not only the generator's exit code. Keep the post-publish route (`:mvn/version` resolves, no rewrite) as the labelled destination, matching Lock 9's branch.

GATE. `bb tests/generator_route_test.clj` resolution arm stays the CI gate; extend the opt-in live arm (RF2_SETUP_RUN_GENERATOR=1) to apply the documented rewrite and run `npm install` + `npx shadow-cljs compile app` in the emitted project, with the unrewritten emission as the red control. If that is judged too heavy for the fixture: no gate -- verify by hand and say so in the PR body.
