RULING 2026-08-29 15:29:24 AUSEST (delegated review per Mike, 2026-08-29): Option A - adopt the content rule "docstring = what it is/returns + the contract + one sentence of why + a repo-relative path into docs/design/hicasso" now, and trim each file under implementation/hicasso/src as the epic's cut task touches it; no sweep, no line cap, no new gate; the four untouched files go to one follow-up task.
BANNER STRUCK 2026-08-29 15:29:24 AUSEST: ruled.

WHAT THE ADDED REVIEW SAID AND HOW IT WAS WEIGHED. After filing, the dossier gained an independent second review ("Codex Recommendation"). It concurs with A and amends it in five ways. All five are adopted, one with a bound:
(1) A content rule, not a line-count regime: no 1:1 enforcement, no 40-line cap, no docstring-link checker, no migration machinery. Adopted. The bead's "roughly 1:1 prose:code" is the expected OUTCOME of applying the rule, not a threshold a reviewer applies.
(2) Move only durable design reasoning; DELETE duplicated, superseded and journey prose rather than preserving it ceremonially. Adopted, with a bound: the dossier's own sample found about half the essay material already on a design page, so moving it would write it twice; but the PR body still names each deleted essay and where its surviving copy is, so nothing goes silently.
(3) A source comment stays only where it protects nearby code from a plausible-but-wrong edit. The epoch-floor proof beside flush! and the rf2-6c12m.19 counter-example on commit-basis are such proofs and stay; module history, benchmark narrative and repeated cross-module explanation go. Adopted.
(4) A public docstring carries the smallest complete contract a caller needs (inputs, outputs, effects, ordering, failure behaviour) plus an example only where it removes real ambiguity; a private docstring says what the var does and the one non-obvious invariant behind its shape. Adopted - it is the dossier's rule with the public/private line made explicit.
(5) One small cleanup pass over untouched files when the wave is done. Adopted as the follow-up bead.
Its lexical scan read 75.8% prose against the dossier's 72%; the methods differ on ^{:doc} metadata and comment classification, both agree the shape is about three prose lines per line of code, and the ruling does not turn on which figure is right. The one material risk it names - over-trimming caller-facing facts into the unpublished design tree - is why the public-contract clause below is stated in full rather than left to taste.

THE RULE (binding on every PR that edits a docstring or comment under implementation/hicasso/src from now on):
1. A docstring carries: (a) what the var is or returns; (b) the contract - what it takes, returns and promises, its effects, ordering and failure behaviour, in full for a public var; for a private var, what it does plus the one non-obvious invariant behind its shape; (c) one sentence of why; (d) where the argument lives, as a repo-relative path into docs/design/hicasso (docs/design/hicasso/architecture.md, docs/design/hicasso/studio/<page>.md, docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md HD-NNN). An example only where it removes real ambiguity.
2. Links are repo-relative paths, NEVER [[wikilinks]]: 892 [[...]] exist across src/ and nothing resolves them (no codox config; scripts/check_doc_slugs.py scans docs/, spec/, skills/, migration/ and tools/*/spec only - DEFAULT_ROOTS line 94; PR #8736's body says "the doc link gates do not cover source docstrings"). The worker checks each retained path exists while editing and says so in the PR body.
3. A measured figure may stay in a docstring only with its page named beside it (e.g. "2.75 vs 1.42 us/read; docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-cold-read-mount-term.md").
4. A source comment stays only where it protects nearby code from a plausible-but-wrong edit (a local correctness proof). Module history, benchmark narrative, rejected alternatives, HD-ruling derivations and explanations of OTHER namespaces' mechanisms do not.
5. A content rule, not a number: no 40-line cap, no 1:1 enforcement, no docstring-link checker, no migration script.
6. Move vs delete: durable design reasoning with no home in docs/design/hicasso is MOVED there (see WHERE CUT MATERIAL GOES in the next note); prose a design page already carries, superseded prose and change-narration is DELETED. The PR body names, per essay, the path it moved to, or "deleted - duplicated at <path>" / "deleted - superseded".
7. Untouched: retained-inventory's :what strings and the rf2:builder-bypass-ok block (as #8736 left them); impl/slot.cljc until rf2-6c12m.1 retires the freeze gate (implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_freeze.py lines 57 and 799 treat a docstring as code - a changed word reds - for pinned rows, of which slot.cljc is the last).

MEASUREMENTS (scratchpad prose.py against implementation/hicasso/src at HEAD d5a73b28c3; a prose line is one inside a string literal directly following (ns ..., (def... name or (defmacro name, or whose first non-blank character is ';'; the scan misses ^{:doc} metadata docstrings, of which hicasso.cljc has 13, so that file reads 64% here where the bead's 87% is nearer right; everything else agrees with the bead):
- src/ (28 files): 17,085 lines = 10,254 docstring + 1,568 comment + 4,514 code; 72% prose
- impl/ (18 files): 12,474 = 7,499 + 1,285 + 3,174; 73%
- impl/codec.cljs: 3,940 = 2,111 + 570 + 1,085; 71%
- impl/collector.cljs: 2,168 = 1,315 + 298 + 477; 77%
- impl/controlled.cljs: 886 = 678 + 18 + 164; 81%
- impl/mount.cljs: 639 = 436 + 53 + 127; 79%
- impl/generation.cljs: 135 = 102 + 0 + 25; 80%
- 451 docstrings: median 10 lines; 137 at 5 lines or fewer (the bulk already meets the rule); 91 over 30 lines; 17 over 100; 4 over 200
- the 5 longest: collector ns 392 lines, controlled ns 328, intent ns 248, server ns 211, codec ns 198; then native ns 188, overlay ns 187, boundary ns 167, defhost 156, defview 153, forms ns 135, mint-view! 129
- collector.cljs opens with the 392-line ns docstring before its first :require; rstate is at line 427 and flush! at 994
- flush! (9 lines) and with-commit (4 lines) already read as the rule asks; commit-basis (58 lines at HEAD, about 80 once PR #8745 lands) and cold-read! (59 lines) do not

WHAT THE PROSE IS (descending volume): design reasoning (why the shell is 2 hooks, why the commit basis has 3 terms, why the memo is per read); measurement (probe 2.75 vs probe-fresh 1.42 us/read, "4 ms is the SHORTEST delay measured", a Chromium epoch-tie trace inside flush!); rejected alternatives (UIx's 3-hook input wrapper, a run-shared memo, useRef in the shell); cross-references (892 [[wikilinks]], HD-numbered rulings, studio pages, test namespaces).

COSTS THAT DECIDED IT: finding a function means paging past essays; editing one mechanism means re-reading essays on three (the collector, generation and intent docstrings each explain the other two); every rename is a multi-paragraph edit (#8736 needed 27 files, +577/-565, to change vocabulary alone); worker context - codec.cljs and collector.cljs together are about 6,100 lines, roughly 75,000 tokens at 12 tokens a line, before a worker opens a test; the prose half of every diff is the half reviewers cannot check mechanically; the review behind this epic judged "nothing is short enough to be seen whole, which is why the dead weight survived".

BENEFITS, FAIRLY, AND THE AI-FIRST TENSION: the whys are real and many are measured against a named test; an AI pair reading cold-read! learns in one place why the memo is per read and what changing it would cost. No repo convention sets a docstring rule (spec/Principles.md, spec/Conventions.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md); Principles.md "Low hidden context" favours discoverable reasoning, Conventions.md "annotation is not removal" says a docstring is not where a disposition lives; neither settles it. The tension with the AI-first principle is about PLACEMENT, not existence: an AI pair benefits from context it can reach by a path; it does not benefit from 1,000 lines between a function and its caller, because that is context budget spent before the caller is in view. The rule keeps the reasoning reachable - one path, one authoritative copy - and takes it out of the read path.
RULING rf2-6c12m.4, part 2 of 2 (2026-08-29 15:29:24 AUSEST) - worked examples, destinations, sequencing, acceptance.

(ns re-frame.hicasso.impl.collector
  "The collector: which boundaries a commit must re-run, how a body reaches
  subscription values, and the generation fence that keeps one render pass
  on one commit. React owns everything else about a boundary.

  Owns the render context, the cell table, the commit window (`with-commit`,
  `flush!`), the two read tiers, the read-set entry cache, and the shell and
  mint doors. Those form one dependency cycle, which is why they share a
  namespace; `generation`, `frames`, `roots`, `evidence` and `inventory`
  each hold a one-directional edge out of it.

(defn commit-basis
  "The number a staged read is judged against: this runtime's flush
  generation + the frame's install epoch (`frame/frame-commit-epoch`) +
  the registry epoch. Monotone within a frame incarnation; install-counting,
  so a value-equal install still advances it (one redundant re-render at
  worst, never a missed one). Pure; allocates nothing.

  Three terms because each sees a movement the other two cannot: the
  generation moves only through a committed cell's watch, the install
  epoch is a plain counter, and only the registry term carries a `reg-sub`
  landing in the render->commit gap. The generation term is load-bearing
  across a same-id reincarnation, where the frame term restarts and can
  tie: any other cell the frame holds is rewired by microtask and that
  flush bumps the generation (staged_reincarnation_basis_cljs_test); a
  frame holding no other cell ties either way, which is Spec 006
  invariant 5's `:node-key` axis, not this number's. Full argument:
  docs/design/hicasso/architecture.md, section The commit basis."
  [frame-kw]
  (+ @!generation (frame/frame-commit-epoch frame-kw) @!registry-epoch))

(defn- cold-read!
  "Read a key no committed cell answers for. Reuses a live sub-cache
  reaction when one exists; otherwise computes pure against one
  frame-state snapshot per body run (the probe on `rstate`), memoised per
  run so a repeated key is a `find`; falls back to `subscribe-once` when
  the frame is missing or destroyed. Runs inside
  `call-with-frame-resolution` so a `reg-sub` from earlier in the tick is
  visible. The memo is per read, not run-shared, because the shared one
  cost more than it saved on the acceptance shape (2.75 vs 1.42 us/read;
  docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-cold-read-mount-term.md)."

title: RULING: the native tier is a second authoring language with one consumer - shrink it to the hooks
description:
native.cljc is 1,116 lines (71% prose), 14 public names (10 surface + 4 public-by-expansion, native.cljc:161-185), 7 refusal ids, its own {:server} roster on defcomponent that duplicates defhost (native.cljc:391-401 says so), n/memo and n/lazy wrappers whose sole job is carrying a marker, a 4-production props grammar and the n/props marker. Consumer-shaped usage across examples/, tools/*/testbeds and the 8 example apps under hicasso/test/.../examples is ONE mention - the ledger docstring saying it was not needed (ledger/views.cljs:86). The guide concedes rung 4 may be a defui and that n/use-sub / n/use-frame work inside UIx (docs/core/hicasso/10-native-tier.md:260-265).

RECOMMENDATION: keep n/use-sub and n/use-frame (the only things React cannot supply) and the two facade bridges; let islands be UIx or raw React mounted through defhost / [:>]. If rung 3 (a defview returning native elements, measured 38% on one example) is judged worth keeping, keep $ alone and drop defcomponent / memo / lazy / props and their 5 grammar refusals (or collapse to 2). Effort: large. Also touches: HMR contract for native, bundle-isolation sentinel for the tier, three_way_parity suites (keep the parity FLOOR test as a perf guard regardless).

HOW THIS WAS DECIDED. The dossier (ai/decisions/rf2-6c12m.3.native-tier.md, deleted after this note was verified) recommended A. A second reviewer appended a "Codex Recommendation" that also chose A and set a proportionate implementation bar. No text in the file argued for B, C or D. The delegate re-verified the evidence at tip on 2026-08-29 and adopted A WITH the Codex conditions: (1) reduce the namespace's public census to the two hooks, everything supporting them private; (2) re-spell the HMR, imperative-host and Xray fixtures in ordinary React or UIx, keeping focused proof that the hooks preserve frame isolation, subscription lifecycle, teardown and Xray visibility; (3) keep one generic direct-React-return test and a raw-React parity floor; commission NO new benchmark run to justify the deletion; retire or clearly qualify the old worked number; (4) keep the reachability rule that ordinary Hicasso does not pull in the hooks namespace; delete the grammar, marker, refusal, ledger and guide machinery that has no subject; (5) replace chapter 10 with a short islands page showing raw React/UIx through defhost and those components using n/use-sub / n/use-frame when they need Hicasso state. Posture: pre-alpha, no deprecation programme, no compatibility shim, trust the programmer - a programmer who crosses into React writes React. If real application work later shows repeated friction, add the smallest helper proven by that code then.

WHY A.
1. Only the two hooks do something React cannot. use-sub hands useSyncExternalStore the same subscribe/getSnapshot a boundary reading that key gets (collector/hook-entry), so an island's read builds the same cell, joins the same reader membership and residue census, is woken by the same commit, and is named by the same re-frame.hicasso.tool rosters Xray consumes. use-frame returns collector/frame-row's incarnation-pinned ops map: destroy :watchlist and recreate it under the same id and a callback still holding the predecessor's ops is refused by core's :rf.error/frame-destroyed fence rather than writing to whoever owns the address now; a memo keyed on the frame keyword would pass every stability test and fail exactly that one (native.cljc:792-879). Both resolve the frame through collector/resolve-frame! - one React context, no spelling reaches a sibling frame. Everything else duplicates UIx, raw React or h/defhost: defcomponent's {:server} roster is a copy of defhost's and the code says so ("A second declaration grammar for it would buy nothing", native.cljc:391-401); memo and lazy are react/memo and react/lazy carrying a marker; $ is a second element grammar with 5 refusals of its own; the 7 remaining names (el, props*, declared-server, component, marker, tier-sentinel, prop-slots) are public only because a macro expansion or a parity fixture calls them (native.cljc:161-185).
2. The second language has one non-test consumer. Consumer-shaped usage across examples/, testbeds/, tools/*/testbeds and the 8 example apps under implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples: zero calls of n/$, n/defcomponent, n/memo, n/lazy or n/props. The one mention is examples/ledger/views.cljs:86-88 - "No n/defcomponent, no ref, no effect, no imperative handle, no memo hint and no second root. The application's whole native-tier surface is h/defhost and h/event" - from the app built to need an imperative SDK. Real consumers: the HMR testbed island (holds no subscription by design), one Xray test, and the reagent-migration skill's prose.
3. The guide already concedes the design. docs/core/hicasso/10-native-tier.md:260-265: a rung-3 defview may return a UIx element, a rung-4 island may be a defui, and n/use-sub / n/use-frame work inside UIx components. Option A makes the concession the design.
4. Performance does not need n/$. MEASUREMENT FACT: chapter 10 line 81 claims "moved a 21 ms p95 tick to 13 ms: 38% and 8 ms recovered" and NO measurement record for that figure exists anywhere under docs/design/hicasso. The repository's actual rung-3 measurement is implementation/hicasso/spec/budgets.md row S8 (rf2-5yn9, re-based 2026-08-18 under rf2-6zc2q; lines 397 and 1596): 0.8081x, 19.2% of mount time recovered, per-round escapes [0.6863-0.9302], observed range 7.0%-31.4% over runs A, B, C pooled across fifteen rounds on a 200-boundary mount, status UNRESOLVED because the range crosses the 20% line. The guide's own keep-rule (10:22-25) is at least 20%, or at least 2 ms at p95, or enough to move a user-visible budget from fail to pass - otherwise remove it. So by the guide's own rule the escape has not earned its place. And S8 measures skipping hiccup interpretation once a React element already exists; a raw React or UIx element returned from a defview takes that same path, so the measured benefit survives without n/$. WHICHEVER option had been chosen, the 38% figure had to be corrected to S8's numbers; under A it is retired with the chapter, and S8 stays as the record of the direct-return escape reworded from n/$ to "a defview returning a React element".
5. What keeping it costs: ~900 of native.cljc's 1,116 lines (71% prose) beyond the hooks, 12 of 14 public names, 7 refusal ids, 10 test suites (113 deftests, 6,311 lines), rows in 6 gates and ledgers, a 345-line chapter plus 114 mentions across 12 other guide pages by the dossier's grep (a broader grep that also matches the phrase "native tier" reaches 17 pages: glossary 33, api-reference 26, troubleshooting 10, 21-code-splitting 9, 18-ssr 7, escape-ladder 7), a 7-row troubleshooting table, and a second grammar with its own rules for every reader.

REJECTED.
Option B (keep n/$ and n/props for rung 3 only; drop defcomponent/memo/lazy/marker; collapse 5 grammar refusals to 2): keeps a second element grammar nobody has written outside tests, on a measurement below the guide's own threshold; would need S8 re-taken and cleared first, and the Codex bar rightly refuses to commission a benchmark to justify an API.
Option C (keep the whole tier): two authoring languages, two :server declaration sites, recurring cost on every refusal, ledger and guide change, for one non-test consumer.
Option D (delete the hooks too): WRONG. The hooks share Hicasso's cell table, census and Xray rosters and the frame row is incarnation-pinned (point 1). The UIx adapter's own use-subscribe / use-frame (implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:140-162) run on the adapter spine, not Hicasso's cell table, and Hicasso may not depend on UIx (docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/design-laws.md, Native boundary clause 1: "UIx is a comparator and optional toolkit, never a Hicasso dependency"). Deleting the hooks forks the read into a second reactive spine or pushes islands to a global rf/capture-frame that loses incarnation pinning.

title: RULING: defhost :callbacks roster - infer the contract from the prop position instead of declaring it
description:
defhost makes the consumer declare :callbacks {:on-close :event, :render-row :render, :x :handler} and learn a 6-row table for what one h/event means by position (docs/core/hicasso/03-events-as-data.md:113-120). But impl/intent.cljs:1200-1210 ALREADY selects the contract by position for every native tag (on* = event, else render, :ref excluded), and lower-declared-prop (intent.cljs:1283-1296) shows :handler has no positive behaviour: h/event -> identity, plain fn -> identity, vector -> refused - and a vector at an undeclared on* host prop is already refused (codec.cljs:2884). :handler appears in zero consumer-shaped code (only host_hatch and intent_cljs_test). The one consumer-shaped declaration in the repo (test/.../examples/ledger/views.cljs:14-16) declares two entries. 11 refusal ids exist solely to validate the defhost declaration map (codec.cljs:1538-2053), ~15 to police this grammar overall. The stated reason for the roster (value-first foreign callbacks) is already caught at runtime by intent-needs-the-event (intent.cljs:107,726).

RECOMMENDATION: infer on* -> event, everything else -> render, exactly as native tags do; keep :slots (genuinely uninferable - a vector is legal data). Delete :callbacks, :handler and ~8 ids (unknown-callback-contract, host-structural-callback, host-callback-slot-collision, intent-at-a-non-event-contract, host-undeclared-callback, host-unclaimed-callback, plus simpler macro-tail guards). Effort: medium. If ruled yes, dispatch with the refusal-shrink task.
notes:
*** AWAITING MIKE - NOT DISPATCHABLE. *** Banner added 2026-08-29 14:38 AUSEST by the merge+dispatch tick (mayor session re-frame2-9a). Type is decision; the epic rf2-6c12m names it as one of five rulings that gate tasks. WHOEVER RULES STRIKES THIS BANNER IN THE SAME ACT.
2026-08-29 14:40 AUSEST - Decision dossier for Mike at ai/decisions/rf2-6c12m.2.defhost-callbacks-roster.md (local-only, untracked): problem, options with consequences, recommendation, how to record the ruling.
RULING 2026-08-29 15:29:54 AUSEST (delegated review per Mike, 2026-08-29): Option B, 2 values - infer the callback contract from the prop position exactly as native tags already do (on* -> :event, anything else walked -> :render, :ref -> React's); keep :callbacks ONLY as an optional override taking :event or :render; delete :handler; keep :slots.
BANNER STRUCK 2026-08-29 15:29:54 AUSEST: ruled.

WHY B (decisive facts)
- The runtime already infers for every native tag: position-contract (impl/intent.cljs:1200-1210) = ref? -> :ref, event-prop? -> :event, else :render; event-prop? is one regex ^on-[a-z]|^on[A-Z] (intent.cljs:916-926). lower-declared-prop (intent.cljs:1255-1302) routes declared :event/:render to the SAME two wrappers the native walk uses (event-callback, render-callback).
- Every declaration in the repo and the guide infers identically. The only consumer-shaped one (test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/ledger/views.cljs:14-16, :137-138: {:render-row :render :on-window :event}) is exactly what inference gives. Guide declarations :on-change/:on-close/:on-pick/:on-value-change -> event and :render-row/:item-content -> render also match; the only two that do not are the two the guide invents to illustrate the roster (:on-imperative :handler, :on-render-row :render).
- :handler has no behaviour: h/event -> identity, plain fn -> identity, vector/map -> refused. A plain function already crosses untouched at every position (intent.cljs:1220-1228; codec.cljs:2865, host-prop-value's fn? arm). Zero consumer-shaped uses, tests only. Its own docstring says a plain fn is the handler contract (intent.cljs:1279-1281). It adds vocabulary, not capability.
- The stated reason for "never infer" (a value-first foreign callback such as onChange(date), where [:x ::h/value] would read date.target) is caught at runtime regardless of any declaration: event-arg! raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-needs-the-event naming the position (intent.cljs:95-117, :710-738). The declaration never prevented the mistake; the runtime check does.
- [:>] gets inference for free: raw-element walks props through host-entry against an EMPTY declared roster (codec.cljs:3465), so today [:> X {:on-pick (h/event ...)}] is refused as unclaimed and [:> X {:on-pick [:x/y]}] as undeclared. Under B host-entry's :else arm infers, so [:>] and defhost share one classifier (the second reviewer's point).
- Both the dossier author and the second reviewer (Codex) recommend B with 2 values. The added review is a clear recommendation, not a partial opinion; I weighed it against the code and found nothing against it. It adds three implementation constraints adopted here: reuse the native classifier (no second one), apply the same default in defhost and the [:>] host walk, and a proportionate test bar (below).

WHY NOT A (infer, delete :callbacks): one paragraph smaller, but no first-class spelling for an on*-named prop whose RETURN the library consumes and which is interactive. Fluent UI DetailsList onRenderItem/onRenderCell/onRenderHeader return UI; Ant Design Table onFilter returns a boolean, onRow/onCell/onHeaderRow return props maps. The event wrapper always returns nil (intent.cljs:551-596), so an h/event there blanks the list or vetoes every row, silently. A plain function is the escape and suffices for predicates and props-returning callbacks, but a plain function gets no frame/dispatch rebinding (render-callback, intent.cljs:598-704), so an intent inside a row it returns raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary at click - loud, not silent, but under A the only fix is an adapter component. Under B it is one line, {:callbacks {:on-render-item :render}}, and the render wrapper supplies the owning frame. The override costs one taught paragraph and one 2-value check that folds into .11's single bad-declaration id. The roster never prevented this hard case either: declaring such a prop :event blanks it the same way (skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md:160 already warns).

WHY NOT C (keep as is): the consumer keeps declaring what the library already knows; the guide keeps a rule that contradicts its own native-tag behaviour; 4 ids, 1 half-id, 1 roster and ~560 lines of validation and commentary police a grammar with no consumer.

THE RULE AFTER B (position table 6 rows -> 4)
1. on*-spelled prop (native tag, defhost, [:>]) -> :event: h/event takes the event wrapper; an intent vector or key-map lowers as at a native event position; a plain fn crosses untouched.
2. Any other walked prop -> :render: h/event takes the render wrapper (frame + dispatch rebound); a vector or map crosses AS DATA via host-prop-value/clj->js exactly as at a native tag (nobody writes {:on-render-item [:x/y]} on purpose; refusing it is a guard a trusted programmer never trips). Plain fn untouched.
3. Declared :slots position -> markup (as-element); an h/event there stays refused (a function as a ReactNode renders nothing, silently) - this is the surviving half of host-unclaimed-callback.
4. :ref -> React's (check-ref!).
Override: {:callbacks {<prop> :event|:render}}, written only where inference is wrong; a declared contract outranks the spelling. Any other value is a bad declaration.

BEFORE / AFTER
;; today
(h/defhost date-picker DatePicker {:callbacks {:on-change :event}})
(h/defhost rows vendor/virtual-rows {:callbacks {:render-row :render :on-window :event}})
(h/defhost picker Widget {:callbacks {:on-pick :event :on-imperative :handler :on-render-row :render}})
;; after
(h/defhost date-picker DatePicker)
(h/defhost rows vendor/virtual-rows)
(h/defhost fluent-list FluentList {:callbacks {:on-render-item :render}})   ; the hard case: on*-named render prop
;; call sites unchanged
[date-picker {:selected (h/sub [:task/due-date]) :on-change (h/event [date _] [:task/set-due date])}]
[:> DatePicker {:on-change (h/event [date _] [:task/set-due date])}]   ; legal now too

REFUSAL IDS
Retired outright (4):
- :rf.error/hicasso-host-undeclared-callback - codec.cljs:2870-2897 refuse-undeclared-host-event!, emitted :2884, call site :3093-3094.
- :rf.error/hicasso-intent-at-a-non-event-contract - intent.cljs:1230-1253 refuse-dispatching-carrier!, emitted :1237, arms :1291 and :1295.
- :rf.error/hicasso-host-structural-callback - codec.cljs:1849 (.11 already lists it for deletion).
- :rf.error/hicasso-host-callback-slot-collision - codec.cljs:1976.
Narrowed (1): :rf.error/hicasso-host-unclaimed-callback - codec.cljs:2899-2954, emitted :2937 - keeps ONLY the node-slot? true branch (h/event at a declared :slots position, call site :3079-3080); the "nothing claims it" false branch (:3105-3106) goes, because inference now claims every position.
Folded (1): :rf.error/hicasso-unknown-callback-contract - codec.cljs:1947-1948 at mint, intent.cljs:1297 in lower-declared-prop - now a 2-value check; fold into the single hicasso-bad-host-declaration id .11 proposes (the :reason string names the fault). If this lands before .11's collapse, keep it as the 2-value check and let .11 fold it.
Kept, reworded (4): host-bad-options, host-unknown-option, host-bad-slots, host-extra-form lose their ":handler" / "never inferred" wording.
Code that goes: the callback-contracts roster (codec.cljs:1328); the :callbacks arms of mint-host!'s declaration block (codec.cljs:1538-2053); refuse-undeclared-host-event!; the false branch of refuse-unclaimed-host-callback!; refuse-dispatching-carrier!; the :handler arm of lower-declared-prop (keep :event and :render arms; a non-callback value at :render routes through host-prop-value so a vector crosses as data); and the HD-011/HD-024 commentary at codec.cljs:1220-1234, intent.cljs:1230-1302 and hicasso.cljc:297-370 (~500 lines; rewrite as a few sentences stating the inferred rule and the override - .4 is the prose-ratio ruling, do not fight it).
host-entry (codec.cljs:3040-3111): the :else arm becomes event? -> intent/lower-prop (vector, map and h/event lowered, else untouched); non-event h/event -> render-callback; then host-prop-value. Reuse position-contract / lower-prop; do NOT add a second classifier, a warning, or a compatibility layer. Declared :slots and :ref keep precedence over inference; a :callbacks override keeps precedence over the spelling.
Every retired id must go from ALL gate-bound places (per .20's landing): src; spec/009-Instrumentation.md catalogue rows :2518-2556 (hot-zone, one-toucher); implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md register rows :108, :112, :113, :114, :116, :151; docs/core/hicasso/troubleshooting.md sections :251-280 and :436-473. description:

title: hic: frameless overlay with :on-dismiss reaches the declared-unreachable two-owners state — needs a ruling
description: Found by rf2-dr90's coverage audit; verified at source. impl/overlay.cljs's dismissal-handler returns nil when there is no frame dispatch (~:655-659), but popover-dismissal-attrs (~:746-751) reads only the props — so a popover mounted with NO frame above it and :on-dismiss written still renders popover="auto" with no handler: the platform light-dismisses it, no intent lands, and app-db keeps open? true — exactly the open-flag/second-owner desync overlay.cljs's docstring (~:80-83) declares unreachable. Same shape on the modal (closedby="closerequest", no cancel handler). The presence module ruled its frameless case explicitly (legal until a child writes an intent, presence_react ~:50-57, tested at presence_intent ~:334-365); overlay has no equivalent ruling or witness. Needs Mike's ruling on direction before any test or fix: refuse a frameless overlay that carries :on-dismiss, or degrade the attrs to manual/none when dispatch is nil. Then the witness follows the ruling.

BANNER STRUCK 2026-08-29 15:31:44 AUSEST: ruled; dispatchable.

WHY D, AND HOW THE REVIEWS WERE WEIGHED. The dossier (ai/decisions/rf2-4e5b.frameless-overlay-on-dismiss.md, now deleted; this note carries everything it held) recommended D. A second review appended to it ("Codex Recommendation") independently chose D on the same grounds and added implementation bounds (small guard, no id, no dispatch threading through the attrs fns, no grammar broadening, amend the one Spec 009 row, no compat layer). The two agreed, so this is adoption of a concurring recommendation rather than a tie-break. Decisive facts: (1) :on-dismiss IS an intent - the public docstring says so (overlay.cljs:79-80 "routed back as an ordinary intent - which is what :on-dismiss is") - and every other intent position in hicasso that cannot land REFUSES (require-dispatch, intent.cljs:397-402; event-callback, intent.cljs:586-595); this is the one silent path in the module. (2) Presence and the error boundary already ruled the identical frameless case exactly this way (presence_react.cljs:51-56, boundary.cljs:153-158). (3) rf2-6c12m.11 is cutting the refusal roster from 59 to ~30; a new id (option A) would add vocabulary carrying no information the existing id does not. (4) Degrading to manual/none (option B) silently ignores a line the programmer wrote - "trust the programmer" means report the impossibility, not hide it. (5) Admitting the state (option C) documents a desync and would have the witness pin a defect as a feature. One alternative both reviews left implicit is closed here: routing :on-dismiss through intent/lower-prop (intent.cljs:1212-1228) so the emitter stays in impl.intent was considered and rejected - it changes :on-dismiss's dispatch mechanics (intent-handler's per-key policy, key-maps, placeholders), which is the grammar broadening the Codex review rules out, and the popover would still need its beforetoggle direction filter wrapped around the result. Direct guard it is.

THE MECHANISM (all paths implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/ unless stated).
- impl/overlay.cljs:687-688: body resolves the frame via adapter-context/context-value->current-frame on react/useContext frame-context; with no provider above, the reader answers nil by design (core/src/re_frame/adapter/context.cljs:330).
- :702: dispatch (when frame-kw (collector/frame-dispatch frame-kw)) - nil when frameless.
- :655-656: dismissal-handler [dispatch on-dismiss closed-only?] is (when (and dispatch on-dismiss) (fn ...)) - returns nil when dispatch is nil, silently.
- :741-744 modal-dismissal-attrs and :750-751 popover-dismissal-attrs read PROPS ONLY: :on-dismiss present => closedby="closerequest" (or "any" with :light-dismiss?) / popover="auto". So the element tells the platform "you may dismiss me" while nothing listens.
- :669 own-keys strips :on-dismiss from the props before element-attrs/lowering, and :706 hands it to dismissal-handler directly, so it BYPASSES intent/with-frame (:726) and require-dispatch (intent.cljs:397-402) - the one intent position in the module that skips the loud path. Children's intents inside the overlay do take the loud path.
- :604-631 make-cell: show! (showPopover/showModal) runs ONLY from the once-attached stable ref callback; body (:681-729) has no effect. A re-render therefore does NOT re-show a platform-closed element.

USER-VISIBLE SEQUENCE (popover, :open? true, :on-dismiss written, no frame): 1. mounts, ref callback calls showPopover once on attach, element in the top layer with popover="auto". 2. user clicks outside; platform fires beforetoggle/toggle, nothing listens, panel hides. 3. the flag driving :open? is still true - no intent ran. 4. a re-render does not re-show it (stable ref, no effect). 5. to reopen the author must flip the flag false (element unmounts; hide! is a no-op) then true again - two actions for one open, and any aria-expanded mirrored from the flag lies in between. Modal: same shape with closedby="closerequest" - Escape closes the dialog, no cancel handler runs, flag stays true. This is exactly the two-owners state overlay.cljs:76-83 declares unreachable.

WHEN FRAMELESS ACTUALLY HAPPENS. Every shipped door installs a frame: h/mount! takes {:frame ::frame} (impl/mount.cljs:141); server/render allocates a per-request frame (server.cljs:333); Story wraps every variant in rf/frame-provider (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/canvas.cljs:622, 673); a UIx/Reagent island under frame-provider or frame-root reads the same context object (context.cljs:38-40, impl/mount.cljs:33-36). An overlay under an h/defview never reaches this code because the boundary shell refuses :rf.error/no-frame-context first (impl/collector.cljs:1753-1760). So the case is reached only when the overlay is the OUTERMOST hicasso component in a React root nobody wrapped: a test mounting it alone (presence's suite does this via mount/root! with adapter-context/no-provider-sentinel), or a consumer's hand-built root / unwrapped island. Rare, mostly test-time - and it is the case where :open? cannot be an h/sub and :on-dismiss can never land, i.e. an authoring error worth naming. A frameless overlay WITHOUT :on-dismiss is a legitimate case (static manual popover, non-dismissible dialog) and stays legal.

PRECEDENT. presence_react.cljs:51-56: "No frame in scope is not an error here. Presence reads nothing, so a tray mounted outside a frame is legal until one of its children writes an intent - at which point the existing loud error fires and names the intent, which is better attribution than a generic no-frame-context throw from the tray." boundary.cljs:153-158 carries the same paragraph. Witness: test/re_frame/hicasso/presence_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs:327-365 - frameless-root! (mount/root! (mount/fresh-container!) adapter-context/no-provider-sentinel hiccup); testing block 1: quiet frameless tray renders; block 2: a child with :on-click [...] under a boundary with :on-error raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary and (:intent (ex-data e)) equals the vector. overlay_dom_cljs_test.cljs has no frameless row (its manual witness is :652-655, :680-694).

OPTIONS REJECTED. A (new id e.g. :rf.error/hicasso-overlay-dismiss-without-frame): same trigger as D, but mints an overlay-specific id for the generic outside-boundary condition, costs rows in complaints.md (:129 area), the naming ledger, Spec 009 and check_complaint_catalogue.py, against rf2-6c12m.11's direction. B (thread dispatch into the two attrs fns so nil dispatch yields manual/none): one owner, docstring stays true, but the :on-dismiss the author wrote is silently dead - the only swallowed intent in hicasso. C (amend the docstring to say two-owners holds only inside a frame): honest but documents a desync; witness would pin a defect.

THE CHANGE (one guard, shared path, covers modal AND popover).
1. impl/overlay.cljs dismissal-handler (:633-659), called once from body at :706 for both heads while :open? is true: when on-dismiss is non-nil and dispatch is nil, (fail! :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary 're-frame.hicasso.impl.overlay/dismissal-handler "<reason>" :lower-intents-inside-a-boundary-render {:intent on-dismiss}) instead of returning nil. Keep the existing (fn [e] ...) branch untouched. Reason text names what happened and the direct recovery: the overlay carries :on-dismiss <intent> but no frame is in scope, so the platform would be told it may dismiss while nothing could route the dismissal; mount the overlay under a frame (h/mount!, rf/frame-provider, frame-root) or drop :on-dismiss if it should be non-dismissable. fail! is already referred at :108 and the anchor refusal at :218 shows the local call shape; write to fail!'s signature AT TIP (rf2-6c12m.5 may drop :recovery/:where - do not pre-empt it). Reuse the recovery keyword above so R10 of check_complaint_catalogue.py stays green without a new row. Placing the guard in body immediately after :702 is an acceptable equivalent; ONE site only, no dispatch threading through the attrs fns, no new abstraction.
2. Docstring: overlay.cljs:76-83 posture paragraph gains one paragraph modelled on presence_react.cljs:51-56 - no frame in scope is not an error for an overlay; without :on-dismiss it is manual/none and single-owner; WITH :on-dismiss and no frame it refuses at render with the existing intent-outside-boundary, naming the intent, so the two-owners state stays unreachable outside a frame too. Also correct impl/overlay.cljs dismissal-handler's first line ("or nil when there is nothing to route" -> nil when there is no :on-dismiss; the loud refusal when there is one and no frame).
3. docs/core/hicasso/13-overlays-and-focus.md: one Troubleshooting row (table at :344ff): Symptom - an open overlay raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary naming the :on-dismiss intent | Cause - it has :on-dismiss but no frame above it (rendered outside h/mount!, frame-provider, frame-root or Story) | Fix - mount it under a frame, or drop :on-dismiss if it must not be dismissable. Optionally one sentence at the :on-dismiss contract (:69-71). Verify the table's column count by hand and say so in the PR body.

Emitted by re-frame.hicasso.impl.intent" with :where 're-frame.hicasso.impl.intent/lower-prop on all three. Add arm (d): an open overlay carrying :on-dismiss with no frame dispatch, refused at render by re-frame.hicasso.impl.overlay, :where the overlay fn, extra :intent; and name the second emitter namespace. implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md:118 needs no change (its cause text already covers it; adding ch13 to its chapter cites is optional). title: hic: review hicasso test coverage and quality — audit the suite against the surfaces, land the clear improvements, file the rest
description:
REQUESTED BY MIKE 2026-08-29 09:57 AUSEST, in chat, verbatim ask: "do a review of hicasso, improving test coverage and quality."

WHAT THIS IS. A review of implementation/hicasso/'s test suite against its actual surfaces, with two deliverables: (1) a findings review of where coverage is thin, weak, or low-quality relative to what the code does; (2) landed improvements for the clear cases, and follow-on beads (filed one at a time, ids appended to this bead's notes) for anything larger, riskier, or needing a ruling.

WHERE TO LOOK. Source surfaces: implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/ — evidence.cljs, forms.cljs, motion.cljs, native.cljc, overlay.cljs, server.cljs, substrate.cljs, tool.cljs, and the impl/ tree. Existing tests: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/ (40+ files: *_cljs_test, *_dom_cljs_test, *_ssr_* variants), plus test_kit/ and testbed/. Map each source module to the tests that exercise it and find the gaps — surfaces with no adversarial or negative case, behaviours only exercised through the happy path, error/complaint shapes never asserted, SSR/DOM parity holes.

QUALITY BAR, from the method and the stance. A coverage or rigour pass must add at least one adversarial or negative case per surface it strengthens — assertion-count growth alone only exercises the happy path. Quality also means the tests themselves: actionable failure output, no tautological assertions, no tests that pin incidental strings where they should pin behaviour (this repo has a measured history of hollow phrase-matcher guards — see rf2-2iaph/rf2-oflj7 for the shape; do NOT touch those files, see fences). Prefer strengthening a weak existing test over adding a near-duplicate.

GATES. npm run test:cljs (substrate contract), test:hicasso-compile, test:hicasso-invariants, test:hicasso-lint, test:hicasso-controlled, test:hicasso-hmr — all from implementation/. Browser/Chromium gates are heavyweight: run them sequentially, never two at once.

WHAT COUNTS AS DONE. The module-to-test gap map is reported (findings doc in ai/findings/, never committed); clear test improvements merged green via PR with a ## Quality gates section; follow-on beads filed for the remainder with this bead named as owner; the delta between what this bead claims and what the tree holds at dispatch time is reported.

WHAT NOT TO TOUCH.
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/** and alloc_null_floor.cjs anywhere: held under rf2-t78z / rf2-oflj7 / rf2-fc7w awaiting Mike's rulings. Read them if useful; edit nothing.
- docs/design/hicasso/** studio/verdict pages: operator-held records.
- implementation/hicasso/spec/ prose: an edit there arms three Chromium lanes (rf2-7rzg, unresolved); do not touch it.
- Hot-zone files: spec/*, top-level implementation/deps.edn, implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, .github/workflows/*.
- examples/ is test-free by lock (rf2-8cevm): no specs under examples/, ever.
- Testbeds must stay idiomatic re-frame2 (app-db + events + subs); no deliberate bugs or teaching layers.

POSTURE. Pre-alpha masterpiece: elegance, clarity, correctness, good practice. Trust the programmer. No over-engineering, no gold-plating, no nag-diagnostics, no test-count inflation. Reject a finding rather than action minutiae; a short list of sourced, load-bearing improvements beats a long plausible one.

title: mayor loop: sweep open nightly-red issues into beads each merge+dispatch tick (loops.md §2 Dispatch + CLAUDE.md Workflow; alerter unchanged)
description:
Split out of rf2-2ohy's third acceptance item, which asked whether the
rf2-6sg25 alerting failed to surface seven consecutive nightly reds.

MEASURED 2026-08-23 13:36 AUSEST, and the answer is that THE ALERT FIRED
CORRECTLY. Issue #8423 'Nightly `expensive tests` is red' was opened
2026-08-16T16:01:50Z — the first red night — labelled `nightly-red`,
assigned to mike-thompson-day8, and its body named the exact failing step:
`Browser, bundle, examples, Story/Xray gates -> Gate — production elision,
browser (test:browser-prod-elision)`. It was edited every night since and
last updated 2026-08-22T16:02:05Z carrying `reds=7 greens=0`. The
alerting self-test step passed on every one of those runs. So the first
disjunct in rf2-2ohy's premise — 'the alerting did not fire' — is FALSE.
Nothing in .github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py is broken, and this
bead is NOT a request to change its signature logic.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED is the second disjunct: the issue went unseen for
seven days, and the alerter's own body says why, in its own words:

  'It is edited in place — which notifies nobody — while the same steps
  keep failing, and comments only when a step that was not failing starts
  to.'

That is a deliberate anti-spam design and it is defensible. The observed
cost of it is that a red lane produces EXACTLY ONE notification, on night
one, and then six nights of silence — and the one notification competes
with normal PR traffic in the same inbox. Seven days later the redness was
found by a manual PR-activity sweep, not by the alert, and no bead existed
until that sweep filed rf2-2ohy.

THE GAP, stated narrowly: nothing escalates a `nightly-red` issue that
stays open, and nothing bridges a GitHub issue into the beads tracker,
which is where work is actually dispatched from in this repo. The alert
lands in a channel the working loop does not read.

NOT PROPOSING A REMEDY — this is an operator call, and there are at least
three shapes with different costs, so it should not be picked by a worker:
  (a) re-notify on an age threshold (comment, not edit, after N reds) —
      cheapest, stays inside the existing script;
  (b) have the mayor loop read open `nightly-red` issues each tick;
  (c) have the alerter file/refresh a bead directly, so nightly redness
      enters the same queue as everything else.
(a) risks the spam the current design avoids. (c) is the most useful and
the most machinery. Mike to rule.

EVIDENCE: gh issue view 8423; gh run list --workflow expensive-tests.yml;
.github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml lines 558-616 (the 'Nightly result ->
tracking issue' job, which succeeded on all seven red runs).

ACCEPTANCE: a ruling on whether nightly redness should escalate past night
one, and if so which shape. If the ruling is 'leave it as is, the mayor
sweep is the backstop', close this — that is a legitimate outcome and the
evidence above is the record of what that choice costs.
notes:
*** AWAITING MIKE — NOT DISPATCHABLE. WHOLLY AN OPERATOR CALL. *** Fence recorded by the mayor's dispatch tick 2026-08-23 13:41 AUSEST at tip e1a1faf9c8, quoting this bead's own description rather than re-reasoning it.

WHY IT IS NOT DISPATCHABLE: the bead states it in terms — 'NOT PROPOSING A REMEDY — this is an operator call, and there are at least three shapes with different costs, so it should not be picked by a worker.' A worker sent here would have to choose between (a) re-notify on an age threshold, (b) the mayor loop reads open nightly-red issues each tick, and (c) the alerter files or refreshes a bead directly. Those differ in cost and in how much machinery they add, which is a judgement rather than a task.

DISCHARGED BY: Mike ruling on whether nightly redness should escalate past night one, and if so which of the three shapes. 'Leave it as is, the mayor sweep is the backstop' is a legitimate ruling and closes this bead — the bead says so itself, and the evidence it carries then stands as the record of what that choice costs.

WHAT IT IS NOT, and this matters because the parent bead's premise said otherwise: the alerting is NOT broken. This bead REFUTED that premise with measurement — issue #8423 opened on the first red night, labelled, assigned, naming the exact failing step, edited every night since, with the alerting self-test passing on all seven runs. Do not dispatch anything at .github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py's signature logic; nothing there is wrong.

THE COST OF THIS HOLD, priced rather than asserted: nothing is queued behind it and no bead is blocked by it. What it costs is the thing that already happened once — seven consecutive red nights on the superset backstop, found by a manual sweep on day seven rather than by the channel built to report it. That cost recurs at the same rate as nightly redness itself, which over the last nine nights was seven times in nine.

NO HOT-ZONE SEQUENCING IS NEEDED. I had expected to fence this behind rf2-2ohy's worker because a remedy would touch .github/workflows/*, which is hot-zone and currently that worker's. That fence is unnecessary: this bead cannot be dispatched at all until it is ruled, and by then that worker will be long finished.
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-08-23 17:05 AUSEST, tip 69a464c76b. THE PRICE OF THIS HOLD HAS CHANGED SINCE IT WAS RECORDED, and the bead's evidence needs the update so the ruling is made on current facts rather than on the state that prompted the bead.

WHAT THE 13:41 FENCE PRICES: "That cost recurs at the same rate as nightly redness itself, which over the last nine nights was seven times in nine."

THAT RATE WAS MEASURED WHILE THE ROOT CAUSE WAS LIVE, AND IT IS NOT LIVE NOW. Verified at source this tick, one item at a time:

  rf2-2ohy                          CLOSED (the browser-prod-elision abort, fixed by PR #8724)
  expensive-tests on main, 04:11    workflow_dispatch, completed/SUCCESS
  expensive-tests on the fix branch completed/SUCCESS at 03:38
  last SCHEDULED run                2026-08-22T15:24, failure -- i.e. BEFORE the fix landed
  schedule, read from the workflow  cron "17 15 * * *" = 01:17 AUSEST

So the first SCHEDULED exercise of the fix has not happened yet; it is tonight. The lane is proven green on main by dispatch, and the 7-in-9 figure describes a condition that has been repaired.

AND THE ALERTER CARRIES A RECOVERY POLICY THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION DOES NOT MENTION. Issue #8423's body reads, at this tick, "reds=7 greens=1" and states: "This issue closes automatically after 3 consecutive green runs -- the gap exists so an intermittent gate that passes tonight does not close and reopen the issue every other night." The 04:11 dispatch already counted as the first green.

WHY THAT MATTERS TO THE RULING RATHER THAN CLOSING IT. The "edited in place, notifies nobody" characterisation is TRUE OF THE RED DIRECTION ONLY. Recovery is automatic, bounded and hysteresis-guarded; it is the escalation on SUSTAINED redness that is absent. That narrows the question rather than answering it, and narrowing is worth recording: the three shapes are still the three shapes, but option (a) -- re-notify on an age threshold -- is now visibly the mirror of a policy the alerter ALREADY implements in the other direction, which is an argument about symmetry rather than about adding machinery.

THE HOLD'S COST, RE-PRICED. Still nothing queued behind it, still no bead blocked by it. What it costs is no longer a 7-in-9 recurring toll; it is the next unrelated breakage going unreported for as many nights as it takes somebody to sweep manually. That is a lower expected cost and a WORSE-SHAPED one -- rarer, and silent exactly when nobody is looking for it, which is when it will next bite.

NOTHING TO DISPATCH AND NOTHING CHANGED ABOUT DISPATCHABILITY. This stays wholly an operator call on the same three shapes, and "leave it as is, the mayor sweep is the backstop" stays a legitimate closing ruling.

ONE THING TO WATCH RATHER THAN FILE: if tonight's scheduled run is green, #8423 goes to greens=2 and closes itself after the third. If it is red, the fix did not hold under the scheduled trigger and rf2-2ohy wants reopening -- but that is a question for the merge tick tomorrow, not a bead today.
MAYOR 2026-08-24 01:57 AUSEST — THE WATCH CONDITION ON THIS BEAD HAS FIRED, AND IT FIRED GREEN.

This bead recorded: 'if tonight's scheduled run is [red], the fix did not hold under the scheduled
trigger and rf2-2ohy wants reopening.' Measured at source rather than inferred:

  2026-08-23T15:25  schedule           completed/SUCCESS  d1c824098d   <- tonight, 01:25 AUSEST
  2026-08-23T04:11  workflow_dispatch  completed/success  249d6ba0e2
  2026-08-23T03:38  workflow_dispatch  completed/success  bef9873398
  2026-08-22T15:24  schedule           completed/FAILURE  8c118b7dc2   <- the last red, BEFORE the fix

So the first SCHEDULED exercise of PR #8724's cache-blocking fix passed. The lane is now proven green
under the trigger that was failing, not only under manual dispatch. rf2-2ohy STAYS CLOSED — no reopen.

THE TRACKING ISSUE HAS MOVED TOO, and its own counter is the evidence: issue #8423 now reads
'reds=7 greens=2' where it read 'reds=7 greens=1' before tonight. It auto-closes after THREE
consecutive greens, so it stays open one more night by design — the gap exists so an intermittent gate
does not close and reopen the issue. Expect it to close after tomorrow's scheduled run.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DISCHARGE: this bead's own subject, which is the ALERTING gap rather than the test
failure — seven reds produced one notification. That question is untouched by tonight's green and is
still wholly an operator call. The banner stands.
RULING 2026-09-02 10:21:52 AUSEST (delegated by Mike 2026-09-02, dossier review; ai/decisions/rf2-4a0c.nightly-red-escalation.md folded here and deleted — THIS NOTE IS THE CANONICAL RECORD). Ruled at tip b26c5ad33e.
BANNER STRUCK — the *** AWAITING MIKE *** banner above is discharged by this ruling.

1. DECISION: (b). The mayor's short Merge + dispatch tick reads the open nightly-red issues and ensures each one has exactly one open bead. The alerter (.github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py) and expensive-tests.yml are NOT touched — signature logic, thresholds, channel, all unchanged. (a), (c) and (d) rejected; one-line reasons under REJECTED in §4.

THE MECHANISM, exactly:
- WHERE: the DISPATCH half of the short tick (loops.md cadence table: "Merge + dispatch", ~10–15 min, and "on most signals"), as the first read BEFORE `bd ready` — its output is a bead, and the same tick can then dispatch it.
- THE READ, one-shot and non-blocking: `gh issue list --repo day8/re-frame2 --label nightly-red --state open --limit 100 --json number,url,title,updatedAt,body`. Check the exit code of the gh call itself. Exit 0 with `[]` = nothing red, done — the normal tick (the dossier measured the label non-empty on 12 of the last 60 days; at ruling time it is empty). Non-zero exit = "the sweep did not run this tick", retried on the next signal — NEVER read a failed query as "no nightly red" (the reviewer's invariant, adopted).
- DEDUP KEY: the canonical issue URL (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/issues/<n>), carried in the bead's `external_ref` field — a field the tracker already uses this way (15 beads carry PR URLs in it at tip) and which `bd list --json` exposes. NOT the bare number: "8423" also matches PR numbers, run counts and commit prefixes. The read: `bd list --status open,in_progress,blocked,deferred,closed --limit 0 --json | jq -r --arg u "$url" '.[] | select(.external_ref==$u) | "\(.id)\t\(.status)"'` (confirm once that `--limit 0` is unbounded on this bd build, as it is for `bd ready`).
- THREE CASES per open issue:
  (i) a bead in open/in_progress/blocked carries the URL → do nothing. The issue stays the live counter and signature record; the bead is the dispatch edge; later ticks do nothing.
  (ii) no bead carries the URL → file one: `bd create "nightly red: <failing steps> (issue #<n>)" --type bug --priority 2 --external-ref <url> --description "<shape in §4>"`. P2 by default; raise with a stated reason when the failing gate warrants it.
  (iii) only CLOSED beads carry the URL → THE HYSTERESIS CASE, and the one the reviewer's draft rule ("reopen it or file a clearly linked follow-up") would get wrong. The issue closes only after THREE consecutive greens (`--close-after 3`, sized above the rf2-7jevo flake), so for two nights after every fix the expected state is "bead closed, issue still open" — that is recovery, not a new failure. Read the body's marker line `<!-- nightly-alert:v1 signature=... reds=N greens=M -->`: `decide()` (nightly_failure_alert.py:246-286) sets greens=0 on ANY red night and increments it on a green one, so `greens>=1` → recovering by design, do nothing; `greens=0` → the most recent nightly was red AFTER the bead closed — the fix did not hold, or a new step joined — so file a NEW bead per (ii) with `--deps discovered-from:<closed-id>`, citing the closed one. Never reopen the closed bead: its close reason is a normative record.
- DUPLICATE ISSUES: the label-index race can open two issues in the same minute (#7537/#7538 on 2026-08-05, recorded in `fetch_open_issues`' docstring and self-healed by `collapse_duplicates` on the next run). Two open nightly-red issues with the same title created within minutes are ONE alert: file against the lower number only.
- BINDING FROM NOW: the doctrine binds the mayor from this ruling; the doc PR is the record, not the trigger. At ruling time (`gh issue list --label nightly-red --state open`, 10:13 AUSEST) there are ZERO open nightly-red issues and the last five scheduled runs are green, so today's sweep is a no-op.

2. HOW THE OPINIONS WERE WEIGHED
Two voices in the dossier: the AUTHOR (sections "Summary", "The problem, carefully and fully", "What is waiting on this", "Options", "Recommendation", "Evidence") and the REVIEWER ("Codex Recommendation": "Independent findings", "Why this option", "Implementation invariant, risks, and next decision"). Both recommend (b). The ruling follows them because their agreement is on the load-bearing FACT rather than on taste: the reviewer independently re-ran the self-test and replayed the 22 runs and got the same classification (open/touch/touch/change/change/touch/touch, then hold/hold/close) — three loud events reached the inbox before discovery, and a manual sweep still found the redness on day seven. That is a channel miss, and (a) is the only option that treats volume instead. The reviewer adds a fact the author did not have: GitHub's own contract subscribes an assignee and routes assignment/update reasons to the inbox, so the events were DELIVERED and still missed — which closes the last door for (a) as a first repair.

AGREEMENTS (author and reviewer): the one-notification premise is wrong (four, three before discovery); channel, not volume; alerter untouched; (c) costs a second credential (GITHUB_TOKEN is repository-scoped by contract; the beads remote is a second repository), bd/Dolt bootstrapped in CI, and a concurrent tracker writer, for no better delivered latency than (b); (d) is coherent only if unbounded discovery time is accepted for the system of record.

DISAGREEMENTS, and how each went:
- WHERE the doctrine lives. Author: one bullet in CLAUDE.md's Workflow section. Reviewer: "the active repository-specific short-loop instructions" (the same file, in this repo's terms). Ruling: BOTH files, per loops.md's own rule at its head ("everything below is the method; the values it needs belong in that repository's agent-instructions file"): the generic paragraph goes in docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md §2 Dispatch, the concrete query/label/dedup in CLAUDE.md Workflow. No loop command files exist in-repo (`.claude/commands/` is gone), so those two files ARE the loop body.
- DEDUP KEY. Author: "no open bead citing that issue number". Reviewer: the canonical issue URL, "exactly one open bead". Ruling: the reviewer's key, carried in `external_ref` — the author's number is a weak grep and the URL is what the tracker already stores for PRs.
- THE CLOSED-BEAD CASE. Reviewer: "reopen it or file a clearly linked follow-up". Ruling: neither reflexively — the marker rule in §1(iii). As written, the reviewer's rule would re-file or reopen on EVERY recovery, because the three-green close delay makes "closed bead, open issue" the expected state for two nights after each fix; the author did not address the case at all. This is the one place the ruling goes beyond both.
- SESSION SCOPE. Reviewer: (b) guarantees discovery on the next live tick, not 24-hour paging; if Mike wants a wall-clock acknowledgement SLO independent of mayor activity, (b) is insufficient and an acknowledged on-call channel or a scoped cross-repo credential with an owner is needed. Author: the red week had live sessions every day (182/82/221/70/155/416/169 commits on main 08-16 to 08-22), so the floor is "next live session" under every bead-ending option anyway. Ruling: no SLO adopted — the posture trusts the operator and does not build paging; the reviewer's condition is recorded as a reassess trigger in §5.

DISSENT PRESERVED: (1) the 2026-08-23 17:05 mayor note's symmetry argument — (a) is the mirror of the recovery hysteresis the alerter already implements in the other direction. The ruling's answer: symmetry into a channel measured not to reach the loop buys appearance, not escalation; the argument is fair and (a) stays available. (2) The reviewer's condition for (a) later: if the bridge is working and acknowledgements STILL stall, periodic comments become justifiable. (3) The author's, and this bead's own, statement that (d) is legitimate — it is, and this note is the record of what it would have cost.
3. PREMISE CORRECTIONS AT TIP (b26c5ad33e, re-verified 2026-09-02 10:13 AUSEST, read-only):
- "Seven reds, one notification" (this bead's title and description) is FALSE for this run. Measured at source: FOUR — the issue-open 2026-08-16T16:01:50Z; two loud github-actions[bot] comments "A nightly step that was not failing is now failing" at 2026-08-19T16:27:11Z and 2026-08-20T16:04:11Z (the cancelled 08-19 night reads as a signature change under commit 2ae34316e3 "a cancelled nightly is not a green nightly", 2026-08-06, which PREDATES the run; the signature changed back on 08-20); and the close comment 08-24. Replay (`--replay 22`, run by the author and independently by the reviewer): open NOTIFY / touch / touch / change NOTIFY / change NOTIFY / touch / touch / hold / hold / close NOTIFY — 4 against a naive alert's 7. title: nightly expensive-tests RED 7 consecutive days: test:browser-prod-elision aborts with uncaught TypeError reading 'me'
description:
Found by the 2026-08-23 PR-activity sweep. The nightly expensive-tests workflow has failed 7 consecutive runs (08-16, 08-17, 08-18, cancelled 08-19, 08-20, 08-21, 08-22; last green 08-15), same job every time: 'Browser, bundle, examples, Story/Xray gates'. The 08-22 log isolates it to the test:browser-prod-elision lane (shadow-cljs release browser-test-prod-elision): the browser run aborts with an uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'me'), no cljs.test summary. Everything before it in the job is green (browser suite 1072 tests/6076 assertions, bundle-isolation self-test, both adapter smokes, Story gates).

TIMING CORRELATION, unconfirmed as cause: first red is 08-16, the day the Freehand/re-frame.ui tree removal (PR #8322) landed. 'me' reads like a minified/advanced-compilation symbol, so the likely shape is the prod-elision browser test (or a namespace it pulls in) still reaching something the removal deleted — but that is a hypothesis to verify, not a finding. The abort-detector text in the log cites rf2-u0j8, which is CLOSED and predates this.

WHY P2: this lane is the nightly superset backstop that rf2-2uy8's ruling relies on — while it is red, every gate family downstream of the abort in that job is NOT running against main nightly, so the ~24h-bounded exposure the ruling accepted is currently unbounded for those families. It is also release-relevant: the prod-elision gate is part of the production bundle story rf2-kmqx3's first tag depends on. Seven days red with no bead means the rf2-6sg25 signature-change alerting either did not fire or its issue went unseen — worth one line in the fix PR saying which.

REPRO: gh run list --workflow expensive-tests; the failing step is in the 'Browser, bundle, examples, Story/Xray gates' job; locally, npm run test:browser-prod-elision from implementation/.

ACCEPTANCE: the lane runs green on a nightly (or workflow_dispatch) against main; the root cause is stated (not just resymptomed); if the alerting failed to surface 7 reds, that defect is either fixed in the same PR or filed as its own bead with the evidence.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED — PR #8724 (branch worker/nightly-2ohy), 2026-08-23 13:40 AUSEST.

## What it is

`shadow.test.env/get-test-data` is a MACRO. It expands, at the moment the
runner namespace is compiled, into a literal map naming every test var the
compiler knows about — the test roster is frozen into the runner's compiled JS.

shadow-cljs keys its per-namespace compile cache off `:immediate-deps`, which
`shadow.build.resolve/stack-pop` fills from the ns form's own requires. The
`:browser-test` target attaches the discovered test namespaces to the runner as
`:extra-requires` (`shadow.build.test-util/inject-extra-requires`), and those
are read only by `shadow.build.compiler/par-compile-one` to ORDER compilation —
they never enter `:immediate-deps`. So the roster can change completely without
invalidating the runner's cache entry.

A namespace LEAVING the roster is the destructive direction: the stale cached
expansion still dereferences vars whose namespaces are no longer in the bundle.
Under :advanced that is a property read on undefined, uncaught, inside `init` —
zero namespaces announced, no cljs.test summary, exactly the observed abort.

## The bead's hypothesis was RIGHT about the trigger, wrong about the mechanism

The correlation with the Freehand / re-frame.ui removal is REAL and causal: PR
#8322 took fourteen `*-elision-prod-test` namespaces out of this lane on 08-16.
But nothing in the prod-elision build 'still reaches a deleted surface' in the
source sense — the source is fine, and a CLEAN local run of
`npm run test:browser-prod-elision` has been green throughout (measured: exit 0,
91 tests / 289 assertions on current main). The reach-into-deleted-surface
happens in a STALE COMPILED ARTEFACT, and it needs a warm cache to exist at all.
`expensive-tests.yml` restores `implementation/.shadow-cljs` with
`restore-keys: <os>-story-xray-shadow-`, so from 08-16 every nightly served the
pre-removal runner out of cache. That is why the failure is CI-only and why it
persisted for seven nights.

The 'me' in the message is not meaningful: it is a Closure-assigned minified
property name, per bundle. The local reproduction produced the identical defect
reading '$j'.

## The fix

`{:dev/always true}` on the ns. Despite the name,
`shadow.build.compiler/is-cache-blocked?` reads that key with NO mode gate, so
it blocks caching under `release` exactly as under :dev. This is not invention —
it is what the stock `shadow.test.browser` and `shadow.test.node` runners
already carry, and what this repo's own `re-frame.test-quiet.shadow-node`
already carries WITH A COMMENT saying it is required because get-test-data is a
macro. The two browser prod runners were written from the stock runner's BODY
without its ns metadata.

Fixed both, because both have the defect:
  - re-frame.prod-elision-runner        (implementation/core/test/...)
  - re-frame.schemas-boundary-prod-runner (implementation/schemas/test/...)

`git grep get-test-data` over tracked .cljs/.cljc returns exactly five
namespaces; the other three already carried the metadata. Inventory complete,
no sixth site.

No workflow / cache-key / shadow-cljs.edn change — those would treat the
symptom. The cache is not wrong to be warm; the runner was wrong to be cacheable.

## Verified in both directions, by planting the real event at 1/14 scale

Removed ONE `*-elision-prod-test` namespace against a warm cache. Exit codes
captured from the runner, not reported by the harness:

  before fix, full roster      —            Ran 91 tests / 289 assertions   exit 0
  before fix, one ns removed   0 compiled   ABORTED, 0 namespaces, TypeError exit 1
  after  fix, one ns removed   1 compiled   Ran 88 tests / 285 assertions   exit 0
  after  fix, full roster      1 compiled   Ran 91 tests / 289 assertions   exit 0

Row 2 IS the CI failure, reproduced locally: same abort text, same '0
namespaces announced', same `Object.<mangled> [as init]` frame. Row 3 is the
discrimination — the identical plant goes green after the fix, with the runner
recompiling (0 -> 1) on a source file that did not change. Plant restored and
verified by git blob hash, not by reading a diff.

Also green: `npm run test:browser-schemas-boundary-prod` (exit 0, 8 tests / 15
assertions), the sibling lane the same fix covers. Both re-run after rebase onto
the final base. Both lanes are PR-gated in test.yml and this diff classes
cljs_prod=true, so CI covers them on the PR too.

## Third acceptance item — alerting

Premise does NOT hold: the alerting FIRED, correctly, on night one. Issue #8423
opened 2026-08-16T16:01:50Z, labelled nightly-red, assigned to
mike-thompson-day8, body naming the exact failing step; edited nightly, last
carrying reds=7 greens=0; self-test green on all seven runs. What failed is
downstream — the alerter edits in place, which notifies nobody, so seven reds
produced one notification, and nothing escalates an open nightly-red issue or
bridges it into beads. Filed as rf2-4a0c with the evidence and three candidate
shapes; it asks for a ruling rather than picking one, because the trade-off
against notification spam is an operator call.

A namespace LEAVING is the destructive direction: the stale expansion dereferences vars whose namespaces are gone, which under :advanced is a property read on undefined, uncaught inside init, hence zero namespaces announced and no cljs.test summary at all.

WHY THE 08-16 CORRELATION WAS REAL BUT THE MECHANISM WAS NOT WHAT THE BEAD GUESSED. PR #8322 removed fourteen *-elision-prod-test namespaces that day; expensive-tests.yml restores implementation/.shadow-cljs across runs, so from 08-16 every nightly served the PRE-REMOVAL runner out of a warm cache. That is why the first red is the day of the removal AND why a clean local run of the same command was green throughout — two facts the source-level hypothesis could not have reconciled.

THE FIX: {:dev/always true} on two namespaces, with shadow.build.compiler/is-cache-blocked? verified to read that key with NO mode gate, so it blocks caching under release exactly as under dev. The worker inventoried the five namespaces that use get-test-data across tracked cljs/cljc and showed the three stock or in-repo runners already carry the key while these two did not, both having been written from the stock runner's body without its ns metadata.

VERIFICATION WORTH RECORDING because it is the discrimination rather than a green: the failure was reproduced at 1/14 scale by removing ONE namespace against a warm cache — before the fix, 0 compiled and an abort at init with 0 namespaces; after the fix, 1 compiled and 88 tests / 285 assertions passing, on a source file that did not change. The minified property differs ( locally, me in CI) because Closure assigns names per bundle; same defect.

AND THE SYMPTOM-VS-CAUSE LINE WAS DRAWN EXPLICITLY, in the worker's own words: 'No workflow, cache-key or shadow-cljs.edn change: those would treat the symptom. The cache is not wrong to be warm; the runner was wrong to be cacheable.'

ACCEPTANCE ITEM 3 IS DISCHARGED BY FILING, WHICH THIS BEAD PERMITTED. It asked whether the alerting failed to surface seven reds. The worker MEASURED it and refuted the premise I briefed: the alert fired correctly on night one — issue #8423, labelled, assigned, naming the exact failing step, edited nightly, self-test passing on all seven runs. description:

A line range against a living document is a measured constant that goes stale exactly where it has to be right.' Adapt only the placeholders.', inside '## The worktree boundary block'. Meanwhile '## Pasting a block' opens 'SEVERAL blocks below travel verbatim into every dispatch' -- plural. title: method: the heavyweight-gate test answers loudness, not whether a peer write voids a measurement bracket
description:
FOUND 2026-08-22 05:5x AUSEST, tip 73b6ae82d8, by a measurement window (rf2-w01c) voiding two of
its three pre-registered runs because the MAYOR wrote inside the bracket twice. Not a worker
error and not a rig fault: five invocations, all exit 0, no rig fault, voided under the window's

THE DOCUMENT GIVES ONE TEST WHERE TWO ARE NEEDED. loops.md §2's heavyweight-gate paragraph tells
the mayor how to decide whether an item may be dispatched while a measurement window is queued or
running. The test it states is about the GATES the item arms: enumerate what covers the item and
confirm each of those gates leaves the machine quiet. That is a correct and well-earned test for
MACHINE LOAD, and it was strengthened only hours earlier (rf2-fif4, PRs #8678 and #8679) to stop
a category being granted the licence a measurement has to earn.

IT IS THE WRONG TEST FOR AN EXCLUSIVITY CONDITION, and nothing in the document says so. A window
may register a condition that no peer WRITES inside its bracket. That is violated by activity
which is nearly free in machine terms and which the gate test therefore waves through:

  - CREATING A WORKTREE for an unrelated doc-only item. Cheap, arms nothing, voided a run.
  - MERGING A PULL REQUEST. Costs the local machine essentially nothing, voided a run.

Both were performed by the mayor's own recurring merge-and-dispatch loop, on an item correctly
measured as arming zero of this repo's 28 test surfaces. The gate test passed and was the wrong
question. The result was a correctly-run, correctly-registered window returning TWO admissible
runs of THREE, with the two-instruments rule forbidding the third being taken later — so the
series cannot be completed, only re-run.

WHY A MAYOR DOES NOT SIMPLY WORK THIS OUT. The heavyweight-gate paragraph reads as complete: it
names the hazard (a loud machine), gives an instrument (the classifier), warns that no single
classifier's answer describes the whole set, and tells you to hold the fleet thin. Having run
that test and passed it, there is nothing left to prompt a second question. "Thin" is also
actively misleading here — it says a smaller fleet is a safer fleet, when for a registered
exclusivity condition the only safe fleet is an EMPTY one, and the mayor must additionally stop
merging.

THE REPAIR, in the heavyweight-gate paragraph where the existing test lives. Two to three
sentences, generic, no counts:

  A gate test answers whether an item makes the machine LOUD. It does not answer whether the item
  BREAKS THE BRACKET. Where a window registers an exclusivity condition, any peer write inside its
  bracket voids the run however cheap that write is — creating a worktree and merging a change
  both cost the machine almost nothing and both are writes — so for such a window the fleet is
  EMPTY rather than thin, and the mayor performs no merges either.

Wording is a starting point. Keep it inside the existing paragraph; do NOT add a section, and do
NOT restate the gate test.

WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH THE WORDS RATHER THAN LEAVING IT TO JUDGEMENT: the two halves point
OPPOSITE WAYS for the cheapest actions. A merge is the single cheapest thing a mayor does on the
machine and one of the most destructive things it can do to a bracket. Any rule ordered by cost
gets that exactly backwards.

RELATED, NOT DUPLICATE: rf2-n3uw is also a loops.md repair (the concurrent-writers block naming
one shared area). Different block, same file. SEQUENCE THESE — two workers in one file is the
collision this method sequences rather than parallelises.

surface is implementation/, tools/, examples/, testbeds/, so docs/ is outside it. Light on all

a registered exclusivity condition.

title: hic: the clock lane's :over-floor resolution gate is necessary but not sufficient for a comparative row
description:
MEASURED DURING rf2-9wmqd ITEM (c)'S WINDOW, 2026-08-22, on slice_broad_clock_app. Filed rather than fixed there because the window's own terms forbid improving the rig mid-measurement.

WHAT THE GATE IS. slice_broad_clock_app's docstring makes :over-floor's :straddles-1? the resolution test a reader must apply before quoting any :comparative range: an arm whose per-round range against an EMPTY FRAME includes 1.0 was not separated from the floor, and no ratio between two such arms is a reading about anything. lane/across-rounds computes it. It is a SOUND NECESSARY CONDITION and it did real work in that window -- :donor-theme straddled 1.0 in two evidence runs of three, so the theme pair was refused outright.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO. :over-floor asks whether ONE arm separated from an empty frame. C3 asks whether TWO arms separate from EACH OTHER at a stated line (1.25x), and C4 at 1.5x. The locale pair answered YES to the first in all three runs and NO to the second, which is the case that shows the two are different questions. Arithmetic on that run's own published p50s and nothing else: because a paint-bounded window is ~96% frame grid, a 1.25x difference in the arms' OWN work displaces the window-level ratio by only 0.3-1.1 percentage points against an observed per-round spread of 1.5-7.5 points, and a 1.5x difference by 0.6-2.2 points. The observed ~1.00x is consistent with 1.00x, 1.25x and 1.5x alike. A reader applying only the shipped gate would have quoted it as a pass.

WHAT IS WANTED, and the choice is open. Everything the second reading needs is ALREADY PUBLISHED -- :summary's per-arm :p50 including the floor's, and :comparative's per-round spread -- so this is a computation the lane does not perform rather than data it does not have. Candidates, to be settled at source: (a) publish a per-pair detectable-difference figure beside :comparative, derived from the floor and the denominator arm's excess over it, so a run says what size of difference it could have seen; (b) leave the arithmetic to the reader and put it in the driver's docstring beside the existing caveat; (c) both. DO NOT add a threshold, a band or a pass/fail -- budgets.md sec.7 routes every distributional row to pinned evidence runs and check_budget_ledger.py enforces it, and a resolution figure is an honesty aid, not a verdict.

WHOEVER TAKES THIS SHOULD READ FIRST: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-u3-c3-c4-window-on-the-slice-broad-clock.md sec.7.7 and sec.7.8, which carry the numbers and the argument. Same mechanism serves slice_echo_clock_app and ledger_frame_clock_app, so a change to lane.cljs reaches all three -- check what each publishes before moving anything shared.

SURFACE: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/lane.cljs and/or slice_broad_clock_app.cljs. Gate: npm run test:hicasso-compile (heavyweight; CI covers it on every PR that arms this surface).
