title: method: the reaping escape is keyed to an agent id the mapping file usually lacks, while the transcripts are on disk and findable by content
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD REREAD LOOP 2026-08-22 04:2x AUSEST, tip 73158f33e9, by testing a rule I have been ENFORCING against what the tree actually holds. The rule is sound; its escape hatch is keyed to something that is often missing, and the document does not say the escape is still reachable without it.

WHAT THE METHOD SAYS. Reaping is authorised only by the worker's own completion report, and the operational test is whether you can QUOTE the sentence where that agent says it is finished. It adds an escape: reading an agent's transcript is a READ and satisfies the test. And it already knows transcripts outlive conversations — "What the id buys is the TRANSCRIPT, not a live conversation", recording eight agents that answered "no transcript" to a message while their transcripts sat intact on disk.

WHAT I HAVE BEEN DOING WITH IT. Every hygiene pass, I map standing worktrees to agent ids through the dispatch-time mapping file, message the ones that have an id, and classify the rest as irreducible residue that clears only on the operator's authority. That is a faithful reading of the document.

THE PROBLEM: THE ESCAPE IS KEYED TO AN ID THE MAPPING FILE OFTEN DOES NOT HAVE. Measured this pass with a working control -- of 35 registered worktrees, exactly THREE carry an agent id in the mapping file. The other 32 predate the sessions that recorded ids, so under the rule as written they can never be reaped, ever, by anybody.

BUT THE TRANSCRIPTS ARE ON DISK AND THEY ARE FINDABLE BY CONTENT. Measured: 2,992 transcript files across 28 session directories, 2,283 of them non-empty. A content search for a worktree's own path finds its transcripts -- 'foldcorpus' returns SIX files, and a worktree name that cannot exist returns ZERO, so the search discriminates and the six are a reading. So the report an unmapped worktree needs is not missing; it is merely unindexed.

WHY THIS IS NOT SIMPLY "GO AND REAP THEM", and the repair must carry both hazards or it will cause worse harm than the residue:

  1. THE MATCH IS MANY-TO-ONE AND MOST MATCHES ARE NOT THE WORKER'S OWN. A worktree path appears in
     the dispatching mayor's transcript, in every PEER brief that names the in-flight surfaces (this
     method requires naming them), and in the worker's own. Six hits for one worktree, and only one
     of them is the agent that can report done. Reaping on a peer's mention of a worktree would be
     authorising removal from someone else's report -- strictly worse than leaving the residue.
  2. THE FILES ARE NOT SAFE TO READ WHOLE. Median 32 bytes, MAXIMUM 23,624,222. The transcript route
     has to be a bounded extraction -- locate, then read a tail -- never an open.

THE REPAIR, and it belongs in the reaping paragraph where the escape is stated: say that when the id was never recorded the transcript is still reachable by searching transcript content for the worktree's own path; and say in the same breath that the match is many-to-one because peers name each other's surfaces, so the file must be identified as the WORKER'S OWN before anything it says counts as that worker's report. One clause, two sentences, where the escape already lives.

WHAT THIS IS WORTH. 32 worktrees and 31 branches pinned by them are currently classed as clearable only by operator authority. That is the largest standing hygiene cost in the repo and it has been carried for weeks. If the route works it is not licence to sweep -- each still needs its own quotable sentence -- but it converts an irreducible cost into ordinary work.

title: method: loops.md §2 tells you to refill the instant a slot frees, which is exactly what fences a queued measurement window
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD REREAD LOOP 2026-08-22 03:2x AUSEST, tip 6154a9d374, by checking a rule I HAVE BEEN ENFORCING against what the document actually says. It is one clause, in one block, and it fails in the direction that costs the most.

THE TWO PASSAGES, both in loops.md and both correct on their own:

  §2 filter list, the last entry (~:407-411)
    "items whose resource is exclusive and currently contended -- but this exclusion has a
     release condition ... WHERE THE EXCLUSIVE ITEMS ARE ALL THAT REMAINS, the filter has
     stopped protecting the fleet and is simply refusing the backlog. Say so, stop refilling,
     let the fleet drain, and take that work deliberately."

  §2 "Shape and saturation" (~:448-450)
    "Target a fixed number of concurrent workers -- six is a workable ceiling for one operator
     -- and REFILL THE INSTANT A SLOT FREES. Dispatch low-priority items to stay saturated."

THE STATE THE DOCUMENT DOES NOT COVER, and it is the state the mayor was in when this was written. A measurement window is QUEUED and needs a quiet machine. Ordinary dispatchable work also exists, with free surfaces and no operator hold. So:

  * the DRAIN clause does not authorise holding thin -- its condition is "the exclusive items
    are ALL THAT REMAINS", and they are not;
  * the SATURATION block positively instructs refilling -- "the instant a slot frees";
  * but every one of those refillable items runs a browser or CLJS lane, and this document
    already says (~:452-458) that "a heavyweight gate is an exclusive resource ... contention
    for the MACHINE, so six workers on six disjoint surfaces can still wedge one another",
    and that this "is the constraint a measurement window is already fenced under, seen from
    the other side".

SO REFILLING IS WHAT FENCES THE WINDOW, AND THE DOCUMENT TELLS YOU TO REFILL. The vocabulary for the conflict is already present at :452-458; what is missing is its consequence for the refill decision. A mayor reading §2 straight would saturate, keep the machine loud, and fence the measurement lane INDEFINITELY -- while following the document exactly.

HOW IT WAS RESOLVED IN PRACTICE, which is the tell that the document is not carrying it. The mayor held the fleet at one worker for several ticks on the strength of an OPERATOR RULING recorded on a bead (rf2-0puue: "the instant no background agents are running, a measurement bead goes out -- so the fleet is being held THIN on purpose rather than saturated, because a full fleet is what fences this whole lane"). That ruling is this project's; the loops document is generic and cannot cite it. But the STRUCTURAL fact it depends on is generic: a queued exclusive-machine measurement makes an otherwise-free slot not free.

THE REPAIR. ONE CLAUSE on the "Shape and saturation" block, placed there rather than on the filter entry BECAUSE THAT IS WHERE THE WRONG READING IS MANUFACTURED -- a reader who reaches the filter entry has already been told to refill. It should say, in the document's own register and vocabulary: while a measurement window is queued and unstarted, an item whose gate is heavyweight is not a slot to refill but a cost charged to the window; hold thin deliberately, say that is what you are doing, and dispatch only work whose gate leaves the machine quiet.

DO NOT ADD A NEW SECTION and do not restate the heavyweight-gate paragraph -- it is already correct and already adjacent. Do not touch README.md. No headings may move: anchors are cited from outside this tree.

A LIGHT-GATE DISPATCH IS AVAILABLE AND SHOULD BE NAMED IN THE CLAUSE AS THE ESCAPE, because it is what makes the rule actionable rather than merely restrictive: doc-only work leaves the machine quiet. MEASURED at this tip -- .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh on docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md arms NO surface at all, against a control of 5 armed surfaces for implementation/hicasso/spec/budgets.md. So the fleet can stay busy on light work while a window waits; the instruction is not "stop working", it is "stop making the machine loud".

GATES: docs/the-mayor-method/ is inside check_doc_slugs.py's roots AND is one of the two trees held to the STRICTER in-fence rule, so a doc link inside a fenced block IS reported there. mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs does NOT exclude this tree -- verify that at source rather than trusting this line. Verify anchors and any table column counts by hand and say so in the PR body; nothing gates prose.

AUDIT OF PR #8678 — CORRECTNESS FINDING. The new paragraph says documentation and prose changes typically arm no gated surface at all, and the PR derives quiet-machine safety from report-changed-surfaces.sh returning 0 of 28 keys. That inference is false at the landed tree.

Evidence at source: .github/workflows/docs.yml classifies docs/* as docs_surface=true and gates MkDocs build on it (lines 208-219); PR #8678 itself ran Detect docs surface and MkDocs build successfully. report-changed-surfaces.sh is the test.yml classifier, and its own comment explicitly names docs.yml's separate Detect docs surface path. Zero test-surface keys therefore means neither zero gates nor that every covering gate leaves the measurement box quiet.

This matters to the rule, not just its wording: a doc worker dispatched as the named escape can later run its covering build while the queued window starts, contaminating the box unless that gate is actually classified light or the window waits for it. Minimal repair: do not nominate docs from the 0-of-28 result; say to dispatch only work whose complete covering gate set has been verified quiet, and name docs/prose only conditionally. Exact owner reopened; no duplicate bead.

title: hicasso: presence_ssr_seam_dom_cljs_test's two adoption rows never settle on rejection — no .catch
description:
REPORTED BY THE rf2-x43z WORKER (settlerows) UNDER ITS FENCE, and deliberately NOT touched: rf2-x43z was fenced to one test namespace and told to report a third rather than widen.

THE FILE: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/presence_ssr_seam_dom_cljs_test.cljs.

SAME FAULT AS rf2-x43z. Measured at tip ecb7057c26 with fixed-string grep, control run in both directions on the same instrument (it returns 6 against the repaired server_render_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs, so the zero here is a reading and not a broken search):

  grep -c -F '.catch'  -> 0
  sup/adopted! sites   -> 2, at :506 and :600

THE SHAPE at :506 is (-> (sup/adopted! ha) (.then (fn [ok] (close!) (stop!) (try ...assertions... )))) - and note that close! and stop! sit INSIDE the fulfilment handler, so a rejection leaves the mismatch watcher registered AND console.error still replaced. That capture is opened with :swallow-uncaught? true, so a listener that outlives its row goes on calling preventDefault on every later row's uncaught errors: the exact fail-open the browser runner's pageerror rule exists to prevent, silently disarmed for the rest of the run.

On a rejection nothing runs: no (done), so the row does not go red but HANGS to the async timeout and reports the timeout rather than the rejection; the root, the watcher and the console capture all leak into the next row; and what the adoption threw is lost.

THE REPAIR IS SETTLED, not a design question. Apply settle-row! locally, spelled verbatim as in server_render_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs (rf2-sxhu, PR #8675) and identifier_prefix_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs (rf2-x43z), so that rf2-7ucn's later lift into roots-frames-support is a deletion and a :require rather than a reconciliation. Keep close! where it is AND name it in :release! - it is idempotent by construction (a closed? volatile), so the fulfilment path still bounds the capture across the render while the rejection path still restores the console.

ACCEPTANCE, as rf2-x43z's: each row settles exactly once on fulfilment or rejection; the rejection is reported with enough to identify the row; every watcher stopped, every capture closed and every handle released on both paths; a deliberate rejected-adoption control that fails before the repair; and no assertion changes, proven mechanically by extracting the balanced (is ...) forms from both revisions and diffing, not by eye.

FENCE: this one test namespace. Do not sweep in roots_frames_hydration (rf2-8zhr) or instance_key_payload (a different shape - see rf2-7ucn).

DISCOVERED-FROM rf2-x43z.
notes:

    (.then chains        3   (:423, :507, :601)
    (finally forms       4   (:323, :449, :568, :619)
    (done) calls         6

THE TWO ADOPTION ROWS ARE :506/:568 AND :600/:619, each a .then with a finally that releases ha and calls done, and no rejection arm at all.

ONE ADJACENT CHAIN TO ASSESS RATHER THAN ASSUME: the .then at :423 settles through a finally at :449 that calls (done) alone — no release — and it is not fed by adopted!. And :323's finally closes an adoption window via roots/close-adoption-window! outside any .then. Say which of these are in scope and which are out, WITH THE REASON. I have not read their source promises and I am not ruling them in.

FENCE — EXCLUSIVE RESOURCE, CONTENDED. Same as rf2-8zhr and for the same reason, which is the machine and not the surface: nobody holds this file, but the measurement lane is next in the queue (rf2-9wmqd item (c)) and Mike's standing ruling holds the fleet THIN on purpose because a full fleet is what fences that lane. A browser-lane run with planted-fault controls is exactly the peer load a clock window cannot tolerate.

CLEARS WHEN: rf2-9wmqd item (c)'s window has been taken. Sequence with rf2-8zhr — same class, adjacent file — and with rf2-7ucn, which is the lift decision and wants both repaired first. Whether these two go as one dispatch or two is a call for whoever briefs them: the surface is genuinely one class across two files, which is the case clustering exists for, but each carries adjacent chains needing individual judgement, which is the case against.
SEVERITY CORRECTED, AND IT IS MUCH WORSE THAN THIS BEAD AND MY OWN VERIFICATION NOTE BOTH SAY. Measured by worker settlerows during rf2-x43z's sabotage run (PR #8677), captured exit 1; recorded here with attribution because I did NOT re-derive it myself.

WHAT THIS BEAD SAYS THE FAULT COSTS: the row hangs to the async timeout and leaks into the next row. That is what I wrote too, from reading the code.

WHAT THE SABOTAGE RUN ACTUALLY SHOWED. With the rejection arm removed, an unsettled rejection is UNHANDLED — it reaches the page as an uncaught error, and the browser runner treats that as TERMINAL. The run stopped at that namespace with 85 namespaces announced, printed NO SUMMARY LINE AT ALL, and every later namespace went SILENTLY UNRUN.

SO THIS IS NOT A HANG COSTING ONE ROW. It is a browser-lane truncation of unknown extent, and the failure mode is the worst kind: no summary line means there is no count to compare against, so a reader looking for "did the lane run everything" has nothing to read. A rejection here does not fail one test — it stops the lane and takes the rest of the suite with it, unreported.

WHY THAT CHANGES THE PRIORITY AND NOT MERELY THE PROSE. A latent defect in a test file is ordinarily P3 hygiene: nothing is broken today because nothing rejects today. But the CONSEQUENCE if something ever does reject is a gate that silently stops testing while looking like it merely failed one thing — and this repo's own standing rule is that a search or instrument returning nothing is not a check that passed. This is that rule's failure mode built into the lane. RAISED P3 -> P2 on that basis.

WHAT IS UNCHANGED: nothing is known to be broken right now, no rejection is known to occur in normal operation, and the repair is the same one either way. This is a re-pricing of the risk, not a new defect, and it is not licence to widen the fix.

That identity is the point: the five operative contract documents rf2-ps7ia moved into implementation/hicasso/spec/ are classified exactly as production CLJS source, because the `implementation/hicasso/*` case arm does not discriminate `.md`. A one-word typo fix in a Markdown register therefore queues cljs_browser, hicasso_controlled and hicasso_hmr -- three Chromium lanes -- plus a ~10-minute CLJS compile.

WHY IT IS A CALL AND NOT A BUG. Two standing principles point opposite ways.
  FOR keeping it: TESTING.md's standing rule is 'when in doubt, over-classify'. Over-arming is the failure mode the repo deliberately prefers, and rf2-8a6s's own comment records that this arm exists precisely because a hicasso-only diff once classified to NOTHING and merged green.
  AGAINST keeping it: the comment block above the complaint-catalogue test in implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs says in terms that 'arming a ~10-minute CLJS compile for a Markdown edit is the trade TESTING.md's placement table exists to refuse'. That sentence was written about these very documents, at their old address.

THE NARROWING, IF MIKE WANTS IT. An `implementation/hicasso/spec/*.md` case placed BEFORE the `implementation/hicasso/*` arm, setting cljs_node_test only. Rationale: what these five documents actually gate is the invariants chain, which is pure Python -- check_complaint_catalogue.py, the budget-ledger reconciliation, the facade-inventory diff -- and Markdown cannot change what React puts on a page, which is the line rf2-drpa3.70 already drew for prose arms and which _changed-surfaces.test.cjs holds for every other prose arm in the file ('prose arms the JVM tier and NO browser/prod/Playwright tier').

WHAT ALREADY STANDS BEHIND THESE DOCUMENTS EITHER WAY, so the narrowing is not as exposed as it looks: all five carry UNCONDITIONAL test.yml jobs of their own -- hicasso-complaint-catalogue, hicasso-budget-ledger and hicasso-facade-inventory each carry no `needs: detect_changed_surfaces` and no `if:`, by design, precisely because a surface gate that did not cover a checker's inputs was the original defect (rf2-hic-021 / rf2-ibje). docs.yml separately arms the warm-allocation scan on implementation/hicasso/spec/budgets.md by name (rf2-ps7ia).

EXECUTION NOTE IF IT IS RULED. .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh and implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs are the one-toucher pair -- the test pins the script's outputs, so this lands in ONE commit touching both, and the row PR #8664 added (implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md arms cljs_node_test=true) stays true under the narrowing while the three Chromium outputs would need new false rows beside it.

title: hicasso: alloc_null_floor.cjs's section E says 'the clean prefix is three rounds long' where its own table four lines above reads round 2 at 12.3%, and it was two rounds on the 242-cell corpus too
description:
FOUND BY THE POST-REPAIR SWEEP rf2-oflj7's remainder asked for, MEASURED 2026-08-21 at
worker/nullfloor-oflj7. NOT one of rf2-oflj7's seven, and NOT stale-by-fold-in: unlike every
claim on that bead, this one appears to have been WRONG WHEN WRITTEN.

THE CLAIM. Section E, four lines below the round-index table it summarises:

  The clean prefix is three rounds long and `warmups` is 3 in every run. THIS READER HAS NOT
  TESTED WHETHER THOSE ARE THE SAME THREE, and proposes no mechanism for the structure.

WHAT THE SAME RUN PRINTS, four lines above it — rounds carrying mode-2 cells:

  round 0 : 0/22   0.0%
  round 1 : 0/63   0.0%
  round 2 : 7/57  12.3%

So the clean prefix is TWO rounds long, not three. The reader's OWN preceding sentence in the
same section says so in as many words: 'round 0 alone, heavily decimated by certification :
0/22 (0.0%)' sits directly above, and the file's header comment (line ~110) states 'Rounds 0
and 1 carry NONE AT ALL'. Three statements in one file, two of them derived, disagreeing with
the third, which is typed.

AND IT WAS NOT THE PHASE-4 FOLD-IN. On the 242-cell corpus the same table read round 0 at
0.0%, round 1 at 0.0% and round 2 at 6.7% (2 of 30) — the frozen studio page
docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-floor-is-two-populations.md prints exactly those rows at its
section E, and its own prose two lines above the claim says 'Rounds 0 and 1 carry none at
all'. The prefix was two rounds long then as well. This is a published error rather than a
figure the corpus moved out from under.

'CLEAN PREFIX' HAS NO OTHER DEFINITION IN THE REPO. git grep -F 'clean prefix' returns three
hits and they are this one sentence in its three copies (the .cjs header comment, the .cjs
report line, the studio page). The sentence's own follow-on — 'whether those are the SAME
THREE' — pairs it with 'warmups is 3', so 'clean prefix' can only mean the leading rounds
carrying no mode-2 cell. Control: git grep -lF 'warmups' returns 189 files, so the pattern
reaches this corpus and the three is a reading.

THE GUARD IS THE HOLLOW SHAPE THIS FAMILY OF BEADS IS ABOUT. The only check on the sentence is

  ck('the report proposes no mechanism for the round structure',
     /THIS READER HAS NOT\n;; {3}TESTED WHETHER THOSE ARE THE SAME THREE/.test(rep), true);

which asks whether a DIFFERENT CLAUSE of the same sentence is present. It passes whatever the
count says, and has done since the sentence was written.

WHY THIS IS A RULING AND NOT A WORKER'S FIX, which is why it was left rather than folded into
rf2-oflj7's PR. The number is load-bearing on the reader's conclusion: 'three' is what makes
the sentence a COINCIDENCE WORTH NOT EXPLAINING ('warmups is 3 ... has not tested whether
those are the same three'). Correcting it to two dissolves the pairing, and the reader then
either says nothing about warmups or says something new about a two-round prefix against a
three-round warmup — which is a claim about MECHANISM, and this reader's standing position is
that it proposes none. Same class as rf2-oflj7's items 5 and 6.

NOT VERIFIED HERE: whether 'warmups is 3 in every run' holds over the 16 runs. It is unguarded
too — no check reads it — but it was out of the sweep's scope.

THE FROZEN PAGE. docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-floor-is-two-populations.md carries the same
sentence at its section E. That page is explicitly frozen at its 242-cell state by its own
banner ('left exactly as it was published'), so whether a published error inside a frozen
record is corrected in place or annotated is part of the same ruling.
notes:
MAYOR — THE ONE THING THIS BEAD RECORDED AS 'NOT VERIFIED HERE' IS NOW MEASURED, and it changes the shape of the ruling rather than merely filling a gap. 2026-08-22 02:3x AUSEST, tip 86702f3ed7.

THE BEAD SAID: 'NOT VERIFIED HERE: whether warmups is 3 in every run. It is unguarded too — no check reads it — but it was out of the sweep's scope.'

MEASURED NOW, by reading the sixteen committed run files the reader's own CORPORA table names (alloc_null_floor.cjs:165-215): alloc-0gjqi/paired-run{1,2}, alloc-fk6pj/seeded-run{1,2}, alloc-legorder/run{1..8}, alloc-passterm/run{1..4}.

CONTROLLED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because a recursive key search returning one constant across sixteen files is exactly the shape a broken search also produces. Asked for a key that does not exist -> ABSENT. Asked for 'samples' on the same files -> sixteen distinct varying arrays. So the finder discriminates and the uniform 3 is a reading, not an artefact.

*** WHAT THIS DOES TO THE RULING. *** The bead's reasoning for calling this Mike's rather than a worker's was that 'three' makes the sentence A COINCIDENCE WORTH NOT EXPLAINING — 'warmups is 3 ... has not tested whether those are the same three' — so correcting the prefix to two DISSOLVES THE PAIRING and forces the reader to say something new about mechanism.

Measured, the sentence carries EXACTLY ONE falsehood and not two: warmups really is 3 everywhere; the clean prefix really is 2. So the pairing the sentence declines to explain DOES NOT EXIST — the two numbers are simply different.

THAT OPENS AN ARM THE BEAD COULD NOT SEE BEFORE THE MEASUREMENT. The reader can state both derived quantities and record that they are NOT the same number. That proposes NO mechanism — it is two counts, differing — which is precisely this reader's standing position rather than a departure from it. The dilemma as written ('say nothing about warmups, or say something new about mechanism') had no third arm; now it has one, and the third arm preserves the position the first two were trying to protect.

I AM NOT RULING IT, and the reasons the bead gives for it being Mike's are not all dissolved: the frozen studio page docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-floor-is-two-populations.md carries the same sentence under an explicit 'left exactly as it was published' banner, and whether a published error inside a frozen record is corrected in place or annotated is a question about the record, not about the number. WHAT GENUINELY REMAINS MIKE'S, and it is one question rather than the two the description implies:
the same sentence exists in three copies, and one of them is the frozen studio page
docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-floor-is-two-populations.md, carried under an explicit "left exactly

The split would decide the reserved question by acting rather than by ruling.

COST OF THE HOLD, priced against a want rather than counted: nothing is queued behind this bead —
no dependants, no edges out. What it costs is that a reader in the tree keeps printing a derived
number that its own table four lines above contradicts, and the only guard on the sentence tests a
DIFFERENT CLAUSE of it, so nothing will ever catch it. That is a live, un-gated falsehood in a

BACKLOG REREAD 2026-08-24 08:12 AUSEST, tip 0bc818e78e. ONE PREMISE ON THIS BEAD IS FALSE. The
conclusion it supports is CORRECT and unchanged; only the evidence for it was wrong.

title: hic: the classifier pair still describes the hicasso contract documents as docs/** — stale premise, fails GREEN
description:
FOUND BY rf2-ps7ia STEP (a) (PR for worker/hicspec-ps7ia). NOT FIXED THERE, deliberately: the two files move in ONE commit by construction (CLAUDE.md's one-toucher pair) and a live peer held .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh at the time.

THE FACT THAT CHANGED. rf2-ps7ia moved five machine-gated documents out of docs/design/hicasso/product/ and into implementation/hicasso/spec/: dispositions.md, complaints.md, invariants.md, naming-ledger.md, budgets.md. Measured at the classifier rather than assumed — the NEW paths return cljs_node_test=true (plus cljs_browser, migration_hicasso_codemod, hicasso_controlled, hicasso_hmr), and the OLD paths returned every output false.

FINDING 1 — A STALE PINNED PREMISE THAT STILL PASSES.
implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs, the test named 'the complaint catalogue reads three families that arm NO expensive tier (rf2-hic-021)', asserts that docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md does not arm cljs_node_test. That file no longer exists. The assertion still PASSES, because the classifier is a lexical path function and does not care whether a path exists — so this is fail-green staleness rather than a break, which is why it is filed rather than urgent. Its ~10-line comment block above it ("reads FOUR file families ... exactly ONE arms cljs_node_test") is now false in the understating direction: the register family arms it now too. The row should either be re-pointed at implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md and INVERTED (it now arms), or dropped with the comment rewritten to say the hole closed. The two SIBLING rows in the same test — spec/009-Instrumentation.md and docs/core/hicasso/02-views-and-reads.md — were re-probed and are STILL false, so they are correct as written and must stay.

FINDING 2 — OVER-ARMING, A JUDGEMENT CALL RATHER THAN A DEFECT.
A markdown-only edit under implementation/hicasso/spec/ now arms cljs_browser, hicasso_controlled and hicasso_hmr as well as cljs_node_test, because the classifier's implementation/hicasso/* arm does not discriminate .md. That is a Chromium lane queued for a prose edit. title: hicasso: alloc_null_floor.cjs's report body still carries six phase-4-stale claims and one unguarded conditional
description:
FOUND BY THE IN-FILE SWEEP rf2-2iaph's brief asked for, MEASURED 2026-08-21 19:24 AUSEST
by running the reader at worker/gapzero-2iaph, not inferred. rf2-2iaph repaired ONE
claim in this file — the verdict's bar clause — and replaced the hollow phrase-matcher
guarding it. Asking the same question of every other claim in the same `report()` found
SIX more of the same class, all made false by the SAME event (a9ec2c662d, the phase-4
fold-in from 242 cells / 3 windows / 3 sessions to 569 / 4 / 5), and one unguarded
conditional. They were left rather than fixed because two of them change what the reader
CONCLUDES, which is a ruling and not a worker's call.

THE DEFECT CLASS, restated: a hardcoded figure or claim in `report()` that the same run's
own derivation contradicts, guarded by nothing or by a check that only tests whether a
string is present.

STALE AGAINST THE PROGRAM'S OWN DERIVED COUNTS — mechanical, no ruling needed:

 1. `WINDOW AND SESSION ARE THE SAME PARTITION HERE ... in this corpus each window is
    exactly one session`. FALSE. The line THREE ABOVE IT prints `TOTAL 569 cells over
    16 runs, 4 windows, 5 sessions.`, and the corpus table above that shows phase 4
    carrying two `sessionStartedAt` values — runs 1-4 at ...T01:23:32.428Z, runs 5-8 at
    ...T02:41:21.789Z. No control at all.
 2. Section C's heading, `THE LADDER, PER WINDOW — which is also per session, see above`.
    False for the same reason. No control.
 3. Section F: `Restricting every window to rounds 0-5, which all eight runs have`.
    There are SIXTEEN runs, which the report also prints itself. No control.
 4. Section D: `its p90 rises from 3 to 9`, in a sentence whose previous clause is
    explicitly first-window-to-last (`1.5 in the first window and 1.5 in the last`).
    The LAST window's mode-1 p90 is 4.5; 9 is phase 3's. No control.

STALE AND ALSO A VERDICT, so these want a ruling rather than a mechanical fix:

 5. The verdict: `IS THE TAIL SESSION-CARRIED? NOT DECIDABLE HERE. Three windows are
    three sessions`. Four windows, five sessions — and this file's OWN HEADER amendment
    3 says the question is now PARTLY ANSWERED: phase 4 is one design held still across
    two sessions, reading 17.7% against 17.2%, `ON THIS EVIDENCE THE SECOND POPULATION
    IS NOT SESSION-CARRIED`. The self-test does not merely miss this — it PINS it:
    `ck('the report says the session question is not decidable here',
    /IS THE TAIL SESSION-CARRIED\? NOT DECIDABLE HERE\./.test(rep), true)`.
 6. The verdict: `WHAT IS MISSING: two sessions on ONE design ... re-running phase 3's
    twelve-round design in a fresh session is the cheapest measurement that would
    separate them`. That measurement has been taken. #8649's doc-side repair of the same
    audit says so in as many words: `That measurement has since been taken.`

A CLAIM WITH NO CONTROL AT ALL:

 7. Section G asserts, unconditionally in prose, that fk6pj's implied delta of 37.8 is
    `below both` — where BOTH are derived and neither is checked. They currently read 60
    (ten times pooled mode-1 p90) and 90 (phase 3's), so the sentence is true today; it
    was 75 and 90 when written, and the header still says 75. Nothing would notice if a
    future window took either below 37.8 and turned `SO THAT REFUSAL STANDS EITHER WAY`
    into a false statement — the only check on it is that the string is present.

WHY THIS IS NOT rf2-2iaph's PR. Items 5 and 6 change what this reader CONCLUDES about
the bead's third question, and 1-4 need a derivation the report does not currently have
(the per-session over-bar breakdown within a window; the 17.7 / 17.2 figures live only in
the header's prose). rf2-2iaph's PR was scoped to the contradiction it names plus the
control that failed to catch it, and its shared-derivation `shape()` object plus the
read-the-numbers-back self-test block are the pattern to extend here.

NOT IN SCOPE HERE: the file's HEADER. Everything above the `const fs = require('fs')` is
deliberately preserved as the record of the 242-cell derivation, under its own amendment
banner, and must stay as written.

title: hicasso: aggregate randomisation band breaks the declared paired two-session assignment
description:
PR #8634's aggregate band samples each of the eight run schedules independently from the 48 per-run admissible schedules (48^8). That is not the assignment support the PR designed or executed: alloc_pass_design.cjs selects two distinct non-complement schedules A/B, adds their exact complements, and pre-registration repeats [A,B,~A,~B] verbatim in session B. The complementary pairing is load-bearing because it is what cancels every round-index nuisance; the cross-session repeat is load-bearing because the page calls the session the independent unit.

Reproduction against the committed eight runs: exhaustively enumerate the ordered design-preserving support [A,B,~A,~B,A,B,~A,~B], B != A and B != ~A. There are 48*46 = 2,208 configurations. The mid-rung result is 6/2208, p=0.002717 (not the published 1/20001 = 0.00005); the null control is 268/2208, p=0.121377 (not 0.0934). Outcome 1 remains at alpha 0.05, but the reported p-values, minimum attainable p, reference quantiles, and claim that the reference uses schedules the design would equally admit are wrong.

Repair the corpus reference so every draw preserves the declared complement pairing and cross-session repeat, add a test pinning that joint support rather than only each run's 48 marginal schedules, and re-adjudicate the published page without rewriting historical provenance pins. If a different reference is intended, state and justify that assignment mechanism without calling it the executed design's randomisation distribution.

title: mayor method: no rule says WHICH CLOCK dates a historical commit in prose, and the liveness rule reads as though it does
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD-REREAD LOOP 2026-08-21, step 2 (checking the rules being ENFORCED against what the tree does). It cost a wrong flag to a live worker the same session.

THE GAP. Both layers state the author-versus-committer distinction, and all FOUR mentions are scoped to LIVENESS — is this worker alive? Measured with a grep over .claude/commands/*.md and docs/the-mayor-method/*.md:

  .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md:12   liveness (tip SHA vs ahead count vs %aI/%cI)
  .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md:30   liveness (same discriminator, stranded sweep)
  docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md:613-616 liveness (generic form of the same)

NOTHING ANYWHERE SAYS WHICH CLOCK TO READ WHEN **DATING** A COMMIT IN PROSE. That is a different question with the OPPOSITE answer, and the liveness rule actively misleads on it.

WHY THE TWO ANSWERS DIVERGE, and it is not a nuance. This repository rebase-merges, so %aI and %cI differ on essentially every merged commit.
  - For LIVENESS, the committer date is right: a rebase rewrites it, so it moves when the worker moves. The author date is replayed unchanged and reads as death.
  - For DATING A HISTORICAL COMMIT IN PROSE, the AUTHOR date is right: it is when the work was actually written. The committer date is an artefact of when the trunk happened to replay it, which is not a fact about the change at all.

A reader who has only ever met the liveness rule has been taught that %aI is the untrustworthy one, and will 'correct' a correct author date to a committer date.

THE MEASURED INSTANCE. A worker dated a set of deletions 2026-08-15 in a design record. The mayor flagged it against CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-16 and had to retract to the operator. Both dates are right and they are different clocks: commit ef3131f4a2 reads author=2026-08-15T20:07:56, committer=2026-08-16T13:29:40. The worker had used the correct clock; the mayor applied the liveness rule to a dating question.

WHERE THE FIX GOES — TWO LAYERS, KEPT APART.
  - docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md, beside the existing liveness passage at 613-616: the GENERIC rule. Which clock answers which question, and why they diverge under rebase. No repository names, bead ids, PR numbers, paths or tool names — that is the method tree's standing constraint.
  - .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md and .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md: the EXECUTING layer, where the concrete command may be named. One clause each, pointing at the generic rule rather than restating it, so the two copies cannot drift.

The point is not to add prose. It is that BOTH questions are now answerable from the same passage, so a reader meeting one cannot mistake it for the other.
notes:
RESOLVED by PR #8630 (branch worker/clockrule-r0hq5).

CENSUS RE-VERIFIED at origin/main before editing: all 4 mentions confirmed, all scoped to liveness. A broad search of the tracked corpus found the dating rule stated nowhere else -- the only other hits are downstream hicasso design records that USE the author date as a practice (the-page-chrome-row-and-what-the-bail-out-costs.md:19 recovers a rebase-merged commit by pairing subject and author date) without ever stating the rule. Corroboration for the fix, not a duplicate of it.

MEASURED INSTANCE verified independently rather than taken from the brief: git log -1 --format=%aI %cI ef3131f4a2 gives author 2026-08-15T20:07:56+10:00, committer 2026-08-16T13:29:40+10:00.

WHAT LANDED, two layers kept apart:
- docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md, +11 lines: the generic rule as a coda to item 1 of The stranded sweep, in the same list item as the liveness passage, so both questions are answerable from one passage. Existing liveness passages untouched. It follows an idiom the file already establishes under Hygiene, where the same rebase invariance is cross-referenced for a third question (containment) rather than restated. Verified mechanically to carry zero repo names, bead ids, PR numbers, paths, tool names or OS mechanics; control: the identical pattern set fires 2x on the command-file half, so the zeros are real.
- mayor-hygiene.md and mayor-posture.md, one clause each, POINTING at the generic rule rather than restating it, so a third and fourth copy cannot drift. mayor-hygiene.md also records the concrete command and the measured instance, which is where this repo already keeps that reasoning.

GATES: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 (covers loops.md) and check_readme_links.py --ci exit 0 (covers the .claude/commands arm). Both were needed -- neither gate covers the other half of the diff. Each was proven to read this worktree by a planted fault that went red naming the plant, then restored and verified by blob hash against the committed object. Both re-run green on the final rebased base. Held off the heavy gates per brief: a clock measurement window was live on the box.

BY HAND (nothing gates prose): the addition introduces 0 markdown links, 0 headings, 0 table rows and 0 code fences, so there are no anchors or column counts to check, and no edit sits inside a fenced block.
MAYOR 2026-08-21 11:30 AUSEST — REOPENED BY THE MERGED-PR AUDIT OF #8630, AND THE FINDING IS CORRECT. FENCED, NOT DISPATCHED.

I read the COMMENT this time rather than the notes field. The marker is a comment created 2026-08-21T01:03:43Z. (An hour earlier I re-closed rf2-csca8 on the strength of an empty notes grep and had to reverse it; see bd memories audit-reopens-are-recorded-as-comments-not-notes.)

WHAT THE AUDIT ESTABLISHED, and it corrects a rule I authored this session. The ef3131f4a2 case is repaired correctly — its author date records the original authoring and its committer date the later rebase replay, so the 2026-08-15 prose needed no correction. But the GENERIC rule overreaches. %aI is Git's AUTHOR-DATE FIELD, not 'when the work was written':
  - git commit --date=<date> overrides it outright.
  - git commit --amend keeps the same author unless --reset-author is passed, so a final commit's %aI can PREDATE content an amend introduced, while %cI dates the rewrite.
  - Autosquashed fixup commits change content or message without changing authorship.
This is not an exotic corner in this repository: scripts/git-hooks/README.md recognises --amend and scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-beads-boundary.sh prescribes it.

THE REPAIR IS TO NAME THE EVENT, NOT TO SWAP ONE UNIVERSAL CLOCK FOR ANOTHER:
  - %aI answers 'what author timestamp is recorded on this commit', and normally survives this repository's ordinary rebase.
  - %cI answers 'what committer timestamp is recorded on this commit object or replay', and normally moves under that rebase.
  - A prose claim about when a particular line or deletion first existed needs ancestry evidence; pick a timestamp only after stating which recorded event the date denotes.
Keep ef3131f4a2 as the concrete case where author-recorded time IS the intended event.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8630 (2026-08-21) — REOPENED THIS EXACT OWNER; NO DUPLICATE BEAD.

CORRECTNESS. The measured ef3131f4a2 case is repaired correctly: its author date records the original authored commit and its committer date records the later rebase replay, so the 2026-08-15 prose need not be “corrected” to 2026-08-16. The generic rule goes further than that evidence permits, however. `%aI` is Git's AUTHOR-DATE FIELD; it is not generally “when the work was written,” and it is not unconditionally the correct clock for dating a change. Git's own documentation says `git commit --date=<date>` overrides the author date; `git commit --amend` creates a new commit with the same author unless `--reset-author` is used, and `--reset-author` is what renews the author timestamp; autosquashed fixup/amend commits can change content or message without changing the original authorship. References: https://git-scm.com/docs/pretty-formats, https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit, https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rebase.

This is not an exotic hostile-input corner here. The tracked workflow explicitly recognizes `git commit --amend` in scripts/git-hooks/README.md and even prescribes it in scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-beads-boundary.sh. A final commit's `%aI` can therefore predate content introduced by an amend/fixup, while `%cI` dates that rewrite; either field can also be explicitly reset or overridden. Neither timestamp proves when particular lines were written.

REPAIR THE RULE BY NAMING THE EVENT, not by swapping one universal clock for another:
- `%aI` answers “what author timestamp is recorded on this commit?” and normally survives this repo's ordinary rebase.
- `%cI` answers “what committer timestamp is recorded on this commit object/replay?” and normally moves under that rebase.
- A prose claim about when a particular deletion or line first existed needs ancestry/commit evidence; choose a timestamp only after stating which recorded event the date denotes.
The ef3131f4a2 example can remain as the concrete case where author-recorded time is the intended event.

COMPLETENESS. The pre-edit census found every existing CLOCK mention but did not inspect the repository's normal history-rewrite operations, so it could not establish the stronger semantic equivalence it landed. Include amend/fixup/explicit-date behavior in the rule's boundary.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY. The PR says the command files “point at the generic rule rather than restating it,” but both execute the same absolute `%aI correct / %cI wrong` conclusion inline, while loops.md carries it a third time. That is three copies of the disputed rule and recreates the drift class the change says it avoids. Keep one authoritative qualified statement and make the command surfaces actual pointers, or mechanically ensure all three remain identical.

title: hicasso: the published non-cancellation floor does not describe the corpus the allocation instrument produces now — 23.2% of the null arm sits above the 45 B/boundary bar
description:
MEASURED by rf2-fk6pj's phase-3 window, 2026-08-21, on 164 null-arm cells. Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-design-control-comes-before-the-window.md, section D. Datasets: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-passterm/.

THE OBSERVATION. The R = 0 null arm reads nothing, so arm minus floor must be zero under either write; it is the only allocation population whose true value is known in advance, and rf2-2rtt6.140 published it as the instrument's NON-CANCELLATION FLOOR — 1.5 B/boundary median, 4.5 B p90 — setting a REFUSAL BAR of 45 B/boundary at ten times the p90. The fraction of that zero-signal population sitting ABOVE that bar has risen across three windows:

  rf2-0gjqi (parity, 2 x 6 rounds)   2 of 38   =  5.3%   p90  4.5
  phase 2   (seeded, 2 x 6 rounds)   4 of 40   = 10.0%   p90 56.5
  phase 3   (seeded, 4 x 12 rounds) 38 of 164  = 23.2%   p90 61

PHASE 2'S EXPLANATION IS REFUTED, and that is the point of filing this. Phase 2 saw its own p90 jump from 4.5 to 56.5 and wrote that it was AN ARTEFACT OF THE COUNT — four outliers in forty putting one exactly at the 90th-percentile index where two in thirty-eight did not. At n = 164 that no longer holds: a quarter of the population above the bar is a distribution, not an index. The full quantile ladder is p50 = 3, p75 = 19.5, p80 = 54.5, p85 = 59.5, p90 = 61, p95 = 64, max 135.5.

WHAT STILL HOLDS, so it is not over-read. The MEDIAN is 0 in every one of the four runs and the ABSOLUTE MEDIAN holds at 3 B/boundary against the published 1.5. The instrument still cancels in the centre. What has changed is the TAIL, and the tail is what the published bar was derived from.

WHY IT MATTERS. Every allocation window's licence to read its mid-rung figures is the null arm reading flat. The mid-rung figures are thousands of bytes per boundary and are unaffected. What IS affected is any statistic of the same order as the tail — and rf2-fk6pj's phase-3 window is exactly that case: its pre-registered band, built at ten times its own null-arm p90, came out at 610 B/boundary and refused a term whose implied delta was 37.8.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED.
* NO MECHANISM IS PROPOSED and none is excluded. The 12-round runs, the seeded pass order, the session length and the box are all confounded with the corpus date.
* IT IS NOT ESTABLISHED THAT THE PUBLISHED BAR IS WRONG. The bar refuses nothing the ladder publishes and nothing here moves it. What is established is that the DISTRIBUTION it was derived from is not the distribution the instrument produces now.
* THE THREE WINDOWS ARE THREE SESSIONS, not 242 independent observations.

WHAT WOULD DECIDE IT. A re-derivation of the floor over the whole committed null-arm corpus rather than one window's 38 cells, reporting the quantile ladder per window and per session, and stating whether the published 1.5 / 4.5 / 45 triple should be re-cut or whether the tail is session-carried. That is a reader over records that already exist and needs no window of its own.

NOT A GATE PROBLEM. Nothing here is fixed by widening a tolerance and no gate behaved incorrectly: all four runs' positive controls passed at 8.00 B/double with 0 unverified read-backs.

title: [bug] check_doc_slugs.py does not validate markdown links inside fenced code blocks — a link gate that fails OPEN
description:

THE FINDING, in the worker's own words: its first planted fault broke a markdown link anchor INSIDE a fenced code block it had just added to spec/Spec-Schemas.md, and scripts/check_doc_slugs.py came back GREEN. A second plant in Spec-Schemas PROSE red at exit 1 naming the planted slug, which both proved the gate read that worktree and pinned the blindness as fence-scoped rather than file-scoped or worktree-scoped.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. This is the same shape as every other fail-open hunted in this repo: a search that returns zero reads identically to a check that passed. A broken link inside a fence is invisible, so an edit confined to a fenced block — and spec/Spec-Schemas.md's *Tags schemas all live inside fences — is UNGATED while the PR body truthfully reports check_doc_slugs.py exit 0. The worker hand-verified its own link because it had caught this; the next author will not know to.

VERIFY THE PREMISE FIRST, at origin/main HEAD, and do it in BOTH directions: plant a broken link target inside a fenced block (expect green, which is the defect) and the same target in prose (expect red, which is the control). A one-direction probe cannot tell blindness from a bad plant.

title: ci: a stale SETUP_PATTERNS entry fails check_fast_pr_gap.py OPEN with exit 0 — nothing in CI catches it
description:
MEASURED BY PLANTING under rf2-mul6w (PR #8539). Every premise is reproducible.

WHAT WAS PLANTED. In a worktree carrying the 14 prefixed Playwright call sites (`timeout -k 10 720 npx playwright install ...`), the SETUP_PATTERNS entry was reverted to its pre-fix form `^npx playwright install\b` — i.e. exactly the drift this bead is about: a setup pattern that no longer matches the call sites it covers.

WHAT HAPPENED. `python scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py` (the default --check mode) EXITED 0 and printed 'fast-PR gap map clean'. The only visible effect was the headline count moving from 'REQUIRED CHECKS THIS SPINE DOES NOT RUN (96)' to (106), with 10 toolchain-setup steps silently reclassified as unrun GATES — each listed with its own reproduce command telling a reader to run `npx playwright install` locally.

WHY THAT IS THE WRONG DIRECTION. The file's own docstring states the safe direction — 'a new CI job or a new step inside an existing one is reported as UNRUN until somebody teaches this file otherwise' — and that is true for the LANES. It is not true for SETUP_PATTERNS, where the same drift inflates the gap map with false entries and no exit code changes. The header of .github/scripts/playwright-install-failed.sh calls this 'a fail-open in the very map the merge criterion consults', which is precisely right, and nothing detects it.

THE DRIFT RATCHET DOES NOT COVER THIS. `--check`'s ratchet fires when a SPINE_LANES signature stops matching any required gate step. A SETUP_PATTERNS entry that stops matching has no equivalent: it produces MORE unrun entries, which reads as normal.

SHAPE OF A FIX (not prescriptive). A floor per setup pattern — 'this entry must match at least one required step' — would catch it the same way MIN_REQUIRED_JOBS and MIN_SPINE_CHECKERS catch an empty parse, and in the same spirit. A pattern that matches nothing is either dead or drifted, and both are worth a red.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN #8539. That PR was fenced to closing the annotation gap without fail-opening this map, and it proved by planting that its own pattern-and-call-site change keeps `--list` byte-identical. Adding a new ratchet arm to the gate is a separate change to a hot-zone file.

VERIFICATION ALREADY DONE, reusable here: planting a NON-timeout prefix (`nice -n 5 npx playwright install ...`) at one site moves the count 96 -> 97, so the map does discriminate — it just does not fail.
close_reason: Fixed in this PR. REPRODUCED the fail-open first: reverting the Playwright SETUP_PATTERNS entry to its pre-timeout form took --check's headline 96 -> 106 with exit 0 and 'fast-PR gap map clean'; --self-test also passed. The bead's sketched fix DOES NOT WORK and the measurement says so: 3 of the 13 required Playwright installs are still written bare, so a per-pattern 'matches at least one required step' floor stays GREEN under that exact drift while 10 steps silently become gates. Fix instead watches the CLASSIFICATION: SETUP_CANARIES names a TOOL where SETUP_PATTERNS names a CALL SHAPE, and a required GATE step whose EVERY line is nothing but toolchain installation is a problem. Post-fix the same plant exits 1 with 10 problems naming each drifted call site. The new arm immediately found two LIVE instances of the same class: both 'npm install --no-audit --no-fund' steps were reported as required checks the spine does not run; '^npm install$' widened to long-flag form, and --list loses exactly those two entries (96 -> 94), a narrowing in the correct direction. Self-tests exercise the arm against the known-WRONG answer, the negative control, and the floor that would have passed the failing case.

title: ci: the 300s Playwright step cap is now 1.8x its worst observed success, not 6.1x — a judgement for Mike
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-mul6w (PR #8539), which was fenced OUT of changing any cap. Filing rather than acting.

MEASURED 2026-08-20 over the 140 most recent completed test.yml runs (window 2026-08-18T05:11Z .. 2026-08-20T10:13Z, ALL attempts, every step named 'Install Playwright*'): 377 non-skipped samples, 370 successes.

THE POPULATION THE CAP NOTE DESCRIBES IS GONE. rf2-g3lv's note above the cljs-reagent-slim-bundle-isolation install step recorded 'p50 13s, p90 21s, max 49s. The 300s cap is 6.1x the observed worst case.' Re-derived: p50 14s and p90 34s still, but p95 113s, p99 424s, MAX 621s. FOUR of the 370 successes finished ABOVE 300s (424s, 556s, 589s, 621s).

WHY THAT IS NOT YET AN EMERGENCY. All four sit at jobs with NO step-level cap. Across the three step-capped sites (cljs-reagent-slim-bundle-isolation, tenant-switcher-testbed-smoke, mcp-conformance-re-frame2-pair) the worst success is 164s over 80 samples, so the 300s cap is 1.8x its own site's worst case. Clear, but not the comfortable margin the note claims.

WHY IT MIGHT BE ONE. Two of the five install stalls measured on 2026-08-19 were at step-capped sites and died at 312s and 313s (jobs 95959283361, 95932283494) — i.e. AT the cap. Given four uncapped-site successes ran past 300s in the same window, those two are consistent with installs that would have completed given more time, which would make them cap-induced reds rather than genuine outages. Not established either way; distinguishing them needs the raw apt/download timings from those two logs.

THE DECISION IS MIKE'S. rf2-g3lv says DO NOT RAISE THIS NUMBER, and its reasoning still stands on its own terms: the cap exists to bound the rf2-e6enf wedge where four PRs sat 15-75+ min on an apt/dpkg lock. Raising it re-widens exactly that window. So this is a trade between two real costs, not a bug with a fix. rf2-mul6w corrected the stale numbers in the comment and left the cap untouched.

PR #8539 already: re-derived the rate, corrected both stale claims in test.yml's comment block, and closed the no-annotation gap at the 14 job-capped sites.
notes: COST OF THIS HOLD, recorded 2026-08-20 23:50 AUSEST, backlog reread. Checked at source: this bead has NO dependants — nothing blocks on it and nothing stops if it stays. It is a standalone judgement about whether the 300s Playwright step cap should move now that it sits at 1.8x its worst observed success rather than 6.1x. The cost of waiting is that the cap stays where it is; the cost of getting it wrong in either direction is a flaky gate or a slow one. Recorded so it does not read as free and does not get re-triaged every tick.
close_reason:
MIKE'S RULING, 2026-08-21: ACCEPT THE TIGHTER MARGIN. The 300s Playwright step cap STAYS where it is. His stated warrant: it has not been tripped recently. No change to any workflow file; this bead closes on a decision to leave things as they are, which is why there is no PR to cross-reference.

WHAT THIS DECIDES, so a future reader does not re-derive it: the cap sitting at 1.8x its worst observed success rather than the original 6.1x is ACCEPTED as a margin, not treated as a defect. The ratio moving is not by itself grounds to raise the cap.

ONE THING I CHECKED AND AM RECORDING RATHER THAN SUPPRESSING, because it neither overturns the ruling nor deserves to be lost: of the last 40 'tests' workflow runs sampled at close time, 5 succeeded, 2 were still running and 1 was CANCELLED. A cancellation is not a cap trip — the method's own discriminator is elapsed time against the declared cap, where landing ON the cap is a timeout kill and finishing well inside it is a superseding push or a hand cancel, and supersessions are routine under a busy fleet. I did not establish which this was, so it is recorded as unexamined rather than as evidence either way.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS: an actual trip — a Playwright step cancelled at or near 300s elapsed. That is the signal, not the ratio.

title: hicasso: the floor arm's mode RATE is not a property of the revision — 0%, 10% and 53% at 4a1537cb71
description:
MEASURED by rf2-c4hhk's seventy-run window (PR #8531), record docs/design/hicasso/studio/does-arming-the-census-move-the-high-level.md, 70 datasets under implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-c4hhk/. Filed rather than chased: rf2-c4hhk was sent to answer the armed/unarmed confound and did, and this is a second finding from the same data.

THE OBSERVATION. Three windows at the SAME revision (4a1537cb71), on the SAME instrument (no bench file has changed since 408dfb0aa8), with the SAME plan (floor, write-all, ROOTS=4, CELLS=6, ROUNDS=18) and the SAME estimator, produce three incompatible rates for the elevated mode:

  rf2-n1b9h    6 runs    0 high     0%
  rf2-77gz8   20 runs    2 high    10%
  rf2-c4hhk   69 runs   37 high    53%

WHY IT IS NOT AN ARMING EFFECT, which is the first thing to exclude and the one thing this data can exclude cleanly. rf2-c4hhk alternated armed and unarmed runs strictly, and BOTH ARMS MOVED TOGETHER: 52.9% armed (18 of 34) against 54.3% unarmed (19 of 35). An arming effect would have separated them; an environment effect moves both, and did. rf2-n1b9h's 0% was all-armed and rf2-77gz8's 10% was all-armed, so neither of those is an arming contrast either.

WHY IT MATTERS. Every measurement window on this arm SIZES ITS RUN COUNT against a prior rate, and a pre-declared count is the one thing in these windows that cannot be revised after the fact. rf2-77gz8 sized twenty runs against a re-derived 1-in-7 and got 2 of 20; rf2-c4hhk sized seventy against a re-derived 8.7% on the binding arm and got 53%, i.e. it took roughly four times the runs it needed. The error runs in the expensive direction here, but a window sized against 53% when the box happens to be in the 0% state would produce a null and report a refusal, and the refusal would be an artefact of the sizing rather than a fact about the arm. So this is a live risk to the METHOD, not only an oddity.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is most of it. Nothing here identifies what the rate depends on. The three windows differ in wall-clock date, in what else the box was doing, and in nothing that any dataset records. Candidates worth separating, none of them supported yet: machine load or thermal state at the time of the window; a resident-runtime difference (the Chromium binary is pinned by playwright but the datasets do not record its build); and a within-window ordering effect, since rf2-c4hhk's runs were back-to-back for ninety minutes where earlier corpora were not.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, or at least bound it. The cheap first move is to record what the datasets currently do not: the Chromium build string, the box's load at window open, and the elapsed time since the previous run, all of which ride free on an existing field the way rf2-n1b9h's census does. That converts the next window into evidence about the rate at no extra runner cost. A DELIBERATE variation — the same plan run cold, run hot, and run after an idle gap — is the confirming second move and should not be taken first.

NOTE this bead is about the RATE only. The LEVELS are settled: rf2-c4hhk established that arming moves neither, and the level values themselves reproduce to the byte across all three windows.

  workcount-n1b9h   6 runs   0 high    0.0%

WHAT THE DATA ALREADY ANSWERS, and it is this bead's own first-named candidate. `generatedAt` is recorded on every run, so the within-window ordering effect is testable NOW without recording anything new:

  session DURATION vs rate      n1b9h  8.2 min -> 0%    77gz8 19.7 min -> 10%    c4hhk 88.3 min -> 53.6%
  c4hhk BY ELAPSED QUARTER      Q1 5/19 = 26.3%   Q2 12/18 = 66.7%   Q3 10/17 = 58.8%   Q4 10/15 = 66.7%

The Q1-vs-rest contrast is a WITHIN-SESSION comparison at ONE revision on ONE box, so it separates elapsed time from wall-clock date and from revision — one-tail hypergeometric P(<=5 high in the first 19 | 37/69 overall) = 0.0054.

And once you condition on the early-session rate the "three incompatible rates" stop being incompatible: at p = 0.263, P(0 high of 6) = 0.16 for n1b9h and P(<=2 of 20) = 0.072 for 77gz8 — neither surprising. Against the POOLED 53.6% they are: 77gz8's 2 of 20 has p = 5.9e-05. So the three rates are consistent with ONE within-session gradient plus sampling, rather than three properties of three revisions.

STATED AT ITS TRUE STRENGTH. This locates the rate on elapsed-time-within-session; it does NOT name a mechanism (thermal, V8 tier accumulation, heap fragmentation over a long session all survive), and across the three corpora duration is confounded with date and time-of-day. The within-c4hhk gradient is the arm that is NOT so confounded.

(1) THE QUARTILE p IS BOUNDARY-SENSITIVE, and the boundary is a choice rather than a measurement. P(at most 5 high among the first k of 69 | 37 high) reads 0.0210 at k=17, 0.0109 at k=18, 0.0054 at k=19 and 0.0025 at k=20 -- an EIGHTFOLD move across a two-run choice -- and a first-half/second-half split gives 0.093. The page therefore leads with a test that has NO cut point: Mann-Whitney on each run's position in its session, high against low, U = 763 against a null mean of 592, z = 2.058, ONE-TAIL p = 0.0198. The gradient is real at about p = 0.02, not p = 0.005. The reader's fixtures REQUIRE the sweep to move at least fourfold across the cut and require the boundary-free test to come out weaker than the best cut, so a change that made the quartile figure look robust reds them.

THE HONEST BOUND, AND IT SURVIVED INTO THE RECORD IN THREE PLACES -- the page's summary, its body at length, and four reader fixtures that pin it as literals, because it is the half a write-up is most likely to lose. alloc-9jrhi's single high run sits at +3.6 min, SECOND of eight, in a 14.9-minute session.   spec/001-Registration.md:85 carries the registration GRAMMAR — that reg-view is the only registration shipping as a defn-shape macro, with reg-view* as the plain-fn partner for runtime and programmatic registration.

title: [hic] TRIAGE ONLY: classify the 64 hicasso product files by KIND — the number rf2-ps7ia turns on
description:
REQUESTED BY MIKE, 2026-08-19 10:13 AUSEST. This is a MEASUREMENT bead. It moves nothing, edits nothing, and rules nothing. Its whole deliverable is a classification and a set of counts.

WHY IT EXISTS. rf2-ps7ia must decide where the hicasso normative set lives, and that decision reads very differently depending on how much of the set is actually normative. Nobody has counted. The mayor twice said 'roughly forty files' in chat; the measured figure is SIXTY-FOUR files and 17,044 lines under docs/design/hicasso/product/, with thirteen of those in the lanes/ subtree, against 131 files across the whole docs/design/hicasso/ tree. So the estimate was low by half, which is itself the argument for counting before deciding.

THE QUESTION THIS ANSWERS: is the hicasso spec tree a four-file job or a thirty-file programme? If it is small, rf2-ps7ia is easy and can be executed in one pass. If it is large, it is a sequenced programme and needs to be planned as one.

=== WHAT TO DO ===

Classify EVERY file under docs/design/hicasso/product/ into exactly one of four kinds. Report the counts, and the per-file assignment as a table.

1. VIEW SPECIFICATION — normative statements about how a view is AUTHORED in hicasso. The thing a consumer must obey to write hicasso views correctly. This is the kind with no current home, which is what makes the count matter.
2. SUBSTRATE CONTRACT — normative statements about what a SUBSTRATE must provide. These already have a home in spec/ proper: 004B carries the structural render-tree ABI, 004C root identity and the mount grammar, 006 the substrate contract. If a file is this kind, name which of those it belongs beside.
3. READER-FACING ANSWER — content a hicasso user needs, which belongs stated on a guide page under docs/core/hicasso/ rather than in a design record. Precedent: rf2-75q3l, where three published pages routed readers into an excluded tree and the fix was to make the pages answer their own questions rather than relocate anything.
4. WORKING RECORD — provenance, measurement windows, budgets, decision history. These stay exactly where they are; docs/design is the right tree for them and their provenance pins are gated there.

A file may be MIXED. Say so explicitly rather than forcing it, and give the rough proportion — a 90% working record with one normative paragraph is a very different problem from a half-and-half file, and the mixed count is one of the numbers the decision turns on.

=== ESTABLISHED CONTEXT — verify each at source, do not inherit ===

MIKE'S DIRECTION, 2026-08-19: an artefact-local implementation/hicasso/spec/ folder IS the likely destination for kind 1, CONDITIONAL on spec/ not carrying view specification. THE CONDITION HOLDS: spec/README.md:66 states in terms 'There is no 004 view contract.' spec/004-Views.md and the S3/S4/S5 view-conformance profiles were deleted under rf2-h89ri (PR #8500), and the hole was DECLARED rather than papered over. What survives — 004B, 004C, 006 — is substrate-facing, not view-authoring.

THE PRECEDENT for an artefact-local spec tree is tools/: seven of them carry one (xray, story, template, machines-viz, mcp-base, story-mcp, re-frame2-pair-mcp). There is currently NO spec/ or design/ directory anywhere under implementation/ — this would be the first.

=== TWO RIDERS TO REPORT ON, NOT TO FIX ===

A. THE GATE GAP. scripts/check_doc_slugs.py has DEFAULT_ROOTS of docs, spec, skills, migration, plus an explicit special case for tools/<tool>/spec/**. implementation/** is in NEITHER, and check_readme_links.py reaches only READMEs beside source. So a normative tree at implementation/hicasso/spec/ would be UNGATED from day one — no link or anchor validation. Confirm that at source and say what the smallest correct fix looks like. DO NOT BUILD IT.

B. A POSSIBLE RULING COLLISION. rf2-h89ri deliberately wrote NO 'see hicasso' pointer into spec when it declared the hole, citing rf2-0yp7w.11. A reader hitting 'there is no 004 view contract' should eventually be told where the view spec lives. Read rf2-0yp7w.11 and say whether it forbids that pointer, or whether it only forbade re-aiming RETIRED freehand/ui material at hicasso. Those are different, and the mayor has not verified which.

=== SCOPE FENCE ===

NO MOVES. NO EDITS to any classified file. NO new spec tree. NO gate change. The deliverable is a report and, if it is useful, ONE new working document recording the classification.

Out of scope: the whole of docs/design/hicasso/ outside product/ (the other 67 files) unless your reading shows product/ cannot be classified without them — in which case say so and stop rather than widening.

DO NOT rule rf2-ps7ia. That decision is Mike's and this bead exists to inform it.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

1. Every one of the 64 files assigned a kind, or explicitly marked mixed with a proportion.
2. Counts per kind, and a line count per kind — a four-file kind carrying 6,000 lines is not small.
3. For kind 2, the spec/ document each file belongs beside.
4. The two riders reported with source citations.
5. A one-paragraph answer to the question that prompted this: is the view-specification set a small job or a programme?
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #8522 (2026-08-20): reopen exact owner. The delivered census is internally inconsistent about the number of view-specification carriers. Its own per-file classification attributes VS content to 12 files (lanes/adversarial-risks, design-laws, ergonomics-api, hot-path-architecture, react-compatibility-notes, testing-xray, use-cases; plus specification, invariants, facade-freeze, dispositions, complaints), while the headline and conclusion say seven documents. The section titled 'What the seven view-specification carriers actually hold' contains eight rows summing about 1,001 VS lines and silently omits four classified carriers totaling about 135 more lines (adversarial-risks ~15, hot-path ~21, use-cases ~7, complaints ~92), which is how the headline total reaches ~1,136. Acceptance: distinguish the seven files whose PRIMARY kind is VS from all 12 files carrying attributed VS; reconcile the headline, carrier table, small-job conclusion, and owner summary; include or explicitly justify excluded carriers; recompute totals if any classification changes.
close_reason: RECONCILED. PR #8551 (draft->ready) closes the AUDIT-REOPEN #8522 finding. No classification changed; the page now states both file counts (7 primary VS, 12 carrying any VS), lists all twelve carriers so the table reconciles with the headline, and re-derives every count at commit 5858e9317a. Counts and both riders are recorded in full on the bead comment above so rf2-ps7ia can read them without opening the file. Answer unchanged and strengthened: a SMALL JOB (~1,138 normative lines, under 7%, three or four authored documents in one pass), NOT a thirty-file programme — but plan the reading against twelve carriers, not seven, and expect a rewrite in voice rather than a move.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RECONCILED, 2026-08-20. PR #8551 (draft) closes the AUDIT-REOPEN #8522 finding. The audit reproduces exactly: the delivered census attributed VS content to 12 files but titled its carrier section 'the seven', listed 8 rows in it (one of them dispositions.md, not a primary carrier), and omitted 4 carriers worth ~135 lines — so the table summed ~1,001 against a headline of ~1,136.

NO CLASSIFICATION CHANGED. Every file holds the kind and proportion first assigned. The fix is presentational + arithmetic: the headline table gains a 'Files (any share)' column beside 'Files (primary)', the carrier section lists all twelve and marks the seven primary, and the conclusion/bullets/closing note are reconciled to the same pair.

=== COUNTS, RE-DERIVED AT COMMIT 5858e9317a (not inherited) ===
Population:  64 files / 17,054 lines under docs/design/hicasso/product/
             13 files / 947 lines in lanes/; 5 files / 707 lines in pilots/;

=== THE 12 VS CARRIERS (7 primary marked *) ===

§§2-3,5 ~136 | *lanes/ergonomics-api.md ~113 | *invariants.md §§1-4 ~95 |

~47 | *lanes/design-laws.md §§1-4 ~44 | lanes/hot-path-architecture.md ~21 |

Seven primary hold ~799; the five minority hold ~339. The four the old section
omitted were complaints/hot-path/adversarial-risks/use-cases = ~134.

=== MIXED ===
18 of 64 mixed; 46 single-kind and ALL 46 are working record. Every one of the
12 carriers is mixed — NOT ONE FILE in this tree is purely view specification.
lanes/ergonomics-api.md is closest at ~95%. Zero files resisted the four
categories.

=== KIND 2 IS EMPTY AT FILE GRANULARITY ===
No file is a substrate contract. Three minority slices only: substrate-decision.md
~82 -> spec/006; invariants.md §7 ~12 -> spec/006; specification.md §4 ~3 ->
spec/004C. Nothing is 004B material as a STATEMENT (the test kit CONSUMES the
structural tree ABI).

=== ANSWER FOR rf2-ps7ia: A SMALL JOB, NOT A PROGRAMME ===
~1,138 normative lines, under 7% of 17,054, heavily transcribed between carriers
(invariants.md and facade-freeze.md both say of themselves they ADD NOTHING).
De-duplicated, plausibly under 1,000 lines across three or four authored
documents — one pass. Plan the READING against 12 and the WRITING against 3-4.
What WOULD be a programme is moving FILES: 53 of 64 are working records, and
every carrier is mixed, so any file-level move drags working record into spec/
or tears a document. Also: it is a REWRITE IN VOICE, not a move — 1 RFC-2119
keyword across all 64 files vs 35 in spec/006 alone.

=== RIDERS, re-confirmed at HEAD ===
A. GATE GAP CONFIRMED. check_doc_slugs.py DEFAULT_ROOTS=(docs,spec,skills,
migration) at :93, TOOLS_ROOT at :101, walk at :716-724. 'implementation' appears
only at :637/:967 as prose. check_readme_links.py reaches only README.md beside
source. mkdocs docs_dir is 'docs'. So implementation/hicasso/spec/ would be
UNGATED from day one. Smallest fix (NOT built): a second root constant giving
implementation/<artefact>/spec the same deep walk as the existing TOOLS_ROOT arm,
~7 lines, plus its own self-test row (a walk finding no directory exits 0).
B. NO RULING COLLISION. rf2-0yp7w.11 forbids RENAMING/RE-AIMING the retired
004D donor document at hicasso; it does not forbid a pointer, and it explicitly
contemplates 'whoever later writes a hicasso-native grammar spec'. Decisive:
such a pointer ALREADY EXISTS, landed and gated — spec/009's Hicasso section
names docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md and says 'When a Hicasso Spec
lands, these rows gain their link'. Correction to how it is cited: rf2-h89ri
calls it 'Mike's own ruling', but rf2-0yp7w.11 records itself as taken under the
rf2-0yp7w landing-order ruling — DELEGATED and operator-reversible.

MEASUREMENT CAVEAT: on this host, mixing a positive pathspec with a ':!'

title: [retire] R6 method+residue: the NUMBER form 'Spec 004' — 102 hits / 55 files no census has ever seen
description:

This is the SAME defect rf2-3l1xe and rf2-g633h recorded for 004D ("a fourth spelling"), recurring one document over — the fix was recorded as a pattern to add, not as a rule that a deleted spec must be swept in BOTH spellings.

Positive control: 'Spec 004B'/'Spec 004C' resolve (both files exist, git ls-files 'spec/004*' returns exactly 004B and 004C). Negative control on the same pattern under skills/ after slice 4's repair returns exit 1.

THE SHAPE OF THE SURFACE:
  implementation/**  ~50 hits / 25 files  (core/src, core/test, ssr/src, adapters/reagent/test, epoch, scripts)
  tools/**           ~19 hits / 15 files  (xray src+spec+testbeds, story src+spec, machines-viz)
  docs/EP/**         ~13 hits /  7 files  -- ARCHIVAL, out of scope by standing ruling
  docs/design/**      ~4 hits /  3 files  -- ARCHIVAL, out of scope by standing ruling
  spec/**             ~7 hits /  7 files  -- HOT ZONE, one toucher
  TESTING.md            1 hit            -- dated measurement, NOT SWEPT per rf2-v68fz

WHY SLICE 4 DID NOT SWEEP IT, three independent reasons:
  1. FENCE. Slice 4's fence was the four named pockets. It repaired the one site it owned (skills/re-frame2-improver/spec/design.md:83) and stopped.
  2. LIVE PEERS. tools/xray/** and spec/Conventions.md were held by one worker and implementation/core/src/** by another at the time of measurement.

title: spec/Conventions.md's 'internal seam' names a direct :require that collector.cljs does not have
description:
*** DISPOSITION: RETIRE THE PORT. HELD FOR MIKE. DO NOT DISPATCH THIS AS A PROSE FIX. ***

READ THIS BEFORE BRIEFING FROM ANYTHING BELOW. The (a)/(b) fork set out in the description
was SETTLED on 2026-08-18 and the answer is (b): re-frame.substrate.observation has NO
consumer outside its own tests, by ANY route. Three workers have now been dispatched at this
fork (2026-08-20 10:07, 2026-08-20 11:46, 2026-08-21 04:20) and all three correctly returned
a source-located NO EDIT. Each cost a full worker cycle for nothing.

WHY IT KEEPS HAPPENING, recorded so it stops: the warning lived only in NOTES while briefs
were being written from this DESCRIPTION, which is the oldest text on the bead. This banner
is the fix. Everything below the fold is history, not instructions.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED, each measured with a positive control rather than a bare zero:
- collector.cljs's ns form carries no port require. It calls subs/compute-sub-with-memo, the
  same fn the port itself calls at observation.cljc:1691 - a PEER consumer of that core seam,
  not a consumer of this port.
- Fork (a) is closed BY DIRECTION OF DEPENDENCY, not by an absent grep. subs.cljc:2232-2234
  marks that fn an observation-port internal entry point. THE PORT CONSUMES SUBS, not the
  reverse. interop requires only goog.async.nextTick and late-bind. Both candidate indirect
  routes are dead.
- Census with .beads excluded: five requires tree-wide, all test namespaces, ZERO under any
  src/. Control: the spine namespace returns 14 edges including four src requires.
- NO BUILD-CONFIG CONSUMER EITHER. Every .edn, .json, .cjs, .sh, .yml and .yaml swept for a
  :preloads, :entries, :modules, deps-alias or gate-script route: zero hits, against two
  positive controls.

THE PROSE IS ALREADY CORRECT AND NEEDS NO EDIT. PR #8490 landed the fix: Conventions.md:1730
no longer names hicasso, no longer names collector.cljs, and asserts no live edge; :1732
states the fact in bold and cites this bead. Nothing unambiguously true is left to land, and
both near-miss candidates sit inside material the RETIRE ruling deletes, so editing them
plants a rebase conflict in the retirement's own path.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY OWED: Mike's product call on retiring re-frame.substrate.observation - live
shipped core code carrying a port-abi-version guard and a DEV-ONLY G-13 witness, exercised
only by its own tests. Ruled RETIRE 2026-08-19 01:20, held for Mike. Nothing else.

--- ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION FOLLOWS (2026-08-18, superseded above) ---

Found by the rf2-0yp7w.9 source-comment slice (PR #8485) while verifying, rather than assuming, whether 'compiled-view substrate' prose in implementation/core/src still described a live consumer class.

THE CLAIM. spec/Conventions.md:1730 defines the INTERNAL SEAM concept: 'a core-shipped namespace a named sibling artefact consumes by direct `:require` â€” neither public API nor an optional-capability hook. There is currently one such seam: `re-frame.substrate.observation`... its named consumer is the `day8/re-frame2-hicasso` view runtime (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/collector.cljs`).'

THE MEASUREMENT. collector.cljs's ns form (line 400) requires re-frame.adapter.context, the six re-frame.hicasso.impl.* siblings, re-frame.frame, re-frame.interop, re-frame.live-frame, re-frame.performance, re-frame.registrar, re-frame.subs and react. There is NO re-frame.substrate.observation require. Its three mentions of the port (lines 234, 607, 657) are all inside docstrings/comments, comparing disciplines.

Tree-wide, the ONLY real requires of the port are TEST namespaces:
  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/observation_port_activates_ratom_node_cljs_test.cljs:59
  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/observation_port_watchable_host_cljs_test.cljs:75
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/read_attribution.clj:176
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/observation_drain_elision_prod_test.cljs:29
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/observation_port_cljs_test.cljc:84,3612
Positive control on the same pattern: `[re-frame.substrate.spine` finds the three adapter requires, so the grep discriminates and the empty src result is not a false empty.

SO ONE OF TWO THINGS IS WRONG, and which one is a design question rather than a typo:
  (a) the seam definition's 'consumes by direct :require' clause overstates how Hicasso
      actually reaches the port (it may go through re-frame.subs / re-frame.interop), in
      which case Conventions' wording and possibly Spec 006's consumer story need
      correcting; or
  (b) collector.cljs is supposed to consume the port directly and does not, in which case
      the port currently ships with no non-test consumer at all.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. The retirement of re-frame.ui removed the port's original consumer.
