MAYOR RULING, 2026-08-18 23:42 AUSEST — CONDITIONAL, WITH A SOURCE-CHECKABLE DISCRIMINATOR. Taken on Mike's standing delegation. The prose half landed in PR #8490; what remained was the disposition, and this settles it.

THE STATE OF PLAY, re-derived at origin/main 4852631958. re-frame.substrate.observation is live shipped core code whose only real requires are TEST namespaces — two reagent adapter tests, bench/read_attribution.clj, observation_drain_elision_prod_test.cljs and observation_port_cljs_test.cljc. Its original consumer went with re-frame.ui. Hicasso's collector.cljs was believed to consume it and does not; it reaches reactivity through re-frame.subs and re-frame.interop. So the port ships with no non-test consumer, and it carries a port-abi-version guard and a DEV-ONLY G-13 witness whose value depends on there being a real one.

RULING: RETIRE THE PORT — UNLESS spec/006 MANDATES IT AS A CONTRACT SURFACE. Establish that first; it decides the whole bead and it is a read, not a judgement.

WHY THE CONDITION IS NOT A FUDGE. The two answers are different KINDS of thing, and only a source read separates them. If spec/006 names the observation port as a seam a substrate MUST provide, the port is a contract with a currently-empty consumer set, and retiring it is a spec change requiring its own ruling — it is not dead code, it is an unexercised obligation. If spec/006 does not, it is an implementation detail whose consumer was deleted, and it is dead code wearing a guard.

WHY RETIRE IS THE DEFAULT AND NOT KEEP-PARKED. The stance is explicit: pre-alpha, no back-compat shims, reject over-engineering. Parking is the 'preserve everything just in case' default, and a stance exists precisely to refuse it. The five test namespaces are not independent value — they test the port itself, so they cannot vote for its survival. And the port-abi-version guard and G-13 witness are the sharper argument FOR retirement rather than against it: a guard whose value depends on a consumer that does not exist is a hollow control, and this project's own rule is that a hollow control is REPLACED, not patched, because the next reader trusts it harder for having a history of being fixed. Keeping it parked keeps two controls that assert nothing while looking like coverage.

WHAT I AM NOT RULING: give-it-a-consumer is OUT, and it needs no investigation. Writing a consumer to justify shipped code is making work to preserve a decision nobody has defended, which is the clearest case of the gold-plating the stance rejects.

SCOPE FOR THIS PASS — DO NOT RETIRE THE PORT IN THIS PR. Establish the discriminator at source, record the answer on this bead with the evidence, and STOP. If spec/006 does not mandate it, the retirement is its own dispatch with its own fence: it deletes shipped core code, five test namespaces and two controls, and it deserves a worker whose whole context is that. If spec/006 DOES mandate it, say so and the bead becomes an operator ruling on the spec, which I will surface to Mike.

OUT-OF-FENCE RESIDUE ALREADY TRACKED, so it is not swept here: rf2-2n92u carries spec/Ownership.md:31 and spec/009:1985, which still name hicasso as the consumer.

This note is a CLAIM. Re-derive every require, line number and the spec/006 text at origin/main HEAD before acting.

EVIDENCE, QUOTED.

1. spec/006:103-111, a blockquote inside the section that DEFINES the adapter contract:
   "**The internal observation port is not part of this contract.** A re-frame-native view substrate reads subscriptions through an adapter-internal observation port ... that lives **outside** this closed ten-fn map: no entry is added to the adapter spec map, no signature here changes, and existing adapters implement nothing new."
   The same blockquote already carries "though no shipped namespace requires the port today (see the scope section below)".

2. spec/006:1192-1193, the port section's own status block:
   "This port is INTERNAL -- it is NOT part of the public adapter API contract; see the scope statement below."

3. spec/006:1204, the scope heading, and 1206-1214 under it:
   "### Scope -- outside the closed public adapter contract, one named consumer"
   "The port is **adapter-internal**: a private surface between the core's sub-cache and a re-frame-native substrate's view runtime ... It is **not** an entry in the adapter spec map. The public adapter API contract remains exactly as [The adapter API contract] states it -- six required functions, three optional functions, one lifecycle function, plus the `:kind` discriminator (the 11-key adapter spec map) -- **closed for v1**. Existing adapters (Reagent, reagent-slim, UIx, plain-atom, SSR) implement none of the port's operations and are unchanged by this section. No feature predicate is added; a consumer cannot branch on the port's presence because the port is not consumable."

THE SENTENCE THAT SETTLES IT is "Existing adapters ... implement none of the port's operations". A seam a substrate MUST provide is one substrates implement. This one is implemented by CORE and consumed, in principle, by a view runtime -- the arrow points the other way. A substrate obligation it is not, and the spec closes the door twice more: the port is not in the spec map, and no feature predicate lets anything branch on it.

It is the second that is absent. But the retirement dispatch's fence must still include spec/006: it would remove a normative section running 1186-1980, the forward blockquote at 103-111, and the override cross-reference at 2502-2512. title: hicasso U1-U4 instrument: the bench lane computes no p95/p99, so no clock driver can pin the user-visible rows
description:
LOCATED BY rf2-85og2's 2026-08-18 window, which took no reading and re-verified all
three of its gates as still refused. This bead is the EDIT-SHAPED half of the first
of those three, and it builds fine on a LOUD box — only the run that follows it
needs the drain.

THE FINDING, and it is sharper than the refusal it replaces. budgets.md sec 4 and
sec 9.2 say "no package-resident clock instrument exists" and conclude that U1-U4
and C3/C4 each need "a clock instrument pointed at implementation/hicasso". That
sentence is now imprecise: TWO clock drivers have landed and one of them IS pointed
at the package —
implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/direct_return_clock_app.cljs
requires re-frame.hicasso itself, and budgets.md sec 4's S8 row calls its reading a
"package figure". The other,
implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/topo/clock_app.cljs (rf2-w01c,
window taken 2026-08-18), requires re-frame.bench.hicasso.arm1.runtime and is a
bench-tree instrument.

SO THE BLOCK IS THE ESTIMATOR, NOT THE INSTRUMENT'S AIM. In
implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/lane.cljs, `summarise` answers
`{:n :min :max :p50}` and NO p95 and NO p99 is computed anywhere on that lane —
while every one of U1, U2, U3 and U4 is registered at p95 or p99 (U2 is "50 ms p95
/ 100 ms p99"). budgets.md already records the same fact about C8's ">= 2 ms p95"
disjunct, in its own words: "the instrument computes no p95". rf2-w01c's published
NOT-concluded list reached it independently from the other side.

A SECOND GAP, and it is not the same one. The population differs as well. U1-U4 are
stated over a slice application's own interactions (budgets.md sec 9.3: "Slice-app
user-visible gates"), and both existing drivers mount a SYNTHETIC bench page inside
one react-dom/flushSync window — which is a MOUNT and not a PAINT. A p95 over the
wrong window would be a fabricated line wearing a real estimator.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS. Build the instrument, on a loud box, and take no reading:
  1. A quantile estimator on the lane, registered and self-tested, with its
     definition stated (linear-interpolated quantile is already spelled out in
     clock_readjudicate.cjs and is the obvious donor rather than a second spelling).
  2. A driver whose window is a discrete interaction through to the paint that
     follows it, on one of the witness applications under
     implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/ — the slice app is the
     one U1-U4 are stated over.
  3. NO threshold, NO band, NO pinned figure. The reading is a separate quiet-box
     window and is NOT this bead's.

DO NOT WIDEN A LINE OR GUESS A THRESHOLD to make U1-U4 shippable. Three windows in
this programme have refused rather than do that and every refusal carried more
information than a pass would have.

FENCE NOTE: implementation/shadow-cljs.edn is hot-zone. rf2-fe0l's precedent is
that a new driver can ride an existing build id rather than mint one — check that
before asking for the hot-zone edit.

THE BLOCK WAS NEVER ONLY THE ESTIMATOR, AND THE SECOND HALF IS STRUCTURAL. lane/rounds! calls measure-one! and takes a NUMBER back, so an arm it can schedule is one whose whole window closes inside a synchronous call — and a window that ends at a PAINT cannot, because the browser produces the frame after the task returns and the only handle on it is a callback. Every arm this lane could schedule was therefore one bracketed by react-dom/flushSync. That is why both landed drivers measure a commit: it is the shape the only shared schedule allowed, not a coincidence of what got written. So the driver needed a schedule as well as an aim.

WHAT LANDED

1. lane/rounds-async! — rounds!'s schedule with the return type widened to a promise. Both loops now walk one private visit-plan, so the reflecting order, the warm-up boundary and observe!'s predecessor tagging cannot become two copies; lane_schedule_async_cljs_test runs one deterministic stub through both and asserts the samples, readings and true execution order are = at arm counts 2/4/5/7/8, that the visits stay serial, and that a plain value is accepted. lane_schedule_cljs_test is the regression net over the refactor and is green.

2. slice_echo_clock_app — the driver. It mounts the slice through h/mount! with the application's own :initial-events, differing only in which route it opens on, and its window runs from a real DOM event through requestAnimationFrame then setTimeout 0 — the first task after that frame's rendering lifecycle. The echo is read out of the DOM INSIDE the rAF callback, before style, layout and paint, and banks into lane/tally with assert-verified! refusing at N unverified of M. Every reading is published decomposed (:commit, :to-raf, :raf-to-paint). Four rows: :idle-frame (the floor), :keystroke (U1), :toggle (U2, the click/change path), :ctl-blocked (the control). U3 and U4 are named at source as NOT served, with what each would need.

THE CONTROL IS INVISIBLE TO THE WINDOW IT REPLACES, which is what makes it the right one here rather than a generic sensitivity check. :ctl-blocked spends its injected 50 ms strictly BETWEEN the commit and the frame, on window!'s after-commit! seam, so a rig that had quietly reverted to a commit-bounded window would report a control that predicted 50 ms and measured nothing.

THE RISK THIS BEAD FLAGGED DOES NOT HOLD. The slice app compiles under :advanced through this driver — release build, zero warnings — and runs there. Budgeted for; it cost nothing.

THE FINDING THE RIG PRODUCED, AND THE REPAIR. The instrument's first run REFUSED, and not for load. A paint-bounded window is PREDECESSOR-DEPENDENT BY CONSTRUCTION: its length is dominated by the wait for the browser's next rendering opportunity, those sit on a grid, and how long a sample waits depends on where in that grid the PREVIOUS sample left the clock. The arm-order guard measured exactly that — :idle-frame read a full rendering interval after :keystroke, which ends just after a paint, and zero after :ctl-blocked, which spans three intervals and ends with a frame already overdue, ranges disjoint; :toggle carried the same contrast. VERDICT: REFUSE.

THE GUARD'S TOLERANCE WAS NOT MOVED. The repair is in the ARM, one line in measure-one!: settle to a fresh frame OUTSIDE the reading so the clock always starts in the first task after a paint, making the grid phase a constant of the instrument rather than a property of whatever ran before it. With it the guard returns REPORTABLE on every arm by predecessor AND by phase, on a loud box.

TWO CONSEQUENCES STATED AT SOURCE rather than left to be found by the reading window: (a) a real interaction arrives at a uniformly random phase in the grid while this one always arrives at the phase with the LONGEST wait, so a reading here is the conservative end of the phase distribution — the end that cannot flatter the application, and the deliberately-randomised-phase alternative is named with its trigger and NOT built; (b) the injected block does not ADD to the wait the unblocked arm pays, it SUBSUMES it, so the control's difference reaches blocked-ms rounded to the grid rather than exactly, which is what control-slack's band is derived from.

WHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS NOT THIS BEAD'S. The READING. The instrument has never been read against a line and must not be: U1's one-60-Hz-frame clause, U2's 50 ms p95 / 100 ms p99 and U3's 100 ms appear nowhere in the code, and the only pass/fail the driver makes are the arm-order guard and the positive control, both instrument-integrity checks. rf2-85og2's gate 1 now needs a quiet-box window and nothing else structural. - THE SCHEDULE KNOBS ARE DELIBERATELY SMALL. {:warmup 8 :samples 12} over 5 rounds is the lane's standard, and a p99 over 12 samples is mostly interpolation — lane/quantile's own docstring prices that. Raise both; the run's wall clock is roughly two frames per sample plus 50 ms per :ctl-blocked sample.
- U3 AND U4 STILL HAVE NO ROWS. U3 (operation latency for a broad operation — a route change, a reset, a save reply) needs per-arm preparation outside the window, because the route the editor rows type into is the route a navigation row would leave. U4 (per-frame latency under dragging or animation) is not one interaction through to one paint at all: it is a run of consecutive frames, and its estimator is a distribution over frame intervals rather than over window lengths. Both want another driver on window!'s mechanism. Neither is built and neither should be guessed at.
- THE FLOOR ROW IS THE ONE TO READ FIRST. :idle-frame is the wait for the next rendering opportunity with no application work at all, and a p95 at the floor and a p95 at twice it are different findings that the figure alone does not distinguish.

THE SLICE HAS NO SUCH FIELD: ::events/edit takes what it is given, verbatim, and nothing on the article route normalises or refuses. Checked at source before designing around it.

So: React keeps a controlled input's committed value in TWO places, and only one of them is reachable by a scripted setup. The `value` PROPERTY is written by HTMLInputElement.prototype's setter and by a checkbox's native activation; the `value` CONTENT ATTRIBUTE (defaultValue) is written ONLY by React's own commit. title: hicasso: the allocation window's SECOND leg pass reads lower than its first — a within-round position term of 0.2–0.7%
description:
MEASURED by rf2-0gjqi's paired window, 2026-08-18. Record:
docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-sign-follows-the-pass-not-the-write.md (PR #8473).
Datasets: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-0gjqi/.

THE OBSERVATION. Under P0_ALLOC_WRITE=paired the two write legs of every arm run
as two passes inside one round, and the rig alternates which leads on round
parity (p0_run.cjs:2418). Taking the round as the block and the median of
(page-all)/all over that round's certified mid-rung (R3, R7) cells as its
statistic, THE PASS THAT RAN SECOND READS LOWER IN 10 OF 12 BLOCKS -- 6 of 6 in
run 1, 4 of 6 in run 2 -- WHICHEVER WRITE OCCUPIED IT. Median second-minus-first
-0.59%.

Decomposed under an additive position model, the pass-order half-difference reads
+0.68% (run 1) and +0.21% (run 2), the same sign on both, while the order-free
write half-sum reads -0.33% and +0.24%, opposite signs.

WHY IT MATTERS. It is the class of term that manufactured this instrument's last
inferential finding. rf2-0gjqi's published 8-of-8 was taken with `all` as run 2
and `page` as run 3, so page was ALWAYS the later measurement; a position term of
this sign produces 8 of 8 in one direction with certainty. The paired mode
removes the confound and the unanimity goes with it -- but the term itself is
still in the instrument, and any future estimator that is not order-balanced will
pick it up again.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, so it is not rediscovered as new.

  - THE MAGNITUDE IS NOT COMPARABLE TO THE OLD EFFECT. This is a WITHIN-ROUND
    pass-position term; the old confound was between two PROCESSES. They are not
    the same quantity, and +0.21..0.68% is smaller than the published mid-rung
    absolute median of 1.68%. Right sign, wrong size, different estimand.
  - NO MECHANISM IS PROPOSED and none is excluded.
  - LEG ORDER IS NOT SEPARATED FROM ROUND PARITY. The rig ties them: every
    page-first round is an even round. Any other even/odd property of a round
    acting differently on a first and a second pass would read the same way.
    Separating them needs a leg order that is not a function of round parity,
    which is a rig change and therefore its own window.
  - THE INDEPENDENT BLOCK COUNT IS 2, not 12. The twelve round blocks share a
    session inside each run. The nominal one-sided sign-test p over twelve is
    79/4096 = 0.019 and is quoted only as what the nominal test says.

WHAT WOULD DECIDE IT. A leg order drawn independently of round parity -- e.g.
seeded per round rather than parity-derived -- would separate the pass-position
term from every other even/odd round property in one window. That is a rig change
and must not be made inside a measurement window.

comments.text:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8601 (2026-08-21) — THE WINDOW CORRECTLY STAYS OPEN, BUT ITS CLAIM THAT RUN 2 “SEPARATED” PASS FROM PARITY IS FALSE, AND THE PRESCRIBED NEXT DESIGN REPEATS THE CONFOUND.

1. DIFFERENT MARGINAL MEDIANS ARE NOT IDENTIFIABILITY. Run 2's six-round schedule has parity·pass = -2, not 0. `decompose` computes two separate marginal median contrasts; it does not jointly fit the correlated columns. A direct synthetic control using the shipped `decompose` proves the failure:
- true PARITY only (even=+1, odd=-1; pass effect 0) reports PASS=-1 and PARITY=+1;
- true PASS only (page-first=+1, all-first=-1; parity effect 0) reports PASS=+1 and PARITY=-1.
Both use run 2's exact schedule `page,page,all,page,all,all`. So run 2's +0.64/-0.22 pair is not a separated pass/parity estimate. Its two numbers merely differ; each can contain the other term. Run 1 makes the same confound visible by returning identical medians, but run 2 does not remove it.

CONSEQUENCES FOR THE LANDED RECORD. The “only run 2 separates,” “independent n=1,” and “four runs, four positive PASS terms” wording is too strong. Three of those four contrasts came from parity-tied or parity-correlated schedules and are page-first GROUPING contrasts, not pass-specific replications. The complementary two-run pooled design has dot=0 and is the only design-level contrast here that balances the columns; it is one paired design and still needs the nonlinear estimator qualified. The cautious terminal conclusion (“not established free of parity”) remains correct, so no shipped decision needs reversal.

THE SUCCESSOR PLAN WOULD REPEAT IT. “Both seeds at symmetric difference 4” gives dot=-2 in every six-round run. It reduces group overlap but does not make either marginal contrast identify its term; the synthetic control above remains maximally wrong. More runs merely replicate that confound. Before another expensive window, pre-register a design/estimator that passes synthetic pure-pass and pure-parity controls. Cheap routes include a round count and schedule with dot=0 WITHIN each run plus an estimator whose behavior is proved on those fixtures, or a joint model/paired contrast that estimates both columns rather than naming two correlated marginal medians. Do not treat “the medians came apart” as the control.

2. THE READER'S ARBITERS DO NOT ARBITRATE. `report()` prints `controlVerdict`, `verification.unverified`, `passOrder`, `parityTied`, and `scheduleDrove`, then unconditionally feeds every row to `blocks`, the headline, both decompositions, and `nullArm`. A copy of seeded-run1 with `controlVerdict.ok=false` still produces all blocks and the “PASS THAT RAN SECOND” headline; reversing round 0's driven legs makes `scheduleDrove=false` and still produces them. The source comments explicitly promise the opposite (“a failed control contributes no data”; disagreement means no figure may be read). Add one fail-closed admissibility boundary used by report/self-test, covering failed/absent control, nonzero/absent verification, wrong mode/seed/tied schedule, and schedule/drive mismatch; prove each rejection.

No duplicate Bead: this open issue already owns the estimator, the window, and its successor design. Keep it open after the terminology/reader repair until a genuinely identifying window exists.

title: hicasso: V2's arm-floor does not cancel the write exactly — write-page reads below write-all at 8 of 8 mid-rung comparisons
description:
MEASURED by rf2-2rtt6.140's V1/V2 re-run window, 2026-08-17. Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-floor-certifies-and-the-control-does-not.md.

CONTEXT: V2's criterion became evaluable for the first time. The floor went from certifying 0 of 6 in BOTH 2026-08-13 runs on BOTH segments to 4-6 of 6, so (arm - floor) finally has a certified floor to subtract. The floor drops 1,769 B (9.1%) on reagent-subs and 1,765 B (8.9%) on uix-subs, which is the half of V2's criterion that HOLDS.

THE FINDING. (arm - floor)/B is meant to cancel the write's fixed cost F exactly, so the two writes must give the same per-boundary figure. Across the 13 comparable rungs they differ by -4.28% to +8.81%, absolute median 1.48%, and 10 of 13 certified per-round ranges overlap. That is close. But the RESIDUAL HAS A CONSISTENT SIGN:

  segment       arm       rung   all      page     page-all
  reagent-subs  hicasso   R3     6,984    6,687    -4.25%
  reagent-subs  hicasso   R7    14,447   13,829    -4.28%
  reagent-subs  reagent   R3     7,795    7,664    -1.67%
  reagent-subs  reagent   R7    15,408   15,180    -1.48%
  uix-subs      hicasso   R3     6,691    6,538    -2.28%
  uix-subs      hicasso   R7    13,752   13,520    -1.69%
  uix-subs      uix       R3     5,211    5,164    -0.90%
  uix-subs      uix       R7    11,405   11,347    -0.51%

Eight of eight in one direction, across both segments and both substrates. Under a null of random sign that is a 1-in-256 arrangement. Estimator: (arm - floor)/B from each window's own leg median, then the MEDIAN across rounds where BOTH the arm and that segment's floor certified — not a mean, and not pooled beyond that median.

The two R=1 hicasso rungs carry the largest disagreements in the OTHER direction (+1.11%, +8.81%) and are also the noisiest cells on the page, with round-to-round spread of 22-35%. The sign consistency is in the mid rungs, whose spread is 1-7%.

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. V2 exists to detect the case where 'the new write provokes different per-boundary work' (allocation-instrument-rework.md:217-220), for which the stated consequence is that the write half is WITHDRAWN rather than re-tuned. This residual is small — a few percent — and at most rungs does not exceed the round-to-round spread. So it is not obviously that case. But it is not obviously noise either, and 8-of-8 is the observation that says so.

THE DECISION NEEDED is whether ~1-4% of non-cancellation is tolerable for the equivalence argument, which is a RULING and not a measurement. The window deliberately did not make it.

SECOND ITEM, RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN SEPARATELY: the R=20 rung still produced certified windows under both writes on only ONE of its four arm families (uix-subs | uix R20). reagent-subs|hicasso, reagent-subs|reagent and uix-subs|hicasso produced NO certified pair. comments.text:
RE-ANALYSIS, rf2-0gjqi, 2026-08-18. Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-eight-signs-are-one-block.md (PR #8458). NO WINDOW WAS TAKEN and no rig file was touched.

VERDICT. The CAUSE of the sign residual is UNRESOLVED and the committed corpus cannot decide it. The INFERENTIAL claim in this bead's description -- eight of eight in one direction, a 1-in-256 arrangement -- is REFUTED at source. The thirteen descriptive cells stand exactly as published; one sentence about eight of them does not.

WHY, and the third reason is new rather than the audit restated.

(1) MEASUREMENT ORDER, ESTABLISHED AT SOURCE. ALLOC_WRITE is read once from process.env at module scope (implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs:1504), and ALLOC_WRITE_SPECS has exactly two members with no paired or interleaved option (:1490). One process therefore drives one write, and the resolved kind is passed into every arm window of the run (:2335, :2342). The two arms of every comparison are two sequential process runs. The record declares the order: all was run 2, page was run 3, brackets 01:48:27 / 01:50:09 / 01:51:44. Write and run-position are perfectly confounded across all eight cells. Within-run position is NOT a confound and that sharpens the point -- segment order alternates on round parity (:2269) and arm order is slot-order(n, round) (order_guard.cljc:149), a pure function, so both runs measured every arm at the same within-run position.

(2) ONE FLOOR PER SEGMENT PER WRITE. The estimator differences each arm window against that segment's floor window in the same round. The reagent-subs floor certified 4 of 6 under all, and all four of that segment's mid-rung cells report n = 4 under all, so those four cells difference against THE SAME FOUR FLOOR WINDOWS. A level term common to them shifts all four cell medians identically. Four cells, one draw.

(3) AND THAT TERM IS PAGE-GLOBAL, WHICH MERGES EVEN THOSE TWO. rf2-77gz8 measured the second floor mode moving reagent-subs and uix-subs by EXACTLY the same 3,792 B. So the segments do not draw separately either. Eight cells, ONE draw, probability 1 -- not 1/256.

MAGNITUDE, first-hand. A shared floor offset of 2,472 B/write on reagent-subs and 928 B/write on uix-subs reverses all eight signs (B = 4, so eps = 4 x |delta|; largest mid-rung deltas are 618 and 232 B/boundary). Re-derived here from the eight committed alloc-9jrhi datasets -- population: the floor arm's certified windows; statistic: median of rise/W across certified rounds, per segment per run -- three runs at ONE revision (4a1537cb71) under ONE write span 3,852 B/write (reagent-subs) and 3,912 B/write (uix-subs). Both exceed what would flip every sign. Two runs at 88411ed803 span 1,645 B/write on uix-subs, which still exceeds that segment's 928.

BUT THE MODE ACCOUNT IS NOT ADOPTED. A shared floor offset is additive and identical across a segment's arms; the observed mid-rung offsets span 1,948 B/write within reagent-subs and 740 B/write within uix-subs, and within an arm family the residual is closer to a constant proportion (page/all reads 0.9575 and 0.9572, 0.9832 and 0.9852, 0.9771 and 0.9831, 0.9910 and 0.9949). So rf2-77gz8 is of sufficient magnitude and the WRONG SHAPE to be the whole of it. Not excluded, not supported.

WHY NO NEW WINDOW, verified at source rather than assumed. All EIGHT alloc-9jrhi datasets carry writeSelector "all", plan floor, B = 24 -- NO committed dataset carries write-page, and none carries a ladder rung under any write selector. The only committed full ladder (alloc-2rtt6-138/run1.json) predates the selector AND predates rf2-erre5, so it carries neither writeSelector nor samples. The V1/V2 re-run window COMMITTED NO DATASET AT ALL: there is no alloc-2rtt6-140 directory, so the eight disputed cells cannot be recomputed from anything in the tree. And a fresh window would reproduce the same confound at a new timestamp, because the rig can only drive one write per process.

LEFT OPEN DELIBERATELY. The audit's obligation -- compare matched certified pairs after the paired mode lands -- is unmet, and closing would drop it. Filed rf2-irxrw as the work that would decide it. Two things it needs, stated so they are not rediscovered: the FLOOR must be paired too, because the floor is the dominant shared term; and rf2-77gz8 must be resolved alongside, because whether the ladder ARMS carry the floor's second mode is untested -- it was observed on a floor-plan run with no arms in it -- and that single unknown decides whether a page-global level cancels in arm minus floor or not.

WHAT THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION SHOULD NO LONGER BE READ AS SAYING: "Under a null of random sign that is a 1-in-256 arrangement." That null is not the one this design admits. Everything else in the description stands.

comments.text:
THE PAIRED MODE HAS LANDED (rf2-irxrw, PR #8461). This bead stays OPEN: its audit obligation -- compare matched certified pairs -- is unmet until a window is taken through the new mode, and closing would drop it.

WHAT IS NOW POSSIBLE THAT WAS NOT. P0_ALLOC_WRITE=paired drives :p0/write-page AND :p0/write-all at every arm inside every round, on the same page, in the same process. That is the same-page/same-run pair allocation-instrument-rework.md:231-232 requires and the instrument could not take, and it removes the confound this bead's re-analysis established at source: the two arms of every published comparison were two sequential PROCESS runs in a fixed order.

FOUR THINGS IT MAKES AVAILABLE TO A LATER WINDOW.

  1. MATCHED WITHIN-ROUND DIFFERENCES. Every recorded window names its own write and carries pairKey -- the arm key its legs share -- so an estimator groups a round's windows by that field and differences the two legs directly. It does not reconstruct a pair from two files, and it does not parse a key.

  2. A PAIRED FLOOR. The floor is an arm of the plan, so the leg pass takes it under both writes like every other arm. This bead's own note said the floor must be paired because it is the dominant shared term, and it is: (arm - floor) can now be formed within one round under each write, against a floor measured under that same write in that same round.

  3. THE WRITE IS NO LONGER CONFOUNDED WITH POSITION. The leg order alternates on round parity exactly as the segment order does, so over six rounds each write leads three times. A drift within a run no longer reads as a difference between the writes.

  4. rf2-77gz8's UNKNOWN BECOMES ASKABLE. The paired mode puts an arm window and a floor window under both writes in one round for the first time, which is what deciding whether the ladder ARMS carry the floor's second mode requires -- and that single unknown decides whether a page-global level cancels in arm minus floor or not.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, stated so it is not assumed. The two legs of a pair are separated by one segment pass rather than being adjacent windows, so a mid-run transition of the kind rf2-77gz8 describes can still fall between them; that is a large improvement on a whole process but it is not zero. NO WINDOW WAS TAKEN and no figure moved -- the build carries no measurement, and the thirteen descriptive cells in this bead's description stand exactly as published.

SEQUENCING UNCHANGED: rf2-77gz8 should be resolved alongside or first.

docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-sign-follows-the-pass-not-the-write.md (PR #8473).

the paired mode landed, an independent-block count over run-pair/order blocks
rather than rungs, and a correction to the measurement page, the studio index and
this bead together. All three move in PR #8473; the block count is below.

DESIGN, FIXED BEFORE THE FIRST RUN. Two runs, P0_ALLOC_PLAN=full
P0_ALLOC_CELLS=1 P0_ALLOC_WRITE=paired, B = 4, six rounds. Two were declared and
two were taken; none added after a result, none dropped. The estimator was
written down before the first run.

THE ESTIMATOR, NAMED FOR WHAT IT IS. Per round r, segment s, arm a:
  d_all  = (arm@all .legMedian - floor@all .legMedian) / B
  d_page = (arm@page.legMedian - floor@page.legMedian) / B
  Delta  = d_page - d_all
A round contributes ONLY IF ALL FOUR windows certified in that round. Cells are
reported twice because they are different statistics: RATIO-OF-MEDIANS (median of
d_page over the cell's rounds over median of d_all over the SAME rounds, less 1 --
the form comparable to the published table) and MEDIAN-OF-RATIOS. Neither is a
mean and neither is a run-mean.

THE RESIDUAL DISSOLVES.
  - Across the 16 mid-rung cell medians (8 cells x 2 runs), page reads below all
    at 10 OF 16 on ratio-of-medians and 9 of 16 on median-of-ratios. The
    published window read 8 OF 8.
  - Magnitudes: 0.06% - 2.98% absolute, absolute median 0.46%. Published: 0.51% -
    4.28%, absolute median 1.68% on the same eight cells.

AND THE SIGN IS SET BY MEASUREMENT ORDER, NOT BY THE WRITE. Block = the ROUND,
because within a round every arm of a segment differences against the same floor
pair and rf2-77gz8's term is page-global. Taking the median of Delta/d_all over
each round's certified mid-rung cells: THE LEG PASS THAT RAN SECOND READS LOWER
IN 10 OF 12 BLOCKS -- 6 of 6 in run 1, 4 of 6 in run 2 -- WHICHEVER WRITE
OCCUPIED IT. Decomposed under an additive position model, the pass-order term
reads +0.68% and +0.21% (same sign both runs) and the order-free WRITE term reads
-0.33% and +0.24% (OPPOSITE signs). Filed as rf2-fk6pj.

INDEPENDENT BLOCKS, COUNTED AS THE AUDIT ASKED. TWO independent process blocks.
The twelve round blocks share a session inside each run and are NOT twelve
independent trials; the nominal one-sided sign test over twelve gives
p = 79/4096 = 0.019 and is quoted only as what the nominal test says. The claim
that survives the stricter count is the weaker one: both process blocks put the
second pass lower.

V2's FLOOR-DROP HALF HOLDS, AND IS NOW WITHIN-ROUND. 1,652 B (8.6%) on
reagent-subs and 1,652-1,658 B (8.4%) on uix-subs, the same number on both
segments to within 6 B, spanning 1,644-1,664 B across 21 paired certified rounds.
Published unpaired: 1,769 / 1,765 B.

THE CONTROLS. Both runs' positive control passed -- differential 8.00 B/double
against a predicted 8, direct 8.08, 0 unverified read-backs. Both captured EXIT 1
on the falls gate (55 and 54 collections inside measured windows), so NO SLOPE IS
QUOTED from either. And a null arm the previous windows did not read: R = 0 mounts
boundaries that read nothing, so arm - floor must be zero under either write --
over 38 paired certified observations its Delta reads a median of 0 B/boundary,
absolute median 1.5, 90th percentile 4.5. That is what licenses reading mid-rung
differences of 5-198 B/boundary at all.

WHAT IS NOT CONCLUDED, and it is a long list on purpose.
  - THE TWO WRITES ARE NOT SHOWN TO BE EQUIVALENT. No interval is offered for the
    write term. Two process blocks give -0.33% and +0.24%: consistent with zero,
    and NOT a bound. Its magnitude is UNRESOLVED.
  - THE CAUSE OF THE PUBLISHED 8-OF-8 IS NOT ESTABLISHED. The measured pass-order
    term is of the right sign but SMALLER than the published 1.68% absolute
    median, and it is a within-round effect where the published confound was
    between two PROCESSES. Different estimand; right sign, wrong size.
  - rf2-77gz8 IS NOT RESOLVED. Its second mode did NOT appear here -- the
    certified floor spans 46-58 B over six rounds in all four (run, segment)
    cells under both writes, with no 3,792 B step -- but that is B = 4 on the
    `full` plan against its B = 24 on the `floor` plan, and absence in two runs is
    not absence. What DID change is that the estimator no longer turns on the
    answer: a page-global level present in a round enters all four of that
    round's windows and cancels. Its sequencing note ("resolve alongside or
    first") is therefore satisfied in the sense that mattered.
  - NO RULING IS MADE ON TOLERABILITY. The description's question -- whether
    ~1-4% of non-cancellation is acceptable -- was posed of a figure this window
    does not reproduce, so as posed it is MOOT. Whether anything is left to rule
    on is Mike's, not this window's.
  - LEG ORDER IS NOT SEPARATED FROM ROUND PARITY (the rig ties them), no
    mechanism is proposed for the pass-order term, and no cause is assigned to the
    two R = 0 excursions (-96.5 and -56.5 B/boundary, both uix-subs|uix at round 3,
    one per run, reproducing across runs).
  - NO BOUND ON WITHIN-RUN QUIETNESS. Brackets are before-and-after only. The box
    was loaded (5.7-8.0% of 24 cores, 0 java at every bracket) and that is
    correct for a census of monotone counters.
  - THE INTRA-LEG GATE SCREENED NOTHING. Stride 2, so allocIntraLegRefusals
    returns [] by construction.

WHAT THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION SHOULD NO LONGER BE READ AS SAYING. The whole
paragraph beginning "THE FINDING" retains its thirteen descriptive cells, which
stand as published; but "Eight of eight in one direction", "Under a null of random
sign that is a 1-in-256 arrangement", and "it is not obviously noise either" are
each now MEASURED not to hold under the pairing the design always required. The
DECISION NEEDED paragraph is moot as posed.

THE SECOND ITEM CARRIED OUT RATHER THAN DROPPED. R = 20 again certified on one of

title: [method] reopened-item shortcut revives the false description-is-stale rule
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-17 00:25 AUSEST on rf2-lo7uy, by the mayor making the mistake.

THE GAP. The timestamp-ordering rule exists in three places and none of them is the
one that was needed:
  - docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md (4 mentions) — WORKER-FACING.
    It is the text the mayor PASTES INTO A BRIEF, so it instructs the worker.
  - .claude/commands/mayor-backlog-reread.md (1 mention) — mayor-facing, but scoped
    to the hourly BACKLOG REREAD loop.
  - docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md (2 mentions).
mayor-dispatch.md, which governs writing a brief FROM a bead, says nothing about it.
Grepped for 'bd history|newest|created_at|timestamp|superseded|stale.*comment' — the
only hit is an unrelated routing paragraph.

WHAT IT COST. The mayor read rf2-lo7uy top-down, took a 03:02Z mayor triage comment
splitting the bead into an EDIT half and a WINDOW half as the newest text, and
dispatched the edit half. A 04:55:51Z comment titled 'RIG HALF LANDED — THIS BEAD IS
NOW WINDOW-ONLY' already recorded that PR #8384 had merged those exact arms at
05:12:23Z the previous day.

PROCEEDING WOULD HAVE BEEN DESTRUCTIVE, NOT MERELY WASTEFUL. 'n' is an input to
lane/slot-order on that instrument, so adding two more nulls takes n from 11 to 13 and
moves EVERY arm's position footprint including the nine published ones — discarding
#8384's layout and starting a third series, on the very rig whose slot-sensitivity the
bead exists to measure.

THE WORKER CAUGHT IT. It walked 'bd history --json' newest-first across adjacent pairs,
found the 04:55:51Z comment, verified #8384 MERGED at source rather than from the
comment, wrote no code, and correctly declined to run a spine or quote an exit code for
a tree it had not changed.

THE FIX — one sentence-group appended to the 'Find + group' paragraph (line 19), whose
neighbours are already the same class of pre-dispatch verification ('A COUNT IS A CLAIM
TOO, AND THE GREP THAT CHECKS IT IS A DIFFERENT ONE'). Proposed text, to append after
'...treat a parent's remainder table as stale until re-derived.':

  **AND ESTABLISH WHICH TEXT ON THE BEAD IS NEWEST BEFORE YOU BRIEF FROM IT — by
  TIMESTAMP, never by position.** Every brief this file sends already tells the WORKER
  to do this, and mayor-backlog-reread.md tells the mayor to do it when rereading the
  backlog; the gap was here, at the one moment a brief is actually written from a bead.
  Comments do not render in timestamp order relative to notes appended into the
  description block, so the visually-last text is routinely not the newest:
  'bd comments <id> --json' sorted by created_at descending, and 'bd history <id> --json'
  walked newest-first to the first change in a text-bearing field, are the only two
  reads that answer it. **The mayor's OWN earlier note is the most dangerous stale
  source**, because it reads as authoritative and you recognise your own words.
  [then the rf2-lo7uy incident as above, and:] That is the 'where the item and this
  brief disagree, the ITEM governs' clause doing the work it is there for — but it
  should not have had to.

WORD IT YOURSELF IF YOU CAN DO IT BETTER; the above is a draft, not a specification.
Keep it PROPORTIONATE — the anti-gold-plating clause applies. Do NOT add a checklist,
a script, or a tracking field, and do NOT restate the reasoning that
dispatch-prompt-template.md already owns; this file's own line 23 warns that a second
copy of the template's text is 'the same drift one level down'.

WHY THE MAYOR DID NOT JUST EDIT IT: the pre-commit hook refused, exactly as designed —
'.claude/commands/' is a worker-tracked surface and the mayor checkout cannot commit to
it. Attempted at 00:47, refused, reverted, filed here.

CONTROLS ALREADY ESTABLISHED, so do not re-derive them: 'scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci'
covers '.claude/commands/*.md' via COMMAND_FILE_PATHSPEC and was proved to bite on THIS
FILE by a planted broken link — exit 1, naming '.claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md:29'.
It is SILENT ON SUCCESS, so a green run alone proves nothing. 'check_doc_slugs.py' also
exits 0 on this file. One caution learned the hard way: the mayor planted its control on
an UNCOMMITTED edit and restored with 'git checkout --', which discarded the edit along

title: [method] workers open PRs before they are done and the mayor merges them green — use draft PRs as the interlock
description:
THE MERGE LOOP AND THE DISPATCH BRIEF CONTRADICT EACH OTHER, AND THE MAYOR IS THE ONE WHO WROTE BOTH. Twice in one session a PR was merged while its author was still working on it.

THE TWO RULES, both of them mine, both individually right:
  DISPATCH BRIEF: "PUSH AS YOU GO, not at the end — pushed commits are the only durable worker state ... OPEN THE PR as soon as commits exist; a PR is not a claim of green."
  MERGE LOOP: merge on the five-clause criterion the moment it is met, and never block on CI.

Put together they say: workers publish PRs before they are finished, and the mayor merges them the moment CI goes green. **The gap between "CI is green" and "the author is done" is where both incidents happened.**

INCIDENT 1, 2026-08-15 ~11:55. #8323 merged while worker/hicaudit-5zmul was live. GitHub's delete_branch_on_merge removed its branch server-side; the worker's next push recreated it against a main that already carried its commits, producing DUPLICATE PR #8325 with a byte-identical three-file diff. Closed by hand after verifying the duplication rather than assuming it.

INCIDENT 2, 2026-08-16 ~01:33. #8333 merged while worker/w-lane-est was still running gates. Its own words: "#8333 — MERGED by the mayor while gates were still running; full gate table posted as a comment on it." It recovered well — cherry-picked the one wording fix the merge had not carried onto current main as #8339, and re-ran the doc gates on that branch — but that is a whole extra PR and an extra review cycle for work that would have ridden the first one.

NEITHER MERGE VIOLATED THE CRITERION. Both PRs were genuinely green on all five clauses when merged. The criterion is not the defect; the missing coordination is.

*** THE FIX, and it uses a mechanism that already exists rather than inventing a rule to remember. *** Brief workers to open the PR as a DRAFT and mark it ready for review as their last act before reporting done. `gh pr merge` REFUSES a draft, so the interlock is enforced by the host rather than by anyone's memory — which is the property the stash ban and the beads-boundary hook both have and the reason they hold. It preserves everything the push-as-you-go rule buys: commits are still pushed continuously and still survive a worker's death, and the mayor can still read the diff and the gate output at any time.

WHAT TO CHANGE:
  - docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md — the push-as-you-go clause gains "open it as a DRAFT; mark it ready as your last act before reporting done."
  - docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md section 1 — the merge criterion gains a line noting a draft PR is not a merge candidate, and WHY: the five clauses test the CHANGE, not whether its author has finished with it.
  - .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md — the same line, concretely: skip drafts in the sweep.

THE ALTERNATIVE, rejected: have the mayor check worker liveness before every merge. It works, but it is a rule that must be remembered on every merge forever, and it re-introduces exactly the worktree-activity sweep the merge loop deliberately does not do. The draft flag costs one command at the end of a worker's run and cannot be forgotten by the mayor at all.

title: [method] added-line triage still says it settles the common case
description:
FOUND BY rf2-cyt80's WORKER, which declined to widen its own scope and flagged this instead — correctly. The mayor's bead text is the defect here, not the worker's reading of it.

WHAT HAPPENED. rf2-cyt80's drift 3 OBSERVED that "neither mayor-hygiene.md nor loops.md section 5 contains the words cherry, patch-id or patch-equivalent". Its FIX clause then named only mayor-hygiene.md. The worker implemented exactly what the fix clause said and reported the gap rather than quietly extending its fence. So the concrete command file now carries the containment test and THE GENERIC PUBLISHED METHOD STILL DOES NOT.

THE GAP. docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md section 5 ("Branches") says to delete merged branches and never one whose change is not verifiably merged. It says nothing about HOW to establish containment — and under rebase-merge the obvious test is wrong in both directions.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE GENERIC DOC SPECIFICALLY. loops.md is the method as published for other repositories, and rebase-merge is not a local quirk. A reader adopting the method there gets the rule and not the trap. Measured here on 2026-08-15 over 63 worktrees: 60 branches read "ahead of main by 1 to 3 commits" and 58 of them were FULLY MERGED, because a rebase gives every merged commit a new SHA so it never becomes an ancestor of the trunk. Deleting on ancestry would have kept all 58 forever; ignoring the reading would have destroyed worker/receipts-hic081's 3 genuinely unmerged spike commits. `git cherry <trunk> <branch>` settled both directions in one command — `-` means an equivalent patch is already upstream, `+` means genuinely new.

WHAT TO WRITE, keeping loops.md's register — GENERIC, no bd commands, no repo paths, no PowerShell, no bead ids:
  - ancestry and the ahead-count are both useless for containment when the project merges by rebase, and they fail in OPPOSITE directions;
  - the test is patch-equivalence (`git cherry`), which answers both directions at once;
  - the measured warrant, stated without repo-specific identifiers: 60 branches read ahead, 58 were merged, 1 was not, one command separated them.

Cross-reference rather than restate: loops.md section 4 and the command files already explain why the ahead count misleads for LIVENESS. This is the same trap on a different question — containment, not liveness — and saying so is cheaper and more durable than a second copy of the reasoning.

SCOPE FENCE: docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md ONLY. mayor-hygiene.md already has its half from rf2-cyt80; do not touch it again. This is a hot-zone method file, so SOLE TOUCHER, never parallel with another method-file bead.

GATE: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py plus mkdocs build --strict, which DOES cover docs/the-mayor-method/. Note that bare `mkdocs` returns exit 127 in Git Bash on this box because it is not on PATH — 127 is NO VERDICT, not a pass; run it as `python -m mkdocs`. No fenced code blocks are added, so the guide-samples digest gate is untouched; say so in the PR body rather than leaving it unstated.
acceptance_criteria: loops.md consistently describes the added-line scan as a non-conclusive triage hint; no sentence says it settles or proves containment. Conclusions still require the whole-patch comparison, and the delete-only-on-minus rule remains unchanged.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8901 — REOPENED EXACT OWNER; NO DUPLICATE.

COMPLETENESS: The PR correctly fixes the asymmetric meaning of git cherry: '-' proves patch-equivalent containment, while '+' only says that equivalence was not found. Its new one-step "discriminating test" is still incomplete, however: searching only for the commit's added lines ignores file/path and location, multiplicity, order, and every deletion. A generic added line may already exist elsewhere at the tip while the branch's actual change is wholly absent, so "all present means the content landed" is false. Conversely, upstream can preserve the change after a rename, formatting edit, or follow-on rewrite while an exact added line is absent, so "any absent means genuinely outstanding" is also false.

CORRECTNESS: Keep the safe deletion rule (delete only on '-'), but do not present added-line presence as a containment verdict. It is at most a cheap triage hint. Before concluding either landed or outstanding, inspect the full patch against the current tip at the intended paths/locations, including deletions and replacements; a three-way comparison from the branch parent is sufficient. This matters even though the prose forbids using the test to delete: the current wording can still dismiss real unmerged work as a phantom.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / NARROW REMEDY: Amend only the new paragraph in docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md. Downgrade the added-line scan to a heuristic and name the full-patch review needed for a conclusion, or remove the purported one-step discriminator. Do not build a containment framework or change the conservative '-' deletion criterion.
AUDIT PR #8920: reopened exact owner. The repair correctly labels the added-line scan triage and explains both false directions, but the preceding sentence still says to run it first because "it settles the common case." That directly contradicts the next sentence ("triage, not a verdict") and the PR body's claim that the scan is no longer described as settling anything. A heuristic that cannot conclude either landed or outstanding does not settle even its common case; that word is the behavioral instruction likely to make a mayor stop before the required whole-patch comparison.

Minimal correction only: say the scan is cheap and useful for prioritising/starting the common investigation, without claiming settlement. Keep the full-patch conclusion and delete-only-on-minus rule unchanged; no new containment machinery or broader method edit.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #8928 (merged 2026-09-01). The added-line scan no longer claims to settle anything: 'run it first because it settles the common case' becomes 'run it first because it costs seconds and tells you where to point the real check — never because it finishes one', removing the contradiction with 'triage, not a verdict' two sentences later. The full-patch conclusion and the delete-only-on-minus criterion are unchanged, per the audit's minimal correction.

the stale index-write row and its dependent narrative — was DISCHARGED by PR

Runs went strictly one at a time on a quiet box.

THE RULE, per the mayor ruling of 2026-08-21 10:22 AUSEST. Each run's NULL SPREAD is the interval its three nulls span (each null is c-local again through the same constructor, so each has a true cost of exactly zero by construction). A term RESOLVES IN A RUN iff its delta is strictly greater than that run's null maximum; RESOLVED iff it resolves in all three. Anything else publishes as UNRESOLVED AT THIS INSTRUMENT'S RESOLUTION with its readings quoted, NO BOUND and NO SHARE. No null subtracted from any term.

CONTROLS. Three runs, exit 0 each; both arm-order guards reportable on every run (38 [ok] verdicts, no refusal, per run); phase-A positive control passing on every run; phase-B residue gate never firing.

NULL MAXIMA: +0.0297 / +0.0281 / +0.0500 (c-null +0.0297/+0.0141/+0.0500, twin +0.0031/+0.0281/+0.0297, curve +0.0109/+0.0172/+0.0359).

TERMS (c-local minus arm), each against ITS OWN run's null maximum:

  reaction build + cache insert  +0.6016 / +0.6156 / +0.5141  RESOLVED  67.4% / 67.0% / 66.5% of c-local
  cell-map insert                +0.0672 / +0.0656 / +0.0797  RESOLVED  7.5% / 7.1% / 10.3%

1. THE SHARE COLUMN IS THE ROBUST STATISTIC AND THE ABSOLUTES ARE THE FRAGILE ONE. c-local moved 19% across three runs of one binary in one session (0.7734-0.9187) while the reaction build's share of it moved 0.9 percentage points (66.5-67.4%). A share divides two arms measured microseconds apart in the same interleave, so between-run box state largely divides out; an absolute carries it whole. This is the case for republishing as same-run shares, and the reason no absolute from this window should be lifted out and quoted as a property of the tree.

2. WATCH WIRING IS A NEAR MISS REPORTED AS A MISS. BOX: queue length and % Processor Utility sampled together, five samples at 1s, 24-core host, before the window and between every pair of runs. comments.text:
MAYOR 2026-08-16 00:35 — I PROPAGATED A REFUTED BOUND INTO A LIVE WORKER'S BRIEF, AND THE AUDIT CAUGHT IT BEFORE THE WORKER PUBLISHED. Recording the error and the correction.

WHAT I DID. rf2-3l6hf's window recovered two of three terms and reported the third, reader membership, as "bounded: < 0.006 ms/commit, under 1% of the commit half". I read that as a finding, wrote it into rf2-07rnj's dispatch brief as guidance — "quote the BOUND, not a figure ... Publish that bound" — and reported it to the operator the same way.

WHY IT IS WRONG, per the merged-PR audit of #8328, whose reasoning I have checked and accept. Let an observed delta y equal an unknown positive true cost t plus estimator error e. A reading of y = -0.0062 proves only that the negative error excursion exceeded 0.0062 + t. It does NOT establish that +/-0.0062 is a calibrated, symmetric floor, and it CANNOT upper-bound t. A most-negative observation is a statement about the error term, not about the quantity.

THE SECOND HALF, same shape: comparing the most-negative readings from DIFFERENT positive-cost arms at 4 frames and 32 frames cannot prove an 8x floor scaling. Two error excursions from two different arms are not two measurements of one floor.

SO READER MEMBERSHIP IS UNRESOLVED, NOT BOUNDED, until a genuine null/control arm exists or another valid bound is derived. And rf2-07rnj stays BLOCKED: rf2-3l6hf owned resolving the decomposition, one of its original terms still does not resolve, and a decomposition with an unresolved term is not one - which is rf2-07rnj's own founding argument turned on itself.

*** THE GENERAL RULE, WHICH IS THE PART TO CARRY. *** An impossible reading tells you the instrument's error reached at least that far. It does not calibrate the error, and it does not bound the thing being measured. Treating "the worst negative I saw" as "the floor" is the same move as treating "no test failed" as "the code is correct" - it converts an absence into a guarantee. Whenever a worker reports a bound derived from readings that should have been positive, ASK WHAT NULL ARM PRODUCED IT. If the answer is "the impossible readings themselves", it is not a bound.

HOW IT REACHED A WORKER, and this is the process failure rather than the arithmetic one. The premises-are-claims sentence was in rf2-07rnj's brief, and it did not protect against this, because I passed the bound as GUIDANCE ("publish that bound") rather than as a premise to check. That is exactly the failure mode docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md already names for a LEAN: a worker reads guidance as instruction and a premise as a claim, so anything phrased as guidance bypasses the check. A NUMBER I ASSERT IS A LEAN TOO. Demand the evidence that produced it before writing it into a brief - here, one question would have caught it: what null arm produced that bound?

RECOVERY: the live worker was messaged the moment the audit was read, before it published. It was told to keep every measurement it had taken, publish no bound, not chase the term by widening the window, report, and leave rf2-07rnj open and blocked.

title: docs(method): equal export row counts are not tracker-state equality
description:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7394 / ledger durability. Before advancing the cursor, the merged main ledger at 43dcd2440a22a42e77d6ab773fb8df2a43a6a5a6 and the Dolt remote each contained 1,938 issues but different facts. Git alone carried rf2-3jw04, rf2-jv36i, rf2-lhdp0 and newer closes/statuses for rf2-2rtt6.52/.63; Dolt carried three newer audit issues. scripts/beads-checkpoint.ps1 exported Dolt wholesale; its row-count floor passed (1,938 == 1,938), and commit 667c744dc875e31e4d4874586afcbec2d01ceb8a silently removed the three Git-only issues and reverted .52/.63. This is the remaining equal-count/set-substitution sibling of rf2-51uz1's time-travel fault.

Recovery proved the bounded mechanism: timestamp-aware bd import of only Git issue rows into Dolt created the three missing IDs, updated exactly the two newer Git rows, skipped stale rows, preserved every newer Dolt row/cursor, and yielded a verified 1,941-ID union with zero field mismatches.

DO: before checkpoint overwrites .beads/issues.jsonl, compare HEAD's issue IDs/updated_at/status to the fresh Dolt export. Either import newer/missing Git issue rows timestamp-safely then re-export, or refuse with exact IDs/fields. Keep the existing row-count floor, but do not treat equal counts as equality. description:
*** HALF (a) IS DONE AND MERGED. HALF (b) IS AN OPERATOR CALL. DO NOT DISPATCH. ***

READ THIS BEFORE BRIEFING FROM ANYTHING BELOW. The description's file paths are DEAD - it
names implementation/freehand/..., a tree deleted by PR #8322 on 2026-08-16. Both files live
under implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/ now.

HALF (a), THE ADJUDICATION CODE, LANDED IN PR #8574 and returned better than asked. The
worker SPLIT the verdict rather than answering yes or no:
- p0_app.cljs is NOT an allocation arm, it is the P0 CLOCK arm, so the Chrome-clamp carve-out
  was RULED ON it rather than needing to transfer. 80 controls re-adjudicated from the
  committed record: 80/80 pass overlap, 64/80 strict, every miss LOW and on the two rows
  whose legs are 1-3 of Chrome's 100 microsecond quanta, while the 20-plus-quantum rows pass
  strict 40/40. REFUSED, with the reasoning replacing a stale pointer in adjudicate's
  docstring.
- p0_heap.cljs IS the allocation arm the HD-008 argument fits, and WENT STRICT. Byte counter,
  no quantum, and there overlap is not merely weaker but ABSENT: under the loose rule one
  round at 0 B beside five good ones PASSES, which is the exact failure the control exists to
  catch.

WHAT REMAINS IS HALF (b) AND IT IS MIKE'S: are the published P0 rows re-adjudicated, or does
the change apply only from the next run? The bead's own instruction was to record that on
rf2-2rtt6.1, which is CLOSED and is the operator-owned STANDARD.

COST OF THAT HOLD IS LOW AND MEASURED: re-adjudication FLIPS NOTHING. Computed from committed
records with no window run, the widest excursion across ten published heap-control figures is
4,690,838 B, 0.195% below a plus-or-minus-25 percent band.

--- ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION FOLLOWS (2026-07-30, paths superseded above) ---

Found while consolidating HD-008 onto the lane (rf2-f5roa, PR #7267).

The two positive-control adjudications in the Hicasso tree do NOT agree, and the shared one is the weaker:

  lane/control-verdict           ok? = (and (<= min hi) (>= max lo))
                                 i.e. the measured RANGE need only OVERLAP the +/- slack band.
  hd8-rows/positive-control!     :within? = (and (>= lo (* p (- 1 tol))) (<= hi (* p (+ 1 tol))))
                                 i.e. EVERY round must be INSIDE the band.

HD-008's own comment argues the stricter rule explicitly: 'a control whose worst round is wrong has caught something, and letting a good round vouch for a bad one is how an instrument stops being one.' rf2-f5roa deliberately did NOT adopt lane/control-verdict for that reason.

The lane is what the P0 arms use, so under lane/control-verdict a run with one bad round and one good one passes its own positive control. That is the shape of thing this programme keeps finding: a gate that cannot go red has not verified anything.

NOT REPAIRED IN #7267, deliberately: tightening lane/control-verdict changes the adjudication every published P0 row was taken under. Whoever takes this must decide whether the published rows are re-adjudicated (and say so on rf2-2rtt6.1) or whether the change applies only from the next run.

Files: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/lane.cljs (control-verdict); implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/hd8_rows.cljs (positive-control!, the stricter rule).

title: Reconcile the 23 Spec 009 Tags-column rows the keys-set arm reds on (blocks rf2-6tags)
description:
BLOCKS rf2-6tags. The Tags-column keys-set arm is designed, measured and proven non-vacuous, but it CANNOT BE ARMED until these rows are reconciled, because it reds on them.

MEASUREMENT (worker/gate-detectors, PR #7027, against origin/main 5026a73078). The arm pairs a catalogue category to its schema by PascalCasing the name (:rf.error/resource-route-plan -> ResourceRoutePlanTags), diffs the schema's key set against the row's :tags column, and excludes exactly the two envelope slots the catalogue's own rule at spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1948 names ("Two envelope-level slots are therefore deliberately absent from every row" — :recovery and :category). That rule also says the column "lists the keys that genuinely ride under :tags on the wire — nothing else", so every finding below is a row the catalogue's own contract requires to change.

  pre-fix ded86cff64 (parent of the rf2-wsopx fix): 90 paired rows, 24 findings, INCLUDING :rf.error/resource-route-plan -> missing :contributor, :plan-cause
  main    5026a73078:                               90 paired rows, 23 findings, resource-route-plan absent (fixed)

So the arm reds on exactly its motivating defect and greens on the fix. The residual 23 are pre-existing instances of the same class — 44 undocumented schema keys.

THE 23 ROWS (schema keys the Tags column omits):
  :rf.error/coeffect-exception        (CoeffectExceptionTags)      :reason :event :event-id :frame :exception-message
  :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded      (DrainDepthExceededTags)     :frame
  :rf.error/effect-handler-bad-return (EffectHandlerBadReturnTags) :event-id :event
  :rf.error/flow-eval-exception       (FlowEvalExceptionTags)      :event
  :rf.error/fx-handler-exception      (FxHandlerExceptionTags)     :failing-id :frame
  :rf.error/handler-exception         (HandlerExceptionTags)       :reason :event :event-id :frame :exception
  :rf.error/interceptor-exception     (InterceptorExceptionTags)   :reason :event :event-id :frame :exception
  :rf.error/machine-action-exception  (MachineActionExceptionTags) :event :handler-id :frame
  :rf.error/machine-grammar-not-in-v1 (MachineGrammarNotInV1Tags)  :substitute
  :rf.error/malformed-schema          (MalformedSchemaTags)        :failing-id :frame
  :rf.error/no-such-sub               (NoSuchSubTags)              :frame
  :rf.error/override-fallthrough      (OverrideFallthroughTags)    :failing-id
  :rf.error/reg-sub-bad-args          (RegSubBadArgsTags)          :frame
  :rf.error/sanitised-on-projection   (SanitisedOnProjectionTags)  :exception-message :returned :reason
  :rf.error/sub-exception             (SubExceptionTags)           :failing-id
  :rf.error/sub-input-fn-bad-return   (SubInputFnBadReturnTags)    :frame
  :rf.error/sub-input-fn-exception    (SubInputFnExceptionTags)    :frame
  :rf.error/system-id-collision       (SystemIdCollisionTags)      :reason
  :rf.http/stale-suppressed           (StaleSuppressedTags)        :carried-token :current-token :event-id
  :rf.route.nav-token/stale-suppressed(StaleSuppressedTags)        :event-id
  :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch          (HydrationMismatchTags)      :first-diff-path
  :rf.warning/multiple-redirects      (MultipleRedirectsTags)      :frame
  :rf.warning/multiple-status-set     (MultipleStatusSetTags)      :frame

THE ADJUDICATION NEEDED. Not all 23 are necessarily row-side. Several are ALIAS divergences: the schema declares :event / :event-id where the row documents :rf.event/v / :rf.trace/event-id. The 009 frame-destroyed row itself states the distinction ("The bare :event spelling is the ERROR-tag spelling ... :rf.event/v is the dispatch-PIPELINE spelling"), so for those the SCHEMA may be the side that is wrong. The rest (:frame on nine rows, :reason on four, :failing-id on four) look like plain row omissions. Each needs a one-line call: fix the row, or fix the schema.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN PR #7027. The dispatch fenced spec/009-Instrumentation.md's row content with an explicit instruction: "you are building the checker, not editing rows; if a row genuinely must change, STOP and tell me". Twenty-three rows genuinely must change. Reporting rather than editing.

ALSO MEASURED, against the ruling's premise. Spec-Schemas.md defines 111 *Tags schemas; the error/warning catalogue has 489 rows, not one schema per row. 89 schemas pair by name derivation, 22 do not (FxHandledTags, MachineUnhandledNoOpTags, SchemaValidationTags, NoSuchCofxTags, RoutePrefetchedTags, InvalidResourceSpecTags, BadAppSchemasArgTags, LargeValueUnschemadTags, ArtefactMissingTags, HttpInterceptorClearedTags, HttpInterceptorRegisteredTags, FxSkippedOnPlatformTags, DbReplacedTags, DecodeDefaultedTags, HeadMismatchTags, EpochCbSilencedOnFrameDestroyTags, InterceptorsInMetadataMapTags, InvalidMutationSpecTags, MachineActionRanTags, MachineGuardEvaluatedTags, MachineTimerCancelledTags, UnwrapBadEventShapeTags). Explicit in-row `Spec-Schemas §`XxxTags`` citations exist on only 3 of 489 rows, so citation is not a usable pairing key either. Closing those 22 needs either row edits or an alias table — and an alias table is the hand-maintained roster the rf2-6tags ruling forbids. Worth a second ruling alongside the 23.

REJECTED VARIANTS, for the record. Restricting the diff to non-optional schema keys gives 13 findings on BOTH the pre-fix and post-fix trees — VACUOUS on the motivating defect, because :contributor and :plan-cause are both {:optional true}. Widening the containment test from the Tags cell to the whole row changes nothing (24/23). Row->schema as the direction cannot catch the defect at all: the pre-fix row was a strict subset of its schema, which a subset check satisfies.
notes:

The PR correctly adjudicated and changed 18 catalogue rows, corrected 3 schemas, documented the http stale-suppressed name collision, and landed its three-commit series exactly with all required CI green. One of the original 23 findings remains despite the PR description claiming it was fixed: the :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch Tags cell still spells the optional wire key :first-diff-path? at merge a337891285 and on current main. The adjacent findings disclosed in #7030 are already durably owned by later current-main Beads/work (rf2-qk8vj, rf2-k91an, rf2-dxuzp), so no duplicate Bead was created.

WORKER rf2-zk1xu (PR #8562, draft): BOTH halves discharged.

(A) REFUSED AT SOURCE — the premise does not hold. The #7030 audit's claim that the :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch Tags cell still spells :first-diff-path? is FALSE at branch base fd06174823. Commit 0eeab48748 ('name the literal :first-diff-path in the hydration-mismatch Tags cell and empty the Tags-column baseline (rf2-zk1xu)') is an ancestor of main; the cell names the literal key with optionality in prose, and tags-column-shrink-only-baseline is #{} with a paragraph recording this row as its last entry. Positive control: git log -S':first-diff-path?' returns that very commit, so the search could find the string it reports absent. No change made.

(B) IMPLEMENTED. HydrationMismatchTags is now a two-arm :or, one arm per emit tier, with required/optional keys and the category/envelope convention modelled per arm (:category present on the hiccup :error arm, absent on the adoption :warning arm). The hiccup arm also declares the keys the emitter genuinely puts on the wire and the schema omitted: :rf.error/id (payload shared with the :on-mismatch :hard-error throw), :where, :frame, :failing-id, :reason. The 009 row's Tags cell lists them, splits the arms, and DROPS the false :head-id (head) claim - verify-hydration! destructures only :first-diff-path / :failing-id / :server-hash and merges nothing else, so no :head-id can reach this category's payload; the head sub-arm is discriminated by :failing-id alone. #8544's no-:root-id rule, two-envelope explanation and retired-tier wording are preserved.

THE PROOF is over EMITTED EVENTS, not a reverse key diff. A cell -> schema diff is not mechanisable here: the cell states a NEGATIVE as part of its contract ('no :root-id, because a React-element root has none') that a cell-key harvest reads as a listing. So the new deftest drives the SHIPPED emitters - the hiccup tier for real through re-frame.ssr.hydrate/verify-hydration! (ssr is a test-only dep of core), the two .cljs adoption emitters by reading their payload maps out of source as data (each site's own :where symbol included) and driving them through the real trace/emit! - then closes both directions: every wire key is declared by some arm AND named in the cell. The pre-fix single-map schema rides inline as a control that must keep rejecting the real adoption event.

The gate's schema reader now unions a schema's top-level [:map ...] ARMS instead of taking the first found; a first-arm-only reading of a two-arm schema loses half its keys from the diff in silence.

GATES (all captured, all re-run on the final rebased base): catalogue namespace exit 0 (28 tests / 177 assertions, against a control at branch base of 27 / 130 - the same 27/130 the #8544 audit note quotes); check_doc_slugs.py exit 0; check_fast_pr_gap.py --list exit 0, heading 94. test-fast-pr.sh deliberately NOT run - a peer held a live allocation-measurement window. Planted-fault proof for both gates: :client-hash -> :client-hazh red three assertions naming :client-hash; the new anchor respelled red 'BROKEN ANCHOR: 009-Instrumentation.md:2013'. MERGED-PR AUDIT #8562 (2026-08-21 AUSEST) — REOPENED ONLY FOR THE BOUNDED `HeadMismatchTags` remainder this issue already identified; the new `HydrationMismatchTags` two-arm model itself is complete, and no duplicate is needed.

At the merged tree, the only `HeadMismatchTags` occurrences are its definition and #8562's new comment saying it is not this category's schema; the “head-model channel of its own” named there has no corresponding contract or producer.

Retire/remove this stale schema, or identify and document the real channel and producer it models. Do not put `:head-id` back on `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch`; #8562's emitted-shape correction stands.
