title: pair-mcp tests: remove eight dead imports and bindings
description:
## Finding
The Pair-MCP test tree retains eight statically proven dead bindings: seven unused namespace/macro requires plus one unused private helper.

## Evidence
A clean `clj-kondo --lint tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test` reports:
- unused `testing` macro in `args_test.cljs`
- unused `testing` macro in `error_boundary_test.cljs`
- unused `applied-science.js-interop` alias in `port_file_stability_test.cljs`
- unused `applied-science.js-interop` alias in `sticky_build_invoke_test.cljs`
- unused `testing` macro in `wire_pipeline_benchmark_test.cljs`
- unused `testing` macro and unused `clojure.string` alias in `with_indicators_test.cljs`
- unused private function `error?` at `conformance_test.cljs:99`

Exact symbol/alias searches confirm no use within the owning files, and repository/bead searches found no existing issue covering these Pair-MCP bindings. The require forms are ordinary test dependencies, not documented side-effect imports.

## Impact
These leftovers add false dependencies and suggest helpers/macros participate in coverage when they do not. They also hide new lint regressions among known noise.

## Proposed disposition
Remove only the listed unused requires and private helper. Do not broaden this task into style rewrites or removal of live test setup.

## Risks / retained contracts
Re-run the lint and tests after editing. If any require is shown to be intentionally loaded for side effects, document that contract locally and retain it rather than deleting it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The seven listed unused require entries and unused private `error?` helper are removed, or an intentional side-effect dependency is documented with evidence and retained.
2. `clj-kondo` emits none of the eight listed unused-binding warnings.
3. The Pair-MCP test suite passes with the same test count/coverage behavior apart from cleanup.
4. No unrelated lint/style cleanup is bundled into this change.
close_reason: Done in PR #9076. All eight clj-kondo findings reproduced at tip 0b82f2e519 before editing; removed the seven unused requires (testing in args_test, error_boundary_test, wire_pipeline_benchmark_test, with_indicators_test; applied-science.js-interop in port_file_stability_test and sticky_build_invoke_test; clojure.string in with_indicators_test) and the unused private error? at conformance_test.cljs:99. js-interop is RETAINED in conformance_test: removing error? deletes one j/get, but four other call sites (lines 88, 92, 94, 229) still use it. No side-effect require found among the seven. clj-kondo over src+test: 0 errors / 12 warnings before, 0 errors / 3 warnings after; the three remaining (two redundant-let, one unresolved clojure.string in eval_form_test) are pre-existing and outside this bead, left alone per AC 4. Suite green on the rebased base: 1120 tests, 4070 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors (captured exit 0).

title: pair-mcp: remove four zero-consumer helper definitions
description:
## Finding
Four public Pair-MCP helper definitions have no production, test, build, or repository consumer and expose misleading or obsolete surface:
- `roots_discovery.cljs`: `project-home->candidate` and `candidates-from-edns`
- `tools/wire.cljs`: `structured-content` and `arg-keyword`

## Evidence and reachability proof
- Whole-repository symbol searches find each name only at its definition/docstring/comment; no invocation exists.
- `clj-kondo` var-usage analysis across Pair-MCP source and tests reports zero source uses and zero test uses for all four definitions.
- Production root discovery calls `discover-via-roots*` with concrete dependencies, and that seam calls `candidates-from-edns*`; tests also call the starred seams directly. The two unstarred wrappers are bypassed. The docstring for `project-home->candidate*` nevertheless claims production callers use the dead wrapper.
- All structured response envelopes call `wire/result`, whose implementation uses private `structured-of`; `structured-content` has had no client since it was introduced alongside `result` in commit `834af6cdd9`.
- `arg-keyword` was used by the progress-stream/list-streams operations removed in commit `89bb4d49f1`; no current frame parser calls it.
- `package.json` publishes compiled `out/server.js`, README, and LICENSE—not these CLJS namespaces as a supported library API.
- Dynamic zero-static-use entrypoints such as `server/main` and `descriptor-manifest-gen/-main` were explicitly excluded because `shadow-cljs.edn` proves their build reachability.

## Impact
The dead definitions enlarge an apparent API, retain stream-era residue, and leave a false production-call claim in a root-discovery docstring. Future maintainers can mistakenly preserve or test paths the server cannot take.

## Proposed disposition
Delete the four zero-consumer definitions and correct the starred root-discovery seam documentation to describe the actual production path. Keep the live starred injection seams, `wire/result`, and private `structured-of` unchanged.

## Risks / retained contracts
Re-run whole-repository searches before deletion to catch concurrent clients. Do not classify build entrypoints or deliberate test seams as dead merely because ordinary static call analysis cannot see them. Do not change response envelope shape or root candidate ordering.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The four listed zero-consumer definitions are removed (or a newly discovered concrete consumer is documented and the applicable definition retained).
2. Root-discovery docstrings accurately describe the real production and test call paths.
3. Whole-repository searches show no dangling references to the removed symbols.
4. Pair-MCP build and tests pass; descriptor generation/check and registry fixture checks remain unchanged/green.
5. Public MCP response envelopes and roots-discovery behavior are unchanged.
close_reason: Done in PR #9076. Reachability premise re-verified at tip and HELD for all four. Two independent instruments, each run against live controls in the same files: (a) line-oriented fixed-string search over tracked files, (b) a whitespace-flattened per-file census over 4810 tracked files. Both returned ZERO call heads for project-home->candidate, candidates-from-edns, structured-content and arg-keyword; controls wire/result, wire/arg, rd/project-home->candidate*, candidates-from-edns* and rd/discover-via-roots* all fired non-zero. Production path confirmed at source: discover-via-roots -> discover-via-roots* -> candidates-from-edns* -> project-home->candidate*, bypassing both unstarred wrappers. structured-content's docstring named server.cljs, cache.cljs and cap.cljs as its consumers; checked each — all three call wire/result instead (cache.cljs:283, server.cljs:586/626, cap.cljs:145). The sibling unstarred walk-for-shadow-edns is LIVE (passed to discover-via-roots* at roots_discovery.cljs:303) and was deliberately left alone — the audit was right to name only two of the three wrappers. Docstring trap fixed: project-home->candidate*'s 'production callers use [[project-home->candidate]]' was false and pointed at a deleted var; it now describes the real call path. Two comments in dispatch.cljs and trace_window.cljs cited wire/arg-keyword as the coercion NOT to use and would have dangled; they now say (keyword ...) directly. No dangling references remain. Envelope shape and root candidate ordering unchanged. Suite green: 1120 tests, 4070 assertions, 0 failures (captured exit 0).

title: pair-mcp docs: retire stale bash-shim compatibility promises
description:
## Finding
The Pair-MCP package still presents the retired bash/babashka shims as a supported, mix-and-match transport in several current-state documents, although the shim implementation was deleted.

## Evidence
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/README.md` lines 7-9 and 651-657 say the shims still ship, still work, and are not slated for removal.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/Principles.md` lines 117-143 and `spec/API.md` lines 379-405 make the same current compatibility promise.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md` Design Lock #6 (roughly lines 485-541) and its summary row (around line 958) still say both transports ship side-by-side with no removal scheduled.
- `git ls-files skills/re-frame2-pair/scripts` returns no files. Commit `31594b44c3` (`chore(pair): remove retired bash/babashka transport`) deleted the wrappers, operations, and shim tests under rf2-dduetj.
- Current repository documentation elsewhere already records MCP as the only implementation (`skills/re-frame2-pair/README.md`, `docs/TESTING.md`, and Pair-MCP input/design specs).

A related closed predecessor, rf2-435ah, corrected this claim only in `skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/**`; it did not cover the Pair-MCP README/spec tree listed above.

## Impact
Operators and agent authors can spend time looking for nonexistent scripts or design integrations around a transport that cannot be invoked. The stale promise also obscures the deliberate MCP-only migration.

## Proposed disposition
Rewrite current-state sections to say Pair MCP is the sole supported transport. Preserve genuinely historical comparisons, but mark Design Lock #6 and its summary entry as superseded by rf2-dduetj / commit `31594b44c3` instead of silently deleting the design history.

## Risks / retained contracts

title: skills: the 16 KB per-leaf byte ceiling is routinely wrong for dense teaching leaves — four beads have now ended in a recorded exception rather than a split
description:
OBSERVATION FILED, NOT ACTIONED. Filed 2026-09-03 04:44:00 AUSEST from the skillsize-a cluster (rf2-cupfi / rf2-ytkt / rf2-j5na). The brief's instruction was explicit: file this, do NOT change the ceiling — that is a maintainer's call and it is bigger than any of the individual beads.

THE PATTERN. Four beads have now reached the same disposition on the 16 KB per-leaf byte ceiling in skills/README.md 'Leaf size discipline', and in every one the honest answer was a recorded exception rather than a split:

  rf2-baso  skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-views-m11.md  261 L / 39,701 B  2.4x
  rf2-ytkt  skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/reg-machine.md 208 L / 20,599 B  1.26x
  rf2-ytkt  skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/spawn.md       199 L / 19,236 B  1.17x
  rf2-j5na  skills/re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md                   220 L / 46,461 B  2.84x
  (and recipes.md, 424 L / 46,086 B, bound by the same rf2-j5na record)

All byte figures LF-normalised and re-measured at 495e70b600.

THE SHAPE OF THE EVIDENCE. rf2-ytkt's own notes record eight FURTHER leaves across three more partitions hitting the identical wall (websocket, resources, form-action, resources-mutations, testing, privacy-and-elision, routing, stories), so the count of leaves is roughly ten, not four. Two leaves WERE brought inside both ceilings by de-duplication (cofx.md 18,865->16,311; forms.md 17,510->16,310) and testing.md was genuinely split, so the ceiling is NOT unreachable in general — the point is narrower and therefore more interesting.

WHY THE CEILING MISFIRES ON THESE LEAVES SPECIFICALLY. The overrun is DENSITY, not duplication. These leaves run 57-78 prose lines carrying 16-23 KB, i.e. 236-315 BYTES PER PROSE LINE (reg-machine.md 68 prose lines / 17,765 B = 261 B/line; spawn.md 65 / 15,360 = 236 B/line). Only 2,680 B of reg-machine.md and 3,757 B of spawn.md are code fences. skills/README.md says the byte ceiling exists precisely to catch leaves whose long unwrapped prose lines pass the line count while still loading tokens — so on these leaves the catch is a TRUE POSITIVE about density that has no available remedy, because both remedies the contract offers are measured unavailable:

  (a) de-duplication is exhausted — a shingle scan over reg-machine.md returns ZERO intra-file near-duplicate pairs at a 0.30 Jaccard threshold;
  (b) splitting fails the catalogue test's OWN criterion in the direction that FORBIDS it — an author needs the whole of one canonical declaration, so a split raises tokens-per-session rather than lowering it, and it costs SKILL.md routing rows and cross-partition roster rows.

THE ARITHMETIC THAT MAKES THIS CONCRETE, re-measured at my own base rather than quoted: spawn.md's :spawn-all section is exactly 1,950 B. Moving it WHOLESALE to a new leaf leaves 17,286 B — still 902 B OVER the ceiling. A remedy that provably cannot reach its own target is not a remedy, and that is what turned rf2-ytkt from a re-run into a ruling.

THE QUESTION FOR THE MAINTAINER, which is a question about the CONTRACT rather than about any leaf. When four rulings in one session all end in 'recorded exception', the exception has stopped being exceptional. Options, none of which this bead takes:
  1. Leave the ceiling and keep recording exceptions (status quo; the cost is that each one needs a mayor ruling).
  2. Raise the byte ceiling for reference/catalogue leaves specifically, keeping the 250-line half as the primary discriminator.
  3. Replace the flat byte ceiling with the test that is already doing the real work — 'would splitting reduce total tokens loaded per session?' — and keep bytes as a prompt to ask that question rather than as a threshold.
  4. Express the ceiling per PROSE LINE (the 236-315 B/line figures above) so density is measured directly instead of inferred.

DO NOT ACT ON THIS WITHOUT MIKE. Nothing is broken, no gate is red, and every affected leaf now carries a recorded exception with its reasoning, so the tree is self-consistent as it stands.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 07:2x AUSEST. WIDEN THE CARVE-OUT; DO NOT MOVE THE NUMBER, DO NOT ADD A GATE, DO NOT SPLIT THE LEAVES.

TWO PREMISES I CHECKED AT SOURCE RATHER THAN INHERITING, AND ONE OF THEM CHANGES WHAT THIS BEAD IS ABOUT.

(1) THE RULE IS ALREADY "SHOULD", NOT "MUST". skills/README.md:240 reads "each leaf file SHOULD be <=250 lines AND <=16 KB (target ~150 lines / ~10 KB)".

(2) NOTHING ENFORCES IT. Measured: a fixed-string search for "16 KB", "16384" and "16_384" across scripts/, implementation/scripts/ and .github/ returns ZERO files. There is no gate. So no bead has ever gone red on this ceiling, and none can.

THAT REFRAMES THE COST. The bead reads as "a ceiling is wrong and keeps failing people". It is not failing anything mechanical. What it costs is FOUR-PLUS WORKER CYCLES SPENT RE-DERIVING THE SAME EXCEPTION, each recorded on its own bead where the next author will not find it. The defect is that the page does not carry the answer, so every author reaches it alone.

AND THE PAGE ALREADY HAS THE RIGHT TEST. skills/README.md:246-253 carves out catalogue-shaped leaves on a real test: "would splitting reduce total tokens loaded per session?", with known-frictions.md worked through it - one trigger, scanned whole, a reader cannot know in advance which half holds their case, so a split loads both.

THE DENSE TEACHING LEAF PASSES THAT SAME TEST FOR A DIFFERENT REASON, AND THE PAGE NAMES ONLY THE FIRST REASON. A catalogue is scanned whole because it is unordered; a teaching leaf is READ whole because it is a single arc - reg-machine.md is not a bag of entries, it teaches one thing end to end, and half of it loads on the same trigger as the other half. Same test, same answer, second shape.

THE RULING.

1. Widen the carve-out to name the dense-teaching-leaf shape alongside the catalogue shape, under the UNCHANGED token test. One added shape, one worked example - reg-machine.md or ops.md, pick whichever reads clearer.

2. Record the measured leaves as exempt on that test, with their figures, so the next author CITES the record instead of re-deriving it. That is the whole point of the edit: turn four scattered bead-notes into one line on the page that owns the rule.

3. The 16 KB figure and the 250-line figure BOTH STAY. They are right for most leaves and the corpus audit behind them is cited at :255-257. Raising a number to stop it being exceeded is how a target stops meaning anything.

4. NO GATE. There is no gate today and adding one would convert a judgement into a refusal, on a rule whose whole content is "apply this test". That is the gold-plating this project's stance names.

WHY THIS WAY UNDER THE STANCE. "Trust the programmer" and "do not drown in the minutiae" both point the same way here: the author applying a stated test is the mechanism, and the repair is one prose edit to the section that already owns it. The alternative readings - move the number, gate the number, split ten dense leaves - each cost more and buy less.

WHAT I AM NOT RULING. Whether any INDIVIDUAL leaf should still be split on its merits. That stays the author's call at the time, which is exactly what a SHOULD is for.
close_reason: Landed on main via PR #9065 (89c56b38cd), one file, skills/README.md +30/-1. The mayor ruling of 2026-09-03 implemented as written: the Leaf size discipline carve-out now names the dense-teaching-leaf shape alongside the catalogue shape under the UNCHANGED token test, the measured exempt leaves are recorded with their figures so the next author cites them instead of re-deriving them, and the honest qualifier stays (two leaves were brought inside both ceilings by de-duplication, testing.md was genuinely split). Neither the 16 KB nor the 250-line figure moved, no gate was added, no leaf was split. The worker corrected three of my premises and I accepted all three: ops.md is catalogue-shaped rather than dense-teaching so reg-machine.md became the worked example; testing.md is still 1.48x over after its split, so the page says only that it was split; and a LEAF-SIZE gate does exist (check_skill_migration_o1617_router_drift.py, MAX_LEAF_LINES = 60) though it enforces a different rule on two named router leaves, leaving my premise that nothing enforces the README ceiling intact. title: spec(008-Testing): the poll-until CLJS example calls done in a downstream .catch — the carrier the skill copied from
description:
FOUND BY worker skillgates-a while resolving rf2-519x5 (PR #9042).

The AUDIT PR #9034 note on rf2-519x5 asked to repair BOTH carriers of the
downstream-catch/done poll-until example. The skill leaf half landed in PR
#9042 (skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing-views.md). The SPEC
half did not: spec/ was outside that dispatch's allowed paths.

TRUTH AT TIP, verified by reading: spec/008-Testing.md, under "#### poll-until
example", carries the CLJS fence

    (deftest cross-frame-drain
      (async done
        (-> (ts/poll-until ...)
            (.then (fn [_] (is ...) (done)))
            (.catch (fn [e] (is false ...) (done))))))

which is exactly the shape implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc
warns against in poll-until's own CLJS docstring: "Put the rejection handler
UPSTREAM of the single trailing step that calls `done`, and call `done` exactly
once with nothing after it (rf2-d3tc / rf2-qpns / rf2-fyba). `cljs.test/run-block`
hands `done` a continuation that runs the WHOLE REMAINDER of the run
synchronously, so a `.catch` sitting downstream of `done` claims whatever a
later namespace throws as this row's failure -- printing it against this row's
label -- and then calls `done` a SECOND time, which re-forces `run-block`'s
unrealized delay and re-runs the offending namespace."

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE SPEC: this is the carrier the skill copied FROM. PR
#9034 cited this exact fence as its authority. Leaving it means the next skill
pass can re-derive the defective shape from it, which is the loop the rf2-519x5
audit note explicitly asked to close ("repair both carriers rather than letting
the skill copy it again").

FIX SHAPE: rewrite that one fence to the docstring's prescribed shape --
assertion .then, rejection .catch that reports and returns nil, ONE trailing
.then that calls done. Consider whether the surrounding prose should name the
run-block reason, as the skill leaf now does. Nothing else in 008 moves.

HOT ZONE: spec/008-Testing.md is a spec file -- sequence it, do not parallel it
with another spec toucher.

The run-block reason (done's continuation runs the whole remainder of the run synchronously, so a downstream .catch claims a later namespace's throw as this row's failure and calls done twice) is now stated in the surrounding prose, as the repaired skill leaf already does. READ THE DOCSTRING AT SOURCE FIRST rather than copying the leaf: the leaf (skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing-views.md) is itself correct against the docstring, so the spec page and the leaf now agree with each other and with the docstring. VERIFICATION: nothing in this repo compiles that fence (check_doc_slugs.py strips fences before reading a line; mkdocs --strict validates links, not Clojure), so it was parsed with a real Clojure reader (babashka, :read-cond :allow, :features #{:cljs}) in both directions - corrected fence exit 0 (2 fences, 3+1 top-level forms), unbalanced control exit 1 ('EOF while reading, expected ) to match ('). HONEST BOUND: the pre-edit defective fence ALSO reads cleanly (measured, exit 0), so the reader proves balance, not the done-once discipline; that half was verified by hand against the docstring.

title: tools/xray(popout): a hard reload of the opener leaves the pop-out silently stale — no re-bootstrap, and opener-gone? does not fire
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-03 02:57 AUSEST by the xray-b worker while disposing rf2-9vm0. Filed rather than fixed: rf2-9vm0 was a spec-drift item and its mayor ruling explicitly says a real bug behind the drift is to be filed, not papered over with a normative-future marker.

THE SPEC SENTENCE. tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md, §Pop-out, last constraint bullet:

  'The pop-out can't survive a hard reload of the opener - atoms get
   garbage-collected. Pop-out re-bootstraps on opener reload by
   re-reading window.opener.xrayRuntime.'

Nothing sets or reads window.opener.xrayRuntime. Census at tip over tools/xray/src: 0 hits line-oriented AND 0 whitespace-collapsed, against an 'opener' control returning 79 and a 'popout' control returning 165. (The one near-miss, make-xray-runtime-fixture in test_support.cljs, is an unrelated test fixture.) That half is spec drift and rf2-9vm0 marks the HANDLE normative-future.

WHAT IS NOT DRIFT, AND IS WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS. The sentence also promises a RECOVERY BEHAVIOUR, and no other mechanism supplies it:

1. There is no re-bootstrap on opener reload. Nothing re-resolves the opener's runtime after a reload.
2. The opener-gone overlay does NOT cover this case. mount.cljs opener-gone? is
     (or (nil? opener) (.-closed opener))
   A SAME-ORIGIN HARD RELOAD of the opener leaves window.opener live (non-nil) and .closed false, so the 500ms watchdog never observes 'opener gone' and never reveals #rf-xray-popout-opener-gone-overlay. The overlay was built for the CLOSED / reference-nulled cases (rf2-h3ekl) and its own design comment names exactly those.

NET OBSERVABLE. After the user hard-reloads the app in the opener window, the pop-out keeps rendering against the PREVIOUS JS realm's atoms. Panels freeze on the old session's data with no UI signal of the cause - which is precisely the failure the rf2-h3ekl overlay was introduced to abolish, reached by a route the overlay's predicate does not detect. Worse than the closed-opener case it was modelled on, because a frozen-but-plausible panel invites the operator to trust stale values.

NOT REPRODUCED IN A BROWSER. This is read from source (mount.cljs popout!, opener-gone?, start-opener-gone-watchdog!, install-opener-gone-overlay!) plus the DOM semantics of window.opener across a same-origin reload. A browser reproduction should be the first step.

DISPOSITION IS OPEN and deliberately not pre-empted. At least three shapes: (a) widen opener-gone? to detect realm replacement (e.g. stamp a per-realm token on the opener and compare) and show the existing overlay - cheapest, honest, no new surface; (b) implement an actual re-bootstrap, which is what the spec sentence promises and what the window.opener.xrayRuntime handle was for; (c) rule the reload case out of scope pre-alpha and correct 011 to say the pop-out must be reopened by hand. Under the project stance (a) looks like the proportionate answer and (b) like the gold-plated one, but that is a call rather than a finding.

The 011 marker landed by rf2-9vm0 cites this bead so the spec does not claim a recovery that does not happen.
notes:
FIXED by PR #9056, https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9056, branch worker/xrayleak-a.

BOTH SOURCE READINGS VERIFIED AT TIP. (1) No re-bootstrap: xrayRuntime census over tools/xray/src returns 0 line-oriented AND 0 whitespace-collapsed, against controls opener=79, popout=165, .-opener=1 flattened — matching the bead. (2) opener-gone? is verbatim (or (nil? opener) (.-closed opener)) inside a defensive try; a same-origin hard reload leaves window.opener non-nil (a WindowProxy survives navigation, now fronting the NEW realm) and .closed false, so the predicate reads 'opener fine' and the watchdog never reveals the overlay.

A THIRD READING, WHICH CHANGES THE DISPOSITION AND IS THE MAIN FINDING HERE. Shape (a) — widen opener-gone? and reveal the existing overlay — CANNOT WORK, because the watchdog does not survive the event it would be asked to detect. Everything Xray runs for the pop-out lives in the OPENER's JS realm: popout! is called from there, substrate-adapter/render paints the pop-out's DOM from there, popout-state is an opener-realm atom, and start-opener-gone-watchdog!'s js/setInterval registers its timer on the OPENER's window. A hard reload discards that realm and every timer, closure and atom it owned, so after the reload there is no tick left to evaluate any predicate however widened. Detecting it after the fact would require Xray code running in the POP-OUT's own realm, which today runs none (the pop-out document is opened blank and rendered into from the opener) — i.e. injecting a script element, real new surface. So the bead's menu of (a) cheap / (b) gold-plated was not the real choice.

WHAT SHIPPED — a fourth shape the bead did not enumerate, and the cheapest honest one: THE OPENER ANNOUNCES ITS OWN DEATH ON THE WAY OUT. At pagehide the opener's realm is still alive and still holds the direct DOM handle to the pop-out's overlay node (same-origin, no serialisation layer — the pop-out's whole posture), so revealing the overlay is the EXISTING show-opener-gone-overlay!, reached from a different edge. The mutation lands in the pop-out's document, which is not reloaded, so it persists after the opener realm is gone. This delivers what (a) wanted — reuse the built machinery, tell the truth, no new surface — and unlike (a) it works. pagehide also fires on navigation and close, so it backstops the cases the watchdog already covers; the watchdog stays for the closed / reference-nulled cases.

TWO DELIBERATE CONSTRAINTS, both load-bearing. pagehide ONLY, never unload/beforeunload: this listener goes on the DEVELOPER'S OWN APPLICATION WINDOW, and an unload handler makes a page ineligible for the back/forward cache in every major browser — a devtool must not degrade the navigation behaviour of the app it inspects in order to report on itself. And a persisted pagehide is IGNORED: that is a bfcache freeze a back-navigation can resume, bringing the opener realm and the pop-out's render tree back alive, so announcing there would cry wolf. Plus a window-identity guard mirroring register-popout-unload-cleanup!, and detachment in teardown-popout-state! so repeated open/close cycles in one opener realm do not accumulate handlers.

OVERLAY COPY CORRECTED. It said 'The host application window has been closed', which is FALSE for a reload — the window is still on screen, and a message contradicting what the user can see reads as a bug in Xray rather than an explanation. Now: 'was closed or reloaded ... close this window and open a fresh pop-out'. The copy was pinned by neither the spec nor any test.

TESTS: five new arms in mount_cljs_test.cljs pinning the premise (opener-gone? reads false across a reload), the reveal, the persisted guard, the identity guard, and teardown detachment. Proved to bite: renaming 'pagehide' to 'unload' in mount.cljs turned npm run test:cljs RED (captured exit 1, 3 failures naming the new tests) — a RENAME, not a move, so a substring-matching assertion would not have caught it; restore verified by blob-hash equality (f873ede26f).

011 NOW DESCRIBES WHAT SHIPS. tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md §Pop-out: the constraint bullet states the pop-out does not re-bootstrap and announces instead, names register-opener-reload-announcer!, and records the pagehide-only / bfcache reasoning; the status note records why widening the predicate was not the answer. THE rf2-9vm0 NORMATIVE-FUTURE MARKER ON THE window.opener.xrayRuntime HANDLE IS UNTOUCHED AND KEEPS ITS REFERENT — the handle sentence was deliberately left in the bullet rather than deleted, so that settled ruling is not orphaned. No heading was changed (headings are anchors).

GATES: as recorded on rf2-ws60 — all foreground, unfiltered, exit codes captured, re-run on the final rebased base. npm run test:cljs exit 0 (11203 tests / 55820 assertions) is the lane that covers mount.cljs; check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 covers 011 and was proved to bite on a planted broken anchor (exit 1 naming file, line 427 and the anchor; restore blob-hash verified 0d97fa813a).
close_reason: Fixed by PR #9056. Both readings verified, plus a third that changed the disposition: widening opener-gone? could not work because the reload destroys the watchdog's timer (it lives in the opener's realm). Shipped the cheaper honest shape instead — the opener reveals the existing overlay at pagehide while it still holds the pop-out's DOM handle; pagehide-only to protect the host app's bfcache, persisted-pagehide ignored, identity-guarded, detached on teardown. Overlay copy corrected for the reload case. 011 now describes what ships; the rf2-9vm0 marker is untouched.

title: pilots briefs + friction-log.md instruct outcome 7 by moving the checkout pin, which rf2-hic-063's 2026-09-02 ruling forbids for the rehearsal
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 02:55 AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal. Tip d1e6a707a3.

THE CONTRADICTION. rf2-hic-063's RULING of 2026-09-02, clause (iii), fixes the rehearsal's method and says outcome 7 is 'recorded BLOCKED' — and its GATES AND TRAPS item 7 is explicit: 'the rehearsal's pinned commit goes in the log header and is not moved mid-pilot; outcome 7 is BLOCKED, not simulated.' rf2-t4jpz's own description repeats it: 'Outcome 7 (upgrade across the RC) is recorded BLOCKED — there is no second published pin — and is not simulated with a git pin move.'

The pilot-facing material, delivered earlier under rf2-v04s, says the opposite and is handed to the agent unmodified:

- brief-realworld.md and brief-linearlite.md, outcome 7: 'Move the version pin and upgrade across it. Your setup pins the library to one commit; record it, then move it to a later one at the end and record what the move cost.'
- friction-log.md, Part 1 rules: 'Outcome 7 needs two pins, and moving the checkout pin is what stands in for an upgrade until a release coordinate exists.'
- friction-log.md's blank template ends with an attestation asking for 'Checkout pin at start' and 'Checkout pin at end', which presupposes the move.

A pilot handed these does exactly what the brief says, moves the pin, and returns an outcome-7 verdict the ruling says must read BLOCKED. The operator then either accepts evidence the ruling excluded or discards work the brief demanded.

WHY IT IS NOT JUST A LABEL. The ruling's reason is substantive: 'UPGRADE on a checkout is moving a git pin, not moving a version across an RC', which is one of the three verbs that makes :local/root fail as §13 adoption proof. A simulated pin move produces a row that LOOKS like upgrade evidence, and the counted run is later read against the rehearsal's dispositioned log. That is the reading the ruling closes.

SCOPE. The briefs and friction-log.md are correct as written for the COUNTED run on a published artefact, where two pins genuinely exist. What is missing is the rehearsal's own override. The cleanest fix is not to edit the briefs' outcome 7 — the ruling wants them untouched for the counted run — but to have the rehearsal's dispatch carry the override explicitly, and to head the copied FRICTION-LOG.md with outcome 7 pre-marked BLOCKED so the pilot cannot spend effort on it.

NOTE ON CUSTODY. pilots/ has a custody rule ('a substantive amendment to any page here names its authorizing bead at the site') and rf2-hic-063's ruling says rf2-v04s is NOT reopened. So whoever fixes this names its authority at the site.

FILED, NOT FIXED.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 03:5x AUSEST. THE COUNTED-RUN INSTRUCTION IS CORRECT AND STAYS. THE REHEARSAL VERSION MUST READ BLOCKED. Do not resolve this by deleting either one.

The bead has this exactly right and its own SCOPE paragraph names the shape: the briefs and friction-log.md are correct AS WRITTEN for the counted run on a published artefact, where two pins genuinely exist. What is missing is that the rehearsal is running on :local/root where they do not, and the pilot-facing material is handed over unmodified.

SO THE FIX IS CONDITIONAL MATERIAL, NOT A CORRECTION. Outcome 7 on a checkout is BLOCKED and is not simulated by moving a git pin. The reason is substantive and rf2-hic-063 states it: "UPGRADE on a checkout is moving a git pin, not moving a version across an RC" is one of the three verbs that makes :local/root fail as section 13 adoption proof. A simulated pin move produces a row that LOOKS like upgrade evidence, and the counted run is later read against the rehearsal dispositioned log — that is the reading the ruling closes, and it closes it for a good reason.

MECHANISM IS YOURS TO CHOOSE, and I am not prescribing one because the package has conventions I have not read. A rehearsal addendum, a conditional block, or a rehearsal-specific copy are all acceptable. WHAT IS NOT ACCEPTABLE: (a) deleting the counted-run instruction, which will be needed and correct the day a release coordinate exists; (b) leaving the friction-log attestation asking for "Checkout pin at start" and "Checkout pin at end" in the rehearsal copy, since that presupposes the move and a pilot will honour it; (c) making a pilot decide which run it is in — the pilot is blinded and must not be asked to reason about the method.

Whatever you choose, the pilot-facing text for a REHEARSAL must be unambiguous on its own, read alone, with no knowledge of the ruling. That is the test to apply to your own wording before you finish.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9049 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9049), per the mayor ruling of 2026-09-03. MECHANISM CHOSEN: a rehearsal variant applied by the OPERATOR, in workspace.md's assembly immediately after step 6, under a new heading 'Rehearsal runs: outcome 7 is BLOCKED'. Chosen from the package's own conventions: workspace.md is the operator's page and the pilot is never sent to it (README.md), so a conditional there can never reach the pilot — which is what rules out (c); step 6 is where the two pilot-facing copies are made, so the delta sits against the step that produces the thing it changes; and the package already expresses variants as base-plus-delta ('Pilot 2 — LinearLite: the same file with the ... rows dropped'). A separate rehearsal PAGE was rejected because README.md's heading is '## The four pages' and a fifth would force a heading change, which the scope fence forbids. THE THREE UNACCEPTABLE OUTCOMES ARE ALL AVOIDED: (a) the counted-run instruction is untouched in both briefs and in friction-log.md; (b) the variant collapses the rehearsal copy's two-pin attestation to the single pin true of the run, and pre-fills outcome 7's row as BLOCKED so no effort is spent reaching it; (c) the pilot is never asked which kind of run it is in — the replacement text names neither 'rehearsal' nor 'counted run'. READ-ALONE TEST APPLIED, as the ruling required. The pilot's outcome 7 becomes: 'Not part of this run. Your project resolves the library from the checkout beside it rather than from a released version, so there is no released version to upgrade across and nothing here to attempt. Record outcome 7 as BLOCKED and move on — that is the expected verdict, not a failure and not a finding. Do not stand in for it by repointing the checkout at a different commit.' Read cold it answers what to do, why, that it is expected rather than a finding, and forecloses the pin move a resourceful agent would otherwise invent. Both facts it rests on are checkable from permitted material: the pilot's own deps.edn uses :local/root, and the published installation page says nothing is released. RESIDUAL CONTRADICTION CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: 'pin' occurs exactly ONCE in each brief — outcome 7 itself — so after the replacement BRIEF.md carries no reference to moving a pin at all; in the blank template the only remaining pin line is the header's singular 'Checkout pin:', which is true of a rehearsal and stays. Custody honoured: every amendment names its authorizing bead at the site, and no bead id was placed inside a pilot-facing fence.

title: the audit process emits bead ids that do not exist — rf2-wyvf2 is cited by rf2-l1hh's own audit note AND its acceptance criteria
notes:
FILED 2026-09-03 02:4x AUSEST by the mayor, on evidence returned by the records-a worker (PR #9041).

THE FINDING. Three bead ids cited in this repo resolve to nothing:
  - rf2-mxkq7 — cited in tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/view_walker.cljs:8 and in commit fe4ff001b9 subject. Tracked as rf2-rn3u.
  - rf2-k0rbk — cited in the bench/hicasso ambient_refusal test as the bead a PROVISIONAL marker is pending on. Tracked as rf2-fgwf.
  - rf2-wyvf2 — and this one is the reason this bead exists.

Each was verified absent with `bd show` returning "no issue found" (exit 1) against a control that resolves, AND against the full id list in the export.

WHY rf2-wyvf2 IS DIFFERENT, AND WHY THIS IS ITS OWN CLASS. The first two are TREE-side: a source comment or a test marker cites a dead id. That is rf2-fgwf and rf2-rn3u, both filed, both narrow, both P4-ish docstring work. rf2-wyvf2 is TRACKER-side: it is cited by rf2-l1hh own audit NOTE and, worse, by rf2-l1hh ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. So a worker dispatched on rf2-l1hh is told to satisfy a criterion that points at nothing, and the pointer was written by the audit process itself rather than by a human typing from memory.

THAT IS THE CLASS: the audit process emits bead ids that were never created. Every other instance of this shape in the repo is a HISTORICAL id — something that existed once, or a commit-subject artefact from a renaming. These are different: they are forward references that never landed. An acceptance criterion citing one cannot be satisfied and cannot be checked, and it reads as authoritative because acceptance criteria are where a worker looks for the definition of done.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS FOR, and it is NOT for fixing the three citations — those have their own beads.
  1. Establish the MECHANISM. Where do these ids come from? A plausible hypothesis, unverified: an audit drafts a follow-up bead id in prose, the create never runs (or fails), and the prose ships anyway. Another: an id is invented as a placeholder. Find out which, because the remedies differ completely.
  2. MEASURE THE POPULATION. How many cited-but-nonexistent ids are there across bead descriptions, notes and acceptance criteria? Note the trap that sank an earlier attempt at this: a census over the whole TREE returned 4,997 of 5,179 cited ids "absent", which is absurd on its face — the tracker holds ~520 issues and the repo deliberately keeps historical citations as provenance. The real class is much narrower: a LIVE CONDITIONAL GATED ON NOTHING (an acceptance criterion, a PROVISIONAL marker, a dependency edge), not a citation to a bead that once existed. Draw the boundary before counting, and state it.
  3. Only then decide whether anything mechanical is worth building. Under the stance this may well end as "record the rule and move on" — do not gold-plate a linter for three instances.

DO NOT close the three citation beads from here; they stand on their own.
MORE CARRIERS, 2026-09-03, from the xray-b worker while fixing rf2-rn3u. The phantom count in ONE FILE is now four, not one.

tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/view_walker.cljs cites rf2-mxkq7 (already known), and ALSO rf2-01il5, rf2-ztxnm8 and rf2-nr7vf2 — all verified absent by bd (exit 1) and against all 477 ids in the export, with a control that resolves. rf2-rn3u had flagged rf2-01il5 as unchecked and suspected; it is confirmed, and it brought two more with it.

WHAT THAT DOES TO THIS BEAD MEASUREMENT STEP. Four phantom ids in a single docstring block is not a scattering of typos — it is a pattern with a source, and it sharpens the hypothesis: these read like ids DRAFTED in prose whose create never ran. Whoever measures the population should start by asking whether all four trace to one authoring event, because if they do, the mechanism is one broken habit rather than a class of drift, and the remedy is correspondingly small.

Note the asymmetry that keeps this bead narrow: these four are TREE-side and inert — a reader follows them nowhere. rf2-wyvf2 is TRACKER-side, in an ACCEPTANCE CRITERION, where it gates a definition of done. Same defect, different blast radius.
PREMISE REFUTED, 2026-09-03, by the phantom-a worker. Measured, with controls in both directions.

THIS BEAD'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS FALSE. The title says "the audit process emits bead ids that do not exist" and the body says "they are forward references that never landed". Neither holds. EVERY id this bead names was a REAL bead that was CREATED, CLOSED, and later GARBAGE-COLLECTED out of the tracker.

METHOD. Absence from the CURRENT export proves nothing, because the tracker has been GC'd hard. Sampled 13 historical snapshots of .beads/issues.jsonl across the whole life of the export (11,413 commits, 2026-05-06..2026-09-03) and unioned their ids: 14,551 distinct ids ever exported, against 539 live today. Row counts show the collection directly - 10,444 rows on 2026-07-11, 2,149 on 2026-07-19, 533 today.

CONTROLS. rf2-2rtt6 (a large real programme, absent today) FOUND in history -> the instrument sees GC'd beads. rf2-fgwf (live) FOUND. rf2-zzzzznotanid NOT found -> no false positives.

THE SIX "PHANTOMS", ALL REAL, ALL CLOSED BEFORE GC:
  rf2-k0rbk  "rf2-2rtt6.122 follow-up: confirm or rename the provisional error id" - closed 2026-08-06, close_reason "ambient-frame-refused stands... Remaining touch: the provisional stamps' removal is a one-line comment/docs touch". That is EXACTLY the rf2-fgwf edit. The marker was correct when written and became stale when the bead was DISCHARGED - the mayor's own "third case", not a phantom.
  rf2-e28wl  "spec 009: the ambient-frame-refused row enumerates :operation as (:dispatch / :subscribe)..." - closed 2026-08-05, fixed in PR #7533.
  rf2-wyvf2  "feat(causa): Reactive panel - rebuild + rename L3 tab 'Views' -> 'Reactive'" - closed 2026-05-20, landed in #1741. So the rf2-l1hh acceptance-criteria citation is HISTORICAL PROVENANCE naming the PR that did the removal - it gates nothing. The "worst case" that motivated this bead is out of class by this bead's own boundary.
  rf2-mxkq7 / rf2-01il5 / rf2-ztxnm8 / rf2-nr7vf2 - all present in sampled history.

POPULATION, boundary stated first. Counted: a forward-looking marker (PROVISIONAL / pending / blocked on / to sequence with / awaiting / revisit / tracked as / see bead / deferred to / future work) in the SAME SENTENCE as an rf2- id absent from the live tracker; word-boundary matched excluding identifier context; over tracked files only. Result: 292 sites, 204 distinct absent ids, 172 files. title: re-frame.hicasso.server is still unscanned by the api-manifest: enrol implementation/hicasso/src in roster-covered-roots with a :cljs-only sidecar row
description:
The third of the three namespaces rf2-8arzr.7 found shipping unscanned. PR #9040 fixed the other two and left this one deliberately: implementation/hicasso/** was held by PR #9035 while that work ran.

Re-measure at tip before acting: #9035 landed on that tree since.

IT IS CLJS-ONLY, so it does NOT go in jvm-namespaces — the JVM generator cannot require it. It needs :cljs-only rows in spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn, which is already one of the three ways the restored roster gate accounts for a namespace: gen.clj's cljs-only-namespaces arm was built for exactly this case and is covered by a test (a-cljs-only-sidecar-row-accounts-for-a-namespace, which pins re-frame.hicasso.server by name in both directions).

THE COST, and it is the reason this is its own bead rather than a one-liner: adding 'implementation/hicasso/src' to roster-covered-roots obliges a classification for EVERY namespace under it — 25 unenrolled at last count — each recorded in internal-namespaces with a grouping comment, or enrolled. That is the same deliberate per-tree work #9040 did for the two SSR trees (33 internal entries). Do not add the root without doing it; the gate refuses to build otherwise, which is the point of it.

Also consider whether the CLJS enumeration probe (implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/, run by npm run test:cljs) should cover the namespace, which is what lets its rows carry :runtime-verified? true rather than false.
notes:
WORKED BY PR #9045 (rf2-8arzr.7 + rf2-3ne8 + rf2-63fw + rf2-ypom cluster). HALF LANDED; THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN FOR THE OTHER HALF.

LANDED: the four :cljs-only sidecar rows for re-frame.hicasso.server (payload-script, document, render, render-body) at :tier :implementation :owner 011 :status v1 :runtime-verified? false. Re-measured at tip: still exactly those four public vars, still zero ^:no-doc. It is CLJS-only because the ns :requires ["react-dom/server"], so ns-publics can never reach it. Manifest 506 -> 510. That closes the SHIPPING defect rf2-8arzr.7 named: the namespace is no longer unmanifested.

NOT LANDED, and this is the finding: implementation/hicasso/src was NOT added to roster-covered-roots.

NAMESPACE COUNT, derived with the generator's own namespaces-under rather than by file count: 26 namespaces under the root (26 .clj* files, all base paths distinct, so no .cljc/.cljs pair collapses). One (re-frame.hicasso) is already enrolled => 25 unenrolled, which matches this bead's own figure exactly. Confirmed by planting the root and running --check: exit 2, all 25 listed by name.

WHY THE ROOT WAS NOT ADDED. This bead assumes the 25 are 'each recorded in internal-namespaces with a grouping comment, or enrolled', with most going internal. They are not. At least FIVE are genuine public authoring surfaces, each with a require-me-directly example in its own ns docstring: re-frame.hicasso.forms (buffered-field), .motion (presence), .overlay (popover, modal), .native (use-sub, use-frame), .substrate (adapter, installed via rf/init!). tool and evidence are :tooling by their own docstrings and would be fine.

Their honest tier is :advanced/:adapter, which is docs-eligible. MEASURED with a control, not inferred, via doc_api_check/coverage-problems (public + pure): forms and substrate each yield {:kind :page-missing}, while the same-shaped control re-frame.hicasso/sub (which HAS docs/api/re-frame.hicasso.md) yields (). So enrolling them honestly obliges FIVE new docs/api/*.md pages. docs/** was outside PR #9045's permitted file list.

The alternatives were all false records and were refused: tiering authoring surfaces :implementation purely to dodge the docs obligation, or putting forms/motion/overlay in internal-namespaces, which contradicts that roster's own docstring ('Nothing here is published, documented or rowed'). The gate was NOT weakened.

WHAT REMAINS: a tiering ruling for those five (plus tool/evidence at :tooling), the docs/api pages that ruling obliges, then adding the root. That is a decision plus a docs dispatch, not a mechanical follow-on.

PROBE QUESTION ANSWERED: NO. :runtime-verified? false is correct. Covering the ns would pull react-dom/server into the api-manifest probe's build graph, which is a shared-build change rather than a row change; #9040 set the same precedent for its two.
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 03:5x AUSEST, on the finding manifest-a returned rather than worked around. THE FIVE ARE PUBLIC, THEY GET PAGES, AND THIS BEAD SPLITS.

WHAT THE WORKER FOUND, and it is the right call to have stopped: both this bead and my brief assumed the 25 unenrolled namespaces under implementation/hicasso/src were mostly internal. AT LEAST FIVE ARE PUBLIC AUTHORING SURFACES — forms, motion, overlay, native, substrate — each carrying a require-me-directly example in its own docstring. It proved the consequence with a control rather than asserting it: doc_api_check/coverage-problems yields :page-missing for the target and () for a same-shaped control that has a page. So the honest tier is docs-eligible, which obliges five new docs/api/*.md pages, and docs/** was outside its fence.

THE RULING: TIER THEM HONESTLY AND WRITE THE PAGES. Do not reach for ^:no-doc to make the gate quiet. substrate is what an app requires to call (rf/init! substrate/adapter); these are not plumbing. Under the stance — excellent ergonomics, low friction, a library that is a masterpiece — a public authoring surface with no documentation page is precisely the friction we exist to remove, and the gate has just done its job by refusing to let five of them ship unrecorded. That is the opposite of gold plating: it is the gate catching a real gap the manifest was blind to.

SO THIS BEAD SPLITS, and the ordering is forced by the gate rather than by preference:
  (1) A DOCS dispatch writes the five docs/api/*.md pages. It needs docs/** and cannot run while another worker holds that tree.
  (2) The SAME PR (or one immediately after, but the same worker) adds implementation/hicasso/src to roster-covered-roots and classifies all 26 namespaces — five enrolled docs-eligible, the rest recorded in internal-namespaces with grouping comments. The gate REFUSES TO BUILD until every namespace under an added root is accounted for, which is the point of it, so the root and the classification are one commit.
Doing (2) before (1) reds the tree; doing (1) without (2) leaves the manifest still blind. One worker, both halves, docs/** free.

WHAT ALREADY LANDED AND MUST NOT BE REDONE: the four :cljs-only rows are in (manifest 506 -> 510), which fixes the actual shipping defect for re-frame.hicasso.server. This bead remainder is the ROOT plus the classification plus the five pages.

AND NOTE THE NUMBER IS CONFIRMED, NOT ASSUMED: the worker derived 26 namespaces using the generator own namespaces-under rather than the 26-FILE count I gave it in the brief, and 1 already enrolled leaves 25 unenrolled — matching this bead original figure exactly, by a different route. That is the kind of agreement worth trusting.

rf2-qvhx (how far the roster gate should widen, 243 namespaces under uncovered trees) is a SEPARATE and larger question and is not settled here. This ruling covers one tree.

title: gate(check_skill_migration_contract_drift): remediation advice names register-error-listener!, a facade fn that does not exist
description:
scripts/check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py prints remediation advice that
names a facade fn which does not exist.

SITES: the module docstring (~line 35) and the M13-FRAME-ONERROR problem message
(~line 731) both read: "Error observability is `register-error-listener!`
(always-on) / `register-listener!` (dev-only)."

TRUTH AT TIP, confirmed by EVALUATION on the JVM for PR #9039 (rf2-qbgy1), not by
reading: re-frame.core exports ONE stream-parameterised pair --
(:arglists (meta #'rf/register-listener!)) => ([stream id f]) and
(:arglists (meta #'rf/unregister-listener!)) => ([stream id]). There is no
rf/register-error-listener!; that name survives only as an INTERNAL error-emit
alias the facade delegates to for the :errors stream. The dev/prod axis is carried
by the STREAM, not by two different verbs: :errors and :events are always-on,
:trace is dev-only.

IMPACT is narrow but real and inverted: this text is what the gate prints to tell
an author how to FIX a drift it just caught, so an author who follows the
remediation writes (rf/register-error-listener! ...) -- an unresolved-symbol
compile error. A gate that steers toward a non-existent symbol is worse than
silence.

FIX SHAPE: both strings become the stream-first form, e.g. "Observability is
`(register-listener! :errors ...)` (always-on) / `(register-listener! :trace ...)`
(dev-only)." This is advice text only -- it is NOT a content pin, so no document
moves with it and no gate output changes shape.

OUT OF FENCE for rf2-qbgy1's dispatch (scripts/ was barred), hence filed rather
than fixed. Same class as rf2-qbgy1: the collapsed listener API stated in its
pre-collapse spelling.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-09-03, worker/skillgates-a, PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9042 (base 70f6cea39b). bd history walked to the item's beginning: zero text-bearing changes since creation, so the description was the live instruction.

Exercised in both directions by evaluation: line_problems() returns exactly 1 problem on the stale claim and 0 on a clean sentence. No change was made to the check.

THE ADVICE WAS WRONG, at both sites the bead names -- the module docstring (~:35) and the M13-FRAME-ONERROR message (~:731). VERIFIED AT SOURCE rather than copied from the brief: implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc defines register-listener! at :2126 with arglist [stream id f] and unregister-listener! at :2161 with [stream id]; register-error-listener! exists ONLY as error-emit/register-error-listener!, the internal delegate the facade calls for the :errors stream (:2157). [stream id], and register-error-listener! exists only as the internal error-emit delegate at :2157 — so the old advice steered authors at an unresolved symbol and also inverted the axis (the dev/prod split is the stream, not the verb).
