title: conformance fixture loaders: an early ] escapes the one-form guard and hides trailing EDN
description:
FOLLOW-ON to rf2-x91a, which landed shape (a) - the corpus scanner - in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9038 and left shape (b) unbuilt.

rf2-x91a PREFERS (b): make the loaders themselves refuse trailing text, because a loader check cannot drift from what the runner actually parses. That was out of the landing dispatch's fence (implementation/**), so only (a) was built. (a) satisfies rf2-x91a's acceptance - a misplaced brace now fails a gate that runs on every PR - and it holds one advantage (b) can never have: a fixture whose capabilities are out of claim is SKIPPED by the runner, so a defect in it is invisible to any load-time check forever. The two are complementary, not alternatives.

PREMISE CORRECTION, MEASURED AT TIP. rf2-x91a describes (b) as 'a few lines in each of the two host-specific loaders' and names conformance_fixtures.clj and conformance_test.clj. There are SEVEN files that slurp + edn/read-string over spec/conformance/fixtures:

  implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_fixtures.clj
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj
  implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_conformance_test.clj
  implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machines_conformance_test.clj
  implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_conformance_test.clj
  implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_conformance_test.clj
  implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_streaming_conformance_test.clj

Five of the seven share a near-identical io/file + file-seq preamble, so the change may well factor into one shared helper rather than seven edits - worth reading before scoping. The CLJS leaf inlines fixtures at compile time and needs the equivalent at its macro seam, per rf2-x91a.

SHAPE. Read with a PushbackReader and assert EOF after the first form, or read (str "[" content "]") and assert exactly one element. A fixture with trailing text then fails LOUD at load, on every host that loads the corpus, in the same run that would otherwise pass it.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH DOING with (a) landed: (a) is a separate lexical scanner and can in principle disagree with what the reader does; (b) cannot, because it IS the reader. (a) is the wide net, (b) is the exact one.

GATE. Plant a trailing form in a fixture the loader actually reads and show the load fail; the JVM conformance suites for the artefacts touched.
close_reason: Fixed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9061. The audit's escape reproduced at base 69b33ca474 by direct call: read-one-form returned #:fixture{:id :first} without throwing on '{:fixture/id :first}' + newline + '] {:fixture/id :silently-hidden}'. All SEVEN loaders now read the ORIGINAL text through a PushbackReader and prove EOF behind the first form with a second edn/read against a sentinel — no synthetic envelope, so nothing to close early. A reader error is re-thrown as ex-info so it still names the fixture. Regression one-form-guard-rejects-early-close-bracket leads with trailing text opening with ']' (discriminating: ordinary trailing text passed against the old body). Bites both ways on a real fixture: planted early-] into machine-actor-isolation.edn -> old body ACCEPTED and discarded the hidden map, new body threw; core and machines suites both exit 1 naming the fixture; restored and verified by git hash-object blob equality. Clean corpus unmoved at 247 fixtures with parsed data IDENTICAL old vs new. Classpath claim CONFIRMED: flows' own :test classpath carries core/src but not core/test, so the seven copies stay and no shared production namespace was added (the aggregate implementation/deps.edn :test alias does pool all test trees, but is documented REPL-only). Spine re-run on the final rebased base: captured exit 0.

title: check_retired_spellings.py does not know machine-has-tag?, so every carrier has been found by hand
description:
FOUND BY worker pairskill-e while fixing rf2-1e8m (PR #9037).

scripts/check_retired_spellings.py is EP-0007 'One Name Per Fact' Enforcement's CI gate, and its roots ALREADY include examples, implementation, tools, skills, testbeds, migration (scripts/check_retired_spellings.py:297-302). But machine-has-tag? is not in its roster: grep for 'has-tag' in that script returns 0. CONTROL: grep for 'retired' in the same file returns 83, so the search instrument bit — the zero is real, not a mis-typed pattern.

CONSEQUENCE, measured across two beads: every carrier of this retired name has been found by a HAND-RUN census. rf2-17wco found the spec + skills carriers by hand; it could not fix examples/, so it filed rf2-1e8m; rf2-1e8m's examples carriers were then found by another hand-run three-way census in PR #9037. Three censuses for one retired name, and the gate that exists to prevent exactly this was green throughout.

TRUTH AT TIP: no src namespace defines machine-has-tag? (git grep -F over implementation/*/src returns nothing). spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:816 records it as facade subscription-sugar REMOVED under rf2-il99l3 (reversing rf2-2cmcas) so a machine read has ONE grammar. The shipped surface is the [:rf.machine/has-tag? <machine-id> <tag>] subscription registered at implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc:407.

WHY I DID NOT JUST ADD IT — and this is the actual work, not a formality. Adding the spelling today REDS THE TREE, because the remaining carriers at tip are legitimate and must be allow-listed FIRST:
- implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/{nine_states,realworld,websocket}_cljs_test.cljs — PRIVATE defn- test helpers named machine-has-tag? / settings-machine-has-tag? / tags-machine-has-tag?. rf2-1e8m classified these DO NOT TOUCH: they are correct. Roughly 60 call sites.
- docs/machines/tags.md:101 — names the fn ONLY TO DENY it ('There is no machine-has-tag? function'). A deny-site must not be flagged; scripts/check_doc_slugs.py:575 already allow-lists its back-compat anchor, so there is precedent for the shape.
- docs/EP/EP-0002-frame-target-resolution.md:606,933,1420 and docs/tools/playground/README.md:20,124 + sci/deps.edn:19 — rf2-1e8m explicitly left these UNCLASSIFIED: 'check before editing'. EP-0002 reads like a historical design record (so probably a legitimate mention); the playground ones read like live surface claims and may be REAL carriers. Classify them as part of this bead.

SO THE SHAPE IS: (1) classify the EP-0002 and playground sites, fixing any that present the name as live; (2) add machine-has-tag? to the retired-spelling roster with an allow-list covering the private test helpers and the deny-site; (3) confirm the gate goes red on a planted carrier before believing its green.

Fenced out of PR #9037 deliberately: scripts/ was outside that PR's allowed paths, and implementation/ was held.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-09-03, worker/skillgates-a, PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9042 (base 70f6cea39b). bd history walked to the item's beginning: zero text-bearing changes since creation, so the description was the live instruction.

THE BEAD'S CENTRAL PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD, and this is the main finding. "Adding the spelling today REDS THE TREE" is false: the measured red list, before allow-listing anything, is EMPTY -- exit 0 across 905 source files. NO allow-list was needed or added.

WHY. Rules (a)-(c) open only .clj/.cljc/.cljs, prune test/ dirs unless --include-tests, and mask string literals and ; comments. CI (.github/workflows/test.yml:511) and scripts/test-fast-pr.sh:942 both invoke the gate WITHOUT --include-tests. The complete census of the spelling at tip is 8 files and not one is visible: docs/EP/EP-0002 (3, .md + not a root), docs/machines/tags.md (1, the deny-site, .md + not a root), docs/tools/playground/README.md (2, .md -- root scanned, suffix never opened), docs/tools/playground/sci/deps.edn (1, .edn), implementation/adapters/reagent/test/{nine_states,realworld,websocket}_cljs_test.cljs (23/15/39, test/ dirs pruned), spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn (1, .edn + not a root).

THE MORE USEFUL FINDING, and it corrects the bead's diagnosis: the gate was green through three hand censuses NOT because the roster lacked the name. Both carriers anyone actually found (PR #9037, commit 26f0b5df59) lived exactly where rules (a)-(c) structurally cannot look -- one in examples/patterns/nine_states/README.md (prose), one INSIDE a ;; comment in examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs, masked before any pattern runs: ";; `:rf.machine/has-tag?` (sugar: `(rf/machine-has-tag? :ws/connection". Adding the name to the existing rules -- the bead's step (2) -- would have changed nothing.

SO THE NEEDLE IS SHAPED FOR WHERE THE CARRIERS LIVE. New rule (e) reads RAW lines (the only rule here that does not mask comments) and matches two shapes: a namespace-QUALIFIED <alias>/machine-has-tag?, and a PUBLIC (defn|def) machine-has-tag?. Three token boundaries do the whole job an allow-list would have done -- a preceding ':' is denied (so the separately-retired keyword :rf/machine-has-tag? and the deny-site cannot fire it); the '/' must sit immediately before the name (so the ~60 unqualified private helpers, their call sites, the settings-/tags- prefixed variants, and every prose roster listing the name after a slash-and-space stay green); and defn- is excluded by requiring whitespace after def/defn. The shipped :rf.machine/has-tag? carries /has-tag?, so it cannot collide.

EXERCISED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Fires on the real historical carrier and 4 other reintroduction shapes; green on all 14 negatives including every one of the 8 live sites. A planted qualified call in the worker worktree took the gate RED naming the planted line (exit 1); restore verified by git blob hash 417fc80832da75a6d488bed5aeecbd89d23b554d against the committed object. The plant caught a real defect in the change itself -- a missing _FIX_HINTS entry crashed _report -- now fixed and re-run. SELF-TEST ARMED AND PROVEN ARMED: 17 rule-(e) cases added as raw pinned lines via the gate's existing _SANCTIONED_PROSE_MENTIONS mechanism (scripts/_test_fixtures/ was outside this dispatch's fence, so no new fixture files); self-tests 37 -> 54; blinding the needle in memory flips the suite exit 0 -> 1 with exactly the 5 positives failing.

STEP (1) DONE AS CLASSIFICATION, NOT AS EDITS -- docs/ was outside this dispatch's fence. docs/tools/playground/README.md:124 and sci/deps.edn:19 DO present the retired name as a live activated surface and are real carriers; EP-0002's three are a historical design record; docs/machines/tags.md is a correct deny-site; spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn is the retirement record. Full classification filed as rf2-wd0h. Rule (e) deliberately does NOT catch those two: both spell the name UNQUALIFIED, which is indistinguishable in shape from the deny-site and the retirement record, so an unqualified prose mention presenting a retired name as live needs human classification. That residual is recorded on rf2-wd0h rather than papered over with a looser needle.
close_reason: PR #9042 adds machine-has-tag? to the retired-spelling gate as rule (e). The bead's premise that this reds the tree does NOT hold: measured red list is empty (exit 0, 905 files) and no allow-list was needed — all 8 carriers are .md/.edn, outside the roots, or in pruned test dirs. Corrected diagnosis: both carriers ever found by hand lived in prose and a masked ;; comment, so adding the name to rules (a)-(c) would have changed nothing; rule (e) therefore reads raw lines and matches the qualified/public-definition shapes only. Fires on the real historical carrier, green on all 8 live sites; planted fault reds the gate, restore verified by blob hash; self-test 37->54 and proven armed. docs/ carriers classified and filed as rf2-wd0h (fenced out here).

title: skill(re-frame2-pair): the ops.md catalogue-exemption ruling and the package's own spec contradict each other
description:
FOUND BY worker pairskill-e while executing rf2-wgvyx's ruling (PR #9037). NOT a re-argument of that ruling — a contradiction it leaves standing, which needs a maintainer call rather than a worker's reflex.

THE MAYOR RULING on rf2-wgvyx (2026-09-03 03:2x AUSEST) says: 'SPLIT THE HICASSO-EVIDENCE BLOCK OUT... THE CATALOGUE EXEMPTION IS REFUSED FOR THIS LEAF.'

THE SPLIT IT ORDERED WAS ALREADY DONE — eaf6591310 took the Hicasso block out WITH the screen-read block, in the same commit. Evidence on rf2-wgvyx.

SO THE REFUSAL NOW HAS NO EXECUTABLE REMAINDER, and that is the problem:

1. ops.md is 220 lines / 46,461 LF-normalised bytes — 2.8x the 16 KB per-leaf ceiling in skills/README.md.
2. Every section left in it is one rf2-wgvyx EXPLICITLY FORBIDS splitting: 'Do NOT split hot-reload or the v1 map (locked + tested), and do not split the op tables (that is the catalogue the exemption is for)'. Remaining headings: Read, Frames, Write, Trace, Live watch, Signal recording, Hot-reload coordination, Time-travel, Dropped from v1.
3. The hot-reload protocol and v1 surface-map placement is LOCKED by skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/design.md:135 and spec/authoring-prompt.md:33, and tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj reads ops.md by anchor (ops.md#hot-reload-coordination).
4. AND THE PACKAGE'S OWN SPEC STILL GRANTS THE EXEMPTION IN WRITING, in both places, unchanged: design.md:135 'the two catalogue leaves (ops.md, recipes.md) run longer where a split would not reduce tokens-per-session', and authoring-prompt.md:49 the same clause. A future re-authoring pass reads those and keeps ops.md whole, because that is what they say.

So the tree currently asserts both things at once: the ruling refuses ops.md the exemption, the package spec grants it.

THE DECISION NEEDED is one of three, and it is Mike's or the mayor's, not a worker's:
(a) RECORD THE EXEMPTION HONESTLY — accept ops.md as a documented exception in skills/README.md Leaf size discipline with the reasoning, and leave design.md:135 as is. rf2-wgvyx's own DESCRIPTION already names this as the honest alternative: 'If the maintainer would rather keep ops.md whole, the honest alternative is to record ops.md as an accepted exception... the current state is neither.'
(b) NAME WHICH LOCKED SECTION MOVES, and lift the lock on it in design.md + authoring-prompt.md in the same PR, re-pointing the prompt-regression anchors.
(c) RESTATE THE REFUSAL as applying only to non-catalogue blocks, which is what it in fact achieved, and strike the ceiling claim against ops.md.

Note recipes.md sits in exactly the same position (424 lines / 46,086 B) and is the exemption's own worked example, so whichever way this goes should say whether it binds recipes.md too.

NOT URGENT AND NOT A BUG: nothing is broken, no gate is red, no reader is misled by ops.md's content. What is wrong is that two normative records disagree, so the next re-authoring pass gets a different answer depending on which it reads.
notes:
MAYOR ACKNOWLEDGEMENT, 2026-09-03 04:2x AUSEST — THIS BEAD EXISTS BECAUSE MY RULING CONTRADICTED A NORMATIVE RECORD I DID NOT CHECK, AND THE WORKER WAS RIGHT NOT TO RE-ARGUE IT.

WHAT I DID. Two hours ago I ruled that ops.md is REFUSED the catalogue exemption, reasoning that a leaf from which a self-contained block can be lifted entire is not catalogue-shaped. I derived that from the first split's success and from the leaf still measuring 46 KB. I did not check whether any record already GRANTED the exemption. Two do, in writing: skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/design.md:135 and spec/authoring-prompt.md:49.

SO THERE ARE NOW TWO NORMATIVE RECORDS IN DISAGREEMENT, and that is a maintainer call rather than something a worker should resolve by picking the newer one. Filing it was the correct response and I am not overriding it here.

AND MY RULING'S FACTUAL PREMISE WAS ALSO WRONG, which the same worker established: the Hicasso-evidence block did NOT remain in ops.md. It came out WITH the screen-read block in the same commit eaf6591310 — 105 lines removed, screen-reads.md created with 106, carrying all three sections the bead's own recommendation nominated, Hicasso evidence among them. ops.md's only case-insensitive hicasso match is a Contents pointer. I inferred a remaining block from the bead's TITLE naming two things and from the leaf still measuring 46 KB; both facts were true and the inference was not. The leaf is 46 KB because of the catalogue the bead ITSELF forbids splitting — which is the same fact that makes the exemption question live rather than settled.

SO THE HONEST STATE IS: my ruling directed work already done, on a premise that was wrong, against a contract that already said the opposite. The worker measured, invoked my own STOP clause rather than inventing a block to lift, and shipped the bead's real live remainder instead — a forbidden SKILL -> screen-reads -> ops chain that skills/README.md and authoring-prompt.md:49 both prohibit, with a regression assertion that had been weak independently (a bare 'ops.md' substring test passes on the provenance sentence 'split out of ops.md' with the safety rule entirely absent).

FOR WHOEVER RESOLVES THIS BEAD: the question is not 'was the mayor right'. It is whether re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md, as a locked catalogue its own bead forbids splitting, should carry the exemption its spec already grants — and if so, whether skills/README.md's exemption bullet should name it the way it now names recipes.md and known-frictions.md. Decide the CONTRACT, then make the three records agree. Do not resolve it by deleting whichever record is easiest to edit.
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 04:2x AUSEST. I AM WITHDRAWING MY OWN REFUSAL. The catalogue exemption APPLIES to ops.md remainder; RECORD THE EXCEPTION and do not split further.

WHY I AM REVERSING MYSELF, stated plainly because a ruling that quietly changes is worse than one that was wrong. On rf2-wgvyx I wrote "THE CATALOGUE EXEMPTION IS REFUSED FOR THIS LEAF". That refusal was wrong on two axes, both of which the pairskill-e worker demonstrated and I acknowledged when filing this bead: the split I ordered had ALREADY BEEN DONE (eaf6591310 took the Hicasso-evidence block out WITH the screen-read block, in one commit), and I refused an exemption that TWO EXISTING RECORDS ALREADY GRANT (skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/design.md:135 and spec/authoring-prompt.md:49). A mayor ruling does not outrank a landed record it did not read.

WHAT IS LEFT IS EXACTLY WHAT THE EXEMPTION IS FOR, and my own ruling says so. ops.md is 220 lines / 46,461 LF-normalised bytes, 2.8x the 16 KB per-leaf ceiling. Its remaining headings are Read, Frames, Write, Trace, Live watch, Signal recording, Hot-reload coordination, Time-travel, Dropped from v1 — and rf2-wgvyx forbids splitting every one of them: "Do NOT split hot-reload or the v1 map (locked + tested), and do not split the op tables (that is the catalogue the exemption is for)". So the refusal has no executable remainder: it forbids an outcome while forbidding every route to it.

THE RULING: record a named EXCEPTION on ops.md, in the same shape as rf2-baso — the reason written down beside it, not a claimed exemption in passing. The reason has three parts and all three are already established: (a) the op tables ARE the catalogue the exemption names; (b) hot-reload coordination and the v1 surface map are LOCKED by design.md:135 and authoring-prompt.md:33; (c) tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj READS ops.md BY ANCHOR (ops.md#hot-reload-coordination), so a split is not merely discouraged, it reds a test.

DO NOT TRIM TEACHING TO REACH A BYTE NUMBER. That is the stance answer and it is the same one rf2-baso got.

AND THE CHECK-ME CLAUSE STAYS, for the same reason it existed on rf2-baso: before implementing, read skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/design.md and spec/authoring-prompt.md and skills/README.md for any existing leaf-size statement. Follow an existing record if one covers this. If a record CONTRADICTS this ruling, STOP and report rather than picking the newer one — that is a maintainer call, and this bead exists because I got exactly that wrong once already.
close_reason: Exception recorded in PR #9051 per the mayor's withdrawal of the rf2-wgvyx refusal. DID THE CHECK-ME CLAUSE FIRST, and it is the reason this close is safe: no record CONTRADICTS the ruling — two already AGREE with it, so I followed them rather than adding a second competing record. WHAT EACH SAID, verified at the exact lines the bead names: skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/design.md:135 already grants the exemption in writing ('the two catalogue leaves (ops.md, recipes.md) run longer where a split would not reduce tokens-per-session') and carries the LOCK on the hot-reload protocol and the v1 map; skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/authoring-prompt.md:49 carries the same grant verbatim and :33 the same lock ('MUST NOT be split out'); skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/inputs.md says NOTHING AT ALL about size; skills/README.md 'Leaf size discipline' is SILENT on ops.md, naming only recipes.md and known-frictions.md, and its closing sentence makes the TEST the discriminator, which agrees. Because two records grant it IN PASSING, I extended design.md with the reason written beside it — the shape rf2-baso used at skills/re-frame-migration/spec/design.md:136 — rather than claiming an exemption in passing a third time. RE-MEASURED AT MY OWN BASE: 220 lines / 46,461 LF-normalised bytes, matching this bead exactly; git cat-file -s on the committed blob confirms 46,461. That is 2.84x the 16 KB ceiling. recipes.md (424 L / 46,086 B) is bound by the same record, which the bead asked be settled either way. THE THIRD REASON VERIFIED AT SOURCE AND THEN EXERCISED, since it was the strongest and the likeliest to have moved: tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj reads ops.md by anchor two ways — line 205 asserts SKILL.md contains the literal 'ops.md#hot-reload-coordination', and section-from @ops-md 'Hot-reload coordination' extracts the section BY HEADING at lines 477, 506 and 541. Clean run 28 tests / 211 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors, captured exit 0. I then PLANTED the split the ruling says would red it (removed the 5,457 B Hot-reload coordination section): captured exit 1, 9 failures across 3 tests. Restored and verified by git blob hash 84fc826a36b559f276f8e1123f4d55f12ae6ba94, green again at exit 0. WORTH RECORDING FOR THE NEXT READER: a weaker first plant came back GREEN — renaming the heading by APPENDING to it still passes, because section-from matches its anchor as a SUBSTRING. The assertion is real but looser than 'reads it by anchor' suggests: it catches a move or a removal, not every rename. NOT split further, NOT trimmed, headings untouched, ceiling unchanged. Gates green post-rebase onto d7ddb22dbb: fast-PR spine PASS exit 0, all 14 check_skill_*.py exit 0 (pair_authoring_drift and mcp_drift among them), doc-slugs 0 (proven to read this worktree by a planted broken anchor going red at exit 1, restored and verified by blob hash b56a6986b1b79183af89717fd4d1a8adf6d5efde), readme-links 0, package-refs --ci 0, mkdocs --strict 0 — though mkdocs covers NONE of this diff, since docs_dir is docs and mkdocs_hooks.py's _STAGE stages only spec/ and migration/. Ceiling observation filed as rf2-wh25, not acted on.

title: examples: two files still present machine-has-tag? as a live fn — the retired facade sugar (nine_states README, websocket connection.cljs)
description:
CLAIM. Found by the rf2-17wco skills-half census (worker/rf2skill-g, PR #9034), which was scoped to skills/ and could not fix these.

examples/patterns/nine_states/README.md:102 — 'control buttons disable themselves by asking `machine-has-tag?` for'.
examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs:773 — '`:rf.machine/has-tag?` (sugar: `(rf/machine-has-tag? :ws/connection'. This one is worse: it names the correct sub and then presents the retired fn as live sugar over it.

TRUTH AT TIP. No src namespace anywhere defines machine-has-tag? — git grep -F over implementation/*/src returns no hits. The shipped surface is the runtime sub registered at implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc:407, taking [_ machine-id tag]. spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:816 records that machine-has-tag? and sub-machine ONCE EXISTED as facade subscription-sugar fns and were REMOVED under rf2-il99l3 (reversing rf2-2cmcas) so a machine read has ONE grammar. So this is a retired name, not one that was never real — which is why it survives in prose.

FIX SHAPE. Two-line edit naming the [:rf.machine/has-tag? <machine-id> <tag>] subscription, matching the wording landed at spec/005-StateMachines.md:530. The websocket site should drop the 'sugar:' parenthetical outright rather than rewording it.

DO NOT TOUCH, these are correct and were checked: spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:816 (deliberate retirement record); docs/machines/tags.md (names the fn only to DENY it — 'There is no machine-has-tag? function' — plus a back-compat <a id="querying-with-machine-has-tag"> anchor that scripts/check_doc_slugs.py:575 allowlists); the private defn- helpers in three adapter test namespaces plus derivation_graph_test.clj and tags_test.clj. docs/EP/EP-0002 and docs/tools/playground/** also carry the name and were not classified — check before editing.

CENSUS METHOD that found these, worth reusing: match the literal three ways over git ls-files — line-oriented, whitespace-COLLAPSED, and whitespace-STRIPPED. The collapsed pass alone has a blind spot: it turns a hyphen-broken token into 'machine-has- tag?' and stops matching. Control 'has-tag?' must bite in each pass.

GATE. Examples are test-free per rf2-8cevm; nine_states/README.md is prose. The connection.cljs site is a comment, so no gate reads it — verify by hand.
notes:
WORKER pairskill-e, PR #9037 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9037). FIXED, both sites, matching in-tree wording rather than inventing phrasing (spec/005-StateMachines.md:530 and docs/machines/tags.md:101).

nine_states/README.md: 'asking machine-has-tag? for :mode/read-only' -> 'asking [:rf.machine/has-tag? :ui/nine-states :mode/read-only]'. Machine id verified real: core.cljs:438 registers :ui/nine-states and core.cljs:742,759 already use that exact subscription vector, so the README now matches the code beside it.

CONFIRMED THE BEAD'S OWN PREDICTION: connection.cljs:773 is a COMMENT (a ;; line in the subs section), not live code. The live code beneath it (778+) already chains off :<- [:rf.machine/has-tag? :ws/connection :websocket/connecting]. So there is NO larger finding and no gate was ever red — the comment advertised retired sugar over the correct sub it named in the same breath. File still parses: 9 top-level forms, :read-cond :allow.

CENSUS over git ls-files examples/ (167 files), all three forms as the bead prescribed. Before: 2 hits/2 files line-oriented, whitespace-collapsed AND whitespace-stripped alike. After: 0 in all three. Hyphen-break variant 'machine-has- tag?' probed explicitly: 0 both times. Control 'has-tag?' bites in every pass: 73 -> 72 hits across 22 files (drops by exactly 1 because the dropped connection.cljs parenthetical held one has-tag? while the README replacement retains one — arithmetic confirming both edits landed). So the post-fix zeros are checks that passed, not patterns that missed.

Not widened beyond examples/. The two skills/ carriers rf2-17wco named were cleared by 4554fdd3d3, which landed on main during this work and is in this branch's base — repo-wide grep now returns no skills/ hits.

title: ssr-node README's Reading 2 prose predates #9024's loader-position rescope; only Reading 1 was updated
notes:
FOUND BY THE FIX-FORWARD REBASE OF PR #9015 (rf2-8arzr.6), 2026-09-03 01:20:24 AUSEST, at base 2e7d21d9cb. NOT FIXED THERE deliberately: implementation/ssr-node/** is #9024's tree (rf2-8arzr.9) and #9015 was fenced from widening its diff.

THE DRIFT. implementation/ssr-node/README.md documents absence.test.cjs in 3 readings. #9024's commit 96ce8bb3d2 rescoped READING 2 ('it is on no build's source path') from a raw-text scan of implementation/shadow-cljs.edn + implementation/deps.edn to a LOADER-POSITION read -- for .edn, the value form after each of EDN_LOAD_KEYS, where :source-paths, :deps and :local/root live. The README's Reading 2 bullet was not updated to match.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC. Reading 1's bullet already carries the equivalent narrowing in prose, at length, citing rf2-6ovv: it explains loader positions, says a format that cannot resolve a module offers no loader position, and states that no allowance list was added. Reading 2's bullet still reads as an absolute claim about MENTIONING -- 'implementation/shadow-cljs.edn names no build reaching it'. Post-#9024 that file DOES name the package: a ;; comment at implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1629 explains which sidecar loads the module the :examples/login-hicasso-server build emits. That comment is what earned the original red, and rescoping the row is exactly how #9024 fixed it.

So a reader checking Reading 2's claim greps shadow-cljs.edn, finds the package named, and concludes the README is wrong -- when the row is correct and the PROSE is merely one revision behind. The two sibling readings now describe the same narrowing at different levels of honesty.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE, not inferred: (a) 96ce8bb3d2 is an ancestor of origin/main; (b) grep -n ssr-node implementation/shadow-cljs.edn returns exactly one hit, line 1629, a ;; comment; (c) main did not touch implementation/ssr-node/README.md since 7f6533dd0b -- the intersection of #9015's changed files with main's was empty, and the README is in #9015's set; (d) the suite is green at this tip: node implementation/ssr-node/test/run.cjs exits 0, 9 suites, absence.test.cjs 18/18.

THE FIX is prose only, in implementation/ssr-node/README.md's Reading 2 bullet: say that the row reads EDN loader positions rather than raw text, that a ;; comment is not a source path, and that nothing was forgiven and no allowance list exists -- mirroring the argument Reading 1's bullet already makes. Cite rf2-8arzr.9. No test change: absence.test.cjs already carries the reasoning in its own header comment, and its control row ('a doctored build config is caught, and a comment about one is not') already pins both directions.
RESOLVED BY PR #9040, 2026-09-03. Premise verified at tip before writing, not taken from the bead.

RE-MEASURED: implementation/shadow-cljs.edn contains exactly ONE ssr-node hit — line 1629, inside a ;; comment above :examples/login-hicasso-server explaining which sidecar loads that build's module. implementation/deps.edn contains none (same instrument, exit 1 there and exit 0 on the hit, so the zero is a real absence and not a broken pattern). So the README's 'implementation/shadow-cljs.edn names no build reaching it' was false as written: the file DOES name the package.

WHAT THE ROW ACTUALLY CHECKS, read from absence.test.cjs itself rather than from #9024's commit message or the dispatch brief. The row 'no shadow-cljs build and no classpath entry reaches this package' does three things: (1) asserts each of BUILD_CONFIGS exists, so a missing config cannot read as a clean scan; (2) asserts each yields AT LEAST ONE loader position, failing with 'the scan has gone blind' — a liveness check on the INSTRUMENT, not on the subject; (3) collects hits only at loader positions — for .edn, valuesAfterKeys(text, EDN_LOAD_KEYS): the value form after each of :source-paths, :paths, :extra-paths, :replace-paths, :deps, :extra-deps, :replace-deps, :local/root, :dependencies — and asserts that set is empty.

So the claim is NOT 'these files never mention the package'; it is 'no classpath-or-source-path value in them names it'. A ;; comment is not one of those keys and cannot host a hit. The paired control plants a real :source-paths entry AND a real :local/root coordinate requiring both to be found, plants a comment naming the package requiring it NOT to be, and then requires that comment fixture to carry both needles — so the scoped scan is shown walking past text a raw scan does hit, rather than passing on an empty fixture.

THE FIX, prose only in Reading 2's bullet, as this bead specified: loader positions rather than raw text, a comment is not one, nothing forgiven and no allowance list exists, the rf2-8arzr.9 rescope named as the SIBLING of Reading 1's own rf2-6ovv move rather than a second and softer one — plus the fail-closed property, which is what this row adds over Reading 1's repo-wide sweep and is why it survives alongside it. Mirrors Reading 1's shape, the worked precedent in the same file. No test changed, as this bead predicted.

GATE: node implementation/ssr-node/test/run.cjs — captured exit 0, 9 suites, absence.test.cjs 18/18, both post-rebase and before. The Reading 2 row and its comment-vs-source-path control are among the passing rows.
close_reason: PR #9040: Reading 2's bullet rewritten from the row itself. Re-verified at tip that shadow-cljs.edn names the package exactly once, in a ;; comment at :1629, and deps.edn not at all — so the old 'names no build reaching it' was false as written. The bullet now states the loader-position reading (the value form after each EDN_LOAD_KEY), that a comment is not one, that nothing was forgiven and no allowance list exists, and the fail-closed property this row adds over Reading 1. Prose only; absence suite green at exit 0, 18/18.

title: effect-map contract drift: public docs and core comments still publish three keys and partial-success behavior
description:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9029, independent correctness/completeness finding. The authoritative implementation is unambiguous: implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc closed-effect-map-keys contains seven keys (:db, :rf.db/runtime, :fx, :sensitive, :large, :clear-sensitive, :clear-large), and effect-map-defect plus router/commit-and-flow! refuse a foreign top-level key before any commit. PR #9029 correctly taught that contract in the migration skill, but a repository census found the old contract still presented as current outside that package.

Normative/public drift at the audited merge: spec/000-Vision.md:113; spec/Ownership.md:32; spec/Implementor-Checklist.md:32; spec/API.md:93,483-489,737 (including an effect-map key table that omits all four classification effects); and spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2734's preferred diagnostic. They say the closed set is only :db/:rf.db.runtime/:fx or only :db/:fx, so a port or app author can reject four valid commit-plane effects.

Core/source-facing drift: implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:288-301 and :1067-1073 contradict the seven-key var immediately below them; re_frame/core.cljc:443-449 and interceptor.cljc:108-115 repeat the three-key set. Test narration is internally contradictory too: event_context_partition_test.clj:12-14 and :30-33 still says a foreign key is dropped and describes the error as dev-only, while its live test at :177-189 proves the current no-partial-commit behavior; fx_test.clj:484-489 still calls the closed set three keys. docs/api/re-frame.core.md:518 repeats the public falsehood.

Historical consumer comments also read as current behavior: tools/xray/.../machine_canvas.cljs:168-173 says the foreign fx is dropped while :db lands; the Hicasso native-IME/testbed accounts use the three-key set and say the timer vanished while the arm-state db write landed (docs/design/hicasso/native-ime-scripted-witness.md:193-197, implementation/hicasso/testbed/spec.cjs:1653-1657, hicasso_testbed/core.cljs:425-430). Either state explicitly that this was the pre-rf2-04tx behavior, or rewrite them to the current refusal semantics; do not erase useful history.

This is one coherence sweep, not a request to redesign effect maps or add machinery. Ordinary examples may continue to show {:db ... :fx ...}; only prose that labels an exhaustive closed set or states recovery behavior must be exact. No exact existing Bead was found (title/description searches for effect-map, seven-key, classification keys, spec/API.md, and partial commit); rf2-n3mya is deliberately skill-scoped and is reopened separately for its two missed sites.
acceptance_criteria: Every exhaustive effect-map claim names all seven legal top-level keys (or clearly says "three everyday keys plus four classification effects"); spec/API.md's key table includes the four commit-plane classification keys. No current-contract prose says a foreign top-level key is dropped/ignored while :db or other siblings commit, or that its error is dev-only; historical narratives explicitly identify the former behavior as pre-rf2-04tx. Core docstrings/comments, the public spec/docs surfaces, and the named Xray/Hicasso/test comments agree with events.cljc and the existing no-partial-commit tests. Existing doc/link/API projection and relevant core test gates are green; no new gate is required solely for this wording sweep.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #9048 — exact owner remains open. PR #9048 correctly closes rf2-n3mya's skills-package remainder: M-8 now describes the seven legal keys and fail-closed refusal. It does not touch this owner's broader current-contract drift. At merged commit fdf7aa230638a12eb6f1c97e653784ca5d47d155, implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:288-301 still says only :db/:rf.db/runtime/:fx live at top level, directly above the seven-key var; the other already-named spec/docs/test carriers also remain for this bounded coherence sweep. No duplicate or widened new issue.
close_reason: PR #9070 lands the NORMATIVE AND PUBLIC half - the half this bead calls the serious one, because it is what makes a port or app author reject four valid commit-plane effects - plus all four core comment/docstring sites. Corrected: spec/000-Vision.md:113, spec/Ownership.md:32, spec/Implementor-Checklist.md:32, spec/API.md:93 + :480 + :734 AND the effect-map key table at :482-486 (three rows to seven, re-counted by hand since nothing validates a table's columns or contents), spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2734's preferred diagnostic (which now matches the string events.cljc actually emits), and events.cljc:288-302 + :1067, core.cljc:445-449, interceptor.cljc:112. Implementation behaviour UNCHANGED - closed-effect-map-keys, effect-map-defect and every refusal path untouched; the diff in core/src is comment and docstring text only. TWO PREMISES DID NOT HOLD and those sites were left alone: spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1998 already says 'plus the four commit-plane classification keys', and spec/Spec-Schemas.md:724-739, the canonical schema owner, already says 'Seven keys' with all seven in its Malli EffectMap - so the drift was never in the owner, only in surfaces paraphrasing it. THE REST OF THIS BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE IS NOT MET HERE and is tracked as rf2-eih4, not dropped: the named Xray/Hicasso/test narration and docs/api/re-frame.core.md:518 all sit in trees this dispatch was fenced out of. The census also found TWO carriers this bead did not name, both in rf2-eih4 and the more serious find - spec/002-Frames.md:471, the OWNING spec's own exhaustive three-key claim, contradicted by its own :561 ninety lines later; and spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2856's machine effect-map note. Gates green on the rebased base with captured exit codes: core JVM 2176/11149, test:cljs 11205/55820, bundle-isolation 40/40 unmoved, doc-slugs (proven live by a planted-anchor sabotage that went red at spec/API.md:482, restored and verified by git blob hash), readme-links, mkdocs --strict, clj-kondo errors 0.

title: three example suites share the rf2-k4oe make-frame-before-register! ordering; latent, not broken
notes:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-k4oe co-load sweep (PR #9027).

rf2-k4oe fixed re-frame.linearlite-example-cljs-test, whose init! created a
:url-bound? frame BEFORE reinstating the :resource/:mutation registrar rows the
shared reset hook clears, so the route-entry resource plan ran inside make-frame
against an empty registrar.

THREE OTHER SUITES SHARE THAT EXACT ORDERING and are green today only because
their "/" route declares no BLOCKING resource:

  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/infinite_feed_example_cljs_test.cljs
  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs
  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/resources_example_cljs_test.cljs

MEASURED. Each was built in its own single-app :node-test bundle on
690b99309f + the rf2-k4oe fixes, and each passed:
infinite-feed-example 5 tests / 38 assertions, realworld-resources 33 / 286,
resources-example 9 / 39 — all 0 failures, captured exit 0.

A census of every reg-route form under examples/ (paren-balanced over flattened
text, control-checked against a known-present site first) found seven apps
registering a route at "/" — infinite_feed, linearlite, realworld_http,
realworld_resources, resources, routing, todomvc — and LinearLite is the ONLY
one with a blocking route resource there. That is the whole reason it was the
only hard failure.

SO THIS IS LATENT, NOT BROKEN. Adding a blocking resource to any of those three
root routes reproduces rf2-k4oe exactly, silently, and only in a bundle where no
sibling owns "/". The cheap prophylactic is to move make-frame last in all three,
matching the committed pilot baseline
(docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/baseline/linearlite/baseline_test.cljs,
which documents "the frame is made last"). Deliberately NOT done under rf2-k4oe:
churning three passing suites was out of that bead's scope, and the call on
whether to harden them prophylactically is worth making explicitly.

RELATED, and the more interesting half: rf2-ma8r stays open for Mike's ruling on
the two framework questions this exposed — whether a :url-bound? frame planning
route resources AT CONSTRUCTION is correct, and whether a FAILED route plan
should ever be retried (today an app that recovers stays wedged in
:transition :error permanently). If either is ruled on, this bead may become
moot: the ordering only matters because the plan is both construction-time and
un-retried.

SWEEP COVERAGE, so the remainder is not lost. Fifteen example suites were run in
single-app bundles (155 tests / 1180 assertions, all green). NOT covered:
the ~11,000-test framework remainder of the :node-test lane was not swept for
co-load masking among framework suites;
re-frame.example-frame-scoping-cljs-test is excluded by construction (it loads
seven apps deliberately and cross-app scoping is its subject).
RESOLVED 2026-09-03 by PR #9043 (branch worker/code-a, commit 0a8838a48b).

WHAT CHANGED. All three suites reordered to the rf2-k4oe shape: everything registers first, the
:url-bound? frame is made LAST. Each init! carries a docstring note explaining WHY (the
construction-time URL sync via make-frame -> upsert-frame! post-create hook ->
:routing/on-frame-registered! -> reconcile-url-listener!, the empty-registrar plan, the sticky
:transition :error / :rf.error/resource-route-plan, and the fact that the suite is green today only
because its "/" route declares no BLOCKING resource) so the constraint cannot be silently undone
again — matching PR #9027 shape and the committed pilot baseline note "the frame is made last".

NOTHING OBSERVABLE CHANGED. Each suite built in a single-app :node-test bundle, sequence
clear -> compile -> run -> clear (the dev bundle SHADOW_IMPORTs from the build-cache directory at
RUN time, so the cache must survive between compile and run; --test=<ns> deliberately NOT used
since it filters what runs while leaving siblings loaded). Single-app isolation confirmed by
compile file counts (222 / 315 / 263 against 1891 for the full bundle).

  infinite_feed_example_cljs_test   before 5 tests / 38 assertions   after 5 / 38     0 failures, exit 0
  realworld_resources_cljs_test     before 33 / 286                  after 33 / 286   0 failures, exit 0
  resources_example_cljs_test       before 9 / 39                    after 9 / 39     0 failures, exit 0

Identical throughout, and all three match the figures this bead recorded.

PREMISE CORRECTION WORTH KEEPING. PR #9027 was still OPEN when this work started, not merged as
the dispatch assumed. On the pre-rebase base (8b617dd529) resources_example_cljs_test could not be
built in a single-app bundle AT ALL: it died at ns load with
"rf/reg-machine requires day8/re-frame2-machines on the classpath [:rf.error/machines-artefact-missing]"
— the exact defect PR #9027 fixes in examples/capabilities/resources/resources/core.cljs,
independently corroborated here. That is also why this bead measurement is recorded as taken "on
690b99309f + THE RF2-K4OE FIXES": the caveat is load-bearing, not decoration. The first before/after
pass used that one-line require planted temporarily (restore verified by git blob hash back to
5e0060754f4a614a1ac1080594a958efc38c77b8, tree clean). PR #9027 has since merged and every figure
above is from the rebased base with NO plant.

SCOPE HELD: not widened into the other four apps registering "/", per this bead census. rf2-ma8r
remains open and untouched — if either framework question there is ruled on, the ordering may stop
mattering, but the prophylactic is cheap and independent of that ruling.

GATES (captured, final rebased base): test:cljs 11190 tests / 55778 assertions exit 0;
implementation/core JVM 2175 / 11144 exit 0; derivation-conformance JVM 23 / 526 exit 0;
test-fast-pr.sh PASS exit 0.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9043 (worker/code-a): all three suites now make the :url-bound? frame last, matching rf2-k4oe/PR #9027, each with a docstring note pinning the constraint. Single-app bundle before/after counts identical for all three (5/38, 33/286, 9/39, zero failures throughout).

title: spec/View-Hierarchy-Capture.md misrecords the retired Fiber hierarchy as never built and says Xray has no Views panel
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-03 by worker specdrift-b while indexing View-Hierarchy-Capture.md for rf2-f9wfd. The document was read-only ground truth for that bead and this finding is outside it, so it is handed back rather than fixed there.

DEFECT. spec/View-Hierarchy-Capture.md's own "Ownership + cross-references" table (the table under the heading at the foot of the document) names SIX paths. FOUR of them do not exist in the tree:

  MISSING  tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/fiber_walker.cljs        (row: Fiber-walker implementation (CLJS))
  MISSING  tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/group_by_tree.cljs       (row: Group-by-tree renderer)
  MISSING  tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/views_view.cljs         (row: Views panel toggle wiring)
  MISSING  tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/fiber_walker_cljs_test.cljs  (row: React-version regression smoke)
  EXISTS   implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs                 (row: Production DCE contract)
  EXISTS   tools/xray/spec/012-Views.md                                      (row: Xray Views panel)

WHAT XRAY ACTUALLY SHIPS. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/view_walker.cljs — the data-rf-view attribute walker, whose own docstring says "Status: FALLBACK SAFETY NET only" and names the Fiber-walker (rf2-mxkq7) as the primary path, citing this same spec document. So the fallback is present and the primary is not.

RELATED, AND PART OF THE SAME PICTURE. The __rf2_view_id__ property the document's §View-id tagging convention specifies appears in NO source file in the repository (grep over implementation/ and tools/ for cljs/cljc/clj: zero hits). The convention is a SHOULD, so its absence is not itself a contract violation, but it means every read path the document specifies as primary is unrealised in the CLJS reference: no Fiber walker, no view-id property, only the fallback.

WHY IT MATTERS. The document is a v1 pattern contract every React-backed port MUST implement (its own Normative-status header), and §React-version regression check requires a smoke test at a path that does not exist. An implementor following the ownership table to see how the reference does it finds nothing there. spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md line 713 also calls the Fiber-walker "the primary path".

THE DISPOSITION IS AN OPERATOR CALL, not a mechanical fix, which is why this is filed rather than patched:

  (a) The walker was never built and the document describes intent. Then the ownership table's four rows should say so (planned / not yet shipped) rather than citing paths, and §React-version regression check's MUST needs a home or a deferral.
  (b) The walker was built and later removed or renamed. Then the rows need re-pointing, and the retirement wants the same bookkeeping treatment as the ui/freehand retirement (a dated statement naming the deciding bead).
  (c) The walker is still wanted. Then this is an implementation gap against a v1 MUST, and the bead is the place to size it.

Not bisected — git log for tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/ would settle (a) vs (b) cheaply.

CONTEXT. The rf2-f9wfd PR adds View-Hierarchy-Capture.md to spec/README.md's index and spec/Ownership.md's surface map. The Ownership row it adds is deliberately worded to avoid asserting WHICH walker ships: its Artefact cell says the walk is tool-side (day8/re-frame2-xray in the CLJS reference) and that the data-rf-view tagging the fallback reads is emitted by the Reagent and UIx adapter artefacts, both of which are true today. Whatever disposition this bead reaches, that cell may want revisiting alongside it.
acceptance_criteria: View-Hierarchy-Capture.md records that the Fiber walker, group-by-tree renderer, associated Views wiring, and React smoke were built under Causa in PR #1533 and deliberately removed by the Reactive-panel rebuild in PR #1741/rf2-wyvf2; it no longer describes them or the smoke as never built. The ownership row distinguishes the currently shipped Views panel from the absent hierarchy/group-by-tree mode. Any claim that reinstatement is tracked separately names an actual durable owner. The normative product call remains unpreempted, and the doc-slug gate passes.
notes:
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 00:5x AUSEST — SPLIT THE BEAD'S TWO QUESTIONS AND DO ONLY THE FIRST. Recorded as my call.

specdrift-b filed this and correctly said the disposition — never built / removed / still wanted — is an operator call. It is, but only HALF of it is, and holding the whole bead for Mike would park a factual defect behind a product question that need not gate it.

THE HALF THAT IS BOOKKEEPING AND IS MINE TO CALL. An ownership table's job is to say WHERE a contract surface lives. Citing four source paths that do not exist (fiber_walker.cljs, group_by_tree.cljs, views_view.cljs, fiber_walker_cljs_test.cljs) is not a normative claim about what the product should become — it is a false statement about the repository as it stands, and it is wrong the same way a stale line number is wrong. Correct the table to cite what SHIPS: view_walker.cljs, the data-rf-view fallback walker. That is dispatchable now.

THE HALF THAT IS MIKE'S AND IS NOT BEING PRE-EMPTED. Whether the Fiber walker is still wanted as the primary path is a product call, and this ruling does not make it. So the correction must NOT quietly demote the Fiber walker to 'never existed' — where the spec means it as the intended primary path, the table says so IN THOSE TERMS (a normative-future row, marked as not yet shipped), rather than deleting the intent or asserting a file. The distinction to hold: the table stops claiming a path exists; it does not stop claiming the design is wanted.

WORTH KNOWING, because it is the evidence that the fallback is a fallback rather than the whole design: view_walker.cljs's own docstring names the Fiber walker as the primary path, and __rf2_view_id__ appears in no source file. So the spec is describing something real that was not built, not something imaginary. Verify both at source before writing.

I am surfacing the product half to Mike in chat as a fourth item alongside rf2-2oug, rf2-9vm0 and rf2-t9rq, which are the same shape. It does not block this bead.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9030 — REOPENED.

The bead itself named three dispositions and said a cheap history bisection would distinguish them; PR #9030 did not perform it and implemented (a), “never built.” Git history proves (b): commit fe4ff001b9 / PR #1533 created the Fiber walker, group-by-tree renderer, Views wiring, and React-prefix smoke under tools/causa; commit 9781aa4e24 / PR #1741 (rf2-wyvf2) explicitly deleted those files while replacing that Views implementation with the Reactive-panel rebuild. Thus the new “not yet built,” “not yet written,” and “no namespace implements it” wording erases a real built-then-retired lifecycle. The existing 2026-05-19 Decisions-log sentence saying it landed is historically accurate; the missing bookkeeping is the 2026-05-20 retirement and its deciding PR/bead.

A second premise is false at current tip: Xray DOES ship a Views panel. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reactive_panel.cljs registers {:id :views :label "Views"}; tools/xray/spec/012-Views.md opens by calling it shipped, and the public skill lists it. What is absent is the old hierarchy/group-by-tree mode and its toggle, not the entire Views panel.

Keep this as the exact owner: both defects are in the same correction and directly satisfy the original bead’s already-enumerated disposition (b). This is bookkeeping only; it does not decide whether the Fiber hierarchy should return.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #9041. Established the history before writing: all four names were real code under tools/causa/ - fiber_walker.cljs, group_by_tree.cljs and fiber_walker_cljs_test.cljs added by fe4ff001b9 (PR #1533, 2026-05-19), views_view.cljs added earlier by 4664501065 (PR #1401, 2026-05-18) and only MODIFIED by fe4ff001b9 - and all four deleted by 9781aa4e24 (PR #1741, 2026-05-20), whose commit body names each deletion individually. __rf2_view_id__ was likewise real (fiber_walker.cljs:84, 'view-id-prop') and went with them; zero hits in source at HEAD against a working control. spec/View-Hierarchy-Capture.md now records that built-then-retired lifecycle in the Ownership table, the Decisions log and the React-version regression section, and the Views row distinguishes the SHIPPED :views tab (reactive_panel.cljs:76-87 registers {:id :views :label "Views"}) from the withdrawn group-by-tree mode (zero hits in tools/xray, control green).

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE AUDIT NOTE, both verified at source. (1) views_view.cljs was NOT added by fe4ff001b9. (2) None of the four ever lived at a tools/xray path: the causa->xray rename (731188b1fb, PR #2067) landed FOUR DAYS AFTER the deletion, so the table's cited paths never existed at any commit - the original bead's conclusion was right for the wrong reason, and the doc now says so.

PREMISE REFUTED: rf2-mxkq7 and rf2-wyvf2 are NOT beads - absent from all 511 issue ids, bd show exits 1 against a control that resolves. rf2-wyvf2 is cited by this bead's own audit note and acceptance criteria. title: docs(hicasso): 04-controlled-inputs.md promises a throw for a controlled :value on contenteditable, and nothing throws
description:
https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/docs/core/hicasso/04-controlled-inputs.md

CLAIM. docs/core/hicasso/04-controlled-inputs.md L93-95 reads: "Unsupported
controlled shapes are rejected rather than approximated. In particular, a
contenteditable region has no single value that Hicasso can reconcile.
Binding :value to it throws at the source."

TRUTH AT TIP. Nothing throws. The controlled converge recognises exactly
`input` and `textarea` (implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/
controlled.cljs:158 `("input" "textarea") true`, and :331 "itself for
everything that is not a controlled input / textarea"), so a :div carrying
:contenteditable and a :value is passed straight through to React with no
refusal on any path.

CENSUS. The 27 distinct :rf.error/hicasso-* ids emitted under
implementation/hicasso/src carry no contenteditable refusal and no generic
unsupported-controlled-shape refusal; the nearest neighbours are
:rf.error/hicasso-revision-not-controlled and
:rf.error/hicasso-file-input-value-marker, both bound to other surfaces.
Control: the same scan returns those 27 ids, and every live id named by
docs/core/hicasso/troubleshooting.md's index resolves to both a spec/009 row
and an emitter, so the instrument bites and the zero is real.

THIS IS THE REFUSAL THAT IS RESERVED, NOT BUILT.
:rf.error/hicasso-contenteditable-not-controllable is one of five ids in
troubleshooting.md's "Reserved" table, whose contract is exactly "a refusal
this guide already teaches by mechanism, on a surface that is not built yet"
and "none of them can appear in an error you caught". Chapter 04 is the
guide's teaching-by-mechanism half — but it states the refusal in the PRESENT
TENSE, which the reservation says is not yet true. The testbed agrees with the
reservation and not with chapter 04: implementation/hicasso/testbed carries a
dedicated case `contenteditable-is-not-a-controlled-field` and says in terms
"NOT a controlled field, and this testbed does not pretend it is".

IMPACT. A reader binds :value to a contenteditable expecting a loud refusal at
the source and gets silence plus whatever React does with a stray :value —
which is the approximation the sentence promises will not happen.

FIX SHAPE, not ruled. Either (1) soften chapter 04 to describe the behaviour
without promising a throw — the reservation stays accurate and nothing else
moves, a one-file docs change; or (2) build the refusal and promote
:rf.error/hicasso-contenteditable-not-controllable out of Reserved into the
index, which is an emitter plus a spec/009 row plus the table move, all in one
change per that table's own "promoted, never drifted into" rule. (1) is the
proportionate one while the surface is unbuilt.

PROVENANCE. Found by the rf2-wr0w0 census (docsdrift-a), which REFUTED its own
premise: troubleshooting.md:531 is correct, because the Reserved table means
precisely "no emitter and no spec/009 row yet". Chapter 04 is where the same
subject is actually overstated. Out of that worker's write fence, so filed.
notes:
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 00:3x AUSEST — OPTION (1), SOFTEN THE CHAPTER. Recorded as my call so Mike can reverse it cheaply.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE FIRST, at 76ffd860b4, because the bead's own premise is the thing the ruling rests on: implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/controlled.cljs:158 recognises exactly ("input" "textarea"), and a grep for contenteditable across that file returns NOTHING — there is no refusal path of any kind, so 'throws at the source' is false in the plain sense, not merely imprecise. docs/core/hicasso/04-controlled-inputs.md carries the sentence verbatim at ~:93-95.

WHY (1) AND NOT (2). Option (2) — build the refusal and promote :rf.error/hicasso-contenteditable-not-controllable out of the Reserved table — is refused on the stance rather than on cost alone, and the reasoning is worth writing down because the opposite conclusion is tempting: a loud refusal DOES read as better ergonomics than silence, and this project does prefer catching a footgun at the source. What decides it against is where the check would have to live. The controlled converge's business is recognising the two shapes it can reconcile; making it also refuse a shape it does not handle means inspecting every non-controlled element for a stray :value, on the converge path, for one footgun that the testbed already documents by name (contenteditable-is-not-a-controlled-field, which says in terms 'this testbed does not pretend it is'). That is a cost on the common path to serve an uncommon mistake, which is the gold-plating the stance names.

AND THE RESERVATION IS ALREADY THE PROJECT'S OWN ANSWER HERE. The Reserved table's contract is 'a refusal this guide already teaches by mechanism, on a surface that is not built yet', with a 'promoted, never drifted into' rule. The reservation is therefore not an omission awaiting repair — it is a deliberate position, and chapter 04's present tense is the thing that drifted away from it. The testbed agrees with the reservation. Only the chapter disagrees, so the chapter is what moves.

WHAT LANDS: chapter 04 describes the behaviour truthfully — Hicasso does not treat a contenteditable region as controlled, so a :value on it is not reconciled and is passed through — while KEEPING the teaching the paragraph exists for (a contenteditable region has no single value to reconcile; use a declared foreign host or named native island). Do not delete the teaching to fix the tense. One file, no emitter, no spec/009 row, no table move.

OPTION (2) STAYS AVAILABLE AND THE ID STAYS RESERVED. If a real user hits this silently, promote it then, in one change per that table's own rule. This ruling closes the drift, not the design question.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #9035 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9035), option (1) per the mayor ruling on this bead. Chapter 04 softened; option (2) NOT built.

PREMISE RE-VERIFIED AT SOURCE before editing, and it holds exactly as filed. impl/controlled.cljs's convergeable-tag? recognises exactly ("input" "textarea"), install! answers 'the tag itself for everything that is not a controlled input / textarea', so a contenteditable element's :value reaches React unchanged with no refusal on any path. git grep -i contenteditable over implementation/hicasso/src returns ONE hit — a focus-trap CSS selector string in impl/overlay.cljs — against a control of 14 'textarea' hits in controlled.cljs, so the instrument bites and the zero is real.

WHAT LANDED, one file, prose only. The paragraph at ~L92-95 now says Hicasso reconciles a controlled value only for the shapes in that table and approximates nothing outside them; that a contenteditable region is the case worth naming because it has no single value Hicasso could reconcile, so it is not treated as a controlled field at all; and that a :value bound to one is passed through to React untouched — nothing refuses it and nothing keeps it in step with app-db, so the binding is silently inert rather than loud. The teaching the paragraph exists for is KEPT, including the closing sentence about a declared foreign host or named native island. The correction adds the consequence a reader now needs: there is no loud error to wait for, which is precisely the IMPACT this bead described.

NOT DONE, per the ruling: no emitter, no spec/009 row, no Reserved-table move. :rf.error/hicasso-contenteditable-not-controllable stays reserved, which is troubleshooting.md's Reserved table working as specified rather than drift — that page is untouched, as rf2-wr0w0 established. No heading changed, no fenced block touched.

Two premise corrections for the dispatcher: that script is at implementation/hicasso/scripts/, NOT scripts/; and bare 'mkdocs' is not on PATH here (exit 127, a no-verdict), 'python -m mkdocs' is the working form. title: impl: re-frame.core facade + late-bind directory still claim resolve-resource-scope emits :rf.resource/scope-resolved
description:

`:rf.resource/scope-resolved` dev-time trace evidence. Both are false, and both
contradict the artefact and the defwrapper in the SAME tree.

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc (the re-frame.core facade `def` for

  resolution site it emits `:rf.resource/scope-resolved` dev-time trace evidence."
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc (the

TRUTH AT TIP (read, not inferred)

- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/scope_registry.cljc, the public
  `resolve-resource-scope` defn: its body is
  `(resolve-scope*-pure scope-id spec db 'rf/resolve-resource-scope)` and its
  docstring says "NO observability side effect either: it routes through the
  trace-free `resolve-scope*-pure` evaluator, so a passive read advertised as pure
  does NOT emit `:rf.resource/scope-resolved` into the trace bus."
- Same file, `resolve-scope*-pure`: "PURE ... WITHOUT emitting any observability
  state (rf2-ru73k6 F3)". Its sibling `resolve-scope*` is "the TRACED wrapper ...
  for use at CAUSAL resolution boundaries (resource events, route entry, mutation
  settle)".
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_resources.cljc, the `defwrapper` for
  `resolve-resource-scope`, is already CORRECT: "It is a PURE data helper
  (rf2-ru73k6 F3): it routes through the trace-free `resolve-scope*-pure`
  evaluator and so does NOT emit `:rf.resource/scope-resolved`".

So core_resources.cljc and the artefact agree; core.cljc's facade docstring and the
late-bind directory entry are stale against them. The facade docstring is the one a
reader reaches from `(doc rf/resolve-resource-scope)`.

skill leaf and the facade docstring. The skill half is fixed on that bead's PR

Neither implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc nor

title: skill(re-frame2-pair-retro): known-frictions.md is saturated at 3 bytes under the 16 KB leaf ceiling — the next addition forces a split
description:
CLAIM. skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/references/known-frictions.md sits at 241 lines / 16,381 LF-normalised bytes against the family ceiling in skills/README.md (Leaf size discipline: each leaf SHOULD be <=250 lines AND <=16 KB, i.e. 16,384 bytes). That is 3 bytes of headroom and 9 lines. Measured at tip after PR #9016.

HISTORY. PR #9006 left it at 241 lines / 16,336 bytes (48 B headroom) and its author predicted the next addition would force a split. rf2-wz1qa (PR #9016) was that next addition: its three corrections cost ~96 bytes gross, which did not fit, so two genuine restatements were trimmed to pay for them -- 'cross-reference the live catalogue rather than the skill's docs alone -- a live-catalogue check is' shortened to 'cross-reference the live catalogue -- that check is', and 'the pair-MCP conformance corpus' to 'the conformance corpus'. Both were honest de-duplications, and that seam is now spent: there is no comparable restatement left to trade.

IMPACT. The leaf is the skill's one on-demand reference and is still growing (rf2-vdqr9 is an open item against this same file, and would breach on its own). The next author either breaches the ceiling silently -- nothing gates it, wc -l -c is the only instrument -- or trims load-bearing content under time pressure.

DECISION NEEDED (not taken here, deliberately). Three options, and this is a judgement call rather than a mechanical fix:
(a) SPLIT the leaf by friction family. But SKILL.md routes to exactly one on-demand leaf and the family rule is one-level routing, so a split needs a routing decision, not just a file move.
(b) CLAIM the catalogue exemption. skills/README.md already carves one out: 'catalogue-shaped leaves (for example re-frame2-pair/references/recipes.md) may exceed the ceiling if splitting would multiply file-handle overhead without reducing tokens-per-session.' known-frictions.md is a catalogue of friction classes and plausibly qualifies -- the stated test is 'would splitting reduce total tokens loaded per session?', and since the whole leaf loads on one trigger, a split arguably would not.
(c) TRIM content rather than structure, accepting the loss.

(b) looks strongest on the file's own shape and is much the cheapest, but it is a family-contract call the mayor/Mike should make, not a worker.

GATE. None -- the ceiling has no gate. wc -l -c before and after, plus check_doc_slugs.py if the routing changes.

Filed from PR #9016 (rf2-wz1qa + rf2-fpeig) rather than splitting on worker initiative, per the dispatch brief.
notes:
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 00:1x AUSEST — OPTION (b), THE CATALOGUE EXEMPTION, IS TAKEN. Recorded as MY call rather than Mike's so he can reverse it cheaply; the bead correctly refused to take it on worker initiative.

MEASURED AT bddc39f415 BEFORE RULING: 241 lines, 16,622 raw bytes, 16,381 LF-normalised. Ceiling at skills/README.md:239 is <=250 lines AND <=16 KB (16,384). So 3 bytes and 9 lines of headroom — the bead's figures reproduce exactly.

WHY (b) AND NOT (a) OR (c). The exemption at skills/README.md:245-248 states its own test: 'would splitting reduce total tokens loaded per session?' known-frictions.md is loaded on ONE trigger — the retro's pattern-check step, SKILL.md:81 — and the whole leaf is consulted to answer 'is this a one-off or a product gap?', which is a question you answer by scanning the classes until one matches. A session cannot know in advance WHICH half holds its friction, so a split into two sibling leaves would load both on most sessions and add a file handle and a routing hop for nothing. The test therefore answers NO for this leaf, which is precisely the case the exemption exists for. (a) is refused on that reasoning, not on the routing objection the bead raises — a split into two siblings is still one level deep and would not be a SKILL->A->B chain. (c) is refused because the bead's own history shows the trim seam is spent: PR #9016 already paid for ~96 bytes by de-duplicating two genuine restatements, and there is no comparable restatement left to trade, so the next trim comes out of load-bearing content.

WHAT LANDS. skills/README.md's exemption bullet names known-frictions.md alongside re-frame2-pair/references/recipes.md, with the one-trigger reasoning stated in a clause so the next reader does not re-derive it. The exemption is for THIS leaf on THIS shape; it is not a family-wide licence and no other leaf inherits it.

THE BOUND, because an exempt catalogue is not an unbounded one: each class stays at the density the existing nine already set. rf2-vdqr9's four new classes are written to that density, not longer. No second numeric ceiling is invented — per the stance, that would be litigating minutiae.

CONSEQUENCE: rf2-vdqr9 is unblocked and dispatches WITH this bead in one cluster, since its four classes are exactly the growth this ruling authorises.
CORRECTION TO MY OWN RULING NOTE, same tick, before dispatch. The last paragraph said 'rf2-vdqr9's four classes are exactly the growth this ruling authorises'. That is wrong and I caught it by reading the file rather than the bead: the four classes ALREADY LANDED — known-frictions.md carries 'Dry-run versus a live write' (:119), 'Wire-boundary privacy elision and the raw-eval carve-out' (:132), 'Wire-size caps and pagination' (:145) and 'Hot-reload baseline misuse' (:156), and the 16,381-byte measurement INCLUDES them. rf2-vdqr9 was reopened by the PR #9006 audit and its live residual is much smaller: split the one Signals bullet at :124 by reason, so :rf.error/writes-disabled (the closed default-OFF gate, lifted at server launch) is separated from :restore-rejected / :reset-rejected (post-gate runtime refusals with their own epoch/drain/frame/schema remedies).

THE RULING IS UNCHANGED AND THE CORRECTION STRENGTHENS IT. Splitting one bullet into two costs bytes against 3 bytes of headroom, so even this small correctness fix cannot land without the exemption — the leaf is saturated at a point where a genuine repair is blocked by structure. That is the situation the exemption is for, and it is a better argument for (b) than the one I wrote.

The density bound stands, now stated against the right work: the split bullet is written at the density the surrounding Signals bullets already set.
close_reason: Ruling recorded, not re-derived. skills/README.md's catalogue-exemption bullet now names re-frame2-pair-retro/references/known-frictions.md alongside recipes.md, with the one-trigger reasoning in a clause (loads on the retro's pattern-check step, scanned whole to classify an unknown friction, so a split would load both halves). Scoped to this leaf on this shape; no family-wide licence, no new mechanism, gate or ceiling number. Re-measured at base: 241 L / 16,381 LF-normalised bytes, reproducing the ruling's 3 bytes of headroom exactly; after the rf2-vdqr9 fix, 242 L / 16,752 bytes = 368 over the byte ceiling under this exemption, still 8 lines under the 250-line half. Sub-question answered NO CHANGE NEEDED: the skill's spec restates no leaf ceiling (authoring-prompt.md:40's '500-line ceiling' is the SKILL.md orchestrator ceiling), consistent with skills/README.md:236-237. PR #9028.

title: re-frame.hicasso.server/render is blind to sub exceptions on a JVM-local Hicasso SSR host: cold reads go through compute-sub, whose :rf.error/sub-exception is stamped :frame nil
notes:
CARRIED FORWARD FROM SLICE E (rf2-8arzr.5, now closed) BY SLICE F (rf2-8arzr.6), 2026-09-02, at base de3f2a00038. Filed so a measured finding does not die with the bead that found it.

THE FINDING, as slice E measured it: the per-frame `pending-error-trace?` buffer reads CLEAN on exactly the failure it was named for. Hicasso s cold reads go through pure `compute-sub`, and `compute-sub` s `:rf.error/sub-exception` is stamped `:frame nil` BY CONSTRUCTION -- it is a pure fn with no frame in scope to stamp. `re-frame.ssr.error-listener` buckets by frame address (`pending-error-traces` swap at error_listener.cljc:178, keyed by `frame/frame-address`), so a `:frame nil` record is not in any frame s bucket and a per-frame peek finds nothing.

WHAT SLICE E DID ABOUT IT: `re-frame.hicasso.server/render-body` (the new body-only entry, implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs:331) watches the ALWAYS-ON error-emit stream instead of the per-frame buffer, so the new crossing path is not affected. That was the right local fix and it shipped.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN: `re-frame.hicasso.server/render` (server.cljs:145), the DOCUMENT door used by a JVM-local Hicasso SSR host, has the same blindness today and was not changed. A sub that throws during a Hicasso server render can therefore go unreported on that path.

NOT A DOCS PROBLEM -- CHECKED. Slice F was asked to verify whether any doc describes the blind instrument as though it worked, and none does. docs/core/hicasso/18-ssr-and-hydration.md s error content is declaration/boot errors (`:rf.error/hicasso-host-bad-ssr-policy`, `:rf.error/hicasso-bad-host-declaration`, `:rf.error/ssr-missing-payload-policy`) and the `window is not defined` Render-assertion case; it makes no claim about sub-exception detection during a server render. spec/009:2125 s `pending-error-trace peek` sentence is about `:rf.error/ssr-ring-error-view-failed`, a DIFFERENT path (error-view rendering under the Ring host) that IS frame-stamped and does work. So nothing needed correcting in prose, and slice F corrected nothing here.

SIZING NOTE for whoever takes it: the likely fix is the one slice E already made one file over -- move `render` s detection to the always-on error-emit stream the way `render-body` does -- so this is probably small and has a worked precedent in the same namespace. Worth confirming that `:frame nil` is the only leak before changing anything: `error_listener.cljc:85-100` carries a long comment about a related skip whose reasoning is adjacent and worth reading first.
MAYOR NOTE, 2026-09-03 00:3x AUSEST — THIS AND rf2-ypom ARE ONE DEFECT, REACHED FROM TWO DIRECTIONS, AND THEY ARE DISPATCHED TOGETHER. rf2-ct24 was carried forward from slice E; rf2-ypom was filed by the PR #8997 audit. Both name re-frame.hicasso.server/render (server.cljs:145) as blind to recovered sub errors, and both prescribe the same fix: give it the verdict render-body already has. Verified at source at 76ffd860b4 — render is at :145, render-body at :331, and the :errors listener is registered at :323 and unregistered at :413, entirely inside render-body's extent. render has no corresponding registration.

NEITHER IS CLOSED AS A DUPLICATE, because each carries measured evidence the other does not: rf2-ct24 has slice E's mechanism (compute-sub stamps :frame nil BY CONSTRUCTION, being a pure fn with no frame in scope, so error_listener.cljc's per-frame bucketing at ~:178 can never see it) plus the instruction to read error_listener.cljc:85-100 first; rf2-ypom has the acceptance criteria (a throwing sub through server/render must get :rf.error/ssr-render-failed, a non-throwing control must return the existing shape unchanged, and the listener and request frame must be released on success, on refusal, and on a direct render throw). One PR closes both with a cross-reference each way.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #9035 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9035), the same PR that closes rf2-ypom — SAME DEFECT reached from two directions, cross-referenced both ways. This bead carried slice E's measured mechanism and the instruction to read error_listener.cljc:85-100 first; rf2-ypom carried the acceptance criteria. One fix, one PR.

THE FIX: re-frame.hicasso.server/render now watches the always-on :errors stream for its render extent and raises :rf.error/ssr-render-failed on any recovered record — the fix this bead's sizing note predicted, the one slice E had already made one file over. The doors share the lifecycle helpers but register under DIFFERENT ids (::render-recovered-error / ::render-body-recovered-error), because the shipped single id's justification rested on the sidecar isolate's one-render-at-a-time guarantee, which is render-body's premise and not render's.

THE BEAD'S QUESTION ANSWERED: ':frame nil is the only leak' — NO, and error_listener.cljc:85-100 is exactly where the adjacent reasoning starts. Those lines are the :rf.error/ssr-ring-error-view-failed paragraph, the second member of non-projection-eligible-errors: a record that is well-formed AND frame-stamped and still never reaches the buffer, skipped so a re-buffered trace cannot flip a 4xx to a 5xx under a custom projector plus a future re-flush. Reading error-emit-projection-listener out, it buffers only when ALL THREE hold: (1) the category is outside that skip set; (2) (:frame record) is non-nil — the leak this bead names, which compute-sub produces by construction; (3) (error-projector/server-frame? frame-id), i.e. the frame's :platform is :server.

CONDITION 3 IS A SECOND LEAK ON THIS DOOR SPECIFICALLY, and it is the finding worth more than the fix: render does NOT set :platform :server on its per-request frame — only render-body does — so on render the buffer could not fill even for a correctly frame-stamped record. Leaks 2 and 3 each independently suffice. NOT repaired here: giving render a :platform would change client-only-fx gating for every existing caller, well outside a bounded correctness fix. Flagged for whoever wants it.

The fix is unaffected and better justified than argued: the always-on stream sits upstream of all three conditions. refuse-recovered-render-error!'s docstring previously asserted the false premise this bug is made of — that a JVM host is survivable because the same process holds the record — and now states the three measured conditions instead.

WITNESS: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/server_render_recovered_error_ssr_cljs_test.cljs (refusal, non-throwing control, release of frame AND listener on all three exits, and the two doors' ids read from INSIDE each render).
