THIS WAS A DANGLING CROSS-REFERENCE, not a cosmetic omission - which the item
did not know and which raises its value. spec/013-Flows.md:474 deliberately
does NOT name the private id, and instead says its "id is nonetheless reserved
(per Conventions Reserved namespaces) so an application registration cannot
shadow it". Spec 013 was delegating the reservation to a roster that was
silent, so at tip NO normative document recorded that the id is reserved.

THE ROSTER ENTRY DOES NOT IMPLY A SECOND REGISTERED STANDARD, per the item's
explicit instruction. It states the distinction: unlike :rf/set-db it is
reserved but NEVER registered - no registrar row, no EP-0023 image-standard row
- because it is materialised through the router's unresolved-handler seam, so
it never reaches an application's event catalogue, tooling projection or
generated code. It is reserved for a DIFFERENT reason: the registrar is
consulted BEFORE that seam, so an app reg-event on the id would silently shadow
the settle and strand every flow-lifecycle effect, and fails loud instead. The
row also carries Spec 013's own caution that applications must not depend on

The row already had vocabulary for this case - :rf/head and :rf/public-error

title: ci(http): no lane runs a solo-namespace ordering, so latent load-order hook dependencies are ungated
description:
DISCOVERED-FROM rf2-zvbm9 (PR #8889), reported by that worker as an observation it deliberately did not file itself.

THE FINDING (verify at source before acting): the jvm-http CI job runs a bare "clojure -M:test", i.e. the full-suite ordering only. rf2-zvbm9 was a namespace that passed in that ordering and failed when run ALONE, because it depended on a late-bind hook published by a namespace load that an alphabetically earlier test namespace happened to perform. No gate would have caught it, and none will catch the next namespace that acquires the same kind of latent dependency.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE BUG: the failure is silent and it accumulates. A namespace acquires an unnoticed dependency on somebody else load-ordering before it, the suite stays green, and the defect only surfaces when someone runs that namespace alone — which is exactly what a developer does when iterating, so the cost lands on the person least equipped to explain it. The specific hook here fails OPEN too: extract-paths returns an empty map when unbound rather than erroring, so the classification silently does nothing.

SCOPE IS A JUDGEMENT AND NOT OBVIOUS — this is filed to be RULED ON as much as fixed. Running every namespace solo multiplies the lane cost; running none leaves the hole. Candidate shapes worth weighing before building anything: a nightly rather than per-PR solo sweep; solo runs for a named set of namespaces with known late-bind dependencies; or making the hook fail LOUD when unbound, which converts a silent misclassification into an error and may remove the need for a solo lane at all. The last one is the smallest change and may be the right one — the stance prefers it over new CI machinery.

NOT URGENT: the specific instance is fixed by #8889, which requires the schemas namespace in the fixture that needed it.
notes:
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-01: make the hook fail LOUD when unbound. Do NOT build a solo-namespace lane, nightly or per-PR, and do not add a named-set sweep.

The bead names three shapes and already leans at the right one. Confirming it as the ruling: extract-paths returning an empty map when unbound is a fail-OPEN, and that is the actual defect - the silent misclassification, not the absence of a lane. Convert it to an error. A namespace that has acquired a latent load-order dependency then fails immediately and says so, on the developer's own solo run, which is where the cost currently lands and where the message is most useful.

This is the smallest change, it removes a silent failure mode rather than adding machinery to detect one, and it may make a solo lane unnecessary - which is the point. New CI machinery to catch a class of bug that a two-line fail-loud converts into an ordinary error is exactly the over-engineering the stance rejects, and it would put a recurring toll on every PR forever.

If, having made the hook loud, you find a case it cannot reach, file that as its own bead with the case - do not widen this one into a lane.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #8943 (branch worker/cilanes). Followed the ruling exactly: the hook now fails LOUD when unbound, and NO CI machinery was added — no solo lane, no nightly, no named-set sweep.

THE DEFECT. privacy-body/extract-paths (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/privacy_body.cljc) returned an empty marks map when the late-bind schema-walker hook was unbound. An unbound hook means the marks are UNKNOWN, not EMPTY, and answering {} for it is the fail-OPEN the ruling names: a :decode schema marking a slot :sensitive? classified nothing and the secret rode the trace verbatim, green either side of it. rf2-zvbm9 was exactly that — four assertions reading their own secret back, visible only in a solo-namespace run because the full-suite ordering happened to load re-frame.schemas first.

THE LOUDNESS IS GATED ON WHETHER A MARK IS DECLARED, AND THAT MATTERS — an unconditional throw would have been wrong in both directions, checked at source rather than assumed. (1) day8/re-frame2-schemas is a TEST-ONLY dep of the http artefact, and the artefact resolves malli.core directly (decode.cljc, which WARNS rather than throws when Malli is absent), so an app can legitimately use a Malli :decode with no schemas artefact at all; an unconditional throw breaks every such app on every successful response, and on the production accept-failure path (transport.cljc, not debug-gated) too. (2) In-tree, http-decode-test, http-managed-test and http-empty-body-parity all use vector :decode schemas WITHOUT requiring re-frame.schemas, so an unconditional throw reddens all three on a solo run for schemas carrying no marks at all.

So extract-paths separates the two cases with declares-marks?, a presence probe asking only whether the schema's EDN form writes a :sensitive? / :large? PROP anywhere — a MAP KEY, so a field merely named :sensitive? is not a mark. It reads no Malli semantics, resolves no registry, derives no paths: not a second walker (the ns doc forbids one), it only decides whether the shared walker is REQUIRED. Declares no mark → {} as before, and a schemas-less app is untouched. Declares a mark with the hook unbound → throws :rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing via the canonical error/throw-error! builder, naming the require that fixes it. Probe and walker agree on the opaque cases (keyword registry ref, compiled m/schema object): both read them as markless leaves, so neither throws.

REUSING THE EXISTING ERROR ID leaves spec/009-Instrumentation.md — hot-zone — untouched; the id is already catalogued there. The contract is recorded in its owning tracked record, spec/014-HTTPRequests.md §Privacy, as a new rule 5 (old rule 5 Composition becomes 6; nothing in the repo references these by number, checked).

GATES, captured exits on the final rebased base: implementation/http 'clojure -M:test' exit 0, 514 tests / 3901 assertions (was 508 / 3883 — the six new tests are §7 of http_privacy_body_test, pinning the throw for both mark axes and the four no-throw cases); scripts/check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 for the spec edit. Both gates were exercised against a planted fault and came back red naming what was planted; restores verified by git BLOB hash against the committed object.

NO CASE FOUND THAT THE LOUDNESS CANNOT REACH, so no follow-up bead was filed. One adjacent surface was checked and deliberately LEFT: resources/classification.cljc's validation-failure-params-marks has the same {}-when-unbound shape but is not a live fail-open — it runs only on a validation failure, which requires the schemas artefact to have validated in the first place, so the unbound branch is unreachable, and its surrounding comment states that posture deliberately.

title: flake(http): supersede-stale poll-until backstop times out under CI load, redding unrelated PRs
description:
implementation/http test `re-frame.http-reply-lowering-test/supersede-distinct-work-ids-and-canonical-stale-trace` (http_reply_lowering_test.clj) fails intermittently on loaded CI runners with `poll-until timed out — supersede-stale`, reported as `0 failures, 1 errors` and exit 1 from `clojure -M:test` in implementation/http.

## Observed

- 2026-09-01, PR #8873 (a routing-only diff that cannot reach this code path): `:elapsed-ms 30022`, i.e. the full 30 s backstop elapsed. Re-running the identical tree on a fresh CI head was green with no code change.
- The test`s own source comment records a PRIOR occurrence of the same class and the mitigation taken then: the backstop was raised from 5 s to 30 s because "the async supersede landed AFTER the window, timing the machine, not the canonicalisation (it redded unrelated PRs, e.g. #6817)".

So the 5 s -> 30 s raise reduced the rate but did not remove the failure mode; 30 s is now demonstrably marginal too.

## Why it matters

This test is inside a surface-gated job, and implementation/http declares day8/re-frame2-routing as a {:local/root} dependency, so ANY routing-only change schedules the http job. A flake here therefore reds PRs whose diff provably cannot reach the code under test, and each red costs a diagnosis dispatch. PR #8873 cost exactly one.

## Shape of the problem, not a prescribed fix

The wait is already signal-based rather than a fixed sleep (`poll-until` on a predicate over delivered replies plus a `:rf.http/stale-suppressed` trace row), which is the right structure — the remaining `:timeout-ms` is a pure backstop. The question is whether the supersede round-trip can be made deterministic at the test boundary (await the transport reply and the trace row on a latch rather than polling), so the backstop is unreachable rather than merely generous. Raising the bound a third time is the option to weigh against that, not the obvious answer.

Deliberately NOT diagnosed here: whether the timeout indicates real contention in the supersede path under load, or purely runner scheduling. Worth one look before choosing a remedy — a genuinely slow supersede under load would be a product finding rather than a test one.

## Non-goals

- No change to supersede/stale-suppression semantics; those are what the test correctly pins.
- Not a licence to delete or weaken the assertion.
notes:
VERDICT (PR #8889, branch worker/http-robust-o9e15): FIXED, and the theory recorded on this bead and in the test source was WRONG.

FINDING 1 - the stale-suppression trace is NOT async. handlers/managed-handler calls registry/supersede! and then transport/emit-superseded-stale-trace! inline in the fx phase, so the :rf.http/stale-suppressed row has already landed before the SECOND dispatch-sync returns. Probed: present with ZERO wait. The source comment claiming a real async round-trip (transport reply -> reply lowering -> app dispatch -> stale trace) was factually wrong and is removed.

FINDING 2 - the failure mode is ABSENCE, not lateness. registry/supersede! returns nil when nothing is in flight under the request-id. The test gate was a CountDownLatch(1) whose FIRST act inside the handler was its own .countDown, so the following .await returned immediately and the gate never held request #1 at all. Request #1 was free to finish its whole loopback round trip in the gap between the two dispatch-sync calls; two app replies were then delivered, no supersede ever happened, and poll-until sat out its full backstop waiting for a row that could not arrive. That is why the 5s -> 30s raise reduced the rate without removing the mode, and why a third raise cannot help: no bound is large enough for an event that is never emitted.

REPAIR - a new start-held-server! holds every exchange until the TEST releases it, so #1 cannot finalise before #2 is issued and the supersede becomes a property of the ordering rather than of machine speed. The stale row is then asserted SYNCHRONOUSLY (the 30s poll is gone entirely), and the one genuinely async step, the surviving request app reply, is awaited on a CountDownLatch the reply handler itself counts down. The sibling supersede-suppresses-prior-app-reply carried the identical no-op gate and the identical latent race and moves to the same harness.

title: patterns/websocket: :ws/fatal out of :active strands in-flight requests (same class as rf2-b2jpr)
description:
rf2-b2jpr routed clean :ws/disconnect through the shared fail-in-flight helper so leaving :active settles every in-flight request exactly once. One door out of :active still bypasses that invariant: :ws/fatal {:target :failed :action :record-error} (examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs, :active :on). Fired from :connected with a non-empty :in-flight, it destroys the socket actor and strands every slot exactly as the clean-disconnect bug did — the scheduled timeout carries the destroyed socket id, :current-socket? rejects it after teardown, and the slot plus its waiting :reply-event survive forever, including across a later manual :ws/connect out of :failed.

Mitigating context: nothing in the example currently dispatches :ws/fatal — it is the documented app-level escape hatch (spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md, ':active / * --:ws/fatal--> :failed'), so the leak is reachable only by consumer code using the pattern as written. :ws/auth-failed -> [:failed] is provably safe by contrast: :in-flight only fills in :connected, and every door out of :active from :connected settles it once this is fixed.

Fix is small now the helper exists: compose fail-in-flight with :record-error on the :ws/fatal transition (one action that does both), plus a wrapper deftest mirroring websocket-clean-disconnect-fails-in-flight-request with :ws/fatal as the exit door. description: The Xray Epoch INTERCEPTOR (exception) row's jump-to-source chip reads :source-coord off the :rf.error/interceptor-exception trace tag; the router takes it from the interceptor map's :source-coord (interceptor.cljc error-record). reg-interceptor (the ONE supported authoring form, EP-0022) captures registration coords into the REGISTRY meta (interceptor_registry.cljc reg-interceptor* -> source-coords/merge-coords), but descriptor->interceptor lowers {:before/:after} descriptors through ->interceptor* WITHOUT threading those coords onto the built value — so an interceptor authored the supported way never gets the exception-row chip; only a VALUE registered at the migration boundary carrying its own :source-coord does. Until rf2-93sxp the ->interceptor macro was the de-facto route to a coord-carrying value (tests and the standard_epochs testbed used it); with the macro gone (PR #8791) those sites author with reg-interceptor descriptors and the testbed's exception-row chip degrades to plain text (the INTERCEPTORS registry-read step's chip is unaffected — spec 021:426 documents it off handler-meta). Candidate fix: descriptor->interceptor stamps :source-coord from the registration meta's coords (registry resolver, one site), making the chip work for the authoring form everywhere. Touches interceptor_registry.cljc + tests; check spec/009 and tools/xray/spec/021 wording. Named as within rf2-93sxp's non-goals ('no redesign of source-coordinate diagnostics'), hence this follow-up.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8817: resolve-ref threads the reg-interceptor registration meta's coords onto every resolved interceptor value as :source-coord (registration-coords helper; value's own coord wins; programmatic/framework/production paths stay coord-free), so a descriptor-authored interceptor's :rf.error/interceptor-exception trace now carries the registration coord the Xray exception-row chip reads. title: hicasso guide ch04: the owned-literal alternate-spelling claim is not delivered by the taught plain merge
description: docs/core/hicasso/04-controlled-inputs.md §Forward caller attributes safely (lines ~116-119 at 1af79839db) claims: 'A caller cannot replace the field's value, checked state, handler, key, or revision by supplying an alternative spelling such as :onInput or "value"; the controlled contract binds to the React slot reached by the authored literal.' The taught spelling — a plain merge with owned keys last — never delivered it: {:onInput f :on-input [...]} survives the merge as two map keys, both land on React's one onInput slot in convert-entry, and which wins is map iteration order. rf2-6c12m.12 removed :& (so no spelling delivers it now) and chose NOT to add a slot-collision refusal in convert-props — the epic's direction is fewer refusals and trust the programmer, and ch02 §Forward attributes with owned keys last already says 'Forward maps should use the same kebab-keyword spelling as Hiccup; a foreign props object's "className" string is a different merge key.' DO: bring ch04's sentence in line with ch02 — the owned literal wins by presence when the caller forwards the SAME key; an alternate spelling of the same slot is a different key, so forward maps in the same kebab spelling (or dissoc the alternates). title: hicasso: commit basis - drop the generation term if the frame epoch already covers it (verify first)
description:
commit-basis = generation + frame-commit-epoch + registry-epoch (generation.cljs:125). bump-generation! has one caller, flush! (collector.cljs:1008); flush! is reached only via mark-dirty!, whose two callers are the cell watch (:681) and the microtask rewire (:768). The watch fires because a reaction input moved, and every frame-state install already bumps frame-commit-epoch at both write chokepoints (core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1734-1749, 1821, 1956, 1981) - so on the watch path the generation never moves without the frame epoch moving first. On the rewire path the affected cell exists and its own re-stamp moves the boundary snapshot; there (max (inc epoch) (commit-basis ...)) (:1031-1033) is load-bearing only through inc - max cannot add correctness to a monotone term. The rest of the machinery (disposal hook, first-registration!, registry epoch, microtask rewire, acquire-cell! re-wire guard :956) each closes a named failure and should stay.

DO: verify-first. Scenario to watch: a STAGED key across a same-id reincarnation (the basis ties there today and the generation bump partially un-ties it as a side effect). Gate: staged_read_tear, reincarnation_*, first_registration and generation_fence_coverage suites. If green with the term removed: basis = frame epoch + registry epoch, cell stamp = inc, delete !generation / bump-generation! / the reset-basis! half. If not, close with the counter-example recorded in generation.cljs. Effort: small in code, medium in verification.
notes: 2026-08-29 15:07:56 AUSEST — VERIFIED-REFUSED: the premise does not hold; the generation term is load-bearing and is KEPT. Discriminating test staged_reincarnation_basis_cljs_test (commit 049ebf2b3e, PR #8745) drives the bead's own scenario at the commit seam: a boundary renders a STAGED key, the frame is destroyed and remade under the same id with its install epoch driven to equal the predecessor's at render (the frame term ties), while ONE other cell is held on the frame; the held cell's microtask rewire flushes and bumps the generation, which the staged boundary reads through the basis at commit. WITH the term: basis@commit != basis@render, 9/9 assertions green (exit 0). WITHOUT (control plant removed @!generation from commit-basis's sum): both read 4, row red (exit 1) — the predecessor's value left on screen, the P0 class generation.cljs names. Restored, blob hash equal to HEAD. Counter-example recorded on commit-basis's docstring per the DO, including the half the term does NOT cover (a frame holding no other cell has nothing to rewire and ties either way — the :node-key axis the docstring already concedes; not this bead's to close). Negative control in the same file: with nothing in the gap the number ties and nothing re-renders. Full node-test-hicasso lane: 1355 tests / 5534 assertions / 0 failures.
close_reason: Verified-refused: the generation term is load-bearing for a staged key across a same-id reincarnation (staged_reincarnation_basis_cljs_test, 049ebf2b3e, PR #8745): with the term the snapshot moves, without it both read 4 and the row is red. Term kept; counter-example recorded on commit-basis.

title: RULING: refusal contract shape - drop the :recovery keyword, :where, and the runtime meta-refusal
description:
impl/error.cljc is 356 lines (~60 code). Every refusal carries id + :where (emitting fn) + :reason + :recovery keyword + coords, and check-complete! mints :rf.error/hicasso-refusal-incomplete at RUNTIME (error.cljc:265) to police the package own call sites. :recovery is a keyword such as :declare-render-or-client-only-with-an-optional-fallback - spelled once, typed by nobody, tracking API renames (complaints.md:236-295 spend 60 lines ruling on when it moves; naming-ledger row 21 shows one option rename moved three recovery keywords across runtime + witnesses + Spec 009 rows). :where duplicates the stack trace. The valuable half - :view and :source from the macro-captured ledger - is ~30 lines.

RECOMMENDATION: (fail! id message extra) with the ambient :view/:source stamp; drop :recovery keyword and :where; delete the meta-refusal (a missing message is a code-review matter, not a runtime law). The message text still names the fix. Effort: ~2 hours + mechanical test edits (error_shape_cljs_test pins the shape). Counter-argument to weigh: a machine-readable recovery keyword could help an AI pair - but the reason string already carries the same words.

title: loops.md: FETCH_HEAD absence does not prove that no fetch ever ran
description:
FOUND BY THE MERGED-PR AUDIT OF PR #8721.

THE DEFECT. docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md now says each linked worktree gets its own fetch-head copy "the first time anything fetches from it", and that an absent file says "nothing has ever fetched from that tree". The first half of the correction is measured and sound: in the current repository, git rev-parse --git-path FETCH_HEAD resolves to a private metadata path for every linked worktree, and exactly four of seven linked worktrees have the file, matching the PR. The absolute inference from absence is not sound.

THE DIRECT COUNTEREXAMPLE IS PART OF GIT'S NORMAL INTERFACE, not a hypothetical deletion. Git 2.53's git fetch -h documents --[no-]write-fetch-head: a fetch can deliberately update refs without writing FETCH_HEAD. That is directly relevant to this paragraph's automated poller case. Such a poller can fetch forever while the per-worktree file remains absent. Therefore absence proves only that no fetch has written this clock in that worktree (or that the file is no longer there); it does not prove that no fetch has ever run.

IMPACT. The safe, load-bearing direction survives: movement is still proof that a writing fetch ran, while stillness proves nothing about liveness. The defect is confined to the new interpretation of absence, but that interpretation is the point of PR #8721 and can send a reader looking for the wrong history on an externally created tree.

MINIMAL REMEDY. Qualify the two new sentences in place: a linked worktree gets this file when a fetch writes FETCH_HEAD there, and absence means no fetch has written this particular clock. Briefly state that a poller configured not to write FETCH_HEAD is invisible to the clock. Preserve the four-of-seven measurement, the movement/stillness asymmetry, and the rest of the paragraph. Do not add machinery or a policy gate for this prose correction.
acceptance_criteria: docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md no longer says every fetch necessarily creates FETCH_HEAD or that file absence proves no fetch ever ran. It preserves the measured four-of-seven observation and the rule that movement is positive proof while a non-moving clock cannot establish liveness. The repair remains prose-only.

THE PREMISE WAS CHECKED BEFORE THE EDIT, not taken from the bead. git 2.53.0 here, and 'git fetch -h' lists --[no-]write-fetch-head, so a fetch can update refs without writing the clock. The finding is correct and the over-claim was mine, made in PR #8721 forty minutes earlier.

WHAT LANDED, one file, +18/-15, prose only, no machinery and no gate as the bead directed:
  * 'the first time anything fetches from it' -> 'the first time a fetch WRITES that clock there', with 'a fetch ORDINARILY writes as it reads' opening the sentence.
  * absence 'says only that nothing has ever fetched from that tree' -> 'says less than it looks like saying: only that no fetch has written that clock there, which is not the same as no fetch having run, because the write is suppressible by a flag on the fetch itself — a poller configured that way is invisible to this test altogether.'
  * the guidance moved with it: absence is now a reason to reach for another signal rather than a history of the tree, while staying a hint about a tree you did not create.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, CHECKED MECHANICALLY rather than asserted: 'first time anything fetches from it' 0, 'ever fetched from that tree' 0, 'four of seven' 1, 'Movement is proof of life' 1, 'stillness restores the ambiguity' 1, 'the write is suppressible' 1. title: method: the write-clock clause needs the worktree's age, and the obvious way to get it is wrong on exactly the worktrees that matter
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-22 10:03 AUSEST at tip 78c229ce28, on two live worktrees, controlled in both
directions. Found by the mayor while using its own clause.

THE CLAUSE THIS IS ABOUT. docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md, the stranded-sweep write-clock bullet,
carries a sentence added earlier today (rf2-1yct's sibling repair, commit c2a1246061): the clock
"says 'no activity' in three voices and you can only tell them apart with a control", one of the
three being "a span shorter than the worktree's own age".

SO THE CLAUSE DEPENDS ON KNOWING THE WORKTREE'S AGE, AND NAMES NO WAY TO GET IT. The obvious way
is to stat the worktree directory. On this platform's coreutils that is `stat -c %y`, "time of
last modification" -- and a directory's modification time is bumped by the worker writing inside
it.

MEASURED, TWO WORKTREES, ONE LIVE AND ONE INERT:

  pasteros (live worker, mid-edit)
    %y (last modification) 2026-08-22 10:03:23
    %w (birth)             2026-08-22 09:54:25
    -> the two disagree by nine minutes, and %y was moving between successive reads

  specsize (inert since 03:18, checked out at 00:28)
    %y 2026-08-22 00:31:35
    %w 2026-08-22 00:28:02
    -> the two agree to within the 3.5 minutes the checkout itself took

THE FAILURE IS INVERTED, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH A CLAUSE RATHER THAN A SHRUG. %y gives the
RIGHT answer on precisely the worktrees where the age does not matter -- the inert ones, where
nothing has written since checkout -- and the WRONG answer on the live one, where it is the whole
question. A mayor reading %y on a live worker sees a directory "seconds old", concludes the span
is longer than the worktree's age, and fires the no-discrimination warning on every live worker
while never firing it on a dead one. That is the opposite of what the clause is for.

AND IT IS SILENT. Nothing errors; both numbers are well-formed timestamps in the same format, and
on the first worktree a mayor happens to check -- typically an idle one -- they agree. This is the
same instrument class the document already names: an instrument that answers plausibly and wrongly
when misused, whose all-clear is complete and well-formed.

THE REPAIR, and it should be SHORT. One clause on the existing write-clock bullet naming the
distinction: the age you need is the CREATION time, not the last-modification time, and a
directory's modification time is bumped by the very writes you are trying to detect. The document
is OS-neutral by its own header's rule, so name the DISTINCTION (creation versus last
modification) rather than any particular tool's flag; `%w` versus `%y` is this platform's
spelling, not the rule.

A SECOND OPTION WORTH CONSIDERING and rejecting or taking on its merits: the dispatch record
already carries a creation timestamp for every worktree, because the mayor writes one at dispatch
time. Reading the age from the record the mayor itself wrote is more robust than asking the
filesystem at all, and needs no OS-specific spelling. If that is the better clause, say so and
write that instead.

BOUNDS. docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md only, and only the existing write-clock bullet. One or two
sentences. No new section, no new bullet, nothing moved. Generic: no OS-specific flag as the rule,
nothing repo-specific, no operator's name, no absolute paths.

FENCE: none on this file. A peer worker (pasteros, rf2-4j1v) is live in the same TREE but on a
different file, docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md -- no overlap. Re-check at
dispatch time.

Took the filesystem-distinction shape, rejected the dispatch-record shape (the method mandates no timestamp in that record, and 'one worker is not one worktree' means a worker-built gate tree has no dispatch line at all -- the sweep starts from the worktrees precisely because the records are incomplete). Control: broken in-page anchor planted mid-line on a line this change authored; slug gate named it by file/line/anchor. Measured that --strict exits 0 on that same plant while printing it at INFO.

title: ci(lint): lint.yml's own comments understate it — the surface omits two armed paths, and a non-linter job rides the same classifier
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD REREAD LOOP 2026-08-22, tip c2a1246061, by testing a claim I have been putting
into dispatch briefs against lint.yml's CODE rather than its COMMENT. Two inaccuracies, both in the
file's description of itself. Neither changed a dispatch outcome; both are fail-open in the
direction that makes a worker skip a gate that would have armed.

*** 1. THE `Lint surface:` COMMENT UNDERSTATES THE CLASSIFIER BY TWO ENTRIES. ***

The comment (around :45) reads "Lint surface: implementation/, tools/ (minus template/resources/),
examples/, testbeds/." The classifier it describes (around :59) reads:

  implementation/*|tools/*|examples/*|testbeds/*|.clj-kondo/*|.github/workflows/lint.yml

So `.clj-kondo/*` and `.github/workflows/lint.yml` arm the lint surface and are named nowhere in
the prose. A worker editing the shared clj-kondo config, or lint.yml itself, and reading the comment
to decide coverage would conclude lint does not arm — when it does. That is the fail-open direction:
understating coverage sends a worker to skip a gate, exactly as CLAUDE.md already warns that
"understating coverage misreports as surely as overstating it".

*** 2. THE FILE CALLS ITSELF A THREE-LINTER GATE AND HAS SIX JOBS, ONE OF WHICH RIDES THE SAME
CLASSIFIER AND IS NOT A LINTER. ***

The header says "Multi-linter CI gate. Three complementary linters run as parallel jobs" and then
describes clj-kondo, Splint and ESLint. The jobs are: detect, clj-kondo, splint, eslint,
api-manifest, provenance-pins-corpus, lint-required.

`api-manifest` ("Public-API manifest drift-check") is gated on `needs.detect.outputs.lint_surface
== 'true'` — the SAME classifier as clj-kondo and Splint. So a change to implementation/ or tools/
arms a public-API manifest drift-check as well as three linters, and the header does not say so. A
worker reading it to decide what its diff arms gets three names and four gated jobs.

(`provenance-pins-corpus` is gated on `github.event_name != 'pull_request'`, so it never runs on a
PR at all — worth stating for the same reason, since its name suggests otherwise.)

WHAT THIS DID NOT BREAK, stated so the priority is not read as higher than it is. My briefs said
"lint.yml's surface is implementation/, tools/, examples/, testbeds/, so docs/ is outside it and its
expensive jobs skip job-side." That CONCLUSION is correct and I re-verified it: on a pull request
touching only docs/, lint_surface and js_surface are both false, so clj-kondo, Splint, ESLint and
api-manifest all skip, provenance-pins-corpus does not run on PR events, and lint-required
aggregates all-skipped to a pass. The reasoning was incomplete; the answer was right.

THE REPAIR: bring both comments into line with the code. Name `.clj-kondo/*` and
`.github/workflows/lint.yml` in the Lint-surface comment, and correct the header so it describes
what the file runs — three linters PLUS a manifest drift-check on the same classifier, plus a
corpus job that skips on PRs. Prose only; no workflow behaviour changes and no job moves.

SAME CLASS AS AN ALREADY-ACCEPTED REPAIR: commit e324988e13 (rf2-0tkx / rf2-xomo) was
"docs(claude)+test(classifier): make the pair's self-description true". This is that, one file over.

HOT-ZONE — SEQUENCE IT. `.github/workflows/*` is on CLAUDE.md's hot-zone list, so this is never
parallel with another workflow change. It is prose-only and not urgent; there is no reason to run it
against a busy fleet.

GATE NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: editing `.github/workflows/lint.yml` ARMS THE LINT SURFACE — the
classifier names that exact path, which is the second half of finding 1. So this change gates
itself, and the honest check is that clj-kondo and Splint actually run on the PR rather than skip.
close_reason:
FIXED by PR #8692 (branch worker/lintdesc-63il), merged and fast-forwarded onto main at ac8637b308.
One file, .github/workflows/lint.yml, +35/-4, COMMENTS ONLY — verified mechanically before merging:
zero job keys added, and zero added lines that are not comments.

*** MY FILED REPAIR WAS WRONG AND THE WORKER REPLACED IT. This is the part worth keeping. ***

I filed "append `.clj-kondo/*` and `.github/workflows/lint.yml` to the Lint-surface comment". That
would have introduced a NEW error, in BOTH directions:
  - still omitting TEN patterns — the arming set is five `case` arms and sixteen patterns, including
    .splint.edn, spec/API.md, both api-manifest EDN files, skills/*, docs/core/*,
    docs/*/concepts.md, spec/Privacy.md, docs/api/*, docs/story/api/*;
  - and newly claiming clj-kondo LINTS a YAML workflow and an EDN config directory, which it does
    not.

THE REAL DEFECT IS ONE LEVEL DEEPER THAN I DIAGNOSED: ONE PHRASE NAMES TWO DIFFERENT SETS. The
`Lint surface:` paragraph was not describing the classifier arm at all — it describes the `--lint`
TARGET paths and says so ("excluded by virtue of the explicit `--lint` paths below"), and as an
account of THOSE it was accurate. The next paragraph then uses "the lint surface" for the ARMING
set, and the job is named "Detect lint surface" with output `lint_surface`. Two sets, one phrase.

drift again — which is a better repair than any list would have been.

FINDING 2 HELD AS FILED, plus two I did not name: ESLint keys on `js_surface`, so the three linters

the prose beneath it enumerates seven. Seven is correct.

verified unique first and restored with git hash-object verified against blob 44ef4c13bd.

title: docs(claude): mkdocs --strict does not gate in-page anchors, so check_doc_slugs.py is the only anchor gate under docs/
description:
FOUND 2026-08-22 06:1x AUSEST by the rf2-n3uw worker during its sabotage run, and RE-VERIFIED AT
SOURCE by the mayor at tip 852abfc48a before filing.

THE MEASUREMENT. A broken in-page anchor was planted mid-line in a page under docs/. Two gates
were run on it:

  python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py    -> exit 1, naming the file, the line and the anchor
  python -m mkdocs build --strict      -> exit 0

THE REASON, read out of mkdocs.yml rather than inferred. The validation block sets exactly one
key:

  validation:
    links:
      unrecognized_links: warn

There is NO `anchors` key, so anchor validation sits at the MkDocs default, and `--strict`
promotes WARNING but not INFO. The file's own comment block already documents this promotion
mechanism for the two `links` levels — it is why `unrecognized_links` was raised to `warn` under
rf2-5exqc — but it stops at links and says nothing about anchors.

THIS IS REDUNDANCY MISSING, NOT COVERAGE MISSING, and the priority reflects that. In-page anchors
under docs/ ARE gated: check_doc_slugs.py catches them, and it runs in test.yml's
verify-readme-links job on every PR, which carries no surface guard. Nothing is currently
shipping unchecked.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH RECORDING: it is a FAIL-OPEN GATE NOMINATION waiting to happen, which is the
class this project already spends words on. CLAUDE.md's Build & Test section carries a careful pin
beginning "Link validation is split across two gates, and the split does not follow the job name",
and it nominates gates by path. A reader of that passage would reasonably take `mkdocs build
--strict` to cover anchors on a page inside docs_dir — it is the strict site build over exactly
that tree. It does not, and a brief nominating it alone for an anchor change gets a green that
inspected nothing. The method's own rule is "never nominate a gate that does not cover the surface
being edited", and this is a case where the non-coverage is invisible from the gate's name, its
scope and its output.

THE REPAIR, and it is one clause in prose that already exists — do NOT add a section:
in CLAUDE.md's link-validation paragraph, say that `mkdocs build --strict` does not gate in-page
ANCHORS at all (it reports them at INFO, which --strict does not promote), so check_doc_slugs.py
is the only anchor gate for pages under docs/. Optionally note the same asymmetry beside the

settle-row! now exists TWICE, verbatim: server_render_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs (rf2-sxhu, PR #8675) and identifier_prefix_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs (rf2-x43z). Both copies are spelled identically on purpose so this lift is a deletion and a :require rather than a reconciliation of two designs.

WHY IT WAS NOT LIFTED AT rf2-x43z. Two reasons, and the first is the fence:

1. rf2-x43z was fenced to ONE test namespace. Lifting into roots_frames_support.cljs while leaving the sibling copy standing gives the corpus TWO definitions of one helper - strictly worse than either clean answer - and removing the sibling copy is outside that fence.

2. Where the helper lives, its CONTROLS have to live too. PR #8675 built two (a-throwing-body-finishes-the-row-once-and-not-twice, a-rejected-adoption-leaves-the-next-row-a-clean-page) and rf2-x43z built its own rejected-adoption control, because settle-row!'s rejection arm is on no green path. roots_frames_support.cljs holds no deftests by convention, so the lift has to decide where the shared helper's coverage sits. That is a design call, not a mechanical move.

WHAT MAKES THE LIFT WARRANTED RATHER THAN SPECULATIVE - and this is the correction to the two-callers premise. Measured at tip ecb7057c26 with fixed-string grep over implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/:

  file                                       sup/adopted! sites   .catch count
  server_render_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs       7                    6   <- repaired, rf2-sxhu
  identifier_prefix_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs   5                    0   <- repaired, rf2-x43z
  roots_frames_hydration_dom_cljs_test.cljs  3                    0   <- SAME FAULT, untouched
  presence_ssr_seam_dom_cljs_test.cljs       2                    0   <- SAME FAULT, untouched
  instance_key_payload_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs 1                   3   <- different shape, see below

So the shape reaches FOUR namespaces, not two. Two callers is the weakest case for a shared abstraction; four is not.

instance_key_payload is NOT the same fault and should not be swept in without reading it: its rows end (.catch (fn [e] (is false ...) nil)) then (.then (fn [_] (done))), so they settle exactly once and DO report the rejection. Their teardown is skipped on the rejection path, and an inline comment argues that case deliberately. Judge it on its own.

DO FIRST, then lift as one move: repair roots_frames_hydration_dom_cljs_test.cljs (:589, :755-756) and presence_ssr_seam_dom_cljs_test.cljs (:506, :600), each with settle-row! applied locally. Then this bead deletes the copies, puts one definition in roots-frames-support, and settles where the controls live.

DISCOVERED-FROM rf2-x43z.

And it gave the local copy its OWN control rather than leaning on the sibling's coverage for a copy that can drift — which is the right thing to do for a deliberately duplicated helper.

SO THIS BEAD'S CONDITION IS UNCHANGED AND ITS GROUND IS NOW BETTER. It blocks on rf2-8zhr and rf2-z17t because only after all four are repaired can a lift collapse four copies into one rather than create a fifth. comments.text:
WORKER settlelift (rf2-8zhr + rf2-z17t, PR #8688) — a VIEW ON THE LIFT, recorded
under the dispatch's fence and NOT acted on. The two remaining suites are now
repaired, so the count this bead waited for is reached: four landed call sites.

THE LIFT IS MECHANICALLY CLEAN, and I checked the three things that could have
made it a reconciliation rather than a deletion.

1. THE FOUR COPIES ARE THE SAME FUNCTION. I diffed the two already on main by
   line range rather than by eye — server_render_ssr_dom_cljs_test and
   identifier_prefix_ssr_dom_cljs_test — and the 14-line body is byte-identical:
   same parameter list, same defaults, same nil-or-[e] carrier. The two I added
   are copies of that exact body. Only the docstrings differ, and only in which
   rows they name.

2. THE LIFT TARGET ALREADY REFERS `is`. `roots_frames_support.cljs`'s ns form is
   `(:require [cljs.test :refer-macros [is]] …)` — `skip!` is an `(is true …)`.
   So hosting `settle-row!` there adds NO new require to the support namespace,
   and the helper takes no dependency on anything else: it touches only `is`,
   the promise, and the fns its opts carry.

3. THE `:release!` PRIMITIVES DIFFER ACROSS SUITES AND THAT DOES NOT MATTER.
   Call sites pass `h/unmount!` in one suite and `mount/release!` in the others;
   the helper never names either. Nothing about the differing teardown vocabulary
   pushes back on a shared definition.

ONE THING THAT IS NOT PART OF THE LIFT, so it is not an objection to it. The H5
row in roots_frames_hydration mints its releasables INSIDE the chain — `ha` needs
the server's bytes and those arrive as a promise — so a tail `settle-row!` cannot
close over them, and that row holds them in a `held` atom populated as they are
created. That is a CALL-SITE shape, not a helper variant: it passes the ordinary
`{:row :done :release!}` and the helper is untouched by it. Do not try to absorb
it into the shared definition.

WHAT I WOULD WATCH. `settle-row!` is `defn-` (private) in all four. The lift makes
it public API of the support namespace — trivial, but it is the one signature
change the lift actually makes, so it is worth stating deliberately rather than
falling out of the move.

SEQUENCING. All four suites are hot for this lift by construction: it deletes a
definition from each and adds a `:require`. PR #8688 is open and unmerged, so the
lift wants to wait for it — otherwise two of the four deletions target text that
is not on main yet.

Verified at source at tip f40207d501. Not dispatched, not started, no files
touched under this bead.

title: hicasso: identifier_prefix_ssr_dom_cljs_test's four adoption rows never settle on rejection — no .catch at all
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-sxhu WORKER (asyncsettle, PR #8675) as a sibling of the fault it was fencing, reported outside its fence and correctly left. IT POINTED AT ONE LINE (~541) AND CALLED IT 'the same shape'. I re-derived it at source and the pointer is right about the FILE and wrong about the SHAPE, which changes the repair — recording the correction here rather than inheriting the characterisation.

THE FILE: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/identifier_prefix_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs, six deftests, four of them async adoption rows.

WHAT rf2-sxhu's FILE HAD: a .catch arm that called (done) alongside a finally that also called it — a DOUBLE-FINISH — plus cleanup skipped on the rejection path.

WHAT THIS FILE HAS IS THE OPPOSITE HALF. There is no .catch anywhere in it. Measured with a working control in both directions: grep -c '\.catch' returns 0 on this file and 4 on server_render_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs at 2d064aec99, the base rf2-sxhu repaired. So the pattern reaches this corpus and the zero is a reading.

THE SHAPE AT ALL FOUR SITES:

  (-> (sup/adopted! handle)
      (.then (fn [ok] ... (try ...assertions... (finally (stop!) (mount/release! handle) (done))))))

  adoption promise   fulfilment handler   finally
  :353               :354                 :397
  :416               :417                 :448
  :492               :493                 :540-544   <- the ~541 the worker pointed at
  :578               :579                 :603

SO ON A REJECTION NOTHING RUNS AT ALL. The .then handler is skipped, the try is never entered, the finally never fires — and therefore (done) is never called, (stop!) never stops the mismatch watcher, and (mount/release! handle) never releases the root. Three consequences, and the first is why this is worth a bead rather than a note:

1. THE FAILURE IS OPAQUE. The row does not fail; it HANGS to the async timeout, and the message names the timeout rather than the rejection. rf2-sxhu's sites at least reported something.
2. THE WATCHER AND THE ROOT LEAK INTO THE NEXT ROW, which is the same second fault rf2-sxhu names, so the following row's census is measuring residue.
3. THE REJECTION IS NEVER REPORTED, so what the adoption actually threw is lost.

:540-544 is the site whose finally spans five lines because it releases TWO roots (ha and hb) — it is the two-simultaneous-roots row, and it is the one where a leak costs most.

WHAT THE REPAIR PROBABLY WANTS, but the worker decides: PR #8675 introduced a shared settle-row! helper in the sibling namespace that carries one .then with BOTH handlers (mutually exclusive, so a throwing body cannot also reach the rejection arm), release and done beyond both, done in a finally, and a :row label carrying what the hand-written messages did. Whether that helper is lifted into the shared support namespace or the pattern is re-applied locally is a judgement about how many callers it will end up with — do not lift it on the strength of two files without saying why.

ACCEPTANCE: each of the four rows settles exactly once on fulfilment or rejection, reports the rejection with enough to identify the row, stops the watcher and releases every handle on both paths. A deliberate rejected-adoption control that fails before the repair and proves the FOLLOWING row sees no retained root, frame or listener. No assertion changes — prove that mechanically, by extracting the balanced (is ...) forms from both revisions and diffing, as PR #8675 did.

FENCE: keep it to this one test namespace. rf2-sxhu's own widening note is the precedent and its reasoning applies — bounded repair bounds the change, not the search — but the search has been done here and it returned this file.

FENCE recorded 2026-08-22 02:3x AUSEST by the dispatch tick — EXCLUSIVE RESOURCE, CONTENDED. Not dispatchable while the quiet-box window is live.

WHY, and it is not about this bead's surface. Nobody holds identifier_prefix_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs, and there is no hot-zone collision. What blocks it is the MACHINE: worker sliceclock is taking rf2-85og2's U1/U2 clock window under Mike's standing quiet-box grant, and the condition for that grant is no worker holding the machine at all — not one bench-class worker, not a peer running any gate. THE FLEET IS BEING HELD THIN ON PURPOSE. Do not read the idle slots as under-saturation and refill them; a full fleet is what fences the whole measurement lane. See the lane posture recorded on rf2-85og2.
WORKER settlerows (worker/settlerows-x43z), premise verification at tip ecb7057c26. Every numbered premise in the bead and the brief VERIFIED AT SOURCE, with one correction and two additions.

VERIFIED. The four adoption promises sit at :353 :416 :488 :574 and their finally forms at :397 :448 :540 :603 - the brief's re-derivation, exact. grep -c -F '.catch' returns 0 on this file and 6 on the repaired server_render_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs; the same instrument returns 5 for '.then' on this file, so the zero is a reading and not a broken search. :488 is indeed the two-roots row and its finally releases ha AND hb - and it also carries an INTERMEDIATE (.then (fn [_] (sup/adopted! hb))) at :489, so a rejection can arise from either adoption.

CORRECTION 1 - THE BEAD'S POINTER TO :492/:578 IS OFF BY FOUR. The bead's table gives the adoption promise for the two-roots row as :492 and for the near-miss row as :578; at tip they are :488 and :574. The brief's re-derived table is the correct one. Recorded because the bead says these numbers have drifted once already.

CORRECTION 2 - THE LEAK ENUMERATION rf2-sxhu's CONTROL CARRIES OVERSTATES BY ONE ITEM, and this file inherits the fixture it describes. That control's prose reads 'it resets frames, the cell table and the runtime, but it does not unmount a root, unregister a trace listener, or hand console.error back'. The trace-listener half is wrong for make-reset-runtime-fixture: its shared reset body calls trace-tooling/clear-listeners! (test_support.cljc:552), and under :async? true that body runs in :before, so a leaked watcher IS swept before the next row. What the fixture genuinely does not take back is the mounted React root with its container still in the document, and the replaced console.error with its window error listener - and THAT one is the sharp end here, because §2 and §5 open their captures with :swallow-uncaught? true, so a listener outliving its row goes on calling preventDefault on every later row's uncaught errors. rf2-x43z's own control asserts stop! ran anyway, on the ground that a row leaning on the fixture to stop its own watcher is measuring the fixture, and says so in the row rather than repeating the overstatement. Not fixing the sibling's prose - outside the fence.

ADDITION - THE FENCE'S THIRD NAMESPACE IS TWO, REPORTED AND NOT TOUCHED. Same fixed-string instrument over implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/:
  roots_frames_hydration_dom_cljs_test.cljs   3 adoptions, 0 .catch  -> rf2-8zhr
  presence_ssr_seam_dom_cljs_test.cljs        2 adoptions, 0 .catch  -> rf2-z17t
Both carry this exact fault. A fifth, instance_key_payload_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs (1 adoption, 3 .catch), is NOT the same shape and should not be swept in: its rows settle exactly once and do report the rejection; only their teardown is skipped on that path, and an inline comment argues that case deliberately.
GATE MECHANICS, recorded for the next worker on rf2-8zhr / rf2-z17t because two of them cost a run each to learn.

THE BROWSER LANE HAS NO NAMESPACE FILTER. implementation/scripts/serve-and-run-browser-tests.cjs takes only --root and --port; the :browser-test build's ns-regexp is '.*-dom-cljs-test$' and compiles the whole corpus (1084 files). So the gate for a one-namespace repair is still the full lane. Split it as two foreground phases with separately captured exit codes - 'shadow-cljs compile browser-test' then the runner - rather than the compound npm script; the compile is ~45s cold and ~19s warm, the run ~3.5 min.

WHICH TREE THE GATE READ: this lane PRINTS its root, twice. The compile logs 'shadow-cljs - config: <worktree>/implementation/shadow-cljs.edn' and the runner logs 'Serving <worktree>/implementation/out/browser-test'. Check those lines rather than planting for discrimination alone.

THE SUMMARY TIMEOUT IS 6 MINUTES (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 360000 in scripts/run-browser-tests.cjs, override $BROWSER_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS). That matters for THIS fault specifically: the pre-repair shape does not produce a failing assertion, it produces a row that never calls done, which stalls cljs.test's async runner. So a sabotage run of this fault costs a full 6-minute timeout rather than a fast red, and the log carries no 'Ran N tests' line at all. Budget for it.

THE CHANGED-SURFACE CLASSIFIER TAKES PATHS, NOT REVISIONS. .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh handed two revisions reports EVERY surface false - indistinguishable from a genuinely unaffected change, and it does not error. Handed the actual path it reports implementation_jvm, cljs_node_test, cljs_browser, migration_hicasso_codemod, hicasso_controlled and hicasso_hmr true. Exercise it against a path it must flag before believing any all-false.

A PLANT ANCHOR NEEDS THIS CHECKOUT'S OWN LINE ENDING. A two-line anchor joined with a bare LF matched ZERO times here - the worktree is CRLF - and would have no-opped silently had the count not been read first. Discover the ending from the file rather than assuming, and read the match count before spending a run; the blob hash convicts a no-op plant only afterwards.
SABOTAGE CONTROL, MEASURED - AND THE CONSEQUENCE IS WORSE THAN THE BEAD PREDICTED. Recording it because it changes how the remaining two suites (rf2-8zhr, rf2-z17t) should be argued.

THE PLANT: settle-row!'s rejection arm removed, restoring the file's pre-repair condition exactly - one .then carrying a fulfilment handler and nothing else, no rejection arm anywhere in the namespace. Applied from a COMMITTED tree; source change proven by git BLOB hash (573103391e9ef55c6b14488bd9ba8951cdd5c01e -> 3eee8476864765950c332f3f3fa2562959844284) and runtime observation proven independently by the compile reporting '2 compiled' rather than 0. Restore verified by hashing back to 573103391e9ef55c6b14488bd9ba8951cdd5c01e, not by reading a diff.

THE VERDICT: captured exit 1 against the repaired tree's captured exit 0. The four ordinary rows are unaffected by the plant because they all fulfil; only the new leak control takes the rejection arm, which is the point of having it.

WHAT THE RUNNER SAID, and this is the finding:

  THE BROWSER RUN ABORTED - no cljs.test summary, and the page emitted 1 uncaught error(s) (rf2-u0j8).
  The run announced 85 namespace(s) before it stopped, the last being re-frame.hicasso.identifier-prefix-ssr-dom-cljs-test. Every namespace scheduled after that point never executed - shadow.test runs the whole lane, and the closing summary, inside ONE cljs.test/run-block, which has no try/catch.
  Error: adoption rejected on purpose

THE BEAD SAID THE ROW WOULD HANG TO THE ASYNC TIMEOUT. Under this repo's browser runner it does something worse and louder: the unhandled rejection reaches the page as an uncaught error, the runner treats that as terminal (rf2-u0j8), and the WHOLE LANE STOPS at this namespace. No 'Ran N tests' line at all, against 1070 tests / 6059 assertions on the repaired tree - so consequence 2 in the bead's list ('the next row's census measures residue') understates it: on the browser lane there IS no next row, and every namespace after this one is silently unrun. title: hicasso: PR #8672's adopted-DOM async witnesses double-finish and leak on rejection
description:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8672 (completeness / correctness / implementation quality).

The product-door byte premise and the adopted-DOM/control readings are strong, but the two new async rows in implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/server_render_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs have an unreliable failure path.

At merge a8641fdc3c, the-door-s-id-survives-the-adoption-and-a-real-client-render (lines 454-508) and the-hand-rolled-bytes-lose-the-id-through-the-same-door (lines 510-574) both call done in the .then callback's finally and then attach a .catch that calls done again.

That creates two distinct faults:
1. If sup/adopted! rejects before .then runs, .catch ends the row without unmounting the hydration handle or stopping the mismatch watcher. The control closes its console capture, but likewise omits unmount/watcher teardown.
2. If code inside .then throws, finally unmounts and calls done, the returned promise rejects, and .catch reports the error and calls done a second time. A failure can therefore advance the runner twice and make the following row's state/reporting unreliable.

The green success path and current sabotage controls do not exercise either branch. Keep the repair local to this test namespace; no runtime, SSR, disposition, or product API change is indicated.
acceptance_criteria: Each new async witness has one settlement path that reports a rejection, stops every watcher/capture, unmounts any created handle, and calls done exactly once on fulfillment or rejection. Add a deliberate rejected-adoption or thrown-body control that fails before the repair and proves the following row sees no retained root, frame, listener, or capture. Preserve the three witness readings and their node/browser coverage.

  :568-:574  same shape — finally (done) at :570, .catch (done) at :574
These are the two rows PR #8672 added, and they carry BOTH faults: double-finish on a throw
inside .then, and no unmount/watcher teardown when adopted! rejects before .then runs.

TWO MORE SITES, FAULT 1 ONLY, and they PREDATE #8672:
  :390-:398  (done) inside the .then body, .catch (done). Correct once-per-path idiom for done —
             NOT a double-finish — but the .catch stops no watcher and unmounts no handle.
  :655-:668  same: (done) at :664, .catch calls (remove!) and (done) but neither
             ((:stop! watch)) nor (h/unmount! handle).
So the leak-on-rejection half is a property of every async row in the namespace, not only of the
two the audit read. The double-finish half is genuinely confined to the new pair.

named site at a time, and the audit that reopens each of them is the same audit. The bead's own

title: docs(claude): the one-toucher classifier-pair rule is stated universally and the tree does not support it
description:

one-sentence repair to CLAUDE.md that I am doing MYSELF, not dispatching — filed so it survives
the tick rather than to hand it to a worker.

WHAT THE DOCUMENT SAYS. CLAUDE.md:91, on '.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh and its
mirror implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs':

  'That last pair is one-toucher by construction rather than by convention: the test pins the
   classifier's outputs, so A CHANGE TO EITHER ALONE LANDS A TREE WHERE THE SUITE CONTRADICTS
   THE SCRIPT — they move in ONE commit, and two workers in that pair conflict every time.'

WHAT THE TREE DID. PR #8664 (rf2-xomo) changed the TEST HALF ALONE — one file,
implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs, 40 insertions / 10 deletions, no script
change — and merged GREEN at 88/88 with every check terminal. The suite did not contradict the
script. Verified just now: gh pr view 8664 reports state=MERGED, files=1.

WHY THE UNIVERSAL FORM IS WRONG, and the distinction is the whole repair. The rule assumes every
change to one half CREATES a contradiction. A change can also REMOVE one. #8664's test carried a
pin naming docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md, an address that ceased to exist when
PR #8661 moved the contract; the script's behaviour was never wrong and needed nothing. Its
worker put it exactly right: 'This change runs the other way: the test contradicted the script's
ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR, and now agrees with it.'

The same shape is queued again on rf2-xomo's reopen: the audit asks for a test NAME rename with
no classifier behaviour change. Under the rule as written a mayor would force a pointless
two-file diff, or block a legitimate one-file fix.

THE REPAIR — narrow the claim to what is true, do not delete it. The pair must move together when
the change alters WHAT THE CLASSIFIER OUTPUTS, or what the test PINS about those outputs. A change
that only corrects the test to match the script's existing, unchanged behaviour — a stale pin, an
overstated test name — is legitimately one file, and saying so is what keeps the rule credible.
The 'two workers in that pair conflict every time' half STANDS and must be kept: that is about
concurrency, not about diff shape, and it is what the dispatch fences rely on.

WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY FIXED: CLAUDE.md is currently held by PR #8666 (worker fhsweep, rf2-wppza),
unmerged. Editing it now would plant a conflict in exactly the file this rule is about. DO IT
AFTER #8666 MERGES.

  #8664 — test half only, 1 file, merged green 88/88.
  #8666 — both halves, comments only, one commit (afe06a9145).
  rf2-xomo reopen — a test-name rename, no behaviour change, one file.

That guard is right and I was wrong. 'One sentence' and 'method work' are not exemptions —
orchestration, not implementation, is the rule, and the hook is the backstop that catches a mayor
reasoning its way past it. I reverted the working-copy edit and verified the blob matches HEAD
before dispatching.

My draft replacement wording is on the bead and in the brief, given to the worker as a STARTING
POINT rather than as text to paste unexamined.

Its bold lead says the pair must move together for any change that alters what the test PINS about classifier outputs. The later sentence then exempts this stale-pin repair, contradicting the lead that operators skim. title: hic: remaining SSR prose still calls hand-rolled renderToString the package's only server path
description:
## Owner: found while auditing rf2-s52w. This stale sentence is what PRODUCED that bead's false root cause.

`implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:66`, under the
header section *## What is deliberately NOT here*, still reads:

> **A Hicasso server entry.** There is none, and none is needed: the consumer calls
> `react-dom/server` and the policy is honoured by rendering. The harness here is
> `renderToString` called by hand, which is the only server path in the package.

Both halves are false at trunk tip.

`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs` — 452 lines, `re-frame.hicasso.server/render`
— landed in commit `30317bfe0e` on 2026-08-14 21:28 +1000 (`feat(hicasso):
re-frame.hicasso.server/render, and h/hydrate! on the door (rf2-b6jkj)`, PR #8236). It is a real
product door, not a stub: `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/roots.cljs:50-58`
names it as one of the TWO minters of the adoption window — "once per REQUEST, closed in that
door's `finally`" — and records that because both doors call `impl.mount/tree` "the fork is
decided once for both sides of the wire". So it is neither absent nor a second server path
beside the hand-rolled harness; it is THE server path, and the hand-rolled `renderToString` in
this file is the harness beside it.

## Why it is worth fixing rather than shrugging at

Checkpoint 3 cited THIS FILE, by name and "in terms", as the evidence for a root cause it then
wrote into rf2-s52w: *"THERE IS NO HICASSO SERVER ENTRY. Every server witness in the package
calls react-dom/server's renderToString by hand — native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs says so in
terms."* From there it propagated into `docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md:89`,
into `checkpoint-3-native.md`, and finally into a mayor note of 2026-08-21 that raised
"Does Hicasso ship a server entry?" as an open decision for Mike — a week after it shipped.

One stale docstring, four downstream records, one moot operator question. That is the cost, and
it is why this is a bead rather than a shrug.

## It is an omission, not a convention

The bullet DIRECTLY ABOVE it in the same section was amended in place when its own condition
changed: "When this file was written the prefix was UNSPELLABLE ... The operator then ruled a
thin pass-through, so `:identifier-prefix` is now an option on both root doors and the clause is
reachable; what has not changed is that it is not a NATIVE-tier claim, which is why it is still
not here." So the file's convention is to amend and keep the reason. The server-entry bullet was
simply missed — including by the 2026-08-20 sweep that touched this file twice (`7a65ab11d7`,
`53df56d29b`).

## The repair

Amend the bullet in place, in the same shape as its neighbour: the file's own harness is still a
hand-rolled `renderToString` and that is still deliberate (these are NATIVE-tier claims and the
product door is dispositioned elsewhere), but say that `re-frame.hicasso.server/render` exists
and is the package's server path, so the sentence cannot be re-read as a fact about the package.
Keep it a *deliberately not here* bullet; do not turn it into a claim this file does not measure.

While there: check the other bullets in that section against the current tree, since this one
survived two sweeps.

## Fences and gates

- Test-file docstring only. No behaviour change; no assertion touched.
- `implementation/**` is OUTSIDE `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`'s roots — a markdown link planted
  there returns that gate GREEN. `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` is the gate for markdown
  beside source, and since rf2-i4nb2 its third roster covers non-README tracked markdown — but a
  CLJS docstring is neither, so NO link gate reaches this text. If the amendment adds or changes
  a link, check it by hand and say so in the PR body.
- `verdictlbl` (rf2-egdaq) holds `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/` — a
  different directory. Re-check holders before editing; the fence is a dispatch-time claim.
acceptance_criteria: native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs's 'A Hicasso server entry' bullet no longer asserts that none exists or that the hand-rolled renderToString is the package's only server path; it names re-frame.hicasso.server/render and keeps its 'deliberately not here' framing with the reason. The section's other bullets re-checked against the current tree. No assertion changed.

PR #8645 accurately fixes the two carriers in native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs, but a repo-wide exact-claim sweep finds seven live carriers of the same now-false present-tense architecture statement across five other source/test files: identifier_prefix_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:24, :93-94 and :204; core_view_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:10; client_only_arms_ssr_cljs_test.cljs:153; facade_roster_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:211; and impl/mount.cljs:182. title: hic: scope row 5's 'mismatch attribution' required result to roots a re-frame2 door opens (rf2-s52w's last acceptance clause)
description:
## Owner: this is rf2-s52w's remaining acceptance clause, not a new finding

rf2-s52w's acceptance option B has three clauses. Two are discharged:

- the source-located statement + measured witness landed in PR #8302 (`473ff5e330`) —
  `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_abi_dom_cljs_test.cljs:30-52` header,
  measured row at `:920`, pointer from `native_abi_cljs_test.cljs:38-46`;
- `docs/design/hicasso/product/dispositions.md:290`'s HS-21 row was amended 2026-08-20 by
  rf2-vwo53 (PR #8559).

The third — *row 5's required-result sentence amended to scope "mismatch attribution" to roots
the package itself adopts* — is still owing, and no open bead owned it before this one.
A later audit re-finding it should recognise it as rf2-s52w's clause, not a second finding.

## The obligation and where it actually lives

Two homes, and it is the SECOND that creates the obligation:

1. `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/hot-path-architecture.md:49` — the native tier's only
   release checklist ("A red row blocks publication of the native namespace"). Row 5's
   *Required result* reads "...including server bytes or source refusal, matching hydration,
   **mismatch attribution** and multiple roots".

2. `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md:34` — the canonical matrix
   row 5 is measured against. Its per-row hydration column for *Root/frame provider and
   outward bridge* (`:24`) does NOT list mismatch attribution. But the blanket sentence at
   `:34` — "Every Render row runs the common hydration states: matching content, **deliberate
   mismatch with source attribution**, two simultaneous roots with stable `identifierPrefix`,
   and unmount cleanup" — puts it back on every Render row, that one included. So the row's
   omission is not a carve-out and the blanket sentence is what has to be scoped.

## What the scope IS, normatively

`spec/011-SSR.md:825` already states it in as many words: the framework reporter rides the
package's own hydrate path, and "hydrating via the substrate-native renderer directly
(`uix.dom/hydrate-root`, react-dom `hydrateRoot`) bypasses the reporter and falls back to
React's default (silent) handling". `onRecoverableError` is an option of an INDIVIDUAL root
(`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/roots.cljs:20-27`), so a root the package
did not open takes none of the package's options.

**Scope it by WHO OPENED THE ROOT, not by which surface.** There are two re-frame2 doors that
install the reporter on a React-element root — `h/hydrate!`
(`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/mount.cljs:546`) and the Spec 006 client
mount entry `(re-frame.substrate.adapter/render tree mount {:hydrate? true})`
(`implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1107`, whose docstring at `:1191-1204`
names itself the only native mount route that installs it). The outward bridge is not special:
any surface under a root the consumer opened with raw `react-dom/client` is equally outside the
channel. Wording that singles out the outward bridge invites a door for the outward bridge,
which is the wrong remedy.

## Why this is worth one small edit rather than leaving it

The release checklist is a publication gate. As written, row 5 can never go green for a reason
everyone already agrees is correct and normative, so every checkpoint re-derives the same
"unmet" and pays a dispatch to refute it —
`docs/design/hicasso/product/checkpoint-3-native.md:194` records the finding,
`checkpoint-4-coverage.md:384` and `correction-ledger.md:89` both record that Checkpoint 4's
conjunct B keeps scoring HS-21 until the sentence is amended. This edit REMOVES a clause; it
adds no gate, no diagnostic and no ceremony.

## Fences

- DO NOT touch `correction-ledger.md` — fenced out by rf2-s52w and by this bead.
- `docs/design/hicasso/product/checkpoint-3-native.md` is a dated checkpoint record. Whether it
  gets an in-place amendment is the ledger keeper's convention; the two lane pages above are
  the live surface and are enough to discharge the clause.
- Re-check holders before editing: rf2-hic-090 (`recertdup`) holds a `docs/design/hicasso/`
  recertification results page, and PR #8634 holds `docs/design/hicasso/studio/**`. Neither is
  a lane page, but the fence is a dispatch-time claim and can go stale.
- Gate: `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` covers `docs/`. `mkdocs build --strict` does NOT cover
  `docs/design/**` (`exclude_docs` in `mkdocs.yml`) — do not nominate it. Verify anchors and
  table column counts by hand and say so in the PR body.
acceptance_criteria: react-compatibility-notes.md:34's blanket sentence and hot-path-architecture.md:49's row-5 Required result both scope 'mismatch attribution' / 'deliberate mismatch with source attribution' to roots a re-frame2 door opens, citing spec/011-SSR.md:825. Anchors and table column counts checked by hand and stated in the PR body. correction-ledger.md untouched.
close_reason:
Discharged by PR #8646 (branch worker/row5scope-0brem), rf2-s52w's last acceptance-option-B clause.

BOTH homes amended, and the scope turns on WHO OPENED THE ROOT rather than on bridging.

- lanes/hot-path-architecture.md:49 (row 5 *Server and hydration*, Required result) now adds: 'Mismatch attribution is owed only on roots a re-frame2 door opens - h/hydrate!, or the Spec 006 client mount entry - because onRecoverableError is an option of an individual root, so a root the consumer opened and adopted themselves carries no framework reporter and nothing rendered inside it is attributed', citing spec/011-SSR.md's Hydration-mismatch detection section (:811, the scoping sentence at :825).
- lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md:35 (the blanket sentence, NOT :34 as the bead said - see correction below) now scopes the mismatch state the same way, states that the boundary is 'which renderer opened the root, not whether a subtree is bridged', and says explicitly that *Root/frame provider and outward bridge* (:24) omits mismatch attribution from its own hydration column for that reason - a scope, not a carve-out. So the asymmetry the audit found is repaired from both ends.

WHY NOT 'the outward bridge is exempt': that wording would be false in BOTH directions. A Hicasso subtree bridged into a root one of the two re-frame2 doors opened IS inside the channel (onRecoverableError fires anywhere in that root's tree), and a Hicasso root the consumer hand-adopts with react-dom/client is OUTSIDE it. title: hicasso: fail-closed gaps in alloc_pass_position.cjs's boundary and session reporting
description:
FOUND by rf2-fk6pj's phase-4 window (PR #8634) and deliberately NOT repaired
there, because an estimator must not change between a pre-registration and the
runs it will be read on. Neither affects any figure that window published;
both are recorded on its page under "Two defects found and deliberately NOT
repaired".

1. THE BOUNDARY CHECKS THE DRAWN SCHEDULE'S BALANCE, NOT THE REALISED ONE.
   admissibleRun verifies q*parity = 0 and q*linear = 0 on passSchedule.flips,
   and separately that the drive covers every scheduled round. It does NOT
   check the balance of the block set that actually CARRIED DATA. A round whose
   four windows all failed to certify yields no block, so the realised
   labelling can be short and unbalanced while the drawn one is neither -- and
   the design's identification is a property of the realised labelling, not of
   the draw. It did not bite in phase 4 (96 blocks of a possible 96, realised
   q*parity 0 in all eight runs, verified by hand and stated on the page), but

title: docs(hicasso): production-server-arm's capability table says 'shipped' about two deleted trees, and async-routing-recipes cites a fixture that matches nothing
description:
MEASURED AT origin/main 2de41e2252, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. Surfaced by the worker that landed PR #8622 (rf2-wbdr7), which correctly declined to action either — both sit outside that bead's live-command scope.

THIS IS NOT THE REPOINTING CLASS, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT. rf2-wbdr7 repointed instructions a reader is meant to RUN, where a live equivalent existed. Neither of these has a live equivalent, and neither is an instruction. They are ASSERTIONS OF FACT that are now false, which is why a path rewrite cannot fix them.

FINDING 1 — A TABLE SAYS "SHIPPED" ABOUT DELETED TREES.

docs/design/hicasso/production-server-arm.md, the capability table:

  line 162 | A live two-sided emitter parity apparatus
           | implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/parity_fixtures.cljc (643 lines, 66 cases)
             + parity_corpus_cljs_test.cljs + parity_html.cljc
           | STATE: "shipped and running"

  line 163 | An interpreted structural walk that runs on the JVM
           | implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/tree.cljc (678)
             + node.cljc (1,438) + conversion.cljc (906)
           | STATE: "shipped, cross-host"

Two more references to the same trees at :389 and :424, the second repeating the 643-line figure.

MEASURED: implementation/ui returns 0 tracked files and implementation/freehand returns 0. Positive control on the same command shape: implementation/hicasso returns 628. Both trees were deleted by PR #8322 on 2026-08-16.

So the table asserts, in its own State column, that a capability is SHIPPED AND RUNNING when the 643-line file it names does not exist. A reader assessing what Hicasso has today is misled in the most direct way a design record can mislead.

FINDING 2 — A LAW IS SAID TO "LIVE" AT A PATH THAT MATCHES NOTHING.

docs/design/hicasso/product/async-routing-recipes.md:132 says the R-C1 law "lives in two places, neither of them a witness that could be elevated", and names spec/conformance/freehand/fixtures/fh-ctrl-013.edn.

MEASURED: `git ls-files | grep fh-ctrl-013` returns 0. Positive control: spec/conformance/** returns 246 tracked files, so the tree is real and the pattern is live.

WHAT IS WANTED, AND WHY IT NEEDS JUDGEMENT RATHER THAN A SWEEP.

There is nothing to repoint to. Each row needs a decision about what it now asserts, and the two findings may not take the same answer:
  (a) the capability MOVED into implementation/hicasso, in which case name where and re-state the figures against the surviving artefact - do NOT carry the old line counts across, they described deleted files;
  (b) the capability WENT with the tree, in which case the State column must say so, and the row becomes a record of what the donor had rather than a claim about what ships;
  (c) it is genuinely unresolved, in which case say that plainly instead of leaving a false "shipped".

ESTABLISH WHICH BY READING THE TREE, not by choosing the tidier answer. A row rewritten to claim something equally unverified is worse than the one it replaced.

DO NOT MECHANICALLY REWRITE PROVENANCE. Where a figure is pinned to a revision at which the file did exist, that is a record and it stays. The discriminator is TENSE AND MOOD: a State column reading "shipped and running" is a present-tense claim about now; a sentence reporting what a donor arm had at a pinned revision is a record.

RELATED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT MERGED INTO THIS BEAD: rf2-wbdr7 covers live reproduce COMMANDS with dead paths and is separately tracked.

title: ci: ladder_band.cjs --selftest runs in no spine, so its band-model guard is dead in CI
description:
