THE GAP. implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/ladder_band.cjs dispatches a real self-test at line 423 (argv[i] === '--selftest', note the UNHYPHENATED spelling) and is referenced by nothing executable: no npm script, no workflow, no .test.cjs. The only references anywhere are two docs/design/hicasso/studio pages, its own usage banner, and a note inside data/ladder-ymi6j.json.

IT IS NOT DECORATIVE. seam.cjs:161-162 treats it as a live guard, in prose: '`ladder_band.cjs --from data/ladder-ymi6j.json` prints both models; its `--selftest` fails if the pooled one is reinstated.' The resampling model that self-test defends is the one behind the ladder band's published q90/q95/q99 figures and the 35% false-fire ceiling. That guard runs nowhere in CI, so a reinstated pooled model would not be caught.

WHY BOTH FLAG SPELLINGS MATTER, and this is the reusable finding. The directory carries TWO self-test flag spellings. '--self-test' (hyphenated) on the alloc_* readers; '--selftest' (unhyphenated) on clock_run.cjs, hd8_run.cjs and ladder_band.cjs. A census run on the hyphenated literal alone returns exactly one unregistered reader and reads as complete. Widening to both spellings is what surfaced this one. Consider whether the two spellings should be unified, which would make the census a single grep rather than a judgement call.

WHAT IS WANTED, and it needs a decision rather than a one-liner. ladder_band.cjs is a data-driven recompute, not a pure fixture reader like the alloc_* siblings. Its '--selftest' path needs checking for whether it can run in CI unattended: does it need a checked-in dataset, how long does it take, is data/ladder-ymi6j.json sufficient? If it runs clean and cheap, register it in test:script-helpers beside the alloc_* readers. If it needs a dataset that is not checked in, say so and close, because the honest answer may be that this guard cannot be a CI gate.

VERIFY BEFORE ACTING. Re-derive at origin/main rather than trusting this description. The full census that produced it is tabulated in PR #8608's body, including the six readers that ARE reached (four invoked directly; alloc_level_witness.cjs, clock_check_standard.cjs, clock_run.cjs and hd8_run.cjs all reached indirectly via a registered .test.cjs that requires them) and the exclusion of seam.cjs, which mentions '--selftest' in prose but has no argv handling at all.

title: method: the generic gate-nomination rule covers an exclusion but not an exclusion's own carve-out
description:
RAISED BY worker/fenceclause 2026-08-21 while landing PR #8600, the repo-specific half of this same defect. It deliberately left the generic tree untouched and referred the question up, which was correct.

THE GAP. docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md carries a bullet at roughly line 620: 'Never nominate a gate that does not cover the surface being edited... Read the exclusion config before naming the gate.' That covers ONE direction — a gate covering LESS than it appears, where nominating it returns a green that inspected nothing.

THE INVERSE IS NOT COVERED, and it is what just bit this project in eight consecutive dispatch briefs. An exclusion can have its OWN CARVE-OUT: a gate that normally skips a construct but reports it in named trees. Stating only the blind spot then UNDERSTATES coverage, and 'read the exclusion config' does not tell a reader to read the exclusion's own exceptions.

WHY THE UNDERSTATING DIRECTION IS NOT HARMLESS, which is the part the existing bullet's reasoning does not reach. A worker told a gate does not cover its edit will hand-check, which costs little, and then REPORT that the gate did not cover it — a false statement in a change body, and the same both-directions misreporting the fast-spine-gap rule already warns about. Worse, it can read a green as having inspected nothing, and go hunting a problem the gate already proved absent.

WHAT IS WANTED: ONE ABSTRACT SENTENCE beside the existing bullet. Nothing more — this is a generic rule in a generic document and the stance's second half applies. Something to the effect that an exclusion may itself carry exceptions, so read the exclusion's carve-outs too, and that understating coverage misreports as surely as overstating it.

KEEP THE LAYERS APART, and this is the whole reason the bead exists rather than the worker just doing it. docs/the-mayor-method/** carries NO repository names, script names, constant names, paths, bead ids or PR numbers. The concrete instance lives in .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md, landed by PR #8600. Do not name it here.

FENCE: docs/the-mayor-method/** is a shared surface and two concurrent editors on it conflict by construction. Check for an open PR against that tree before dispatching and sequence if there is one.

title: hic: U4 needs a per-frame driver on the LEDGER witness — the slice has no continuous interaction to measure
description:
SPLIT OUT OF rf2-9wmqd, 2026-08-21, when that bead's donor-arm half landed as PR #8599. Edit-shaped and loud-box-safe: it needs NO window and can be dispatched beside anything.

WHY U4 CANNOT BE SERVED WHERE U1-U3 ARE. budgets.md section 4 registers U4 as 'Dragging/animation stay inside frame budget', estimand PER-FRAME LATENCY, and section 9.4 governs it on a witness application under implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/. Both landed clock drivers sit on the SLICE, and the slice publishes NO DRAG AND NO ANIMATION — every interaction it has is discrete (a keystroke, a click, a select). A per-frame estimator driven by repeating one of those once a frame would publish a scripted repetition of a DISCRETE interaction against a line written about a CONTINUOUS one, which is the same class of error rf2-xa8wo's driver exists to have stopped making (a p95 of a mount against a line about a paint). Adding a drag to the slice is not the repair either: it would move the population, and U1-U4 are governed on the application's own interactions rather than on interactions added to reach a row. PR #8599's driver states all of this in its own docstring rather than leaving it to be discovered.

WHERE IT IS REACHABLE. re-frame.hicasso.examples.ledger publishes a VIRTUALIZED 10,000-ROW LIST over a real scroll viewport — its virtualized_dom_cljs_test.cljs drives scrollTop and dispatches a real scroll event, and vendor.cljs's own note names 'host-local animation/drag state'. A scroll over a windowed list is a genuinely continuous interaction and is the population U4 is stated over.

WHAT IS WANTED. A third driver, on the ledger, on the SAME mechanism the two slice drivers share — slice_echo_clock_app's window! and after-paint, REQUIRED rather than transcribed, the way slice_broad_clock_app requires them — but with an ESTIMATOR OVER FRAME INTERVALS rather than over window lengths. A run of consecutive frames under a sustained scroll, publishing the distribution of intervals between them; a floor arm (the same rAF chain with no application work, which is the box's own frame grid); and a positive control whose prediction is a FLOOR rather than a band (a busy-wait of N ms inside each frame cannot produce an interval shorter than N).

Note that lane/rounds-async! schedules a sample as a promise of ONE NUMBER, and a frame run yields K-1 intervals, so the frame estimator does not fit that loop. Use lane/slot-order for the per-round arm ordering rather than hand-rolling one — visit-plan's docstring records what a second copy of the schedule has cost this lane twice.

THE PROHIBITIONS, carried over and not negotiable. DO NOT WIDEN A BAND OR GUESS A THRESHOLD. DO NOT BUILD A GATE: section 7 routes every distributional row to pinned evidence runs on P-DEV-1 and FORBIDS converting one into a PR threshold, section 9.1 says such a row may never name the first lane, and check_budget_ledger.py enforces it. Building an INSTRUMENT is in scope; building a GATE is not. MOVE NO LEDGER CELL — 49 rows / 31 MET / 5 BREACH / 3 UNRESOLVED / 10 UNPINNED, and U4 keeps UNPINNED whatever this bead builds.

VERIFY BEFORE BUILDING. Re-read the ledger example and its virtualized_dom_cljs_test at the tip and confirm the scroll viewport is still there and still real; re-read PR #8599's driver docstring for the row-set reasoning it already states. If a per-frame driver has landed meanwhile, say so and close.

title: hicasso: the twenty-run window record states its realised rate over a control-refused run
description:
RAISED BY PR #8598 (rf2-6kxub/rf2-csca8/rf2-z2xir), which imposed ONE admissibility rule across both analysis readers, their pages and their fixtures: a failed positive control is not an observation. Two committed datasets carry alloc.controlVerdict.ok=false -- alloc-77gz8/run12-a4a1537cb71 and alloc-9jrhi/bisect-5-a-4a1537cb71-replicate -- and both were previously counted as low-mode readings.

THE RESIDUE, and it is OUTSIDE that PR's fence. docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-second-mode-a-pre-registered-twenty-run-window.md:76 states 'The realised rate was 2 of 20 (10%)', and docs/design/hicasso/studio/README.md:124 restates it in that page's index row ('THE MODE REPRODUCED in 2 of 20 runs at 4a1537cb71 (10%, against the 1-in-7 prior)'). run12 is one of those twenty. On the admissibility rule now applied everywhere else, the realised rate of admissible READINGS is 2 of 19 (10.5%).

WHY IT WAS NOT CHANGED THERE. The page is rf2-77gz8's record, not rf2-6kxub's, and README.md was fenced to another worker in the same wave. More substantively, THE CLAIM MAY BE CORRECT AS WRITTEN and this bead should test that before changing anything: '2 of 20' there is a statement about a PRE-REGISTERED DESIGN -- twenty runs were committed before the first was taken and twenty were taken -- rather than about an admissibility census. A pre-registered count is honoured by running the runs, and a run whose control later failed was still run. The README row's own words support that reading: it says the two HIGH runs both had 'a passing positive control', which is true and is the claim that actually matters there.

SO THE QUESTION IS NARROW. Does the page distinguish (a) the DESIGN's realised count, 2 of 20, from (b) the admissible READING rate, 2 of 19? If it conflates them -- in particular where it compares the realised rate against the '1 in 7' prior, which IS an inference about rates -- the comparison should be restated on 19. title: hicasso: the allocation datasets record nothing about the box, so the mode-rate's mechanism stays unnameable
description:
SPLIT OUT OF rf2-6kxub when its ANALYSIS half was answered in PR #8593, record docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-mode-rate-tracks-elapsed-session-time.md. This is rf2-6kxub's own SECOND MOVE, carried out rather than dropped.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED AND WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH. The floor arm's high-mode RATE tracks elapsed time within a session: 0/6 at 8.2 min, 1/8 at 14.9, 2/20 at 19.7, 37/69 at 88.3, with a within-session gradient inside the long corpus at one-tail p = 0.0198 (Mann-Whitney on position-in-session, boundary-free). That locates the rate on elapsed-time-within-session and NAMES NO MECHANISM: thermal state, V8 tier accumulation and heap fragmentation over a long session all survive it equally. Across the sessions, duration is confounded with date and clock time (11:23, 13:52, 23:54 -- the last running past midnight).

THE CHEAP MOVE, which is this bead. Record what the datasets currently do not, all of which rides free on an existing field the way the work census does:

  - the Chromium build string (pinned by playwright, but NOT recorded in any dataset),
  - the box's load at window open,
  - the elapsed time since the previous run in the same session.

That converts the NEXT window into evidence about the rate at no extra runner cost. generatedAt is already recorded and is what made the analysis half answerable at all; these three are the same kind of free rider.

HERMETIC, AND NEEDS NO WINDOW. It is a change to implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs (4,733 lines, hot, one-toucher) and is shared with rf2-fk6pj, rf2-csca8 and rf2-onozm, each of which wants its own arm in the same file.   - CHROMIUM BUILD STRING, read off the launched browser at the first launch (`chromium/<version>`). Captured in `newPage`, which is the only place a build string exists, and FIRST LAUNCH ONLY -- the clock row takes one page per round and a snapshot per page would record the last round rather than the open.
  - THE BOX'S LOAD, at window open and again at close. os.loadavg() is [0,0,0] on Windows and that is where these windows are taken, so loadavg alone would have recorded NOTHING. The portable reading is the CPU time accumulated across all cores: the open snapshot gives the busy fraction since boot, and the open-to-close difference gives the busy fraction the run actually saw, at no sleep cost. `loadavgSupported` travels beside it so a reader can tell a dead field from an idle box. Also carried: freemem, totalmem, cpu count, box uptime (a box that rebooted between two runs is not the same box under the thermal account).
  - ELAPSED SINCE THE PREVIOUS RUN, as BOTH `sinceStartMs` and `sinceEndMs` -- the second is the idle gap, which is the axis the confirming second move is defined on. Plus `runsInSession` and `sessionStartedAt`, computed against a RECORDED threshold (P0_BOX_SESSION_GAP_MIN, default 60 min) so an analysis can redraw the session boundary from the raw timestamps rather than inherit this one.

TWO DECISIONS WORTH NOT REDISCOVERING. The session marker lives in the OS temp directory, never the repository, and its PATH IS DELIBERATELY NOT RECORDED -- a dataset is committed and a home-directory path has no business travelling into one. And no failure of this rider can refuse a window: a missing, malformed or unwritable marker yields null and is reported. The record is assembled in the finally-adjacent block beside the raw write, so a REFUSED run carries the box provenance too.

THE DELIBERATE COLD/HOT/AFTER-AN-IDLE-GAP VARIATION WAS NOT TAKEN. rf2-6kxub's note holds it as the confirming second move and that stands.

NOTHING MEASURED MOVED. tau untouched, ALLOC_MIN_WRITES 6 / ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B 600000 / ALLOC_LEG_TOLERANCE 0.25 / R=20 byte-identical to origin/main. Every reading is taken outside any measured window.

GATE: node core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs -- captured exit 0, 100 passed (96 on origin/main; four new tests, one of them THE BOX RIDERS). Proved to have read this worktree by a planted fault: boxBusyFraction's numerator off by one reds it at 'a zero interval is not a zero load', and the restore verified against the identical blob hash.

title: mayor-dispatch's fence-derivation rule names two bad sources and misses the third — 'what I briefed them to DO'
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-21 by the method-reread loop grading its own briefs, and it had already produced a wrong fence in TWO live dispatches when it was found.

WHAT HAPPENED. I wrote the file-ownership fence for worker/ladder-onozm and worker/modeconf-6kxub naming PR #8590's holdings as README.md, the-bisect-is-flat-and-the-floor-has-a-second-mode.md, and alloc_heap_trajectory.cjs. Measured with gh pr view 8590 --json files, the real list is README.md, the-bisect-is-flat..., and the-second-mode-is-per-write-and-the-controls-never-move.md. So the fence was wrong in BOTH directions at once: it named a file the PR does not hold, and OMITTED one it does — and the omitted one is the page a peer bead's findings bear on.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS A SOURCE THE RULE DOES NOT NAME. .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md says, correctly: 'DERIVE that enumeration at dispatch time from gh pr list --state open --json number,headRefName,files plus git worktree list, NEVER from your own memory of who you dispatched', and separately 'write each fence entry from the FILE LISTS, never from the branch names'. Two bad sources named. I used a THIRD: my memory of what I had BRIEFED that worker to do.

WHY THAT ONE IS THE MOST SEDUCTIVE OF THE THREE. Memory-of-who is obviously a guess. Branch-names is obviously a guess about files. But memory-of-what-I-briefed FEELS like file-level knowledge — it is a list of paths, I wrote it, and I wrote it deliberately. It is nonetheless a PREDICTION, and a worker that does its job well falsifies it: #8590's worker dropped alloc_heap_trajectory.cjs because it fixed the prose instead of the script, and picked up the-second-mode page because reconciling three places was the audit's actual instruction. A GOOD worker diverges from its brief's file list more than a bad one does.

THE FIX, and keep it to one clause: add the third source to the existing prohibition. Something of the shape 'never from your own memory of who you dispatched, from the branch names, or from what you BRIEFED them to touch — a brief is a prediction, and a worker doing its job well falsifies it.' Cite the measurement above.

DO NOT restructure the surrounding paragraph. It is long, dense, load-bearing and already correct; this adds one clause to a list that already has two members.

SURFACE: .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md ONLY. That is a repository-specific command file, so it may name PR numbers, bead ids, paths and tool names freely — do NOT put any of this in docs/the-mayor-method/**, which is the generic tree and carries none of those.

SHARED SURFACE: .claude/commands/** is single-toucher. Check for an open PR against it before starting.

GATE: scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci carries an arm that resolves path-shaped REFERENCES in .claude/commands/*.md — bare or backticked alike. It validates no anchors or markdown links there (those files carry none), so a path you name must resolve. check_doc_slugs.py does NOT reach .claude/commands/ at all; do not nominate it. Nothing validates the PROSE — read it back by hand and say so.

CLOSING THIS AS MINUTIAE IS NOT THE RIGHT CALL unless the re-derivation shows the clause is already there. It cost a wrong fence in two live briefs the day it was measured, and the stale-NARROW direction — omitting a file a PR holds — is the one that puts two workers on one file.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8592. One clause added to mayor-dispatch.md's first fence-derivation prohibition: '...never from your own memory of who you dispatched, and never from what you BRIEFED them to touch - a brief is a PREDICTION, and a worker doing its job well falsifies it, which is what makes it the most seductive of the three bad sources...', with the 2026-08-21 measurement cited inline (PR #8590's real file list re-verified with gh pr view 8590 --json files before editing: the bench script the fence named was never in it; the second-mode studio page it omitted was). Surrounding paragraph not restructured - word-diff shows exactly one deleted token, 'dispatched**', re-emitted inside the insertion. Nothing added to docs/the-mayor-method/. Gate: scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci, exit 0 on the change, exit 1 on a planted broken reference at the edited line (proving it read this worktree), exit 0 again after a hash-verified restore; check_doc_slugs.py measured green on the identical fault, so it was correctly not nominated.

title: method: the gate block's plant-verification rule misses the CRLF class — an EOL-anchored plant matches nothing, silently, and the green reads as a passing control
description:
FOUND BY the rf2-ue4kv worker (PR #8584, 2026-08-21), which hit it and caught it, and propagated it deliberately: 'a plant silently failed to apply first time — an end-of-line-anchored regex against a CRLF file matched nothing, with no error. Caught only by checking the match count BEFORE running the gate. Had I not, the green sabotage would have read as "the control does not bite".'

WHERE IT BELONGS: docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, section 'Quality gates — how a gate is run', in the four-caution list under 'Verify a restore by hashing the bytes, never by reading a diff.'

WHAT THAT LIST ALREADY SAYS AND WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH. The third caution is 'Anchor a patch to a single line. One worker's multi-line anchor matched nothing, with no error and no edit, and only the hash caught it.' That is the same FAILURE (a plant that no-ops) reached by a different MECHANISM (multi-line anchor) with a different DETECTOR (the hash, after the fact). The CRLF mechanism defeats a single-line anchor too, so the existing caution does not cover it — an EOL-anchored pattern against a CR-terminated line is exactly one line and still matches nothing.

TWO THINGS TO ADD, and the second is the more valuable:

1. The MECHANISM. core.autocrlf is true on this checkout, so every file .gitattributes does not pin carries a CR before each line ending. A pattern anchored at end-of-line — a trailing dollar in a regex, or a tool's own line-anchoring — therefore matches nothing. This is the SAME class the method-reread loop already documents for git grep censuses (rf2-woy7g, commit 89b315d213); the plant path is a second door onto it and the block does not name it.

2. The DETECTOR, which is cheaper and earlier than the hash: CHECK THE MATCH COUNT BEFORE RUNNING THE GATE. The hash catches a no-op plant only after a whole gate run has already been spent, and it catches it as an ambiguous signal the worker then has to interpret. A match count of zero, read before the run, is unambiguous and costs nothing.

DO NOT RESTATE THE CENSUS RULE HERE. The generic method tree carries no repository names, bead ids, PR numbers, paths, tool names or OS mechanics — say it as 'a checkout whose line endings are translated', which is the register the first caution in that same list already uses ('On a checkout whose line endings are translated, use version control's own content hash...'). Match that voice.

SIZE: one caution, a few lines. Do not expand the section. Do not renumber or restructure the list beyond adding to it.

SURFACE: docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md only. SHARED SURFACE — two concurrent editors conflict by construction, so this is a one-toucher.

GATE: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py covers docs/ link targets and heading anchors. Note what it does NOT cover: a broken markdown link inside a FENCED CODE BLOCK is invisible to it EXCEPT in the two trees named by FENCED_DOC_LINK_TREES in that script — and docs/the-mayor-method IS one of them, so a fenced doc link in this file IS reported. mkdocs build --strict does cover docs/the-mayor-method (it is not in mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs).
close_reason:
FIXED — PR #8585. The premise held: searched dispatch-prompt-template.md for `match count`, `carriage`, `line endings`, `anchor` and the only hits were the "a rewrite that flips line endings reads clean" paragraph, the hash caution, and the single-line-anchor caution. Neither the mechanism nor the detector was stated anywhere. The third caution does NOT cover this class, exactly as filed — an EOL-anchored pattern against a CR-terminated line is one line and still matches nothing.

Added as the fifth caution under "Verify a restore by hashing the bytes": the mechanism (a carriage return sits between the text and the line ending, so the anchor never reaches the text) and the detector (read the match count BEFORE running the gate; zero is unambiguous and free, where the hash convicts only after a whole gate run and convicts ambiguously). "Four cautions" -> "Five" because it is a count. Nothing else in the file touched; list not restructured.

Register held: no repo names, tracker ids, PR numbers, paths, tool names or OS mechanics. Opens on the failure rather than repeating the first caution's opening clause verbatim.

GATE python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py, exit codes captured by the worker (never harness-reported): control 0, sabotage 1, restored 0, re-run on the final base after rebase 0. The gate prints no root banner (its green log is empty), so tree-verification was by planted fault: a broken link target in the new bullet, match count read BEFORE the plant (1) and after (1), gate red naming exactly the planted target at :820. Restore verified by the identical blob hash 1ec99efaf6272451b793c5c4f242f7d19618fab4 against the committed object. Fast spine NOT run; check_fast_pr_gap.py --list reports 94 required checks it does not run. mkdocs build --strict not run — CI owns it.

The detector this caution documents was USED here: both of the PR's plants had their match count read before the gate ran.

title: method: the reread loop's duplicate-block check is a false zero — a $-anchored git grep never matches on this CRLF tree
description:
FOUND BY the method-reread loop, 2026-08-20 23:55 AUSEST, step 1 — the duplicate-block check that loop prescribes returned a false zero on its own surface.

THE DEFECT. `.claude/commands/mayor-method-reread.md` tells the mayor to diff the worktree-boundary and gate-mechanics blocks against any second copy rather than trusting that they match. Run as an anchored `git grep`, that check CANNOT FIND EITHER BLOCK, because on this checkout a `$` placed directly after literal text never matches.

MEASURED. `git grep -l "^WORKTREE BOUNDARY — MANDATORY$" -- ':!.beads'` returns EMPTY. The heading exists at docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md:478. Unanchored, `git grep -c "WORKTREE BOUNDARY — MANDATORY"` returns exactly 1 file, which is the correct answer and also the reassuring one — so the false zero and the true answer look identical to a reader who does not already know there is one copy.

MECHANISM, pinned on .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md:
  leading `^` only ......................... 1 hit
  `.*$` ..................................... 1 hit   (`.` matches the CR)
  full literal line + `$` ................... 0 hits  FALSE
  same literal line, no `$` ................. 1 hit
The files carry CRLF terminators, so a `\r` sits between the last literal character and end-of-line.

SPREAD — this is why it is worth a bead rather than a note. `file -b` reports CRLF for ALL of docs/the-mayor-method/{dispatch-prompt-template,loops,bootstrap}.md, ALL of .claude/commands/mayor-{merge,dispatch,posture,hygiene,method-reread}.md, and CLAUDE.md. dispatch-prompt-template.md is 900 of 900 lines CRLF. The whole surface this loop audits is affected, and so is any census the dispatch loop runs over these files.

NO DISPATCH WAS HARMED, and the fix must not disturb what works. The block EXTRACTION uses `sed`, and `sed` on this Git Bash strips the CR on read: `sed -n '/^WORKTREE BOUNDARY — MANDATORY$/,/^```$/p'` still returns its 51 lines and the extracted text is clean LF. Only the VERIFICATION path was blind. DO NOT change the extraction, and do not convert any file's line endings — a mass line-ending rewrite would touch every line of nine governing files for no benefit and is explicitly out of scope.

THE FIX, and it is small. Add to .claude/commands/mayor-method-reread.md, at the block-divergence bullet where it bit: never end a `git grep` pattern with a `$` straight after literal text on this repo — drop the `$` or use `.*$` — and run a positive control before believing any census zero. Repo/OS mechanics belong in the command file, NOT in docs/the-mayor-method/**, which by its own rule carries no OS mechanics or tool names. Consider whether the same caution earns a line in .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md, where the census rules live; add it only if it is load-bearing there, since that file already carries the "a search returning zero is not a check that passed" rule in the pasted gate block.

Durable memory recorded under key `git-grep-dollar-anchor-false-zero-on-crlf`.

GATE: scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci covers .claude/commands/*.md (it resolves path-shaped references there, bare or backticked). scripts/check_doc_slugs.py does NOT reach that path. Nominate by PATH, never by job name.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8561 (2026-08-21 AUSEST) — REOPENED AS THE EXACT METHOD OWNER; no duplicate filed.

The diagnosed CRLF false zero is real, but both prescribed remedies — “drop the `$`” and append `.*$` — are not semantics-preserving for an exact-line census. They turn an exact line into a prefix match, so the fix can exchange a false zero for a false-high count. This PR's own namespace example demonstrates it: on the current CRLF checkout, `git grep -E '^\(ns re-frame\.core'` returns 17 files because it also matches `re-frame.core-artefact`, `re-frame.core-http`, tests, and every other namespace sharing that prefix; the CR-aware exact query `git grep -P '^\(ns re-frame\.core\r?$'` returns the one actual `re-frame.core` namespace. Searching the tree object is cleaner still for the origin/main census this method already requires: the original `$`-anchored exact pattern against `origin/main` returns that one hit because committed blobs are LF.

The positive control prevents a constant zero, but it does not prove that the broadened query counts the intended population. Repair both command-file lines to prescribe an exact, CRLF-safe route — preferably search the explicit `origin/main` tree object when auditing origin/main, or use a tested optional-CR end anchor — and keep the non-zero control as the independent fail-open guard. Preserve the sound diagnosis and the untouched extraction/line-ending fences.
close_reason:
Corrected by PR #8570. The audit's finding is CONFIRMED by measurement, not merely accepted: on this CRLF checkout the namespace census reads 0 files ($-anchored, false zero), 17 files (broadened - the remedy #8561 landed, and the count that file presented as CORRECT), and 1 file by both exact routes - CR-aware -P '\r?$' against the working tree, and the original $-anchored pattern against the origin/main tree object where blobs are LF.

BOTH command files now rank two EXACT routes in place of the broadening one: (1) search the tree object, since both loops already census at origin/main HEAD and the $ anchor works unchanged there - not an extra step but the step already prescribed; (2) only where a working-tree search is genuinely needed, an optional-CR end anchor via -P; (3) never broaden. The 17-file exemplar in mayor-dispatch.md is corrected from 'the answer the fix recovers' to the over-count it is.

The audit's subtler half is addressed: the control is now TWO-DIRECTIONAL. A positive control rules out a dead pattern and nothing else - every broadened form passes it, so a positive control alone would have certified the seventeen. Both files now require reading the HIT LIST rather than its length and confirming prefix-sharing near-misses are absent. Demonstrated: re-frame.core-http is absent from the exact census and present in the broadened one, while both censuses are non-empty.

Diagnosis preserved verbatim - CRLF mechanism, measured spread, fails-OPEN framing, sed extraction fence, MSYS_NO_PATHCONV caution. No line endings converted. Layering respected: docs/the-mayor-method/** untouched.

title: [retire] docs/api/re-frame.core.md carries freehand residue and is GENERATED — needs a regeneration through the api-manifest chain, not a hand-edit
description:
FOUND BY the rf2-0yp7w.9 configuration/root-markdown slice (PR #8552) and correctly REPORTED rather than reached for — the file is generated and the slice's fence said regenerate via its own chain or report.

MEASURED at origin/main 0c5833b9a9, .beads excluded: docs/api/re-frame.core.md carries 1 hit for the retired-substrate pattern. Re-derive before acting; a count is a claim.

WHY IT IS NOT A HAND-EDIT. docs/api/*.md are produced by the api-manifest chain. Hand-editing a generated artefact makes the file disagree with its generator, and the next regeneration silently reverts the fix. This repo has been bitten by committed generated artefacts before: they serial-bottleneck merges, because any change to the generator re-drifts them and a merge race leaves main stale.

WHAT TO DO. Find the generator, run it, and commit what it produces. If the regenerated output STILL carries the residue, that is a finding about the GENERATOR or its input, not about this page — say so and stop rather than editing the output. If the generator cannot be run cleanly in a worker worktree, report that; it is a legitimate refusal.

FENCE: docs/api/** only, plus whatever the generator itself reads if the residue proves to originate upstream. Check for any open PR touching docs/api/ or the manifest chain before dispatching.

Also check whether mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs reaches docs/api/ before nominating mkdocs build --strict — read the block at source, do not trust a prose list.

title: hicasso: a second ~1,050-1,224 B term at the SECOND-driven window, seen only under the fixed segment order
description:

docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-rider-follows-the-position-not-the-substrate.md.
Filed rather than actioned: naming it was outside that bead's scope fence.

THE OBSERVATION. Under P0_ALLOC_SEG_ORDER=fixed, the SECOND-driven arm window of
a round — which under that mode is always uix-subs — carries a cluster of 8 of 38
collection-free windows whose worst leg sits at 1,050-1,224 B over the window's
own leg median. It is present in all three fixed runs separately (fixed-1: 1050,
1062; fixed-2: 1056, 1062, 1068, 1224; fixed-3: 1050, 1224).

IT IS NOT THE +748 B RIDER. It is outside that term's 700-800 B band, at a
different magnitude, and at the position the rider does not occupy — position 1
carries the rider once in those same 38 windows.

THE COMPARISON, which is what makes it worth a bead rather than noise. The
paired parity runs, taken in the same session on the same revision and box, read
1 of 23 in the same 1,000-1,300 B band at uix-subs/position-1 and 0 of 26 at
reagent-subs/position-1. The committed parity corpus is available for a wider
baseline and was not pooled for this.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and n is small so the first move is more data rather than a
mechanism hunt: replicate at higher n under both segment orders and check whether
the cluster tracks the SUBSTRATE (uix), the POSITION, or the segment ORDER mode
itself. Under fixed those three are confounded exactly as position and substrate
were before — position 1 is always uix — so a fixed-order run alone cannot
separate them, and the discriminator is a fixed run with the segment order
REVERSED (uix leading), which p0_run.cjs does not currently offer.

DO NOT DISCHARGE BY WIDENING tau. rf2-e9wr's refusal stands and rf2-rs8q6's fence
against widening is restated.

  parity  reagent-subs pos0   0 / 20

The bead says "the discriminator is a fixed run with the segment order REVERSED (uix leading), which p0_run.cjs does not currently offer".   SUBSTRATE is CONFIRMED as necessary.  Pooling both modes: uix 11/81 vs reagent 0/89. Fisher p = 1.96e-04. Not one reagent window in 89 lands in the band.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #8593 (completeness, correctness, implementation quality): exact open owner updated; no duplicate.

Two corrections are required before this analysis can support its headline verdicts.

1. THE CORPUS INCLUDES CONTROL-REFUSED RUNS. `alloc_cluster_carrier.cjs` filters for `plan=floor`, `falls===0`, and `controlSlot=first`, but never checks `controlVerdict.ok`. It therefore includes `alloc-77gz8/run12-a4a1537cb71` and `alloc-9jrhi/bisect-5-a-4a1537cb71-replicate`, both of which have `controlVerdict.ok=false`. The latter is the exact refused control this same PR correctly excludes on `the-eight-signs-are-one-block.md`. Filtering those two changes the claimed corpus from 118 runs / 3,308 collection-free / 3,140 positional windows to 116 / 3,258 / 3,090, and changes parity denominators (uix pos0 747→733, uix pos1 724→712, reagent pos0 675→666, reagent pos1 913→898). Primary-band numerators remain 8/3/2/0 and the qualitative descriptive pattern survives, but the reader, page, fixtures, and close/update record must use one admissibility rule consistently.

2. THE INFERENTIAL VERDICTS OUTRUN THE DESIGN. Fisher is applied to individual windows as though they were independent trials, although windows are repeated within runs and the `fixed` exposure consists of only three runs in one session. The page itself concedes the controlled same-session mode comparison is 8/38 vs 1/23 with p=0.1344 and the pooled p=2.67e-9 carries session/date/revision as uncontrolled terms. That supports a large pooled association worth the reversed-fixed arm, not the headline `MODE CONFIRMED` / `the MODE carries it`. Likewise 8/747 vs 3/724, p=0.2254 is failure to reject equality, not `POSITION REFUTED`; its window-level odds ratio is about 2.6 and no power/equivalence bound is supplied. Reword these as associated/unresolved unless a run/session-blocked analysis or the planned reversed-fixed matched arm establishes them.

The bead correctly stays open and already owns the discriminating rig arm. Preserve the valid estimator split, ordinal finding, and descriptive counts after admissibility repair; do not create a new statistics or rig bead.

NO cluster-robust or mixed-effects estimate is offered and none should be: with three clusters in one arm a variance component is not identifiable and a cluster-robust SE is badly biased. The right answer to three clusters is more clusters.

WINDOW TAKEN, PR #8611 (worker/revarm-csca8). BEAD STAYS OPEN. Record:

was used exactly as PR #8596 shipped it. TAU UNTOUCHED in either direction.

WHAT WAS TAKEN. Fifteen runs, one session, one revision, one box, interleaved ONE AT A
TIME: five fixed-reversed, five fixed, five parity. Configuration identical to
segorder-rs8q6's six. PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE THE RUNNER RAN ONCE (commits fb93d522cb and
3f85e96ef7 on the branch): run count, interleave, statistic, worst-leg reading, band,
admissibility rule, level read and stopping rule all fixed in advance, Result section
committed deliberately empty. All fifteen taken, none dropped or re-rolled, all fifteen
control-certified. 540 arm windows, 430 collection-free. Every run exited 1 on the falls
gate (4-16 collections) and the leg-tolerance gate (9-24 windows) -- this row's normal
verdict and by construction outside a statistic defined over falls === 0.

THE ARM DRIVES CORRECTLY, pinned as a positive control: every round of every
fixed-reversed run drove uix-subs then reagent-subs; every fixed round drove reagent then
uix; parity alternated.

(1) THE SLOT HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED. With reagent-subs in the second-driven slot the
cluster does not go with it: 1 of 82 windows against the same session's 8 of 63 at
fixed|uix-subs|pos1, p = 0.0105 -- and 1 of 82 against 10 of 63 on the masking-free
companion, p = 0.0011. That is the one arm this window closes.

(2) THE SUBSTRATE HYPOTHESIS IS NOT SETTLED, AND THE REASON IS A DEFECT IN THE
PRE-REGISTERED STATISTIC RATHER THAN A SHORTAGE OF RUNS. The statistic counts a window
only when the in-band leg is that window's WORST. fixed-reversed|uix-subs|pos0 has a
median |worst leg| of 1,488 B -- ABOVE the band top -- with 35 of its 68 windows worse
than 1,224 B. The competing term is already on the record: POSITION 0 IS WHERE THE ~748 B
RIDER LIVES, and the-rider-follows-the-position-not-the-substrate.md established it is
position-locked rather than substrate-locked. So the reversed arm's uix cell reads 1 of 68
on the pre-registered statistic largely because a bigger term wins the maximum.

A MASKING-FREE COMPANION -- windows carrying an in-band leg whether or not it is the worst
-- puts that cell at 7.4% in FOUR OF FIVE RUNS, against fixed's 20.8% and parity's 1.3% at
the same substrate and position. IT IS POST-HOC, written after the window was read, and it
is labelled post-hoc everywhere it appears in the reader and on the page. It carries no
verdict on its own and none is rested on it. Of the windows carrying an in-band leg, the
share where it IS the worst is 80% under fixed and 20% under fixed-reversed -- that is the
masking, as a number.

So the pre-registered branch taken is NEITHER; the companion says the cluster DOES follow
uix at about a third the rate. Both are published; neither is discarded and neither stands
alone.

(3) THE METHODOLOGICAL FINDING, AND IT WAS KNOWABLE IN ADVANCE. The discriminator's DESIGN
and its STATISTIC are in tension. The reversed arm exists to move uix to position 0;
position 0 is where the rider inflates the worst leg; the statistic is a per-window
MAXIMUM. A reversed-arm read was always going to under-count at uix, and the rider record
predates this window by days. RECORDED RATHER THAN REPAIRED: repairing it means
pre-registering a masking-free statistic and taking the window AGAIN, and choosing the
statistic after seeing which one gives the wanted answer is what pre-registration exists
to prevent.

(4) THE MATCHED MODE BASELINE NOW EXISTS, which is what the bead said had no power. This
window is 4 of 5 fixed runs against 0 of 5 parity runs at run level, p = 0.0476. With
segorder-rs8q6's 3 of 3 against 1 of 3 that is 7 of 8 against 1 of 8 across TWO matched
sessions, p = 0.0101 -- the first run-level separation the record has that controls
session, date and revision. BUT MODE NARROWS: fixed-reversed is exactly as non-alternating
as fixed and does not carry the term, so what separates from parity is THE FORWARD FIXED
ORDER SPECIFICALLY -- reagent-subs driven first and uix-subs second, every round -- and not
"a plan that does not alternate". The bead's own "seen only under the fixed segment order"
is now closer to true than the corpus suggested, but only for the forward order.

THE FLOOR READ, PUBLISHED BEFORE ANY COMPARATIVE, because worker/passwin-fk6pj had just
reported an unexplained ~20% floor excursion on this box. THERE IS NONE HERE. Three levels
appear and the THREE HIGH-MODE RUNS ARE ONE PER ARM, so level is not confounded with the
property under test. reversed-1 settled on the IDENTICAL reagent-subs level to
segorder-rs8q6/fixed-1 (21,844 B) and agrees to 6 B on uix-subs, across two sessions, two
dates and two segment-order modes. Null arm: 4,818 control legs, 0 in band.

NO CLUSTER-ROBUST OR MIXED-EFFECTS ESTIMATE IS OFFERED and none should be at five clusters
per arm. Every window-level p is published beside its run-level counterpart.

CORPUS after this window: 131 admissible floor runs / 3,688 collection-free / 3,520
positional, from 116 / 3,258 / 3,090. The two control-refused runs are still named and
still refused. Reader fixtures 54 -> 64, including a scoped set for this window that
pins the CARRIER contrast, the 4-of-5-against-0-of-5 matched run-level contrast, the
one-high-mode-run-per-arm level result and the arm's own positive control.

WHAT NOW KEEPS THIS BEAD OPEN, and it is a narrower question than before:
- The SLOT arm is closed. Do not re-run it.
- The SUBSTRATE arm needs ONE more window, under a MASKING-FREE statistic PRE-REGISTERED
  AS SUCH before the runner is invoked. The rig needs no change -- the arm exists and this

- Do not widen tau. Nothing here asks for it and nothing here moved it.

against PR #8598 -- it still reads POSITION REFUTED / MODE CONFIRMED over 118 runs /
3,140 windows, which that PR corrected to unresolved/associated over 116 / 3,090. The
README is another bead's and was not touched; a suggested replacement row plus this

MERGED-PR AUDIT #8619 (2026-08-21) — REOPENED THIS EXACT OWNER; NO DUPLICATE BEAD.

CORRECTNESS. The page and reader correctly identify CARRIER as the only within-run contrast, but then discard that pairing at the decisive step. The ten paired runs contain 5 uix-only hits, 0 reagent-only hits, 5 neither, and 0 both. `alloc_cluster_carrier.cjs` nevertheless pins `fisherExactTwoSided(5, 5, 0, 10) = 0.0325`, which treats the two arm-level run censuses as independent. The corresponding two-sided exact McNemar/sign result is 2 / 2^5 = 0.0625. Therefore the new pre-registered window does NOT support the page's statements that the primary “survives at run level” or resolves the substrate arm. The window-level p=0.0017 cannot rescue that claim because the page itself correctly says those repeated windows are not independent. Pooling the older five pairs gives 6 discordances and a paired two-sided p=0.03125, but those older records informed selection of `any-leg` and are explicitly POST-HOC under this page's own pre-registration; they cannot turn the new window into confirmatory evidence.

COMPLETENESS. The pre-registration names the within-run contrast but no paired test, sidedness, or inferential decision threshold. The landed result retrofits a two-sided independent Fisher calculation. Add the paired run table and paired exact calculation to the reader/report and pin them; then retract the standalone resolution or take a properly pre-registered continuation. Do not silently switch to a one-sided test after seeing the five discordances.

A SECOND CLAIM NEEDS CORRECTION. The primary compares `uix-subs | pos0` with `reagent-subs | pos1`; POSITION is deliberately changed, not “held constant by construction.” The same run holds mode, session, revision, box, and level. The broader crossover evidence may still distinguish position, but this primary contrast alone cannot be described as holding it fixed.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY. The corpus fixture currently makes the independent-sample p-value an invariant, so the test suite protects the defect. Replace that pin with the actual paired table/test. Also retract “more runs were never going to settle this”: 3/136 versus 0/161 at n=10 does not establish that a persistent nonzero rate could never resolve at larger n; it establishes only that this window did not.

title: hicasso: the restore-hash rule and check_provenance_pins.py collide on docs/design/hicasso/ pages
description:
TWO OF THIS PROJECT'S OWN RULES COLLIDE, and the collision will recur for every worker on a docs/design/hicasso/ page.

RULE ONE (the gate-mechanics brief, pasted into every dispatch): verify a planted-fault restore by HASHING THE BYTES, using version control's own content hash against the committed object — never by reading a diff, because a patch that never applied and a correct restore produce the same diff. Workers are told to record that hash as evidence.

RULE TWO (scripts/check_provenance_pins.py, gated by .github/workflows/docs.yml job 'Provenance pins'): every 40-hex token on a changed page under docs/design/hicasso/ is extracted and classified as a cited authored head unless its nearest left-context word says digest. An unclassifiable token is a FINDING by design — the gate fails toward refusal.

THE COLLISION. A restore-verification hash is a SHA-1 BLOB hash, and it is naturally written in commit-flavoured prose: 'compared against the committed object'. 'committed' is in _COMMIT_WORDS; 'hash' is in _DIGEST_WORDS but sits further left. Nearest wins, so the token is read as a pin, resolves to no commit, and reds the job.

CONCRETE INSTANCE. PR #8536, docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-level-witness-armed-within-one-run.md:292. Gate output: '1 page inspected, 14 cited pins — 13 landed, 0 stranded, 1 unresolvable ... (commit word `commit` nearest on the left)'. `git cat-file -t 3dd95e0c268db8b517c802142b2a37de0acbae67` returns `blob`. Worked around in that PR by naming the token a blob so the nearest-word rule classifies it as a digest — the gate's own designed escape, which WORKS and needs no gate change to be usable.

SO THIS IS NOT URGENT AND MAY BE A DOC FIX RATHER THAN A CODE FIX. The escape exists and is discoverable only by reading a 2,300-line script. Options, in ascending cost: (a) add one line to the gate-mechanics brief telling workers to write 'blob' beside a restore hash, which costs nothing and fixes it at the source; (b) note the same in scripts/git-hooks/README.md or beside the gate; (c) teach the gate a restore-verification idiom. (a) is probably the whole fix.

DO NOT bundle this with a hicasso measurement bead — scripts/ and the dispatch briefs are separate surfaces.
close_reason: PR #8547: option (a) taken — one caution added to the restore-hashing block in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md telling workers to call a restore hash a blob hash in the words immediately before the token. Premise verified at source: _DIGEST_WORDS matches blob|digest|sha-?256|fnv|checksum|hash, _COMMIT_WORDS matches committed, classify() takes the nearest left signal with ties going to PIN, and the three phrasings were driven directly against classify() — the commit-flavoured one returns is_pin=True with reason 'commit word commit nearest on the left', the blob-named ones return is_pin=False. scripts/check_provenance_pins.py untouched; _DIGEST_WORDS not widened.

title: dehistoricalise implementation/hicasso: comments and docstrings state the present contract, not the journey
description:
Ruled by Mike (19 August 2026, chat). Rewrite comments and docstrings across implementation/hicasso so they state the PRESENT contract rather than the story of how it got here. Git history and the tracker own the archaeology; the source should read as if the current design had always been the design.

TARGET REGISTER, by example:
  BEFORE: ;; rf2-hic-009 carved the copied 2,120-line runtime into six owned
  ;;       modules after audit #7743 reopened the false green (2026-08-10)...
  AFTER:  ;; Six owned modules; each call site names the module that answers
  ;;       for the var it uses.
Rules:
- present tense, contract first: what is true, what it guards, what breaks if violated. Keep any constraint the code cannot show.
- delete pure narrative: dates, PR numbers, audit blow-by-blow, 'used to', 'before/after', superseded designs, reopened-over stories.
- remove ALL bead references. A citation of a closed bead is history: delete it (git blame recovers it from the commit message). Keep an id only where the comment documents a live obligation and the bead is still open or deferred — verify with bd show before keeping it, and delete the citation if the bead has closed.
- shrink, never pad: if a comment block is pure history, delete it whole.
- docstrings: same rules; they are consumer-facing, so plain contract statements only.

HARD FENCES — check before editing each file:
1. Do NOT touch src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/slot.cljc — the freeze gate (hicasso/frozen-sources.edn + hicasso/scripts/check_freeze.py) pins it byte-for-byte; any comment edit reds CI. Do NOT touch frozen-sources.edn — its retirement is a separate ruled change; if that retirement lands first, slot.cljc unfreezes and joins this sweep as a follow-up slice.
2. Do NOT touch implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/** — measured evidence; its history IS the content.
3. Machine-read text is law: rf2:builder-bypass-ok marker comments (checker input, not citations), every refusal/complaint string (the complaint-catalogue gate round-trips them), diagnostic ids, and anything a checker parses. Byte-identical.
4. Pinned prose: some tests assert regexes against the SOURCE TEXT of other files (example: clock_exit_path.test.cjs pins comment sentences in clock_readjudicate.cjs). Before rewriting any distinctive sentence, grep the repo for a fragment of it; if a test or checker references it, leave it and list it in the PR body instead.
5. Comments and docstrings ONLY. Zero code changes, zero string changes, zero whitespace churn inside code. The diff must show no behaviour surface at all.

PROCESS:
- worker worktree off origin/main; run sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh before editing and report WORKTREE_ROOT. Check open PRs touching implementation/hicasso first and avoid files a live worker holds.
- slice: src/ in one PR; test/ (minus bench) in a second if the first grows past review size. Small reviewable PRs beat one mega-diff. The mayor may split this bead at dispatch.
- gates before each PR, foreground to completion: npm run test:hicasso-invariants, npm run test:hicasso-lint, and the focused hicasso CLJS suites (or npx shadow-cljs compile :node-test).
- PR body declares: comments and docstrings only, no behaviour change; lists any sentence left because pinned; names files where whole history blocks were deleted.

ACCEPTANCE:
- no dates, PR numbers, audit narratives or closed-bead citations remain in implementation/hicasso comments/docstrings outside the fenced files and pinned sentences
- every kept bead id resolves to an open or deferred bead
- slot.cljc, frozen-sources.edn and bench/** byte-identical
- all listed gates green; diff is comment/docstring-only
acceptance_criteria:
1. The non-bench `implementation/hicasso/test/**` comments and docstrings state the present contract under the same rules as #8535; machine-read markers, test descriptions/assertions, refusal text, evidence records, and other runtime strings are classified and preserved unless separately authorised.
2. `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/**`, `impl/slot.cljc`, and measured/frozen sources remain outside the sweep.
3. The `impl/inventory.cljs` `retained-inventory :what` Bead references receive an explicit contract-surface ruling: either a separately verified runtime-string rewrite or a documented retained exception.

informative rung remains unassessed on three quarters of the arms.

WHAT THE REFUSALS LOOK LIKE, first-hand from the 2026-08-18 datasets
(implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-0gjqi/). They are
dominated by a SINGLE leg -- usually leg 5 or leg 6 of 6 -- reading approximately
-800,000 B against a cohort median near 170,000 B. That is a collection of about
800 KB landing inside the window, which the leg witness catches correctly: a leg
below its cohort is a leg something removed bytes from, and nothing in the work
unit removes bytes.

DO NOT WIDEN A GATE TO ADMIT IT. The refusal is correct. An R20 window at B = 4
allocates a rise large enough that a collection inside it is close to certain, and
a tolerance wide enough to admit a -800 KB leg would admit every masked window the
leg witness exists to refuse. rf2-2rtt6.140 retired the previous bound for exactly
that reason.

CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS, none preferred and none authorised here: fewer measured
writes per window at the top rung so the window's cumulative rise stays under the
first collection; a rung ladder that stops below 20; or accepting that R = 20 is
not measurable on this instrument and saying so in the validity witness rather
than carrying an unassessed rung. Each is a rig change and belongs in its own
window.

WHY uix-subs | uix SURVIVES AND THE OTHER THREE DO NOT is not established. It is
the cheapest of the four per boundary, which is consistent with the
window-size account above and is not evidence for it.

title: MEASURE: split the AUTHOR'S share of the :& price — the z143r ladder resolves it only as a sum
description:
RAISED by rf2-z143r's window (2026-08-16, worktree w-z143r), which apportioned the ':&' spelling and could go two-thirds of the way.

WHAT LANDED. The ladder :expanded -> :helper -> :no-dissoc -> :merged prices the CODEC'S 'merge-caller' cleanly (rung 2: no-dissoc/helper, positive in 5 rounds of 5, per-round ratio [1.1333-1.2500]) and the AUTHOR'S share only as a SUM (rungs 1+3 combined: [-250 -500 -625 375 125] ns/field, straddling zero).

WHY THE SUM AND NOT THE PARTS. One helper cannot omit a key for three fields out of four without an 'assoc', so 'field-explicit' writes ':class' unconditionally and BOTH new arms carry ':class nil' on the three classless fields. That is what keeps the two arms key-for-key identical and rung (2) clean, and it makes the key a passenger ADDED to rung (1) and SUBTRACTED from rung (3) in equal measure. It is not small: with the nil class the merged attribute map holds NINE entries on all four fields, without it EIGHT on three of them, and PersistentArrayMap promotes to a PersistentHashMap at exactly the ninth — so on 300 of 400 fields the arms are one map REPRESENTATION apart. Rung (3) came back NEGATIVE for that reason (:merged mounts faster than :no-dissoc), which is not a dissoc paying for itself.

THE REPAIR IS AN ARM, and it is a rig change, so it was not made inside z143r's own window. RULING: BRING EP-0030 THROUGH EP-0033 TO THE EP-0034/0035/0036 BANNER SHAPE. Both events, in the order they happened, in each banner.

And the whole point of a historical record is that a reader who lands on it cold is not misled: 'withdrawn' without 'removed' invites someone to go looking for code that is not there, which is the artefact-a-consumer-copies defect in its mildest form. Six records of one programme should not disagree about what happened to that programme.

THIS IS A BANNER EDIT AND NOTHING ELSE. Do not touch the EPs' bodies. docs/EP/** is archival prose that REMAINS, per this bead's own 2026-08-15 ruling — the banner is the one part of an archival record that is supposed to describe the present, which is exactly why it is in scope while the body is not. title: hic: admit zero-arity rf/capture-frame and rf/current-frame-id inside a Hicasso body (the row-18 seam)
description:
**Filed by rf2-hic-066.** Naming-ledger row 18 RETIRES `hframe` by operator ruling (Mike, 2026-08-11), in favour of core `rf/current-frame-id` plus zero-arity `rf/capture-frame` admitted during a Hicasso body. rf2-hic-066 STOPPED on the row rather than sweeping it, because the alternative the retirement is *in favour of* does not work today.

## The seam

Zero-arity `rf/capture-frame` inside a Hicasso body REFUSES — `:operation :capture-frame`, `:substrate :hicasso`, extent `hicasso/boundary-render` (rf2-lvelh). Re-derived at source by rf2-hic-066 on 2026-08-15 and unchanged.

So the ambient-refusal seam must first admit exactly `:current-frame-id` and `:capture-frame` in-body, resolving to the body's `:extent-frame`, while ambient `rf/subscribe` and `rf/dispatch` stay refused. That is behaviour, not a spelling, which is why it is not rf2-hic-066's.

## What is waiting on it

- 152 `hframe` occurrences across 39 files (measured with rg 14.1.1, repo-wide) stay put until this lands. That is the header rule working as intended, not drift.
- `check_guide_samples.py`'s `("re-frame.hicasso", "frame") -> "hframe"` DIVERGENCES row, and its matching Status-block bullet on `docs/core/hicasso/index.md`. R3 will red the row the day the door changes, which is the designed forcing function — do not pre-emptively delete either half.
- Facade inventory row HS-43 carries `h/hframe`. Per the packet, an inventory row records what is ON the door and does not endorse membership, so HS-43 is not an argument against the retirement.

## Order

This bead lands the seam. The `hframe` retirement sweep is then a diff-sized second pass over row 18 — small, and mechanical once the seam exists.

WHAT WAS RUN. One feasibility invocation, DECLARED UNQUOTABLE BEFORE IT WAS TAKEN, then three evidence invocations, three admissible, none excluded. The pre-registration -- invocation count, admissibility rule and adjudication rule -- was committed before the runner was invoked once, so the count and the rule are commitments rather than descriptions. All five of the driver's exit-bearing checks affirmative on every run and read out of each run's OWN OUTPUT: the arm-order self-test's 12 cases, the echo's negative control, 0 unverified of 400 windows, the positive control inside its band EVERY round, and a reportable arm-order verdict. NO INSTRUMENT EDIT, AND THAT IS A DERIVATION RATHER THAN A DEFAULT. The driver's sampling docstring invites the reading run to raise {:warmup 8 :samples 12}, because a tail quantile over a short sample is mostly interpolation. It was NOT raised. At n=60 pooled a p99 sits between the top two order statistics -- but no quantile estimator can answer above the SAMPLE MAXIMUM, summarise publishes :max, and the maximum meets the line by a factor of 2.65, so the estimator is not load-bearing and lengthening the schedule would have bought a tail the verdict does not use. The driver's blob is byte-identical to the one rf2-xa8wo landed and the studio page pins it.

U2 = MET, DECIDED BY A READING RATHER THAN BY AN ESTIMATOR. Line: <= 50 ms p95 and <= 100 ms p99 to next paint. The worst single window of the 360 measured across BOTH event paths and all three runs is 18.9 ms. Keystroke p95 18.00/18.02/18.21 ms, toggle p95 18.01/18.00/17.80 ms; run-to-run spread 1.1% and 1.2%. Both halves met on readings that were TAKEN. The phase alignment cuts in the meeting direction, so the verdict is conservative twice over.

THE POPULATION CELL MOVED, ON THE ONE ROUTE THE GATE ITSELF NAMES. check_budget_ledger.py's POPULATION_PIN pinned U1-U4 to "-" and its own comment names the only way out: "a new measurement window and an edit here -- which is the whole point". This is that window and the edit is beside it. Subject = the slice witness application mounted through re-frame.hicasso's own h/mount!, which is `package` on the same rule that puts D17-D25 there. The gate's "-"-population self-test control moved from U2 to U3 in the same commit, because it needs a row nothing has measured and U2 had stopped being one. REVERSING ALL OF THIS IS A ONE-LINE EDIT IN EACH OF TWO FILES.

U1 = NOT DECIDED, AND THE BLOCKER IS ITS UNIT RATHER THAN ITS SIZE. FOR MIKE, ONE SENTENCE SETTLES IT. U1 is registered "within one 60 Hz frame" -- a line in FRAMES -- and this instrument aligns every window to the first task after a paint, the phase with the LONGEST wait to the next rendering opportunity, so a whole rendering interval is inside every reading by construction. Two readings were pre-registered and neither privileged:
  (i)  LITERAL, p95 of the keystroke window against 16.7 ms: 18.00 / 18.02 / 18.21 ms -- MISSES, by 1.30-1.51 ms.
  (ii) FLOOR-RELATIVE, that same p95 less the no-work floor's p50: 2.45 / 2.47 / 2.81 ms -- MEETS, with ~14 ms spare.
They disagree in all three runs, so by the rule declared before the first invocation the row is not decided and neither figure is written into the ledger.

AND THE LITERAL READING CANNOT DECIDE IT EITHER, WHICH IS THE STRONGER HALF. The miss of 1.30-1.51 ms is under a TENTH of the measured rendering interval (floor p50 15.4-15.6 ms), squarely inside the region the driver names as the one where the difference between the worst phase and the mean phase decides the row -- and for which it records that the randomised-phase driver IS NOT BUILT. THE TRIGGER ITS DOCSTRING SETS HAS FIRED. So U1 has exactly two ways forward and a worker may take neither: (1) Mike rules which reading the line means -- "within one 60 Hz frame" is unambiguous about the quantity and silent about whether the grid the interaction waits on is charged to the application; or (2) somebody builds the randomised-phase driver, which reproduces the user's phase distribution at the cost of far more samples to resolve a tail. RECOMMENDATION: rule it. The second option costs a driver and a window to answer a question one sentence answers.

REPORTED AND DELIBERATELY NOT A VERDICT. (a) 0 unverified of 400 in every run witnesses U1's STRUCTURAL clause -- controlled updates correct same-turn -- on every window rather than at p95; sec 9.2 already refuses that substitution for rf2-hic-045's census and it is refused again here. (b) The application's own contribution, the :commit leg and the whole of what a flushSync window would have seen, reads p50 0.6 ms and NEVER EXCEEDED 1.1 ms across 180 measured keystroke windows -- the rest of each ~17 ms window is the browser's frame grid. Under any operationalisation charging the application only for its own work, U1 clears its line by more than an order of magnitude. That is context for the ruling, not a substitute for it.

THE POSITIVE CONTROL READ ~34.3 ms AGAINST A 50 ms PREDICTION AND THAT IS THE INSTRUMENT BEHAVING AS DESIGNED. Both arms start at the same phase, so each round's figure is a difference of two paint-bounded windows; the injected block SUBSUMES the wait the unblocked arm pays rather than adding to it. Residual 50 - 34.3 = 15.7 ms = one measured rendering interval. Exactly what control-slack derives from the grid, which is why its band is +/-50% and why the studio page reports the number rather than the word ok.

THE BOX. Bracketed at both ends, standalone, never sampled inside a run: processor queue length 0 on 7 of 8 samples at each bracket, 0 java, 0 processes whose command line names shadow-cljs/clojure/a bench runner/Playwright, 0 headless_shell, 14.5-14.6 GB free. THE QUESTION: what does U1's line MEAN?

Its line is stated in FRAMES, and the instrument spends one frame by construction. So the two pre-registered readings of the same line disagree, and they disagree the same way in all three runs:

NEITHER READING IS WRONG. The gap between them is exactly the one frame the instrument spends by construction, so the disagreement is definitional rather than empirical -- more measurement does not resolve it.

  (b) SOMEBODY BUILDS a randomised-phase driver -- a third driver, real work, and it decides

DEFERRAL LIFTED — MIKE 2026-08-14: 'I want hicasso fully implemented, nothing deferred. I want a complete library. I want a sophisticated library.'

This bead was parked under the earlier direction to run measurement later. That direction is superseded. It is now live work.

ONE PHYSICAL CONSTRAINT REMAINS AND IS NOT A DEFERRAL. A clock estimand needs a quiet box: one measurement at a time, controls arbitrating, no other worker compiling. That is a property of the instrument, not a scheduling preference — a reading taken against six concurrent compiles measures the fleet, not the library. COUNTER estimands have no such constraint; monotone counters read the same on a loaded box, which is why the deterministic censuses landed while the clock tables did not.

SO THE PLAN IS: build every instrument NOW, in parallel, on a loaded box — that work is edit-shaped and unconstrained. Then run the windows themselves back to back when the fleet is idle. That is the same split that produced rf2-w01c from rf2-hic-036 and rf2-d6ai8 from rf2-hic-088, and it means the quiet-box time is spent measuring rather than writing drivers.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWES, restated: if it needs an instrument that does not exist, that half dispatches immediately. If the instrument exists and only the window is missing, it queues for the next quiet period. Whoever picks it up should say which case it is in the first paragraph of its report.

title: hic: outward-bridge hydration mismatch attribution is unreachable by construction (no Spec 011 reporter)
description:
## The finding

CHECKPOINT 3 (rf2-hic-038), main@f455316fbf, 2026-08-14. ROW 5 (Server and
hydration), §2 Correctness.

Row 5 requires every native surface to satisfy its row "including server bytes or
source refusal, matching hydration, MISMATCH ATTRIBUTION and multiple roots".

The native tier's own SSR rows are the best-evidenced part of the row: HS-24 to
HS-30 are witnessed through real react-dom/server bytes on BOTH policy arms by
native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs, and that file records the defect it was written
against — a Client-only island appearing in the server bytes because the recorded
:server policy was consulted by nothing (rf2-u9lk, rf2-ggnp) — as found and fixed.
Checkpoint 3 searched specifically for a semantic-tree claim standing in for
server bytes and found none anywhere.

MISMATCH ATTRIBUTION for the OUTWARD BRIDGE is a different matter, and it is not a
missing test — it is unsatisfiable without a door. HS-21's bytes half is proved
(native_abi_cljs_test.cljs:124, renderToStaticMarkup). But an outward-bridged root
is built by the CONSUMER'S own createElement, so impl.mount/hydrate-root! cannot
adopt it, and a hand-rolled hydrateRoot installs no Spec 011 reporter. There is
therefore no path by which a mismatch inside a bridged subtree is attributed to
source.

Root cause, shared with two other open gaps: THERE IS NO HICASSO SERVER ENTRY.
Every server witness in the package calls react-dom/server's renderToString by
hand — native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs says so in terms ("There is no Hicasso server
entry... the only server path in the package"). Row 5 is therefore proved against
a hand-rolled harness rather than a shipped door.

## Not this bead's, and named so they are not duplicated

- HS-11/HS-14 (root/frame provider Client-only under a measured, unrepaired
  obstruction: the package's only server path emits no counterpart to the adoption
  closer, so a tree minting a useId hydrates into an id mismatch).
- HS-33 (motion/presence measured to satisfy NEITHER policy, repair decided and
  unlanded).
Both are outside the native tier and already carried. Checkpoint 3 files nothing
against them.

## Surface fence

- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/mount.cljs and/or impl/roots.cljs
  (only if a door is the chosen route)
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_abi_cljs_test.cljs
- docs/design/hicasso/product/dispositions.md HS-21 row

DO NOT touch correction-ledger.md.

## Acceptance

EITHER a hydration path for an outward-bridged root that installs the Spec 011
reporter, with a deliberate-mismatch row attributing to source; OR a source-located
statement on HS-21 that mismatch attribution is out of reach for a consumer-built
root, with row 5's required-result sentence amended to scope "mismatch attribution"
to roots the package itself adopts. The second is a defensible line — the consumer
owns that root — but it must be written down rather than left as an unmet clause.
notes:

A slot is free now. I read the bead instead of taking it, and it splits into two halves that do not belong to the same person.

THE FENCE QUESTION IS SETTLED AND THE ANSWER IS PARALLEL-SAFE. That note asked whether spec/011 collides with spec/009 in the hot zone. Measured at CLAUDE.md:91 today: the hot-zone list is an ENUMERATION of eight named spec pages — 002-Frames, 005-StateMachines, 006-ReactiveSubstrate, 009-Instrumentation, API, Conventions, Spec-Schemas, Tool-Pair. spec/011-SSR.md is NOT among them, so this bead never needed to queue behind a spec/009 toucher. That fence was over-broad, not wrong, and it is now retired.

WHY IT STILL DOES NOT GO OUT. The bead's own surface fence says "implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/mount.cljs and/or impl/roots.cljs (ONLY IF A DOOR IS THE CHOSEN ROUTE)". Whether to ship a door is the question, not the work. The bead's stated root cause is THERE IS NO HICASSO SERVER ENTRY — every server witness in the package calls react-dom/server's renderToString by hand, and native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs says so in terms. Adding a shipped server entry is a PUBLIC-SURFACE product decision for Mike, not a bounded fix, and dispatching a worker at an undecided design is how a migration gets performed on a false premise.

So the record is truthful today; what is missing is the capability, not the description of it.

FOR MIKE — THE DECISION AND ITS COST. Does Hicasso ship a server entry? P1 "no Spec 011 reporter" — FALSE AS WRITTEN. Spec 011 defines the reporter for exactly this

React-element roots), :846-856 (the trace shape). Hicasso implements it —

hydrate-root-options, installed at :546 inside hydrate-root!. What the BODY of this bead says

:891 consumer-element (deliberately not reaching impl.mount/tree), :920 the deftest, :952 the

stay green on a broken mechanism. The zero is additionally bounded below by three live readings
in its own arm (the server bytes really said "#7 server"; React really recovered to

listener is not shared — watch-mismatches! (roots_frames_support.cljs:424) mints a gensym key
per call, so the second watch is a fresh registration, which was the specific way this row
could have been vacuous. It is the good version of the pattern, not the bad one.

P3 "unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION" — OVERSTATED, AND THE OVERSTATEMENT IS WHAT KEEPS GENERATING
THE FINDING. The boundary is not the outward bridge; it is which renderer opened the root, and
the bridge is not special in it. TWO re-frame2 doors install a root-scoped Spec 011 reporter on
a React-element root: h/hydrate! (impl/mount.cljs:546) and the Spec 006 client mount entry
(re-frame.substrate.adapter/render tree mount {:hydrate? true}) at spine.cljs:1107, whose
docstring at :1191-1204 names itself the only native mount route that installs it and repeats
Spec 011's boundary sentence verbatim. onRecoverableError fires for recoverable errors ANYWHERE
in that root's tree, so a consumer whose app is mounted through the Spec 006 door with a
Hicasso view bridged in under mount/provider would get :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch for a text
divergence inside the bridged subtree — tagged :where re-frame.substrate.spine/make-render
rather than Hicasso's site, but emitted. REASONED FROM REACT'S ROOT-OPTION CONTRACT PLUS THE
TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS; NOT MEASURED FOR THE BRIDGED CASE, and not claimed as measured — no suite
renders Hicasso under a UIx parent at all (rf2-ap7w's subject). The accurate wording is the one
spec/011-SSR.md:825 already uses: attribution is scoped to roots a re-frame2 door opens.

P4 "root cause: THERE IS NO HICASSO SERVER ENTRY" — FALSE AT TIP, AND IRRELEVANT EVEN WHERE IT
WAS TRUE. implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs (452 lines,
re-frame.hicasso.server/render) landed in commit 30317bfe0e on 2026-08-14 21:28 +1000
(rf2-b6jkj, PR #8236) — about seven hours after this bead was filed and a week before the
2026-08-21 note that repeats the claim. It is a real door: impl/roots.cljs:50-58 names it one
of the TWO minters of the adoption window, "once per REQUEST, closed in that door's finally",
the fork decided once for both sides of the wire. The rest of the tree already describes it as
shipped (naming-ledger.md rows 22 and 50, invariants.md:85, globals.md:192,
architecture-census.md:168, dispositions.md:336, docs/core/hicasso/18-ssr-and-hydration.md,
api-reference.md:376). AND THE PREMISE IS IRRELEVANT: a server entry produces BYTES; the
reporter is a CLIENT root option. No server door of any design can install an option on a root
the consumer opens on the client. The two facts were never causally linked. The stale sentence
that produced the claim is native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:66 — filed as rf2-981ka.

ACCEPTANCE STATUS — option B is 2/3 discharged. (a) source-located statement plus measured
witness: DONE, PR #8302 / 473ff5e330. (b) dispositions.md:290 HS-21 row amended: DONE
2026-08-20 by rf2-vwo53 / PR #8559. (c) row 5's required-result sentence scoped: OWING, and no
bead owned it — now rf2-0brem. Its two homes are hot-path-architecture.md:49 (the native tier's
only release checklist) and, the one that actually creates the obligation,
react-compatibility-notes.md:34's blanket sentence "Every Render row runs the common hydration
states: matching content, deliberate mismatch with source attribution, ...". The matrix ROW for
Root/frame provider and outward bridge (:24) omits mismatch attribution, so that omission is
not a carve-out — the blanket sentence puts it back on every Render row.

THE OPERATOR QUESTION, RE-PUT. The 2026-08-21 note asks "Does Hicasso ship a server entry?" —
it does, since 2026-08-14, and it would not have helped. The live question is narrower: SHOULD
THE PACKAGE EXPOSE A WAY FOR A ROOT THE CONSUMER OPENED TO CARRY THE FRAMEWORK REPORTER?
RECOMMENDATION: NO. (1) A consumer who wants the diagnostic already has two doors — h/hydrate!,
or the Spec 006 adapter render with {:hydrate? true} if their app is React-rooted. Trusting the
programmer means letting them mount through a door rather than shipping a second mechanism for
not doing so. (2) It is not the one-liner it looks like: exporting hydration-reporter alone
would emit NOTHING, because the emit is gated on roots/adopting? and a consumer-built tree
carries no adoption window and no adoption-window-closer, so the flag reads closed —
impl/roots.cljs:59-64 states exactly this for a hand-rolled renderToString. A real door means
publishing the window, the closer and the option-builder, which naming-ledger.md row 50 already
flags as "a larger decision" (making impl.mount/tree and impl.roots/open-adoption-window!
public). (3) Nothing is broken: React still complains on its own channel and the divergence is
a deterministic bug either way; what is missing is a TRACE, on a root the framework does not
own. If Mike wants it anyway it is a public-surface programme, not a bounded fix. rf2-0brem
does NOT wait on this ruling — the doc clause is true under either answer.

DECLINED, and why: no PR (read-only brief, and both candidate edits are the ledger keeper's
surface — native_abi_dom_cljs_test.cljs:48-52 states the principle, "a witness may not amend
the row it witnesses", which binds an auditor the same way); no third bead for the door (the
stance rejects the remedy, so a bead filed to be refused costs more than this recommendation);
no edit to correction-ledger.md (fenced out by this bead); no edit to checkpoint-3-native.md (a
dated checkpoint record — whether it is amended in place is the ledger keeper's convention, not
an auditor's); no bead for the drifted line numbers in correction-ledger.md:89.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS BEAD: Mike ruling on the door question above. rf2-0brem then discharges
the last acceptance clause independently. Nothing else on this bead is owed.
FOLLOW-ONS FILED BY THIS AUDIT (both name rf2-s52w as owner, so a later audit re-finding either recognises it as this bead's clause rather than a second finding): rf2-0brem — scope row 5's 'mismatch attribution' required result to roots a re-frame2 door opens (this bead's last acceptance clause; react-compatibility-notes.md:34 and hot-path-architecture.md:49). rf2-981ka — native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:66 still says 'there is no Hicasso server entry', false since 2026-08-14, and it is the sentence Checkpoint 3 cited that seeded this bead's P4 root cause. NOTE ON THIS BEAD'S TITLE: '(no Spec 011 reporter)' is false as written — Spec 011 defines the reporter and Hicasso installs it on its own doors. Title left unchanged because several committed docs cite this bead by id beside that phrasing; the P1 paragraph above is the correction. Returning to open — no worker holds it.
close_reason: Operator ruling (Mike, 2026-08-21): Option A — no consumer-opened-root reporter door. Attribution stays scoped to roots a re-frame2 door opens (spec/011:825 wording). Two doors already exist (h/hydrate!, Spec 006 adapter render with :hydrate?). Audit's recommendation adopted in full. rf2-0brem carries the remaining doc clause; rf2-981ka the stale test sentence. Reopen only on real consumer demand; then it is a public-surface programme, not a fix.
