title: hic-036 clock driver: instrument the 4x4 clock table (DEFERRED — measurement lane)
description:
*** THE BUILD HALF IS DONE AND MERGED. THIS BEAD IS WINDOW-ONLY. DO NOT DISPATCH IT TO BUILD A DRIVER. ***

READ THIS BEFORE BRIEFING FROM ANYTHING BELOW. The description says "topo/ has no clock
driver at all". THAT IS FALSE AT THE TIP, and it has been false since 2026-08-16.

MEASURED 2026-08-21, before a worker was sent:
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/topo/clock_app.cljs EXISTS, 673 lines.
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/topo/clock_witness_dom_cljs_test.cljs
  EXISTS, 288 lines.
- The driver was landed by commit 23f3d13064 on 2026-08-16, whose subject is
  "feat(hicasso): the topology tournament's clock table gets a driver (rf2-w01c)" - THIS BEAD.
- It was refined again by 858cf77e9d on 2026-08-18 (rf2-yorfi), which states the arm-specific
  floor the window measured in the :noop docstring.
- clock_app.cljs names the 4x4 table 11 times.

So the bead built its own driver five days ago and its description was never updated. A
dispatch reading the description would have sent a worker to build something that already
exists, authored under this very bead id.

WHAT ACTUALLY REMAINS: the WINDOW. Take the 4 arms x 4 operations table on a QUIET BOX. This
is Shape 6 measurement work and the estimand is CLOCK, so unlike the allocation beads it is
NOT box-exempt - a free bench slot is not enough, the machine must be quiet.

TWO CONSTRAINTS CARRY FORWARD UNCHANGED AND ARE NOT TO BE RELITIGATED:

1. FROM rf2-m6i0's WINDOW: a manipulation certifies an instrument ONLY WHEN EVERY COST IN THE
   WINDOW MOVES WITH IT. Both predecessor controls were right about one arm and degenerate
   elsewhere - one fault in two directions - because each moved only part of the cost.

2. FROM rf2-4t36: the WINDOWED arm's clock cells are UNRESOLVABLE at the committed window size.
   Its whole commit is 0.125-0.195 ms against Chrome's 100 microsecond quanta, and a fitted
   floor of about 0.059 ms is 47% of the reading - so a healthy instrument on a quiet box
   certifies that arm about one run in four. THOSE CELLS STAY UNADDRESSED. Do not widen a band
   to admit them.

A NOTE ON THE BLOCKING CLAIM BELOW: the description says an uninstrumented clock table holds
"roughly a dozen implementation beads" through rf2-hic-036. That chain has largely since
closed - hic-066 and the rename sweep landed, and hic-090 is held on rf2-t32wg rather than on
this. Re-derive the dependency picture before quoting that sentence.

--- ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION FOLLOWS (2026-08-13, its first paragraph superseded above) ---

SPLIT OUT OF rf2-hic-036 under the operator's 2026-08-14 direction: 'get on with fully implementing hicasso, run measurement later'.

WHY THE SPLIT. rf2-hic-036 carries two halves. The DETERMINISTIC WORK CENSUS is done â€” 48 cells, published, merged, dispositions for every one. The CLOCK TABLE was never instrumented: topo/ has no clock driver at all, and the control refusing first masked that absence. Those halves have different costs and, now, different priorities.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS BEAD. rf2-hic-036 is the ROOT of the entire hicasso implementation chain: it blocks hic-038 and hic-048, which block hic-065 (the naming packet), which blocks hic-066 (the mechanical rename sweep), which alone blocks five further beads including hic-060, hic-068, hic-069 and hic-090. So an uninstrumented clock table is currently holding roughly a dozen implementation beads, and the operator has asked for implementation to proceed.

THIS BEAD IS THE DEFERRED HALF. Build a clock driver for topo/ and take the 4 arms x 4 operations table. It is real measurement work under Shape 6 and needs a quiet box.

THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT IS ALREADY ESTABLISHED, from rf2-m6i0's window: A MANIPULATION CERTIFIES AN INSTRUMENT ONLY WHEN EVERY COST IN THE WINDOW MOVES WITH IT. Both predecessor controls were right about one arm and degenerate elsewhere â€” one fault in two directions â€” because each moved only part of the cost. A driver built without that constraint will reproduce the same failure.

KNOWN LIMIT, already ruled and not to be relitigated: rf2-4t36 established that the WINDOWED arm's clock cells are unresolvable at the committed window size. Its whole commit is 0.125-0.195 ms against Chrome's 100 microsecond quanta, and a fitted floor of about 0.059 ms is 47% of the reading â€” so a healthy instrument on a quiet box certifies that arm about one run in four. Those cells stay UNADDRESSED. Do not widen a band to admit them and do not enlarge the window to rescue them, which would certify a regime the cells are not published in.

WHAT THE CHECKPOINTS SHOULD DO IN THE MEANTIME is recorded on rf2-hic-036 itself: proceed on the census and record the clock table as NOT INSTRUMENTED, using the same vocabulary rf2-hic-080 used successfully â€” score what exists, mark the rest unaddressed, never substitute one estimand for another.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8466 (2026-08-20). The published second attempt does not satisfy its own fixed-before-run plan. topology-tournament.md §2.9.1 says the three runs are serial and "nothing else is run beside them"; §2.9.3 then records that a second documentation agent was demonstrably active on the box during run 1. The Shape 6 rule already present at the PR base says a clock window run beside a peer produces a worthless-looking measurement and requires one run at a time. Passing rendered-scale controls and disclosing the overlap are useful evidence, but they do not turn the pre-registered condition into an optional caveat. Because §2.9.2 itself rejects completing a partial series later as "two instruments", replacing only run 1 would repeat that defect. Resolve by taking a fresh end-to-end three-run clock series under the registered exclusive/quiet condition, or obtain and record an explicit methodological ruling that narrows the condition before treating the current table as publishable. Preserve the present table as a transparent record; the actionable defect is its publication as the fully honoured rf2-w01c window.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8471 (2026-08-20), downstream impact of the #8466 audit finding. PR #8471 embeds the challenged clock series' exact three-run values and derived fine/coarse ranges in implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/topo/clock_app.cljs, presenting them as the measurement that falsified the shared-floor premise. The qualitative conclusion is supported independently by runs 2 and 3 (fine remains about 4x coarse), so no separate rf2-yorfi reopen or immediate revert is warranted. But the accepted resolution of rf2-w01c must also revalidate this code docstring and topology-tournament.md §2.9.7 together: if a fresh exclusive three-run series or methodological ruling changes the published values or inference, update both surfaces in the same repair. This is the exact existing owner; do not create a duplicate.
MAYOR DISPATCH TICK 2026-08-21 06:15 AUSEST — NOT DISPATCHED, AND DELIBERATELY SO EVEN THOUGH A SLOT IS FREE. FENCED ON A PEER, NOT ON THE BOX.

THREE SLOTS ARE FREE and no bench-class worker is in flight, so the machine is not what holds this. What holds it is that ANOTHER WORKER IS ALREADY ANSWERING THIS BEAD'S CENTRAL QUESTION.

THE OVERLAP, and rf2-85og2 named it before I did: 'the clock instrument this needs is the same gap rf2-w01c carries for the tournament. Whoever plans the measurement lane should look at both together rather than building two instruments.' worker/budgetgates-85og2 is live right now re-testing rf2-85og2's three refusal grounds, and ground 1 is precisely 'no package-resident clock instrument exists'. Dispatching this bead now would put two workers at one instrument, which is the collision the method spends a section forbidding — and worse, the two could build DIFFERENT instruments for the same gap.

WHAT MAY HAVE CHANGED UNDER BOTH BEADS: rf2-xa8wo closed and merged as PR #8589 on 2026-08-21, landing an interaction-to-paint clock on the slice app with p95 in lane.cljs and a lane_quantile_cljs_test.cljs beside it. Whether that satisfies 'package-resident' is exactly what budgetgates is determining. Its answer decides whether this bead needs an instrument BUILT or merely POINTED AT one.

THE ESTIMAND HERE IS CLOCK, so unlike the allocation beads its window genuinely needs a QUIET box, not merely a free bench slot. Three live workers running intermittent node and python checks is not a quiet box. That fence is independent of the peer fence above and binds only the window.

MAYOR 2026-08-21 (backlog reread) — THE WORKER FENCE IS DISCHARGED. THE MACHINE FENCE IS NOT.

Tested at source rather than remembered. The recorded fence read "CLEARS WHEN
worker/budgetgates-85og2 REPORTS". That branch no longer exists on origin and its PR
#8595 is MERGED, so the condition is met and the fence is retired.

WHAT STILL HOLDS THIS BEAD is the machine, and it is a different kind of fence. The
estimand here is CLOCK, so unlike the allocation beads it is NOT box-exempt: a free bench
slot is not enough, the box must be quiet. worker/revorder-csca8 is taking an allocation
window right now.

RE-DISPATCH WHEN the box is quiet. Nothing else is owed.
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-08-22 02:1x AUSEST, tip c725b54660. LANE POSTURE RECORDED ON rf2-85og2 THIS TICK — read it there rather than restating it here. In summary, verified at source: Mike's standing quiet-box grant is confirmed on rf2-2rtt6.140 ('no further grant is needed per bead or per window') and this lane is held by a LIVE WORKER, not by an operator decision. Current holder: asyncsettle on rf2-sxhu, branch pushed at 951be47bf2, no PR yet. CLEARS WHEN no worker holds the machine at all. rf2-0puue is NOT in this queue — it is PARKED by a 2026-08-04 ruling with a take-condition of v0 heap-hardening, and that same ruling assigns the box to the CLOCK rows, which is this lane.
WORKER topoclock, 2026-08-22 05:1x AUSEST. THE EXCLUSIVE WINDOW WAS TAKEN AND IT RETURNED AN
INCOMPLETE SERIES PLUS ONE RULING REQUEST. PR #8682 open, not merged. Branch worker/topoclock-w01c,
base 2a93f2c112 (an ancestor of main). Nothing was built.

*** FIRST, TWO CORRECTIONS AT SOURCE. ***

1. THE DESCRIPTION'S STALE PARAGRAPH IS STILL STALE and this note does not fix it: the ORIGINAL
   DESCRIPTION block still reads "topo/ has no clock driver at all". The correcting header above it
   is right, and I verified both commits it names -- 23f3d1306446375dd97ba2cc87a164aa04661c1d
   ("feat(hicasso): the topology tournament's clock table gets a driver (rf2-w01c)", 2026-08-16) and
   858cf77e9df51709713c391901ed74bb9d085e1c (rf2-yorfi, 2026-08-18). Both exist, both say what the
   header claims.
2. THE DISPATCH BRIEF CARRIED A WRONG FIGURE. It gave clock_app.cljs as 643 lines. It is 673, which
   is what this bead's own description says. wc -l at the tip agrees with the bead and not the brief.

*** WHAT WAS TAKEN. ***

Five invocations of topo/clock_app.cljs through run.cjs, serial, nothing tuned, 04:52-05:13 AUSEST.
All five reached the page and returned exit 0, so NONE was a rig fault. The window shape was read
off the instrument rather than chosen: warmup 3 / samples 12, rounds 5, batch-k 20, all inherited
from control_app; 3 arms x 5 rows x 3 row counts = 45 cells; virtual UNADDRESSED with no clock
started on it.

THE PRE-REGISTRATION WAS COMMITTED AND PUSHED BEFORE THE RUNNER WAS INVOKED ONCE (5caab9184f,
topology-tournament.md Part 3 sec 3.2, that page and nothing else). It carries sec 2.9.1's six
clauses unchanged and adds an exclusivity condition, a comparative adjudication rule and an explicit
"this window adjudicates no ledger row".

TWO OF THE FIVE WERE VOIDED, by the condition I registered before running: any file not this
worker's own, modified inside a run's wall-clock bracket, voids that run. That check exists because
it is exactly how the #8466 audit caught the original overlap.
  - invocation 1 (04:52:34-04:56:07): peer write at 04:55:55 -- the dispatch loop's own tick, which
    MERGED PR #8680 mid-invocation. VOID.
  - invocation 3 (05:09:26-05:13:04): peer write at 05:12:14 -- another worker's gate artefact
    (reaproute-qche), whose worktree appeared at 05:13:33 and which was running mkdocs seconds later.
    VOID.

RUN 3 COULD NOT BE RE-TAKEN because that peer then held the machine, and sec 2.9.2's
"a series completed later is two instruments" -- the rule the audit itself used to refuse replacing
only run 1 -- forbids finishing it another time. TWO ADMISSIBLE RUNS OF A PRE-REGISTERED THREE.
So sec 2.9.5 and sec 2.9.6 are NOT replaced and nothing published moves. Part 3 is a RECORD.

*** RULE 1 -- THE INFERENCE SURVIVES. ***

sec 2.9.7's falsification is confirmed in all six readings (floor arm-specific, always larger on the
arm with more boundaries and reads). The narrow/broad reversal holds in ALL EIGHT readings. bulk
still orders the arms; reorder still reads mostly floor on fine (51-82% against competitors at or
under 16%). Instrument certified: 30 control rounds across the two runs, every one in band
[1.4997, 2.4995] spanning [2.0118, 2.4092], 0 unverified of 300 writes per arm per run, 18 of 18
reportable arm-order verdicts per run, no PROBE MISS in either, both builds 0 warnings.
THE ONE HALF THAT DOES NOT REPRODUCE is sec 2.9.8's "and the three runs agree".

*** RULE 2 -- THE VALUES MOVED, AND AGAINST THE AUDIT'S PREMISE. ***

1 of 45 cells lands inside the published series' own three-run envelope; 12 SPLIT, 32 MOVED. The
exclusive series reads SLOWER on 36 of 45 (median 1.094x the published centre, min 0.901, max 1.341)
and is THREE TIMES NOISIER on the published series' own statistic:
  raw cell spread   published median 9.0% / max 25.1%   exclusive median 28.6% / max 75.5%
  ratio-cell spread published median 3.9% / max 10.1%   exclusive median 3.8%  / max 22.0%
Three runs give a range more chances to widen than two, so a two-run series ought to score LOWER on
both. On the raw cells it scores three times higher; on the ratios it matches. THE ABSOLUTE CELLS
MOVED WITH THE BOX AND THE ARM-TO-ARM RATIOS DID NOT -- which is what within-round interleaving is
for and the first direct evidence on this lane that it works.

*** THE MECHANISM, MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. ***

A 5s per-process CPU census: 2.29 busy cores of 24. Every AGENT process on the box summed to 0.52 --
23% of the busy time, 2% of the machine -- against 1.07 cores for ONE editor language service. THE
EXCLUSIVITY CONDITION REACHES A QUARTER OF THE LOAD. And the bracket counters do not predict the
readings: run 1 began at the busiest bracket (LoadPercentage 82) and run 2 at the quietest (8), yet
run 2 is the slower run on 27 of 45 cells. An admissibility rule keyed to those counters would have
admitted and refused the wrong runs.

*** THE RULING THIS ASKS FOR -- ONE SENTENCE, MIKE'S OR THE MAYOR'S. ***

DOES THE PRE-REGISTERED EXCLUSIVITY CONDITION BIND AGENT OVERLAP ONLY, OR THE WHOLE BOX?
  - Agent overlap only: sec 2.9's published series has a defect this window has now shown does not
    reach its conclusions -- every sec 2.9.8 ordering reproduced under exclusivity -- and the honest
    repair is the audit's OWN SECOND REMEDY, a narrowing ruling plus a note, not a third full
    window. This window is the evidence for it that the audit could not have had.
  - The whole box: then NO window taken on this machine has ever met the condition, sec 2.9's and
    this one's included, and what is needed is a different box. That is a programme decision, not a
    worker's.
NOT ASKED FOR, and all three are refused in the record: no wider band, no enlarged window, no
threshold fitted to the bracket counters.

*** THE #8471 SURFACE PAIR, REVALIDATED TOGETHER IN ONE COMMIT. ***

sec 2.9.7 and clock_app.cljs's docstring both carry a dated note. "about 4x" is RETIRED as this
series' number rather than the instrument's: the floor factor REPRODUCES at B=100 (2.15x/2.12x
against a published 2.18/2.22/2.17) and at B=300 (3.19x/3.00x against 3.10/2.97/3.08), reads
3.35-3.54x at B=1000 against 3.79-3.97, and GROWS WITH B -- which one row count could not show. The
claim sec 2.9.7 limits itself to survives; only the magnitude beside it softens. No figure replaced,
because two runs are not three.

*** SCOPE LIMITS, STATED SO A LATER READER CANNOT MISS THEM. ***

- NO LEDGER ROW MOVES, in either direction, and that was registered before any number was seen.
  Verified at source on the branch AND against current origin/main: 49 rows, 32 MET, 5 BREACH,
  3 UNRESOLVED, 9 UNPINNED, identical on both.
- Every cell stays UNASSESSED against U1-U3 for sec 2.9.9's reason, which exclusivity does not
  touch: this window is a commit bracketed by flushSync on a SYNTHETIC BENCH PAGE, and those lines
  are stated over a slice application's interactions THROUGH TO A PAINT. C3/C4 are a different
  population and are not addressed.
- virtual: UNADDRESSED, no clock started, NO BOUND SUPPLIED IN EITHER DIRECTION, not even an upper

cheap that write is — creating a worktree is nearly free and still voided a run, and so did a
merge, which costs the machine almost nothing at all.

correctly judged not to make the machine LOUD; it is not thereby judged not to BREAK THE BRACKET.

a live agent. A condition that cannot be met at the quietest moment the project ever reaches is not
a condition; it is a veto on the whole lane, and it would retroactively void every window ever taken

reaches a quarter of the load. The rest is the box being a workstation, which is a procurement fact

stance rejects: we are not litigating every last fine detail, and a standard that voids all evidence

DEFERRAL LIFTED — MIKE 2026-08-14: 'I want hicasso fully implemented, nothing deferred. I want a complete library. I want a sophisticated library.'

This bead was parked under the earlier direction to run measurement later. That direction is superseded. It is now live work.

ONE PHYSICAL CONSTRAINT REMAINS AND IS NOT A DEFERRAL. A clock estimand needs a quiet box: one measurement at a time, controls arbitrating, no other worker compiling. That is a property of the instrument, not a scheduling preference — a reading taken against six concurrent compiles measures the fleet, not the library. COUNTER estimands have no such constraint; monotone counters read the same on a loaded box, which is why the deterministic censuses landed while the clock tables did not.

SO THE PLAN IS: build every instrument NOW, in parallel, on a loaded box — that work is edit-shaped and unconstrained. Then run the windows themselves back to back when the fleet is idle. That is the same split that produced rf2-w01c from rf2-hic-036 and rf2-d6ai8 from rf2-hic-088, and it means the quiet-box time is spent measuring rather than writing drivers.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWES, restated: if it needs an instrument that does not exist, that half dispatches immediately. If the instrument exists and only the window is missing, it queues for the next quiet period. Whoever picks it up should say which case it is in the first paragraph of its report.

# hic-088 — Requirements-mine consolidation

**Phase**: 4/6 · **Est.**: S · **Depends**: hic-004
**Surface**: `docs/design/hicasso/product/requirements-mine.md` (the one consolidation owner)

## Goal
The mine must be current when the audits read it. This bead owns the updates hic-004 only seeded.

## Deliverables
Two consolidation passes recorded in the file: one before the coverage checkpoint (every row's witness link resolves; "owed by" rows re-pointed to landed evidence or open corrections) and one before the final audit (same, plus final-name updates after the sweep).

## Acceptance
At each pass: zero stale witness links; zero rows owing to closed beads without landed evidence; pass dates recorded in the file.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates: foreground a gate that fits inside the harness ceiling; DETACH one that does not and poll BOTH its log and its `.exit` file in a bounded loop within the same turn — never end the turn waiting for a completion event. Never pipe a gate through `tail` or any filter; redirect to a log and echo the runner's own exit code on the same command line. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn. DOC-SURFACE GATE: for an edit confined to docs/design/hicasso/, `mkdocs build --strict` is NOT the gate — mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs keeps that tree out of the site. `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` validates its markdown link targets and heading anchors, and `scripts/check_provenance_pins.py` validates changed pages under docs/design/hicasso/; nothing validates its tables, rendering or nav, so verify anchors and table column counts BY HAND and say so in the PR body.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/issues.jsonl` or `.beads/metadata.json` from a worker branch — they are whole-database EXPORTS, not database files, and your branch carries the snapshot taken when its worktree was created, so committing one TIME-TRAVELS the tracker: beads closed since reopen, beads filed since vanish (PR #6677 did exactly this, 135 insertions / 136 deletions of pure collateral). Any other database-derived path likewise. The human-authored config — `.beads/README.md`, `.beads/config.yaml`, `.beads/.gitignore`, `.beads/hooks/**` — IS fair game. CLAUDE.md's Beads durability section is the authority.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files only if this bead flags them — and the hot zone INCLUDES the spec/*.md hot files (spec/004-Views.md, spec/002-Frames.md, spec/API.md, spec/Conventions.md among others), not just implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn and .github/workflows/*. CLAUDE.md's Workflow section carries the canonical list; read it there rather than treating this line as complete.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues AND a row in docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md. The checkpoint's own report PR writes the `open` row; a CORRECTIVE PR never edits that file — every later transition is the ledger keeper's. Read the file's own stated protocol before touching it.

title: hic-051 — Forms: recipes first, the buffered-draft field at its second consumer
description:
# hic-051 — Forms: recipes first, the buffered-draft field at its second consumer

**Phase**: 5 · **Wave**: F · **Est.**: L · **Depends**: hic-020, hic-025
**Surface**: optional forms namespace/recipes + tests (new files)

## Goal
The highest-traffic optional product: the draft/validation patterns that kill the five hand-rolled trap classes (twin-atom stack, same-value blindness, commit flicker, arity-sniffed done-fn, re-minted ephemeral state).

## Deliverables
- The documented recipes: buffered draft (commit/cancel/blur incl. cancel-unmounts-then-blur), touched/submit-attempt validation gating, mutation status display — each with structural tests on the kit.
- The `draft-field` helper extracted **when the second consumer appears** (the slice app + the vendor screen may already be the two — if so, extract now); zero reachable production code when the namespace is unused (sentinel proof).

## Acceptance
Recipes runnable; trap-class regression tests green (each of the five traps has a witness proving this pattern avoids it); reachability proof green.

## Worker notes
Read synth-codex §4.2 tail, §7 forms row; the A1/A2 rows in the requirements mine.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7971 (merged 2026-08-12T07:12:16Z; completeness/correctness/implementation quality) — REOPENED. The recipes and their synchronous/model coverage are strong, but the two poll-until chains in implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/forms/flow_dom_cljs_test.cljs (the refused-submit marker wait and valid-submit transport wait) have only a fulfillment handler. If the bounded poll rejects, cljs.test done is never called and the live hm/mount! handle is never unmounted/asserted clean; the row hangs and can contaminate later browser tests. The sibling slice suite already has the bounded finish-after shape: report the rejection upstream, tear down on both arms, and keep exactly one trailing done. Apply that shape to both rows and add a deliberate rejected-poll control proving the following row sees no retained mount/residue. Keep the correction local; no runtime or forms API change.
PR #8668 AUDIT RESIDUAL (correctness / implementation quality; the teaching-set completeness work is otherwise sound). Reopened this exact forms-recipe owner because the rule promoted into the published guide contradicts the accessibility state it exposes. At merge, docs/core/hicasso/05-forms.md says an invalid submit button stays "focusable and activatable" and relies on that activation to set :submit-attempted?, while rendering :aria-disabled true; forms-recipes.md:53 and the shipped example view/tests pin the same pattern. WAI-ARIA 1.2 defines aria-disabled=true as perceivable but disabled, "so it is not editable or otherwise operable" (https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria/#aria-disabled). The page therefore tells assistive technology the action is unavailable while the application requires the user to activate it to reveal errors; current DOM/L2 tests pin both halves without testing their semantic coherence. Repair the guide, recipe, example view and witnesses together: normally keep invalid submit genuinely enabled (omit aria-disabled), let submit validation reveal the error summary, and describe the errors with the appropriate relationship/live-region semantics; reserve disabled/aria-disabled for an action the handler really suppresses. Do not merely change the prose while leaving the example and tests contradictory.
close_reason: PR #8671 — the aria-disabled/activatable contradiction is repaired across every layer at once: guide chapter (prose, worked form, field sample, two troubleshooting rows), forms-recipes.md rule + dated correction note, the shipped example view/subs/db/events, and both witnesses. The invalid submit button now claims nothing — validity is carried by the fields as aria-invalid + aria-describedby + role=alert, and aria-disabled is reserved for controls the handler really suppresses. New L2 row and DOM assertions pin the semantic coherence that nothing tested before. Two consequent pins moved in the same commit: the guide-samples roster (blocks 5 and 8) and the pooled read-set census (dropping the gate read left save-button and save-failure on an identical one-key set; verdict unmoved). Gates captured green: hicasso-invariants 0, node lane 0 (11811 tests), browser lane 0 (1064 tests), doc-slugs 0, provenance-pins 0, mkdocs --strict 0; each lane also driven red from a planted fault and restored blob-hash-verified.

title: hicasso: the fused reader array costs 91-92 B/read — the largest term this page has attributed to a container rather than a value
description:
MEASURED, NOT SPECULATED. rf2-zei9w's ablation attributes 91 B/read (Reagent segment) / 92 (UIx) to the cell's fused reader array — the container itself, not the membership it holds. Per-round bands are disjoint across all six rounds, the R=0 shell does not move, and donors moved 0.05/0.19 B/read, so this is a per-KEY term and the attribution is solid. Published in docs/design/hicasso/studio/reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md (2026-08-04 section), PR #7452.

WHY IT IS WORTH A LOOK. rf2-dabt3's fusion banked -60 B/read in both segments — real, and it won — but that is only ~40% of the ~151 B/read the old reverse edge cost, because the replacement array is ~2x what ONE PersistentHashSet membership costs (+46/+47 B/read, PR #7418 run D). The design predicted the surviving array would be cheap residue; it is not. It is now the largest single term this page has attributed to a CONTAINER rather than to a value.

THE OBVIOUS SHAPE, and it is only a sketch. At the fan-out this table actually sees, the overwhelmingly common case is ONE reader per key. A scalar slot that holds the single reader directly and promotes to an array on the SECOND reader would retain a pointer instead of a JSArray-plus-backing-store for that case. arm1/runtime.cljs's own section header already argues a JS array beats a persistent set here; this asks the next question down, which is whether a container is needed at all in the common case.

THIS IS NOT A DISPATCH. It wants a ruling first, for three reasons:
• release-cell!'s .indexOf, arm-cell-reaper!'s alength and stats's alength all read .-readers directly, and cell-readers/stats are witness surfaces the six laws and the ladder's structural gate are written against — a polymorphic slot touches all of them.
• It is a byte shave on a pre-alpha arm, and the stance is explicit that not every measured term needs actioning.
• The bill it would attack is +331 B/read against Reagent; 91 of that is this term. Worth knowing the size before deciding it is worth the branch in a hot path.

Precondition if it is ever taken: a quiet box, p0_run.cjs --only ladder 6 rounds with both donors as same-run controls, and the same ablation discipline rf2-zei9w used — attribute, do not infer.
notes:
FENCE recorded 2026-08-21 by the dispatch tick — EXCLUSIVE RESOURCE, CONTENDED. Not dispatchable while the fleet is loud. This bead's own newest note states the rule: 'that is exactly why one bench-class worker at a time is the rule and why a second allocation window is not admissible merely because the estimand is exempt.' The estimand is ALLOCATION (91-92 B/read), box-exempt for VALIDITY per rf2-ojehu / PR #8419 but NOT exempt for CAPACITY, so it needs a quiet box rather than merely a tolerant one. Five workers are live at the time of writing, one of them editing the bench harness. CLEARS WHEN: the operator authorises a deliberate fleet drain and no other bench-class worker holds the machine. Per the method a measurement window is dispatched SOLO as Shape 6 and is never folded into a cluster. This is a decision the mayor announces, not one that happens by default — it is surfaced to Mike alongside rf2-85og2, rf2-w01c, rf2-9wmqd and rf2-v5oto, which are fenced on the same resource.
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-08-22 02:1x AUSEST, tip c725b54660. MY OWN FENCE ON THIS BEAD MIS-STATES THE HOLD, and I have been carrying the error into tick reports for hours. Correcting it here rather than in a transcript.

THE FENCE I RECORDED says this bead is held by an EXCLUSIVE, CONTENDED BOX and clears when the box goes idle. That is true of the precondition and FALSE as an account of why the bead is not dispatched. Read at source just now:

  * THE DESCRIPTION SAYS 'THIS IS NOT A DISPATCH. It wants a ruling first.'
  * AND THE RULING WAS GIVEN, 2026-08-04, delegated dossier review, operator-overturnable:
    '(b) PARK as K3's priced paper path. P2 -> P3, stays open, UNDISPATCHED. Take at v0
    heap-hardening if P2 rules go; sooner only if a P2 advisory names heap pivotal.'

SO THIS BEAD IS PARKED WITH A NAMED TAKE-CONDITION, not queued behind a box. An idle box does NOT release it. What releases it is v0 heap-hardening, or a P2 advisory naming heap pivotal — neither of which has happened.

AND THE SAME RULING RULES OUT SPENDING THE BOX HERE EVEN IF IT WERE IDLE, in terms that decide the whole lane's ordering: 'quiet boxes are the scarce pre-P2 resource and BELONG TO THE CLOCK ROWS THAT DECIDE P2.' This bead's estimand is allocation. So when the box frees, this is not the bead that takes it — rf2-85og2, rf2-w01c, rf2-v5oto and rf2-9wmqd item (c) are, and they are clock rows.

WHY THE ERROR HAPPENED, recorded because it is the same shape twice this session: I grouped this bead with the measurement lane BY TOPIC — it is a bench bead with a quiet-box precondition in its last paragraph — and the fence note I then wrote described the topic rather than the hold. The park ruling is a COMMENT dated 2026-08-04, four notes above the fence, and a tail-first read never reached it. Same failure as rf2-9wmqd, where I read a bead as needing a window when its own first paragraph said it needed none.

WHAT IS UNCHANGED AND STILL CORRECT ON THIS BEAD: the estimand reading (allocation, 91-92 B/read, box-exempt for validity per rf2-ojehu / PR #8419, not exempt for capacity), the staged paper path S1/S2, and the rider that P2 heap discussions quote the bill itemised. Nothing above touches the substance.
MAYOR DISPATCH TICK 2026-08-22 09:4x AUSEST, tip 1b22778172. THE MACHINE FENCE ON THIS BEAD IS
SPENT, AND THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS THE ONE IN THE DESCRIPTION, NOT THE ONE IN THE NOTES. Both
halves checked at source this tick rather than carried forward; nothing below is re-derived from
an earlier note of mine.

THE RECORDED FENCE IS MET. The 2026-08-21 08:10 note restated it as "CLEARS WHEN
worker/passterm-fk6pj's window completes and no other bench-class worker holds the box."
  * Conjunct one: `bd show rf2-fk6pj` reads CLOSED (updated 2026-08-21). Its window completed.

SO THE FENCE THIS BEAD HAS BEEN CARRYING SINCE 2026-08-21 NO LONGER HOLDS IT. Recording that
plainly, because a tick that reads only the newest note would keep waiting on a window that has
already been taken.

BUT THIS BEAD IS STILL NOT DISPATCHABLE, and the reason is older and stronger than the fence.
Its DESCRIPTION says so in its own words: "THIS IS NOT A DISPATCH. It wants a ruling first",
and gives three reasons -- the polymorphic slot touches release-cell!, arm-cell-reaper! and
stats, all witness surfaces the six laws and the ladder's structural gate are written against;
it is a byte shave on a pre-alpha arm where the stance is explicit that not every measured term
needs actioning; and the bill it attacks is +331 B/read against Reagent, of which this term is 91.

THE CORRECTION IS THEREFORE ABOUT WHICH CONSTRAINT IS BINDING, NOT ABOUT WHETHER THE BEAD MOVES.
It has been sitting in the machine-fence pile through several ticks. It belongs in the awaiting-a-
ruling pile, where the fence is irrelevant: when Mike rules that this is worth taking, the
precondition the description already names still applies -- a quiet box, p0_run.cjs --only ladder
6 rounds with both donors as same-run controls, and rf2-zei9w's ablation discipline. That is a
condition on EXECUTION, to be established fresh at that time, not a hold on the decision.

CLEARS WHEN: Mike rules on whether the scalar-slot shape is worth taking. No machine condition
attaches to the ruling itself.
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-08-22, tip 56b6f7a370 — THE MACHINE FENCE READS AS MET AND IS NOT. Measured,
not inferred, and the gap between those two is the whole of this note.

WHAT PROMPTED THE CHECK. The fleet is empty: `bd list --status=in_progress` returns "No issues
found", no PR is open, and every worker dispatched this session has been reaped. Both bench-class
fences on this bead and its peer name a quiet box, and an empty fleet is the obvious proxy for one.

WHAT THE BOX ACTUALLY SHOWS AT THAT SAME MOMENT: 22 node processes and 109 chrome processes
resident, plus a listener still bound on the SSR testbed port. None belongs to a live worker. They
are residue — reaped worktrees leave their build servers and browser processes running, which is a
known property of this platform, and nothing in the tracker records their existence.

SO "FLEET ZERO" IS NOT "QUIET BOX", and the failure is silent in the reassuring direction: the
instrument that would tell a tick the fleet is empty answers correctly, and the conclusion drawn
from it is wrong. This is the same shape as any instrument that can answer "nothing here" — the
answer is right about what it measures and wrong about what it is being used for. A tick that
reads the fleet count and dispatches a measurement window would take its numbers against 131
resident processes and never know.

THE FENCE THEREFORE STANDS, on its own terms and unchanged. Nothing here is a clearance.

WHAT IS NEW AND WORTH THE OPERATOR'S ATTENTION: the fence is now CHEAP to clear rather than met.
No live worker contends for the box, so reaching a genuinely quiet one is a process sweep plus a
hold on dispatch for the window's duration — not a fleet drain, which is what the fence was
written to require back when five workers were live. That is a smaller ask than the recorded
condition implies.

AND A NATURALLY QUIET MOMENT IS STILL NOT A WINDOW. The dispatch loop refills the fleet on its own
cadence, so quiet-right-now decays without warning. A window needs dispatch deliberately held for
its duration, which is precisely why this remains a decision the mayor announces rather than one
that happens by default. Surfaced, not taken.
*** MY 2026-08-22 MACHINE-FENCE NOTE ON THIS BEAD IS WRONG TWICE OVER AND IS RETRACTED. Read this
before anything above it. ***

BACKLOG REREAD 2026-08-22, tip 1af2c07505. Two errors, and the second one I made while writing a
note whose whole subject was the first.

ERROR 1 — I RE-ASSERTED A FRAMING THIS BEAD HAD ALREADY CORRECTED. The 02:1x note above says
plainly: "MY OWN FENCE ON THIS BEAD MIS-STATES THE HOLD ... The fence I recorded says this bead is
held by an EXCLUSIVE, CONTENDED BOX and clears when the box goes idle. That is true of the
precondition and FALSE as an account of why the bead is not dispatched." It then quotes the
description — "THIS IS NOT A DISPATCH. It wants a ruling first" — and the 2026-08-04 park ruling,
and concludes "CLEARS WHEN: Mike rules on whether the scalar-slot shape is worth taking. No machine
condition attaches to the ruling itself."

I then appended a long note about the machine fence on this bead, treating it as one of two
"bench-class fences" that "name a quiet box". That is the retracted framing, restated by me, hours
later, on the same bead. AND MINE IS NOW THE NEWEST TEXT, so a reader doing the correct
newest-first walk lands on my error and never reaches the correction beneath it. That is exactly
the writer-side hazard the method carries a clause about — a stale note that IS the newest text,
which a reader cannot defend against.

WHAT ACTUALLY HOLDS THIS BEAD, unchanged and restated so this note does not merely say "not that":
a RULING. The 2026-08-04 delegated dossier review PARKED it as K3's priced paper path, P2 -> P3,
stays open, undispatched, to be taken at v0 heap-hardening or on a P2 advisory naming heap pivotal.
Neither has happened. The box being idle does not release it, and the same ruling says the box is
not to be spent here even if idle: "quiet boxes are the scarce pre-P2 resource and BELONG TO THE
CLOCK ROWS THAT DECIDE P2." This bead's estimand is allocation, not clock.

ERROR 2 — "131 RESIDENT PROCESSES" IS NOT A LOUD BOX, AND I MEASURED THE WRONG THING. My note
counted 22 node and 109 chrome processes with the fleet empty and concluded the machine was loud.
Counted again with a 5-second per-process CPU census at this tick:

    TOTAL BUSY: 2.56 cores of 24 — the box is about 89% idle.
    node + chrome COMBINED: 0.135 cores across 21 processes showing any CPU at all.
    Largest single consumer: the editor, at 1.329 cores. My own agent processes: ~0.4.

The residue is REAL and IDLE. Presence is not load, and a process count answers presence. So I
replaced one wrong proxy — the fleet count — with another wrong proxy one level down, in a note
whose entire argument was that proxies for machine state should be distrusted. This reproduces the
topoclock worker's independent census almost exactly (2.29 busy of 24, one editor language service
at 1.07, all agent processes 0.52), which is corroboration rather than coincidence.

WHAT SURVIVES FROM THAT NOTE, because not all of it was wrong: an empty fleet genuinely is not
evidence about the machine, and the machine genuinely should be measured at both brackets rather
than inferred. What does not survive is the conclusion I drew — that the box was loud. It was idle
then and it is idle now. The instrument to use is LOAD, not a count of anything.
*** AWAITING MIKE - NOT DISPATCHABLE. *** Banner added 2026-08-22 21:48 AUSEST by the dispatch tick. This
bead's hold was already recorded at length and correctly; what it lacked was the phrase a scan
finds, so every tick re-derived it by reading the notes end to end.

THE HOLD, restated from this bead's own newest note and not re-reasoned: NOT the machine fence.
That framing was retracted here already. What holds it is the standing ruling that quiet boxes are
the scarce pre-P2 resource and belong to the operator's chosen lane - so the box is not to be spent
here even if it were idle. What is owed is a RULING that this measurement is worth taking.

DISCHARGED BY: Mike deciding the 91-92 B/read term is worth a window. The execution precondition the
description names (a quiet box, p0_run.cjs --only ladder, 6 rounds, both donors as same-run controls)
is a condition on EXECUTION to be re-established at that time, not part of this hold.

WHOEVER DISCHARGES THIS STRIKES THIS BANNER IN THE SAME ACT.

comments.text: FENCE REFINED (mayor, 2026-08-14). I had fenced the whole measurement lane behind one-window-at-a-time. rf2-hic-045's worker reported — unprompted, and put it on its own published page — that a DETERMINISTIC COUNTER census does not need a quiet box at all: every monotone counter reads the same on a loaded machine, per budgets section 2. So the fence should follow the ESTIMAND, not the bead label. If this bead's deliverable is counters, structural censuses or work-unit counts, it can be scheduled freely and in parallel. If it is wall-clock, a ratio of durations, or allocation bytes with a predicted band, it needs the quiet box and Shape 6 in full. WHOEVER TAKES IT: state which half you are measuring before you ask for the box, and split the bead's halves if they differ — rf2-hic-036 and rf2-hic-045 both published a counter half and refused a clock half, and their workers found that seam themselves.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DEFERRAL LIFTED — MIKE 2026-08-14: 'I want hicasso fully implemented, nothing deferred. I want a complete library. I want a sophisticated library.'

This bead was parked under the earlier direction to run measurement later. That direction is superseded. It is now live work.

ONE PHYSICAL CONSTRAINT REMAINS AND IS NOT A DEFERRAL. A clock estimand needs a quiet box: one measurement at a time, controls arbitrating, no other worker compiling. That is a property of the instrument, not a scheduling preference — a reading taken against six concurrent compiles measures the fleet, not the library. COUNTER estimands have no such constraint; monotone counters read the same on a loaded box, which is why the deterministic censuses landed while the clock tables did not.

SO THE PLAN IS: build every instrument NOW, in parallel, on a loaded box — that work is edit-shaped and unconstrained. Then run the windows themselves back to back when the fleet is idle. That is the same split that produced rf2-w01c from rf2-hic-036 and rf2-d6ai8 from rf2-hic-088, and it means the quiet-box time is spent measuring rather than writing drivers.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWES, restated: if it needs an instrument that does not exist, that half dispatches immediately. If the instrument exists and only the window is missing, it queues for the next quiet period. Whoever picks it up should say which case it is in the first paragraph of its report.

title: Consolidate 73 ad-hoc IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT set/restore sites onto one shared fixture
description:
Carried over from rf2-76lhy step 2, which closed on PR #7190 having delivered step 1 (the capture-time profile). This half was never done and should not be lost with the parent.

73 test files set and restore the process-global IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT by hand, with no shared fixture. A test that throws between the set and the restore leaks the flag into every subsequent namespace in the bundle - a cross-namespace coupling that no assertion can catch and that only shows up as unexplained slowness or flakiness later in the run.

IMPORTANT CONTEXT, so this is not over-sold. rf2-76lhy originally advanced the leak as the explanation for a suspected 3-4x CI slowdown. The per-namespace profile shipped in PR #7190 dissolved that: 73% of the lane's wall clock is 7 benchmark namespaces, the three recorded CI stop points all sit at 92-97% of the lane, and the CI/local gap is a uniform ~1.7x. There is no longer evidence pointing at the leak.

So this is a HYGIENE bead, not a bug hunt. It retires a real hazard class on its own terms - one use-fixtures with the restore in a finally - and it is worth doing, but nothing is currently known to be broken by it. Size it accordingly and do not let it grow into an audit.

Fenced away from the PR #7190 runner work; this is implementation/**/test/** across many artefacts, so it wants its own dispatch.
notes:
INVESTIGATED, NOT DONE (PR #7193 worker, 2026-07-28). Recommendation: leave it, or do it per-artefact later. This is the honest 'not worth doing now'.

CENSUS IS BIGGER THAN THE BEAD SAYS: 78 files, 175 `set!` sites, across NINE trees — freehand 43, ui 15, adapters 7, ssr 6, tools/story 2, tools/machines-viz 2, machines 1, core 1, scripts 1. Not 73, and not one artefact.

THERE IS NO SMALL, OBVIOUSLY-CORRECT CONSOLIDATION TO ADOPT. The nearest existing shared fixture is `re-frame.ui.test/act-operation!`, which already does exactly the right thing (reads the prior value, sets true, restores the PRIOR value — not `false` — after React settles). But it lives in implementation/ui/SRC, a published and EXPERIMENTAL artefact surface. Adopting it from freehand / ssr / adapters / machines test trees would make those artefacts' tests depend on re-frame.ui. That is an architectural decision, not hygiene, and it is Mike's. The alternative — mint a new shared test-support surface every artefact may require — is also a decision, not a sweep.

WHAT DOES EXIST is per-artefact convergence: freehand already has mount_support.cljs and bench/b6_harness.cljs; ssr has SIX files carrying byte-identical `disable-act-env!`/`restore-act-env!` pairs. So the tractable shape is PER-ARTEFACT, ONE PR EACH — freehand first (43 of the 78 files, landing spot already present), then ssr (6 files, pure duplication), then ui.

WHY NOT NOW. (1) The motivation is gone: PR #7190's profile dissolved the 3-4x CI-slowdown hypothesis this was step 2 of, and PR #7193 confirmed it on a second box — the whole gap was seven benchmark namespaces (71% of the browser lane's wall clock), and the CI factor is a uniform ~1.7x. There is still no observed instance of the leak. (2) A 78-file mechanical edit across nine trees is a maximal merge-conflict change against every open PR touching a mounted test. (3) Every one of those trees was outside PR #7193's fence, so it could not have been done there in any case.

If someone does pick it up: rule FIRST on whether re-frame.ui.test's act door may be the repo-wide answer, because that ruling decides whether this is one shared fixture or nine private ones.
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-28, dossier review):

DECISION — leave the sweep undone now; bead DEFERRED. No 78-file mechanical edit during the current mounted-test churn: the motivating CI-slowdown hypothesis was dissolved by measurement (seven benchmark namespaces + a uniform ~1.7x CI factor), and the sweep is a maximal merge-conflict change against every open mounted-test PR. Pick this up only when the high-conflict Freehand work settles AND either a real leak instance bites or an artefact's mounted tests are being reworked anyway — then land it artefact-sized, not repo-wide.

RECORD CORRECTION (from the Codex second opinion; commits verified in this checkout): "no observed instance" is true of the PERFORMANCE theory only. Flag leakage itself has occurred and been repaired — 43ce4cf9f6 and 1fff5b618b (shared-page act-discipline, ~361 warnings) and 0dd432b9ed (un-restored act boundary after a negative-control run, 755 warnings). The hazard class is real and observed; the slowdown attribution is what was disproved. P3 stands.

ARCHITECTURAL ANSWER (binding — do not re-litigate):
1. DONOR DEPENDENCY FORBIDDEN. No artefact's tests may require re-frame.ui (src or test): F6e deletes the artefact, and re-frame.ui.test/act-operation! is a private defn- coupled to donor internals in any case. Its invariant is the SHAPE to copy, never the namespace to require: capture the incoming flag value and restore the PRIOR value — not a blanket false — on every exit path (synchronous throw, Promise fulfilment, Promise rejection).
2. ONE repo-private implementation, NOT nine per-artefact copies. Home: the existing lightweight dependency-free shared surface implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_test_support.cljs (or a narrowly named sibling in the same core/test root). Verified: it is already required across an artefact boundary today (adapters/uix test) and sits on the consolidated Shadow classpath, so this mints no new architecture and survives F6e. Per-artefact is the DELIVERY boundary — artefact-sized PRs, freehand first (43 files, through its existing mount_support.cljs facade), ssr second (6 byte-identical disable/restore pairs) — not the implementation boundary. Nine permanent copies would reproduce at repo scale exactly the drift ssr's six copies already demonstrate.
3. Design floor for whoever lands it (from Codex, ratified): the helper takes the desired mode — both true (act-disciplined renders) and false (timing discriminators, hydration, deliberate un-acted negative controls) are legitimate, so no runner-wide constant. One save/restore engine with thin sync-wrapping and async-map fixture adapters (cljs.test forbids mixing the two fixture kinds; async tests need the map form) plus a Promise-aware operation bracket for callbacks that reject before done; overlapping async scopes rejected or serialized. Leave re-frame.ui.test self-contained until F6e and skip migrating ui test files the deletion gate removes.

Disposition: deferred (was open P3). Reopen against the conditions above.

RULING 2026-09-02 10:23:48 AUSEST (delegated by Mike 2026-09-02, dossier review; ai/decisions/rf2-3t2nq.act-environment-fixture-home.md folded here and deleted — THIS NOTE IS THE CANONICAL RECORD). Tip at ruling: b26c5ad33e.

HOLD STRUCK — the placement question "held for Mike" in the 2026-08-21 comment is discharged by this ruling.

DECISION — CLOSE AS MINUTIAE. No fixture sweep, no hicasso-only dedupe, no publish on re-frame.test-support, no further deferral. Three findings carry it, each re-measured at tip b26c5ad33e rather than inherited from the bead's earlier numbers:

(1) The hazard the bead is written around — a throw between a set and a restore leaking the flag bundle-wide — has ONE candidate site in the whole repo, and it is not in hicasso. Repo-wide there are exactly two prior-value restores: implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:3280/3351 (act-prev, restored under `finally`) and implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/ssr_startup_recipe_dom_cljs_test.cljs:218-223 (prev, restored by `teardown!` at :243, called from the async continuation at :306 — NOT under `finally`; see PREMISE CORRECTIONS). Every one of the 43 `set!` lines under implementation/hicasso sets `false`; zero restore anything. There is no restore in that tree for a throw to skip.

(2) What the flag does makes the residual "hazard" a warning-policy leak, not a scheduler or timing leak (Codex's semantic correction, accepted — see WEIGHING). A `false` left behind suppresses "not wrapped in act" warnings in later tests of the same browser build; it does not defer renders or change what a test measures. The three repaired incidents the 2026-07-28 ruling cited (43ce4cf9f6, 1fff5b618b, 0dd432b9ed) were warning-state repairs of a `true` leaking across the shared page, consistent with that reading.

(3) What is left is a two-line duplicated helper (`leave-act-environment!` at checkpoint_support.cljs:161 and roots_frames_support.cljs:82) whose stated reason for existing twice — the freeze gate forbidding a `:require` of the bench helper — was retired by 8a10915ed8 on 2026-08-29, and whose 35 callers split 22/13 for structural reasons: 34 of the 35 use other functions from the same support namespace, and exactly one (state_dom_cljs_test.cljs) requires checkpoint-support solely for the setter. A dedupe would touch ~35 files in the repo's hottest test tree to remove one redundant require and one redundant defn, retiring no hazard. That is the trade that got the 2026-08-21 lift withdrawn, and the stance (pre-alpha, trust the programmer, do not drown in minutiae) says close it rather than action it.

The placement question that was held for Mike needs no ruling. The repo-private cross-artefact home implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_test_support.cljs already exists, is dependency-free (requires only clojure.string), sits on the consolidated Shadow classpath beside hicasso/test (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:34 "core/test", :137 "hicasso/test"), and is required today from three places: implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/reg_view_devtools_dom_cljs_test.cljs, implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_source_coord_dom_elision_prod_test.cljs and implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs. "Can hicasso's tests reach a core test-support namespace" is yes, today, without publishing anything. The 2026-07-28 ARCHITECTURAL ANSWER (items 1-3: no donor dependency; one repo-private implementation in that home; the save/restore design floor) stands as the SHAPE for any act-environment fixture that is ever genuinely needed; nothing here overturns it. What this ruling adds is that no such fixture is needed now, and the trigger for one is a diagnostic-policy decision, not this bead.

HOW THE OPINIONS WERE WEIGHED

Dossier author (sections "Summary" through "Evidence"; recommends A, close). Accepted on its main line: the census both ways, the disproven hazard, the drifted docstrings, the dead freeze gate, the existing home, and the rejection of C. Two of its facts are corrected at tip below: "both restore brackets are correct" (the ssr one restores the prior value but is not throw-safe) and "one parameterised on? helper" (there are two, one of them prose in docs). Its option B ("rule the home and dispatch a hicasso-only dedupe") is described as viable and it is, but its own cost line — a wide mechanical diff for zero hazard retired — is why it loses.

Codex ("Codex Recommendation"; also recommends close, and adds "do not dispatch a standalone hicasso dedupe as a substitute"). Weighed heavily on three points, each re-measured here rather than taken on trust. (a) The semantic correction: IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT is React's `isConcurrentActEnvironment()` predicate gating the "not wrapped in act" warnings, while the act queue is `ReactSharedInternals.actQueue`, controlled by `act()` itself. I did not re-read React's source; the citation (ReactFiberAct.js at the v19.2.0 tag, matching the installed react-dom 19.2.0) is specific and consistent with the three repaired incidents, and it changes the disposition in no direction, so it is recorded as Codex's reading, accepted. It DOES sharpen one thing the worker and the mayor both wrote: "a finally-restore would re-enter the act environment and change behaviour" overstates it — a restore would change later WARNING policy, not scheduling — but the conclusion survives, because the hicasso disable is a deliberate lane-wide policy with nothing anyone wants to restore to. (b) The caller split is structural, not arbitrary: verified at tip, 35 callers, 34 use other functions from their chosen support namespace, one (state_dom_cljs_test.cljs, alias `checkpoint`) does not. This overturns the worker's 2026-08-21 claim that native_abi_dom_cljs_test, foreign_root_bridge_dom_cljs_test, imperative_sdk_dom_cljs_test and native_hooks_dom_cljs_test require the multi-root harness SOLELY for the setter: the first and fourth no longer exist under any tracked path, and the second and third use cell-keys / make-reset-runtime-fixture / skip! and census / poll-until / released / teardown-census! respectively. The "latent wart in the converted half" is one file, not a class. (c) The freeze-gate residue is wider than the two docstrings — nine lines across nine hicasso test files by `freeze gate|freeze-gate` at tip (Codex counted ten) — and is independent of where the setter bodies live. Codex's reframing of any future work as "warning-state isolation, not scheduler fixture" is adopted below as the reopening condition.

Where the two disagree: the dossier presents B as a live option that a later irritation could justify; Codex says a dedupe would "centralise the spelling of a global write without establishing a correct shared policy for that global" and must not be done as a substitute for the real question. Codex's position is the one recorded, with one preservation of the dossier's view: if somebody is ALREADY refactoring both support namespaces, folding the two defns into one is a free by-product and needs no bead (recipe below). It is not worth a dispatch on its own.

The worker's 2026-08-21 refusal and the mayor's 05:20 acceptance are both upheld in substance; the mayor's "one genuine item" (the arbitrary split) is what this ruling downgrades, on Codex's measurement, from "real wart, held for Mike" to "one file, not worth a ruling". Dissent preserved: the 2026-08-18 comment's case for keeping the bead open ("closing would discard a real hazard on the grounds it has not bitten yet") was written before the value histogram existed; it is answered by (1) and (2) above, not dismissed. The 2026-07-28 RECORD CORRECTION that "flag leakage itself has occurred and been repaired" stays true and is re-characterised as warning-state leakage, not withdrawn.

Recipe if a dedupe is ever wanted (only as a by-product of real work in those two support namespaces, never as a standalone dispatch): keep ONE definition — either roots_frames_support.cljs:82 (13 callers, the fuller docstring) or, if the setter is wanted cross-artefact, a `leave-act-environment!` added to implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_test_support.cljs per the 2026-07-28 design item 2; delete the other package copy; re-point its callers (22 files if checkpoint-support's copy goes, 13 if roots-frames-support's); rewrite both docstrings to drop the freeze-gate citation (say instead: set outright because the bench is a separate Shadow project off this classpath, and the disable is lane-wide policy — warnings off, not scheduling). Gate: hicasso's own `npm run test:cljs` from implementation/ (heavyweight, browser), plus the usual CI. Sequence it against any open PR touching implementation/hicasso/test/**.

What would make new act-environment work worth doing — and it would be a NEW bead titled for warning-state isolation, briefed from this note, not a reopening of this one: (i) an observed cross-test act-warning leak that someone has to chase; (ii) a decision to make act warnings uniformly ON by default in the browser runner (today the shared :browser-test runner leaves whatever the last suite set); or (iii) a fixture refactor already touching these suites. Under any of those, first pin the runner default, then provide exact-prior-value brackets for both `true` and deliberately-`false` regions covering sync throw, promise fulfilment and promise rejection — the 2026-07-28 design floor (item 3) is the spec for that helper and it still holds.

Rejected options, one line each. B (rule the home, dispatch a ~35-file hicasso dedupe now): viable, but removes one redundant require and one redundant defn for zero hazard, in the hottest test tree — the trade already refused on 2026-08-21. C (publish on re-frame.test-support): core/src ships in the jar; a CLJS-only React test flag is not a published API, and pre-alpha is when the surface stays small. D (stay deferred with conditions): the bead's premise is disproven and its census has mis-briefed two passes already; a hold with no hazard behind it is a trap for the next backlog reread, not a plan. The original sweep (one fixture with restore-in-finally across all sites): the sites are deliberate lane-wide disables; a restoring fixture is the wrong shape for them and there is nothing to restore to.

FOLLOW-UPS — none filed. The nine-file stale freeze-gate prose is incidental cleanup for whoever next edits those files; the ssr non-finally restore is a one-line change with no observed symptom; neither clears the bar for a bead. Sibling beads under other rulings this pass (rf2-zq34m, rf2-4a0c, rf2-7rzg, rf2-8arzr, rf2-ahjbc, rf2-y8jjk, rf2-lau0u, rf2-kmqx3, rf2-uelji, rf2-y1jkm, rf2-8urba, rf2-hic-063) were not touched.

MAYOR 2026-08-18, BACKLOG REREAD — THIS IS A DEFERRAL WITH NO DATE AND NO STATED RELEASE CONDITION, WHICH IS THE ONE SHAPE THAT NEVER GETS RE-EXAMINED. Giving it a condition rather than a date, so a future tick can test it.

THE STATE I FOUND: status DEFERRED, defer_until NONE, untouched since 2026-07-28. Of ten deferred beads it is one of only two with no date at all; the other (rf2-2hpxo) has a real condition written into it — API-freeze. This one had neither.

THE BEAD IS HONEST ABOUT ITS OWN VALUE AND I AM NOT OVERRIDING THAT. It says so itself: rf2-76lhy originally advanced the flag leak as the explanation for a suspected 3-4x CI slowdown, and PR #7190's per-namespace profile DISSOLVED that — 73% of the lane's wall clock is 7 benchmark namespaces, the three recorded CI stop points sit at 92-97% of the lane, and the CI/local gap is a uniform ~1.7x. 'There is no longer evidence pointing at the leak.' It is a HYGIENE bead, and it says so.

SO WHY NOT CLOSE IT AS MINUTIAE. Because the hazard class is real and is exactly the kind this project takes seriously: a test that throws between the set and the restore leaks a process-global into every subsequent namespace in the bundle, and NO ASSERTION CAN CATCH IT — it surfaces later as unexplained slowness or flakiness, which is the hardest possible failure to attribute. The remedy is small and correct: one use-fixtures with the restore in a finally. Closing it would discard a real hazard on the grounds that it has not bitten yet.

THE RELEASE CONDITION, which is what was missing: DISPATCH THIS WHEN THE FLEET IS QUIET — no more than one other worker out, and no open PR touching implementation/ test namespaces. NOT because it is risky, but because 73 test files across the tree is the largest merge-conflict surface any single bead in this backlog carries, and a mechanical sweep that has to rebase past several landings will cost more in conflicts than the change is worth. Measured context for that: on 2026-08-18 the fleet ran 6 workers with 5 PRs open and the trunk moved 11 commits inside one worker's run.

SIZE IT WHEN IT GOES OUT: 73 files is above the single-dispatch comfort line here, so expect to split by artefact rather than send one worker at all of them.

NOT A NEW DEFERRAL DATE — deliberately. A date would fire on a day that may be just as busy. The condition is about fleet state, and the backlog-reread loop is the tick that can test it.

comments.text:
WORKER worker/actenv-3t2nq, 2026-08-21 03:30 AUSEST — REFUSAL for the dispatched
artefact, with the measurement. NO code change; no PR. The bead stays open.

The dispatched scope reproduces EXACTLY: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/**
carries 45 files / 51 raw `set!` sites at tip. Nothing below disputes that count. What
the count MEANS is what changed.

FOUR OF THE FIVE PREMISES DO NOT HOLD IN THIS TREE.

1. THERE ARE NO SET/RESTORE PAIRS. All 51 in-scope sites are
   `(set! (.-IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT js/globalThis) false)`. Zero set `true`; zero
   restore anything; zero `finally` within six lines of any site (checked per file by
   awk, and by a value histogram taken two independent ways). So the hazard the bead is
   written around — "a test that throws between the set and the restore leaks the flag"
   — HAS NO INSTANCE HERE. There is no restore for a throw to skip.

   Repo-wide the pattern is nearly as rare: of 90 raw `set!` lines, 66 set `false`, 22
   set `true`, and exactly TWO restore a captured prior value —
   implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:3351 and
   implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/ssr_startup_recipe_dom_cljs_test.cljs:223. Both
   are outside hicasso. The set/restore bracket the bead describes is 2 of 90 sites
   repo-wide, in two files, in two other artefacts.

2. THE PACKAGE ALREADY HAS THE SHARED HELPER, AND MOST OF THE TREE ALREADY USES IT.
   `leave-act-environment!` is defined at checkpoint_support.cljs:161 and
   roots_frames_support.cljs:76, and 34 files / 38 call sites in this very tree already
   call it. Repo-wide there are 98 converted call sites — 59 in the bench tree, 38 in
   the hicasso package, 1 in core. The tree is roughly 43% consolidated already
   (38 converted vs 51 raw), not 0%.

3. THE CENSUS METHOD UNDERCOUNTS BY CONSTRUCTION, and this is the correction that
   reframes the bead. A CONVERTED site does not contain the literal
   `IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT` — it reads `(support/leave-act-environment!)`. So
   `git grep IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT` measures the UNCONVERTED TAIL, never the
   population. The recorded "69 files / 100 sites, nine trees" is a remainder. The real
   population is that remainder plus 98 already-converted call sites, and the shape of
   the remaining work is "finish a migration already 50%+ done", not "introduce a
   fixture into a tree that has none".

4. THE SPECIFIED BAR CANNOT BE MET WITHOUT A BEHAVIOUR CHANGE. "One shared fixture with
   the restore in a `finally`" would RE-ENTER the act environment after each test. Every
   docstring in the tree says the disable is deliberate and LANE-WIDE, not a bracket:
   roots_frames_support.cljs:76-85 — "React's `act` queue is not the browser's scheduler,
   and every reading in these suites is taken outside it — a commit measured here is the
   commit a user's page performs." A `finally`-restore would contradict that and would
   violate the dispatch's own "no behaviour change" requirement. The one restoring idiom
   in the repo (ssr) captures the PRIOR value rather than forcing `true`/`false`, which
   is right for a bracketed region and wrong for a lane.

   The fifth premise — that the population might be heterogeneous — is wrong in the safe
   direction: it is perfectly homogeneous. 51 of 51 set `false`.

WHY FINISHING THE MIGRATION IS NOT A SMALL, OBVIOUSLY-CORRECT CONSOLIDATION.

The two helper definitions are byte-identical and the 34 existing callers split between
them with no principle: 22 files take it from checkpoint-support (THE MICROTASK-CHECKPOINT
INSTRUMENT), 12 from roots-frames-support (THE MULTI-ROOT WITNESS HARNESS). Several
already require a heavyweight, purpose-specific harness namespace SOLELY to reach a
two-line flag setter — native_abi_dom_cljs_test, foreign_root_bridge_dom_cljs_test,
imperative_sdk_dom_cljs_test and native_hooks_dom_cljs_test all require the multi-root
witness harness for exactly that. That is a latent wart in the converted half.

Of the 45 raw files, only 8 already require one of the two support namespaces (a free
one-line conversion). The other 37 would each GAIN a `:require` on a namespace whose
stated purpose is unrelated to theirs — deepening that wart 37 more times rather than
fixing it.

Doing it PROPERLY means minting one canonical act-env home, deleting both duplicate
definitions, re-pointing all 34 existing callers AND converting the 45 raw files: ~80
files in the tree, for ZERO hazard retired, against a tree with live peers. That is the
same maximal merge-conflict change with no motivating defect that got this bead deferred
in the first place, merely confined to one artefact. Per the stance — reject
over-engineering, close minutiae rather than actioning it — I am refusing it rather than
landing it.

ANSWER TO THE QUESTION THE DISPATCH ASKED (reusable, or hicasso-specific?)

In SUBSTANCE the helper is not hicasso-specific at all — it is a two-line global setter
with a docstring. In PLACEMENT it is, and that is the whole difficulty. It lives in the
hicasso package TEST tree, which the other eight artefacts have no business importing
(and which the freeze gate already fences in the other direction:
frozen-sources.edn :forbidden-import-prefixes ["re-frame.bench." "re-frame.freehand."]).
A repo-wide answer therefore needs a shared home every test tree can reach. The only
existing candidate is `re-frame.test-support` — but that is
implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc, inside core's `:paths ["src"]`, i.e.
a PUBLISHED surface. Putting a test-only React flag setter there is exactly the
architectural decision PR #7193 flagged and left to Mike, and it is unchanged by the
re-frame.ui / re-frame.freehand retirement. So: NOT reusable as it stands, and making it
reusable is Mike's call, not hygiene.

REMAINING RAW `set!` CENSUS AT TIP (files / sites, .beads excluded)

  implementation/hicasso (package)   45 / 51   <- dispatched scope, refused above
  implementation/adapters             7 / 13
  implementation/core                 2 /  9
  implementation/ssr                  2 /  3
  tools/xray                          3 /  3
  implementation/routing              2 /  2
  implementation/machines             1 /  2
  tools/machines-viz                  2 /  2
  implementation/hicasso (bench)      2 /  2
  tools/story                         1 /  1
  implementation/hicasso (test_kit)   1 /  1
  implementation/hicasso (testbed)    1 /  1
                                     ---------
                                     69 / 90

  (90 raw `set!` lines. The recorded "100 sites" counts every LINE mentioning the
  literal, which includes ten that are not `set!` calls — docstring and comment prose
  explaining why the flag is set outright. In the dispatched scope the same split is
  54 mentions / 51 `set!` calls / 3 prose lines.)

RECOMMENDATION

Retire the bead's hazard framing rather than the sites. As written it describes a
set/restore leak that exists in 2 sites repo-wide, neither in hicasso. What actually
remains is a half-finished DRY migration with no defect behind it and no shared home
available without a published-surface ruling. Either close it as minutiae, or re-file the
narrow real item: "hicasso has two byte-identical `leave-act-environment!` definitions and
callers split arbitrarily between them" — which is a genuine wart, but a ~35-file
re-point, and still retires no hazard.

Gates: none run, and none needed — no file was modified. The box was also not free
(24 node processes, three started within the minute), so a heavyweight CLJS suite would
have been the wrong thing to start regardless.

title: Grow the 009 ratchet by a Tags-column keys-set diff (NOT a trace-op arm) — ruled after rf2-wsopx
description:
MAYOR RULING: YES, and only the Tags arm (2026-07-26). The rf2-wsopx worker recommended this and asked rather than filing it, per its brief. I am adopting its reasoning as filed.

WHY THIS IS WORTH BUILDING AT ALL: the 009 ratchet pins the Channel column and the error/warning emit sites — not trace ops and NOT the Tags column. That blind spot is why spec/009 never received the EP-0037 planner rows: :rf.route/prefetched appeared ZERO times in the catalogue while shipping, and :rf.error/resource-route-plan Tags column omitted both :plan-cause and :contributor while its narrative still taught partial planning against the ratified atomicity rule. A gate whose coverage never reaches the column where drift accumulates will keep reporting green over it.

THE RULED SHAPE — Tags-column keys-set diff, and nothing else: Spec-Schemas.md ALREADY defines one *Tags schema per catalogue row, and both files are ALREADY parsed by existing gates. So the arm is a keys-set comparison between the schema and the row, which the worker describes as "a parser away". It would have caught the Tags omission directly.

WHY NOT THE TRACE-OP ARM, which is the tempting other half: there is no per-op schema roster to diff against, so the only available check is "is every emitted op documented somewhere in 2500 lines of prose?" — a scan with a bad false-positive rate. That is the expensive half for the weaker signal, and this repo has already learned that a census whose pattern cannot distinguish a correction from a defect will fight every fix. Declined.

CONSTRAINTS: extend the EXISTING gate, do not add a new script. No new vocabulary. If the keys-set diff turns out to need a second source of truth to be meaningful, STOP and report — a gate needing a hand-maintained roster is the drift generator this repo keeps removing (see the derived evidence-producer roster that ended its class after going stale twice by hand-copying).

NON-VACUITY IS MANDATORY: prove the arm reds against the PRE-rf2-wsopx catalogue state, where :plan-cause and :contributor were genuinely missing from the row. An arm that cannot red on the defect that motivated it has not been tested — and this repo has shipped exactly that mistake before, where an audit method could not have caught its own motivating instance.

title: skills/README.md claims every spec/authoring-prompt.md defers on leaf size; two restate the figures
description:
Found while executing rf2-wh25 (PR #9065), which was scoped to skills/README.md only, so this was reported rather than fixed.

skills/README.md:237-238 states: 'Single source of truth for the per-leaf size ceiling - per-skill spec/authoring-prompt.md files defer here instead of restating.'

Measured across all 8 spec/authoring-prompt.md files, two RESTATE the numbers rather than defer:

  skills/re-frame2-implementor/spec/authoring-prompt.md:16  'leaf-size discipline (each leaf <=250 lines AND <=16 KB)'
  skills/re-frame2-implementor/spec/authoring-prompt.md:39  'Every leaf <=250 lines and <=16 KB.'
  skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/authoring-prompt.md:49         '<=250 lines AND <=16 KB; catalogue-shaped leaves (ops.md, recipes.md) may run longer where a split would not reduce tokens-per-session'

The other six defer correctly by link or pointer (re-frame2-setup, re-frame2, re-frame-migration are the explicit ones).

NOTHING IS STALE TODAY. rf2-wh25 deliberately did not move the 250-line or 16 KB figures, so the restatements still agree with the README. The pair one additionally carries its own catalogue carve-out, which is consistent with the README's - and is arguably useful locally. So this is a single-source-of-truth accuracy nit, not a live defect: the exposure is that a FUTURE change to either figure now has three places to update, and the README says there is one.

Two defensible dispositions, a maintainer's call:
  (a) make the two prompts defer (delete the restated figures, point at skills/README.md#leaf-size-discipline), or
  (b) soften the README's line to say the figures MAY be restated locally but the README governs.

Low priority - the numbers are not expected to move, and rf2-wh25 ruled they stay.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 08:0x AUSEST. TAKE DISPOSITION (a): MAKE THE TWO PROMPTS DEFER. DO NOT SOFTEN THE README.

I CONSIDERED CLOSING THIS AS MINUTIAE AND DECIDED AGAINST IT, so the reasoning is recorded rather than the verdict alone. The stance says not to litigate every last fine detail, and this bead argues its own case honestly: nothing is stale today, the restatements still agree, and the pair's local carve-out is arguably useful. That is a real argument for closing.

WHAT DECIDES IT THE OTHER WAY IS THAT THE README'S SENTENCE IS FALSE, NOT MERELY UNTIDY. It says "per-skill spec/authoring-prompt.md files defer here instead of restating", and two of eight do not. That is the same class of defect this project has just chosen to fix twice in a week on beads of the same size: rf2-yk2d, a code comment making measurably false claims, and rf2-sy1l, a classification reason asserting something untrue. Closing this one while fixing those two would be inconsistent, and the inconsistency would be invisible later.

(a) OVER (b) FOR ONE REASON: (b) makes the README describe the mess, (a) removes it. Softening the line to "figures MAY be restated locally but the README governs" buys a sentence that is true and a rule that is worse — three places to update and a written licence to add a fourth. (a) makes the claim true and leaves ONE source of truth, which is what the section is for.

THE PAIR'S CATALOGUE CARVE-OUT IS THE ONE JUDGEMENT CALL INSIDE (a). skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/authoring-prompt.md:49 restates the figures AND adds its own catalogue carve-out naming ops.md and recipes.md. Delete the restated FIGURES; whether the local carve-out survives is the worker's call on reading both texts — it names specific local leaves, which the README cannot, so keeping it as prose that carries no numbers is legitimate.
