"WORKTREE-LOCAL" IS ONLY HALF THE RULE FOR WORKER SCRATCH FILES — IT MUST ALSO BE GITIGNORED (2026-08-09).

THE SEQUENCE. Earlier in the day two concurrent workers overwrote each other's helper files and PR-body drafts in the SHARED scratchpad, and one nearly published another bead's PR body. The fix put into later briefs was "write every file you create inside your own worktree". Both workers complied exactly. Both worktrees then REFUSED to reap: REMOVE_REFUSED_DIRTY, each holding one untracked pr-body-<bead>.md that the disposability classifier will not accept as build output.

SO THE TWO HAZARDS TRADE OFF AND THE BRIEF MUST CLOSE BOTH. dispatch-prompt-template.md already says it: put EVERY gate artefact where git ignores it, and warns that one leftover is enough to make a tree unreapable (nine accumulated that way once). The ignored extensions are *.log, *.exit and *-exit.txt. A file named pr-body-something.md is worktree-local, safe from collision, and still blocks the reap.

THE COMPLETE INSTRUCTION FOR A DISPATCH BRIEF: write every file you create inside your own worktree AND give it an ignored name (*.log / *.exit), or delete it before you report done. Never a shared temp directory; never an unignored leftover.

RESOLVING IT WHEN IT HAPPENS IS CHEAP BUT MUST NOT BE BLIND. --dry-run prints each offending path tagged [KEEP] or [build output]; a PR-body draft whose content is already published on the merged PR is genuinely disposable, so --force is correct AFTER looking. Do not reach for --force-disposable (it refuses anything not recognised as build output) and never spray a blanket --force across a sweep list: when that guard was written, one worktree held four analysis files for an OPEN bead and three others carried uncommitted source and doc edits.

A WORKTREE YOU DID NOT EXPLICITLY DISPATCH MAY BE YOUR OWN WORKER SPAWNING A SECOND WORKTREE — not a concurrent session. Misdiagnosed 2026-07-24. I dispatched a 4-bead cluster to ONE worker; it did 3 beads in worktree A (PR one) then created worktree B for the 4th bead (PR two). My hygiene scan found worktree B, had no record of creating it, and I concluded a concurrent session was also dispatching workers. WRONG — it was my own worker branching per bead. THE COST: the false belief made me over-cautious about that surface being externally contested. THE DISCRIMINATOR before concluding concurrent-session: a branch named worker/<desc>-<beadid> whose bead you assigned to a live worker IS that worker, even as a second worktree. Check worker completion reports and open PRs first — a worker report names every worktree and PR it created. Track by BEAD ownership (who did I give this bead to), never by worktree count: one worker is NOT necessarily one worktree or one PR. The genuinely-separate process here (the pr-audit loop) FILES beads, it does not dispatch code-editing workers, so it never contests a code surface. No harm done — I correctly did not touch the worktree or re-dispatch the bead.

A WORKER STRANDS BY ENDING ITS TURN ON A BACKGROUNDED GATE, AND IT WILL DO IT REPEATEDLY UNLESS THE BRIEF SAYS HOW TO WAIT. Observed again 2026-08-08 on rf2-2rtt6.142, twice in a row after a resume.

THE SHAPE. A gate exceeds the tool's foreground time ceiling. The worker detaches it — correctly — and then ENDS ITS TURN "waiting" for a completion notification. Nothing is guaranteed to wake it. It reports "still progressing, continuing to wait", the turn ends, and the same thing happens on the next nudge. The work is usually fine; only the waiting is broken.

WHAT DOES NOT FIX IT: telling the worker again that gates must be foreground. It already believes that, which is exactly why it detached and then waited politely. The instruction it is missing is what to do INSTEAD of waiting.

WHAT FIXES IT — put this in every brief, not just the ones with long gates:
  "If a gate exceeds the tool's time ceiling, run it detached and BLOCK ON IT INSIDE THE SAME TURN by polling its exit file in a loop. Never end a turn with a gate outstanding."
and give the literal shape:
  for i in $(seq 1 240); do [ -f gate-<id>.exit ] && break; sleep 15; done; cat gate-<id>.exit

TWO RIDERS THAT MATTER AS MUCH AS THE LOOP:
- The detached invocation must use an ABSOLUTE path to the gate script. These scripts derive their repo root from BASH_SOURCE, and a relative invocation that gets detached adopts whatever cwd the shell really has — one did that inside ANOTHER live worker's checkout and produced a complete, internally consistent verdict about somebody else's diff. Check the run's "gate root:" first line names your own worktree.
- If the invocation writes no exit file at all, that is the real defect, not the waiting. Re-run as: sh <ABS>/scripts/test-fast-pr.sh > g.log 2>&1; echo "$?" > g.exit

MAYOR-SIDE RECOVERY, cheap and reliable: check the ground truth yourself rather than nudging twice. `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD` and a remote-vs-local sha comparison in the worktree tell you whether the work is durable; `ls *.log *.exit` plus the log's mtime tell you whether the gate is genuinely still running or dead. On this occasion the work was already committed AND pushed, so nothing was at risk — the only outstanding step was reading an exit code.

DO NOT MISREAD THE SPINE LOG WHILE CHECKING. test-fast-pr.sh prints lines like "ok  unexpected extra dependency -> FAILED" from a negative-test harness confirming its own mutations fail correctly. Those are PASSES. The verdict is the echoed exit code, never a line in the log.

WORKER TRAP — git mv then edit (2026-07-25, found by the misc-cluster-a worker on PR #6946): after 'git mv old.cljc new_cljs_test.cljc', a subsequent 'git add <path>' does NOT pick up content edits made after the mv. The worker's first pushed commit therefore carried the RENAMED file with the OLD ns name still inside it — a commit that would not compile. It was caught only by noticing a stray 'M' in git status, then fixed by rebuilding both commits from the base and force-pushing with --force-with-lease. This is the exact shape of the rf2-dn6v7 / rf2-lgozq lane-suffix work (rename file + edit ns in one change), so it will recur. Put in briefs for any rename-plus-edit bead: after a git mv, re-run 'git add' on the path AFTER the content edit, and verify with 'git diff --cached' that BOTH the rename and the content change are staged before committing; a rename-only commit of a .cljc test file is a non-compiling commit.

A FRESH WORKER WORKTREE CANNOT RUN THE FAST-PR SPINE'S NODE TIER WITHOUT THE node_modules JUNCTION (measured 2026-08-13).

A worker on a clean worktree captured exit 1 at 'FAIL CLJS node integration' with 'Cannot find module shadow-cljs/cli/runner.js'. Nothing in its diff could reach shadow-cljs resolution. THE CAUSE WAS THE MISSING implementation/node_modules. Creating the junction turned the SAME spine green with no source change.

SO THE BRIEF'S INSTRUCTION 'run scripts/test-fast-pr.sh' IS INCOMPLETE for a doc-only worker that never expected to need npm. The failure looks like a real red, and a worker that trusts it will hunt a defect that does not exist - or worse, report a red PR as blocked.

SAY THIS IN BRIEFS THAT NOMINATE THE SPINE: if the node tier fails on module resolution, create the implementation/node_modules junction, re-run, and REMOVE THE LINK with cmd /c rmdir as your last act. Never a recursive delete - it follows the junction and empties the mayor's real tree, which has happened twice. Re-verify the canary with the script's own instrument either side.

THE SAME WORKER ALSO HIT THE HARNESS-DISAGREEMENT TRAP ON THAT RUN, which is the sixteenth observed instance: the harness reported 'completed (exit code 0)' while the runner's own .exit file read 1. It quoted the file. Had it trusted the harness it would have shipped a red spine as green. EVERY observed disagreement so far has surfaced as a harness-reported 0.

A FRESH WORKER WORKTREE HAS NO `implementation/node_modules`, AND THE SPINE FAILS ENVIRONMENTALLY THERE — the harness then misreports it (2026-08-11, rf2-gxry).

WHAT HAPPENED. A worker ran `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` in a newly-created worktree. It captured exit **1** on `CLJS node integration`, with `Cannot find module 'shadow-cljs/cli/runner.js'` — nothing compiled, because the worktree had no `node_modules`. **The harness announced "completed (exit code 0)" against that captured 1.** The worker junctioned `node_modules` at the mayor's real one, deleted the stale `.exit` and `.log`, re-ran the gate whole, and captured **0** with `[:node-test] Build completed. (2307 files, 2306 compiled, 0 warnings)`.

THE HAZARD IS NOT THE FAILURE, IT IS THE SHAPE OF IT. A missing-module error is not a test failure, but it PRESENTS as a red gate, and if a worker reads the harness's number instead of the captured one it presents as a GREEN gate over a build that never ran. Both readings are wrong in opposite directions, and the second is the dangerous one: a green that compiled nothing.

WHAT TO PUT IN A BRIEF for any worker that will run a compiling gate:
  - A fresh worktree has NO `implementation/node_modules`. If a gate needs one, create the junction to the mayor's real tree, and REMOVE THE LINK (never its target) as your last act — a later `git worktree remove` follows it and empties the shared tree. Canary the mayor's count before and after.
  - `Cannot find module` or `command not found` from a gate is ENVIRONMENTAL, not a verdict. Fix the environment and RE-RUN THE GATE WHOLE. Do not report the first number, and do not report it as a failure of the diff.
  - DELETE the stale `.exit` and `.log` before the re-run. A stale `.exit` survives the next run's `>` on its log, so the pair can disagree and the older verdict is the one you quote.

TWELFTH SIGHTING TODAY of the harness reporting a captured 1 as exit 0. The rule stands and is now in the method: THE NUMBER YOU QUOTE IS THE ONE YOU CAPTURED.

Worker worktrees have NO node_modules, so browser/shadow-cljs gates cannot run there by default. Do NOT junction into the mayor checkout's node_modules to fix it — that is the configuration that destroyed the mayor's real node_modules once and nearly again. THE SAFE ANSWER IS `npm ci` INSIDE THE WORKTREE (one worker did exactly this today, exit 0, no junction created, canary unmoved). Cost is a few minutes; the alternative is deferring every browser gate to CI. Put this in any brief whose gate menu includes `npm run test:browser`, a shadow-cljs build, or an adapter testbed spec.cjs — otherwise the worker hits 'shadow-cljs is not recognized', concludes the gate is unrunnable, and defers coverage that actually matters (the real-DOM gate catches repaint bugs test:cljs structurally cannot see). Related: [[windows-junction-detection-two-wrong-answers-before-the]].

Workers can get stuck in a monitor-wait loop on slow test suites (rul3ov burned ~770K tokens over 3 segments re-arming a Monitor for the full CLJS conformance run before committing). Recovery: SendMessage the agentId with a firm 'do NOT arm another Monitor — commit FIRST, push, gh pr create NOW; CI runs the full suite so CI is the gate, not your local terminal.' Over-cautious 'won't PR until local green' is the anti-pattern; the PR's CI is the real gate.

CONCURRENT WORKERS SHARE THE SESSION SCRATCHPAD AND OVERWRITE EACH OTHER'S FILES — including PR bodies (2026-08-09).

WHAT HAPPENED. Six workers ran in parallel on the hic-* Wave A set. The rf2-hic-004 worker reported that its verify.py and pr-body.md were BOTH overwritten mid-run by the rf2-hic-005 worker. Same filenames, same shared scratchpad directory. Its PR body survived only because gh had already read the file before the overwrite landed. A slower run would have published another bead's PR body under its own PR number.

WHY THE EXISTING RULE DID NOT COVER IT. The brief said 'use worktree-local log paths', and every worker complied FOR GATE LOGS — they all wrote gate-slugs.log inside their own worktree. The collision was in the HELPER FILES nobody thought to fence: scratch scripts, PR-body drafts, temp verification output. The known hazard was written narrowly as a gate-log hazard; it is really a shared-temp-directory hazard and applies to every file a worker writes outside its worktree.

THE FIX FOR FUTURE BRIEFS. Say: write EVERY file you create - gate logs, helper scripts, PR-body drafts, scratch output - inside your own worktree, never in a shared temp or scratchpad directory. If you must use a shared directory, prefix every filename with your bead id.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A WRONG GATE LOG. A clobbered gate log yields a plausible-but-wrong exit code, which the echo-the-exit-code rule catches. A clobbered PR body is published verbatim to GitHub under the wrong PR and nothing checks it.

THREE WORKERS IN ONE NIGHT STALLED WAITING FOR A "COMPLETION NOTIFICATION" THAT DOES NOT EXIST (2026-08-10).

WHAT THEY EACH DID. rf2-8a6s: "Still running. I'll stop here and resume when the watcher fires - no more polling." rf2-hic-009: "The spine is still running ... I have a waiter armed on its exit code and will report the moment it lands." rf2-hic-016: "The fast-PR spine is still running; I'll wait for its completion notification rather than end the turn" - and then the turn ended. All three had briefs that said, in terms, run gates in the foreground to completion and never background one.

THE BELIEF IS SPECIFIC AND WRONG, WHICH IS WHY THE EXISTING WORDING DOES NOT PREVENT IT. They do not think they are abandoning the task. They think a watcher/notification will wake them. Nothing does. A stopped subagent resumes ONLY when the mayor sends it a message, and the mayor only knows to because the completion report reads oddly. "Run gates in the foreground" does not contradict the belief - a worker can believe it ran the gate in the foreground AND that something will tell it the answer later.

THE WORDING THAT ADDRESSES THE BELIEF, not the behaviour: "There is no completion notification. No watcher wakes a stopped worker. If you end your turn waiting for a gate, the task stops until a human notices. Run the gate in the foreground, block on it, read its exit code yourself. A long foreground gate is fine; an unfinished turn is not."

THE REAL COST IS UNPUSHED WORK, AND IT VARIES. rf2-8a6s had committed AND pushed - fully durable, only the PR was missing. rf2-hic-009 had pushed and opened a PR - only the spine result and PR body were missing. rf2-hic-016 had THREE COMMITS AND HAD NOT PUSHED - one lost worktree from losing an entire three-engine browser suite. So the recovery order is: check `git log origin/main..HEAD` and `git ls-remote` FIRST, and if it is unpushed, make PUSH step 1 of the resume message before anything else.

RECOVERY IS CHEAP AND RELIABLE: SendMessage to the agent id resumes it from its transcript with full context. All three resumed and continued correctly. Do not re-dispatch a fresh worker - it would redo work that is already committed.

DETECTION: a completion report that says "still running", "I'll report when", "waiting for", or "watcher armed" is a stall, not a status. Treat it as a resume trigger immediately, and check push state before replying.

Workers strand because the long gate outlives their TURN budget, not because they disobeyed 'run foreground'. Three workers in one session (dispatch-sync, ci-test-lanes, tags-ratchet) ended their turn mid-gate with 'Waiting on the spine/watcher' — commits pushed, NO PR, nothing mergeable. A brief that says 'run test-fast-pr.sh foreground to completion, THEN open the PR' makes stranding likely on a loaded box, because the spine can exceed the budget. BETTER BRIEF ORDER: commit -> run only the FOCUSED, fast, arm-specific gates (plus any non-vacuity/mutation proof, which is cheap and is the evidence that actually matters) -> OPEN THE PR -> name the slow gates as 'deferred to CI' in the ## Quality gates section. CI runs the same surface and IS the merge gate; the local spine never was. Recovery is SendMessage-resume, which works and keeps the worker's context.

Workflow rule (Mike, 2026-06-10): beads marked in_progress are LOCKED - never update their title/description/notes/scope (a worker is executing against them). To add findings or scope to in-progress work, CREATE A FOLLOW-UP BEAD (dep on the in-progress one if sequenced). Check status with bd show before any bd update.

`git worktree add` CAN BE KILLED BY THE HARNESS FOREGROUND TIMEOUT MID-CHECKOUT, LEAVING A STALE LOCK (2026-08-11; hit by two workers in one tick).

This repo's checkout is ~5308 files, and a fresh `git worktree add` can exceed the harness's 2-minute foreground limit. When it is killed partway (~25% in one observed case) it leaves BOTH a stale `.git/worktrees/<name>/index.lock` AND a `locked` marker reading `initializing`. The worktree exists, is registered, and is unusable; the guard script fails.

RECOVERY, in this order:
1. remove `.git/worktrees/<name>/index.lock`
2. `git reset --hard HEAD` from inside the worktree, BACKGROUNDED - it re-runs the full checkout and took ~9 minutes on this box
3. `git worktree unlock <path>`
Then the worker guard passes normally.

PUT THE MITIGATION IN THE DISPATCH BRIEF: every brief I write opens with `git worktree add`, so this is a first-command failure that costs a worker ten minutes before it has done anything. Tell workers to run the create BACKGROUNDED by absolute path and poll, exactly as they are already told to do for the 25-minute test spine - the same 10-minute ceiling applies to it and nobody expects it to.

Two workers hit this in a single tick (thirdsite-fbi4 and presence-5gka), so it is not rare. Both recovered without data loss, and both reported it rather than silently retrying - which is what made it diagnosable.

Worktree cleanup: a directory can be REUSED and re-pointed at a different branch mid-session, so a name-based safe-list goes stale while you are acting on it. Observed live: a hygiene agent was handed 'ci-test-lanes-cluster - safe to remove, PR #7116 merged', but between the list being written and the removal, a worker reused that same directory on a NEW branch (worker/xray-fuzzy-regression-pin) carrying an open PR #7119. Removing by name would have destroyed an in-flight PR worktree. Re-read `git worktree list --porcelain` IMMEDIATELY BEFORE each removal and re-verify the branch AND its PR state at that moment; never trust a safe-list compiled minutes earlier. Corollary: 'PR merged' is a fact about a BRANCH, not about a DIRECTORY. Related: [[rebase-merge-makes-a-worker-branch-look-unmerged]].

Worktree hygiene: `git status` ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH to decide whether a worktree holds work. The `/ai/` tree is GITIGNORED, so findings docs, gate logs, PR-body drafts and ad-hoc probes are INVISIBLE to git status — a worktree that looks pristine can hold real content. Sweep `ai/` (and any `.worker-logs/`, `.wt-logs/`) separately and READ any non-log file before discarding. Observed: three worktrees held hidden content (20 gate logs, a pr-body.md draft, an ad-hoc probe .clj) — all correctly judged residue, but only because they were looked at. Corollary for the other direction: a hygiene brief that says 'clean tree = safe to remove' is wrong on this repo.

A WORKTREE'S INDEX CLOCK MEASURES THAT WORKTREE, NOT THE FUNCTION IT WAS DISPATCHED FOR (2026-08-24, correcting my own reading across ~six sweeps).

WHAT I HAD BEEN SAYING. Every stranded sweep reported the pr-audit worktree as "alive, polling on a ~40s cadence, index still 11:41, so nothing audited since 11:43". The first half is right. The second half quietly asserted that the AUDIT FUNCTION had produced nothing, and that does not follow.

WHAT THE PARENT CHAIN SHOWS.
* 10ade546c4 "audit PR #8721", 11:43:26, parent ebc7e737bd -- which IS that worktree's HEAD and its branch tip. So that commit was made from that revision, and the index write at 11:41:02, two minutes earlier, is genuine evidence of it staging. That inference was sound.
* d1c824098d "audit PR #8730", 01:22 the next morning, parent 3c9e358a0f -- a revision that worktree has NEVER been at (its branch reflog has exactly two entries: created, then one fast-forward to ebc7e737bd, and `git cherry` reads 0 ahead).

SO AUDITS KEPT HAPPENING WHILE THAT WORKTREE DID NOTHING BUT FETCH. Tonight's audit filed a bead against my own merge and pushed a commit, from a checkout at main's tip, not from there. At least two things perform this role, and the worktree I was watching is not the one that has been working.

THE CORRECTION, and it is about the shape of the claim rather than the number: an index mtime is evidence about ONE CHECKOUT. Reading it as a health signal for the capability that checkout was dispatched to provide is a category error, and it fails in the reassuring direction -- "nothing has been audited" was false every time I said it, while the audit was in fact catching my own defects.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE PARENT CHAIN, not the clock: take a commit the function produced and ask whether its PARENT is a revision that checkout has actually been at. Its branch reflog answers that in one command and cannot be faked by a fetch.

STILL TRUE, and worth keeping: FETCH_HEAD movement proves that worktree is alive (measured twice, 40 seconds apart, against a mayor clock that stayed still), and it remains unreapable and unmessageable because no dispatch row records an agent id for it.

THE 'NEVER WRITE THE WORKTREE PATH INTO A COMMITTED FILE' RULE IS NARROWER THAN THE RISK, AND THE CI GATE DOES NOT CLOSE THE GAP (2026-08-18).

Adopted into mayor dispatch practice on the report of the worker on rf2-f5cma, which was fixing that very rule and is the best-placed reader of it.

THE GAP: a PR body and a bead close reason are both DURABLE and PUBLIC, and neither is a committed file. The 'No hardcoded personal/home paths' CI gate does not see either. So a worker that obeys the rule as written can still publish an absolute home path where it persists. That worker kept paths out of both only by extending the rule on its own initiative.

ADOPTED WORDING for every dispatch: report the printed WORKTREE_ROOT to the mayor in your completion message, and never write it, or any absolute home path, into any COMMITTED FILE, PR BODY OR TRACKER TEXT.

AND CARRY THE POSITIVE FORM, which the template now has and my briefs lagged a revision behind: if the deliverable is itself a written record, what makes the guard evidence is that it RAN and exited 0, not the machine-specific path it printed. A worker told only what not to write still has evidence to produce and will improvise something.

SEPARATE OBSERVATION FROM THE SAME REPORT, not yet actioned: the guard prints an MSYS-style root (/c/Users/...) while the boundary block in every brief states the worktree as C:/Users/.... A worker comparing the two LITERALLY sees a mismatch, on the one rule where a directory-level error is expensive. Every worker so far has resolved it from context. If it ever bites, the fix is to state both forms in the boundary block rather than to change either producer.

GENERAL SHAPE: the worker fixing a rule is the best reviewer of the brief that carries it. Ask. Two of the three improvements here came from asking one worker whether its own setup instruction was well worded.

WRITE EVERY DISPATCH BRIEF TO A FILE BEFORE SENDING IT, BECAUSE THE POSTURE LOOP'S FIDELITY CHECK IS OTHERWISE TESTIMONIAL RATHER THAN MECHANICAL (2026-09-03).

THE PROBLEM. loops.md section 4 asks the mayor to confirm that every dispatch since the last posture tick pasted the stance VERBATIM and carried the boundary and gate-mechanics blocks. If the brief was assembled inline in the Agent call and never written down, there is nothing left to check against afterwards — the mayor's own recollection is the only witness, and a mayor that had summarised the stance would recall having pasted it. That is precisely the failure mode the loop exists to catch, so the check silently degrades to self-report at exactly the moment it matters.

THE FIX IS ONE EXTRA STEP AND IT COSTS NOTHING. Build the brief mechanically into a scratchpad file — stance header, then the extracted preamble / boundary / gates blocks appended, then the task body — and dispatch by telling the worker to read that file as its FIRST action. Then the posture check is three greps with counts, run against bytes that still exist: grep -c on a distinctive line of each block. Anything other than 1 is a defect you can name.

TWO SECOND-ORDER WINS, BOTH REAL. (1) Telling the worker to cat the file is MORE faithful than pasting, because the bytes it reads are the extractor's output rather than anything that passed through the mayor's hands again. (2) The file survives compaction. Measured this session: four dispatches made before a compaction could not be re-verified at all, because their briefs had only ever existed inside the Agent call, and the only surviving evidence was one worker's report happening to describe gate-block-specific behaviour (planted-fault runs, git blob-hash restore). That is corroboration, not verification, and it was luck.

THE ANCHOR-DUPLICATION DETAIL. Repeat the worktree path, branch, base oid, bead ids and the premises-are-claims sentence INLINE in the Agent prompt as well. A worker that fails to read the file then contradicts an anchor visibly instead of improvising a task silently — the failed read becomes detectable rather than silent.

DO NOT read this as licence to skip the extractor. The file is where the extractor's output lands; it is not a substitute for extracting. See never-retype-a-verbatim-block.

WSL bash.exe DOUBLE-EXPANDS a -c command string. Found by rf2-sefx0 (#6357, 2026-07-18) with a decisive probe: bash -lc with FOO=hello then printf of the escaped dollar-FOO prints the literal dollar-FOO under Git Bash (single pass) but prints hello under WSL bash (an outer pass already substituted it). CONSEQUENCE: any -c string that READS BACK a variable the SAME string assigns is broken under WSL — the outer pass substitutes the not-yet-assigned name to empty. That is how a PATH= assignment referencing a FIXTURE_DIR assigned immediately to its left silently produced /bin:<real PATH>, so stub executables were never found and 15 of 15 cases failed before reaching the code under test. Pre-existing vars (PWD, PATH) survive both passes, which is why the bug looks selective. FIX SHAPE: build one env-prefixed command whose every dollar-NAME already exists in the parent environment; let the child script read the rest from its own environment rather than from the command string. DISPROVED on the way: the semicolon separator is fine, and double-quoting is fine — do not chase those. TESTING LESSON (the important half): a BEHAVIOURAL test for this cannot protect you, because Git Bash and the Ubuntu CI runner both expand ONCE — a reintroduced self-reference stays green on CI while breaking only for Windows contributors. sefx0 pinned the STRUCTURE instead (assert the command references only pre-existing variables) with a non-vacuity guard. Generalise: when a defect is invisible on the platform your CI runs, a structural pin beats a behavioural one.

A RULING DETAIL WAS EMPIRICALLY WRONG: notifications CAN arrive before dispatch returns on the stock-Reagent adapter (found 2026-08-07, rf2-ynved).

THE RULING SAID (item 8) that notifications never arrive before dispatch returns. FALSE on this adapter: :flush-render! is (fn [f] (f) (r/flush)), so dispatch-sync DRAINS THE QUEUE ITSELF. A test written to assert the ruling literally went red.

HOW IT WAS HANDLED, and this is the part to copy: the worker did not quietly conform the test to observed behaviour, and did not quietly conform the docs to the ruling. It reported the ruling was wrong, and changed the DOCS to say the re-feed rides a Reagent flush rather than an inline callback inside the app-db write — while telling the author to code as though it lands on the FOLLOWING commit. That last clause is the useful part: teach the WEAKER guarantee even when the stronger one currently holds, because the stronger one is an implementation detail of one adapter.

SECOND FINDING from the same run: a sibling unmount COMMIT re-runs a surviving tracker against an unchanged value, so the survivor takes one idempotent re-feed. The DOM-free counterpart drives the identical release with NO React commit and sees no duplicate. So it is a property of the commit cycle, not of the recipe — and the assertion was rewritten property-based with the reason recorded.

GENERAL RULE: when a test contradicts a recorded ruling, the ruling is a hypothesis like anything else. Report the contradiction, establish which is true FROM THE ADAPTER SOURCE, and fix whichever is actually wrong. Do not assume the ruling wins; do not assume the observation wins.

title: effect-map contract drift: the remaining carriers outside PR #9070's fence (002-Frames, Spec-Schemas, docs/api, Xray, tests, Hicasso)
description:
Split out of rf2-18tt by PR #9070 (worker coretruth-a), which was dispatched with a hard file fence and could correct only the core/src + spec/ half. The implementation is right and unchanged: events.cljc closed-effect-map-keys is SEVEN keys and effect-map-defect refuses a foreign top-level key pre-commit, with no partial commit.

LANDED in #9070 (do not redo): spec/000-Vision.md:113, spec/Ownership.md:32, spec/Implementor-Checklist.md:32, spec/API.md:93 + :480 + the key table at :482-486 (three rows -> seven) + :734, spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2734, and the four core comment/docstring sites in events.cljc (:288-302, :1067), core.cljc (:445-449), interceptor.cljc (:112).

ALREADY CORRECT at that base, measured, leave alone: spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1998 (the error-catalogue row already says "plus the four commit-plane classification keys") and spec/Spec-Schemas.md:724-739 (the canonical schema owner already says "Seven keys" and its Malli EffectMap carries all seven). The drift was never in the schema owner - only in surfaces that paraphrased it.

REMAINING carriers, none touchable by that PR's fence. Two of these were NOT named by the original audit and are the more serious find:

1. spec/002-Frames.md:471 - the OWNING spec's own exhaustive claim: "It returns the closed effects map (..., top-level keys `#{:db :fx :rf.db/runtime}`, ...)". Contradicted ninety lines later by its own :561, which correctly says the map "carries four further commit-plane effects". NEW - the audit did not name it. This is the most serious remaining site: 002 is where every other surface points.

2. spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2856 - the machine effect-map note: "The closed `:rf/effect-map` contract (`:db` + `:rf.db/runtime` + `:fx`) is preserved at the handler boundary." Same file that gets it right at :727. NEW - the audit did not name it.

3. docs/api/re-frame.core.md:518 - "The effect map is closed: app handlers return `:db` + `:fx` only. (A third reserved top-level key, `:rf.db/runtime`, exists ...)".

4. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_canvas.cljs:168-173 - the SET is already right (it names the four EP-0025 keys) but the BEHAVIOUR is wrong: it says the top-level fx-id is "policed ... and DROPPED, so the localStorage write never happened" while "the `:db` write landed either way". That is the pre-rf2-04tx partial-commit narrative told as current. Either date it explicitly as pre-rf2-04tx or rewrite to the refusal semantics.

5. implementation/core/test/re_frame/event_context_partition_test.clj:12 and :153, and fx_test.clj:485 - the test narration the original bead flagged as internally contradictory: it still calls the closed set three keys and describes a foreign key as dropped with a dev-only error, while the live test at :177-189 proves the current no-partial-commit refusal. Comment-only; do not touch the assertions.

6. The Hicasso historical accounts - implementation/hicasso/testbed/hicasso_testbed/core.cljs:425-430, implementation/hicasso/testbed/spec.cjs:1653-1657, docs/design/hicasso/native-ime-scripted-witness.md:193-197. These describe the timer vanishing while the arm-state db write landed. Per the original bead: do NOT erase the history - state explicitly that this was the pre-rf2-04tx behaviour.

RULE (from rf2-18tt): ordinary examples may keep showing {:db ... :fx ...}. Only prose that labels an EXHAUSTIVE closed set, or states recovery/partial-commit behaviour, must be exact.

HOT-ZONE WARNING: spec/002-Frames.md and spec/Spec-Schemas.md are both hot-zone files; sequence rather than parallelise. Items 4-6 sit in tools/, tests and docs/design - different trees, safe to parallel against each other.

CENSUS TRAPS measured on this machine and worth reusing: GNU grep 3.0 returns 0 for `-rnFi` where `-rnF` returns 4 on the same needle, so never combine -F with -i here; and run any census three ways (line-oriented, whitespace-flattened, de-hyphenated) with a control needle known to be present, because a hyphen-wrapped token is invisible to the first two. The needle that carried the census was the structural `\{:db\s+:rf\.db/runtime\s+:fx\}`.
close_reason: PR #9071 corrects every remaining carrier, and the census found EIGHT rather than the six this bead named. Six as named: spec/002-Frames.md:471 (the owning spec's own exhaustive three-key claim, contradicted by its EP-0025 section ninety lines below - the most serious of them, since 002 is where the other surfaces point); spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2856's machine effect-map note; docs/api/re-frame.core.md:518; tools/xray/.../machine_canvas.cljs:168-173; the narration in implementation/core/test/re_frame/event_context_partition_test.clj (ns docstring + the section-3 banner) and fx_test.clj; and the three Hicasso accounts. TWO MORE the bead did not name, both unambiguous exhaustive claims and both fixed: skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/events.md ('the only legal top-level keys are :db ... :rf.db/runtime ... :fx', contradicted by its OWN gotcha list carrying all seven) and docs/core/glossary.md ('Only :db and :fx may appear at the top level'). Partial-commit narratives were DATED, not erased: the Xray persist-fx comment and the three Hicasso accounts now say explicitly that the dropped-key-while-:db-commits account is the pre-rf2-04tx contract, and state the current refusal beside it. Implementation UNTOUCHED - comment and prose only, no assertion changed, nothing under implementation/core/src. FOUR PREMISES CHECKED THAT DID NOT NEED WORK, left alone and reported: spec/Spec-Schemas.md:724-758 (the canonical schema owner, already 'Seven keys'), spec/conformance/fixtures/effect-map-shape-bad-top-level-key.edn and migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:326 (both already frame drop-and-commit as 'the old contract'), and docs/core/effects.md (an app-facing 'two top-level keys plus the privacy classifications' teaching frame, not an exhaustive claim). ONE BRIEF PREMISE DID NOT HOLD: PR #9070 was still OPEN when this branch was cut, so its spec/ and core/src corrections were not on main; it merged as d1ad67cb2d during the gate runs. Its file set and this PR's are disjoint either way, verified against the merge base before pushing, so nothing here reverts it. GATES, all captured exit codes, none through a pipe: fast-PR spine 0 (PASS fast PR spine; attempt 1 exited 1 on a transient shadow-cljs par-compile abort in re_frame/story/play under three concurrent peer spines - a surface this diff cannot reach - and the identical tree recompiled and re-ran green); core JVM 0 (2176/11149); CLJS node suite 0 (11206/55823) split into compile and run; per-ns isolation 0 (16 namespaces, 190 tests); hicasso invariants/lint/compile 0; mkdocs --strict 0; doc-slugs 0 + self-test 0; readme-links 0; provenance pins 0 + self-test 0; clj-kondo errors 0. TWO GATES PROVEN LIVE BY PLANTED FAULTS rather than assumed: a broken anchor on one line of spec/002-Frames.md turned check_doc_slugs.py red naming file, line 471 and anchor, and a planted deftest turned the core JVM namespace red at 19/64 against an 18/63 control - both restored and each restore verified by git blob hash against the committed object, not by reading a diff. One CLJS re-run was killed by the harness cap leaving no exit file and is reported as NO VERDICT, superseded by the run that completed. Hand-checked because no gate reads them: the four code files are comment/docstring text that both link gates strip or never see, no table row is touched, and both anchors the new 002 text cites resolve (the sabotage proves it directly).

title: ssr-node latency envelope ignores the runtime partition
description:
## Evidence

- The pre-registered condition in implementation/ssr-node/src/envelope.cjs:40 and the ENVELOPE property at :71-72 bound only state EDN text to 64 KiB.
- The measured request in test/envelope.test.cjs:67-79 contains no runtime partition and computes only the byte lengths of two state values. It omits key bytes as well.
- Runtime became a second cloned request partition in crossing commit 9a42302f7a. Current protocol.cjs:329-373 counts every UTF-8 key and value per partition, and :458-468 enforces one combined state.bytes + runtime.bytes ceiling.
- The runtime-partition change did not touch envelope.cjs or envelope.test.cjs; git log --follow shows the registration still comes solely from f39829caa6.
- As written, the claimed condition admits any runtime payload below the separate body/protocol ceiling, while the witness measures none of it. The test therefore does not falsify the published envelope over the request domain the prose now describes.
- No existing bead found by ssr-node, runtime-partition, state-budget, or envelope searches owns this drift; rf2-8arzr.3 added the combined protocol ceiling but explicitly left the latency witness outside its fence.

## Impact

The pre-registered latency promise can be read as covering a runtime-heavy request that its only witness never measures. The test also uses a byte definition different from the validator it is meant to condition, making its green verdict weaker than the stated contract.

## Disposition

Amend or version the registration without refitting the p50/p95/max ceilings: define the 64 KiB condition over state and runtime together, rename stateBudgetBytes accordingly, and have the witness send non-empty data in both partitions. Count UTF-8 key plus value bytes with the same semantics as validatePartition. Record the amendment explicitly so the original pre-measurement provenance remains auditable.

## Risks

Do not silently rewrite history or tune ceilings after measurement. The latency numbers and sample count were pre-registered and must remain unchanged unless a separately preregistered successor envelope is introduced. The reference entry allowlists constrain which runtime key can be used.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The registration and README describe one explicit 64 KiB condition over state plus runtime, while preserving the existing latency ceilings and sample count.
2. The measured request contains non-empty allowlisted state and runtime partitions.
3. The witness byte calculation includes every UTF-8 key and value and matches protocol.cjs semantics.
4. A runtime-heavy controlled request that exceeds the combined condition is rejected by the witness precondition rather than counted as an eligible sample.
5. git history or an explicit amendment note continues to distinguish the original preregistration from this contract repair.
6. The ssr-node suite is green, including the envelope row.
close_reason:
Confirmed and fixed in PR #9078. Every element of the premise held at my tip: src/envelope.cjs bounded only state EDN text to 64 KiB (condition at the header, ENVELOPE.stateBudgetBytes); test/envelope.test.cjs's measured request carried no runtime partition and summed the byte lengths of two state VALUES, omitting every key as the bead says; and src/protocol.cjs's validatePartition counts Buffer.byteLength(key) + Buffer.byteLength(value) per partition and enforces ONE combined state.bytes + runtime.bytes ceiling.

ONE CLARIFICATION ON THE CEILING, since the two numbers differ and the difference is not a disagreement: protocol.cjs's ceiling is maxRequestBytes, default 1 << 20 = 1 MiB, a REFUSAL ceiling; the envelope's 64 KiB is a narrower pre-registered SAMPLING CONDITION under which the latency figures are claimed. Two layers, and both are kept. What they must share is how a byte is counted, and now do.

REPAIR (AC1-AC3): stateBudgetBytes -> requestBudgetBytes, same 64 KiB, restated over state + runtime together; a new exported requestBytes() counts keys and values across PARTITIONS read from protocol.cjs rather than naming the two fields locally, so a third partition cannot be added to the wire and leave the condition measuring two of three — which is exactly how this drift happened; the measured request now carries a non-empty allowlisted runtime partition (:rf.runtime/routing, the only key app/root's runtimeAllowlist permits) and is asserted inside the budget as a PRECONDITION before any sample is taken. README's condition row and a new paragraph say the same thing. Zero residual references to stateBudgetBytes repo-wide.

AC3 is pinned rather than asserted in prose: a new row admits a request at maxRequestBytes exactly N and requires validateRequest to REFUSE it at N-1, which is only true if requestBytes and validatePartition agree key for key.

AC4 PROVEN, and the false-green is MEASURED rather than argued. Permanent control row: a request busting the condition on runtime alone is over budget by requestBytes while validateRequest still accepts it — so the row is about the envelope's condition, not the protocol ceiling. Plant on the measured row (single-line anchor, match count 1 read first): runtime oversized to 70000 bytes gives 'AssertionError: the sample request must sit inside the registered 65536-byte budget; it is 70155 bytes', captured exit 1, 5 pass / 1 fail. On that SAME request the pre-repair formula computes 124 bytes and admits it — 124 vs 70155 is the size of the false green. Restore verified by git blob hash (cdee2d42bd94950c818118c2af886da811c3ddb1), not by reading a diff.

AC5: no ceiling and no sample count moved — p50 5 ms, p95 25 ms, max 250 ms, 200 samples are the values registered in f39829caa6, and an explicit AMENDMENT block in src/envelope.cjs records what was corrected (the condition's DOMAIN) and what was not (every number), keeping git log --follow provenance readable. Measured overhead with the runtime partition added: p50 0.18 ms, p95 0.28 ms, max 1.59 ms — well inside the untouched ceilings.

AC6: 9 suites green, 107 tests, 107 pass, 0 fail, captured exit 0 on the final rebased base; envelope.test.cjs 4 rows -> 6.

title: ssr-node boot-once test never observes the boot hook
description:
## Evidence

- implementation/ssr-node/test/isolation.test.cjs:121-133 claims to prove that the module boots once per isolate, but the row only proves that two renders used the same worker thread and each observed overlapMax === 1.
- overlapMax is render-concurrency state (test/fixtures/reference.cjs:24-26,78-94). It has the same value if boot() is never called, called once, or called before every sequential render, so neither asserted outcome discriminates the stated contract.
- The fixture's only boot signal is module.exports.booted: initialized at test/fixtures/reference.cjs:73, written at :75, and never read anywhere in the repository. A whole-repo exact-identifier search finds only those two fixture sites.
- The worker's actual contract is load-bearing: src/worker.cjs invokes the optional module hook during isolate boot, and the Hicasso server bundle has a real hook that initializes its substrate. A regression in that call site would remain green in the dedicated package row.
- The row and inert booted signal date to the initial isolation witness (8ab673ea78); later egress changes did not make the assertion observe boot.

## Impact

The package gate can report that per-isolate boot is protected after the hook is removed, skipped, or moved to per-request execution. That leaves a real application initialization contract without the regression witness named for it.

## Disposition

Replace the inert boolean with a boot-call count (or an equally direct observation) owned by each loaded fixture instance, include it in the emitted observations, and assert that both sequential renders on one isolate observe exactly one boot. Keep the existing same-thread precondition so the row still proves the requests reached one isolate.

## Risks

The reference fixture is also required directly by some in-process controls, so the observation must not let the main process module cache contaminate the worker-thread measurement. Do not weaken the separate overlapMax concurrency rows; they protect a different guarantee.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The normal two-render, one-isolate case reports exactly one boot invocation on both responses.
2. A controlled mutation that removes the worker boot call makes this row fail.
3. A controlled mutation that invokes boot for each render makes this row fail.
4. The dead booted write-only boolean is removed or replaced by the direct measured signal.
5. All 9 ssr-node suites (currently 104 rows) remain green after restoring the controls.
close_reason:
Confirmed and fixed in PR #9078. The premise held exactly: test/isolation.test.cjs's row 'the module boots once per isolate, not once per request' asserted overlapMax === 1 on two sequential responses, and overlapMax is render-concurrency state that reads 1 whether the boot hook is called never, once, or before every render. The fixture's booted boolean was written at reference.cjs:75 and read nowhere — a scoped census over implementation/ssr-node found it only at :73 and :75 as an identifier (the two other hits are prose), line-oriented and whitespace-flattened agreeing, with a control needle that fired.

REPAIR: the fixture counts boots on the isolate's own globalThis (Symbol.for key) rather than in module scope, and publishes the count in its observations. Module scope was rejected deliberately: a counter a re-require resets would report 1 for a per-request require-and-boot too, which is one of the two failures the row exists to catch. Each worker thread has its own global, so the count cannot see another isolate's boots nor the main process's copy of the fixture, which addresses the bead's stated contamination risk (the in-process controls require reference.cjs directly). AC4: the dead boolean is removed.

AC1/AC2/AC3 PROVEN BY NEGATIVE CONTROL, both directions, each plant anchored to a single line with its match count read first (=1) and each restore verified by git blob hash against the committed object, not by reading a diff. AC1: normal case reports boots === 1 on both responses, captured exit 0. AC2: deleting 'if (typeof mod.boot === function) mod.boot();' from src/worker.cjs gives 'AssertionError: the isolate must have booted the module exactly once', actual 0 expected 1, captured exit 1, 6 pass / 1 fail. AC3: calling mod.boot() before every render gives the same row '2 !== 1', captured exit 1, 6 pass / 1 fail. Each plant failed exactly ONE row — the repaired one — so neither broke the file out from under its neighbours. Both restores hashed to e0eab3d1f6a674613277bc8ffbb1b782dd1d4086.

AC5: all 9 ssr-node suites green after restore — 107 tests, 107 pass, 0 fail, captured exit 0, on the final rebased base. Baseline before any edit was 104/104; the +3 are the two envelope rows and the bytes row from siblings .71 and .72. isolation.test.cjs stays at 7 rows: this was repaired in place, not added to. overlapMax remains asserted in concurrency.test.cjs where it is the subject, per the bead's risk note.

title: Remove ssr-node compatibility guards below its Node 24 floor
description:
## Evidence

- implementation/ssr-node/package.json declares engines.node >=24, a deliberate crossing requirement recorded by closed feature rf2-8arzr.2.
- The code still treats four much older core APIs as optional: bootTimer.unref?.() at src/isolate.cjs:81, render timer.unref?.() at :154, waiter.timer.unref?.() at src/pool.cjs:148, and server.closeAllConnections?.() at src/http.cjs:250.
- Node's official API history records Timeout.unref() since v0.9.1 and http.Server.closeAllConnections() since v18.2.0. Both methods are unconditional under the supported Node 24+ floor:
  https://nodejs.org/download/release/latest-v24.x/docs/api/timers.html#timeoutunref
  https://nodejs.org/download/release/latest-v24.x/docs/api/http.html#servercloseallconnections
- Every call receives a real Node Timeout or http.Server; no repository test double omits these methods.
- These guards predate the package manifest/floor: isolate/pool came from b2b35bf6e9 and HTTP from 939d439ad9, while the Node >=24 package contract landed later in rf2-8arzr.2.
- No existing bead found by ssr-node, unref, closeAllConnections, or Node-floor searches owns these compatibility remnants.

## Impact

The impossible fallback paths imply that failure to detach lifecycle timers or force-close active HTTP connections is an accepted runtime mode. That obscures the actual shutdown/timeout guarantees and leaves below-floor compatibility code after the project chose a firm runtime floor.

## Disposition

Call unref() and closeAllConnections() directly. Preserve the calls themselves and their ordering; only retire the optional compatibility branches. Keep this separate from any redesign of graceful shutdown.

## Risks

server.closeAllConnections() is still needed for active connections even though modern server.close() also reaps idle connections. Do not remove it. Direct calls intentionally make an unsupported or malformed runtime fail loudly rather than degrade lifecycle behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No optional call remains for Timeout.unref or Server.closeAllConnections in implementation/ssr-node.
2. The three timers are still unrefed and HTTP shutdown still force-closes active connections before completing.
3. The Node >=24 engine floor remains explicit.
4. Timeout, admission, shutdown, serve, and full ssr-node tests are green.
close_reason:
Confirmed and removed in PR #9078. THE FLOOR WAS RE-VERIFIED FIRST, since it is the whole justification: implementation/ssr-node/package.json declares engines.node '>=24' at my tip, unchanged; every .github/workflows/*.yml that pins a runtime pins node-version '24'; and the node running these gates is v24.13.0. Probed both APIs on that runtime directly rather than trusting the docs: typeof setTimeout(...).unref === 'function' and typeof http.createServer().closeAllConnections === 'function' both true. Timeout.unref() has existed since v0.9.1 and http.Server.closeAllConnections() since v18.2.0, so both are unconditional under the declared floor.

All four sites were exactly where the bead said, re-derived at my tip: src/isolate.cjs:81 (bootTimer.unref?.()), src/isolate.cjs:154 (render timer.unref?.()), src/pool.cjs:148 (waiter.timer.unref?.()), src/http.cjs:250 (server.closeAllConnections?.()). Each patch was anchored to a single line with its match count read first (=1 in every case). AC1: a repo-wide grep for 'unref?.' and 'closeAllConnections?.' under implementation/ssr-node now returns nothing.

AC2: the calls and their ordering are untouched — the three timers are still unrefed at the same points, and closeServer still calls closeAllConnections() before server.close(), which the bead's risk note is explicit about keeping (server.close() reaps idle connections only; active ones still need the force-close). Only the branches that could never be taken are gone, so an unsupported or malformed runtime now fails loudly instead of silently degrading shutdown behaviour, which was the stated intent.

AC3: the >=24 engine floor is untouched and still pinned by test/serve.test.cjs's row 'the manifest points its bin at this launcher, exports the two entry points, and pins the Node CI runs'. package.json was not edited — this bead reads the floor, it does not move it.

AC4: timeout, concurrency (admission), serve and all 9 ssr-node suites green — 107 tests, 107 pass, 0 fail, captured exit 0 on the final rebased base. Note the shutdown paths are genuinely exercised rather than merely compiled: serve.test.cjs spawns bin/serve.cjs as a real process and stops it on SIGTERM, and timeout.test.cjs drives real render deadlines and isolate termination, so the unrefed timers and the force-close both ran.

title: Retire ssr-node alternate streaming selectors with no consumers
description:
## Evidence

- implementation/ssr-node/src/http.cjs:145-147 selects streaming through three routes: documented query stream=1, undocumented request header x-rf-ssr-stream: 1, or the serve option streamingDefault unless query stream=0.
- A whole-repository search finds x-rf-ssr-stream only at that branch and streamingDefault only in handleRender/serve plumbing at http.cjs:127,147,221,226. No CLI flag, README contract, test, JVM adapter, example, or build wiring sets either one.
- The only exercised and documented selector is POST /render?stream=1 (README.md:516 and test/bytes.test.cjs:112).
- The stream=0 exception is reachable only when the zero-consumer streamingDefault option is enabled.
- Both alternate selectors were introduced in the first HTTP implementation (939d439ad9) and have never acquired a consumer or contract.
- The package is private and version 0.1.0; its explicit exports expose serve, but the repository's consumer-facing README does not advertise either alternate path. No existing streaming bead concerns this surface; rf2-6r9j.42 is about an unrelated Ring streaming-root retention.

## Impact

The HTTP entry point carries two invisible ways to change response framing plus an otherwise meaningless stream=0 branch. They expand the behavior and compatibility surface without a witness. A caller can accidentally receive chunked semantics from a magic header or unpinned in-process option that the operational docs do not teach.

## Disposition

Keep the documented and byte-tested stream=1 query selector. Remove x-rf-ssr-stream, streamingDefault plumbing, and its stream=0 exception after one final supported-consumer check. Pin the remaining default as buffered and the query opt-in as streamed.

## Risks

Changing framing can break an out-of-repository checkout consumer even though the selectors are undocumented and the package cannot currently be published. Check release notes and known deployment config before removal; if a real supported consumer is found, promote that selector into the README and tests instead of leaving it implicit.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The supported streaming contract has one documented selector: query stream=1.
2. Normal POST /render remains buffered and byte-identical; query stream=1 remains chunked and byte-identical.
3. x-rf-ssr-stream, streamingDefault, and the stream=0-only override have no production plumbing after the supported-consumer check.
4. A focused HTTP row pins that the former magic header no longer silently changes framing, unless a real supported consumer caused it to be documented and retained instead.
5. The bytes, serve, and full ssr-node suites are green.
close_reason:
Confirmed and retired in PR #9078. The reachability census reproduced the bead's claim exactly, run per the anti-false-negative discipline: fixed-string matching (never -F combined with -i, which returns 0 on this GNU grep 3.0 where -F alone returns hits), over git-tracked files, .beads/issues.jsonl and .beads/metadata.json excluded, each census run TWICE — once line-oriented and once whitespace-flattened — and every run paired with a CONTROL needle known to be live.

CONTROL FIRED: 'stream=1' returned exactly its two known sites, README.md:516 and test/bytes.test.cjs:112, in both instruments. TARGETS: 'x-rf-ssr-stream' -> 1 hit, src/http.cjs:146 and nowhere else. 'streamingDefault' -> 4 hits, all src/http.cjs (:127, :147, :221, :226), i.e. the handleRender/serve plumbing passing it to itself. Both instruments agreed. The supported-consumer check the disposition asks for: bin/serve.cjs sets neither (its only serve() call passes port, host and maxRequestBytes); README's in-process serve example sets neither; no CLI flag, test, JVM adapter, example or build wiring anywhere. The literal 'stream=0' returns 0 hits because the source spells it as searchParams.get('stream') !== '0' — the bead described that branch semantically and correctly.

DISPOSITION AS ORDERED: kept the documented and byte-tested ?stream=1 query; removed the x-rf-ssr-stream header branch, the streamingDefault parameter from both handleRender and serve, and the ?stream=0 escape, which was reachable only when streamingDefault was on. Buffered is now the default and the query is the opt-in, unconditionally (AC1, AC3).

AC4: a new focused row in test/bytes.test.cjs sends the retired header and requires the response to come back BUFFERED — content-length equal to the UTF-8 length of the body, which a chunked response cannot carry, and bytes sha256-identical to the plain POST. The pin is load-bearing, not decorative: restoring the header branch in src/http.cjs (single-line anchor, match count 1 read first) makes it fail with 'the header must not have selected streaming — a streamed response carries no content-length', captured exit 1, 15 pass / 1 fail. Restore verified by git blob hash 6e761df8f7421b52a898c98fa3c734c4dfc41a0d.

AC2/AC5: bytes, serve and all 9 ssr-node suites green — 107 tests, 107 pass, 0 fail, captured exit 0 on the final rebased base. The pre-existing row asserting that streamed and buffered output are byte-identical still passes, so ?stream=1 remains chunked and a plain POST remains buffered and byte-identical. No README change was needed for AC1: neither retired selector was ever documented there, so ?stream=1 was already the sole documented selector.

title: core/derivation/graph.cljc:819-836 repeats rf2-yk2d's dead do-not-rename sentinel and its two false claims
description:
Found while fixing rf2-yk2d in PR #9070. implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/graph.cljc:819-836 carries the IDENTICAL defect that rf2-yk2d recorded for its egress sibling, and it was left standing because #9070's file fence did not include graph.cljc.

The site: `defonce ^:private bundle-isolation-sentinel "rf.derivation.graph/sentinel:rf2-6xm07h-2026-06-12:do-not-rename"` at :835-836, under a comment at :819-833 asserting the same two things rf2-yk2d measured false for egress:

  (1) "implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs greps the counter bundle for this exact string" - it does not. The roster entry for `derivation-graph` in check-bundle-isolation.cjs uses the sentinel `rf/family` ("re-frame.derivation.graph family marker"), not this literal.

  (2) "The string survives :advanced because string literals are not renamed" - the var is `^:private` and nothing consumes its value, so Closure DCEs it exactly as it does the egress one.

SAME HISTORY, and the tree already records it: commit 4e43784ec7 (2026-07-15, "test: require emitted bundle isolation controls") moved BOTH entries - egress and its derivation-graph sibling, the latter onto `rf/family` - off the planted strings when these controls became emitted-module greps. check-bundle-isolation.cjs's roster comment says so in as many words. Both vars were simply left behind; #9070 removed one.

MEASURE BEFORE ACTING, do not take this bead's word for it. The check that settles it is a fixed-string grep of the EMITTED module, never the .cljc:
  grep -cF "rf.derivation.graph/sentinel:rf2-6xm07h-2026-06-12:do-not-rename" implementation/out/bundle-isolation-positive-control/derivation-graph.js
Expect 0. Run a control in the same file with the same instrument - `grep -cF "rf/family"` on the same artefact - so a zero is a measurement rather than a broken needle. Build the artefact with `npm run test:bundle-isolation` (or just the `shadow-cljs release ... bundle-isolation-positive-control` half of it) first.

SUGGESTED FIX, matching what #9070 did for egress so the two siblings stay symmetrical: remove the var, and replace the comment with one that says the sentinel for this namespace is not in this file, names `rf/family` as the literal the gate actually greps, and records that the defonce was removed. Weigh removal against keeping-and-correcting on its own merits - #9070's reasoning for removing was that a corrected comment still leaves the false `do-not-rename` instruction inside the string literal itself, and that the roster already teaches a removed literal perfectly well (its first named trap, `re-frame.derivation.egress/no-egress-frame`, no longer exists in source either).

IF THE VAR IS REMOVED, check whether check-bundle-isolation.cjs's roster comment needs a matching correction the way egress's did - #9070 had to change "still planted at the bottom of egress.cljc" to past tense. Read the `derivation-graph` roster entry's comment before deciding; the two records must agree afterwards.

DO NOT change the live sentinel (`rf/family`) or any gate behaviour. `npm run test:bundle-isolation` must still read exit 0 with 40 internal sentinels absent and 40 positive-control sentinels present - both numbers were unmoved by #9070's removal of the egress twin, which is the evidence that removing a Closure-dropped var cannot move them.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 08:2x AUSEST. REMOVE THE VAR AND ITS COMMENT BLOCK, MATCHING WHAT #9070 DID TO THE EGRESS SIBLING. AND THIS BEAD IS NOT FENCED — I measured the overlap rather than assuming it.

NOT FENCED, MEASURED. I expected this to be sequenced behind PR #9070 because that PR holds implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs, and I checked instead of assuming:
  grep -F "rf.derivation.graph/sentinel" check-bundle-isolation.cjs  -> NO HITS
  grep -F "rf.derivation.egress/sentinel" check-bundle-isolation.cjs -> ONE HIT at :515 (the control, proving the instrument works)
The roster entry for derivation-graph at :478-480 uses the source 're-frame.derivation.graph family marker', not the literal, exactly as this bead says. And the .cjs comment at :521 ALREADY records the graph sibling correctly — "4e43784ec7 moved this entry — and its `derivation-graph` sibling, onto `rf/family`". So nothing in that file claims the graph literal is planted, and nothing in it needs to change. THIS IS A SINGLE-FILE CHANGE TO graph.cljc.

THE RULING: REMOVE, do not correct. PR #9070's worker removed the egress var rather than correcting its comment, and gave the reason: a corrected comment still leaves the false `do-not-rename` instruction inside the STRING LITERAL ITSELF, where the next reader meets it first. That reasoning applies here unchanged and the two sites should not diverge. It also confirmed nothing consumed the egress var before removing it; do the same here.

WHAT COMES OUT: the `defonce ^:private bundle-isolation-sentinel` at graph.cljc:835-836 and the seventeen-line comment block above it at :819-833. That block asserts two things this bead measured false — that check-bundle-isolation.cjs greps the counter bundle for this exact string, and that the string survives `:advanced`. It also asserts the string "sits outside any `interop/debug-enabled?` gate so DCE cannot drop the literal independently", which is beside the point once the var itself is dropped.

MEASURE FIRST, as the bead already instructs, and do not take either the bead's word or mine. The check that settles it is a fixed-string grep of the EMITTED module, never the .cljc, with a same-file same-instrument control so a zero is a measurement rather than a broken needle. #9070's worker ran exactly this pattern and got 0 for the planted literal against a control of 1 for the live `rf.resource/opaque`.

WHAT IS NOT RULED AND STAYS THE WORKER'S CALL: whether to add a do-not-re-plant note for graph alongside the one #9070 added for egress. IF YOU CONCLUDE check-bundle-isolation.cjs NEEDS ANY EDIT, REPORT IT — DO NOT MAKE IT. That file is inside PR #9070's diff and a second toucher conflicts. The reporting costs a follow-up bead; the edit costs a merge.
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 11:2x AUSEST, on the conflict the worker reported rather than resolving unilaterally. NO FOLLOW-UP IS WANTED. graph.cljc stays as it landed, with no sentinel comment at all.

THE CONFLICT WAS REAL AND THE WORKER WAS RIGHT TO SURFACE IT. This bead's ruling said "REMOVE THE VAR AND ITS COMMENT BLOCK, MATCHING WHAT #9070 DID TO THE EGRESS SIBLING" and enumerated both under WHAT COMES OUT. But #9070 merged mid-run and the worker read the LANDED diff rather than trusting the description: #9070 removed the var and KEPT a comment, replacing the false block with a corrected account that now opens "THE SENTINEL FOR THIS NAMESPACE IS NOT IN THIS FILE" and names rf.resource/opaque. So the two halves of one instruction pointed opposite ways, and reading the tree is what exposed it.

IT FOLLOWED THE EXPLICIT ENUMERATED ACTION, which is the correct tie-break: an enumerated action outranks a comparison to a sibling that moved after the ruling was written.

WHY NO SYMMETRY FOLLOW-UP. Three reasons, in order of weight. (1) The stance refuses it: "not over-engineering or gold plating... we don't need to litigate every last fine detail". A comment added so two files look alike, rather than because a reader needs it, is precisely that. (2) The two cases are NOT symmetrical in substance, which is the worker's own argument and it holds: egress MINTED a keyword and needed to explain where its sentinel went; graph ASSOCS a family marker (rf/family) it does not own, so there is less to explain. Equal treatment of unequal cases is not consistency. (3) The account already exists in two places a reader reaches first -- the roster entry (source 're-frame.derivation.graph family marker', sentinel rf/family) and check-bundle-isolation.cjs at ~:521, which the worker re-measured and found already records the graph sibling's history correctly.

WHAT THE WORKER ESTABLISHED THAT IS WORTH KEEPING. check-bundle-isolation.cjs needs NO edit, and it reproduced that measurement rather than trusting the mayor's: "rf.derivation.graph/sentinel" returns nothing, the egress control returns one hit at :515. The consumer census found EXACTLY ONE hit tree-wide, the defonce itself -- against three for the egress half, the difference being egress's roster citation. Three-legged emitted-module measurement on a rebuilt artefact with mtime confirmed later than the source: planted literal 0, rf/family control 1, pre-change source 1. Bundle-isolation counts 40 absent / 40 present, unmoved either side. Sabotage witness red naming exactly the plant, restore verified by git blob hash a4aef0f7 both sides.

TWO SPINE RUNS WERE CORRECTLY READ AS NO VERDICT, not failures: shadow-cljs par-compile aborts pending #{re-frame.router-transducer} then #{re-frame.websocket-cljs-test}, neither reachable from a 19-line deletion in graph.cljc, the pending namespace differing between runs, and the identical command passing standalone twice with identical counts. Scheduler abort under five concurrent peers. This is now the third and fourth instance of that abort recorded today across three workers; treat it as a known concurrency artefact of this fleet size, never as a signal about a diff.

LANDED as PR #9072 at 2fa8afcd68, +0/-19, one file.
close_reason:
PR #9072. Both premises verified at source before acting, then the ruled removal made. graph.cljc lost 19 lines: the defonce ^:private bundle-isolation-sentinel and the seventeen-line comment block above it. Nothing added; one file; no other path touched.

MEASURED, THREE LEGS, on a freshly built out/bundle-isolation-positive-control/derivation-graph.js (artefact mtime confirmed later than the source read, so no stale out/ answered): ZERO occurrences of the planted literal rf.derivation.graph/sentinel:rf2-6xm07h-2026-06-12:do-not-rename, against a same-file same-instrument control of 1 for the live rf/family, with the literal present exactly once in the pre-change source. title: test(story): stop treating the no-op reg-variant row as a browser probe
description:
Finding

`tools/story/test/story_feature_load.cjs` classifies the `reg-variant` coverage row as a live browser `probe`, but its body only prints `SKIP` and returns. The replacement CLJS test named by the comment already landed, so this is a stale migration shim that makes the feature-load coverage report falsely claim execution.

Evidence

- The file's coverage contract at lines 28-49 defines `kind: 'probe'` to mean the function actually exercises the named feature, says a non-probed row must be `kind: 'owned-by'`, and explicitly says never wire a probe whose body does not exercise the feature.
- The `reg-variant` row at lines 1185-1219 is `kind: 'probe'`, but its `_page` body ends in only `console.warn('SKIP: reg-variant scenario · migrating to CLJS unit per rf2-8awk1'); return;`. It performs no browser or product operation. A repo-wide search finds this as the only unconditional `SKIP:` in Story source/tests/testbeds.
- The row comment says this is temporary until `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/panels_e2e/reg_variant_e2e_cljs_test.cljs` is merged. That replacement exists and says it replaces the Playwright probe; it covers the four named variants plus registration shape. Git commit `c47f1925c3` (2026-05-20) added the CLJS replacement and converted the browser row to the no-op in the same landed change, so the temporary state has already outlived its condition.
- `validateCoverageMatrix` at lines 1538-1575 checks only that a probe is a function. `assertCoverageMatrix` at lines 1578-1596 awaits the no-op and records only `owned-by` rows as declared out-of-scope. Thus the row completes green as if directly exercised, and verbose output does not disclose it among ownership skips (apart from an easy-to-miss warning inside the fake probe).
- `tools/story/spec/015-Test-Coverage.md:82` still lists `test:story-feature-load` as an owning gate and promises selecting every sidebar variant, including post-burst verification. The same file's helper table at line 425 still binds `assertMatrixVariant` to the `reg-variant` row, although this row never calls it. The separate live `Sidebar navigation` probe deliberately skips `clicked-three-times` and owns navigation, not the no-op row's claimed lifecycle/state contract.
- The adjacent `reg-decorator composition` row documents the same former no-op pattern and has already been correctly demoted to `owned-by`, providing the intended local precedent.
- Bead searches for `SKIP reg-variant`, `feature-load reg-variant`, `reg-variant scenario`, `coverage matrix no-op`, and historical id `rf2-8awk1` returned no existing issue; `bd show rf2-8awk1` also found no local issue.

Impact

A required browser coverage row is false-green: CI records a successful probe without executing the feature, the spec overstates direct browser ownership, and future reviewers can mistake a warning for coverage. The long stale block also obscures which gate actually owns the contract.

Proposed disposition

Replace the row with `kind: 'owned-by'`, naming `npm run test:cljs` and the exact CLJS replacement as its owner, and delete the no-op body/stale temporary narrative. Update spec/015 so the reg-variant lifecycle/state portions point to the CLJS test and the separately live Sidebar navigation row retains only its real browser contract. Add a policy-level guard or structural fixture that rejects `kind: 'probe'` rows whose implementation is an unconditional skip/return so this precise false-green cannot recur.

Risks

Do not remove the separate live sidebar-navigation or other `assertMatrixVariant` call sites; they cover real browser surfaces. If the coverage policy still requires every variant to be selected in a browser after the burst, implement a deterministic live probe rather than claiming the CLJS owner satisfies that browser-specific requirement.
acceptance_criteria:
- The `reg-variant` coverage row either performs a real browser assertion or is explicitly `kind: 'owned-by'` with the exact live CLJS owner; there is no unconditional warn-and-return probe.
- Verbose feature-load output reports the row honestly as executed or declared out-of-scope.
- `tools/story/spec/015-Test-Coverage.md` accurately separates CLJS reg-variant lifecycle/registration coverage from live sidebar-navigation coverage and names no helper the row does not call.
- A policy/unit witness fails if a coverage-matrix `probe` is replaced with an unconditional `SKIP`/return implementation.
- Node syntax/policy tests, the Story CLJS replacement suite, `test:story-feature-load`, and relevant browser scenarios pass.
close_reason:
Done in PR #9075. Premise re-verified first: the CLJS replacement named in the skip (tools/story/test/re_frame/story/panels_e2e/reg_variant_e2e_cljs_test.cljs) EXISTS and is RUN — its ns ends in -cljs-test, `../tools/story/test` is on the consolidated :node-test source paths, and the build's :ns-regexp is "cljs-test$", so `npm run test:cljs` selects it; the compiled bundle carries it (grep of implementation/out/node-test.js hits, control returns 0 for a fabricated ns). Had it been missing, demoting the row would have dropped real coverage.

The row is now kind: 'owned-by' naming `npm run test:cljs` and the five owning deftests, mirroring the reg-decorator composition precedent beside it. Coverage matrix went 37 probe / 13 owned-by to 36 / 14, and the real browser gate now prints reg-variant among the declared out-of-scope rows in BOTH phases with zero SKIP warnings left in the run.

validateCoverageMatrix now REJECTS a kind: 'probe' row whose body, comments stripped, is only console.<method>(...) calls and an optional bare return; it fails OPEN on any shape it cannot read, so it can never red a real probe. Demonstrated: planting that body on a live row takes the witness from exit 0 to exit 1 naming the row. COVERAGE_MATRIX and validateCoverageMatrix are exported so the policy is checkable without a browser.

spec/015 corrected on two counts: the reg-variant row listed test:story-feature-load as an owning gate and promised a sidebar sweep plus a post-burst re-check the no-op never performed; and the cross-reference index bound assertMatrixVariant to reg-variant and reg-decorator composition, neither of which calls it (both are owned-by). It now names the eight rows that do.
