title: Test-React inspection API: distinguish components from roots and live children
description:
## Naming finding

The public inspection helpers in `implementation/adapters/test-react/src/re_frame/adapter/test_react.cljc:539-554` no longer name the population they return:

- `mounted-roots` returns every live `MountedComponent` in `active-mounts`, including recursively mounted children. Its own docstring calls the result "the whole live forest, parents AND recursively-mounted children." The name predates child mounting (`fefee4a403`); commit `8e3dfe545f` added child roots and broadened the result without changing the original name.
- `children` filters the record's retained `:children` vector to only still-mounted entries. Unqualified `children` can be read as all recorded children, while the function intentionally returns only mounted children.

No tracked code outside this local-only adapter consumes either helper, but both are public vars in the documented test-kit namespace and therefore remain compatibility contracts.

## Ambiguity cost

Tests use the first helper as a leak detector over the entire mounted forest, not a root count. Calling it a root query makes assertions such as "parent + child = 2 roots" conceptually wrong and obscures why an orphaned descendant is visible. The second name hides its liveness filter, so a post-unmount empty result can be mistaken for removal from the record rather than filtering of retained dead child records.

## Proposed change

Add precise canonical helpers `mounted-components` and `mounted-children`. Move the current implementations/docstrings under those names and update the adapter's tests and README to use them. Retain `mounted-roots` and `children` as deprecated delegating compatibility wrappers with explicit historical-name documentation; do not make an unannounced breaking rename.

## Compatibility / exclusions

Preserve return collection shapes/order, `MountedComponent`, the serialized/record `:children` field, public mount/update/unmount names, lifecycle log keys/phases, and React interop. Do not touch the duplicate cache section or stale UIx/CI prose already owned by Phase-1 beads `rf2-6r9j.81` and `rf2-6r9j.85`. All-status searches for `mounted-roots`, mounted components/children, and live-forest Test-React vocabulary found no existing owning bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- New code and documentation use `mounted-components` for the complete live forest and `mounted-children` for one mount's live children.
- Historical public vars `mounted-roots` and `children` remain callable compatibility wrappers, are visibly deprecated, and state their misleading legacy semantics.
- Canonical and legacy helpers preserve the existing lazy-sequence/vector return shapes, order, and mounted-state filtering.
- Exact searches show legacy names only in their compatibility definitions/documentation; no call site continues teaching the ambiguous vocabulary.
- Test-React JVM and CLJS suites pass with the public mount/lifecycle/error and record contracts unchanged.
notes: Implemented mounted-components and mounted-children as canonical helpers; retained mounted-roots and children as ^:deprecated delegating wrappers with precise legacy-semantics docstrings. All production/test teaching uses canonical names except two explicit compatibility tests, which dereference the legacy Vars, assert :deprecated metadata, and verify delegation on JVM and CLJS without compiler warnings or changing the 35/160 count. README updated. Broad CLJS namespace run separately encountered only the pre-existing duplicated sub-cache test failures owned by rf2-6r9j.81; all naming/lifecycle contract selectors passed.
close_reason: Implemented canonical inspection names with deprecated compatibility wrappers, migrated callers/docs, and verified metadata, delegation, shapes, and host behavior.

title: Test-React runtime: name descendant teardown by its real scope
description:
## Naming finding

`implementation/adapters/test-react/src/re_frame/adapter/test_react.cljc:204-237` names a recursive helper `roll-back-speculative-children!`, but that is only one of its two call contexts. It recursively force-tears down every descendant under the supplied mount.

The name was accurate when commit `488bf70df6` introduced it for failed initial-mount rollback. Six hours later commit `bd14ef705e` added `force-teardown-subtree!` for failed updates and reused the helper on an already-committed live root. In that path the descendants explicitly include pre-existing children as well as children speculatively mounted by the failed attempt (`:225-226`), so "roll back speculative children" understates both the operation (forced teardown) and population (all descendants).

## Ambiguity cost

This is teardown code whose correctness depends on draining pre-existing and newly-mounted descendants alike. A maintainer following the old name can reasonably narrow the walk to attempt-local children or assume it is unsafe to reuse for adapter disposal/future forced teardown, reintroducing the live-child leak the failed-update path exists to prevent. The surrounding docstring currently has to explain the contradiction.

## Proposed change

Rename the private helper to `force-teardown-descendants!`, update its recursive call, both callers, and source commentary. Keep `force-teardown-record!` for one record and `force-teardown-subtree!` for descendants plus root; the three names then express the actual hierarchy. This is private and has no repo consumer outside the source file.

## Compatibility / exclusions

Do not alter recursion order, lifecycle phases, the `:children` record field, render-error propagation, or public APIs. Do not touch the Phase-1 `log-phase!` extras arm (`rf2-6r9j.83`) or duplicate cache tests (`rf2-6r9j.81`), both already assigned their own removals. All-status searches for the old/new terms and Test-React teardown naming found no owning bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- The recursive descendant-only primitive is named `force-teardown-descendants!`; `roll-back-speculative-children!` has no source/test/doc occurrence.
- `force-teardown-subtree!` calls the descendant primitive before tearing down its root, and failed initial mount calls it only for the never-committed parent's descendants.
- Leaf-upward order, clearing/eviction, exactly-one `:forced-teardown` per mounted record, and original-exception propagation are unchanged.
- Focused Test-React JVM and CLJS suites pass, including failed-initial, failed-update, nested-subtree, and sibling-scope cases.
- No Phase-1 removal target is renamed or otherwise changed.
notes: Implemented the private force-teardown-descendants! rename across recursion, failed-initial rollback, failed-update subtree teardown, and commentary. Exact old-name search is empty. JVM: 35 tests/160 assertions, exit 0. CLJS: warning-free node-test compile plus 15 changed-contract tests/95 assertions, exits 0, covering failed-initial, failed-update, nested, sibling, and leaf-upward order. Pinned focused clj-kondo: exit 0.
close_reason: Implemented scope-accurate private teardown naming and verified unchanged descendant-first semantics on JVM and CLJS.

title: vestigial(story): retire the standalone duplicate extends resolver
description:

`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/extends.cljc` is a 155-line standalone `:extends` resolver that is no longer on Story's runtime path. It is a duplicate, now-divergent implementation whose only actual consumer is a pair of focused tests of the duplicate itself.

Evidence

- Repo-wide search for `re-frame.story.extends`, `extends/resolve-extends`, and `extends/*max-extends-depth*` finds only: the namespace itself; the require at `tools/story/test/re_frame/story_test.clj:26`; calls in `extends-cycle-detection` and `extends-depth-cap` at lines 312/333; and a docstring cross-reference in `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/plan.cljc:163`. No production namespace, example, testbed, build alias, Story-MCP code, public facade, API page, or skill requires/calls it.
- The registration test immediately above those self-tests states that registered bodies keep raw `:extends` and that `re-frame.story.plan` is the single merge authority. Runtime compilation calls `plan/resolve-source-chain` (`plan.cljc:161-212`) and plan-owned merge logic; it never calls this namespace.
- The two implementations no longer express the same operation. `extends/resolve-extends` performs a straight parent-first map merge plus optional exclusive key groups. The compiled-plan authority applies field-specific semantics (for example setup append, local script/assertion ownership, deep/context merges). A passing standalone test therefore cannot prove the shipped runtime.
- `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/plan_test.cljc:229` already tests cycle failure through the actual plan compiler. Runtime inheritance/decorator behavior is also exercised in `story_test.clj`, `story_authoring_surface_test.clj`, and `story_decorator_chain_test.clj`; only the depth-cap witness still targets the duplicate rather than `plan/*max-extends-depth*`.
- History shows the standalone implementation arrived in `660fead138` (2026-05-11). The compiled-plan authority arrived later; by `82cd4bd1c8` (2026-07-10) the namespace doc explicitly acknowledged `re-frame.story.plan` as runtime authority and described this copy only as a helper for tooling/focused tests. No tooling consumer exists. The August vocabulary edit was mechanical (`:play-script` -> `:script`) and did not add a consumer.
- `tools/story/spec/015-Test-Coverage.md:303` still cites `story_test.clj`'s standalone bare-merge test as coverage even though runtime merge authority and semantics have moved to the plan compiler.
- Bead searches for `re-frame.story.extends`, `resolve-extends`, `extends resolver`, `Story extends`, `max-extends-depth`, and `standalone pure helper` returned no existing issue.

Impact

The duplicate ships code and a second public dynamic depth knob without a runtime/tooling consumer, lets tests go green against behavior the product does not execute, and invites error-id/depth/merge semantics to drift from the plan compiler. The coverage matrix overstates runtime coverage by naming the stale test.

Proposed disposition

Remove `re-frame.story.extends`. Move the still-useful depth-cap witness (and any missing unknown/cycle witness) to `re-frame.story.plan` through `variant-plan`/`resolve-source-chain`; delete redundant self-tests; remove the stale plan docstring cross-reference and update the spec/015 coverage row to name runtime-authority tests. Do not introduce a third facade shim. If a previously unknown downstream direct-require is discovered, consolidate both callers on one shared resolver rather than retaining divergent implementations.

Risks

Although the namespace is not facade-exported or documented as public API, a downstream project could direct-require it. Check published artifact/API policy and call out the removal in migration notes if required. Preserve the runtime error ids and the configurable depth-cap behavior at the plan authority.
acceptance_criteria:
- Repo-wide search finds no `re-frame.story.extends` namespace/file, `extends/resolve-extends`, or `extends/*max-extends-depth*` reference.
- The actual plan/runtime path has tests for unknown parent, cycle detection, the bound at `plan/*max-extends-depth*`, and representative field-specific inheritance (including setup/script/decorator behavior).
- `tools/story/spec/015-Test-Coverage.md` names tests that execute the plan/runtime authority and no longer claims the standalone bare merge proves runtime behavior.
- Story JVM and CLJS suites, source lint, API/spec drift checks, and affected feature-load/static build gates pass.
close_reason:
Done in PR #9075. Reachability re-proved at tip before deleting, twice per needle (line-oriented and whitespace-flattened over 4810 tracked files, .beads excluded) and each against a live control in the same files with the same instrument: `re-frame.story.extends` 3 hits / control `re-frame.story.plan` 74; `resolve-extends` 5 / control `resolve-source-chain` 4; `extends/*max-extends-depth*` only inside the namespace and its self-test. The two censuses agreed everywhere, so nothing was broken across a line. After the change `git grep -nF resolve-extends` returns nothing (exit 1) while `resolve-source-chain` still returns four.

The two self-tests were READ before being dropped, per the rule that a test encoding a guarantee the live resolver should also have is a finding rather than something to delete. Cycle was already witnessed at the live authority (plan_test.cljc extends-cycle-fails) and unknown-parent twice over (plan_test.cljc missing-parent-fails; story_test.clj extends-unknown-parent, which goes through plan/variant-plan). The DEPTH CAP was not — its only witness bound extends/*max-extends-depth*. That is the finding, and it is fixed rather than reported: the witness now lives at plan_test.cljc extends-depth-cap-fails, bound on plan/*max-extends-depth* and driven through variant-plan. plan/resolve-source-chain raises the identical three error ids with the same messages, so no guarantee is dropped.

Reach measured, not assumed: `.cljc` makes the witness host-free but buys no second gate — the :node-test build selects on "cljs-test$" and a plain -test ns does not match, so it runs under jvm-tools-story only. That is exactly the reach the JVM-only witnesses it replaced had. A first commit claimed CLJS reach too; a follow-up commit corrects it.

Also corrected: plan.cljc's docstring cross-reference to the retired namespace; a stale narration in story_authoring_validation_test.clj naming resolve-extends as the mechanism (registration stores the raw body and the compiler lowers :script/:plays to one slot); and spec/015's :extends row, which cited story_test.clj §extends-resolves-at-registration-time — a test name that no longer exists — now naming the tests that execute the plan/runtime authority.

Two `re-frame.story.extends` mentions survive on purpose, both in comments this PR wrote recording where the retired tests went: retirement bookkeeping, not live references.

Gates (captured exits): jvm-tools-story 1889/6959 0 failures exit 0 (and a planted wrong error id in the new witness took it to exit 1 with test/assertion counts unchanged, proving the plant stopped no namespace); npm run test:cljs 11209/55849 exit 0; test-fast-pr.sh exit 0; check_doc_slugs.py exit 0. All re-run after rebase onto current origin/main.

title: Make UIx registered-view diagnostic facts self-describing
description:
## Scope

The UIx registered-view diagnostic test family:
- implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_reg_view_direct_mount_dom_cljs_test.cljs
- implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_boot_order_source_coord_dom_cljs_test.cljs
- implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_source_coord_dom_elision_prod_test.cljs

This partition covers private helpers, locals, and private result-map keys only.

## Naming finding

Two capture helpers misstate their channels: with-captured-errors also records console.warn and window error events, while capture-warnings also records console.error. Their internal calls/orig-* names and returned :msgs facts conceal that the values are diagnostic messages. The direct-mount result uses context-free :initial, :after, :child, :children, and :ops keys; the source-coordinate result similarly uses :node?, :coord, and :view. Production-elision rows use user-fn/render/out for the registered view function, component head, and rendered React element.

## Ambiguity cost

These tests distinguish several subtle failure channels and multiple phases of one mount. Generic or channel-inaccurate names make an assertion's provenance unclear and encourage future coverage to inspect the wrong channel or confuse a view head with its rendered element.

## Proposed names

- with-captured-errors -> capture-render-diagnostics; capture-warnings -> capture-console-diagnostics.
- calls -> messages; orig-warn/orig-error -> original-warn/original-error; matching -> matching-messages; re/msg(s) -> pattern/message(s).
- Direct-mount facts: :msgs -> :diagnostics, :initial -> :initial-text, :after -> :updated-text, :child -> :child-text, :payload -> :observed-payload, :children -> :children-present?, :ops -> :frame-ops; give corresponding locals full names.
- Source-coordinate facts: :msgs -> :diagnostics, :node? -> :view-root-present?, :coord -> :source-coordinate, :view -> :view-id-attribute; expand output locals.
- Production-elision locals: user-fn -> view-fn, render/wrapped -> view-head, out -> rendered-element, props -> element-props where applicable.

## Compatibility and risks

All names are private to tests. Preserve public rf/reg-view*, rf/view, adapter functions, UIx/React interop properties, data-rf2-source-coord/data-rf-view attributes, regex contents, event ids, and classifier filenames. Result-map key changes must update every producer/destructure/assertion atomically.

## Acceptance criteria

- Helper names accurately describe every channel they capture.
- Result facts distinguish mount phase, DOM text, observed CLJS values, hook operations, and annotation attributes without reading producer code.
- Repository searches find no stale old private helper names or old result-key destructures in these files.
- Focused registered-view browser and production-elision tests pass.
- git diff --check and focused lint pass with no new warnings.

title: reagent-slim adapter tests: replace opaque fixture and spy helper names
description:
## Finding

Several private helpers in the reagent-slim adapter contract tests are harder to understand than the production behavior they isolate: `fresh-slim`, `fake-root`, `spy-rdc!`, `of-kind`, `a-mock-emitter`, `with-cleared-emitter`, and repeated `mk-fake-root` spellings. ## Evidence and ambiguity cost

- `test/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim_client_root_cljs_test.cljs:16-54` uses `fresh-slim`, `fake-root`, `spy-rdc!`, and `of-kind`; only the spy docstring reveals it runs a body and returns captured Root API calls. `rdc` is a namespace alias, not the behavior under test, and `of-kind` does not say it filters calls.

title: reagent-slim static renderer: name helpers by serialized output role
description:
## Finding

The pure static HTML serializer in `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs` mixes abbreviated attribute/value names with helpers whose names describe input representation rather than emitted output: `attr-name`, `emit-attr(s)`, `merge-shorthand`, `react-component-comment`, `emit-dom-vector`, and `emit-vector`.

## Evidence and ambiguity cost

- `attr-name`, `named->str`, `style-value->str`, and `attr-value-string` span lines 355-515; each sits in security/parity-sensitive serialization code where spelling out attribute/string roles reduces context switching.
- `emit-attr`/`emit-attrs` at lines 618-694 perform filtering plus mutation of the output buffer, not merely attribute formatting.
- `merge-shorthand` at lines 704-725 merges parsed tag id/class shorthand; the unqualified name does not say what shorthand.
- `react-component-comment` at lines 733-737 is an emitting operation that appends the opaque placeholder.
- `emit-dom-vector` and `emit-vector` at lines 744-890 require readers to remember one emits a DOM element and the other dispatches every Hiccup vector head.
- The serializer's only external surface is `render-to-static-markup`; exact searches show these candidates are private. Targeted history traces them to the original Stage 4-E serializer, with no compatibility consumers.

## Recommendation

Adopt consistent `attribute`/`string` spellings and emitted-shape names: `attribute-name`, `named-value->string`, `style-value->string`, `attribute-value-string`, `emit-attribute`, `emit-attributes`, `merge-tag-shorthand`, `emit-react-component-placeholder`, `emit-dom-element`, and `emit-hiccup-vector`; align private constant names and in-slice comments/spec references where needed.

## Contracts and risk

Preserve byte-for-byte HTML output, attribute order/filtering, escaping, React casing tables, boolean/style/event behavior, placeholder literal, exception payloads, and public `render-to-static-markup`. The names are private; no compatibility aliases should be introduced. The IMPL-SPEC reconciliation owned by `rf2-6r9j.33` must not be broadened here: only mechanically update names directly made stale by this patch.

title: reagent-slim template: clarify prop conversion, key lookup, and shared interop path
description:
## Finding

The private Hiccup/React conversion pipeline in `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs` obscures three important distinctions with abbreviated or misleading names: nested versus top-level prop mutation (`kv-conv`/`top-prop-conv`), the already-located key rule versus argv key lookup (`react-key`/`get-react-key`), and the shared DOM-plus-`:>` path named `native-element` even though the source explicitly says it handles foreign React components too.

## Evidence and ambiguity cost

- Lines 490-548 show both `*-conv` helpers mutate a JS accumulator with `aset`; only their long docstrings reveal nested-map versus target-aware top-level behavior, and neither name signals mutation.
- Lines 740-789 distinguish a rule receiving an already-located props slot from a finder that searches argv, but `react-key` and `get-react-key` do not communicate that distinction.
- Lines 988-996 name the value tested by `props-slot?` `head`, then immediately warn in prose that it is a slot value, not a vector head.
- Lines 998-1033 state `native-element` is the path for both native DOM tags and `:>` interop; lines 1148-1158 create a synthetic tag for the foreign component and call it. The current name therefore makes the interop call look categorically wrong.
- `dont-camel-case` and `capitalize` at lines 358-381 omit that the values are prop-name prefixes/segments.
- Exact searches find no external Var consumers because these candidates are private. The remaining matches are comments/spec text, tests, or independent benchmark-local functions. History shows `native-element` began as a DOM path and later accumulated interop responsibilities, explaining the drift.

## Recommendation

Use `add-converted-nested-prop!`, `add-converted-top-level-prop!`, `react-key-from-meta-or-props`, `react-key-from-argv`, `converted-props-element`, `verbatim-prop-prefixes`, and `capitalize-prop-segment`; rename `head` to `slot-value`, `native?` to `dom-element?`, and `synth-*` locals to `synthetic-*`. Update every in-slice source/test/doc reference.

## Contracts and risk

Preserve public template Vars, Hiccup sentinel heads, dynamic vars, metadata/prop keys, React element/props shapes, cache objects, mutation and lookup order, source-coordinate consumption, and hot-path allocation behavior. Do not rename namespaces/files or add compatibility wrappers. Do not change the callable-prop branches/tests owned by `rf2-6r9j.30`.

## Duplicate search

All-status bead data was searched for each old name plus template/interop naming concepts. No bead owns this naming cluster; `rf2-6r9j.30` is a separate test-validity/correctness task and remains untouched.
acceptance_criteria:
- The proposed private/local names replace their ambiguous predecessors in template source and all directly referencing reagent-slim comments/tests/docs.
- Exact old-name searches over `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim` are empty, apart from any explicitly retained historical quotation that is justified in the bead close notes.
- Nested versus top-level prop conversion, DOM versus interop target awareness, meta-over-props key precedence, source-coordinate stamping, and React output remain behaviorally identical.
- The callable-prop behavior/tests owned by `rf2-6r9j.30`, public Vars, keys, metadata, and interop heads are unchanged.
- Focused template tests plus lint/compile checks pass, and `git diff --check` is clean.

Branch order, hot-path shapes, reserved-key filtering, public convert-prop-value/props-slot?/vec-to-elem names, emitted keys, and React interop fields are unchanged. title: reagent-slim component lifecycle: name helpers and locals by role
description:
## Finding

The private Form-3 lifecycle plumbing in `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs` contains names that omit their decisive context (`validate-spec!`, `prev-argv-from`, `bind-and-call`, `install-lifecycle!`) and generic locals (`klass`, `proto`, lifecycle `f`, `cached-rea`). This makes a contract-heavy bridge harder to follow than its behavior warrants.

## Evidence and ambiguity cost

- `validate-spec!` at lines 135-155 validates specifically a `create-class` spec against the seven-key cap, not an arbitrary spec.
- `prev-argv-from` at lines 358-362 extracts `__rfArgv` specifically from React previous props; the omitted source is the important distinction fixed/documented by `rf2-08hx1`.
- `bind-and-call` at lines 364-371 is not a generic binding helper: it establishes `*current-component*` around one callback.
- `install-lifecycle!` at lines 382-495 installs several React prototype/static methods, not one lifecycle value. Nearby `klass`/`proto` and three unrelated `f` bindings force readers to reconstruct which class/prototype/callback each closure captures.
- `make-render-method` uses `cached-rea`/`new-rea` for the component render Reaction, even though `rea` is otherwise the namespace's scheduler abbreviation.
- Exact repository searches show the helpers are private and source-confined. Targeted history shows the lifecycle names originated in Stage 4-C; later correctness fixes changed behavior without establishing them as public compatibility seams.

## Recommendation

Rename to `validate-class-spec!`, `previous-argv-from-props`, `call-with-current-component`, and `install-lifecycle-methods!`; use `component-class`, `prototype`, lifecycle-specific callback names, and `render-reaction` locals where those values cross closure boundaries.

title: ssr-node HTTP launcher: name buffers, parsed requests, and launch settings
description:
## Coverage and evidence

The HTTP/launcher edge has several names that conceal the represented phase. `src/http.cjs:92-123` calls buffered request chunks `parts`, the over-ceiling state `over`, and each chunk/error `c`/`e`; `handleRender` calls the decoded protocol request `parsed` and buffered response HTML `buffered`. `bin/serve.cjs` calls its numeric parser `integer`, the parsed number `n`, and the combined numeric launch settings `limits` even though the map also includes `port`; the live transport is `http` and its bound address is only `bound`. These all descend from the initial transport/launcher commits (b2b35bf6e9 and 608b2a24b1).

The ambiguity costs the most at boundaries: `parts` could be decoded request partitions, `buffered` could be a boolean mode, `limits.port` is not a limit, and `http` does not say that it is the closeable transport returned by `serve`.

## Recommendation

Use edge-role names such as `bodyChunks`, `receivedBytes`, `overLimit`, `chunk`, `renderRequest`, `bufferedHtmlChunks`, `parseIntegerFlag`, `minimum`, `numericOptions`, `transport`, and `boundAddress`. Keep conventional Node handler `req`/`res` names, public transport API, CLI flags, and wire fields unchanged.

## Compatibility and exclusions

This is private/local identifier work only. Preserve exported `serve`, `statusFor`, `STATUS`, the returned `{server, port, host, close}` object, CLI flags/help/ready-line/exit codes, request selection semantics, response headers, and serialized body/refusal shapes. Do not edit the stale help/README wording owned by rf2-6r9j.86 or the retired-selector behavior pinned by rf2-6r9j.72.
acceptance_criteria:
1. HTTP body intake names distinguish raw chunks, received byte count, and the over-limit state; rendering names distinguish decoded requests from buffered response chunks.
2. Launcher names distinguish flag parsing, numeric launch options, the running transport, and its bound address.
3. Exported API, returned object shape, CLI flags/help text, ready line, headers, status mapping, selector behavior, and all wire keys remain unchanged.
4. rf2-6r9j.86's documentation targets remain untouched.
5. Exact searches, serve/bytes/protocol tests, lint, and the full ssr-node gate pass.

title: ssr-node isolate pool: name lifecycle state by ownership and phase
description:
## Coverage and evidence

`src/isolate.cjs` and `src/pool.cjs` implement the worker lifecycle. The isolate's private state machine uses `_nextRequestSeq` for an internal render-dispatch ID distinct from public `requestId`, `_settle(id, act)`, `_fail`, `_die`, and repeated `p`/`w`/`msg` locals. The pool calls its boot-and-register operation `_spawn`, its replacement-only race-safe wrapper `_spawnTracked`, stores only replacement boots in a generic `spawning` set, and stores the full membership in `all`; teardown and replacement paths use `fresh`, `w`, `i`, and another `all`. `_spawnTracked`/`spawning` were added by 8ab673ea78 specifically to close the replacement-vs-close race, so their lifecycle purpose is stable and more precise than the mechanism name.

These names blur ownership and phase in code whose correctness depends on exactly those distinctions: public versus isolate-local IDs, initial boots versus replacement boots, pending render settlement versus worker termination, and all isolates versus idle isolates.

## Recommendation

Use private role names such as `_nextRenderId`, `_settlePendingRender`, `_failPendingRender`, `_terminateWorker`, `pendingRender`, `worker`, `_startIsolate`, `_startReplacement`, `startingReplacements`, `isolates`, `startedIsolates`, `failedStart`, and `replacement`. Keep public stats and refusal payload keys unchanged.

## Compatibility and exclusions

The affected methods/fields are package-private and have no repository consumer outside these two files. Preserve public `Isolate.render/start/close`, `Pool.acquire/release/stats/close`, `busy`, worker message keys, refusal detail keys, and health JSON. Do not remove `renders` or the `WORKER_PATH` export; rf2-6r9j.84 owns those vestiges.

title: ssr-node render pipeline: distinguish frames, dispatch IDs, and module returns
description:
## Coverage and evidence

`src/service.cjs` bridges an isolate callback into the public async generator with `req`, `queue`, `wake`, `nudge`, `finished`, `failure`, `terminal`, and `run`. The names hide which side owns each value: the queue holds pending public frames, `wake` is the suspended generator continuation, `terminal` is the isolate's render result, and `run` is the completion/release promise. `src/worker.cjs` uses `mod`, `post`, `id`, `seq`, `snapshot`, `call`, and especially `out` for the application module's returned value at the fail-closed egress check. These names date to b2b35bf6e9; the body-only egress hardening in 67d4d9338a made the returned value security-significant without renaming it.

A reader currently has to infer whether `id` is the caller's `requestId` or the isolate-local render ID, and whether `out` is emitted HTML or the forbidden second-channel return. The callback/generator bridge similarly makes `run` and `terminal` easy to confuse with frames.

## Recommendation

Name service values by asynchronous role (`validatedRequest`, `pendingFrames`, `resumeConsumer`, `wakeConsumer`, `renderFinished`, `renderFailure`, `renderResult`, `renderCompletion`). Name worker-private values by boundary role (`renderModule`, `renderId`, `chunkSeq`, `stateSnapshot`, `runtimeSnapshot`, `renderCall`, `moduleReturnValue`, `postMessage`). Update comments and internal calls together.

## Compatibility and exclusions

Do not rename public `Service`, `renderFrames`, `renderToString`, `createService`, the render-module `render`/`emit` contract, message discriminators or keys (`t`, `id`, `seq`), request/frame fields, or serialized refusal details. Do not edit the worker `stack` payloads owned for removal by rf2-6r9j.77, and do not absorb the `chunkFrame` integration owned by rf2-6r9j.74.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Service bridge bindings identify pending frames, the suspended consumer, render completion, result, and failure without generic `queue`/`wake`/`run`/`terminal` names.
2. Worker bindings distinguish the isolate-local render ID, state/runtime snapshots, render call, and forbidden module return value.
3. Public APIs, render-module contract, worker message schema, frame schema, refusal behavior, and stack-removal target remain byte/shape compatible.
4. Exact old/new searches, lint, focused egress/streaming tests, and the full ssr-node gate pass.

title: ssr-node protocol validation: name boundary values by role
description:
## Coverage and evidence

`implementation/ssr-node/src/protocol.cjs` is the fail-closed module/request grammar. Its internal validation names obscure the values being adjudicated: `validateAllowlist(where, id, entry, { allowlist, keys })` uses `keys` for the human partition label (`app-db`/`runtime-db`), not keys; `validateModule(mod, where)` hides that `where` is a diagnostic module label; `validatePartition(req, entry, entryId, ...)` then uses `k`, `v`, and `bytes` at the security boundary; `validateRequest(req, tables)` names the two validation results `state` and `runtime` even though each is `{partition, bytes}`, and `why` is the deliberate-refusal explanation. These names date to initial commit b2b35bf6e9; 9a42302f7a added the second partition without resolving the role ambiguity.

The ambiguity makes review of the most security-sensitive path need repeated lookups: `keys` sounds like a collection, `entry` alternates between an ID and a config, and `state`/`runtime` sometimes mean maps and sometimes validation results.

## Recommendation

Use role names such as `moduleLabel`, `entryId`, `entryConfig`, `allowlistField`, `partitionLabel`, `partitionField`, `partitionKey`, `ednText`, `partitionBytes`, `stateValidation`, `runtimeValidation`, `requestBytes`, and `intentionalRefusalReason`. Keep the public/exported validator names and every field/refusal spelling unchanged.

## Compatibility and exclusions

This is identifier-only: JavaScript parameter names and private locals are not call contracts. Preserve exported `validateModule`/`validateRequest`, `PARTITIONS`, `CODE`, all serialized request/detail keys, and the `STATE_KEY_NOT_ALLOWED` wire member. Do not touch `chunkFrame`, `KEY_TEXT`/`refuse` exports, or other residue owned by rf2-6r9j.74/.84.

title: Clarify SSR Ring HTTP metadata helper roles
description:
## Finding

In headers.clj, the folds use m/k/v, v*, key*, and existing across case-folding and multi-value promotion. trust.clj similarly validates k/v. These names make security-sensitive wire code harder to audit.

## Evidence

- implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/cookie.clj:37-112: url-encode is specifically a cookie-value encoder; validate-attribute-string! is specifically the Set-Cookie attribute injection gate.
- implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/headers.clj:17-122: m/k/v and starred temporaries cover the Ring header map, logical header name/value, wire-coerced value, emitted key, and existing value.

- API-manifest configuration classifies these sub-namespaces as internal. The public facade name cookie->set-cookie-header and every header/error/wire key remain contracts.
- History shows these helpers were extracted as implementation plumbing; repository-wide searches find no external call to the private cookie helpers.
- Phase-1 beads rf2-6r9j.47/.50 own removal/lint residue, not these surviving names.

## Recommendation

title: spec-resource race control: name cold-load actors and phases
description:
## Coverage and evidence

`implementation/spec-resource/test/re_frame/build/spec_resource_test.clj` is the deterministic control for the cold-load race closed by `resolve-after-require`. Its concurrency harness uses generic names that obscure which actor and phase each value belongs to: `counter` generates unique namespace and gate names, `fixture-root` is specifically a temporary classpath root, `generate-fixture!` writes a namespace whose initializer is deliberately blocked, and `run-probe` observes a resolver while that load is held open. Inside the probe, `answer`, `loaded`, `armed`, `observed`, `loader`, `observer`, `sym`, and `in-window` require repeated backtracking to distinguish loader-thread results, observer-thread results before/after release, the probe Var, and the held-open phase. The returned keys repeat that ambiguity (`:sym`, `:in-window`, `:observed`, `:loaded`).

This matters because the test's proof depends on actor and phase identity: the known-broken resolver must return an unbound Var during the held-open load, while the shipped resolver must block and both actors must see a bound Var after release. Misreading `loaded` as a load-status flag or `observed` as the during-window observation weakens review of the one deterministic witness for the defect.

History confirms these are original names from `5311835961`, when the whole control was introduced. Searches across all-status beads for `spec-resource`, `run-probe`, `recording-slurp`, and `resolve-after-require` found only Phase-1 removal beads `rf2-6r9j.80` and `.82`; neither owns this retained race control.

## Recommendation

Rename private test helpers, locals, and result keys by role and phase: for example `cold-load-iterations`, `unique-name-sequence`, `fixture-classpath-root`, `write-blocked-fixture-namespace!`, `observe-resolver-during-load`, `probe-var-symbol`, `observe-var-state`, `loader-result`, `observer-entered-resolver`, `observer-result`, `loader-thread`, `observer-thread`, and `:during-load` / `:observer-result` / `:loader-result`. Update docstrings and every test consumer together.

## Compatibility and exclusions

This is test-private vocabulary only. Preserve the public namespace/file names, `resolve-after-require`, `slurp-resource`, the known-broken `requiring-resolve` control, thread/gate timing, assertion semantics, and production serialized data. Do not rename or edit `classpath-root`, `spec-file`, the non-CLJS branch, the root dependency, or bench classpath entries: those are Phase-1 deletion targets owned by `rf2-6r9j.80` and `.82`.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The cold-load harness names every generated identity, actor, synchronization point, and result by its role and phase; generic `counter`, `run-probe`, `answer`, `loaded`, `armed`, `observed`, `loader`, `observer`, and old result-key roles are absent.
2. The known-broken control still deterministically observes an unbound Var during load, while `resolve-after-require` still blocks during load and both actors observe bound Vars after release.
3. Public source APIs, namespace/file names, production data, Phase-1 deletion targets, iteration count, synchronization, and assertion behavior are unchanged.
4. Exact old/new searches, the artifact JVM suite with a planted negative control, and diff validation pass.
close_reason: Implemented in 1145dcda8e: private cold-load control names now distinguish generated identities, loader/observer actors, synchronization facts, and during/post-release results. Public APIs and Phase-1 targets are unchanged; artifact tests, pinned clj-kondo, exact searches, and diff checks pass.

title: Xray Epoch: prune fourteen unreachable private helpers and styles
description:
## Finding

The live Xray Epoch implementation retains fourteen private definitions that are statically unreachable: two projection helpers and twelve view helpers/styles. Several adjacent comments still describe these dead values as active maintenance contracts.

## Evidence

- A clean `clj-kondo --lint tools/xray/src` reports `Unused private var` for exactly these Epoch projection definitions: `op->row-kind` and `state-keyword-or-leaf` in `panels/epoch/projection.cljc`.
- The same run reports the following private definitions in `panels/epoch/view.cljs`: `link-button-nowrap-style`, `table-glyph-cell-header-style`, `disposed-th-60-style`, `disposed-th-40-style`, `views-th-50-style`, `schema-violation-headline-style`, `schema-violation-headline-id-style`, `schema-violation-explain-toggle-style`, `coeffect-row-view`, `source-coord-display`, `schema-violation-where-label`, and `where->handler-kind`.
- Repo-wide exact-symbol searches find no executable call/reference for any of the fourteen. The only extra hits are comments: for example the projection doc instructs maintainers to update the unused `op->row-kind` table, and the live view contains a "companion swap" comment naming unused `coeffect-row-view`.
- Every definition is private, so there is no supported external var contract to preserve. Current render/projection paths use other helpers/inline styles and compile without reaching these names.
- File history shows the values are residue across successive Epoch view/projection revisions rather than entries in a reflection-driven registry; no dynamic symbol-resolution mechanism or string-key catalogue names them.
- Bead searches for `unreachable Epoch helpers`, `dead Epoch helpers`, `unused private definitions`, and description search for `op->row-kind` found no existing issue.

## Impact

These definitions add false branches and false styling authorities inside two already-large Epoch namespaces, keep standing lint warnings noisy, and misdirect maintainers with comments that require updates to tables/components the runtime never reads.

## Proposed disposition

Delete only the fourteen listed private definitions and repair the comments that present them as live. Keep behavior-bearing callers and the currently selected styles/helpers unchanged. Treat any newly discovered computed consumer as evidence to retain and document that one definition rather than broadening the cleanup.

## Risks

The Epoch view is large and some similarly named helpers are live. Make the change symbol-by-symbol, avoid adjoining style consolidation, and verify no macro/string/dynamic resolution exists. Preserve all current Epoch projection rows, schema-violation rendering, source-link behavior, and coeffect display.
acceptance_criteria:
- The fourteen named private definitions and stale comments referring to them are removed, unless a concrete current runtime consumer is demonstrated and documented for an individual symbol.
- Repo-wide exact-symbol searches return no orphan definition/comment residue.
- A fresh `clj-kondo --lint tools/xray/src` no longer reports these fourteen `Unused private var` warnings; unrelated pre-existing findings are not silently suppressed.
- Xray CLJS/JVM tests, the Epoch view tests, node-test build, and relevant panel-gallery/feature smoke gates pass with unchanged rendered behavior.

title: Xray: retire the unused perf-tier module
description:
## Finding

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/perf_tier.cljc` is an orphaned duration-to-colour classification module. No production Xray namespace calls it; only its dedicated test and a theme variable-resolution test require it, while its namespace contract still presents retired panels as live consumers.

## Evidence

Searches for its classification/render helpers find no production source, testbed, example, facade, or skill caller.
- The namespace doc says the Performance panel re-exports it and marks `performance` and `event_detail` tier-dot surfaces `LIVE`. Commit `646e38273d` removed the Performance panel and helpers in the dead-panel sweep. Commit `aeb34400c0` retired the Handler/Event panel and its caller. No replacement consumer was introduced.

Current `tools/xray/testbeds/panel_gallery/fixtures.cljs` mentions perf-tier dots only in fixture prose/data; it does not require or call this module, so fixture comments do not establish reachability.

## Impact

The bundle and test matrix maintain a design-system abstraction with no rendering consumer, while source/spec prose incorrectly says retired panels are live. This creates a false extension point and lets future duration thresholds drift between actual UI code and an unused supposed authority.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the orphaned module and tests that exist only to pin it, and reconcile stale Performance/Event catalogue and source-ledger claims. If a current tier-dot surface genuinely needs the shared classifier, wire that caller and add integration coverage before retaining the module; do not treat fixture prose as a consumer.

## Risks

title: (BUG) reagent-slim error-boundary integration tests are guaranteed green
description:
## Correctness finding

Two reagent-slim tests advertised as React error-boundary integration proofs are guaranteed green without exercising React error propagation.

## Evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/impl/component_cljs_test.cljs:512-532` creates `outer` and `inner` boundary classes, but never uses or mounts `outer`. It manually invokes only `inner.prototype.componentDidCatch`, then asserts `outer-fired` remains zero. `clj-kondo` independently reports the `outer` binding unused at line 519. The assertion cannot detect broken nested-boundary isolation.
- Lines 534-555 name a test `error-boundary-during-commit-via-component-did-mount`, but create no child, invoke no `componentDidMount`, and mount no React tree. They manually call the boundary's `componentDidCatch`, duplicating the direct callback-forwarding proof at lines 470-486.
- The suite header at lines 11-14 claims it proves errors during child render/commit and nested isolation. Lines 462-467 acknowledge the tests use no React render and say a real-DOM test belongs in the browser target.
- A repository-wide search for `reagent2.core/create-class` / `component-did-catch` in tests finds no real-DOM reagent-slim error-boundary scenario. The other slim DOM create-class tests cover lifecycle prev-state and shouldComponentUpdate, not error propagation.
- These tests and claims originated in `21d4b06aae`, whose commit message likewise reports child-render, commit-error, and nested-isolation coverage.

## Impact

The retained seven-key Form-3 compatibility feature can break at its React integration boundary while the suite continues to report coverage. The unused outer class also adds dead test setup and makes a tautology look like behavioral evidence.

## Proposed disposition

Replace the two pseudo-integration tests with a real browser/DOM scenario using reagent-slim's actual `create-root` and `create-class` path. Exercise a descendant render or mount-lifecycle throw beneath nested slim boundaries; prove the inner boundary handles it, the outer does not, fallback commits, and callback payload/counts are correct. Keep the direct unit test for wrapper argument forwarding. If nested/commit propagation is intentionally delegated entirely to React and not a reagent-slim contract, remove the false tests and suite claims instead of retaining guaranteed-green proxies.

## Risks

React deliberately reports caught errors to the console and development StrictMode may replay work. The harness must capture/restore expected console output, assert actual mounts/callback counts, and avoid accepting an early render failure or skipped test as green.

## Duplicate search

Searched every bead state/field for `nested boundary`, `component-did-catch`, `error boundary`, `component_cljs_test`, and reagent-slim. `rf2-08hx1` owns lifecycle argv; `rf2-wdvlp` owns a Hicasso error-boundary defect; neither covers these tests. No duplicate exists.
acceptance_criteria:
- No test named or documented as child-render, child-commit, or nested-boundary integration proves the claim by directly invoking `componentDidCatch` in isolation.
- A real-DOM reagent-slim proof mounts nested boundaries and a throwing descendant through the production renderer; it asserts the descendant path ran, the inner catch fired with the expected error/info, the fallback committed, and the outer catch count remained zero.
- The commit-phase arm proves the throwing lifecycle actually ran; the render-phase arm, if retained as a separate claim, proves its throwing render actually ran.
- A negative control that removes the inner boundary or breaks its lifecycle installation makes the focused test fail rather than merely changing console noise.
- The existing direct callback-forwarding, derived-state, rethrow, and no-boundary unit contracts remain green without duplicate tautological tests.
- Suite/header/IMPL-SPEC coverage prose names only behavior the executed tests actually prove.
close_reason: Confirmed at tip and fixed. Both tests were vacuous exactly as filed: error-boundary-nested-isolation built an outer boundary, never mounted it, invoked only the inner prototype's componentDidCatch, then asserted the outer counter was zero; error-boundary-during-commit-via-component-did-mount created no child and mounted no tree. The file's ns docstring also claimed the boundary tests 'use a real ReactDOM root' -- false since 21d4b06aae introduced both. Both removed and replaced by a mounted proof under a real React 19 createRoot: reagent2.dom.error-boundary-dom-cljs-test (child-render throw, child-commit componentDidMount throw, nested isolation), each asserting the throwing path actually ran, the fallback committed to the DOM, and React reported via the root's onCaughtError. Its outer-boundary-catches-when-inner-is-absent arm mounts the same throwing descendant under the outer boundary alone, so the nested arm's zero is a measurement. Non-vacuity proved by negative control: disabling the getDerivedStateFromError auto-install turns the browser lane red with 3 failures, one in EACH new test, each naming its own uncommitted fallback; restore verified by blob hash. Production behaviour was NOT changed and no production defect was exposed -- the boundary contract holds as specified. Browser lane green 781 tests/4249 assertions/0 failures. PR #9077.

title: (BUG) reagent-slim callable-prop regressions never reach the Fn/IFn branches
description:
## Correctness finding

The two callable-prop regression tests added for rf2-wyocr do not execute the production branches their names and comments claim to protect.

## Evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:485-486,596-618` puts `(js-val? v)` before `(fn? v)` and `(ifn? v)`. `js-val?` is true for every ordinary JavaScript function (`goog/typeOf` is `function`), so the plain `(fn ...)` values used by `convert-prop-value-fn-preserves-identity-rf2-wyocr` at test lines 197-216 return from the first branch. Deleting both explicit `fn?` arms would leave that regression green.
- ClojureScript 1.12.42's `cljs.core/with-meta` wraps a JavaScript function in object-backed `MetaFn`; `fn?` is true because `MetaFn` satisfies `Fn`, while `goog/typeOf` is `object`. That is the ordinary value shape that actually reaches the explicit `fn?` branch, but the test never supplies one.
- `convert-prop-value-non-fn-ifn-still-wrapped` at test lines 218-234 explicitly admits its keyword reaches `named?` and its map reaches `map?`. It never supplies a value reaching `(ifn? v)`, never invokes a wrapper, and would remain green if the `ifn?` arms were deleted.
- Commit `874eb9ef49` introduced both branches/tests and states the identity regression is pinned. Its claim that every fn had previously been wrapped overlooks the pre-existing `js-val?` first arm; the implementation change materially protects object-backed Fn values, not the plain JS function used in the regression.

## Impact

Future cleanup or condition reordering can silently remove MetaFn identity preservation or non-fn IFn wrapping while the named regressions stay green. Metadata-bearing callbacks would then receive fresh wrappers and defeat React memoisation; custom object-backed callable props could cease to be invokable from JavaScript.

## Proposed disposition

Make the tests branch-real: add metadata to a function for both public arities and assert exact identity; define a focused object-backed value that satisfies `IFn` but not `Fn`, `named?`, `map?`, or `coll?`, then prove conversion returns an invokable JS function with correct argument/return behavior. Correct the production docstring's examples (`keywords`, maps, sets, and vectors are intercepted by earlier branches and are not evidence for the `ifn?` wrapper).

## Risks

Do not reorder the production ladder merely to make the old examples true: map/coll/named conversion is part of the published prop-conversion behavior. The fixture must model a genuinely reachable callable object and avoid compiler-specific accidental classification.

## Duplicate search

Searched all 575 bead records in every state for `convert-prop-value`, `MetaFn`, `wyocr`, `callable`, `fn identity`, and the test path. The only matches (`rf2-y1jkm`, `rf2-6sqv`, `rf2-oz7wr`) concern Hicasso performance, console rendering, and UIx registry heads; none owns these reagent-slim branches.
acceptance_criteria:
- The 1-arg and 2-arg identity regressions use an object-backed metadata-bearing Fn and prove `identical?` with the input and across repeated conversions.
- A focused non-fn IFn fixture actually reaches the wrapper arm, returns a JavaScript-invokable function, forwards representative arities, and preserves the fixture's return values.
- Non-vacuity is demonstrated: removing/bypassing the `fn?` arm fails the MetaFn identity test, and removing/bypassing the `ifn?` arm fails the callable-object test.
- Plain JS functions still pass through unchanged; named values, maps, and collections retain their current earlier-branch semantics.
- The `convert-prop-value` docstring and test names no longer claim that keywords/maps/sets/vectors exercise a wrapper they cannot reach.
- Focused template tests pass in the normal CLJS test target and production build mode remains unaffected.
close_reason: Confirmed at tip. This is a TEST defect, NOT a production ordering defect -- the bead's own Risks section rules the ladder must not be reordered, and that is correct: map/coll/named conversion is published prop-conversion behaviour. js-val? is (not (identical? 'object' (goog/typeOf x))), so it is true for every plain JS function; the plain fns in convert-prop-value-fn-preserves-identity-rf2-wyocr and the keyword and map in convert-prop-value-non-fn-ifn-still-wrapped all returned from earlier arms, and both tests would have stayed green with the fn? and ifn? arms deleted. Repaired by moving each test to the value shape that actually reaches its arm: a MetaFn ((with-meta f m), object-backed and satisfying Fn) for the identity regressions in both public arities, and a deftype satisfying IFn but not Fn/named?/map?/coll? for the wrapper, proven to come back as a real JS function invoked via .call with arguments forwarded to the fixture's own -invoke. Each test now asserts its routing preconditions rather than assuming them. Non-vacuity proved both ways: removing the fn? arm reds ONLY the MetaFn test (4 failures, identity replaced by the wrapper); removing the ifn? arm reds ONLY the callable test (3 failures, 'function' vs 'object'); both restores verified by blob hash. Docstring corrected -- it cited keywords, maps, sets and vectors as ifn?-arm examples and all four are intercepted earlier; it now walks the cond in the order taken. No executable production change. PR #9077.

title: reagent-slim tests: remove five dead imports and static-prop
description:
## Finding

The reagent-slim test slice carries one unreachable private helper and five unused imports/referred macros.

## Evidence

`clj-kondo --lint implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test --cache false` reports:

title: reagent-slim StrictMode test still says the fixed bug fails by design
description:
## Finding

The live StrictMode regression test still tells contributors that its assertions fail by design and that the production bug is unfixed, although the fix landed immediately afterward and the test is now a required green regression.

## Evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim_strict_mode_dom_cljs_test.cljs:6-12` says assertions `(a)` and `(b)` `FAIL BY DESIGN`, the substrate does not honor the contract, and the fix belongs to a separate bead.
- Its `FINDING` block at lines 29-51 speaks in present tense: StrictMode leaves every slim component reactively dead and a production fix is still needed.
- Commit `2c4a87e3df` (`fix(adapters/reagent-slim): re-establish render Reaction after StrictMode remount (rf2-6b6pex)`) landed the repair after test commit `66e9e2af0e`.
- Current production code at `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs:389-415,432-442` installs a remount marker, queues a render on the second `componentDidMount`, and documents the fixed sequence.
- The test remains discovered by both browser and node selectors, so this is live test guidance rather than archived design history.

## Impact

The header normalizes red output from a required acceptance test and directs maintainers to file/fix work that is already complete. During a genuine regression, a reader could dismiss the failure as expected.

## Proposed disposition

Rewrite the header as regression history: state the former failure, name the fixing commit/bead, and describe the invariants the now-green test protects. Remove all present-tense `FAIL BY DESIGN`, `not yet honour`, and separate-fix instructions. Do not weaken the assertions or erase the useful explanation of the StrictMode lifecycle sequence.

## Risks

The historical diagnosis is valuable and should remain clearly marked as past behavior. Avoid turning the header into a terse comment that loses the reason for the remount marker or the two non-vacuous assertions.

## Duplicate search

Searched all bead states/fields for `StrictMode`, `a07937`, `6b6pex`, `FAIL BY DESIGN`, the test filename, and `reagent-slim`. StrictMode matches concern Hicasso or unrelated surfaces; the historical IDs are no longer live bead records. No current bead owns this stale header.
acceptance_criteria:
- The live test file contains no present-tense claim that its assertions are expected to fail or that production lacks the repair.
- The header records the former failure and fixing commit/bead as history, then states the current green invariants: post-remount reactive update and watch-count cleanup.
- The production/test explanation agrees on the remount marker and forced re-render path.
- The StrictMode DOM test remains enrolled and passes; a focused negative control that disables the reattach behavior makes its reactive-update assertion fail.
- Any now-unused `cljs.test/testing` import may be removed, but no assertion or browser gating is weakened.
close_reason: Confirmed at tip: the STATUS block still read FAIL BY DESIGN and directed maintainers to file work already complete, and the FINDING block was present tense. Verified 2c4a87e3df (rf2-6b6pex) exists and landed 2026-07-12, the same day as the test's own commit 66e9e2af0e. Header rewritten as dated history rather than erased, per the standing rule on retired states: STATUS now says the file is a required green regression, then records what it used to say and when that ended; the FINDING block is retitled FORMER BUG, moved to past tense and KEPT because it is the diagnosis the remount marker was built from; a new section describes the fix (cljsRemountReattach set by the transient componentWillUnmount, read by the now-unconditional componentDidMount, which queues a render so make-render-method recreates the Reaction) and states what each assertion fails on. Those claims were verified rather than asserted: disabling the reattach reds the test with exactly (not (= 'n=2' 'n=1')) for (a) and (not (= 1 0)) twice for (b) -- the two failure modes the new prose names; restore verified by blob hash. No assertion or browser gating weakened; the now-unused cljs.test/testing refer removed as the acceptance criteria permit. PR #9077.

title: Remove override-applies? superseded by classified FX dispositions
description:

The predicate embodied the two-phase preflight that the next-day race fix deliberately replaced. Keeping it exposes the obsolete, unsafe shape as an apparently current helper and leaves current policy documentation inaccurate.

title: Remove evaluate-flow!'s unread dirty-result slot
description:

Remove the Boolean slot and simplify the sole caller/result contract while preserving the transformed-db left fold and the distinct stale-incarnation outcome.

Risk
Owner-loss short-circuiting, derive/output-write error attribution, dirty-cache rollback, validation, trace ordering/elision, and the documented three-argument compatibility path of `run-flows-on-db` are deliberate contracts and must remain unchanged. Do not make a legitimate pending db indistinguishable from the stale marker.
acceptance_criteria:
- `evaluate-flow!` no longer returns or documents an unread dirty Boolean.
- Its sole caller consumes the simplified successful result without a second-slot discard.
- Tests cover both equal-input skip and computed-output paths plus owner loss before/after the derive callback, with the same transformed db and stale behavior as today.
- Flow failure attribution and rollback tests, default JVM/CLJS flows suites, and exact-incarnation tests pass.
close_reason: PREMISE HELD — evaluate-flow! now returns the transformed db rather than [db dirty?] (PR #9082). The bead's evidence was truncated at the point where it said what the caller checks, so the caller was read directly: at flows.cljc:330-336 it does (if (= stale-incarnation result) stale-incarnation (recur (rest remaining) (first result))) — it discriminates the stale marker and then takes (first result), and NEVER reads the second element. Census: no source, test, tool, trace, spec or public API destructures or indexes it; every tree-wide mention of evaluate-flow! outside its own file is a comment, a docstring or spec prose, and no test reaches the private var through #'. No new marker ambiguity, which was the bead's stated risk: run-flows-on-db* ALREADY returns either a bare db or stale-incarnation to its own caller (both its (empty? remaining) and empty-flow-map arms return db unwrapped), so evaluate-flow! now returns the same two outcomes its enclosing fold does, discriminated the same way. Owner-loss short-circuiting, derive/output-write phase attribution, dirty-cache rollback, validation, trace ordering/elision and the three-argument run-flows-on-db path are untouched. Gates: flows JVM 250 tests / 6102 assertions / 0 failures; test:cljs 11209 tests / 55849 assertions / 0 failures.

title: Remove the unused frame-id hop from flows tooling metadata
description:
Evidence
- `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/tooling.cljc:39-47` defines private `with-metadata` as `[node _frame-id flow]`; its body reads only `node` and `flow`.
- Its sole call at line 62 is `(with-metadata frame-id flow)` in a thread-first form. `frame-id` is already consumed by `node-for` to build `:owner [:frame frame-id]` and has no role in metadata attachment.
- `d8bc29e2e0` replaced `frame-matched-source-coords [frame-id flow-id]` with `flow-source-coords [flow]` after flows moved to a frame-scoped single store. That migration renamed the now-unused parameter `_frame-id` but retained the call hop.
- Exact source and test searches find no other call to this private helper.

Impact and disposition
The extra argument falsely suggests source/schema/doc/derive metadata depends on frame identity and preserves a remnant of the retired frame-blind registrar lookup. Remove the parameter and stop passing it; keep frame ownership construction in `node-for` unchanged.

Risk
The change must not remove or alter `:owner [:frame frame-id]`, same-id cross-frame isolation, source-coordinate projection, schema/doc projection, or the opaque derive token.
acceptance_criteria:
- `with-metadata` accepts only the node and flow values it reads, and its sole call no longer passes `frame-id`.
- `node-for` still projects the selected frame as `:owner [:frame frame-id]`.
- Existing flows tooling JVM/CLJS projection tests cover source metadata and same-id flows in different frames and pass.
- Bundle-isolation controls for the tooling sibling remain green.
close_reason: with-metadata now takes [node flow] and its sole call passes only flow (PR #9082). Premise held: line numbers re-derived exactly as filed (defn- at :39, sole call at :62), body read only node and flow, and a fixed-string census found exactly two tree-wide hits — the defn- and that one call. The same-named private helpers in the machines and resources tooling siblings are separate vars in separate namespaces, and the two hits in core's handler_source_test.clj are deftest NAMES, not calls. node-for still projects :owner [:frame frame-id] unchanged. Closure had already inlined the hop away, so this is source hygiene with no emitted-output change. Gates: flows JVM suite 250 tests / 6102 assertions / 0 failures; test:cljs 11209 tests / 55849 assertions / 0 failures; CLJS compile 0 warnings (an arity mismatch would surface there); bundle-isolation 40 absent / 40 present, unmoved.

title: Remove flows tooling's obsolete private bundle sentinel
description:
Evidence

acceptance_criteria:

close_reason: Removed the defonce ^:private bundle-isolation-sentinel and its false comment from flows/tooling.cljc (PR #9082). Premise held. Three-legged emitted-module measurement on a fresh build: planted literal in out/bundle-isolation-positive-control/flows-tooling.js = 0; live 'after-event' in the SAME file with the SAME instrument = 1 (control); literal in pre-change source = 1. The zero is Closure DCE of an unread private var, so do-not-rename guarded nothing. check-bundle-isolation.cjs needed NO edit: fixed-string search of the checker for the flows literal = 0 against the rf.derivation.egress twin = 1 as the control that fires; its flows row needle is sentinel: 'after-event'. Comment removed with the var per the rf2-f8fo ruling, no replacement added. Gate proved live by sabotage witness: renaming the live keyword drove check-bundle-isolation.cjs to exit 1 naming exactly "emitted module 'flows-tooling' present ... expected >= 1, was 0"; restored and verified by git blob hash, counts back to 40 absent / 40 present.

title: Resources ledger: remove prune-record superseded by indexed batch pruning
description:
Evidence
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/work_ledger.cljc:516-526 defines prune-record, but exact repository search finds no production caller; its only executable consumer is a direct unit test at resources_work_ledger_cljs_test.cljc:843.
- The live operation is prune-terminal-for-key at work_ledger.cljc:548-599. It already holds byte work-id ids and removes all drop-ids in one reduce, then updates the inverse-index bucket in bulk; it cannot use prune-record, which accepts a structured work-id and recomputes its byte identity.
- Comments at work_ledger.cljc:416 and :562 nevertheless claim the live index is maintained through put-record/prune-record.
- Commit 0813d08aa1 introduced prune-record. Commit b0edd0265c added the inverse index and the batch prune implementation, leaving the now-superseded helper, its direct test, and stale comments.

Impact
A superseded single-row deletion API and its direct-only test imply that production pruning exercises code it bypasses. The stale comments obscure the actual atomic/batched inverse-index maintenance path and can misdirect future fixes.

Proposed disposition
Remove prune-record and replace/delete its direct-only test in favor of assertions through prune-terminal-for-key. Correct comments to name put-record plus the batch prune as the live incremental maintainers. Preserve bounded tail retention, non-terminal rows, byte-key isolation, index self-heal, and empty-bucket cleanup.

Risks
Do not regress the O(rows-for-key) index path into a whole-ledger scan or repeated structured-id conversion. Internal namespace consumers outside the repository are not a documented API but should be considered under normal release policy.
acceptance_criteria:
- prune-record is absent and comments describe the actual batch prune path.
- Tests through prune-terminal-for-key prove old terminal rows and their inverse-index members are removed, the retained tail/non-terminal rows survive, empty buckets disappear, and an absent installed index self-heals.
- Vector/list identity collision coverage and resource work-ledger JVM/CLJS suites pass.
close_reason: Removed work-ledger/prune-record (implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/work_ledger.cljc) and corrected the two comments (at the inverse-index preamble and inside prune-terminal-for-key) that named it as a live incremental index maintainer. Premise verified at tip by two instruments: fixed-string census over 4818 tracked files (line-oriented AND whitespace-flattened) and clj-kondo var-usage analysis. Both agree: ZERO production callers; the only executable consumer was the resources work-ledger test. Control put-record fired in both, across 6 namespaces incl. production events and mutation-events. CASCADE NOT NAMED IN THE BEAD: prune-record was the sole caller of the private index-remove, so that helper is removed with it (leaving it would have added an Unused-private-var warning - the after-lint confirms none appeared). The live path is unchanged: prune-terminal-for-key still holds byte work-id ids, removes all drop-ids in one reduce and updates the inverse-index bucket in bulk, with no regression to a whole-ledger scan or repeated structured-id conversion. WHAT THE DELETED TEST WAS GUARANTEEING, and whether the live path still does: prune-record's only executable consumer was NOT a dedicated unit test of it but one of three operations interleaved in a randomised 500-op property test asserting the incrementally-maintained inverse index equals a full rebuild after EVERY op, with no empty buckets. That property is retained over the two remaining operations, and the criteria this bead sets are already met by dedicated tests that were not touched: prune-terminal-for-key-matches-full-scan-reference (old terminal rows and their index members removed, retained tail and non-terminal rows survive), prune-self-heals-on-wholesale-installed-ledger (absent installed index self-heals), the randomised test's own no-empty-buckets assertion, and the event-level succeeded-completes-and-prunes-record / succeeded-prunes-old-terminal-rows-beyond-tail. No guarantee was dropped. Landed in PR #9079.

title: Resources state: remove the inert lifecycle-states constant
description:
Evidence
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/state.cljc:174-179 defines lifecycle-states and says the closed set is pinned so sibling namespaces agree.
- Exact repository search finds no source caller, validator, test, documentation reference, or API-manifest entry for this var. Resource handlers and state constructors use status literals directly.
- clj-kondo usage analysis likewise reports no consumer. The constant was added in the initial resources skeleton commit 2cd05677fb and has never been wired into the runtime.

Impact
The var is inert documentation masquerading as an enforcement/source-of-truth mechanism. Because siblings do not read it, adding or removing a lifecycle state can leave the claimed closed set stale without any failure.

Proposed disposition
Remove lifecycle-states and its false source-of-truth claim. If the project wants a machine-readable closed set, first connect it to a real schema/validator or exhaustive transition check and test that contract; do not retain a decorative constant.

Risks
Do not alter the five shipped lifecycle states or transition behavior as part of this cleanup. Search for macro/generated consumers before deletion and retain normative FSM prose in Spec 016.
acceptance_criteria:
- lifecycle-states is removed, or a real runtime/schema/tooling consumer enforces it with a non-vacuous test.
- No documentation claims sibling agreement through an unread var.
- Existing idle/loading/fetching/loaded/error transition and serialization tests pass on JVM and CLJS.
close_reason: Removed state/lifecycle-states (implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/state.cljc). Premise verified at tip by two independent instruments before deletion: a fixed-string census over 4818 tracked files (line-oriented AND whitespace-flattened, .beads exports excluded) and clj-kondo var-usage analysis over implementation/ + tools/. Both found ZERO usages of any kind - no source caller, validator, test, doc reference or API-manifest entry. Controls in the same namespace fired in both instruments (terminal-work-statuses: 6 files incl. the production work_ledger consumer; entry-revision: 4 namespaces incl. production mutation-runtime). The only other repo hit was an unrelated hicasso deftest NAME containing the substring, not a consumer. The var's docstring claimed the closed set was pinned so siblings agree on it; since no sibling read it, adding or removing a lifecycle state could leave that claim stale with nothing failing - inert documentation masquerading as enforcement, exactly as filed. The five shipped states and their transition behaviour are untouched. Landed in PR #9079.

title: Resources routing: remove the zero-consumer plan-identities getter
description:
Evidence
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc:176-181 defines plan-identities as a wrapper around get-in(runtime-db, plan-path(nav-token)). Exact repository search finds no caller, test, documentation, or API-manifest entry for the symbol.

- Commit 39142d0d6a added the helper with EP-0037 R2, but no production consumer was ever introduced. Routing deliberately avoids a static dependency on the optional resources artefact, so replacing its direct read with this resources-namespace helper would violate the existing late-bound boundary.

Impact
The unused getter suggests one authoritative access path while the actual owners use another. It adds an unsupported internal seam and maintenance surface without abstracting any live behavior.

Proposed disposition
Remove only plan-identities. Keep the slot path constructors, clear behavior, direct routing reads, and optional-artifact boundary unchanged.

Risks
Do not remove the :resource-plan slot or plan-path/clear-plan-slot functions; those are live persistence and cleanup contracts. Out-of-repository code should not rely on this internal namespace, but release notes may mention removal if policy requires it.
acceptance_criteria:
