- Route activation and replan still diff against the prior nav-token resource-plan slot, including failed-plan recovery and attach-before-release behavior.
- Routing remains buildable without a static resources dependency and bundle optionality checks remain green.
- Resource/routing integration suites pass.
close_reason: Removed route/plan-identities (implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc). Premise verified at tip by two independent instruments: a fixed-string census over 4818 tracked files (line-oriented AND whitespace-flattened) and clj-kondo var-usage analysis. Both found ZERO usages of any kind - the symbol appeared in exactly one file, its own definition. Controls fired in both (plan-path; put-record across 6 namespaces incl. production). Confirmed the bead's mechanism: both live plan-diff consumers read the routing slot path directly, which is what keeps routing free of a static dependency on the optional resources artefact - so the getter was an unsupported internal seam abstracting no live behaviour. plan-path, plan-slots-map-path, clear-plan-slot and the :resource-plan slot are all retained per the ruling. ONE PREMISE REFINEMENT worth recording: the bead states plan-path, plan-slots-map-path and clear-plan-slot are 'independently used and remain live'. That holds for clear-plan-slot (called from events.cljc) and for plan-slots-map-path (called from clear-plan-slot), but NOT for plan-path: its only non-test caller was plan-identities itself, so with the getter gone plan-path is now referenced by three route tests and no production code. It was kept as the ruling directs and nothing was changed about it; flagging only because a future vestige sweep will find it and should have this context rather than re-deriving it. Landed in PR #9079.

title: Stop retaining the unused streaming root Hiccup tree
description:
## Finding

`render-streaming-shell!` returns the fully resolved root tree in `rendered[:hiccup]`, but the streaming writer no longer reads that field. The detached writer receives a map that can retain an arbitrarily large Hiccup tree for the lifetime of the stream even though every live operation uses `:shell-html`, `:doc-hash`, and (when continuations exist) a fresh post-drain root resolution.

## Evidence

- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj:123-210` documents and returns `:hiccup hiccup`.
- The sole production consumer, `run-streaming-writer!` at lines 270-404, destructures `head-html`, attribute bags, `doc-hash`, `head-hash`, `shell-html`, and `continuations`; it never reads `:hiccup`.
- Final payload hashing at lines 383-399 either re-resolves `root-view` after a continuation drain or reuses `doc-hash`; the carried tree participates in neither arm.
- A repository search finds no read of this result key. The only other ssr-ring occurrences are three hand-built writer-test maps (`streaming_writer_trace_test.clj:83,332` and `streaming_robustness_test.clj:207`), where it is an ignored extra key.
- History proves the disconnect: commit `375fc36ec2` introduced the field for the writer's final-hash computation. Commit `185c149a53` stopped destructuring it when hashing moved to `doc-hash`; later commit `80d28623a4` moved continuation-sensitive final hashing to a fresh `root-view` resolution. Old comments retained it "for diagnostics", but no diagnostic path ever consumes it, and the current docstring still incorrectly says it is "for the final-hash".
- `re-frame.ssr.ring.streaming` is explicitly on the API-manifest generator's internal-namespace roster (`implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj`); the public façade, API docs, specs, examples, and Node crossing expose `stream-handler`, not this intermediate result shape.

Duplicate searches for `render-streaming-shell hiccup final hash`, `streaming hiccup rendered map`, and `ssr-ring hiccup retention` found no owning bead.

## Impact

Every streamed request retains both rendered HTML and the original in-memory tree across the daemon writer, with the worst retention on slow clients or long continuation drains. The stale field and docstring also suggest final-hash logic depends on a pre-drain tree when the correctness fix deliberately made it post-drain-sensitive.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `:hiccup` from the internal rendered map and its result-shape docstring, and remove the three ignored fixture keys. Keep the local `hiccup` binding: it remains required to build `doc-hash` and `shell-html`. Do not change root resolution count or hash timing.

## Risks

The common no-continuation path must still resolve a fn-form root exactly once and reuse `doc-hash`; continuation requests must still re-resolve after draining. This cleanup must not move shell rendering onto the writer thread, alter failure projection, or expose a new public result contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- `render-streaming-shell!` no longer returns or documents a `:hiccup` field, and writer-test fixtures do not carry the ignored key.
- The local resolved tree remains used to compute `doc-hash` and call `streaming/render-shell`; shell bytes are unchanged.
- `run-streaming-writer!` still uses `doc-hash` when no continuation exists and a fresh post-drain `root-view` resolution when continuations exist.
- Streaming tests pass, including exact-once root resolution, post-drain hash/state parity, writer trace/failure, and nested continuation ordering coverage.
- A repo-wide search within ssr-ring finds no stale claim that the carried Hiccup tree drives the final hash.
close_reason:
Confirmed and fixed in PR #9081. NOTE FOR THE EPIC: this bead's subject is implementation/ssr-ring/, not implementation/http/ — it was dispatched clustered with three http beads as one artefact, and only the other three are http.

WHAT HELD THE TREE ALIVE, established before the fix. stream-rendered-response builds the daemon writer as an anonymous fn closing over the WHOLE rendered map and hands that closure to a Thread. The holder is the closure FIELD, not a stack local, so Clojure's locals-clearing never reaches it, and the thread lives until the stream drains — bounded by the client's read rate through a 16 KiB PipedInputStream, so a slow-loris client extends it arbitrarily. Chain: live Thread -> closure field -> rendered -> :hiccup -> the whole resolved root tree, retained alongside the rendered HTML for the request's lifetime. That is the bead's stated impact, confirmed.

THAT THE WRITER NEVER READS IT. run-streaming-writer! destructures exactly seven keys (head-html, html-attrs, body-attrs, doc-hash, head-hash, shell-html, continuations); :hiccup is not among them. The symbol rendered occurs at only three executable sites in streaming.clj — created at the handler, passed to stream-rendered-response, destructured once in the writer — with no (:hiccup rendered), no get, and no other key access (the reduced? check only derefs). Two-instrument census over git-tracked ssr-ring files, line-oriented and whitespace-flattened AGREEING: :hiccup at exactly 5 sites — streaming.clj:128 (docstring row) and :201 (map construction), plus the three ignored writer-test fixture keys the bead named (streaming_robustness_test.clj:207, streaming_writer_trace_test.clj:83 and :332). Every line number in the bead re-derived and correct. CONTROL needle shell-html fired at 22 line-oriented / 23 flattened.

MEASURED. A WeakReference harness reproducing the exact shape — a parked thread holding a closure over the map, the tree scoped out of the constructing frame so the map is the only holder, identical GC pressure both runs — reads tree-retained-by-live-writer? true WITH the field and false WITHOUT it. The field is the only difference between the runs. Two earlier harness shapes were discarded as inconclusive rather than reported: the first held the tree in a live local of the GC frame (both runs read retained), the second let locals-clearing drop the map after its destructure (both read collectable). Sample tree serialises to 106,986 pr-str chars; real magnitude is page size, unbounded.

DISPOSITION AS ORDERED: :hiccup gone from the returned map and from the result-shape docstring row (which still claimed 'for the final-hash'); the three ignored fixture keys gone. The local hiccup binding KEPT — it still builds doc-hash and feeds streaming/render-shell. Root-resolution count and hash timing untouched: the no-continuation path still reuses doc-hash and the continuation path still re-resolves post-drain. AC5: no stale claim that the carried tree drives the final hash survives in ssr-ring.

GATES: ssr-ring clojure -M:test 231 tests / 1163 assertions / 0 failures, captured exit 0 — identical to the pre-change baseline, and re-run green on the rebased final base. clj-kondo --cache false over ssr-ring src+test: 0 errors / 31 warnings, identical to its merge base.

title: http privacy-body: remove the orphaned direct-projector helper layer
description:
## Finding

`re-frame.http.privacy-body` ships a test-only direct-projection layer that is disconnected from the actual off-box path: `off-box-classify-body` plus `off-box-body-marker`. The same namespace also exposes `whole-body-sensitive-mark?`, a zero-production-consumer predicate duplicating behavior already exercised through `classify-decoded`.

## Evidence

- Repo-wide resolved-var analysis and fixed-string searches find zero production calls to `whole-body-sensitive-mark?` (`privacy_body.cljc:219`), `off-box-classify-body` (`:309`), or `off-box-body-marker` (`:237`). Their only executable consumers are focused assertions in `http_privacy_body_test.clj:102-108,182-224`; remaining hits are self-docstrings/comments.
- The shipped off-box path is different. HTTP emit sites call `off-box-body-disposition` and stamp `:rf.http/off-box-body` on trace tags (`transport.cljc:435,768` and other raw-failure paths). `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1430-1512` reads that stamp and applies its own `omit-off-box-http-bodies` projection; it cannot call the HTTP helper because Epoch deliberately has no HTTP-artifact dependency.
- The real projector is extensively covered in `epoch_egress_trace_events_test.clj` and `epoch_egress_redaction_cljs_test.cljc`; HTTP integration tests cover the emit-side `:omit` / `:classify` stamps. Removing the disconnected helper tests does not remove runtime-path coverage.
- Current privacy-body namespace prose and `off-box-body-disposition` docs incorrectly claim Epoch “applies” `off-box-classify-body`. The integration-test comment around `http_privacy_integration_test.clj:551-556` similarly treats its unit test as part of the end-to-end path, although no call edge exists.
- `whole-body-sensitive-mark?` only asks whether `(decode-schema-marks decode)` contains root path `[]`. The neighboring `whole-body-root-sensitive-redacts-everything` test already proves the product behavior through `classify-decoded`; the standalone predicate is neither used to decide runtime policy nor listed in the API manifest.
- History confirms these were never connected: `whole-body-sensitive-mark?` arrived in `59bffbceaf`; `off-box-classify-body`/marker arrived in `39dcc2c889`, while that same commit implemented the actual stamp/Epoch projector split. Subsequent history added no production consumer. Bead searches by all three exact symbols and off-box/body terms found no existing issue.

## Impact

The orphaned layer adds public vars and tests for code the product never executes, duplicates the Epoch projector semantics in a package that cannot be its authority, and leaves architecture documentation claiming a nonexistent call path. Future security fixes could update the helper, turn its tests green, and still leave the real off-box projector unchanged.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `off-box-classify-body`, `off-box-body-marker`, and `whole-body-sensitive-mark?` plus only their direct self-tests. Correct namespace/doc/test comments to describe the real stamp -> Epoch enforcement path. Preserve `off-box-body-disposition`, `introspectable-schema-decode?`, `decode-schema-marks`, `classify-decoded`, all emit-side stamping, and the Epoch projector/tests.

## Risks / retained contracts

The vars are public at the namespace level but are absent from the generated API manifest and user API docs; an unknown downstream direct-require remains possible. Do not weaken fail-closed behavior or remove tests that exercise the actual projector. Keep schema root-mark behavior covered through `classify-decoded` and keep opaque schemas classified `:omit` by the live disposition function.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The three zero-production-consumer vars and their direct self-tests are removed, or a real shipped consumer is added and the documented call path is made true.
2. Privacy-body and integration-test prose names `off-box-body-disposition` stamping plus Epoch `omit-off-box-http-bodies` as the actual off-box path; it does not claim Epoch calls an HTTP direct projector.
3. Root sensitive and large marks remain tested through `classify-decoded`; introspectable schemas still stamp `:classify`, and unschematized/opaque decodes still stamp `:omit`.
4. Existing Epoch JVM/CLJS off-box projection tests and HTTP privacy JVM/CLJS tests pass, including raw 4xx/5xx/decode-failure and retry-body fail-closed cases.
5. Repo-wide searches show no stale reference to the removed helper/marker names and the API manifest remains unchanged unless compatibility policy explicitly promotes a retained API.
close_reason:
Confirmed and removed in PR #9081. This is PRIVACY code, so the disposition was gated on two questions answered before anything was deleted.

ONE — DOES THE LIVE OFF-BOX PATH DEPEND ON IT? No, and it never could have. The shipped path is: the emit site applies classify-decoded ON-BOX (transport.cljc:401 for :rf.http/replied's :value, :868 for :rf.http/accept-failure's :decoded, :1466) and stamps off-box-body-disposition forward under :rf.http/off-box-body (transport.cljc:435, :768); re-frame.epoch.tool-pair's omit-off-box-http-bodies then reads that stamp and substitutes :rf/redacted at the operation's body-slot paths for an :omit event, passing a :classify event through because its per-slot marks were already applied on-box. Epoch deliberately carries no HTTP-artefact dependency, so it could not call off-box-classify-body even in principle — the bead's claim that the documented call path does not exist is correct.

TWO — IS ANY PRIVACY GUARANTEE DROPPED? No: the live composition is EXACTLY the removed function on both arms. Introspectable schema -> classify-decoded applied on-box, stamp :classify, Epoch passes through = off-box-classify-body's first arm. Anything else — unschematized, opaque keyword registry ref, compiled schema object — -> classify-decoded is an identity or mark-less no-op, but the stamp is :omit and Epoch substitutes :rf/redacted, the SAME sentinel off-box-body-marker held = its second arm. The fail-closed property for an opaque ref (rf2-y1pgdl) comes from the stamp gating on introspectable-schema-decode?, not from the removed helper, so it is untouched.

AND NO DELETED TEST WAS THE SOLE ASSERTION OF AN INVARIANT. Each removed row has a live counterpart on the shipped path, checked one by one: unschematized omission and opaque-registry-ref / compiled-schema omission are asserted through off-box-body-disposition returning :omit (off-box-disposition-omits-* rows, kept), and schema classification through the classify-decoded per-slot rows (kept). For whole-body-sensitive-mark? the deftest whole-body-root-sensitive-redacts-everything asserted BOTH the predicate and the PRODUCT behaviour; only the predicate's own call was dropped and the (= :rf/redacted (classify-decoded ...)) assertion beside it was KEPT (AC3). CONTROL needle off-box-body-disposition fired at 17/17 across five files INCLUDING transport.cljc and spec/014-HTTPRequests.md — a live control, not a zero.

PROSE CORRECTED (AC2): the namespace docstring, the two section comments and off-box-body-disposition's own docstring no longer claim Epoch applies an HTTP direct projector; they name the real stamp -> Epoch enforcement path. The http_privacy_integration_test.clj:551 comment no longer cites the deleted unit test as part of the end-to-end path. Worth recording as a process note: three of these prose replacements silently NO-OPPED on the first attempt because the anchors used LF against this CRLF tree — nothing errored and the edit read clean; caught only by re-running the residual grep, which is why every removal here was verified by census afterwards rather than by inspecting the patch.

title: http decode: remove the unreachable raw-body fallback
description:
## Finding

`re-frame.http.decode/decode-response-body` ends with a raw `body-text` fallback that is unreachable under the decoder normalization immediately above it.

## Evidence

- In `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/decode.cljc:248-340`, `requested-decode` maps a nil `:decode` to `:auto`, preserves `:auto`, and otherwise preserves the supplied value. It therefore cannot be nil.
- `resolved` maps `:auto` through `sniff-decoder`; `sniff-decoder` has an exhaustive `cond` returning exactly `:json`, `:text`, or `:blob`. For every non-`:auto` input, `resolved` is the already-non-nil `requested-decode`. Thus `resolved` cannot be nil.
- The main `cond` first handles a decoder fn, JSON, text, and the binary modes. Its next predicate is `(some? resolved)`, which is necessarily true for every remaining input. The final `:else body-text` at lines 339-340 has no possible input.
- History shows this shape arrived with the decode extraction (`c8f80850c9`) and survived the later strict malformed-JSON correction (`5abbf20977`). The live schema/unknown-decoder arm deliberately parses JSON and propagates parse failure; the dead tail is not the earlier malformed-JSON fallback fixed by that commit.
- Repository and bead searches for the symbol, decoder normalization, decode fallback, and HTTP decode found no issue covering this unreachable branch.

## Impact

The dead tail falsely suggests a nil/unknown decoder can bypass schema/JSON handling and return raw text. That makes security-sensitive malformed-JSON reasoning harder and creates a branch no test can honestly exercise.

## Proposed disposition

Make the schema/unknown-decoder arm the final `:else` and remove the unreachable trailing fallback. Keep the binary arm's separate synthetic-context `body-binary` -> `body-text` fallback intact.

## Risks / retained contracts

This is intended to be behavior-neutral. Preserve nil/omitted `:decode` as `:auto`, custom decoder raw-text ownership, unknown non-mode values as schema candidates, strict malformed-JSON propagation, and binary response behavior on both hosts.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `decode-response-body` has no trailing branch that requires `resolved` to be nil; the schema/unknown-decoder path is structurally exhaustive.
2. Omitted/nil and explicit `:auto`, `:json`, `:text`, all binary modes, custom fns, valid Malli schemas, invalid schemas, unknown keyword refs, malformed JSON, and empty-body parity retain their current results/errors.
3. The JVM HTTP decode suite and consolidated CLJS HTTP tests pass.
4. A source search and/or focused branch proof confirms there is no unreachable raw-body fallback, while the intentional binary synthetic-context fallback remains.
close_reason:
Confirmed and removed in PR #9081. The premise held exactly, and was proved two independent ways rather than by reading alone.

BY CONTROL FLOW. requested-decode maps nil :decode to :auto, preserves :auto, and otherwise preserves the supplied value, so it is never nil. resolved then maps :auto through sniff-decoder — an exhaustive cond returning exactly :json, :text or :blob — and otherwise IS requested-decode. So resolved is never nil. The main cond's penultimate predicate (some? resolved) was therefore true for everything that reached it, and the trailing :else body-text required resolved to be nil. Unreachable. One edge worth recording because it is the arm where a naive reading goes wrong: a :decode of FALSE also reaches the schema arm, not the fallback — some? is (not (nil? x)), so false passes it.

BY PROBE, WITH A CONTROL THAT FIRED. A side-effecting probe was planted in the fallback — a marker file rather than a throw, since a throw is caught by the transport's decode try/catch and classified as :rf.http/decode-failure, which could have been swallowed into a passing test. Across the whole 514-test suite the marker was ABSENT: the branch was never entered. The SAME probe mechanism planted in the live (= :text resolved) arm produced the marker with 2 hits. Zero versus two, same suite, same run shape, so the instrument works and the fallback is genuinely dead. (A first plant attempt was paren-unbalanced and failed to read the file — treated as NO VERDICT and redone, not interpreted.) Both plants restored and verified by git blob hash against the committed object, not by reading a diff.

DISPOSITION AS ORDERED: the schema/unknown-decoder arm is now the final :else and the trailing fallback is gone, so the cond is structurally exhaustive with no branch requiring a nil resolved (AC1, AC4). The binary arm's separate synthetic-context body-binary -> body-text fallback is INTACT — that one is deliberate and fires for a test ctx that populated only :body-text (AC2, retained contract).

Behaviour-neutral as intended: http clojure -M:test 506 tests / 3884 assertions / 0 failures, captured exit 0, with the empty-body-parity, binary-decode, malformed-JSON and schema decode rows all still green (AC2, AC3). The consolidated CLJS bundle — where a cross-host decode divergence would surface — ran 11209 tests / 55849 assertions / 0 failures, captured exit 0.

ONE PREMISE CORRECTION, cosmetic but worth the record: the bead cites the symbol as util-json/json-parse at decode.cljc:248-340. Main renamed that alias to http-json between filing and landing (commit f148f863c2), which is what the rebase conflicted on; resolved by keeping BOTH intents — main's rename and this removal.

title: skills: six of nine SKILL.md descriptions exceed the Agent Skills 1,024-char description cap — verify runtime truncation and trim so the tail disqualifier survives
description:
CLAIM. The Agent Skills spec caps the frontmatter description at 1,024 characters. Measured at tip: re-frame2-xray 1,712; reagent-migration 1,486; re-frame2 1,243; re-frame2-improver 1,149; re-frame2-pair-retro 1,137; re-frame2-setup 1,062. No repo gate checks it.
IMPACT. If the loader truncates, the clause at the END of each description is what is cut — in xray that tail is the Xray-vs-pair disqualifier the family README treats as the routing rule; in setup it is the greenfield-only disqualifier.
FIX SHAPE. First verify (do not assume) whether Claude Code truncates or refuses; then either trim the six descriptions to the cap with the disqualifier moved to the front, or record in skills/README.md that the cap does not apply and why. Do not add a gate unless truncation is confirmed.
GATE. none reads this today; hand-measure with wc -c on the frontmatter field.
Surfaced by the 2026-09-02 independent skills review (15 reviewers, tip 72df4dd915); routed out of the reviewing skill's scope. Re-verify line numbers at dispatch. Filed 2026-09-02 12:16:19 AUSEST. Reported by the xray reviewer.
acceptance_criteria: Truncation behaviour verified against the Agent Skills spec and Claude Code; every SKILL.md description is at or under the cap, or the cap is shown not to apply and that is recorded in skills/README.md
notes:
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-09-03 (mayor) — THE CONDITIONAL ON THIS BEAD HAS RESOLVED, AND IT RESOLVED THE WAY THAT CREATES WORK.

This bead said "Do not add a gate unless truncation is confirmed", and my brief made that an order of operations. The skillsize-a worker ran the verification and TRUNCATION IS NOW CONFIRMED — it filed rf2-w9p2 ("add a gate for the SKILL.md description cap — truncation is now CONFIRMED") off the back of it.

So the branch that was conditional is now live: a gate IS warranted, because the cap is enforced by the runtime and the clause that gets cut is the disqualifier at the END of each description — in xray the Xray-vs-pair routing rule, in setup the greenfield-only rule. A silent truncation removes exactly the sentence that stops the wrong skill loading.

NOTHING TO RE-DECIDE HERE. rf2-w9p2 owns the gate; this bead owns the six descriptions. Read rf2-w9p2 before working either, and take the measured truncation behaviour from it rather than re-establishing it.

I am recording this so the next reader does not re-run the verification: the answer exists, it is on rf2-w9p2, and it cost a worker real effort to get.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9051 — exact owner reopened. The Claude Code v2.1.258 measurement is useful, but it does not discharge the package contract this repository advertises: skills/README.md says every skill is distributable as an Agent Skill via `npx skills add`, while the canonical Agent Skills specification requires `description` to be 1–1,024 characters (https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills/blob/main/docs/specification.mdx#description-field). A particular runtime not enforcing that validation does not make an over-limit package conforming. PR #9051 leaves seven advertised Agent Skills above 1,024 and adds guidance saying that limit is not one to author against, institutionalising the incompatibility. Minimal completion: retain the useful Claude-specific 1,536/list-budget warning, but treat 1,024 as the portable package ceiling, bring all shipped descriptions under it with disqualifiers first, and make the pending description gate cover that contract. The three leaf-size exceptions need no reopening.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9057 — existing exact owner remains open. The pending guard has now landed, but scripts/check_skill_description_budget.py explicitly treats descriptions above the portable Agent Skills 1,024-character limit as fine and enforces only Claude Code 2.1.258's configurable 1,536-character listing default plus a family ratchet. That does not discharge this repository's advertised npx skills add package contract: seven shipped descriptions remain non-conforming to the canonical Agent Skills 1–1,024 requirement. Minimal completion remains the same: bring the descriptions under 1,024 with routing/disqualifier clauses first and retarget or simplify the gate to enforce that portable ceiling. The Claude-specific aggregate budget can remain useful diagnostic output, but it is not a substitute for package validity. The testing-leaf and MkDocs-nav parts of PR #9057 are sound.
close_reason: PR #9084. 1,024 is now treated as the portable Agent Skills package ceiling, per the #9051 audit note. All nine shipped descriptions are under it, each leading with its disqualifier clause and trailing its trigger phrases: reagent-migration 1487->1015, re-frame2-xray 1482->991, re-frame2 1251->1012, re-frame2-pair-retro 1203->989, re-frame2-implementor 1186->996, re-frame2-improver 1150->990, re-frame2-setup 1068->971, re-frame-migration 963 (reordered only), re-frame2-pair 747 (untouched). No when_to_use field exists on any of them, so resolved length is the description alone. scripts/check_skill_description_budget.py now FAILS at 1,024 rather than 1,536; the 1,536 slice and the ~8,000 listing budget are RETAINED and reported, because they are what makes the tail the part at risk, and a C1 failure escalates its message when a description is past 1,536 too (self-tested both directions, 17 cases). Family listing footprint 10,727 -> 8,864 and the ratchet ceiling drops with it; it still exceeds the ~8,000 whole-listing budget, which no amount of trimming can reach with nine routing contracts, and the gate prints that comparison every run. skills/README.md's section rewritten: it previously told authors 1,024 was not a number to write against. The three leaf-size exceptions untouched, per the audit. Truncation behaviour NOT re-measured: the audit's ruling is that the packaging spec is the contract regardless of one runtime's enforcement, so 1,024 comes from the spec and 1,536 is carried forward from rf2-w9p2. Gates: description-budget self-test 0, --verbose --ci 0, check_doc_slugs.py --self-test 0 and --verbose 0 (no broken links). Plant: re-frame2-setup pushed 971->1125, gate exit 1 naming that file with the runtime-slice escalation correctly silent; restored and verified by blob hash 2a6796e1e367a2c0930161de7c4204b4c89bb19e. Surface classifier: skills_structural=true, all else false.

title: story-mcp specs contradict explain-variant raw-author-data policy
description:
Evidence
- The authoritative Story-MCP privacy table says `explain-variant`'s entire map, including every plan-resolved value slot, is static author data and ships raw (`tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md:158-168`, rf2-7k5mce).
- The very next paragraph at lines 169-172 still promises that a declared-sensitive value redacts whether it arrives through a live derived tree “or a plan-resolved arg.” That is no longer true for explain-variant.
- Runtime docs and API are internally consistent with the new policy (`tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/docs.cljc:365-383`, `spec/API.md:324-344`), and focused tests at `tools_test.clj:3514-3616` prove classified `:db-seed`, `:effective-args`, `:network`, sub-overrides, and step payloads ship raw.
- The document claimed as the single-sourced peer, `tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md:119-198`, still places explain-variant among live/value-bearing tools, says its plan-resolved slots path-project, excludes its resolved step values from static metadata, and implies an include-sensitive escape hatch. That contradicts both implementation and the Story-MCP table.

Impact
This is a safety-contract contradiction, not cosmetic wording: readers can believe classification marks protect authored values exposed through explain-variant when the intentional runtime behavior sends them raw and offers no `:include-sensitive` gate. The same section simultaneously states the opposite, so clients and reviews cannot infer the actual boundary.

Recommendation
Rewrite the stale paragraphs in both normative specs to consistently state the rf2-7k5mce policy: explain-variant is a no-run author-data projection; its whole map ships raw; it is excluded from the live-value scrub set and sensitive-read gate. Cross-check the remaining tool lists and examples against the four actual value-surfacing tools.

Risks / contracts
Do not silently reintroduce scrubbing as a documentation fix: raw author data is deliberate, matches get-variant/variant->edn and the human Explain panel, and is pinned by tests. If that policy itself is reconsidered, treat it as a separate security decision with migration and protocol review.
acceptance_criteria:
- `spec/002-Tool-Registry.md` contains no claim that explain-variant plan-resolved args redact.
- `tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md` classifies explain-variant consistently as wholly raw author metadata and removes it from live/value-bearing/gated tool sets.
- Both specs clearly warn that classification marks do not scrub authored registration values exposed by explain-variant.
- The four runtime-value tools and their sensitive-read gate remain accurately enumerated.
- Existing explain-variant raw-value tests and Story-MCP test suite pass unchanged in semantics.
close_reason: PR #9089. Contradiction resolved in favour of the SHIPPED CODE: tool-explain-variant wraps story/explain in result/edn-result and reaches no egress projector; spec/API.md and three pinned tests agree; the Story-MCP privacy table already stated the rf2-7k5mce policy. Rewrote the stale prose on both sides. tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md no longer claims plan-resolved args redact and now states plainly that classification marks do not reach author metadata (keep secrets out of a variant's registration). tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md removes explain-variant from the live-state and value-bearing sets, moves its ENTIRE explain map into the author-published static class, and marks the rf2-q8ebq.1 setup-order/script-order carve-out retired. The four runtime-value tools and the --allow-sensitive-reads gate remain accurately enumerated. No scrubbing reintroduced; explain-variant tests unchanged in semantics and green.

title: Disambiguate Event Conformance reply and correlation values
description:
## Finding

The two retained reply/event integration cases use generic locals at the boundary where four distinct values coexist: the reply target, the completed event vector, the reply envelope delivered on that vector, and carried/current correlation state. `observe-stale-reply!` destructures a local named `reply` beside the `reply` namespace alias, yielding `reply/complete target reply`; the success row similarly calls both the source envelope and delivered envelope `reply`, while `completed` omits that it is an event. The observer row uses `pool`, `img`, `target`, `carried`, `current`, `outcome`, and `delivered`, obscuring image setup and suppression roles.

## Evidence

- `implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_reply_envelope_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:74-76` visually overloads the `reply` namespace alias and local envelope in one expression.
- Lines 83-114 distinguish observed event/coeffects, completion, and delivered envelope using `seen-cofx`, `target`, `reply`, `completed`, and `delivered`.
- Lines 130-196 build an explicit image-loaded frame and a stale-suppression correlation pair under `pool`, `img`, `target`, `carried`, `current`, `outcome`, and `delivered`.
- Managed-Effects names these concepts reply target, completed event, reply map/envelope, carried/current correlation facts, and stale-suppression outcome. EP-0023 names registration sets and image values.
- History shows the observer helper replaced an older delivery gate; its current local names were inherited through that semantic shift.
- No all-status bead owns these naming changes. Phase-1 bead `rf2-6r9j.97` owns the separate vacuous stale non-delivery row, which is excluded entirely.

## Recommendation

Rename retained-case locals to `seen-coeffects`, `reply-target`, `completed-event`, `delivered-reply`, `stale-reply`, `dispatch-options`, `image-registrations`, `event-image`, `carried-correlation`, `current-correlation`, `suppression-outcome`, and `handler-call-count`. Update the observer helper's destructuring explicitly so the namespace alias is never shadowed. Preserve all registered ids and reply/correlation map keys.

## Risks / contracts

This is test-private naming only. Do not change the canonical reply envelope, `:deliver?`, correlation data, reply target shape, registered event/image/frame ids, dispatch options, handler routing, assertions, or namespace/file names. Do not edit the `rf2-6r9j.97` deletion/replacement target or its namespace prose.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The retained success and observer paths clearly distinguish target, completed event, delivered/stale reply, image setup, correlation inputs, and suppression outcome.
2. No local reply envelope shadows the `reply` namespace alias in retained code.
3. The Phase-1-owned stale non-delivery test remains unchanged.
4. Event-conformance JVM and consolidated CLJS Node suites, focused lint, exact searches, and diff checks pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified role-bearing private naming in event-conformance fixtures, event-model observations, and reply/correlation integration cases; JVM/CLJS focused suites and pinned clj-kondo pass.

title: Name Event Model conformance observations by domain role
description:
## Finding

The large event-model conformance suite repeatedly abbreviates the exact concepts it is meant to distinguish. Private helpers take `f` and catch `e`; `chain-ids` accepts generic `chain`/`entry` even though it projects interceptor references; coeffect rows alternate among `seen-cofx`, `cofx`, `c`, and `coeffects`; trace rows use `ev`, `warns`, `t`, `errs`, and `ops`; registration checks use `meta`, `imeta`, and `emeta`. These names force readers to reverse-map values to the normative event/coeffect/interceptor/trace vocabulary across a correctness-oriented 800+ line suite.

## Evidence

- `implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_model_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:42-71` defines the exception and interceptor-chain helpers with `f`, `e`, `chain`, and `entry`.
- Lines 75-224 use four spellings for observed coeffects and generic trace-event/generation variables.
- Lines 226-452 use `calls`, `thrown`, `prev-validate`, `prev-explain`, `errs`, and generic `seen` values across generator, validation, and provided-fact boundaries.
- Lines 456-648 use `ev`, `fw-traces`, `ops`, `db-seen`, and `sentinel?` in effect-map/observability rows.
- Lines 652-709 use `meta`, `imeta`, and `emeta` for event versus interceptor registration metadata.
- Spec 001 and EP-0018 consistently say coeffects, event vector, interceptor reference/chain, handler metadata, and effects; EP-0017 names generated/recorded facts and mint policy.
- Full clj-kondo local analysis confirms these names occur symmetrically in the `.cljc` JVM and CLJS arms. No existing all-status bead owns their naming.
- Phase-1 beads `rf2-6r9j.99` and `rf2-6r9j.101` own the explicit-live and duplicate-wrapper tests; their deletion/reshape targets are excluded.

## Recommendation

Use role-bearing private/local names: `thunk`/`exception`, `interceptor-chain-ids`/`interceptor-ref`, `seen-coeffects`/`coeffects`, `trace-event`, `warning-traces`/`warning-tags`, `generation-traces`, `generator-call-count`, `caught-error-id`, `previous-validator`/`previous-explainer`, `framework-traces`, `operations`, `seen-db`, `sentinel-ran?`, and `event-metadata`/`interceptor-metadata`. Apply only where the longer name distinguishes a real role; retain established public vocabulary such as `db`, `event`, and `ctx` when already unambiguous.

## Risks / contracts

All changes are private test helpers/locals. Preserve test names, namespace/file names, registered ids, listener ids, error ids/reasons, map/metadata keys, trace operations/tags, dispatch options, reader-conditionals, and assertion behavior/counts. Do not touch code slated for removal by Phase 1.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Surviving helper/local names identify coeffect, trace, interceptor, metadata, generator, and error roles without single-letter or unexplained abbreviations.
2. Every renamed binding has all JVM/CLJS uses updated; exact old-name searches leave only deliberate conventional or Phase-1-owned cases.
3. The explicit-live and duplicate-wrapper Phase-1 targets remain unchanged.
4. Event-conformance JVM and consolidated CLJS Node suites, focused lint, exact searches, and diff checks pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified role-bearing private naming in event-conformance fixtures, event-model observations, and reply/correlation integration cases; JVM/CLJS focused suites and pinned clj-kondo pass.

title: Clarify Event Conformance image and frame fixture roles
description:
## Finding

The surviving image/frame isolation cases use terse locals that conceal the distinction EP-0023 makes normative between registration descriptors, image values, live frames, and the runtime-db partition. In `event_frame_isolation_conformance_cljs_test.cljc`, `todo-pool`/`counter-pool`, `todo-img`/`counter-img`, and especially the coeffect alias `rt` require the reader to reconstruct which layer each value represents. ## Evidence

- `implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_frame_isolation_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:57-64` carries descriptor vectors, image values, and live frames side-by-side under `*-pool`, `*-img`, and `*-frame` names.
- Lines 105-143 use `rt` for the `:rf.db/runtime` coeffect in four handlers, beside `todo-pool`/`todo-img` and their counter/sibling variants.
- Lines 227-263 use `target-pool`, `sibling-pool`, `target-img`, `sibling-img`, then bind the resulting target app-db as generic `db`.
- EP-0023 defines the preferred nouns explicitly: registration/descriptor, image, frame, and runtime-db; it warns against adding substitute conceptual nouns.
- History shows the runtime partition row was added after the original image-isolation fixture, preserving the older short local style rather than deliberately naming its extra layer.

## Recommendation

Keep helper/public/test names and all ids, descriptor/map keys, image selectors, handler behavior, and assertions unchanged. Do not edit the three tests slated for removal by `rf2-6r9j.96`.

## Risks / contracts

This is test-local naming only. Preserve the image descriptor shape, `:rf.db/runtime` wire/key vocabulary, registered event/image/frame ids, selected namespace strings, dispatch order, and assertion values. Do not rename files or namespaces because their `-cljs-test` suffix and paths are CI/build enrollment contracts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The retained image/frame tests distinguish registrations, image values, live frames, runtime-db, and target app-db directly in their local names.
2. Every use is updated with no behavioral or data-shape change.
3. No line inside the three `rf2-6r9j.96` deletion targets is changed solely for naming.
4. Event-conformance JVM and consolidated CLJS Node tests, focused lint, exact searches, and diff checks pass.

title: mcp-conformance: prune eight unconsumed private CommonJS exports
description:
Evidence
- tools/mcp-conformance/lib/overflow-marker.cjs exports 12 bindings. Its two importers consume eight; OVERFLOW_KEY, REQUIRED_FIELDS, parseOverflowText, and canonicalize are used only inside their defining module. The JVM cross-encoding gate source-greps the REQUIRED_FIELDS table text and does not require its CommonJS export.

title: mcp-conformance: remove the zero-consumer transport handle from the runner contract
description:
Evidence
- tools/mcp-conformance/test/_runner.cjs:15-29 constructs a StdioClientTransport, gives it to client.connect(), then returns { client, transport }.
- runWithWatchdog at lines 55-90 retains a transport local solely to call body(client, transport).
- Repo-wide call-site inspection found 11 runWithWatchdog bodies and the direct connectServer consumers; every body uses only client, direct callers destructure only { client } or read aux.client, and no consumer reads .transport or a second callback argument.
- The extra parameter dates to d16cf18641, which centralized the old per-test ceremony and documented async (client, transport), but no current test exercises that part of the private contract.
- The pinned @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.29.0 contract says Protocol assumes ownership of the Transport. Its close() calls this._transport?.close(), matching _runner's existing closeQuietly(client) teardown.

Impact
The runner advertises and threads a second teardown handle that callers must not own under the SDK contract. This widens a private harness API, obscures the single owner, and creates needless destructuring/local state without providing any current capability.

Recommendation
Keep transport local to connectServer long enough to wire stderr and call client.connect(transport), but return only the connected client handle (or { client }, whichever minimizes call-site churn). Remove runWithWatchdog's transport local and invoke body(client). Update the private contract comments.

Risks and contracts
Preserve onClient publication before the initialize await, AUX_CLIENTS registration, prefixed stderr, connect-failure closeQuietly(client), watchdog behavior, and all 0/1/2 exit grading. Do not close the transport separately: Client owns it. This package is private and _runner.cjs is not a published API, but all in-repo direct callers must update atomically.
acceptance_criteria:
- connectServer no longer exposes transport to callers, while still passing it to client.connect().
- runWithWatchdog calls bodies with only client and carries no transport-only local/destructuring.
- Every direct connectServer and runWithWatchdog caller remains green.
- npm --prefix tools/mcp-conformance run test:unit passes, including connect-hang and auxiliary-client watchdog coverage.
- Repo-wide search finds no stale documentation claiming body receives transport.
close_reason: PR #9086 (head 79b2ee56a6). connectServer now returns { client } only; runWithWatchdog calls body(client) with no transport local. Proved zero consumers two ways: fixed-string census of 'transport' across tools/mcp-conformance (every hit outside _runner.cjs is transportSpec or prose; 'client, transport' appears nowhere else in the repo) plus enumeration of all 12 runWithWatchdog sites — the 11 bodies are async (client) x7, async (rawClient) x2, async () x2, none taking a second arg — and all four direct connectServer callers destructure { client } or read aux.client. Control: the same method over 'client, called' returned 3 files. Returning { client } kept call-site churn at zero. Gates: mcp-conformance node unit cluster exit 0 (124 tests, 0 fail), wire-vocab clojure -M:test exit 0 (94 tests / 1031 assertions).

title: Remove unreachable legacy region scan from machines-viz raw-node-at
description:
Evidence
- chart/layout.cljc raw-node-at has a no-:region fallback: after a top-level lookup misses, it scans every parallel region for the same path.
- Its sole source call is attach-consumer-requires, which passes nodes produced by project-definition. project-parallel assigns :region to every region state and the synthetic region container; the layout regression suite explicitly asserts every parallel state knows its region.
- Flat and compound nodes lack :region but live under definition :states, so their first lookup resolves. Synthetic root nodes have empty paths and are rejected before lookup.
- Therefore the cross-region scan can run only for a hand-built obsolete node shape: non-empty region-relative path with its required :region identity removed. No source/test/Xray caller constructs that shape, and raw-node-at is absent from spec/API.md's enumerated public surface.
- The fallback was deliberately retained as legacy wording in commit 700767339d4 when region-aware identity fixed wrong-region lifecycle metadata; retaining it now preserves the ambiguous behavior that fix made unnecessary.

Impact
The dead branch encodes a dangerous first-region-wins lookup. If a malformed projected node loses :region, silently borrowing a sibling region's lifecycle requirements is worse than returning nil and exposes the old correctness bug as compatibility behavior.

Recommendation
For nodes without :region, resolve only under top-level :states. Remove the region scan and legacy wording; keep strict region-qualified lookup for parallel nodes.

Risks and contracts
Preserve flat/compound lookup, strict per-region resolution, empty/synthetic-node nil behavior, and lifecycle requirement projection. Do not change the machine grammar or region-scoped IDs. Reassess only if a supported external constructor of raw projected nodes is identified.
acceptance_criteria:
- raw-node-at never scans all regions for a node missing :region.
- Flat/compound nodes still resolve through top-level :states; valid parallel nodes resolve only through their own region.
- A regression proves a no-:region region-relative node returns nil rather than first-region data.
- Existing duplicate-path parallel-region lifecycle requirement tests pass on JVM and CLJS.
- raw-node-at remains absent from the documented public API, or any newly discovered compatibility obligation is documented before changing behavior.
close_reason: PR #9085: raw-node-at's no-:region cross-region fallback removed. Verified unreachable — project-parallel stamps :region on every region state and the region container, the parallel-root chip's path segment is the namespaced :rf.machines-viz.layout/parallel-root (cannot name a real state), the machine-root chip has an empty path, and a flat definition has no :regions to scan. New regression raw-node-at-no-region-node-never-borrows-a-sibling-region pins nil-not-first-region plus unchanged flat/nested/absent/empty-path lookup; gate liveness proved by restoring the scan (red at layout_cljs_test.cljc:1543, actual {:entry :enter-a}) then restoring to the identical blob. raw-node-at absent from spec/API.md and tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md — no compatibility obligation found.

title: Retire four unread machines-viz density constants
description:

Remove the four keys from compact, regular, and cosy maps; remove their docs and expected-key/invariant entries. Keep the replacement container/context keys and all live action-pill geometry.

title: Make the security runtime harness fail honestly
description:
Scope: `with-runtime*` in implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/validation_redaction_invariant_security_cljs_test.cljc.

Evidence: the namespace's outer `make-reset-runtime-fixture {:clear-app-schemas? true}` disposes any installed adapter before every test and, in its post-test finally, resets frames and calls the loaded flows reset hook. `with-runtime*` nevertheless catches every Throwable/default value from `rf/init!` and ignores it, even though `rf/init!` is documented as idempotent; in this fixture state an exception indicates a real setup failure or partial initialization and should fail the security test. The helper's own finally also catches and ignores a flow reset immediately before the outer fixture performs the same reset without swallowing failure. Finally, its docstring promises "then dispose" and says "we dispose eagerly too", but the implementation never disposes the adapter; disposal occurs only on the next fixture setup. All current callers use the helper once around their production-path test body, so no demonstrated intra-test lifecycle requires these hidden fallback paths. The broad catch and inaccurate lifetime prose have been present since the helper was introduced in b58952c673.

Impact: a broken runtime setup can become a misleading downstream assertion failure or even a false green, cleanup failures can be hidden, and future maintainers are told the adapter lifetime is shorter than it really is.

Recommendation: let initialization failures propagate; choose and document one truthful lifetime (either actually dispose in the helper's finally or explicitly delegate disposal to the outer fixture); and remove the duplicate swallowed flow cleanup unless a concrete within-test isolation need is demonstrated.

Risks/contracts: preserve the adapter-less behavior needed by app-schema rows, the plain-atom runtime for the flow/subscription production-path rows, per-test flow/schema/frame isolation, and CLJ/CLJS fixture compatibility. Do not move all tests onto an adapter if that would synthesize frame state for cases intentionally testing context behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `with-runtime*` no longer blanket-catches and discards `rf/init!` failures; a targeted setup-failure control proves such an error reaches the test runner.
2. Its adapter-lifetime documentation matches behavior: disposal is either performed in its finally or accurately delegated to the outer fixture.
3. Duplicate flow cleanup is removed, or a distinct within-test requirement is documented and cleanup failure is not silently swallowed.
4. Adapter-less app-schema/context tests and plain-atom flow/subscription tests retain their intended setup.
5. `clojure -M:test` from implementation/security and `npm run test:security` from implementation both pass.
close_reason: with-runtime* no longer blanket-catches rf/init!; setup failures propagate. Adapter-lifetime docstring now names the outer make-reset-runtime-fixture (reset-runtime! -> dispose-adapter! on the way IN) instead of promising a disposal the helper never performed; the duplicate swallowed :flows/reset-flows! removed (finish-runtime-reset! already does it unswallowed in the fixture finally). Control: planted (rf/init! nil) -> 4 ERRORs naming rf/init! + :rf.error/no-adapter-specified, exit 1; the pre-fix blanket catch on the SAME fault reported :rf.error/adapter-disposed from make-state-container instead - the bead's misleading-downstream impact, live. Plant restored, verified by blob hash. Gates: security clojure -M:test 94/723 exit 0; npm run test:security 95/730 exit 0. PR #9088.

title: Stop Story-host DOM tests leaking hashchange listeners across cases
description:
Evidence:
- tools/testbed-support/test/re_frame/testbed/story_host_dom_cljs_test.cljs runs two tests against the real browser window.
- Each mount leaves the installed hashchange function in host/hash-listener* and registered on js/window, as production is designed to do.
- The :after fixture unmounts React roots, then reset-host-handles! resets host/hash-listener* to nil without calling removeEventListener. That discards the only exact function identity able to unregister the listener.
- The next :before repeats the reset, so the second test's mount cannot remove the first test's listener; it registers another. The final fixture similarly leaves listeners on the shared browser page.
- The fake-window Node suite does not expose this because clear-window! discards the entire fake window/Set between tests.

Impact:
The suite named no-listener-or-root-leak itself leaks real hashchange listeners between tests and into later browser namespaces. Later hash changes can invoke stale host code against a removed #app node, creating order-dependent failures; the current assertions inspect only the stored handle, not the real window registry, so they remain green.

Recommendation:
Add teardown that removes the exact recorded host/hash-listener* from js/window before resetting the atom. Add a browser-visible assertion/probe proving one test leaves no registered host listener (or otherwise prove balanced add/remove) so the cleanup cannot regress silently.

Risks/contracts:
Remove only the listener owned by the host using its recorded identity. Do not blanket-replace window handlers or weaken the production defonce/hot-reload behavior. Keep Node fake-window cleanup valid.

Acceptance:
- DOM-test teardown unregisters the recorded hashchange listener before discarding its handle.
- A regression that resets the handle without unregistering makes the browser suite red.
- Both Story-host tests can run repeatedly/in either order without accumulating listeners; browser and focused Node gates pass.
acceptance_criteria: Unregister the exact recorded host hashchange listener before fixture state is reset, add non-vacuous browser coverage for balanced listener ownership, and keep production hot-reload plus Node fake-window contracts passing.
close_reason: PR #9089. Premise held exactly as described: the DOM fixture nilled host/hash-listener* without removeEventListener, so the next mount's remove-then-add became add-only and stacked a second listener on the shared page. Fix: reset-host-handles! now unregisters the EXACT recorded listener from js/window before discarding the handle (stored identity only; no blanket handler replacement; production defonce/hot-reload untouched; Node fake-window cleanup unchanged). Added fixture-teardown-leaves-no-hashchange-listener-on-the-page, which wraps js/window's listener API for one mount+teardown cycle, asserts the census saw exactly one add (non-vacuity) and that the cycle nets to zero - so a reset-without-unregister regression makes the browser suite red. SCOPE NOTE: the file is tools/testbed-support/test/, outside this dispatch's fence; the change is confined to that one test file and is flagged in the PR body. Verified locally with the focused node build (npm run test:testbed-support): 684 files, 0 warnings, 17 tests / 63 assertions, exit 0 - the new test's body gates on (browser?) and no-ops there. The :browser-test gate that runs the real-DOM assertion was NOT run locally (needs a full browser-test compile plus Chromium); CI owns it.

title: Clarify trace-egress recursive projection roles
description:
Partition: implementation/resources trace-egress classification and foreign-carrier projection.

Recommendation:
Rename lexical roles without changing behavior: classification-axis/declaration-path/normalized-path, sensitive-paths/large-paths/component-index, projected-key, sensitive-found?, project-value, record-sensitive-projection!, original-value/declaration-projected-value, resource-reply-carrier?/family-reply-carrier?/owner-requires-redaction?/runtime-payload?, project-map-value, projected-tags/tag-name/tag-value, projected-row/map, and explicit nested projected-value/sensitive? pairs. Remove argument shadowing. Keep all public function names, keywords, trace shapes, classification policy, traversal order, collection-kind preservation, and reference-preserving no-op behavior.

Compatibility/risk:
Only local bindings/callback arguments change. The boundary is security-critical, so accidental behavioral drift could leak or over-redact. Exercise focused trace-egress suites on JVM and CLJS, including foreign fx carriers, declaration paths, error envelopes, correlation scopes, idempotence, and collection-kind cases.
acceptance_criteria:

- Names distinguish original/projected values, resource/family reply proofs, owner redaction, component indexes, tag names/values, and sensitive evidence.

title: Spell out witness and run-context roles in Hicasso browser drivers
description:
## Evidence
- `implementation/hicasso/testbed/spec.cjs` passes a `Witness` instance as `w` through 24 long browser sections, while `implementation/hicasso/testbed/hmr_spec.cjs` does the same across 10 HMR sections and passes the run control object as `ctx`.
- Those functions span dozens of assertions, reloads, navigation deadlines, and sabotage controls; the parameter roles are stable and repeatedly accessed as `w.eq`, `w.record`, `ctx.save`, and `ctx.navTimeoutMs`.
- The functions and parameters are module-local driver machinery; section IDs, testbed globals, runner context fields, and exported `module.exports.run` shape are contracts and remain unchanged.

## Actionable insight
Rename the local parameters/bindings to `witness` and `runContext` throughout both browser drivers, including helper signatures and comments, without changing any section name, operation, or context property.

## Ambiguity cost
A reader of a long failure witness currently has to remember that `w` is the verdict collector and `ctx` owns navigation/save controls. Explicit names make assertions and destructive HMR transitions self-describing, especially where page, witness, and run context interact.

## Risks / migration
Lexical-only JavaScript rename. Preserve PAGE_HELPERS ABI, global keys, selectors, section IDs, serialized reports, callback arity/order, and runner-owned context fields. Verify with syntax checks and the closest pure/self-test gates; do not require a browser solely for a parameter rename unless the normal gate is available.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Browser testbed section signatures and bodies spell out witness and run-context roles.
2. No `page, w`/`w.eq`/`w.record` or applicable local `ctx` residue remains in the two drivers.
3. Node syntax/checker tests and diff checks pass; functional behavior is unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented and validated lexical role renames; focused Hicasso compile, kondo, invariants, node syntax, controlled browser, HMR, and diff gates pass.

title: Replace one-letter Hicasso test lookup helpers with domain names
description:
## Evidence
- Nineteen tracked Hicasso tests/examples define a file-private helper named only `k` or `q`; `k` constructs the runtime cell key `[frame-id query-v]`, while `q` performs a DOM selector lookup. Two ledger examples add `q*` for querySelectorAll, and `tool_reads_cljs_test.cljs` adds `bk` for the exported boundary-read identity.
- Several of these helpers have 10–39 call sites, so their one-letter names recur throughout long concurrency, read-extent, SSR, portal, keyboard, and tool evidence tests.
- Exact definition/call census confirms all are private test helpers; `examples/slice/i18n.cljs`'s public `t` translation API is a separate established idiom and is retained.

## Actionable insight
Rename private `k` helpers to `sub-key`, `q` to `query-node`, `q*` to `query-nodes`, and the distinct exported-key helper `bk` to `boundary-read-key`, updating each file's references and explanatory links.

## Ambiguity cost
The current names conceal the key distinction tests are proving (raw runtime key versus privacy-projected boundary key) and make long DOM tests read as algebra rather than interactions with selected nodes.

## Risks / migration
Test-local only. Do not rename public APIs, selectors, fixture IDs, test names, namespaces/files, or the public example translation function `t`. Preserve test expressions exactly aside from symbol spelling.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Every private Hicasso test helper whose complete name is `k`, `q`, `q*`, or `bk` states its runtime/DOM role.
2. Exact old-definition searches are empty, with the intentional public `t` untouched.
3. Affected node/browser suites or their closest focused build gates pass, plus lint/diff checks.
close_reason: Implemented and validated lexical role renames; focused Hicasso compile, kondo, invariants, node syntax, controlled browser, HMR, and diff gates pass.

title: Clarify reference and candidate roles in Hicasso shadow diffs
description:
## Evidence
- `implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test/mounted.cljs` compares reference and candidate DOM/intent state, but the core difference walk uses private helper names `at`, `checkpoint`, and `red` plus repeated `a`/`b`, `x`/`y`, `rt`/`ct` locals.
- In this file those values are not generic pairs: they are reference versus candidate attributes, properties, children, node tags, intent entries, and the resulting checkpoint difference.
- The public `shadow!` API and its result keys are already ledger-settled and must remain stable; the ambiguous names are internal only.

## Actionable insight
Rename private comparison helpers and multi-step locals by side and role, e.g. `path-description`, `checkpoint-difference`, `red-verdict`, `reference-attrs`, `candidate-attrs`, `reference-child`, `candidate-child`, and explicit tag/intent roles.

## Ambiguity cost
A side swap in a differential harness produces a plausible but inverted diagnostic. Single-letter symmetric names make that class of review error unnecessarily easy and make failure reports harder to trace back through the comparison walk.

## Risks / migration
Keep public kit functions, result-map keys, selectors, status/reason keywords, traversal order, and comparison precedence byte-for-byte. Only private names and lexical bindings move; update internal references and any direct test/doc references if found.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Reference/candidate sides and checkpoint/path roles are explicit throughout the shadow comparator.
2. `hm/shadow!` output shape and semantics do not change.
3. Focused test-kit/shadow suites, lint, and diff checks pass.
close_reason: Implemented and validated lexical role renames; focused Hicasso compile, kondo, invariants, node syntax, controlled browser, HMR, and diff gates pass.

title: Name Hicasso tool projection joins by evidence role
description:
## Evidence
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/tool.cljs` performs privacy projection, grouping, joining, and cross-frame attribution in a single pipeline, but complex transforms use locals such as `n`, `m`, `e`, `bkey`, `fs`, `fid`, `sid`, `r`, and `k`.
- These scopes distinguish raw subscription keys from projected boundary keys, read-set entries from registrations, and frame ids from sub ids. The surrounding evidence contract makes those distinctions correctness-critical.

Rename private/local projection roles to explicit names such as `view-name`, `views-by-read-set`, `projected-boundary-key`, `entry`, `frame-id`, `sub-id`, `boundary-row`, and `candidate-key`. Keep the algorithms and public evidence vocabulary unchanged.

## Ambiguity cost
A reader currently has to infer whether `k` is a raw cell key, an exported boundary key, or a `[frame-id sub-id]` join key. Misreading those categories risks bypassing privacy projection or correlating evidence across the wrong frame.

## Risks / migration
Lexical-only change. Do not rename public reader vars, namespaces/files, evidence schema keys, wire values, sentinel strings, or private function vars referenced by tests. Preserve ordering and fail-closed projection behavior exactly.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Multi-stage tool projection/join locals identify the data role they carry.
2. Public reader names and emitted envelope/schema bytes remain unchanged.
3. Tool-focused tests, production-erasure checks as applicable, lint, and diff checks pass.
close_reason: Implemented and validated lexical role renames; focused Hicasso compile, kondo, invariants, node syntax, controlled browser, HMR, and diff gates pass.

title: Clarify Hicasso collector queue and snapshot roles
description:
## Evidence
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/collector.cljs` implements two reaper queues and snapshot/notification loops with one-letter roles such as `q`, `x`, `id`, `r`, `n`, `c`, `ks`, and `k` across multi-stage mutation paths.
- The queue helpers carry distinct concepts (queue object, queued item, timer generation, target/due timestamps), while the snapshot loop distinguishes read keys from retained cells; the current names force readers to reconstruct those roles from property access.
- Whole-repo consumer and history review shows these are lexical/private implementation names only. Public vars, JS property strings, timing contracts, and documented `run-once` vocabulary need not move.

## Actionable insight
Rename only private arguments and locals to their semantic roles, e.g. `queue`, `item`, `arm-id`, `due-at-ms`, `now-ms`, `registration`, `notify`, `read-keys`, `read-key`, and `cell`. This makes timer supersession and snapshot fallback logic reviewable without altering executable structure.

## Ambiguity cost
The same one-letter name currently changes meaning between a queue, a registration, a callback, a read key, and a cell. That is especially expensive in the reaper and commit paths, where an incorrect role assumption can invert lifecycle or notification reasoning.

## Risks / migration
No public API migration. Preserve every public/private var name, JS object property (`items`, `due`, `target`, `seq`, etc.), serialized value, timeout ordering, and hot-path structure. Apply lexical renames only and verify exact old-name patterns plus runtime tests.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Collector queue, notification, entry-match, and snapshot locals state their roles rather than relying on one-letter names where the scope spans multiple operations.
2. No public var, JS property string, runtime operation, timing, or allocation structure changes.
3. Hicasso focused tests/lint pass and `git diff --check` is clean.
close_reason: Implemented and validated lexical role renames; focused Hicasso compile, kondo, invariants, node syntax, controlled browser, HMR, and diff gates pass.

title: Remove unused API-manifest projection index helpers
description:
Evidence
- implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/projection.clj defines public index-by-var-name and index-by-ns+var helpers.
- Repository-wide exact-symbol searches find no executable call to either helper: index-by-var-name appears only in its definition and a stale doc_api_check.clj comment; index-by-ns+var appears only in its definition and historical duplicate-row comments in gen.clj/gen_test.clj.
- Both date to the initial projection module (commit 70a1b11bc2) and targeted history finds no consumer. Live checks build purpose-specific sets/indexes instead: API.md needs tier sets, docs need a bare-name set, and Xray needs a strict [namespace var] set.
- index-by-ns+var uses assoc and would overwrite duplicates; generation now rejects duplicate [namespace var] rows before projection.

Impact
These public helpers imply a shared projection contract that no caller uses and whose value shapes do not match current validators. Their stale references obscure which duplicate and name-resolution semantics each checker actually relies on.

Recommendation
Delete both helpers and rewrite the three historical/doc comments to describe the live purpose-specific projections rather than nonexistent functions.

Risks / contracts
Do not consolidate live checker indexes merely to retain these helpers: bare-name latitude, tier sets, strict namespace identity, and duplicate rejection are distinct contracts. Confirm there is no external consumer of this internal, unpublished JVM tool namespace.
acceptance_criteria:
- projection.clj no longer defines index-by-var-name or index-by-ns+var, and repository search finds no stale symbol references.
- doc_api_check.clj and duplicate-generation commentary accurately name the live set/index behavior.
- Bare-name docs resolution, strict Xray resolution, API.md tier checking, and duplicate [namespace var] rejection retain their existing tests and semantics.
- clojure -M:test passes in implementation/scripts/api-manifest with 0 failures/errors.
close_reason: Deleted index-by-var-name and index-by-ns+var from api_manifest/projection.clj; the three stale references now name the live purpose-specific projections (doc_api_check.clj builds a bare-name SET; gen.clj and gen_test.clj duplicate-generation commentary now cite xray-spec-check's strict [namespace var] SET, which cannot represent a duplicate at all). A note at the deletion site records why there is deliberately no shared index - bare-name latitude, tier sets, strict namespace identity and duplicate rejection are distinct contracts, and bare-name resolution is unsound for the Xray panels where ten namespaces carry the same :var Panel. Two instruments + controls: git grep -F finds both only at their definitions and the three comments, while controls rows-in-ns/manifest-rows/table-var-rows hit 3/7/1 real call sites; clj-kondo var-usage analysis over src+test reports 0 usages for both against the same controls at 3/7/1, out of 2213 var-usages analysed. No external consumer: this is an internal unpublished JVM tool namespace. Gate: clojure -M:test in implementation/scripts/api-manifest exit 0, 91 tests / 189 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors. PR #9088.

title: mcp-conformance: remove the stale descriptor exemption from the indicator gate
description:
Evidence
- indicator_field_test.clj's no-inline-indicator-slot-emit-outside-the-helper skips every file in inline-emit-whitelist before reading and applying fx/strip-comments-and-strings.
- The whitelist includes tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors.cljs solely because its descriptor docstrings mention :dropped-sensitive and :elided-large.
- Commit efd0c8dbf32 changed this gate to strip comments, docstrings, and strings before matching specifically so descriptor prose no longer needs exclusion.
- Executing the gate's actual stripper and variant-regex against descriptors.cljs returns false for both indicator literals. Therefore removing that path from the whitelist is green today.
- Because the pre-read whitelist bypasses the whole file, any future real code emission of either slot in descriptors.cljs would also be skipped and the conformance gate would falsely pass. wire.cljs is different: it is the deliberate central helper location and remains a valid exception.

Impact
A compatibility exemption outlived the false-positive it addressed and now forms a whole-file blind spot in a MUST-level single-emit-path gate. The current source is conformant, but a later inline emission in descriptors.cljs would evade CI.

Recommendation
Remove descriptors.cljs from inline-emit-whitelist and update the surrounding comments/docstring to describe only the central wire.cljs helper exception. Continue stripping strings before the scan so user-facing descriptor prose remains permitted.

Risks and contracts
Do not remove the wire.cljs exception or forbid indicator names in descriptor documentation. Preserve keyword-boundary matching, filesystem source discovery, and the central with-indicators contract. This change tightens only test coverage; it does not alter an MCP tool/schema/protocol surface.
acceptance_criteria:
- descriptors.cljs is scanned by no-inline-indicator-slot-emit-outside-the-helper after comments/docstrings/strings are stripped.
- wire.cljs remains the explicit central-helper exception.
- The current wire-vocab Clojure suite passes.
- A temporary real-code occurrence such as (assoc envelope :dropped-sensitive 1) in descriptors.cljs makes the focused test fail, while existing descriptor prose does not.
- Comments no longer describe descriptors.cljs as whitelisted.
close_reason: PR #9086 (head 79b2ee56a6). descriptors.cljs removed from inline-emit-whitelist; wire.cljs remains the sole central-helper exception; the surrounding comment and docstring no longer describe descriptors.cljs as whitelisted, and the docstring now records WHY prose needs no row (the gate strips comments/docstrings/strings first, per efd0c8dbf32) and that a row is strictly stronger because it skips the file whole. PREMISE DRIFT worth recording: the bead says the whitelist exists because descriptor docstrings mention :dropped-sensitive and :elided-large — on the current tree descriptors.cljs contains NEITHER literal in any form (grep over tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src returns only descriptors_data.cljs, wire.cljs and wire_pipeline.cljs). descriptors_data.cljs is NOT whitelisted and passes purely on the strip, which is the working proof that the strip suffices. So the exemption was doubly stale and the recommendation held. Gate liveness proved directly, both directions: planting (assoc envelope :dropped-sensitive 1) in descriptors.cljs turned no-inline-indicator-slot-emit-outside-the-helper RED naming the file and the literal (exit 1, 119 assertions); with the same fault in place, temporarily restoring the old whitelist row turned it GREEN (exit 0, 117 assertions) — the whole-file blind spot reproduced exactly as the bead describes. Both temporary edits reverted; descriptors.cljs verified byte-identical by blob hash 6cbd4df82d18a212c4b69ecd1ce4f211aa06a349 and carries no diff in the PR. Gate: wire-vocab clojure -M:test exit 0 (94 tests / 1031 assertions) re-run on the final shipping tree.

title: mcp-conformance wire-vocab: remove three dead namespace requires

Gate: wire-vocab clojure -M:test exit 0 (94 tests / 1031 assertions, unchanged coverage).

title: story-mcp: remove unreachable JVM CLJS-var auto-probes
description:
Evidence
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/cljs_resolve.cljc:77-113` retains `resolve-cljs-var`, `registered-substrates-var`, and `violations-by-frame-var`; their only production purpose is to auto-discover two browser-side providers from the JVM process.
- Both targets are impossible in the shipped JVM artifact: `re-frame.story/registered-substrates` is defined only inside `#?(:cljs ...)` (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc:1816-1822`), and `re-frame.story.ui.a11y/violations-by-frame` lives in a `.cljs` namespace (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/a11y.cljs:59-64`). Story-MCP is JVM-only and has no in-process browser bridge.
- Commit `82ec7aa84f` established the symmetric contract: neither provider auto-wires; a future bridge binds both dynamic seams. The old CLJ probe defaults at lines 132-133 and 190-191 survived that migration.
- Repo-wide usage finds no consumer of `resolve-cljs-var` outside its dedicated unit test (`tools_test.clj:637-644`); the two private probe vars are source-only. `[re-frame.story]` at line 75 exists only to support this probe path.

Impact
The package loads the large Story facade and maintains/test-documents an auto-wiring mechanism that can never make either capability available. This obscures the actual explicit-provider contract and creates false confidence that browser state may be reachable from the JVM.

Recommendation
Remove the resolver, both private probes, the resolver-only test, and the resolver-only Story facade require. Initialize both dynamic provider vars to nil on every platform, while retaining the dynamic provider seams, availability predicates, accessor semantics, and capability-unavailable behavior.

Risks / contracts
`resolve-cljs-var` is a public var in an internal namespace even though it is absent from Story-MCP's documented/package/protocol API. Check downstream source consumers before deletion. Do not remove or rename `*substrate-provider*`, `*a11y-provider*`, `substrate-provider-available?`, `a11y-provider-available?`, or their explicit binding behavior; those are deliberate test/future-bridge seams.
acceptance_criteria:
- A repo-wide consumer check documents that no supported caller depends on `resolve-cljs-var`.
- The resolver, its two cached probe vars, resolver-only test, and now-unused Story facade require are removed (or a concrete supported external contract is documented instead).
- Both provider vars default to nil and remain independently bindable; availability distinguishes absent providers from reached providers returning empty data.
- Story-MCP unit tests, descriptor drift check, and stdio round-trip pass.

Removed resolve-cljs-var, registered-substrates-var, violations-by-frame-var, the resolver-only unit test, and the [re-frame.story] require that existed only to feed the probe; both provider vars now read a plain nil on every platform. Consumer check: repo-wide search finds resolve-cljs-var only in its own ns and the deleted test - absent from the documented/package/protocol API. Seams kept intact: *substrate-provider*, *a11y-provider*, substrate-provider-available?, a11y-provider-available?, accessors, capability-unavailable routing. Verified: clojure -M:test exit 0 (278 tests / 1473 assertions), clojure -M:gen --check exit 0 (in sync, 19 tools). Gate proved live by planting the exact removed auto-wire ((fn [] []) as the substrate default): exit 1, 9 failures including list-substrates returning a false-empty {:substrates []} success.

title: Remove discarded stderr write from open-in-editor capability decline
description:
