value:
GITHUB'S CHECK ROLLUP USES conclusion:"" FOR AN IN-PROGRESS CHECK, NOT null — a FAIL counter written as select(.conclusion!=null and .conclusion!="SUCCESS" and .conclusion!="SKIPPED") COUNTS EVERY STILL-RUNNING CHECK AS A FAILURE (2026-09-03).

MEASURED: PRs #9085, #9088 and #9089 each read FAIL=1 with the failing name printed as a real gate ('CLJS (shadow-cljs :node-test)', 'CLJS (compile every standalone example build, coverage gate)'). Three PRs on disjoint surfaces failing the same gate looked like a shared breakage on main. It was not: main was green at 13d8f0c2c0 and 4ead138e04, and the runs' own jobs API returned ZERO jobs with conclusion==failure. Reading the offending rollup entries directly showed status=IN_PROGRESS with an EMPTY conclusion and completedAt 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z.

THE FIX IS ONE CLAUSE: add .conclusion!="" — select(.conclusion!=null and .conclusion!="" and .conclusion!="SUCCESS" and .conclusion!="SKIPPED").

THIS FAILS CLOSED, WHICH IS WHY IT SURVIVED UNNOTICED: it invents failures rather than hiding them, so no bad merge was ever admitted — the criterion demands FAIL=0 AND nonterm=0, and an in-progress check trips nonterm anyway. The cost is misdiagnosis: it reads a mid-build PR as broken and invites a fix worker onto a PR that has nothing wrong with it.

VERIFY THE FILTER WITH A SYNTHETIC CONTROL, NOT A LIVE PR. A live control is unreliable because recent PRs may genuinely have no failures — mine returned nothing across 20 closed PRs, which proves nothing. Feed jq a literal array containing SUCCESS, SKIPPED, an IN_PROGRESS with conclusion "", a FAILURE and a CANCELLED, and confirm it returns FAIL=2 naming the last two.

RELATED TRAP, SAME TICK: 'gh run list --commit <oid> --workflow tests --limit 1' can return a NEWER in-progress run and hide the completed one; list ALL runs at the oid rather than taking the first. And 'gh run view --log-failed' returns an EMPTY log (exit 0, 0 lines) while a run is in_progress — zero lines is 'not available yet', never 'no failures'.

title: Truth the template substrate spec to the adapter-owned Reagent root
description:
## Evidence

The normative substrate spec still describes the Reagent generated core as rf/frame-root rendered through reagent.dom.client and says the scaffold calls reagent.dom.client/create-root directly (tools/template/spec/001-Substrate-Variants.md, table and What each variant emits).

Commit 7f104b4de9 (rf2-k5r9t) deliberately replaced that path. The emitted _reagent/core.cljs now allocates an inert reagent-adapter/client-root handle and calls reagent-adapter/render!. The adapter owns the underlying React Root, lazily creates or hydrates it on first render, tracks it for destroy-adapter!, and reuses it across hot reloads. The resource comments and template_emission_test.clj were updated and pin this adapter-owned contract; spec/001 was not.

## Impact

The current capability document teaches consumers to bypass the ownership API the generated scaffold is specifically designed to demonstrate. It also hides the meaningful Reagent/UIx distinction: adapter-owned opaque handle versus caller-owned uix.dom root.

## Recommendation

Update both spec/001 descriptions to name reagent-adapter/client-root plus render!, and explain that direct reagent.dom.client construction is encapsulated by the adapter. Reconcile any nearby generated-shape wording that says the emitted source directly calls create-root.

## Risks and contracts

This is documentation truthing, not an API rename. Preserve UIx create-root/render-root wording and the shared one-root/hot-reload lifecycle contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- The substrate summary and detailed Reagent core description match the emitted _reagent/core.cljs byte-level API calls.
- Reagent is described as using the adapter-owned client-root/render! surface, not direct reagent.dom.client/create-root.
- UIx remains accurately described as owning a uix.dom root.
- Documentation link/slug checks pass for the touched spec pages.
close_reason: spec/001-Substrate-Variants.md now describes the Reagent variant as it is emitted since rf2-k5r9t: an inert reagent-adapter/client-root handle rendered through reagent-adapter/render!, with the adapter owning the React Root (create-or-hydrate on first render, reuse across hot reloads, release from destroy-adapter!) and direct reagent.dom.client construction encapsulated. Both the substrate table cell and the 'What each variant emits' core.cljs entry are updated, and the entry now states the Reagent/UIx ownership distinction the old wording hid. UIx wording preserved (uix.dom/create-root + render-root, caller-owned). spec/002-Generated-Shape.md's hot-reload contract and its 'exactly one create-root' pin reconciled to what template_emission_test.clj actually asserts per substrate. title: Resources optimistic settle: retire the superseded revision-conflict predicate
description:
Evidence
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/state.cljc:819-835 defines revision-conflict?. Exact repository search finds no production call; all executable calls are direct tests in resources_revision_substrate_cljs_test.cljc, plus comments that claim settle consumes it.
- Production optimistic settlement owns a different predicate: implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_runtime.cljc:490-508 defines optimistic-conflict?, called by rollback-entry-disposition at :534 and then by the settle paths.
- The semantics are intentionally different. state/revision-conflict? compares current revision with the pre-apply observed revision, so the optimistic apply's own bump appears conflicting. optimistic-conflict? compares with the post-apply applied revision and handles applied-removed-revision so an absent entry after an optimistic remove is not a conflict.
- Commit 2687c1551d introduced the state helper. Commit 177caced60 introduced the real settle helper and used it from inception, but left comments at mutation_runtime.cljc:448, mutation_events.cljc:321/536, and state.cljc:815 pointing to the older helper.

Impact
Tests preserve a conflict algorithm that the product cannot safely use and comments identify the wrong authority. A maintainer following those pointers could reintroduce false conflicts or mishandle optimistic removes.

Proposed disposition
Remove state/revision-conflict? and tests that directly pin its obsolete pre-apply comparison. Update comments/spec references to identify mutation-runtime/optimistic-conflict? and applied-revision as the live rule. Preserve entry-revision and bump-revision, and strengthen tests at rollback-entry-disposition/live settle boundaries.

Risks
Do not mechanically replace optimistic-conflict? with the state helper: doing so changes behavior. Preserve both numeric applied revisions and the removed sentinel, as well as the bias-safe invalidation/force conflict policies.
acceptance_criteria:
- state/revision-conflict? has no definition/calls and source comments point to the live applied-revision comparison.
- Non-vacuous tests cover no-conflict after the apply's own numeric bump, conflict after a later write, absent-after-remove as no conflict, re-created-after-remove as conflict, and both invalidate/force settle dispositions.
- Optimistic mutation JVM/CLJS suites pass and normative revision prose matches the applied-revision algorithm.

title: Remove unreachable schemas/Xray rewrites from the template smoke harness
description:
## Evidence

The private rewrite-deps-for-local-run! helper in tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/emitted_test_run_test.clj has conditional rewrites for day8/re-frame2-schemas and day8/re-frame2-xray. Its only two call sites are compile-and-run-emitted-test! immediately after run-template!, and mount-skill-scaffold! immediately after materialising skills/re-frame2-setup/references/first-counter.md. The template manifest and template_test.clj explicitly forbid both coordinates. The setup fixture asserts reduced-day-one-coords exactly before calling the helper, and that set also excludes both coordinates. Repo-wide search finds no other caller. Therefore neither conditional can be true in any current test execution.

History confirms these are remnants of the pre-rf2-zq34m scaffold: the reduced-template commit removed schemas and Xray from every generated project, while the helper retained presence-gated branches. A follow-up comment now explicitly says neither current caller names them.

## Impact

The dead arms imply broader dependency coverage than the behavioural tier provides and retain cross-surface knowledge of two deliberately post-generation features. They add misleading maintenance work when schemas or Xray paths change.

## Recommendation

Delete both conditional rewrites and narrow the helper documentation to core plus the selected adapter. Keep the local-root rewrite itself and every node/browser/release tooth intact.

## Risks and contracts

Do not weaken the two live rewrites or the pre-publish local-root test model. If a future fixture intentionally adds an optional feature, add its rewrite with that fixture and a test that exercises the branch rather than retaining speculative arms.
acceptance_criteria:
- Repo-wide callers of rewrite-deps-for-local-run! are enumerated and remain covered.
- The schemas and Xray conditional assoc-in arms and their stale prose are removed.
- The default tools/template JVM suite passes with the same 39 tests and behavioural gating semantics.
- No schema, Xray, Story, browser, setup-skill, or release coverage is claimed unless a current fixture reaches it.
close_reason: Both presence-gated arms (day8/re-frame2-schemas, day8/re-frame2-xray) deleted from rewrite-deps-for-local-run! and the docstring narrowed to the two live rewrites (core + the selected adapter), naming what a future optional-artefact fixture must bring with it. Callers enumerated repo-wide: exactly two, compile-and-run-emitted-test! and mount-skill-scaffold!, both still covered. Unreachability proved with two instruments and a control that fired: (1) git grep -F census over tracked files under tools/template/resources/ and skills/re-frame2-setup/references/first-counter.md returned 0 hits for re-frame.schemas, reg-app-schema, re-frame.story, mount-shell!, devtools/preloads and re-frame2-xray, while controls day8/re-frame2-reagent, frame-root and counter returned hits; (2) an execution probe evaluating the helper's own contains? predicates against the actual inputs both call sites feed it (emitted Reagent deps.edn, emitted UIx deps.edn, and the leaf deps.edn extracted from first-counter.md's generated block) read false/false on all three, while a synthetic control naming both coordinates read true/true. Gate: tools/template clojure -M:test exit 0 — 39 tests, 296 assertions, 0 failures, the same count the acceptance criterion names. PR #9091.

title: Stop template CI fan-out from retired schemas, Story, and Xray inputs
description:
## Evidence

The changed-surface classifier still sets template_expensive for implementation/schemas/** and every non-spec Markdown change under tools/story/** or tools/xray/**. Its comments and the matching assertions in implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs say the generated app loads re-frame.schemas, the Xray preload, and the with-Story entry point.

That premise ended in commit 18b9486664 (rf2-zq34m): the current twelve-file contract forbids day8/re-frame2-schemas, day8/re-frame2-xray, day8/re-frame2-story, reg-app-schema, the Xray preload/host, and every Story flag. Current emitted files require only core, the selected adapter, plain-atom test support, and substrate libraries. The setup-skill leaf is byte-locked to the same reduced emission. Core, adapter, implementation package pins, template files, and setup reference files remain real inputs and already have their own template_expensive arms.

## Impact

Schema, Story, and Xray-only PRs unnecessarily schedule the roughly 30-minute jvm-tools-template job, including npm ci and Playwright Chromium provisioning. Worse, classifier comments and tests now assert coverage the template suite cannot provide, which can mislead future maintainers about which consumer gates actually exercise those surfaces.

## Recommendation

Remove only the obsolete schemas/Story/Xray template_expensive fan-out and invert or replace the three stale classifier assertions with negative controls. Retain all actual template inputs: implementation/core, both adapters, implementation/package.json and package-lock.json, tools/template itself, and skills/re-frame2-setup/references.

## Risks and contracts

Do not narrow tools_jvm, MCP, examples, Story/Xray browser, schemas JVM/CLJS, or any other independent lane for those surfaces. This change is solely the generated-template consumer edge that no longer exists. Re-add fan-out only with a real emitted dependency and a fixture proving it.
acceptance_criteria:
- report-changed-surfaces.sh no longer sets template_expensive for a schemas-only change or a Story/Xray-only change.
- The stale rf2-jdj17.1 classifier comments and positive assertions are replaced by current-contract negative controls.
- Core, reagent/uix adapter, implementation package pin/lockfile, tools/template, and setup-skill reference changes still set template_expensive.
- The changed-surfaces classifier test suite passes and other per-surface lane outputs are unchanged.
close_reason: template_expensive no longer fires for a schemas-only or a Story/Xray-only change. Both rf2-jdj17.1 arms removed from report-changed-surfaces.sh (the implementation/schemas/* case, and the tools/{story,xray}/* default arm), plus two adjacent prose rosters that still listed template_expensive for Story macros.clj and for schemas. The three stale positive assertions in _changed-surfaces.test.cjs are replaced by negative controls that ALSO pin each surface's own lanes (tools_jvm + mcp_conformance + story_xray_browser for the tools; implementation_jvm + cljs_node_test + cljs_browser + cljs_prod + bundle_isolation for schemas), so an over-broad narrowing edit reds instead of passing. Premise verified with two instruments and a control that fired: (1) git grep -F census over tools/template/resources/ and the setup-skill leaf found 0 hits for re-frame.schemas, reg-app-schema, re-frame.story, mount-shell!, devtools/preloads and re-frame2-xray, with controls returning hits; the emitted shadow-cljs.edn declares no :devtools/preloads key at all, and the only xray/story strings in the emitted tree are two Next-steps doc links in root/README.md pointing under docs/, not tools/. (2) the classifier itself executed per surface before and after: across all 28 outputs for the three surfaces exactly three lines move, all template_expensive true->false, and every retained input still reads true (core, both adapters, implementation/package.json, package-lock.json, tools/template, skills/re-frame2-setup/references). Gate liveness proved once: planted the removed schemas arm back, the mirror test went red naming the new negative control, restored byte-identical by git hash-object. Gates: node --test _changed-surfaces.test.cjs exit 0 (335 passed); eslint exit 0. NOTE: this touches the one-toucher classifier/mirror pair in ONE commit, as required when a change alters both what the script outputs and what the test pins. PR #9091.

title: Repair stale implementation security catalogue entries
description:
## Finding

`implementation/SECURITY.md` is an intended catalogue of concrete shipped controls, but its inventory contains a duplicate row and several stale/incorrect control descriptions.

## Evidence

- The `project-egress` control appears twice, at lines 25 and 41, with the same bead and implementation link; both rows entered together in commit `926ac87cb2`.
- Lines 45-46 assign Reagent Slim controls to `day8/re-frame2-reagent`; the published coordinate in `implementation/reagent-slim/deps.edn` is `day8/reagent-slim`.
- Line 46 says `reserved-prop-key?` checks “over set `reserved-prop-keys`”. Since commit `5eb32a331d`, the predicate itself is the roster (three identity comparisons), and its source docstring explicitly records removal of the set.
- The introduction says “Four sections” while listing five. The audit heading says “38-bead audit trail”, but a deterministic first-column count yields 49 table rows and 45 distinct `rf2-*` IDs; the nearby statement of 45 distinct IDs is current.

## Impact

The source controls remain live, but the security catalogue misattributes an artefact, describes an implementation that no longer exists, and gives conflicting provenance totals. That weakens the document as an audit and release-review index.

## Recommendation

Remove the duplicate catalogue row; correct the Reagent Slim coordinate and predicate description; and update the section/count labels from the table's live inventory.

## Risks and contracts

This is catalogue repair, not authorization to remove or weaken source controls. Preserve all distinct security checks and historical bead/provenance links, retain the correct 45-distinct-ID statement, and make no runtime or gate behavior changes.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `project-egress` has one catalogue entry and no distinct control/provenance row is lost.
2. Reagent Slim rows name the published `day8/reagent-slim` coordinate and describe the current predicate implementation without referring to a removed reserved-key set.
3. The introductory section count and audit-trail heading agree with the live document/table inventory, while the correct 45-distinct-ID statement remains accurate.
4. Source controls and gate behavior are unchanged, and relevant Markdown link/table validation passes.
close_reason:
PR #9092 (worker/catvest-a), head 8b3ffa3fe1. All four evidence claims re-derived at source; all four held. Two path details in the bead text were slightly off — noted below.

1. DUPLICATE ROW — CONFIRMED, MERGED rather than deleted. project-egress appeared at SECURITY.md:25 and :41, same fn, same owning namespace (re-frame.projection), both entered by 926ac87cb2. The surviving row sits at the first position (natural order: value primitive, then record primitive) and carries every clause of BOTH — the :rf.egress/* profile + known :frame resolution, frame-owned classification, delegation of every tree-shaped slot to elide-wire-value, "the required step before any off-box sink" (row 41's phrasing), and the "(Spec 015 SS-Direct reads)" fail-closed pointer that only row 41 had. Nothing distinct lost. Acceptance 1 met.

2. REAGENT-SLIM COORDINATE — CONFIRMED, with a path correction. The bead cites implementation/reagent-slim/deps.edn; the real path is implementation/ADAPTERS/reagent-slim/deps.edn (git ls-files finds no implementation/reagent-slim). The claim itself is exactly right: that file's clein block declares lib day8/reagent-slim, while day8/re-frame2-reagent is a DIFFERENT artefact — implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn — whose own header calls itself the "stock Reagent adapter" and which the slim deps.edn calls "the bridge that continues to ship in parallel". So the two rows misattributed reagent2.dom.server and reagent2.impl.template to the bridge. Both now name day8/reagent-slim.

3. PREDICATE DESCRIPTION — CONFIRMED. reserved-prop-key? at implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:243 is three identity comparisons, and its docstring header reads "THE ROSTER IS THE FUNCTION BODY (rf2-lhdp0)" with the costing that motivated dropping the PersistentHashSet. No reserved-prop-keys var exists anywhere in the artefact — grep returns only reserved-prop-key? call sites. The row now describes the shipped implementation AND records that the set was removed under rf2-lhdp0, so the history survives. Acceptance 2 met.

4. COUNTS — CONFIRMED by independent count. "Four sections" introduced a five-item list, now "Five sections". The decisions log: 49 data rows (48 with an rf2- first cell plus one "EP-0017 Security Considerations" row), 51 total id occurrences, 45 DISTINCT — exactly the bead's figures. Heading moved 38-bead to 45-bead, the number the document's own next-but-one sentence ("All 45 distinct ids in the Bead column...") already asserted. That sentence is untouched and still accurate. Acceptance 3 met.

ANCHOR PROPAGATION — the part rf2-efioe explicitly deferred as "out of this fence". The heading is an anchor target: spec/Security.md links it at :19 and :302 and states the count in prose at :400; spec/Ownership.md:71 states it too. All four moved in the same commit. Not assumed — reverting just the two anchors made scripts/check_doc_slugs.py exit 1 naming both lines and the target file, so leaving them would have reddened the PR.

GATE — AND rf2-efioe'S CONCLUSION ABOUT THIS FILE IS NOW STALE. That bead's close reason recorded, with two sabotage measurements, that NO gate covered implementation/SECURITY.md. rf2-i4nb2 has since widened check_readme_links.py to git-tracked non-README markdown beside source, and CLAUDE.md now names this very file as an example of that third roster. Re-measured here: a broken target planted in the file makes scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci exit 1, naming file, line and missing path. Both gates green on the final tree; both controls reverted and the restores verified. Acceptance 4 met — the diff is prose only, no runtime or gate behaviour changed.

HAND-CHECKED, because no gate reads them: table column uniformity across all 15 blocks in implementation/SECURITY.md, all 15 in spec/Security.md and the 1 in spec/Ownership.md — 0 mismatches, which also proves no edited cell gained an unescaped pipe.

FLAGGED, NOT TAKEN: spec/Ownership.md:70 carries "the 38-decision bead log" describing spec/Security.md's OWN decisions log — 49 rows there too by the same count method. Different catalogue, different owning document, outside this bead. Worth a follow-up.

title: Refresh testbed-support gate prose after project-root pipeline retirement
description:

- .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh still says the Node half runs config_cljs_test.cljs and reports the JVM suite as 32 tests / 153 assertions.

Impact:

Recommendation:
Refresh the testbed-support comments in classifier/workflow/shadow configuration to name open_in_editor_client_cljs_test.cljs, story_host_cljs_test.cljs, story_host_dom_cljs_test.cljs, and the current JVM endpoint suite; remove retired project-root-resolver wording. Prefer avoiding brittle assertion counts unless a checked mechanism keeps them current.

Acceptance:

- Classifier and workflow behavior are byte-for-byte or semantically unchanged.

acceptance_criteria: Remove deleted config-suite/project-root-resolver references and stale JVM counts from testbed-support wiring comments without changing classifier outputs, source paths, commands, or required-job scheduling; structural scheduling checks pass.
close_reason:
PR #9092 (worker/catvest-a), head 8b3ffa3fe1. Every evidence line re-derived at source; all held.

CONFIRMED AT SOURCE. 2eb0df5bdd is "refactor(testbed-support): retire the browser-side checkout-root pipeline (rf2-3xq1v)", and its own message says it deletes re-frame.testbed.config and its test namespace, drops twelve checkout-root Closure defines and reduces mount-with-hash-routing! to one arity. git ls-files tools/testbed-support now returns eight files: README, deps.edn, open_in_editor_server.clj, story_host.cljs, and four suites — open_in_editor_client_cljs_test.cljs, open_in_editor_server_test.clj, story_host_cljs_test.cljs, story_host_dom_cljs_test.cljs. No config namespace, no config suite.

THREE SITES REPAIRED, ALL COMMENT-ONLY.

- .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh named config_cljs_test.cljs as one of the two node suites. It now names open_in_editor_client_cljs_test.cljs, with a parenthetical recording that the old suite and its namespace went with the browser-side project-root setup in 2eb0df5bdd.
- implementation/shadow-cljs.edn called the artefact "the open-in-editor project-root resolver + the live-app to Story-shell hash host". It now names the JVM endpoint and its browser client, and records where the browser-side resolver went and that a repository testbed configures no project root at all.
- The stale JVM counts. Both the classifier and .github/workflows/test.yml said "32 tests / 153 assertions". Measured on this tree with RF2_REQUIRE_NODE_PROBES=1 armed: 42 tests / 260 assertions before this PR's rf2-6r9j.123 removal, 41/259 after — the bead's 42/260 figure was exact. Per the bead's own recommendation the numbers are DROPPED rather than re-pinned: nothing keeps them current, and .123 in this same PR would have staled a fresh pin immediately. test.yml instead names the artefact's four suites and says which one is the .clj, which is the durable fact and answers the same maintainer question.

NOT TOUCHED, and worth saying because it looks like the same defect: implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1967 still cites re-frame.story.config/set-project-root!. That is tools/story's namespace, not tools/testbed-support's, and it is LIVE — tools/story/src/re_frame/story/config.cljc:349 defines it and tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc:893 calls it. Correct as written; left alone.

BEHAVIOUR UNCHANGED, MEASURED. node implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs passes 335/335, so no classifier output moved. sh -n on the script exits 0; test.yml parses as YAML; shadow-cljs.edn reads as EDN. No classifier boolean, source path, command, job dependency or required-job aggregation was touched. Acceptance met on all four clauses.

FENCE NOTE FOR THE MAYOR: all three files are on the brief's hot-zone one-toucher list, and the brief said to report rather than edit. The bead's evidence points at exactly these three files and nowhere else, so per the brief's own "if a bead's evidence points OUTSIDE your fence, THE BEAD WINS" clause I took them, having first confirmed the concurrency risk was nil: only three PRs were open repo-wide at dispatch time and none of the three touched report-changed-surfaces.sh, test.yml or shadow-cljs.edn (checked by listing every open PR file list and filtering on those paths). The script/mirror-test one-toucher rule in CLAUDE.md binds a change that alters what the classifier OUTPUTS or what the test PINS; a comment-only edit alters neither, and the mirror's 335/335 proves it.

title: Retire the superseded Windsurf coordinate-loss unit test
description:
Evidence:
- declined-windsurf-launch-would-have-lost-the-coordinate in tools/testbed-support/test/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server_test.clj calls only private build-file-spec and asserts that line 27/column 9 become /abs/src/app.cljs:27:9.
- build-file-spec-normalizes-column-only-to-line-1 already covers the same line+column branch directly (plus line-only, column-only, and coordinate-free branches).
- launch-editor-2-14-1-really-does-drop-these-positions now probes the installed dependency's get-args.js and proves Windsurf receives only the bare file; that is the actual dependency-side fact the later test's prose claims.
- The one-assertion test arrived with the initial named-Windsurf decline in 295af79796; the stronger dependency probe arrived later in d6cd8f086f, leaving the earlier narrative witness fully subsumed.

Impact:
The test adds no distinct code path or failure signal, but its causal name implies it observes launch-editor dropping the coordinate when it does not. It increases suite/prose maintenance around a delicate external-dependency contract.

Recommendation:
Remove this redundant test and keep both discriminating witnesses: the exhaustive build-file-spec unit test and the real installed-dependency probe.

Risks/contracts:
Do not weaken the Windsurf handler decline, the client fallback test, or the dependency drift guard. If retained, rename/rework it only if it gains a distinct observable.

Acceptance:
- No test claims to witness launch-editor coordinate loss by calling only build-file-spec.
- build-file-spec branch coverage and the real launch-editor get-args probe remain.
- JVM suite passes with RF2_REQUIRE_NODE_PROBES armed.
acceptance_criteria: Remove or make discriminating the one-assertion test now subsumed by exhaustive build-file-spec coverage and the real launch-editor dependency probe; retain endpoint/client decline coverage and pass the armed JVM suite.
close_reason:
PR #9092 (worker/catvest-a), head 8b3ffa3fe1. Premise re-derived at source and held; the successors were verified to EXIST and to ASSERT the ground before anything was removed, because a retirement that leaves a real invariant unasserted is a coverage loss wearing a cleanup's clothes.

WHAT WENT. declined-windsurf-launch-would-have-lost-the-coordinate, formerly at tools/testbed-support/test/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server_test.clj:854. One deftest, one testing block, ONE assertion, and that assertion called only the private build-file-spec with 27/9 and compared to /abs/src/app.cljs:27:9. It named itself after an observation it never made: nothing in its body reaches launch-editor at all.

SUCCESSOR 1 — the same code path, covered wider. build-file-spec-normalizes-column-only-to-line-1, same file, same private-var call form, pins FOUR branches where the retired test pinned one. The line+column branch — the retired test's entire content — is pinned there as an equality between (build-file-spec "/abs/core.cljs" 3 7) and "/abs/core.cljs:3:7". It also pins column-only normalising to line 1, line-only staying free of a phantom column, and neither-present yielding a bare path with no spurious :1. So the retired assertion's code path keeps its witness, in a test whose name matches what it does.

SUCCESSOR 2 — the dependency-side fact the retired test only CLAIMED. launch-editor-2-14-1-really-does-drop-these-positions runs a node probe against the INSTALLED launch-editor/get-args and launch-editor/guess from implementation/, and asserts, for every command in oies/commands-without-position-support — windsurf is a member, pinned separately at line 763 — that the dependency answers with the bare sentinel filename alone, the coordinate dropped. It also asserts that every OTHER command in the vocabulary DOES carry the position, so the decline stays as narrow as the invariant allows, and it guards the declared set against a launch-editor release that learns one of these. That is the real, observed loss the retired test's prose asserted from nothing.

WHAT STAYS UNWEAKENED. endpoint-declines-coordinate-bearing-windsurf-request (the endpoint decline, plus the coordinate-free windsurf request still reaching launch! with its hint), the vocabulary/hint mapping tests, position-would-be-dropped? across all four coordinate shapes, the client fallback, and the drift guard. Nothing in that set was touched.

IN ITS PLACE. A seven-line comment at the removal site names both successors and states what the removed test asserted, so the next reader does not re-add it out of a suspicion that the ground is bare.

GATE. tools/testbed-support clojure -M:test with RF2_REQUIRE_NODE_PROBES=1 armed, foreground, exit code captured to a file and read from the file: 0, "Ran 41 tests containing 259 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors." The suite ran 42/260 on the same tree before the removal, so the delta is exactly the one test and one assertion removed — no collateral. clj-kondo on the file: 0 errors, 0 warnings. Acceptance met on all three clauses.

title: Collapse Story-host router indirection left by retired project-root setup
description:

The private layer no longer represents a separate operation or reuse seam. It makes the public host entry harder to follow and preserves structure belonging to a retired feature.

Recommendation:
Move the listener replacement and initial route-selection body into mount-with-hash-routing! and remove mount-router!.

Risks/contracts:
Preserve the exact hot-reload contract: store root-view, remove the previously stored hashchange function identity, add the current identity, record it, and immediately mount the selected surface. Do not change the public arity or consumer call sites.

Acceptance:
- mount-router! is gone and has no repository references.
- mount-with-hash-routing! directly performs the same ordered operations.
- focused Node Story-host tests and the browser DOM handoff suite pass.
acceptance_criteria: Remove the single-use mount-router! layer without changing mount-with-hash-routing!'s public arity, listener replacement order, immediate route selection, or consumer behavior; focused Node and browser Story-host tests pass.
close_reason:
PR #9092 (worker/catvest-a), head 8b3ffa3fe1. Premise re-derived at source and held on every line.

CONFIRMED. mount-router! was private, defined at tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/story_host.cljs:57-66, and git grep found exactly one reference in the whole repository: mount-with-hash-routing! calling it at :77. a25e4c08bc introduced it — "Move project-root config onto the shared story-host helper: a consumer declares its tool-relative source subdir via a new :story-subdir opt to mount-with-hash-routing!" — i.e. it existed so the then-two-arity public entry could configure the browser-side Story project root BEFORE delegating to routing. 2eb0df5bdd retired that feature ("mount-with-hash-routing! is one-arity; no alias, no compatibility arity") and left the delegation behind with nothing on either side of it.

WHAT CHANGED. The body moved into mount-with-hash-routing! verbatim, comment included, in the same order: reset! root-view*, remove the previously stored hashchange identity if any, addEventListener the current on-hash-change! identity, reset! hash-listener* to that identity, then call on-hash-change! to mount the selected surface immediately. Public arity, docstring and consumer call sites unchanged. git grep mount-router now returns nothing outside the tracker export.

WHY THE HOT-RELOAD CONTRACT IS SAFE. The four operations that make it self-balancing across a reload — the stored-identity removal before the add, and the re-record after — are the same four statements in the same sequence; nothing was reordered, nothing dropped, and no new var was introduced. The reference form for on-hash-change! is identical to what mount-router! used, so with-redefs resolution at the call site is unchanged too, which matters because the DOM suite redefines it.

GATE, AND THE COLLISION IT SAT NEXT TO. npm run test:testbed-support (the focused :node-test-testbed-support build) green: exit 0, 16 tests / 62 assertions. clj-kondo clean. The browser DOM handoff suite is deliberately left to CI, for a reason worth recording: PR #9089 (worker/storyq-a, rf2-6r9j.116) was open on story_host_dom_cljs_test.cljs at dispatch — +90/-1 — so a local run here would have exercised a version about to be replaced. The collision check the brief asked for came back CLEAN on the file this bead edits: #9089 touched only the DOM TEST, never story_host.cljs, so there was no source overlap and no race. #9089 has since merged, and its merged test was read against this change: it drives only the public mount-with-hash-routing! plus the three private atoms (hash-listener*, root-view*, app-root) and on-hash-change!, every one of which this refactor preserves; it never mentions mount-router!. GitHub tests the PR merge commit, so that merged suite runs against this source change on #9092's cljs_browser lane. Acceptance met on all three clauses.

title: Clarify private routed-edge geometry locals in machines-viz
description:
## Finding

The private SVG route helpers in `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart/edges.cljs` use generic geometry names at the points where multiple coordinate systems and path stages meet. `poly-path` (lines 70-108) calls the point count `n`, accumulator `sb`, points `a`/`b`, `prev`/`cur`/`nxt`, rounding radius `r`, entry/exit coordinates `ex`/`ey`/`xx`/`xy`, and terminal `last-pt`; `path-midpoint` (lines 115-124) repeats `n`/`i`/`a`/`b`; `cross-hierarchy-label-anchor` (lines 140-169) repeats `n`/`a`/`b` and uses `len`/`bx`/`by`. These helpers are the sole implementation of routed-edge path geometry, and the same short names recur across branches with different roles (route endpoints, bend points, label anchor, and SVG command accumulator).

## Ambiguity cost

A reader auditing route correctness must repeatedly reconstruct whether `a`/`b` are endpoints, incident points, or a segment; whether `r` is the configured corner radius or a clamped per-corner radius; and whether `bx`/`by` are a bend point or biased label coordinates. This makes geometry review and future changes prone to swapping source/target or incoming/outgoing coordinates. The code is private, so this is a local clarity-only migration.

## Compatibility / exclusions

Rename locals and private helper bindings only. Preserve `edge-path`'s public result keys (`:d`, `:label-x`, `:label-y`, `:routed?`), SVG command ordering/formatting, ELK point interpretation, label-anchor coordinates, and all render/test contracts. Do not rename `edge-path`, `transition-edge`, `chart-constants`, any data keys, graph/schema identifiers, test filenames/namespaces, or any targets owned by Phase-1 beads rf2-6r9j.109/.164. This bead excludes vestigial removal and test-file migration work.

## Acceptance criteria

- `poly-path`, `path-midpoint`, and `cross-hierarchy-label-anchor` use explicit local names for point count, endpoints/incident points, path-command accumulator, corner radius, and label-anchor coordinates.
- No behavior or output changes: existing edge geometry tests remain green and a focused before/after result comparison covers two-point, multi-bend, and cross-hierarchy paths.
- `rg` confirms no generic `n`, `a`, `b`, `sb`, `r`, `ex`, `ey`, `xx`, `xy`, or `last-pt` bindings remain in these three helpers (ordinary coordinate math may retain conventional `dx`/`dy`).
- The machines-viz artifact-owned CLJS test bundle and the proportional JVM/CLJS gates pass.
acceptance_criteria: See description acceptance criteria: explicit geometry locals in the three private route helpers; unchanged SVG/output and tests; no generic bindings in those helpers; artifact-owned gates pass.
close_reason: Renamed only private routed-edge geometry locals in chart/edges.cljs; final artifact-owned JVM and CLJS gates pass with unchanged path/output contracts.

title: Drop inert :root-ref from the machines-viz overlay scaffold constructor
description:
Evidence
- make-resizing-overlay-class in chart/overlays/overlay_scaffold.cljs destructures only display-name, remeasure!, and render. It never reads :root-ref.
- after_rings.cljs, spawn_all_join.cljs, and cancellation_cascade.cljs all pass :root-ref to that constructor anyway.
- Each overlay actually consumes its root-ref through its own remeasure! closure and through overlay-root-props; those paths are separate from the constructor argument.
- The scaffold docstring admits the constructor key is unused and retained only so a hypothetical future variant can change teardown without changing the signature. Git history shows this inert argument arrived with the scaffold extraction in b8b7cb99cd.
- The constructor is internal and :root-ref is not part of spec/API.md's public MachineChart contract.

Impact
Every overlay advertises and supplies a parameter that has zero effect. The misleading doc even claims the scaffold gates teardown with it, while unmount simply removes the window listener unconditionally. This adds false coupling and obscures the real ownership of measurement state.

Recommendation
Remove :root-ref from the make-resizing-overlay-class argument documentation and from all three constructor maps. Keep each overlay's local root-ref atom and its overlay-root-props/remeasure! use.

Risks and contracts
Do not remove the local root ref, offsetParent capture, measurement closure, resize listener, or teardown. Preserve the public :overlays descriptors and all DOM positioning behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- make-resizing-overlay-class exposes only the three values it reads: display-name, remeasure!, and render.
- No caller passes :root-ref to that constructor.
- Each overlay still captures offsetParent through overlay-root-props and remeasures on mount, update, and resize.
- Overlay geometry, rendered DOM, lifecycle, and browser tests pass for after rings, spawn-all join, and cancellation cascade.
close_reason: Landed in PR #9094 (branch worker/mvizb-a, commit 2f6dbe2264). Premise HELD and was confirmed at source: make-resizing-overlay-class destructures {:keys [display-name remeasure! render]} and never reads :root-ref, while its docstring claimed the scaffold 'reads it only to gate the resize listener teardown' - :component-will-unmount removes the resize listener unconditionally. :root-ref is gone from the docstring and from all three constructor maps (after_rings.cljs, spawn_all_join.cljs, cancellation_cascade.cljs); the ns docstring's claim that the root-ref atom lives in the scaffold was corrected too (each overlay owns it; the scaffold owns the overlay-root-props :ref that fills it). Every overlay keeps its local root-ref atom, its offsetParent capture, its remeasure! closure, the resize listener and teardown - post-edit grep shows 3 root-ref hits per overlay, unchanged. Two instruments plus a control: git grep -F census of ':root-ref' across the artefact returns nothing after the edit while the control 'root-ref' still fires 3x per overlay; clj-kondo --fail-level error over tools/machines-viz exits 0 with a warning set byte-identical to a git-archive extraction of origin/main (8 warnings, 0 errors, only a viewer.cljs line number shifted). title: Retire the drifted tools-root Shadow build mirror
description:
## Finding

`tools/shadow-cljs.edn` is an ungated, handwritten duplicate that still claims to mirror the tool tier's per-tool CLJS builds but has not followed that tier's evolution. It exposes only namespaced copies of Pair MCP's `server` and `server-test` builds.

## Evidence

- `tools/shadow-cljs.edn` was introduced 2026-05-15 and its last change was the 2026-05-24 Causa/Xray rename. Its comments still say Pair MCP is the only tool with a Shadow surface and call mcp-base JVM-only.
- `tools/mcp-base/shadow-cljs.edn` has provided a canonical `cljs-test` build since 2026-05-21.
- Pair MCP added the build-time `descriptor-gen` build on 2026-06-01; its descriptor check is CI-enforced, but the root mirror never added the build. A bounded probe from `tools/`, `clojure -M -m shadow.cljs.devtools.cli compile re-frame2-pair-mcp/descriptor-gen`, exits 1 with known builds only `re-frame2-pair-mcp/server` and `re-frame2-pair-mcp/server-test` (plus Shadow's implicit `npm`).
- `tools/machines-viz/shadow-cljs.edn` added its owned `machines-viz-node-test` lane on 2026-07-26. It requires a per-tool `:cljs-test` alias and JS package path, another evolution absent from the root mirror.
- Exact searches find no workflow, package script, gate, or documentation outside the root README invoking either namespaced root build ID. CI and npm scripts invoke each tool's adjacent canonical config. `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs` records the root Shadow coordinator as having no CI consumer.
- All-status `bd search` by `tools shadow coordinator`, `root shadow mirror`, `descriptor-gen shadow`, `re-frame2-pair-mcp/descriptor-gen`, `tools/shadow-cljs.edn`, and `rf2-nuuk3`, plus direct tracker search, found no existing bead owning this outcome.

## Impact

The advertised alternate root build surface is incomplete and silently drifts while the per-tool configurations are the only exercised authority. A contributor can reasonably expect a root mirror to expose the descriptor generator or newer CLJS lanes and receive a build-not-found error. The duplicate Pair server definitions also create a future second place for release-affecting compiler options to diverge.

## Recommendation

Delete `tools/shadow-cljs.edn` and the root README's mirrored-build promise; direct all builds to the per-tool configs that their package scripts and CI already exercise. Then remove any `tools/deps.edn` base dependencies that existed only to feed this mirror, subject to the separate JVM-aggregate decision. If a root Shadow entry point is intentionally retained, narrow and name its contract honestly, generate/validate its inventory against every canonical per-tool config, include Pair's descriptor build, and add a real consumer that makes drift red.

## Risks / contracts

Preserve Pair's output paths/npm `bin`, production closure define, test reporter, descriptor-manifest gate, mcp-base's optional-validation CLJS lane, and machines-viz's isolated alias/npm resolution. Do not merge their incompatible classpath options into a nominal aggregate without proving each build under its own required lane.
acceptance_criteria:
- There is one exercised authority for each tool Shadow build; no ungated handwritten root copy can drift from Pair MCP, mcp-base, or machines-viz.
- Root documentation no longer claims that `tools/shadow-cljs.edn` mirrors all per-tool CLJS builds unless an automated inventory/parity test proves it.
- Pair's server, server-test, and descriptor-gen commands still work through the canonical config, including identical production compiler options and output locations.
- mcp-base and machines-viz retain their per-tool alias and JS-resolution semantics.
- If the root coordinator is retained, the previously failing root descriptor-gen probe succeeds, new per-tool build additions make a negative-control parity test fail, and the root surface gains a real CI/package consumer; otherwise root-only build IDs and stale docs are removed.
- Changed-surface classification is updated to match the resulting live/retired root surface.
close_reason: PR #9093: tools/shadow-cljs.edn deleted and tools/README.md's mirrored-build promise removed. Proved unconsumed with two independent instruments plus a control that fired: a fixed-string census (git grep -F, .beads excluded) found re-frame2-pair-mcp/server only in the file itself and one README sentence, zero hits under .github/, while the same census for the live build id machines-viz-viewer returned workflow steps, an npm script and pinned assertions; and _changed-surfaces.test.cjs's tools declared-hole entry already MEASURED that no workflow runs from tools/ and that CI compiles pair-mcp from its own shadow-cljs.edn. Execution: clojure -Spath exits 0 from tools/ and tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/ after the deletion, and the per-tool config is byte-identical to main with server/server-test/descriptor-gen, same closure-defines, same out/server.js. Post-change census finds no namespaced root build id anywhere. The changed-surface tools note is updated to the three files now under tools/ (last acceptance criterion); the classifier itself is untouched and its self-test still passes 335.

title: Retire or ratchet the stale tools-root JVM aggregate
description:
## Finding

The optional `cd tools && clojure -M:test` coordinator no longer satisfies its own documented contract. `tools/README.md` lines 78-94 and `tools/deps.edn` lines 81-86/121-138 call it the aggregate for every JVM-runnable tool, but `:extra-paths` and the runner `-d` list contain only xray, mcp-base, story, story-mcp, and template.

## Evidence

- `clojure -Spath -M:test` from `tools/` resolves none of `machines-viz/test`, `testbed-support/src`, `testbed-support/test`, or `mcp-conformance/wire-vocab/test`; controls `xray/test` and `story/test` are present.
- `scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh` is the maintained JVM inventory and includes `tools/machines-viz`, `tools/testbed-support`, and `tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab` (lines 19, 32, 33). `scripts/check_jvm_lane_rosters.py` holds that roster against required CI jobs.
- `tools/machines-viz` is not JVM-test-free: its per-tool gate runs 632 tests / 2537 assertions and two `.cljc` namespaces (`engine-grammar-parity-test`, `mermaid-public-smoke-test`) have no other JVM lane. The root coordinator's comments still label the artefact CLJS-only.
- `tools/testbed-support/deps.edn` and its `.clj` endpoint suite landed 2026-06-15, but the root alias never adopted them. The per-tool lane runs 32 tests.
- The changed-surface classifier explicitly records both root build coordinators as having no CI consumer; therefore a root aggregate false-green cannot be caught by the per-tool required jobs.
- All-status `bd search` by `tools-root aggregate`, `JVM aggregate machines-viz`, `testbed-support aggregate`, `every JVM-runnable tool`, and `root tools test alias`, plus direct tracker search, found no existing bead owning this outcome.

## Impact

A developer using the advertised single-command sanity check can get green while skipping active JVM-only contracts. CI remains protected by per-tool jobs, which makes the alternate root command's narrower result especially easy to mistake for equivalent coverage.

## Recommendation

Prefer retiring the duplicated root `:test` aggregate and point the root README at the already-complete `scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh` roster. If the convenience alias is retained, derive or ratchet its directory/dependency inventory against the canonical roster (with explicit, tested exemptions for non-composable entries) instead of maintaining another hand-written list. Remove the obsolete machines-viz CLJS-only rationale either way.

## Risks / contracts

Preserve per-artefact `clojure -M:test` commands, required CI jobs, template's JVM-only resource isolation, and the dedicated CLJS lanes. Do not flatten tools into one release/classpath contract merely to preserve this convenience command.
acceptance_criteria:
- The documented tool-tier JVM command either routes to the canonical `scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh` roster or has an automated parity check against it.
- Machines-viz's JVM-only suites, testbed-support's JVM suite, and wire-vocab are not silently omitted from a command described as covering every JVM-runnable tool; any deliberate exclusion is named and mechanically held.
- A negative-control test that removes/adds a roster entry makes the parity guard fail.
- Existing per-tool JVM/CLJS CI lanes and template placeholder isolation remain green.
- Root README and `tools/deps.edn` comments no longer promise broader coverage than the command executes.
close_reason: PR #9093: RETIRED, not ratcheted. The aggregate :test alias is removed from tools/deps.edn and tools/README.md now points at scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh, which satisfies acceptance clause 1 by the routing branch (so the parity-guard and negative-control clauses do not apply). title: Clarify private locals in reply egress projection conformance
description:
## Finding
The egress projection conformance suite uses terse private helper and loop bindings whose roles are needlessly opaque during review.

## Evidence
implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_egress_projection_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:109-130 uses [v] in redacted? and large-marker?, and [[k v]] in tree-contains?; lines 299-315 uses [p] for each egress profile and [out] for the projected result; lines 317-338 repeat the out binding. These are test-private lexical names, not exported vocabulary.

## Impact
A reviewer must infer value/map-key/map-value/profile/projected-result roles while validating privacy and projection assertions. This increases ambiguity cost without adding test coverage.

## Recommendation
Rename only the private lexical bindings to role-revealing names (value, map-key, map-value, profile, projected-result or equivalent) and update their local references. Preserve every test name, input/output key, sentinel, payload, profile keyword, assertion, and control flow.

## Compatibility and exclusions
No public API, namespace, file, operation keyword, wire/storage key, or behavior change. Do not alter the projection semantics or the existing rf2-6r9j.88/.90/.91 work: descriptor metadata, matrix gating, stale inventory/path references, and any docs outside this bounded surface are explicitly excluded.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Every identified terse binding in lines 109-130 and 299-338 is renamed to a semantically clear role with no missed local reference.
2. The rendered test forms and assertion counts remain unchanged; no test names, keys, sentinels, or profile values change.
3. Focused CLJS/JVM test and lint gates pass, and git diff --check is clean.

title: Prune retired root-verb metadata from the API.md parser
description:
Evidence

- section-heading-namespace, namespace-shaped?, heading-level, and the parser's section-ns/section-ns-level state exist solely to populate the ignored :section-ns field. - documented-kind exists solely to populate ignored :doc-kind. The var marker still has a live purpose—classifying API table rows—so marker recognition must remain, but retaining each marker's manifest kind no longer affects a verdict.
- This machinery supported the retired two-sided re-frame.ui root-verb kind/attribution guard. UI retirement commit ef3131f4a2 removed that guard but deliberately left parser tests.

The checker parses and tests namespace/kind facts that cannot change any gate verdict. Stale fixtures claim removed API.md headings are live and substantially enlarge a critical policy test without protecting current behavior.

Recommendation
Stop emitting ignored :doc-kind/:section-ns metadata; remove the heading-attribution machinery, retired guard-only fixtures/tests, and kondo-proven dead bindings. Simplify the kind-marker representation only as far as needed for active row recognition.

title: Remove unnecessary re-frame adapter boot from the machines-viz viewer
description:
Evidence
- page/.../viewer.cljs calls rf/init! reagent-adapter/adapter, then mounts viewer-view directly with reagent.dom.client/create-root and render. It registers no frame, event, subscription, or re-frame view.
- MachineChart is a Reagent component and does not consult re-frame.core or the installed substrate adapter. The chart DOM suite independently mounts that same component through adapters.react-chart/chart-element plus raw react-dom/client createRoot without rf/init!, proving adapter boot is not a rendering prerequisite.
- The only machines-viz require/use of re-frame.adapter.reagent is this viewer. The :cljs-test alias carries day8/re-frame2-reagent solely to compile it.
- rf/init! installs a framework substrate and reseeds framework registrations; it does not initialise Reagent rendering. The viewer's direct Reagent root already does that.
- The mistaken rationale dates to initial viewer commit 9644e0b4d8 and now drives lengthy coupling commentary across viewer.cljs, deps.edn, README.md, and API.md.

Impact
A presentation-only static viewer performs unrelated framework-global boot, loads an adapter dependency, and documents a false requirement. This increases bundle/classpath coupling and makes embedding/reusing the page more stateful than its no-runtime contract promises.

Recommendation
Remove the re-frame.core and re-frame.adapter.reagent requires and the rf/init! call from viewer/run; remove day8/re-frame2-reagent from :cljs-test; update the affected docs to say the page mounts Reagent directly. Keep viewer.cljs in page/ because it remains an application entry and non-jar delivery surface.

Risks and contracts
Do not remove the main day8/re-frame2 dependency: library namespaces still use re-frame.error, trace, and interop. Preserve the exported run symbol, URL decoding, DOM output, read-only behavior, page/source-root split, and staged viewer artifact.
acceptance_criteria:
- viewer/run mounts with reagent.dom.client only and has no re-frame adapter/core boot call.
- No machines-viz dependency alias declares day8/re-frame2-reagent solely for the viewer.
- Viewer and dependency documentation no longer claims Reagent rendering requires rf/init!.
- page/ remains excluded from the published jar and included in the viewer build/test classpath.
- Viewer unit/DOM tests and npm run build:machines-viz-viewer pass; the staged HTML finds a callable exported run and renders valid share URLs.

title: Enroll published Hicasso in the implementation root coordinator
description:
## Finding

The root Clojure coordinator did not follow Hicasso's transition to a published artefact. `implementation/deps.edn` says its top-level `:deps` pulls every artefact onto one classpath, but the map has no `day8/re-frame2-hicasso {:local/root "hicasso"}`. Its `:test` alias nevertheless adds `hicasso/test`, leaving the tests on a classpath that lacks `hicasso/src` (and the supported kit root `hicasso/test_kit/src`). `implementation/README.md:46` repeats the every-artefact claim, while lines 165-166 still call Hicasso pre-publication with no `:clein` deploy alias. The same inventory also still says core depends on Reagent at line 52, although commit d44c4f7d20 moved that dependency to the Reagent adapter.

## Evidence

`clojure -Spath -M:test` from `implementation/` exits 0 and lists `hicasso/test`, but contains no `implementation/hicasso/src` or `hicasso/test_kit/src`; it does list every other published artefact's source root. `implementation/hicasso/deps.edn` has declared `day8/re-frame2-hicasso` under `:clein/build` since commit f35ba5d13e (2026-08-15), and `.github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh` plus `.github/workflows/release.yml` both enumerate and deploy it. `hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/slot_cljs_test.cljc` directly requires `re-frame.hicasso.impl.slot`, demonstrating that a test-only path is not a self-contained substitute for the missing source root. The shadow coordinator is not affected: its explicit source-path list already includes `hicasso/src`, `hicasso/test`, and both test-kit roots.

## Impact

The advertised aggregate classpath is incomplete specifically for a shipped artefact; ad-hoc root REPL/test selection cannot load the Hicasso implementation through this coordinator even though its test path is present. The root inventory also tells maintainers obsolete publication and core-dependency facts, making future classpath/release reviews unreliable.

## Recommendation

Add the Hicasso local-root dependency to the root coordinator and make the aggregate test alias match the Hicasso artefact's intentional test roots (including the supported test kit where the aggregate promises the full CLJS test classpath). Refresh the adjacent `implementation/README.md` inventory: Hicasso is published, and core's production deps are Clojure + ClojureScript, not Reagent.

## Risks and contracts

Do not add Hicasso to core or to an adapter artefact, change its published dependency DAG, publish the test kit as a second coordinate, or alter shadow's already-correct explicit source paths. Preserve Hicasso's optional-by-reachability bundle contract and post-matrix release ordering.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `implementation/deps.edn` names `day8/re-frame2-hicasso` as a root `:local/root` dependency and the aggregate test classpath exposes every Hicasso root it claims to support.
2. A read-only classpath probe from `implementation/` includes `implementation/hicasso/src` (and the test-kit source root if `hicasso/test` remains part of the aggregate test surface).
3. `implementation/README.md` no longer calls Hicasso pre-publication or claims core has a production Reagent dependency; its every-artefact coordinator claim agrees with the live map.
4. Existing shadow builds, Hicasso publish/release metadata, optional-module reachability, and bundle-isolation behavior remain unchanged and relevant coordinator/doc gates pass.
close_reason: PR #9096 (head 5918c4f52b). All four acceptance criteria met. (1) implementation/deps.edn now names day8/re-frame2-hicasso {:local/root "hicasso"} in the root :deps and lists it in the header published-artefact inventory; the :test alias adds hicasso/test_kit/src beside the hicasso/test it already carried — that root is deliberately off the artefact's :paths (rf2-hic-020) so the :local/root dep cannot carry it, and Hicasso's own :test alias names it as an :extra-path. (2) Read-only probe: clojure -Spath -M:test from implementation/ exits 0 and now lists implementation/hicasso/src, implementation/hicasso/resources and hicasso/test_kit/src; a load probe of re-frame.hicasso.impl.slot plus re-frame.hicasso.slot-cljs-test off that classpath exits 0, which is the failure the bead described. (3) implementation/README.md's hicasso row no longer says pre-publication/no :clein deploy aliases — it names the ../core + ../ssr deps and the :clein + :clein/build aliases, published as day8/re-frame2-hicasso since rf2-gra70 — and the core row no longer lists reagent (core/deps.edn names only org.clojure/clojure and org.clojure/clojurescript; d44c4f7d20 moved Reagent to the adapter). The every-artefact coordinator claim is now true rather than reworded. (4) Shadow untouched: implementation/shadow-cljs.edn enumerates its own :source-paths, has no :deps true, and does not read this map — it already listed hicasso/src, hicasso/test and both test-kit roots. No change to the published dependency DAG, no second coordinate for the test kit, no adapter/core dep added. Gates: check_readme_inventories.py exit 0, check_adapter_disposition.py exit 0, check_readme_links.py --ci exit 0, check_jvm_lane_rosters.py exit 0 (31 rostered artefacts), check_test_lane_bijection.py exit 0 (1547 files / 45 lanes). Note for reviewers: the README rows edited sit inside the fenced layout block, which neither link gate inspects, so column alignment (description column 29) was checked by hand.

title: Reconcile Machines-Viz design rationale with the shipped architecture
description:

title: Make reply completion-time pair coverage exhaustive
description:
## Finding

The non-success completion-time matrix checks a pair only when at least one of its `*-with-time` / `*-no-time` builders exists. If both keys are deleted or misspelled, `:when (or with-builder no-builder)` silently removes that family/situation from both the primary propagation/omission test and its adversarial controls. `time-pair-exclusions` is a separate manually maintained vector, but no test proves that every omitted pair has an explicit exclusion.

## Evidence

- `implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:428-460` defines the three pair axes and the three deliberate exclusions.
- Lines 616-649 assert that a half-pair is invalid, but the `:when (or with-builder no-builder)` filter means a zero-pair is invisible.
- Lines 847-871 repeat the same declared-pairs-only traversal for the drop/nil-fill controls.
- Lines 651-665 validate entries already present in `time-pair-exclusions`; they do not establish completeness or exclusivity against the supported `:error`, `:cancel`, and `:stale` builders in `families`.
- Concrete false-green: delete both `:error-with-time` and `:error-no-time` from the HTTP descriptor. HTTP still has its ordinary `:error` builder, all envelope/status/work-id validations still run, and the completion-time pair plus controls silently skip HTTP error. No exclusion is required or reported.
- The current JVM tier passes 27 tests / 533 assertions. The issue is structural non-vacuity under matrix drift, not a present production failure.

## Impact

A future descriptor refactor can remove an entire completion-time obligation while keeping the suite green. That reopens the exact umbrella gap this tier exists to close: a family can stop proving that a supplied causal completion timestamp propagates and an absent timestamp is omitted.

## Recommendation

Add an executable partition/bijection check over every supported non-success family/situation: it must declare exactly one of (a) a complete with-time/no-time pair or (b) one explicit exclusion with a reason. Unsupported baseline situations should declare neither. Reuse that validated partition to drive the primary and adversarial tests, avoiding independent skip logic.

## Risks and contracts

Do not impose `:completed-at` on terminals whose production builder deliberately does not accept or durably use it (HTTP stale, machine cancel, timer cancel). Preserve unsupported route/timer error/cancel distinctions. This is a test-matrix completeness fix, not a production timestamp policy change.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every supported `:error`, `:cancel`, or `:stale` row is classified as either a complete time pair or one explicit exclusion.
2. A family/situation with neither classification fails with a diagnostic naming the family and situation.
3. A half-pair, duplicate pair-plus-exclusion, duplicate exclusion, or exclusion for an unsupported situation fails.
4. A focused mutation proves deleting both keys from one currently paired row makes the suite red.
5. Existing propagation, omission, reply validation, and drop/nil-fill controls remain green in JVM and consolidated CLJS lanes.
close_reason:
PR #9095 (head e99777468d). Premise HELD: ':when (or with-builder no-builder)' made a family/situation row with BOTH pair keys deleted invisible to the propagation/omission gate AND to its drop/nil-fill controls, with no exclusion required and no diagnostic emitted, and time-pair-exclusions had no completeness or exclusivity check against it.

Criteria 1-3 are that classifier. Criterion 5's reuse requirement is met by paired-rows / time-paired-rows: completion-time-propagates-and-omits-across-nonsuccess-terminals and nonsuccess-completion-time-gate-fails-closed-on-drop-and-nil-fill now BOTH drive off the validated partition instead of their own independent skip logic, so a row can never be in one and absent from the other.

Criterion 4 proved by mutation: deleting :error-with-time AND :error-no-time from the HTTP descriptor (the bead's own worked example) exits 1 with the partition naming ':http / :error is a SUPPORTED terminal with neither a complete pair nor an explicit exclusion' plus the arithmetic failure '18 cells vs 11 paired + 3 excluded + 3 unsupported'. The exclusions were already correct and none was added or removed; no production timestamp policy changed, and the HTTP-stale / machine-cancel / timer-cancel exclusions are untouched.
