title: Make reply work-id descriptor metadata fail closed
description:
## Finding

`every-work-id-is-a-comparable-edn-tuple` says every family descriptor supplies `:work-head` and that missing identity metadata fails explicitly, but its comprehension uses `:when (and builder work-head)`. A missing or accidentally renamed `:work-head` therefore removes every supported situation for that family from the work-id gate. The explicit `wid` presence, vector, expected-head, and EDN round-trip assertions never execute.

## Evidence

- `implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:489-505` contains the fail-closed claim and the `work-head` skip.
- All six current descriptors at lines 315-421 carry `:work-head`; it is not an optional field. The only legitimate filter is the situation builder, because `:error`/`:cancel` can be unsupported.
- `:work-head` has no other executable consumer in the repository. Removing it from a descriptor leaves the other vocabulary/status tests green; this work-id test silently omits that family's rows.
- History confirms the mismatch is accidental residue. Commit `55c28a5558` removed the old `wid` skip specifically to make the gate fail closed and stated every descriptor has a non-nil `:work-head`, but retained the older `work-head` guard. Later commit `5806d23efe` simplified the comment to “Missing ids fail explicitly” without changing the guard.
- The current JVM tier is healthy (`clojure -M:test`: 27 tests, 533 assertions), so this is a mutation false-green rather than an existing runtime failure.

## Impact

A future family-row edit can drop or misspell the expected work-id head and silently lose the tuple/head/EDN checks for that family. That defeats the cross-family conformance tier at exactly the metadata boundary it claims to lock.

## Recommendation

Filter only on `builder`. Assert that `work-head` is present before comparing it to `(first wid)`, or validate required descriptor metadata once for every family and then run the situation matrix. Add a mutation/non-vacuity control demonstrating that a descriptor without `:work-head` makes the gate red.

## Risks and contracts

Preserve optional situation builders: route and timer legitimately omit some error/cancel paths. Do not make `:error` or `:cancel` universal. This change is test-only and must not alter reply builders or the public reply vocabulary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every descriptor with a supported situation is exercised even when `:work-head` is nil or absent.
2. Missing `:work-head` produces an explicit, family-labelled failure rather than zero assertions.
3. Existing work-id presence, vector, head, and EDN-round-trip checks remain for all current supported family/situation rows.
4. A focused mutation/control proves deleting one descriptor's `:work-head` makes the suite fail.
5. Both JVM and consolidated CLJS reply-conformance lanes remain green after restoring the real matrix.
close_reason:
PR #9095 (head e99777468d). Premise HELD and was measured before the fix: deleting :work-head from the :http descriptor left the reply-conformance suite GREEN at exit 0 with 517 assertions instead of 533 — 16 assertions silently skipped by the ':when (and builder work-head)' filter, nothing on screen.

Fixed test-only, in implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc. The filter is now the situation builder ALONE (:error / :cancel stay legitimately optional for route and timer); a new family-level assertion requires :work-head to be a keyword; and work-id-head-matches? is a SHARED predicate the primary gate asserts TRUE and the new control work-id-gate-fails-closed-on-missing-descriptor-metadata asserts FALSE, so weakening it reddens one side or the other. work-id-rows makes the row set an explicit value, and the control pins that deleting :work-head does NOT reduce the visited row count — the silent-skip axis, which the value-only check would have missed.

Criterion 4 proved by mutation AFTER the fix: the same :work-head deletion now exits 1 with 556 assertions still running (five failures, family-labelled), where before it exited 0 with 16 fewer. Acceptance criteria 1-4 met; 5 (JVM lane) green at 30 tests / 556 assertions, up from 27 / 533. The CLJS lane was not run locally (no implementation/node_modules in the worker checkout) — the change is portable .cljc and CI owns that lane.

title: adapters/reagent: linearlite_example_cljs_test is green only because a co-loaded sibling owns "/" (false green; 16/51 red in a single-app bundle)
description:
FOUND 2026-09-02 by the rf2-ma8r diagnosis (PR #9000, closed no-change).

re-frame.linearlite-example-cljs-test passes in the consolidated :node-test
bundle for a reason unrelated to its own subject, and fails 16 of 51 assertions
across 7 of 10 tests the moment it runs in a bundle where the LinearLite app is
the only app.

MECHANISM. Its init! calls (rf/make-frame {:id :rf/default :url-bound? true})
BEFORE reinstating the :resource/:mutation registrar rows the shared fixture's
reset hook cleared. A :url-bound? frame performs a synchronous initial URL sync
at construction (frame/upsert-frame! post-create hook -> routing's
:routing/on-frame-registered! -> reconcile-url-listener!, syncing
history/current-url, which is "/" under Node). The example registers
:linearlite.app/board at "/" with :resources [{:resource :linearlite/board
:blocking? true}], so the route-entry resource plan runs INSIDE make-frame,
finds the registrar empty, and records :transition :error /
:rf.error/resource-route-plan on the slice. The suite's own navigate never
re-plans, so the error is sticky and 16 assertions read nil.

WHY IT PASSES IN-REPO. At least seven in-tree apps register a route at "/"
(infinite_feed, linearlite, resources, routing, todomvc, realworld_http,
realworld_resources), plus many test suites. In the consolidated bundle "/"
resolves to a SIBLING's route, so LinearLite's board resource is never planned
at construction and the explicit navigate is a genuine transition with
everything registered. The suite's colour therefore depends on which siblings
happen to be co-loaded — it is not evidence about its own subject, and it would
flip red on an unrelated co-load change.

MEASURED. Workspace built per docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/workspace.md
on the :local/root route: committed baseline exit 0 (10 tests / 51 assertions);
adapter suite verbatim exit 1, 16 failures; changing ONLY the example's route
path from "/" to "/board" -> exit 0, 0 failures.

FIX SHAPE (one line, but NOT dispatched here — the file is inside a live peer's
fence, worker/clientroot-k5r9t owns implementation/adapters/reagent/**):
reorder init! so the registrar/register! reinstatement loop runs BEFORE
(rf/make-frame {:id :rf/default :url-bound? true}), matching the committed
pilot baseline's ordering. That removes the masking dependence entirely.

RELATED. rf2-ma8r carries the full diagnosis and stays open for Mike's ruling
on the two framework questions this exposed: whether a :url-bound? frame
planning route resources at construction is correct, and whether a FAILED route
plan should ever be retried (today an app that recovers stays wedged in
:transition :error permanently).

WORTH A SWEEP: whether any OTHER in-repo example suite is green only by the
same co-load masking. The "/" census above is where to start; the cheap test
is to build each app's suite in a single-app bundle.
notes:
FENCE 2026-09-02 20:41:11 AUSEST (mayor): filed by the rf2-ma8r worker. Its one-line repair (reinstate the registrar rows BEFORE the :url-bound? make-frame) sits in implementation/adapters/reagent/**, which worker/clientroot-k5r9t holds. Dispatch after that PR merges. NOTE WHAT THIS BEAD IS: not a flaky test but a FALSE GREEN — the suite passes in-repo only because a co-loaded sibling owns the "/" route, so its colour is not evidence about its own subject. The worker's residual question is worth carrying into the dispatch: no other in-repo example suite has been swept for the same co-load masking, and the cheap test is one single-app bundle per app.
FENCE STRUCK 2026-09-02 22:52:40 AUSEST (mayor): the 20:41 fence is DISCHARGED — worker/clientroot-k5r9t's PR #8992 MERGED at cd6fd08587 (53 files, the adapter client root plus the examples sweep), so implementation/adapters/reagent/** is held by nobody. Dispatched solo this tick.

RE-DERIVE BEFORE EDITING: #8992 changed this very adapter — it added public client-root / render! / unmount! on re-frame.adapter.reagent and reagent-slim, regenerated the api manifest 491->494, and rewrote 24 example entrypoints plus 3 SSR examples to mount through the adapter's client root. The example whose route path this bead discusses is among the files it touched. Every line number here predates it.
RESOLVED 2026-09-03 by PR #9027 (head 051f8976a7, base c06b76dc36).

REPRODUCED FIRST, on a tree that had moved past PR #8992. The bead's mechanism
held verbatim at tip: init! still created the :url-bound? frame before the
registrar/register! reinstatement loop. Built in a single-app :node-test bundle
(ns-regexp anchored to this suite alone), the committed tree gave
"Ran 10 tests containing 51 assertions. 16 failures, 0 errors.", captured
exit 1 — the bead's 16-of-51 across 7-of-10 exactly. After the fix, same bundle:
"Ran 10 tests containing 51 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.", captured exit 0.
That red-then-green pair is the control; it is also what proves the instrument
was reading the worker's own worktree.

WHICH REPAIR. The bead's FIX SHAPE section rules for reordering init! so the
registrar reinstatement runs BEFORE the :url-bound? make-frame, matching the
committed pilot baseline. That is what landed, and it is the right call: the
alternative one-liner the bead records under MEASURED — moving the example's
route off "/" — also goes green, but only by dodging the collision, leaving the
ordering bug intact and the suite still dependent on nobody else owning "/".
Followed the baseline's stricter form (make-frame LAST, after the fx stubs and
install-routing-integration! too, not merely after the doseq), since the baseline
is what the bead nominates and it documents the rule as "the frame is made last".
The ordering constraint and its cause are now in the init! docstring so a future
edit cannot silently undo it.

SECOND DEFECT, found by the sweep and fixed in the same PR.
re-frame.resources-example-cljs-test was green by the same disease through a
different organ: examples/capabilities/resources/resources/core.cljs calls
rf/reg-machine :resources.app/reader but required neither re-frame.machines nor
anything pulling it in. Machines are an optional artefact, so the call resolves
only when a co-loaded sibling has already loaded it. Alone, the example's ns-load
throws :rf.error/machines-artefact-missing before a single test runs (captured
exit 1, 0 tests). Every other example calling reg-machine already requires
re-frame.machines in the same file; this was the sole omission. After: 9 tests /
39 assertions, 0 failures.

CO-LOAD SWEEP — the bead's residual question, answered. Fifteen example suites
each built in their own single-app bundle: 155 tests / 1180 assertions, all green
on the final base. All SEVEN apps registering a route at "/" are covered
(infinite_feed, linearlite, realworld_http, realworld_resources, resources,
routing, todomvc). A census of every reg-route form under examples/
(paren-balanced over flattened text, control-checked first) shows LinearLite is
the ONLY app with a BLOCKING route resource at "/", which is exactly why it was
the only hard failure of that mechanism.

NOT COVERED, named rather than left open: the ~11,000-test framework remainder of
the :node-test lane was not swept for co-load masking among framework suites, and
re-frame.example-frame-scoping-cljs-test is excluded by construction (it loads
seven apps deliberately; cross-app scoping is its subject). Three suites share
the make-frame-before-register! ordering and are green only because their "/"
routes declare no blocking resource — infinite_feed_example,
realworld_resources, resources_example. Latent rather than broken; carried by
rf2-djqm rather than churned here.

METHOD NOTE for the next person building a single-app bundle. Narrowing
:ns-regexp against the shared :node-test id is what rf2-6t03c forbids doing
directly, so go through scripts/compile-node-test.cjs's cache-isolation helper
(core/test/re_frame/bench/lane_cache.cjs). But that script clears the build cache
AFTER compiling, and a dev-target :node-test bundle SHADOW_IMPORTs its modules
from that same directory at RUN time — so running the bundle after the script
exits dies with ENOENT on goog.debug.error.js before any test executes. The run
must happen inside the isolated window: clear -> compile -> RUN -> clear.
Runtime selection (node out/node-test.js --test=<ns>) does NOT substitute: it
filters which tests RUN while leaving every sibling namespace LOADED, which is
precisely the co-load this bead is about.

STILL OPEN AND NOT ADDRESSED HERE: rf2-ma8r's two framework questions — whether a
:url-bound? frame planning route resources AT CONSTRUCTION is correct, and
whether a FAILED route plan should ever be retried (an app that recovers stays
wedged in :transition :error permanently). This fix removes the masking; it does
not answer either question.
AUDIT PR #9027: REOPENED FOR COMPLETENESS. Both repairs are source-correct, and the isolated red/green probes are persuasive, but neither repair has a durable non-vacuous gate. This matters because the PR proves the ordinary consolidated :node-test bundle was green before both fixes: a sibling route masked LinearLite's make-frame ordering, and a sibling namespace loaded re-frame.machines for the resources example. The committed diff changes only those two subjects. The fifteen single-app builds were one-off audit evidence, not a checked-in regression instrument; test:cljs-isolation also runs selectors against the already consolidated bundle and therefore cannot remove ns-load co-loading. Moving make-frame back up or deleting the new machines require can consequently leave current CI green again.

Minimal completion: add one focused, durable bundle-isolation control covering the two fixed subjects. It must compile/load each subject without sibling example namespaces, go red on the pre-fix LinearLite ordering and missing machines require, and stay cheap enough for the existing example/adapter lane; do not institutionalise the full fifteen-build sweep. Keep the three merely latent fixture orderings on rf2-djqm and the route-retry ruling on rf2-ma8r.
AUDIT COMPLETION LANDED 2026-09-03 by PR #9066 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9066), branch worker/isolation-a, merge base 4893d007b6.

PREMISE VERIFIED FIRST, not taken from the audit. Reproduced the exact pre-#9027 tree
(the resources plant restores blob 5e0060754f, byte-identical to the 'index
5e0060754f..132a287c1e' the PR's own diff header records) and ran both subject suites in
the ordinary consolidated :node-test bundle. At tip: 'Ran 19 tests containing 90
assertions. 0 failures', captured exit 0. With BOTH pre-fix states restored: identical
numbers, captured exit 0. The audit's central claim holds.

THE AUDIT ASKED FOR ONE CONTROL; IT NEEDS TWO, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. The two repairs
are different KINDS of fact and no single instrument reaches both. The LinearLite repair
is an ordering inside an adapter test fixture -- it never enters any app bundle, so no
bundle grep can see it and only executing it under the isolated condition can. The
resources repair is a missing :require in an example ns form -- invisible at runtime in
any bundle that carries re-frame.machines for another reason, which is precisely the
co-load being ruled out, so only a single-app build or the ns form itself can witness it.
Neither control builds a second bundle; together they cost milliseconds plus one
in-process test. The fifteen-build sweep is NOT institutionalised.

CONTROL A -- LinearLite ordering, behavioural, in the suite it protects
(implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/linearlite_example_cljs_test.cljs section
0). Reproduces IN PROCESS the two conditions a single-app bundle supplies: '/' owned by
this app's board route alone (every rival row sequestered through the provenance-safe
sequester/reinstate pairing the suite already uses for :rf.route/not-found, restored in a
finally), and the :resource/:mutation kinds cleared. Then runs the REAL init! against a
cleared frame registry so make-frame genuinely constructs and its post-create URL sync
really runs. Calling init! itself rather than a copy is the point: a refactor that puts
the frame back in front of the registrar reinstatement BY ANY ROUTE fails there. Chosen
over a source-order text check deliberately -- a text check on a moving target degrades
to a vacuous pass, which is the failure mode this gate's own positive-control section
exists to prevent. Its FIRST assertion is its own positive control: if the sequestering
silently stops working the URL sync lands on a sibling's route id and it fails loud.

CONTROL B -- the resources machines require, an ns-form co-load rule added to
implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs. Rule: an example that CALLS an
optional artefact's registration facade must :require that artefact in its OWN ns form,
because the :require -- not the Maven dep, and not a sibling's require -- is what fires
the load-time hook registrations. Read on SOURCE deliberately, and the code says why: the
roster comment's insist-on-the-emitted-artefact rule governs claims about a bundle's
CONTENTS, while this claim is about an ns FORM, whose only possible bundle witness is the
single-app build the audit ruled out on cost. Seven facade rows (reg-machine, defmachine,
reg-route, reg-resource, reg-mutation, reg-flow, reg-app-schema) over 83 example sources:
111 call sites, each backed by its own :require, zero violations at tip. NON-VACUITY IS
BUILT INTO THE CONTRACT rather than left to a one-off plant -- a facade row that finds no
call site anywhere, or an ns reader that stops seeing requires, fails the gate; both are
exercised as mutations in check-bundle-isolation.test.cjs, which the lane already runs
FIRST, so the rule is re-proven on every CI run rather than once by me.

TWO PLANTED REDS, one per subject, blob-hash-verified restores.
(1) make-frame moved back above the registrar/register! loop: 'expected (not= :error
(:transition slice)) / actual (not (not= :error :error))' and 'expected (nil?
(:rf.error/id (:error slice))) / actual (not (nil? :rf.error/resource-route-plan))' --
exactly the bead's mechanism -- 'Ran 11 tests containing 54 assertions. 2 failures',
captured exit 1, and THE OTHER TEN TESTS STAYED GREEN, which is the false green
demonstrated directly. The positive control passed on that same run, so the setup was
real. Restored: the init! region hashes 88481e756e38c8867d6a6e186668342571b5a9d4 on both
sides and the whole-file diff is 86 additions / 0 deletions.
(2) [re-frame.machines] deleted from examples/capabilities/resources/resources/core.cljs
(blob 5e0060754f): ok=false naming the file, the call, the artefact and
rf.error/machines-artefact-missing, hits=1 and no collateral. hits=1 rather than 2 is
itself evidence the comment stripper works, since that file names rf/reg-machine in a
comment two lines above the real call. Restored to blob 132a287c1e.
BOTH REDS RE-PROVEN ON THE FINAL BASE after the rebase, since the incoming commits
touched implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc, which control A exercises.

TWO THINGS THE BUILD ITSELF CAUGHT, recorded because each is the shape that fails open.
The new self-test caught a real defect in my own checker mid-build: a facade named inside
a STRING -- (def doc "call (rf/reg-flow ...)") -- counted as a call site. Fixed in the
checker (string bodies are now blanked, not just comments) rather than by relaxing the
fixture. And one plant SILENTLY NO-OPED: a perl -0pi patch left the blob hash unchanged
(CRLF) while reporting success, and the hash check caught it before a run was spent on a
green that would have read as 'the control does not bite'.

GATES, all foreground, unfiltered, exit codes captured, ALL RE-MEASURED ON THE FINAL BASE
4893d007b6: npm run test:bundle-isolation exit 0 (23 artefacts, 40 internal sentinels
absent / 40 positive-control present, 83 example sources co-load isolated, 111 facade
call sites); gate self-test exit 0 (40 sentinel mutations + 11 new co-load mutations);
reagent adapter suite 458 tests/2459 assertions BEFORE and 459/2462 AFTER, both exit 0,
delta exactly the one control; sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 with the full CLJS suite
at 11206 tests / 55823 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors -- which is what proves the
control leaves no registrar or trace residue for the other ~11k tests in the bundle;
check_doc_slugs.py, check_readme_links.py --ci and all 15 check_skill_*.py exit 0.
node-test compiled 1893 files with 0 warnings on every run.

SCOPE HELD. The three merely-latent fixture orderings stay on rf2-djqm; the route-retry
ruling stays on rf2-ma8r. Neither widened. Nothing weakened or deleted to reach green.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9066 — REOPENED. The new example co-load gate misclassifies rf/defmachine as a registration facade. defmachine is the re-frame.core macro for defining and source-stamping a machine-spec value; it registers nothing. Confirmed against the shipped code by requiring re-frame.core alone and macroexpanding a defmachine form: re-frame.machines remained unloaded and the expansion head was plain def. Only the later reg-machine call needs the optional artefact and its load-time hook.

A valid split can therefore define a machine value in one namespace and require re-frame.machines only in the boot namespace that registers it. The new per-file checker rejects that shape and forces an unnecessary side-effecting require into the definition namespace. Its self-test misses the distinction because one fixture contains both defmachine and reg-machine and removes their shared require.

Minimal repair: remove defmachine from OPTIONAL_ARTEFACT_FACADES while retaining reg-machine, and make the self-test distinguish the contracts: a defmachine-only namespace requiring re-frame.core is valid; a reg-machine call without re-frame.machines still fails. No parser or runtime redesign is needed.

VERIFIED THE PREMISE AT SOURCE rather than taking the audit's word: the two expanders settle it directly — expand-reg-machine emits a real (re-frame.core-machines/reg-machine ...) call, which is what needs the artefact's load-time hooks, while expand-defmachine emits (def name <stamped-spec>) and nothing else, its own docstring reading '`def` is not a registration'. So defmachine was misclassified in OPTIONAL_ARTEFACT_FACADES and the gate demanded a [re-frame.machines] require from any namespace merely DEFINING a machine value, forbidding the valid split where the boot ns alone requires the artefact. REPRODUCED FIRST: a defmachine-only fixture against the committed checker returned ok=false naming defmachine/re-frame.machines; after the fix, no violation. NO EXAMPLE WAS AFFECTED — every current defmachine caller also calls reg-machine in the same file, so the defect was LATENT (it forbade a valid shape, it did not break a present one). Live corpus before->after: 83 example sources, 0 violations both ways; facade call sites 111->100, the difference being exactly the 11 defmachine call sites that were never the gate's business; 0 dead rows, 0 unproven artefacts. WHY THE SELF-TEST MISSED IT AND WHAT NOW STOPS IT: the single compliant fixture carried reg-machine and defmachine over ONE shared require, so the drop-one-require loop implicated both rows at once and the contracts were indistinguishable. They now get a namespace each — a defmachine-only ns must PASS, and a reg-machine call in that same ns must still FAIL naming reg-machine ALONE. Restoring the roster row fails the first BY NAME: planted it back, exit 1 on that exact assertion, then restored byte-exact (git hash-object 9478af0fb3 both sides, so the plant was real and not the silent CRLF no-op recorded on the previous PR). Both new fixtures assert on violations rather than ok, deliberately: ok also folds in the corpus-level non-vacuity guards, which a one-file fixture can never satisfy, so !ok in the negative case would have held whatever the rule did and passed for an unrelated reason — the self-test caught exactly that in my own first draft. GATES (foreground, unfiltered, exit codes captured to files): check-bundle-isolation.test.cjs exit 0 with 12 co-load mutations (was 10); planted-red exit 1 / restored exit 0; live assertExampleCoLoadIsolation() exit 0. npm run test:bundle-isolation front-loads a 7-build shadow-cljs release and this worktree has no node_modules, so CI owns that half; the only part of the gate this diff can affect is the co-load rule, run directly against the live corpus.

title: Name derivation conformance synthetic fixture roles explicitly
description:
## Scope

implementation/derivation-conformance/test/re_frame/derivation_algebra_conformance_cljs_test.cljc, limited to private synthetic fixture helpers and private fixture constants/locals.

## Evidence

- Lines 448-518 define a concrete non-route live-composition fixture as k3-nav-token, k3-scoped-key, k3-generation, k3-work-id, and k3-live-contributors. The k3 prefix has no local meaning; each value has a distinct navigation, resource identity, attempt-generation, work-id, or contributor-map role.
- Lines 596-655 use perm-permutations, perm-sub-node, perm-res-key, perm-route, perm-contributors, and perm-expected-edges. perm compresses permutation/canonical-edge semantics across helpers and obscures whether a value is a subject node, resource key, route, contributor assembly, or expected result.
- The ambiguity is material during review: these fixtures pin identity, owner, edge, and serialization invariants, so misreading a helper can lead to changing fixture data rather than only improving names. All helpers/constants are private test-only bindings; no public API, event ID, payload, wire/storage key, or runtime behavior depends on their Var names.

## Compatibility and exclusions

Rename only private Clojure/CLJS test helpers, constants, and local bindings in this suite. Preserve every literal fixture value, map shape, contributor key, edge endpoint, assertion, test discovery namespace, and conformance-fixture intent. Do not touch rf2-6r9j.98 targets (the re-frame.trace require or unused sub-val binding), rf2-6r9j.100 coverage prose, public implementation names, or serialized/protocol vocabulary.

## Acceptance criteria

1. No k3- or perm- private fixture symbol remains in this namespace.
2. Replacement names state the actual role (non-route live composition versus registration-permutation canonical-edge fixture; navigation token, scoped key, generation, work ID, contributors, sub node, resource key, route, expected edges, and permutation generator).
3. A structural comparison confirms only symbol/name tokens changed: all fixture literals and test assertions retain their values and behavior.
4. Focused derivation-conformance JVM and shared CLJS node tests pass with unchanged test/assertion totals; focused lint introduces no naming or unused-binding diagnostics.

title: Clarify private locals in reply vocabulary conformance matrices
description:
## Finding
The reply vocabulary conformance suite uses one-letter or abbreviated private lexical bindings in its EDN helper, family matrix loops, correlation helper, and time-pair loops.

## Evidence
implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:51 defines edn-roundtrip [x]; lines 467, 492, 619, 849, 862 bind family specs as :as f; lines 619-622 and 849-864 bind descriptor keys as with-k/no-k; lines 746-804 bind projected replies as out in correlation helpers and stale-row loops. These names are lexical only and do not alter vocabulary keys.

## Impact
The suite has a large cross-product of reply families and situations. Abbreviated bindings make it harder to distinguish family descriptors, key names, and projected outcomes while reviewing conformance failures, increasing maintenance and review ambiguity.

## Recommendation
Rename only lexical bindings to role-revealing names (value, family-spec, with-key/no-key, outcome or equivalent), updating local references mechanically. Keep all descriptor map keys, test names, statuses, payloads, and control-flow predicates byte-for-byte semantic equivalents.

## Compatibility and exclusions
No public API, namespace, file, operation keyword, wire/storage key, or behavior change. Do not change the matrix predicates or coverage owned by rf2-6r9j.88/.90, nor stale descriptor/inventory/path targets owned by rf2-6r9j.91 (including :error-work-status and the phantom filename); docs and files outside this bounded surface are excluded.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. All identified abbreviated locals at lines 51, 467, 492, 619-622, 746-804, and 849-864 are renamed consistently with no missed references.
2. Matrix cardinality, predicate semantics, test names, reply keys, statuses, and assertion counts remain unchanged.
3. Focused CLJS/JVM test and lint gates pass, and git diff --check is clean.
notes: Detailed scope: exact evidence is implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc lines 51 ([x] in edn-roundtrip), 467 and 492 (:as f family descriptor aliases), 619-622 (with-k/no-k descriptor key locals), 746-804 (out projected outcome helper/control locals), and 849-864 (with-k/no-k time-pair controls). Ambiguity cost is reviewer inference across a large family x situation matrix. Rename lexical bindings only to value, family-spec, with-key/no-key, outcome; preserve all descriptor map keys, test names, statuses, payloads, predicates, cardinality, and assertion counts. Explicitly exclude semantic matrix predicates and coverage in rf2-6r9j.88/.90 and stale :error-work-status, phantom filename, inventory/docs targets in rf2-6r9j.91. Acceptance is a lexical-only diff, no public/wire/storage change, green focused CLJS/JVM/kondo and git diff --check.

title: Remove retired CSP/SSR remnants from the template browser proof
description:
## Evidence

The emitted browser driver still describes and diagnoses the retired CSP/SSR scaffold. tools/template/test-support/dev-page-boot-proof.cjs says the emitted index.html carries a Content-Security-Policy meta tag, contrasts itself with a synthetic SSR page, and has two diagnose() branches dedicated to CSP refusal and unsafe-eval errors. The current root/resources/public/index.html has no CSP. template_test.clj explicitly bans the Content-Security-Policy string, and skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/setup_drift_test.clj locks the default route as CSP-free. The driver server deliberately emits no CSP response header, so those two branches have no policy source in any current positive or mutation run.

The same pre-collapse story remains in .github/workflows/test.yml, .github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml, and .github/workflows/template-release.yml: comments say this tier contains two Chromium proofs including an SSR DOM-adoption proof. The current emitted_test_run_test.clj contains only the generic emitted-page driver, used for Reagent, UIx, the setup-skill leaf, and its mount/click witnesses; no SSR fixture remains.

History shows the CSP and SSR scaffold disappeared in the rf2-zq34m reduction while this driver and CI narrative were not fully reconciled.

## Impact

Dead diagnostic code and false CI descriptions make a generic boot test look like it still validates a retired security/SSR feature. This obscures the actual teeth: mount, live click, package declaration completeness, pageerror cleanliness, and red witnesses.

## Recommendation

Delete the unreachable CSP-only diagnose branches and rewrite the driver plus CI comments around the current SPA proof. Keep the useful missing-bundle diagnostic and all functional proof/witness behavior.

## Risks and contracts

Do not remove browser provisioning, CI-hard browser launch failure, static-server containment, the mount/click/pageerror checks, or either red witness. A future CSP recipe should have its own policy-bearing fixture rather than dormant diagnostics in a CSP-free scaffold.
acceptance_criteria:
- The driver no longer claims the emitted page has a CSP or compares current coverage to a retired SSR fixture.
- CSP-only diagnose branches with no current policy source are removed or are backed by a new reachable fixture; generic resource-load diagnostics remain.
- Template PR, nightly, and release workflow comments describe the current browser runs accurately and no longer claim an SSR DOM-adoption proof.
- Default and enabled behavioural suites retain mount, 0-to-1 click, zero-pageerror, package completeness, launch-verdict, and mutation-witness coverage.

description:

title: story-mcp: truth stale tool inventories after surface contractions
description:

- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/schemas.cljc:297-301` still lists “register / unregister / record” even though `record-as-variant` was retired by `ff0b7c3e02` / rf2-5saz7.
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/wire_pipeline.cljc:219` says three dedup-eligible tools and `spec/Principles.md:271-273` says adding a fourth; the registry, schema helper, dedicated exact-set test, and the same Principles section all pin exactly two: preview and run.
- `tools/story-mcp/test/stdio-roundtrip.js:10` says list-substrates may return an empty vector on JVM, while the test body and runtime contract require capability-unavailable when no provider is reachable.
- Directly coupled consumers retain the same retirement drift: `.github/workflows/test.yml:5432-5434` includes record in the Story agent-loop sequence, and `tools/mcp-base/spec/dedup.md:15` still claims Story-MCP emits recorder replay tuples.

Impact
These inventories are the breadcrumbs maintainers use to update shared argument schemas, exact-set guards, SDK conformance, and wire behavior. Wrong counts and retired operations can send a future change toward nonexistent call sites or reintroduce false-empty/recorder assumptions.

Recommendation
Re-census the current registry and update each stale inventory/header to the live operation names and counts, including directly coupled CI/shared-spec prose. Keep descriptions semantic where possible so another tool removal does not leave ordinal wording behind.

Risks / contracts
Preserve deliberate retirement regression guards: the manifest/registry absence assertions, stdio and SDK method-not-found probes, README retirement note, and normative “not shipped” statements are active contract tests, not vestiges. Do not change runtime behavior or the documented permissive `:dedup` handling on ineligible tools.

title: vestigial(story): retire the inert run-variant render contract
description:
Finding

Story still exposes and internally passes a `run-variant` `:render?` option, and every run result still carries `:rendered-hiccup`, but the option is unread and the result slot is permanently nil. This began as a staged placeholder and is now a retired architecture preserved as an active-looking compatibility contract.

Evidence

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc:68` puts `:rendered-hiccup nil` in `empty-result`; `record-result-map` at lines 686-694 unconditionally writes `:rendered-hiccup nil` with the comment that rendering is performed by the UI shell or `render-variant`; and the `run-variant` docstring at lines 1276-1278 explicitly says rendering is separate and the compatibility slot remains nil.
- Repo-wide source search finds no branch that reads `:render?` to render anything. Nevertheless the live shell passes it at `ui/shell.cljs:312`, `ui/canvas.cljs:432`, and `ui/workspace.cljc:328`; `prepare-run!` advertises it at `runtime.cljc:1376`; and `run_owner_cljc_test.cljc:85` passes it without asserting any rendered result. These calls are inert configuration noise.
- The documented contract claims the opposite: `spec/007-Stories.md:425,432` says `:rendered-hiccup` is populated under `:render? true` and is the screenshot-test input; `tools/story/spec/002-Runtime.md:718-722`, `tools/story/spec/000-Vision.md:114`, `tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md:117,891`, and `docs/story/api/runtime.md:47,98-114` repeat the active-looking option/result shape.
- Story-MCP consumes the impossible slot as if live. `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/testing.cljc:160` and `dev.cljc:170` scrub and return it; tool descriptors promise rendered output; `wire_pipeline.cljc:37,89-90` says it dominates token cost; the MCP spec/docs classify its egress. Tests manufacture non-nil hiccup in stubbed outcome maps, so they prove the scrubber but never prove that a real Story run can produce it.
- Git history proves the retirement path: `fa993fa5e4` (2026-05-11 Stage 3) introduced nil with `Stage 4 fills this in`; no later implementation populated it. `82cd4bd1c8` (2026-07-10) changed runtime prose to say rendering is outside headless orchestration and relabelled the nil as a reserved compatibility slot, while the normative/API/MCP promises remained.
- Bead searches for `rendered-hiccup`, `rendered hiccup`, `run-variant render`, and `compatibility slot` returned no existing issue.

Impact

The public and MCP contracts advertise a screenshot/tooling feature that cannot be reached, callers carry ignored options, and substantial MCP egress/dedup/token-budget prose and tests defend data that Story never emits. A consumer following the API receives nil even when explicitly requesting render. The contradictory authorities also make future work liable to test the stubbed shape rather than the real integration.

Proposed disposition

Retire `:render?` from run/prepare opts and retire `:rendered-hiccup` from the unified run-result. Keep `render-variant` as the single explicit visual-rendering API and rewrite screenshot guidance around its structured `:rendered` result. Remove the inert opts from shell/canvas/workspace. Reconcile normative Story docs, API docs, tests, Story-MCP payload projections/descriptors/specs, dedup hints, and token guidance. If `preview-variant` genuinely needs visual output, have that tool call a supported renderer explicitly and describe its substrate/capability boundary; do not infer rendering from `run-variant` or preserve a permanent nil slot.

Risks

This is a documented result-map field, so downstream destructuring may depend on key presence even though its value is always nil. Treat the removal as an API migration and update compatibility/release notes as policy requires. Story-MCP runs on a headless JVM where render capability may be unavailable; it must return an honest capability refusal/omission rather than synthesize success-shaped hiccup.
acceptance_criteria:
- `run-variant`/`prepare-run!` and shell callers no longer accept or pass the inert `:render?` option, and unified run results no longer carry a permanently nil `:rendered-hiccup` compatibility slot.
- Story normative specs, API docs, examples, and screenshot guidance consistently name `render-variant` (and its actual result shape) as the rendering authority; no text claims `run-variant` populates hiccup.
- Story-MCP run/preview payloads, egress projection, descriptors, dedup/token hints, specs, and tests reflect data reachable from real production calls. Any preview rendering is an explicit renderer call with capability/error coverage.
- An integration test exercises the real Story-to-consumer path so a stubbed non-nil outcome cannot reintroduce the false contract.
- Story JVM/CLJS, shell feature-load/static build, Story-MCP, API/spec drift, and egress tests pass.

title: Correct the private dedup cacheability predicate spelling
description:
## Finding

`tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc` defines the private predicate `cachable?` and invokes it at the cache-counting and dedup traversal sites. The established English term in this artefact and its consumers is “cacheable”; the misspelling makes the predicate harder to search and obscures its role in a codec whose cache-element vocabulary is security-sensitive.

## Evidence

A fixed-symbol search finds exactly one definition and three private call sites in `dedup.cljc`, with no public export, protocol method, serialized key, CLI option, MCP operation, or fixture depending on that spelling. Repository search finds only explanatory comments in `tools/mcp-conformance/lib/dedup-envelope.cjs` and its test, not callable consumers. History shows the predicate entered with the vendored dedup codec and retained the typo through subsequent collision/escaping fixes. The predicate answers whether a form is eligible for pooling, so `cacheable?` is the precise role name.

## Recommendation

Rename only the private predicate and its three in-file calls from `cachable?` to `cacheable?`. Update explanatory comments only if necessary and do not alter conformance contracts. Preserve `de-dupe-eq`, `dedup-value`, cache marker spellings, `cache-element-ns`, marker grammar, map-entry behavior, public namespace/file, and all wire/protocol keys.

## Risks / contracts

This is private source vocabulary and should be behavior-neutral, but dedup marker names and serialized payload shapes are contracts. Do not rename public functions, namespaces, files, MCP operations, JSON/EDN keys, test fixture identifiers, or protocol terms. Exclude Phase-1/vestigial beads rf2-6r9j.104, .105, .65, .19 and active mcp-conformance transport/codec work; those targets are fenced.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `cachable?` is absent from mcp-base source and the private predicate is consistently named `cacheable?`.
2. No public var, marker, key, operation, or behavior changes; a repository diff confirms only private spelling.
3. mcp-base JVM and CLJS suites, pinned clj-kondo, and relevant dedup/conformance checks pass.
4. A planted edited-line syntax/arity fault makes each no-banner focused gate red, then exact source restoration returns both gates green.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 6fb6d39c68: renamed private dedup predicate cachable? to cacheable? and corrected the adjacent prose, preserving all public and wire contracts. JVM 288 tests/998 assertions, CLJS 48/289 assertions, pinned clj-kondo 0 warnings, and dedup conformance 21/21 passed; edited-line fault controls were red and restoration reruns green.

## Finding

The shadow coordinator's executable source-path and build maps match the current concept-grouped examples tree, but several present-tense comments still describe the removed `examples/reagent/<name>` / `examples/<substrate>/<name>` topology.

## Evidence

- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1177-1182` says hand-written examples live under `examples/<substrate>/<name>` and that Playwright specs sit beside each example/7GUIs under `examples/reagent`; the live examples tree is concept-grouped and the source-path inventory at lines 392-419 correctly describes that model.
- Line 1249 points Counter to `examples/reagent/counter/core.cljs`; the live file is `examples/core/counter/core.cljs`.
- Lines 1678 and 1756 describe RealWorld and Linearlite as using `../examples/reagent`; their live roots are `../examples/real-apps` plus capability/resource roots.
- Line 1772 points SSR to sibling `examples/reagent/ssr`; the live root is `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr`.
- Lines 1835/1846 and 1863/1875 point Nine States and Login to old Reagent paths; the live roots are `examples/patterns/nine_states` and `examples/core/login`.
- `Test-Path implementation/examples/reagent` is false, while every configured source path exists. Commit `210f812fe2` performed the concept reorganization.

## Impact

These comments are maintainer-facing documentation embedded in the authoritative build coordinator. They send reviewers and future editors to nonexistent locations and make an otherwise-correct build map look inconsistent.

## Recommendation

Update only the present-tense build comments to name the current concept-grouped roots and current test ownership. Keep the source-path/build data unchanged.

## Risks and contracts

Do not erase intentional archaeology: line 350 explicitly says a path was “formerly under” the old tree and line 1813 says a test was “relocated from” it. Preserve those clearly past-tense references, every build id, compiler option, module dependency, dev server, and source-path entry.

title: Clarify private testbed editor process-stream lifecycle locals
description:
## Finding

The private process/stream lifecycle code in `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server.clj` uses short locals at the concurrency boundary. `drain-stream` (around lines 208-227) binds `sb` for the retained diagnostic builder, `buf` for the read buffer, `cap` for the retained-character limit, `r` for the UTF-8 reader, and `n` for each read count. `launch!` (around lines 254-296) binds `pb` for the process builder, `proc` for the child process, and `err-drain` for the concurrent stderr future. These names are private but sit beside timeout, pipe-draining, and bounded-diagnostic behavior where each value has a distinct lifecycle role.

## Ambiguity cost

A maintainer changing the deadlock/timeout protection must infer whether `cap` bounds the stream or only retained text, whether `n` is bytes or characters, and whether `err-drain` is a stream or a future. The generic builder/process names also obscure which object owns stdout redirection versus stderr draining. That raises the chance of accidentally stopping the drain, changing UTF-8 character accounting, or dereferencing the wrong lifecycle value while preserving green ordinary tests.

## Phase-1 exclusions and compatibility

This is a private/local naming-only slice. Do not rename `launch!`, `drain-stream`, endpoint paths, query flags (`file`, `line`, `column`, `editor`), error tokens, exit codes, JSON keys, editor command vocabulary, public handler vars, test filenames/namespaces, or any Phase-1 vestigial/removal target. Preserve subprocess argv order, stdout/stderr redirection, timeout and termination behavior, UTF-8 decoding, retained diagnostic cap, response bodies/statuses, fixtures, and all browser/JVM contracts. Risky public terminology or CLI migrations remain open and are excluded.

## Acceptance criteria

- `drain-stream` uses explicit names for the diagnostic builder, character buffer, retained-character cap, reader, and read count; `launch!` uses explicit names for the process builder, child process, and stderr-drain future.
- No behavior or output changes: the full focused JVM suite and testbed-support CLJS/browser proportionate gates remain green.
- The private process/stream code contains no bindings named `sb`, `buf`, `cap`, `n`, `r`, `pb`, `proc`, or `err-drain` for these roles; public keys, flags, paths, IDs, and error text remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Diff is limited to safe local names/comments in `open_in_editor_server.clj`.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit process/stream lifecycle locals; unchanged subprocess, timeout, diagnostics, and response contracts; focused JVM and testbed-support gates pass; diff limited to private names/comments.

title: Refresh ssr-node CLI and README after the runtime expansion
description:
## Evidence

Two consumer-facing inventory strings were left behind by the September crossing expansion:

- bin/serve.cjs:53 and README.md:506 describe --max-request-bytes as a ceiling on the request body and on its state. Current protocol.cjs:458-468 instead applies one ceiling to state and runtime together, a contract introduced by rf2-8arzr.3.
- README.md:685 still says the package has 9 suites and 96 rows. The authoritative runner currently executes 9 suites and 104 passing rows; .github/workflows/test.yml:5273 was already updated by rf2-8arzr.4 to record 104 rows across 9 files.
- History explains the split: rf2-8arzr.2 wrote the README at 96 rows; rf2-8arzr.3 then added 8 runtime-partition rows; rf2-8arzr.4 corrected the workflow count but did not own this README section.
- The current JVM adapter sends both state and runtime, so the state-only flag text is operationally misleading rather than hypothetical.
- Closed rf2-1vvx owned earlier pre-crossing README status prose and a classifier suite/fixture comment; its description explicitly excluded test.yml, and it predates this remaining 96-to-104 README drift. No current parent child or ssr-node/runtime-partition search owns these strings.

## Impact

An operator sizing the sidecar can infer that runtime data sits outside the protocol budget, while it actually shares the state ceiling. Contributors also receive contradictory test inventories from the README and CI. Both make the post-crossing surface look partly reverted.

## Disposition

Update the CLI help and matching README flag table to say that the numeric option caps the body and the combined state-plus-runtime EDN text. Reconcile the test inventory with the runner; prefer wording that does not hard-code a volatile row count unless that count is intentionally maintained.

## Risks

Do not imply that the parsed JSON body and partition-text limits are additive or independent: maxRequestBytes is separately used as the body ceiling and as one combined partition ceiling. Do not change runtime behavior or the option name in this documentation repair.
acceptance_criteria:
1. CLI --help and README describe max-request-bytes consistently with protocol.cjs: one body ceiling and one state-plus-runtime combined ceiling.
2. README's suite/row inventory agrees with test/run.cjs output (currently 9 suites, 104 rows), or omits the volatile row count without weakening test instructions.
3. No stale state-only ceiling sentence or 96-row claim remains in implementation/ssr-node.
4. CLI/serve tests, README link checks, and the full ssr-node suite are green.
close_reason: PR #9099. bin/serve.cjs and the README's copy of the same flag table now read 'ceiling on the body, and on state + runtime together' -- matching protocol.cjs:490 (one combined state+runtime ceiling) and http.cjs:133 (the separate body ceiling), and not implying the two are additive. The README's request-too-large refusal-code gloss ('over the state or body ceiling') was the same stale claim and moved with them. PREMISE THAT DID NOT HOLD: the bead says the runner executes 104 rows; it executes 107 on current main (measured foreground, 30+12+7+5+9+16+6+4+18), 108 with rf2-6r9j.74's new row. Took criterion 2's second branch and OMITTED the volatile count rather than restating a third number -- the count has gone stale twice, nothing checks it, and each suite prints its own tally. The nine suites stay named (that number is the length of run.cjs's FILES list). test.yml's comparable count is explicitly dated and self-described as 'a record, not a pin', so it is correct as written and was left alone (fenced besides). Gate nominated BY PATH: a README beside source belongs to scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci, exit 0, control fired (a planted broken relative target reds it naming this file). Neither link gate reads fenced blocks and nothing validates prose or tables, so the usage block's column alignment, the two-column refusal table row and the live --help output were checked by hand and stated in the PR body.

title: Prune ssr-node zero-consumer internal and test residue
description:
## Evidence

A whole-repository identifier/import census found seven internal or test-only residues with no consumer:

- src/isolate.cjs initializes this.renders at :54 and increments it at :134, but no code ever reads the counter.
- src/isolate.cjs exports WORKER_PATH at :241. The constant remains live inside that file at :38/:65, but no caller imports the export; tests import only Isolate.
- src/protocol.cjs exports KEY_TEXT and refuse at :523/:525. Both remain live implementation details inside protocol.cjs, but no caller imports either name. The package exports map does not expose protocol.cjs as a public subpath.
- test/_support.cjs exports boot at :75. boot is used only locally by withService at :12/:20; all suite destructuring imports omit it.
- test/observations.cjs exports ATTR at :70. ATTR is used only locally to build RE and encode; the three consumers import encode or observationsIn, never ATTR.
- test/fixtures/reference.cjs allowlists :bytes at :67, but that fixture neither reads :bytes nor receives it in any repository request. Every byte fixture request uses test/fixtures/bytes.cjs (bytes.test.cjs:109,138,168).

The render counter and internal exports date to the initial package; the test exports/allowlist survived later witness changes. No existing bead found by the exact identifiers, zero-consumer export, render counter, or ssr-node searches owns them.

## Impact

The unread counter looks like operational telemetry but can never inform health or scheduling. The extra exports imply supported seams that do not exist. The unused allowlist member weakens the reference fixture's fail-closed role by accepting state it never reads. Together they create false surface area and misleading future maintenance choices.

## Disposition

Remove the renders state and increment; narrow the isolate/protocol/test module export objects to names actually consumed; keep WORKER_PATH, KEY_TEXT, refuse, boot, and ATTR as local implementation details where still used; remove :bytes from the reference entry allowlist.

## Risks

Do not delete the live local helpers merely because their exports are dead. Do not touch the documented package entry points or their named Service/statusFor/STATUS exports in this cleanup: absence of an in-repo importer is not enough to prove those public API names unused outside the checkout. Keep the separate bytes fixture and byte tests intact.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Isolate has no unread renders property or increment.
2. WORKER_PATH, KEY_TEXT, refuse, boot, and ATTR remain available locally where needed but are not exported from their internal/test modules.
3. The reference fixture no longer allowlists :bytes; all requests accepted by its app/root entry use keys the fixture actually reads for behavior or observations.
4. Whole-repository import searches find no broken consumer.
5. ESLint and all 9 ssr-node suites remain green with no test-count drop.
close_reason: PR #9099. All six residues confirmed dead with two independent instruments (fixed-string git grep -F over tracked files excluding .beads, plus a reading of every require of the four modules and the names each destructures) and removed. Isolate.renders init+increment gone. WORKER_PATH, KEY_TEXT, refuse, boot and ATTR dropped from their module.exports and kept as live locals where still used. reference.cjs no longer allowlists :bytes (every byte request goes to chunked.cjs/bytes.cjs, which carry their own); the documented mirror of that table in envelope.test.cjs moved with it. Public entry points and Service/statusFor/STATUS untouched. Census proven live rather than vacuous: ATTR returns 50-odd hits repo-wide, renders 27 in-package. eslint exit 0 (control fired: a planted unused const reds no-unused-vars), suite 9/9 green at 108 rows vs a 107-row baseline, so no test-count drop.

title: Epoch listeners: remove the dead frame-id binding from fan-out
description:

Impact

title: Epoch: retire the superseded reserve-only delayed-silence helpers
description:
Evidence
- implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc:1238-1265 defines claim-delayed-silence!, a reserve-only operation. Its own contract says it emits an unqualified signal, leaves a claim-to-emit race, and remains only for staged tests or hypothetical callers that cannot race registry mutation.
- state.cljc:1377-1388 defines the matching rollback-delayed-silence!. Exact repository search finds both functions called only from epoch tests; there is no production, tool, example, skill, specification, or API consumer.
- The live destroy path at implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/listeners.cljc:478-507 calls claim-and-publish-delayed-silence! instead. That current helper uses the same private eligible-and-reserve! primitive and implements compare-and-prune rollback in its exception path at state.cljc:1355-1375.
- Commit e9475426bf moved production publication to claim-and-publish-delayed-silence! so the generation-qualified emit runs outside ledger locks and avoids the ledger-to-drain-lock deadlock. The older reserve/rollback pair remained as a test seam, not a runtime path.
- Existing direct users are tests at epoch_silencing_lineage_285_test.clj:235-246,344, epoch_cljs_test.cljs:719, and docstring assertions in epoch_silence_contract_test.clj:170-189.

Impact
The shipped source exposes two operations for delayed-silence claiming although only the integrated generation-qualified operation is safe on the live concurrent path. The test-only pair duplicates rollback protocol, preserves an incomplete unqualified-call workflow, and can invite a future caller onto the known race-prone seam.

Proposed disposition
Remove claim-delayed-silence! and rollback-delayed-silence! while retaining eligible-and-reserve! as the private shared implementation and claim-and-publish-delayed-silence! as the sole live operation. Rewrite staged tests through integrated behavior or a test-local/private seam, and update source comments/docstring ratchets that describe the retired pair.

Risks
The helper pair currently makes reservation ordering and compare-and-prune behavior easy to test and seeds marks in CLJ/CLJS reset tests. Preserve equivalent behavioral coverage: one winner, failed publication permits retry, a stale rollback cannot remove a fresher mark, and reset/cleanup boundedness. Do not move external publish under either ledger lock or remove observed-gen qualification.

title: Stop serializing ssr-node worker stacks that receivers discard
description:
## Evidence

- The worker serializes err.stack into both cross-thread error messages: boot-error at implementation/ssr-node/src/worker.cjs:80-86 and render error at :210-223.
- The boot receiver at src/isolate.cjs:91-95 reads only msg.code and msg.message, then creates detail containing modulePath. It never reads msg.stack.
- The render receiver at src/isolate.cjs:186-195 reads code, message, detail, and afterChunks. It never reads msg.stack.
- A whole-repository search finds no consumer of either posted stack field. The stack assertions in egress.test.cjs concern the parent-created Refusal stack, not these worker-message properties.
- The separate Worker error-event handler at isolate.cjs:98-101 reads err.stack directly; that live diagnostic does not depend on the message fields and must remain.
- Both discarded message properties date to b2b35bf6e9. No existing bead found by worker stack, boot-error stack, render-error stack, or ssr-node searches owns them.

## Impact

Every application boot/render exception needlessly serializes a potentially large, path-bearing stack across the worker boundary and then drops it. The presence of the field falsely suggests that this diagnostic survives into the service refusal, which makes debugging and egress review harder.

## Disposition

Remove stack from the worker's boot-error and render-error payloads. Preserve the live Worker error-event stack handling and the normal parent Refusal stack. Do not wire an application stack into HTTP/client egress as a way to make the field live; the existing boundary intentionally limits diagnostics.

## Risks

The worker error payloads are security-sensitive egress. Removing the dead field is safer than broadening the receiver, but tests should continue proving that refusal objects and HTTP bodies do not leak application stack contents. Avoid conflating an application-thrown render error with a worker_threads error event.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Neither boot-error nor render-error worker messages serialize err.stack.
2. No application stack is added to the parent detail or HTTP refusal body.
3. The live Worker error-event path still retains err.stack in its internal Refusal detail.
4. Boot failure, render failure, post-chunk failure, egress, and full ssr-node tests remain green.
close_reason: PR #9099. Discard proven at BOTH receivers before the sends were removed. Boot receiver: isolate.cjs handleBootMessage reads message.code and message.message only, then builds new Refusal(code, message, {modulePath: this.modulePath}) -- the detail is the parent's own field, message.stack never appears. Render receiver: _handleRenderMessage's message.t==='error' branch reads code, message, detail and afterChunks, spreading message.detail only. Those two handlers are the whole of worker.on('message') in the parent, so no third consumer exists. err.stack removed from both worker.cjs payloads (boot-error and render error). The live worker.on('error') handler, which holds the real Error, still keeps err.stack in its internal Refusal detail (criterion 3). No stack added to parent detail or HTTP refusal body. egress.test.cjs:292's stack assertion was always about the parent-created Refusal's own JS stack, not these message properties -- verified. Suite 9/9 green, 108 rows; eslint exit 0.

title: Epoch: remove the redundant pre-state argument from the halt hook
description:
Evidence
- implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:353 declares frame-state-before in the single-arity commit-halt-record! hook, but lines 355-372 never read it; clj-kondo reports that exact binding as unused.
- The only production caller is implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:3420-3422, which passes fs-now in both the before and after positions.
- The documented and implemented contract at epoch.cljc:334-370 deliberately derives both halted-depth snapshots from the last retained record :frame-state-after, falling back only to the supplied frame-state-after when no epoch has settled. The pre-state value cannot affect the record.
- Repository-wide hook inventory finds no other executable consumer. The late-bind directory and specifications name :epoch/commit-halt-record! but do not promise its arity.
- History shows frame-state-before became inert when commit 27a4b1d77e9 made last-settled :frame-state-after authoritative; later exact-incarnation work retained the redundant slot.

Impact
The optional epoch artefact and core router maintain a misleading extra protocol argument. The duplicate fs-now call implies two meaningful snapshots even though the halt event never ran and the implementation always commits one durable value into both slots.

Proposed disposition
Remove frame-state-before from the private hook signature and remove one fs-now argument at the sole router call. Keep the hook single-arity, preserve exact-owner-token gating, causal committed-at, residual-buffer harvest, last-settled lookup, first-halt fallback, and equal before/after snapshots.

Risks
This is a late-bound cross-artefact seam, so core and epoch must change atomically. Do not introduce a compatibility multi-arity: the source documents that multi-arity changed Closure advanced reachability and violated production elision (rf2-cprm0q).
acceptance_criteria:
1. commit-halt-record! has no frame-state-before parameter and the router passes one frame-state value.
2. Halted-depth records still use the last settled canonical frame-state, use the router value only for the no-prior-record fallback, and store equal :frame-state-before/:frame-state-after.
3. Exact-incarnation owner loss still cannot harvest or commit a same-id successor store.
4. Focused core/epoch JVM and CLJS tests pass, and the epoch production-elision gate stays green.
5. clj-kondo no longer reports the epoch.cljc unused binding.
close_reason: PR #9098. Premise held: frame-state-before was declared and never read (clj-kondo epoch.cljc:353 before, clean after). Removed from the private hook and one fs-now dropped at the sole caller router.cljc:3421 — core and epoch in ONE commit because the seam is late-bound and an arity mismatch is a runtime fault. Kept single-arity (rf2-cprm0q elision trap). Full caller/implementor sweep: router.cljc:3421 (only executable caller), epoch.cljc:329 (only implementor), epoch.cljc:737 registration, late_bind/directory.cljc:823 (describes the key, promises no arity), spec/002-Frames.md:2023 (illustrative 3-arg pseudocode, carries no frame-state at all), spec/Conventions.md + migration README + conformance fixture (name the key only) — NO spec change needed, no hot-zone file touched. Liveness control: restoring the two-snapshot call reds re-frame.epoch-test/depth-exceeded-commits-halted-record with ArityException (8 args), so the halt seam is exercised end to end. Green: epoch-test (219), core frame-destroy-incarnation-jvm-test (29), scripts/test-epoch-prod-gate.sh (25). NOTED GAP, pre-existing and unaltered: no test covers the first-cascade fallback arm where the router-passed frame-state is the value actually used.

title: Use the orphaned ssr-node chunk-frame constructor at its live boundary
description:
## Evidence

- implementation/ssr-node/src/protocol.cjs:497-498 defines chunkFrame(seq, html) as the canonical public body-frame constructor and exports it at :528.
- A whole-repository exact-identifier search finds no call to chunkFrame; its only sites are the definition and export.
- The actual worker-to-service boundary independently rebuilds the identical object literal at src/isolate.cjs:165-168: { type: 'chunk', seq: msg.seq, html: msg.html }.
- The adjacent completeFrame constructor is live: service.cjs imports and calls it to create the terminal public frame. The chunk constructor is the orphaned half of that intended pair.
- Both the helper and duplicate literal have existed since the initial implementation b2b35bf6e9. No existing bead found by chunkFrame, chunk-frame, or ssr-node searches owns the duplication.

## Impact

There are two sources of truth for the public chunk-frame shape, but only the hand-written isolate copy is exercised. A future field-list or hardening change can update the named protocol constructor while leaving every real response unchanged, or update the live literal while leaving a misleading exported helper behind.

## Disposition

Import chunkFrame into isolate.cjs and use it exactly where the parent translates a worker chunk into the public service frame. This mirrors completeFrame and preserves the boundary's explicit named-field projection. If the helper is rejected as an abstraction, delete it instead; do not retain both representations.

## Risks

Do not pass or spread the raw worker message. The explicit projection is an egress boundary that intentionally drops unrecognized application-controlled fields. The constructor must continue accepting only seq and html and returning only type, seq, and html.
acceptance_criteria:
1. There is one source of truth for the public chunk-frame object shape.
2. The live Isolate chunk path exercises chunkFrame, or the unused helper/export is removed completely.
3. No raw worker-message spread or extra field crosses the boundary.
4. Protocol, bytes, egress, and full ssr-node tests remain green.
5. A focused assertion or coverage reading shows the retained constructor executes on a streamed response.
close_reason: PR #9099. chunkFrame is now the single source of truth for the public chunk-frame shape: isolate.cjs imports it and calls it at the worker->service boundary, mirroring completeFrame's live use in service.cjs. No raw-message spread, no extra field; the constructor still takes only seq/html and returns only type/seq/html. A new egress.test.cjs row reads a MULTI-chunk response and asserts each frame's key set is exactly html/seq/type, so the retained constructor is proven to execute on a streamed response (criterion 5). Control fired: with the boundary spreading the raw worker message instead, the row reds on the t and id fields. Suite 9/9 green, 108 rows, eslint exit 0.

title: pair-mcp tests: make the second nREPL candidate regression case reachable
description:
## Finding
One Pair-MCP nREPL regression test contains two independent `cljs.test/async` forms in a single `deftest`. ClojureScript runs only the first async branch, so the `.nrepl-port` fallback assertions in the second branch are unreachable.

## Evidence
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/nrepl_test.cljs`, test `discover-port-shadow-probe-surfaces-each-candidate-file`, has a first async block for `.shadow-cljs/nrepl.port` at lines 776-795 and a second async block for `.nrepl-port` at lines 796-814.
- `clj-kondo --lint tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test` reports `multiple-async-in-deftest` at line 797: only the first async test of a deftest will run.
- The test name and comments promise coverage of each candidate-file probe, but the second branch cannot contribute assertions or a failure.
- Git blame traces this shape to commit `8b65440c7f4`; repository/bead searches found no existing issue for this unreachable branch.

## Impact
A regression in `.nrepl-port` probe-error reporting can pass the suite because its claimed test never executes. This weakens confidence in a live, documented port-discovery fallback.

## Proposed disposition
Either split the two candidate cases into separate `deftest`s or sequence both cases under one `async`/`done` lifecycle. Make execution of both cases observable so the test cannot silently regress to one branch again.

## Risks / retained contracts
Retain both `.shadow-cljs/nrepl.port` and `.nrepl-port` discovery behavior; both are active compatibility paths, not removal candidates. Avoid timing-dependent assertions.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Both candidate-file probe-error cases execute in the test suite and can independently fail.
2. The test uses separate deftests or a single correctly sequenced async lifecycle; no deftest contains multiple sibling `async` forms.
3. `clj-kondo` no longer emits `multiple-async-in-deftest` for `nrepl_test.cljs`.
4. The Pair-MCP test suite passes, including an assertion/counter or equivalent negative-control proof that both candidate branches ran.
notes: AUDIT PR #9076 (2026-09-03): REOPENED. The code split is correct, but the new comment at tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/nrepl_test.cljs:776-779 repeats the mechanism this PR and the close reason explicitly disproved: it says ClojureScript runs only the first async form, so the sibling never executes, can never fail, and silently drops assertions. The recorded negative control on the original shape proves the second branch did execute and fail; the actual defect is that it ran outside the awaited lifecycle and lacked independent completion/attribution. Minimal repair: rewrite only this comment to state the real one-async-per-deftest lifecycle reason. No test or production-code redesign is needed.
close_reason: PR #9101 (2026-09-03 15:14 AUSEST). Audit repair as ruled: comment only, no test or production-code change. nrepl_test.cljs:776-779 justified the one-async-per-deftest rule by the DISPROVED mechanism ('ClojureScript runs only the FIRST async form ... a sibling never executes and can never fail'). Rewritten to the real lifecycle reason: a deftest carries ONE async lifecycle, so a sibling async runs OUTSIDE the lifecycle the runner awaits — it DOES execute and its failures DO surface, but with no completion the runner blocks on and no attribution back to the case it covers, so the suite can settle before it finishes and its red can land under the wrong name. The two-deftest split from PR #9076 is untouched and still stands. clj-kondo --lint on the file: exit 0, 0 errors 0 warnings, no multiple-async-in-deftest.

title: Clarify duplicated nine-states todo generator names
description:
## Finding
The live and Story variants of the nine-states pattern copy the same private todo generator but call it the abbreviated gen-todos, with one-letter count/index locals. The surrounding prose calls this a generator and the helper is example-facing teaching code, so the role should be explicit.

## Evidence
- examples/patterns/nine_states/core.cljs:148 mentions the demo server's gen-todos; :204 defines (defn- gen-todos [n]) and the for binding [i (range n)]; :229 invokes it from the managed demo stub.
- examples/patterns/nine_states/stories.cljs:108-113 defines the copied private (defn- gen-todos [n]) and [i (range n)]; :128 invokes it for the Story request value.
- Both helpers produce the same Todo shape, making the duplicated abbreviated name especially likely to be copied into future example code without communicating that it generates synthetic todos.

## Ambiguity cost
Readers must expand gen to generate and infer whether n is an item count and i is a row index in two parallel implementations; this is avoidable ambiguity in the canonical pattern example and its Story twin.

## Recommendation
Rename the two private helpers to generate-todos and their count/index locals to todo-count/index, updating only local references and the explanatory comment. Keep all event names, :n query keys, /api/todos URLs, :value payload slot, Todo schema, generated values, and control flow unchanged.

## Compatibility, exclusions, and Phase-1 fence
These helpers are private and have no public API or selector contract. Do not rename the public run/mount!/register-all! entry points, namespace/file paths (including nine_states), event/sub/machine IDs, DOM/test/build IDs, routes, serialized keys, or behavior. Do not migrate naming across other examples or touch any existing Phase-1 removal/vestigial target, shared pattern docs, or files outside examples/patterns/nine_states; risky cross-example/public migrations remain open work.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Both private gen-todos definitions and all in-slice references become generate-todos; no stale token remains in this pattern.
2. The helper arguments and loops use todo-count/index consistently, with no change to generated Todo IDs/titles/counts.
3. A semantic review confirms :n, :value, event IDs, URLs, schemas, routes, DOM/build selectors, and test-facing entry points are unchanged.
4. Focused example CLJS/JVM/lint gates and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Implemented in the two nine-states private helpers and verified: generate-todos replaces gen-todos in core.cljs and stories.cljs; todo-count/index clarify local roles; :n query keys, :value payloads, event IDs, URLs, schemas, routes, and behavior unchanged. Consolidated CLJS gate exit 0: 11,167 tests / 55,726 assertions, 0 failures/errors; compile 1,889 files / 432 compiled / 0 warnings; patterns clj-kondo exit 0 (0 errors; 2 pre-existing warnings); no-banner lint_kondo self-test exit 0; git diff --check clean.

title: spec/Ownership.md calls spec/Security.md's decisions log a 38-decision BEAD log; it has 49 rows and an empty Bead column
description:
FOUND BY rf2-6r9j.138's worker (PR #9092) while repairing the twin count in implementation/SECURITY.md. Reported rather than taken: .138 was fenced to the IMPLEMENTATION catalogue, and this row describes a different document's log.

THE CLAIM — re-derive at origin/main HEAD before acting.

spec/Ownership.md:70 describes spec/Security.md and ends its Surface cell with "...the four-proposition pragmatic stance, and the 38-decision bead log."

TWO THINGS ARE OFF, and they are not the same defect.

1. THE COUNT. spec/Security.md's own "## Decisions log" section holds 49 data rows by a deterministic first-column count over the section, not 38. (The same count method on implementation/SECURITY.md gave 49 rows / 45 distinct ids, which is what .138 fixed there.)

2. THE WORD "bead", WHICH IS THE MORE INTERESTING HALF. Every row in spec/Security.md's decisions log has an EMPTY Bead column — the table still carries the `| Bead | Call | Rationale |` header and the leading `| |` cell, but no id was found in any row. So calling it a "bead log" describes a column that is present and blank. Establish WHY before editing: were the ids stripped deliberately (the parallel case is implementation/SECURITY.md, where rf2-efioe established that all 45 ids sit below the tracker's 2026-07-11 retention floor and a preamble sentence was added saying so), or were they lost? A verified "the ids were deliberately removed and the column should go / the description should stop calling it a bead log" is a complete answer. Do NOT invent ids, and do not copy implementation/SECURITY.md's ids across — they bind a different set of calls.

SCOPE NOTE. If the fix touches the empty Bead column itself rather than only Ownership.md's one-line description, that is a spec/Security.md table-shape change and should be weighed on its own merits, not smuggled in as a count repair.

GATE, BY PATH NOT BY JOB NAME. Both files are under spec/, so scripts/check_doc_slugs.py is the gate for link targets and heading anchors, and it runs unguarded in test.yml's verify-readme-links job (the job whose NAME misleads — check_readme_links.py --ci is the OTHER gate and does not reach spec/). mkdocs build --strict also covers spec/ via mkdocs_hooks.py's staging, but validates link RESOLUTION only, never anchors. Neither gate reads prose, counts or table columns: verify the column count by hand (Ownership.md's table is 4 columns; Security.md's decisions-log blocks are 3) and say so in the PR body.

FENCE: spec/Ownership.md and possibly spec/Security.md. Neither is on the hot-zone one-toucher list, but both are frequently touched — verify no live toucher at dispatch time.
close_reason: PR #9101 (2026-09-03 15:14 AUSEST). Both errors fixed in one edit on spec/Ownership.md:70: 'the 38-decision bead log' -> 'the 49-decision log'. WHY THE BEAD COLUMN IS BLANK — established, not assumed: the ids were removed DELIBERATELY by commit 2d64e1f7c2 'docs(spec): strip bead refs + historical commentary — spec states what IS, not how it evolved' (rf2-bqys8, Mike, 2026-05-27), which deleted 48 '| rf2-...' first cells from this exact table under a spec-tree-wide policy; ccdcfd99f8 finished the remainder. They were NOT lost. The only non-blank first cell left is a bare '(part 1)' fragment carrying no id. This is the OPPOSITE disposition from implementation/SECURITY.md, which keeps its 45 ids under an explicit preamble calling them provenance-not-lookups (rf2-efioe) — that doc sits outside the spec tree's policy. NOT DONE, per this bead's own scope note: the empty Bead column itself and the now-dead preamble sentence in spec/Security.md ('The bead's bd show <id> carries the full context', pointing at ids the doc no longer contains) are a spec/Security.md table-shape change to be weighed on its own merits; filed separately.
