value:
TWO SEPARATE gh HAZARDS, OFTEN CONFLATED — keep them distinct (2026-09-03, corrected same day).

=== HAZARD 1: the 100-file cap is REAL, and it truncates a PR's FILE LIST ===
'gh pr view N --json files' and 'gh pr list --json files' return at most 100 filenames, silently — well-formed JSON, no marker. MEASURED on day8/re-frame2 PR #9103: 'gh pr view 9103 --json files --jq .files|length' = 100; 'gh api --paginate repos/day8/re-frame2/pulls/9103/files --jq .[].filename | wc -l' = 401.

It matters because the mayor's overlap check is
  comm -12 <(git diff --name-only <merge-base> origin/main | sort) <(gh pr view N --json files ...)
so on a PR over 100 files the right side is a truncated sample and a real overlap in files 101..N reads as NO OVERLAP. Fails OPEN.
FIX: gh api --paginate repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<N>/files --jq '.[].filename'
DETECTOR: 'gh pr view --json changedFiles' reports the TRUE total even when files[] is capped. changedFiles != (files|length), or a length of exactly 100, means truncated.

=== HAZARD 2: gh/git LISTINGS CAN RETURN A STALE VIEW — this is NOT the cap ===
DO NOT attribute a missing PR to the 100-file cap. A worker A/B'd it: 'gh pr list --state open --json number,headRefName' and the same call WITH files both returned the same 3 PRs. The cap truncates a PR's file list; it does NOT drop PRs from a listing. Its 'git ls-remote --heads origin refs/heads/worker/<prefix>*' pattern form was also control-tested and works.

What actually happened: at one instant, THREE independent probes — two different 'gh pr list' shapes and one 'git ls-remote' — all returned a view stale by 3-9 MINUTES, missing a PR created 9 minutes earlier and a branch that existed on the remote. The worker read their agreement as corroboration when it was CORRELATED STALENESS. Root cause not reproduced; do not invent one.

THE DEFENCE FOR BOTH: a NEGATIVE from any listing needs a POSITIVE CONTROL THROUGH THE SAME COMMAND SHAPE — 'does this return something I know exists RIGHT NOW?' Independent probes agreeing is not corroboration when they share a stale cache. This is the census-control discipline applied to listings, and the listing is usually the load-bearing negative.

=== AND: PR-vs-TRUNK OVERLAP IS NOT PR-vs-PR OVERLAP ===
The mayor's tick checks each PR against the trunk. That never sees TWO OPEN PRs editing the same file. Measured: #9108 and #9105 both edited tools/template/spec/005-Repo-Split.md and neither worker nor the tick knew, because no one compared the two PRs to each other. When several PRs are open, cross-check them pairwise with the paginated file lists before choosing a merge order.

/tmp ON THIS BOX IS THE SHARED WINDOWS TEMP DIRECTORY — every agent, worker and codex process writes there, so a generic filename WILL be clobbered (2026-09-03).

MEASURED: '/tmp' resolves to C:\Users\miket\AppData\Local\Temp. It holds hundreds of foreign '<uuid>.tmp' files from unrelated Windows processes, and '/tmp/open.json' appeared there written by something other than the mayor. A worker reported the concrete failure: it read '/tmp/open.json' twice seconds apart and got BEADS DATA back from a file it had written with something else — another process had overwritten it in between.

WHY IT IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN MERELY UNTIDY: the mayor and its workers all reach for the same obvious names — /tmp/open.json, /tmp/files.txt, /tmp/out.log, /tmp/nred.json. A clobbered intermediate does not error; it yields a WRONG ANSWER that looks well-formed, and it is read as fact. That is the same failure class as a census with no control.

USE THE SESSION SCRATCHPAD instead — the per-session directory named in the environment preamble (C:/Users/miket/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/<project>/<session-id>/scratchpad). It is session-scoped and isolated. If /tmp must be used, embed a session-unique prefix in every filename and re-verify content after writing.

A worker caught this only because it applied a control — reading the same file twice and comparing. Intermediates are exactly where an unverified assumption hides.

title: Prune unused default-seed arities from the security generator
description:
Scope: implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/gen.cljc and its repository-wide consumers.

Evidence: `sample` exposes a two-argument `[g n]` form that silently selects seed 0 plus the used `[g n seed]` form. `for-all` similarly exposes `[g n pred]` plus `[g n seed pred]`. A repository-wide symbol search found no consumer of either default-seed arity: the parity test calls sample with three arguments, and every security property calls for-all with an explicit seed. No namespace outside implementation/security imports re-frame.security.gen. Targeted history shows the unused overloads were present from the helper's initial commit (05ca3070f8) while its initial callers were already explicitly seeded.

Impact: these dead overloads expand a test-helper API, imply an unsupported convention around an invisible global seed, and create two ways to express every property without serving a compatibility consumer.

Recommendation: remove the two default-seed arities and make the seeded signatures the only API; update docstrings/spec prose if necessary to state that determinism is explicit.

Risks/contracts: preserve generator parity across CLJ and CLJS, stable replay for existing explicit seeds, shrink/reproduction diagnostics, and every current property call. This helper is internal to the security tier, but search again before removal in case a new consumer has appeared.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `sample` and `for-all` expose only their explicitly seeded forms, unless a concrete live consumer of a default-seed form is documented.
2. All repository call sites remain explicitly seeded and deterministic.
3. Generator parity coverage remains intact in both runtimes.
4. `clojure -M:test` from implementation/security and `npm run test:security` from implementation both pass.
close_reason: PR #9111. Removed sample's [g n] and for-all's [g n pred] default-seed arities; the seeded signatures are now the only API, and both docstrings state that determinism is explicit rather than defaulted. Premise re-verified at HEAD with two independent instruments plus controls that fired. git grep -F over tracked files: 17 gen/for-all sites, ALL four-argument; 2 gen/sample sites (5 calls), ALL three-argument; control gen/gen-elem = 9, a non-existent name = 0. clj-kondo var-usages into re-frame.security.gen: for-all appears only at arity 4 (36 usages across both reader-conditional arms), sample only at arity 3 (12). The sole uses of the default-seed forms were the two self-delegating bodies removed. No namespace outside implementation/security requires the ns; the only two other files naming it (.github/workflows/test.yml, scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh) do so in prose comments about the LCG cross-runtime contract, not in code. No spec or docs page documents the helper API, so no fenced/hot-zone file needed a change. Generator parity and seed replay unchanged -- every call site was already explicitly seeded. Security JVM 92/717 and npm run test:security 93/724, 0 failures 0 errors; clj-kondo over implementation/security reports 1 warning, byte-identical to the origin/main baseline (mask32 unused under the :cljs reader arm, pre-existing).

title: Remove the reply security suite's duplicate generic projector test
description:
Scope: implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/reply_envelope_egress_security_cljs_test.cljc and implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/public_profile_projection_security_cljs_test.cljc.

Evidence: reply-value-projects-through-project-egress (reply_envelope_egress_security_cljs_test.cljc:255-272) never exercises re-frame.reply or a reply envelope. It calls rf/project-egress directly and checks four generic projector contracts: framed off-box sensitive redaction, large-value elision, public sibling preservation, and frameless fail-closed behavior. Those same contracts are already exercised in the dedicated public-profile projection suite (including its off-box profile, no-frame, and large-marker cases), and both suites run in the same JVM and focused CLJS security lanes. The tests arrived minutes apart in the same June 17 merge batch (80f78d8377 and 98777011dc), consistent with overlapping concurrent coverage rather than a distinct reply invariant.

Impact: the mislocated duplicate adds maintenance and runtime cost while making the reply suite appear to cover a reply-specific path that it does not touch.

Recommendation: remove reply-value-projects-through-project-egress from the reply-envelope suite. Keep every test that actually constructs or projects a reply envelope, and keep the canonical generic projector coverage in public_profile_projection_security_cljs_test.cljc.

Risks/contracts: do not weaken reply-envelope coverage, the public/on-box projection contract, framed off-box redaction, frameless fail-closed behavior, or deterministic large-value elision. This is test deduplication only; production behavior must not change.
acceptance_criteria:
1. reply-value-projects-through-project-egress is removed from the reply-envelope suite, or is rewritten to exercise a genuinely reply-specific path not covered elsewhere.
2. Generic project-egress contracts remain covered in public_profile_projection_security_cljs_test.cljc.
3. All actual reply-envelope security tests remain intact.
4. `clojure -M:test` from implementation/security and `npm run test:security` from implementation both pass.
close_reason: PR #9111. Removed reply-value-projects-through-project-egress from the reply-envelope suite. Premise confirmed at source: it never touched re-frame.reply or a reply envelope -- it called rf/project-egress on a plain map. NAMED SUCCESSOR: public_profile_projection_security_cljs_test.cljc. Framed contracts are pinned by off-box-profiles-redact-frame-owned-app-db, which loops off-box-tool/off-box-observability/local-redacted and asserts (is (gen/redacted? (get-in out [:auth :token]))), (is (gen/large-marker? (get-in out [:docs :blob]))), (is (= 3 (get-in out [:public :count])) "unmarked sibling passes through") and (is (not (contains-sentinel? out))). Frameless fail-closed is pinned by no-frame-egress-fails-closed: (binding [frame/*current-frame* nil] ... (is (gen/redacted? out) "frameless egress fails closed to :rf/redacted")). The one apparent gap -- the retired row used off-box-observability frameless where the successor uses off-box-tool -- is not a distinct contract: projection.cljc delegates the whole no-live-frame decision to elide-wire-value, one profile-independent control point, and observability is separately exercised framed by the successor's profile loop and by sensitive-wins-over-large-at-projection. Every reply-envelope row survives, frameless-trace-summary-fails-closed included. Security JVM 92/717, npm run test:security 93/724, 0 failures 0 errors.

title: Remove the security tier's fixed-corpus pseudo-property
description:
## Scope

Remove or genuinely diversify the pseudo-property `every-schema-kind-rejects-every-malformed-schema` and its private `gen-malformed-schema` from `implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/fail_closed_invariant_security_cljs_test.cljc`.

## Evidence

`malformed-schemas` is a closed six-value vector. `boundary-seam-never-passes-a-malformed-schema` already exhaustively invokes `validate-with-registered-fn` for every one of those six values. `meta-bearing-surfaces-never-pass-a-malformed-schema` already exhaustively invokes `validate-event!`, `validate-fx!`, and `validate-sub!` for every one. The later "property" wraps that exact vector in `gen/gen-elem` and randomly re-invokes the same four functions 80 times; it cannot produce a new schema shape and, unlike the earlier `doseq` checks, its sampling does not itself guarantee that every corpus member was selected despite its title. `app-db` has a separate exhaustive test and is not part of the pseudo-property.

The test came in with the exhaustive rows in commit d4a33175d7; no later production contract made its sample distinct. Current JVM and CLJS security lanes are green (94/723 and 95/730 respectively), confirming the suite is live rather than orphaned.

## Impact

The row adds repeated validator work and expected malformed-schema emissions to both runtimes while supplying no additional input or invariant. It also presents random sampling as stronger "every malformed schema" evidence than the exhaustive loops immediately above it.

## Recommendation

Delete the generator binding and redundant test. If a future contributor can define a generator that produces malformed schema structures outside the named corpus, add that as a genuinely generative property instead of sampling the fixed vector.

## Risks / contracts

Retain the exhaustive boundary, event/fx/sub, app-db, and throwing-validator tests. Do not weaken the fail-closed contract or remove named malformed cases.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `gen-malformed-schema` and the fixed-corpus re-sampling test are removed, or the generator is changed to produce demonstrably new malformed structures not already exhaustively enumerated.
2. Every entry in `malformed-schemas` remains exhaustively checked against `validate-with-registered-fn`, `validate-event!`, `validate-fx!`, and `validate-sub!`.
3. The app-db malformed-schema and throwing-validator fail-closed rows remain.
4. Both `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/security` and `npm run test:security` pass.
close_reason: PR #9111. Deleted gen-malformed-schema and every-schema-kind-rejects-every-malformed-schema. Premise confirmed at source: gen/gen-elem over the closed six-value malformed-schemas vector cannot produce a shape outside the corpus, and the two doseq tests immediately above already invoke all four validators (validate-with-registered-fn; validate-event!/-fx!/-sub!) over every member exhaustively, so the property asserted a strict subset. Chose deletion over honest relabelling because the invariant is asserted more strongly four lines above -- an honest label would have named a duplicate. Retained the exhaustive boundary-seam, meta-bearing, app-db and throwing-validator rows and every named malformed case. Also corrected the ns docstring, which claimed generated coverage for EVERY boundary. Security JVM 92/717 and npm run test:security 93/724, both 0 failures 0 errors; the -2 tests / -6 assertions against the bead's recorded 94/723 and 95/730 baselines are exactly this row plus rf2-6r9j.94's. Gate proven live (planted false?->true? gave 6 FAILs naming line 60; restored, hash-object identical).

title: Remove dead imports and bindings from schemas tests
description:
## Finding

The schemas test slice contains a bounded set of imports, local bindings, and nested `let` wrappers with no reader or behavioral effect. They are test-maintenance residue from earlier fixture/reset and handler shapes, distinct from namespaces intentionally required only for load/build side effects.

## Evidence

A focused clj-kondo run over `implementation/schemas/src` and `implementation/schemas/test`, followed by manual symbol and history checks, proves:

- Seven dead namespace aliases/imports: `re-frame.schemas.digest` in `schemas_concurrency_stress_test.clj`; `re-frame.substrate.adapter` in both `schemas_conformance_test.clj` and `schemas_reg_side_effects_test.clj`; `re-frame.schemas.validator` in `schemas_fail_open_test.clj`; `re-frame.registrar` and `re-frame.trace` in `schemas_test.clj`; and `re-frame.trace` in `schemas_validator_unavailable_warning_test.clj`. Repository searches find no qualified use of any alias in its file.
- Fifteen unused locals: three `db` destructurings in `schemas_cljs_test.cljs` (currently lines 62, 85, 342); two in `schemas_fail_open_test.clj` (169, 246); five in `schemas_sensitive_test.clj` (1561, 1597, 1632, 1728, 1753); four in `schemas_test.clj` (97, 124, 165, 297); plus the never-read `secret` binding in `schemas_sensitive_test.clj` (1161). The affected init handlers return fixed maps, so replacing their unused cofx destructure with `_` is behavior-neutral; the secret test dispatches integer `12345`, not that binding.
- Four single-body nested `let` forms in `schemas_fail_open_test.clj` (currently 178, 233, 255, 273) merely wrap an immediately enclosing `let` and are reported as redundant. Merging binding vectors preserves evaluation and assertion order.
- History ties several imports to superseded local reset fixtures. For example `c6017e7f32` moved registrar/frame/adapter cleanup to `schemas.test-fixture/reset-runtime` but left some caller imports behind.
- All-status bead searches for schemas test imports, schemas unused bindings, lint, and the named test paths found no owning issue.

## Deliberate exclusions

Do not remove `re-frame.core` from `schemas_bundle_control.cljs` or `schemas_bundle_probe.cljs`: both files explain that the unused alias is an intentional matched-build require and removing it invalidates the A/B. Do not blindly remove effect-only `re-frame.schemas` loads, unresolved macro/API references, or the app-db source's nested `let` around stale-incarnation checkpoints. Redundant direct Malli adapter test requires and their stale posture are owned separately by `rf2-6r9j.51`.

## Impact

Dead imports make test dependency boundaries look broader than they are; unused handler bindings and wrapper lets add noise to already large security/error-path suites and keep focused lint output noisy enough to hide new regressions. There is no intended runtime, public API, diagnostic, or fixture-isolation contract behind these items.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the seven proven-unused imports, replace only the fifteen unused locals with appropriately ignored parameters or delete the inert binding, and flatten the four test-only nested lets without changing their assertions or setup/cleanup order.

## Risks

Clojure namespace loads can be side-effectful and the bundle fixtures deliberately exploit that. Keep the change to the enumerated items, verify each require's absence does not alter hook/adapter initialization, and preserve `try/finally`, trace recorder, and stale-incarnation ordering.
acceptance_criteria:
- Focused clj-kondo no longer reports the seven enumerated unused namespaces, fifteen enumerated unused bindings, or four enumerated redundant lets.
- The intentional unused `re-frame.core` requires in both matched schemas bundle fixtures remain, with their explanatory contract intact.
- Effect-only facade/adapter wiring required for schema validation remains covered by `schemas_implies_validation_test` and `rf2-6r9j.51`; no load-order regression is introduced.
- Schemas JVM and CLJS suites pass, including conformance, fail-open, sensitive redaction, concurrency stress, validator-unavailable warning, and production boundary targets.
- Test names, assertion counts/semantics, `try/finally` restoration, and trace capture order are unchanged except for removal of inert syntax.
close_reason: PR #9111. All three enumerated groups landed; focused clj-kondo over implementation/schemas/{src,test} went 33 -> 7 warnings with errors 0, and the 26 cleared are exactly the enumerated set. Seven unused requires removed (schemas.digest in concurrency-stress; substrate.adapter in conformance and reg-side-effects; schemas.validator in fail-open; registrar and trace in schemas_test; trace in validator-unavailable-warning), each proven by TWO instruments -- a boundary-anchored git grep for the alias in its own file plus clj-kondo's alias resolution -- with a control alias in the SAME file returning a stable non-zero count every time. Worth recording: a naive substring grep for 'digest/' and 'trace/' returns FALSE HITS inside the qualified keywords :utdxg.digest/seed and :rf.trace/phase; the anchored form reads 0. Fifteen locals: fourteen cofx destructures on fixed-map init handlers replaced with _, plus the never-read secret binding at the container-level sensitive test (which dispatches the integer 12345, not the binding) -- adjacent sibling handlers that DO read db were left alone. Four single-body nested lets in fail-open merged into their enclosing let; the inner init depends on the outer binding so evaluation and assertion order are preserved. Kept per the bead's exclusions: both matched-build re-frame.core requires in the schemas bundle fixtures, the effect-only re-frame.schemas loads in conformance and reg-side-effects, and validate.cljc's nested let. Gates: schemas JVM 372 tests / 19221 assertions and npm run test:cljs 11168 / 55740, both exit 0, 0 failures 0 errors. Gate proven live by planting (is (neg? (count mal))) inside a FLATTENED let -- exit 1 naming schemas_fail_open_test.clj:178, the flattened block's own body line -- then restoring, hash-object identical. Test names, assertion counts and try/finally ordering unchanged.

title: adapters README + core adapter.cljc count test-react as one of the 'six shipped adapter kinds'; Spec 006 says hicasso is the sixth
notes:
Found while landing rf2-6r9j.85 (PR #9100), out of that worker's fence.

implementation/adapters/README.md:37 reads: '3 of the 6 shipped adapter kinds install it — Reagent, reagent-slim and UIx. The other 3 omit it deliberately: plain-atom (in core) and the SSR substrate render without a live commit, so there is nothing to flush, and the test-react fixture hands the render clock to the test.'

That makes the six: reagent, reagent-slim, uix, plain-atom, ssr, test-react. Spec 006's canonical inventory (spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2155-2160) lists a different six: reagent, reagent-slim, uix, HICASSO, plain-atom, ssr — and its repository-home paragraph says test-react has 'no :kind in the shipped set'. So the README substitutes test-react for hicasso.

The wording is not local to the README. implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:643-647 says almost the same thing in the flush-render! docstring: 'Three of the six shipped adapter kinds install one — Reagent, reagent-slim and UIx. The other three omit it, each for its own reason: plain-atom and SSR render without a live React commit ... and test-react hands the render clock to the test'. The two must move together or the README ends up contradicting core.

Before editing, MEASURE which adapters actually carry a :flush-render! slot rather than trusting either text — the question is whether hicasso installs one, which decides whether the corrected sentence reads 'three of six' or 'four of six'. git grep -n -F 'flush-render!' -- implementation/ (excluding test dirs) is the starting instrument; implementation/hicasso/ is the surface to settle.

Not urgent and not a correctness bug — it is a roster count in two docstrings. Sequence it behind whoever holds implementation/core.
close_reason: PR #9112. MEASURED, not inherited: FOUR of the six shipped kinds install :flush-render!, not three. Reagent + reagent-slim inject it into make-ratom-spine (reagent.cljs:113, reagent_slim.cljs:50) and make-ratom-adapter re-emits it (spine.cljs:3848); UIx AND HICASSO both get it from make-react-adapter (spine.cljs:3371), which wires (:flush-render! spine-fns) unconditionally over make-react-spine's own top-level defn (spine.cljs:1773, :3239). plain-atom (plain_atom.cljc:153-162) and SSR (ssr/substrate.cljc:80-88) carry no such key. So the corrected sentence reads 'four of six' and the two omissions share ONE reason (no live React commit to flush) rather than the old three-way split. Corrected in ONE commit in both mirrored texts: implementation/adapters/README.md:37 and implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:643-647. Spec 006 read, NOT edited (hot-zone one-toucher); its inventory is the source of truth and test-react correctly has no :kind in the shipped set. Also fixed the README's factory-family bullet, which said the React-hook pair was UIx-only and would have contradicted the new sentence. RESERVED-VALUE CALL: nothing deleted from any kind roster; the :rf.adapter/ui and :rf.adapter/freehand reserved-kind rows and the struck-through retirement bookkeeping are untouched. Gates: check_readme_links.py --ci exit 0 (proved live by a control that fired - breaking the new #cljs-reference-scope anchor took it 0 to 1, restored and hash-verified); lint_kondo.py exit 0, errors 0. Prose/table/fence content hand-checked, as no link gate reads it.

title: defwrapper CALLS a hook whose value may be a COMPONENT — the sharp edge under rf2-nvcp
description:
Discovered while fixing rf2-nvcp (PR #9050). NOT urgent: no known live instance
remains, and this is a design question rather than a defect.

`defwrapper` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_artefact.cljc) emits, for an
`:apply` arity, a body of the shape `(if-let [f (late-bind/get-fn <hook>)] (apply f args) <absent>)`.
That is correct for every hook whose value is a FUNCTION. It is silently wrong for
a hook whose value is a COMPONENT, because a component that is CALLED never becomes
a component: on Reagent it renders inside its caller's component instance, so it
reads that instance's React context rather than its own, and any `:contextType`
the head carries is inert.

That is exactly how rf2-nvcp blanked every routed application. `rf/route-link` is
a defwrapper over `:routing/route-link`, whose value was the registered
`:route/link` view head. The head was called, not mounted, so `(.-context cmp)`
answered React's empty default and route-link-render's render-time
`require-current-frame!` raised `:rf.error/no-frame-context` on FIRST RENDER.

rf2-nvcp fixed it at the PUBLICATION side — the hook now carries an
element-emitting shim, `[(views/view-head :route/link) props & children]` — which
is the right fix for that bead and leaves defwrapper untouched. `route-link` is
the only component-valued hook in the table today, so nothing else is currently
broken.

THE QUESTION, for whoever holds core: should `defwrapper` be able to say "this
hook's value is a component, emit an element rather than a call" — a body-kind
beside `:delegate` / `:apply` / the recursion form — so the next
component-valued hook cannot repeat this by construction? Or is
publish-an-element the convention, in which case the constraint belongs in the
late-bind directory's contract prose for any such hook rather than in the macro?

Note the failure mode when weighing it: nothing errors, nothing warns, the unit
suites stay green (they call the render fn directly under `rf/with-frame`, which
answers from the dynamic-var tier), and the symptom is a blank page in a real
browser only. rf2-nvcp went ~2.5 months undetected on exactly that profile.

Fence note: rf2-nvcp's worker could not touch `core_routing.cljc` or
`core_artefact.cljc` (held / out of fence), which is why this is filed rather
than folded in.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 04:5x AUSEST. MEASURE FIRST, AND THE MEASUREMENT DECIDES. Do not start by designing a defwrapper change.

THE BEAD IS RIGHT THAT THIS IS A DESIGN QUESTION AND NOT URGENT — the publication-side fix landed with rf2-nvcp and route-link is no longer an instance. But "no KNOWN live instance" is not "no live instance", and the whole reason this class is dangerous is that it fails SILENTLY: a component that is called instead of mounted reads its callers React context, any :contextType on the head is inert, and nothing errors until something downstream needs the context. rf2-nvcp is what that looks like when it finally surfaces — every routed application blank on first render, for two and a half months, with every existing test green.

STEP 1, AND IT SETTLES THE REST: CENSUS EVERY defwrapper HOOK AND CLASSIFY ITS VALUE AS FUNCTION OR COMPONENT. That is a bounded, mechanical question with a real answer. Report the full list, not just the hits.
  - IF THE CENSUS FINDS ANOTHER COMPONENT-VALUED HOOK, this stops being a design question: it is a live defect of the same class that blanked every routed app, and it should be reported as such before anything is designed. Fix it the way rf2-nvcp did — at the PUBLICATION side, with an element-emitting shim — because that fix is proven and leaves defwrapper untouched.
  - IF THE CENSUS FINDS NONE, the honest answer under the stance is to RECORD THE CONSTRAINT where the next author will meet it: a defwrapper :apply hook value must be a FUNCTION, because the emitted body CALLS it, and a component that is called never becomes a component. Put that in defwrapper own docstring in core_artefact.cljc, with rf2-nvcp named as the worked instance. Do not build a runtime check for a constraint with zero live violations — that is gold plating, and the stance says so.

WHAT I AM EXPLICITLY NOT ORDERING: do not change defwrapper emission shape to handle component values. The :apply arity is correct for functions, which is what every other hook is; teaching it a second calling convention to accommodate one case that has already been fixed elsewhere buys nothing and costs a fork in a hot code path.

AND IF THE CENSUS TURNS OUT TO BE HARD TO RUN — if hook values are not statically determinable — SAY SO AND STOP. That is a finding, and it would mean the constraint cannot be checked by any means, which changes the answer to the docstring option by default rather than by preference.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9050 — reopened the exact follow-on for two residual contract carriers. The runtime repair is correct, and PR #9060 later documented the general defwrapper constraint, but current tip still says the opposite at the worked instance: implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_routing.cljc:67-69 says the CLJS hook publishes the Reagent-wrapped render fn returned by reg-view*, and implementation/routing/test/re_frame/late_bind_missing_test.clj:87-89 repeats that model. PR #9050 deliberately changed the hook to publish route-link-element, an element-emitting shim that resolves and mounts the current view head; publishing the head itself is the failure shape that blanked routed apps. Minimal completion: update these two statements to the element-emitting contract. No runtime/macro change or new gate.
close_reason: PR #9112, prose only, per the MERGED-PR AUDIT #9050 note's minimal completion. Both residual statements corrected to the element-emitting contract: implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_routing.cljc:64-69 (route-link's docstring said the CLJS hook publishes the Reagent-wrapped render fn returned by reg-view*; it publishes routing/route-link-element, an ELEMENT-emitting shim - routing.cljc:437-470, set-fn! at :553) and implementation/routing/test/re_frame/late_bind_missing_test.clj:87-89 (same model in a comment). No runtime, macro or gate change, as ruled. PR #9060's general constraint verified present on tip at core_artefact.cljc:62-92 (section 'A hook value MUST be a FUNCTION, never a COMPONENT'). CENSUS (the ruling's step 1), full result: 51 defwrapper forms across the seven core_*.cljc files (epoch 10, flows 2, http 3, resources 15, routing 2, schemas 10, ssr 9), 51 distinct hooks, 1:1. Every value is a plain FUNCTION - registration verbs, clear verbs, query getters, setters, the SSR render/head family (':ssr/*-head' is the HTML head, not a component head). :routing/route-link was the only view-shaped one and is now element-emitting. INDEPENDENT INSTRUMENT: of the 207 set-fn!/chain-fn! publications in non-test source, ZERO close over view-head or reg-view* (control fired: the unfiltered grep returns 207, the filtered one exits 1). So NO component-valued hook remains, the ruling's 'census finds none' branch is the live one, and no runtime check was built. title: Remove inert machine-timer rewrite from schemas fixture loader
description:
## Finding

The schemas conformance loader rewrites every bare auto-resolved keyword `::name` to `:rf.machine.timer/name`, even though no schema fixture contains such a token and the timer namespace belongs to the machines corpus. The code and its `clojure.string` dependency are an inert copy retained only "for symmetry"; if it ever activates on a future schemas fixture, it assigns an unrelated namespace rather than resolving that fixture's namespace.

## Evidence

- `load-fixture` in `implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_conformance_test.clj` (currently lines 146-156) slurps text, applies `str/replace` with `#"::([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*)"` to `":rf.machine.timer/$1"`, then parses it.
- Its own docstring states that schemas fixtures do not use auto-resolved keywords, that the rewrite is for machines/SSR timer events, and that it is a no-op on this subset.
- The runner's exact selected corpus is five files: `error-schema-failure.edn` plus the four `schema-*.edn` fixtures. A controlled token census over those files returns zero `::name` matches, so `raw` and `fixed` are identical for every reachable input today.
- Applying the transform to a probe `::probe` yields `:rf.machine.timer/probe`, proving the claimed future robustness is not schema-generic; it silently invents a machines timer identity.
- The rewrite and commentary entered with the initial schemas runner in `54a3531931` and have never had a schemas-corpus consumer.
- All-status title/description searches for `auto-resolved`, `timer rewrite`, `rf.machine.timer`, and schemas conformance found no issue owning this residue. The one bead description mentioning `rf.machine.timer` concerns retired SSR skill guidance and is unrelated.

## Impact

Every current schemas fixture pays an unnecessary textual preprocessing step and the runner advertises support it does not implement correctly. A future schema fixture using `::foo` would not be rejected or resolved in its authoring namespace; it would be silently changed to a machine timer keyword, potentially making expectations pass or fail under a false identity.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the schemas-only auto-resolved-keyword rewrite, its now-unused `clojure.string` require if nothing else consumes it, and the copied timer-specific prose. Parse the original fixture text directly with `read-one-form`. If schema fixtures later need an alias/namespace facility, define it explicitly in the conformance format instead of borrowing a machines rewrite.

## Risks

Do not remove the analogous transform from machine/SSR/core runners without auditing their selected fixtures; this issue proves only that the schemas subset has zero consumers. Preserve exact-one-form throwing behavior and fixture filename diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria:
- `load-fixture` passes the original schemas fixture text directly to `read-one-form`; it contains no `:rf.machine.timer/$1` replacement or claim of auto-resolved-keyword support.
- `clojure.string` is removed from the schemas conformance namespace if the rewrite was its last use.
- The five selected schemas fixtures still parse and execute with unchanged IDs, capabilities, expectations, and results.
- A focused regression demonstrates that an injected bare `::probe` is not silently reclassified as `:rf.machine.timer/probe` (a parse failure is acceptable until the format defines such syntax).
- Schemas conformance and the full schemas JVM suite pass; machine, SSR, flows, and core fixture loaders are untouched by this slice-local cleanup.
close_reason: PR #9113 (head 6711fbafe1). load-fixture now passes the fixture text to read-one-form verbatim; the ::name -> :rf.machine.timer/name rewrite and the copied timer prose are gone. A focused regression (loader-does-not-restamp-auto-resolved-keywords) pins that a bare ::probe never arrives as :rf.machine.timer/probe; it is live, verified by a negative control that restored the rewrite and turned both assertions red with actual :rf.machine.timer/probe, reproducing the exact silent restamping the bead describes. edn/read rejects ::probe outright (Invalid token), so the loader throws, which the bead permits. The five selected fixtures still load and execute unchanged (373 tests / 19223 assertions, exit 0). PREMISE THAT DID NOT HOLD: the conditional criterion 'remove clojure.string if the rewrite was its last use' does not fire — schema-fixture-file? still calls str/starts-with? and str/ends-with?, so clojure.string stays in the ns. Machine, SSR, flows and core fixture loaders untouched.

title: Delete unreachable schemas conformance load-error skip branch
description:
## Finding

`implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_conformance_test.clj` retains a `(:fixture/load-error fixture)` skip branch even though its loader can no longer return that datum. The branch became unreachable when fixture parsing was changed to throw on every load failure.

## Evidence

- `read-one-form` (currently lines 118-144) throws for an empty fixture, malformed EDN, or more than one top-level form. Its docstring explicitly says it throws rather than returning `:fixture/load-error` because the runner classifies that shape as a skip.
- `load-fixture` (currently lines 146-156) has no catch and returns only the parsed EDN form; `all-schemas-fixtures` invokes it directly before entering the test result loop.
- Nevertheless `run-schemas-conformance-corpus` (currently lines 508-514) still tests `(:fixture/load-error fixture)` and appends a `{:skipped? true :reason "load error" ...}` result. No loader output reaches this arm. The skipped-summary fallback `(:error s)` exists only for this retired result shape.
- Commit `b6e26366a8` removed every loader catch and `{:fixture/load-error ...}` producer specifically because a parse failure must fail the suite rather than disappear as a skip, but it left this consumer branch behind. The follow-up PushbackReader implementation (`f2b899cc497`) preserves the throwing contract.
- All-status title/description searches for `fixture/load-error`, `load error`, and `schemas conformance` found no owning issue. Closed `rf2-98ni` owns the exactly-one-form loader fix; it does not remove this unreachable runner residue.

## Impact

The dead arm preserves and documents precisely the failure policy the loader migration retired: malformed fixtures represented as skips. It makes the runner harder to audit and invites a future loader change to reuse the stale shape, silently weakening the conformance gate. The extra `:error` summary fallback similarly suggests skipped parse failures remain supported.

## Proposed disposition

Delete the `:fixture/load-error` condition/result arm and its error-only skipped-summary rendering from the schemas conformance runner. Keep spec-version and out-of-capability skips intact. Load/parse errors must continue to escape before the result loop and fail the test process.

## Risks

Do not convert thrown fixture errors into ordinary failed or skipped corpus records. The security property of `rf2-98ni` is that malformed/trailing fixtures abort the gate. Preserve the non-empty runnable floor, capability filtering, and ordinary runtime `run-fixture` exception reporting.
acceptance_criteria:
- `rg -n ":fixture/load-error|reason +\"load error\"" implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_conformance_test.clj` finds only explanatory historical text if retained, and no executable branch/result construction.
- A malformed, empty, and two-form selected schemas fixture each makes the focused conformance invocation exit nonzero before results are summarized; none is counted as skipped.
- The five current selected fixtures still load and execute, and the runnable-floor assertions remain non-vacuous.
- Spec-version and unsupported-capability fixtures, when exercised, retain their current explicit skip behavior.
- The schemas JVM suite passes; a planted trailing-form negative control turns the focused gate red and restoring the fixture turns it green.
close_reason: PR #9113 (head 6711fbafe1). Deleted the (:fixture/load-error fixture) cond arm and its skip-result construction from run-schemas-conformance-corpus, plus the (:error s) slot in the skipped-summary that existed only to render that retired shape. A comment in its place records why there is no such arm. Unreachability proven by execution probe, not census alone: a marker in the load-error arm fired 0 times while the same marker in the live :else arm fired 5, matching the five selected fixtures exactly. Negative control fired: a trailing form planted in schema-event-payload-validates.edn turned the focused run red with 1 ERROR and exit 1 ('must hold exactly ONE top-level EDN form'), counted as an error and NOT as a skip; the fixture was restored and verified identical by git hash-object (88cf0752). rg for :fixture/load-error and reason "load error" in the file now finds nothing. Spec-version and capability skips, the runnable-floor assertions (pos? and >= 4) and run-fixture's ordinary runtime exception reporting are untouched. Schemas JVM suite exit 0, 373 tests / 19223 assertions.

title: Remove unreachable walk-schema? branch from schemas validation
description:
## Finding

The private `run-validation` helper in `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc` still accepts a `walk-schema?` boolean and guards both schema sensitivity/opacity inspection and `:large?` inspection with it, but every surviving production caller passes the literal `true`. The false branch is unreachable residue from a retired validation topology.

## Evidence

- `run-validation` declares `[reg-meta value walk-schema? build-base-tags continue?]` (currently line 454).
- Its only reads are the guards around `walker/schema-has-sensitive?` / `schema-has-opaque-child?` (currently lines 544-546) and `walker/schema-has-large?` (currently lines 553-555).
- Repository caller census finds exactly three source calls: `validate-event!`, `validate-sub!`, and `validate-fx!` (currently lines 921, 957, and 1003). Each passes literal `true`; there is no dynamic caller and `run-validation` is private.
- History establishes why the knob existed and why it no longer does. Commit `f899bdd8e4` introduced it as `false` for event validation and `true` for cofx/fx/sub. Commit `14a91d956f` changed event validation to `true` so event payload schemas could drive fail-closed sensitive redaction. Injection-time cofx validation was subsequently retired (`99d37fa6bf`, `f56f5495e7`). The three remaining callers are therefore all on the walking arm.
- All-status bead title and description searches for `walk-schema`, `run-validation walk`, and the validate helper/path found no issue owning this residue.

## Impact

The parameter and two conditional branches advertise a per-surface privacy/size policy choice that no caller can make. That obscures the current invariant: every meta-bearing validation failure consults its schema for sensitivity, opaque children, and large-value elision. A future caller could accidentally pass false and bypass fail-closed diagnostic protection even though no supported contract needs that posture.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `walk-schema?` from the private helper's parameter vector and from all three calls. Make the existing sensitivity/opacity and large-schema walks unconditional within the already-failing branch, preserving sensitive-wins-over-large ordering and all existing redaction markers/tags.

## Risks

This is privacy-sensitive code. Do not move either walk onto the successful hot path, weaken opaque-schema fail-closed handling, change the whole-payload versus leaf-scoped decisions, or disturb the outer `interop/debug-enabled?` gates required for production DCE. Keep the edit mechanical and behavior-neutral for every reachable call.
acceptance_criteria:
- `run-validation` no longer declares or documents `walk-schema?`, and its three callers no longer pass a boolean in that slot.
- A source census shows no `walk-schema?` occurrence and exactly the same three private-helper callers.
- Event, fx, and sub-return tests prove sensitive schema slots and nested opaque children still redact failure payloads; non-sensitive failures remain verbatim.
- Large-schema tests prove non-sensitive values still use `:rf.size/large-elided`, while sensitivity continues to win over large classification.
- Schemas JVM and CLJS suites pass, including stale-incarnation checkpoints.
- The schemas production bundle/elision gate remains green and confirms the dev-only validation body is not newly retained under `:advanced` plus `goog.DEBUG=false`.
close_reason: PR #9113 (head 6711fbafe1). Removed walk-schema? from run-validation's parameter vector and from all three callers (validate-event!/sub!/fx!), which each passed the literal true; both the sensitivity/opacity walk and the :large? walk are now unconditional inside the already-failing branch. Sensitive-wins-over-large ordering, fail-closed opaque handling, whole-payload decision scope, redaction markers and the outer interop/debug-enabled? gates are unchanged. Unreachability proven by execution probe, not census alone: a marker in the false direction fired 0 times across the schemas JVM suite while the same marker in the live true arm fired 50. The parameter bullet's substance was folded into the fn's opening prose rather than deleted. Schemas JVM suite exit 0 (373 tests / 19223 assertions); clj-kondo exit 0, errors 0, and identical findings on the HEAD and changed versions of the file. One walk-schema? token survives repo-wide: a dated past-tense comment at schemas_sensitive_test.clj:1118 recording the rf2-a5kzs fix, which is accurate history in a file rf2-6r9j.55 owns, deliberately left alone.

value:
A CI JOB FAILING WITH 'Failed to read artifact descriptor' IS USUALLY MAVEN CENTRAL RATE-LIMITING US, NOT A CODE DEFECT (2026-09-03).

MEASURED on PR #9110: 'JVM tools/story-mcp (clojure -M:test)' FAILED with
  org.eclipse.aether.resolution.ArtifactDescriptorException: Failed to read artifact descriptor for org.clojure:clojure:jar:1.12.6
  Caused by: ... Could not transfer artifact org.clojure:clojure:pom:1.12.6 from/to central (https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/): status code: 429, reason phrase: Too Many Requests
The PR's eight files were UIx tests, a UIx testbed and ssr-ring — ZERO story-mcp files. It cannot have caused a dependency-resolution failure in another artefact.

WHY IT HAPPENS HERE: the mayor runs six concurrent workers and an automated naming pass runs beside them, so a dozen-plus CI jobs can hit repo1.maven.org at once. 429 is OUR OWN concurrency coming back at us. Expect it to recur whenever the fleet is saturated.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, in order — do NOT dispatch a fix worker before running it:
1. Does the diff touch the failing artefact at all? (paginated file list; gh pr view --json files caps at 100)
2. Is the SAME named check green on other open PRs right now?
3. Was main's last COMPLETED run green on it?
Diff can't reach it + siblings green + main green => infrastructure. Then read the log for the actual exception — 429 / connection reset / 'Could not transfer artifact' names it outright.

REMEDY: 'gh run rerun <run-id> --failed'. NOTE it REFUSES while the workflow is still running ('cannot be rerun; This workflow is already running'), so wait for the run to reach completed. A still-in-progress run also makes 'gh run view --log-failed' return an EMPTY log at exit 0 — zero lines means 'not available yet', never 'no failures'.

ALSO: 'All required checks passed' will fail alongside it. That is test.yml's all-required-passed aggregator reflecting the real failure, not a second independent one — do not count it as two problems.

title: http source/tests: remove sixteen proven dead imports and bindings
description:
## Finding

The HTTP source/test slice retains sixteen statically proven dead imports, aliases, referred macros, or local destructurings after excluding reader-conditional and intentional load-time registrations.

## Evidence

A clean `clj-kondo --lint implementation/http/src implementation/http/test --cache false` plus exact-symbol searches identifies:

Production (4 findings):
- `reply.cljc:169`: explicitly destructured `origin-event` and `issuance` locals are unused; `:as ctx` is what `work-id` consumes, so the keys remain available without these local bindings.
- `transport.cljc:1248`: `request-id` is destructured in `maybe-retry!` but never referenced.
- `transport_jvm.cljc:40`: `java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture` is imported but never used or type-hinted in that adapter (the shared `transport.cljc` has its own live import/use).

Tests (12 findings):
- `http_jvm_headers_shape_test.clj:34`: unused `java.util.List` import.
- `http_managed_test.clj:18`: unused `re-frame.http.encoding` alias, plus unused `server` destructurings at lines 402, 426, 455, and 491 (`srv` is retained for teardown and `port` is the only key read).
- `http_privacy_integration_test.clj:20`: unused `re-frame.registrar` alias.
- `http_restore_quiesce_test.clj:28`: unused `re-frame.http.transport` alias; the namespace is already reached through the required `re-frame.http.managed` closure.
- `http_transport_security_test.clj:4,6`: unused `use-fixtures` refer and unused `re-frame.http.privacy` alias; transport already loads privacy.
- `http_url_percent_encoded_redaction_cljs_test.cljc:17-18`: unused `use-fixtures` refer on both CLJ and CLJS branches.

Exact searches find no symbol use in the owning files. History explains several leftovers (for example privacy integration/core registration tests and transport security changed while their old imports remained). Bead title/description searches for these imports and lint findings found no existing HTTP cleanup issue.

The audit deliberately excludes clj-kondo noise that is not dead: opposite-host adapter requires and `ctx`/`abort-signal` are reader-conditional; explicit `re-frame.http.managed` test requires trigger effect/hook registration; `with-new-frame [f ...]` establishes dynamic frame scope even where the local symbol is unread; test interleave and registry snapshots are documented diagnostics.

## Impact

These remnants imply dependencies/dataflow that do not exist and keep the HTTP lint baseline noisy, making a newly introduced unused binding easier to miss. The four stale server locals and duplicate imports also obscure what each test actually controls.

## Proposed disposition

Remove only the listed unused imports/requires/refers and narrow the listed destructuring forms. Do not mechanically delete load-bearing side-effect requires or cross-host bindings.

## Risks / retained contracts

Namespace requires can be intentional for load effects. For each removal, run the owning namespace in its normal and focused/isolated lane; if an alleged alias is proven load-bearing despite its transitive closure, retain it with a local comment explaining the effect. Preserve `:as ctx`, `srv`, frame macros, and platform reader branches.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The sixteen listed clj-kondo findings are removed, or any demonstrated load-bearing require is retained with an explicit side-effect comment and evidence.
2. `clj-kondo --lint implementation/http/src implementation/http/test --cache false` no longer reports these findings; opposite-host reader-conditional warnings are not “fixed” by breaking platform namespaces.
3. Focused HTTP JVM namespaces and the full HTTP JVM suite pass with unchanged test counts; consolidated CLJS tests pass, including the cross-host URL test.
4. Tests that rely on `re-frame.http.managed` registration, frame-scoping macros, transport adapter selection, and diagnostic seams retain those contracts.
5. No unrelated formatting, naming, or behavior change is bundled into the cleanup.
close_reason: PR #9115. Census RE-DERIVED from the current tree (post-PR #9081) rather than taken from the bead: all SIXTEEN listed findings were still present, only line numbers had moved (transport.cljc 1248 -> 1243), and #9081 had created no new orphan in this artefact. All sixteen removed. clj-kondo --lint implementation/http/src implementation/http/test --cache false went 50 -> 34 warnings, the diff being exactly those sixteen lines with no new finding surfaced. Each deletion proven with two instruments plus a firing control (exact git grep -F over tracked files + clj-kondo var-usage); the control earned its keep - a coarse grep -F 'rf/' read 59 hits in http_privacy_test.clj that are all the :rf/redacted KEYWORD, not an alias. Transitive closures verified rather than assumed: re-frame.http.transport reached via managed -> handlers -> transport (handlers.cljc:29), re-frame.http.privacy via that same transport require. The four server destructurings narrowed to {:keys [port] :as srv}, the form 27 sibling sites in the file already use. Dangling prose fixed rather than deleted: http_transport_security_test.clj:203 now reads re-frame.http.privacy/prepare-emit-tags. Gates: http JVM 506 tests/3882 assertions 0 failures exit 0; npm run test:cljs 11169 tests/55740 assertions exit 0. Gate proven LIVE - a planted assertion break in http_reply_lowering_test.clj reddened the JVM suite (exit 1, FAIL in work-id-head), restored and verified byte-identical by git hash-object cedc9166ab43. THREE findings deliberately left, all outside this census: http_privacy_test.clj:22 and http_retry_on_validation_test.clj:19 unused re-frame.core aliases are NOT dead - core.cljc:228 carries a top-level (rf.late-bind/set-fns! ...) publishing :core/dispatch-impl / :core/dispatch-sync-impl / :core/subscribe-impl and nothing else in either file's closure loads the facade, so these are load-bearing requires per this bead's own Risks section (the first was newly orphaned by #9081); routing_http_composed_corners_test.clj:265 unused binding url is real but a different class - the fx-handler arity [_ url] is load-bearing so the repair is a rename to _url, neither a removal nor a narrowing and outside the stated disposition.

title: http reply: remove the never-consumed duplicate transport-request-id helper
description:
## Finding

`re-frame.http.reply/transport-request-id` is a never-consumed duplicate constructor for `[:rf.req frame-id work-id]`. The only shipped producer of that token is the Resources work-ledger’s separate `managed-request-id` implementation.

## Evidence

- Fixed-string and resolved-var searches across implementation, tools, examples, skills, docs, and specs find no production call to `http-reply/transport-request-id` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/reply.cljc:99-107`). Its only calls are shape assertions in `http_reply_lowering_test.clj:138-140` and `http_reply_lowering_cljs_test.cljc:38-40`; the remaining hit is its own namespace prose.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/work_ledger.cljc:148-169` defines the byte-for-byte equivalent `managed-request-id` and is the actual runtime authority. Resources transport/teardown code and multiple Resources tests use that function to issue, supersede, and abort managed HTTP work.
- History makes the duplication explicit: Resources added `managed-request-id` in `450cdd44a1` at 11:53 on 2026-06-11. HTTP added the identical helper later that day in `b6789084b2` while introducing reply lowering, but no runtime call edge was ever added; `git log -S` shows creation only.
- The HTTP artifact accepts a caller-chosen `:request-id` and does not itself know when a caller needs frame qualification. The frame-local Resources owner is therefore the layer that has both identities and constructs the transport token.
- The helper is absent from the generated API manifest and HTTP user facade/docs. Specs require the token shape, not this unused constructor. Exact-symbol, title, description, and broader transport-correlation bead searches found no existing issue.

## Impact

Two implementations claim authority for a security-relevant process-global correlation identity, while HTTP’s copy has no consumer. Its focused tests can stay green if the real Resources constructor or lowering path changes, overstating coverage and inviting tuple-shape drift.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `re-frame.http.reply/transport-request-id`, its two direct shape assertions, and the namespace sentence claiming it builds the identity. Keep the canonical token shape documented and tested through the live `re-frame.resources.work-ledger/managed-request-id` path. Do not add an HTTP -> Resources dependency. If a second production owner emerges, extract one genuinely shared lower-layer constructor rather than retaining parallel copies.

## Risks / retained contracts

The var is public at the namespace level but is unmanifested and has never had an in-repo production caller, so an unknown downstream direct-require is the only compatibility risk. Preserve `http-reply/work-id` and all reply correlation behavior; this finding concerns only the unused frame-qualification helper, not the `:request-id` accepted by managed HTTP.
acceptance_criteria:
1. HTTP reply code no longer ships an unconsumed duplicate `transport-request-id`, or a concrete production caller and ownership rationale is added.
2. The `[:rf.req frame-id work-id]` contract remains implemented once on the live Resources lowering/teardown path (or in a truly shared dependency-safe owner) and is covered on JVM/CLJS as applicable.
3. HTTP reply-lowering tests continue to cover HTTP work IDs and canonical replies without asserting a helper the runtime never invokes.
4. Resources managed-HTTP issuance, cross-frame isolation, supersession, and opportunistic-abort tests pass; HTTP JVM/CLJS suites pass.
5. Repo-wide searches show no stale HTTP helper/doc reference and no new HTTP -> Resources dependency cycle.
close_reason: PR #9115. Removed re-frame.http.reply/transport-request-id, its two shape assertions (http_reply_lowering_test.clj:138-140, http_reply_lowering_cljs_test.cljc:38-40) and the namespace sentence claiming it builds the identity. Proven unconsumed with two instruments plus firing controls: repo-wide git grep -F over tracked files returned only its own defn, its own prose and the two test assertions (control 'success-reply' hit 24 files); clj-kondo var-usage analysis over implementation/ returned 3 usage records, all test namespaces, 0 from src (controls: success-reply 21, work-id 33). Surviving original named and verified equivalent: re-frame.resources.work-ledger/managed-request-id at work_ledger.cljc:148, identical body [frame-id work-id] -> [:rf.req frame-id work-id], with four production callers (resources/events.cljc 653/977/1149, resources/mutation_events.cljc 1271). Namespace prose now names that constructor so the token shape stays documented; no HTTP -> Resources dependency added. CLJS deftest work-id-and-transport-id renamed work-id-head (no other reference existed). Gates: http JVM 506 tests/3882 assertions exit 0; npm run test:cljs 11169 tests/55740 assertions exit 0.
