title: Remove UIx's no-doc direct warn-cache reset export
description:
## Scope

Remove only the undocumented direct UIx namespace export re-frame.adapter.uix/clear-warned-non-dom-roots! and the tests/configuration that keep that export alive. Preserve the spine's private clear thunk, its registration in the canonical :adapter/clear-warn-once-caches! chain, the warn-once cache itself, and fixture isolation. Reconcile the UIx public-surface guard with the actual supported UIx API while touching that stale roster.

## Vestigial finding

The UIx adapter exposes a ^:no-doc cache-reset Var that has no caller outside its own legacy shared-suite configuration. The reset behavior was superseded by the canonical chained reset hook, which the standard fixture and governance tests already drive. The namespace export is therefore a second, unsupported door to an internal test seam.

## Evidence and reachability proof

- implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:192-197 defines ^:no-doc clear-warned-non-dom-roots! as a direct alias of the spine thunk.
- A repository-wide exact search for uix-adapter/clear-warned-non-dom-roots! finds only implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_react_shared_cljs_test.cljs:75 and :88. There are no production, documentation, example, skill, tool, or other test consumers.
- spec/api-manifest.edn:59-67 enumerates the supported UIx namespace as adapter plus eight functions and deliberately omits this ^:no-doc Var. The generated API docs and Spec 006 likewise omit it.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:3405-3410 consumes the underlying (:clear-warned-non-dom-roots! spine-fns) directly and registers it through install-clear-warn-once-step!, independent of the UIx namespace alias.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc:450-472 makes :adapter/clear-warn-once-caches! a post-dispose reset hook; all UIx tests using make-reset-runtime-fixture therefore reach the canonical chain without calling the namespace Var.
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:1219-1240 already proves the chain re-arms the same warning id end-to-end. implementation/core/test/re_frame/warn_once_clear_governance_cljs_test.cljs:109-133 independently arms every enrolled cache, fires the canonical chain, and proves each cache cleared.
- The only direct-seam proof is react_shared_suite.cljs:1242-1255, fed by the UIx cfg's :clear-warn! key. It duplicates behavior already proven at the public fixture/chained boundary.
- The same shared suite's so-called public-surface roster is stale: react_shared_suite.cljs:2497-2534 and the UIx cfg at :78-88 call seven functions public, omit the supported frame-root and use-frame exports, but include this unsupported no-doc reset. The manifest instead has eight supported functions.
- git history shows the standalone alias arrived with the original fixture-cache repair (724a018b49, 2026-05-12), was moved through the shared spine (e0a659445d), and was marked ^:no-doc during API-manifest governance (994c4e3489, 2026-06-01). No later consumer appeared.

## Impact

The extra Var expands the callable namespace surface without an API contract, encourages tests to bypass the reset mechanism whose chaining/governance is the actual invariant, and makes the "public surface" test guard assert the wrong API. Because that guard omits frame-root and use-frame, it can stay green if a real supported export disappears while failing if an internal reset alias is removed.

## Recommended disposition

Delete the UIx alias. Remove or internalize the direct-clear shared-suite row and its :clear-warn! configuration so tests exercise the canonical hook/fixture boundary. Update the UIx public-surface roster to the eight supported functions from the API manifest: add frame-root and use-frame, omit clear-warned-non-dom-roots!, and avoid maintaining another contradictory hand-written API count if the manifest metadata can drive the assertion.

## Risks

The Var is technically callable by an external program despite ^:no-doc, so removal can break an unsupported caller that discovered it from source. Do not delete the underlying spine thunk or chain registration: that would recreate cross-test warn suppression and is explicitly outside this task. Hicasso reads its private spine map in the shared suite; preserve its internal coverage or migrate it to the same canonical chain rather than treating that map key as a public Hicasso export.
acceptance_criteria:
- re-frame.adapter.uix no longer defines clear-warned-non-dom-roots!, and no UIx test/config refers to it.
- The spine still creates the per-adapter warn cache, registers its clear thunk through install-clear-warn-once-step!, and exposes no new public reset API.
- make-reset-runtime-fixture still fires :adapter/clear-warn-once-caches! after disposal; a focused UIx proof emits once, suppresses a duplicate, runs the canonical reset, and observes the same id emit once again.
- The warn-once governance test still enumerates and clears the UIx/Hicasso spine cache. Non-vacuity/control: disabling the spine's chain registration makes the focused or governance proof fail.
- Remove or internalize the direct-only assert-clear-warned-non-dom-roots-resets-directly test and :clear-warn! cfg dependency; do not replace the public alias with another test-only namespace export.
- The UIx public-surface guard matches the supported manifest surface: eight functions (set-hiccup-emitter!, use-current-frame, frame-provider, frame-root, use-subscribe, use-frame, flush-views!, wrap-view), with adapter checked separately. It omits the internal cache reset.
- Reconcile shared-suite comments/assertion counts so they do not claim a seven-Var cross-adapter public surface that conflicts with the UIx API manifest or treat Hicasso's private spine map as an exported namespace.
- API manifest output remains unchanged for UIx, and the UIx/shared React-adapter, fixture-isolation, and warn-once governance suites remain green.
notes:
2026-09-03, worker/uixring-a (PR #9110 landed .38 and .50 only). NOT DONE — fence-blocked, not premise-failed. The public-surface question is settled in favour of removal: re-frame.adapter.uix/clear-warned-non-dom-roots! is ^:no-doc; spec/api-manifest.edn lists re-frame.adapter.uix as 'adapter' plus EIGHT fns (flush-views!, frame-provider, frame-root, set-hiccup-emitter!, use-current-frame, use-frame, use-subscribe, wrap-view) and deliberately omits it, so it was never a documented or supported export; and a repo-wide exact census of 'uix-adapter/clear-warned-non-dom-roots!' over tracked files excluding .beads returns exactly TWO hits, both in its own shared-suite entry file (uix_react_shared_cljs_test.cljs:75 as :clear-warn! and :88 inside :public-surface). Zero production, docs, examples, skills, tools or other-artefact consumers. Every other clear-warned-non-dom-roots! hit in the repo reaches the seam through a DIFFERENT door — re-frame.views/, warn-once/, or (:clear-warned-non-dom-roots! spine-fns) — so none routes through the UIx namespace and none breaks.

WHY IT COULD NOT LAND HERE. The change set spans four files, three outside this worker's fence (implementation/adapters/uix/**, implementation/ssr-ring/**, tools/machines-viz/**), and partial application is strictly worse than none:
  1. implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:192-197 — delete the alias. IN FENCE.
  2. implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_react_shared_cljs_test.cljs:75,88 — drop :clear-warn! and fix :public-surface. IN FENCE.
  3. implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs — OUT OF FENCE. Holds def ^:private public-surface-keys (:2527-2534), a SHARED cross-adapter roster naming all seven keys including :clear-warned-non-dom-roots!, iterated by assert-public-vars-present-and-callable as (is (fn? (get public-surface k))). Also holds assert-clear-warned-non-dom-roots-resets-directly (:1242-1255), which calls (clear-warn!).
  4. implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite_tests.clj:172 — OUT OF FENCE. The forwarder row {:fn 'assert-clear-warned-non-dom-roots-resets-directly}.
  5. implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/substrate_react_shared_cljs_test.cljs:63,66 — OUT OF FENCE. The ONLY other supplier of :clear-warn! / :public-surface, feeding them from (:clear-warned-non-dom-roots! substrate/spine-fns).
Removing the two keys from the UIx cfg alone makes (get public-surface :clear-warned-non-dom-roots!) return nil -> (fn? nil) false -> RED, and (clear-warn!) on nil -> RED. Deleting the alias without also editing the UIx cfg is a compile error.

DISPATCH SHAPE. This needs ONE worker holding implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/** + implementation/hicasso/test/** + implementation/adapters/uix/**, in a single PR. Note the acceptance criterion's eight-function roster adds frame-root and use-frame, which the shared seven-key roster does not carry at all — so public-surface-keys must become per-adapter (cfg-supplied) rather than a shared constant, since Hicasso's supported set is not UIx's. Only UIx and Hicasso drive that assertion; reagent and reagent-slim supply neither key.
close_reason: Landed in PR #9117 (head 9ee10373af). re-frame.adapter.uix/clear-warned-non-dom-roots! DELETED. Public-surface account: ^:no-doc, no spec/api-manifest.edn row (UIx is rowed as adapter + eight fns; the generator drops ^:no-doc vars, so manifest output is unchanged and 'clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check' exits 0 with 'in sync (528 public vars)' and spec/ untouched); exact census of uix-adapter/clear-warned-non-dom-roots! returned exactly two hits, both in its own shared-suite entry file, zero production/docs/example/skill/tool callers; every other clear-warned-non-dom-roots! hit reaches the seam via re-frame.views/, warn-once/ or (:clear-warned-non-dom-roots! spine-fns) and is unaffected. Spine unchanged: per-adapter warn cache, install-clear-warn-once-step! registration and governance enrolment all intact. The :clear-warn! cfg key is GONE from the shared-suite contract and both entry files; MUST(3) idempotent-post-dispose and the G5 fire-once re-arm now fire the chained :adapter/clear-warn-once-caches! late-bind hook (exactly what make-reset-runtime-fixture does after disposal), and assert-clear-warned-non-dom-roots-resets-directly plus its test-specs forwarder row are deleted as a duplicate of assert-chained-clear-warn-once-empties-cache. Seven-key-vs-eight-fn wrinkle resolved by making the roster cfg-supplied per adapter (:public-surface-keys): UIx now carries its eight manifest fns (frame-root and use-frame ADDED, clear thunk dropped), Hicasso its six published spine surfaces, and a new assertion pins roster == :public-surface map keys so neither side can drift into decoration; assert-public-vars-distinct-fns derives its count from the roster instead of hard-coding 7. Gates: npm run test:cljs (consolidated node-test covering core + UIx + Hicasso) exit 0, 11167 tests / 55739 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors; liveness control (dropping :frame-root from the UIx :public-surface map only) exit 1 with 2 failures both naming frame-root in the new roster machinery, then reverted and confirmed byte-identical by git hash-object.

title: Machines namespaces: canonical rf.* require-alias migration
description:
Sibling of rf2-6r9j.161 (core, landed in PR #9103) and rf2-6r9j.167 (routing, same PR). implementation/machines was NOT covered by either bead and has no owner.

Measured on the PR #9103 tree with the same scanner that reproduced both beads' clj-kondo censuses exactly (core 1616, routing 438):

  implementation/machines: 835 noncanonical require edges across 192 files.

The rule is spec/Conventions.md §Require-alias dialect: re-frame.core keeps the bare root alias rf, every other re-frame.<tail> takes the dotted rf.<tail>, and the bare leaf form is reserved for application namespaces. Machines currently spells them bare throughout (machines/, mtest/, plain-atom/, frame/, trace/, timer/, parallel/, spawn-order/ …).

Two things the core/routing pass learned, which this one will meet again:

1. HOST-CONDITIONAL ALIASES ARE AN EXEMPTION, NOT A MISS. birth_always_cljs_test.cljc binds one alias to two namespaces across reader arms — #?(:clj [re-frame.substrate.plain-atom :as substrate-adapter] :cljs [re-frame.adapter.reagent :as substrate-adapter]). The shared name IS the point; per-arm dotted tails would give the single use site two names. Leave it and say so. (Eight routing suites had the same shape.)

2. SOURCE-SCANNING GATES READ CALL SITES AS TEXT. destroyed_reason_channel_conformance_test.clj:468 matches the fixed string "trace/emit!" — that one still matches after the rename because rf.trace/emit! contains it, but the class is real: core's late_bind_drift_test and warn_once_clear_governance_test both had to widen, and the governance one would have FAILED OPEN (it forbids a call shape, so a spelling it cannot see is an offender it waves through). Grep for regex/fixed-string gates over machines src before assuming a green means anything.

Scope note: PR #9103 deliberately left the three machines test files it renamed (rf2-6r9j.164) in the artefact's current dialect rather than migrating them mid-move — a half-migrated artefact reads worse than a uniformly unmigrated one. This bead migrates the artefact as a whole.

The syntax-aware CI ratchet both parent beads asked for is still unbuilt (see rf2-6r9j.161 acceptance); it belongs in scripts/ + .github/workflows/ and should be one ratchet for the whole repo, not one per artefact.
notes:
SWEEP LANDED — PR #9114 (head 69d26d2e23c4a719d42718b9a7a456eef02d861c), branch worker/machalias-a.

839 noncanonical require edges across 194 files migrated to the dotted rf.<tail> dialect, plus the 3449 qualified use sites that move with them (auto-resolved ::alias/key keywords included — ::result/depth-abort? and ::rf.machines.result/depth-abort? denote the same keyword). The bead's 835/192 reproduces: a textual scan counts 841 edges across 194 files, of which 2 are the documented host-conditional exemption in ONE file, leaving exactly 835 in 192 files once .cljc reader arms are deduplicated the way the bead's clj-kondo census did.

EXEMPTION HONOURED, exactly as the bead predicted: birth_always_cljs_test.cljc binds one alias `substrate-adapter` to two namespaces across reader arms. It is the ONLY such shape in machines, and the check that found it is DERIVED rather than listed — an alias bound to 2+ distinct namespaces within one file — so it cannot rot.

SOURCE-SCANNING GATES: NO WIDENING NEEDED, and this was measured rather than assumed. late_bind_drift_test and warn_once_clear_governance_test were already widened by PR #9103 to accept both spellings via an optional rf. prefix, so machines' rename lands inside a pattern that already covers it. Re-run against the migrated tree: 9 tests / 696 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0. destroyed_reason_channel_conformance_test.clj's (str/includes? s "trace/emit!") pre-filter still matches because rf.trace/emit! contains it, and its structural call-name reads (name (first form)), which is alias-insensitive. tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab reads five machines source files but reader-parses them and asserts on keyword map keys — 94 tests / 1031 assertions green. No route-hook! call site exists in machines src, so the drift gate's substrate-adapter/route-hook! pattern has no machines subject.

GATES: machines JVM 1241 tests / 4495 assertions exit 0; node bundle 11170 tests / 55746 assertions exit 0; clj-kondo identical to a pristine baseline of the same tree once columns and alias text are normalised (1623 warnings both sides, zero delta; the single kondo error-level finding is in implementation/epoch, present on the baseline, and an artefact of local kondo v2025.10.23 vs CI's pinned 2026.04.15). JVM gate proven live first: a planted rf.machines.pathsX/snapshot-path returned exit 1 naming classification.cljc:110:9, and restoring returned blob 0aa312e11b024e2a9de853c26cdacfe305d76fcd.

===========================================================================
DESIGN FOR THE REPO-WIDE SYNTAX-AWARE RATCHET (not built here — scripts/ + .github/workflows/ are hot-zone; this is for a workflow lane)
===========================================================================

WHERE. One checker, scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py, in the same Python house style as check_doc_slugs.py / check_readme_links.py (no JVM start-up, so it can also join the fast-PR spine). One job in .github/workflows/lint.yml, which already owns the lint_surface gating — NOT a new workflow file, and NOT one ratchet per artefact. Per-artefact is what makes this rot: machines went unowned precisely because rf2-6r9j.161 and rf2-6r9j.167 each fenced their own tree.

WHY SYNTAX-AWARE AND NOT GREP. Four textual traps, each measured on this sweep, each of which a line-oriented regex ratchet gets wrong:

  (1) A LITERAL SINGLE-COLON KEYWORD IS NOT AN ALIAS REFERENCE, AND A DOUBLE-COLON ONE IS. machines carries 179 sites of the shape :machines/rearm-after-hydration!, :router/dispatch!, :cofx/eval-recordable-sub, :frame/destroyed, :corner.timer/scoped — late-bind keys, trace channels and frame ids whose first segment collides with a live alias — against 7 sites of ::result/... , which MUST move. A first pass here that treated the colon as a word boundary rewrote 42 late-bind keys into new keyword values; nothing failed, because a renamed late-bind key is only read back by another renamed site in the same file. The control that caught it was counting :rf.machines/ — 0 before, 42 after, a count that should have been constant.

  (2) FULLY-QUALIFIED, QUOTED AND VAR-QUOTED FORMS EACH NEED DIFFERENT HANDLING. re-frame.machines.paths/snapshot-path must not move; a quoted 're-frame.fx/dispatch-later-timers and (requiring-resolve 're-frame.conformance/eval-value*) must not move; but #'parallel/reduce-regions MUST move, and an apostrophe is both a quote reader macro and a legal symbol-body character, so the two are told apart only by what precedes the quote.

  (3) REPO-RELATIVE DOC PATHS SHARE A FIRST SEGMENT WITH LIVE ALIASES. spec/conformance/fixtures/, docs/machines/..., core/test/re_frame, ../../spec/conformance. This is the same class the core sweep met as spec/API.md (33 spared sites) and it recurs in every artefact.

  (4) MULTI-LINE REQUIRE VECTORS DEFEAT ANY SINGLE-LINE REGEX, AND THE MISS IS SILENT. parallel.cljc opens [re-frame.machines.result :as result and closes the vector on the NEXT line. A regex anchored on the closing bracket skipped that libspec and, with it, 116 use sites — while reporting a clean run. The scanner has to find the libspec vector by balanced brackets, not by line.

MECHANISM. For each git-tracked .clj/.cljs/.cljc under implementation/, tools/, examples/, testbeds/ and skills/: locate every libspec vector whose head symbol is re-frame or starts re-frame. by balanced-bracket scan; read its :as / :as-alias; require the alias to be rf for re-frame.core and rf.<tail> otherwise. Count edges per (file, ns, alias) triple so a .cljc binding the same alias in both reader arms is ONE edge, not two — that is the dedup the bead's own census applied and the reason a naive count reads 841 where the bead reads 835.

EXEMPTION RULE, DERIVED NOT LISTED. A libspec is exempt when the SAME alias is bound to two or more distinct namespaces within the same file. That is exactly the host-conditional reader-arm shape and it needs no allowlist to maintain — machines has one instance, routing had eight, core one. An allowlist of file paths would go stale on the first rename; this predicate cannot.

SHAPE: A PER-SURFACE FLOOR, NOT A ZERO GATE. core, routing, http and (with this PR) machines are clean, but adapters/, schemas/, flows/, epoch/, resources/, ssr/, ssr-node/, security/, tools/, examples/, testbeds/ and skills/ are NOT — skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:72 still spells [re-frame.machines :as machines], and docs/, migration/ and spec/006 line 2022 carry noncanonical examples in prose. So: a checked-in scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn mapping top-level surface to allowed violation count, failing when a surface EXCEEDS its baseline. Migrated surfaces sit at 0 and can never regress; unmigrated ones ratchet down as beads land. Same shape as scripts/check-ai-tracking-ratchet.sh, which is the in-repo precedent.

IT MUST SHIP WITH A POSITIVE FIXTURE. A checker whose subject is ABSENCE is green when it stops firing — the defect class this repo keeps finding in its own instruments, and the reason lint.yml already carries a fixture-witness step for hicasso's kondo export. Plant one bare alias under scripts/_test_fixtures/ and assert the checker names it, in the same job.

FOLLOW-ON (separate beads, not this ratchet): the noncanonical spellings left OUTSIDE implementation/machines that this sweep observed but did not own — skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs, docs/resources/tutorial/05-test-and-ship.md, docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md, docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/baseline/**, migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md line 1698, spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md line 2022, and the ~15 reagent-adapter examples across docs/. The user-facing machines docs (docs/machines/*, docs/api/re-frame.machines.md, spec/005, spec/008) already teach rf.machines and need nothing.
close_reason:
PR #9114. implementation/machines migrated as a whole to the spec/Conventions.md §Require-alias dialect: 839 noncanonical require edges across 194 files, plus the 3449 qualified use sites that move with them. Matches what core and routing landed in PR #9103 — full dotted tail, so re-frame.machines.lifecycle-fx.resolver takes rf.machines.lifecycle-fx.resolver — rather than inventing a shorter variant.

The bead's 835/192 reproduces exactly: 841 textual edges across 194 files, minus the 2 host-conditional exemption edges in one file, is 835 across 192 once .cljc reader arms are deduplicated the way the bead's clj-kondo census did.

EXEMPTION, as the bead predicted: birth_always_cljs_test.cljc binds one alias `substrate-adapter` to two namespaces across reader arms. The only such shape in machines, and the predicate that finds it is derived (an alias bound to 2+ namespaces within one file), not a path list, so it cannot rot.

NEITHER NAMED SOURCE-SCANNING GATE NEEDED WIDENING — measured, not assumed. late_bind_drift_test and warn_once_clear_governance_test were already widened by PR #9103 to accept an optional rf. prefix, so machines' rename lands inside patterns that already cover it; re-run against the migrated tree they give 9 tests / 696 assertions, 0 failures. destroyed_reason_channel_conformance_test's "trace/emit!" pre-filter still matches (rf.trace/emit! contains it) and its structural call-name is alias-insensitive. tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab reads five machines src files but reader-parses them and asserts on keyword map keys: 94 tests / 1031 assertions green. No route-hook! call site exists in machines src.

A THIRD GATE DID FIRE, and it is the one this class had not met before. scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py CHECK B reads every :rf.* keyword NAMESPACE out of implementation/**/src and demands a reserved-namespace row in spec/Conventions.md; its extractor cannot tell `::rf.x/y` from `:rf.x/y`. The sweep's one auto-resolved keyword in framework SOURCE — `(dissoc info ::rf.machines.result/depth-abort? ...)` in machines.cljc — therefore read as a literal reserved-root keyword and demanded a row that would have been a FALSE reservation. This is inherent to the dialect: the canonical rf.<tail> alias textually shadows the :rf.<area> reserved keyword root, and machines is the FIRST artefact to produce such a form (`git grep '::rf\.' -- implementation/*/src` returned nothing on main). Fixed inside the fence by spelling the sentinel fully-qualified, `:re-frame.machines.result/depth-abort?` — same keyword, unambiguous to reader and scanner alike — with a comment recording why so a later sweep does not canonicalise it back. The checker's own gap is carried on rf2-ydpr with the one-line correction written out.

NO KEYWORD ID MOVED, and this is the control that proves it rather than a claim: the multiset of every literal single-colon :ns/name keyword across the artefact is IDENTICAL before and after, zero entries changed. title: test-quiet exit-integrity regression misses both safeguarded branches
description:
## Correctness finding

The CLJS exit-integrity regression added with the two production safeguards does not exercise either safeguarded failure mode. It repeats a normal red fixture invocation that was already covered before the safeguards landed, so both safeguards can be removed while the named regression remains green.

## Evidence

- `implementation/test-quiet/src/re_frame/test_quiet/shadow_node.cljs:122-156` documents and implements two independent protections: catch a throw from `replay-buffered-warnings!` before `js/process.exit 1`, and seed `process.exitCode = 1` before a run so a missing `:end-run-tests` dispatch cannot drain to exit 0.
- Commit `45fbaaa4dd` introduced both protections and `deliberately-failing-test-exits-nonzero` together. Its parent already had the ordinary default reporter branch `(do (replay-buffered-warnings!) (js/process.exit 1))`, so a normal red run already exited 1 whenever replay completed.
- `implementation/test-quiet/test/re_frame/test_quiet_shadow_node_cljs_test.cljs:712-756` invokes the ordinary armed warning fixture and ordinary unarmed fixture. It neither makes replay throw nor prevents/delays the custom `:end-run-tests` method. Therefore it traverses the pre-existing normal red/green exits, not either new protection.
- The exact armed child invocation was already present before the fix in `red-run-replays-buffered-console-warn` (introduced by `a89226ca3f`): current lines 612-635 use the same namespace and `RF2_TQ_RED_WARN_FIXTURE=1`, and already assert no spawn error, no timeout, nonzero status, and the replayed marker. Current lines 636-657 already repeat the same fixture unarmed and assert exit 0 and quiet canonical output. The later test adds only `Ran`/`FAIL in` assertions to duplicate child processes.
- `end-run-tests-exit-decision` at lines 270-281 calls upstream `cljs.test/successful?` and checks only that some method exists. ClojureScript 1.12.145 itself defines a no-op `[:cljs.test/default :end-run-tests]` method at `cljs/test.cljs:359`, so method presence does not prove that test-quiet owns the exit behavior.
- All-state bead searches for the regression names, seeded exit, replay exception, copied/default predicate, and duplicate spawn found no existing issue. The legacy `rf2-jmrdhn` identifier referenced by the commit is not present in the current bead store.

## Impact

A regression can remove the replay exception guard or the seeded fallback while every current exit-integrity assertion stays green. The suite therefore claims protection against the exact false-green hazards described by the production code without discriminating them, while paying for two redundant Node child starts.

## Proposed disposition

Replace or augment the ordinary red process row with controlled process-level fixtures for the two protected branches. Add an env-gated seam that makes replay throw after a genuine failure, and a separate env-gated seam that lets a started run drain without the test-quiet `:end-run-tests` exit (for example a controlled no-op reporter dispatch). Fold the ordinary `Ran`/`FAIL in` checks into the existing warning-replay row instead of spawning the same armed/unarmed pair twice. Remove or repurpose `end-run-tests-exit-decision`; a direct pure helper is acceptable only if it is the helper the production defmethod invokes.

## Risks / retained contracts

Keep the real child-process boundary because exit status cannot be proven in-process. A control must prove its fixture ran and reached the intended exceptional/missing-dispatch state; an unrelated parse error, uncaught fixture error, timeout, or skipped suite also exits nonzero and must not satisfy it. Preserve normal red warning replay, normal green quietness, both focused and whole-suite seeding call sites, and the compile-cycle boundary that keeps `shadow-node` out of the test namespace's requires.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the existing `deliberately-failing-test-exits-nonzero` regression and confirm its ordinary armed-red and unarmed-green child rows pass.
2. In a disposable branch, remove the `seed-failure-exit!` calls from the focused and whole-suite entry points, leaving the ordinary reporter path intact; rerun the named regression. It remains green because the normal `:end-run-tests` path still exits 1.
3. Restore the seed, remove the `try`/`catch` around `replay-buffered-warnings!`, and rerun the same regression. It remains green because its fixture never makes replay throw.
4. Compare the child invocations with `red-run-replays-buffered-console-warn`; they use the same ordinary warning fixture, demonstrating that neither protected exceptional branch is selected.
5. Treat a future control as valid only when it emits a reached-state marker for the replay-throws or missing-dispatch branch; a generic nonzero child status is not sufficient.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A real spawned red run forces warning replay itself to throw, proves a genuine test failure was reached, and still exits nonzero; removing the replay `try`/`catch` makes this control fail for the intended reason.
2. A real spawned run starts tests but deliberately bypasses or no-ops the test-quiet `:end-run-tests` exit, then drains with status 1 from the seeded `process.exitCode`; removing `seed-failure-exit!` makes this control fail with status 0.
3. Each fault fixture emits an unambiguous reached-state marker and assertions reject spawn errors, timeouts, parse failures, skipped tests, and unrelated uncaught exceptions as alternate explanations for nonzero status.
4. Ordinary armed red warning replay and unarmed green quietness remain covered once each, including `Ran`/`FAIL in`, warning marker, canonical green output, and exit status; the duplicate armed/unarmed child invocations are removed.
5. `end-run-tests-exit-decision` no longer treats upstream `successful?` behavior or mere presence of ClojureScript's default no-op method as proof of test-quiet's custom exit logic.
6. Both focused `run-test-vars` and whole-suite `run-all-tests` paths retain the seeded-failure behavior.
close_reason: PR #9120. Premise held. Both safeguards now have their own fault fixture in the new re-frame.test-quiet-exit-integrity-fixture-cljs-test, each proven by a plant: removing the replay try/catch reds red-replay-throw-cannot-mask-the-nonzero-exit at :833:11 (the poison message escapes as an uncaught crash - status alone cannot discriminate, since an uncaught exception also exits 1), and neutering seed-failure-exit! at both call sites reds run-that-never-dispatches-the-exit-defmethod-drains-nonzero at :867:11 with 'got status 0'. Each fixture emits a reached-state marker and the rows reject spawn errors, timeouts, parse errors, unmatched selectors and skipped suites. deliberately-failing-test-exits-nonzero deleted, its Ran/FAIL-in pins folded into red-run-replays-warnings-and-exits-nonzero (renamed); duplicate armed/unarmed spawn pair gone. end-run-tests-exit-decision retired - the seeded exit code makes the green process row prove defmethod ownership instead. Both seed-failure-exit! call sites retained. 16/16 contract rows green, exit 0.

title: tools/xray(local_render): exposed singleton keeps dead-frame sentinel registrable
notes:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-g1vu worker (cluster code-a) while censusing the sentinel defect class. OUT OF THAT WORKER FENCE (tools/xray/**), so filed rather than fixed.

THE DEFECT, third instance of the class. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/local_render.cljc:106 defines

  (def ^:private dead-frame-sentinel "..." ::no-egress-frame)

which expands to the ORDINARY PUBLIC KEYWORD :day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.local-render/no-egress-frame, and local-render-opts (:175) stamps it as the :frame opt whenever the named frame is nil / unreachable:

  :frame (if reachable? frame-id dead-frame-sentinel)

Its docstring carries the SAME false claim the other two carriers did: "The keyword is namespaced into this panel so it can never collide with a real frame id." make-frame validates no :id type and the frame registry is keyed by whatever id it is handed, so an app CAN register a live frame under that literal. The stamp then RESOLVES, rf/elide-wire-value takes its live-frame branch, and the value egresses under that frame empty declaration registry — the fail-CLOSED stamp becomes a fail-OPEN one. Note local-render also passes :rf.size/include-large? true and, under the :rf.egress/local-raw profile, include-sensitive?, so the blast radius differs from the off-box carriers; the leak arm is the local-redacted default.

THE CLASS, now three carriers, each found only after the previous fix scope was drawn too tight:
1. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/egress.cljs — ::no-frame. FIXED by rf2-7htk7 third pass, PR #8987 commit 449bfd21c7 (private identity value (js/Object.)), with a collision regression at tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_cljs_test.cljs:559.
2. implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc — ::no-egress-frame. FIXED under rf2-g1vu on branch worker/code-a: #?(:clj (Object.) :cljs (js/Object.)) plus the collision regression g-graph-egress-nil-frame-fails-closed-under-sentinel-id-collision in implementation/derivation-conformance/test/re_frame/derivation_algebra_conformance_cljs_test.cljc. The premise was REPRODUCED first: with a live frame under the literal id, project-graph with a nil frame-id egressed {:cart {:items "tenant-jwt-9f3a-SECRET"}} raw instead of :rf/redacted (captured exit 1, two failing assertions).
3. THIS BEAD — tools/xray/.../panels/local_render.cljc:106/123/175. NOT fixed.

CENSUS INSTRUMENT, so the next pass does not have to re-derive it: git grep -n "dead-frame-sentinel" over *.clj/*.cljc/*.cljs finds every carrier by its shared var name (control-checked: it returns 2 hits in the already-known egress.cljc). The class is "a keyword literal used as an unregisterable-frame substitute stamped into a :frame opt". One NEAR-MISS was inspected and CLEARED: implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:1145 passes ::no-frame to elide-against-frame, but only on the branch where the caller has explicitly waived sensitive redaction, and a colliding registry there supplies :large declarations that cause MORE elision, not less — it fails closed, so it is not this defect.

FIX SHAPE, settled by precedent, no design needed: make dead-frame-sentinel a fresh host object (the file is .cljc, so #?(:clj (Object.) :cljs (js/Object.)) as in the core fix), correct the docstring sentence that claims a namespaced keyword cannot collide, and ADD A COLLISION REGRESSION — register a live frame under the literal id, leave the target unselected, assert :rf/redacted. The regression is the point: this class has now been found three times precisely because the first two fixes shipped without one covering the sibling.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9044 — REOPENED. The object replacement does not satisfy the claimed "NO frame can be registered under it" invariant because the public `local-render-opts` function returns the singleton itself in `:frame` for every nil or unreachable target. A caller need not manufacture an equal object; it receives the identical value.

Reproduced at merged commit 7369668070 on the JVM lane without editing source: take `(:frame (local-render-opts nil))`, pass that exact value to `rf/make-frame` as `:id`, then call `local-render-value` with a nil observed frame. Result: `{:same-sentinel? true, :registered? true, :rendered {:auth {:token "secret-session-jwt-abc123"}}}`. The value ships raw, so the fail-CLOSED branch is still fail-OPEN.

The added regression misses this because it registers only the retired keyword and structurally asserts merely that the replacement is not a keyword. Minimal repair: generate a fresh opaque identity for each unreachable projection (or otherwise keep the identity from being reusable across calls), then add the discriminating control: extract and register one call's `:frame`, make a subsequent `local-render-value` call, and prove it uses a distinct unreachable identity and redacts the whole value. Preserve the existing explicit `local-raw` opt-out; no profile redesign is needed.
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-09-03 (mayor) — I CHECKED WHETHER THE SIBLING CARRIERS HAVE THE SAME ESCAPE, AND THE ANSWER IS THE USEFUL PART OF THIS NOTE.

The audit finding is that a PRIVATE identity value is not enough when a PUBLIC function HANDS IT TO THE CALLER. local-render-opts returns the singleton itself in :frame for every nil or unreachable target, so nobody has to manufacture an equal object — they receive the identical one, register a frame under it, and the fail-CLOSED branch is fail-OPEN. Reproduced at the merged commit with a raw secret shipping. That is a real P2 and it stands.

CARRIER 2 DOES NOT HAVE IT, and I verified at source rather than assuming the class was uniform. In implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc the sentinel is bound into walk-opts INSIDE project-graph (a let, at :421) and consumed by the local redact-node fn; project-graph returns the TRANSFORMED GRAPH, never the opts map. So the value has no public exit. The fix under rf2-g1vu stands as made.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THEREFORE NOT "private def" BUT "does any public fn RETURN a structure containing it". That is the rule to carry, and it is sharper than the one all three carriers were fixed against. A private identity value is necessary and not sufficient; what makes it sufficient is that it never leaves the namespace as a value.

WHAT THE NEXT WORKER SHOULD CHECK, and I did not: CARRIER 1 — tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/egress.cljs, fixed under rf2-7htk7 in PR #8987 with a bare (js/Object.). Does anything public there return a structure carrying it? If it does, this class has a fourth instance and the same repair applies. If it does not, the class is closed after this bead.

AND THE REGRESSION NEEDS THE SAME UPGRADE THE FIX DOES. The audit notes the added test misses this because it registers only the RETIRED KEYWORD and then asserts structurally that the replacement is not a keyword. That is a test about the SHAPE of the sentinel. The test that would have caught this takes (:frame (local-render-opts nil)) — the value a real caller actually receives — passes THAT to make-frame as :id, and asserts the value still redacts. Write the regression against the caller-visible value, not against the definition.
FIXED (second pass) by PR #9056, https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9056, branch worker/xrayleak-a.

LEAK REPRODUCED FIRST, at base 146ee34b85 (which contains #9044's 8258cb5d70), JVM lane, source untouched: registering a frame under (:frame (local-render-opts nil)) and projecting a nil observed frame yielded {:same-sentinel? true, :registered? true, :rendered {:auth {:token "secret-session-jwt-abc123", :user-id 42}}} with captured exit 1. The audit's premise holds exactly as stated.

THE FIX. dead-frame-sentinel (a shared ^:private def) becomes fresh-dead-frame-sentinel (a defn-), minting a new identity PER CALL. The identity governing any one projection is created inside that call and is not observable before the walk consumes it, so there is no durable identity left to poison; what a direct caller of the public local-render-opts receives is single-use and governs nothing else. Zero cost on the hot path (the call sits on the unreachable branch of an if), and frame/frame is a plain registry get with no interning or per-id caching, so fresh identities are immediately garbage. local-render-opts stayed public: it has no production callers outside its own namespace, and the alternative (returning :frame nil for an unreachable target) is the ambient-borrow shape the seam exists to abolish.

THE REGRESSION, written against the CALLER-VISIBLE value as instructed. Two new arms in local_render_cljs_test.cljc: local-render-fails-closed-when-a-frame-is-registered-under-the-handed-out-sentinel (takes (:frame (local-render-opts nil)), registers a live frame under THAT EXACT VALUE, asserts nil / unreachable / path-aware local-render-value-at all still redact whole) and dead-frame-sentinel-is-single-use-per-projection (two calls must not share an identity; a live frame is still carried verbatim). PROVED THEY BITE: restoring the pre-fix source from base (plant verified by blob-hash equality with the base blob 3d540bcd82) turned the namespace RED with captured exit 1 and 7 failures, both new tests failing — while the #9044 collision test stayed GREEN under the same plant, which is precisely the blindness being repaired. Restore verified by blob-hash equality (93810892d5).

CARRIER 1 ANSWER — THE CLASS IS CLOSED. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/egress.cljs has NO fourth instance. Its one public fn, egress-value, builds its opts map INLINE as the argument to rf/elide-wire-value and returns that walker's result — the projected value, never the opts map. no-frame is ^:private, never returned, consumed only inside the cond-> immediately passed to the walker. Census: only egress-value is required elsewhere (7 files); nothing reaches no-frame. Same structural shape as carrier 2, re-verified at the rebased tip where rf2-g1vu's identity fix has now landed (4944195bff): walk-opts is bound inside project-graph's let and project-graph returns the transformed graph. NOTE FOR THE RECORD: at my original base carrier 2 was STILL the ::no-egress-frame keyword — the rf2-g1vu fix merged mid-flight — but the escape-route verdict is the same either way, because the discriminator is the return shape, not the spelling.

THE RULE, now written into the fresh-dead-frame-sentinel docstring so the next pass need not re-derive it: not 'is the definition private' but 'does any PUBLIC fn RETURN a structure containing it'. Carriers 1 and 2 answer no (no public exit); carrier 3 answered yes by design, and is repaired by making what escapes single-use.

GATES (all foreground, unfiltered, exit codes captured, re-run on the final rebased base origin/main=3009c45058): tools/xray JVM clojure -M:test exit 0, 1315 tests / 6227 assertions (#9044 measured 1313 / 6217 — exactly +2 tests / +10 assertions, my two new deftests); npm run test:cljs exit 0, 11203 tests / 55820 assertions; clj-kondo exit 0 with zero findings on any changed file; nine documentation gates exit 0; mkdocs build --strict exit 0. test:xray-feature-gate NOT run — #9044's caveat still holds, no scenario mounts an unreachable frame, so it does not exercise the changed branch.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9056 — REOPENED. The per-call identity does not make the public local-render-opts result safe: the caller can register a frame under (:frame opts) and then pass that SAME opts map to rf/project-egress. Reproduced at current tip in tools/xray with the real JVM runtime: {:registered? true, :projected {:auth {:token audit-secret}}}; exit 0. The new regression misses this path because it obtains a sentinel from one local-render-opts call, then invokes local-render-value/local-render-value-at, which each call local-render-opts again and mint a different identity. The source itself says there are no production callers of local-render-opts outside this namespace, so the minimal repair is to withdraw that builder from the public surface and keep sentinel creation plus consumption inside the public projection functions, matching the two sibling carriers whose identity has no public exit. Pin the actual public-surface invariant; do not add a larger sentinel framework. The opener pagehide announcement is independently sound.

THE RULE, now in the fresh-dead-frame-sentinel docstring so the next pass need not re-derive it: not "is the definition private", not "is the identity fresh", but DOES ANY PUBLIC FN RETURN A STRUCTURE CONTAINING IT. title: test-quiet CLJS var-filter regression tests only a copied predicate
description:
## Correctness finding

The CLJS shadow-node contract suite's `find-matching-test-vars-filtering` test does not execute `re-frame.test-quiet.shadow-node/find-matching-test-vars`. It tests a local copy of the predicate, so the advertised namespace-versus-qualified-var selection contract can break while the named regression remains green.

## Evidence

- `implementation/test-quiet/src/re_frame/test_quiet/shadow_node.cljs:173-180` is the production selector. It reads `env/get-test-vars` and filters simple symbols by namespace and qualified symbols by fully-qualified var name.
- `implementation/test-quiet/test/re_frame/test_quiet_shadow_node_cljs_test.cljs:148-175` explicitly says it cannot inject the registry, then defines a local `select` function at lines 157-166 that reproduces the production predicate. The assertions call only that local function; the test namespace cannot require the `:dev/always` runner because doing so forms the documented compile cycle.
- The parser assertions at lines 49-65 prove only that `--test=my.ns/a-test` becomes a symbol. `unmatched-selectors-guard` at lines 191-226 starts from an already-selected `matched-vars` collection. Neither reaches the production filter.
- The process-level `spawn-runner` calls at lines 487-756 use valid namespace selectors or deliberately absent selectors. None selects an existing fully-qualified var, and no process row proves that a namespace selector returns all vars in that namespace.
- Repository-wide `--test=` consumer searches likewise found operational scripts selecting namespaces, not a valid `ns/var`; the only positive qualified-var examples are parser/copy assertions in this test file. A production mutation that ignores `test-var-syms`, treats qualified symbols as namespace symbols, or selects only one var per namespace does not affect the local `select` function and is not discriminated by the process rows.
- Git blame/history shows the copied test was introduced in `953dffc80d` and has never called the production selector. Searches across all bead states/fields for `find-matching-test-vars`, `var filtering`, `fake-var`, `copied predicate`, `shadow-node filtering`, and the test name found no existing issue.

## Impact

The suite reports direct coverage of a supported CLI contract that it does not execute. A regression can make focused single-var runs select nothing or the wrong tests while the parser, copied unit test, unmatched-selector unit test, and ordinary whole-namespace process rows stay green. This is especially hazardous because focused runs are used to reduce large consolidated builds.

## Proposed disposition

Move the pure selection decision into the compile-cycle-safe `re-frame.test-quiet.shadow-node-cli` namespace (for example, a helper accepting `test-syms` and a supplied var collection), make `shadow-node/find-matching-test-vars` delegate to it with `env/get-test-vars`, and point the existing synthetic-var assertions at that shared production helper. An equivalent injectable seam is acceptable, but do not retain a second handwritten predicate in the test. Add one real focused `ns/var` process proof if the cost is acceptable; the shared-helper test is the minimum non-vacuous pin.

## Risks / retained contracts

Do not make the test namespace require `re-frame.test-quiet.shadow-node`; its `:dev/always` test-data macro dependency creates the compile cycle this split exists to avoid. Preserve input order, namespace-wide selection, exact qualified-var selection, mixed selectors, metadata shape (`{:ns :name}`), the unmatched-selector refusal, and the existing public CLI spelling.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `find-matching-test-vars-filtering` in the consolidated test-quiet Node suite and confirm it passes.
2. In a disposable branch, change production `shadow-node/find-matching-test-vars` so either qualified symbols no longer match fully qualified var names or simple symbols no longer select a namespace.
3. Rerun `find-matching-test-vars-filtering`; it still passes because the assertions invoke the test-local `select` predicate rather than the mutated production function.
4. Search the process-level rows for a successful existing `--test=namespace/var` selection; none provides a positive production-path control for the qualified-symbol branch.
5. Restore the mutation after observing the false green.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The var-filtering test invokes the same selection function used by `shadow-node/find-matching-test-vars`; it contains no local copy of the namespace/FQN predicate.
2. Tests cover a namespace selecting every matching var, an existing qualified symbol selecting exactly one var, mixed namespace/FQN selection, and absent selectors.
3. A controlled mutation that removes either the simple-symbol branch or the qualified-symbol branch makes the focused test fail.
4. The `:dev/always` runner remains out of the test namespace's require graph, and the consolidated node-test build compiles without a cycle.
5. A valid namespace-focused real runner still exits 0, an unmatched selector still exits nonzero, and (if added) a real existing `ns/var` selector runs exactly the requested test.
close_reason: PR #9120. Premise held. The rule moved to shadow-node-cli/select-matching-test-vars (the compile-cycle-safe ns unmatched-selectors already lives in) and find-matching-test-vars now delegates to it over env/get-test-vars; the test drives the shipped function and the copy is gone. Plants: removing the simple-symbol branch reds find-matching-test-vars-filtering at :184/:190; removing the qualified-symbol branch reds it at :187/:190 and the FQN selector then matches nothing at the real runner. Control fired: the identical whole-ns invocation on the restored tree reports 0 failures for that row vs 2 under the plant. Added the optional real ns/var process row - the green fixture ns now carries two tests so the namespace selector must see 'Ran 2 tests' and the qualified selector 'Ran 1 tests'. NOTE: driving the shipped selector immediately exposed a real defect, fixed in the same PR - (symbol <ns-symbol> <name-symbol>) keeps both parts unconverted and CLJS hashes a symbol by hashing those parts as strings, so every such symbol hashes to one constant while staying = to the reader's ns/name; a set matched it while array-map-backed (<=8) and stopped above that, so --test= selected correctly up to eight qualified selectors and NOTHING at nine (measured: 8 of 9 real vars reported unmatched). Both call sites now route through one test-var-names helper; the regression pins nine selectors.

title: Collapse the duplicate event-wrapper conformance test
description:
## Finding

Two adjacent tests in `implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_model_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` assert the same registration shape. `reg-event-registers-under-event-kind-with-the-one-wrapper` requires `(mapv :id (:interceptors meta))` to equal exactly `[:rf/event-handler]`, then checks the sole wrapper id and `:rf/default?`. `reg-event-no-per-kind-wrapper-ids-survive` registers another ordinary event, converts the same interceptor ids to a set, again requires exactly `#{:rf/event-handler}`, and separately asserts that `:rf/db-handler`, `:rf/fx-handler`, and `:rf/ctx-handler` are absent. Those three negatives are logical consequences of the exact singleton equality in the first test, so the second row exercises no additional branch, runtime, or metadata path.

## Recommendation

Delete `reg-event-no-per-kind-wrapper-ids-survive`, keeping the first test as the canonical wrapper lock. If the named retired ids are valuable migration documentation, mention them in the first test's assertion message/comment without executing a second registration. Alternatively parameterize a genuinely distinct historical registration path; currently there is none because all calls use the one `reg-event` form.

## Risks and contracts

Keep the exact ordered interceptor vector assertion, the wrapper's `:rf/default? true`, handler-fn reachability, and absence of `:event/kind`. Do not weaken singleton equality to only a membership check.

## Evidence

The first test at lines 652-669 asserts the exact one-element vector and wrapper metadata. The second at lines 671-679 asserts the set form of the same one-element vector plus redundant non-membership checks. Both use the same public registrar, fixture, platform matrix, and ordinary no-metadata `reg-event` path.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Only one ordinary-registration test owns the exact singleton `:rf/event-handler` wrapper contract.
2. That surviving test still fails for any extra wrapper, any retired per-kind wrapper, wrong order/id, missing handler-fn, or missing `:rf/default? true`.
3. Test/docs commentary no longer implies the duplicate registration covers a distinct path.
4. Event-conformance JVM tests and the consolidated CLJS Node suite pass with the expected lower test/assertion tally.
close_reason: Premise held. Verified by plant, not census: renaming events/event-handler-interceptor-id :rf/event-handler -> :rf/db-handler (a retired per-kind id, exactly what the duplicate's three negatives claim to guard) reds BOTH rows -- survivor reg-event-registers-under-event-kind-with-the-one-wrapper exit 1 with 2 failures/6 assertions, duplicate reg-event-no-per-kind-wrapper-ids-survive exit 1 with 2 failures/4. The survivor's exact-vector equality (= [:rf/event-handler] (mapv :id ...)) entails the set equality and all three non-memberships, and additionally refuses an extra wrapper and a wrong order, so the duplicate exercised no branch, runtime or metadata path the survivor misses. Deleted; the retired ids ride as commentary on the exact-vector assertion per the bead's own recommendation. AC1-4 met: one owner, unweakened singleton equality, no prose implying a distinct path, event-conformance JVM 44 tests/186 assertions exit 0 and the consolidated node suite 11163/55721 exit 0. PR #9123.

title: Make the event-conformance explicit-live test discriminate the policy override
description:
## Finding

`reg-event-explicit-live-mint-policy-mints-the-declared-nondeterminism-escape` in `implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_model_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` dispatches into the fixture's ordinary `:rf/default` frame, whose no-config mint policy is already `:live`. A missing generator-backed fact therefore mints whether `{:rf.cofx/mint-policy :explicit-live}` is honored, ignored, renamed, or removed. The test cannot detect the policy behavior named by its title; it only repeats the immediately preceding live-generation coverage.

Core's dual-runtime `explicit-live-overrides-strict-frame-generates` has the discriminating setup: a `:preset :test` frame defaults to `:strict`, the per-call `:explicit-live` value must override it, and the generator/run result prove the escape was used. Core also separately proves strict refuses the same class of missing fact.

## Recommendation

Remove the non-discriminating conformance row as a strict subset of the core owner, or reshape it around a strict frame with a paired control: without the per-call override, the generator stays at zero and dispatch fails missing-required; with `:explicit-live`, it runs exactly once and delivers the fact. Prefer one canonical dual-runtime owner rather than two copies.

## Risks and contracts

Preserve the public dispatch-options path and dual JVM/CLJS coverage for `:explicit-live`; do not replace it with a direct call to the internal policy resolver. The negative and positive legs must use equivalent frame/fact setup so the option is the only discriminator.

## Evidence

The conformance row creates no strict/test frame and supplies only `:rf.cofx/mint-policy :explicit-live`; the documented/default runtime policy is `:live`. `implementation/core/test/re_frame/cofx_cljs_test.cljc` already contains `router-default-is-live-generates`, `test-preset-default-is-strict-does-not-generate`, and `explicit-live-overrides-strict-frame-generates`, all through `rf/dispatch-sync` in a `.cljc` suite.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The event-conformance row is removed or changed so ignoring/removing the `:explicit-live` option makes it fail.
2. If retained, the test establishes a strict baseline/control and then proves the per-call option alone enables one mint and handler delivery.
3. Dual-runtime public-dispatch coverage remains in at least one canonical suite.
4. Event-conformance JVM tests and the consolidated CLJS Node suite pass.
close_reason: Premise held, proven by plant. Planting cofx/resolve-mint-policy to DROP its per-call argument -- the option honoured nowhere -- left the old row reg-event-explicit-live-mint-policy-mints-the-declared-nondeterminism-escape GREEN at exit 0 while core's explicit-live-overrides-strict-frame-generates went exit 1. Chose the bead's RESHAPE option over removal (the title asks for a discriminating row, and the public dispatch-options path is worth keeping at the conformance tier): renamed to reg-event-explicit-live-mint-policy-overrides-a-strict-frame, built on a :preset :test frame whose mint policy defaults to :strict, with a paired CONTROL that dispatches WITHOUT the opt (asserts :rf.error/missing-required-cofx, zero generator calls, handler never ran) and then the same dispatch WITH :explicit-live (exactly one mint, flat delivery). The new row was re-planted in BOTH directions: per-call ignored -> exit 1, escape leg errors missing-required; frame :strict ignored -> exit 1, control leg 4 failures. AC1-4 met: ignoring the option now makes it fail, the strict baseline/control is established, core keeps the dual-runtime owner, gates green (event-conformance JVM 44/186 exit 0, node suite 11163/55721 exit 0). PR #9123.

title: Replace the vacuous stale non-delivery event-conformance case
description:
## Finding

`a-stale-completion-is-non-delivering-without-an-explicit-observer` in `implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_reply_envelope_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` builds global and image handlers, then calls only the pure `reply/suppress` function. It never calls `dispatch`, `dispatch-sync`, a delivery helper, or any managed-effect completion path. Therefore its zero call count and unchanged app-db assertions follow from the test performing no delivery operation at all; they cannot detect a runtime that ignores `:deliver?` and dispatches stale app replies.

The row had real teeth before commit `ca7fd0bd93`: it invoked `deliver-through-gate!`, which consumed `:deliver?`. That commit correctly deleted the delivery gate under the new observer-self-dispatch model, but left the negative row's handler/frame apparatus after removing its sole dispatch site. Its remaining pure assertions (`:deliver? false`, valid `:stale`/`:suppressed` envelope, no `:value`) are already owned more strongly by core's `suppress-does-not-deliver-app-target` and `suppress-is-universally-non-delivering`, the cross-family reply-conformance stale matrix, and the production-elision stale suite.

## Recommendation

Delete this row and update the namespace prose from “both stale cases,” unless a real production-path integration gap exists. If app non-delivery needs an event-conformance test, drive an actual managed-effect family completion/lowering path that conditionally could dispatch the target; assert that a superseded completion reaches the suppression branch and leaves both explicit and ambient frames untouched. Do not simulate non-delivery by simply omitting the delivery call.

## Risks and contracts

Retain `an-observer-self-dispatches-a-stale-reply-on-its-own-authority`, which genuinely composes `suppress` + `complete` + frame-targeted dispatch and proves the authorized observation path. Retain the natural success dispatch case. A replacement must depend on production code that consumes the suppression outcome, not a new test-local gate that merely restates it.

## Evidence

The current row's only operational call after setup is `reply/suppress`; `seen-event`, `call-count`, and both app-db values are read before any dispatch. `ca7fd0bd93` removed `deliver-through-gate! outcome ...` from exactly this row. Core and reply-conformance already assert universal suppression and envelope shape in dual-runtime suites.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The no-operation stale case is removed, or replaced by a test that executes a real production completion path with a reachable delivery branch.
2. A replacement demonstrably fails when that production path dispatches despite `:deliver? false`; zero calls cannot be established merely by never invoking delivery code.
3. The observer self-dispatch and natural-success event-pipeline cases remain green on JVM and CLJS.
4. Namespace/deps commentary accurately names the integration boundaries still exercised, and focused JVM plus consolidated Node tests pass.
close_reason: Premise held; vacuity proven by plant. Planting reply/complete's :append leg to stop appending the reply reds reply-completion-is-an-ordinary-reg-event-dispatch (13 failures) and an-observer-self-dispatches-a-stale-reply-on-its-own-authority (6), and leaves a-stale-completion-is-non-delivering-without-an-explicit-observer with ZERO failures -- it is blind to the entire delivery path it names. REMOVED rather than replaced, and the reason is a finding worth keeping: NO production code anywhere reads :deliver?. reply/suppress returns false unconditionally with no branch, and every family (http/registry, http/transport, resources/reply_handlers, routing/nav_token, machines/reply) branches on its OWN staleness decision instead, never on the outcome's :deliver?. So AC1's alternative -- 'a real production completion path with a reachable delivery branch' -- has no target that does not first re-invent the delivery gate ca7fd0bd93 deliberately deleted, which the bead's own risk note forbids. Coverage is not lost: the RETAINED observer row keeps a LIVE non-delivery tooth (zero call-count read BEFORE the observer self-dispatch, exactly-one AFTER, so a runtime that app-delivered a stale reply itself fails the pair), and the pure suppress laws (universal :deliver? false, stale envelope shape, absent :value) are re-frame.reply-cljs-test's across six target shapes including forged stale-authority. AC2 moot under removal; AC3 both retained rows green on JVM and CLJS; AC4 ns prose rewritten to name the narrower ownership. PR #9123.

title: Prune strict-subset frame-resolution cases from event-conformance
description:
## Finding

`implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_frame_isolation_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` carries three cases whose observable contract is already exercised more strongly by `implementation/core/test/re_frame/live_run_frame_resolution_cljs_test.cljc`:

- `two-frames-sharing-one-image-keep-independent-app-db` repeats the same image, seeds (0/100), three-dispatch stream, distinct runnable ids, numeric results, and non-global resolution as core's `two-frames-from-one-image-keep-independent-state`; the core owner additionally proves independent subscription values and cache identity. The conformance-only second `not= :global` is implied by the exact `= 101` assertion.
- `absence-is-default-no-image-frame-uses-the-global-registrar` repeats core's `no-image-frame-resolves-through-the-global-registrar`: same image-less explicit frame, global event + sub, committed marker, subscription value, and nil generation binding.
- `the-global-sentinel-is-genuinely-registered` repeats that same absence/default path again. The headline isolation test registers its sentinel in its own fixture scope, and its exact `:todo` / `:counter` results already establish that the image handlers ran; a cross-test registration probe cannot arm another fixture's sentinel.

Both files are `.cljc` namespaces ending `-cljs-test`, so all of these rows ride the consolidated Node suite and JVM test lanes. The duplication adds maintenance and runtime without another platform or code-path boundary.

## Recommendation

Delete the three strict-subset cases, or consolidate their genuinely useful assertion into the canonical core owner. Keep the conformance rows that add independent teeth: exact two-image app-db shape + distinct generations, runtime-db partition isolation, and child-dispatch sibling-frame isolation. Update suite commentary/counts to describe that narrower ownership.

## Risks and contracts

Do not weaken dual-runtime coverage of image resolution or delete the unique runtime-db/sibling-isolation assertions. Preserve at least one positive absence-is-default event+subscription test and one directly armed global-fallback sentinel in the canonical owner.

## Evidence

The event-conformance file has 6 tests; the core owner has the corresponding live-run cases plus stronger state/sub-cache assertions. History shows core's live resolution suite predates the conformance copy (`22229d483c` / `78d4d2eca8` before `4bacc2f05c`), and both remain enrolled through `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` plus their JVM aliases.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The three strict-subset cases are removed or reduced to assertions not present in the core owner.
2. The canonical core suite still proves image-less global event+sub resolution, nil generation, and shared-image independent event/sub-cache state on JVM and CLJS.
3. Event-conformance retains the distinct-generation/exact-db headline, runtime-db isolation, and child/sibling isolation teeth.
4. Event-conformance JVM tests and the consolidated CLJS Node suite pass, with updated test/assertion tallies and no stale ownership prose.
close_reason: Premise held for all three; containment demonstrated per case. (1) absence-is-default-no-image-frame-uses-the-global-registrar is OPERATIONALLY IDENTICAL to core's no-image-frame-resolves-through-the-global-registrar -- same frame id, event, sub and three assertions, differing only in prose strings (verified by a paren-balanced form extraction and string-elided compare: identical True). Two copies of one program cannot be distinguished by any fault, which is stronger evidence than a plant. (2) the-global-sentinel-is-genuinely-registered repeats that same path plus a registrar/lookup some? probe; the probe's value is real but its PLACEMENT was not -- the :each fixture means it could never arm another test's sentinel -- so it was MOVED INTO the headline isolation row, where it backs the not= :global assertions that actually depend on it. (3) two-frames-sharing-one-image-keep-independent-app-db: five of its six assertions are textually identical to core's two-frames-from-one-image-keep-independent-state; the sixth (not= :global on frame B) is entailed by the exact = 101. Core adds frame-object?, subscription values and sub-cache identity. Plant (a constant frame/anon-frame-id collapsing two no-id frames onto one record) reds both: conformance 3 failures/6 assertions, core 6 failures/11 -- core strictly stronger. All three deleted. AC1-4 met: core still owns image-less global event+sub resolution and nil generation and shared-image independent state on JVM+CLJS; event-conformance retains its three teeth (exact two-image app-db with distinct generations, runtime-db partition isolation with untouched sibling, child/sibling isolation); ns prose rewritten to name the narrower ownership; JVM 44 tests/186 assertions exit 0 and node suite 11163/55721 exit 0. shadow-cljs.edn NOT touched -- the file stays enrolled, no build-id change needed. PR #9123.

title: Remove superseded test-quiet green subprocess rows
description:
## Vestigial test coverage

Two green subprocess rows in the test-quiet contract suites are strictly superseded by stronger rows that execute the same production paths. They add no unique assertion but retain real process-start cost.

## Evidence

### JVM

- `implementation/test-quiet/test/re_frame/test_quiet_runner_contract_test.clj:189-209` (`green-runner-contract`) creates one passing fixture, invokes the real runner, then asserts exit 0, absence of `Running tests in`, at most three nonblank lines, and the `0 failures, 0 errors.` tally.
- Lines 222-258 (`green-runner-exact-shape`) create the same one-test passing suite and invoke the same `run-runner` path. They assert exit 0, absence of the identical `Running tests in` marker, exactly two nonblank lines, `Ran ...` first, the exact zero tally second, and the single permitted leading blank. Every assertion made by the older row follows from these stronger assertions.
- History shows the generic row arrived in `953dffc80d`; the exact-shape regression arrived the next day in `f1ce33adbd` and did not retire the superseded row. `green-runner-contract` has no references or distinct fixture semantics elsewhere.

### CLJS

- `implementation/test-quiet/test/re_frame/test_quiet_shadow_node_cljs_test.cljs:487-518` (`real-shadow-node-green-run-is-quiet`) spawns `--test=re-frame.test-quiet-green-fixture-cljs-test` and asserts no spawn error, exit 0, canonical summary-only output, no `Unknown arg`, no `Testing` banner, a `Ran ...` line, and the zero tally.
- Lines 563-575, the clean negative control inside `unknown-arg-is-fatal-not-false-green`, spawn that exact same argument and assert only no spawn error, exit 0, and no `Unknown arg`. Those are a strict subset of the earlier real-green row's assertions; the malformed plural and space-separated argument cases remain independently covered at lines 527-562.
- History shows the real green row arrived in `cdd684b2ec`; the weaker duplicate was added later in `23442f1c76` as a local negative control.
- The suite documents at lines 355-390 that every CLJS spawn reloads a 4,201-module / 484 MB dev build and has measured healthy runtimes from roughly 10 seconds to 449 seconds under load. Removing an exact duplicate therefore has material gate value.
- All-state bead searches for both test names, green runner shape, clean focused invocation, duplicate child process/spawn, and superseded green coverage found no existing issue.

## Impact

The redundant rows lengthen routine JVM and especially CLJS contract runs without expanding behavioral coverage. They also split the authoritative green-output contract across weaker and stronger tests, making future maintainers compare duplicate fixtures before knowing which assertion set is definitive.

## Proposed disposition

Delete `green-runner-contract` and retain `green-runner-exact-shape` as the single JVM one-test green process contract. Delete the clean focused-invocation branch from `unknown-arg-is-fatal-not-false-green` and retain `real-shadow-node-green-run-is-quiet` as the single CLJS valid-selector/green-output control. If locality is valuable, reference the authoritative green test in a comment rather than spawning the fixture again.

## Risks / retained contracts

Do not merge genuinely distinct red, namespace-load, fixture-error, malformed-argument, unmatched-selector, timeout, warning-replay, or multi-test rows. Retain a real process boundary once per runtime, the exact JVM leading-blank contract, the CLJS valid `--test=` parser/runner path, canonical green summary assertions, platform newline normalization, and useful failure diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `green-runner-contract` is removed; `green-runner-exact-shape` remains the sole JVM one-passing-test subprocess row and still proves exit 0, no discovery banner, one leading blank, exactly `Ran ...` plus the zero tally, and cross-platform CRLF normalization.
2. The clean focused-invocation branch at CLJS lines 563-575 is removed; `real-shadow-node-green-run-is-quiet` remains and still invokes the exact valid green selector, rejects spawn errors, requires exit 0, rejects `Unknown arg`/`Testing`/other non-summary output, and requires `Ran ...` plus the zero tally.
3. Both malformed-argument branches still prove nonzero status, name their offending tokens, and prove the suite did not run.
4. No distinct red/error/timeout/replay/discovery/lifecycle process row is removed.
5. The relevant JVM and consolidated CLJS contract suites pass, with one fewer JVM runner process and one fewer CLJS runner process than before.
close_reason: PR #9120. Premise held on both rows; each successor named and its pins quoted. JVM: green-runner-contract removed. Successor green-runner-exact-shape spawns the same one-passing-test fixture through the same -main and asserts strictly more - (is (zero? exit)), (is (not (str/includes? out "Running tests in"))) which is literally discovery-banner-marker's value, (is (= 2 (count non-blank))) subsuming the old <=3, (is (str/blank? (nth lines 0 nil))), (is (str/starts-with? (first non-blank) "Ran ")), (is (= "0 failures, 0 errors." (second non-blank))) subsuming the old str/includes?, over lines CRLF-normalised by (str/replace out "\r" ""). Every clause of the deleted row follows. CLJS: the clean-focused-invocation branch of unknown-arg-is-fatal-not-false-green removed. It spawned the exact same --test=re-frame.test-quiet-green-fixture-cljs-test invocation real-shadow-node-green-run-is-quiet already spawns and asserted a strict subset (nil err, zero status, no 'Unknown arg'); that row also pins canonical-lines-only, no Testing banner, Ran 2 tests, and the zero tally. Both malformed-argument branches and every distinct red/error/timeout/replay/lifecycle row kept. Each deletion leaves a comment naming the surviving row. JVM suite 53 tests / 275 assertions exit 0; the CLJS rows green.

title: Finish schema-implies-validation migration in schemas tests
description:
## Finding

The schemas test surface did not complete the `schema implies validation` migration. Twelve test namespaces that already require the public `re-frame.schemas` facade still separately require `re-frame.schemas.malli`, and two CLJS suites continue to describe that direct adapter require as the canonical application opt-in. One test named `cljs-no-adapter-soft-passes` models an application posture that the facade deliberately made impossible; what it actually exercises is the supported defensive missing-hook/substitute-port fallback.

## Evidence

- Current source and Spec 010 state that `re-frame.schemas` itself requires `re-frame.schemas.malli`; requiring the artefact automatically publishes the Malli validate/explain hooks. Commit `d0b95fdc54` made this Ruling A specifically to eliminate the "schemas loaded but adapter not required" posture.
- A line-oriented census finds 12 direct `[re-frame.schemas.malli]` requires under `implementation/schemas/test`; every one of those namespaces also directly requires `re-frame.schemas`. No test calls an adapter var (the adapter is load-side-effect-only). The dedicated `schemas_implies_validation_test.clj` intentionally requires only the facade and already proves the transitive wiring contract.
- `schemas_cljs_test.cljs` (currently lines 18-25 and 96-111) still says direct adapter require is the "canonical opt-in" and that omitting it soft-passes. Its `cljs-no-adapter-soft-passes` test (currently around lines 136-161) manually clears late-bind hooks; because the same namespace requires the facade, this is not an app-without-adapter scenario.
- `schemas_boundary_prod_test.cljs` (currently lines 48-55) repeats the obsolete instruction that CLJS apps must require the adapter at boot, despite also requiring the facade on line 58.
- Spec 010 currently says there is "nothing extra to opt into" (around lines 652-660) and reserves the soft-pass for a cross-port default-absent posture or an explicitly installed substitute validator. The stale test prose contradicts that normative contract.
- Blame dates the obsolete CLJS comments/direct requires to `80119fc1a9`, before Ruling A. The June 15 vestigial sweep `2980649a9c` edited the same file but only repaired a retired event-registration spelling, leaving this older posture untouched.
- All-status title/description searches for `adapter require`, `schema implies validation tests`, `canonical opt-in`, and `cljs-no-adapter-soft-passes` found no owning issue. Closed `rf2-tiymn` covers production elision of Malli's humanizer, not test import/posture cleanup.

## Impact

The redundant requires make broad schemas tests bypass the public load contract they are ostensibly exercising and stale comments teach consumers the exact extra boot step Ruling A retired. The no-adapter test name/text presents a reachable consumer configuration that cannot occur after loading the facade, obscuring the real reason the soft-pass branch remains: alternate ports or deliberate hook invalidation.

## Proposed disposition

Remove redundant direct adapter requires from schemas tests that already load the facade, leaving the dedicated facade-only regression as the authority. Rewrite the two CLJS comment blocks to state automatic facade wiring. Keep the missing-hook behavior test, but rename/reword it around deliberate hook absence/substitute-port fallback rather than an app forgetting a separate require.

## Risks

Do not remove `re-frame.schemas.malli` from the facade or change the default validator. Do not delete the defensive soft-pass branch/test: alternate ports and deliberate unbinding still need it. Preserve the production boundary build's validator/humanizer assertions and the matched bundle probes.

- The former `cljs-no-adapter-soft-passes` test is named and documented as a deliberate missing-hook/substitute-port fallback and still proves the default validator soft-passes when that hook is explicitly absent.
- `schemas_implies_validation_test.clj` still proves that requiring only the facade binds validate/explain hooks and makes a bad registered value fail.
- Schemas JVM, ordinary CLJS, production-boundary CLJS, and bundle A/B gates pass; a negative control removing the facade's adapter require makes the facade-only regression fail.
- Public schema registration, custom-validator installation, nil-validator opt-out, and production boundary semantics are unchanged.
