title: reagent-slim: remove the zero-consumer tag-form-meta compile helper
description:
## Finding

`reagent2.impl.component/tag-form-meta` is a public-looking compile-time helper with no production consumer. It has been test-only since its introduction and duplicates the literal metadata construction already performed by the only real consumer of this namespace.

## Evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/component.clj:14-25,71-76` advertises `tag-form-meta` as consumed by `reg-view` and defines it as only `{:reagent2/form form-tag}`.
- A repository-wide exact-symbol search finds only that source declaration/docstring and its dedicated test at `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/impl/component_test.clj:60-68`; there is no production call.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_view_macro.cljc:60-73` dynamically resolves only `classify-form-body`. The expansion constructs slot metadata directly with `(assoc :reagent2/form form-tag)` at lines 132-138 and fn metadata directly with `with-meta` at lines 196-197.
- `git log -S tag-form-meta` finds only its introduction in `21d4b06aae` and a later comment pass `0eeb8d079a`; history contains no consumer.
- This is not a shipped compatibility promise: `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/README.md:3-10` identifies `reagent2.core`/the adapter as the target surface and says reagent-slim is pre-alpha and has never shipped. No README or implementation-spec API table promises this helper.

## Impact

The extra public Var and dedicated test imply an extension seam that does not exist in the actual `reg-view` integration. They add maintenance and invite downstream coupling to an accidental one-line abstraction.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `tag-form-meta`, its dedicated unit test, and the false namespace-doc claim that `reg-view` consumes it. Keep `classify-form-body` and the macro expansion's current direct metadata construction unchanged. Do not add a deprecation shim to an unpublished, zero-consumer helper.

## Risks

A local, out-of-repository macro could have called the public Var despite the absence of a documented/released contract. Before removal, repeat exact searches over any maintained external consumer corpus if one exists; otherwise the explicit pre-alpha status makes removal the safer pre-release choice.

## Duplicate search

Searched all 575 current bead records (all states; title, description, notes, acceptance) for `tag-form-meta`, `reagent2.impl.component`, `compile-time form`, `metadata`, and the source path. No bead owns this finding. `rf2-08hx1` concerns Form-3 lifecycle argv and is unrelated.
acceptance_criteria:
- `tag-form-meta` and its test-only coverage are removed; `rg tag-form-meta` is empty across tracked source/tests/docs.
- `classify-form-body` remains the only CLJ helper dynamically resolved by core, and Form-1/Form-2 macroexpansion metadata remains byte-for-byte equivalent in meaning.
- The component namespace documentation names only helpers with a real consumer and does not claim a general macro-extension contract unless one is deliberately specified and tested.
- Reagent-slim JVM tests and the core `reg-view` macroexpansion tests pass; a negative control that removes the classifier resolution makes the focused fold test fail.
- No compatibility alias or dead forwarding wrapper replaces the removed helper.
notes: AUDIT 2026-09-03 — PR #9127 (merge 213a43ae7791dbe0a7feadab3a46077a38d804a9) correctly removed the zero-consumer `tag-form-meta` Var and its dedicated test, but the integrated tree still contains three claims that the helper exists: `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md:609`, its coverage table at `:1128`, and `src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs:26`. At the same merge, exact searches of `component.clj` and `component_test.clj` return zero definitions/tests. This violates the existing acceptance criterion that tracked source/tests/docs contain no `tag-form-meta` and leaves runtime/developer documentation pointing at a removed Var. Reopened this exact owner rather than creating a duplicate. Reconcile those three references with the surviving `classify-form-body` plus the metadata construction in `re-frame.core/expand-reg-view`; do not restore the dead helper.
close_reason: RE-CLOSED; the first close evaporated to the .beads checkout race. Landed on main as 213a43ae77 (PR #9127, worker slimdead-a): the zero-consumer tag-form-meta compile helper removed from reagent-slim's impl/component.clj. A macro-time consumer was ruled out FOUR ways, which matters because a runtime var-usage census cannot see macroexpansion-time use: (1) census line-oriented AND whitespace-flattened found only docstring, defn and test; (2) every external reference to the namespace enumerated and read, all naming classify-form-body / wrap-render / create-class* / reagent-class?; (3) both requiring-resolve sites pass a LITERAL symbol, and a sweep for dynamically-constructed symbols - the one shape a literal census misses - found none; (4) the removal is itself the macro-time instrument, since the JVM suite macroexpands reg-view through expand-reg-view, so a surviving macro-time consumer would fail to COMPILE. Green. Control fired: planting a fault in classify-form-body's Form-2 branch took the JVM gate to exit 1 with four failures including fold-reg-view-form-2-expansion-tags-form-2, proving the fold test is not passing vacuously.

value:
A WORKER's `bd close` is reverted by the mayor's `git checkout HEAD -- .beads`, and the loss is SILENT on both sides. Measured three times on 2026-09-03/04: rf2-6r9j.52 once, then rf2-6r9j.37 and rf2-6r9j.28 together.

MECHANISM, and why the CLAUDE.md bullet does not fully cover it. That bullet warns the MAYOR not to checkout .beads after its OWN `bd close`. But workers run `bd close` from the mayor checkout too, at a time the mayor does not control. So the sequence that loses data is: worker closes a bead -> mayor's checkpoint exports (may or may not catch it) -> mayor runs `git checkout HEAD -- .beads` -> the export reverts -> the NEXT checkpoint writes that revert back over the Dolt database. The close is gone from BOTH the export and the database, along with its close reason. Nothing errors. `bd list` looks normal. The worker's completion report still says "CLOSED", so the mayor believes it.

THE DETECTOR, and it must be built carefully because the obvious form fails open. For every OPEN bead, look for a payload commit on the trunk:

  git log origin/main --oneline -E --grep="<escaped-id>([^0-9A-Za-z.]|$)"

Two traps, both of which produced a WRONG answer in this repo:
- `jq -r '.[].id'` on Windows emits ids with a TRAILING CARRIAGE RETURN. Fed through a `while read` loop every grep misses and the sweep reports a clean zero over 48 ids. A control using hardcoded literals PASSES while the pipeline returns nothing - the control must share the shape of the target, i.e. come through the same pipeline. Pipe through `tr -d '\r'`.
- An unanchored grep treats `.` as a wildcard, so `rf2-6r9j.1` matches `.101` and `.161`. Escape the dots AND anchor the trailing boundary, or the sweep reports a page of false positives.

Run BOTH controls every time: a known-closed id that IS on the trunk (must hit) and a nonsense id (must miss).

A HIT IS A POINTER, NOT A VERDICT. Most hits are legitimately open: deliberate partials, a bead whose code half landed while its spec half waits on an unmerged PR, epics, and beads held for Mike. The revert signature specifically is: a worker's completion report SAYS closed, the payload is on the trunk, and the bead reads OPEN in both `bd show` and `git show HEAD:.beads/issues.jsonl`.

RECOVERY is cheap and complete: re-close with the full reason reconstructed from the worker's report, then run `sh scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh` IMMEDIATELY, before any `git checkout HEAD -- .beads`. Verify in both places afterwards - `bd show` and the committed export - because verifying only one is how the second occurrence went unnoticed.

MITIGATION for the mayor's own loop: run the closes, then checkpoint, and only then do the checkout/rebase/push sequence. Never close a bead between the checkpoint and the checkout.

title: hic tooling: chapter 20 step 2 of 3 (hm/shadow! comparison) is unreachable - it inherits the L3 DOM gap, and its :reference premise needs the original the same chapter tells you to delete
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 1 (RealWorld/Conduit), a
BLINDED agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation - evidence about the surface, not a ratified design, since a pilot
proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own rule.
Full log: ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-realworld.friction-log.md (local-only).

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P1-F13 · outcome 2 · `unresolved` · `tooling`

**Trying to**

Execute step 2 of the migration chapter's three-step process. The chapter is
emphatic about the order — "Do not start with the codemod. Read the report,
port **and prove** a screen, then apply mechanical edits and run the proof
again" — and §3 is the proof: `hm/shadow!` mounts the Reagent original and the
Hicasso candidate against isolated copies of one seeded frame, drives both with
one script, and compares canonical DOM and intent streams.

**Instead**

Could not run it, for two independent reasons, and the second is the
interesting one.

**(a) It is a mounted-tier door.** `hm/shadow!` lives in
`re-frame.hicasso.test.mounted`, so it needs the DOM that P1-F12 says the
documentation never provisions. That alone blocks it.

**(b) Its premise conflicts with the chapter's own advice, in the ordinary
case.** `hm/shadow!` needs `:reference` — the Reagent original — *still
mounted*, and the sample makes that concrete with two namespaces,
`app.views.article-row-reagent` and `app.views.article-row`. So proving a port
requires keeping the original alongside the port for the length of the
migration. But the same chapter says, three paragraphs later, "When the screen
is green and its browser tests pass, remove the Reagent original." Those are
compatible in principle — keep it, prove it, then delete it — and the chapter
never says so, never shows the intermediate two-namespace state, and never
mentions that the *unported* callers (P1-F08) are pointing at one of the two.

Concretely, for a `reg-view` application (P1-F06) there is a further problem
neither half addresses: to keep a `:reference` at all I would have had to keep
the old `reg-view` **and** the old `dispatch`-closure props **and** a second
copy of every shared view, in one namespace, compiling. That is a substantial
amount of scaffolding to stand up for a comparator I then could not run.

**Looked at**

- `20-migration-from-reagent.md` §3 in full, including the sabotage-control
  paragraph
- `15-testing.md` "Migration shadow tests"
- `api-reference.md` `hm/shadow!` row (the `:reference` / `:candidate` /
  `:initial-events` / `:script` roster)

**Resolved by**

Nothing. I substituted a different proof, and I want to be explicit that it is
weaker in one specific way and stronger in another. Weaker: it is not a
DOM-for-DOM comparison against the original, so a cosmetic divergence I did not
think to assert on would pass unnoticed — and shadow comparison's whole value is
catching exactly that. Stronger: it drives the *real* release bundle through a
real interaction sequence (sign in → open the editor → type → publish →
navigate → page the feed → favourite a card), which the chapter's own §3 note
concedes shadow comparison does not do ("It does not prove untested paths").

I also could not perform the chapter's sabotage control, since there was no
comparator to sabotage.

**Bead**

Two: (i) `hm/shadow!` inherits the L3 DOM gap and is the single most costly
place to inherit it, since it is a named step of the migration process; (ii) §3
should show the intermediate state — original kept, port beside it, callers
pointing where — because that state is what a migrator actually has to build.
close_reason:
Chapter 20 §3 rewritten (PR #9131). Both halves of the bead's ask are addressed at the chapter, and one thing the bead did not name turned out to be the concrete reason step 2 is unusable.

THE SAMPLE WAS WRONG. §3 passed the Reagent original as a plain Hiccup head, :reference [old/article-row {:article-id 7}]. shadow!'s own docstring says both sides are handed to Hicasso by mount!, so a foreign original arrives 'through the runtime's own crossing, [:> C props] or a declared h/defhost' - and a plain function in Hicasso head position is a loud refusal, not a Reagent render. The sample is now [:> old-article-row {:id 7}] with (def old-article-row (r/reactify-component old/article-row)) hoisted to top level, and the paragraph beneath says why :reference is a crossing and :candidate is a plain head.

Two consequences of that crossing are now stated. Prop names do NOT round-trip on this route - codec/host-entry camelCases the key, reagent impl.util/shallow-obj-to-map keywordizes the name React carried, so :article-id reaches the original as :articleId - which is why the sample crosses :id and lets both sides read the rest from the seeded frame. And the original's callbacks reach the frame through the crossing's declared contract, not through its own ambient dispatch closures.

(ii) THE INTERMEDIATE STATE, the bead's explicit ask: '### The intermediate state' is a three-namespace table - the original moved verbatim into app.views.article-row-reagent and rendered only by the shadow test; the port at app.views.article-row rendered by the shell and the test; the unported shell. Callers point at the PORT, including unported ones, which is what the new 'Views shared across the boundary' section (rf2-4387) is for. The removal advice is sequenced rather than free-floating: delete the original and the shadow test together, after checking no caller still points at it.

(i) THE L3 GAP: §3 now opens with '### What this step needs first' - hm/shadow! is an L3 door needing the test kit and a target with real React and a real DOM - so a reader is not ambushed at step 2 of 3, and the last section is named for when that is more than the screen is worth. The underlying gap (chapter 15 never says where the DOM comes from) is rf2-w4yz and is untouched here.

NOT RUN, and stated as such in the PR body. No in-repo test drives hm/shadow! with a foreign :reference - test_kit/test/re_frame/hicasso/shadow_dom_cljs_test.cljs uses Hicasso views on both sides of every row. The correction is derived from shadow!'s docstring and from reading Reagent's reactify-component and Hicasso's host-entry. The docstring's own example carries the same :article-id mis-naming and the same inline reactify-component; filed as rf2-rx99 (test_kit was outside this fence), which also notes the missing witness for the foreign-:reference route.

Gates: check_doc_slugs.py 0, mkdocs build --strict 0, check_guide_samples.py 0, each sabotage-controlled, all re-run green after rebase.

title: hic docs: chapter 20 says nothing about views SHARED across the migration boundary, and 09-interop.md does not say what a Reagent parent's props do at the crossing
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 1 (RealWorld/Conduit), a
BLINDED agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation - evidence about the surface, not a ratified design, since a pilot
proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own rule.
Full log: ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-realworld.friction-log.md (local-only).

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P1-F08 · outcome 2 · `unresolved` · `docs`

**Trying to**

Port "the feed" as a screen. Two of its views — `article-preview` (the article
card) and `pagination` — are also rendered by `profile.cljs`, which is not one
of my two screens and stays on Reagent.

**Expected**

Chapter 20 to say something. Its §2 is called "Port one screen by hand" and its
whole argument is that a screen is the right unit: "Migrate a complete screen
rather than changing all component declarations… A screen-level port gives
shadow comparison a useful unit." A shared view is what makes "a complete
screen" ambiguous, and in any real application there is always one.

**Instead**

Silence. The chapter's only nearby advice points the other way — "When the
screen is green and its browser tests pass, remove the Reagent original.
Keeping both copies invites future divergence" — which forbids the duplication
route without offering the alternative.

**Looked at**

- `20-migration-from-reagent.md` §2, §3
- `09-interop.md` "Render a Hicasso view from native React"
- `escape-ladder.md` — the `h/as-component` rung, which is about "going
  outward" generally rather than about this boundary

**Resolved by**

Choosing to move both shared views to Hicasso and bridge them back out with
`h/as-component`, so `profile.cljs` mounts them as `[:> article-preview-component
{…}]`. This worked and I now think it is right — the boundary lands on the
*view*, so there is one implementation — but I want to record how uncertain it
was at the time. I nearly duplicated instead, which the chapter would have let
me do without a word of warning beyond a general one about divergence.

One consequence I did not anticipate and should have: bridging a view outward
makes its props cross React, so the props contract stops being a CLJS-only
concern. It worked here (a CLJS map at `:article` and a vector at `:on-select`
both survived the round trip intact through the Reagent adapter's `[:>]`), but
nothing in the docs promised that, and `09-interop.md` only says React props
come back "with canonical names… and identity-preserved values" from the
*Hicasso* side. I could not find a statement about what a **Reagent** parent
does to a CLJS value on the way in.

**Bead**

Chapter 20 needs a short section on views shared across the migration
boundary, and `09-interop.md`'s `h/as-component` section should say what a
Reagent parent's props do at the crossing.
close_reason:
Chapter 20 now carries '### Views shared across the boundary' (PR #9131). Premise HELD for the chapter half: §2 argued a screen is the right unit and said nothing about a view rendered by both a ported and an unported screen, while its only nearby advice ('remove the Reagent original ... keeping both copies invites future divergence') forbade duplication without offering the alternative.

The section says the boundary lands on the VIEW - port it once with the first screen that needs it and bridge it back out with h/as-component, so there is one implementation - and shows both sides, the Hicasso view with its minted component and the Reagent caller rendering ^{:key id} [:> article-preview-component {:id id}].

ONE HALF OF THE PREMISE DID NOT HOLD, and the chapter now states the opposite. The bead reports that a CLJS map at :article and a vector at :on-select 'both survived the round trip intact through the Reagent adapter's [:>]'. Reagent 2.0.1's own source contradicts both: impl.template/convert-prop-value sends a keyword to its name, a CLJS map to a camel-cased JS object with values recursively converted, and any other coll? through clj->js (deep); only js-val? things - strings, numbers, booleans, nil, functions - cross unchanged. Prop NAMES do round-trip (dash-to-prop-name camel-cases, codec/prop-key decodes back), which is probably what the pilot was seeing. So the chapter now states the conversion and gives the shape that avoids it: cross an id, read the rest with h/sub - which is what re-frame2 wants anyway - and prefer h/as-element where the Reagent caller is an ordinary body, since those props never cross React at all.

09-INTEROP HALF NOT DONE: docs/core/hicasso/09-interop.md was outside this dispatch's fence. Filed as rf2-d4n8 with the verified mechanism sentence ready to lift.

Gates: check_doc_slugs.py 0, mkdocs build --strict 0, check_guide_samples.py 0, each sabotage-controlled, all re-run green after rebase.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P1-F01 · outcome 2 · `inferred` · `docs`

**Trying to**

Work out how a Hicasso screen gets rendered inside an application whose root is
already mounted by another substrate. The brief scopes the migration to two
screens and says the rest stays on Reagent, so the two view layers have to
coexist inside one page and one frame.

**Expected**

The migration chapter to open with this, since a partial migration is the
normal case it is written for. Chapter 20 §2 is titled "Port one screen by
hand" and its whole premise is one screen at a time — so the mechanics of a
half-migrated tree are the first thing a reader needs.

**Instead**

Chapter 20 never says how a ported screen is reached from the unported shell.
Its translation table has a row `r/reactify-component → h/as-component, the
outward bridge`, which is the answer, but it is presented as one of thirteen
mechanical spellings rather than as *the* joint that makes a screen-at-a-time
migration possible. `00-installation.md` teaches the only mounting story the
chapters carry — `h/mount!` onto a bare DOM node — which is the whole-app case
and is not what a screen-at-a-time port does.

**Looked at**

- `20-migration-from-reagent.md` §2 (translation table), §3 (shadow comparison)
- `00-installation.md` "Mount a first screen", "More than one root"
- `09-interop.md` "Render a Hicasso view from native React"
- `api-reference.md` `h/as-component` row
- `escape-ladder.md` line 201

**Resolved by**

Inferring the shape from `09-interop.md`: `(def home-page* (h/as-component
home-page))` at top level, then rendering `[:> home-page*]` from the existing
Reagent `root-view`. Nothing in the docs shows a Reagent parent doing this —
`09-interop.md` names "UIx, raw React, JavaScript, or TypeScript parents" and
does not name Reagent, which is the one parent a *migration from Reagent*
guarantees you have.

**Bead**

Migration chapter should carry the half-migrated-tree recipe explicitly: the
`h/as-component` bridge, a Reagent parent, and the fact that one frame serves
both subtrees.
close_reason:
Chapter 20 §2 now opens with '### The half-migrated tree' (PR #9131, docs/core/hicasso/20-migration-from-reagent.md). Premise held: the chapter carried the outward bridge only as one of thirteen table rows and never said how a ported screen is reached from the unported shell.

The recipe states three facts and shows both doors from a Reagent parent:
(1) ONE FRAME SERVES BOTH HALVES - impl.collector/resolve-frame! reads re-frame.adapter.context/frame-context and re-frame.views.provider/frame-context IS that same var, so a shell already under [rf/frame-root ...] or [rf/frame-provider ...] supplies the frame to a Hicasso subtree; no h/mount!, no second frame, no second React root.
(2) KEEP THE ADAPTER YOU HAVE - re-frame.hicasso.substrate's own docstring: 'installing one of them under a Hicasso tree is supported ... every React-shaped adapter reads the one shared context object'. The Hicasso substrate adapter is what lets a FINISHED application drop its view-library dependency, not a prerequisite for rendering a Hicasso view.
(3) TWO BRIDGE DOORS - h/as-element inside the Reagent body (props never cross React's prop channel) and h/as-component minted once at top level (when the parent must own mount/key/re-render), with the mint-once law stated.

close_reason: PR #9132 (head d98e796bb5). PREMISE HOLDS, reproduced: the default report path was the bare name reagent-to-hicasso-report.edn, which resolves against the process's WORKING DIRECTORY - and the chapter's first command is a cd into the tool's own directory, so the documented invocation wrote into the re-frame2 checkout the migrator had been told to treat as a read-only build input. value:
`git grep` with a pattern that STARTS WITH `/` is MSYS path-mangled on this Windows host and silently returns ZERO for everything — including patterns that certainly match. Found by a worker on 2026-09-04 and reproduced by the mayor on the same tree:

  git grep -c "/client-root" -- 'examples/real-apps/realworld_http/*'   -> no output, exit 0
  git grep -c "client-root"  -- 'examples/real-apps/realworld_http/*'   -> core.cljs:1
  grep -rn "client-root" examples/real-apps/realworld_http/             -> 1 hit

MSYS sees a leading `/` as a Unix path and rewrites it to a Windows path before git ever sees it, so the pattern searched for is not the pattern written.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY BUG: it fails OPEN and it defeats the standard control. A census over qualified names — `/render!`, `/mount!`, `"/client-root"` — is a normal thing to write when looking for a var by its unqualified tail. The zero looks exactly like "this symbol is not used", which is usually the conclusion the census exists to support. And a control that SHARES THE SHAPE of the target (the advice that catches most census bugs) is mangled identically, so the control reads zero too and confirms the wrong answer. Only a SECOND, DIFFERENT instrument catches it — `grep -rn` is not MSYS-mangled the same way.

WHAT TO DO:
- Never start a `git grep` pattern with `/`. Anchor on the namespace side instead (`census.clj` not `/census`), or match the bare tail and filter, or escape as `[/]client-root`.
- Keep the two-instrument rule for every census, and make the second instrument a DIFFERENT TOOL rather than a different pattern in the same tool. This is the case that proves why "two independent instruments" means independent in mechanism, not just in wording.
- The already-recorded sibling trap is the pathspec one: `git grep -- 'implementation/*/src'` matches NOTHING because a git wildcard pathspec matches the whole path — use `implementation/*/src/*`. That is a PATHSPEC bug; this one is a PATTERN bug. They are different and both fail open.

RELATED, from the same worker: every file in `migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod/` is pure CRLF and carries non-ASCII, so edits there need byte verification (crlf==lf count, UTF-8 decode) and emitted EDN is worth hex-checking for U+FFFD. Console `?` glyphs on this host are terminal rendering, NOT corruption — do not chase them.

title: hic docs: there is no inward bridge from Reagent INTO a Hicasso tree, and the corpus never says so - chapter 00's 'two subtrees resolve one frame' reads as a promise it does not make
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 2 (LinearLite), a BLINDED
agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on

recommendation, and it is evidence about the surface rather than a ratified design -
a pilot proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own
rule. The log is at ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-linearlite.friction-log.md
(local-only) and in the pilot workspace.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P2-F18 · outcome 2 · `unresolved` · `docs`

**Trying to** Honour the brief's scope note — "Leave anything else on Reagent;
the two view layers coexisting is expected and is itself worth observing" — by
keeping one view on Reagent and rendering it from the Hicasso tree.

**Expected** Some documented crossing. Chapter 00 is encouraging: "A Reagent or
UIx adapter under a Hicasso tree keeps working exactly as it did, and is what
you want when the page also renders that substrate's own components: every
React-shaped adapter writes the same frame context, so **the two subtrees
resolve one frame**." That sentence describes exactly the arrangement I wanted.

**Instead** There is no such crossing, and the corpus never says so. Measured:
a `rf/reg-view` rendered as `[reagent-footer]` from inside `board-page`
compiles clean, then refuses at first paint and **blanks the page**:

```clojure
{:head #object[cljs.core.MetaFn]
 :rf.error/id :rf.error/hicasso-bad-head
 :view "linearlite.core/board-page" …}
```

Note the head is reported as `cljs.core.MetaFn` — for this mistake the
diagnostic cannot name the offender the way it named `status_picker` in P2-F16,
because a Reagent view *is* an anonymous meta-carrying function.

The asymmetry is the finding. Hicasso **out** to a foreign parent has a named
door: `h/as-component`, "the outward bridge — a real React component for a
Hiccup head, so a native parent, a UIx component or plain JavaScript can mount a
minted view under the frame it is already in". Hicasso **in** from Reagent has
none. `[:>]` and `h/defhost` take real React components, and a Reagent view is
not one. Thirteen of the 29 pages mention Reagent and not one addresses this.

**Looked at** `00-installation.md` §"Hicasso needs a substrate adapter" and
§"More than one root"; `09-interop.md`; `10-native-tier.md`;
`escape-ladder.md`; `api-reference.md` §Markup (`h/as-component`);
`20-migration-from-reagent.md` §2 and §"When not to use the full process";
grepped all 29 pages for `reagent`, `coexist`, `side by side`, `alongside`.

**Resolved by** Not resolved. I reverted the probe and finished with every view
on Hicasso. **What the two layers coexisting actually means here — and it does
work — is the SUBSTRATE, not the markup**: this application ran the entire
session on `re-frame.adapter.reagent` with a Hicasso view tree above it, exactly
as chapter 00 promises, and that half cost nothing and produced no friction at
all. What does not work is nesting one layer's *views* inside the other's.

The migration chapter's advice — "Migrate a complete screen rather than changing
all component declarations… A screen-level port gives shadow comparison a useful
unit" — turns out to be load-bearing rather than stylistic: a screen is the
smallest unit that *can* migrate, because the boundary between the two layers
has to fall at a root. Chapter 00 §"More than one root" is the mechanism for a
page that genuinely needs both (a Reagent root and a Hicasso root naming the
same `:frame`), but it is written about two Hicasso roots and never connected to
this problem.

**Bead** One short section, probably in chapter 20 beside the screen-at-a-time
advice: *a Hicasso view cannot appear inside a Reagent tree or vice versa; the
boundary is a root.* Name `h/as-component` as the one direction that has a door,
and point at §"More than one root" for a page that must show both — two roots on
one frame. Right now the encouraging sentence in chapter 00 about "the two
subtrees resolv[ing] one frame" reads like permission to interleave markup, and
a reader who tries it gets a blank page and an id that cannot name what it
refused.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9137. Premise HALF-REFUTED, and the correction is the useful half. There is no HICASSO-OWNED inward door and the refusal is real (impl/codec HD-016 raises :rf.error/hicasso-bad-head for a plain fn in head position; impl/error/fail! throws with :recovery :no-recovery, so it is a throw and the page does blank) - but a crossing DOES exist: r/reactify-component plus the raw [:>] escape. That is what this repo's own hm/shadow! reference mount uses (test_kit mounted.cljs), what MIG-22 in skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-judgment.md already documents, and what the chapter 20 that merged today relies on for its :reference. Outward confirmed real and not restated here: h/as-component and h/as-element, with foreign_root_bridge_dom_cljs_test driving five mounting routes including a Reagent parent through both doors. Fix landed in ch00 (mine; ch20 was another worker's): the 'two subtrees resolve one frame' sentence now says which crossing it is about - the frame context IS shared (impl.mount/provider writes re-frame.adapter.context/frame-context, impl.collector/resolve-frame! reads it) but that is what a COMPONENT crossing reads, not permission to interleave markup - followed by the asymmetry as two bullets and the rule that the practical boundary is a root. No contradiction with ch20, which states the same head-position refusal in its shadow-comparison section.

**Looked at**

**Resolved by**

Not resolved through the documentation. What I did instead: kept the migrated
screens' view coverage at L2 (`ht/tree`, 17 tests, 170 assertions, green), and
proved the React-level and DOM-level claims *outside* the test kit — by booting
the release bundle in a jsdom I installed myself and driving it with real DOM
events (`realworld/boot-check.cjs`, `realworld/drive-check.cjs`). That is

title: hic docs: chapter 15 never says a view body returning nil answers a root with empty :children rather than nil
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 1 (RealWorld/Conduit), a
BLINDED agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation - evidence about the surface, not a ratified design, since a pilot
proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own rule.
Full log: ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-realworld.friction-log.md (local-only).

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P1-F10 · outcome 1 · `inferred` · `docs`

**Trying to**

Assert that `pagination` renders nothing when there is only one page — the body
is `(when (> page-count 1) …)`, so it returns `nil`.

**Expected**

`(nil? (ht/tree …))`. Chapter 15's troubleshooting has a row for exactly this
symptom: "Tree assertion sees `nil` | A `when` returned `nil`; it renders
nothing but still appears in authored data | Assert that `nil`, or filter it
before comparing."

**Instead**

```
expected: (nil? (ht/tree [articles/pagination {…}] {:subs {}}))
  actual: (not (nil? {:rf.ui/tree-version 1, :children []}))
```

The troubleshooting row is about a `nil` **child** inside a tree. A body whose
whole return is `nil` still answers a versioned root with no children, and the
chapter does not say so anywhere — `ht/tree` is described as answering "its
versioned semantic tree" with no statement about the empty case.

**Looked at**

- `15-testing.md` L2 section and its troubleshooting table
- `api-reference.md` `ht/tree` row

**Resolved by**

Asserting `(empty? (:children tree))` instead, plus a positive check that no
`<nav>` wrapper exists. Correct, and arguably a better assertion — but reached
by failure, not by reading.

**Bead**

One sentence in chapter 15: a body returning `nil` answers a root with empty
`:children`, not `nil`.
close_reason: PR #9136. Premise HELD, verified at source AND by running. Source: ht/tree's root construction is (if (and (= 1 (count children)) (map? (nth children 0))) (assoc ... tree-version-key) {tree-version-key tree-version :children children}) -- with a code comment saying the empty case is {:children []} and NOT {} because :children is the fragment's required discriminator. ht/tree-version is 1. Run: re-frame.hicasso.test-kit-runtime-parity-cljs-test carries the row 'a body that renders nothing roots in an EMPTY FRAGMENT' with :form nil driven through (ht/tree [(fn [_] form)]) and asserted against :tree {:rf.ui/tree-version v :children []}; ran green with the slice L2 suite -- 29 tests / 130 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0. New subsection 'The root is always a node' plus a troubleshooting row; the pre-existing 'Tree assertion sees nil' row was about a nil CHILD, a different symptom, and is left as is.

title: hic docs: chapter 15's ht/intents example compares the whole intent stream, which a route-link's navigate head (carrying a frame id) breaks
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 2 (LinearLite), a BLINDED
agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation, and it is evidence about the surface rather than a ratified design -
a pilot proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own
rule. The log is at ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-linearlite.friction-log.md
(local-only) and in the pilot workspace.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P2-F10 · outcome 1 · `inferred` · `tooling`

**Trying to** Assert on the intents a Hicasso view carries, using `ht/intents`
the way chapter 15's L2 example does: `(is (= [[:todo/toggle 7]] (ht/intents
tree)))` — an exact equality over the whole intent stream.

**Expected** A stream of application intents.

**Instead** Any tree containing an `h/route-link` also carries routing's own
click decision, and that decision embeds **the frame id**:

```clojure
[:re-frame.hicasso.impl.intent/navigate
 {:frame :re-frame.hicasso.test/probe-1
  :payload [:rf.route/url-requested {:url "/issues/srv-1" …}] …}]
```

Under `ht/tree` that frame id is a per-probe counter. My two probe tests
produced `probe-1` and `probe-2` **in deftest order**, so an exact-equality
assertion over an intent stream containing a link is stable only until somebody
adds a test above it. Chapter 07 shows this shape and says "It is not an
authoring spelling", and chapter 15 recommends the exact-equality assertion —
neither warns that the two combine into a positional dependency.

**Looked at** `15-testing.md` §L2 (the `ht/intents` example) and §"Prevent
vacuous tests with a sabotage twin"; `07-routing-and-navigation.md` §"Render an
application route link" (the generated-Hiccup fence); the printed trees from my
own probes.

**Resolved by** Not using `ht/intents` at all on any tree containing a link.
Every link assertion in `views_test.cljs` reads `:href` instead — the router
built it from `:to` + `:params`, which is the fact worth pinning, and it is
stable. Guessed, and I am confident it is right, but nothing told me.

**Bead** Chapter 15's `ht/intents` example is on a tree with no link in it. One
line under it — "a `route-link`'s navigation decision appears in this stream and
carries a frame id; assert its `:href`, or filter the stream, rather than
comparing it whole" — would close it. Alternatively `ht/intents` could omit
navigate heads, or the probe frame id could be constant.
close_reason: PR #9136. Premise HELD, verified at source AND by running. Source: impl/route_link.cljs mints :on-click as [intent/navigate-head {:frame frame-kw :payload payload :native? native? :veto on-click}] -- the ambient frame is embedded in the intent VECTOR; ht/intents collects (vals (:events n)) keeping vectors, so the navigate head IS in the stream. Under ht/tree the frame is (keyword "re-frame.hicasso.test" (str "probe-" (swap! !probe-seq inc))) off a defonce atom, so it is a global monotonic counter across the run -- exactly the positional dependency the pilot measured. Run: re-frame.hicasso.route-link-cljs-test, 17 tests / 40 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0; its 'the-click-decision-is-readable-off-the-tree' reads {:keys [frame payload native? veto]} off (second on-click) and its 'two-renders-of-one-link-are-equal-data' pins :href as '/profile/jane', routing's own synthesis -- which is why the chapter now recommends asserting :href for the link. Chapter 15 keeps the whole-stream equality in the todo example (that tree has no link) and adds a subsection giving the membership form (contains? (set (ht/intents tree)) ...) and the filtered-stream form for when order is the claim, plus a troubleshooting row. NOT actioned: the pilot's alternatives (ht/intents omitting navigate heads, or a constant probe frame id) are framework changes outside a docs bead -- file separately if wanted.

title: TESTING.md's surface-signal table does not know about test_react_jvm (rf2-6r9j.87 follow-up)
description:
PR #9125 (rf2-6r9j.87) added a `test_react_jvm` output to .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh and carved implementation/adapters/test-react/** out of the generic shipped-adapter arm. TESTING.md is the canonical surface-signal table (CLAUDE.md names it as such) and was outside that dispatch's fence, so it now carries a falsehood plus an omission.

WHAT IS WRONG, precisely, at TESTING.md as of PR #9125:

1. Line 193, the `adapter_diagnostic` row. Its TRIGGER column reads 'an adapter artefact changes (and implementation/core/**, which every adapter resolves by :local/root)'. That is now false for one of the four adapters: a change under implementation/adapters/test-react/ no longer sets adapter_diagnostic at all. The row's GATES column is still correct -- jvm-adapters-test-react IS still gated on adapter_diagnostic, because the job condition is now a DISJUNCTION and adapter_diagnostic is the reverse edge from core, which the fixture depends on. So the fix is to the trigger clause, not the gates clause.

2. There is no row for the new `test_react_jvm` output. It should read roughly: trigger = implementation/adapters/test-react/{src,test}/** or its deps.edn; gates = jvm-adapters-test-react. Note the asymmetry worth stating in the row: src/test also arm cljs_node_test (the fixture is CLJC so it runs under BOTH hosts, which is the point of it), while deps.edn arms the JVM lane only, because shadow reads its source paths from implementation/shadow-cljs.edn and its deps from implementation/deps.edn and so cannot see this artefact's own deps.edn. A prose-only README edit arms NOTHING executable -- its markdown links and inventory are still covered by the always-on verify-readme-links job.

3. Line 241, the 'Adapter JVM classpath probes' row, says 'Two siblings on the same adapter_diagnostic gate' and names jvm-reagent-slim and jvm-adapters-test-react. After #9125 jvm-adapters-test-react is no longer on the SAME gate -- it is on a superset. The substance of the row (it is real coverage, 35 deftests, not a skip-ok probe) is unchanged and worth keeping.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN #9125: the dispatch fence was report-changed-surfaces.sh + its mirror + test.yml + test-fast-pr.sh, plus implementation/adapters/test-react/**. TESTING.md is none of those. It is not on CLAUDE.md's hot-zone list either, so this should be a low-conflict single-file edit for whoever picks it up.

VERIFY AFTER EDITING: no gate validates TESTING.md's prose or its table semantics. Its markdown links and heading anchors are covered by scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci (repo-root markdown is that gate's surface, NOT check_doc_slugs.py's -- nominate by path, not by job name), which runs in test.yml's always-on verify-readme-links job. Column counts and the truth of the trigger clauses have to be checked by hand and said so in the PR body.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9133 (branch worker/tierpin-a). All three defects corrected in TESTING.md. (1) The adapter_diagnostic row's TRIGGER no longer claims 'an adapter artefact changes' unqualified -- it names the implementation/adapters/test-react/** carve-out and routes the reader to the new output, and it now also explains why jvm-adapters-test-react still appears in the GATES column: adapter_diagnostic is the REVERSE edge (the fixture depends on core), so the job reads a disjunction rather than either output alone. (2) A test_react_jvm row was added, stating the asymmetry the bead asked for: src/** and test/** also arm cljs_node_test because the fixture is .cljc and runs under both hosts, while deps.edn arms the JVM lane ONLY, since shadow takes its source paths from implementation/shadow-cljs.edn and its deps from implementation/deps.edn and cannot see this artefact's own deps.edn; a prose-only README edit arms nothing executable and is still covered by the always-on verify-readme-links job. (3) The skip-ok table's 'Two siblings on the same adapter_diagnostic gate' is reworded -- jvm-reagent-slim is on adapter_diagnostic alone while jvm-adapters-test-react is on the superset -- and the row's substance (real coverage, not a probe) is kept. MEASURED, not read off the script: every trigger claim was exercised against the classifier using the real tracked paths, controls firing. test-react src/test/deps/README all return adapter_diagnostic=false, while reagent-slim src and core src both return adapter_diagnostic=true with test_react_jvm=false. The superset claim was checked against the job's actual if: condition in test.yml. HAND-VERIFIED because no gate covers it: column counts across all eight TESTING.md tables are uniform. That check caught a real defect before it landed -- a draft of the skip-ok row wrote the gate as a code span containing two pipe characters, and GitHub splits table rows on a pipe even inside a code span, taking that row to 5 pipes against the table's 3; reworded as prose. GATES: check_readme_links.py --ci captured exit 0 (the correct gate by path -- check_doc_slugs.py does not cover repo-root markdown), and a planted broken link in TESTING.md prose returned captured exit 1 naming TESTING.md:242, proving the gate read this worktree. Restore verified by git blob hash.

title: Synchronize reply-conformance inventory with its live suites
description:
## Finding

The reply-conformance implementation was deliberately narrowed to vocabulary plus egress projection, but several surrounding inventory comments still describe the deleted synthetic family functor suite or names that never exist. The changed-surface policy test also uses a nonexistent reply-conformance filename instead of a tracked file.

## Evidence

- Commit `540c8af134` deleted `reply_functor_law_cljs_test.cljc` because it only re-proved core laws with synthetic transforms. It updated `implementation/reply-conformance/deps.edn` and both surviving namespace docstrings to say core plus the timer probe own functor laws.
- `implementation/README.md:225-232` still says this surface holds “the family-level functor/naturality law at the target-relocating families.”
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:223-240` carries the same retired ownership claim and names route-loader relay / machine-spawn `:on-done` even though the deleted suite never exercised production relocation seams.
- `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs:3706-3710` names `implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocabulary_conformance_cljs_test.cljc`; the tracked file is `reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc`. History shows the phantom spelling entered in `863a00b85c` and was never a tracked path. The classifier glob still returns the expected flags, so this is a weak/stale fixture rather than current routing failure.
- `reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:99-111` documents an `:error-work-status` descriptor field, but no `families` row or executable consumer defines it; history shows it has been documentation-only since the surface was introduced.
- The live surface consists of exactly four tracked files: `deps.edn`, the shared completion-time fixture, the vocabulary suite, and the egress-projection suite. Both suites are enrolled in the consolidated Node build and JVM `clojure -M:test` lane (currently 27 tests / 533 assertions).
- Searches of all tracker text for the deleted suite, phantom filename, and descriptor key found no existing owner.

## Impact

Maintainers are told a conformance guarantee exists at a family integration seam that has no such test, while the CI policy pin demonstrates routing with a filename no developer can edit. The dead descriptor field also invites a future author to populate inert metadata. None changes runtime today, but together they make coverage and ownership harder to reason about.

## Recommendation

Synchronize the implementation layout, Shadow build commentary, CI classifier fixture, and descriptor documentation with the live two-suite surface. Name vocabulary and egress projection as the owned guarantees; point the classifier test at the tracked vocab filename (and optionally the tracked egress file as an additional real-path row); remove the nonexistent descriptor field from the matrix documentation. Keep functor-law ownership explicitly at core plus timer-probe.

## Risks and contracts

Do not restore the deleted synthetic functor suite or weaken the actual core/timer functor tests. Do not change changed-surface outputs: reply-conformance remains source-less and should arm JVM plus consolidated Node only. Do not rename the tracked namespace/file as part of this cleanup unless a separately justified naming migration covers every selector and reference.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No implementation inventory/build comment claims reply-conformance owns family-level functor/naturality integration.
2. Core `re-frame.reply` plus timer-probe remain named as the functor-law owners where useful.
3. Changed-surface policy tests use tracked reply-conformance file paths and retain the same positive and negative outputs.
4. The descriptor documentation lists only keys the `families` matrix actually consumes.
5. Repository search finds no live reference to the deleted `reply_functor_law_cljs_test.cljc`, the phantom `reply_vocabulary_conformance_cljs_test.cljc`, or the inert `:error-work-status` descriptor.
6. Focused classifier tests and both reply-conformance runtime lanes pass.
notes:
PARTIAL 2026-09-03 17:56 AUSEST — PR #9124 (branch worker/shadlane-a, head ed9ecc12771ed305312a594df611bf2bfe32f876). LEFT OPEN: AC3 and the phantom-filename limb of AC5 are outside the dispatched fence.

DONE in #9124:
- AC1 met. The retired ownership claim 'the family-level functor/naturality law at the target-relocating families' is gone from BOTH inventory comments — implementation/README.md and implementation/shadow-cljs.edn. Both now name the two guarantees the tier actually holds: the cross-family reply VOCABULARY and the shared EGRESS-PROJECTION boundaries (trace-summary, project-egress). The shadow-cljs.edn edit is comment-only, 3 lines out / 4 in, inside the :node-test source-path block; no build id, source path, port or root changed, and the file was re-parsed with clojure.edn/read-string afterwards (80 builds, :dev-http keys intact) to prove the EDN still reads.
- AC2 met. Functor ownership is pointed at core plus the timer probe in both edited comments. No change was needed to implementation/reply-conformance/deps.edn or to either surviving namespace docstring — 540c8af134 had already corrected all three, so that premise of the bead was already satisfied and is recorded here rather than re-litigated.
- AC4 met. :error-work-status is removed from the descriptor doc block in reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc. title: Test-React tests: retire the superseded duplicate cache-lifecycle case
description:
## Finding

The single-frame dispose/reinstall cache regression is maintained twice under `implementation/adapters/test-react/test/` even though both copies now run on both hosts:

- `test_react_cljs_test.cljc:240-312` defines `default-sub-cache-keys`, `default-entry-ref-count`, and `dispose-adapter-clears-frame-sub-cache-no-stale-cross-lifecycle-reads`.
- `test_react_dispose_sub_cache_cljs_test.cljc:35-72` defines the same two queries and `dispose-adapter-clears-sub-cache-and-recomputes-fresh`.

Both cases register the same seed event/sub, seed `1`, materialise `[::n]` at ref-count 1, dispose, assert the slot/ref-count vanished, reinstall, seed `99`, and prove a fresh subscription reads 99 at ref-count 1. The companion docstring says this directly: "The substantive assertion lives in both" (`:5`) and identifies its only unique coverage as the second multi-frame case (`:16-18`).

## Supersession evidence

Commit `bd492e37c9` added both copies because the then-main namespace was `re-frame.adapter.test-react-test`: Cognitect discovered it on the JVM, while Shadow's `cljs-test$` selector did not, so the separate `-cljs-test` namespace supplied CLJS coverage. Commit `1a14917bda` renamed the main namespace/file to `test-react-cljs-test` specifically so that whole suite also runs under Shadow. Commit `1708179722` then removed the old JVM-only rationale but retained the duplicate. Today both files end in `-cljs-test`, both are `.cljc`, `clojure -M:test` discovers both, and `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:650-653` selects both. The current standalone run is green at 35 tests / 160 assertions.

## Impact

The same seven assertions and setup/teardown execute and must be maintained twice on the JVM and twice in Node. The copies already use different lifecycle fixtures (hand-reset state in the main suite versus `make-reset-runtime-fixture` in the cache companion), so a future edit can create apparent coverage while only one copy matches the real fixture contract. The main copy also keeps three otherwise-unused requires (`re-frame.core`, `re-frame.subs`, `re-frame.frame`) and two one-consumer helpers in the lifecycle suite.

## Disposition

Keep the focused cache companion as the owner of both cache tests: retain its single-frame fresh-recompute case and its unique every-live-frame case, and delete the duplicated cache section/helpers from the main lifecycle suite. Remove imports made dead by that deletion. While touching these two test ns forms, remove the unreferenced `:as ctest` aliases (the referred test vars remain) and replace the seed handlers' unread `{:keys [db]}` bindings; clj-kondo currently reports the three unread `db` bindings at main `:264` and companion `:47,78` (the main one disappears with the duplicate). Do not weaken or delete the companion's multi-frame assertion.

## Risks and boundaries

This is test consolidation only. Preserve `dispose-adapter!`'s all-frame cache clearing, ref-count removal, reinstall freshness, JVM+CLJS coverage, and the standard fixture. Do not simplify the lifecycle simulator or fold the two genuinely different single-frame/multi-frame cache properties into one opaque assertion.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Exactly one single-frame dispose/reinstall/fresh-recompute regression remains, alongside the existing multi-frame regression.
2. `test_react_cljs_test.cljc` no longer contains the duplicate cache helpers/test or its now-dead `rf`/`subs`/`frame` requires; both test namespace forms carry no unused `ctest` alias or unread seed-handler binding.
3. `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/adapters/test-react` passes with the expected duplicate removed (currently 34 tests / 153 assertions), and `npm run test:cljs` or a focused Shadow run proves both surviving Test-React namespaces execute under CLJS.
4. Any hard-coded Test-React suite counts in `TESTING.md` and `.github/workflows/test.yml` are updated from actual runner output.
5. The multi-frame case still fails under a negative control that clears only `:rf/default`, proving consolidation did not erase the all-frame tooth.

BOOT DEADLOCK: non-nilable app-db path schemas + whole-registry per-commit validation = an app that never leaves `{}`, silently, in DEV ONLY. Diagnosed 2026-09-04 on rf2-2xzc (PR #9134) after two blinded pilots and an operator had each mis-attributed it.

THE MECHANISM. Register N app-db path schemas against a named frame at ns-load. App-db starts `{}`, and each slice is seeded by its own feature's `:*/initialise` — separate events, therefore SEPARATE COMMITS. The candidate validator walks EVERY registered path over the WHOLE candidate app-db at EVERY `:db` commit, with no exemption for a path nothing has written yet (spec/010 states this outright). An unwritten path reads `nil`, which is not a `[:map …]`, so the FIRST seed is rejected by the N-1 siblings still absent — and so is every later one. App-db never leaves `{}`.

WHY IT PRESENTS AS AN HTTP BUG, which is what cost three investigations: a rejected candidate does not walk `:fx` either (spec/010 row 4), so the feature's HTTP effect never fires. The symptom reads exactly like "replies do not settle in Chrome". No request is ever ISSUED. A patched `set-timeout!` recorded ZERO timers armed.

WHY DEV ONLY: the validator's whole body sits inside `(if interop/debug-enabled? … true)`. A release build returns `true` and installs everything — so dev is broken and release is fine, which inverts the usual intuition and is why "it works in the release build" was read as a rendering or timing difference.

THE DISCRIMINATOR THAT EXPLAINS THE CONFUSING PART: any panel whose state lives OUTSIDE app-db keeps working. A state machine's snapshot is runtime-db, validated against the machine's own `[:schemas :data]`, and its events return only `:fx`, never `:db` — so `app-effect?` is false and the app-db validator never runs. On the failing page the one working panel was the only one that never touched app-db. An app registering no app-db schemas at all is unaffected entirely.

THE CORRECT IDIOM, already taught in the corpus with its rationale — `examples/patterns/boot/schema.cljs`: "Each slot below starts out nil … so every registration wears a `:maybe` to stay valid through the loading phases."

THE COVERAGE GAP THAT LET IT SHIP: `reg-app-schemas` is FRAME-LOCAL to the named frame, and every existing test drives an anonymous frame, where the registry is inert. So no suite could see it. Closing that needs a test that installs the app's real registry on its own frame — which means naming the registry as a value rather than only registering it as a side effect.

HOW TO RECOGNISE IT FAST: app-db `{}` after boot, zero page errors at any level, zero failed requests, a small constant `#app` innerHTML, and a `:trace` listener showing `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` with `:rollback? true` and no `:rf.fx/handled`. Note the trace stream is DEV-ONLY and the always-on `:errors` stream never sees these — that silence is the whole reason this took three attempts.

GitHub splits a markdown TABLE ROW on every `|`, INCLUDING pipes inside a backticked code span. So writing a gate name, a shell alternation or any `||` inside a code span in a table cell silently adds columns to that row and breaks the table's rendering. Nothing in this repo catches it: no gate validates prose, tables or rendering at all, and the two link gates strip fences before extracting.

Caught 2026-09-04 by a worker's own hand check before it landed — its first draft of a TESTING.md row wrote the gate as a code span containing `||`, which took that row to 5 pipes against the table's 3. Reworded as prose. This is the concrete case for the standing rule that table column counts are verified BY HAND and said so in the PR body: the check is not ceremony, it has caught a real defect.

If a pipe is genuinely needed inside a table cell, escape it as `\|`. Prefer rewording to prose.

RELATED, same worker, same run — the harness's reported exit code disagreed with the captured one on TWO of three sabotage runs: the harness said "exit code 0" while the file the runner wrote read 1. Both were deliberately sabotaged runs, so believing the harness would have read as "the control does not bite" and inverted the conclusion. Quote the number the runner itself wrote to a file; never the harness's report about the same run.

title: hic docs: neither chapter 00's mount section nor chapter 07's routed-root recipe puts an h/error-boundary at the root, so any refusal blanks the whole page
description:

agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation, and it is evidence about the surface rather than a ratified design -
a pilot proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own
rule. The log is at ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-linearlite.friction-log.md
(local-only) and in the pilot workspace.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P2-F19 · outcome 2 · `inferred` · `docs`

**Trying to** Decide whether the application root needed an error boundary. I
only asked because P2-F16's induced failure blanked the whole page.

**Expected** The boot recipes to have told me.

**Instead** `h/error-boundary` is a first-class Hiccup head — it is in the
api-reference §Markup with its three options, and chapter 17 owns it — but
**none of the three boot recipes in the corpus uses one**: not
`00-installation.md` §"Mount a first screen", not `cookbook.md` §Boot, not
`07-routing-and-navigation.md`'s routed `app-root`. So the shape a reader builds
by following the guide in order has no boundary anywhere, and a single refused
head — the very mistake chapters 01, 02 and 16 all warn about — takes the
application to a white screen with the error only in the console.

**Looked at** `api-reference.md` §Markup; `17-errors.md` (skimmed for the
boundary's contract); `00-installation.md`, `cookbook.md` and
`07-routing-and-navigation.md` boot/root recipes.

**Resolved by** Left it alone, deliberately: adding a root boundary is a
framework-shaped design decision the brief tells me not to make on my own
initiative, and it would have masked the outcome-5 evidence. Recorded as
friction instead, which is what the brief asks for.

**Bead** Put an `h/error-boundary` in chapter 07's routed-root recipe, or add
one line to chapter 00's mount section pointing at chapter 17. The routed root
is the natural home: it is already the place the corpus teaches you to key and
focus a page region, and it is the last common ancestor of everything that can
refuse.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9137, but NOT by the bead's literal remedy - that one collides with chapter 17. Consequence verified rather than asserted: impl/error/fail! THROWS (:recovery :no-recovery on every Hicasso refusal), and React unmounts a root whose tree throws with no boundary above it, which is what ch17's own opening paragraph and troubleshooting row already say. So the blank page is real. What does not hold is 'put an h/error-boundary at the root': ch17 'Place boundaries at useful recovery regions' argues against exactly that - 'a single boundary around the root turns every failure into a whole-page fallback and may remove navigation along with the broken content' - and names the region it wants instead, 'a route's main content while the surrounding shell remains usable'. That region IS ch07's routed root, which had none. The boundary is therefore placed inside <main>, below site-nav, where ch17 asks. It needs no :reset-key: the :key route already on <main> remounts the subtree on a route change, which ch07's own prose already states. Ch00's mount section gets the one-line pointer at ch17 the bead also asked for. Gates: check_guide_samples.py 0 (h/error-boundary resolves), check_doc_slugs.py 0, mkdocs --strict 0.

title: hic docs: chapter 07 never says a route deeper than one segment changes what relative asset paths resolve against - the page silently loses its stylesheet
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 2 (LinearLite), a BLINDED
agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation, and it is evidence about the surface rather than a ratified design -
a pilot proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own
rule. The log is at ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-linearlite.friction-log.md
(local-only) and in the pilot workspace.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P2-F13 · outcome 2 · `inferred` · `docs`

**Trying to** Deep-link straight to the new card-detail URL, `/issues/srv-1`,
and have the page look right.

**Expected** It to work, since the routing chapter treats `"/articles/:id"` as
the ordinary case.

**Instead** The application booted and rendered correctly, and the page was
**unstyled**. The host page `index.html` carries `href="_shared/css/style.css"`
— a *relative* URL, which was fine while every route was `/`. On `/issues/srv-1`
it resolves to `/issues/_shared/css/style.css`, 404. Same for the favicon.
Only `<script src="/js/main.js">` survived, because it happens to be absolute —
which is exactly why the failure is quiet: the app boots and behaves, and only
the styling is gone.

**Looked at** The browser console (one bare `Failed to load resource: 404`, with
no URL in the message); then `[...document.querySelectorAll('link')].map(e=>e.href)`
in the page, which named it. `07-routing-and-navigation.md` in full — nothing on
host-page assets.

**Resolved by** Making the three asset paths absolute in
`app/public/index.html`. Verified: `document.styleSheets` now reports the sheet
with 52 rules, and the console is clean.

Logged because it is a self-inflicted bug that **arrived with the first nested
route** — every application adding its first `/:id` page hits it — and neither
chapter 07 nor chapter 00 mentions it. Chapter 00 prints an `index.html` with
`<script src="/js/main.js">` absolute, so the guide's own example is safe by
accident while saying nothing about why.

**Bead** One line in chapter 07, near "Deep links, Back, and Forward": a route
deeper than one segment changes what relative URLs in the host page resolve
against; use absolute asset paths, or a `<base>`. Cheap to say, and the failure
it prevents is silent.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9137. Premise HOLDS. Mechanism confirmed rather than assumed: it is browser URL resolution, not Hicasso - a relative URL resolves against the DOCUMENT url, and under the default history strategy the document url IS the route. Measured with new URL() over four cases: '_shared/css/style.css' on '/' gives /_shared/css/style.css, on '/issues/srv-1' gives /issues/_shared/css/style.css; a leading-slash path is unaffected; a '<base href="/">' restores the root resolution. The silence is because the script tag is usually absolute already, so the app boots and routes with no stylesheet. Fix: an admonition in ch07 'Deep links, Back, and Forward' naming the mechanism and both remedies - absolute asset paths (as ch00's own index.html already uses for /js/main.js) or one <base href="/">, with rf.routing/with-base-path on the frame's :url-strategy for a sub-path deployment (verified to exist at implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc) - plus a troubleshooting row for the symptom. NOT FIXED, for the mayor: examples/capabilities/routing/routing/index.html carries href="_shared/css/style.css" beside an /articles/:id route, so the repo's own routing example is latently this bug; examples were outside the dispatch fence.

makes this a documentation defect and not only a workspace one.

resolving the module through NODE_PATH into the REPOSITORY's own
implementation/node_modules. The pilot's read fence bars implementation/
outright, so the route the operator used is not available to the instrument it
is checking. That asymmetry is the defect in one sentence: the operator proves
the page renders by a means the pilot is forbidden.

title: hic: every outward link in the app README the manifest copies is dead in the workspace (12/12 resolve outside the pilot root) and most aim into spec/, which the read fence bars
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 ~18:1x AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, from the
operator's chair, at pin 6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba.

workspace.md step 2 copies each application's README.md into the pilot's app/
verbatim, and workspace.md's own section "On the app's own README" invites the
pilot to read it: "That is the pilot's own codebase and a real adopter would
have exactly this." Both briefs repeat the invitation - "Its README explains
what the application does and which patterns it is built from - read it freely."

BUT THE README'S LINKS ARE WRITTEN FOR ITS POSITION IN THE REPOSITORY, and the
copy sits somewhere else entirely. Measured on the assembled pilot 1 workspace:
of the 31 links in app/README.md that leave app/, there are 12 unique ../
targets, and ALL TWELVE resolve OUTSIDE the pilot root and NONE of them exists.
They land in the directory ABOVE the pilot root - the parent folder the pilot
was never told about - because the README's paths count levels from
examples/real-apps/realworld_http/ and the copy is two levels shallower. Pilot 2
is the same shape at a different depth: 14 leaving links, targets computed from
examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/.

So a pilot reading its own README as instructed meets a document with dozens of
references it cannot follow, and no explanation, in the FIRST hour, in the one
file it has been told is unambiguously its own.

AND THE DEAD ONES POINT AT THE FORBIDDEN TREES. Ten of pilot 1's and two of
pilot 2's aim into spec/ - spec/014-HTTPRequests.md, spec/005-StateMachines.md,
spec/012-Routing.md, spec/016-Resources.md and more - which the read fence bars
by name ("Reading spec/, docs/design/, or any other example under examples/"),
and others aim at sibling examples (../../core/flows/, ../resources/,
../infinite_feed/), barred by the same row. The briefs do cover this ("Any file
your app's README links to outside app/. The README is yours; the things it
point at are not"), so the blinding holds - but the package is handing the pilot
a 35 KB document whose every outward reference is simultaneously dead and
forbidden. A pilot that tries one, finds nothing, and tries a second is spending
its attention on the instrument rather than on Hicasso.

WHY IT IS NOT MERELY COSMETIC. The friction log's "Looked at" field is the
blinding evidence, and its rule is that "an entry citing anything that is not a
published page is a recorded leak". A README full of paths INTO spec/ is the
single most likely way an honest pilot generates a leak row it did not mean to,
and the audit rf2-hic-069 consumes cannot tell "followed a link and read the
spec" from "tried a link and found nothing" unless the pilot happens to say so.

CHEAPEST HONEST FIXES, in increasing order of work: (a) step 2 strips or
de-links the outward references when it copies the README, which is one sed in
the manifest and makes the copy self-consistent; (b) the copy keeps them but
step 2 appends one line saying the references point into the framework's own
repository and are not part of this project; (c) leave it and accept the noise.
(a) is the only one that leaves the pilot with a document that is true about
where it now lives.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #9138. PREMISE RE-MEASURED AND IT HOLDS, with one clarification: the 12/12 is a count of unique FILE targets, not of links. Pilot 2 has 14 relative links, 12 landing above <pilot-root> and two inside it at paths that do not exist. Two genuinely different instruments were used - a Python link parser and grep -oE over the raw bytes - each run line-oriented and whitespace-collapsed, agreeing at 33 and 14 inline links; no target begins with '/', so the MSYS pattern-mangling trap does not bite here (']( /' reads 0 against a '](../' control reading 14 lines). No link sits inside a fenced block. THE FIX IS NOT A BLANKET DELETION, because the fence and the targets disagree. REPAIRED, 29 links: every docs/ target either README names is under a tree the site builds - docs/core/glossary.md, docs/machines/glossary.md, docs/machines/concepts.md, docs/resources/glossary.md, docs/EP/EP-0019-optimistic-mutation-rollback.md, none under an exclude_docs prefix - which the read fence ALREADY ADMITS since rf2-lpfz, so stripping them would deny the pilot something it is allowed to read. They are repointed at ../re-frame2/docs/ and all 29 resolve from app/ afterwards with every anchor present, verified by assembling a workspace and resolving each link. DE-LINKED, 16 links: 11 for pilot 1 (10 into spec/, one sibling example) and 5 for pilot 2 (2 into spec/, three sibling examples) - the trees the fence bars by name. Link text stays, so no prose is lost. EXPLAINED: readme-note.md joins the package and step 2b prepends it to the copy, one paragraph saying where the framework's documentation now lives and why the named spec/ files and sibling examples do not resolve here; it names no bead, no experiment and no repository path, so blinding is untouched. The mechanism is three sed/cat commands in workspace.md step 2b, identical for both pilots and depth-agnostic, and they were run verbatim in an assembled workspace rather than reasoned about, because neither link gate reads inside a fenced block. ONE ADJACENT DEFECT FIXED IN THE SAME PASS: workspace.md's 'On the app's own README' said 'Its links into spec/ AND docs/ ... following one is a logged leak', which has contradicted the fence's own documentation row since rf2-lpfz amended it; the paragraph now matches the table. MEASURED 2026-09-04 in the mayor checkout: `ls implementation/node_modules | wc -l` = 101, `ls -A` = 103, `ls -a` = 105. scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh prints its own CANARY_BEFORE/CANARY_AFTER as 103/2933/2, so the SCRIPT counts dotfiles and the bare `ls` does not.

WHY THIS MATTERS: a worker reported 'implementation/node_modules 101' and every prior hygiene tick in the session had recorded 103. Read naively that is a loss of two directories in a tree whose accidental emptying is a known, twice-realised incident (a bare `git worktree remove` follows the junction into the mayor's real node_modules). It is not a loss; it is a different flag.

SO DO NOT CHASE THE DELTA — RESOLVE IT BY FLAG FIRST, then by integrity. The integrity check is cheap and is the one that actually answers the question: probe for playwright, shadow-cljs, .bin and ws, and run `node -e "require.resolve('playwright')"`. All four present and the resolve true means the tree is intact whatever the count says.
