title: hic: hot reload REPLACES every DOM node (focus and caret lost) while api-reference.md says h/render! reconciles - state survives, the DOM does not, and no page says so
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 2 (LinearLite), a BLINDED
agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE.

FILED AGAINST THE PILOT S OWN CLASSIFICATION, DELIBERATELY. The pilot graded this row
published / none, and it was right to: the documented shape worked first time and nothing
it read was wrong about what it claimed. But the measurement underneath it contradicts a
sentence in api-reference.md, and a factual contradiction in a published page is a defect
whatever the row is graded. The operator files it; the grading stands.

THE CONTRADICTION IN ONE LINE. api-reference.md calls h/render! the hot-reload door and
says React reconciles the new tree against the one on the page. Measured on a hot reload,
nothing is reconciled: every DOM node is replaced, <main> included, and focus and caret go
with them. State survives completely (app-db, the resource cache, an open inline edit,
scroll position); the DOM does not. The mechanism the pilot names is that a reload
redefines each h/defview var, so React sees a new component TYPE and remounts.

Chapter 00 promises the state half and is silent on the DOM half, so a reader meets the
loss of focus mid-typing with nothing in the corpus that predicted it.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P2-F14 · outcome 4 · `published` · `none`

**Trying to** Change a Hicasso view with the build running and see what
survived. Set up first: a card created through the UI (so the **resource cache**
differed from its seeded value), an unsubmitted draft in the new-issue field, the
fail-next-write toggle armed, an inline edit open on a card, the caret parked at
offset 5 inside that edit field, and the page scrolled to y=299.

**Expected** Chapter 00 §"Hot reload": "The root, frame, app-db, and
subscriptions survive, so changing the view does not reset the counter or leak
registrations."

**Instead** Exactly that, and no more. Editing `[:h1 "Linearlite — optimistic
issue board"]` to `[:h1 "Linearlite — HOT RELOADED"]` with `npx shadow-cljs
watch app` running, measured in the live page before and after:

| Fact | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the edited `h1` | old text | **new text** — the edit arrived |
| cards on the board | `srv-3, srv-4, srv-1, srv-2` | **unchanged** — `srv-4` was created through the UI before the reload, so the **resource cache survived** |
| unsubmitted draft (app-db) | `"an unsubmitted draft"` | **unchanged** |
| fail-next-write toggle (app-db) | armed | **still armed** |
| inline edit open (app-db) | yes | **still open** |
| scroll position | 299 | **299** |
| `document.activeElement` | the edit input | **lost** — no longer the field |
| caret offset in that field | 5 | **lost** |
| the card's DOM node is the same object | — | **false** |
| that node is still in the document | — | **false** |
| even `<main>` is the same node | — | **false** |

Console confirmed the documented route ran:
`shadow-cljs: load JS linearlite/core.cljs` then
`shadow-cljs: call linearlite.core/rerender!`.

**Looked at** `00-installation.md` §"Hot reload" and §"Mount a first screen"
(the `^:dev/after-load` shape); `api-reference.md` §Roots, where `h/render!` is
"the hot-reload door: React reconciles the new tree against the one on the
page."

**Resolved by** Nothing needed — the documented shape worked first time. The
finding is in the gap between what the docs promise and what a developer
actually experiences. **State survives completely; the DOM does not.** Every
node was replaced and focus and caret went with them, because a reload redefines
each `h/defview` var, React sees a new component *type*, and a changed type is a
remount rather than a reconcile. So the api-reference's "React reconciles the new
tree against the one on the page" is true of `h/render!` in general and
misleading about the case it is named for: on a hot reload there is nothing left
to reconcile against.

That matters most for the thing you are most likely to be doing — tweaking a
form's markup while mid-edit in that form. Your app-db draft survives; your caret
does not.

**Bead** Chapter 00's hot-reload paragraph is accurate and incomplete. Add the
other half: "The DOM is rebuilt: a reload redefines each view, so React remounts
rather than reconciles, and focus, caret, scroll-into-view and any DOM-owned
state are lost. App-db, the resource cache and subscriptions are not." A reader
who knows this stops hunting for the bug when their caret jumps.
notes:
CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE SECOND BLINDED PILOT. This bead was filed from pilot 2
(LinearLite); pilot 1 (RealWorld/Conduit) hit hot reload keeping state and losing the DOM in the same
session, in a different application, from the same 29 pages, without either agent
seeing the other's workspace, log or output. Two independent readings landing on one
gap is the strongest signal this instrument produces, and it moves the finding out of
the range where one reader's idiosyncrasy explains it.

Pilot 1's entry, verbatim:

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P1-F16 · outcome 4 · `inferred` · `docs`

**Trying to**

Change a migrated view with the build running and record what survived.

**What happened**

It works, in both directions, and the state that should survive did. Measured in
headless Chrome against the live `shadow-cljs watch`, with the app first put
into a non-default state (a tag filter applied, so the home machine's `:filter`
region is `:tagged` and the URL is `/realworld/tag/intro`):

| | before | after reload | after revert |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| banner text | "A place to share your knowledge." | "…knowledge. (hot-reloaded)" | "A place to share your knowledge." |
| route | `/realworld/tag/intro` | `/realworld/tag/intro` | `/realworld/tag/intro` |
| machine state (active chip) | `intro` | `intro` | `intro` |
| app-db (sidebar tags) | 4 tags | 4 tags | 4 tags |

**Survived**: the frame, app-db, the machine's region state, the route, and the
subscriptions feeding all of them. **Did not survive**: DOM node identity —
every node was rebuilt. I stamped a JS property on three live nodes before the
edit; all three came back `null` afterwards, including the one in the *Reagent*
shell that the edit did not touch.

**The friction**

`00-installation.md`'s hot-reload section is written for one shape — a
`defonce` root handle plus `^:dev/after-load` calling `h/render!` — and states
the guarantee as "The root, frame, app-db, and subscriptions survive". Every
word of that held here. But it says nothing about **node identity**, which is
the half a developer actually notices: a rebuilt subtree loses focus, caret,
scroll position and any uncontrolled input's text on every save.

And for a half-migrated tree there is a specific reason to expect a rebuild
that the docs never mention. `h/as-component` is "Declared once at top level,
beside the view" — a plain `def` — so a namespace reload re-evaluates it and
mints a **new React component type**. I measured that directly:

```
"after": {"bridgeIdentical": false, "toggleMarker": null}
```

`window.__probe0 === realworld_http.articles.home_page_component` is `false`
after the reload. A new component type is a remount by React's own rules, so a
bridged screen cannot reconcile across a reload of its own namespace, ever.

I want to be careful about what I proved: in this application the whole tree
was rebuilt anyway — editing `articles.cljs` reloads `core.cljs`, which
redefines the shell's own views — so I could not isolate the bridge's
contribution. What I measured is that the bridge's identity does change, which
is sufficient on its own for the subtree it heads.

**Looked at**

- `00-installation.md` "Hot reload", "Production builds"
- `09-interop.md` "Render a Hicasso view from native React"
- `api-reference.md` `h/render!` ("The hot-reload door"), `h/as-component`
- `cookbook.md` "Boot an application" (the `defonce` handle and why)

**Bead**

Say what hot reload costs as well as what it keeps, and say what
`h/as-component`'s `def` means for a reloaded namespace — it is the one door
whose identity a reload changes, and it is the door a partial migration is
built on.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9149 (2026-09-04): REOPENED. The corrected Markdown now contradicts shipped contract surfaces. implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:660-669 still tells users that reloaded code meets its existing DOM and contrasts render! with mount! discarding every node/component state. consumer_app.cljs:129-136 says nothing is torn down and DOM/component state survive; the editor, typeahead, todo, and slice example reload docstrings repeat that guarantee. The real HMR gate and hmr_remount_cljs_test assert the opposite: changed types replace nodes, lose focus/caret and child hook state, while durable re-frame state survives. Update these existing surfaces to distinguish same-root reconciliation from changed-type remount; inspect cookbook.md's same implication while doing so.
close_reason:
RE-CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor: same .beads race. Payload verified in the working tree at HEAD==origin/main — docs/core/hicasso/api-reference.md carries 4 focus/caret references where it previously claimed reconciliation preserved the DOM.

Delivered by worker/hicinterop-a in PR #9149, MERGED. The worker CORRECTED THIS BEAD'S OWN FRAMING at source and the correction is the valuable part: 'nothing is reconciled' is wrong. h/render! calls .render on the SAME React root inside flushSync — the distinction it draws is against createRoot-ing a second time. But a reload re-evaluates the namespace, mint-view! allocates a new component and memo wrapper per evaluation, and as-component mints a fresh component per call, so React meets a CHANGED TYPE at every position, and a changed type is a remount by React's own rule. So the reconcile is real and resolves to replace-everything. State survives because none of it lived in React.

It also refuted the bead's loss list: the suggested wording named scroll position among the losses, but the pilot's own table recorded scroll SURVIVING (299 before and after). The pages now say focus and caret, which is what was measured.

title: hic docs: 09-interop.md's h/as-component section does not say what a Reagent parent's props do at the crossing
notes:
FOUND while closing rf2-4387 (PR #9131, chapter 20).

09-interop.md "Render a Hicasso view from native React" names "UIx, raw React, JavaScript, or TypeScript parents" and does not name Reagent - the one parent a *migration from Reagent* guarantees you have. It then says React props return "with canonical names ... and identity-preserved values", which is true of the DECODE half and says nothing about what the parent did before the decode.

The statement to add, verified against Reagent 2.0.1 (the version implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn declares) and against implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs:

- reagent.impl.template/convert-prop-value: a keyword or symbol becomes its `name`; a CLJS map becomes a camel-cased JS object with its values recursively converted; any other `coll?` goes through `clj->js` (deep); anything `js-val?` - strings, numbers, booleans, nil, functions - crosses unchanged.
- Prop NAMES round-trip on this route: reagent.impl.util/dash-to-prop-name camel-cases `:article-id` to "articleId" and codec/prop-key reads "articleId" back to `:article-id`. VALUES do not.

So a Reagent parent rendering `[:> bridged {...}]` hands the Hicasso view converted values under correctly-spelled keys. The practical consequence - cross an id and read the rest with h/sub - is now written in chapter 20's new "Views shared across the boundary" section; 09-interop.md wants the mechanism sentence at h/as-component so a reader who never opens chapter 20 still meets it.

NOTE this refutes half of rf2-4387's reported observation: the pilot recorded a CLJS map and a vector surviving "intact", which Reagent's source contradicts for both.

FENCE: docs/core/hicasso/09-interop.md. Gates: scripts/check_doc_slugs.py and mkdocs build --strict (both apply; the page is under docs/ and not under docs/design/). implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_guide_samples.py gates any h/ verb in a new fence.

title: Mayor dispatch drift: the boundary and gate-mechanics blocks were retyped, not extracted - and the gate paraphrase inverts the detach ruling
description:
The mayor has been RETYPING the two travel-verbatim dispatch blocks instead of
extracting them mechanically, across every dispatch this session. The method doc is
correct; the defect is entirely in dispatch practice.

docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md:661-673 rules on this directly:
"Get them there by extracting mechanically, then pasting the result into the prompt...
the extraction is what makes paraphrase impossible - a matched range cannot reword,
where a mayor retyping two hundred lines of gate mechanics can and does."

That is precisely what happened.

## Drift 1 - the gate-mechanics block, and it INVERTS the ruling

Canonical block: template lines 920-1010+ ("## Quality gates - how a gate is run",
paste from that heading down to the rule before "## Reviewing what comes back").
Roughly 90 lines.

What the mayor pasted instead, in full:
  "GATE MECHANICS: run gates in the FOREGROUND to completion - never background one,
   never pipe through tail/head."

The canonical block says the OPPOSITE of the first clause:
  - "Split a compound gate before you reach for detaching."
  - "Where it genuinely does not split, DETACHING IS CORRECT - ending the turn is the
     defect. Detach, then poll both the log and the exit-code file in a bounded loop
     within the same turn."
  - "Word this as the sanctioned path, not as a concession; a worker who thinks it has
     erred reads for how to atone and straight past the instruction that would save it."

The real rule is a TERMINAL CONDITION - the turn ends only once the exit file exists
and its number is quoted - not a ban on backgrounding. The mayor's paraphrase kept the
memorable half (foreground) and dropped the operative one (poll in-turn), which is the
same failure mode ai/stance.md warns about for the stance block.

OBSERVED COST: Mike asked 2026-09-03 why background tasks were taking almost an hour.
A worker whose gate is too heavy to foreground and who is FORBIDDEN to detach has no
option but to sit in the foreground. This is a direct, measured throughput cost.

Also dropped from that block:
  - the WEDGE diagnosis: a gate heavy enough that two cannot coexist wedges rather than
    fails (no progress, no exit file, no error). Contention is for the MACHINE, so
    per-attempt naming does nothing. Recover by correlating your own build artefact's
    mtime against candidate run start times and killing ONLY the one you can show is
    yours; a peer's run recovers by itself.
  - "Read the clock before killing anything on elapsed time" - fails BOTH ways; one
    worker killed a healthy run believing 17 minutes had passed when it had been 2.
  - "Invoke a backgrounded gate by its ABSOLUTE path" - an interpreter handed a relative
    script path resolves it against the working directory, so a wrong directory hands it
    a SIBLING WORKTREE's copy. One run did exactly that inside another live worker's
    checkout and reported the resulting verdict as its own.
  - "Verify which tree the gate actually read", by root-print or by planted-fault red -
    "the discrimination is the red itself", since a repository-relative path cannot tell
    two checkouts apart.
  - "A green sabotage run is a reason to stop, not to proceed."
The never-pipe rule was the one part carried correctly.

## Drift 2 - the worktree-boundary block

Canonical block: template lines 739-798 (the fenced text under "## The worktree boundary
block"). The mayor substituted a retyped 6-point numbered list. Dropped:

  - "Before EVERY edit, confirm you are in your worktree... A start-of-session guard is
    NOT sufficient - verify per edit." The mayor's version asks for ONE guard run. The
    template's own rationale: the leak happens mid-session, in one tool call, and a guard
    script can be fooled by the path resolution that causes it.
  - Never write the worktree root, or any absolute home path, into any committed file, PR
    body or tracker text.
  - After the first edit, and after writing any NEW file, confirm it landed in your
    worktree and NOT the mayor checkout - CHECK BOTH TREES, because a new ignored file
    leaking into the mayor checkout is invisible in the worker's own status.
  - If anything landed outside: STOP, report both paths, do not repair, commit or push.
  - Scratch-file naming: concurrent workers SHARE one SESSION-keyed scratch dir; name
    every file for the worktree AND the attempt - gate-<name>-<worktree>-1.log /
    .exit - bumping the number each re-run. The attempt number closes a hole the worktree
    suffix cannot, because both writers are YOU: a harness that caps runtime kills the
    SHELL, not what it spawned, and the orphan keeps writing to the .log and .exit the
    restarted run is using. A hole of NUL bytes or two summary lines in one log is the
    tell. (The mayor substituted "write scratch to your worktree, not /tmp" - same hazard,
    weaker route, and no attempt number at all.)
  - THE INSTALLER HAZARD, which is live in this repo: a link into shared dependencies is
    WRITABLE through, not only deletable through. An installer a gate runs (npm ci, npm
    install, any tool that reinstalls a dependency tree) rewrites the SHARED target, not
    your copy - "one emptied the coordinator's real tree while the worker's own read as a
    fresh install." If a nominated gate runs an installer, do NOT link that tree: install
    your own from the lockfile, or STOP and say the gate cannot run against a link.
    Workers here junction implementation/node_modules and then run npm-based gates, so
    this is the live shape. The mayor's version said only "remove the junction as your
    last act", which addresses deletion and not writes.
  - "Kill any poll loops you armed before you report done" - each survivor fires its own
    completion notification after the work has landed, costing a turn apiece.

## The fix

1. Extract both blocks MECHANICALLY into the dispatch, by matched line range, and paste
   the result. Never retype either. Adapt only the placeholders (<ASSIGNED_WORKTREE>,
   <MAYOR_CHECKOUT>) and scope the gate block to the gate the brief names.
2. Ranges as of this filing - RE-DERIVE them from the headings rather than trusting these
   numbers, which go stale exactly the way the template's own "Counts are claims" section
   says:
     - worktree boundary: the fenced text block under "## The worktree boundary block"
     - gate mechanics: from "## Quality gates - how a gate is run" down to the rule

title: reagent-slim pr-atom: the *ratom-context* nil binding pops before pr-writer runs, so it guards nothing
description:
In reagent-slim's `ratom.cljs`, `pr-atom` reads:

  (pr-writer (binding [*ratom-context* nil] body) writer opts)

The `binding` scopes the nil `*ratom-context*` to evaluating `body` — which is an ALREADY-COMPUTED LOCAL — and pops the binding before `pr-writer` ever runs. So the guard covers no nested printing whatsoever.

The apparent intent is to stop printing from being captured as a reactive dependency: printing a ratom dereferences it, and doing that inside a live `*ratom-context*` would register a spurious dependency on whatever is currently tracking. If that is the intent, the binding must wrap the `pr-writer` call, not the argument.

ESTABLISH THE INTENT BEFORE MOVING IT. Two possibilities and they have different repairs:
- The guard is meant to cover the whole print, and its position is a bug. Repair: move the `binding` to wrap `pr-writer`. Prove it with a plant — construct a print inside a live `*ratom-context*` and show a dependency IS registered today and is NOT after the fix.
- The dereference genuinely all happens while computing `body`, and `pr-writer` cannot deref anything. Then the binding is correctly placed and merely looks wrong, and the deliverable is a comment saying so. A verified "this is correct as written" is a complete deliverable.

Do NOT move it on the strength of how it reads. This is a reactive-substrate seam; a wrong move here changes dependency capture.

CONTEXT: found while working rf2-6r9j.29 (PR #9127), which removed `pr-atom`'s unused receiver argument and ADDED the print pins that were previously absent — the suite had asserted nothing about either type's printed form, so "representation unchanged" had no instrument at all. Those new pins are your starting instrument. The line was explicitly outside .29's fence and is unchanged by its diff.

Surface: `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/ratom.cljs`.
close_reason: PR #9155. Intent ESTABLISHED, not assumed: the guard is real but mispositioned - the bead's first branch. binding wrapped 'body', an already-computed local, so it popped before pr-writer ran; but pr-writer recurses into the value and a NESTED ratom's own -pr-writer derefs it, and -deref calls notify-deref-watcher!. Demonstrated with a new test that prints a ratom-inside-a-ratom inside a live reactive context: BEFORE the fix both assertions failed - the nested ratom was in the reaction's .-watching set, and the printer re-ran (2 vs 1) when that nested ratom changed; AFTER moving the binding to wrap the pr-writer call both pass, suite totals unchanged at 11174 tests / 55752 assertions, 0 failures. Deliberately NOT changed: the receiver's own deref stays at the call site ({:val (-deref a)} in both -pr-writer methods), because a Reaction's -deref branches on *ratom-context* and a nil context additionally forces flush! plus an on-demand recompute - draining the reaction queue from inside pr-str is a behaviour change beyond suppressing capture, and is the wrong move at this seam the bead warns about. Rationale and residual recorded in the source comment. PR #9127 did not cause this; the shape dates from the file's first commit.

The bead's 'entirely inside realworld_http' is also wrong - the unkeyed seq comes from realworld_shared/markdown.cljs and has no call-site fix. title: hic: as-component's docstring says 'outside every Hicasso root' where the code means 'outside every frame' (codec.cljs) — the likely origin of the guide sentence rf2-x97h fixed
description:
Found while fixing rf2-x97h (PR #9149), which corrected the same wrong wording in docs/core/hicasso/09-interop.md.

implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs, inside as-component's docstring:

  'the frame is the surrounding React context's, and outside every Hicasso
   root the shell refuses with :rf.error/no-frame-context.'

That is narrower than the code. The boundary shell reads re-frame.adapter.context/frame-context — one defonce'd createContext — and collector/resolve-frame! refuses only when that context holds nil or the no-provider sentinel. h/mount!'s provider, rf/frame-provider and rf/frame-root all write that SAME object (views/provider.cljs aliases it rather than minting its own; frame_boundary.cljs goes through provider-element). This is the ONLY place in the package with that framing. native.cljc says 'outside every frame' twice; resolve-frame!'s own docstring says 'from the one context every React-shaped substrate in this repo writes'; the raise message says 'no frame in scope'. So the fix is a one-line docstring correction to match its siblings.

title: hic tooling: hm/shadow!'s own docstring example crosses :article-id, which reaches a reactified Reagent original as :articleId
notes:
FOUND while fixing chapter 20 §3 for rf2-z1cz (PR #9131). NOT RUN - derived by reading source on both sides, not by executing a shadow comparison.

implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test/mounted.cljs, shadow!'s docstring, opens with:

    :reference [:> (r/reactify-component old/article-row) {:article-id 7}]

The crossing renames the prop, silently, and the original's destructuring of :article-id gets nil:

- Hicasso side: impl.codec/host-entry - 'The caller (host-entry) camelCases the top-level KEY' - so {:article-id 7} is emitted as #js{articleId: 7}.
- Reagent side: reactify-component -> impl.component/as-class; a React parent's props carry no .argv, so props-argv falls to [(.-constructor c) (util/shallow-obj-to-map p)], and shallow-obj-to-map is (keyword k) on the RAW JS key name. "articleId" becomes :articleId, not :article-id.

The asymmetry is real rather than a bug in either half: codec/prop-key decodes "articleId" back to :article-id on the INWARD route (h/as-component), so names round-trip there. Nothing performs that decode on the OUTWARD route into a reactified Reagent component.

Two other infelicities in the same example, both minor:
- (r/reactify-component ...) is called INLINE, so a fresh component type is allocated per evaluation. as-component's own docstring states the law for the mirror-image case ('Call it ONCE, at top level ... a fresh one per render is a fresh element type that remounts the subtree, React.memo's own law').
- There is no in-repo witness for a FOREIGN :reference at all: test_kit/test/re_frame/hicasso/shadow_dom_cljs_test.cljs uses Hicasso views on both sides of every row. So the documented migration route is the one the door's own witness does not drive.

REMEDY, in preference order: cross a single-word prop (:id) in the example, hoist the reactify-component call to a top-level def, and consider a shadow_dom_cljs_test row with a genuinely foreign :reference so the route has a witness.

Chapter 20 §3 was corrected to :id and a hoisted def in PR #9131 and now states the renaming rule; this bead is the docstring and the missing witness, both under implementation/hicasso/test_kit/**, which was outside that dispatch's fence.

FENCE: implementation/hicasso/test_kit/**. A docstring-only edit does not change what check_guide_samples.py resolves; a test row is a CLJS browser-lane change (-dom-cljs-test).

Corrected hm/shadow!'s docstring example in implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test/mounted.cljs per the bead's stated preference order: crosses {:id 7} instead of {:article-id 7}, hoists (r/reactify-component old/article-row) to a top-level def with the reason stated, and adds a 'Cross single-word props' paragraph to the section explaining the crossing. The bead's mechanism was verified at source rather than assumed: OUT, raw-element reduces props through codec/host-entry whose slot comes from slot/prop-name, the camelCaser, so :article-id emits as articleId and raw-gate hands that object on untouched; IN, Reagent's reactify-component -> as-class, and a React parent's props carry no .argv so props-argv falls back to util/shallow-obj-to-map, which is (keyword k) on the raw JS key, giving :articleId; and nothing decodes it back on that route, codec/prop-key having only two call sites, both inward. Note for the record: the brief attributed the rename to Reagent's convert-prop-value, which is NOT on this path - Hicasso is the parent here, so the emitted key is entirely codec/host-entry's work. title: Clarify Hicasso reverse-edge MCP tool name
description:
Scope: public Hicasso reverse-edge operation naming across tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp. Exact evidence: src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs defines read-read-attribution with wire name read-read-attribution; tools/hicasso_tool.cljs exports read-read-attribution-tool and registry.cljs binds the handler; tool-descriptors.edn, README.md, spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md, test/fixtures/tool-names.json, live-hicasso-wire.cjs, and conformance_test.cljs repeat the operation name. The doubled read verb obscures that this operation is the reverse edge from subscription to reading boundaries, while the payload already calls the concept read-attribution. Ambiguity cost is discoverability and prompt/tool-selection friction, plus inconsistent source symbol versus payload vocabulary. Compatibility constraint: this is a public MCP tools/call name embedded in generated descriptor artifacts, closed-world allowlists, live fixtures, and wire conformance; do not silently rename or change payload keys, schemas, IDs, paths, handler behavior, or fixtures. Phase-1 fences: do not touch unrelated vestigial or generated-manifest cleanup targets, and do not alter MCP conformance wire-vocabulary scanner beads rf2-6r9j.239, .240, or .241. Recommendation: choose a migration-compatible canonical name such as read-attribution, retain the old name as an explicitly deprecated alias for a compatibility window, update descriptors and generated manifest together, then update docs, allowlists, tests, and live fixtures. Acceptance: canonical and deprecated alias behavior is specified; tools/list advertises the policy without duplicate ambiguous entries; both names produce identical reverse-edge envelopes during migration; old callers remain functional until the documented removal gate; tool-descriptors.edn is regenerated and drift-check passes; focused CLJS conformance and live-wire tests pass; no public JSON or EDN schema keys change.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A canonical reverse-edge wire name and a time-bounded deprecation policy for `read-read-attribution` are documented before the public rename lands.
2. During the compatibility window, canonical and deprecated names invoke the same handler and return identical envelopes; tools/list presents an unambiguous discovery policy.
3. Descriptor source, registry binding, generated `tool-descriptors.edn`, docs, fixture allowlists, conformance tests, and live-wire tests move together.
4. Descriptor drift, focused CLJS conformance, and live Hicasso wire checks pass for the migration.
5. Payload keys, schemas, IDs, paths, handler behavior, and unrelated MCP vocabulary remain unchanged.

4. Descriptor drift, focused CLJS conformance, and live Hicasso wire checks pass for the migration.

notes:
2026-09-03 — PREMISE REFUTED for the RENAME half; the CLARIFY half landed in PR #9121 (head e78349f355e683ea5a7acbdd08228c8b201f4d34). LEFT OPEN for a ruling, because meeting acceptance criteria 1-3 as written would override an existing naming ruling, which is not a worker's call.

Three grounds, each checked at source.

(1) IT IS ALREADY RULED. docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md row 51 (rf2-hic-065) reads the re-frame.hicasso.tool reader door name by name — read-mounted-boundaries, read-read-attribution, read-intents, explain-render — and rules 'keep all four as shipped', with a stated reason rather than a default: the read- prefix is 'load-bearing rather than decorative', marking the reads as pure PROJECTIONS of state the runtime already retains, against a namespace whose whole design is no accumulator, no occurrence index, no history store and no second knob. explain-render is deliberately unprefixed because it FOLDS Spec 009's ring rather than reading a current table. The same row is restated in naming-packet.md row 249. This bead's evidence section does not cite that ruling.

(2) THE WIRE NAME IS THE PROVIDER FN NAME — one string, not two. hicasso_tool.cljs's projection-form interpolates (pr-str read-fn) into (cljs.core/unchecked-get d (cljs.core/munge ...)), so the literal 'read-read-attribution' passed to door-read-tool is munged and looked up on the door's namespace object at RUNTIME. The ns docstring states the invariant outright ('The wire names and the framework fn names AGREE, exactly') and hicasso_wire_test.cljs is the both-sides witness: it parses the ACTUAL EMITTED FORM and asserts every reader fn named there is defined publicly in the provider's own source.

MEASURED, not argued. Renaming the wire string to 'read-attribution' while the provider keeps read-read-attribution reds four suites: hicasso-wire-test/every-emitted-read-is-defined-by-the-provider, hicasso-wire-test/the-emitter-names-nothing-the-provider-does-not-publish, hicasso-tool-test/each-tool-emits-a-runtime-resolved-door-call, and the pair-mcp conformance corpus (4 failures, 0 errors). Control applied and restored; the restored suite is green at 1120 tests / 4070 assertions, exit 0. So a wire-only rename is not available: it would require decoupling wire name from emitted fn name — a structural change contradicting the invariant the witness exists to keep — or renaming the provider fn, which is in implementation/hicasso/ and consumed by tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/hicasso_reads.cljs, skills/re-frame2-pair/, spec/api-manifest.edn and spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn.

(3) THE STATED AMBIGUITY COST IS ALREADY PAID. The bead's harm is discoverability and prompt/tool-selection friction, and the descriptor's FIRST CLAUSE already reads 'Which boundaries read each subscription — the reverse edge, exactly.' A model reading tools/list is not left guessing what the operation does; the descriptor also names the provider fn and gives three worked examples. Nothing about tool selection is improved by the rename, and lengthening the description would add tokens to every tools/list for a naming footnote.

Also worth stating: acceptance criteria 1 and 2 require a deprecated alias and a compatibility window. That is a back-compat shim, and the standing posture is pre-alpha with no back-compat shims. If Mike ever does rule the rename in, the right shape here is a clean cut across provider + wire + xray + skills + manifests in one PR, not an alias.

WHAT DID LAND (PR #9121, docstring only): hicasso_tool.cljs now explains the doubled verb beside the wire/provider table — the outer read- is the door's own prefix marking a pure projection, read-attribution is the payload's noun and the literal the envelope's :read slot carries — cites row 51, and records that the string is both the wire tool name and the provider fn name so the two move together or not at all. No wire name, payload key, schema, id, path, handler or fixture changed. tool-descriptors.edn untouched; its drift check is in sync (30 tools, exit 0). descriptors_data.cljs was deliberately NOT edited: its description already leads with the reverse edge.

TO WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: the question for Mike is narrow — override naming-ledger row 51 for this one name, or close this bead as ruled-against. The mechanics are settled and recorded above; do not re-litigate them, and do not attempt a wire-only rename, which is measured red.
close_reason:
CLOSED AS RULED-AGAINST 2026-09-04 by the mayor, on the project's stated stance rather than by a new decision. This was held for Mike across many ticks; re-reading it, it does not need him, and holding it was the over-deference the method warns about.

THE PRIOR WORKER LEFT THE QUESTION NARROW and did the work properly (PR #9121 landed the clarify half, docstring only). Its stated question: override naming-ledger row 51 for this one name, or close as ruled-against. Four grounds settle it against, and none is mine — all four are already on the record:

(1) IT IS ALREADY RULED, WITH A REASON. docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md row 51 (rf2-hic-065) names the four reader-door operations and rules 'keep all four as shipped'. The reason is stated rather than defaulted: the read- prefix is LOAD-BEARING, marking these as pure PROJECTIONS of state the runtime already retains, against a namespace whose whole design is no accumulator, no occurrence index, no history store and no second knob — and explain-render is deliberately unprefixed because it FOLDS Spec 009's ring rather than reading a current table. Restated at naming-packet.md row 249. Overriding a reasoned ruling needs a reason of comparable weight, and the bead offers an aesthetic one.

(2) THE STATED HARM IS ALREADY PAID. The bead's cost is discoverability and prompt/tool-selection friction. The descriptor's FIRST CLAUSE reads 'Which boundaries read each subscription — the reverse edge, exactly.' A model reading tools/list is not guessing. Nothing about tool selection improves; lengthening the description would add tokens to every tools/list for a naming footnote.

(3) THE CHEAP REMEDY IS MEASURED RED. The wire name IS the provider fn name — one string, munged and looked up on the door's namespace object at runtime, with hicasso_wire_test.cljs as the both-sides witness and the ns docstring stating the invariant outright. A wire-only rename reds four suites (measured by that worker, control applied and restored, restored suite green at 1120 tests / 4070 assertions). So the only available shapes are decoupling wire from fn name — a structural change contradicting the invariant a witness exists to keep — or a clean cut across implementation/hicasso, tools/xray, skills/re-frame2-pair and two api-manifest files. That is a large, risky diff to buy a shorter name.

(4) ITS OWN ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA VIOLATE THE POSTURE. Criteria 1 and 2 require a deprecated alias and a time-bounded compatibility window. We are PRE-ALPHA WITH NO BACK-COMPAT SHIMS. The bead cannot be satisfied as written without contradicting the stance.

ON THE STANCE, THEREFORE: 'we are not over-engineering or gold plating... we do not need to litigate every last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.' A doubled verb whose meaning is already stated in the first line of its own descriptor, protected by a reasoned ruling, whose repair is structurally contradicted and whose acceptance criteria require a shim we do not do — that is the minutia the stance names.

IF MIKE WANTS IT ANYWAY, the shape is recorded and does not need rediscovering: a clean cut across provider + wire + xray + skills + manifests in ONE PR, no alias. Reopen with that instruction and it is a straightforward dispatch. What I will not do is keep it open as a question when the project's own stated position answers it.

NOT CLOSING THE UNDERLYING WORK: PR #9121's docstring already explains the doubled verb beside the wire/provider table, cites row 51, and records that the string is both the wire tool name and the provider fn name so the two move together or not at all. A future reader meets the explanation where the confusion arises.

title: method: the dispatch preamble tells every worker to walk history fields that do not exist — notes and design are absent from bd history's schema, so the currency walk fails OPEN on the one field the mayor writes rulings into
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-04 by worker/machvest-a, which controlled the instrument in both directions before trusting it, and re-verified by the mayor on rf2-6r9j.2.

docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md's common preamble instructs every worker: 'WALK ADJACENT PAIRS NEWEST-FIRST UNTIL THE FIRST CHANGE TO A TEXT-BEARING FIELD (description, notes, acceptance, design)'.

THE FIELDS A bd history --json SNAPSHOT ACTUALLY CARRIES on this build, measured:
  acceptance_criteria, close_reason, closed_at, created_at, created_by,
  description, id, issue_type, owner, priority, status, title, updated_at

So of the four the preamble names: description EXISTS; acceptance is spelled acceptance_criteria; and notes and design DO NOT EXIST AT ALL.

WHY THIS FAILS OPEN, which is the whole defect. A worker keying its walk on 'notes' or 'design' reads null in every snapshot. Null hashes constant across every adjacent pair, so the walk reports NO TEXT-BEARING CHANGE — the exact false-clean the preamble exists to prevent, arrived at by following the preamble exactly. Nothing errors and the answer is well-formed. machvest-a hit this and only caught it because it controlled the detector against a field it knew varied.

AND THE MISSING FIELD IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. 'notes' is where the mayor writes rulings, sequencing fences, audit reopenings and salvage records — via bd update --append-notes. It is the field whose currency the walk exists to establish. bd history cannot order notes by mutation time AT ALL on this build, so the instruction promises a capability the tool does not have. Workers DO see notes rendered by bd show; what they cannot do is establish WHEN a note arrived relative to a description edit, which is precisely the ordering problem the paragraph was written to solve.

THE FIX, and it needs both halves:
1. Correct the field list to what the schema carries: description and acceptance_criteria. Drop notes and design from the enumeration.
2. State the consequence rather than hiding it — that notes are NOT in the history schema, so history orders description/acceptance_criteria/title/status/priority only, and a note's arrival time cannot be established this way. Tell the worker what to do instead: read bd show's notes in full and treat the LAST note as newest by position (which is how --append-notes writes), while using history for the fields it does cover. Say plainly that this is a weaker guarantee than the paragraph currently implies.
3. Keep the existing control instruction and strengthen it: exercise the walk against a field known to vary before believing any 'no change' answer — that control is what caught this.

ALSO WORTH FIXING WHILE THERE: the same preamble's jq guidance needs to say that a history entry's fields nest under .Issue on this build. A walk keyed at the top level matches nothing and produces the identical false 'no change' — a second worker hit that separately today.

MAYOR CHECKOUT HAS A COMMIT GUARD ON METHOD DOCS, so this is filed with the fix written out rather than edited in place. Dispatch it to a worker with docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md in its fence.

RELATED: rf2-4wko covers a different defect in the same file (blocks retyped rather than extracted, and a gate paraphrase that inverts the detach ruling). Sequence the two — the file is one-toucher by contention, not by rule.
notes:
CORRECTION BY THE MAYOR, 2026-09-04 — THIS BEAD'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS WRONG AND THE FIX MUST CHANGE. Read this note before the description; the description's headline is refuted.

WHAT I CLAIMED: 'notes and design are NOT in this build's history schema at all', with a field list I presented as the schema.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, measured across four beads chosen for differing field populations:

  bead          notes len   acc len   keys contain notes?   keys contain acceptance_criteria?
  rf2-6r9j.2        0         637            NO                        YES
  rf2-ydpr       9804           0           YES                         NO
  rf2-lo9s       1518           0           YES                         NO
  rf2-xpd8          0           0            NO                         NO

bd history --json OMITS EMPTY FIELDS. The key set is PER BEAD and tracks exactly which fields are populated on that bead. So 'keys' on one bead's snapshot is that bead's populated field set, NOT the build's schema. I derived a general claim from rf2-6r9j.2 alone, which happens to carry no notes — the same relay-without-checking error this session has made four other times, except the source was my own single measurement rather than a worker's report.

worker/ratchettool-a caught it independently while walking rf2-ydpr: notes IS carried there and DOES vary, with 7 real change points. Its control found what mine could not, because it walked a bead that has notes.

THE DEFECT IS STILL REAL, AND STILL FAILS OPEN — only the cause changes. A jq walk keyed on a field that is EMPTY on that bead sees the key ABSENT from every snapshot, so .notes yields null, null hashes constant across every adjacent pair, and the walk reports 'no text-bearing change'. Identical false clean, reached by emptiness rather than by absence-from-schema. And it is worse than it looks, because the same walk on a DIFFERENT bead works perfectly — so the instruction is not reliably broken, it is intermittently broken, which is harder to notice.

THE REVISED FIX:
1. DO NOT write 'notes is not in the history schema'. It is false. Do not write a field list presented as the schema at all — there isn't one visible this way.
2. DO say: bd history --json omits empty fields, so a key's ABSENCE from a snapshot means 'empty on this bead', not 'not tracked'. A walk must therefore treat absent and null as the same thing and must not conclude 'no change' from a field that was never populated.
3. KEEP the spelling correction: the preamble says 'acceptance'; the field is acceptance_criteria. That half was right.
4. KEEP the .Issue nesting note. That half was right and a second worker hit it independently.
5. STRENGTHEN the control instruction, which is now doubly earned: it is what caught the original defect AND what caught my wrong diagnosis of it. Exercise the walk against a field KNOWN TO VARY ON THE BEAD IN FRONT OF YOU before believing any 'no change'. A control run on a different bead proves nothing about this one.
6. 'design' — I have NOT established whether it is tracked. None of the four beads shows it, but all four may simply have it empty. Say nothing about it rather than repeating my error; or measure it and report.

The worker holding this bead (worker/methodfix-a) has been sent this correction directly.
close_reason: PR #9157: preamble history-walk now names .Issue-nested fields with acceptance_criteria spelled correctly, states that bd history --json omits empty fields (absent key = empty on this item, not untracked), and requires the control to run against a field known to vary ON THE BEAD IN FRONT OF YOU. Mayor's mid-task correction applied: notes and design ARE tracked (design measured present in 771/771 snapshots on a bead that populates it, 4 of 1685 beads), so no field list is presented as a schema. Gates: check_doc_slugs.py 0, mkdocs --strict 0, require-alias ratchet 0 (unmoved).

title: Repo-wide syntax-aware require-alias dialect ratchet (scripts/ + lint.yml)
description:
Both parent beads of the rf.* require-alias migration (rf2-6r9j.161 core, rf2-6r9j.167 routing, rf2-j5or machines) list a syntax-aware CI ratchet in their acceptance criteria, and all three deliberately did not build it: scripts/ and .github/workflows/ are hot-zone and the ratchet should be ONE repo-wide instrument, not one per artefact. Per-artefact is exactly what let machines go unowned — .161 and .167 each fenced their own tree and nothing covered the third.

The full design, with the four textual traps measured on the machines sweep, the derived (not listed) exemption rule, the per-surface floor shape and the positive-fixture requirement, is written up in the notes on rf2-j5or (PR #9114). Read it there rather than re-deriving; every trap in it was hit for real, and one of them silently rewrote 42 late-bind keys on a first pass.

Summary of the design:
- scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py (Python, no JVM start-up) + one job in .github/workflows/lint.yml, which already owns lint_surface gating. Not a new workflow file.
- Find libspec vectors by BALANCED BRACKET scan, never by line: a multi-line [re-frame.machines.result :as result / :refer [...]] defeats any single-line regex and the miss is silent (116 use sites skipped on a clean-looking run).
- Distinguish ::alias/key (auto-resolved, MUST move) from :alias/key (a literal keyword, MUST NOT); machines alone carries 179 of the latter against 7 of the former.
- Skip fully-qualified re-frame.x/y and quoted 're-frame.x/y; do NOT skip #'alias/y var-quotes. Skip repo-relative paths whose first segment collides with an alias (spec/conformance/..., docs/machines/...).
- Exemption is DERIVED: an alias bound to 2+ distinct namespaces within one file is the host-conditional reader-arm shape and is exempt. No path allowlist, which would go stale on the first rename.
- Dedup .cljc reader arms: count per (file, ns, alias) triple.
- Ship as a PER-SURFACE FLOOR (scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn: surface -> allowed count), not a zero gate — core/routing/http/machines are clean, adapters, schemas, flows, epoch, resources, ssr, ssr-node, security, tools, examples, testbeds and skills are not. Same shape as scripts/check-ai-tracking-ratchet.sh.
- MUST ship with a positive fixture under scripts/_test_fixtures/ asserting the checker names a planted bare alias: a checker whose subject is ABSENCE reads green when it stops firing, which is the defect class this repo keeps finding in its own instruments (cf. lint.yml's hicasso kondo fixture-witness step).

Hot-zone: scripts/ and .github/workflows/lint.yml. One toucher, sequenced against other workflow edits.
notes:
ADDITIONAL FINDING FROM THE MACHINES SWEEP (PR #9114) — a scanner the ratchet should also account for.

scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py CHECK B reads every :rf.* keyword NAMESPACE out of implementation/**/src and demands a matching `:rf.<ns>/*` row in spec/Conventions.md's reserved set. Its extractor (_RF_KEYWORD_RE = r":(rf(?:\.[a-z][\w.-]*)?)/[\w.*+!?<>=-]+") CANNOT TELL `::rf.x/y` FROM `:rf.x/y`.

That matters because the canonical `rf.<tail>` require alias TEXTUALLY SHADOWS the `:rf.<area>` reserved keyword root. An auto-resolved `::rf.machines.result/depth-abort?` denotes `:re-frame.machines.result/depth-abort?` and reserves nothing at all, but the checker reads it as a literal reserved-root keyword and demands a Conventions row that would be a FALSE reservation.

Machines is the first artefact to produce one: `git grep '::rf\.' -- implementation/*/src` returned NOTHING on main before PR #9114, which is why the core and routing sweeps never met it. Every remaining artefact with an auto-resolved keyword in src will meet it — schemas, flows, epoch, resources, ssr, ssr-node, security, adapters.

PR #9114 resolved its one instance INSIDE its fence, by spelling the sentinel fully-qualified (`:re-frame.machines.result/depth-abort?`) with a comment recording why, rather than by editing scripts/. That is defensible on the merits — a fully-qualified literal says the same thing to a reader and to a scanner — but it is a per-site remedy, and the scanner gap is still open.

The one-line correction, when a lane owns scripts/: add a negative lookbehind for the second colon, `(?<!:):(rf(?:\.[a-z][\w.-]*)?)/...`. It is strictly safe — `::x/y` ALWAYS resolves through an alias, and every framework namespace is `re-frame.*`, so no `::` form can ever denote a literal `:rf.*` value. Pair it with a self-test fixture asserting that `::rf.foo/bar` does NOT fire CHECK B while `:rf.foo/bar` still does; the checker already carries a self-test suite in the same shape.

Worth deciding at the same time whether the ratchet should simply FORBID `::rf.<tail>/key` in framework source, which is the stronger and simpler rule: the fully-qualified spelling is unambiguous to every consumer (Xray, the MCP catalogues, this checker and any future one), and the auto-resolved form buys only brevity.
SEQUENCING FENCE (mayor, this tick): do NOT dispatch this ratchet until rf2-6r9j.161 (core) AND rf2-6r9j.209 (resources) have LANDED ON MAIN. The ratchet is repo-wide by design - that is the whole point of it, per this bead's own rationale that per-artefact is what let machines go unowned. But a repo-wide instrument landing while core or resources still speak the bare dialect reds the trunk on arrival, and the fix would then be to weaken the ratchet, which defeats it. machines is done (rf2-j5or, PR #9114, on main as 32701c1260). Verify the other two by payload - git log origin/main --oneline --grep=<id> - never by git merge-base --is-ancestor on a PR head oid, which is always false here because PRs merge with --rebase. Also carried on this bead already: the scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py CHECK B gap that machalias-a hit, where the checker cannot tell ::rf.x/y from :rf.x/y and would demand a false reservation row in the one-toucher spec/Conventions.md. That fix belongs to whichever lane owns scripts/, which is this one.
RATCHET SCOPE CORRECTION, measured on the core sweep (rf2-6r9j.161, PR #9128) — this changes the design recorded above, do not build the ratchet without it.

The core residue after PR #9103 was exactly ONE edge in ONE file, and the reason it survived is the reason this ratchet must be wider than currently specified: it is NOT an (ns ... (:require ...)) edge at all. It is a runtime TOP-LEVEL (require '[re-frame.late-bind.directory :as directory]).

clj-kondo's namespace-usage analysis does not report runtime require forms. That is precisely why the bead's own clj-kondo census read 1616 where a textual scan of the same tree read 1617 — the one-edge delta IS this edge, and it is why a whole 312-file sweep missed it.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DESIGN: the balanced-bracket libspec scan specified above is necessary but NOT sufficient. Runtime (require ...) forms must be in the ratchet's scan surface, or it reproduces this exact miss and reports a clean run over it. Add a positive fixture for the runtime-require shape specifically, not only the ns-form shape.

TWO MORE MEASUREMENTS worth having before building it:
- Core carries ZERO host-conditional exemptions (derived predicate over all 349 files, 143 of them .cljc). rf2-j5or's notes say 'core one'; that is refuted. Core's re-frame requires sit in the common part of reader conditionals. Machines has 1 file, routing 8, resources 12 (24 edges, all one alias 'substrate').
- Trap 1 IS live in core: 39 libspec vectors span lines, all already canonical — which is exactly why a line-oriented census would have reported a clean run anyway. The line-spanning hazard is real here and invisible to the obvious instrument.

PREREQUISITE STATUS: machines (rf2-j5or) is MERGED. core (rf2-6r9j.161, PR #9128) and resources (rf2-6r9j.209, PR #9129) are CLOSED but their PRs were still OPEN when this note was written — verify all three by payload before dispatching, per the sequencing fence above.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9135 (2026-09-04): REOPENED. check_require_alias_dialect.py calls its mask reader-level but does not consume the Clojure #_ discard macro. In-memory reproduction against the merged code: read_file on (ns x (:require #_[re-frame.machines :as machines] [re-frame.core :as rf])) reports re-frame.machines -> machines as a live edge even though the reader discards that entire libspec. The same mechanism also scans a #_(require ...) body. This makes the new required repo-wide gate false-red on valid discarded code; #_ is live vocabulary here (37 occurrences across 18 tracked Clojure files), even though no current occurrence immediately wraps a framework require. Repair the mask/scanner so a discard consumes exactly its next reader form while preserving offsets. Add negative fixtures for a discarded ns libspec and discarded runtime require, plus identical live twins that must still fire; run the self-test and live ratchet.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9144 (2026-09-04): the two manual floor reductions are correct, but this PR documents a second live tool hazard for the ratchet owner. --write-baseline rewrites every existing surface floor to the current count and returns success, so if any surface has regressed above its floor the advertised repair command silently raises that floor and blesses the regression. The #9144 worker had to diff and hand-apply only downward moves. Make the default baseline writer monotonic for existing surfaces: refuse/report any proposed increase rather than writing it, while retaining an explicit path for adding a genuinely new surface. Add self-tests proving a downward refresh succeeds and an upward refresh cannot alter the baseline. Also ensure the write path refuses unparseable input rather than bypassing the normal usability check.
SEQUENCING FENCE, set by the mayor 2026-09-04 10:1x AUSEST. DO NOT DISPATCH UNTIL PR #9142 IS ON MAIN.

This bead now owns TWO merged-PR audit remainders, both in scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py — the #_ discard mis-read (from the #9135 audit) and the --write-baseline monotonicity hole (from the #9144 audit). Both are repairs to THE TOOL.

WHY THE FENCE. worker/httpfix-a is live on PR #9142 right now, measuring implementation/http against that exact tool and rewriting its baseline row from 272 to whatever the tool reports. Changing what the tool COUNTS while a worker is deriving a baseline number FROM it produces a baseline that is correct against neither version. Two workers here do not conflict on files — the tool and the baseline are different paths — they conflict on the MEASUREMENT, which no merge check can see.

BOTH REMAINDERS ARE REAL AND THE FIRST IS A LIVE RISK TO THE MERGE QUEUE, so this is a fence rather than a downgrade:

(1) THE #_ DISCARD. The gate is REQUIRED and repo-wide as of #9135. Its mask is called reader-level but does not consume Clojure's #_ discard macro, so a discarded libspec reads as a live edge. Measured this tick: 18 tracked Clojure files carry #_. No current occurrence immediately wraps a framework require, so the gate is not false-red TODAY — it is one ordinary edit away from being so, and when it fires it will block every open PR exactly as the floor bug did this morning (rf2-ril5). Treat it as a latent trunk-red, not a nicety.

(2) --write-baseline IS NOT MONOTONIC. It rewrites every surface floor to the current count and exits 0, so where a surface has regressed ABOVE its floor the advertised repair command silently RAISES that floor and blesses the regression. Confirmed independently twice: the #9144 audit reached it by reading the code, and #9144's own worker hit it in practice and had to diff and hand-apply only the downward moves.

A THIRD HAZARD, FOUND BY #9144's WORKER AND NOT YET ON THIS BEAD, WHICH INVERTS THE OBVIOUS FIX: :min-edges is NOT a ratchet floor. It is a blind-scanner guard checked as total < min_edges -> fail, so LOWERING it LOOSENS the gate. A monotonicity rule written as 'floors may only decrease' would therefore be exactly WRONG for that key, and --write-baseline recomputes it as int(len(edges) * 0.9) on every run. title: skills: add a gate for the SKILL.md description cap — truncation is now CONFIRMED at 1,536 chars, and a second whole-listing budget can drop a description entirely
description:
Filed 2026-09-03 04:44:00 AUSEST from the skillsize-a cluster. rf2-cupfi said 'do not add a gate unless truncation is confirmed'. IT IS NOW CONFIRMED — but at a different number than that bead assumed, and the gate could not be written in that bead's PR because scripts/ was outside its fence.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, against the shipped Claude Code v2.1.258 runtime on this machine rather than from documentation:

1. THE 1,024-CHARACTER FIGURE IS NOT ENFORCED. It comes from the Agent Skills packaging spec. Claude Code's own SKILL.md frontmatter validator checks that description is a string and warns when it is missing; it applies NO length check whatsoever. No repo gate checks one either.

2. THE ENFORCED CAP IS 1,536, PER SKILL. The setting is skillListingMaxDescChars, default 1536. The listing builder applies it as a hard slice — no ellipsis, no warning in the listing the model reads, and the cut lands mid-word. The value capped is the description alone, or '<description> - <when_to_use>' when a when_to_use field is present. So the TAIL is always what is lost, which is exactly the risk rf2-cupfi identified even though it had the wrong threshold.

3. THERE IS A SECOND, BLUNTER MECHANISM rf2-cupfi did not know about. The listing also carries a TOTAL budget: context window x 4 bytes/token x skillListingBudgetFraction (default 0.01) — roughly 8,000 characters at a 200K window. When the listing exceeds it, Claude Code stops truncating tails and starts dropping ENTIRE descriptions, lowest-priority first, rendering those skills as a bare '- <name>' with nothing to route on. Skills BUNDLED with Claude Code are exempt from that pass; consumer-installed skills — every skill in skills/ — are not. This family alone totals ~10.8K characters of listing across nine skills, i.e. already past an 8,000-character budget before the consumer adds a single skill of their own.

STATE AFTER PR (all nine descriptions now load intact): re-frame2-xray 1,482 (was 1,713 and being silently cut by 177 chars — and what was cut was precisely its re-frame2-pair disqualifier, mid-word); reagent-migration 1,487; re-frame2-pair-retro 1,203; re-frame2 1,251; re-frame2-implementor 1,186; re-frame2-improver 1,150; re-frame2-setup 1,068; re-frame-migration 963; re-frame2-pair 747.

NOTE re-frame2-implementor AT 1,186: it is a SEVENTH description over the 1,024 figure that rf2-cupfi's list of six did not include. It is comfortably under the enforced 1,536 so nothing is being cut, and it was outside that bead's edit fence, so it was left alone deliberately.

WHAT THE GATE SHOULD DO, and the ordering matters more than the number:
  - fail any SKILL.md whose resolved description (folded YAML, plus ' - ' + when_to_use where present) exceeds 1,536 characters;
  - warn when the sum across skills/*/SKILL.md approaches the ~8,000-character listing budget, since that mechanism drops whole descriptions and no per-skill check can see it;
  - ideally assert that a '**Do not use**' / disqualifier clause appears BEFORE the trigger-phrase list, because ordering is what makes a truncation survivable and it is the half that actually protects routing.

The mechanism and both numbers are already recorded for authors in skills/README.md '§SKILL.md frontmatter description — the cap that actually bites'; this bead is only the machine-checked half.

CAVEAT WORTH CARRYING: 1,536 and 0.01 are DEFAULTS of user-configurable settings, and both were read out of one shipped version. Pin the gate to the documented default and cite the version, rather than treating either as a constant of the platform.
notes:
Audit of PR #9084: the gate behavior is correct, but scripts/check_skill_description_budget.py argparse help still says it guards the 1,536-character per-description hard slice plus the family footprint. The gate now hard-fails at the portable 1,024-character Agent Skills package ceiling, retains 1,536 only as a diagnostic escalation, and separately ratchets family footprint. Update this user-visible help so it states the live contract.

Every PR this bead was sequenced behind has MERGED, and the remainder was re-verified in SOURCE at origin/main rather than inferred from the bead text. Details in the per-bead line below; the surface is free of every live worker as of this reading, but re-check before dispatching because that changes hourly.
SPECIFICS: the remainder is REAL and precisely located. scripts/check_skill_description_budget.py's argparse help at :598-599 still reads 'Guard the enforced SKILL.md description limits: the 1,536-char per-description hard slice, and the family's listing footprint' — the stale contract. The module docstring at :2 is already CORRECT ('the portable 1,024 and the Claude 1,536'), so the file contradicts itself, which is worth saying in the fix. Pair with rf2-bn5f: one worker, one contract statement across the help text and both integration comments.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9153 — exact whole-listing-budget owner reopened. The new argparse/help and both integration comments repeat that nine routing contracts cannot fit in 8,000 characters however written, so an absolute gate would have no in-repo remedy. The arithmetic disproves the premise behind that conclusion: the current footprint is 8,860, including 8,674 description characters, so clearing 8,000 needs 860 characters of trimming — about 10 percent, or 96 characters per skill on average. Bringing each description below the 1,024 maximum did not show that further shortening is impossible; a maximum is not a minimum, and several descriptions still carry long trigger/catalogue lists. This matters because the measured runtime drops whole descriptions beyond the budget. Repair the one contract across the checker docstring/help, skills/README.md, test.yml, and test-fast-pr.sh: first attempt the bounded 860-character reduction while preserving routing quality and make 8,000 the guard if it succeeds; otherwise record evidence for the product tradeoff rather than asserting mathematical impossibility. Pair any integration-comment edit with rf2-bn5f, but keep this one exact owner to avoid duplicate tracking.

It is not: the surviving mention is in the CORRECTED text at :598-604 — 'Guard the SKILL.md description limits: the portable 1,024 and the Claude 1,536. Hard-fails a description over the 1,024-char Agent Skills packaging cap, and escalates that message when the description is ALSO past Claude Code's 1,536-char hard slice (skillListingMaxDescChars), which is otherwise only reported.' That is exactly right. Reading the CONTEXT rather than trusting the count is what distinguished it, and a control (PACKAGE_MAX_DESC_CHARS = 12 hits) had already proved the instrument was reading the file.

title: Remove the post-Freehand JVM fallback from spec-resource
description:
Evidence
- implementation/spec-resource/src/re_frame/build/spec_resource.clj:114-120 selects the shadow recording read only when env carries :ns; otherwise it reaches private spec-file, classpath-root, and clojure.java.io.
- The only tracked production call is implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/src/re_frame/api_manifest/cljs_publics.clj:113. Both callers of read-sidecar are macros consumed only from .cljs test namespaces, so their &env carries the ClojureScript :ns. The classifier audit in commit 93b110c20b independently established this as the single current macro path.
- The last tracked no-:ns call was implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/unpublished_head_absence_jvm_test.clj, which passed nil. It and every other Freehand consumer were deleted in c951808b47.
- implementation/deps.edn:113 still adds day8/re-frame2-spec-resource to the root :test alias even though the Freehand test path that required it was removed in the same retirement; the only live API-probe consumer paths are not present in that alias.
- .github/workflows/test.yml:2560-2564 still says the reader is shared by the Freehand fixture loader and API probe, contradicting the current source and the 2026-08-18 singular-consumer cleanup.

Impact
The unpublished artifact retains an unreachable filesystem walk that can bind to the wrong ancestor spec/ tree if reused accidentally, keeps an unnecessary root test dependency, and leaves CI documentation asserting a deleted consumer.

Recommended disposition
Remove the non-ClojureScript fallback and its io/classpath-root/spec-file support, make slurp-resource explicitly require the ClojureScript macro-expansion environment, remove the unused root :test extra-dep, and update current-consumer prose. Preserve resolve-after-require, recording-slurp, and the deterministic cold-load race test: those protect the live shadow-cljs path.

Risks/contracts
The only plausible lost behavior is manually expanding the API-probe macros from a JVM REPL. This artifact is explicitly unpublished and no tracked caller or documented workflow does that. If maintainers intend that workflow as a contract, keep it only with a direct test and documentation naming the supported consumer.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A tracked-call-site census confirms every remaining slurp-resource call supplies a ClojureScript macro &env with :ns.
2. The io require, classpath-root, spec-file, and non-:ns branch are removed, or a documented current JVM consumer plus a direct test justifies retaining them.
3. The unused day8/re-frame2-spec-resource entry leaves implementation/deps.edn :test unless a current namespace on that alias is demonstrated.
4. Current CI/source comments no longer name the deleted Freehand fixture loader as a live consumer.
5. implementation/spec-resource JVM tests and the consolidated CLJS node/API-manifest probe lane pass.

Both macros are consumed only from implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/test/re_frame/api_manifest/cljs_manifest_probe_cljs_test.cljs, a .cljs namespace, so both &env carry the ClojureScript :ns. The gen.clj read-sidecar that appears in a repo-wide grep is a DIFFERENT function on the JVM generator's own path and does not go through spec-resource. The spec-resource test suite itself never calls slurp-resource — only resolve-after-require.

Criterion 2 DONE. Removed the clojure.java.io require, classpath-root, spec-file and the non-:ns branch; classpath-root and io were confined to spec-file, so nothing else referenced them. slurp-resource now throws an actionable ex-info when :ns is absent. resolve-after-require, recording-slurp and the deterministic cold-load race test are untouched.

The consolidated node/API-manifest probe lane: implementation npm run test:cljs, 11170 tests / 55749 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0 — that build compiles cljs_manifest_probe_cljs_test.cljs, so the macro path is exercised through the changed reader.

STILL OPEN:

Nothing on that alias requires re-frame.build.spec-resource (the only requiring namespace is the api-manifest probe, which is not on it), so the entry is still unused and the removal still stands.
  * Criterion 4 — two comments still describe the removed path, and neither is reachable from that fence:

  resources/route.cljc:722  materialize-occurrences calls resolve-entry-scope (inside the planner try/catch at route.cljc:1117-1132 and the prefetch twin at 1518-1530)
  resources/route.cljc:507  resolve-entry-scope

  resources/scope_registry.cljc:616  resolve-from-db-reference

Possibly deliberate, possibly a mis-tag.

value:
`bd ready` DOES NOT SHOW NOTES-RECORDED FENCES — it filters dependency blockers only, so a bead fenced in prose reads as dispatchable. READ THE BEAD'S NOTES BEFORE DISPATCHING, never the ready list alone.

MEASURED 2026-09-04. I dispatched rf2-nvbz off the ready list, where it appeared as an ordinary unblocked P3. Its newest note read: "FENCED - DO NOT DISPATCH UNTIL: (a) Mike rules between options (i)-(iv), AND (b) PR from worker/isolation-a merges" and "no work goes out on it." I had not read it. The worker found the fence in its own first minutes and correctly measured instead of editing, so nothing reached the trunk — but a full worker cycle went to a task that was explicitly not to be started.

WHY THE READY LIST CANNOT HELP. Its filter is the dependency graph: blocked-by edges, open children. A fence written with `bd update --append-notes` is prose in a field the scheduler does not read. There is no status for "ruled un-dispatchable pending an operator decision" — `deferred` exists but carries a defer_until date and a different meaning. So the fence lives only where a human reads it.

THE RULE: before dispatching any bead, read its notes for a fence — and note that the fence may be PARTIALLY cleared, which is the case that looks most like a green light. Here fence (b) HAD cleared (PR #9066 merged forty minutes after the note was written) while fence (a), the operator ruling, had not. A worker checking only the PR would have concluded it was free.

THE CHEAP CHECK: search the bead's notes for FENCE / DO NOT DISPATCH / HOLD / awaiting a ruling before writing the brief. That is seconds against a worker cycle, and it is the same economics as every other premise check.

AND THE MAYOR-SPECIFIC SHARP EDGE: I HAD BEEN DOING THIS CORRECTLY FOR FENCES I MYSELF WROTE (rf2-ydpr behind PR #9142, rf2-c2q3 behind rf2-ydpr) and missed one written by a PREVIOUS mayor. The fences you remember are not the fences that exist. The backlog-reread loop reads all notes and is where an inherited fence surfaces; the dispatch loop must not assume that loop has already run this tick.
