title: vestige(reagent-adapter): remove ten redundant test imports
description:
## Finding

The Reagent adapter test surface retains ten imports/refers that have no live use:

- `:require-macros [re-frame.core :refer [reg-view]]` is unused in seven namespaces: `reg_view_devtools_cljs_test.cljs`, `source_coord_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, `source_coord_warn_once_cljs_test.cljs`, `view_rendered_op_cljs_test.cljs`, `view_id_attr_cljs_test.cljs`, `view_render_trigger_handler_cljs_test.cljs`, and `view_side_capture_cljs_test.cljs`.
- `[re-frame.trace :as trace]` is unused in `render_key_cljs_test.cljs` and `view_render_trigger_handler_cljs_test.cljs`.
- `testing` is referred but unused in `views_synthetic_event_frame_dom_cljs_test.cljs`.

## Evidence

`clj-kondo --lint implementation/adapters/reagent --cache false` reports each of these exact clauses as referred/required but never used. Repo-wide lexical inspection confirms there are no unqualified `reg-view` calls in the seven listed namespaces: they use `rf/reg-view`, or only the plain function `rf/reg-view*`. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc` lines 170-188 explicitly self-requires its macros and states that `(:require [re-frame.core :as rf])` is the only import CLJS callers need; many neighboring Reagent tests compile with `rf/reg-view` and no explicit macro refer. The two trace aliases have no `trace/` reference; each namespace already requires `re-frame.core`, which itself requires `re-frame.trace`, and their recorder macro comes from `re-frame.test-support`, which requires `re-frame.trace.tooling`. The synthetic-event test contains no `(testing ...)` form.

All-status bead searches for `reagent unused`, `reagent require`, `unused require`, `macro import`, `test imports`, plus description scans for `require-macros`, `dead import`, and every affected file name found no existing owner. `rf2-6r9j.12` is limited to dead imports in pair-mcp tests and is a different slice.

## Impact

The clauses add lint noise and falsely suggest that qualified `rf/reg-view` needs a second macro import, or that these tests directly exercise the trace namespace. That makes dependency intent harder to audit. Runtime impact is otherwise negligible.

## Proposed disposition

Remove only the ten proven-unused imports/refers. Keep every bare-macro import that has an unqualified call and keep side-effect-only namespace loads that are not proven redundant. Do not change test behavior or production code.

## Risks

ClojureScript macro loading is sensitive to namespace declarations. The `reg-view` removals are supported by core's self-macro contract, but the normal node/browser compilation lanes must remain the authority. Removing whole require clauses instead of the specific unused entries could accidentally remove a load dependency.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The seven unused `re-frame.core/reg-view` macro refers, two unused `re-frame.trace` aliases, and one unused `cljs.test/testing` refer listed in the description are removed, with no unrelated import cleanup.
2. A focused `clj-kondo --lint implementation/adapters/reagent --cache false` run no longer reports those ten warnings; unrelated pre-existing diagnostics need not be resolved in this bead.
3. The Reagent node test build and browser test build compile and pass, proving qualified `rf/reg-view`, trace capture, and the real-DOM synthetic-event test still work.
4. A source check confirms namespaces containing a bare `(reg-view ...)` still retain the required macro refer.
5. No production source, public API, test discovery regex, or dependency coordinate changes.
close_reason: Re-counted at tip: ten is right. EIGHT landed in PR #9161 (seven :require-macros [re-frame.core :refer [reg-view]] clauses and one unused testing refer); the TWO [re-frame.trace :as trace] requires are split to rf2-b38y because removing them takes implementation/adapters from 339 to 337 against a floor of 339 and check_require_alias_dialect.py fails from below, so the removal and the baseline lowering must land in one commit against a file this dispatch was fenced from. Each removal established unused in ITS OWN file, namespace included: the seven reach the macro as rf/reg-view or the function rf/reg-view*, and rf is [re-frame.core :as rf] in all seven, which core.cljc's self-:require-macros covers. AC4 holds: the six sibling namespaces calling reg-view bare keep their refer, and they are the census control (3,2,1,1,3,1 vs 0 on all seven). Gates on the final base, captured exits: CLJS compile 0 (0 warnings), suite 0 (11174 tests / 55752 assertions, 0 failures), examples-compile 0 (58 builds), alias ratchet 0. A planted load-bearing refer removal in auto_inject_form2_cljs_test.cljs reddened the compile at exit 1 with :undeclared-var at the exact line, which is the control for the seven made.

title: Remove the response argument superseded by the post-render flush
description:
## Finding

The non-streaming response builder still accepts and forwards a pre-render `resp` argument that no longer participates in response materialisation. Both the private implementation and its internal public wrapper preserve an obsolete arity from before the pipeline began re-reading the live accumulator after rendering.

## Evidence

- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:569-658` defines private `build-full-response*` as `[frame-id resp opts]`; its body never reads `resp`. `clj-kondo` reports `pipeline.clj:576:13: warning: unused binding resp`.
- The wrapper at lines 709-765 also accepts `resp`, but only forwards it to the private helper. Its catch arm derives the current response from `ssr/peek-response` through `project-render-throw->ring-response`; it does not need the argument.
- The sole production call at `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:325` passes the response obtained before rendering. Three focused tests call the private helper with a dummy `{:status 200}` (`resource_payload_projection_test.clj:178,230,306`); no other code call exists.
- History identifies the superseding change. Before commit `2a97334c07` (2026-06-05), `build-full-response*` materialised from `resp`. That fail-closed fix replaced the read with `post-render-resp = (ssr/flush-response! frame-id)` so render-time response effects and projected failures cannot be lost, but left both parameter vectors and every call argument intact. Commit `555038b12f` later strengthened that re-read to `flush-response-result!`; the old input remained irrelevant.
- `re-frame.ssr.ring.pipeline` is explicitly internal in the API-manifest generator. The façade API is `ssr-handler`; no API page or spec promises this helper's arity.

Duplicate searches for `ssr-ring unused resp build-full-response`, `build-full-response obsolete response argument`, and `post-render-resp unused parameter` found no owning bead.

## Impact

The argument falsely suggests the wire result may be based on a pre-render response snapshot, obscuring the load-bearing invariant that response status/headers/cookies and post-render error projection are re-read after the render walk. Test calls reinforce the obsolete model with meaningless dummy maps, and the binding leaves a permanent lint warning.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `resp` from `build-full-response*`, `build-full-response`, the façade call, and the three direct private-helper tests. Preserve the pre-render `response` binding in `ssr-handler`, because redirect and projected-5xx branches still consume it before the happy-path builder.

## Risks

Do not replace the post-render flush with the caller snapshot or move it earlier. Render-time `:rf.server/*` effects, recovered-to-nil sub failures, projected 5xx diversion, and render-throw response materialisation must continue to use the live per-frame accumulator.
acceptance_criteria:
- `build-full-response*` and `build-full-response` accept only `frame-id` and `opts`; their production and test callers pass no dummy response map.
- The `ssr-handler` drain result still feeds redirect and projected-5xx branches, while the happy path calls the updated builder arity.
- `build-full-response*` still calls `flush-response-result!` after body/head/payload/shell work and materialises from `post-render-resp`; no behavior is changed to use a stale pre-render snapshot.
- Focused clj-kondo no longer reports the unused `resp` binding.
- ssr-ring tests pass, especially render-time sub fail-closed, drain-time projection, response headers/cookies accumulated during render, resource payload projection, and renderer-seam coverage.
notes: 2026-09-03 (httpvest-b worker, PR #9115 session) — NOT STARTED, premise mismatch in the dispatch, not in the bead. This bead was dispatched to me in a bundle briefed as 'all in implementation/http', with a fence that explicitly excluded implementation/ssr-ring because another worker holds it. Every file this bead names is in ssr-ring: implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj (build-full-response* at 578, build-full-response at 724, the forwarding call at 771), implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:325 (the sole production call), and implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring/resource_payload_projection_test.clj:178,230,306 (the three dummy {:status 200} calls). Verified by git grep -F 'build-full-response' over tracked files: zero hits under implementation/http. NOTHING was done on this bead and no ssr-ring file was touched by PR #9115. The bead's own evidence and disposition still look sound on inspection — the dataflow claim was NOT disproved, merely not tested, because proving it requires reading and running ssr-ring, which was out of fence. Re-dispatch to whoever holds implementation/ssr-ring. Note for that worker: the .46 sibling in this bundle also names a JVM/CLJS gate pair, but the gate for this one is the ssr-ring suite, and the acceptance criteria call out render-time sub fail-closed, drain-time projection, response headers/cookies accumulated during render, resource payload projection and renderer-seam coverage specifically.
close_reason: PR #9162: build-full-response*/build-full-response drop the pre-render resp argument superseded by the post-render flush (2a97334c07, strengthened by 555038b12f). Body never read it; wrapper only forwarded it. ssr-handler keeps its pre-render response binding, still consumed by the redirect and projected-5xx branches. Three focused tests stop passing a dummy {:status 200}. ssr-ring suite exit 0 (231 tests/1163 assertions); reinstating the 3-arity call reds it with ArityException. Bead line numbers had drifted (588 not 569) because the :renderer seam landed in between; the dataflow claim held exactly.

title: Remove redaction helper pair superseded by collect-redaction-paths
description:
Evidence
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/privacy.cljc:272-284` defines `user-redaction-paths`; its only executable dependency is private `redact-interceptor?` at lines 267-270.
- Repository-wide exact search finds no caller of `user-redaction-paths`; `redact-interceptor?` is referenced only by that dead helper. Their remaining occurrences are self-references and stale prose.
- Commit `2a9c0656e2` (2026-06-20) replaced the router's separate `schema-redaction-paths` and `user-redaction-paths` walks with the single-pass `collect-redaction-paths`; current `prepare-handler-ctx` consumes that fused result.
- `user-redaction-paths` still claims “Read by the router,” and `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2036-2038` still calls `redact-interceptor?` a router consumer, although the fused collector performs its own id comparison and calls neither symbol.
- Neither symbol is API-manifested. By contrast, `schema-redaction-paths` was explicitly retained for callers and is outside this finding.

Why this is vestigial
The old half-walk and its private predicate are a superseded implementation path. They duplicate the fused collector's logic and leave misleading reachability documentation around privacy plumbing.

Proposed disposition
Delete `user-redaction-paths` and its now-exclusive private helper `redact-interceptor?`; update current comments/docstrings to name `collect-redaction-paths` as the router consumer. Preserve `schema-redaction-paths`, `redact-interceptor`, `redact-interceptor-id`, and all redaction semantics.

Risks / constraints
Privacy behavior is security-sensitive. This cleanup must not change path collection order/deduplication, the handler's raw event, pre-chain trace projection, schema/classification overlap, or egress redaction. Treat `schema-redaction-paths`' explicit compatibility retention as authoritative.
acceptance_criteria:
- `user-redaction-paths` and private `redact-interceptor?` are absent; repository search finds no executable reference or stale claim that the router calls them.
- `schema-redaction-paths`, `redact-interceptor`, `redact-interceptor-id`, and `collect-redaction-paths` remain.
- `prepare-handler-ctx` still obtains both `:schema-paths` and `:user-paths` from one `collect-redaction-paths` call.
- Core redaction/privacy tests pass on supported hosts, including `redact_interceptor_test.clj` and `privacy_production_egress_test.clj`; event/error projections remain byte-for-byte equivalent for covered cases.
close_reason: PR #9162: removed user-redaction-paths and its now-exclusive private helper redact-interceptor? from re-frame.privacy, superseded by the single-pass collect-redaction-paths which does its own redact-interceptor-id match. FACADE UNCHANGED: re-frame.core exports exactly one privacy symbol (sensitive?); user-redaction-paths appeared nowhere in core.cljc and redact-interceptor? only inside a comment, and neither is pinned in spec/api-manifest.edn or its metadata sibling (both zero against a control reading 2 and 3 hits). So this is internal plumbing, not a public-surface change. Retained and verified resolving: schema-redaction-paths, redact-interceptor, redact-interceptor-id, collect-redaction-paths. Stale claims naming redact-interceptor? as the router's consumer corrected in core.cljc (EP-0015 s7 comment) and in redact_interceptor_test.clj, per the acceptance criteria. Core JVM exit 0 (2177 tests/11155 assertions), core CLJS exit 0 (11171 tests/55746 assertions); reintroduced calls fail with No such var / Unable to resolve var.

value:
A CLJS COMPILE GATE CAN FAIL OPEN ON EXIT CODE: shadow-cljs grades a reference to a REMOVED VAR as a WARNING and still exits 0. For a deletion, the discriminating signal is the WARNING COUNT against a zero baseline, not the exit status.

MEASURED 2026-09-04 by worker/vest-a while removing three superseded vestiges (PR #9162). It ran the panel-gallery compile as a check that nothing still referenced what it deleted. A planted reference to a removed var produced a warning and exit 0. Anyone gating a CLJS deletion on exit status alone gets a green over a broken tree.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN AN ORDINARY GATE QUIRK: the standing rule everywhere else is "quote the captured exit code, never the harness's". That rule is right, and it is NOT SUFFICIENT HERE — the captured code is a truthful 0 about a compile that emitted a real defect. The gate is not lying about its status; the status simply does not carry the finding.

THE RULE FOR A CLJS DELETION:
1. Record the warning count on a CLEAN baseline first (vest-a's was 0 across 710 files, and 0 across 1892 for the main build).
2. Re-run after the deletion and compare COUNTS, not exit codes.
3. The reintroduced-call check remains the strongest single probe, and there it DID bite properly: a 3-arity call gave an ArityException, a removed var gave "No such var", a removed private gave "Unable to resolve var". Those are the checks to lean on.

GENERALISE CAREFULLY RATHER THAN BROADLY: this is a property of how shadow-cljs grades undeclared/removed vars in that build, not a claim that every compile gate fails open. Check the tool's own grading before assuming either way — and note the same repository has a gate that grades a missing markdown ANCHOR at INFO while --strict promotes only WARNING, so exit 0 over a real finding has now been measured twice here through two unrelated tools.

title: Retire the orphaned route-link prefetch hook trio
description:
## Problem

Routing still publishes three optional-artifact hooks for a substrate-neutral `:prefetch :intent` route-link integration, but no current code reads any of them. Their original view-artifact consumer was retired, and the shipped replacement view explicitly declines this integration. The hook directory nevertheless says Hicasso consumes all three, so the integration catalogue describes reachability that does not exist.

## Evidence

- Repo-wide fixed-string searches find `:routing/prefetch-payload`, `:routing/prefetch-on-intent!`, and `:routing/prefetch-intent-keys` only at their `late-bind/set-fn!` publications in `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:572-580`, their catalogue rows in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:540-551`, and prose/comments. There is no `late-bind/get-fn`, `require-fn!`, wrapper, or other reader for any key.
- The shipped Hicasso route-link consumes only `:routing/link-model` and `:routing/activate-link!` (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/route_link.cljs`). Its namespace contract explicitly says the prefetch trio is "Not wired in v0", and `control-keys` merely prevents `:prefetch` leaking into HTML. `docs/core/hicasso/07-routing-and-navigation.md:144-163` likewise teaches authors to dispatch `:rf.route/prefetch` themselves and states that `h/route-link` installs none of routing's prefetch handlers.
- The ordinary Reagent `rf/route-link` is still a live consumer of `link/prefetch-payload`, `link/prefetch-on-intent!`, and `link/prefetch-intent-keys`, but calls them directly inside the routing artifact. It does not traverse these hooks, so deleting only the publications does not remove route-link prefetch.
- History confirms the lost-consumer path: commit `fa3bc36bae4` introduced the first two hooks for `ui/Freehand consumers`; commit `4da020a5af2` added the intent-key hook and changed `implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/route_link_seam.cljc`. Those view artifacts are retired. Commit `c07b9f84674` later rewrote the directory prose to name Hicasso, but today's Hicasso implementation never adopted the hooks.
- Bead searches for each exact hook name, `substrate-neutral prefetch`, and `Hicasso prefetch` found no existing issue covering the orphaned trio.

## Impact

Every routing load installs three unread global hook-table entries, including one host-conditional operation and a thunk whose only purpose was cross-artifact sharing. More importantly, the authoritative late-bind directory falsely promises a supported Hicasso integration, making drift checks green while maintainers reason from an imaginary consumer.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the three `late-bind/set-fn!` publications and their directory rows, and update the nearby routing comments that describe them as seams. Keep the underlying `re-frame.routing.link` functions/data and the documented `rf/route-link :prefetch :intent` behavior unchanged because those are directly consumed. If a non-Reagent route-link is intentionally being changed to support prefetch, land that real reader first and keep only the keys it actually needs rather than preserving speculative hooks.

## Risks

The directory may be consumed by generic drift tooling, so publisher and catalogue changes must land together. Recheck any concurrent Hicasso work before removal because recent design notes discuss a possible future acceptance even though current runtime and user guide explicitly decline it. Do not delete or change the underlying prefetch event, resource warm-plan, or Reagent route-link behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `:routing/prefetch-payload`, `:routing/prefetch-on-intent!`, and `:routing/prefetch-intent-keys` are either removed from both publisher and late-bind directory, or each retained key has a shipped, tested `get-fn`/`require-fn!` consumer; catalogue prose names only real consumers.
2. `rf/route-link {:prefetch :intent}` still validates on both hosts and installs its CLJS hover/focus/touch behavior through the live direct `re-frame.routing.link` functions.
3. Hicasso route-link tests and documentation agree on whether `:prefetch` is supported; no key is silently stripped under a catalogue claim that it is consumed.
4. Routing tests plus core late-bind directory drift/coverage tests pass, and repo-wide fixed-string searches show no orphaned reader or publisher.
close_reason: PR #9165. The three prefetch late-bind publications and their three directory rows removed together; verified at tip that no get-fn/require-fn!/wrapper read any of them, with :routing/link-model as a control that DOES have real readers. rf/route-link's :prefetch :intent is untouched (it calls re-frame.routing.link directly), and :prefetch stays in Hicasso's control-keys so it still never reaches the anchor. Hicasso's route-link contract corrected: it claimed routing published a trio it no longer does. Gates: late-bind drift JVM 8 tests/683 assertions exit 0 (pins both directions), routing JVM 553 tests/3451 assertions exit 0, CLJS 11175/55753 exit 0, browser 783/4253 exit 0. Deletion run backwards: re-adding one publication without its directory row turned the drift test exit 1 with exactly one failure naming :routing/prefetch-payload. NOTE the bead's file list was stale in two ways: the implementation/freehand/ path it cites is retirement HISTORY (rf2-0yp7w / PR #8322, git ls-files returns zero) and needed no work, and three docstrings in re-frame.routing.link still call these functions late-bind seams - out of this fence, follow-up filed.

title: examples(realworld-resources): align host-page base with the /realworld-resources URL/deployment contract
description:
The rf2-do50 census (PR #9155) swept all 31 example index.html files against the route table each example ships. Four examples register routes deeper than one segment AND carry relative asset hrefs, so a deep link or refresh resolves every asset against the route directory. PR #9155 fixed two of them and left these two, which were outside its scope:

  examples/capabilities/resources/resources/  - depth 2, /articles/:slug
  examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/     - depth 3, /profile/:username/favorites

Both are :url-bound? true, so the document URL really is the route.

The fix is the identical one line PR #9155 used, added to <head> BEFORE any
asset reference:

  <base href="/">

Do NOT convert the hrefs to absolute paths instead. check-examples-assets.cjs's
resolveRef special-cases a _shared/-prefixed ref and resolves it against the
examples root; a leading slash falls through to path.resolve(pageDir, '/...')
and misses on disk, turning that gate red. <base> leaves every href untouched.

Measured under rf2-do50 with new URL() over the shipped route shapes: 16 of 28
route x asset combinations resolve wrong without a base, 0 of 28 with one. Note
that main.js is relative too, so the symptom is not merely a lost stylesheet -
the application never boots on a deep-linked route.

The remaining 27 examples ship one-segment routes or none and are correct as
they stand; capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr mentions reg-route only in prose and
is route-free.

Gates: node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs and
implementation's test:examples-compile. Examples are test-free (rf2-8cevm) - no
*.spec.cjs under examples/.
notes:
AUDIT PR #9161 (2026-09-04) — REOPENED. The plain resources example half is correct; the RealWorld-resources half is not complete.

The landed host page now says `<base href="/">`, but this app's own deployed-URL contract says the opposite: `routing.cljs` defines `(routing/with-base-path routing/history-url-strategy "/realworld-resources")`, and `core.cljs` explicitly says the orchestrator mounts it at `/realworld-resources/`. Its build/stager places `main.js` and `_shared/` under `out/examples/realworld-resources/`. At a shipped deep URL such as `/realworld-resources/profile/bob/favorites`, browser URL resolution with the landed base asks for `/main.js` and `/_shared/css/style.css`; the staged artifacts are `/realworld-resources/main.js` and `/realworld-resources/_shared/css/style.css`. A control with `<base href="/realworld-resources/">` resolves both to those staged paths.

The other advertised posture does not rescue the claim. `npm run dev:example` serves this one output directory at `/`, while the app's URL strategy still emits `/realworld-resources/...`; the shared `http-server` argv has no push-state fallback. A navigation can push that URL in-place, but a deep refresh cannot serve the host page. Thus the PR's claimed deep-link/refresh fix is not demonstrated in either declared posture.

The green gates do not cover this boundary: `check-examples-assets.cjs` resolves source-tree references and never parses `<base>`; the examples compile gate never serves a page; `ADAPTER_SMOKES` contains only the Reagent and UIx testbeds, so the PR body's claimed live-mount coverage does not include this app.

Completion: choose one coherent mount contract and make the host-page base, `with-base-path`, staging root, printed dev URL, and history fallback agree. Pin a deep document request plus `main.js`/`_shared` resolution in the existing script/substrate test surface; keep `examples/` test-free. No open PR currently touches any of these target files.

RE-CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor: the .beads checkout/checkpoint race, fifteenth instance today. Delivered by worker/exfix-b in PR #9161, MERGED.

THE SYMPTOM IS WORSE THAN THE BEAD RECORDED, and that is the part worth keeping. main.js is relative on both pages across six distinct routes, so THE APP NEVER BOOTS on a deep link — not merely unstyled. Chapter 07's warning describes the unstyled case because it assumes an absolute script tag; these two were not that case.

MY RELAYED FIGURE WAS WRONG AND THE WORKER RE-MEASURED. I briefed '16 of 28 route x asset combinations' — that is rf2-do50's figure for the OTHER two examples. The true measurement here is 24 of 64 wrong without a base, 0 of 64 with one.

IT RE-VERIFIED THE WHOLE CENSUS rather than trusting the bead: 8 files under examples/ contain reg-route, exactly 4 are deep-routed, 2 were #9155's. The /api/... hits a naive sweep returns are :request {:url ...} values, and resources_ssr's four reg-route mentions are all comment prose.

ABSOLUTE PATHS WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG, and the brief said so for a reason the worker confirmed at source: examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs special-cases _shared/ in resolveRef, so an absolute path breaks the gate. <base href="/"> is what chapter 07 documents and what #9155 used.

Gates: check-examples-assets 0 (33 pages), check-examples-compile 0 (58 builds, 0 warnings), CLJS compile 0, CLJS suite 0 (11174 tests / 55752 assertions), alias ratchet 0. A planted broken _shared ref reddened the asset gate at exit 1 naming it.

title: examples(realworld-http): align host-page base with the /realworld URL/deployment contract
description:
`examples/capabilities/routing/routing/index.html` carries a RELATIVE asset href (`href="_shared/css/style.css"`) beside a route with a path parameter. That is latently the rf2-g1gt defect in the repo's own routing example: on a one-segment route the relative path resolves to `/_shared/css/style.css` and works; on a deeper route it resolves against the route's directory (e.g. `/issues/_shared/css/style.css`) and the page silently loses its stylesheet.

VERIFIED MECHANISM (from rf2-g1gt, PR #9137, measured with `new URL()` over four cases): `_shared/css/style.css` on `/` -> `/_shared/…`; on `/issues/srv-1` -> `/issues/_shared/…`. Browser behaviour, not a Hicasso or re-frame2 behaviour.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN NOTING: an example is a teaching surface, and this one teaches routing specifically. A reader who copies its `index.html` inherits a bug that only appears once their routes get deeper than one segment — which is exactly when they stop reading the example and start writing their own routes.

BUT VERIFY BEFORE CHANGING: establish whether this example's routes actually GO deeper than one segment today. If every route it ships is one segment, the page is correct as it stands and the fix is a comment rather than an edit — a verified "correct today, fragile if extended" is a complete deliverable, and saying that plainly may serve a reader better than a silent correction.

THE TWO REMEDIES, both already verified in this repo and now documented in `docs/core/hicasso/07-routing-and-navigation.md`: absolute paths (which `docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md`'s own `index.html` already uses), or `<base href="/">`, with `rf.routing/with-base-path` for a sub-path deploy (present at `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc`). Prefer whichever the repo's other examples already use — check them rather than choosing fresh.

SCOPE: `examples/**` only. **EXAMPLES ARE TEST-FREE (locked 2026-05-19, rf2-8cevm)** — no `*.spec.cjs` may be added under `examples/`. If this warrants regression coverage it belongs in a substrate contract test; say so rather than adding one.

CHECK THE OTHER EXAMPLES TOO. A census of relative asset hrefs across every `examples/**/index.html` against the route depth each example ships is the real deliverable — one confirmed instance means the pattern is worth a sweep. Two independent instruments plus a control that fires; note that `git grep` with a pattern STARTING WITH `/` is MSYS path-mangled on this host and silently returns zero for everything, so use `grep -rn` as the second instrument rather than a second `git grep` pattern.

Discovered on PR #9137 (rf2-g1gt), reported by that worker and deliberately left unfixed as out of fence.
notes:

`realworld_http/routing.cljs` defines `(routing/with-base-path routing/history-url-strategy "/realworld")`; `core.cljs` says the orchestrator serves the app under `/realworld/`; the build stages its bundle and `_shared` tree under `out/examples/realworld/`. At `/realworld/profile/bob/favorites`, `<base href="/">` resolves `main.js` and `_shared/css/style.css` to `/main.js` and `/_shared/...`, not the staged `/realworld/...` paths. `<base href="/realworld/">` is the matching control.

`cmd /c` INVOKED FROM GIT BASH SILENTLY DOES NOTHING AND RETURNS EXIT 0 — it drops into an interactive shell instead of running the command. From PowerShell the identical command works. RESOLVES an earlier memory that recorded this as unresolved with conflicting evidence.

MEASURED 2026-09-04 on a scratch directory, three invocations of the same junction:
  Bash:        cmd /c mklink /J <link> <target>   -> printed only the Windows banner, EXIT 0, NO LINK CREATED
  PowerShell:  cmd /c mklink /J <link> <target>   -> "Junction created for <link> <<===>> <target>", link present
  PowerShell:  New-Item -ItemType Junction        -> link present, readable through
The tell in the Bash case is the output: the Windows version banner followed by a prompt string (`C:\...>`), which is an interactive shell waiting, not a command that ran.

THIS RESOLVES THE CONFLICT that made the earlier memory unresolved. One worker reported cmd /c mklink silently failing; others created junctions the same day with what looked like the same recipe. Both were right — the difference was never the command, it was WHICH SHELL invoked it. Workers using PowerShell succeeded; workers using Bash got a silent no-op and exit 0.

CONSEQUENCE FOR DISPATCH BRIEFS, and it is not only the create: EVERY `cmd /c rmdir "<junction>"` cleanup line in a brief has the same defect when a worker runs it from Bash. It reports success and removes nothing. That is the more dangerous half, because a surviving junction is what later cleanup follows into the mayor's real node_modules — the failure mode that emptied it twice historically.

WHAT TO PUT IN A BRIEF:
  create:  powershell -NoProfile -Command "New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path '<worktree>\implementation\node_modules' -Target '<mayor>\implementation\node_modules'"
  remove:  powershell -NoProfile -Command "(Get-Item '<worktree>\implementation\node_modules').Delete()"
AND VERIFY BOTH, because exit 0 proves nothing here: after creating, list the linked path; after removing, confirm the link is gone AND that the mayor's node_modules still counts what it did before (the canary reads 103 with `ls -A`).

THE GENERAL RULE THIS BELONGS TO: on this machine, a Windows-native tool invoked through Git Bash can no-op with exit 0. Do not trust an exit code from a cross-shell invocation — verify the EFFECT.

GIT BASH MANGLES `git show <ref>:<path>` WHEN BOTH THE REF AND THE PATH CONTAIN SLASHES — and it fails LOUDLY, not silently. This CORRECTS an earlier memory of mine that was wrong in three ways.

MEASURED 2026-09-04, all four combinations, same repo, same session:
  git show HEAD:CLAUDE.md                          -> 140 lines   CORRECT
  git show HEAD:.github/workflows/test.yml         -> 6563 lines  CORRECT
  git show origin/main:CLAUDE.md                   -> 140 lines   CORRECT
  git show origin/main:.github/workflows/test.yml  -> fatal: ambiguous argument 'origin\main;.github\workflows\test.yml'

THE TRIGGER IS BOTH SIDES HAVING A SLASH. MSYS reads `a/b:c/d/e` as a POSIX path LIST — colon-separated — and helpfully converts it to Windows form: slashes to backslashes, colon to SEMICOLON. Git then sees one nonsense argument. A ref without a slash (HEAD) or a path without one (CLAUDE.md) never trips the heuristic.

WHAT MY EARLIER MEMORY GOT WRONG, all three corrected here:
1. It said `git grep <ref> -- dir/` returns false empties. IT DOES NOT. Measured: `git grep -c -F 'beads' origin/main -- CLAUDE.md` returns 19, matching the working tree, and a directory pathspec at origin/main returns its hits correctly. That claim was false.
2. It said `git show <ref>:<path>` SILENTLY returns a truncated file. IT IS NOT SILENT — it prints `fatal: ambiguous argument` to stderr and produces nothing on stdout. I believed it silent because I piped stdout into grep and never read stderr. The lesson is about MY reading, not git's behaviour.
3. It generalised to "ref-addressed git search is unreliable on this machine", which sent every worker to the working tree unnecessarily. Ref-addressed search is fine.

THE FIXES, any one of which works:
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 git show origin/main:.github/workflows/test.yml     (measured: 6563 lines)
  git grep -F <needle> origin/main -- .github/workflows/test.yml          (measured: 5, matches working tree)
  git show origin/main -- .github/workflows/test.yml                      (two-arg form, no colon at all)
Prefer the second: no colon, no path conversion, and it is a search rather than a dump.

THE STANDING LESSON THAT SURVIVES: read stderr. A command whose stdout is piped into a counter can fail loudly and still present as a clean zero, because the error went somewhere nobody looked. That is the real defect here, and it is mine rather than the tool's.

A STALE-PROSE CENSUS NEEDS TWO TOKEN AXES, NOT JUST TWO INSTRUMENTS — because the same mechanism is described in different WORDS in different files, and a single-token sweep reports a clean zero over the sites that word it differently.

MEASURED 2026-09-04 by worker/hicvest-a on rf2-8esm (PR #9164). The task was finding prose that still described a "non-ClojureScript walk-up fallback" removed by PR #9106. Two sites were known. The worker ran the census on TWO token axes — the hyphenated `walk-up`, and the rare `CWD` — and the second axis surfaced a THIRD site at implementation/README.md:218 that neither the bead, the reporting worker, nor the mayor had named. Running only the first axis would have reported a complete-looking result missing a third of the population.

AND THE INVERSE CONFIRMED IT: the file a previous worker had flagged, cljs_publics.clj, NEVER USES THE PHRASE "walk-up" AT ALL. So the mayor's zero on that file was a correct zero about the wrong token — the site was real, worded differently, and only the bead's own notes carried it.

THIS IS A DIFFERENT AXIS FROM THE INSTRUMENT ONE. The instrument question is line-oriented versus whitespace-collapsed, because a target can break across lines. This one is about the TARGET: the same concept has several names, and prose written by different hands at different times picks different ones. A perfect instrument on one token still misses the rest.

THE RULE FOR ANY STALE-PROSE OR RESIDUE CENSUS:
1. Enumerate at least two tokens for the concept before searching — one distinctive phrase, and one rare word likely to co-occur (here: the mechanism's name, and the thing it operated on).
2. Prefer a token that CANNOT break across a line — a hyphenated compound is line-break-immune where a multi-word phrase is not, which makes it the better primary axis.
3. Control every zero against a directory known to contain hits.
4. Report the axes you used, so the next reader can judge the coverage rather than inherit a number.

USE RIPGREP, NOT BASH grep, FOR ANY OF THIS. Two hazards I previously recorded as findings — a `-iF` combination returning empty, and a repo-wide recursive scan timing out and printing nothing — were artefacts of reaching for bash grep when a ripgrep-backed search tool was available and is the standing preference. Both memories were deleted as self-inflicted. Ripgrep handles case-insensitive fixed-string search correctly and scans this repo in a fraction of the time.

AND THE COROLLARY FOR THE MAYOR: a zero I measure on one token is NOT evidence the site does not exist. I filed rf2-8esm saying a relayed second site could not be confirmed because my search of it returned zero against a working control. The control was fine, the instrument was fine, and the conclusion was still wrong — I had searched for the wrong word.

title: xray: 15 of 22 panel-gallery fixtures are zero-consumer, not just long-handler-buffer

value:
A CENSUS PIPED THROUGH `head -N` REPORTS THE CAP AS THE POPULATION — and it reads as a complete finding because the number is real, just truncated. Measured on myself 2026-09-04, while writing a brief whose own gate block warns about census completeness.

WHAT HAPPENED. Briefing rf2-6r9j.16, I ran the equivalent of a fixed-string search piped through `head -8`, got eight lines, and wrote "Eight surviving hits" into the brief as the population — then triaged all eight and told the worker which three were candidates. worker/xrayvest-a re-censused and found TWENTY-FIVE. My number was my own display cap.

WORSE, THE TRUNCATION HID THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE. The 25th hit — reachable only by a third axis, the token broken across a line as "film-" / "strip" — was a backlog item proposing to ADD a header that had already been REMOVED. That is the single highest-value finding on the bead, and my census could not see it for two independent reasons at once.

AND TWO OF MY THREE "CANDIDATES" WERE ALREADY CORRECT. One sat under a bold "Removed" heading four lines up, the other was explicitly past tense and self-correcting. Truncating to eight lines stripped exactly the surrounding context that would have told me so, because head gives you lines without neighbourhoods.

THE RULE:
1. NEVER pipe a census through `head`, `tail`, or any limiter when the COUNT is the deliverable. Get the count first — `-c`, or pipe to `wc -l` — and only then sample lines for reading.
2. If you must cap the display, SAY SO IN THE BRIEF: "first 8 of N". A worker handed "eight hits" reasonably believes eight is the population; a worker handed "8 of 25 shown" re-censuses.
3. A count and a listing are DIFFERENT MEASUREMENTS. Do not derive one from the other.
4. And read hits WITH CONTEXT before calling any of them a defect — a line that looks live can sit under a heading that retires it.

THIS IS NOT A TOOL BUG AND NOT A WINDOWS QUIRK, which is why it is worth recording separately: every tool involved behaved exactly as documented. The defect was entirely in what I asked for versus what I claimed I had. The same shape applies to any limited read — a JSON query with a limit, a log tail, a paginated API's first page.

THE SHARPEST VERSION: I wrote a gate block for that very dispatch telling the worker that a census needs two token axes and that a zero is not a check that passed — and then handed it a truncated count in the same document. The brief was right and I did not follow it. Check the brief's own numbers against the brief's own rules before sending it.

title: routing: routing.cljc's no-seam NOTE says rf/route-link reaches prefetch-on-intent! by direct call — link.cljc 45 lines away says it does NOT
description:
FOUND 2026-09-04 by worker/benchdoc-a during rf2-g8pf (PR #9169), and VERIFIED AT SOURCE BY THE MAYOR at tip before filing. Two files 45 lines apart contradict each other on the same fact.

THE CLAIM — implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc, the NOTE at ~573:
  "there is deliberately no late-bind seam for `:prefetch :intent` (rf2-6r9j.15).
   `rf/route-link` reaches `rf.routing.link/prefetch-payload`, `prefetch-on-intent!`
   and `prefetch-intent-keys` by direct call, and no view artefact consumes them
   through the hook table, so publishing them only promised reachability that did
   not exist."

THE DENIAL — implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc, prefetch-on-intent!'s docstring at ~531:
  "`rf/route-link` does NOT route through here — its `prefetch-intent-attrs`
   composes the same behaviour from `compose-intent-handler` at every
   `prefetch-intent-keys` position."

THE DENIAL IS THE CORRECT ONE, and it was established by reading the code rather than the prose: worker/routedoc-a traced route-link-render -> prefetch-intent-attrs -> prefetch-payload / prefetch-intent-keys on rf2-fhwd (PR #9167) and found no path from rf/route-link to prefetch-on-intent!. That is also why it DEPARTED from its own bead, which had asked it to write "called directly by rf/route-link" on all three: true of two, false of the third.

SO THE DEFECT IS PRECISE: routing.cljc's three-item list has a false middle item. prefetch-payload and prefetch-intent-keys ARE reached by direct call; prefetch-on-intent! is not reached at all. Everything else in that NOTE is correct and load-bearing — the no-seam decision, the rf2-6r9j.15 attribution, the Spec 012 pointer and the guidance to land a reader first should all stay.

WHY IT SURVIVED: #9167 corrected link.cljc's side of the story and never touched routing.cljc, so the fix created the contradiction rather than inheriting it. benchdoc-a found it because its bead's newest note said nothing in implementation/routing needed changing — it read anyway, and reported rather than editing out of fence. That is the fence working, not a miss.

SCOPE: narrow the NOTE's middle item so the list distinguishes the two reached-by-direct-call functions from the one that is not. Do NOT delete the NOTE and do NOT restate link.cljc's docstring here — one statement of the law, cross-referenced, is the shape both files already use.

GATES: implementation/routing reads 0 found / 0 floor on the two-sided alias ratchet, so it has NO HEADROOM IN EITHER DIRECTION — a comment edit must not move it. From implementation/routing/, clojure -M:test reads 553 tests / 3451 assertions. NOTHING VALIDATES A COMMENT'S TRUTH: the check is reading route-link-render, prefetch-intent-attrs and prefetch-on-intent! and confirming what reaches what. Name in the PR body what you read.

title: docs(design): architecture-census.md:146 claims check_guide_samples.py digest-pins guide chapters — the script's own docstring says 'It pins nothing'
description:
FOUND 2026-09-04 by worker/aliasslice-b while doing rf2-7sx1 slice 2 (PR #9168), and VERIFIED AT SOURCE BY THE MAYOR before filing.

THE DEFECT. docs/design/hicasso/product/architecture-census.md line 146 reads, in its KEEP table:

  | implementation/hicasso/test_kit/ | re-frame.hicasso.test, the public test kit | 40+ package suites plus four guide chapters, digest-pinned by check_guide_samples.py | KEEP |

That claim is FALSE AT TIP, and the script it names says so itself. implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_guide_samples.py's own module docstring reads: "It pins nothing: a prose edit, or a sample edit that names no new verb, is a [no-op]". What the script actually does is resolve every hicasso verb a guide sample NAMES against the def* heads of that namespace's source — a naming check, not a content hash.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A SHRUG: a false claim that a gate pins content is EXPENSIVE IN EXACTLY ONE DIRECTION. It does not break a build; it makes every future worker treat a doc code-block edit as a two-file change requiring a digest regeneration, and it makes a mayor brief that hazard into dispatches. THAT HAPPENED TODAY: I briefed aliasslice-b to expect digest-pinned fences in docs/ and migration/, and told it to STOP rather than regenerate blindly if a gate reddened. The worker read the source, disproved the premise, and reported it. The cost was one worker's attention; the next reader may simply believe it.

THE HISTORY, so the fix is not re-litigated. There WAS such a gate. It died twice:
  - the freehand roster went with commit 4c683c449d, and implementation/freehand/ is now RETIRED AND REMOVED (git ls-files returns 0 tracked files under it, and 0 under docs/core/freehand/, against a control of 29 under docs/core/hicasso/).
  - check_guide_samples.py lost its own roster in commit 0e77c4c519, which is when the "It pins nothing" sentence was added.
So the claim was true once and was never swept when the mechanism went.

SCOPE OF THE FIX: correct line 146 so it describes what check_guide_samples.py actually guards — that every hicasso verb a guide sample names resolves to a public def. Do NOT delete the row; the test kit and its four guide chapters are genuinely KEEP, and only the parenthetical mechanism is wrong.

AND CENSUS FOR SIBLINGS BEFORE CLOSING. aliasslice-b reported "a test.yml step name" as a second site; I checked and could not confirm it — test.yml's job is named hicasso-guide-samples and its steps say "Self-test the guide-sample rules", which are accurate descriptions of a naming check and NOT claims of digest pinning. Treat that as UNCONFIRMED rather than as a second defect, and re-census yourself: search for the CONCEPT on more than one token (digest, pinned, hash, roster, "exact text") rather than a single phrase, because the same idea is worded differently in different documents.

FENCE: docs/design/hicasso/** only, unless your census finds a sibling elsewhere, in which case report before widening. NOTE that mkdocs build --strict does NOT cover docs/design/** — mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs block deliberately keeps the design trees out of the site — so do not nominate it as the gate here. scripts/check_doc_slugs.py DOES cover docs/, and scripts/check_provenance_pins.py validates changed pages under docs/design/hicasso/ as its own docs.yml job; read that one before editing, since this page is in its surface.

NOTHING VALIDATES THE TRUTH OF THE CORRECTED SENTENCE. The check is reading check_guide_samples.py's docstring and body and confirming the new wording matches. Say in the PR body what you read.

RELATED CLEANUP ALREADY DONE: the mayor's memory store carried TWO memories asserting the false claim (one scoped to docs/core/freehand/, one general) alongside a 2026-09-02 correction that struck it. Both false ones are deleted; only the correction remains. This bead is the tracked half of the same repair.
notes:
VERDICT 2026-09-04, worker/truthfix-a, PR #9170. Premise HELD, verified at source.

WHAT I READ in implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_guide_samples.py (260 lines): first docstring line 'Every hicasso verb a guide sample names resolves to a public def'; the explicit denial 'It pins nothing: a prose edit, or a sample edit that names no new verb, is a one-file change with no roster to regenerate'; the body — _QUALIFIED_RE finds alias/verb in code position, _DEF_RE finds (def... name) heads, _REQUIRE_RE learns the guide's own aliases, SOURCE_ROOTS includes test_kit/src because the testing chapter is written against the ht/ and hm/ kits. The only 'pin' in the file is the sentence saying it pins nothing.

FIXED — TWO rows, not one. The same false claim appeared twice in architecture-census.md's retained-tooling table, worded differently, which is why a single-token search would have missed one:
- line 146 (the row this bead names): 'digest-pinned by check_guide_samples.py' -> the naming check it actually is.

Controls: samples_coverage returns 0 tracked files against a control of 1 for check_guide_samples; implementation/freehand/ and docs/core/freehand/ return 0 tracked against a control of 29 under docs/core/hicasso/.

(1) THE 'UNCONFIRMED SECOND SITE' IS CONFIRMED, and the bead's own check looked at the wrong step. .github/workflows/test.yml:1215 is a step NAMED 'Verify every fenced guide sample against its pin and the sources', and the comment at :1211 says 'how many fenced blocks it pinned'. (4) implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs:6382 already reads 'The guide-samples gate pins nothing any more' — correct, needed nothing.

Table column counts checked by hand: both edited rows carry 5 pipes, matching the 4-column header, and every row in that table reads 5.

The census also CONFIRMED the site this bead recorded as unconfirmed: test.yml:1215's step name claims a pin, which the earlier check missed by reading the job name and the first step instead of the second. That site plus TESTING.md:24 are out of fence and are filed as rf2-48kd. reactive-substrate-adapter-costing.md:279 was examined and deliberately left: it is a frozen dated sizing whose claim was true when written, eleven days before the roster died. title: routing: the bench route-link comment still names the retired :routing/prefetch-on-intent! seam — and the fn itself now has no caller
description:
FILED 2026-09-04 by the mayor from worker/routedoc-a's out-of-fence report on rf2-fhwd (PR #9167). Two related things on one symbol; the first is verified by that worker, the second by me.

PART 1 — THE STALE MENTION, verified by routedoc-a and OUT of its fence.
bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/route_link.cljs:127 names :routing/prefetch-on-intent! as what would replace a declined passthrough. That seam was RETIRED by PR #9165 (the orphaned route-link prefetch hook trio: three set-fn! publications and three late_bind/directory.cljc rows removed together). The comment is not describing its own direct call, so it is genuinely stale rather than retirement bookkeeping — routedoc-a judged it against the code and left it only because bench/ was outside its fence.

PART 2 — THE SYMBOL MAY NOW BE A VESTIGE, and this is the part that needs a judgement rather than a fix.
routedoc-a established that rf/route-link does NOT call prefetch-on-intent! — prefetch-intent-attrs composes the same behaviour itself from compose-intent-handler. With the seam retired, the function has NO IN-REPO CALLER AT ALL. Its control for that zero: activate-link!, its click sibling, reads 46 references across 14 files under the same search, so the instrument bites.

MY OWN CENSUS, taken untruncated and with the count read separately from the listing:
  6 occurrences total, across 3 real files (plus the .beads export, which is not a source):
    bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/route_link.cljs   (the stale comment above)
    implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc
    implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc
  NOT in spec/api-manifest.edn (0 hits), against a control on route-link returning 3 — so that zero is a check that passed rather than a broken instrument.
  NOT in spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn (0 hits).

SO THE QUESTION IS: is prefetch-on-intent! a public affordance a consumer is expected to call, or a vestige of the retired seam? Absence from the api-manifest is EVIDENCE, not proof — do not treat it as decisive on its own. Read what the function does and whether any documented consumer path reaches it before recommending anything.

THREE HONEST OUTCOMES, and the worker should pick with reasons rather than defaulting:
(a) It is a live public affordance -> fix the bench comment only, and say what consumer path justifies keeping an uncalled public fn.
(b) It is a vestige -> retire it with its docstring and the bench comment, in one PR.
(c) It is ambiguous -> fix the bench comment, report the ambiguity, and leave the symbol for a ruling. That is a complete deliverable.

FENCE WHEN DISPATCHED:
  bench/hicasso/**  and  implementation/routing/**  are the surfaces.
  WATCH THE ALIAS RATCHET: bench is a BASELINE SURFACE reading 701, and implementation/routing reads 0 found / 0 floor — so routing has NO HEADROOM IN EITHER DIRECTION. The gate is TWO-SIDED: it fails when a surface rises above its floor AND when it falls below. Removing a require can red it from below. If a count moves, STOP and report — scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn belongs to whichever alias-campaign slice holds it, and rf2-7sx1 is live.
  Do not touch spec/009-Instrumentation.md: its :rf.error/route-link-bad-prefetch row names prefetch-payload as a validation site and is STILL ACCURATE. That row separately names ui/route-link, a retired artefact — pre-existing, unrelated, hot-zone, and reported by routedoc-a rather than touched.

GATE: from implementation/routing/, clojure -M:test reads 553 tests / 3451 assertions. NOTHING VALIDATES A DOCSTRING'S OR COMMENT'S TRUTH — the check is reading the code each sentence sits on, and the PR body should name what was read for each.
notes:
SEQUENCED 2026-09-04 by the mayor — DO NOT DISPATCH UNTIL PR #9167 MERGES. This is a file-collision hold, not a ruling; no operator decision is needed.

WHY. This bead's Part 2 asks whether prefetch-on-intent! is a vestige, and that symbol's docstring lives in implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc. PR #9167 (worker/routedoc-a) is OPEN and rewrites four docstrings in that exact file, including prefetch-on-intent!'s. Two workers editing one file is a merge conflict, and worse, the stale-copy hazard: a branch that started before #9167 landed would silently revert the four corrected docstrings while passing every gate, because a revert of a merged change is well-formed and compiles.

RELEASE CONDITION: PR #9167 merged. Then re-read link.cljc at tip BEFORE briefing — #9167 rewrote prefetch-on-intent!'s docstring to record the no-caller state, so this bead's Part 2 starts from that text rather than from the text it was filed against.

AND NOTE bd ready CANNOT SHOW THIS. It filters dependency blockers only; a hold written in prose is invisible to the scheduler. I dispatched a fenced bead off that list earlier today for exactly this reason. Read this bead's notes before briefing it.

PART 1 IS NOT BLOCKED BY #9167 — the bench comment at bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/route_link.cljs:127 is in a different tree entirely. If a future tick wants to move sooner, Part 1 alone is dispatchable the moment nothing else holds bench/. But splitting buys little: both halves are small, they concern one symbol, and the Part 2 judgement is what makes the Part 1 fix say the right thing.
FENCE STRUCK 2026-09-04 by the mayor — PR #9167 MERGED, so the file-collision hold is released. AND RE-READING AT TIP CHANGED THIS BEAD, exactly as the fence note said it might; do not brief from the description alone.

WHAT #9167 ALREADY DID TO PART 2. It rewrote prefetch-on-intent!'s docstring in implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc:519 to record the no-caller state honestly. At tip it now reads, after describing the behaviour: "NO in-repo caller at present. This was published as the :routing/prefetch-on-intent! late-bind seam for a view artefact's own..." So the docstring no longer makes a false claim, and the URGENT half of Part 2 is discharged. What remains is the JUDGEMENT — is an uncalled, unmanifested public fn a vestige or a live affordance — and that is now a considered question rather than a defect on the tree.

WHAT PART 1 ACTUALLY IS, read in context rather than from the filing. bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/route_link.cljs, in the docstring of the prefetch-decline path, says:

  "If HD-027 is deliberately reopened to admit prefetch, what replaces this is
   routing's full three-handler behaviour (`:routing/prefetch-on-intent!` at
   `:on-mouse-enter` / `:on-focus` / `:on-touch-start`). A passthrough is not
   the middle ground between the two."

THAT IS A CONDITIONAL FUTURE STATEMENT, NOT A CLAIM ABOUT TODAY, which makes it narrower than "a stale mention". The BEHAVIOUR it describes — routing's three-handler prefetch — still exists and is still what would replace the decline; it is reached through prefetch-intent-attrs and compose-intent-handler. What is stale is only that it names the mechanism by its RETIRED SEAM KEYWORD, :routing/prefetch-on-intent!, which no longer resolves to anything. So the fix is to name the live mechanism instead of the dead seam, keeping the sentence's meaning intact.

MY OWN CENSUS AT TIP, count taken separately from the listing and excluding the .beads export: 4 occurrences across 3 files — the bench comment above, implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc, and link.cljc. Down from 6 before #9167.

SO THE SCOPE IS SMALLER THAN FILED: one comment in bench/, plus a judgement recorded on this bead. Nothing in implementation/routing needs changing — #9167 handled it.
AUDIT PR #9167 (2026-09-04) — scope correction after independent call-graph read. The newer note says “Nothing in implementation/routing needs changing”, but origin/main implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:573-575 still states that rf/route-link reaches prefetch-on-intent! by direct call. That is false: link.cljc:203-220 builds the live handlers through prefetch-intent-attrs -> compose-intent-handler, while link.cljc:530-535 correctly says rf/route-link does NOT route through prefetch-on-intent!. A non-ledger fixed-string census finds the symbol only in this false retirement note, its own zero-caller definition/docstring, and the already-owned bench comment. Add routing.cljc:574 to this bead's repair surface; the existing keep/delete judgement and bench wording remain the exact owner. No separate bead filed for this symbol.

WORKED 2026-09-04 by worker/benchdoc-a — PR #9169. Both parts discharged.

PART 1 DONE. bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/route_link.cljs,
prefetch-declined!'s docstring. The retired seam keyword
`:routing/prefetch-on-intent!` is replaced by the live mechanism:
"(`rf.routing.link/prefetch-on-intent!`, called directly at each
`prefetch-intent-keys` position — `:on-mouse-enter` / `:on-focus` /
`:on-touch-start`)". Conditional framing and meaning unchanged; the surrounding
fail-open argument untouched. One hunk, one file, comment-only.

WHY THAT NAME AND NOT prefetch-intent-attrs. The dispatching brief steered toward
naming `prefetch-intent-attrs` / `compose-intent-handler`. THAT PREMISE DOES NOT
HOLD FOR THIS FILE, and the item's own framing is what settles it. Those two are
`defn-` PRIVATE and CLJS-only (link.cljc:191, :203), and they are `rf/route-link`'s
internal path. This bench front is NOT rf/route-link — it is a VIEW ARTEFACT'S OWN
route-link, consuming routing through `:routing/link-model` and
`:routing/activate-link!` (its ns docstring says so in terms). It cannot reach a
private var. The symbol routing publishes for exactly that consumer class is the
public `prefetch-on-intent!`, whose own docstring at link.cljc:519 names it: "Kept
as routing's one statement of the intent-dispatch law, for a view artefact that
needs it to call directly." "called directly" is load-bearing because routing.cljc:572
records that there is deliberately no late-bind seam for the trio.

PART 2 VERDICT: KEEP. prefetch-on-intent! is a live public affordance, not a vestige.
Three reasons, all re-checkable:
(1) THE CONSUMER PATH IS NAMED AND CONCRETE, not speculative — it is the one the
    Part 1 comment documents: a view artefact's own route-link that reopens HD-027.
(2) THE ALTERNATIVE IS CLOSED TO THAT CONSUMER. Retiring it leaves a link-model seam
    consumer able to VALIDATE AND ACCEPT `:prefetch :intent` (link-model calls
    validate-prefetch!) with no published way to HONOUR it — exactly the fail-open
    shape both link.cljc and the bench front exist to refuse. Retirement would
    manufacture the defect the bench comment is about.
(3) THE API-MANIFEST EVIDENCE DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE — this REFINES the description's
    premise rather than contradicting it. The description reads the 0 hits against a
    route-link control of 3 and concludes the instrument bites. It does. But the
    broader control settles the inference: the string `prefetch` appears 0 times in
    spec/api-manifest.edn ENTIRELY. prefetch-payload and prefetch-intent-keys are
    equally absent and are indisputably live (both called directly by rf/route-link).
    So manifest-absence is SILENT on this question, not evidence of vestige. The
    description was right to say "evidence, not proof"; measured, it is not even
    evidence here.
Under the stance — pre-alpha, no back-compat obligation, trust the programmer — an
uncalled public helper with an honest docstring is not a defect, and #9167 already
made that docstring honest. Nothing manufactured to close a bead.

CENSUS AT TIP, count taken separately from the listing: 4 occurrences across 3
source files (7 across 4 including the .beads export, not a source) — matching the
mayor's count. bench front_route_link.cljs:127, routing.cljc:574, link.cljc:519 and
:531. Control: activate-link! reads 72 occurrences across 27 files under the
identical search.

ONE RESIDUAL INACCURACY REPORTED, NOT TOUCHED — needs a ruling or a follow-up bead.
implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:574 states that `rf/route-link`
"reaches rf.routing.link/prefetch-payload, prefetch-on-intent! and
prefetch-intent-keys BY DIRECT CALL". True of prefetch-payload and
prefetch-intent-keys; FALSE of prefetch-on-intent!, which rf/route-link does not
call at all — link.cljc:531 says so explicitly ("rf/route-link does NOT route
through here"). Two files 45 lines apart contradict each other at tip. #9167 fixed
link.cljc and did not reach this clause. It is inside the item's declared surface
(implementation/routing/**) but outside the dispatching brief's MAY-EDIT fence, and
this item's newest note says nothing in implementation/routing needs changing — so
it was left alone deliberately rather than silently.

GATE: python scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py --verbose — exit 0, 2773 files /
10773 edges / 5586 non-canonical, identical to trunk. RATCHET DID NOT MOVE in either
direction. Routing suite not run: the verdict is KEEP, so no code changed.
Provenance proven by planted fault (gate red exit 1, "bench: 702 violation(s), floor
701", naming route_link.cljs:77), restored and verified by git blob hash
15bd145e51de3e13afdb5e748ae46cca8ed23c02. That proves the gate reads this worktree;
it proves nothing about whether the prose is true — that rests on the reading above.
AUDIT PR #9169 (2026-09-04) — REOPENED. The PR fixed the bench comment and made a defensible KEEP ruling, but it closed this exact owner while explicitly leaving implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:573-575 false. That comment says rf/route-link reaches prefetch-on-intent! by direct call; link.cljc:203-220 and :385 show the live path is prefetch-intent-attrs -> compose-intent-handler, while the public helper at :519 has no caller and its own docstring says rf/route-link does not route through it. Correct that one retirement note; do not duplicate the bead or revisit the KEEP ruling.
close_reason:
RE-CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor: the .beads checkout/checkpoint race, seventeenth instance today. Payload verified in the WORKING TREE at HEAD==origin/main with a control that fired (29 'prefetch' hits in the file, so the instrument read it): the retired seam name :routing/prefetch-on-intent! reads ZERO, and the live name rf.routing.link/prefetch-on-intent! reads ONE.

Delivered by worker/benchdoc-a in PR #9169, MERGED.

MY BRIEF WAS WRONG ABOUT THE REPLACEMENT NAME AND THE WORKER CAUGHT IT. I steered it to name prefetch-intent-attrs / compose-intent-handler. Both are defn- PRIVATE and CLJS-only (link.cljc:191, :203), and they are rf/route-link's INTERNAL path — the bench file is a view artefact's own route-link consuming routing through late-bound seams, so it cannot reach them. Naming them would have produced a fresh false statement in place of a stale one. It read the bench file's own ns docstring to establish which consumer class it belongs to, then named rf.routing.link/prefetch-on-intent! called directly at each prefetch-intent-keys position.

PART 2 VERDICT: KEEP, and argued rather than defaulted. Retiring prefetch-on-intent! would leave a link-model seam consumer able to validate and ACCEPT :prefetch :intent — link-model calls validate-prefetch! — with no published way to honour it. That is the exact fail-open shape both files exist to refuse.

IT ALSO CORRECTED MY REASONING ON MANIFEST EVIDENCE. I had said absence from spec/api-manifest.edn was 'evidence, not proof' of privateness. Measured: 'prefetch' appears ZERO times in that manifest at all, against a control where route-link returns a row — so prefetch-payload and prefetch-intent-keys, indisputably live and directly called, are equally absent. For this family manifest-absence is not even evidence.

AND IT FOUND A CONTRADICTION #9167 CREATED, reported rather than edited out of fence: routing.cljc claimed rf/route-link reaches prefetch-on-intent! by direct call while link.cljc 45 lines away denied it. Filed as rf2-w0s6 and fixed in PR #9170.

Gates: alias ratchet exit 0, unmoved at 2773/10773/5586 on its base. Planted a non-canonical alias because the counts came back byte-identical to trunk (the reassuring-constant failure mode) — gate went red at exit 1 with 'bench: 702 violation(s), floor 701' naming its own line; restored and verified by git blob hash.

title: xray(spec): finish retiring per-panel film-strip claims from Issues and summary prose
description:
## Finding

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/shared/film_strip/header.cljc` is a 215-line shared panel component whose only current consumer is its dedicated unit test. Its namespace still claims every L4 panel mounts it, but spine navigation moved to the L2 Epoch list and the production callers were removed.

## Evidence

- A repo-wide exact namespace search for `day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.shared.film-strip.header` finds only the namespace definition and `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/shared/film_strip/header_cljs_test.cljc`; no production namespace, testbed, example, build entry, public facade, or skill requires it.
- The namespace doc says it is "consumed by every L4 panel" and the dedicated test still asserts that premise. Current `skills/re-frame2-xray/references/panels-epoch.md` explicitly says "No film-strip header — the L2 events list owns spine navigation"; `trace_view_cljs_test.cljs` asserts the Trace panel has no film strip.
- Git history proves the lost-consumer path. Commit `4b4d1beb18` introduced the shared header. Commit `02aae4c239` removed Trace's require and `film-strip/header` render because the L2 list owns navigation. Commit `aeb34400c0` retired the Handler/Event panel, removing another former caller. No current source caller remains.
- `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md` and `skills/re-frame2-xray/references/shared-components.md` still contain active-looking film-strip design/usage prose even though the current Epoch reference records the retirement.
- Bead title searches for `film strip header` and `film-strip`, plus description search for `film_strip/header`, found no existing issue.

## Impact

The shipped bundle retains an unreachable component and a large self-test suite that proves only the orphan itself. Contradictory docs tell panel authors to reuse a component the current navigation architecture deliberately stopped mounting, increasing the chance of reviving a superseded L4 navigation model.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the orphaned namespace and its dedicated test. Reconcile active Xray specs/skill references so the L2 Epoch list is the single stated navigation owner; retain genuinely historical design notes only when clearly marked superseded. If a current panel is intentionally meant to restore the header, first identify and land that real consumer rather than preserving the component speculatively.

## Risks

Do not remove Epoch/L2 navigation, issue filtering, or the current panel focus events. Recheck concurrent panel work and out-of-repo published API policy before deletion, although the component is not facade-exported and no current in-repo caller exists.
acceptance_criteria:
- Repo-wide namespace and var searches show no remaining call site before removal, or identify a newly landed real consumer and close this issue with that evidence.
- The orphan source file and dedicated self-test are removed if no consumer exists.
- Current Xray specs and `skills/re-frame2-xray` references consistently name the L2 Epoch list as spine-navigation owner and do not claim every L4 panel mounts a film strip.
- The Xray CLJS/JVM tests and relevant build/testbed smoke gates pass; current Epoch/Trace navigation assertions remain green.

AUDIT PR #9166 (2026-09-04) — REOPENED: the 19-fixture deletion is clean, but the documentation half closes on a false no-exception premise and its token census misses semantic UI references.

At merged commit 7c0be363258c7b589b8d2133897a02f192ee215e, tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_inspector.cljs still defines and mounts prev-next-nav in the panel header (lines 451-494, 635-643), dispatching :rf.xray/machine-focus-prev/-next to walk prior/next epochs touching the focused machine. Its focused tests assert the nav renders and moves spine focus. tools/xray/spec/003-Machine-Inspector.md lines 24-31 and 172-203 likewise specify this as the live Dynamic Machines surface.

PR #9166 nevertheless marks 021 §6.5's exact per-machine behavior retired, while §5.5 says the L2 events list is the single navigation owner and any panel-owned epoch stepper is a second one. That directly contradicts shipped code and canonical Spec 003. The claimed 25-hit film-strip census also misses glyph-only semantics: active-looking §6.2 and §17.4 Machines mockups still draw [◀ Prev] [Next ▶], as do Routing/Issues mockups whose later subsections now say the control is retired. skills/re-frame2-xray/references/panels-epoch.md compounds the mismatch by saying Trace “opts out of the shared [◀ Prev] [Next ▶] header” while shared-components.md correctly says no such shared header exists. No open PR currently owns this reconciliation.

Reconcile the intended architecture rather than restoring the deleted generic component: if the implemented high-value filtered Machines navigator is intentional, explicitly distinguish it as the argued exception, keep §003/§6.5/live Machines mockups normative, narrow the global no-exception claims, and remove or clearly retire glyph-only steppers from panels that do not implement one. If L2 truly must be the sole owner, remove the Machines implementation/tests deliberately and update Spec 003. In either case, census semantic shapes such as the button labels/mockups across current specs and skill references, not only film-strip tokens.

title: Retire React 18 act fallbacks below the React 19 adapter floor
description:
## Scope

Retire the pre-React-19 act-resolution compatibility path discovered in the UIx adapter audit, across the one shared runtime and every live test harness that copied it. Preserve the public flush-views! entry points and their React-19 test behavior. This includes:

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs (the resolver used by UIx, Hicasso, and stock Reagent's adapter-level flush);
- implementation/adapters/uix/src plus its five DOM harness copies;
- the three stock-Reagent DOM harness copies;
- the shared React-adapter suite, SSR hydration harness, two machines-viz harnesses, and Story harness;
- the stale reagent-slim resolver commentary and its inert (or (.-act react) nil) shape.

Root rendering, flush-render!, scheduler ordering, and support for React 18 applications are not being redesigned here.

## Vestigial finding

The repository now has an explicit React-19 floor, but the shared spine still probes react-dom/test-utils as a React-18 fallback, the UIx public helper promises both React 18 and 19, and fourteen live source/test files require react-dom/test-utils. That fallback predates the current floor and no longer provides a valid path on any supported build.

## Evidence and reachability proof

- docs/core/25-from-re-frame-v1.md:49 says every re-frame2 adapter targets React 19 and React 17/18 applications must bump.
- skills/re-frame-migration/references/floor-gate.md:7-11 repeats that React-19 floor and specifically says UIx hits it.
- spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:286-290 and :1336-1338 define adapter flush-views! as a dev/test boundary around direct React 19 act.
- implementation/package.json:19-20 pins react and react-dom 19.2.0. tools/template/src/day8/re_frame2_template/hooks.clj:191 pins generated consumers to 19.2.0, with a lockstep test against package.json.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1717-1744 still documents users on React 18.x, probes React.act, then requires react-dom/test-utils. UIx repeats the React-18 promise at implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:173-181.
- The exact require appears in fourteen files: core spine; core react_shared_suite; five UIx DOM tests; three stock-Reagent DOM tests; one SSR DOM test; two machines-viz DOM tests; and one Story DOM test. Repository-wide rg found no other live require sites.
- Runtime proof against the installed lock: with the React 19.2 development build, typeof React.act is "function", so the fallback is unreachable. With NODE_ENV=production, typeof React.act is "undefined"; react-dom/test-utils exports a function, but implementation/node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-test-utils.production.js:14-22 shows it is only a deprecated forwarding wrapper. Invoking it prints the deprecation and throws TypeError: React.act is not a function. It therefore cannot rescue the supported production build either.
- implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/client.cljs:73-113 already says this artifact is React-19-only and probes only React.act, but still claims implementation tests use React 18.3, claims the shared fallback remains load-bearing, and spells the resolver as (or (.-act react) nil). implementation/package.json disproves the test-tree claim.
- git blame attributes the shared fallback to e0a659445d (2026-05-14), before the current dependency floor and template pin.

## Impact

The branch and its copies preserve a support promise the product explicitly rejects, add deprecated module edges to browser test bundles, and obscure the actual contract. In React 19 development they are dead. In React 19 production the apparent rescue is worse than a no-op: the deprecated wrapper calls a missing React.act and throws. The copied compatibility prose also makes future audits and dependency changes reason from an obsolete React-18 test matrix.

## Recommended disposition

Use React.act as the sole supported dev/test implementation. In shared code, retain the current unavailable-act no-op only where production elision/node safety requires it, but remove the react-dom/test-utils require. Simplify local test helpers to React.act, remove stale React-18 compatibility prose, and simplify reagent-slim's resolver to its one real expression. Do not rename or remove any public flush-views! function and do not change its nil return contract.

## Risks

Some downstream project may have relied on the undocumented implementation detail that this helper happened to work on React 18, despite the explicit React-19 migration gate. That unsupported compatibility is the only behavior removed. React's production bundle intentionally omits act, so the shared helper must keep its documented safe behavior there rather than unconditionally calling an absent export.
acceptance_criteria:
- No live source or test file requires react-dom/test-utils; a repository-wide exact search for js/require "react-dom/test-utils" returns zero.
- Current comments and docstrings no longer claim React-18 compatibility or an React-18.3 implementation test tree for the adapter test-flush path.
- UIx, Hicasso, stock Reagent, reagent-slim, SSR, machines-viz, and Story test helpers obtain act from React on the supported React-19 development/test build.
- Shared flush-views! keeps both arities and returns nil. On a supported development build its callback runs inside React.act; when act is absent in the production React bundle, the intended safe/no-op behavior remains and no deprecated forwarding wrapper is invoked.
- Simplify reagent2.dom.client/resolve-act to the single React-19 lookup and replace its obsolete asymmetry commentary with the current contract.
- Add or retain a non-vacuous focused proof that spies on React.act and observes the callback pass through it; removing/bypassing that call makes the proof fail.
- The existing UIx, Reagent, reagent-slim, shared React-adapter, SSR hydration, machines-viz DOM, and Story DOM suites remain green.
- Do not change public flush-views! names, arities, nil return value, flush-render!, root APIs, or scheduler ordering.

PLANT proving it bites: replacing (let [act (resolve-act)] with (let [act (fn [thunk] (thunk))] turned the CLJS suite RED with captured exit 1 and EXACTLY ONE failure, this test at client_cljs_test.cljs:60:26, every other test still green.
