FOUND 2026-09-03 incidentally by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal (operator half), while sizing disk before assembling fresh pilot workspaces. Not a pilot finding; filed because it is adjacent to the disk question rf2-t4jpz already flags to Mike, and because it dwarfs it.

MEASURED, mayor checkout C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2, "git count-objects -vH":

  count:           162409          <- loose objects
  size:            61.06 GiB       <- loose object bytes
  in-pack:         530979
  packs:           77
  size-pack:       1.72 GiB        <- the SAME history, packed
  prune-packable:  63979           <- loose objects that ALREADY exist in a pack
  garbage:         3 (2.72 MiB, stale tmp_obj_* files)

So the repository's real content is about 1.72 GiB, and there is 61 GiB of loose objects sitting beside it -- roughly 35x the packed size. Nearly 64,000 of those loose objects are redundant by definition: they are already inside a pack. For scale, a fresh "git clone" of this repo from GitHub produces a .git of 38 MB (measured twice today while assembling pilot workspaces).

CAUSE, measured rather than assumed. Sampling 300 loose objects with "git cat-file --batch-check":

  blob    count=73   total=410.3 MB   avg=5756 KB
  commit  count=53   total=0.1 MB     avg=1 KB
  tree    count=174  total=0.2 MB     avg=1 KB

Blobs are about a quarter of the objects by count and 99.9% of the bytes, averaging 5.6 MB each. .beads/issues.jsonl is currently 9,658,691 bytes (9.7 MB) and was smaller historically, so 5.6 MB is squarely its size range. Extrapolating the sample: 162,409 objects x ~24% blobs x ~5.6 MB ~= 61 GB, which matches the measured 61.06 GiB.

The mechanism is the one CLAUDE.md already describes for a different reason. .beads/issues.jsonl is a full-database export, and bd rewrites it in EVERY checkout. With a mayor loop checkpointing on a heartbeat and roughly 27 live worker worktrees each running bd, every tick hashes a fresh multi-megabyte, near-identical copy into a new loose blob. Loose objects are zlib-compressed but NOT delta-compressed, so each revision is stored at close to full size. The same blobs delta-compress superbly once packed -- which is exactly why the packed store holds the entire history in 1.72 GiB.

This is therefore normal git behaviour meeting an unusual workload, not corruption and not a bug in bd. Nothing is broken: every gate, clone and checkout in this session behaved correctly, and disk is not tight (376 GiB free of 953 GiB on C:). But it grows monotonically with every checkpoint in every worktree, so it is a slow leak rather than a one-off.

REMEDY, and it is NOT mine to run. "git gc" (or "git gc --prune=now") packs the loose objects and drops the prune-packable duplicates, and should reclaim close to the full 61 GiB. Two cautions for whoever does it:

  1. TIMING. Run it in a quiet moment. At the time of measurement this checkout had roughly 27 linked worktrees and a live mayor loop committing on a heartbeat; gc rewriting the object store underneath concurrent git processes is the kind of thing to do deliberately, not mid-tick. Worktrees share the primary checkout's object store, so this is one gc for all of them.
  2. The 3 "garbage found: .git/objects/*/tmp_obj_*" warnings are stale temporary files from interrupted writes, 2.72 MiB total. gc clears them; they are a symptom of killed git processes, which is expected given how often worker runs are killed, and are not themselves a problem.

NOT filed as a fix and NOT actioned: the rehearsal brief scoped me to measurement and forbade repairs, and a 61 GiB object-store rewrite across 27 live worktrees is an operator action regardless.

WORTH CONSIDERING SEPARATELY, if this recurs after a gc: whether the checkpoint cadence needs to be the thing that changes rather than the cleanup. That is a design question about how often a 9.7 MB full-database export is committed, and it belongs to whoever owns the checkpoint loop -- not to this bead, which is only asking for the space back.
MAYOR NOTE 2026-09-03 06:2x AUSEST — VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, AND THE CAUSE IS MINE. I re-ran git count-objects -vH in the mayor checkout myself rather than taking the report: count 162,409 loose / 61.06 GiB, in-pack 530,979 across 77 packs / 1.72 GiB, prune-packable 63,979, plus 3 stale tmp_obj_ files. So the same history packs to 1.72 GiB and sits beside 61 GiB of loose objects, ~35x, with roughly 64,000 of them redundant by definition. 27 worktrees live.

THIS IS NOT A bd BUG AND NOT CORRUPTION. It is normal git meeting an unusual workload: .beads/issues.jsonl is a full-database export, currently 9,658,691 bytes, and LOOSE OBJECTS ARE ZLIB-COMPRESSED BUT NOT DELTA-COMPRESSED. Near-identical multi-megabyte copies delta beautifully once packed - which is exactly why 77 packs hold everything in 1.72 GiB - and cost ~5.7 MB each while loose. The worker sampling supports it: blobs are a quarter of sampled objects by count and 99.9% of the bytes, averaging 5,756 KB, squarely in issues.jsonl range.

WHERE I DIFFER FROM THE REPORT FRAMING, AND I HAVE NOT PROVEN IT EITHER WAY. It attributes the volume to "a heartbeat checkpoint loop". My checkpoint commits cannot be the bulk: roughly 75 of them this session at ~9.6 MB is ~700 MB, not 61 GiB. The likelier amplifier is that bd AUTO-STAGES .beads/issues.jsonl in EVERY checkout (CLAUDE.md records "bd auto-stages, never commits"), and git add writes a loose blob every time - across 27 worktrees each running many bd calls, that is the right order of magnitude. I checked one live worktree and found .beads clean there, which does not settle it. WHOEVER TAKES THIS SHOULD ESTABLISH WHICH BEFORE CHANGING ANY CADENCE, because the two have completely different remedies: fewer checkpoints, versus bd invocation volume in worktrees.

THE ONE-TIME CLEANUP IS AN OPERATOR ACT AND I AM NOT DOING IT. The worker was right not to. A 61 GiB object-store rewrite underneath 27 live worktrees and a running mayor loop is not something to slip into a tick, and worktrees SHARE the primary object store, so it is one gc for all of them and it must happen in a quiet moment. Flagged to Mike.

WHAT I CAN DO WITHOUT AN OPERATOR ACT, and will: the reap backlog is the multiplier. 27 worktrees is well above what the fleet needs (6), and the hygiene loop has fallen behind eleven merged PRs. Reaping the reap-eligible set does not delete objects, but it stops new worktrees from adding bd traffic against the shared store. That is queued for the next hygiene tick and is now its highest-value item rather than tidiness.

NOTE FOR THE RECORD: the rehearsal verdict is unaffected. The precondition still holds; rf2-lh7b remains the blocker before two blinded pilots.
DOSSIER 2026-09-04 15:45:28 AUSEST (mayor, at Mike's request): decision dossier written at ai/decisions/rf2-ah6r.mayor-checkout-git-gc.md (local-only, lives until the ruling lands; paste-ready pre-flight/run/post-check runbook inside). RECOMMENDATION: at the next moment with zero live worker agents, the mayor loop stopped between ticks, and no git.exe/java.exe running, run plain "git gc" (default two-week prune - NOT --prune=now, NOT --aggressive) from an interactive terminal Mike keeps open, budget up to an hour; FIRST set "git config gc.auto 0" and delete the two stale lock files from 2026-07-11 (.git/gc.pid and the 0-byte .git/objects/maintenance.lock); leave the checkpoint cadence alone; file one follow-up bead for "git maintenance start" (fallback: a weekly scheduled git gc). FACTS THAT CORRECT THIS BEAD: (1) the mayor's "~75 checkpoints/session at ~9.6 MB = ~700 MB, cannot be the bulk" is wrong by two orders of magnitude: main carries 6,544 commits touching .beads/issues.jsonl since Jul 11 and 150-200 per day now (Sep 1: 196 of 411 commits; Sep 3: 200 of 441); at ~5 MB zlib'd each that is ~0.75-1 GiB/day, matching measured growth (+5,886 objects / +0.78 GiB in 33 h). (2) The "bd auto-stages in 27 worktrees" hypothesis is NOT the amplifier now: in a 1/256 sample of the store all 44 large loose blobs are issues.jsonl exports, 19 committed on main and 25 dangling - but EVERY dangling one is dated 2026-06-30..2026-07-29 and every large blob after that (13/13) is a committed version; bd 1.1.2 reports export.auto=false, the installed pre-commit hook carries no bd block, worker worktrees' issues.jsonl mtimes equal their HEAD commit time. By bytes ~60% is the dead June-July mechanism and ~40% committed checkpoints; by growth 100% checkpoint commits. (3) NEW: git's own auto-gc has been silently DISABLED since 2026-07-11 21:09 by a stale .git/objects/maintenance.lock (0 bytes) plus .git/gc.pid - "git maintenance run --auto" (invoked by every commit/fetch/merge/rebase) returns silently when that lock exists. The commit at 21:09:32 that day was 270268ba36; on Windows auto-gc runs in the foreground of the triggering command, so it was killed mid-run (kill reason inferred; files measured). This is also why merely re-enabling gc.auto is the wrong cadence fix - it would run a multi-minute foreground gc inside a mayor tool call roughly daily. MEASURED: 168,295 loose / 61.84 GiB; 80 packs (not 77) / 1.72 GiB; prune-packable 64,882; 27 worktrees including three ~/.grok/worktrees/.../subagent-* outside re-frame2-worktrees/; 377 GB free; git count-objects -vH took 1m47s (a first attempt exceeded 5 min under load). Actual gc duration not measured (estimated 20-60 min).
RULING 2026-09-04 21:11:35 AUSEST (delegated by Mike 2026-09-04, operator-reversible; dossier ai/decisions/rf2-ah6r.mayor-checkout-git-gc.md and its Codex Recommendation section folded here and deleted). Ruled by a delegated agent from the mayor checkout at tip 1ad17a77fe (== origin/main), read-only throughout: no gc, repack, prune, lock deletion, config change or worktree change was made. Re-measured at 21:03-21:05: 169,356 loose / 62.02 GiB; 532,332 in 81 packs / 1.72 GiB; prune-packable 65,069; garbage 3 / 2.72 MiB; count-objects -vH wall 2m11s; 31 registered worktrees; 384 GB free; both Jul 11 lock files still present; no gc.* or maintenance.* config at any scope; no Git Maintenance scheduled task.

THE RULING. Mike runs plain "git gc" (default two-week expiry; cruft packs are on by default in git 2.53) ONCE, from an interactive Git Bash terminal in the mayor checkout, at the next SESSION BOUNDARY: after a mayor session's Session Completion push has landed and before the next session starts, with the fleet reaped and no git.exe alive. Before the run he sets "git config maintenance.auto false" and deletes the one stale lock that matters, .git/objects/maintenance.lock (0 bytes, 2026-07-11 21:09); .git/gc.pid is left for git, which overwrites a gc.pid older than 12 hours and removes it on a clean exit, so its ABSENCE afterwards is a post-check. The checkpoint cadence does not change. One follow-up bead, rf2-fmst (discovered-from this bead, status blocked until this closes), trials "git maintenance start" for recurring background packing with a weekly operator gc as the fallback. This is one act with a runbook, owned by Mike; not a hygiene-loop task, and no longer an open decision.

WHY THESE CHOICES. Session boundary and not a tick: the loop commits every 5-7 minutes (107 checkpoint commits today by 21:00), its tool calls carry timeouts, and a timeout is what killed the 2026-07-11 auto-gc and left the locks; the quiet window the job needs cannot exist inside the loop. Mike and not the hygiene loop: same reason, plus the Windows unlink retry prompt needs a tty, and a session boundary is a moment Mike already owns. Plain git gc and not the maintenance form for this one run: no scheduler exists yet so there is no lock to honour, and "git maintenance run" FAILS OPEN on a stale objects/maintenance.lock (warns, exits 0, does nothing) whereas git gc's exit status means what it says; once rf2-fmst arms a scheduler, later manual runs use "git maintenance run --task=gc", which the git 2.53 manual asks for so they take the same object-database lock as the scheduled runs. maintenance.auto=false and not gc.auto=0: it is the single switch every porcelain command consults before spawning "maintenance run --auto", it is exactly what "git maintenance register/start" sets, so the config end-state is identical whether or not rf2-fmst lands, and one knob is enough. Quiet, operationally: (a) no loop - the mayor session has completed its push and ended, or its /loop is stopped; (b) fleet at zero - every ledger row from the session has REPORTED (the reap test is the report, never a field of the row) and tasklist shows no git.exe and no java.exe; (c) no lock files in .git or any .git/worktrees/*/; (d) tree clean. An idle claude.exe or an editor's node.exe is fine, but an editor with git integration open on any worktree spawns git.exe during the run - close it or expect the retry prompt.

OPTIONS REJECTED.
- --prune=now: discards the only margin that protects an object a concurrent process wrote seconds ago; on a quiet machine it gains a few MB, on a busy one it is the corruption path the git manual names.
- --aggressive: ~25x the delta work over ~11,000 near-identical 10 MB blobs for a somewhat smaller pack nobody needs.
- git repack -a -d && git prune: the two halves of gc without reflog expiry, pack-refs, worktree prune and commit-graph; more typing, no benefit.
- Two-stage gc with gc.pruneExpire=never first, default expiry later (Codex): premised on other worktrees' indexes not being reachability roots, which is false on this tree (REVIEWER POSITIONS 1). It would pack ~50 GB of dead June-July exports into a cruft pack only to delete them on a second pass.
- Re-enabling git's auto-gc alone (delete the lock, leave defaults): on Windows gc --auto cannot detach, so it runs the whole job in the foreground of whichever mayor commit or fetch trips the 6,700-object threshold - roughly daily at current growth - inside a tool call with a timeout; that is the 2026-07-11 failure repeated.
- Running it inside a hygiene tick: repack is safe under the two-week grace, but deleting 81 old packs hits files mapped by concurrent git processes and stalls on the Windows "Should I try again?" prompt, and the tick's timeout kills it.
- Fewer checkpoint commits: cuts growth proportionally but trades away the durability window rf2-51uz1 and rf2-rjqtj were built for; disk is not a reason to reopen that.
- Shrinking the export (bd prune of closed beads, dropping memory rows): deletes normative records to answer a disk question.
- Leaving it: ~6,000 objects and 0.6-1 GiB a day, ~120 GiB by November, every object-enumerating git command in 31 worktrees slowing further.
- A separate "git worktree prune" first (this bead's own text): dry run empty twice today (Codex 20:4x, this ruling 21:0x) and gc runs it itself; the pre-flight keeps the dry run as a check only.

REVIEWER POSITIONS. Both reviewers concur on the diagnosis, on compacting now, on no --prune=now and no --aggressive, on an interactive terminal with no agent timeout, on keeping the checkpoint cadence, and on git maintenance start as the follow-up. They dissent on three points; each was settled by reading the tree, not by preference.

(1) Reachability of other worktrees' index blobs. Codex asserted, citing reachable.c, that git's walk adds other worktrees' HEADs but not their indexes, so blob 36c019fd7dc03c57fbffe048a914e0eeb43938f8 (a 10,174,366-byte issues.jsonl export, loose, mtime 2026-07-25, staged in all three ~/.grok/worktrees/code-re-frame2/subagent-* worktrees and committed nowhere) could be expired by a default gc, and built a two-stage plan plus an owner-disposition step on it. Measured 2026-09-04 21:0x AUSEST with git 2.53.0.windows.2: "git rev-list --objects --indexed-objects --no-walk HEAD" lists that blob at path .beads/issues.jsonl; "git rev-list --objects --single-worktree --indexed-objects --no-walk HEAD" does not; "git rev-list --objects --no-walk HEAD" (HEAD tree only) does not; "git rev-list --objects --all -- .beads/issues.jsonl" does not. The installed git-rev-list manual says it outright: "By default, all working trees will be examined by the following options when there are more than one: --all, --reflog and --indexed-objects." gc, prune and repack use that same machinery (prune's mark_reachable_objects calls add_index_objects_to_pending with single_worktree unset; repack hands --all --reflog --indexed-objects to pack-objects), and the git-gc manual's NOTES promise that objects "referenced by the index" are kept. So the dossier's sentence "objects staged in any worktree's index count as reachable" stands, the safety hole does not exist, and the two-stage plan falls with it. Trap for anyone re-testing: --indexed-objects is applied when parsed, so --single-worktree must come BEFORE it or it has no effect - the reverse order reports the blob under both and looks like a contradiction. What survives of Codex's point, and is in the runbook: enumerate staged state in EVERY worktree (git -C wt diff --cached --name-status), since the mayor's own git status says nothing about the others, and prove afterwards that the blob survived (git cat-file -e). The three .grok worktrees are another tool's leftovers, detached at 0f6fa33cb7 (2026-07-25 20:44), directories untouched since 20:48 that day; their staged export must never be committed (a worker checkout never carries issues.jsonl, and a July export would time-travel the tracker) - that is hygiene for whoever owns them, and gc neither needs nor touches them.

(2) Which lock files to delete and which config to set. Dossier: delete gc.pid and maintenance.lock, set gc.auto 0. Codex: delete only maintenance.lock (git's own stale-pid rule - a gc.pid older than 12 hours or naming a dead pid is overwritten - makes gc.pid inert, and manual deletion of git internals should not be normalised), set maintenance.auto false. Ruled for Codex on both, for the reasons in WHY THESE CHOICES; gc.pid absent after the run becomes a success signal, present means the run was killed.

(3) Command form. Dossier: git gc. Codex: git -c gc.pruneExpire=never maintenance run --no-detach --task=gc now, default-expiry maintenance run later. Ruled: plain git gc for this one run (reachability finding above; fail-open lock behaviour of the maintenance form); the maintenance form for manual runs once a scheduler exists.

Distinct contributions preserved - dossier: the amplifier measurement (6,544 issues.jsonl commits on main since Jul 11, 150-200 a day, ~5 MB zlib'd each, matching measured growth of +5,886 objects / +0.78 GiB in 33 h; in a 1/256 sample every dangling large blob is dated 2026-06-30..07-29 and every later one is a committed version, so the worktree-bd-staging hypothesis is dead - bd 1.1.2 export.auto=false, no bd block in the installed pre-commit hook, worker issues.jsonl mtimes equal to their HEAD commit time - and the growth is 100% mayor checkpoints); the stale-lock finding and its mechanism (maintenance run --auto returns silently while objects/maintenance.lock exists; on Windows auto-gc cannot detach, so the 2026-07-11 21:09 run inside commit 270268ba36 ran in the foreground and was killed - kill reason inferred, files measured); 25 of 44 large loose blobs in the sample dangling and all older than two weeks, so default expiry removes every one; the 20-60 minute estimate with a phase description; interrupt safety by write-then-rename; the Windows unlink-prompt drill; the loose store already taxing plain git (count-objects 1m47s then, 2m11s now). Codex: an independent re-measurement (169,295 loose / 62.00 GiB, 81 packs, 65,069 prune-packable at 20:4x; fan-out a7: 676 objects, 160 blobs = 99.85% of bytes, 30 of 51 large blobs exact reachable issues.jsonl versions); the wording correction that 1.72 GiB is the size of what is ALREADY packed, not a measured packed equivalent of the 62 GiB, so final pack size and duration are both estimates - compare before and after, never promise a byte count; the schedule correction that under the incremental strategy loose-objects and incremental-repack run DAILY not hourly (confirmed in the installed manual), with a 50,000-object batch per run (maintenance.loose-objects.batchSize, 0 = unlimited) and a two-step delete-then-pack design; verify over two daily cycles, not one; the Windows schtasks console-window caveat (a visible console per run unless "Run whether user is logged in or not" is set, which needs a password, so git does not set it; rename customised tasks so start/stop cannot overwrite them); the manual's instruction not to mix git gc with scheduled maintenance runs and to prefer maintenance run --task=gc once a scheduler exists; maintenance.prefetch.enabled false before start; if interrupted, keep the transcript and rerun in a new window rather than treating Ctrl-C as free. Both: no worktree-prune candidates; no Git Maintenance scheduled task; no gc.* or maintenance.* config at any scope.

Corrections to this bead's own text, for the record: the "~75 checkpoints per session, cannot be the bulk" reasoning is wrong by two orders of magnitude (see the amplifier); "git worktree prune first because a stale entry holds refs" is moot; and the rf2-7ngc ep-corpus-coherence risk named in the description is CLOSED - its tip is byte-identical to merged PR #8812, the worktree and local branch were removed 2026-09-04, no ref matching corpus exists - so there is nothing for gc to lose there and the runbook carries no special step for it.

WHAT THIS BEAD NOW IS. An operator act with a paste-ready runbook, owned by Mike, executed once at a session boundary; retitled to name the act; P2 because it is bounded (about an hour, unattended) and gets longer every day it waits while every object-enumerating git command across 31 worktrees pays now. Not a hygiene-loop task. Close it only when the RESULT note (before/after counts, wall time) is on it.
THE RUNBOOK. Git Bash, mayor checkout. Not through an agent tool call; not piped through a filter (a pipe hides git's exit status and, with stderr no longer a tty, its progress meter). Each block runs to completion before the next.

PRE-FLIGHT (every line must hold; if one does not, stop and come back at the next boundary):

    cd /c/Users/miket/code/re-frame2
    date "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z"

    # 1. Quiet: loop stopped, fleet reaped, nothing holding the object store.
    tail -8 ai/worktree-agent-ids.tsv                 # every row from this session has reported
    tasklist | grep -iE '^(git|java)\.exe'            # expect NOTHING (close editors with git integration too)
    ls .git/index.lock .git/HEAD.lock .git/worktrees/*/index.lock 2>/dev/null   # expect nothing
    git log -3 --format='%ci %h %s'                   # last checkpoint minutes old, not seconds

    # 2. Tracker committed, tree clean, refs recorded, staged state known in EVERY worktree.
    git status --short                                # expect empty; if .beads is dirty: sh scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh
    git rev-parse HEAD origin/main                    # note both
    git worktree prune --dry-run --verbose            # expect no output
    for w in $(git worktree list --porcelain | awk '/^worktree /{print $2}'); do
      s=$(git -C "$w" diff --cached --name-status 2>&1); [ -n "$s" ] && echo "STAGED $w :: $s"; done
    # expect exactly the three ~/.grok subagent worktrees, each "M .beads/issues.jsonl" (blob 36c019fd, protected);
    # anything else staged is a worker mid-flight - not quiet, stop.

    # 3. Before-state.
    mkdir -p ai/findings
    git count-objects -vH   | tee ai/findings/gc-before-count.txt      # ~2 min
    git worktree list       | tee ai/findings/gc-before-worktrees.txt
    df -h /c                                          # 384 GB free on 2026-09-04; the run needs a few GiB

    # 4. Keep gc out of the foreground of future commits; clear the dead maintenance lock.
    git config maintenance.auto false
    ls -l .git/objects/maintenance.lock .git/gc.pid   # expect both, dated Jul 11 21:09
    rm .git/objects/maintenance.lock                  # gc.pid stays: git overwrites a >12 h pid file and removes it on exit

THE ACT (leave the terminal open; it needs no attention unless it asks):

    time git gc
    echo "gc exit=$?"                                 # this line, not the screen, is the verdict

Expect a progress meter through Enumerating / Counting / Compressing / Writing objects (~700k total), then a long quiet delete phase. Phases: pack-refs; reflog expire; repack -d -l --cruft --cruft-expiration=2.weeks.ago into one new pack plus, if any unreachable object is younger than two weeks, one cruft pack; prune --expire=2.weeks.ago of unreachable loose objects older than that (this removes the June-July dangling exports and the three tmp_obj_ garbage files from Jul 12/14/23); rerere gc; commit-graph write; worktree prune. Duration NOT measured - estimate 20-60 min (inflate 62 GiB of zlib, delta ~11,000 near-identical 10 MB blobs over 24 threads, write a pack on the order of 2 GiB, delete ~170k files on NTFS with Defender inspecting each). If Windows prints "Unlink of file ... failed. Should I try again? (y/n)", a process still has that pack mapped: find it (tasklist | grep -i git.exe), close it, answer y; or answer n and rerun later - neither loses anything. Ctrl-C at any point loses no data (every writer here writes a temp file and renames it into place at the end; the worst residue is a tmp_pack_ file in .git/objects/pack or duplicate loose objects, both removed by the rerun) but it does cost a full rerun: keep the transcript, run the post-checks, rerun in the next quiet window. Do not kill it from Task Manager unless Ctrl-C is impossible.

POST-CHECKS:

    git count-objects -vH | tee ai/findings/gc-after-count.txt
    # expect: count in the hundreds at most and size in KiB/MiB (0 if truly quiet), packs 1 or 2 (main + cruft),
    # size-pack on the order of 2 GiB (unmeasured), prune-packable 0, garbage 0
    ls .git/objects/pack                              # a handful of files, not 241
    ls .git/gc.pid .git/objects/maintenance.lock 2>&1 # expect BOTH absent (a surviving gc.pid means the run was killed)
    git rev-parse HEAD origin/main                    # identical to the pre-flight reading

    git cat-file -e 36c019fd7dc03c57fbffe048a914e0eeb43938f8 && echo "staged .grok blob survived"

title: spec/xray: retire the Fiber-walker contract (rf2-2vpm ruling) - delete spec/View-Hierarchy-Capture.md, fold hierarchy capture into 006 as tool-side optional, delete the unwired data-rf-view walker, correct every Fiber-primary carrier

BACKLOG REREAD 2026-09-03 (mayor) — COSTING THE HOLD.

WHY: genuinely NEEDS-A-DECISION, and the bead is right that it is Mike and not a worker. The spec locks the Fiber-walker as the primary runtime view-hierarchy capture path (Mike, 2026-05-19, a v1 MUST for React-backed ports); the CLJS reference BUILT it (fe4ff001b9, PR #1533) and RETIRED it a day later (9781aa4e24, PR #1741). A worker proved that built-then-retired history with commit-level evidence this session — my own earlier ruling had said "not yet shipped", which was wrong, and the correction is on rf2-l1hh.

WHAT IT COSTS TODAY: less than it looks, and the reason matters. The contract binds PORTS, not the reference, so the reference being absent is not itself a violation — the bead says so and it is right. Nothing is blocked. rf2-rn3u (the view_walker.cljs docstring calling the retired walker "the primary path") is NOT waiting on this: its brief fences it explicitly to stop the docstring asserting a present-tense path that is absent, and to leave the RETURN question here. That fence holds either way this is ruled.

THE REAL COST IS DRIFT WITH A HALF-LIFE: spec/View-Hierarchy-Capture.md section React-version regression check is a MUST with no home in the reference, and spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:713 still calls the Fiber-walker the primary path. Every session that reads either page reads something the tree contradicts, and this session alone has spent three separate beads (rf2-l1hh, rf2-rn3u, this one) on carriers of that one unmade decision. That is the number worth showing Mike: not a blocked queue, but a recurring tax.

STAYS ON MIKE LIST. Two options, both cheap to state: (a) rebuild the walker and the regression smoke returns with it, or (b) rewrite the contract around the shipped data-rf-view path and move 006:713 with it.
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-09-03 07:5x AUSEST (mayor). ONE OF THIS BEAD'S TWO PREMISES IS NOW DISCHARGED. The question it exists to ask is untouched; the evidence it cites for it has been overtaken.

THE DESCRIPTION SAYS: "today the reference ships ONLY the data-rf-view fallback (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/view_walker.cljs), whose own docstring calls itself a FALLBACK SAFETY NET and names the Fiber-walker as primary."

THAT IS NO LONGER TRUE AT TIP, and I checked the source rather than the commit subject. PR #9062 (rf2-amz1, landed a94ddd8dc0) rewrote that docstring. It now reads, in the file:

  "## Status: the ONLY runtime view-hierarchy capture path the reference ships"
  "Nothing implements a Fiber-walker at HEAD, so this namespace is NOT a safety
   net standing beside a live primary path: it is the whole of runtime
   view-hierarchy capture in the CLJS reference. Whether the Fiber-walker
   returns is an open product question owned by rf2-2vpm."

So the docstring no longer misdescribes itself, it no longer names a primary path that does not exist, and it now cites THIS BEAD by id as the owner of the open question. The record half of the problem is fixed and this bead is the durable owner the description asked for.

WHAT REMAINS IS THE WHOLE OF THE ACTUAL QUESTION, UNCHANGED AND STILL MIKE'S: is the Fiber-walker wanted back as the primary runtime capture path? (a) Yes -> an implementation gap against a v1 MUST; size and schedule the rebuild, and the React-version regression smoke returns with it. (b) No -> spec/View-Hierarchy-Capture.md's contract is rewritten around the data-rf-view path, and spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:713's "the primary path ... is the Fiber-walker" moves with it.

WHY THIS NOTE MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING BOOKKEEPING: a reader arriving at the description would go looking for a docstring that contradicts itself, find one that does not, and could reasonably conclude the bead was stale and close it. It is not stale. The product question has never been answered. Only its supporting evidence moved.

DO NOT DISPATCH THIS. Neither branch is a worker's call, and (b) touches spec/006, a hot-zone file.
DOSSIER 2026-09-04 15:45:28 AUSEST (mayor, at Mike's request): decision dossier written at ai/decisions/rf2-2vpm.fiber-walker-return.md (local-only, lives until the ruling lands). RECOMMENDATION: option (b) NO - rewrite spec/View-Hierarchy-Capture.md around the shipped data-rf-view path; tagging stays a MUST (already normative in 006, elision-tested); the WALK becomes a tool-side MAY; Fiber moves to a dated decision record. FACTS THAT CORRECT THIS BEAD: (1) option (a) is NOT a "rebuild": the walker's only consumer (the group-by-tree toggle) went with PR #1741, views_view.cljs and group_by_tree.cljs are gone, the panel is now an SVG flow graph, and reactive_panel_subs.cljs:197-198 / tools/xray/spec/021:537-538 record that the parent is deliberately never named - so (a) is walker + smoke + an UNDESIGNED consumer plus a UX decision Mike has not made. (2) The spec's "shipped and dormant, both paths coexist" never happened: fallback PR #1780 merged 2026-05-20 15:07Z, five hours AFTER PR #1741 deleted the primary at 10:08Z. (3) Even the shipped fallback walker is unwired: no caller of walk!/tagged-elements outside its own file and test; Xray's only data-rf-view reads are two hover-highlight selectors. (4) Hicasso (a React adapter per Mike's 2026-07-31 ruling) registers defview via registrar/register!, bypassing rf/reg-view*, so it carries no data-rf-view and sits outside 006's cross-host roster - a separate gap neither ruling changes. (5) rf2-8ve8z, cited in code and spec as the permanent parent-never-named ruling, does not resolve in the tracker (nor do rf2-mxkq7, rf2-01il5, rf2-wyvf2). (6) React 19.2.0 still stamps __reactFiber$ (react-dom-client.development.js:24279), so the retired walker would work today; the coupling risk is real but not biting. Docstring premise confirmed discharged at view_walker.cljs:5-19.
RULING 2026-09-04 21:05:59 AUSEST (delegated by Mike 2026-09-04, operator-reversible; dossier ai/decisions/rf2-2vpm.fiber-walker-return.md and its Codex Recommendation section folded here and deleted). Verified read-only at tip df66b1679496 (HEAD == origin/main at 20:58 AUSEST): no build, no test, no git state change, no worktree.

THE RULING. Option (b), in its narrow form. The React Fiber-walker is NOT the primary runtime view-hierarchy capture path and does not return; the 2026-05-19 lock is superseded. What a React-backed port owes is exactly what 006 section View tagging contract already requires and every shipped adapter already does: the dev-mode data-rf-view tag (and its sibling data-rf2-source-coord) on each registered view's rendered root, elision-gated, mutate-not-wrap. That tagging stays a MUST because it has live consumers today: forward index by id (Xray hover-highlight in panels/reactive_panel_view.cljs:245-262 and panels/epoch/view.cljs:1820-1840; Pair ui/read view-element at skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:2598-2606) and reverse index by nearest tagged ancestor (Pair nearest-view-root, runtime.cljs:2609-2619, the one live instance of the DOM-containment rule). HIERARCHY capture, a walk that produces a parent/children tree, becomes tool-owned and OPTIONAL: no port owes a walker, no React-version smoke is a MUST, no conformance surface grades it, and the reference ships no walker because no reference tool consumes one (the Views panel is a flow graph whose design never names a parent). Consequently: spec/View-Hierarchy-Capture.md is DELETED rather than rewritten, because every normative sentence that survives the ruling already lives in 006 and Ownership.md forbids a second home; 006 section View tagging contract drops the (fallback) qualifier and the primary/coexist/dormant framing, keeps the edge cases as known limits of DOM-containment inference, keeps the nearest-tagged-ancestor rule as an optional tool-side inference, and gains a dated decision note naming this bead and the commits; the unwired tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/view_walker.cljs and its DOM test are DELETED; and every carrier of the Fiber-primary wording (spec, skills, core docstrings, adapter test docstrings, check-elision comment, Pair runtime docstrings) is corrected in the same PR. One worker, one PR, hot-zone sequenced. Nothing is rebuilt.

OPTIONS REJECTED.
(a) Rebuild the Fiber-walker in the reference: it has no consumer (the group-by-tree renderer, views_view.cljs toggle and smoke all went with PR #1741, and tools/xray/spec/021:537-538 plus reactive_panel_subs.cljs:197-198 record that the parent is never named), so (a) is walker + smoke + an undesigned tree UI plus a reversal of a standing panel design, and the retired code was not a correct restore candidate anyway (see Codex findings below). Rejected as over-engineering by contract.
(b-wide) Keep spec/View-Hierarchy-Capture.md and rewrite it around data-rf-view (the dossier's shape): rejected because the tagging contract, attribute format, injection rules, edge cases, elision and containment rule are ALL already normative in 006 and Spec-Schemas; a second page would be a duplicate owner, which is the drift this bead measured (four beads and four PRs on carriers in 48 hours). Also rejected as a kept-but-historical page in spec/: the corpus states what IS (the 2d64e1f7c2 and 56afb09472 sweeps strip history from spec/), and docs/design/retirement/ is the home for retirement records if one is ever wanted; the bead notes carry the full record for now.
(b-keep-walker) Keep view_walker.cljs as a tested helper: rejected. Unwired for fifteen months, its docstring needed three corrective PRs in two days (#9041, #9044, #9062) and would need a fourth, its parse-view-id is a pure alias of core's canonical fn, tagged-elements has no consumer, and the one live user of its containment rule (Pair) reimplements the ~10 lines rather than requiring it. Pre-alpha, no dormant machinery.
(c) Keep the MUST for ports, release the reference: rejected; it asks ports to build and self-certify an ungraded reader for a surface the reference never consumed, on an exemplar that was not end-to-end correct.
(d) Leave as is: rejected; the tax is measured and recurring.
Walker = MUST (Q2): rejected; a MUST no fixture grades and no reference tool consumes is unverifiable by construction (spec/conformance/README.md:601) and is friction without power.

REVIEWER POSITIONS. Both reviewers recommended (b); they differed on the page's fate and the walker's fate. The dossier (mayor, 15:31 AUSEST) recommended keep-and-rewrite the page around data-rf-view, walk = MAY, keep view_walker.cljs with a softened docstring, Fiber to a dated decision record. Codex (independent, at ff79cc1a2d) recommended retire Fiber as primary, keep tagging MUST because it has live lookup consumers, hierarchy = tool-owned MAY, do NOT promote the DOM walker into a new obligation or call it primary, delete the unwired walker and its test, rewrite the page as a short record or fold it into 006. GATED. Do NOTHING here until rf2-kmqx3 is CLOSED, which happens only when the cold-repo artefact-install proof of the framework set is pasted on it. The ruling puts the tool tags AFTER that proof deliberately: each tool jar pins its published siblings at the lockstep VERSION, so if the framework set turns out broken (missing packed content, an old-group dependency surviving in a pom) every tool jar cut against it is pinned to a bad set and all nineteen bump together. The tool workflows' resolution gates catch only ABSENCE of a sibling, never a bad one. Nothing requires cutting these merely because the framework tag exists.

MIKE'S ACTS (three tag pushes, each watched to completion before the next; no worker pushes a tag). The order is forced by structure, not by this text: machines-viz consumes core only; xray consumes ten published siblings including machines-viz and hicasso (tools/xray/deps.edn ~71, ~75 at tip); story-v* publishes mcp-base, then story (which declares xray, tools/story/deps.edn ~67), then story-mcp (which pins story and mcp-base). docs/release-process.md section Release order (lines 149-158 at tip) says the same. For each tag, from the mayor checkout at origin/main:
  git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main

  git tag -a machines-viz-v0.0.1.alpha -m "re-frame2 machines-viz 0.0.1.alpha" HEAD

then xray-v0.0.1.alpha (release-xray.yml), then story-v0.0.1.alpha (release-story.yml). Each workflow's own first job refuses a tag that is not prefix + the VERSION file, so if the framework tier had to recover to 0.0.1.alpha-1 the tool tags are machines-viz-v0.0.1.alpha-1 etc. — re-read VERSION before typing anything.

title: mayor checkout: keep loose objects packed after the rf2-ah6r gc - trial git maintenance start (schtasks, prefetch off, verify two daily cycles); fallback weekly operator gc
description:
FILED 2026-09-04 21:11 AUSEST by the rf2-ah6r ruling (delegated by Mike 2026-09-04). Blocked by rf2-ah6r: do not start before that one-time gc has run, because the scheduled loose-objects task packs at most 50,000 objects per nightly run, never prunes the dead June-July exports, and on Windows shows a console window per run - the first packing must be the one-shot gc.

GOAL. Keep the mayor checkout's loose objects bounded in the background, without any foreground gc inside a tool call, after rf2-ah6r's gc. Growth resumes the moment the loop restarts: ~150-200 checkpoint commits a day, each a new loose ~5 MB zlib'd copy of .beads/issues.jsonl (10.6 MB), ~6,000 loose objects and 0.6-1 GiB a day (measured 2026-09-04). Git's own auto-maintenance is deliberately OFF (maintenance.auto=false, set by the rf2-ah6r runbook) because on Windows gc --auto cannot detach and would run the whole job in the foreground of a mayor commit or fetch under a tool timeout - that is what left the stale locks on 2026-07-11.

WHO. Mike, or a mayor tick with Mike's explicit go, in the mayor checkout C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2: git maintenance start writes Mike's GLOBAL git config (maintenance.repo) and Task Scheduler entries for his user, and its Windows console-window behaviour is his to accept. Everything else here is mechanical.

PRE-CHECKS.
- rf2-ah6r closed with its RESULT note; git count-objects -v shows loose count near zero.
- ls .git/objects/maintenance.lock must print nothing. A stale objects/maintenance.lock makes EVERY git maintenance run (scheduled or manual) warn "lock file exists, skipping maintenance" and exit 0 having done nothing - fail-open, and invisible when the run is a background task. This is the first thing to check whenever the scheduled runs seem not to work.
- git config --get maintenance.auto prints false (register sets it too).
- git --version is still 2.53.x; the schedule facts below are from its installed manual.

THE TRIAL.
    cd /c/Users/miket/code/re-frame2
    git config maintenance.prefetch.enabled false        # hourly prefetch against origin is noise here; the loop fetches on its own cadence
    git maintenance start --scheduler=schtasks
    git config --global --get-all maintenance.repo        # expect this checkout's path
    git config --get maintenance.strategy                 # incremental
    git config --get maintenance.auto                     # false
    schtasks /query /fo LIST | grep "Git Maintenance"     # hourly / daily / weekly entries

WHAT THAT SCHEDULES (git 2.53 manual, incremental strategy): commit-graph hourly; prefetch hourly (disabled above); loose-objects DAILY (at midnight - NOT hourly, an error the dossier carried and the Codex review corrected); incremental-repack DAILY (multi-pack-index expire then repack); pack-refs weekly. The gc task is NOT scheduled and must not be added beside loose-objects (the manual: not advisable to enable both). loose-objects is race-safe by design: step one deletes loose objects that already exist in a pack, step two packs the next batch into a new loose-*.pack; batch size 50,000 per run (maintenance.loose-objects.batchSize; 0 = unlimited). At ~6,000 new objects a day one nightly run keeps pace with a large margin. Incremental maintenance never prunes unreachable objects, so dangling objects from killed processes accumulate PACKED (delta-compressed, cheap); an occasional operator gc removes them - and once this scheduler exists that manual run is "git maintenance run --task=gc" in a quiet window, NOT plain git gc, because the manual says git gc does not take the object-database lock the way maintenance run does and should not be combined with scheduled maintenance runs. Cadence for that: driven by measured cruft growth (watch size-pack and the cruft pack), not guessed; quarterly is a plausible starting point.

WINDOWS CAVEAT (manual, Background Maintenance / Windows): git is a console application, so each scheduled run creates a console window visible to the logged-in user. It can be silenced in Task Scheduler by selecting "Run whether user is logged in or not", which needs a password, which is why git maintenance start does not do it. If the tasks are customised, RENAME them so a later git maintenance start/stop does not overwrite them.

VERIFY OVER TWO COMPLETE DAILY CYCLES (two midnights), not one:
- git count-objects -v each morning: count should drop to near zero after each midnight run instead of climbing ~6,000/day; a new .git/objects/pack/loose-*.pack should appear; packs count should stay small (incremental-repack consolidates).
- Task Scheduler history for "Git Maintenance (daily)" shows a completed run at midnight.
- ls .git/objects/maintenance.lock prints nothing between runs (a lock that persists = a killed run, after which every later run silently skips).
- No worker or mayor tick reports a git collision; commits are not delayed.
Success = loose count/bytes bounded (never more than about one day's growth), no foreground gc in any tool call, no collisions, console window tolerated or silenced.

FALLBACK if the scheduler is unreliable or the window is unacceptable: git maintenance unregister && git maintenance stop (unregister does NOT restore maintenance.auto - leave it false), then run the rf2-ah6r runbook (plain git gc at a session boundary) weekly: about 40,000 objects / 5 GiB / ~10 minutes a week at the current cadence. Do not build repository-specific cleanup machinery to hide one stock task.

NOT IN SCOPE, ruled on rf2-ah6r: the checkpoint cadence (unchanged - it is a durability decision, rf2-51uz1 / rf2-rjqtj) and the export's size. Revisit cadence only if, after two daily cycles with the scheduler verified running, loose growth still outpaces it.

Full analysis, reviewer positions and the one-shot runbook: the RULING note on rf2-ah6r.

title: hygiene: delete remote worker/liveframe-ma8r and worker/retire-delete (+ local retire-delete ref) on the rf2-7ngc ruling of 2026-09-04 — lease-protected verify-before-delete drill inside; receipts-hic081 stays
description:
AUTHORISED by the delegated ruling on rf2-7ngc (RULING 2026-09-04 21:04:52 AUSEST, Mike delegated 2026-09-04, operator-reversible), which folds in rf2-lafmr's standing measurements and the independent Codex review. This bead is the EXECUTABLE END of that ruling: two remote branch deletions and one local ref deletion, nothing else. Read the ruling on rf2-7ngc for the reasoning; everything needed to act safely is repeated here.

WHY THE STANDING DELETE TEST REFUSES THESE AND WHY THE RULING OVERRIDES IT. loops.md section Branches deletes only on git cherry reading "-" for every commit (proof of containment); "+" is only the absence of proof. Both branches read "+" and neither has a MERGED PR, so no hygiene tick will ever delete them on its own. The ruling authorises deletion on containment proofs stronger than cherry:

worker/liveframe-ma8r (remote only; no local ref). Tip c3924bece3e5999128297330a4163c5e952abb58 = scratch probe d923a84356 + its exact revert. The branch tip's TREE OBJECT equals its merge-base's tree object (58818f8fd2923731cc7e5df87911b06e00041225 on both sides at merge-base bb07ef531d): the complete snapshots are identical, so there is no change that could be unmerged. PR #9000 CLOSED not merged, its closing comment holds the no-code diagnosis; rf2-ma8r is closed. GitHub still retains refs/pull/9000/head = c3924bece3 (verified 2026-09-04 20:59 AUSEST), so even the probe text stays reachable, though the ruling does not depend on that.

worker/retire-delete (remote + local ref). Tip 87571272d87b725d0c9eff43976ffd1f81e872b4, one PARTIAL commit from parent 2ab9a42843 changing 273 paths (256 D + 17 M). Its content landed via the ATOMIC commit ef3131f4a28eec9b4f1843a609c727896d048541 (PR #8322, merged 2026-08-16), which is an ancestor of origin/main. Measured 2026-09-04 20:59 AUSEST at origin/main df66b1679496: all 17 modified paths have blob oid at 87571272d8 EQUAL to blob oid at ef3131f4a2 (17/17), and all 256 deleted paths are absent from origin/main (0 present). Main once held the branch's exact postimage for every modified path and holds none of the deleted ones: complete containment. This comparison is against a FIXED commit, so it does not go stale as main moves (rf2-lafmr's 2026-09-03 note recorded the tip-relative form going stale; this form ends that cycle).

worker/receipts-hic081 is NOT in scope: KEEP under rf2-lafmr (release condition: counts-only capability receipts implemented on main with both owed witnesses discharged, or the design explicitly abandoned). Its tip must still read ae14841ab3ac1401ddb2803e8ab4a86bc08ea15c after you are done.

THE DRILL (mayor checkout; read-only until the push). Any deviation from an expected value means STOP and re-read the ruling; do not delete.

1. date "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z"
2. git ls-remote --heads origin worker/liveframe-ma8r worker/retire-delete worker/receipts-hic081
   expect exactly: c3924bece3e5999128297330a4163c5e952abb58, 87571272d87b725d0c9eff43976ffd1f81e872b4, ae14841ab3ac1401ddb2803e8ab4a86bc08ea15c. A moved tip means new commits the ruling never saw: review them independently, do not delete.
3. gh pr view 9000 --json state,mergedAt   (expect state CLOSED, mergedAt null)
   gh pr list --state all --head worker/retire-delete --json number   (expect [])
4. liveframe tree identity:
   mb=$(git merge-base origin/main c3924bece3e5999128297330a4163c5e952abb58); git rev-parse "$mb^{tree}" "c3924bece3e5999128297330a4163c5e952abb58^{tree}"
   expect two identical lines.
5. retire-delete containment against the fixed atomic commit:
   git merge-base --is-ancestor ef3131f4a28eec9b4f1843a609c727896d048541 origin/main && echo ancestor-ok
   git diff --name-status 2ab9a42843 87571272d8 | awk '$1=="M"{print $2}' | while read -r p; do [ "$(git rev-parse "87571272d8:$p")" = "$(git rev-parse "ef3131f4a2:$p")" ] || echo "DIFFERS $p"; done
   git diff --name-status 2ab9a42843 87571272d8 | awk '$1=="D"{print $2}' | while read -r p; do git cat-file -e "origin/main:$p" 2>/dev/null && echo "PRESENT $p"; done
   expect ancestor-ok and no DIFFERS/PRESENT lines.
6. Delete, lease-protected so a concurrently moved tip turns the push into a refusal rather than deleting new work:
   git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/worker/liveframe-ma8r:c3924bece3e5999128297330a4163c5e952abb58 --force-with-lease=refs/heads/worker/retire-delete:87571272d87b725d0c9eff43976ffd1f81e872b4 origin :refs/heads/worker/liveframe-ma8r :refs/heads/worker/retire-delete
   (Equivalent without the lease, only after step 2 read clean seconds earlier: git push origin --delete worker/liveframe-ma8r worker/retire-delete)
7. Local ref, only if it still points at the ruled tip:
   [ "$(git rev-parse refs/heads/worker/retire-delete)" = "87571272d87b725d0c9eff43976ffd1f81e872b4" ] && git branch -D worker/retire-delete
   (git branch -d would refuse: the branch is not an ancestor of main; the containment proof is step 5.)

description:

DEFECT 1 — spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2159 describes a REMOVED surface in the present tense.

The :rf.error/frame-destroyed catalogue row narrates the retired implementation/ui (frame) operation bundle as a live throwing surface. Verbatim, at tip: "A substrate's (frame) operation bundle (rf2-vxgfnd.230) is a further throwing surface for the SAME category ... The incarnation fence emits at the ui source BEFORE delegating to core's dispatch/subscribe, so the same failure is never ALSO fanned by the router/subs recover-and-emit path ... all four bundle arms route through one ui-frame emit-and-throw helper so their two-channel contract cannot drift."

implementation/ui was RETIRED AND REMOVED (rf2-0yp7w, executed by PR #8322 on 2026-08-16); git ls-files returns nothing under it. So there is no ui source emitting anything, no incarnation fence, and no four bundle arms. A reader takes this row as a description of live behaviour because every verb in it is present tense.

SCOPE AGAINST #9179, and this is the part to get right: #9179 removes the :capture enum value and the clauses that attribute it to the ui surface. IT DOES NOT TOUCH THE REST OF THE PASSAGE. So do not read a merged #9179 as having fixed this — check what survives, then decide per sentence whether it is (a) live behaviour that outlived the ui and should be re-attributed to router/subs, (b) retirement bookkeeping that should be past-tensed and dated to rf2-0yp7w, or (c) a claim about a surface that no longer exists and describes nothing, which is rf2-63t1i's rule and the ground #9179 stood on.

CLAUDE.md's Architecture Overview is the governing distinction: a donor reference is either retirement bookkeeping or the reserved-kind contract, and is never a surface to build on. Neither exemption obviously covers a present-tense operational narration, but read both before deleting anything.

DEFECT 2 — the tree contradicts itself on whether :op is PUBLIC or PRIVATE.

  spec/Spec-Schemas.md:1201            ";; enum ratified PUBLIC on this category (per the 009 catalogue row)"
  spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2159     ":op (the failing operation realm ... a small closed-enum public realm attribution"
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/on_error_cljs_test.cljc:823
                                       ";; PRIVATE steering input (read from the record's attribution, never promoted to"

Two normative documents say PUBLIC; a test header says PRIVATE and never-promoted. One of the three is wrong. This matters beyond tidiness because :op's publicness is what licenses consumers to switch on it, and a test header is exactly where an implementer looks to learn whether a slot is contractual.

DETERMINE WHICH IS AUTHORITATIVE RATHER THAN HARMONISING THE WORDING. The spec is the artefact and the code is downstream, so the presumption is that the two spec documents govern and the test header is stale — but check whether the header is describing something narrower and true (:op as a steering input to error-source-coord's realm-exact resolution, which IS an internal use) that has merely been worded as a global claim. If so the fix is to narrow the header, not to invert it.

FENCE — DO NOT DISPATCH UNTIL PR #9179 MERGES. Both spec/Spec-Schemas.md and spec/009-Instrumentation.md are HOT ZONE and #9179 edits BOTH in one commit. The hazard is the stale-copy revert: a branch cut before #9179 lands silently undoes its :capture removal while passing every gate, because a revert of a merged change is well-formed and every checker reads it as clean. RE-READ BOTH FILES AT TIP AFTER IT MERGES; the line numbers above will have moved.

GATES. The cross-file gate is tags-column-keys-are-documented, a JVM deftest at implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj:1483 — it REDS if 009 and Spec-Schemas disagree, so both files move in ONE commit. NEITHER DOC GATE COVERS THE SCHEMA HALF: check_doc_slugs.py and mkdocs build --strict share one extractor that strips fences before reading a link, and the FrameDestroyedTags schema lives inside a fence. Run them for the 009 prose row, but hand-check the fenced block and the row's pipe count (7, matching its siblings) and say so in the PR body. mkdocs is not on PATH here; use python -m mkdocs.

title: release: post-publish consumer artefact-install gate in release.yml — cold-repo resolution of io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso (+core, +ssr) after every v* tag
description:
FILED 2026-09-02 10:15 AUSEST by the delegated ruling on rf2-kmqx3 (tip b26c5ad33e). This bead is the REPEATABLE form of rf2-kmqx3's artefact-install proof: a post-publish job in release.yml that resolves the just-published set from Clojars into a cold Maven local repo and compiles a minimal consumer. It publishes nothing and gates nothing irreversible; it observes.

BLOCKED ON rf2-kmqx3, and the block is structural: this job resolves a PUBLISHED artefact, so it cannot be authored, run or exercised before io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso 0.0.1.alpha exists on Clojars and the one-off proof on rf2-kmqx3 has passed. Do not dispatch before rf2-kmqx3 closes. rf2-fo4ng (the 19-coordinate rename) is upstream of rf2-kmqx3 and will have merged by then.

HOT ZONE — .github/workflows/release.yml. One workflow toucher at a time: at dispatch, re-measure `bd list --status=open --limit 0 --desc-contains ".github/workflows"` and sequence behind any live one. At filing time rf2-zq34m, rf2-4a0c and rf2-8arzr named .github/workflows in their descriptions; do not trust that list.

## Deliverable

1. One new job `verify-consumer-install` in .github/workflows/release.yml with `needs: [github-release]` (runs on the same tag run, after the whole publish DAG and the GitHub Release). No deploy job's `needs` changes. No second trigger on release.yml — the v* glob at lines 162-165 stays the only one; the DAG policy test pins that shape.

2. A script .github/scripts/verify-consumer-install.sh (POSIX sh, CI-only, runnable under Git Bash locally) taking VERSION as its argument, so the worker can run it against the already-published 0.0.1.alpha — the exercised half of acceptance, because a tag-only workflow cannot be run on a PR. The job passes `${{ needs.deploy-core.outputs.version }}` (the value the release body at ~926-939 already uses).

3. What the script does, in order:
   a. `mktemp -d` a scratch directory OUTSIDE $GITHUB_WORKSPACE; never read the repo's deps.edn.
   b. Write deps.edn: `{:paths ["src"] :deps {io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso {:mvn/version "<VERSION>"}} :mvn/local-repo "<fresh empty dir>"}`. Do NOT declare core or ssr — they must arrive transitively through the published pom; that transitivity working is the proof.
   c. `clojure -Srepro -P` with a bounded retry for Clojars propagation lag (e.g. up to ~10 minutes, 30s apart) before failing. `-Srepro` ignores ~/.clojure/deps.edn so no mirror or local-repo override leaks in. Never use an actions/cache-warmed ~/.m2 as the resolution source; the fresh :mvn/local-repo is what makes the gate honest even when a cache action is present.
   d. `clojure -Srepro -Stree` captured to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY and asserted: io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso, io.github.day8/re-frame2 and io.github.day8/re-frame2-ssr all present at exactly VERSION, and ZERO old-group `day8/` coordinates anywhere in the tree (an old-group dependency surviving in a pom is the rename campaign's miss, and this is where it shows).
   e. Minimal compile: `npm i react@19.2 react-dom@19.2 shadow-cljs@3.4.10` in the scratch dir (npm, not the repo's node_modules); a shadow-cljs.edn with `:deps true` and one :browser build whose single namespace requires re-frame.core and re-frame.hicasso; `npx shadow-cljs compile app` exits 0. This catches a jar that resolves but is missing packed content (hicasso's :src-dirs are ["src" "resources" "test_kit/src"], implementation/hicasso/deps.edn 169-176). Versions per the compatibility matrix in docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md.

4. SCOPE: hicasso is the mandatory entry point because it exercises the deepest transitive chain (core + ssr). Extending to all 14 framework coordinates is RECOMMENDED if it is one loop and the list is DERIVED — from .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh's ARTEFACTS inventory (line 139 at filing) or from the workflow's own matrix — never a hand roster in the new job or script. A roster cannot report what it does not list (the lesson recorded at the top of preflight-tool-package.sh). If the 14-loop is included, the compile step stays hicasso-only; resolution runs per coordinate.

5. Policy test: implementation/scripts/_release-dag-policy.test.cjs asserts exactly 14 publishers (line ~282) and the ordering edges. The new job publishes nothing and must not be discovered as a publisher. Add a negative-control case asserting (i) `verify-consumer-install` is not in the publisher set, (ii) no deploy job lists it in `needs`, (iii) publisher count is still 14.

6. Failure semantics, written as the job's header comment AND as one paragraph in docs/release-process.md (under §Topological deploy DAG or a short new §Post-publish consumer gate): the job is post-publish and can un-publish nothing. Red from propagation lag → re-run the failed job only (`gh run rerun <run-id> --failed`); NEVER re-push the tag (deploy-core 409s on the duplicate upload; docs/release-process.md §Recovery). Red from an unresolvable pom or missing packed content → bump-and-supersede per §Recovery (0.0.1.alpha → 0.0.1.alpha-1).

## Acceptance

- release.yml carries the one new job with `needs: [github-release]`; `git diff` shows no change to any deploy job's `needs`, matrix or steps, and no new trigger.
- The DAG policy test passes with the new negative-control case; publisher count 14.
- The script, run locally by the worker from a fresh :mvn/local-repo against the published 0.0.1.alpha, exits 0; its -Stree output is pasted in the PR body and shows the three coordinates at 0.0.1.alpha and no day8/* coordinate.
- The same script against a deliberately absent version (e.g. 9.9.9) exits non-zero after its bounded retry — the gate has teeth.
- No hand-rostered coordinate list beyond the hicasso entry point; if the 14-loop is included it derives from the lockstep inventory or the workflow.
- docs/release-process.md paragraph landed; scripts/check_doc_slugs.py green; verify-version-lockstep.sh --self-test green; fast-PR spine green; actionlint if the repo runs it. Gates foreground, to completion, never backgrounded or piped through a filter.
- First real CI exercise is the NEXT v* tag (0.0.1.alpha-1 or 0.0.2.alpha); say so in the PR body rather than claiming the YAML ran.

## Traps

Warm ~/.m2 or a cache action = a green that asked Clojars nothing; Clojars propagation lag after publish is minutes — retry, do not conclude; no yank exists; same-tag re-run 409s; no :local/root, no :git/url, no `clein install` anywhere in the proof (clein install is a pre-tag pom REHEARSAL, never the proof); do not touch the deploy DAG; hot-zone sequencing; the worker is on Windows-capable Git Bash locally but the script targets ubuntu-latest — keep it POSIX sh.

## Provenance

Ruled on rf2-kmqx3 (RULING 2026-09-02, delegated by Mike). The one-off proof that precedes this bead is defined there and on docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md's compatibility matrix; the release DAG facts are release.yml 162-165, 176-902 and docs/release-process.md 15-19, 128-160, 198-225 at tip b26c5ad33e.

title: xray(spec 018): Copy path and Ctrl+click copy cascade-id are described but unbuilt — annotate as not built or retire
description:

## Finding

tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md describes three copy gestures on the Epoch panel that nothing in tools/xray/src implements:

- :478 — the row-interaction table: "Ctrl+click row | Copy cascade-id to clipboard".
- :921 — the diff mockup's breadcrumb line carries a [Copy path] control.

Copy cascade-id is value-free (an id), so it would not be a value-egress site, but it is still an unbuilt interaction the spec presents as current.

(c) Build Copy path in the Epoch breadcrumb — this is a B.9 reopen and belongs with the deferred focused-copy design bead filed alongside this one from rf2-6r9j.24, not here.

title: Xray: focused-value copy designed from the data owner outward (reopens B.9; deferred until demand and Mike's go)
description:
DEFERRED DESIGN BEAD, filed 2026-09-04 by the delegated ruling agent for rf2-6r9j.24 (Mike's delegation of 2026-09-04). NOT dispatchable as filed: it exists so the design analysis two reviewers produced is not lost when the dossier is deleted. It becomes live only if Mike says there is demand for per-value copy in Xray AND agrees to reopen the B.9 lock; either signal alone is not enough.

## What was decided upstream

rf2-6r9j.24 RETRACTED the dead universal value-copy affordance (the edn-widget copy-affordance glyph, its CSS, the :copy? no-op, and the dispatcher-less :rf.xray/copy-value-to-clipboard and :rf.xray/copy-path-to-clipboard events) and honoured tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md sections 10.1 and 10.5 (LOCKED per B.9: no copy-path, no copy-value on the canonical renderer; re-proposals must reopen the lock with the mayor first). The published skill (skills/re-frame2-xray/references/shared-components.md:22-26) carries the same contract. This bead is the ONLY sanctioned route back.

## Why a universal root glyph was wrong, so the next design does not repeat it

The retracted event received only [_ value] with no absolute path, origin, partition or record kind. Xray's egress.cljs:53-58 and spec/API.md (Off-box egress section) say a slice egress'd in isolation must pass its absolute app-db :path or the path-keyed :sensitive / :large declarations cannot match. The canonical inspector is handed: app-db slices at a path (panels/app_db_segment_inspector.cljs), raw managed-fx request/response/handler values (panels/managed_fx_template.cljs) which spec/Security.md section Epoch privacy posture says are NOT app-db-rooted and MUST be default-redacted off-box, raw trace before/after (panels/trace.cljs), registry values (static flows/routes/schemas), and runtime-db machine snapshots. Those do not share one projection rule; a shared renderer cannot infer provenance from a naked value. The old tests proved only app-db-root-shaped fixtures through direct dispatch.

## What is lost without it (the case FOR building this, kept honest)

Browser text selection copies the render projection: collapsed nodes give their {N keys} / [N items] preview, diff annotations come along, and the app-db path is lost. Snapshot app-db is the whole focused-frame db, much coarser. There is no route for "paste this event's :fx vector / this exception's ex-data / this sub's value into a bug report or REPL". Demand evidence is nil either way: the glyph was user-reachable four days (2026-05-21 to 05-25) and nobody asked for it in the ~100 days after.

## Design sketch (from the Codex review, corrected at tip)

- Design from the DATA OWNER outward. Each enabled call site supplies a typed copy projection rather than a value: an app-db slice with its absolute :path; a projected trace/epoch record (record-aware, fx :args redacted by default, per Security.md); a runtime-db projection under its own axis; registry/static values that are value-free by contract and may ride the fx directly (the Copy Mermaid pattern at static/machines/panel.cljs).
- Opt-in per call site where such a projection exists; never default-on from the renderer root. App-DB stays OUT unless Mike changes it (his rf2-ilubp ruling, 95d92180bb).
- Precedent: re-frame-10x (upstream a3c309430d, src/day8/re_frame_10x/popup.cljs) exposes copy CONTEXTUALLY as Copy Path and Copy Subtree in the inspector popup, derived from the selected data path. The natural home here is therefore the edn-inspector popup (views/edn_inspector_popup.cljs), which at tip has only a close button — an action strip would be new chrome, not existing chrome. Do not stack a second absolute-positioned button at right: 2px beside the popup affordance.
- Egress: every value-bearing projection goes through day8.re-frame2-xray.egress/egress-value naming :frame (the fail-closed gesture; nil / destroyed / colliding-id frames egress :rf/redacted — pinned by the re-pointed rf2-7htk7 proofs in test/.../panels/app_db_diff_cljs_test.cljs) and passing :path for slices. The clipboard fx :rf.xray.fx/copy-to-clipboard already offers :on-success / :on-failure; use them for honest Copied / Copy failed feedback.
- Acceptance for that future bead: a REAL rendered click through frame routing (N parallel shells isolated; captured dispatch-fn pattern of popup-affordance-button in views/edn_inspector.cljs), each privacy axis, stale/nil frame, clipboard rejection (NotAllowedError), keyboard focus, and browser user-activation — the current suites stub the fx or run on node, and nobody has established that queuing rf/dispatch from the click before writeText keeps activation in supported browsers.
- Spec: reopen B.9 explicitly in 021 section 10.5 (and 10.1) with the narrow form chosen; update the skill's shared-components.md in the same PR; correct spec/API.md's Off-box egress inventory and README.md to enumerate the new sink; any PR touching tools/xray/ updates tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR or states why the spec is unchanged.

## Not this bead

The 007-UX-IA long-keyword click-to-copy glyph on elided keywords is a separate design. The 018-Event-Spine Copy path / Ctrl+click copy cascade-id items are tracked separately (see the sibling bead filed from rf2-6r9j.24).

title: skills: reconcile install prose and packaging metadata with the distribution channels that actually exist (marketplace sentence with no manifest, 3 private vs 6 public, npx skills add)
description:
FILED 2026-09-04 from the rf2-nvbz ruling (measured read-only at tip 1ad17a77fe). The nine skills promise three different things about how they are distributed, and the rf2-nvbz link rewrite deliberately does NOT touch this prose; it is a product call first and a mechanical alignment second.

WHAT THE TREE SAYS TODAY.
- Every skill under skills/ carries package.json plus .claude-plugin/plugin.json. Three package.json are private:true (re-frame2, re-frame2-pair, re-frame2-setup); six carry publishConfig access public and are publishable the day someone runs npm publish (re-frame-migration, re-frame2-implementor, re-frame2-improver, re-frame2-pair-retro, re-frame2-xray, reagent-migration). All nine carry claude-code-plugin or claude-code-skill keywords.
- No npm publish job, no NPM_TOKEN, no registry.npmjs reference and no marketplace manifest is tracked anywhere (git grep over .github/, scripts/, skills/; git ls-files | grep -i marketplace is empty).
- skills/README.md:213-214 (Layout convention) says each skill "is also distributable as an Agent Skill via npx skills add" - a LIVE channel: the public repo needs no publish step for it, and the skills CLI installs the selected skill directory alone (Codex review, from the vercel-labs/skills installer source: it records the directory containing SKILL.md and copies that directory to the canonical install).
- Seven per-skill READMEs say a full-clone link is the only supported install today and call npm/plugin distribution eventual (re-frame-migration/README.md:93, re-frame2-improver/README.md:31, re-frame2-setup/README.md:169, re-frame2/README.md:44, re-frame2-xray/README.md:50, reagent-migration/README.md:86, re-frame2-pair-retro/README.md:54).
- Two of those same READMEs name "a Claude Code marketplace plugin" as a SUPPORTED channel (skills/re-frame2/README.md:44, skills/re-frame2-setup/README.md:169) with no manifest behind it.
- re-frame-migration/README.md:93 and re-frame2-improver/README.md:31 claim the package is "self-contained"; after rf2-nvbz that is true for links, and for operational reads only via the pinned local checkout each skill names (re-frame-migration/references/setup.md section "Pin the migration corpus"; re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md cardinal rule 1).

THE CODEX REVIEW'S FRAMING, kept verbatim in substance: the repo currently promises both "clone-only for now" and "standalone distribution unit"; what should not remain is the third state where metadata says portable, prose says clone-only, and the gate certifies only the part of the package boundary that links happen not to cross. Pre-alpha is the cheap time to pick one coherent promise.

NEEDS MIKE (one ruling): which channels are real - (a) clone plus link only, (b) npx skills add from the public repo, (c) npm registry, (d) Claude Code marketplace plugin. Any subset.

THEN MECHANICAL, one worker: align the nine READMEs' install sentences and the package.json private / publishConfig fields to the answer; drop the marketplace sentence or add the manifest; keep or retire the plugin keywords accordingly. Before ANY registry or marketplace release: inspect all nine payloads with npm pack --dry-run --json --ignore-scripts (Codex ran it on re-frame-migration: 28 entries - SKILL.md, README, metadata, licence, references/ - and no migration corpus) and run a small extracted-package smoke for each skill's required local reads. Once a release tag exists, decide whether the blob/main citation URLs rf2-nvbz introduces move to the tag: one constant in the transform and in check_doc_slugs.py's unwrap.

GATES BY PATH: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py --verbose owns skills/** (skills is a DEFAULT_ROOTS entry); scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci is NOT the gate for skill READMEs. python scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py --self-test then the live scan if files[] changes. Neither link gate looks inside a fenced block.

Not blocking rf2-nvbz; discovered from it.

title: hygiene: two worker branches carry unmerged work with no PR and closed beads — receipts-hic081 and retire-delete need a disposition
description:
FOUND BY the hygiene loop, 2026-08-20 23:55 AUSEST, sweeping worktrees and branches. Both branches survived a cleanup that deleted 12 others, because git cherry reports them as carrying patches NOT upstream. That protection is working as designed; what is missing is a recorded reason for keeping them, so every future sweep re-derives it.

MEASURED at origin/main (git cherry origin/main <branch>, plus a direct read of the trunk):

1. worker/receipts-hic081 — THREE commits, 3 files, last commit 2026-08-11. A capability-receipts spike: implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/receipt.cljs (which does NOT exist on main), a change to impl/collector.cljs, and test/re_frame/hicasso/receipt_spike_cljs_test.cljs. Its bead rf2-hic-081 is CLOSED. So a spike was built, the bead closed, and the spike never landed. This is the exact branch .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md names as the measured case that patch-equivalence protects — 'ignoring it would have destroyed the 3 genuinely unmerged spike commits on worker/receipts-hic081' — so it is known and deliberately preserved, but nothing records whether the spike is wanted.

2. worker/retire-delete — ONE commit, 273 files, last commit 2026-08-15, subject 'refactor(ui): PARTIAL R2b — delete implementation/ui and its in-fence consumers (rf2-0yp7w.4)'. Its bead rf2-0yp7w.4 is CLOSED. PARTLY SUPERSEDED: implementation/ui is already gone from main (0 tracked files, executed by PR #8322 on 2026-08-16), so that half is done. BUT examples/real-apps/realworld_resources still holds 14 tracked files on main and this branch deletes them. So the branch carries a deletion main did not take, and it is not obvious whether those 14 files were deliberately KEPT or simply missed when #8322 landed the retirement by another route.

THE QUESTION FOR EACH: keep the branch, land the work, or delete the branch on a recorded decision. Do NOT delete either without one — a branch is the only copy of unmerged work, and both beads are closed so the tracker no longer points at them.

CHEAPEST NEXT STEP for retire-delete, and it is a read not a change: establish whether examples/real-apps/realworld_resources' 14 surviving files still reference the removed re-frame.ui tree. If they do, they are residue and rf2-0yp7w.9's prose sweep or a sibling owns them. If they do not, they were correctly kept and this branch is fully superseded and safe to delete.

NOT URGENT. Both branches are inert and cost nothing but a line in a listing. Filed P4 so the next hygiene sweep reads a decision instead of re-deriving the measurement.
notes:
