title: bug(hicasso-ssr): server/render leaves its Node request frame on the client effect platform
description:
## Correctness finding

`re-frame.hicasso.server/render` is the whole-page Node renderer, but the private request frame it creates is not tagged `:platform :server`. In a ClojureScript process the host-wide default is `:client`, so the frame runs the wrong platform contract unless an application supplies an undocumented workaround.

The mismatch is visible inside one file:

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs:345-363` destructures `:frame-opts` and calls `rf/make-frame` with the private `:id` and setup `:initial-events`, but no `:platform`.
- The sibling `render-body` at `server.cljs:478-495` explicitly associates `:platform :server`, with the contract at lines 466-467: the tag gates client-only effects out of a render with no client.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.cljs:195-214` initializes CLJS's host marker to `:client`. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:208-222` resolves platform as frame `:config :platform` first, then that host marker.
- Installing the documented `re-frame.ssr/adapter` does not change the marker: `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/substrate.cljc:68-89` is only the adapter map, and `rf/init!` installs it without inferring a platform. `rf/init-platform :server` is a separate operation.

This contradicts the public recipe and promise. `docs/core/hicasso/18-ssr-and-hydration.md:48-78` tells a Node host to call only `(rf/init! ssr/adapter)` before `server/render`; lines 111-118 say that render does not run client effects and specifically tells authors to put browser work behind `:platforms #{:client}`. The MIG-23 consumer recipe and executable cold-start fixture use the same boot shape (`skills/reagent-migration/references/ssr-hydrate.md:33-67`, `skills/reagent-migration/tests/fixture/test/reagent_migration/mig23_cold_start_test.cljs:81-95`). No in-repo `server/render` caller supplies `:frame-opts {:platform :server}` or pairs the call with `rf/init-platform :server`.

## Verified behavior

A read-only core probe was run from outside the checkout, using this worktree's `implementation/core` as a local dependency. It installed the plain-atom adapter, set the host marker to `:client` (the CLJS default), registered one `#{:client}` effect and one `#{:server}` effect, then created two otherwise identical frames whose initial event returned both effects:

- untagged frame: `rf/frame-meta` contained no `:platform`; observed effects were exactly `[:client]`;
- `:platform :server` frame: metadata contained the tag; observed effects were exactly `[:server]`.

That is the exact branch `server/render` and `render-body` respectively select. Source inspection additionally confirms the former is untagged and the latter tagged. The worktree stayed clean.

Consequences are not cosmetic. A correctly declared browser-only effect or coeffect reached from `:initial-events` can execute in Node (DOM/storage access, host calls, or duplicate external work), while a server-only one is skipped. The request can fail, mutate an unintended host resource, or render/build a payload from the wrong settled state without a platform error. Passing `:frame-opts {:platform :server}` masks the defect, but neither public recipe teaches that and a renderer's server identity should not depend on every caller remembering it.

## Recommended bounded change

Make `server/render` own `:platform :server` in the same final `assoc` that already owns `:id` and `:initial-events`, mirroring `render-body`. This also means a contradictory `:frame-opts {:platform :client}` cannot hijack the server request frame. Amend the local docstring/public recipe only as needed to state that `:platform` is renderer-owned.

Add a focused row to `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/server_render_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs` beside `frame-opts-ride-under-the-modules-id...`:

1. deliberately leave/set the host-wide marker to `:client`;
2. register one server-only and one client-only spy effect, dispatch both from a `server/render` initial event, and prove exactly the server effect runs;
3. pass `:frame-opts {:platform :client}` in the adversarial arm and prove it cannot reverse the result;
4. keep a non-vacuity/control assertion showing the same untagged frame shape selects the client effect (or perform the standard source mutation control by temporarily removing the new `:platform` assoc).

The existing `render-body` platform behavior remains unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Do not mutate the host-global platform inside each render; request-local frame configuration is already the right seam.
- Do not make `rf/init!` infer platform from adapter kind, change core platform fallback rules, or redesign the SSR adapter.
- Do not add an option, diagnostic, platform abstraction, or broader effect policy.
- Do not change host-component `:server` policies, hydration, payload projection, recovered-error handling, or the body-only renderer.

## Posture rationale

This is one owned map entry plus a focused regression test. It removes a silent cross-platform semantic inversion on a public SSR door and makes the older renderer match its already-correct sibling. It is high correctness and ergonomics leverage without adding machinery or asking trusted programmers to repeat hidden boot knowledge.

## Duplicate and history search

All-status bead title/description/notes/design/acceptance/close-reason searches covered: `hicasso platform`, `render platform`, `server render client`, `server/render effect`, `server/render fx`, `server-only effect`, `client-only effect`, `whole-page renderer`, `untagged frame`, `active-platform`, `init-platform`, `skipped-on-platform`, and `frame-opts`. No bead owns this runtime defect.

Related but distinct:
- closed `rf2-ypom` / `rf2-ct24`: recovered render errors, not platform routing;
- closed `rf2-8arzr.5`: added the correctly tagged `render-body` and explicitly fenced the existing `render` from change;
- closed `rf2-umi1w` / `rf2-33lfn`: fixed test fixtures whose missing client tag was masked by CLJS's client fallback; they provide direct precedent for why an untagged frame is not equivalent to a tagged one;
- closed `rf2-vpdrf` / `rf2-byig6`: adapter installation preconditions, not active-platform selection.

History confirms commit `30317bfe0e` introduced `server/render` untagged on 2026-08-14; `bbc97a5678` introduced `render-body` with `:platform :server` on 2026-09-02. No later commit adds the tag to `render`, and the current `origin/main` has no diff on the source/test paths.

## Uncertainty

A fresh Hicasso Node compile was not run because this worker checkout intentionally has no `node_modules` and the review brief forbids creating the shared junction or mutating files. The core probe exercised the exact platform resolver and effect dispatcher without repository writes; the remaining link is direct source inspection of the two `rf/make-frame` option maps. No in-repo caller demonstrates an intentional need to force `:client` through `server/render`; if such an external caller exists, it conflicts with the renderer's documented server-only semantics and should migrate rather than preserve the inversion.
design: Prefer the existing per-frame override seam: add `:platform :server` to `server/render`'s final `assoc`, beside its private id and setup vector. This is request-local, deterministic, and already proven by `render-body`; avoid a process-global `rf/init-platform` mutation or adapter-kind inference.
acceptance_criteria:
- `re-frame.hicasso.server/render` creates every private request frame with an explicit renderer-owned `:platform :server`, including when `:frame-opts` contains a contradictory `:platform :client`.
- In a CLJS test whose host marker is `:client`, a render initial event returning paired `#{:client}` and `#{:server}` spy effects executes only the server effect; the test is shown to fail when the request-frame tag is removed.
- Existing snapshot/initial-event ordering, frame-id ownership, payload/document output, cleanup-on-throw, recovered-error verdicts, and `render-body` behavior remain green.
- The Hicasso Node test lane and focused server-render suite pass, and any touched public prose consistently states that the renderer owns the server platform.

title: schemas: an app-db candidate rejection (:rollback? true) also reports on the :errors stream under the dev gate (Option A, PR1: :where :app-db)
description:
RULED 2026-09-04 21:03:56 AUSEST (delegated ruling; see the RULING note for the full analysis, the reviewer positions, the contract wording, the implementation guidance, traps and acceptance criteria). This bead is PR1 of Option A: in a DEV build, an app-db candidate rejection (:rf.error/schema-validation-failure, :where :app-db, :rollback? true) ALSO fans one STRUCTURAL-ONLY record per failing registered path onto the always-on :errors stream, from inside validate-app-schema!'s existing debug-enabled? gate, through the :error-emit/dispatch-error-record late-bind hook (the union-record helper the :rf.schema/at-boundary arm uses). The dev trace stays byte-identical; production is untouched by construction; the rf2-fu75 dev console fallback then prints the rejection for free when nothing owns the stream. This is an additive SPEC AMENDMENT (spec/009 promotion criterion + row 1984, spec/010 row 4) plus code in implementation/schemas, a docstring in error_emit.cljc, three docs pages and tests. spec/009 and spec/010 are one-toucher hot-zone files - sequence at dispatch. PR2 (machine-data + malformed-schema rollback sites) is the follow-up bead created from this one and waits for this PR to MERGE.

WHAT WAS MEASURED (2026-09-04 on worker/dispatchlater-a, with a control that fired). :rf.error/schema-validation-failure (:where :app-db) is emitted through re-frame.trace/emit-error! only - implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc, emit-validation-failure! and its emit-malformed-schema! sibling - and NOT through the both-axes emitter the router uses for other errors (re-frame.error-emit/emit-error-both!). So it reaches the DEV-ONLY :trace stream and never the always-on :errors stream. On one live page, one frame, one dispatch: a listener on :errors recorded 0 records while a listener on :trace recorded 17 :rf.error/schema-validation-failure records with :rollback? true for the SAME dispatch, whose :events-stream outcome was :rolled-back. CONTROL, same frame, same listener: dispatching an unregistered event id DID reach :errors as {:error :rf.error/no-such-handler ...}, so the listener was live and the zero is real. Codex independently reproduced the split in a fresh JVM: {:db {:n 0}, :errors 0, :traces 1, :outcome :rolled-back}.

WHY IT MATTERS. This is what made rf2-2xzc cost a pilot a third of its run. An application-wide, permanent app-db rollback loop produced 0 page errors, 0 console messages of any level, 0 failed requests, and nothing on the stream an application registers to hear about its own errors. The only surface that said anything was the dev trace, which has no default listener - so unless the developer already had Xray open and knew to look, the app simply rendered empty. The class is every reg-app-schema in every app, not the boot window.

THE ARGUMENT FOR THE OLD BEHAVIOUR, weighed and overruled: the candidate validator is dev-only by design (spec/010 Production builds), so there is no production error to report, and :errors is documented as the always-on stream; error_emit.cljc 421-424 recorded trace-only as correct, not a gap. The ruling: the promotion criterion governs what MUST ride the always-on axis in every build; it does not forbid a check that is compiled out of production from reporting, in the build where it runs, that it discarded a whole transaction. Always-on describes the stream's survival, not a promise that every producer exists in every build.
notes:
DOSSIER 2026-09-04 15:45:28 AUSEST (mayor, at Mike's request): decision dossier written at ai/decisions/rf2-xpd8.schema-rollback-errors-stream.md (local-only, lives until the ruling lands). RECOMMENDATION: Option A - fan the rejection onto the :errors axis too, under the validator's existing debug gate, as a structural-only record (one per failing registered path) through the :error-emit/dispatch-error-record union helper the :rf.schema/at-boundary arm already uses; production untouched by construction (the validator does not run there). Scope to every :rollback? true producer (:app-db first, then :machine-data + :rf.error/malformed-schema in a second PR). One-line reason: rf2-fu75 (2026-08-13) already ruled that an untooled dev build must surface a framework refusal, and a transaction rejection is the one refusal that ruling's mechanism cannot reach because it never enters the axis the console fallback and the listener hang off. FACTS THE BEAD DOES NOT SAY THAT CHANGE THE WEIGHING: (1) the current behaviour is a RECORDED decision, not an oversight: error_emit.cljc:421-424 says dev schema checks staying trace-only "is correct, not a gap", and spec/009's promotion criterion leg 1 names dev-only schema validation as staying diagnostic - so Option A is a SPEC AMENDMENT (additive: a MAY route under the check's own gate), not a bug fix. (2) The rf2-fu75 dev console fallback already exists and fires for free under A (reached from both dispatch-on-error! and dispatch-error-record*), which makes Option C (a second printer in the validator) strictly dominated. (3) reason-string interpolates type-of-value, never the value ("..., got nil."), so the app-db arm's :reason can ride the always-on record - unlike the boundary arm, whose :reason was omitted for interpolating attacker-controlled payload. (4) The always-on :events stream DOES carry the rollback today as :outcome :rolled-back; it is absent only from the stream built for errors. The 0-vs-17 measurement was not re-run (no builds); it is consistent with the code.
RULING 2026-09-04 21:03:56 AUSEST (delegated by Mike 2026-09-04, operator-reversible; dossier ai/decisions/rf2-xpd8.schema-rollback-errors-stream.md and its Codex Recommendation section folded here and deleted). Verified read-only at tip 1ad17a77fe (== origin/main, clean). rf2-fu75 does not resolve as a bead id on this build (bd show fails, no memory) - the ruling it names survives verbatim in error_emit.cljc lines 90-160 (RULED rf2-fu75, 2026-08-13, commit fcf866ea1d), in error_emit_dev_console_dom_cljs_test.cljs, and in spec/009 line 1283; nothing here depends on the bead itself.

THE RULING. Option A, with the Codex record-shape correction, in two PRs. A dev-gated candidate-transition rejection (:rollback? true) ALSO fans one STRUCTURAL-ONLY record per failing registration onto the always-on :errors stream, from inside the validator's existing debug-enabled? gate, through the :error-emit/dispatch-error-record late-bind hook (the union-record helper the :rf.schema/at-boundary arm already uses). The dev trace is byte-identical to today. No new printer, no knob, no new category, no aggregation, no dedup. Production is untouched by construction: the record is emitted from inside the same outermost gate as the check, so a release build carries neither. The rf2-fu75 console fallback then fires for free (reached from dispatch-error-record*) when nothing owns the stream, which is what turns a permanent silent rollback loop into red console lines naming the registered path, the event and got nil. This is a SPEC AMENDMENT (the trace-only behaviour was recorded as correct, not a gap, in error_emit.cljc 421-424 and in spec/009 promotion-criterion leg 1), not a bug fix; the amendment is additive and its exact wording is under IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE. Scope: PR1 (this bead) = the :where :app-db arm. PR2 (follow-up bead, filed below) = :where :machine-data at its :rollback? true phases plus the two :rf.error/malformed-schema :rollback? true sites. One semantic ruling, two PRs, PR2 waits for PR1 to MERGE (spec/009 hot-zone). Granularity: one record per failing registered entry (the trace's shape); the single-bounded-report idiom is NOT pre-built - its trigger is a measured unusable console, and the note records that trigger rather than a bead.

OPTIONS REJECTED. B (docs only): a doc helps only a reader who already suspects the mechanism; the incident's whole cost was that three investigators did not. Fixes nothing. C1 (console.error from the validator): a second printer with a second gate beside the one rf2-fu75 built; prints even when an app owns :errors (the nag rf2-fu75 avoided); gives the listener and the frame sink nothing. Dominated by A, which gets the console line from the existing fallback. C2 (a default :trace listener that logs :rf.error/*): the framework deliberately ships no default trace listener (spec/009 section User-side listener registration, line ~1124); would duplicate Xray on every row and need an off-switch. C3 (reg-app-schema registers a default :errors listener): registering ANY listener silences the fallback for every other category. Strictly harmful. D (do nothing): the class is every reg-app-schema in every app, not the boot window; PR #9134 and rf2-aaam reduced the odds of THIS mistake only. Also rejected: flipping :rf.error/malformed-schema's Channel column to always-on in PR2 (the dossier proposed it) - the column states what SURVIVES ELISION and nothing on that category does; the dev-gated route is named in row prose instead, so always-on-categories and the channel conformance test stay untouched in both PRs.

REVIEWER POSITIONS. Dossier (mayor, 15:32 AUSEST): recommends A, per-path, structural-only, two PRs (app-db first; machine-data + malformed-schema second), one additive criterion paragraph; proposed carrying :path and the existing :reason on the record because reason-string interpolates type-of-value rather than the value. Codex Recommendation: CONCURS on A, per-path, two PRs, no second printer, no knob, no aggregation; DISSENTS on the record shape, and the tree says Codex is right: (1) :path is NOT intrinsically structural - validate.cljc lines 58-62 and 822-847 document that a :set failure's segment is the failing ELEMENT VALUE and a :map-of key rides as the key; sanitize-sensitive-path scrubs only when the leaf is :sensitive?, so a non-sensitive set element or map-of key ships verbatim in :path today; (2) reason-string (lines 297-303) interpolates (pr-str schema) - unbounded - and the same path, so it is neither bounded nor purely an identifier even though the failing value itself is absent. So the record is BUILT FROM a closed allow-list of structural inputs, never filtered down from tags (the spec's own rule for the boundary arm, spec/010 ~line 235 and spec/009 row 1984 prose). Codex's independent evidence: reproduced the split in a fresh JVM at df66b1679496 - frame with [:n] [:int], valid seed, one event writing {:n "bad"} -> {:db {:n 0}, :errors 0, :traces 1, :outcome :rolled-back}; the always-on :events ledger carries the consequence but never the cause and never activates the console fallback. Codex's other contributions, all verified: emit the small record BEFORE the trace, matching emit-error-both!'s axis-1-then-axis-2 ordering (error_emit.cljc ~690-705), so the SSR last-write-wins buffer's final input is the richer trace; JVM SSR dual delivery is benign and documented (ssr/error_listener.cljc 333-360) but must be pinned; a non-:event schema failure must stay the projector's generic 500, never the boundary arm's 400 (error_projector.cljc 133-137 gates the 400 on :where :event, so this holds without code); cover only :rollback? true - do NOT promote recover-and-continue arms (:fx-args, :sub-return, :sub-override, :flow-output, :machine-output, machine :spawn / :update-snapshot with :rollback? false); Xray (panels/epoch/projection.cljc 2022-2186, view.cljs 5320-5383) and Story derive rollback from the trace and keep receiving it unchanged; the only material uncertainty is console volume, unmeasured. Dossier contributions preserved: the :events stream DOES carry the rollback today as :outcome :rolled-back (so the fact is absent only from the stream built for errors); the router's (false? commit-result) branch at router.cljc 2686-2689 is the single point a bounded report would hang off, but it holds only a boolean, so a single report would need the validator hook to return the paths - more surface, deferred; the Sentry bridge in docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md 62-65 is gated on production AND (not debug-enabled?), so a dev :errors listener is deliberate and rare, and one that wants to drop rollbacks keys on :rollback? true; the rf2-fu75 fallback's three conditions (debug-enabled?, browser host via js/document, EMPTY registry) all hold on a fresh dev app; the four things the dossier could be wrong about: criterion amendable additively (ruled yes - see wording), N-per-dispatch acceptable (ruled yes, bounded), dev listeners rare (yes, documented-filter problem), elision holds (the probe is the witness). CONDENSED what-the-developer-sees table (dev build, browser host, no :errors listener): Today - page renders pre-event/empty state; console nothing at any level; :errors 0 (control: no-such-handler arrives); frame :observability :errors sink nothing; :events {:outcome :rolled-back}; :trace one schema-validation-failure per failing path; Xray open shows the :db row red + Schema Violation card + rollback mute, Xray closed nothing; window.onerror nothing (no throw); network no request; release build installs everything and reports :ok. Under A - page unchanged; console one [re-frame2] :rf.error/schema-validation-failure - <reason> line + the record per failing path via the existing fallback; :errors one structural record per failing path; sink receives the projected record (dev only); :events, :trace, Xray, onerror, network, release all unchanged (a console line may coexist with an Xray row, accepted under rf2-fu75). With an :errors listener registered: the listener receives the records and the console stays quiet (the rf2-fu75 ownership rule). Under B and D every cell is today's; under C1 only the console cell changes, printed regardless of listeners.

WHAT THIS BEAD NOW IS. A dispatchable worker task (status open, type task - the behaviour it changes was a recorded decision, now amended; priority stays P2). Title amended to name PR1. One worker, one worktree, one PR. spec/009-Instrumentation.md and spec/010-Schemas.md are one-toucher hot-zone files: at ruling time PR #9182 (worker/specdoc-a, rf2-6g6e) was OPEN against spec/009 - sequence this dispatch behind its merge and re-check gh pr list for both files at dispatch.
IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (PR1, :where :app-db).
Emitter. implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc. Add a private helper (e.g. emit-app-db-rejection-record!) beside emit-validation-failure! (line 325) and call it at the app-db emit site (the (emit-validation-failure! tags) at ~line 884), immediately BEFORE the trace emit and under the SAME (continue?) guards (a stale incarnation emits nothing on either axis). Do NOT put a :where dispatch inside emit-validation-failure! - that seam serves all eight arms and a :where switch there is the shape that lets a future arm leak onto the axis by default. Reach the hook with (late-bind/get-fn-cached :error-emit/dispatch-error-record) - validate.cljc already requires re-frame.late-bind, re-frame.error and re-frame.interop, so no new require; nil hook (core's error-emit ns not loaded) -> skip silently. Never static-require re-frame.error-emit from the schemas artefact. Precedent for the call shape: router.cljc emit-boundary-rejection-record! (lines 2747-2775) and the machines / SSR union records named in spec/009 row prose. The call sits inside validate-app-schema!'s outermost (if interop/debug-enabled? ...) (line ~651), so a release build reaches neither the call nor its literals; keep the @validator-fn deref outside the gate predicate as the existing comment requires.
Record shape - BUILT FROM structural inputs (registered-path, event-id, frame-id, and the type tag of the failing leaf), never (select-keys tags ...): {:error :rf.error/schema-validation-failure :where :app-db :registered-path <registration root> :event-id <event id> :failing-id <event id> :frame <frame-id> :rollback? true :recovery :no-recovery :reason <sentence> :time (interop/now-ms)}. Both :event-id and :failing-id are always PRESENT (nil only on a direct validate call outside a run - the elision probe and unit tests - which no runtime path produces), so the key set is closed and fixed. :reason is composed ONLY from the registered path and (error/type-of-value leaf-value) - a closed type vocabulary plus class names, never the value, never (pr-str schema), never the leaf path - e.g. "App-db candidate at registered path [:articles] failed its schema (got nil); the transaction was rejected and nothing installed." The got-<type> is what makes the incident self-diagnosing on the console line (seventeen lines all ending got nil), and it discloses nothing. Give the sentence a distinctive literal tail so the elision probe can prove it absent (reason-string's docstring states this convention). OMIT :path (may carry a set element value or a map-of key - see REVIEWER POSITIONS), :value, :explain, :explain-humanized, :schema, :received. The trace keeps all of those; Xray and Story keep working off it unchanged. If the leaf path proves needed on the record later, it needs a structural-path projection first (drop set-element and map-of-key segments); not in this PR.
Noise. N records per rejected commit where N = the number of FAILING registered entries for that frame - bounded above by the frame's registry size, and each record names a distinct violated registration (17 on the incident = 17 distinct absent slices). In a boot deadlock every :db-writing dispatch is rejected, so volume tracks the breakage exactly; that is the point. No dedup, no knob, no single-report shape now. Trigger for revisiting: a measured case where repeated rejected dispatches make the browser console unusable; the remedy then is one bounded record per rejected transaction with the paths as a payload vector (the spec/009 single-bounded-report idiom), which requires the validator hook to return the failing paths to the router's (false? commit-result) branch.
spec/009-Instrumentation.md (hot-zone, one toucher). (a) Section The promotion criterion (heading ~line 1688): after "Categories failing any leg stay on the diagnostic channel." add ONE paragraph, this wording or tighter: "Failing leg 1 keeps a category off the OBLIGATION, not off the stream. The criterion says what MUST ride the always-on axis in every build. A check that is itself compiled out of production - dev-only schema validation is the case in point - can still report on the :errors stream in the build where it runs, and for one class it does: a dev-gated refusal that discards a whole candidate transition (:rollback? true - Spec 010 rows 4 and 7, and the fail-closed :rf.error/malformed-schema rejection) is a leg-2(b) no-op whose silence compounds (leg 3), so from inside its own debug-enabled? gate it fans one structural-only record per failing registration onto the :errors stream beside its dev trace. spec/010-Schemas.md (hot-zone). Row 4 (~line 181): one sentence - "In the build where it fires, the rejection also fans one structural-only record per failing registration onto the always-on :errors stream, so it reaches error listeners, the frame's :observability :errors sink and, when nothing owns the stream, the dev console fallback (per 009 The promotion criterion)." Section Production builds (~line 206) stays true; optionally append "and no :errors record" to "there is no trace, no :rollback? true tag, and nothing for an operator to see".

title: reagent-slim: ordinary after-render callbacks can precede the React 19 DOM commit
description:
## Correctness finding

`reagent2.core/after-render` promises to run after the next React commit, but reagent-slim's ordinary production microtask path can invoke the callback while React 19 still exposes the old DOM. This is a live-path ordering bug, not a request for broader Reagent compatibility.

## Exact evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/batching.cljs`: `RenderQueue.flush-queues` calls `ratom/flush!`, then `flush-render`, then `flush-after-render`. `flush-render` only invokes each dirty class's bare `.forceUpdate`; there is no React commit boundary or commit callback. Therefore "forceUpdate was requested" is treated as "React committed" before callbacks run.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/client.cljs`: the `flush-render!` implementation and its load-bearing comment document the opposite React-19 fact: under `createRoot`, bare `forceUpdate` outside a React batching boundary is scheduled rather than committed, and the DOM remains OLD when `batching/flush!` returns. That is why `flush-render!` wraps the same drain in `react-dom/flushSync`. Commit `3d89c29c61` records the browser proof: the post-flush assertion read the old value without that boundary.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/core.cljs`: public `after-render` says "after the next React commit" and routes to `batching/do-after-render`. `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim.cljs` publishes that function as `:adapter/after-render`, so `re-frame.interop/after-render` reaches this exact queue.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md` §2.3/§2.9/§4 repeats the post-render contract, while `spec/002-Frames.md` names after-render effects as the canonical "show this, then run the heavy block" replacement for queue-pausing. `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/dispatch.cljs` also treats the adapter hook as post-commit/pre-paint for `:await-render`.
- Existing slim coverage does not exercise this boundary. `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/impl/batching_cljs_test.cljs` uses fake JS objects whose `forceUpdate` body runs synchronously, so its `[:render :after]` assertion proves call order only. `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/dom/client_cljs_test.cljs` similarly uses fake components and/or `act`; `reagent_slim_flush_render_dom_cljs_test.cljs` tests the explicit `flushSync` API. `reagent_slim_late_bind_publication_cljs_test.cljs` pins hook publication, not DOM timing. There is no reagent-slim counterpart to the real-DOM post-commit assertion used by the React spine.
- Independent substrate comparison: the repository-pinned Reagent 2.0.1 `reagent.impl.batching/run-queue` wraps dirty component updates in an injected `react-flush`, and `reagent.dom.client/render` installs `react-dom/flushSync`; only after that wrapper returns does stock `flush-after-render` run. Slim copied the queue order but omitted the commit-bearing seam on its ordinary path.

## Concrete failure sequence and impact

A ratom/app-db change queues a slim component, and application or framework code queues an after-render callback. The shared microtask drains dependencies, calls bare `forceUpdate` (React schedules the class update), and immediately invokes the callback. The callback can read stale DOM. Worse, the documented long-running-work pattern can start its heavy block before React paints the requested "working" state, delaying the very feedback the API exists to provide. The Pair `:await-render` path is consequently founded on accidental later-rAF timing rather than the adapter hook's promised post-commit invariant.

## Recommended bounded fix

Make the ordinary scheduled queue defer `flush-after-render` until the dirty updates in that turn have actually committed. Keep `reagent2.impl.batching` host-neutral; a small client-installed commit wrapper (analogous to stock Reagent's `react-flush`) used when a pending after-render queue requires the guarantee is one plausible minimal shape. A reliable class-update commit callback is another. Let the real-DOM regression choose the smallest correct seam.

Preserve the current callback FIFO order, once-only drain, per-callback throw isolation, no-dirty callback behavior, next-turn cascade rule, and explicit `flush-render!`/`flush-views!` semantics. Reconcile the local docstrings/IMPL-SPEC only where they currently equate a bare `forceUpdate` call with a completed render.

## Posture and non-goals

This repair makes a retained minimal API tell the truth and directly supports responsive SPA feedback. Do not add a general scheduler abstraction, copy the React-spine driver-root machinery, expand the public API, emulate transitions/Suspense policy, or litigate arbitrary unmounted/cross-root edge cases. Do not globally force every ratom microtask synchronous merely as an easy workaround if a narrower commit-bearing path for queued after-render work preserves the intended React-19 concurrency.

## Duplicate and history search

Searched every current bead in every state across title, description, acceptance, design, and notes for `after-render`, `after render`, `flush-after-render`, `post-commit`, `commit phase`, `forceUpdate`, `stale DOM`, `React commit`, `microtask`, and reagent-slim/render variants. The only `after-render` matches were closed `rf2-6r9j.33` (stale IMPL-SPEC architecture prose) and closed `rf2-6r9j.44` (an unrelated SSR response parameter); neither owns runtime commit timing. Broader matches were unrelated surfaces. Git history searches for `flush-after-render`, `after-render`, `forceUpdate`, and `flushSync` found: initial scheduler commit `1d621015bd`, callback-throw isolation `a834ab9bbd`, and explicit synchronous `flush-render!` repair `3d89c29c61`; none repairs or tests the ordinary microtask path. The UIx post-commit work (`e616aabbbd` and shared-suite tests) is a different substrate implementation.

## Uncertainty

No new browser bundle was built in this review-only worker because the assigned worktree intentionally has no `node_modules` link and no source/test edits were authorized. The stale-DOM timing is nevertheless independently established by the current control flow, the stock-Reagent implementation, and this repository's prior React-19 browser failure/fix in `3d89c29c61`. The exact narrowest repair seam remains intentionally open; the required real-DOM ordinary-path test below resolves it behaviorally.
design: Favor the smallest commit-aware seam that keeps the queue node-safe and preserves ordinary concurrent behavior when no post-commit callback is pending. A client-installed wrapper around the dirty-component phase is worth testing because stock Reagent already demonstrates that shape; if used, avoid unnecessary `flushSync` on queue turns without after-render work and avoid double-drain/nested-boundary surprises under the existing explicit `flush-render!`. Acceptance is behavioral rather than prescribing that mechanism.
acceptance_criteria:
- Add `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim_after_render_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (or an equivalently named reagent-slim browser test) that installs the slim adapter, mounts a ratom/subscription-backed view through `reagent2.dom.client/create-root` + `render`, commits the initial value, changes the value, and calls `re-frame.interop/after-render`.
- In the callback, read the mounted node's `textContent` and prove it contains the new value; also assert the callback fires exactly once. The test must assert the old DOM before the scheduler turn so a synchronous mutation cannot make it vacuous.
- The regression must exercise the ordinary queued microtask path. It must not use `reagent2.dom.client/flush-views!`, adapter `flush-render!`, `react/act`, a manual `react-dom/flushSync` around the update/drain, or an extra `requestAnimationFrame` before the callback assertion, because each masks the defect.
- On the pre-fix implementation the test fails specifically because the callback observes the old committed DOM while the class update is only scheduled. On the fix it observes the new DOM after the actual commit under the repository's React 19 floor.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/batching.cljs` preserves callback FIFO/once-only/throw isolation, callbacks scheduled with no dirty component still fire asynchronously, and components queued during a drain remain for the next turn.
- `reagent_slim_flush_render_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, the focused batching tests, the slim node tests, and browser tests remain green. Any changed contract prose in `reagent2.core`, `batching.cljs`, or `IMPL-SPEC.md` agrees that after-render means post-commit, not merely after calling `forceUpdate`.
- The implementation stays private and bounded: no new public symbol and no broad React-spine/scheduler redesign.
notes: Review scope was `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/**`; consumers/spec/history were read only to establish contract and impact. No tracked file was edited, no test artifact was created, and no bead was updated. Evidence is source/history-based with the remaining uncertainty explicitly captured in the description.

title: surface-review(uix-adapter): imperative effect retains the old frame dispatcher after provider swaps
description:
## Scope

Correct the canonical UIx imperative-lifecycle recipe so a listener installed by `uix/use-effect` follows the frame selected by `re-frame.adapter.uix/use-frame`. This is the public copy/paste path for DOM listeners and third-party widgets, not a request to expand the adapter API.

## Verified behavior

`implementation/adapters/uix/README.md:56-66` currently does this in `tile-inner`:

```clojure
(let [ref (uix/use-ref)
      {:keys [dispatch]} (uix-adapter/use-frame)]
  (uix/use-effect
    (fn []
      (let [listener (fn [_evt]
                       (dispatch [:tile/finished-merging tile-id]))]
        (.addEventListener (.-current ref) "animationend" listener)
        (fn [] (.removeEventListener (.-current ref) "animationend" listener))))
    [tile-id]))
```

The effect closes over TWO reactive render values, `tile-id` and `dispatch`, but its dependency vector names only `tile-id`. The same README immediately says at `:79` to include every value the effect reads.

This omission is routing-significant, not merely lint style:

1. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/adapter/use_frame.cljs:99-128` consumes the shared React context and memoizes the capture bundle only for one resolved frame incarnation. A provider change re-renders the component and returns a new ops map/new `dispatch`; the public contract says so at `implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:160-168` and `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:120-122`.
2. UIx 1.4.4's published source (`uix/core.clj`, `make-hook-with-deps`; `uix/hooks/alpha.cljs`, `use-clj-deps` + `use-effect`) sends the declared vector to React and only changes that dependency array when the CLJS vector is unequal. Function equality is identity, so adding `dispatch` does exactly what this API designed its reference stability to support: no rerun for the same frame, rerun for a changed frame bundle. UIx's official hook docs confirm the vector/dependency comparison: https://github.com/pitch-io/uix/blob/master/docs/hooks.md#dependency-array . Its exhaustive-deps linter also reports component-body free variables omitted from the vector (`uix/linter.clj`, `lint-exhaustive-deps!` / `::missing-deps`).
3. React runs effect cleanup/setup again only when a declared dependency changes and requires every reactive value used by setup to be listed: https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffect#parameters .

Therefore, with frame A and frame B both live, rerendering the same mounted `tile-inner` beneath a provider changed from A to B while `tile-id` is unchanged yields a fresh B-locked `dispatch` in the render, but DOES NOT replace the installed listener. `animationend` still invokes the closure installed under A and silently dispatches `:tile/finished-merging` into A. If A was destroyed instead, the stale capture fence drops the event and emits the destroyed-frame error. Either result contradicts the recipe's promise to carry “the surrounding frame” and the hook's provider-retarget contract.

## Existing coverage and the gap

- `implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_use_subscribe_dom_cljs_test.cljs:465-476` forwards the shared `use-frame` shape/stability/reincarnation assertions.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:3904-3978` proves the bundle is stable for the same frame and that an extracted op dispatches after render.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:3980-4079` proves a forced next render after same-id reincarnation returns a new bundle and the old bundle is inert.
- No adapter test composes `use-frame` with a long-lived `use-effect`/DOM listener while the provider target changes. The README snippet is not compiled by the existing docs-pin test (`uix_component_recipe_docs_pin_test.clj` pins the separate component-testing recipe), so UIx's exhaustive-deps warning and the stale listener both escape CI.

## Bounded recommendation

- Change the canonical effect deps to `[tile-id dispatch]` and make the adjacent sentence say that the deps include every reactive value captured by the effect, explicitly including frame-bound callbacks from `use-frame`.
- Add one focused UIx browser regression, near `uix_use_subscribe_dom_cljs_test.cljs` or in a small dedicated `*_dom_cljs_test.cljs`: create live frames A and B with distinguishable handlers/state; mount one listener-bearing `defui` under `frame-provider` A; rerender the same component/key under provider B without changing its domain prop; fire the DOM event; assert B alone changes. Also assert the old listener was cleaned up (one event => one dispatch) and unmount in `finally`.
- Compile the real recipe shape in that test so UIx's own exhaustive-deps analysis guards the dependency list. Keep the browser-lane test narrow; no general Markdown-snippet compiler is needed.

## Impact

This is a cross-frame correctness failure in the exact escape hatch recommended for maps, editors, charts, animation callbacks, browser APIs, and third-party stores. A tenant/tab/provider switch can mutate the previously selected live frame while the UI shows the new one—a silent isolation failure. The minimal dependency fix uses the stability guarantee `use-frame` already provides and imposes no effect churn within one frame.

## Posture rationale

Pre-alpha is the right time to make the one canonical SPA recipe exact. One dependency plus one behavioral pin is high leverage: it preserves a tiny API, trusts normal React/UIx dependency semantics, and prevents a class of wrong-frame writes without inventing an event wrapper, effect-event helper, provider generation counter, or adapter machinery.

## Non-goals

- No new public API or hook, and no change to `use-frame`, `capture-frame`, provider, or frame lifecycle semantics.
- No generalized hook linter/doc-snippet framework and no audit of every effect in the repository.
- No requirement to remount providers/components on frame changes; provider retargeting is already a supported contract.
- Do not fold the separate README claim about bare no-arg `capture-frame` context resolution into this fix; it is independent of the stale-effect dependency.

## Duplicate search

Searched all 922 beads (open/deferred/closed) by title/description/notes and repository history before filing. Description searches for `tile-inner`, `finished-merging`, `stale dispatch`, `dispatch dependency`, `use-effect`, `effect deps`, `provider swap`, `stale closure`, and `imperative escape` each returned zero. Broader `UIx`/`use-frame` results were reviewed; the closest are closed `rf2-9hcyf` (copy-complete UIx component *testing*, a different recipe), `rf2-yrq9n` (adapter wording/retired Helix), and `rf2-oz7wr` (registered-view head cache). Commit history shows the affected snippet arrived in `4d24ca4376`, switched to `use-frame` in `f013dd2807`, and has retained `[tile-id]`; `bbdcc8ba53` explicitly introduced the provider-swap/reference-stability guarantee that makes `dispatch` a cheap and necessary dependency. No tracked or already-fixed issue matches this behavior.

## Uncertainties

I did not execute the browser lane in this review worktree because it intentionally has no `node_modules` link and the review brief prohibited creating one. The failure is derived from the checked-in adapter implementation, the exact published UIx 1.4.4 sources already in the dependency cache, the official UIx/React hook contracts, and the uncompiled README code. The focused acceptance test should be the final executable proof and should use a live A -> live B provider swap; a destroy/recreate-only test would exercise the stale-frame fence but miss the more serious silent write into still-live A.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The UIx README's `tile-inner` effect declares both captured reactive values, `[tile-id dispatch]`, and adjacent guidance explicitly includes frame-bound callbacks returned by `use-frame`.
2. A real-browser UIx test mounts a listener-bearing component under live frame A, rerenders the same component/key under live frame B with its domain prop unchanged, fires the event, and proves B changes while A does not.
3. The test proves effect cleanup/reinstall is balanced (one event produces one dispatch), guarantees unmount/runtime cleanup, and exercises the actual `uix/use-effect` + `uix-adapter/use-frame` spelling.
4. The UIx browser test lane and relevant docs/link gates pass. No public API or runtime adapter machinery is added.
notes: Surface-review partition: implementation/adapters/uix/**. Reviewed adapter source, README/public API/spec contract, all adapter test entry points and the shared React suite they forward, standalone testbed and real UIx examples, published UIx 1.4.4 source, official React/UIx hook docs, existing beads, and relevant history. Worker guard passed immediately before creation with WORKTREE_ROOT=C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2-worktrees\codex-reviewpool-d, BRANCH=worker/codex-reviewpool-d.

title: core/configure!: non-map calls silently no-op when host builds elide assertions
description:
## Slice reviewed

implementation/core/**, with the actionable center at implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc, public symbol re-frame.core/configure!. Governing contract and focused coverage inspected at spec/API.md and implementation/core/test/re_frame/configure_test.clj. This is the one finding selected after source/API/spec/test/call-site/history review of the slice.

## User-visible and maintainer impact

configure! is a front-porch process-configuration API. Its public contract says it accepts one nested map and that a non-map argument fails loudly. Today that safety depends on the host compiler retaining language assertions. In a legitimate assertion-elided consumer build, a stale keyed-form call such as (rf/configure! :trace-buffer), a vector, or nil silently returns nil and applies nothing. The programmer can therefore believe trace, epoch, or elision configuration was installed when it was ignored. This is especially awkward in pre-alpha, where the retired keyed form is exactly the mistake migration can produce.

The correction is high leverage and low friction: one always-on public-boundary check, one canonical structured error, and focused dual-posture tests. It strengthens the minimal API without adding a validator framework or policing unknown map keys.

## Independently verified current behavior

At repository tip 1ad17a77fe:

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2594-2596 implements the entire top-level shape check as (assert (map? config-map) ...).
- With the namespace compiled normally on Clojure 1.12.0, direct calls with :trace-buffer, [:trace-buffer {:events-retained 3}], and nil each throw java.lang.AssertionError.
- In a fresh JVM process, loading re-frame.core inside (binding [*assert* false] (require 're-frame.core)) and then making those same three calls makes every call return nil. No subsystem runs and no diagnostic is emitted.
- The upstream Clojure 1.12.0 assert macro explicitly omits its check when *assert* is false.
- The locally resolved ClojureScript 1.12.145 compiler binds *assert* false when :elide-asserts is true, and the CLJS assert macro only emits code when *assert* is true. Therefore the same source check is absent from such CLJS output.
- The current focused test command, run from implementation/core, is green: clojure -M:test -n re-frame.configure-test ran 5 tests / 28 assertions with zero failures. This demonstrates the coverage gap, not safety under assertion elision.

## Concrete evidence and history

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2554-2605 — configure! docstring and implementation; lines 2578 and 2595-2596 promise/enforce the map shape via assert.
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/configure_test.clj:281-293 — configure-non-map-arg-fails-loud explicitly couples all three examples to AssertionError, but compiles only in the ordinary assertion-on posture.
- spec/API.md:872 and :896 — the API is front-porch and says a non-map argument fails loud / MUST be a map.
- git blame attributes the assert to 6730961c897 (2026-06-19), refactor(api): configure! single nested-map entry point (rf2-dzxixe). That commit deliberately retired the keyed form and described non-map input as fail-loud, so silent acceptance under elision contradicts the intended change rather than introducing a new policy.
- bd show rf2-dzxixe reports no matching issue in the current tracker.

## Recommended change

Replace the language assert with an explicit always-on when-not map? check routed through the existing re-frame.error/throw-error! helper already required by re-frame.core. Add one canonical category (suggested name :rf.error/configure-bad-arg), with :where rf/configure!, a short recovery hint to pass one nested map, and bounded/type-oriented received context rather than echoing arbitrary application configuration. Update the error catalogue/projection where project conventions require it.

Preserve the deliberately ergonomic map behavior exactly: valid composed maps still configure known subsystems in the present order; missing keys leave state untouched; unknown top-level keys remain silent no-ops. The reason to use the existing structured-error chokepoint is consistency and AI/tool discoverability, not a broader validation system.

## Bounded implementation scope and non-goals

In scope: the top-level argument guard, its canonical error entry/projection, the focused configure tests, and a genuine assertion-elided verification posture for both runtimes.

Non-goals: do not reject unknown top-level keys; do not validate every nested subsystem option here; do not restore the retired keyed arity; do not redesign configuration schemas/order/merge semantics; do not introduce a general argument-validation abstraction.

## Duplicate search

Tracker searches were run across all statuses before filing:

- bd search "configure" --status all --limit 200 --long: no matches.
- "elide asserts configure", "non-map configure", "configure assertion", "AssertionError", "assertions disabled", and "elide-asserts": no matches.
- broad "assert" search returned four closed issues, all unrelated (routing fixture syntax, Hicasso prose, API-manifest classification, and a prefetch roster assertion).
- description search for configure! returned five unrelated surface/doc facade issues; none concerns core configure argument validation.
- The historical rf2-dzxixe reference is not present in the current tracker.

## Uncertainties

The JVM failure and silent-no-op postures were executed directly. The CLJS conclusion was verified from the resolved compiler and macro sources, but this review did not build a standalone release bundle; the acceptance criteria intentionally require that executable CLJS probe. The exact new error-id spelling should follow the catalogue owner's naming convention; the stable requirement is an always-on canonical structured error, not the suggested token.
design: Keep the patch local to the existing public boundary. A representative shape is (when-not (map? config-map) (rf.error/throw-error! ...)); re-frame.core already requires re-frame.error. Do not move known-key dispatch or tighten the additive top-level vocabulary. Prefer a focused compile-time negative control over a test that merely rebinding *assert* after re-frame.core has already loaded.
acceptance_criteria:
- A non-map passed to re-frame.core/configure! throws one canonical ExceptionInfo error in ordinary Clojure and when re-frame.core is compiled with *assert* false; tests cover at least the retired keyword form, a vector, and nil.
- A ClojureScript test/probe compiled with :elide-asserts true proves the same non-map call still throws the same :rf.error/id; an assertions-on CLJS control remains covered.
- Existing valid-map semantics stay unchanged: all known keys in one map are applied in documented order, a missing key leaves that subsystem untouched, and an unknown top-level key remains a nil-returning no-op.
- The focused tests no longer require AssertionError as the public contract; they assert the canonical id, :where, recovery/reason shape, and avoid requiring raw arbitrary config values in ex-data.
- The error catalogue/API projection is updated as required, and the implementation/core Clojure suite plus the relevant CLJS and production/elision probes pass.

title: [OPERATOR ACT - Mike, not worker work] Verify io.github.day8 on Clojars: create public repo day8/clojars-mikethompson, submit its URL at clojars.org/verify/group; discharge test = https://clojars.org/groups/io.github.day8 answers 200 AND users/mikethompson lists it verified (never /api/groups, which 404s on empty groups)
description:
Surfaced by rf2-2ii52 (ruling caveat, deliberately not solved inside the vendoring PR).

Vendoring day8/de-dupe fixed the DEPENDENCY GRAPH for day8/re-frame2-mcp-base and
day8/re-frame2-story-mcp — both now generate a complete pom, and PR #7169 wires their
deploy jobs onto the existing story-v* glob. It did NOT make the coordinates CLAIMABLE.

THE POLICY. Clojars requires NEW projects to live in a *verified* group, and verification
requires a reverse-domain group name. `day8` is not reverse-domain, so it cannot be
verified. Existing projects in an old group may publish new versions; a NEW project may
not be created. This is not theoretical: day8/de-dupe's own tag-triggered publish workflow
ran on 2026-05-13 and received a 403 — "Group 'day8' isn't verified, so can't contain new
projects". That 403 is the reason route (a) (publish de-dupe) was ruled out.

THE SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THE TWO NEW JARS. The same rule applies to EVERY day8/re-frame2-*
coordinate that has never been published — which, as far as anyone has checked, is all of
them: the thirteen implementation/ artefacts as well as the five tool jars. If the day8
group cannot take new projects, then no v* tag can cut a first release either, and the
whole release pipeline is gated on this rather than on any code.

WHAT NEEDS DECIDING (Mike's, not a worker's):
  1. Does day8's Clojars standing permit new projects today? (An older group may have been
     grandfathered, or the account may hold a verified group already — VERIFY against
     Clojars rather than inferring from the 2026-05-13 403, which was a different group
     path.) If yes, nothing to do: tag and publish.
  2. If no: the artefacts need a verified reverse-domain group — io.github.day8/* is the
     obvious candidate, verifiable via the GitHub org. That renames EVERY published
     coordinate, which touches deps.edn :clein/build :lib for 18 artefacts, the lockstep
     gate, every release workflow's rewrite + preflight, docs/release-process.md, the
     template's pins, CHANGELOG, and every consumer-facing usage snippet in the repo.

VERIFY BEFORE TAGGING ANYTHING. Clojars has no yank, and a half-published set at a given
VERSION is recovered only by bump-and-supersede.

Flagged in .github/workflows/release-story.yml's header and docs/release-process.md
\u00a7How story-mcp and mcp-base got their publish path.
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-28, dossier review): recorded 2026-07-28 07:48 AUSEST from ai/decisions/rf2-uelji.clojars-verified-group.md (primary analysis + independent Codex second opinion, reconciled; the dossier file is deleted after this note — THIS NOTE IS THE CANONICAL RECORD).

DECISION, in three parts:
(1) VERIFICATION-FIRST SEQUENCING STANDS, but the canary-by-tag route is REJECTED as the verification instrument (Codex position, adopted). Mike's authoritative act is the zero-mutation one: verify io.github.day8 via Clojars' self-service GitHub-org proof (see MIKE'S ACT below), optionally glancing at day8's standing from his logged-in account or asking Clojars support as belt-and-braces.
(2) RULED FALLBACK GROUP if day8 is blocked (and the evidence below says it is): io.github.day8 for ALL 18 Maven coordinates, moved in ONE sequenced rename campaign BEFORE anything publishes.
(3) NO-TAG RULE: NO v*, story-v*, xray-v*, or machines-viz-v* tag is pushed until this bead resolves (io.github.day8 badge confirmed + rename campaign merged + lockstep/preflight/release-DAG gates green on the new coordinates). This is STEP 0 of the rf2-vxgfnd.99 cut-time checklist, ahead of its existing step 1 (credentials); rf2-2ii52 step 3 (manual first publish of mcp-base/story-mcp) is equally blocked on it.

EVIDENCE AND ITS LIMITS (three independent sources; two re-verified from primary sources 2026-07-28):
- The 2026-05-13 403 on day8/de-dupe's tag-triggered publish — "Group 'day8' isn't verified, so can't contain new projects" — is real but was a DIFFERENT project path; on its own it is suggestive, not conclusive (the bead itself warns against inferring from it alone).
- Clojars' Verified Group Names wiki (fetched 2026-07-28): since 2021-04-18 "creating new libraries in non-verified groups will be disabled", while "the group does not need to be verified for new versions" of EXISTING libraries. Bare `day8` is neither reverse-domain nor a githost-org pattern, so it is STRUCTURALLY UNVERIFIABLE — there is no route to a verified bare day8, and seeking a policy exception would couple every release to an exception Clojars explicitly designed away.
- clojars.org/users/mikethompson (fetched 2026-07-28): `day8` is listed WITHOUT the verified badge; only net.clojars.mikethompson and org.clojars.mikethompson carry it. Codex traced the badge to find-group-verification in clojars-web's web/user.clj (not cosmetic) and the enforcement to check-group+project in db.clj: an unverified group is accepted ONLY when that exact group/artifact pair already exists; a new artifact is rejected as group-non-verified.
- All 18 intended day8/* coordinates 404 on Clojars (re-verified 2026-07-27, per-coordinate) — every one is a NEW project as far as Clojars is concerned, so every one enters the rejected branch. The day8 group page returning 200 with mikethompson permitted proves only maintenance rights over existing projects, not creation rights.
- LIMIT: what stays unobservable read-only is Mike's account-side view and any bespoke admin exception. That residual is why this bead stays with Mike — but it is small, and it does not justify a canary.

VERIFICATION ROUTES WEIGHED (canary trade-offs recorded):
- (a) Account/settings check or asking Clojars admins: zero-risk, zero-mutation. Fine as belt-and-braces; not required given (c).
- (b) Canary publish by pushing the ready machines-viz-v0.0.1.alpha tag: REJECTED as a probe. A 403 merely re-demonstrates documented policy at the cost of a burned tag-push cycle; a surprise success is an IMMUTABLE public act that permanently pins machines-viz to day8/* — either splitting the family when the rest moves, or accidentally committing the whole family to an unverifiable legacy group. Never use an immutable registry operation to learn an observable fact; if state might have changed, re-read the profile/API or ask support instead. (The primary analysis's "nothing is wasted on success" framing undercounts this: success is exactly the outcome that forecloses the group decision.)
- (c) The act that actually advances things — verify io.github.day8 NOW: create the empty public repo github.com/day8/clojars-mikethompson, submit its URL at clojars.org/verify/group while logged in as mikethompson, confirm the badge appears. Cheap, self-service, and harmless even in the unlikely event day8 turns out grandfathered (verifying a group publishes nothing). It doubles as the authoritative test: Clojars' own flow granting io.github.day8 while day8 stays unverified closes the question.

FALLBACK GROUP CHOICE (io.github.day8), alternatives weighed:
- io.github.day8 — CHOSEN. GitHub-org-verifiable self-service; matches the existing in-repo precedent io.github.day8/re-frame2-template; expresses the durable owner users already see (the day8 GitHub org).
- com.github.day8 — the verification flow verifies both com. and io. simultaneously, but io. is the cleaner match to the existing precedent. Publish under ONE only — Clojars itself warns that the same library under two group IDs can put both on a classpath.
- au.com.day8 — DNS-TXT-verifiable via day8.com.au; defensible if Day8 deliberately wants DNS (not GitHub) as the permanent package identity, but it adds a separate DNS proof and stewardship path, has zero consumer precedent, and buys no ergonomics.
- net.clojars.mikethompson — already verified and usable today, but makes organisation-owned libraries look personally owned. Rejected.
- Policy exception for bare day8 — structurally impossible (not reverse-domain) and bad posture even if grantable. Rejected.

WHY DECIDE BEFORE FIRST PUBLISH (irreversibility): Clojars has no yank; a deployed non-SNAPSHOT version is immutable. Any rename AFTER a first publish leaves permanently orphaned day8/* coordinates and creates the two-groups-one-library classpath hazard. The current all-404 state — pre-alpha, zero consumers — is the cheapest this move will ever be.

RENAME BLAST RADIUS (one sequenced hot-zone campaign, NOT parallel work; coordinate work ONLY):
- :clein/build :lib in all 18 publishable deps.edn (13 implementation/ + 5 tools/), plus the internal cross-artefact dependency maps the :local/root rewrite resolves (31 in-repo coordinates inventoried by the lockstep gate).
- .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh (inventories + assertions).
- Release workflows and their scripts: release.yml (13-coordinate DAG + generated-POM assertions), release-story.yml (mcp-base -> story -> story-mcp ordering), release-machines-viz.yml, .github/scripts/rewrite-in-repo-coords.sh, preflight-tool-package.sh, preflight-story-package.sh.
- docs/release-process.md; CHANGELOG (its roster is gate-pinned to the publishable-runtimes authority); migration guide dep edits; every consumer-facing usage snippet; the setup skill; the template's emitted coordinates (tools/template — interacts with rf2-57bjg, whose template-coordinate fix should land on the NEW group).
- The pre-staged rf2-snjn5 docs-flip PR #7167 (8 sites teaching day8/* coords) must be RE-CUT on the new group.
- day8/reagent-slim — the one deliberately off-pattern coordinate (publication-time rename) — becomes io.github.day8/reagent-slim; give it its final eyeball in the same pass.
- Credentials: the planned group-scoped reusable Clojars deploy token must be scoped to io.github.day8, not day8 (rf2-vxgfnd.99 checklist step 1 wording changes accordingly).
- EXPLICIT NON-SCOPE (Clojars documents that the Maven group does not constrain Clojure namespaces): NO Clojure namespace renames, NO repo URL changes, NO npm @day8 scope change.

INTERACTIONS: this bead is now STEP 0 of the rf2-vxgfnd.99 cut checklist (cross-ref appended there) — its steps 3 (404 re-probe: probe the NEW coordinates), 4/6 (PR #7167 re-cut) and 1 (token group scope) all shift under this ruling. rf2-2ii52's remaining step 3 (manual first publish per release-machines-viz.yml's header protocol) proceeds only after this resolves, on io.github.day8 coordinates.

MIKE'S ACT (why this stays OPEN and assigned to him): 1. create the empty public repo day8/clojars-mikethompson; 2. submit https://github.com/day8/clojars-mikethompson at clojars.org/verify/group as mikethompson; 3. confirm io.github.day8 shows the verified badge (optionally also glance at day8's standing / ask support); 4. say go — the rename campaign is then worker-dispatchable as one sequenced campaign, and this bead closes when the badge is confirmed AND the campaign is merged with gates green.
RUNBOOK CONSOLIDATION (dossier review, 2026-07-28): Codex second-opinion review of the operator runbook (ai/decisions/rf2-uelji.clojars-group-verification.md, written 2026-07-28 16:36 AUSEST) CONCURS with the morning RULING on every decision point — io.github.day8 destination, canary-by-tag rejected, no-tag rule, verification-first sequencing, and the group-alternatives weighing all match. No contradictions; this is a consolidation, not a re-ruling. It adds the following NEW verified mechanics the ruling did not yet carry. The dossier file is deleted after this note — this note is the canonical record of its Codex section.

(1) VERIFY-FORM MECHANICS (verified against clojars-web verification.clj, 2026-07-28): the clojars.org/verify/group flow's GitHub/GitLab repository section takes the FULL proof-repo URL (https://github.com/day8/clojars-mikethompson) — the form does NOT ask for the group name. It accepts exactly https://github.com/<org>/clojars-<clojars-user>, checks the public repo exists, and creates/verifies BOTH com.github.day8 AND io.github.day8 in one act. Publish under io.github.day8 as the ONE public Maven identity (per the ruling; never both). KEEP THE PROOF REPO PUBLIC PERMANENTLY — it is the standing evidence of org control, not a one-shot token. (As of the 2026-07-28 check, github.com/day8/clojars-mikethompson returned 404 — the verification act has not yet happened.)

(2) TOKEN ORDER (inserts a step between MIKE'S ACT and the rf2-vxgfnd.99 checklist's credentials step): create or replace the CI deploy token scoped to io.github.day8 only AFTER verification — Clojars does not allow a group-scoped token before the group exists (Deploy-Tokens wiki, Scoping). Verification usefully creates the group before any artifact exists, which is what makes the scoped token mintable at all. Sequence: badge confirmed -> mint io.github.day8-scoped token -> cut checklist step 1 (credentials) proceeds with that token, never a bare-day8-scoped one.

(3) ENFORCEMENT CONFIRMATION: current clojars-web db.clj check-group+project structurally confirms the ruling's reading — it first accepts an exact EXISTING group/artifact pair, then rejects a NEW artifact when the group has no verification record. Existing day8 projects therefore do NOT grandfather any new day8/re-frame2-* artifact.

(4) CAMPAIGN COMPLETION CRITERION (tightens the ruling's "gates green" close condition): a hand-written file roster is NOT a safe completion criterion — an exact-token scan (2026-07-28 snapshot) found ~428 candidate references to the 18 published coordinates across hundreds of tracked files, and the repo is still moving, so the count itself must not be relied on. Required instead: a structural re-scan at campaign START and again at COMPLETION; then generate and INSPECT all deploy POMs, proving every in-family GAV uses io.github.day8 at the lockstep version with NO old-group dependency (a partial migration can publish a valid jar whose POM points at an old-group coordinate that will never exist); plus verify-version-lockstep.sh --self-test, the normal lockstep gate, the release-script policy tests, and each tool/package preflight — ALL green before the tag freeze lifts. Re-cut any staged documentation change (PR #7167) against the new group from the same structural inventory.

(5) COORDINATE-SPECIFIC FENCE (sharpens the ruling's explicit non-scope): NO repository-wide day8 -> io.github.day8 text replacement. GitHub org URLs, @day8 npm packages, Clojure namespace names, and ordinary prose about the Day8 organisation do not change. Any RETAINED legacy day8/* Maven coordinate must be an intentional historical example or negative test, and explicitly allowlisted as such.

(6) GROUP-ALTERNATIVES RECORD: Codex's independent weighing matches the ruling exactly — au.com.day8 defensible only as an explicit branding decision (adds DNS access/propagation/stewardship without solving anything the GitHub route leaves open); net.clojars.mikethompson rejected for org stewardship (org-owned libraries under a personal account); bare day8 / policy exception / publish canary all rejected. Recorded as concurrence.

Codex go/no-go, adopted as the operational phrasing of the ruling: go on verification now; go on the rename campaign as soon as the io.github.day8 badge is visible; no-go on every v*, story-v*, xray-v*, and machines-viz-v* tag until the migrated release graph and generated POMs are green.
FINAL CONSOLIDATION (dossier review, 2026-07-29): Codex Recommendation in the final revision of ai/decisions/rf2-uelji.clojars-group-verification.md (2026-07-28 23:02 AUSEST) CONCURS with the ruling and both prior consolidations on every point; its four-step path (verify -> badge + io.github.day8-scoped token -> one coordinate-only migration -> lockstep/preflight + structural old-coordinate scan + generated-POM inspection before the first tag) matches the bead's runbook exactly. Three deltas recorded; the dossier file is deleted after this note.
(1) PUBLICATION RULE, now stated as a hard rule: publish under io.github.day8 ONLY. The proof-repo verification necessarily also creates com.github.day8, but publishing under both would split the family's identity (and invites the two-groups-one-library classpath hazard already recorded). com.github.day8 exists solely as a verification by-product — never a publication target.
(2) INDEPENDENT RE-CONFIRMATION: Codex's own repository scan found the same 18 day8/* :clein/build declarations; its own per-coordinate Clojars checks returned 404 for all 18; and it independently read the current db.clj enforcement path (unverified group exempted only for an exact EXISTING group/artifact pair). Third independent confirmation of the evidence base, and further grounds that a publish canary adds no information.
(3) NO-OVER-BUILDING FENCE (new): a simple operator tag pause is enough — no new permanent policy layer, registry probe, or migration framework is warranted. The freeze stays exactly the recorded rf2-vxgfnd.99 step-0 no-tag rule; do not grow it into infrastructure.
STATUS (dossier review, 2026-07-31): DORMANT after the release cancellation (rf2-vxgfnd.99 closed — no tag on this timeline). The gate no longer queues anything; it stands alone for whenever a first publish happens (rf2-2ii52 step 3 also waits on it, unscheduled). Ruling (io.github.day8), runbook, and the no-publish-before-badge-and-rename rule are unchanged; the ten-minute verification act remains Mike's — do-whenever, never expires. DISPOSITION: status moved to deferred — an operator-owned dormant gate belongs out of the open list; the full canonical record stays on this bead. REACTIVATION TRIGGER: any decision to publish anything (framework or tools) — reactivate this bead first; badge and rename campaign before any tag. The 2026-07-31 dossier refresh carried no Codex Recommendation and proposed no ruling change; the dossier file is deleted after this note.

RULING 2026-09-04 21:10:40 AUSEST (delegated by Mike 2026-09-04, operator-reversible; dossier ai/decisions/rf2-uelji.clojars-verified-group.md and its Codex Recommendation section folded here and deleted). THE RULING, four parts:

(a) GROUP IDENTITY: io.github.day8 for every publishable Maven coordinate (19 at tip: 14 implementation/ + 5 tools/, 0 already on io.github.day8). CONFIRMED, and the two contingencies the reviews kept open are CLOSED unless Mike names one explicitly BEFORE rf2-fo4ng dispatches: net.clojars.mikethompson (already verified, zero account act, but presents organisation-owned libraries as personally owned, permanently, since Clojars has no yank) and a DNS-verified custom domain such as au.com.day8 (a brand decision; adds DNS stewardship; nobody can establish from outside whether Mike controls day8.com.au DNS). Both are ownership-model choices only Mike can make, neither reviewer recommends either, nothing on the tracker asks for either, and a change AFTER the campaign is a second rename with orphaned coordinates. io.github.day8 is the smallest coherent choice: it names the durable owner users already see (the day8 GitHub org), it is self-service, and it matches the one io.github.day8 coordinate already live in the tree (the git-coordinate template in .github/workflows/template-release.yml). Publish under io.github.day8 ONLY; com.github.day8 is created by the same act and stays a by-product, never a publication target.

(b) TIMING: DO THE ACT NOW. Delegated and operator-reversible: Mike parks it by saying "not now" on this bead, and the mayor then re-defers this bead and rf2-fo4ng with the release condition restated. Grounds, none new but now eleven passes deep with zero dissent: the act publishes nothing and is reversible in every part that matters (Codex: "the meaningful irreversible point is the first public artifact, not creation of the proof repository"); it turns the one premise every pass has relied on ("io.github.day8 will verify; bare day8 cannot") into an observed fact via Clojars' own flow; it moves the only operator-only step off the critical path of a release nobody has scheduled; the reactivation trigger fired 2026-08-15 (PR #8314) and was never explicitly re-parked; and two calendar slots (the rf2-4l67v pairing ~2026-08-10, the 2026-08-13 "this week") have already evaporated, which is the do-whenever-becomes-never drift the timing decision exists to stop. Cost of dormancy today is zero; its cost at the moment a publish is wanted is the act, the campaign, the token and the tag all becoming the critical path at once, with any account or org surprise surfacing at the most expensive time.

(c) THE DISCHARGE TEST, corrected. The 2026-09-03 test (GET https://clojars.org/api/groups/io.github.day8 non-empty) is WRONG and is withdrawn: that endpoint answers 404 for any group with no jars even when the group exists and is verified (routes/api.clj at clojars-web pin 836604152d answers not-found on an empty jar list; reproduced today on net.clojars.mikethompson, which is verified: API 404, group page 200). Under it the badge would never read as done until the first jar published, which is precisely the point the badge must precede, and rf2-fo4ng would never dispatch. The group page alone is ALSO insufficient: it carries no verified marker even for a verified group (measured today: 0 verified-group spans on https://clojars.org/groups/net.clojars.mikethompson), so a 200 there proves existence, not verification. THE TEST THE MAYOR RUNS, unauthenticated; both probes must read their AFTER value:

  curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://clojars.org/groups/io.github.day8
    404 today -> 200 after (the group exists)
  curl -sL https://clojars.org/users/mikethompson | grep -c -F 'io.github.day8</a></span><span class="verified-group'
    0 today -> 1 after (the group is listed on Mike's profile WITH the verified marker)

Coarser cross-check on the same page: grep -o 'verified-group' | wc -l reads 2 today and 4 after (io.github.day8 and com.github.day8 both appear, because verify-group* at pin 836604152d calls db/add-group, which adds the submitting user as admin of the new group, then db/verify-group!). The per-group grep was validated today: it reads 1 for net.clojars.mikethompson (verified), 0 for io.github.day8 (absent) and 0 for day8 (exists, unverified), so it discriminates existence from verification. The RULING/BADGE note Mike appends (runbook step 4) is the human record; these probes are the machine test, and the mayor acts on the probes, not on the note alone.

(d) THE TICK AFTER THE BADGE. When both probes read AFTER, the mayor, in one tick and in this order: (1) CLOSES rf2-uelji with a close reason citing the probe values and the badge time - this bead's close condition is SHARPENED by this ruling, see WHAT THIS BEAD NOW IS; (2) un-defers rf2-fo4ng (bd update rf2-fo4ng --defer "" --status open) - closing this bead releases the blocks edge uelji -> fo4ng, so fo4ng lists as ready instead of blocked; (3) dispatches rf2-fo4ng as ONE sequenced hot-zone campaign, the only worker on implementation/deps.edn, implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, .github/workflows/*, spec/Conventions.md, spec/API.md, spec/006, spec/009 and spec/Ownership.md while it runs, briefed from fo4ng's own description plus the RENAME CAMPAIGN GUIDANCE note above and the FOLLOW-UPS below. rf2-kmqx3 stays blocked by fo4ng until the campaign merges, and kmqx3 is Mike's acts (scoped token, then the first tag), never worker work. - Keep this bead's close condition as badge + merged campaign + green gates: rejected - it makes the bead a duplicate holder of rf2-fo4ng's acceptance and, with the blocks edge uelji -> fo4ng, a graph deadlock (fo4ng cannot be ready until uelji closes; uelji cannot close until fo4ng merges).
REVIEWER POSITIONS:

tools/xray/deps.edn:64-65 "NOT PUBLISHABLE YET ... carries no :clein/build"); (6) PR #7167 (the rf2-snjn5 docs-flip) was CLOSED UNMERGED 2026-07-30, so "re-cut the staged docs-flip" in fo4ng's scope is moot - the "not published" wording stays until a tag lands; FULL CONCURRENCE. Contributions preserved: (1) the posture framing, adopted as the answer to "is this gold plating": "This is foundational release correctness, not gold plating: the repository currently presents nineteen publication descriptors and four deployment workflows whose day8/* coordinates cannot create new Clojars projects.
