- Ruling agent's own additions, measured at source today: (1) verification.clj at pin 836604152d rejects the act with a named message in each of four cases, so a failure at step 3 is self-diagnosing: "The format of the URL is invalid" (shape must be https://github.com/<org>/clojars-<clojars-username>); "Groups already verified by user '<x>' on <date>" (someone else claimed io./com.github.day8 first - both 404 today, so only a race between now and the act could produce it); "The verification repo is for user '<x>', not '<you>'" (the repo name must carry the CLOJARS username mikethompson, not the GitHub login mike-thompson-day8); "The verification repo does not exist" (the check is an unauthenticated HTTP HEAD expecting 200, so a private repo or a typo fails here). (2) The group page carries no verified marker, which is why the discharge test needs the user page. (3) Census at tip 1ad17a77fe: 19 day8/ :lib declarations, 0 io.github.day8/.

THE OPERATOR RUNBOOK as it now stands (Mike's act, about ten minutes, publishes nothing, STOP after 4):
1. (Optional) Logged in to clojars.org as mikethompson, glance at https://clojars.org/groups/day8 and https://clojars.org/users/mikethompson - expect no verified marker on day8. Confirms only; decides nothing.
2. Create an empty PUBLIC repository named exactly clojars-mikethompson in the day8 org: https://github.com/organizations/day8/repositories/new - no README needed; Clojars accepts an empty repo. Leave it public afterwards (the verifier's HTTP HEAD needs 200 at submission; keeping it public thereafter is the auditable ownership marker - an operational recommendation, no primary source says Clojars re-checks it).
3. At https://clojars.org/verify/group, in the GitHub/GitLab repository section, submit the FULL URL https://github.com/day8/clojars-mikethompson. The form does not ask for a group name. Then https://clojars.org/groups/io.github.day8 answers 200 and https://clojars.org/users/mikethompson lists io.github.day8 with the verified marker. com.github.day8 is a by-product; publish under io.github.day8 ONLY.

   Or say it in chat and the mayor records it. If step 2 or 3 surprises, record the exact message here and STOP: Clojars support route, no tag, no fallback to bare day8, no probe.
   STOP HERE. No deploy token (non-expiring by default, and a group-scoped token cannot exist before the group does - verification makes it mintable, not wanted; mint it only when a tag is imminent, in rf2-kmqx3). No tag (every descriptor still names day8/*; verification alone does not make the workflows safe).
The mayor's discharge test, as in (c):
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://clojars.org/groups/io.github.day8            # 404 -> 200
   curl -sL https://clojars.org/users/mikethompson | grep -c -F 'io.github.day8</a></span><span class="verified-group'   # 0 -> 1
Never https://clojars.org/api/groups/io.github.day8 (404 on an empty group even when verified).
5. Mayor, the tick after both probes read AFTER: close this bead; un-defer and dispatch rf2-fo4ng (one sequenced hot-zone campaign; acceptance 1-4 on fo4ng; guidance in the RENAME CAMPAIGN GUIDANCE note above; FOLLOW-UPS below).
6. Credentials and the first tag are rf2-kmqx3's, after the campaign merges: mint an io.github.day8-scoped token, update CLOJARS_USERNAME / CLOJARS_PASSWORD (release.yml:150-153: the password IS the token), re-probe the 19 new coordinates for 404 and the policy page, inspect generated POMs, then push v0.0.1.alpha. Then rf2-8urba, rf2-2hpxo, rf2-lb566, rf2-59bgn and rf2-hic-063 become dispatchable in the order their own fences say.

WHAT THIS BEAD NOW IS: an OPERATOR ACT - verify io.github.day8 on Clojars - and nothing else. Two amendments follow from that.
- CLOSE CONDITION SHARPENED (ruled here): this bead closes when the discharge test reads AFTER and the RULING/BADGE line is on record. The 2026-07-28 conjunction (badge + merged campaign + green gates on the new coordinates) is preserved as the NO-TAG RULE - the condition under which any v*, story-v*, xray-v* or machines-viz-v* tag may be pushed - and it is carried where it belongs: the campaign half by rf2-fo4ng's acceptance 1-4, the tag half by rf2-kmqx3, which depends on both this bead and fo4ng and whose title already says the tag is Mike's act. Nothing is weakened: no tag bead can become ready before the campaign closes, because kmqx3 is edge-blocked by fo4ng. What is removed is the deadlock - with the blocks edge uelji -> fo4ng retyped 2026-08-22, a close condition that includes fo4ng's own merge meant fo4ng could never list as ready and the mayor would have had to dispatch a blocked bead by hand.
- STATUS: returned to OPEN, defer cleared, title carries the marker [OPERATOR ACT - Mike, not worker work]. The 2026-07-31 defer was set for a dormant gate after a cancelled release; the trigger fired 2026-08-15 and the ruling since 2026-08-16 has been "do the act now", yet the bead stayed deferred - hidden from every open-only list, which the mayor's own 2026-08-21 note measured as the reason it went unsurfaced ("NINE beads were invisible, and this one is the most expensive"), and which is how two calendar slots evaporated. A bead whose ruling is "now" and whose owner is Mike belongs on Mike's queue and in every tick's ready list, where the title fences it. THE TICK'S INSTRUCTION when it sees this bead in bd ready: never dispatch it to a worker; run the two probes; if both read AFTER, do step 5; otherwise leave it exactly as it is. Clearing the defer also takes this bead out of the 2026-09-16 batch lapse (fo4ng, 8urba, 8o66x remain in it; fo4ng and 8urba are edge-blocked so their lapse is inert; 8o66x is not this chain's).

WHAT THE MAYOR DOES NEXT (now, before the badge): nothing on this chain. Surface this bead to Mike as the single operator act on the release side, with the four-step runbook and the URLs, once; do not re-defer it; do not dispatch rf2-fo4ng; do not mint or ask for a token. EVENING DOSSIER-REVIEW CONSOLIDATION (operator-directed, 2026-08-07 ~21:40 AUSEST). Second review pass of the day; dossier file deleted after this note. DECISION UNCHANGED: the recorded do-the-act-now timing decision stands (Codex's fresh independent pass concurs), with one sharpening adopted below (the stop-boundary). The act remains irreducibly Mike's. Deltas only — the morning note's items (enforcement re-read at pin 05c870ae, zero-mutation correction, proof-repo reclassification, token posture) are NOT re-pasted.

NEW EVIDENCE (Codex, independent, read-only, 2026-08-07 evening):
(1) COORDINATE CENSUS RE-DERIVED FROM SOURCE, not from this bead: rg over implementation/ + tools/ deps.edn :lib declarations at repo commit abcb342 finds EXACTLY 18 day8/* publication coordinates — matching this bead's standing inventory item-for-item (re-frame2, -epoch, -flows, -http, -machines, -machines-viz, -mcp-base, -reagent, -resources, -routing, -schemas, -ssr, -ssr-ring, -story, -story-mcp, -uix, -xray, plus day8/reagent-slim). The inventory is confirmed current, no drift.
(2) ALL 18 STILL 404 on the Clojars artifact API tonight — every one remains a NEW project at check time, i.e. still the rejected branch of the verified-group policy.
(3) GRANDFATHERING RULED OUT WITH LIVE STATE: the day8 group page exists and lists four unrelated legacy projects with no verified marker; Mike's public Clojars profile shows net.clojars.mikethompson and org.clojars.mikethompson verified but NOT day8; io.github.day8 and com.github.day8 group pages both 404; the proof repo day8/clojars-mikethompson is 404 on both the public URL and the GitHub REST endpoint (a private repo could hide from REST, but a private repo cannot satisfy Clojars' unauthenticated-HEAD-200 check, so no qualifying proof repo exists now). Per db.clj:965-996 the deploy bypass covers only an exact EXISTING group/artifact pair — the four legacy day8 projects confer nothing on the 18 new artifacts.
(4) EMPTY-REPO ALLOWANCE is explicit in Clojars' own group-policy instructions (an empty public repository qualifies); the form takes the full URL shaped https://github.com/<org>/clojars-<user>.
(5) WHY-NOW, SHARPENED: the act exercises the only two facts read-only research cannot establish — whether mikethompson can create a public repo in the day8 org, and whether the authenticated Clojars account completes the flow. Discovering a permissions wrinkle with no release under way is materially cheaper than discovering it after a date or tag is chosen. Waiting saves only the clutter of an empty repo and two unused group records.
(6) DOWNSIDE STATED PRECISELY: verification mutates GitHub and Clojars (proof repo + BOTH group records created, though only io.github.day8 becomes a package identity); it uploads no JAR, reserves none of the 18 artifact IDs, forces no migration.

THE RULING. Option (iii), under the two-promise package-boundary rule the Codex review stated and which the implementor skill already enforces on itself. Promise 1: anything a skill's normal operation must READ ships inside the package and is linked skill-root-relative, or is read through a verified PINNED LOCAL CHECKOUT at a user-supplied path, per that skill's own cardinal rule. Promise 2: everything a shipped doc merely CITES outside the package is spelled as an absolute repository URL - https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/blob/main/<path>[#anchor] for a file, tree/main/<path> for a directory. Consequently NO relative link in a shipped skill doc may resolve outside its package; check_skill_package_refs.py makes that a finding; and check_doc_slugs.py learns to unwrap this repo's own blob/main and tree/main URLs so the rewritten links keep rename-safety. All 427 escaping links are rewritten in SOURCE, in one PR, by one worker. No skill is marked clone-only: the classification the Codex review asked for has a measured answer (below) - the two operational corpora are already pinned-checkout reads by each skill's own design, so the rewrite changes no runtime dependency.

WHY (iii), AND WHY THE TWO-PROMISE FRAMING RATHER THAN "ALL LINKS CLICKABLE". Both reviewers recommend rewriting the citations; they part on whether the 50 SKILL.md escapes hide operational reads that a URL cannot serve. The tree answers this, and neither reviewer read the two leaves that do. (a) skills/re-frame-migration/references/setup.md:134-148, "Pin the migration corpus before reading it": MIGRATION.md must be pinned, not fetched live; load it from a local checkout of day8/re-frame2 pinned to a commit or tag at <path-to-re-frame2>, verified by rev-parse, remote get-url and ls-tree (identity by structure, never by name); verbatim "Do not fetch MIGRATION.md from GitHub at runtime"; record the pinned hash in the migration report. (b) skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md:48, cardinal rule 1: "Spec is the contract - pinned before reading. Verify the checkout's HEAD and origin against the pin recorded in the port profile, and resolve every contract read through that checkout at the pin - the live-site URLs in this skill are citations, never the reading route"; :70 kickoff prompt "The spec corpus is at <path-to-re-frame2>/spec/, pinned at <sha-or-tag>"; references/cardinal-rules.md:11-13 and phase-1-decisions.md:23-32 repeat it, and references/conformance.md:3 ALREADY links spec/conformance/ by https URL. So the relative links in those two SKILL.md files were never the reading route: the reading route is a user-supplied pinned checkout, which is neither the monorepo around the skill nor the network. Rewriting the citation to a URL changes nothing operationally. The dossier's argument that "the agent can fetch a URL it cannot Read" is therefore NOT why the migration skill survives standalone - it survives because setup.md routes the read through a pinned checkout, and fetching from GitHub is exactly what that leaf forbids. VERIFIED at source in this act (clojars-web 836604152d, src/clojars/routes/api.clj: if-let (seq (db/find-jars-information db group-id)) ... (not-found nil)) and independently measured on rf2-uelji's dossier (net.clojars.mikethompson: API 404, group page 200). Recorded on this bead because this bead is what closes them; they are NOT separate work and no bead is being filed for them.

G1 — THERE IS NO PUBLISHED COORDINATE, so docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md routes a reader through a monorepo clone and :local/root. A pilot following the published instructions CORRECTLY ends up with the whole repository on disk.

G2 — THE MIGRATION REPORTER IS STEP 1 OF THE PUBLISHED MIGRATION PROCESS AND CANNOT BE REACHED FROM THE PUBLISHED SITE. Cutting the first tag on io.github.day8/* and proving artefact-install is exactly what lets 00-installation.md stop routing through a clone, which is what puts the migration reporter within reach of a reader who has not cloned anything. Filing them separately would create two beads that can only close when this one does.

MAYOR — BACKLOG REREAD 2026-08-19 11:05 AUSEST. THE HOLD IS REAL, EXTERNAL, AND WORTH WRITING A COST AGAINST.

RE-TESTED AT SOURCE. rf2-uelji reads DEFERRED with deferred_until 2026-09-16, and its description states the mechanism: Clojars requires a NEW project to live in a VERIFIED group, verification requires a reverse-domain group name, and 'day8' is not reverse-domain and therefore cannot be verified. Existing projects in an old group may publish new versions; a new project may not be created. So no worker clears this — it is a policy question about a coordinate, not work.

WHAT THE HOLD IS COSTING, recorded because a hold with no cost written on it reads as free. This bead is the ONLY thing between Hicasso and a consumable artefact. Measured this morning: 86 of 90 hic-NNN beads closed, 28 source files and ~17,200 lines shipping under implementation/hicasso/src, 446 test files, 29 published guide pages carried in mkdocs nav, and the adapter registered in every roster. The documentary half of the original rf2-hic-061 clause — versioning and release automation, the 14-row compatibility matrix, the upgrade policy including complaint-id stability — is done and closed. What cannot be demonstrated is the one clause that matters to a consumer: that an app can install Hicasso from the artefact rather than from this repository.

THE DECISION THIS SURFACES FOR MIKE, and it is his because it names the project in public and is not cheaply reversed: the group coordinate. io.github.day8/* is the reverse-domain form Clojars will verify, and it is what rf2-uelji's deferral implicitly assumes; this bead's own title already says io.github.day8/*. If that is the intended coordinate, verification can start now rather than in September, and the deferral date is measuring a wait nobody is actually blocked on. If a different coordinate is wanted, that is the call to make.

I am not ruling it. Publishing under a coordinate is outward-facing and effectively permanent, which is the class the standing grant reserves.

value:
A DISPATCH FENCE IS NOT ALWAYS SPELLED "DO NOT DISPATCH" — the pre-dispatch grep needs the POSITIVE forms too. Measured 2026-09-04, the third gap found in this instrument in one session.

THE CHECK. Before dispatching any bead, grep its notes for a hold, because `bd ready` reads dependency EDGES and can never see a PROSE fence. The pattern I had been using was: FENCED | DO NOT DISPATCH | SEQUENCED | RELEASE CONDITION | HOLD UNTIL | Mike rules | STILL MIKE | DOSSIER | RECOMMENDATION | operator call.

WHAT IT MISSED. rf2-i6kh carries, in capitals: "DISPATCH ONLY AFTER rf2-2hpxo's PR HAS MERGED, never merely opened." The old pattern returns ZERO on that bead. I dispatched it; the worker read the bead, found the line, and correctly STOPPED without a PR, having first measured the surface and banked the results. One worker cycle spent, nothing damaged.

WHY THE GAP IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. Every term in my pattern was a PROHIBITION ("do not", "hold", "fenced"). A precondition can equally be written as a PERMISSION with a condition attached — "dispatch only after X", "once Y merges", "after Z lands" — and those share no substring with the prohibitions. A keyword list built from the prohibitions will therefore keep missing the permissions, and adding one more term does not fix the class.

THE WIDENED PATTERN, verified to fire on rf2-i6kh where the old one was silent (it returns "DISPATCH ONLY", "AFTER rf2-2hpxo's PR HAS MERGED", "precondition"):

  grep -o -i -E '(DISPATCH ONLY|ONLY AFTER|DO NOT DISPATCH|FENCED|SEQUENCED|RELEASE CONDITION|HOLD UNTIL|precondition|MUST MERGE|after .{0,20} HAS MERGED|Mike rules|STILL MIKE|operator call|DOSSIER|RECOMMENDATION)'

TWO THINGS THAT MAKE THIS SURVIVABLE RATHER THAN A LOOMING FAILURE. First, the grep is a cheap FILTER, not an authority — a hit means read the bead, a miss means nothing. Second, the real backstop is the worker: the preamble's "check your dispatch preconditions before you begin" plus "premises are claims, not findings" is what caught this, as it has caught every mayor-side gap this session. So widen the pattern, and keep the clause in the brief that makes the worker check independently.

AND NOTE THE TRACKER ITSELF WAS WRONG AT DISPATCH TIME: rf2-i6kh WAS in `bd ready` when I read it, and a dependency edge was added afterwards, so it is correctly blocked now. Both instruments failed together; only the worker did not.

RELATED: [[grep-notes-for-a-fence-before-every-dispatch]], [[jq-output-carries-cr-and-poisons-every-loop]].

title: routing navigate: reject non-map :query-merge before it mutates or throws
description:
## Slice reviewed

`implementation/routing/**`, with the actionable center at the public `:rf.route/navigate` in-place-edit path. I inspected the implementation, Spec 012, API/guide examples, focused routing tests, representative repository consumers, all-status beads, and the introducing/refactoring history. This is the single cohesive finding selected from the review.

## Problem and user impact

A present `:query-merge` is documented and used as a map of query deltas, but the routing always-on structural gate validates only its key relationships, not its value shape. `re-frame.routing.navigate/navigate-handler` then hands the value to Clojure `merge` outside the protected `route-url` construction boundary.

That produces two materially bad outcomes from one missing boundary check:

- A two-element vector is accepted by Clojure as a map entry. `[:rf.route/navigate {:query-merge [:page 2]}]` silently performs a real navigation, changes the route query, and advances the nav token even though the edit value is not the documented map.
- Other non-map values can raise host errors from the handler. For example `:query-merge "oops"` reaches a raw `ClassCastException` with no structured ex-data instead of the promised `:rf.error/navigate-bad-request` rejection.
- `:query-merge nil` also passes and becomes a silent no-op because the fold uses `if-let`, despite key presence being the grammar's discriminator.

This is an ergonomics and correctness defect at a common SPA operation (filters, pagination, tabs). A programmer or generated call site that passes one map entry, a sequence, or a conditional nil should get one immediate, local explanation; it must not sometimes navigate, sometimes disappear, and sometimes fall into generic event-handler exception containment according to incidental Clojure collection semantics.

## Independently verified behavior

At repository tip `52b2579e9b53816abddd3406f72db5a5278bed1c`:

- Direct calls to `re-frame.routing.address/classify` returned `nil` (accepted) for all three requests `{:query-merge [:page 2]}`, `{:query-merge "oops"}`, and `{:query-merge nil}` when a current route was supplied.
- Through the real public dispatch path in a fresh plain-atom frame, with the JVM launched using `-Dre-frame.debug=false`, starting from query `{:q "x"}` and token `"nav-1"`, dispatching `[:rf.route/navigate {:query-merge [:page 2]}]` produced query `{:q "x", :page 2}` and token `"nav-2"`. This proves the malformed value is not merely a diagnostic mismatch: it commits navigation in the production posture.
- Calling `navigate-handler` with `{:query-merge "oops"}` raised `java.lang.ClassCastException` (`Character cannot be cast to java.util.Map$Entry`) with `ex-data nil` at the merge fold. The outer event engine contains handler exceptions, but that is the generic failure channel, not this operation's structural rejection contract.

## Exact evidence

- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/address.cljc:186-251`, `classify`: validates the closed roster and cross-key exclusions, but has no present-`:query-merge` `map?` branch. Its docstring says the gate is total and rejects malformed requests before guards.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/navigate.cljc:409-412`, `navigate-handler`: `(if-let [merge-in (:query-merge request)] (merge (:query current) query-params merge-in) ...)`; the fold is before the `route-url` try/catch at lines 442-459.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:277-282`: the event registration supplies allocation coeffects but no independent request schema, so the always-on gate is the relevant boundary in both postures.
- `spec/012-Routing.md:433-470`: the canonical request grammar names `:query-merge` as an edit and promises malformed requests reject through `:rf.error/navigate-bad-request` before guards; lines 475-499 describe it as query-delta folding and every example supplies a map.
- `docs/routing/concepts.md:205-225` and `docs/api/re-frame.routing.md:501`: the public recipes likewise use map deltas and advertise loud structural rejection.
- `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_navigation_test.clj:1729-1904`: positive `:query-merge` coverage uses maps (ordinary fold, nil member deletion, falsy member values, precedence, exact no-op). Lines 2319-2336 cover only relationships with `:url`, `:query`, and destination forms. No test gives the key a non-map value.
- Repository-wide non-test/non-doc search found no intended non-map consumer; the only executable example outside the implementation is a checker fixture using `(select-keys ...)`, also a map.

## History

- `bfde6b4fb7` (2026-07-03, rf2-ue2d4t) introduced `:query-merge` as a delta fold.
- `3b9f457674` (2026-07-21, rf2-vwwvp.1) moved navigation to the flat request-map grammar and added the structural gate, but kept the unchecked fold.
- `c60cb3ebf0` (2026-07-21, rf2-oq0ld) made top-level navigate/route-url map boundaries exact and total; it did not close this nested edit-value boundary.
- `git blame` attributes the current fold at `navigate.cljc:409-412` to `1ae6555f640` (2026-07-26). No later commit adds a value-shape guard.

## Bounded recommendation and posture rationale

Extend the existing always-on `re-frame.routing.address/classify` boundary: when `:query-merge` is present, require its value to be a map and return a stable `navigate-bad-request` reason (suggested `:query-merge-not-map`, `:keys [:query-merge]`) before guard evaluation or query folding. Keep the check plain and local; do not add a schema dependency or a general request-builder abstraction.

An empty map remains a valid exact no-op. Nil values *inside* a valid delta map continue to remove keys, and falsy non-nil member values continue to round-trip. A present nil for the delta map itself should reject rather than silently vanish: omission is already the unambiguous spelling for “no merge”. This is the small pre-alpha correction that makes the minimal API trustworthy for both people and generated code.

## Non-goals

- Do not redesign the flat navigation grammar or add a builder/record type.
- Do not broaden this bead into validating every navigation policy/value slot.
- Do not change query merge precedence, nil-member deletion, canonical URL encoding, guard semantics, or no-op classification.
- Do not make Schemas/Malli mandatory for routing.
- Do not change `merge` behavior elsewhere in the library.

## Duplicate search

All searches were run across all statuses before creation:

- `bd search "query-merge" --status all --limit 200 --long`: no issues.
- Description searches for `query-merge`, `query merge`, `navigate-bad-request`, `ClassCastException`, and `non-map query`: zero issues.
- `bd search "navigate" --status all`: three closed Hicasso intent/testing issues (`rf2-3q38`, `rf2-6c12m.20`, `rf2-6c12m.15`), none about routing request values.
- A broad all-status `non-map` description search found `rf2-xn13` about `core/configure!`; it is a different public API and failure mechanism.
- Historical ids `rf2-ue2d4t`, `rf2-vwwvp.1`, and `rf2-oq0ld` are referenced by commits but are not present in the current tracker.

## Uncertainties

The malformed-value verdict, raw exception, ordinary public dispatch, and genuine JVM production posture were executed. I did not compile a CLJS bundle for this review; ClojureScript must be pinned by acceptance because the user-facing SPA runtime is CLJS and its collection protocol could present a different accidental symptom. The exact reason keyword may follow the catalogue owner's convention; the required behavior is the always-on operation-specific rejection, not the suggested spelling.
design: Keep the correction at the existing shared structural gate, before `navigate-handler` resolves the current query or evaluates guards. A focused branch of the form “key present and value not map” is enough. Preserve the gate's existing precedence for unknown keys and mutually-exclusive forms; add one stable reason for the value-shape failure. Exercise both the pure classifier and the real dispatch path so a future refactor cannot leave the verdict disconnected from behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- With an active route, present non-map `:query-merge` values including `nil`, `[:page 2]`, and `"oops"` are rejected by the always-on navigate gate; the current route slice/query/nav-token are unchanged, no URL effect commits, and neither guard runs.
- In a debug-enabled run the rejection emits `:rf.error/navigate-bad-request` with a stable reason and `:keys [:query-merge]`; no raw host exception or generic handler-exception diagnostic is required to explain the misuse.
- The semantic rejection is proven in the routing production gate (`-Dre-frame.debug=false`) and in CLJS, not only by a dev-only schema/trace assertion. Include the two-element-vector case because it currently commits a real navigation on the JVM.
- Existing valid-map behavior remains pinned: `{}` is an exact no-op; map entries with nil values delete keys; false, zero, and empty-string values survive; caller deltas retain current precedence.
- Focused coverage lands in `routing_address_extraction_test.clj` for the classifier and `routing_navigation_test.clj` (plus the appropriate CLJS/prod witness) for the public dispatch behavior. Public API/spec prose states that the `:query-merge` value is a map if the current wording is not already explicit enough.

title: resources: reject non-function request handlers at registration
description:
## Finding

The public reg-resource and reg-mutation authoring boundary accepts any value in the required third request-fn slot. Both validators check only that the reconstructed spec contains :request, so 42 registers successfully. The runtime later invokes that value and the first ensure/execute fails with a raw host ClassCastException and nil ex-data.

This is a material correctness and ergonomics defect: a deterministic definition error survives application registration/boot and is displaced to the first user interaction, outside the library's structured registration-error contract.

## Governing contract

- spec/016-Resources.md:576-585 defines the strict three-slot forms and calls the third value a handler fn / request-fn.
- spec/016-Resources.md:752 and 1105 describe :request as the resource handler with signature (fn [params ctx] -> managed-http-args).
- docs/api/re-frame.resources.md:33-37 and 133-137 document request-fn as the third slot for resources and mutations.
- docs/resources/concepts.md:61-62 describes the same strict grammar.
- The sibling resource-scope registrar already enforces this shape with fn? in implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/scope_registry.cljc:311-321.

## Implementation evidence

- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc:260-384, especially 328-337: validate-resource-spec! checks only contains? for :request. reg-resource at 435-535 reconstructs metadata plus the unchecked third value before validation.
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_registry.cljc:59-183, especially 78-86: validate-mutation-spec! has the same presence-only check. reg-mutation at 187-296 stores the unchecked third value.
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:753-754 invokes (:request spec) unconditionally during ensure.
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc:1280-1283 invokes (:request spec) unconditionally during execute.
- Existing boundary tests cover missing/mislocated request and malformed metadata but not a non-function third slot: implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_skeleton_cljs_test.cljs:109-151 and implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_mutation_cljs_test.cljc:207-247.

## Verified behavior

Reproduced from implementation/resources at HEAD ac778f089a by registering a resource and mutation with valid metadata and integer request values:

    (r/reg-resource :review/nonfn-resource
      {:scope :rf.scope/global :params-schema [:map]} 42)
    (r/reg-mutation :review/nonfn-mutation
      {:params-schema [:map]} 42)

Both calls returned their IDs and both introspection APIs reported :request 42. Directly exercising ensure-handler and execute-handler then produced:

    :ensure  java.lang.ClassCastException ... Long cannot be cast to clojure.lang.IFn :ex-data nil
    :execute java.lang.ClassCastException ... Long cannot be cast to clojure.lang.IFn :ex-data nil

The reproduction process exited 0 because it caught and printed the exceptions; registration itself did not throw.

## Bounded recommendation

At the shared registration-validation boundary, require the reconstructed :request value to satisfy the library's documented function predicate, matching the existing reg-resource-scope convention. Reject a bad resource with :rf.error/resource-bad-spec and a bad mutation with :rf.error/mutation-bad-spec, include the definition ID and offending value/type in ex-data, use :recovery :fix-registration, and do so before registry mutation. Add focused resource and mutation registration regressions in the existing boundary suites.

Non-goals: do not introspect callback arity; do not invoke request functions during registration; do not validate the managed-HTTP result until normal invocation; do not broaden this bead into auditing every optional callback or redesigning metadata validation.

## Posture rationale

This is a small fail-fast guard on a core public API, not defensive gold-plating. It removes a low-information delayed crash and makes both human and AI-authored SPA definitions faster to diagnose while preserving the minimal three-slot API and trusting valid programmer-supplied functions.

## Duplicate and history search

Searched all bead statuses for request-fn, request function, non-fn, resource-bad-spec, mutation-bad-spec, ClassCastException, request handler, callable, and third slot; repeated description/notes searches for request-fn, request function, non-fn/non-function, and third slot. There was no matching resources issue. The only callable hit was closed rf2-6r9j.30 in reagent-slim; the only third-slot hit was closed rf2-td8oe about reg-resource-scope documentation.

Searched all Git refs by commit message and diff for the same terms plus fn?/request combinations. Commits 06303b9ade, 3d22a1d776, and 04c585b6aa introduced/migrated the strict request-fn grammar; 06261ac1a9 added metadata-slot guards; 56fe742fac introduced mutation registration. None validates request function-ness, and current-tree search finds no such guard or regression.

## Uncertainty

The contract and sibling registrar point to fn? rather than the broader ifn?. If deliberately supporting custom IFn objects is desired, that should be stated and tested explicitly; keywords/maps/sets should not become accidental request handlers merely because they are invokable on one host. Portable two-argument arity validation is intentionally outside scope.
acceptance_criteria:
- reg-resource synchronously rejects a non-function third request slot before registration, using :rf.error/resource-bad-spec with the resource ID, offending value/type, and :recovery :fix-registration in structured ex-data.
- reg-mutation does the same using :rf.error/mutation-bad-spec and the mutation ID.
- Focused tests in resources_skeleton_cljs_test.cljs and resources_mutation_cljs_test.cljc prove the invalid entries are not introspectable after rejection and valid request functions still register unchanged.
- The regressions run in every supported host exercised by those existing CLJS/CLJC suites and assert canonical structured errors rather than only matching host exception text.
- No callback arity probing, eager request invocation, managed-HTTP return validation, or optional-callback audit is added.
