title: tools/xray(popout): detached shell has no keyboard listener, so its keyboard workflow is inert
description:
CLAIM
`mount/popout!` renders a live shell into a second document, but Xray never attaches its keyboard listener to that document. DOM key events do not cross from the pop-out document to the opener document, so the keyboard-first Xray workflow is inert whenever focus is in the pop-out. The existing handler is also opener-surface-aware rather than pop-out-aware: its bare spine branch gates on `mount/visible?` (which reads only `mount-state`), and Cmd/Ctrl+K can call `mount/toggle!`, which controls the in-app shell rather than the already-visible pop-out.

EVIDENCE AT REVIEW TIP
Reviewed `cacace4e1803cfe6441d32b7ededa3b8da1a7fc1`; local `origin/main` has no later change to the relevant files.

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/keybinding.cljs:435-455`, `attach!`: a process-wide `attached-state` CAS installs exactly one capture listener, always on opener-realm `js/document`. `detach!` at :458-482 removes from that same `js/document`. There is no API for a second document.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs:1457-1541`, `popout!`: creates `win` / `doc`, injects styles, renders `shell-view`, installs opener-gone/lifecycle listeners, and records `popout-state`; it never installs a `keydown` listener on `doc`. `register-popout-unload-cleanup!` is pagehide/unload cleanup only.
- `mount.cljs:100-121`, `visible?` / `status`: visibility is derived only from `mount-state`; `popout-state` is a separate singleton. `keybinding.cljs:389-433`, `handle-keydown`: Cmd/Ctrl+K routes through `mount/toggle!` when that in-app state is hidden, while bare Space/L/j/k/G require `mount/visible?`. Even mechanically reusing the handler on the pop-out document without surface context would therefore be wrong when no inline shell is visible.
- `tools/xray/spec/API.md:842-849` explicitly describes `popout!` as its own document context with its own React root, theme cascade, and keybinding. `tools/xray/README.md:243-251` documents Cmd/Ctrl+K, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+M, and the in-shell Space/L/j/k/G workflow; its “not bound to a global chord” sentence is specifically about LAUNCHING the pop-out, not disabling keyboard operation inside it.
- Existing proof misses this boundary. `tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs:554-599` proves only that the pop-out root/shell exists; :1758-1845 proves shared cascade rendering under load, but sends no key in the pop-out. `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount_cljs_test.cljs:1485-1498` asserts only pagehide/unload registrations on the pop-out window. `keybinding_cljs_test.cljs` stubs the single ambient `js/document`, never a second document.

VERIFIED IMPACT
A programmer who moves Xray to a second monitor and gives that window focus cannot use the documented keyboard-first operations there: Cmd/Ctrl+K, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+M, Space/L/j/k/G, comma/s, or the contextual Esc path are never received by Xray. This is not an edge-case protocol concern; pop-out is a shipped top-bar action and the keyboard map is a primary low-friction debugging surface. Mouse controls and live data rendering still work, which makes the failure look like intermittent shortcut breakage rather than an unsupported mode.

BOUNDED RECOMMENDATION
Give each live pop-out document one lifecycle-owned keydown listener that reuses the canonical predicates/dispatch logic with explicit surface context. For a pop-out, “visible shell” means the pop-out shell, and Cmd/Ctrl+K must open its palette without mounting/reopening the in-app shell. Dispatch mode/spine/settings actions through the existing `:rf/xray` frame exactly as today. Remove the exact listener on pop-out pagehide/unload and `teardown!`; reopening must install one fresh listener, not accumulate handlers. Resolve the current mount<->keybinding dependency direction with the smallest internal hook or injected callback; do not duplicate the keyboard map.

NON-GOALS / POSTURE FIT
- No new shortcut for launching a pop-out (011's “No keybinding is wired pre-alpha” launch decision remains intact).
- No BroadcastChannel/postMessage protocol, second runtime, general multi-window registry, configurable chord editor, or per-panel pop-outs.
- No changes to opener-document attach/detach semantics or existing chords.
- Do not let Ctrl+Shift+C pressed in the pop-out accidentally toggle the opener's inline shell; either keep that opener-owned or define a narrowly surface-local behavior while implementing the listener.

This is one small lifecycle seam that restores an already-promised, high-frequency ergonomic contract; it does not expand Xray's API or feature set.

DUPLICATE / HISTORY SEARCH
All-status search used `bd list --all --limit 0 --json`: 17 Xray+keyboard hits and 9 popout hits, with no bead covering a listener or shortcuts in the pop-out document. Exact all-status searches for “popout keybinding”, “pop-out keybinding”, “popout shortcut”, “detached keybinding”, “own keybinding”, and “popout keydown” returned none. Closest beads are non-overlapping: closed `rf2-uong` handles opener reload staleness, closed `rf2-9vm0` removes a phantom `xrayRuntime` contract, and `rf2-jy64`/`rf2-v0rw` only repair keyboard-count prose. `git log --all` found no popout-keyboard fix; blame traces the own-keybinding contract to `c3efe341f8f` (2026-05-20) and the ambient-document attach to `67a1efc6706` (2026-05-13), with later hot-reload work preserving that one-document shape.

UNCERTAINTY
I did not compile or alter the worktree (the assignment forbids file edits and node_modules links). The missing registration is established directly by the only `addEventListener(..., "keydown", ...)` production call being against `js/document`, the complete `popout!` setup containing no such call, and the browser document event boundary. A focused browser regression is still required as acceptance because unit invocation of private `handle-keydown` would bypass the bug.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Opening Xray with `popout!` installs exactly one keydown listener on the pop-out document; external close, teardown, and reopen remove/recreate the exact listener without leaks or duplicate dispatch.
2. A focused browser test sends a documented in-shell spine key (j or k) in the pop-out and observes one corresponding focus step on the existing `:rf/xray` frame.
3. The browser test sends Cmd/Ctrl+K in the pop-out and observes the palette in that pop-out without mounting, showing, hiding, or reparenting the opener's inline/overlay shell.
4. Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+M and comma/s continue to route through the canonical keyboard map from the pop-out; editable/modal/activatable-target and repeat guards retain their current behavior.
5. A pop-out Ctrl+Shift+C does not mutate the opener's in-app mount accidentally, and the existing opener `keybinding/attach!`/`detach!` tests remain green.
6. Extend `keybinding_cljs_test.cljs` or `mount_cljs_test.cljs` for listener ownership/cleanup and `testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs` for the real two-document behavior; no duplicate chord table or new public API is introduced.

title: Canonical reply integration/security fixtures pin ledger work keys instead of envelope keys
description:
## Finding

Two contract-support suites build hand-authored maps that they call canonical managed-async reply envelopes, but put work identity on bare `:work/id` / `:work/kind`. Those are the durable work-ledger / verification-payload spellings. A transient reply envelope is single-rooted under `:rf.reply/work-id` / `:rf.reply/work-kind`.

This is not merely prose drift: the tests assert the bare keys and therefore positively pin the wrong record layer.

## Exact evidence

- `implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_reply_envelope_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:52-59` defines `canonical-reply` with top-level `:work/id` and `:work/kind`. Lines 87-91 call it a canonical uniform envelope; lines 114-124 call these canonical reply facts and assert the bare keys after ordinary event delivery. `rf.reply/valid-reply?` does not expose the mistake because the canonical work fields are conditional/optional to the generic validator and the unknown bare fields are allowed.
- `implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/reply_envelope_egress_security_cljs_test.cljc:52-88` feeds `trace-summary` a reply with bare `:work/id`, then explicitly calls the returned bare key canonical. The same stale spelling recurs in its framed, frameless, generated, suppression, and host-handle reply fixtures (notably lines 97-126, 131-160, 181-201, and 234-252). `trace-summary` projects only wire slots and otherwise preserves the supplied map, so these tests can stay green without ever proving that the canonical namespaced identity survives egress.
- `spec/Managed-Effects.md:92-100` shows live delivery with `:rf.reply/work-id`; lines 122-154 define the reply map, and line 151 explicitly distinguishes namespaced transient-envelope keys from bare durable-ledger / verification / `:current-work` keys. `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3582-3587` and 3622-3624 carry the same boundary.
- The comparison surface is already correct: `implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_egress_projection_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:91-105,174-176,212,253-254,277-278,370` uses and asserts `:rf.reply/work-id` / `:rf.reply/work-kind`; `reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` also reads family builders through those keys.
- History makes this an evidenced missed migration. Commits `01d9e4ae2f` (production), `084892baa2` / `e5e5a4aa84` (reply tests), and `2b1e536514` (spec) migrated the envelope to `:rf.reply/*` on 2026-07-09 under rf2-l7s7b7. Blame shows the bare fixture keys in both files remain from their 2026-06-17 introductions. Later 2026-09-03 event-conformance cleanup edited the surrounding assertions without correcting this layer mismatch.

## Impact

A regression that drops or reintroduces the wrong work-identity spelling at ordinary reply-event delivery or trace egress can leave these integration/security suites green, even though app handlers and tools consume the namespaced envelope contract for correlation. The fixtures also serve as executable examples, so preserving the ledger spelling here teaches a caller to read a key real family replies do not expose. The production builders currently appear correct; this is a meaningful contract-pin defect, not evidence of a current runtime leak.

## Bounded recommendation

Correct the two suites at the reply-map boundary:

1. Use `:rf.reply/work-id` and `:rf.reply/work-kind` for every top-level reply envelope and corresponding assertion.
2. Keep bare `:work/id` only where it is genuinely correlation/verification/ledger data, such as the carried/current maps passed to `reply/suppress`; do not mechanically rename those nested facts.
3. Add a small explicit tooth at each distinct boundary: ordinary delivered event and trace/suppression summary must retain the namespaced identity and must not grow top-level bare aliases.
4. Keep the existing status, redaction, stale non-delivery, and host-handle assertions intact.

## Non-goals

- No production API or runtime change.
- Do not rename durable work-ledger, verification-payload, entry `:current-work`, or carried/current gate keys.
- Do not tighten the generic reply validator into inferring whether arbitrary data is ledger-backed.
- Do not expand the family matrix, invent a second schema, or duplicate the broader egress suite.

## Posture rationale

This is a small correction at a user/tool-visible contract seam: one fact should have one spelling per record layer. Fixing the executable examples is lower-friction and more valuable than adding machinery. It protects ergonomic SPA continuation handling and debuggable correlation without litigating unrelated reply details.

## Duplicate search

An all-status in-memory scan covered 935 current beads across title, description, notes, design, acceptance criteria, and external ref for `rf.reply/work`, bare `work/id`, cross-record spelling, both fixture names, and work-id spelling. No bead owns this residual. The nearest closed issues are distinct: rf2-6r9j.217 renamed private event/reply roles only; rf2-6r9j.97 replaced a vacuous stale non-delivery row; rf2-6r9j.94 removed a duplicate generic projector row. Historical rf2-l7s7b7 is visible in the migration commits above, but its landed test migration missed these two files.

## Uncertainty

The runtime builders and the dedicated reply-conformance matrix appear canonical today, so the immediate risk is a false-green/misleading-fixture seam rather than a demonstrated production failure. The security file overlaps some projection coverage with reply-conformance, but its adversarial stale/host-handle rows remain independently useful; this issue asks only that their envelope inputs stop modeling the wrong layer.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every top-level reply envelope constructed in the two named suites uses `:rf.reply/work-id` and, where kind is present, `:rf.reply/work-kind`; bare `:work/id` remains only in genuine ledger/verification/carried-current correlation data.
2. The event integration test proves ordinary delivery preserves the namespaced work id/kind and does not expose top-level bare aliases.
3. The security reply-egress tests prove framed/frameless projection and stale suppression preserve canonical namespaced identity while retaining their existing leak, redaction, non-delivery, and data-only teeth.
4. Focused JVM and consolidated CLJS Node coverage for both suites passes.
5. A temporary focused mutation that removes or replaces the canonical namespaced work-id at each distinct boundary makes the new assertion red; the mutation is restored before handoff.

title: compile-node-test returns exit 0 when shadow-cljs is killed by a signal
description:
## Correctness finding

`implementation/scripts/compile-node-test.cjs` turns a signal-killed `shadow-cljs` child into an exit-0 wrapper result. Node's ChildProcess `close` event supplies `(code, signal)` and sets `code` to `null` when a signal terminated the child. `runCapturing` currently accepts only `status` (lines 185-203), so it discards the signal. `main` correctly enters its nonzero/abnormal branch because `null !== 0`, but returns `result.status` unchanged (lines 263-268). The CLI then executes `process.exit(code)` (lines 313-315); `process.exit(null)` is success.

This contradicts the wrapper's central contract: an aborted compile must fail loudly, never hand an orchestrator a green status. The stderr and process status currently disagree: the human sees "did not complete (exit null)" while automation sees 0.

## Steps to Reproduce

A read-only process-boundary probe required the real module, replaced only `node:child_process.spawn` with an EventEmitter child that emitted `close(null, "SIGTERM")`, patched only `require.resolve` for the unused shadow runner path, and used an output path proven absent before and after. The real exported `main` and real CLI terminal operation produced:

```
compile-node-test: shadow-cljs compile signal-proof did not complete (exit null); out/codex-reviewpool-d-signal-proof-never-created.js was cleared before the attempt, not left stale.
RETURNED=null
OBSERVED_CLI_EXIT=0
```

Independent runtime controls produced `NODE_PROCESS_EXIT_NULL=0` and `NODE_PROCESS_EXIT_UNDEFINED=0`. The proof target remained absent and the worktree remained clean.

Source/history evidence:

- `runCapturing` was introduced in commit `91d7f6050b` when the wrapper moved from `spawnSync` to streaming `spawn`; that change retained the older `return result.status` branch from `01c54d87fd` but stopped carrying `spawnSync`'s `signal` field or the async close callback's second argument.
- `implementation/package.json` has five consumers of the wrapper (`test:cljs`, `test:cljs-isolation`, `test:security`, `test:testbed-support`, `test:cljs-perf-emit-nightly`). They normally chain a second command with `&&`, and because the wrapper deletes the output first, a signal before output emission will usually fail at that later command. That limits the current blast radius; it does not make this status truthful. A signal after emission can also leave a runnable output, and direct callers see the false success immediately.
- Repository census found direct compile-only usage documented in `docs/design/hicasso/defhost-ssr-provider-costing.md` and two certification records. No current CI workflow invokes the wrapper alone; current CI reaches it through the chained npm scripts.

## Impact

A developer, agent, or future gate that invokes this explicitly documented compile wrapper and checks its exit status can record a successful compile after OOM/administrative child termination, even though the wrapper itself says compilation did not complete. In chained npm lanes the missing-output defence often makes the overall command red one step later, but that gives worse feedback and is not guaranteed once an output was written. Gate status is an API to automation; contradictory red text plus exit 0 is particularly hazardous for AI/human orchestration.

## Bounded fix

Capture the `signal` argument from the ChildProcess close event and normalize every signal/`null`-status completion to a nonzero wrapper result (a stable 1 is sufficient), while naming the signal in the existing diagnostic. Preserve real numeric child exit codes. Keep output pre-deletion, warning-tally parsing, config-merge cache cleanup, streaming output, and the five package commands unchanged.

Do not build a general signal-forwarding/process-tree framework, redesign cancellation, alter shadow-cljs, or change the runner's compilation/warning policy. This is one outcome-normalization seam plus a focused regression test.

## Posture fit

The fix is a tiny honesty repair at a high-leverage tooling boundary: programmers and agents should be able to trust a command's exit code without learning Node's `null` signal convention. It improves low-friction feedback without adding API surface or speculative infrastructure.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status searches covered title/description/notes for `compile-node-test`, `exit null`, `process.exit(null)`, `terminated by signal`, `SIGTERM`, `return result.status`, `child signal`, `child-only`, `status null`, and `exit status null`; no bead owns this outcome. Closed `rf2-7r9w` is distinct: it corrected a pair-MCP consumer that treated shadow-cljs's successful compile status as an autorun TEST verdict. This finding is the wrapper converting an OS-signal/abnormal compile termination into success. Historical commit/bead citations `rf2-6t03c` and `rf2-4a6ei` created and hardened this wrapper for stale output and warning tallies; neither exists in the current tracker and neither handled the signal-null branch.

## Uncertainty

No real shadow/JVM process was killed in this review; the deterministic probe exercised the real wrapper logic with Node's documented/actual close-event shape. The canonical npm scripts normally become nonzero later when their deleted bundle is missing, and no current CI workflow was found calling the wrapper alone. The confirmed defect is the wrapper's own false exit status; how often a real child-only signal leaves the parent alive or leaves a runnable emitted bundle is environment-dependent.
acceptance_criteria:
- Add a focused process-boundary or equivalently faithful contract test in the existing compile-wrapper test surface: a child outcome `(code=null, signal=SIGTERM)` makes the CLI exit nonzero and the diagnostic names SIGTERM or clearly says signal termination. The test must fail against the current implementation by observing exit 0.
- Preserve ordinary outcome mapping: a numeric child exit 0 continues into output/tally validation, and representative nonzero numeric statuses remain nonzero rather than being collapsed to success.
- Preserve output pre-deletion, config-merge cache cleanup before and after the child, streamed stdout/stderr, missing-output rejection, and warning-tally rejection.
- The existing compile-node-test warning parser/self-tests and implementation JS harness tests pass.
- No general process supervisor, new public option, environment waiver, or package-script redesign is introduced.

title: hic: RULING — can a protocol section whose subject was retired discharge its ledger row? (rf2-s52w / rf2-hic-038 §2)
description:
Filed by rf2-nf8w's closure re-run (2026-09-04, main@4f54988b07). NOT a repair bead: the deliverable is one operator ruling.

THE SITUATION. correction-ledger.md's rf2-s52w row (rf2-hic-038 §2 Correctness, outward-bridge mismatch attribution) reads 'resolved'. Its own stated condition for 'closed' is the §2 Correctness section re-run against landed main, passing. rf2-nf8w took that re-run. Result: of §2's four conjuncts, three pass with captured exits (three-way matrix node lane 11170/55743 exit 0, browser lane 783/4253 exit 0; bundle gate exit 0 with both self-tests and both scans; parity-witness naming verified on inspection) and ONE CANNOT BE RUN AT ALL — 'independently re-run the native-language-leakage sabotages'. Its subject was deleted under it by aa01f0e8a6 (2026-08-29, rf2-6c12m.31, wave 2 of ruling rf2-6c12m.3 Option A): native.cljc went 1116 lines to 82, the grammar and prop-slots went with it, and the eight native_* suites (91 deftests, 5234 lines) including native_fence_cljs_test.cljs were deleted. There is no plant to make and no witness to redden.

WHY A WORKER CANNOT DECIDE IT. Both available readings move a row, and the ledger's rule allows neither on this evidence. Reading A: a section is discharged by re-running the conjuncts that still have a subject, so the row closes on the evidence above. Reading B: the row closes as 'withdrawn — the surface the finding is about was retired', which is the transition this ledger already provides for a finding that is no longer live. Reading C: it stays 'resolved' permanently, which is what it does today. rf2-nf8w left it at 'resolved' and wrote the full evidence into the cell, because writing 'closed' on a partial re-run is exactly the failure mode the ledger's 'resolved is not closed' section exists to prevent.

WHAT IS NOT AT STAKE. The rf2-hic-064 gate's colour. PR #9181 (ff79cc1a2d) appended that audit's own seven rows, all 'open' by construction, so the ledger now reads 41 rows with 8 unresolved. Clearing rf2-s52w would not make the correction-ledger conjunct green, so this ruling is about the ledger's integrity and not about unblocking anything.

WHAT IS ALSO TRUE, so the ruling is taken on the merits. The finding's MECHANISM is untouched and still holds at tip: impl/roots.cljs:23 states onRecoverableError is an option of an individual hydrateRoot, so a root the consumer opens carries no framework reporter. What has gone is the outward BRIDGE that made it reachable. And the requirement itself was already narrowed by 137bd927db (PR #8646, rf2-0brem) to owe mismatch attribution only on roots a re-frame2 door opens.

THE GENERAL QUESTION BEHIND IT, which is why this is worth one ruling rather than one edit: rf2-s52w is the first row to hit this, and it will not be the last. Checkpoints 1-4 score surfaces the rf2-6c12m waves have been retiring since 2026-08-29, so any future closure bead against a retired surface meets the same wall. A ruling that names the general rule settles the class.
acceptance_criteria: One operator ruling recorded on this bead saying which of the three readings governs a ledger row whose protocol section has lost its subject, stated generally enough to cover the next one; and the rf2-s52w row in correction-ledger.md transitioned (or explicitly left) to match, by the ledger keeper.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9185 (2026-09-04, merge cacace4e18) — CORRECTED THIS RULING'S PREMISE.

Do not rule rf2-s52w on the premise that its subject or outward bridge was retired. h/as-component and its current foreign-root bridge suite remain. Only one conjunct of the old §2 protocol — the native-language-leakage sabotage — and the old native_abi mismatch witness were deleted with the native authoring grammar. Thus reading B (withdraw because the surface is retired) is not available for rf2-s52w as written. The general question about a protocol whose one conjunct lost its subject may remain, but it must be separated from the live outward-bridge finding and coordinated with rf2-o8qk and reopened rf2-nf8w.

title: mcp-conformance: Windows hermetic cleanup grades the npx wrapper, not the shadow-cljs JVM
description:
## Correctness finding

The live hermetic runner can emit its GREEN sentinel and exit 0 on Windows after only the direct `cross-spawn` wrapper exits, while the shadow-cljs JVM descendant remains alive.

`makeCleanup` grades shadow teardown solely from `hasShadowExited()` (`tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/run-re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite.cjs:367-414`). That predicate is driven solely by the `exit` event on the child returned by `crossSpawn(...)` (`:1013-1021`, wired at `:1041-1044`). On Windows, the exact installed cross-spawn 7.0.6 parsing path turns the trusted bare `C:\Program Files\nodejs\npx` into `C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe /d /s /c ...` targeting `npx.CMD`. The returned handle therefore represents the command wrapper, not the downstream shadow-cljs JVM. Node's official child-process documentation explicitly warns that killing a shell child does not terminate the child processes it launched.

The current unit model collapses those separate lifetimes into one EventEmitter: `makeFakeShadow().kill()` emits that same fake object's `exit` (`tools/mcp-conformance/test/runner-cleanup.test.cjs:61-71`). It proves direct-child timing and escalation, but cannot detect a wrapper that exits while a grandchild survives.

## Impact

This defeats the verifier's defining hermetic guarantee. A false-green run can leave the shadow/JVM/watch server holding the fixture's fixed port 8030 (`run-re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite.cjs:65`) and runtime metadata, contaminating or wedging the next human/AI run or causing it to exercise stale state. This is a certification defect rather than cosmetic cleanup: `finalizeConformance` converts `report.clean` into the pass sentinel and exit 0 (`:420-440`, `:1361-1368`).

## Evidence and history

- Read-only execution of the exact installed cross-spawn parser yielded command `C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe`, `/d /s /c` arguments, and `file=C:\Program Files\nodejs\npx.CMD` for the runner's spawn shape.
- Read-only local process-table inspection confirmed shadow's ordinary Node-to-Java descendant shape.
- Node's primary documentation covers both Windows `.cmd` shell handling and the fact that killing a shell does not terminate its child processes: https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html
- Cross-spawn's primary source/documentation confirms its `.cmd` shim handling: https://github.com/moxystudio/node-cross-spawn
- Commit `ba8c8a20d6` introduced dirty teardown grading specifically so a leaked shadow JVM/port-8030 owner cannot pass, but the implementation equates wrapper exit with JVM exit.
- The repository already has a scoped Windows process-tree precedent: `scripts/test-core-jvm-windows.ps1:163-171` uses `taskkill.exe /pid <owned-root> /T /F`; `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh:697-762` documents and handles the native descendant tree.

## Bounded fix

Make Windows teardown own, terminate, and grade the process tree rooted at the exact PID spawned by this runner. Adapt the existing scoped `/T` pattern, or use a graceful shadow stop with that verified fallback, while the root relationship is still observable. Do not mark cleanup clean merely because the npx/cmd wrapper emitted `exit`. Keep current POSIX behavior unless an equivalent demonstrated defect requires a change.

Add a small regression fixture/test that separates wrapper exit from grandchild liveness. Prefer an outcome-focused local helper or test seam over a generic process-supervision abstraction.

## Posture fit

This is a narrow truthfulness and ergonomics repair using a process-tree pattern already proven in the repository. It makes the powerful one-command hermetic verifier trustworthy and removes expensive rerun contamination for programmers and their AI tools, without adding public API or framework machinery.

## Non-goals

- Dynamic or parallel port allocation.
- A generic cross-platform process supervisor.
- Global stale-process reaping or killing unrelated Java/Node processes.
- Redesigning the fixture or MCP wire contracts.
- Expanding the host matrix.

## Duplicate check

Focused `rg` searches over `.beads/issues.jsonl` for mcp-conformance combined with Windows, cleanup, teardown, orphan, JVM, 8030, npx, and server.pid, plus exact symptom phrases, found no issue owning this outcome. Related closed `rf2-j538f7.19`/commit `ba8c8a20d6` established the intended guarantee but did not handle descendants; closed `rf2-ahjbc` and `rf2-a9l6e` have different scopes. A tracker memory records prior observed Windows false-green leftovers, but this finding was independently established from the runner, dependency source, platform semantics, process hierarchy, tests, and history.

## Uncertainty

The live suite was not booted in the review worktree because that would require the prohibited dependency link/install and runtime mutations; no process was listening on 8030 during inspection. The exact cross-spawn transformation, direct-handle control flow, official Node semantics, repository process-tree precedent, and observed Node-to-Java hierarchy establish the mechanism. The implementer should choose the smallest graceful-stop/tree-kill detail and verify the outcome below.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A regression launches or faithfully models a Windows wrapper with a separately long-lived grandchild; wrapper exit alone cannot produce `shadow.clean === true` or the overall GREEN sentinel.
2. Normal cleanup and SIGTERM/SIGKILL/watchdog paths terminate the runner-owned shadow process tree within the existing bounds; unrelated Node/JVM processes are never targeted.
3. Cleanup returns dirty, exit 2, and no pass sentinel whenever owned-descendant teardown cannot be proven.
4. Two consecutive Windows hermetic-suite runs both pass from their own state; after each, no fixture-owned process/listener remains on port 8030 and the next run does not trust stale runtime metadata.
5. Existing browser cleanup, live-test inventory, trusted-executable checks, wire assertions, sentinels, and exit-code contracts remain green.

title: story: Step Debugger Start runs the script before step 1
description:
## Finding

The Test-mode Step Debugger does not start from pre-play state for the normal/default `:script` shape. `re-frame.story.ui.test-mode.stepper-state/begin!` says it re-allocates the frame "so the run starts fresh," but at `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/stepper_state.cljs:104-147` it calls `(rf.story.runtime/reset-variant variant-id)` and waits for that promise before calling `begin-stepper!` and publishing cursor 0. `reset-variant` is deliberately a full rerun: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc:1715-1728` destroys the frame and delegates to `run-variant`; `run-variant` enters `run-phase-4!` (`runtime.cljc:979ff`, `:1260ff`), where `auto-runnable-plays` executes the script. Bare `:script` defaults `:auto-run?` to true (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/runner.cljc:324-356`). `begin-stepper!` (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play.cljc:366-385`) then merely seeds the complete script into `:remaining`; it does not restore setup state. The UI therefore says "ready · N steps" with cursor 0 while app-db already reflects all N mutating steps.

This is reproduced against current production JVM primitives at HEAD `2c61dafd702db9672163ee9d2028db34c70c978d`, not inferred from prose. A registered variant with `:setup [[:probe/seed 0]]` and three default-auto-run `[:dispatch-sync [:probe/inc]]` steps, followed by the same `reset-variant -> begin-stepper!` sequence used by the CLJS UI, printed:

`{:after-reset {:count 3}, :frame-db {:count 3}, :stepper {:remaining [inc inc inc], :ran []}}`

The existing prepare-only lifecycle proves the expected shape is already available: the same probe through `runtime/prepare-run!` (documented at `runtime.cljc:1364-1378` as phases 0-2 "WITHOUT executing the play script") printed:

`{:prepared-frame-db {:count 0}, :stepper {:remaining [inc inc inc], :ran []}}`

The repository's own exemplary `:story.counter/clicked-three-times` makes the user-visible failure concrete (`tools/story/testbeds/counter_with_stories/stories.cljs:353-375`): setup seeds 0 and the script increments three times. Pressing Start first advances it to 3 while displaying cursor 0; pressing Step once advances it to 4 while displaying "step 1". Rewind restores the incorrectly captured post-script epoch (3), not the specified initial state (0). This contradicts `tools/story/spec/009-Test-Mode.md:462` (`begin!` re-allocate + prime), `:465`, `:482`, and `:498-501` (rewind restores the pre-play state), plus `tools/story/README.md:28-34` (canvas reflects each step's app-db).

## Impact

This is not a cosmetic counter mismatch: the debugger repeats every default-auto-run interaction and side effect before the programmer can inspect step 1. State mutations, HTTP stubs/effects, DOM gestures, and assertions may execute twice, and displayed cursor/outcomes describe a different run from the frame being debugged. A debugging tool that changes the program before presenting its initial state is actively misleading to both SPA authors and agents.

## Bounded recommendation

Make Step Debugger Start allocate/prepare the variant only through the pre-play lifecycle (loaders/setup, phases 0-2), then capture that epoch and seed `begin-stepper!`; do not call a full `reset-variant`/phase-4 run. Reuse the existing prepare-only runtime path or extract the narrow shared primitive it already embodies rather than duplicating lifecycle logic. Keep `reset-variant`, ordinary shell auto-run, and `:auto-run?` semantics unchanged.

Non-goals: redesigning the stepper controls or script DSL; changing normal run/reset behavior; changing the default `:auto-run?`; solving multi-play selection; a broad runtime ownership rewrite.

## Acceptance

1. Add a CLJS/browser regression using a mutating default-auto-run script: immediately after Start, cursor is 0 and frame app-db is setup state (for example count 0), not post-script state (3).
2. The first Step executes exactly the first script step once (count 1); subsequent steps remain 1:1 with cursor, and Rewind returns to setup/pre-play state (count 0).
3. Assert no script checkpoint, effect, or terminal phase-4 work runs as part of Start itself; failures in preparation still return the section to an honest inactive/error state.
4. Existing `run-variant`/`reset-variant` full-run behavior and ordinary on-mount auto-run remain unchanged.
5. Exercise `begin!` itself (or the Start DOM path), not only a directly seeded local slot.

## Why the current gates miss it

`tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/stepper_state_cljs_test.cljs:25-27` explicitly seeds slots "without going through begin!" and has no begin test. The only live Start probe is `tools/story/test/story_feature_load.cjs:829-881`; it uses `:story.counter/loaded`, whose script is assertions only (`stories.cljs:340-346`), and checks controls/progress but never frame app-db. Thus the full `clojure -M:test` suite is green (1889 tests, 6959 assertions, 0 failures/errors) while this path is wrong.

## Duplicate and history check

Targeted `rg` against `.beads/issues.jsonl` found no title/body occurrence of `stepper-state`, `step-debugger`, `play stepper`, `begin-stepper!`, `pre-play epoch`, or `step-by-step run`; broader title scans for reset/auto-run/debugger found no matching Story issue. Git history shows the reset-before-begin sequence dates to the feature's original commit `c5f6ca44c15` / rf2-ulw5m (#1390). That commit advertised a full Start -> Step -> Back -> Rewind -> Stop browser flow but deliberately used `:story.counter/loaded`; later `c438c6cfaf` / rf2-4e545l fixed step-back epoch indexing while continuing to assume `begin!`'s seed was truly pre-play. No commit fixes or tracks this start-state defect.

## Uncertainty

The CLJS browser lane was not run because this dedicated review worktree has no `node_modules` and the review assignment forbade creating a link. The exact production lifecycle composition reproduces on the JVM, and the CLJS `begin!` calls those same cross-platform runtime/play functions around a JS Promise. The implementation worker should choose the cleanest way to carry the current shell run context into the existing prepare-only seam, but that integration choice does not affect the demonstrated phase-4-before-cursor bug.

## Posture fit

This is one high-leverage correction to a marquee programming tool, using an existing lifecycle split. It removes deception and friction without adding author-facing API or general machinery.

title: story-mcp: reject unknown run-option identifiers instead of executing a different scenario
description:
## Problem

`preview-variant`, `run-variant`, and `snapshot-identity` advertise `:active-modes` and `:cell-overrides` as scenario/identity inputs, but their shared MCP coercer silently removes unknown identifiers.

- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/args.cljc:311-315` resolves active modes with `(keep #(args/safe-keyword % mode-set))`; a typo or stale mode disappears.
- `args.cljc:125-144` resolves override keys against the effective arg-key allowlist and explicitly drops misses; its contract says a typo'd override “simply doesn't apply.”
- All three handlers run only shape and substrate guards before consuming those filtered opts (`tools/dev.cljc:134-143`; `tools/testing.cljc:96-106,183-185`). Preview also builds the share URL from the filtered tuple.
- `tools_test.clj:4570-4582` pins the loss by expecting an unknown override key to be dropped. There is no handler-level diagnostic for an unknown mode or override key.

These values are semantically material. `spec/API.md:414-417` says cell overrides are identity-bearing, and `tools/testing.cljc:337-341` says mode/override changes produce a different snapshot hash. The focused Story consumer contract says runtime resolution is tolerant so UI/play can ignore stale modes, but “tools surface the mismatch as a validation warning” (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/args.cljc:85-89`); Story-MCP currently does not.

The MCP boundary's established ergonomic rule points the other way: unknown argument keys are rejected because otherwise an agent gets “a successful-looking call that silently defaulted” (`tools/wire_pipeline.cljc:178-205`); malformed run-option shapes are likewise called a “successful-looking WRONG result” and rejected on all three tools (`tools_test.clj:1253-1290`). History confirms the exact failure class is material: commit `b4477057` changed a silently dropped explicit substrate to an error because an agent could believe the requested render substrate was honoured; `0d224b1e` made unknown top-level knobs fail loudly for the same reason; `0c9de86f` records a dropped override producing the wrong render value. The older `8c1b9dc6` no-intern change introduced today's drop, but no-interning does not require success.

## Impact

An agent can request dark/high-contrast/etc., typo the mode or override key, then receive `:status :pass`, a share URL, or a visual-regression hash for the default/different tuple. That is false test evidence at precisely the automation boundary intended to make Story productive for AI. The programmer gets no short recovery loop and may bless the wrong state.

## Bounded fix

Add one shared semantic run-options guard in `tools.args`, reused by the three existing handlers after shape/substrate validation and before lifecycle/hash/share work:

1. Resolve every supplied active-mode id against the live mode set without interning. If any are unresolved, return one `isError true` result carrying the raw unknown strings and an actionable `list-modes` recovery hint; do not partially execute known modes.
2. Once all modes are valid, derive the existing effective arg-key allowlist and reject unresolved `:cell-overrides` keys the same way (raw strings, no interning; report the bounded allowed set or direct the agent to the variant/effective-args read).
3. Use the same stable structured error shape across preview/run/snapshot and describe the behavior in their descriptors, API, and wire contract.

## Non-goals / posture

Do not change tolerant Story runtime or UI hydration. Do not add a generic validation framework, fuzzy matching/autocorrection, a new tool, a second registry, or keyword interning, and do not broaden which override keys are legal. This is one MCP-boundary guard around existing allowlists. Passive UI hydration may reasonably discard stale persisted state; an explicit agent command should fail loudly rather than certify another tuple. The change trusts the programmer, keeps the API minimal, and removes false confidence without gold-plating.

## Duplicate and history audit

A targeted `rg` over `.beads/issues.jsonl` for unknown/reject/drop/ignore near `active-modes` or `cell-overrides` returned no matches; the wider Story-MCP issue inventory has no open issue on this behavior. Related historical work is distinct: rf2-3luf3 / `8c1b9dc6` is no-intern ingress; rf2-to3q7 / `0c9de86f` fixes the allowed-key universe; rf2-ldfrp0 / `f6b82ab8` rejects wrong container shapes; rf2-3fc89f.21 / `b4477057` handles substrate/capability; rf2-ovmc5e / `0d224b1e` handles unknown top-level knobs. Those are precedents and leave these nested semantic identifiers untouched.

## Uncertainty

The silent behavior was deliberate in the original security hardening, so this is a recommended MCP-boundary policy correction rather than an accidental branch typo. The security invariant remains satisfiable by reporting raw strings without interning them.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each of `preview-variant`, `run-variant`, and `snapshot-identity` returns `isError true` for a supplied unknown active-mode id, names the raw rejected value, and does not invoke lifecycle/hash/share work.
- A mixed known+unknown mode list rejects atomically rather than running the known subset.
- Each tool rejects an unknown cell-override key instead of running or hashing with it removed; the diagnostic names the raw key and gives a bounded recovery path.
- Existing valid modes and overrides remain unchanged, including the mode-introduced override case at `tools_test.clj:4584-4608`.
- Wire-level regression probes prove random unknown mode values and override keys remain uninterned.
- Descriptor/spec text states that absent options default but present unknown identifiers fail loudly.
- Focused Story-MCP tests pass.

title: bug(mcp-base): sorted collection comparators crash default-on structural dedup when cache refs replace keys or elements
description:
## Scope

Make the shared structural-dedup walk in tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc safe for ordinary persistent sorted maps and sorted sets. Add focused cross-host base coverage and one small Story-MCP wire-boundary integration pin. Keep the dedup wire format, reference grammar, envelope, default-on posture, and public tool APIs unchanged.

## Correctness finding

The generic side-walk rebuilds each collection with (into (empty form) (map inner form)). During the substitution pass, process-element replaces a repeated cacheable subtree with a de-dupe.cache/cache-N symbol. If that subtree occurs as a sorted-map key or sorted-set element, the original collection comparator receives the temporary symbol.

A default sorted collection with one replaced vector key/element and one unreplaced vector key/element therefore compares a Symbol with an IPersistentVector and throws ClassCastException. This is valid persistent application data, not a malformed cache or hostile input. The default-on shrink step turns an otherwise successful AI/devtools read into a boundary failure.

## Evidence

- tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc:351-363 documents side-walk as recognizing every Clojure collection, then rebuilds the generic coll branch into (empty form).
- dedup.cljc:369-381 makes vectors longer than two elements cacheable.
- dedup.cljc:480-497 replaces a repeated cacheable subtree with a cache-element symbol before the enclosing collection is rebuilt.
- The measured stack reaches PersistentTreeMap.assoc through clojure.core/into and re_frame.mcp_base.dedup$side_walk at dedup.cljc:362.
- tools/mcp-base/spec/dedup.md:8-17 says the codec walks persistent data and expand reconstructs it exactly; lines 36-45 make de-dupe-eq and its exact inverse the owned surface.
- tools/mcp-base/test/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup_test.cljc:425-436 is named expand-round-trips-every-collection-kind, but covers list, seq, hash-set, and nested hash maps only. It never puts a cacheable repeat in a comparator-bearing key/element position.
- The real Story consumer reproduces the same throw through re-frame.story-mcp.tools.wire-pipeline/apply-dedup. tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/wire_pipeline.cljc:121-161 applies the base transform to structuredContent; lines 373-406 place it after the handler catch.
- Story run-variant and preview-variant are default-on dedup-eligible and carry app-db/snapshot values (tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/testing.cljc:305-319 and tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/dev.cljc:223-237).
- Pair-MCP's epoch/snapshot paths call the same default-on dedup-value (tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/wire_pipeline.cljs:167-200 and snapshot_pipeline.cljs:245-261).
- Sorted maps are explicitly legitimate SPA state in this repository: examples/core/todomvc/db.cljs:28-30,40-50,65-82 says its sorted map is non-incidental. That example's numeric keys do not trigger this exact comparator mismatch, but the collection class is deliberately supported application state.

## Steps to Reproduce

From tools/mcp-base, evaluate the real codec with shared-key [1 2 3], unique-key [4 5 6], and:

    {:index (sorted-map shared-key :old unique-key :new)
     :again shared-key}

Call (dedup/dedup-value payload true).

Observed controls and failure:

- The equivalent hash-map shape returns a real rf.mcp/dedup-table wrapper and expand round-trips true.
- The sorted-map shape with dedup disabled passes through and remains equal.
- The sorted-map shape with dedup enabled throws java.lang.ClassCastException: clojure.lang.Symbol cannot be cast to clojure.lang.IPersistentVector.
- Replacing sorted-map with sorted-set produces the same ClassCastException.
- Passing the sorted-map payload through Story-MCP wire-pipeline/apply-dedup with enabled true throws the identical exception.

## Failure scenario / invariant

An SPA stores an index in a sorted map keyed by path vectors. Across epoch snapshots, or across Story's app-db/snapshot/evidence duplication, an existing vector key repeats while a newly added vector key appears only once. Dedup substitutes the repeated key with a cache symbol, rebuilds it beside the unique vector key through the tree comparator, and the AI's read fails instead of returning state.

Invariant: default wire shrinking must accept ordinary persistent sorted maps/sets and either compress them or safely keep comparator-position values inline. It must never feed codec-only placeholders into a collection comparator that cannot compare them.

## Recommended minimal fix

Make the shared CLJC walk comparator-safe specifically for sorted maps and sorted sets. The smallest likely rule is to lower sorted collections to comparator-neutral wire maps/sets before placeholder substitution; EDN/JSON does not preserve a custom comparator in any case. Another acceptable small rule is to keep comparator positions inline while still handling their descendants, provided the existing reference-collision escaping remains correct.

Choose one local rule in the shared walker. Preserve semantic Clojure equality on expand and retain a real dedup win for repeated data. Do not add a fallback serialization framework or a second codec.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A cross-host dedup_test.cljc regression builds a default sorted-map with two vector keys and repeats only one key elsewhere, forcing the pre-fix mixed Symbol/vector comparator case. dedup-value with enabled true does not throw, produces a real dedup-table wrapper with a substitution beyond cache-0, and expand is equal to the input.
2. The same root cause is pinned compactly for sorted-set elements so both comparator-bearing core collection shapes cannot regress.
3. Story-MCP wire-pipeline/apply-dedup accepts the sorted-map structuredContent and keeps its text and structuredContent slots consistent rather than throwing. No consumer production logic should be needed.
4. An unordered-map control still wraps and round-trips, and enabled false remains strict pass-through. The de-dupe.cache/cache-N grammar, rf.mcp/dedup-table wrapper, cache-0 root, defaults, and tool names/arguments do not change.
5. Focused mcp-base JVM dedup, mcp-base CLJS, and Story-MCP dedup suites pass. A red control restoring the comparator-unsafe branch reproduces the focused failure before restore.

## Non-goals

- Preserving or serializing sorted comparator identity across EDN/JSON.
- A general serializer, arbitrary Java collection support, or an exhaustive exotic-collection taxonomy.
- Changing equality-vs-identity pooling, compression thresholds, default-on behavior, cache-id allocation, or the wire format.
- Optimizing compression ratios beyond retaining the existing real substitution.
- Combining malformed hand-authored cache hardening (dangling references or cycles); the earlier rf2-kjv05 explicitly left that separate case out of scope.

## Posture fit

This is one local correctness repair at an existing generic boundary: valid SPA state should be transparent to default-on AI tooling. It adds no public API and does not litigate every collection detail.

## Related / duplicate search

An all-status rg census covered all 938 issue records in .beads/issues.jsonl and was repeated against origin/main. Searches covered sorted-map, sorted map, sorted-set, sorted set, comparator, PersistentTreeMap, side-walk, empty form, cacheable map key, ClassCastException, dedup, de-dupe, and mcp-base across titles/descriptions/notes. No issue owns this outcome.

Closest records are not duplicates:

- rf2-kjv05 (closed) owns reference-token collisions between payload data and cache ids. Its implementation notes explicitly leave malformed dangling-cache behavior as a non-goal; it does not cover valid sorted collections or comparator failure.
- rf2-6r9j.238 (closed) only corrects the private cacheability predicate's spelling.
- rf2-ntbd1 (closed) proposed relocating the pair-only diff codec and was rejected as gold-plating; it does not concern dedup collection semantics.

Git history confirms the generic (into (empty form) ...) branch is unchanged since vendoring commit 9a4f5553f4 (2026-07-27). Later dedup commits change reference escaping and naming, not sorted-collection handling. No matching commit subject was found.

## Uncertainty

The failure is directly reproduced on the JVM in both mcp-base and the real Story wire adapter. CLJS was not executed during this read-only review because the dedicated worktree has no node_modules and the review explicitly prohibited creating a junction. The comparator-unsafe branch is shared CLJC, but the acceptance test must establish the CLJS result rather than treating that as proven.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-host base regressions cover mixed substituted/unsubstituted vector keys in a default sorted-map and elements in a sorted-set, force a real dedup wrapper, and prove expand equality without a comparator exception. Story apply-dedup returns consistent text/structured slots for the same payload. Unordered and disabled controls remain intact; wire grammar and tool API are unchanged. Focused JVM, CLJS, and Story dedup suites pass with a red control for the pre-fix branch.

title: bug(pair-mcp): get-path turns operating-frame ambiguity into false missing-path answers
description:
## Finding

`get-path` does not honor Pair's normative operating-frame refusal. With no explicit `frame`, `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/get_path.cljs:170-175` emits `(re-frame2-pair.runtime/snapshot)` and separately uses `(current-frame)` only as an elision option. Runtime `snapshot` (`skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:394-399`) calls `(rf/app-db-value (current-frame))` directly. In a genuine multi-app session with no pin, `current-frame` returns nil (`runtime.cljs:303-318`), and `rf/app-db-value nil` returns nil for the unregistered frame (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1918-1925`). The singular form then runs `get-in` against nil and constructs `{:ok? false :reason :path-not-found ...}` (`get_path.cljs:55-95`); the batch form constructs a successful map in which every requested path is `{:exists? false :value nil}` (`get_path.cljs:97-126`). The tool is answering a different question than the caller asked.

This contradicts the authoritative Tool-Pair contract: every frame-targeted call must resolve explicit override -> session pin -> sole app frame -> nil (`spec/Tool-Pair.md:477-490`), and a tier-4 read must refuse with `:ambiguous-frame`, never read another/default frame (`spec/Tool-Pair.md:506-516`). The Pair-MCP descriptor says `frame` defaults to the operating frame (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs:1044-1045`). The preload itself explains that callers must turn nil into a clear refusal (`runtime.cljs:311-315`), and sibling reads already do so: `sub-cache-info` calls `ambiguous-frame-error` at `runtime.cljs:1024-1028`; `read-sub!` does the same at `runtime.cljs:1118-1119`.

History makes the omission legible: the generated `snapshot` call in get-path dates to 2026-05-31 (`git blame` commit `410f2202a43`), while the reserved-aware operating-frame policy arrived 2026-06-02 (`28cc8c959b`) and subsequently tightened; that policy commit did not touch `get_path.cljs`. Current conformance fixtures cover happy/missing-arg/path-miss by stubbing the eval result (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/conformance_test.cljs:1195-1232`), so they never execute the emitted browser form under a multi-frame runtime.

## Impact

In the exact situation where frame identity matters most, an agent/programmer receives false evidence about application state. A singular query sends them down a pointless path-discovery chase; a batch query can falsely assert that several values are absent. The recovery that already exists (`available-frames` plus the `set-operating-frame`/explicit-frame hint) is withheld. This is a correctness break and avoidable pairing friction, not a request for more machinery.

## Bounded fix

Make both singular and batch get-path forms resolve the target frame once before reading app-db. If resolution is nil, return the existing runtime `ambiguous-frame-error` envelope for `:get-path` without doing path lookup/elision; otherwise read and elide against that resolved id. Route the refusal through the existing `run-eval` `:ok? false` -> `wire/err-text` path. Add one focused emitted-form/live-runtime-level regression for each shape (singular and batch), plus positive guards for an explicit frame and the sole/pinned-frame path.

## Non-goals

Do not redesign the four-tier resolver, invent a new error vocabulary/helper layer, change `snapshot`'s broad multi-frame mega-op semantics, or add policy/gates. Reuse `ambiguous-frame-error`, existing result envelopes, and operating-frame tools.

## Duplicate search

Used `rg` over `.beads/issues.jsonl` for `get-path.*ambiguous|ambiguous.*get-path`, `path-not-found.*frame|frame.*path-not-found`, `get-path.*current-frame`, `get-path.*multi-frame`, and `snapshot.*ambiguous-frame`: zero direct matches. Broader `rg 'get-path|ambiguous-frame|operating frame'` produced only closed, tangential skill/spec issues (notably `rf2-3cjhl` about retro prose); no bead owns this behavior.

## Posture fit

This is a small correction at an existing resolution boundary: no new abstraction, option, policy, or compatibility layer. It makes the minimal ergonomic API tell the truth and immediately presents the programmer/agent with the recovery tools that already ship. That is high-leverage pre-alpha polish without gold-plating.

## Uncertainty

Static proof is high-confidence and closes through source composition. No browser/runtime was launched during review because the review brief forbade runtime mutations. The best regression may sit in the Pair preload runtime tests rather than the current canned conformance corpus; acceptance requires executing the emitted form/real branch, not a particular test file.

Reviewed at `afe446ea71bf7d0eb2e4ce5960caca864a091778` on 2026-09-04.
acceptance_criteria:
- With two app frames, no session pin, and no `frame` arg, singular `get-path` returns MCP `isError: true` with `{:ok? false :reason :ambiguous-frame :operation :get-path :available-frames [...] :hint ...}`; it does not emit `:path-not-found`.
- The same setup with `paths` returns the same refusal; it does not emit an `:ok? true` all-missing results map.
- An explicit `frame`, a valid session pin, and a sole-app-frame session continue to return the existing hit/miss shapes and use the resolved frame for elision.
